\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{C++11 standard compliance}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:c-11-standard-compliance}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:cxx11}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A C++11 standard compatible compiler is a requirement for compiling LAMMPS.
LAMMPS version 3 March 2020 is the last version compatible with the previous
C++98 standard for the core code and most packages. Most currently used
C++ compilers are compatible with C++11, but some older ones may need extra
flags to enable C++11 compliance.  Example for GNU c++ 4.8.x:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{CCFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}g\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}std\PYG{o}{=}c++11
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Individual packages may require compliance with a later C++ standard
like C++14 or C++17.  These requirements will be documented with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{individual packages}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{FFT library}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:fft-library}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:fft}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the KSPACE package is included in a LAMMPS build, the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style pppm}}}} command performs 3d FFTs which
require use of an FFT library to compute 1d FFTs.  The KISS FFT
library is included with LAMMPS, but other libraries can be faster.
LAMMPS can use them if they are available on your system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, LAMMPS can use the \sphinxhref{https://icl-utk-edu.github.io/heffte/}{heFFTe} library for the MPI
communication algorithms, which comes with many optimizations for
special cases, e.g. leveraging available 2D and 3D FFTs in the back end
libraries and better pipelining for packing and communication.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{              }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} FFTW3 or MKL or KISS, default is FFTW3 if found,}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} else KISS}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}KOKKOS}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} FFTW3 or MKL or KISS or CUFFT or HIPFFT,}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default is KISS}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}SINGLE}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no (default), no = double precision}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}PACK}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} array (default) or pointer or memcpy}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}HEFFTE}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no (default), yes links to heFFTe}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the Kokkos variant of a package is compiled and selected at run time,
the FFT library selected by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_KOKKOS}} variable applies. Otherwise,
the FFT library selected by the FFT variable applies.
The same FFT settings apply to both. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_KOKKOS}} must be compatible with the
Kokkos back end \sphinxhyphen{} for example, when using the CUDA back end of Kokkos,
you must use either \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUFFT}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KISS}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually these settings are all that is needed.  If FFTW3 is
selected, then CMake will try to detect, if threaded FFTW
libraries are available and enable them by default.  This setting
is independent of whether OpenMP threads are enabled and a package
like KOKKOS or OPENMP is used.  If CMake cannot detect the FFT
library, you can set these variables to assist:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFTW3\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to FFTW3 include files}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFTW3\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to FFTW3 libraries}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFTW3\PYGZus{}OMP\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to FFTW3 OpenMP wrapper libraries}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}FFTW\PYGZus{}THREADS}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable using OpenMP threaded FFTW3 libraries}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{MKL\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ditto for Intel MKL library}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}MKL\PYGZus{}THREADS}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable using threaded FFTs with MKL libraries}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{MKL\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to MKL libraries}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}HEFFTE\PYGZus{}BACKEND}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} FFTW or MKL or empty/undefined for the stock}
\PYG{+w}{                            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} heFFTe back end}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Heffte\PYGZus{}ROOT}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to an existing heFFTe installation}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
heFFTe comes with a builtin (= stock) back end for FFTs, i.e. a
default internal FFT implementation; however, this stock back
end is intended for testing purposes only and is not optimized
for production runs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To change the FFT library to be used and its options, you have to edit
your machine Makefile. Below are examples how the makefile variables
could be changed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}\PYGZlt{}NAME\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} where \PYGZlt{}NAME\PYGZgt{} is KISS (default), FFTW3,}
\PYG{c}{                              \PYGZsh{} FFTW (same as FFTW3), or MKL}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}KOKKOS\PYGZus{}\PYGZlt{}NAME\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} where \PYGZlt{}NAME\PYGZgt{} is KISS (default), FFTW3,}
\PYG{c}{                              \PYGZsh{} FFTW (same as FFTW3), MKL, CUFFT, or HIPFFT}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}SINGLE\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} do not specify for double precision}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}FFTW\PYGZus{}THREADS\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable using threaded FFTW3 libraries}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}MKL\PYGZus{}THREADS\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable using threaded FFTs with MKL libraries}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}PACK\PYGZus{}ARRAY\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} or \PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}PACK\PYGZus{}POINTER or \PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}PACK\PYGZus{}MEMCPY}
\PYG{c}{                             \PYGZsh{} default is FFT\PYGZus{}PACK\PYGZus{}ARRAY if not specified}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}I/usr/local/include
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}L/usr/local/lib

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} hipFFT either precision}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lhipfft

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} cuFFT either precision}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lcufft

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} FFTW3 double precision}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lfftw3

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} FFTW3 double precision with threads (needs \PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}FFTW\PYGZus{}THREADS)}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lfftw3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lfftw3\PYGZus{}omp

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} FFTW3 single precision}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lfftw3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lfftw3f

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} serial MKL with Intel compiler}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}intel\PYGZus{}lp64\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}sequential\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}core

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} serial MKL with GNU compiler}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}gf\PYGZus{}lp64\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}sequential\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}core

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} threaded MKL with Intel compiler}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}intel\PYGZus{}lp64\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}intel\PYGZus{}thread\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}core

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} threaded MKL with GNU compiler}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}gf\PYGZus{}lp64\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}gnu\PYGZus{}thread\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}core

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} MKL with automatic runtime selection of interface libs}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}lmkl\PYGZus{}rt
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As with CMake, you do not need to set paths in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_INC}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_PATH}}, if the compiler can find the FFT header and library
files in its default search path.  You must specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_LIB}}
with the appropriate FFT libraries to include in the link.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Traditional make can also link to heFFTe using an existing installation

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{include \PYGZlt{}path\PYGZhy{}to\PYGZhy{}heffte\PYGZhy{}installation\PYGZgt{}/share/heffte/HeffteMakefile.in}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}HEFFTE\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}HEFFTE\PYGZus{}FFTW\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}heffte\PYGZus{}include\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}heffte\PYGZus{}link\PYG{k}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}heffte\PYGZus{}libs\PYG{k}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The heFFTe install path will contain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HeffteMakefile.in}}.
which will define the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heffte\_}} include variables needed to link to heFFTe from
an external project using traditional make.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_HEFFTE}} is required to switch to using heFFTe, while the optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_HEFFTE\_FFTW}}
selects the desired heFFTe back end, e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_HEFFTE\_FFTW}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_HEFFTE\_MKL}},
omitting the variable will default to the \sphinxtitleref{stock} back end.
The heFFTe \sphinxtitleref{stock} back end is intended to be used for testing and debugging,
but is not performance optimized for large scale production runs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://github.com/mborgerding/kissfft}{KISS FFT library} is
included in the LAMMPS distribution.  It is portable across all
platforms.  Depending on the size of the FFTs and the number of
processors used, the other libraries listed here can be faster.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, note that long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombics are only a portion of the
per\sphinxhyphen{}timestep CPU cost, FFTs are only a portion of long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombics,
and 1d FFTs are only a portion of the FFT cost (parallel communication
can be costly).  A breakdown of these timings is printed to the screen
at the end of a run when using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style pppm}}}} command. The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Screen and logfile output}}}} page gives more details.  A more detailed (and time
consuming) report of the FFT performance is generated with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_modify fftbench yes}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
FFTW is a fast, portable FFT library that should also work on any
platform and can be faster than the KISS FFT library.  You can download
it from \sphinxhref{https://www.fftw.org}{www.fftw.org}.  LAMMPS requires version
3.X; the legacy version 2.1.X is no longer supported.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Building FFTW for your box should be as simple as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./configure; make;
make install}}.  The install command typically requires root privileges
(e.g. invoke it via sudo), unless you specify a local directory with
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}} option of configure.  Type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./configure \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}help}} to see
various options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Intel MKL math library is part of the Intel compiler suite.  It
can be used with the Intel or GNU compiler (see the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_LIB}} setting
above).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cuFFT and hipFFT FFT libraries are packaged with NVIDIA’s CUDA and
AMD’s HIP installations, respectively. These FFT libraries require the
Kokkos acceleration package to be enabled and the Kokkos back end to be
GPU\sphinxhyphen{}resident (i.e., HIP or CUDA).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Performing 3d FFTs in parallel can be time\sphinxhyphen{}consuming due to data access
and required communication.  This cost can be reduced by performing
single\sphinxhyphen{}precision FFTs instead of double precision.  Single precision
means the real and imaginary parts of a complex datum are 4\sphinxhyphen{}byte floats.
Double precision means they are 8\sphinxhyphen{}byte doubles.  Note that Fourier
transform and related PPPM operations are somewhat less sensitive to
floating point truncation errors, and thus the resulting error is
generally less than the difference in precision. Using the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_SINGLE}} setting trades off a little accuracy for reduced memory
use and parallel communication costs for transposing 3d FFT data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_SINGLE}} with FFTW3, you may need to ensure that
the FFTW3 installation includes support for single\sphinxhyphen{}precision.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When compiler FFTW3 from source, you can do the following, which should
produce the additional libraries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{libfftw3f.a}} and/or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{libfftw3f.so}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }clean
./configure\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}enable\PYGZhy{}single\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Performing 3d FFTs requires communication to transpose the 3d FFT
grid.  The data packing/unpacking for this can be done in one of 3
modes (ARRAY, POINTER, MEMCPY) as set by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFT\_PACK}} syntax above.
Depending on the machine, the size of the FFT grid, the number of
processors used, one option may be slightly faster.  The default is
ARRAY mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DFFT\_HEFFTE}} CMake will first look for an existing
install with hints provided by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DHeffte\_ROOT}}, as recommended by the
CMake standard and note that the name is case sensitive. If CMake cannot
find a heFFTe installation with the correct back end (e.g., FFTW or
MKL), it will attempt to download and build the library automatically.
In this case, LAMMPS CMake will also accept all heFFTe specific
variables listed in the \sphinxhref{https://mkstoyanov.bitbucket.io/heffte/md\_doxygen\_installation.html}{heFFTe documentation}
and those variables will be passed into the heFFTe build.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\clearpage


\subsection{Size of LAMMPS integer types and size limits}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:size-of-lammps-integer-types-and-size-limits}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS uses a few custom integer data types, which can be defined as
either 4\sphinxhyphen{}byte (= 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit) or 8\sphinxhyphen{}byte (= 64\sphinxhyphen{}bit) integers at compile time.
This has an impact on the size of a system that can be simulated, or how
large counters can become before “rolling over”.  The default setting of
“smallbig” is almost always adequate.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With CMake the choice of integer types is made via setting a
variable during configuration.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}SIZES}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} smallbig (default) or bigbig or smallsmall}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the variable is not set explicitly, “smallbig” is used.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want a setting different from the default, you need to edit the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LMP\_INC}} variable setting your machine Makefile.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}SMALLBIG\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} or \PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}BIGBIG or \PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}SMALLSMALL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default setting is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_SMALLBIG}} if nothing is specified
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\(1 \le i \le 2^{31} (= 2.147 \cdot 10^9)\)
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(1 \le i \le 2^{63} (= 9.223 \cdot 10^{18})\)
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(1 \le i \le 2^{31} (= 2.147 \cdot 10^9)\)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
Image flag values
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(-512 \le i \le 511\)
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(- 1\,048\,576 \le i \le 1\,048\,575\)
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(-512 \le i \le 511\)
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabular}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “bigbig” setting increases the size of image flags and atom IDs over
“smallbig” and the “smallsmall” setting is only needed if your machine
does not support 64\sphinxhyphen{}bit integers or incurs performance penalties when
using them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are limits for the core of the LAMMPS code, specific features or
some styles may impose additional limits.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-atc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{ATC}}}} package cannot be compiled with the “bigbig” setting.
Also, there are limitations when using the library interface where some
functions with known issues have been replaced by dummy calls printing a
corresponding error message rather than crashing randomly or corrupting
data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom IDs are not required for atomic systems which do not store bond
topology information, though IDs are enabled by default.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify id no}}}} command will turn them off.  Atom
IDs are required for molecular systems with bond topology (bonds,
angles, dihedrals, etc).  Similarly, some force or compute or fix styles
require atom IDs.  Thus, if you model a molecular system or use one of
those styles with more than 2 billion atoms, you need the “bigbig”
setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of the total system size limits, the maximum number of atoms
per MPI rank (local + ghost atoms) is limited to 2 billion for atomic
systems and 500 million for systems with bonds (the additional
restriction is due to using the 2 upper bits of the local atom index
in neighbor lists for storing special bonds info).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Image flags store 3 values per atom in a single integer, which count the
number of times an atom has moved through the periodic box in each
dimension.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} manual page for a discussion.  If
an atom moves through the periodic box more than this limit, the value
will “roll over”, e.g. from 511 to \sphinxhyphen{}512, which can cause diagnostics
like the mean\sphinxhyphen{}squared displacement, as calculated by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_msd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
msd}}}} command, to be faulty.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that the GPU package requires its lib/gpu library to be
compiled with the same size setting, or the link will fail.  A CMake
build does this automatically.  When building with make, the setting
in whichever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/Makefile}} is used must be the same as above.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Output of JPEG, PNG, and movie files}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:output-of-jpeg-png-and-movie-files}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:graphics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} command has options to output JPEG or
PNG image files.  Likewise, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump movie}}}} command
outputs movie files in a variety of movie formats.  Using these options
requires the following settings:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{WITH\PYGZus{}JPEG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no}
\PYG{+w}{                      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default = yes if CMake finds JPEG development files, else no}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{WITH\PYGZus{}PNG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no}
\PYG{+w}{                      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default = yes if CMake finds PNG and ZLIB development files,}
\PYG{+w}{                      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} else no}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{WITH\PYGZus{}FFMPEG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no}
\PYG{+w}{                      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default = yes if CMake can find ffmpeg, else no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually these settings are all that is needed.  If CMake cannot
find the graphics header, library, executable files, you can set
these variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{JPEG\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to jpeglib.h header file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{JPEG\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to libjpeg.a (.so) file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PNG\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to png.h header file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PNG\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to libpng.a (.so) file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{ZLIB\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to zlib.h header file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{ZLIB\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to libz.a (.so) file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FFMPEG\PYGZus{}EXECUTABLE}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to ffmpeg executable}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}JPEG\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}PNG\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}FFMPEG\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZlt{}other\PYG{+w}{ }LMP\PYGZus{}INC\PYG{+w}{ }settings\PYGZgt{}

\PYG{n+nv}{JPG\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}I/usr/local/include\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to jpeglib.h, png.h, zlib.h headers}
\PYG{c}{                                 \PYGZsh{} if make cannot find them}
\PYG{n+nv}{JPG\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}L/usr/lib\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} paths to libjpeg.a, libpng.a, libz.a (.so)}
\PYG{c}{                                 \PYGZsh{} files if make cannot find them}
\PYG{n+nv}{JPG\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}ljpeg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lpng\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lz\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} library names}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As with CMake, you do not need to set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JPG\_INC}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JPG\_PATH}},
if make can find the graphics header and library files in their
default system locations.  You must specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JPG\_LIB}} with a
list of graphics libraries to include in the link.  You must make
certain that the ffmpeg executable (or ffmpeg.exe on Windows) is
in a directory where LAMMPS can find it at runtime; that is
usually a directory list in your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PATH}} environment variable.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffmpeg}} to output movie files requires that your machine
supports the “popen” function in the standard runtime library.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On some clusters with high\sphinxhyphen{}speed networks, using the fork()
library call (required by popen()) can interfere with the fast
communication library and lead to simulations using ffmpeg to hang or
crash.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Read or write compressed files}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:read-or-write-compressed-files}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:gzip}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If this option is enabled, large files can be read or written with
compression by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gzip}} or similar tools by several LAMMPS commands,
including {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}.  Supported compression tools and algorithms are currently
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gzip}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bzip2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{zstd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xz}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lz4}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lzma}} (via xz).
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{WITH\PYGZus{}GZIP}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no}
\PYG{+w}{                    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default is yes if CMake can find the gzip program}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}GZIP\PYG{+w}{   }\PYGZlt{}other\PYG{+w}{ }LMP\PYGZus{}INC\PYG{+w}{ }settings\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option requires that your operating system fully supports the
“popen()” function in the standard runtime library and that a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gzip}}
or other executable can be found by LAMMPS in the standard search path
during a run.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On clusters with high\sphinxhyphen{}speed networks, using the “fork()” library call
(required by “popen()”) can interfere with the fast communication
library and lead to simulations using compressed output or input to
hang or crash. For selected operations, compressed file I/O is also
available using a compression library instead, which is what the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-compress}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{COMPRESS package}}}} enables.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Support for downloading files}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:support-for-downloading-files}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:libcurl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{geturl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{geturl command}}}} command uses the \sphinxhref{https://curl.se/libcurl/}{the libcurl library} to download files.  This requires that
LAMMPS is compiled accordingly which needs the following settings:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{WITH\PYGZus{}CURL}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no}
\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default = yes if CMake finds CURL development files, else no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually these settings are all that is needed.  If CMake cannot
find the graphics header, library, executable files, you can set
these variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CURL\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to folder which contains curl.h header file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CURL\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to libcurls.a (.so) file}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}CURL\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZlt{}other\PYG{+w}{ }LMP\PYGZus{}INC\PYG{+w}{ }settings\PYGZgt{}

\PYG{n+nv}{CURL\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}I/usr/local/include\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to curl folder with curl.h}
\PYG{n+nv}{CURL\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}L/usr/lib\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} paths to libcurl.a(.so) if make cannot find it}
\PYG{n+nv}{CURL\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lcurl\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} library names}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As with CMake, you do not need to set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CURL\_INC}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CURL\_PATH}},
if make can find the libcurl header and library files in their
default system locations.  You must specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CURL\_LIB}} with a
paths or linker flags to link to libcurl.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Memory allocation alignment}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:memory-allocation-alignment}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:align}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This setting enables the use of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{posix\_memalign()}} call instead of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{malloc()}} when LAMMPS allocates large chunks of memory.  Vector
instructions on CPUs may become more efficient, if dynamically allocated
memory is aligned on larger\sphinxhyphen{}than\sphinxhyphen{}default byte boundaries.  On most
current operating systems, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{malloc()}} implementation returns
pointers that are aligned to 16\sphinxhyphen{}byte boundaries. Using SSE vector
instructions efficiently, however, requires memory blocks being aligned
on 64\sphinxhyphen{}byte boundaries.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}MEMALIGN}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 0, 8, 16, 32, 64 (default)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS\_MEMALIGN}} value of 0 to disable using
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{posix\_memalign()}} and revert to using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{malloc()}} C\sphinxhyphen{}library
function instead.  When compiling LAMMPS for Windows systems,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{malloc()}} will always be used and this setting is ignored.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}MEMALIGN\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 8, 16, 32, 64}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_MEMALIGN}}, if you want to have memory
allocated with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{malloc()}} function call
instead. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_MEMALIGN}} \sphinxstylestrong{cannot} be used on Windows, as
Windows different function calls with different semantics for
allocating aligned memory, that are not compatible with how LAMMPS
manages its dynamical memory.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Workaround for long long integers}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:workaround-for-long-long-integers}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:longlong}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If your system or MPI version does not recognize “long long” data
types, the following setting will be needed.  It converts “long long”
to a “long” data type, which should be the desired 8\sphinxhyphen{}byte integer on
those systems:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}LONGLONG\PYGZus{}TO\PYGZus{}LONG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no (default)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}LONGLONG\PYGZus{}TO\PYGZus{}LONG\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZlt{}other\PYG{+w}{ }LMP\PYGZus{}INC\PYG{+w}{ }settings\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Exception handling when using LAMMPS as a library}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:exception-handling-when-using-lammps-as-a-library}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:exceptions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS errors do not kill the calling code, but throw an exception.  In
the C\sphinxhyphen{}library interface, the call stack is unwound and control returns
to the caller, e.g. to Python or a code that is coupled to LAMMPS. The
error status can then be queried.  When using C++ directly, the calling
code has to be set up to \sphinxstyleemphasis{catch} exceptions thrown from within LAMMPS.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When LAMMPS is running in parallel, it is not always possible to
cleanly recover from an exception since not all parallel ranks may
throw an exception and thus other MPI ranks may get stuck waiting for
messages from the ones with errors.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Trigger selected floating\sphinxhyphen{}point exceptions}
\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:trigger-selected-floating-point-exceptions}}\label{\detokenize{Build_settings:trap-fpe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Many kinds of CPUs have the capability to detect when a calculation
results in an invalid math operation, like a division by zero or calling
the square root with a negative argument.  The default behavior on
most operating systems is to continue and have values for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} (= not
a number) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Inf}} (= infinity).  This allows software to detect and
recover from such conditions.  This behavior can be changed, however,
often through use of compiler flags.  On Linux systems (or more general
on systems using the GNU C library), these so\sphinxhyphen{}called floating\sphinxhyphen{}point traps
can also be selectively enabled through library calls.  LAMMPS supports
that by setting the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_TRAP\_FPE}} pre\sphinxhyphen{}processor define.  As it is
done in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{main()}} function, this applies only to the standalone
executable, not the library.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}TUNE\PYGZus{}FLAGS}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}TRAP\PYGZus{}FPE
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}TRAP\PYGZus{}FPE\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZlt{}other\PYG{+w}{ }LMP\PYGZus{}INC\PYG{+w}{ }settings\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After compilation with this flag set, the LAMMPS executable will stop
and produce a core dump when a division by zero, overflow, illegal math
function argument or other invalid floating point operation is encountered.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Include packages in build}
\label{\detokenize{Build_package:include-packages-in-build}}\label{\detokenize{Build_package::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In LAMMPS, a package is a group of files that enable a specific set of
features.  For example, force fields for molecular systems or
rigid\sphinxhyphen{}body constraints are in packages.  In the src directory, each
package is a subdirectory with the package name in capital letters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An overview of packages is given on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Packages}}}} doc
page.  Brief overviews of each package are on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Packages details}}}} page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When building LAMMPS, you can choose to include or exclude each
package.  Generally, there is no need to include a package if you
never plan to use its features.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you get a run\sphinxhyphen{}time error that a LAMMPS command or style is
“unknown”, it is often because the command is contained in a package,
and your build did not include that package.  If the command or style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{is} available in a package included in the LAMMPS distribution,
the error message will indicate which package would be needed.
Running LAMMPS with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}h command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}}
will print \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} optional commands and packages that were enabled
when building that executable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the majority of packages, if you follow the single step below to
include it, you can then build LAMMPS exactly the same as you would
without any packages installed.  A few packages may require additional
steps, as explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build extras}}}} page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These links take you to the extra instructions for those select
packages:


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabulary}{\linewidth}[t]{TTTTTT}
\sphinxtoprule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:adios}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{ADIOS}}}}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
The mechanism for including packages is simple but different for CMake
versus make.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D \PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}NAME}\PYG{o}{=}value          \PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no (default)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D \PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}MANYBODY}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\PYGZhy{}D \PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}INTEL}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All packages are included the same way.  See the shortcut section
below for how to install many packages at once with CMake.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you switch between building with CMake and make builds, no
packages in the src directory can be installed when you invoke
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake}}.  CMake will give an error if that is not the case,
indicating how you can uninstall all packages in the src dir.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }lammps/src
make\PYG{+w}{ }ps\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} check which packages are currently installed}
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install a package with name}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} uninstall a package with name}
make\PYG{+w}{ }mpi\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build LAMMPS with whatever packages are now installed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}rigid
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}intel
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All packages are included the same way.  See the shortcut section
below for how to install many packages at once with make.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You must always re\sphinxhyphen{}build LAMMPS (via make) after installing or
uninstalling a package, for the action to take effect. The
included dependency tracking will make certain only files that
are required to be rebuilt are recompiled.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot install or uninstall packages and build LAMMPS in a
single make command with multiple targets, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make
yes\sphinxhyphen{}colloid mpi}}.  This is because the make procedure creates
a list of source files that will be out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}date for the build
if the package configuration changes within the same command.
You can include or exclude multiple packages in a single make
command, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make yes\sphinxhyphen{}colloid no\sphinxhyphen{}manybody}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\subsection{Information for both build systems}
\label{\detokenize{Build_package:information-for-both-build-systems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Almost all packages can be included or excluded in a LAMMPS build,
independent of the other packages.  However, some packages include files
derived from files in other packages.  LAMMPS checks for this and does
the right thing.  Individual files are only included if their
dependencies are already included.  Likewise, if a package is excluded,
other files dependent on that package are also excluded.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default no packages are installed.  Prior to August 2018, however,
if you downloaded a tarball, 3 packages (KSPACE, MANYBODY, MOLECULE)
were pre\sphinxhyphen{}installed via the traditional make procedure in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}}
directory.  That is no longer the case, so that CMake will build
as\sphinxhyphen{}is without needing to uninstall those packages.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{CMake presets for installing many packages}
\label{\detokenize{Build_package:cmake-presets-for-installing-many-packages}}\label{\detokenize{Build_package:cmake-presets}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of specifying all the CMake options via the command\sphinxhyphen{}line,
CMake allows initializing its settings cache using script files.
These are regular CMake files which can manipulate and set CMake
variables (which represent selected options), and can also contain
control flow constructs for more complex operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS includes several of these files to define configuration
“presets”, similar to the options that exist for the Make based
system. Using these files, you can enable/disable portions of the
available packages in LAMMPS. If you need a custom preset, you can
make a copy of one of them and modify it to suit your needs.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable just a few core packages}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/basic.cmake\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable most packages}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/most.cmake\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable packages which download sources or potential files}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/download.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} disable packages that do require extra libraries or tools}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/nolib.cmake\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} change settings to use the Clang compilers by default}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/clang.cmake\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} change settings to use the GNU compilers by default}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/gcc.cmake\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} change settings to use the Intel compilers by default}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/intel.cmake\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} change settings to use the PGI compilers by default}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/pgi.cmake\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable all packages}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/all\PYGZus{}on.cmake\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} disable all packages}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/all\PYGZus{}off.cmake\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}  compile with MinGW cross\PYGZhy{}compilers}
mingw64\PYGZhy{}cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/mingw\PYGZhy{}cross.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} compile serial multi\PYGZhy{}arch binaries on macOS}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/macos\PYGZhy{}multiarch.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Presets that have names starting with “windows” are specifically for
compiling LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_windows::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{natively on Windows}}}} and
presets that have names starting with “kokkos” are specifically for
selecting configurations for compiling LAMMPS with {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:kokkos}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{KOKKOS}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Running cmake this way manipulates the CMake settings cache in your
current build directory.  You can combine multiple presets and options
in a single cmake run, or change settings incrementally by running
cmake with new flags.  If you use a present for selecting a set of
compilers, it will reset all settings from previous CMake runs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{Build_package:example}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build LAMMPS with most commonly used packages, but then remove}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} those requiring additional library or tools, but still enable}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GPU package and configure it for using CUDA. You can run.}
mkdir\PYG{+w}{ }build
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }build
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/most.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/nolib.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}GPU}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}API}\PYG{o}{=}cuda\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} to add another package, say BODY to the previous configuration you can run:}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}BODY}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} to reset the package selection from above to the default of no packages}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} but leaving all other settings untouched. You can run:}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/all\PYGZus{}off.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Make shortcuts for installing many packages}
\label{\detokenize{Build_package:make-shortcuts-for-installing-many-packages}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following commands are useful for managing package source files
and their installation when building LAMMPS via traditional make.
Just type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} in lammps/src to see a one\sphinxhyphen{}line summary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These commands install/uninstall sets of packages:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}all\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install all packages}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}all\PYG{+w}{                         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} check for changes and uninstall all packages}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}installed\PYG{+w}{                   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} only check and uninstall installed packages}
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}basic\PYG{+w}{                      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install a few commonly used packages\PYGZsq{}}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}basic\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} remove a few commonly used packages\PYGZsq{}}
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}most\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install most packages w/o libs\PYGZsq{}}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}most\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} remove most packages w/o libs\PYGZsq{}}
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}lib\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install packages that require extra libraries}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}lib\PYG{+w}{                         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} uninstall packages that require extra libraries}
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}ext\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install packages that require external libraries}
make\PYG{+w}{ }no\PYGZhy{}ext\PYG{+w}{                         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} uninstall packages that require external libraries}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
which install/uninstall various sets of packages.  Typing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make
package}} will list all the these commands.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Installing or uninstalling a package for the make based build process
works by simply copying files back and forth between the main source
directory src and the subdirectories with the package name (e.g.
src/KSPACE, src/ATC), so that the files are included or excluded
when LAMMPS is built.  Only source files in the src folder will be
compiled.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following make commands help manage files that exist in both the
src directory and in package subdirectories.  You do not normally
need to use these commands unless you are editing LAMMPS files or are
updating LAMMPS via git.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make package\sphinxhyphen{}status}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make ps}} to show which packages are
currently installed.  For those that are installed, it will list any
files that are different in the src directory and package
subdirectory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make package\sphinxhyphen{}installed}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make pi}} to show which packages are
currently installed, without listing the status of packages that are
not installed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make package\sphinxhyphen{}update}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make pu}} to overwrite src files with
files from the package subdirectories if the package is installed.  It
should be used after the checkout has been {\hyperref[\detokenize{Install_git::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{updated or changed
with git}}}}, this will only update the files in the package
subdirectories, but not the copies in the src folder.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make package\sphinxhyphen{}overwrite}} to overwrite files in the package
subdirectories with src files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make package\sphinxhyphen{}diff}} to list all differences between pairs of
files in both the source directory and the package directory.

\sphinxstepscope
