\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{COMPRESS package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:compress-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:compress}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package you must have the \sphinxhref{https://zlib.net}{zlib compression library} available on your system to build dump styles with
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/gz}} suffix.  There are also styles using the
\sphinxhref{https://facebook.github.io/zstd/}{Zstandard} library which have a
‘/zstd’ suffix.  The zstd library version must be at least 1.4.  Older
versions use an incompatible API and thus LAMMPS will fail to compile.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If CMake cannot find the zlib library or include files, you can set
these variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{ZLIB\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to zlib.h header file}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{ZLIB\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to libz.a (.so) file}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for Zstandard compression is auto\sphinxhyphen{}detected and for that
CMake depends on the \sphinxhref{https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/pkg-config/}{pkg\sphinxhyphen{}config} tool to
identify the necessary flags to compile with this library, so the
corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{libzstandard.pc}} file must be in a folder where
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pkg\sphinxhyphen{}config}} can find it, which may require adding it to the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PKG\_CONFIG\_PATH}} environment variable.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To include support for Zstandard compression, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_ZSTD}}
must be added to the compiler flags.  If make cannot find the
libraries, you can edit the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/compress/Makefile.lammps}}
to specify the paths and library names.  This must be done
\sphinxstylestrong{before} the package is installed.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{GPU package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:gpu-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:gpu}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must choose options for precision and
which GPU hardware to build for. The GPU package currently supports
three different types of backends: OpenCL, CUDA and HIP.


\subsubsection{CMake build}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:cmake-build}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}API}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = opencl (default) or cuda or hip}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}PREC}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} precision setting}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = double or mixed (default) or single}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} primary GPU hardware choice for GPU\PYGZus{}API=cuda}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = sm\PYGZus{}XX (see below, default is sm\PYGZus{}50)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}DEBUG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable debug code in the GPU package library,}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} mostly useful for developers}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = yes or no (default)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = path to HIP installation. Must be set if}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GPU\PYGZus{}API=HIP}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} primary GPU hardware choice for GPU\PYGZus{}API=hip}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value depends on selected HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} default is \PYGZsq{}gfx906\PYGZsq{} for HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM=amd and \PYGZsq{}sm\PYGZus{}50\PYGZsq{} for}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM=nvcc}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}DEVICE\PYGZus{}SORT}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enables GPU sorting}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = yes (default) or no}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CUDPP\PYGZus{}OPT}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use GPU binning with CUDA (should be off for modern GPUs)}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enables CUDA Performance Primitives, must be \PYGZdq{}no\PYGZdq{} for}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} CUDA\PYGZus{}MPS\PYGZus{}SUPPORT=yes}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = yes or no (default)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CUDA\PYGZus{}MPS\PYGZus{}SUPPORT}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enables some tweaks required to run with active}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} nvidia\PYGZhy{}cuda\PYGZhy{}mps daemon}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = yes or no (default)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CUDA\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}MULTIARCH}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enables building CUDA kernels for all supported GPU}
\PYG{+w}{                               }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} architectures}
\PYG{+w}{                               }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = yes (default) or no}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{USE\PYGZus{}STATIC\PYGZus{}OPENCL\PYGZus{}LOADER}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} downloads/includes OpenCL ICD loader library,}
\PYG{+w}{                                   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} no local OpenCL headers/libs needed}
\PYG{+w}{                                   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = yes (default) or no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU\_ARCH}} settings for different GPU hardware is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_30}} for Kepler (supported since CUDA 5 and until CUDA 10.x)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_35}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_37}} for Kepler (supported since CUDA 5 and until CUDA 11.x)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_50}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_52}} for Maxwell (supported since CUDA 6)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_60}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_61}} for Pascal (supported since CUDA 8)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_70}} for Volta (supported since CUDA 9)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_75}} for Turing (supported since CUDA 10)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_80}} or sm\_86 for Ampere (supported since CUDA 11, sm\_86 since CUDA 11.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_89}} for Lovelace (supported since CUDA 11.8)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_90}} for Hopper (supported since CUDA 12.0)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A more detailed list can be found, for example,
at \sphinxhref{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA\#GPUs\_supported}{Wikipedia’s CUDA article}

\sphinxAtStartPar
CMake can detect which version of the CUDA toolkit is used and thus will
try to include support for \sphinxstylestrong{all} major GPU architectures supported by
this toolkit.  Thus the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU\_ARCH}} setting is merely an optimization, to
have code for the preferred GPU architecture directly included rather
than having to wait for the JIT compiler of the CUDA driver to translate
it.  This behavior can be turned off (e.g. to speed up compilation) by
setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDA\_ENABLE\_MULTIARCH}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When compiling for CUDA or HIP with CUDA, version 8.0 or later of the
CUDA toolkit is required and a GPU architecture of Kepler or later,
which must \sphinxstyleemphasis{also} be supported by the CUDA toolkit in use \sphinxstylestrong{and} the
CUDA driver in use.  When compiling for OpenCL, OpenCL version 1.2 or
later is required and the GPU must be supported by the GPU driver and
OpenCL runtime bundled with the driver.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When building with CMake, you \sphinxstylestrong{must NOT} build the GPU library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu}} using the traditional build procedure. CMake will detect
files generated by that process and will terminate with an error and a
suggestion for how to remove them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are compiling for OpenCL, the default setting is to download,
build, and link with a static OpenCL ICD loader library and standard
OpenCL headers.  This way no local OpenCL development headers or library
needs to be present and only OpenCL compatible drivers need to be
installed to use OpenCL.  If this is not desired, you can set
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{USE\_STATIC\_OPENCL\_LOADER}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The GPU library has some multi\sphinxhyphen{}thread support using OpenMP.  If LAMMPS
is built with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D BUILD\_OMP=on}} this will also be enabled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are compiling with HIP, note that before running CMake you will
have to set appropriate environment variables. Some variables such as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HCC\_AMDGPU\_TARGET}} (for ROCm \textless{}= 4.0) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDA\_PATH}} are
necessary for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hipcc}} and the linker to work correctly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Aug2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the CHIP\sphinxhyphen{}SPV implementation of HIP is supported. It allows one to
run HIP code on Intel GPUs via the OpenCL or Level Zero backends. To use
CHIP\sphinxhyphen{}SPV, you must set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DHIP\_USE\_DEVICE\_SORT=OFF}} in your CMake
command line as CHIP\sphinxhyphen{}SPV does not yet support hipCUB. As of Summer 2022,
the use of HIP for Intel GPUs is experimental. You should only use this
option in preparations to run on Aurora system at Argonne.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} AMDGPU target (ROCm \PYGZlt{}= 4.0)}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM}\PYG{o}{=}hcc
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/HIP/install
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HCC\PYGZus{}AMDGPU\PYGZus{}TARGET}\PYG{o}{=}gfx906
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}GPU}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}API}\PYG{o}{=}HIP\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{o}{=}gfx906\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}COMPILER}\PYG{o}{=}hipcc\PYG{+w}{ }..
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}j\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} AMDGPU target (ROCm \PYGZgt{}= 4.1)}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM}\PYG{o}{=}amd
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/HIP/install
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}GPU}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}API}\PYG{o}{=}HIP\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{o}{=}gfx906\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}COMPILER}\PYG{o}{=}hipcc\PYG{+w}{ }..
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}j\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} CUDA target (not recommended, use GPU\PYGZus{}ARCH=cuda)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} !!! DO NOT set CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}COMPILER !!!}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM}\PYG{o}{=}nvcc
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/HIP/install
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CUDA\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/usr/local/cuda
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}GPU}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}API}\PYG{o}{=}HIP\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{o}{=}sm\PYGZus{}70\PYG{+w}{ }..
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}j\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} SPIR\PYGZhy{}V target (Intel GPUs)}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PLATFORM}\PYG{o}{=}spirv
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{HIP\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/HIP/install
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}COMPILER}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZlt{}hipcc/clang++\PYGZgt{}
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}GPU}\PYG{o}{=}on\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GPU\PYGZus{}API}\PYG{o}{=}HIP\PYG{+w}{ }..
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}j\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Traditional make}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:traditional-make}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must build the GPU library in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu}}.
You can do this manually if you prefer; follow the instructions in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/README}}.  Note that the GPU library uses MPI calls, so you must
use the same MPI library (or the STUBS library) settings as the main
LAMMPS code.  This also applies to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_BIGBIG}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_SMALLBIG}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_SMALLSMALL}} settings in whichever
Makefile you use.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also build the library in one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir,
using a command like these, which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/Install.py}}
script with the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}gpu

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build GPU library with default Makefile.linux}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}gpu\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create new Makefile.xk7.single, altered for single\PYGZhy{}precision}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}gpu\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m xk7 \PYGZhy{}p single \PYGZhy{}o xk7.single\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build GPU library with mixed precision and P100 using other settings in Makefile.mpi}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}gpu\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi \PYGZhy{}a sm\PYGZus{}60 \PYGZhy{}p mixed \PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this procedure starts with a Makefile.machine in lib/gpu, as
specified by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}m}} switch.  For your convenience, machine makefiles
for “mpi” and “serial” are provided, which have the same settings as
the corresponding machine makefiles in the main LAMMPS source
folder. In addition you can alter 4 important settings in the
Makefile.machine you start from via the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}c}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}}
switches (as in the examples above), and also save a copy of the new
Makefile if desired:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDA\_HOME}} = where NVIDIA CUDA software is installed on your system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDA\_ARCH}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sm\_XX}}, what GPU hardware you have, same as CMake \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU\_ARCH}} above

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDA\_PRECISION}} = precision (double, mixed, single)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTRAMAKE}} = which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.*}} file to copy to Makefile.lammps

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.cuda}} is set up to include support for multiple
GPU architectures as supported by the CUDA toolkit in use. This is done
through using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}gencode}} flag, which can be used multiple times and
thus support all GPU architectures supported by your CUDA compiler.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To enable GPU binning via CUDA performance primitives set the Makefile variable
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDPP\_OPT = \sphinxhyphen{}DUSE\_CUDPP \sphinxhyphen{}Icudpp\_mini}}.  This should \sphinxstylestrong{not} be used with
most modern GPUs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To support the CUDA multiprocessor server you can set the define
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DCUDA\_MPS\_SUPPORT}}.  Please note that in this case you must \sphinxstylestrong{not} use
the CUDA performance primitives and thus set the variable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDPP\_OPT}}
to empty.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The GPU library has some multi\sphinxhyphen{}thread support using OpenMP.  You need to add
the compiler flag that enables OpenMP to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CUDR\_OPTS}} Makefile variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the library build is successful, 3 files should be created:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/libgpu.a}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/nvc\_get\_devices}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/Makefile.lammps}}.  The latter has settings that enable LAMMPS
to link with CUDA libraries.  If the settings in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} for
your machine are not correct, the LAMMPS build will fail, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/Makefile.lammps}} may need to be edited.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you re\sphinxhyphen{}build the GPU library in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu}}, you should always
uninstall the GPU package in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}}, then re\sphinxhyphen{}install it and
re\sphinxhyphen{}build LAMMPS.  This is because the compilation of files in the GPU
package uses the library settings from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/gpu/Makefile.machine}}
used to build the GPU library.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{KIM package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:kim-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:kim}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, the KIM library with API v2 must be downloaded
and built on your system. It must include the KIM models that you want to
use with LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you would like to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim query}}}}
command, you also need to have libcurl installed with the matching
development headers and the curl\sphinxhyphen{}config tool.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you would like to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim property}}}}
command, you need to build LAMMPS with the PYTHON package installed
and linked to Python 3.6 or later. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:python}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{PYTHON package build info}}}}
for more details on this. After successfully building LAMMPS with Python, you
also need to install the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kim\sphinxhyphen{}property}} Python package, which can be easily
done using \sphinxstyleemphasis{pip} as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip install kim\sphinxhyphen{}property}}, or from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{conda\sphinxhyphen{}forge}
channel as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conda install kim\sphinxhyphen{}property}} if LAMMPS is built in Conda. More
detailed information is available at:
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/openkim/kim-property\#installing-kim-property}{kim\sphinxhyphen{}property installation}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to installing the KIM API, it is also necessary to install the
library of KIM models (interatomic potentials).
See \sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/usage/obtaining-models}{Obtaining KIM Models} to
learn how to install a pre\sphinxhyphen{}build binary of the OpenKIM Repository of Models.
See the list of all KIM models here: \sphinxurl{https://openkim.org/browse/models}

\sphinxAtStartPar
(Also note that when downloading and installing from source
the KIM API library with all its models, may take a long time (tens of
minutes to hours) to build.  Of course you only need to do that once.)
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}KIM}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download OpenKIM API v2 for build}
\PYG{+w}{                                }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}DEBUG\PYGZus{}CURL}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} set libcurl verbose mode on/off}
\PYG{+w}{                                }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = off (default) or on}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}NO\PYGZus{}SSL\PYGZus{}CHECK}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} tell libcurl to not verify the peer}
\PYG{+w}{                                }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{KIM\PYGZus{}EXTRA\PYGZus{}UNITTESTS}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enables extra unit tests}
\PYG{+w}{                                }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_KIM}} is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{yes}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on}}), the KIM API library
will be downloaded and built inside the CMake build directory.  If
the KIM library is already installed on your system (in a location
where CMake cannot find it), you may need to set the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PKG\_CONFIG\_PATH}} environment variable so that libkim\sphinxhyphen{}api can be
found, or run the command \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source kim\sphinxhyphen{}api\sphinxhyphen{}activate}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extra unit tests can only be available if they are explicitly requested
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KIM\_EXTRA\_UNITTESTS}} is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{yes}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on}})) and the prerequisites
are met. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:kim-extra-unittests}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{KIM Extra unit tests}}}} for
more details on this.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download and build the KIM library manually if you prefer;
follow the instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/kim/README}}.  You can also do
this in one step from the lammps/src directory, using a command like
these, which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/kim/Install.py}} script with
the specified args.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (re\PYGZhy{})install KIM API lib with only example models}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ditto plus one model}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b \PYGZhy{}a Glue\PYGZus{}Ercolessi\PYGZus{}Adams\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}324507536345\PYGZus{}001\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} install KIM API lib with all models}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b \PYGZhy{}a everything\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} add one model or model driver}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}n \PYGZhy{}a EAM\PYGZus{}Dynamo\PYGZus{}Ackland\PYGZus{}W\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}141627196590\PYGZus{}002\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use an existing KIM API installation at the provided location}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}p \PYGZlt{}prefix\PYGZgt{}\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ditto but add one model or driver}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}p \PYGZlt{}prefix\PYGZgt{} \PYGZhy{}a EAM\PYGZus{}Dynamo\PYGZus{}Ackland\PYGZus{}W\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}141627196590\PYGZus{}002\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}b}} option, the KIM library is built using its native
cmake build system.  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/kim/Install.py}} script supports a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CMAKE}} environment variable if the cmake executable is named other
than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake}} on your system.  Additional environment variables may be
provided on the command line for use by cmake.  For example, to use the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake3}} executable and tell it to use the gnu version 11 compilers
to build KIM, one could use the following command line.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (re\PYGZhy{})install KIM API lib using cmake3 and gnu v11 compilers}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} with only example models}
\PYG{n+nv}{CMAKE}\PYG{o}{=}cmake3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CXX}\PYG{o}{=}g++\PYGZhy{}11\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{CC}\PYG{o}{=}gcc\PYGZhy{}11\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{FC}\PYG{o}{=}gfortran\PYGZhy{}11\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}kim\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Settings for debugging OpenKIM web queries discussed below need to
be applied by adding them to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LMP\_INC}} variable through
editing the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.machine}} you are using.  For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{LMP\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLMP\PYGZus{}NO\PYGZus{}SSL\PYGZus{}CHECK
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\subsubsection{Debugging OpenKIM web queries in LAMMPS}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:debugging-openkim-web-queries-in-lammps}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LMP\_DEBUG\_CURL}} is set, the libcurl verbose mode will be turned
on, and any libcurl calls within the KIM web query display a lot of
information about libcurl operations.  You hardly ever want this set in
production use, you will almost always want this when you debug or
report problems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The libcurl library performs peer SSL certificate verification by
default.  This verification is done using a CA certificate store that
the SSL library can use to make sure the peer’s server certificate is
valid.  If SSL reports an error (“certificate verify failed”) during the
handshake and thus refuses further communicate with that server, you can
set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LMP\_NO\_SSL\_CHECK}} to override that behavior.  When LAMMPS is
compiled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LMP\_NO\_SSL\_CHECK}} set, libcurl does not verify the peer
and connection attempts will succeed regardless of the names in the
certificate. This option is insecure.  As an alternative, you can
specify your own CA cert path by setting the environment variable
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CURL\_CA\_BUNDLE}} to the path of your choice.  A call to the KIM web
query would get this value from the environment variable.


\subsubsection{KIM Extra unit tests (CMake only)}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:kim-extra-unit-tests-cmake-only}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:kim-extra-unittests}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
During development, testing, or debugging, if
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_development::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unit testing}}}} is enabled in LAMMPS, one can also
enable extra tests on {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{KIM commands}}}} by setting the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KIM\_EXTRA\_UNITTESTS}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{yes}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enabling the extra unit tests have some requirements,
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It requires to have internet access.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It requires to have libcurl installed with the matching development headers
and the curl\sphinxhyphen{}config tool.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It requires to build LAMMPS with the PYTHON package installed and linked to
Python 3.6 or later. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:python}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{PYTHON package build info}}}} for
more details on this.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It requires to have \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kim\sphinxhyphen{}property}} Python package installed, which can be
easily done using \sphinxstyleemphasis{pip} as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip install kim\sphinxhyphen{}property}}, or from the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{conda\sphinxhyphen{}forge} channel as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conda install kim\sphinxhyphen{}property}} if LAMMPS is built in
Conda. More detailed information is available at:
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/openkim/kim-property\#installing-kim-property}{kim\sphinxhyphen{}property installation}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is also necessary to install the following KIM models:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EAM\_Dynamo\_MendelevAckland\_2007v3\_Zr\_\_MO\_004835508849\_000}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EAM\_Dynamo\_ErcolessiAdams\_1994\_Al\_\_MO\_123629422045\_005}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LennardJones612\_UniversalShifted\_\_MO\_959249795837\_003}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/usage/obtaining-models}{Obtaining KIM Models}
to learn how to install a pre\sphinxhyphen{}built binary of the OpenKIM Repository of
Models or see
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/usage/obtaining-models/\#installing\_models}{Installing KIM Models}
to learn how to install the specific KIM models.

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{KOKKOS package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:kokkos-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:kokkos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the KOKKOS package requires choosing several settings.  You have
to select whether you want to compile with parallelization on the host
and whether you want to include offloading of calculations to a device
(e.g. a GPU).  The default setting is to have no host parallelization
and no device offloading.  In addition, you can select the hardware
architecture to select the instruction set.  Since most hardware is
backward compatible, you may choose settings for an older architecture
to have an executable that will run on this and newer architectures.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you run Kokkos on a different GPU architecture than what LAMMPS
was compiled with, there will be a delay during device initialization
while the just\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}time compiler is recompiling all GPU kernels for
the new hardware.  This is, however, only supported for GPUs of the
\sphinxstylestrong{same} major hardware version and different minor hardware versions,
e.g. 5.0 and 5.2 but not 5.2 and 6.0.  LAMMPS will abort with an
error message indicating a mismatch, if that happens.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The settings discussed below have been tested with LAMMPS and are
confirmed to work.  Kokkos is an active project with ongoing improvements
and projects working on including support for additional architectures.
More information on Kokkos can be found on the
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kokkos}{Kokkos GitHub project}.


\subsubsection{Available Architecture settings}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:available-architecture-settings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the possible choices for the Kokkos architecture ID.
They must be specified in uppercase.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This list was last updated for version 4.3.0 of the Kokkos library.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Basic CMake build settings:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For multicore CPUs using OpenMP, set these 2 variables.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ARCH\PYGZus{}HOSTARCH}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HOSTARCH = HOST from list above}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}OPENMP}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BUILD\PYGZus{}OMP}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please note that enabling OpenMP for KOKKOS requires that OpenMP is
also {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_basics:serial}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{enabled for the rest of LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Intel KNLs using OpenMP, set these variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ARCH\PYGZus{}KNL}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}OPENMP}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For NVIDIA GPUs using CUDA, set these variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ARCH\PYGZus{}HOSTARCH}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HOSTARCH = HOST from list above}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ARCH\PYGZus{}GPUARCH}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GPUARCH = GPU from list above}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}CUDA}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}OPENMP}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This will also enable executing FFTs on the GPU, either via the
internal KISSFFT library, or \sphinxhyphen{} by preference \sphinxhyphen{} with the cuFFT
library bundled with the CUDA toolkit, depending on whether CMake
can identify its location.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For AMD or NVIDIA GPUs using HIP, set these variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ARCH\PYGZus{}HOSTARCH}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HOSTARCH = HOST from list above}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ARCH\PYGZus{}GPUARCH}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GPUARCH = GPU from list above}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}HIP}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Kokkos\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}OPENMP}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This will enable FFTs on the GPU, either by the internal KISSFFT library
or with the hipFFT wrapper library, which will call out to the
platform\sphinxhyphen{}appropriate vendor library: rocFFT on AMD GPUs or cuFFT on
NVIDIA GPUs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To simplify compilation, five preset files are included in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake/presets}} folder, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}serial.cmake}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}openmp.cmake}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}cuda.cmake}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}hip.cmake}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}sycl.cmake}}.  They will enable
the KOKKOS package and enable some hardware choices.  For GPU
support those preset files must be customized to match the
hardware used. So to compile with CUDA device parallelization with
some common packages enabled, you can do the following:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mkdir\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYGZhy{}kokkos\PYGZhy{}cuda
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYGZhy{}kokkos\PYGZhy{}cuda
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/basic.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/kokkos\PYGZhy{}cuda.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Basic traditional make settings:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose which hardware to support in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.machine}} via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_DEVICES}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_ARCH}} settings.  See the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MAKE/OPTIONS/Makefile.kokkos*}} files for examples.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For multicore CPUs using OpenMP:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}DEVICES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }OpenMP
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }HOSTARCH\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HOSTARCH = HOST from list above}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Intel KNLs using OpenMP:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}DEVICES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }OpenMP
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }KNL
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For NVIDIA GPUs using CUDA:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}DEVICES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }Cuda
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }HOSTARCH,GPUARCH\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HOSTARCH = HOST from list above that is}
\PYG{c}{                                \PYGZsh{}            hosting the GPU}
\PYG{c}{                                \PYGZsh{} GPUARCH = GPU from list above}
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}CUDA\PYGZus{}OPTIONS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}enable\PYGZus{}lambda\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}CUFFT\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable use of cuFFT (optional)}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lcufft\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} link to cuFFT library}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For GPUs, you also need the following lines in your
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.machine}} before the CC line is defined.  They tell
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpicxx}} to use an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nvcc}} compiler wrapper, which will use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nvcc}} for compiling CUDA files and a C++ compiler for
non\sphinxhyphen{}Kokkos, non\sphinxhyphen{}CUDA files.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} For OpenMPI}
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ABSOLUTE\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}shell\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}KOKKOS\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{k}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{pwd}\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{k}{export }\PYG{n+nv}{OMPI\PYGZus{}CXX}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ABSOLUTE\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{k}{)}/config/nvcc\PYGZus{}wrapper
\PYG{n+nv}{CC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }mpicxx
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} For MPICH and derivatives}
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ABSOLUTE\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}shell\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}KOKKOS\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{k}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{pwd}\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{n+nv}{CC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }mpicxx\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}cxx\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ABSOLUTE\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{k}{)}/config/nvcc\PYGZus{}wrapper
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For AMD or NVIDIA GPUs using HIP:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}DEVICES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }HIP
\PYG{n+nv}{KOKKOS\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }HOSTARCH,GPUARCH\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HOSTARCH = HOST from list above that is}
\PYG{c}{                                \PYGZsh{}            hosting the GPU}
\PYG{c}{                                \PYGZsh{} GPUARCH = GPU from list above}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}INC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DFFT\PYGZus{}HIPFFT\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable use of hipFFT (optional)}
\PYG{n+nv}{FFT\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lhipfft\PYG{+w}{              }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} link to hipFFT library}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\subsubsection{Advanced KOKKOS compilation settings}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:advanced-kokkos-compilation-settings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are other allowed options when building with the KOKKOS package
that can improve performance or assist in debugging or profiling. Below
are some examples that may be useful in combination with LAMMPS.  For
the full list (which keeps changing as the Kokkos package itself evolves),
please consult the Kokkos library documentation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As alternative to using multi\sphinxhyphen{}threading via OpenMP
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_OPENMP=on}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_DEVICES=OpenMP}}) it is also
possible to use Posix threads directly (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_PTHREAD=on}}
or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_DEVICES=Pthread}}).  While binding of threads to individual
or groups of CPU cores is managed in OpenMP with environment variables,
you need assistance from either the “hwloc” or “libnuma” library for the
Pthread thread parallelization option. To enable use with CMake:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_HWLOC=on}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_LIBNUMA=on}}; and with
conventional make: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_USE\_TPLS=hwloc}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_USE\_TPLS=libnuma}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CMake option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_LIBRT=on}} or the makefile setting
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_USE\_TPLS=librt}} enables the use of a more accurate timer
mechanism on many Unix\sphinxhyphen{}like platforms for internal profiling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CMake option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_DEBUG=on}} or the makefile setting
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_DEBUG=yes}} enables printing of run\sphinxhyphen{}time
debugging information that can be useful. It also enables runtime
bounds checking on Kokkos data structures.  As to be expected, enabling
this option will negatively impact the performance and thus is only
recommended when developing a Kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}enabled style in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CMake option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DKokkos\_ENABLE\_CUDA\_UVM=on}} or the makefile
setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KOKKOS\_CUDA\_OPTIONS=enable\_lambda,force\_uvm}} enables the
use of CUDA “Unified Virtual Memory” (UVM) in Kokkos.  UVM allows to
transparently use RAM on the host to supplement the memory used on the
GPU (with some performance penalty) and thus enables running larger
problems that would otherwise not fit into the RAM on the GPU.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please note, that the LAMMPS KOKKOS package must \sphinxstylestrong{always} be compiled
with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{enable\_lambda} option when using GPUs.  The CMake configuration
will thus always enable it.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{LEPTON package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:lepton-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:lepton}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must build the Lepton library which is
included in the LAMMPS source distribution in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/lepton}} folder.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the recommended build procedure for using Lepton in
LAMMPS. No additional settings are normally needed besides
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_LEPTON=yes}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On x86 hardware the Lepton library will also include a just\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}time
compiler for faster execution.  This is auto detected but can
be explicitly disabled by setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D LEPTON\_ENABLE\_JIT=no}}
(or enabled by setting it to yes).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, one must build the Lepton library in lib/lepton.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be done manually in the same folder by using or adapting
one of the provided Makefiles: for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.serial}} for
the GNU C++ compiler, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.mpi}} for the MPI compiler wrapper.
The Lepton library is written in C++\sphinxhyphen{}11 and thus the C++ compiler
may need to be instructed to enable support for that.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In general, it is safer to use build setting consistent with the
rest of LAMMPS.  This is best carried out from the LAMMPS src
directory using a command like these, which simply invokes the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/lepton/Install.py}} script with the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}lepton

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}lepton\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}lepton\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “machine” argument of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}m}} flag is used to find a
Makefile.machine to use as build recipe.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build}} folder and the library \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/lepton/liblmplepton.a}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{MACHDYN package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:machdyn-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:machdyn}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must download the Eigen3 library.
Eigen3 is a template library, so you do not need to build it.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}EIGEN3\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download Eigen3, value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{EIGEN3\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to Eigen library (only needed if a}
\PYG{+w}{                              }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} custom location)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_EIGEN3}} is set, the Eigen3 library will be
downloaded and inside the CMake build directory.  If the Eigen3
library is already on your system (in a location where CMake
cannot find it), set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EIGEN3\_INCLUDE\_DIR}} to the directory the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Eigen3}} include file is in.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download the Eigen3 library manually if you prefer; follow
the instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/machdyn/README}}.  You can also do it in one
step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like these,
which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/machdyn/Install.py}} script with the
specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}machdyn

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download to lib/machdyn/eigen3}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}machdyn\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use existing Eigen installation in /usr/include/eigen3}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}machdyn\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}p /usr/include/eigen3\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that a symbolic (soft) link named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includelink}} is created
in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/machdyn}} to point to the Eigen dir.  When LAMMPS builds it
will use this link.  You should not need to edit the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/machdyn/Makefile.lammps}} file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-iap-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:mliap}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Building the ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP package requires including the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-ml-snap}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{ML\sphinxhyphen{}SNAP}}}} package.  There will be an error message if this requirement
is not satisfied.  Using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy} model also requires enabling
Python support, which in turn requires to include the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-python}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{PYTHON}}}} package \sphinxstylestrong{and} requires to have the \sphinxhref{https://cython.org}{cython} software installed and with it a working
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cythonize}} command.  This feature requires compiling LAMMPS with
Python version 3.6 or later.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{MLIAP\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}PYTHON}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable mliappy model (default is autodetect)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Without this setting, CMake will check whether it can find a
suitable Python version and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cythonize}} command and choose
the default accordingly.  During the build procedure the provided
.pyx file(s) will be automatically translated to C++ code and compiled.
Please do \sphinxstylestrong{not} run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cythonize}} manually in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP}} folder,
as that can lead to compilation errors if Python support is not enabled.
If you did it by accident, please remove the generated .cpp and .h files.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build uses the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/python/Makefile.mliap\_python}} file in the
compile/link process to add a rule to update the files generated by
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cythonize}} command in case the corresponding .pyx file(s) were
modified.  You may need to modify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/python/Makefile.lammps}}
if the LAMMPS build fails.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To enable building the ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP package with Python support enabled,
you need to add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DMLIAP\_PYTHON}} to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LMP\_INC}} variable in
your machine makefile.  You may have to manually run the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cythonize}} command on .pyx file(s) in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}} folder, if
this is not automatically done during installing the ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP
package.  Please do \sphinxstylestrong{not} run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cythonize}} in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP}}
folder, as that can lead to compilation errors if Python support
is not enabled.  If you did this by accident, please remove the
generated .cpp and .h files.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{OPT package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:opt-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:opt}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_OPT=yes}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The compiler flag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}restrict}} must be used to build LAMMPS with
the OPT package when using Intel compilers.  It should be added to
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CCFLAGS}} line of your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.machine}}.  See
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MAKE/OPTIONS/Makefile.opt}} for an example.

\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{POEMS package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:poems-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:poems}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_OPT=yes}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must build the POEMS library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/poems}}.  You can do this manually if you prefer; follow
the instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/poems/README}}.  You can also do it in
one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like these,
which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/poems/Install.py}} script with the
specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}poems

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}poems\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}poems\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with Intel Classic compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}poems\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m icc\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce two files: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/poems/libpoems.a}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/poems/Makefile.lammps}}.  The latter is copied from an
existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.*}} and has settings needed to build
LAMMPS with the POEMS library (though typically the settings are
just blank).  If necessary, you can edit/create a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/poems/Makefile.machine}} file for your system, which should
define an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTRAMAKE}} variable to specify a corresponding
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.machine}} file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{PYTHON package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:python-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:python}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Building with the PYTHON package requires you have a the Python development
headers and library available on your system, which needs to be a Python 2.7
version or a Python 3.x version.  Since support for Python 2.x has ended,
using Python 3.x is strongly recommended. See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/python/README}} for
additional details.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{Python\PYGZus{}EXECUTABLE}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to Python executable to use}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Without this setting, CMake will guess the default Python version
on your system.  To use a different Python version, you can either
create a virtualenv, activate it and then run cmake.  Or you can
set the Python\_EXECUTABLE variable to specify which Python
interpreter should be used.  Note note that you will also need to
have the development headers installed for this version,
e.g. python2\sphinxhyphen{}devel.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build uses the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/python/Makefile.lammps}} file in the
compile/link process to find Python.  You should only need to
create a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.*}} file (and copy it to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}}) if the LAMMPS build fails.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{VORONOI package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:voronoi-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:voronoi}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must download and build the
\sphinxhref{https://math.lbl.gov/voro++/}{Voro++ library} or install a
binary package provided by your operating system.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}VORO}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download Voro++ for build}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{VORO\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Voro++ library file}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (only needed if at custom location)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{VORO\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Voro++ include directory}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (only needed if at custom location)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_VORO}} is set, the Voro++ library will be downloaded
and built inside the CMake build directory.  If the Voro++ library
is already on your system (in a location CMake cannot find it),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VORO\_LIBRARY}} is the filename (plus path) of the Voro++ library
file, not the directory the library file is in.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VORO\_INCLUDE\_DIR}} is the directory the Voro++ include file is
in.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download and build the Voro++ library manually if you
prefer; follow the instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/voronoi/README}}.  You
can also do it in one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a
command like these, which simply invokes the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/voronoi/Install.py}} script with the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}voronoi

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build the default version in lib/voronoi/voro++\PYGZhy{}\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}voronoi\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use existing Voro++ installation in \PYGZdl{}HOME/voro++}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}voronoi\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}p }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}HOME}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/voro++}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build the 0.4.6 version in lib/voronoi/voro++\PYGZhy{}0.4.6}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}voronoi\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b \PYGZhy{}v voro++0.4.6\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that two symbolic (soft) links, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includelink}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblink}}, are created in lib/voronoi to point to the Voro++
source dir.  When LAMMPS builds in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}} it will use these
links.  You should not need to edit the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/voronoi/Makefile.lammps}} file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ADIOS package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:adios-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:adios}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ADIOS package requires the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/ornladios/ADIOS2}{ADIOS I/O library}, version 2.3.1 or newer. Make
sure that you have ADIOS built either with or without MPI to match if
you build LAMMPS with or without MPI.  ADIOS compilation settings for
LAMMPS are automatically detected, if the PATH and LD\_LIBRARY\_PATH
environment variables have been updated for the local ADIOS installation
and the instructions below are followed for the respective build
systems.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{ADIOS2\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path is where ADIOS 2.x is installed}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}ADIOS}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Turn on the ADIOS package before building LAMMPS. If the
ADIOS 2.x software is installed in PATH, there is nothing else to
do:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}adios
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
otherwise, set ADIOS2\_DIR environment variable when turning on the package:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{ADIOS2\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}adios\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path is where ADIOS 2.x is installed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ATC package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:atc-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:atc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ATC package requires the MANYBODY package also be installed.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_ATC=yes}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_MANYBODY=yes}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must build the ATC library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc}}.  You can do this manually if you prefer; follow the
instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc/README}}.  You can also do it in one
step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like these,
which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc/Install.py}} script with the
specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}atc

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler and MPI STUBS (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}atc\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}atc\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with Intel Classic compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}atc\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m icc\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce two files: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc/libatc.a}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc/Makefile.lammps}}.  The latter is copied from an
existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.*}} and has settings needed to build
LAMMPS with the ATC library.  If necessary, you can edit/create a
new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc/Makefile.machine}} file for your system, which
should define an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTRAMAKE}} variable to specify a corresponding
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.\textless{}machine\textgreater{}}} file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the Makefile.lammps file has settings for the BLAS and
LAPACK linear algebra libraries.  As explained in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/atc/README}} these can either exist on your system, or you
can use the files provided in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}}.  In the latter case
you also need to build the library in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}} with a
command like these:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU Fortran compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m g++\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{AWPMD package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:awpmd-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:awpmd}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_AQPMD=yes}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

Before building LAMMPS, you must build the AWPMD library in

which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/awpmd/Install.py}} script with the
specified args:

make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}awpmd\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

Note that the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} file has settings for the BLAS

you also need to build the library in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}} with a
command like these:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m g++\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{COLVARS package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:colvars-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:colvar}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This package enables the use of the \sphinxhref{https://colvars.github.io/}{Colvars}
module included in the LAMMPS source distribution.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the recommended build procedure for using Colvars in
LAMMPS. No additional settings are normally needed besides
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_COLVARS=yes}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As with other libraries distributed with LAMMPS, the Colvars library
needs to be built before building the LAMMPS program with the COLVARS
package enabled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From the LAMMPS \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}} directory, this is most easily and safely done
via one of the following commands, which implicitly rely on the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/colvars/Install.py}} script with optional arguments:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}colvars

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}colvars\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}colvars\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler and colvars debugging enabled}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}colvars\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m g++\PYGZhy{}debug\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “machine” argument of the “\sphinxhyphen{}m” flag is used to find a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.machine}} file to use as build recipe.  If such recipe does
not already exist in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/colvars}}, suitable settings will be
auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated consistent with those used in the core LAMMPS makefiles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 8Feb2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please note that Colvars uses the Lepton library, which is now
included with the LEPTON package; if you use anything other than
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make lib\sphinxhyphen{}colvars}} command, please make sure to {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:lepton}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{build
Lepton beforehand}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional flags may be specified as environment variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build with debug code (much slower)}
\PYG{n+nv}{COLVARS\PYGZus{}DEBUG}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}colvars\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m machine\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build without Lepton (included otherwise)}
\PYG{n+nv}{COLVARS\PYGZus{}LEPTON}\PYG{o}{=}no\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}colvars\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m machine\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce two files: the library
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/colvars/libcolvars.a}} and the specification file
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/colvars/Makefile.lammps}}.  The latter is auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated,
and normally does not need to be edited.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ELECTRODE package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:electrode-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:electrode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This package depends on the KSPACE package.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}ELECTRODE}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} enable the package itself}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}KSPACE}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} the ELECTRODE package requires KSPACE}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{USE\PYGZus{}INTERNAL\PYGZus{}LINALG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Features in the ELECTRODE package are dependent on code in the
KSPACE package so the latter one \sphinxstyleemphasis{must} be enabled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ELECTRODE package also requires LAPACK (and BLAS) and CMake
can identify their locations and pass that info to the ELECTRODE
build script.  But on some systems this may cause problems when
linking or the dependency is not desired.  Try enabling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{USE\_INTERNAL\_LINALG}} in those cases to use the bundled linear
algebra library and work around the limitation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must configure the ELECTRODE support
libraries and settings in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/electrode}}.  You can do this
manually, if you prefer, or do it in one step from the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like these, which simply
invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/electrode/Install.py}} script with the specified
args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}electrode

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler and MPI STUBS (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}electrode\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}electrode\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} file has settings for the BLAS
and LAPACK linear algebra libraries.  These can either exist on
your system, or you can use the files provided in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}}.
In the latter case you also need to build the library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}} with a command like these:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m g++\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The package itself is activated with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make yes\sphinxhyphen{}KSPACE}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make yes\sphinxhyphen{}ELECTRODE}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-pace-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-pace}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This package requires a library that can be downloaded and built
in lib/pace or somewhere else, which must be done before building
LAMMPS with this package. The code for the library can be found
at: \sphinxurl{https://github.com/ICAMS/lammps-user-pace/}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of including the ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE package directly into LAMMPS, it
is also possible to skip this step and build the ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE package as
a plugin using the CMake script files in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGE/pace/plugin}}
folder and then load this plugin at runtime with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{plugin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{plugin command}}}}.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default the library will be downloaded from the git repository
and built automatically when the ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE package is enabled with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE=yes}}.  The location for the sources may be
customized by setting the variable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PACELIB\_URL}} when
configuring with CMake (e.g. to use a local archive on machines
without internet access).  Since CMake checks the validity of the
archive with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{md5sum}} you may also need to set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PACELIB\_MD5}}
if you provide a different library version than what is downloaded
automatically.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download and build the ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE library
in one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using these commands,
which invoke the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/pace/Install.py}} script.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}pace

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build the default version in lib/pace}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}pace\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You should not need to edit the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/pace/Makefile.lammps}} file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ML\sphinxhyphen{}POD package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-pod-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-pod}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_ML\sphinxhyphen{}POD=yes}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must configure the ML\sphinxhyphen{}POD support
settings in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/mlpod}}.  You can do this manually, if you
prefer, or do it in one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a
command like the following, which simply invoke the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/mlpod/Install.py}} script with the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}mlpod

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU g++ compiler and MPI STUBS (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}mlpod\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} same as above but use the bundled linalg lib}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}mlpod\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi \PYGZhy{}e linalg\PYGZdq{}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} file has settings to use the BLAS
and LAPACK linear algebra libraries.  These can either exist on
your system, or you can use the files provided in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}}.
In the latter case you also need to build the library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/linalg}} with a command like these:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI C++ compiler (settings as with \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU C++ compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}linalg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m g++\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The package itself is activated with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make yes\sphinxhyphen{}ML\sphinxhyphen{}POD}}.
