\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ML\sphinxhyphen{}QUIP package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-quip-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-quip}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must download and build the QUIP
library.  It can be obtained from GitHub.  For support of GAP
potentials, additional files with specific licensing conditions need
to be downloaded and configured.  The automatic download will from
within CMake will download the non\sphinxhyphen{}commercial use version.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}QUIP}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download QUIP library for build}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{QUIP\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to libquip.a}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (only needed if a custom location)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{USE\PYGZus{}INTERNAL\PYGZus{}LINALG}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the internal linear algebra library}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} instead of LAPACK}
\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
CMake will try to download and build the QUIP library from GitHub,
if it is not found on the local machine. This requires to have git
installed. It will use the same compilers and flags as used for
compiling LAMMPS.  Currently this is only supported for the GNU
and the Intel compilers. Set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QUIP\_LIBRARY}} variable if you
want to use a previously compiled and installed QUIP library and
CMake cannot find it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The QUIP library requires LAPACK (and BLAS) and CMake can identify
their locations and pass that info to the QUIP build script. But
on some systems this triggers a (current) limitation of CMake and
the configuration will fail. Try enabling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{USE\_INTERNAL\_LINALG}} in
those cases to use the bundled linear algebra library and work around
the limitation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The download/build procedure for the QUIP library, described in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/quip/README}} file requires setting two environment
variables, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QUIP\_ROOT}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QUIP\_ARCH}}.  These are accessed by
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/quip/Makefile.lammps}} file which is used when you
compile and link LAMMPS with this package.  You should only need
to edit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} if the LAMMPS build can not use its
settings to successfully build on your system.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{PLUMED package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:plumed-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:plumed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS with this package, you must first build PLUMED.
PLUMED can be built as part of the LAMMPS build or installed separately
from LAMMPS using the generic \sphinxhref{https://plumed.github.io/doc-master/user-doc/html/\_installation.html}{PLUMED installation instructions}.
The PLUMED package has been tested to work with Plumed versions
2.4.x, 2.5.x, and 2.6.x and will error out, when trying to run calculations
with a different version of the Plumed kernel.

\sphinxAtStartPar
PLUMED can be linked into MD codes in three different modes: static,
shared, and runtime.  With the “static” mode, all the code that PLUMED
requires is linked statically into LAMMPS. LAMMPS is then fully
independent from the PLUMED installation, but you have to rebuild/relink
it in order to update the PLUMED code inside it.  With the “shared”
linkage mode, LAMMPS is linked to a shared library that contains the
PLUMED code.  This library should preferably be installed in a globally
accessible location. When PLUMED is linked in this way the same library
can be used by multiple MD packages.  Furthermore, the PLUMED library
LAMMPS uses can be updated without the need for a recompile of LAMMPS
for as long as the shared PLUMED library is ABI\sphinxhyphen{}compatible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third linkage mode is “runtime” which allows the user to specify
which PLUMED kernel should be used at runtime by using the PLUMED\_KERNEL
environment variable. This variable should point to the location of the
libplumedKernel.so dynamical shared object, which is then loaded at
runtime. This mode of linking is particularly convenient for doing
PLUMED development and comparing multiple PLUMED versions as these sorts
of comparisons can be done without recompiling the hosting MD code. All
three linkage modes are supported by LAMMPS on selected operating
systems (e.g. Linux) and using either CMake or traditional make
build. The “static” mode should be the most portable, while the
“runtime” mode support in LAMMPS makes the most assumptions about
operating system and compiler environment. If one mode does not work,
try a different one, switch to a different build system, consider a
global PLUMED installation or consider downloading PLUMED during the
LAMMPS build.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of including the PLUMED package directly into LAMMPS, it
is also possible to skip this step and build the PLUMED package as
a plugin using the CMake script files in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGE/plumed/plugin}}
folder and then load this plugin at runtime with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{plugin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{plugin command}}}}.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_PLUMED=yes}} flag is included in the cmake
command you must ensure that \sphinxtitleref{the GNU Scientific Library (GSL)
\textless{}https://www.gnu.org/software/gsl/\textgreater{}} is installed in locations
that are accessible in your environment.  There are then two
additional variables that control the manner in which PLUMED is
obtained and linked into LAMMPS.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}PLUMED}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download PLUMED for build}
\PYG{+w}{                           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PLUMED\PYGZus{}MODE}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Linkage mode for PLUMED}
\PYG{+w}{                           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = static (default), shared,}
\PYG{+w}{                           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}         or runtime}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_PLUMED}} is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{yes}}, the PLUMED library will be
downloaded (the version of PLUMED that will be downloaded is
hard\sphinxhyphen{}coded to a vetted version of PLUMED, usually a recent stable
release version) and built inside the CMake build directory.  If
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_PLUMED}} is set to “no” (the default), CMake will try
to detect and link to an installed version of PLUMED.  For this to
work, the PLUMED library has to be installed into a location where
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pkg\sphinxhyphen{}config}} tool can find it or the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PKG\_CONFIG\_PATH}}
environment variable has to be set up accordingly.  PLUMED should
be installed in such a location if you compile it using the
default make; make install commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUMED\_MODE}} setting determines the linkage mode for the
PLUMED library.  The allowed values for this flag are “static”
(default), “shared”, or “runtime”.  If you want to switch the
linkage mode, just re\sphinxhyphen{}run CMake with a different setting. For a
discussion of PLUMED linkage modes, please see above.  When
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_PLUMED}} is enabled the static linkage mode is
recommended.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
PLUMED needs to be installed before the PLUMED package is
installed so that LAMMPS can find the right settings when
compiling and linking the LAMMPS executable.  You can either
download and build PLUMED inside the LAMMPS plumed library folder
or use a previously installed PLUMED library and point LAMMPS to
its location. You also have to choose the linkage mode: “static”
(default), “shared” or “runtime”.  For a discussion of PLUMED
linkage modes, please see above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Download/compilation/configuration of the plumed library can be done
from the src folder through the following make args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}plumed

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build PLUMED in lib/plumed/plumed2}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}plumed\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use existing PLUMED installation in \PYGZdl{}HOME/.local}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}plumed\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}p }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}HOME}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/.local}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use existing PLUMED installation in /usr/local and}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use shared linkage mode}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}plumed\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}p /usr/local \PYGZhy{}m shared\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that two symbolic (soft) links, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includelink}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblink}}
are created in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/plumed}} that point to the location of the PLUMED
build to use. A new file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/plumed/Makefile.lammps}} is also
created with settings suitable for LAMMPS to compile and link
PLUMED using the desired linkage mode. After this step is
completed, you can install the PLUMED package and compile
LAMMPS in the usual manner:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }yes\PYGZhy{}plumed
make\PYG{+w}{ }machine
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Once this compilation completes you should be able to run LAMMPS
in the usual way.  For shared linkage mode, libplumed.so must be
found by the LAMMPS executable, which on many operating systems
means, you have to set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LD\_LIBRARY\_PATH}} environment variable
accordingly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for the different linkage modes in LAMMPS varies for
different operating systems, using the static linkage is expected
to be the most portable, and thus set to be the default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to change the linkage mode, you have to re\sphinxhyphen{}run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make
lib\sphinxhyphen{}plumed}} with the desired settings \sphinxstylestrong{and} do a re\sphinxhyphen{}install if
the PLUMED package with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make yes\sphinxhyphen{}plumed}} to update the
required makefile settings with the changes in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/plumed}}
folder.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{H5MD package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:h5md-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:h5md}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package you must have the HDF5 software package
installed on your system, which should include the h5cc compiler and
the HDF5 library.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_H5MD=yes}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This should auto\sphinxhyphen{}detect the H5MD library on your system.  Several
advanced CMake H5MD options exist if you need to specify where it
is installed.  Use the ccmake (terminal window) or cmake\sphinxhyphen{}gui
(graphical) tools to see these options and set them interactively
from their user interfaces.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must build the CH5MD library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/h5md}}.  You can do this manually if you prefer; follow the
instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/h5md/README}}.  You can also do it in one
step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like these,
which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/h5md/Install.py}} script with the
specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}h5md\PYG{+w}{                     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}h5md\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m h5cc\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with h5cc compiler}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce two files: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/h5md/libch5md.a}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/h5md/Makefile.lammps}}.  The latter is copied from an
existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.*}} and has settings needed to build
LAMMPS with the system HDF5 library.  If necessary, you can
edit/create a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/h5md/Makefile.machine}} file for your
system, which should define an EXTRAMAKE variable to specify a
corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.\textless{}machine\textgreater{}}} file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{ML\sphinxhyphen{}HDNNP package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-hdnnp-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:ml-hdnnp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with the ML\sphinxhyphen{}HDNNP package it is required to download and build the
external \sphinxhref{https://github.com/CompPhysVienna/n2p2}{n2p2} library \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v2.1.4}}
(or higher). The LAMMPS build process offers an automatic download and
compilation of \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} or allows you to choose the installation directory of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} manually. Please see the boxes below for the CMake and traditional build
system for detailed information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In case of a manual installation of \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} you only need to build the \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} core
library \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{libnnp}} and interface library \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{libnnpif}}. When using GCC it should
suffice to execute \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make libnnpif}} in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}} directory. For more
details please see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/hdnnp/README}} and the \sphinxhref{https://compphysvienna.github.io/n2p2/topics/build.html}{n2p2 build documentation}.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}N2P2}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download n2p2 for build}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{N2P2\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} n2p2 base directory}
\PYG{+w}{                          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (only needed if a custom location)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_N2P2}} is set, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} library will be downloaded and
built inside the CMake build directory.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} library is already
on your system (in a location CMake cannot find it), set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N2P2\_DIR}}
to path where \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} is located. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} is located directly in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/hdnnp/n2p2}} it will be automatically found by CMake.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download and build the \sphinxstyleemphasis{n2p2} library manually if you prefer;
follow the instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/hdnnp/README}}. You can also do it in
one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like these, which
simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/hdnnp/Install.py}} script with the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}hdnnp

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build in lib/hdnnp/n2p2\PYGZhy{}...}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}hdnnp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build specific version}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}hdnnp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b \PYGZhy{}v 2.1.4\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use the existing n2p2 installation in /usr/local/n2p2}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}hdnnp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}p /usr/local/n2p2\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that three symbolic (soft) links, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includelink}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblink}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}}, will be created in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/hdnnp}} to point to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n2p2/include}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n2p2/lib}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n2p2/lib/Makefile.lammps\sphinxhyphen{}extra}},
respectively. When LAMMPS is built in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}} it will use these links.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{INTEL package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:intel-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:intel}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must choose which hardware you want to
build for, either x86 CPUs or Intel KNLs in offload mode.  You should
also typically {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_extras:openmp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{install the OPENMP package}}}}, as it can be
used in tandem with the INTEL package to good effect, as explained
on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_intel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{INTEL package}}}} page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using Intel compilers version 16.0 or later is required.  You can
also use the GNU or Clang compilers and they will provide performance
improvements over regular styles and OPENMP styles, but less so than
with the Intel compilers.  Please also note, that some compilers have
been found to apply memory alignment constraints incompletely or
incorrectly and thus can cause segmentation faults in otherwise correct
code when using features from the INTEL package.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{INTEL\PYGZus{}ARCH}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = cpu (default) or knl}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{INTEL\PYGZus{}LRT\PYGZus{}MODE}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = threads, none, or c++11}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose which hardware to compile for in Makefile.machine via the
following settings.  See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MAKE/OPTIONS/Makefile.intel\_cpu*}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.knl}} files for examples. and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/INTEL/README}} for additional information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For CPUs:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{OPTFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}xHost\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}fp\PYGZhy{}model\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{fast}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}prec\PYGZhy{}div\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qoverride\PYGZhy{}limits\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qopt\PYGZhy{}zmm\PYGZhy{}usage\PYG{o}{=}high
\PYG{n+nv}{CCFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYGZhy{}g\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qopenmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}MEMALIGN\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{64}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}offload\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}fno\PYGZhy{}alias\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}ansi\PYGZhy{}alias\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}restrict\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}OPTFLAGS\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{n+nv}{LINKFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}g\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qopenmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}OPTFLAGS\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{n+nv}{LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYGZhy{}ltbbmalloc
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For KNLs:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{OPTFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}xMIC\PYGZhy{}AVX512\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}fp\PYGZhy{}model\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{fast}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}prec\PYGZhy{}div\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qoverride\PYGZhy{}limits
\PYG{n+nv}{CCFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYGZhy{}g\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qopenmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DLAMMPS\PYGZus{}MEMALIGN\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{64}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}offload\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}fno\PYGZhy{}alias\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}ansi\PYGZhy{}alias\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}restrict\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}OPTFLAGS\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{n+nv}{LINKFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}g\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}qopenmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}OPTFLAGS\PYG{k}{)}
\PYG{n+nv}{LIB}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYGZhy{}ltbbmalloc
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In Long\sphinxhyphen{}range thread mode (LRT) a modified verlet style is used, that
operates the Kspace calculation in a separate thread concurrently to
other calculations. This has to be enabled in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{package intel}}}} command at runtime. With the setting “threads” it used the
pthreads library, while “c++11” will use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in thread support
of C++11 compilers. The option “none” skips compilation of this
feature. The default is to use “threads” if pthreads is available and
otherwise “none”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Best performance is achieved with Intel hardware, Intel compilers, as
well as the Intel TBB and MKL libraries. However, the code also
compiles, links, and runs with other compilers / hardware and without
TBB and MKL.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{MDI package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:mdi-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:mdi}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}MDI}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download MDI Library for build}
\PYG{+w}{                         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} value = no (default) or yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must build the MDI Library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/mdi}}.  You can do this by executing a command like one
of the following from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/mdi}} directory:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }Install.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }gcc\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build using gcc compiler}
python\PYG{+w}{ }Install.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }icc\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build using icc compiler}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce two files: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/mdi/includelink/mdi.h}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/mdi/liblink/libmdi.so}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{MOLFILE package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:molfile-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:molfile}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{MOLFILE\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (optional) path where VMD molfile}
\PYG{+w}{                              }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} plugin headers are installed}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}MOLFILE}\PYG{o}{=}yes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_MOLFILE=yes}} enables the package, and setting
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D MOLFILE\_INCLUDE\_DIR}} allows to provide a custom location for
the molfile plugin header files. These should match the ABI of the
plugin files used, and thus one typically sets them to include
folder of the local VMD installation in use. LAMMPS ships with a
couple of default header files that correspond to a popular VMD
version, usually the latest release.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/molfile/Makefile.lammps}} file has a setting for a
dynamic loading library libdl.a that is typically present on all
systems.  It is required for LAMMPS to link with this package.  If
the setting is not valid for your system, you will need to edit
the Makefile.lammps file.  See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/molfile/README}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/molfile/Makefile.lammps}} for details. It is also possible
to configure a different folder with the VMD molfile plugin header
files. LAMMPS ships with a couple of default headers, but these
are not compatible with all VMD versions, so it is often best to
change this setting to the location of the same include files of
the local VMD installation in use.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{NETCDF package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:netcdf-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:netcdf}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package you must have the NetCDF library installed
on your system.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_NETCDF=yes}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This should auto\sphinxhyphen{}detect the NETCDF library if it is installed on
your system at standard locations.  Several advanced CMake NETCDF
options exist if you need to specify where it was installed.  Use
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ccmake}} (terminal window) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake\sphinxhyphen{}gui}} (graphical)
tools to see these options and set them interactively from their
user interfaces.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/netcdf/Makefile.lammps}} file has settings for NetCDF
include and library files which LAMMPS needs to build with this
package.  If the settings are not valid for your system, you will
need to edit the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} file.  See
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/netcdf/README}} for details.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{OPENMP package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:openmp-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:openmp}}\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are required besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D
PKG\_OPENMP=yes}}.  If CMake detects OpenMP compiler support, the
OPENMP code will be compiled with multi\sphinxhyphen{}threading support
enabled, otherwise as optimized serial code.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To enable multi\sphinxhyphen{}threading support in the OPENMP package (and
other styles supporting OpenMP) the following compile and link
flags must be added to your Makefile.machine file.  See
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MAKE/OPTIONS/Makefile.omp}} for an example.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
CCFLAGS: \PYGZhy{}fopenmp               \PYGZsh{} for GNU and Clang Compilers
CCFLAGS: \PYGZhy{}qopenmp \PYGZhy{}restrict     \PYGZsh{} for Intel compilers on Linux
LINKFLAGS: \PYGZhy{}fopenmp             \PYGZsh{} for GNU and Clang Compilers
LINKFLAGS: \PYGZhy{}qopenmp             \PYGZsh{} for Intel compilers on Linux
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For other platforms and compilers, please consult the
documentation about OpenMP support for your compiler.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Adding OpenMP support on macOS}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Apple offers the \sphinxhref{https://developer.apple.com/xcode/}{Xcode package and IDE} for compiling software on
macOS, so you have likely installed it to compile LAMMPS.  Their
compiler is based on \sphinxhref{https://clang.llvm.org/}{Clang}, but while it
is capable of processing OpenMP directives, the necessary header
files and OpenMP runtime library are missing.  The \sphinxhref{https://www.r-project.org/}{R developers} have figured out a way to build those
in a compatible fashion. One can download them from
\sphinxurl{https://mac.r-project.org/openmp/}.  Simply adding those files as
instructed enables the Xcode C++ compiler to compile LAMMPS with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D
BUILD\_OMP=yes}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{QMMM package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:qmmm-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:qmmm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For using LAMMPS to do QM/MM simulations via the QMMM package you
need to build LAMMPS as a library.  A LAMMPS executable with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qmmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
qmmm}}}} included can be built, but will not be able to do a
QM/MM simulation on as such.  You must also build a QM code \sphinxhyphen{} currently
only Quantum ESPRESSO (QE) is supported \sphinxhyphen{} and create a new executable
which links LAMMPS and the QM code together.  Details are given in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm/README}} file.  It is also recommended to read the
instructions for {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_link::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{linking with LAMMPS as a library}}}}
for background information.  This requires compatible Quantum Espresso
and LAMMPS versions.  The current interface and makefiles have last been
verified to work in February 2020 with Quantum Espresso versions 6.3 to
6.5.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using CMake, building a LAMMPS library is required and it is
recommended to build a shared library, since any libraries built
from the sources in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lib} folder (including the essential
libqmmm.a) are not included in the static LAMMPS library and
(currently) not installed, while their code is included in the
shared LAMMPS library.  Thus a typical command line to configure
building LAMMPS for QMMM would be:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}C\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake/presets/basic.cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PKG\PYGZus{}QMMM}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BUILD\PYGZus{}LIB}\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DBUILD\PYGZus{}SHARED\PYGZus{}LIBS\PYG{o}{=}yes\PYG{+w}{ }../cmake
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After completing the LAMMPS build and also configuring and
compiling Quantum ESPRESSO with external library support (via
“make couple”), go back to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm}} folder and follow the
instructions on the README file to build the combined LAMMPS/QE
QM/MM executable (pwqmmm.x) in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm}} folder.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before building LAMMPS, you must build the QMMM library in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm}}.  You can do this manually if you prefer; follow the
first two steps explained in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm/README}}.  You can also do
it in one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a command like
these, which simply invokes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm/Install.py}} script with
the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}qmmm

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU Fortran compiler (settings as in \PYGZdq{}make serial\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}qmmm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m serial\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with default MPI compiler (settings as in \PYGZdq{}make mpi\PYGZdq{})}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}qmmm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m mpi\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build with GNU Fortran compiler}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}qmmm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}m gfortran\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build should produce two files: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm/libqmmm.a}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm/Makefile.lammps}}.  The latter is copied from an
existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.*}} and has settings needed to build
LAMMPS with the QMMM library (though typically the settings are
just blank).  If necessary, you can edit/create a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm/Makefile.\textless{}machine\textgreater{}}} file for your system, which should
define an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTRAMAKE}} variable to specify a corresponding
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps.\textless{}machine\textgreater{}}} file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can then install QMMM package and build LAMMPS in the usual
manner.  After completing the LAMMPS build and compiling Quantum
ESPRESSO with external library support (via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make couple}}), go
back to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm}} folder and follow the instructions in the
README file to build the combined LAMMPS/QE QM/MM executable
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pwqmmm.x}}) in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/qmmm}} folder.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{RHEO package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:rheo-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:rheo}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package you must have the \sphinxtitleref{GNU Scientific Library
(GSL) \textless{}https://www.gnu.org/software/gsl/\textgreater{}} installed in locations that
are accessible in your environment.  The GSL library should be at least
version 2.7.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If CMake cannot find the GSL library or include files, you can set:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{GSL\PYGZus{}ROOT\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} path to root of GSL installation}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS will try to auto\sphinxhyphen{}detect the GSL compiler and linker flags
from the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pkg\sphinxhyphen{}config}} file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gsl.pc}}), otherwise
you can edit the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/rheo/Makefile.lammps}}
to specify the paths and library names where indicated by comments.
This must be done \sphinxstylestrong{before} the package is installed.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{SCAFACOS package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:scafacos-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:scafacos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package, you must download and build the
\sphinxhref{http://www.scafacos.de}{ScaFaCoS Coulomb solver library}
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{DOWNLOAD\PYGZus{}SCAFACOS}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download ScaFaCoS for build, value = no (default) or yes}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{SCAFACOS\PYGZus{}LIBRARY}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ScaFaCos library file (only needed if at custom location)}
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{SCAFACOS\PYGZus{}INCLUDE\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}path\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ScaFaCoS include directory (only needed if at custom location)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DOWNLOAD\_SCAFACOS}} is set, the ScaFaCoS library will be
downloaded and built inside the CMake build directory.  If the
ScaFaCoS library is already on your system (in a location CMake
cannot find it), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SCAFACOS\_LIBRARY}} is the filename (plus path) of
the ScaFaCoS library file, not the directory the library file is
in.  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SCAFACOS\_INCLUDE\_DIR}} is the directory the ScaFaCoS include
file is in.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download and build the ScaFaCoS library manually if you
prefer; follow the instructions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/scafacos/README}}.  You
can also do it in one step from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}} dir, using a
command like these, which simply invokes the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/scafacos/Install.py}} script with the specified args:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} print help message}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}scafacos

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} download and build in lib/scafacos/scafacos\PYGZhy{}\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}scafacos\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use existing ScaFaCoS installation in \PYGZdl{}HOME/scafacos}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lib\PYGZhy{}scafacos\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{args}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}p }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}HOME}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/scafacos}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that two symbolic (soft) links, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includelink}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblink}}, are
created in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/scafacos}} to point to the ScaFaCoS src dir.  When LAMMPS
builds in src it will use these links.  You should not need to edit
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/scafacos/Makefile.lammps}} file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{VTK package}
\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:vtk-package}}\label{\detokenize{Build_extras:vtk}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build with this package you must have the VTK library installed on
your system.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{CMake build}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional settings are needed besides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}D PKG\_VTK=yes}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This should auto\sphinxhyphen{}detect the VTK library if it is installed on your
system at standard locations.  Several advanced VTK options exist
if you need to specify where it was installed.  Use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ccmake}}
(terminal window) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake\sphinxhyphen{}gui}} (graphical) tools to see these
options and set them interactively from their user interfaces.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Traditional make}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/vtk/Makefile.lammps}} file has settings for accessing
VTK files and its library, which LAMMPS needs to build with this
package.  If the settings are not valid for your system, check if
one of the other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/vtk/Makefile.lammps.*}} files is compatible
and copy it to Makefile.lammps.  If none of the provided files
work, you will need to edit the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Makefile.lammps}} file.  See
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lib/vtk/README}} for details.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Build the LAMMPS documentation}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:build-the-lammps-documentation}}\label{\detokenize{Build_manual::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on how you obtained LAMMPS and whether you have built the
manual yourself, this directory has a number of subdirectories and
files. Here is a list with descriptions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
README\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} brief info about the documentation}
src\PYG{+w}{              }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} content files for LAMMPS documentation}
html\PYG{+w}{             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HTML version of the LAMMPS manual (see html/Manual.html)}
utils\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} tools and settings for building the documentation}
lammps.1\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} man page for the lammps command}
msi2lmp.1\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} man page for the msi2lmp command}
Manual.pdf\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} large PDF version of entire manual}
LAMMPS.epub\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Manual in ePUB e\PYGZhy{}book format}
LAMMPS.mobi\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Manual in MOBI e\PYGZhy{}book format}
docenv\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} virtualenv folder for processing the manual sources}
doctrees\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} temporary data from processing the manual}
doxygen\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} doxygen configuration and output}
.gitignore\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} list of files and folders to be ignored by git}
doxygen\PYGZhy{}warn.log\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} logfile with warnings from running doxygen}
github\PYGZhy{}development\PYGZhy{}workflow.md\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} notes on the LAMMPS development workflow}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you downloaded LAMMPS as a tarball from \sphinxhref{https://www.lammps.org}{the LAMMPS website},
the html folder and the PDF files should be included.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you downloaded LAMMPS from the public git repository, then the HTML
and PDF files are not included.  You can build the HTML or PDF files yourself,
by typing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make html}}  or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make pdf}} in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{doc}} folder.  This requires
various tools and files.  Some of them have to be installed (see below).  For
the rest the build process will attempt to download and install them into
a python virtual environment and local folders.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A current version of the manual (latest feature release, that is the state
of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{release} branch) is is available online at:
\sphinxurl{https://docs.lammps.org/}.
A version of the manual corresponding to the ongoing development (that is
the state of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{develop} branch) is available online at:
\sphinxurl{https://docs.lammps.org/latest/}
A version of the manual corresponding to the latest stable LAMMPS release
(that is the state of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{stable} branch) is available online at:
\sphinxurl{https://docs.lammps.org/stable/}


\subsection{Build using GNU make}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:build-using-gnu-make}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS manual is written in \sphinxhref{https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/restructuredtext/index.html}{reStructuredText} format which
can be translated to different output format using the \sphinxhref{https://www.sphinx-doc.org/}{Sphinx} document generator tool.  It also
incorporates programmer documentation extracted from the LAMMPS C++
sources through the \sphinxhref{https://doxygen.nl/}{Doxygen} program.  Currently
the translation to HTML, PDF (via LaTeX), ePUB (for many e\sphinxhyphen{}book readers)
and MOBI (for Amazon Kindle readers) are supported.  For that to work a
Python interpreter version 3.8 or later, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{doxygen}} tools and
internet access to download additional files and tools are required.
This download is usually only required once or after the documentation
folder is returned to a pristine state with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make clean\sphinxhyphen{}all}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the documentation build a python virtual environment is set up in
the folder \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{doc/docenv}} and various python packages are installed into
that virtual environment via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip}} tool.  For rendering embedded
LaTeX code also the \sphinxhref{https://www.mathjax.org/}{MathJax} JavaScript
engine needs to be downloaded.  If you need to pass additional options
to the pip commands to work (e.g. to use a web proxy or to point to
additional SSL certificates) you can set them via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PIP\_OPTIONS}}
environment variable or uncomment and edit the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PIP\_OPTIONS}} setting
at beginning of the makefile.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual translation is then done via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} commands in the doc
folder.  The following \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} commands are available:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }html\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} generate HTML in html dir using Sphinx}
make\PYG{+w}{ }pdf\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} generate PDF  as Manual.pdf using Sphinx and PDFLaTeX}
make\PYG{+w}{ }epub\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} generate LAMMPS.epub in ePUB format using Sphinx}
make\PYG{+w}{ }mobi\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} generate LAMMPS.mobi in MOBI format using ebook\PYGZhy{}convert}

make\PYG{+w}{ }fasthtml\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} generate approximate HTML in fasthtml dir using Sphinx}
\PYG{+w}{                   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} some Sphinx extensions do not work correctly with this}

make\PYG{+w}{ }clean\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} remove intermediate RST files created by HTML build}
make\PYG{+w}{ }clean\PYGZhy{}all\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} remove entire build folder and any cached data}

make\PYG{+w}{ }anchor\PYGZus{}check\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} check for duplicate anchor labels}
make\PYG{+w}{ }style\PYGZus{}check\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} check for complete and consistent style lists}
make\PYG{+w}{ }package\PYGZus{}check\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} check for complete and consistent package lists}
make\PYG{+w}{ }link\PYGZus{}check\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} check for broken or outdated URLs}
make\PYG{+w}{ }spelling\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} spell\PYGZhy{}check the manual}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Build using CMake}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:build-using-cmake}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is also possible to create the HTML version (and \sphinxstylestrong{only} the HTML
version) of the manual within the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_cmake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{CMake build directory}}}}.  The reason for this option is to include the
installation of the HTML manual pages into the “install” step when
installing LAMMPS after the CMake build via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}build . \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}target
install}}.  The documentation build is included in the default build
target, but can also be requested independently with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmake \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}build . \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}target doc}}.  If you need to pass additional options
to the pip commands to work (e.g. to use a web proxy or to point to
additional SSL certificates) you can set them via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PIP\_OPTIONS}}
environment variable.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{}D\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BUILD\PYGZus{}DOC}\PYG{o}{=}value\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} yes or no (default)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Prerequisites for HTML}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:prerequisites-for-html}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To run the HTML documentation build toolchain, python 3, git, doxygen,
and virtualenv have to be installed locally.  Here are instructions for
common setups:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Ubuntu}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }git\PYG{+w}{ }doxygen
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{RHEL or CentOS (Version 7.x)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }yum\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }git\PYG{+w}{ }doxygen
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Fedora or RHEL/CentOS (8.x or later)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }dnf\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }git\PYG{+w}{ }doxygen
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{macOS}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Python 3}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If Python 3 is not available on your macOS system, you can
download the latest Python 3 macOS package from
\sphinxurl{https://www.python.org} and install it.
This will install both Python 3 and pip3.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}


\subsection{Prerequisites for PDF}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:prerequisites-for-pdf}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the tools needed for building the HTML format manual,
a working LaTeX installation with support for PDFLaTeX and a selection
of LaTeX styles/packages are required.  To run the PDFLaTeX translation
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{latexmk}} script needs to be installed as well.


\subsection{Prerequisites for ePUB and MOBI}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:prerequisites-for-epub-and-mobi}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the tools needed for building the HTML format manual,
a working LaTeX installation with a few add\sphinxhyphen{}on LaTeX packages
as well as the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dvipng}} tool are required to convert embedded
math expressions transparently into embedded images.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For converting the generated ePUB file to a MOBI format file (for e\sphinxhyphen{}book
readers, like Kindle, that cannot read ePUB), you also need to have the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ebook\sphinxhyphen{}convert}} tool from the “calibre” software
installed. \sphinxurl{https://calibre-ebook.com/}
Typing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make mobi}} will first create the ePUB file and then convert
it.  On the Kindle readers in particular, you also have support for PDF
files, so you could download and view the PDF version as an alternative.


\subsection{Instructions for Developers}
\label{\detokenize{Build_manual:instructions-for-developers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When adding new styles or options to the LAMMPS code, corresponding
documentation is required and either existing files in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src}}
folder need to be updated or new files added. These files are written in
\sphinxhref{https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/restructuredtext/index.html}{reStructuredText} markup for translation with the Sphinx tool.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before contributing any documentation, please check that both the HTML
and the PDF format documentation can translate without errors.  During
testing the html translation, you may use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make fasthtml}} command
which does an approximate translation (i.e. not all Sphinx features and
extensions will work), but runs very fast because it will only translate
files that have been changed since the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make fasthtml}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please also check the output to the console for any warnings or problems.  There will
be multiple tests run automatically:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A test for correctness of all anchor labels and their references

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A test that all LAMMPS packages (= folders with sources in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/src}}) are documented and listed.  A typical warning shows
the name of the folder with the suspected new package code and the
documentation files where they need to be listed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Found 88 packages
Package NEWPACKAGE missing in Packages\PYGZus{}list.rst
Package NEWPACKAGE missing in Packages\PYGZus{}details.rst
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A test that only standard, printable ASCII text characters are used.
This runs the command \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{env LC\_ALL=C grep \sphinxhyphen{}n \textquotesingle{}{[}\textasciicircum{} \sphinxhyphen{}\textasciitilde{}{]}\textquotesingle{} src/*.rst}} and
thus prints all offending lines with filename and line number
prepended to the screen.  Special characters like Greek letters
(\(\alpha~~\sigma~~\epsilon\)), super\sphinxhyphen{} or subscripts
(\(x^2~~\mathrm{U}_{LJ}\)), mathematical expressions
(\(\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{N}~~x\to\infty\)), or the Angstrom symbol
(\(\AA\)) should be typeset with embedded LaTeX (like this
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:math:\textasciigrave{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}sigma \textbackslash{}epsilon\textasciigrave{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:math:\textasciigrave{}x\textasciicircum{}2 \textbackslash{}mathrm\{E\}\_\{LJ\}\textasciigrave{}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:math:\textasciigrave{}\textbackslash{}frac\{1\}\{2\}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{N\} x\textbackslash{}to\textbackslash{}infty\textasciigrave{}}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:math:\textasciigrave{}\textbackslash{}AA\textasciigrave{}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Embedded LaTeX is rendered in HTML output with \sphinxhref{https://www.mathjax.org/}{MathJax} and in PDF output by passing the embedded
text to LaTeX.  Some care has to be taken, though, since there are
limitations which macros and features can be used in either mode, so
it is recommended to always check whether any new or changed
documentation does translate and render correctly with either output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A test whether all styles are documented and listed in their
respective overview pages.  A typical output with warnings looks like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Parsed style names w/o suffixes from C++ tree in ../src:
   Angle styles:      21    Atom styles:       24
   Body styles:        3    Bond styles:       17
   Command styles:    41    Compute styles:   143
   Dihedral styles:   16    Dump styles:       26
   Fix styles:       223    Improper styles:   13
   Integrate styles:   4    Kspace styles:     15
   Minimize styles:    9    Pair styles:      234
   Reader styles:      4    Region styles:      8
Compute style entry newcomp is missing or incomplete in Commands\PYGZus{}compute.rst
Compute style entry newcomp is missing or incomplete in compute.rst
Fix style entry newfix is missing or incomplete in Commands\PYGZus{}fix.rst
Fix style entry newfix is missing or incomplete in fix.rst
Pair style entry new is missing or incomplete in Commands\PYGZus{}pair.rst
Pair style entry new is missing or incomplete in pair\PYGZus{}style.rst
Found 6 issue(s) with style lists
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition, there is the option to run a spellcheck on the entire
manual with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make spelling}}.  This requires \sphinxhref{https://github.com/AbiWord/enchant}{a library called enchant}.  To avoid printing out \sphinxstyleemphasis{false
positives} (e.g. keywords, names, abbreviations) those can be added to
the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps/doc/utils/sphinx\sphinxhyphen{}config/false\_positives.txt}}.
