clicking on the “palette” button in the status bar of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Editor}
window, LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI sends a custom {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_dump image}}}}
command to LAMMPS and reads back the resulting snapshot image with the
current state of the system into an image viewer.  This functionality is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{not} available \sphinxstyleemphasis{during} an ongoing run.  In case LAMMPS is not yet
initialized, LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI tries to identify the line with the first run or
minimize command and execute all commands from the input buffer up to
that line, and then executes a “run 0” command.  This initializes the
system so an image of the initial state of the system can be rendered.
If there was an error in that process, the snapshot image viewer does
not appear.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When possible, LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI tries to detect which elements the atoms
correspond to (via their mass) and then colorize them in the image and
set their atom diameters accordingly.  If this is not possible, for
instance when using reduced (= ‘lj’) {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}, then
LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI will check the current pair style and if it is a
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones type potential, it will extract the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sigma} parameter
for each atom type and assign atom diameters from those numbers.
For cases where atom diameters are not auto\sphinxhyphen{}detected, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atom size} field
can be edited and a suitable value set manually. The default value
is inferred from the x\sphinxhyphen{}direction lattice spacing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If elements cannot be detected the default sequence of colors of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} command is assigned to the different atom
types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.480\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-image}.png}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.480\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-funnel}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default image size, some default image quality settings, the view
style and some colors can be changed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog
window.  From the image viewer window further adjustments can be made:
actual image size, high\sphinxhyphen{}quality (SSAO) rendering, anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliasing, view
style, display of box or axes, zoom factor.  The view of the system can
be rotated horizontally and vertically.  It is also possible to only
display the atoms within a group defined in the input script (default is
“all”).  The image can also be re\sphinxhyphen{}centered on the center of mass of the
selected group.  After each change, the image is rendered again and the
display updated.  The small palette icon on the top left is colored
while LAMMPS is running to render the new image; it is grayed out when
LAMMPS is finished.  When there are many atoms to render and high
quality images with anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliasing are requested, re\sphinxhyphen{}rendering may take
several seconds.  From the \sphinxstyleemphasis{File} menu of the image window, the
current image can be saved to a file (keyboard shortcut \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}S}) or
copied to the clipboard (keyboard shortcut \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C}) for pasting the
image into another application.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From the \sphinxstyleemphasis{File} menu it is also possible to copy the current
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}
commands to the clipboard so they can be pasted into a LAMMPS input file
so that the visualization settings of the snapshot image can be repeated
for the entire simulation (and thus be repeated in the slide show
viewer). This feature has the keyboard shortcut \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}D}.


\subsubsection{Editor Window}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:editor-window}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Editor} window of LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI has most of the usual functionality
that similar programs have: text selection via mouse or with cursor
moves while holding the Shift key, Cut (\sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}X}), Copy (\sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C}),
Paste (\sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}V}), Undo (\sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}Z}), Redo (\sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}Shift\sphinxhyphen{}Z}), Select All
(\sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}A}).  When trying to exit the editor with a modified buffer, a
dialog will pop up asking whether to cancel the exit operation, or to
save or not save the buffer contents to a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The editor has an auto\sphinxhyphen{}save mode that can be enabled or disabled in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog.  In auto\sphinxhyphen{}save mode, the editor buffer is
automatically saved before running LAMMPS or before exiting LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI.


\paragraph{Context Specific Word Completion}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:context-specific-word-completion}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI displays a small pop\sphinxhyphen{}up frame with possible
choices for LAMMPS input script commands or styles after 2 characters of
a word have been typed.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.75]{{lammps-gui-complete}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The word can then be completed through selecting an entry by scrolling
up and down with the cursor keys and selecting with the ‘Enter’ key or
by clicking on the entry with the mouse.  The automatic completion
pop\sphinxhyphen{}up can be disabled in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog, but the completion
can still be requested manually by either hitting the ‘Shift\sphinxhyphen{}TAB’ key or
by right\sphinxhyphen{}clicking with the mouse and selecting the option from the
context menu.  Most of the completion information is retrieved from the
active LAMMPS instance and thus it shows only available options that
have been enabled when compiling LAMMPS. That list, however, excludes
accelerated styles and commands; for improved clarity, only the
non\sphinxhyphen{}suffix version of styles are shown.


\paragraph{Line Reformatting}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:line-reformatting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The editor supports reformatting lines according to the syntax in order
to have consistently aligned lines.  This primarily means adding
whitespace padding to commands, type specifiers, IDs and names.  This
reformatting is performed manually by hitting the ‘Tab’ key.  It is
also possible to have this done automatically when hitting the ‘Enter’
key to start a new line.  This feature can be turned on or off in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Editor Settings} with the
“Reformat with ‘Enter’” checkbox. The amount of padding for multiple
categories can be adjusted in the same dialog.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally this functionality is achieved by splitting the line into
“words” and then putting it back together with padding added where the
context can be detected; otherwise a single space is used between words.


\paragraph{Context Specific Help}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:context-specific-help}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.480\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-popup-help}.png}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.480\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-popup-view}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A unique feature of LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI is the option to look up the LAMMPS
documentation for the command in the current line.  This can be done by
either clicking the right mouse button or by using the \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}?} keyboard
shortcut.  When using the mouse, there are additional entries in the
context menu that open the corresponding documentation page in the
online LAMMPS documentation in a web browser window.  When using the
keyboard, the first of those entries is chosen.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the word under the cursor is a file, then additionally the context
menu has an entry to open the file in a read\sphinxhyphen{}only text viewer window.
If the file is a LAMMPS restart file, instead the menu entry offers to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:inspect-restart}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{inspect the restart}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The text viewer is a convenient way to view the contents of files that
are referenced in the input.  The file viewer also supports on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly
decompression based on the file name suffix in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings:gzip}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{similar fashion
as available with LAMMPS}}}}.  If the necessary decompression
program is missing or the file cannot be decompressed, the viewer window
will contain a corresponding message.


\paragraph{Inspecting a Restart file}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:inspecting-a-restart-file}}\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:inspect-restart}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI is asked to “Inspect a Restart”, it will read the
restart file into a LAMMPS instance and then open three different
windows.  The first window is a text viewer with the output of an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{info::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{info command}}}} with system information stored in the
restart.  The second window is text viewer containing a data file
generated with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data command}}}}.  The third
window is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:snapshot-viewer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Snapshot Image Viewer}}}} containing a
visualization of the system in the restart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the restart file is larger than 250 MBytes, a dialog will ask
for confirmation before continuing, since large restart files
may require large amounts of RAM since the entire system must
be read into RAM.  Thus restart file for large simulations that
have been run on an HPC cluster may overload a laptop or local
workstation. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Show Details…} button will display a rough
estimate of the additional memory required.


\subsubsection{Menu}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:menu}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The menu bar has entries \sphinxstyleemphasis{File}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Run}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{View}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{About}.  Instead of using the mouse to click on them, the individual
menus can also be activated by hitting the \sphinxtitleref{Alt} key together with the
corresponding underlined letter, that is \sphinxtitleref{Alt\sphinxhyphen{}F} activates the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{File} menu.  For the corresponding activated sub\sphinxhyphen{}menus, the key
corresponding the underlined letters can be used to select entries
instead of using the mouse.


\paragraph{File}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{File} menu offers the usual options:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{New} clears the current buffer and resets the file name to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*unknown*}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Open} opens a dialog to select a new file for editing in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Editor}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{View} opens a dialog to select a file for viewing in a \sphinxstyleemphasis{separate} window (read\sphinxhyphen{}only) with support for on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly decompression as explained above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Inspect restart} opens a dialog to select a file.  If that file is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{LAMMPS restart}}}} three windows with {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:inspect-restart}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{information about the file are opened}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Save} saves the current file; if the file name is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*unknown*}}
a dialog will open to select a new file name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Save As} opens a dialog to select and new file name (and folder, if
desired) and saves the buffer to it.  Writing the buffer to a
different folder will also switch the current working directory to
that folder.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Quit} exits LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI. If there are unsaved changes, a dialog will
appear to either cancel the operation, or to save, or to not save the
modified buffer.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition, up to 5 recent file names will be listed after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Open}
entry that allows re\sphinxhyphen{}opening recently opened files.  This list is stored
when quitting and recovered when starting again.


\paragraph{Edit}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:edit}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit} menu offers the usual editor functions like \sphinxstyleemphasis{Undo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Redo},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cut}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Copy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Paste}, and a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Find and Replace} dialog (keyboard
shortcut \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}F}).  It can also open a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog (keyboard
shortcut \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}P}) and allows deleting all stored preferences and
settings, so they are reset to their default values.


\paragraph{Run}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:run}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Run} menu has options to start and stop a LAMMPS process.  Rather
than calling the LAMMPS executable as a separate executable, the
LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI is linked to the LAMMPS library and thus can run LAMMPS
internally through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library:lammps-c-api}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{LAMMPS C\sphinxhyphen{}library interface}}}}
in a separate thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically, a LAMMPS instance will be created by calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv418lammps_open_no_mpiiPPcPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_no\_mpi()}}}}}.  The buffer contents are then executed by
calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_execute:_CPPv422lammps_commands_stringPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_commands\_string()}}}}}.  Certain commands and
features are only available after a LAMMPS instance is created.  Its
presence is indicated by a small LAMMPS \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} logo in the status bar
at the bottom left of the main window.  As an alternative, it is also
possible to run LAMMPS using the contents of the edited file by
reading the file.  This is mainly provided as a fallback option in
case the input uses some feature that is not available when running
from a string buffer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS calculations are run in a concurrent thread so that the GUI
can stay responsive and be updated during the run.  The GUI can retrieve
data from the running LAMMPS instance and tell it to stop at the next
timestep.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Stop LAMMPS} entry will do this by calling the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_utility:_CPPv420lammps_force_timeoutPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_force\_timeout()}}}}} library function, which is equivalent
to a {\hyperref[\detokenize{timer::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timer timeout 0}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Set Variables…} entry opens a dialog box where
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{index style variables}}}} can be set. Those variables
are passed to the LAMMPS instance when it is created and are thus
set \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} a run is started.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.5]{{lammps-gui-variables}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Set Variables} dialog will be pre\sphinxhyphen{}populated with entries that
are set as index variables in the input and any variables that are
used but not defined, if the built\sphinxhyphen{}in parser can detect them.  New
rows for additional variables can be added through the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Add Row}
button and existing rows can be deleted by clicking on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{X} icons
on the right.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Create Image} entry will send a {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}}
command to the LAMMPS instance, read the resulting file, and show it
in an \sphinxstyleemphasis{Image Viewer} window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{View in OVITO} entry will launch \sphinxhref{https://ovito.org}{OVITO}
with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data file}}}} containing the current state of
the system.  This option is only available if LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI can find
the OVITO executable in the system path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{View in VMD} entry will launch VMD with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data file}}}} containing the current state of the system.  This option
is only available if LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI can find the VMD executable in the
system path.


\paragraph{View}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:view}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{View} menu offers to show or hide additional windows with log
output, charts, slide show, variables, or snapshot images.  The
default settings for their visibility can be changed in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog.


\paragraph{About}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:about}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{About} menu finally offers a couple of dialog windows and an
option to launch the LAMMPS online documentation in a web browser.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{About LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI} entry displays a dialog with a summary of the
configuration settings of the LAMMPS library in use and the version
number of LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI itself.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Quick Help} displays a dialog with
a minimal description of LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI Howto} entry
will open this documentation page from the online documentation in a web
browser window.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{LAMMPS Manual} entry will open the main page of
the LAMMPS online documentation in a web browser window.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{LAMMPS Tutorial} entry will open the main page of the set of
LAMMPS tutorials authored and maintained by Simon Gravelle at
\sphinxurl{https://lammpstutorials.github.io/} in a web browser window.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Find and Replace}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:find-and-replace}}
\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.33]{{lammps-gui-find}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Find and Replace} dialog allows searching for and replacing
text in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Editor} window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dialog can be opened either from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit} menu or with the
keyboard shortcut \sphinxtitleref{Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}F}. You can enter the text to search for.
Through three check\sphinxhyphen{}boxes the search behavior can be adjusted:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If checked, “Match case” does a case sensitive search; otherwise
the search is case insensitive.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If checked, “Wrap around” starts searching from the start of the
document, if there is no match found from the current cursor position
until the end of the document; otherwise the search will stop.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If checked, the “Whole word” setting only finds full word matches
(white space and special characters are word boundaries).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Clicking on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Next} button will search for the next occurrence of the
search text and select / highlight it. Clicking on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Replace} button
will replace an already highlighted search text and find the next one.
If no text is selected, or the selected text does not match the
selection string, then the first click on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Replace} button will
only search and highlight the next occurrence of the search string.
Clicking on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Replace All} button will replace all occurrences from
the cursor position to the end of the file; if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Wrap around} box is
checked, then it will replace \sphinxstylestrong{all} occurrences in the \sphinxstylestrong{entire}
document.  Clicking on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Done} button will dismiss the dialog.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Preferences}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:preferences}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Preferences} dialog allows customization of the behavior and
look of LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI.  The settings are grouped and each group is
displayed within a tab.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.240\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-prefs-general}.png}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.240\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-prefs-accel}.png}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.240\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-prefs-image}.png}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.240\linewidth]{{lammps-gui-prefs-editor}.png}


\paragraph{General Settings:}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:general-settings}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Echo input to log:} when checked, all input commands, including
variable expansions, are echoed to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Output} window. This is
equivalent to using \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}echo screen} at the command line.  There is no
log \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} produced by default, since LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI uses \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}log none}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Include citation details:} when checked full citation info will be
included to the log window.  This is equivalent to using \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}cite
screen} on the command line.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Show log window by default:} when checked, the screen output of a
LAMMPS run will be collected in a log window during the run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Show chart window by default:} when checked, the thermodynamic
output of a LAMMPS run will be collected and displayed in a chart
window as line graphs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Show slide show window by default:} when checked, a slide show
window will be shown with images from a dump image command, if
present, in the LAMMPS input.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Replace log window on new run:} when checked, an existing log
window will be replaced on a new LAMMPS run, otherwise each run will
create a new log window.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Replace chart window on new run:} when checked, an existing chart
window will be replaced on a new LAMMPS run, otherwise each run will
create a new chart window.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Replace image window on new render:} when checked, an existing
chart window will be replaced when a new snapshot image is requested,
otherwise each command will create a new image window.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Path to LAMMPS Shared Library File:} this option is only visible
when LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI was compiled to load the LAMMPS library at run time
instead of being linked to it directly.  With the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Browse..} button
or by changing the text, a different shared library file with a
different compilation of LAMMPS with different settings or from a
different version can be loaded.  After this setting was changed,
LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI needs to be re\sphinxhyphen{}launched.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Select Default Font:} Opens a font selection dialog where the type
and size for the default font (used for everything but the editor and
log) of the application can be set.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Select Text Font:} Opens a font selection dialog where the type and
size for the text editor and log font of the application can be set.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Data update interval:} Allows to set the time interval between data
updates during a LAMMPS run in milliseconds.  The default is to update
the data (for charts and output window) every 10 milliseconds.  This
is good for many cases.  Set this to 100 milliseconds or more if
LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI consumes too many resources during a run.  For LAMMPS runs
that run \sphinxstyleemphasis{very} fast (for example in tutorial examples), however, data
may be missed and through lowering this interval, this can be
corrected.  However, this will make the GUI use more resources.  This
setting may be changed to a value between 1 and 1000 milliseconds.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Charts update interval:} Allows to set the time interval between redrawing
the plots in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Charts} window in milliseconds.  The default is to
redraw the plots every 500 milliseconds.  This is just for the drawing,
data collection is managed with the previous setting.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Accelerators:}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:accelerators}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This tab enables selection of an accelerator package for LAMMPS to use
and is equivalent to using the \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix} and \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}package} flags on the
command line.  Only settings supported by the LAMMPS library and local
hardware are available.  The \sphinxtitleref{Number of threads} field allows setting
the maximum number of threads for the accelerator packages that use
threads.


\paragraph{Snapshot Image:}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:snapshot-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This tab allows setting defaults for the snapshot images displayed in
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Image Viewer} window, such as its dimensions and the zoom factor
applied.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Antialias} switch will render images with twice the
number of pixels for width and height and then smoothly scale the image
back to the requested size.  This produces higher quality images with
smoother edges at the expense of requiring more CPU time to render the
image.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{HQ Image mode} option turns on screen space ambient
occlusion (SSAO) mode when rendering images.  This is also more time
consuming, but produces a more ‘spatial’ representation of the system
shading of atoms by their depth.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Shiny Image mode} option will
render objects with a shiny surface when enabled.  Otherwise the
surfaces will be matted.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Show Box} option selects whether the
system box is drawn as a colored set of sticks.  Similarly, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Show
Axes} option selects whether a representation of the three system axes
will be drawn as colored sticks. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{VDW Style} checkbox selects
whether atoms are represented by space filling spheres when checked or
by smaller spheres and sticks.  Finally there are a couple of drop down
lists to select the background and box colors.


\paragraph{Editor Settings:}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_lammps_gui:editor-settings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This tab allows tweaking settings of the editor window.  Specifically
the amount of padding to be added to LAMMPS commands, types or type
ranges, IDs (e.g. for fixes), and names (e.g. for groups).  The value
set is the minimum width for the text element and it can be chosen in
the range between 1 and 32.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The three settings which follow enable or disable the automatic
reformatting when hitting the ‘Enter’ key, the automatic display of
the completion pop\sphinxhyphen{}up window, and whether auto\sphinxhyphen{}save mode is enabled.
In auto\sphinxhyphen{}save mode the editor buffer is saved before a run or before
exiting LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}GUI.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Moltemplate Tutorial}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate:moltemplate-tutorial}}\label{\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In this tutorial, we are going to use the tool {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools:moltemplate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moltemplate}}}} to set up a classical molecular dynamic simulation using
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate:oplsaa96}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{OPLS\sphinxhyphen{}AA force field}}}}. The first
task is to describe an organic compound and create a complete input deck
for LAMMPS. The second task is to map the OPLS\sphinxhyphen{}AA force field to a
molecular sample created with an external tool, e.g. PACKMOL, and
exported as a PDB file.  The files used in this tutorial can be found
in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/moltemplate/tutorial\sphinxhyphen{}files}} folder of the LAMMPS
source code distribution.


\subsubsection{Simulating an organic solvent}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate:simulating-an-organic-solvent}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This example aims to create a cubic box of the organic solvent
formamide.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first step is to create a molecular topology in the
LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}template (LT) file format representing a single molecule, which
will be stored in a Moltemplate object called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_FAM inherits OPLSAA \{\}}}.
This command states that the object \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_FAM}} is based on an existing
object called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OPLSAA}}, which contains OPLS\sphinxhyphen{}AA parameters, atom type
definitions, partial charges, masses and bond\sphinxhyphen{}angle rules for many organic
and biological compounds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The atomic structure is the starting point to populate the command
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{write(\textquotesingle{}Data Atoms\textquotesingle{}) \{\}}}, which will write the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atoms}} section in the
LAMMPS data file. The OPLS\sphinxhyphen{}AA force field uses the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atom\_style full}},
therefore, this column format is used:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\# atomID molID atomType charge coordX coordY coordZ}}.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atomID}}s are replaced with Moltemplate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$}}\sphinxhyphen{}type variables, which
are then substituted with unique numerical IDs. The same logic is applied
to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{molID}}, except that the same variable is used for the whole
molecule. The atom types are assigned using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}}\sphinxhyphen{}type variables. The
assignment of atom types (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@atom:177}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@atom:178}}) is done using
the OPLS\sphinxhyphen{}AA atom types defined in the “In Charges” section of the file
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{oplsaa.lt}}, looking for a reasonable match with the description of the atom.
The resulting file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{formamide.lt}}) follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZus{}FAM\PYG{+w}{ }inherits\PYG{+w}{ }OPLSAA\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} atomID    molID  atomType  charge  coordX  coordY  coordZ}
\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}Data Atoms\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:C00\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}\PYG{+w}{   }@atom:177\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m}{0}.100\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.490\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:O01\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}\PYG{+w}{   }@atom:178\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m}{1}.091\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}0.250\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:N02\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}\PYG{+w}{   }@atom:179\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00\PYG{+w}{   }\PYGZhy{}1.121\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}0.181\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H03\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}\PYG{+w}{   }@atom:182\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00\PYG{+w}{   }\PYGZhy{}2.013\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.272\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H04\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}\PYG{+w}{   }@atom:182\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00\PYG{+w}{   }\PYGZhy{}1.056\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}1.190\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H05\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}\PYG{+w}{   }@atom:221\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m}{0}.144\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{1}.570\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} A list of the bonds in the molecule:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} BondID   AtomID1   AtomID2}
\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}Data Bond List\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:C1\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:C00\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:O01
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:C2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:C00\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H05
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:C3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:C00\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:N02
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:C4\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:N02\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H03
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:C5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:N02\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H04
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You don’t have to specify the charge in this example because they will
be assigned according to the atom type. Analogously, only a
“Data Bond List” section is needed as the atom type will determine the
bond type. The other bonded interactions (e.g. angles,
dihedrals, and impropers) will be automatically generated by
Moltemplate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the simulation is non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral, or Moltemplate complains that you have
missing bond, angle, or dihedral types, this means at least one of your
atom types is incorrect.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second step is to create a master file with instructions to build a
starting structure and the LAMMPS commands to run an NPT simulation. The
master file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solv\_01.lt}}) follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Import the force field.}
import\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/local/moltemplate/moltemplate/force\PYGZus{}fields/oplsaa.lt
import\PYG{+w}{ }formamide.lt\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} after oplsaa.lt, as it depends on it.}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create the input sample.}
\PYG{n+nv}{solv}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }new\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZus{}FAM\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{o}{]}.move\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}.6,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{+w}{                }\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{o}{]}.move\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}.6,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{+w}{                }\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{o}{]}.move\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}.6\PYG{o}{)}
solv\PYG{o}{[}*\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{o}{[}*\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{o}{[}*\PYG{o}{]}.move\PYG{o}{(}\PYGZhy{}11.5,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}11.5,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}11.5\PYG{o}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the simulation box.}
write\PYGZus{}once\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Data Boundary\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}11.5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{11}.5\PYG{+w}{ }xlo\PYG{+w}{ }xhi
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}11.5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{11}.5\PYG{+w}{ }ylo\PYG{+w}{ }yhi
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}11.5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{11}.5\PYG{+w}{ }zlo\PYG{+w}{ }zhi
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create an input deck for LAMMPS.}
write\PYGZus{}once\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}In Init\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Input variables.}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }string\PYG{+w}{ }solv\PYGZus{}01\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} output name}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }ts\PYG{+w}{     }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} timestep}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }temp\PYG{+w}{   }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} equilibrium temperature}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }p\PYG{+w}{      }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}.\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} equilibrium pressure}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }d\PYG{+w}{      }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} output frequency}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }equi\PYG{+w}{   }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{5000}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Equilibration steps}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }prod\PYG{+w}{   }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{30000}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Production steps}

\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} PBC (set them before the creation of the box).}
\PYG{+w}{ }boundary\PYG{+w}{ }p\PYG{+w}{ }p\PYG{+w}{ }p
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run an NPT simulation.}
write\PYGZus{}once\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}In Run\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Derived variables.}
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }tcouple\PYG{+w}{ }equal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}ts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}*100
\PYG{+w}{ }variable\PYG{+w}{ }pcouple\PYG{+w}{ }equal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}ts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}*1000

\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Output.}
\PYG{+w}{ }thermo\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}d
\PYG{+w}{ }thermo\PYGZus{}style\PYG{+w}{ }custom\PYG{+w}{ }step\PYG{+w}{ }etotal\PYG{+w}{ }evdwl\PYG{+w}{ }ecoul\PYG{+w}{ }elong\PYG{+w}{ }ebond\PYG{+w}{ }eangle\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }edihed\PYG{+w}{ }eimp\PYG{+w}{ }ke\PYG{+w}{ }pe\PYG{+w}{ }temp\PYG{+w}{ }press\PYG{+w}{ }vol\PYG{+w}{ }density\PYG{+w}{ }cpu
\PYG{+w}{ }thermo\PYGZus{}modify\PYG{+w}{ }flush\PYG{+w}{ }yes

\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Trajectory.}
\PYG{+w}{ }dump\PYG{+w}{ }TRJ\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{ }dcd\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}run\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}.dcd
\PYG{+w}{ }dump\PYGZus{}modify\PYG{+w}{ }TRJ\PYG{+w}{ }unwrap\PYG{+w}{ }yes

\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Thermalisation and relaxation, NPT ensemble.}
\PYG{+w}{ }timestep\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}ts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }fix\PYG{+w}{             }NPT\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{ }npt\PYG{+w}{ }temp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}temp\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}temp\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}tcouple\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }iso\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}pcouple\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }velocity\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}temp\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{858096}\PYG{+w}{ }dist\PYG{+w}{ }gaussian
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Short runs to update the PPPM settings as the box shinks.}
\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}equi\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }post\PYG{+w}{ }no
\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}equi\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }post\PYG{+w}{ }no
\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}equi\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }post\PYG{+w}{ }no
\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}equi\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} From now on, the density shouldn\PYGZsq{}t change too much.}
\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}prod\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }unfix\PYG{+w}{ }NPT
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first two commands insert the content of files \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{oplsaa.lt}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{formamide.lt}} into the master file. At this point, we can use the
command \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solv = new \_FAM {[}N{]}}} to create N copies of a molecule of type
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_FAM}}. In this case, we create an array of 5*5*5 molecules on a cubic
grid using the coordinate transformation command \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.move( 4.6, 0, 0)}}.
See the Moltemplate documentation to learn more about the syntax. As
the sample was created from scratch, we also specify the simulation box
size in the “Data Boundary” section.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS setting for the force field are specified in the file
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{oplsaa.lt}} and are written automatically in the input deck. We also
specify the boundary conditions and a set of variables in
the “In Init” section. The remaining commands to run an NPT simulation
are written in the “In Run” section. Note that in this script, LAMMPS
variables are protected with the escape character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}} to distinguish
them from Moltemplate variables, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}\$\textbackslash{}\{run\textbackslash{}\}}} is a LAMMPS
variable that is written in the input deck as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$\{run\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compile the master file with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
moltemplate.sh\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}overlay\PYGZhy{}all\PYG{+w}{ }solv\PYGZus{}01.lt
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
And execute the simulation with the following:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }lmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }solv\PYGZus{}01.in\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}l\PYG{+w}{ }solv\PYGZus{}01.log
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{solv_01}.png}
\caption{Snapshot of the sample at the beginning and end of the simulation.
Rendered with Ovito.}\label{\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate:id1}}\end{figure}


\subsubsection{Mapping an existing structure}
\label{\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate:mapping-an-existing-structure}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Another helpful way to use Moltemplate is mapping an existing molecular
sample to a force field. This is useful when a complex sample is
assembled from different simulations or created with specialized
software (e.g. PACKMOL). As in the previous example, all molecular
species in the sample must be defined using single\sphinxhyphen{}molecule Moltemplate
objects.  For this example, we use a short polymer in a box containing
water molecules and ions in the PDB file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.pdb}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is essential to understand that the order of atoms in the PDB file
and in the Moltemplate master script must match, as we are using the
coordinates from the PDB file in the order they appear. The order of
atoms and molecules in the PDB file provided is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
500 water molecules, with atoms ordered in this sequence:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ATOM      1  O   MOL D   1       5.901   7.384   1.103  0.00  0.00      DUM
ATOM      2  H   MOL D   1       6.047   8.238   0.581  0.00  0.00      DUM
ATOM      3  H   MOL D   1       6.188   7.533   2.057  0.00  0.00      DUM
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 polymer molecule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 Ca$^{\text{2+}}$ ion.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2 Cl$^{\text{\sphinxhyphen{}}}$ ions.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the master LT file, this sequence of molecules is matched with the
following commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create the sample.}
\PYG{n+nv}{wat}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }SPC\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{o}{]}
\PYG{n+nv}{pol}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }PolyNIPAM\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{]}
\PYG{n+nv}{cat}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }Ca\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{]}
\PYG{n+nv}{ani}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }Cl\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the first command would create 500 water molecules in the
same position in space, and the other commands will use the coordinates
specified in the corresponding molecular topology block. However, the
coordinates will be overwritten by rendering an external atomic
structure file. Note that if the same molecule species are scattered in
the input structure, it is recommended to reorder and group together
for molecule types to facilitate the creation of the input sample.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The molecular topology for the polymer is created as in the previous
example, with the atom types assigned as in the following schema:

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.3]{{PolyNIPAM}.jpg}
\caption{Atom types assigned to the polymer’s repeating unit.}\label{\detokenize{Howto_moltemplate:id2}}\end{figure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The molecular topology of the water and ions is stated directly into
the master file for the sake of space, but they could also be written
in a separate file(s) and imported before the sample is created.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The resulting master LT file defining short annealing at a fixed volume
(NVT) follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the OPLS\PYGZhy{}AA force field for all species.}
import\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/local/moltemplate/moltemplate/force\PYGZus{}fields/oplsaa.lt
import\PYG{+w}{ }PolyNIPAM.lt

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define the SPC water and ions as in the OPLS\PYGZhy{}AA}
Ca\PYG{+w}{ }inherits\PYG{+w}{ }OPLSAA\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Data Atoms\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:a1\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}:.\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:354\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.000000
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
Cl\PYG{+w}{ }inherits\PYG{+w}{ }OPLSAA\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Data Atoms\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:a1\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}:.\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:344\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.000000
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
SPC\PYG{+w}{ }inherits\PYG{+w}{ }OPLSAA\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Data Atoms\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:O\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}:.\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:76\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0000000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.000000
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H1\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}:.\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:77\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}.8164904\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.5773590
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}mol}:.\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:77\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}0.8164904\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.00000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.5773590
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Data Bond List\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:OH1\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:O\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H1
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}bond}:OH2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:O\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}atom}:H2
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create the sample.}
\PYG{n+nv}{wat}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }SPC\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{o}{]}
\PYG{n+nv}{pol}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }PolyNIPAM\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{]}
\PYG{n+nv}{cat}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }Ca\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{]}
\PYG{n+nv}{ani}\PYG{o}{=}new\PYG{+w}{ }Cl\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{o}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Periodic boundary conditions:}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{26}\PYG{+w}{ }xlo\PYG{+w}{ }xhi
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{26}\PYG{+w}{ }ylo\PYG{+w}{ }yhi
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{26}\PYG{+w}{ }zlo\PYG{+w}{ }zhi
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define the input variables.}
write\PYGZus{}once\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}In Init\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Input variables.}
\PYG{+w}{  }variable\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{    }string\PYG{+w}{ }sample01\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} output name}
\PYG{+w}{  }variable\PYG{+w}{ }ts\PYG{+w}{     }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} timestep}
\PYG{+w}{  }variable\PYG{+w}{ }temp\PYG{+w}{   }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{298}.15\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} equilibrium temperature}
\PYG{+w}{  }variable\PYG{+w}{ }p\PYG{+w}{      }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}.\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} equilibrium pressure}
\PYG{+w}{  }variable\PYG{+w}{ }equi\PYG{+w}{   }equal\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{30000}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} equilibration steps}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} PBC (set them before the creation of the box).}
\PYG{+w}{  }boundary\PYG{+w}{ }p\PYG{+w}{ }p\PYG{+w}{ }p
\PYG{+w}{  }neighbor\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }bin
\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run an NVT simulation.}
write\PYGZus{}once\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}In Run\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the output.}
\PYG{+w}{  }thermo\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{+w}{  }thermo\PYGZus{}style\PYG{+w}{    }custom\PYG{+w}{ }step\PYG{+w}{ }etotal\PYG{+w}{ }evdwl\PYG{+w}{ }ecoul\PYG{+w}{ }elong\PYG{+w}{ }ebond\PYG{+w}{ }eangle\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }edihed\PYG{+w}{ }eimp\PYG{+w}{ }pe\PYG{+w}{ }ke\PYG{+w}{ }temp\PYG{+w}{ }press\PYG{+w}{ }atoms\PYG{+w}{ }vol\PYG{+w}{ }density\PYG{+w}{ }cpu
\PYG{+w}{  }thermo\PYGZus{}modify\PYG{+w}{ }flush\PYG{+w}{ }yes
\PYG{+w}{  }compute\PYG{+w}{ }pe1\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{ }pe/atom\PYG{+w}{ }pair
\PYG{+w}{  }dump\PYG{+w}{ }TRJ\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{ }custom\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}run\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}.dump\PYG{+w}{ }id\PYG{+w}{ }xu\PYG{+w}{ }yu\PYG{+w}{ }zu\PYG{+w}{ }c\PYGZus{}pe1

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Minimise the input structure, just in case.}

\PYG{+w}{  }write\PYGZus{}data\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}run\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}.min

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the constrains.}
\PYG{+w}{  }group\PYG{+w}{ }watergroup\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:76\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:77
\PYG{+w}{  }fix\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }watergroup\PYG{+w}{ }shake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0001\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }b\PYG{+w}{ }@bond:042\PYGZus{}043\PYG{+w}{ }a\PYG{+w}{ }@angle:043\PYGZus{}042\PYGZus{}043

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Short annealing.}
\PYG{+w}{  }timestep\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}ts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }fix\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{ }nvt\PYG{+w}{ }temp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}temp\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}temp\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{l+m}{100}*dt\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{+w}{  }velocity\PYG{+w}{    }all\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}temp\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{315443}
\PYG{+w}{  }run\PYG{+w}{             }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZob{}}equi\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }unfix\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this example, the water model is SPC and it is defined in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{oplsaa.lt}} file with atom types \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@atom:76}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@atom:77}}.  For
water we also use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix shake}} commands with
Moltemplate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}}\sphinxhyphen{}type variables, to ensure consistency with the
numerical values assigned during compilation. To identify the bond and
angle types, look for the extended \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@atom}} IDs, which in this case
are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
replace\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:76\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:76\PYGZus{}b042\PYGZus{}a042\PYGZus{}d042\PYGZus{}i042\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
replace\PYG{o}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:77\PYG{+w}{ }@atom:77\PYGZus{}b043\PYGZus{}a043\PYGZus{}d043\PYGZus{}i043\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
From which we can identify the following “Data Bonds By Type”:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@bond:042\_043 @atom:*\_b042*\_a*\_d*\_i* @atom:*\_b043*\_a*\_d*\_i*}} and
“Data Angles By Type”: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@angle:043\_042\_043 @atom:*\_b*\_a043*\_d*\_i*
@atom:*\_b*\_a042*\_d*\_i* @atom:*\_b*\_a043*\_d*\_i*}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compile the master file with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
moltemplate.sh\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}overlay\PYGZhy{}all\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}pdb\PYG{+w}{ }model.pdb\PYG{+w}{ }sample01.lt
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
And execute the simulation with the following:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }lmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }sample01.in\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}l\PYG{+w}{ }sample01.log
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
