\subsection{Using the GDB debugger to get a stack trace}
\label{\detokenize{Errors_debug:using-the-gdb-debugger-to-get-a-stack-trace}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are two options to use the GDB debugger for identifying the origin
of the segmentation fault or similar crash. The GDB debugger has many
more features and options, as can be seen for example its \sphinxhref{https://www.sourceware.org/gdb/documentation/}{online
documentation}.


\subsubsection{Run LAMMPS from within the debugger}
\label{\detokenize{Errors_debug:run-lammps-from-within-the-debugger}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Running LAMMPS under the control of the debugger as shown below only
works for a single MPI rank (for debugging a program running in parallel
you usually need a parallel debugger program).  A simple way to launch
GDB is to prefix the LAMMPS command line with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gdb \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}args}} and then
type the command “run” at the GDB prompt.  This will launch the
debugger, load the LAMMPS executable and its debug info, and then run
it.  When it reaches the code causing the segmentation fault, it will
stop with a message why it stopped, print the current line of code, and
drop back to the GDB prompt.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{run}
\PYG{g+go}{[...]}
\PYG{g+go}{Setting up Verlet run ...}
\PYG{g+go}{  Unit style    : lj}
\PYG{g+go}{  Current step  : 0}
\PYG{g+go}{  Time step     : 0.005}

\PYG{g+go}{Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.}
\PYG{g+go}{0x00000000006653ab in LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::PairLJCut::compute (this=0x829740, eflag=1, vflag=\PYGZlt{}optimized out\PYGZgt{}) at /home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/pair\PYGZus{}lj\PYGZus{}cut.cpp:139}
\PYG{g+go}{139      comx += atom\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{}rmass[i]*x[i][0]; /* BUG */}
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Now typing the command “where” will show the stack of functions starting from
the current function back to “main()”.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{where}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{  }0x00000000006653ab\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::PairLJCut::compute\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{this}\PYG{o}{=}0x829740,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{eflag}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{vflag}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZlt{}optimized\PYG{+w}{ }out\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }at\PYG{+w}{ }/home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/pair\PYGZus{}lj\PYGZus{}cut.cpp:139
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{  }0x00000000004cf0a2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Verlet::setup\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{this}\PYG{o}{=}0x7e6c90,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{flag}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }at\PYG{+w}{ }/home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/verlet.cpp:131
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }0x000000000049db42\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Run::command\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{this}\PYG{o}{=}this@entry\PYG{o}{=}0x7fffffffcca0,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{narg}\PYG{o}{=}narg@entry\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{arg}\PYG{o}{=}arg@entry\PYG{o}{=}0x7e8750\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{    at /home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/run.cpp:177}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{  }0x000000000041258a\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Input::command\PYGZus{}creator\PYGZlt{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Run\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{lmp}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZlt{}optimized\PYG{+w}{ }out\PYGZgt{},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{narg}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{arg}\PYG{o}{=}0x7e8750\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{    at /home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/input.cpp:878}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{  }0x0000000000410ad3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Input::execute\PYGZus{}command\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{this}\PYG{o}{=}0x7d1410\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }at\PYG{+w}{ }/home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/input.cpp:864
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{  }0x00000000004111fb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Input::file\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{this}\PYG{o}{=}0x7d1410\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }at\PYG{+w}{ }/home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/input.cpp:229
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{  }0x000000000040933a\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }main\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{argc}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZlt{}optimized\PYG{+w}{ }out\PYGZgt{},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{argv}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZlt{}optimized\PYG{+w}{ }out\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }at\PYG{+w}{ }/home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/main.cpp:65
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also print the value of variables and see if there is anything
unexpected.  Segmentation faults, for example, commonly happen when a
pointer variable is not assigned and still initialized to NULL.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{print x}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{n+nv}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}double\PYG{+w}{ }**\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }0x7ffff7ca1010
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{print i}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{n+nv}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{print x[0]}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{n+nv}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}double\PYG{+w}{ }*\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }0x7ffff6d80010
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{print x[0][0]}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{n+nv}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{print x[1][0]}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{n+nv}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.83979809569125363
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)} \PYG{g+go}{print atom\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{}rmass}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{n+nv}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}double\PYG{+w}{ }*\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }0x0
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Inspect a core dump file with the debugger}
\label{\detokenize{Errors_debug:inspect-a-core-dump-file-with-the-debugger}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When an executable crashes with a “core dumped” message, it creates a
file “core” or “core.\textless{}PID\#\textgreater{}” which contains the information about the
current state.  This file may be located in the folder where you ran
LAMMPS or in some hidden folder managed by the systemd daemon.  In the
latter case, you need to “extract” the core file with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coredumpctl}}
utility to the current folder. Example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coredumpctl \sphinxhyphen{}o core dump lmp}}.
Now you can launch the debugger to load the executable, its debug info
and the core dump and drop you to a prompt like before.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }gdb\PYG{+w}{ }lmp\PYG{+w}{ }core
\PYG{g+go}{Reading symbols from lmp...}
\PYG{g+go}{[New LWP 1928535]}
\PYG{g+go}{[Thread debugging using libthread\PYGZus{}db enabled]}
\PYG{g+go}{Using host libthread\PYGZus{}db library \PYGZdq{}/lib64/libthread\PYGZus{}db.so.1\PYGZdq{}.}
\PYG{g+go}{Core was generated by `./lmp \PYGZhy{}in in.melt\PYGZsq{}.}
\PYG{g+go}{Program terminated with signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{  }0x00000000006653ab\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::PairLJCut::compute\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{this}\PYG{o}{=}0x1b10740,\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{eflag}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1},\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{vflag}\PYG{o}{=}\PYGZlt{}optimized\PYG{+w}{ }out\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{    at /home/akohlmey/compile/lammps/src/pair\PYGZus{}lj\PYGZus{}cut.cpp:139}
\PYG{g+go}{139      comx += atom\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{}rmass[i]*x[i][0]; /* BUG */}
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(gdb)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
From here on, you use the same commands as shown before to get a stack
trace and print current values of (pointer) variables.


\subsection{Using valgrind to get a stack trace}
\label{\detokenize{Errors_debug:using-valgrind-to-get-a-stack-trace}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://valgrind.org}{valgrind} suite of tools allows to closely
inspect the behavior of a compiled program by essentially emulating a
CPU and instrumenting the program while running.  This slows down
execution quite significantly, but can also report issues that are not
resulting in a crash.  The default valgrind tool is a memory checker and
you can use it by prefixing the normal command line with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{valgrind}}.
Unlike GDB, this will also work for parallel execution, but it is
recommended to redirect the valgrind output to a file (e.g. with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}log\sphinxhyphen{}file=crash\sphinxhyphen{}\%p.txt}}, the \%p will be substituted with the
process ID) so that the messages of the multiple valgrind instances to
the console are not mixed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }valgrind\PYG{+w}{ }./lmp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.melt
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642== Memcheck, a memory error detector}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642== Copyright (C) 2002\PYGZhy{}2017, and GNU GPL\PYGZsq{}d, by Julian Seward et al.}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642== Using Valgrind\PYGZhy{}3.15.0 and LibVEX; rerun with \PYGZhy{}h for copyright info}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642== Command: ./lmp \PYGZhy{}in in.melt}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==}
\PYG{g+go}{LAMMPS (19 Mar 2020)}
\PYG{g+go}{OMP\PYGZus{}NUM\PYGZus{}THREADS environment is not set. Defaulting to 1 thread. (src/comm.cpp:94)}
\PYG{g+go}{  using 1 OpenMP thread(s) per MPI task}
\PYG{g+go}{Lattice spacing in x,y,z = 1.6796 1.6796 1.6796}
\PYG{g+go}{Created orthogonal box = (0 0 0) to (16.796 16.796 16.796)}
\PYG{g+go}{  1 by 1 by 1 MPI processor grid}
\PYG{g+go}{Created 4000 atoms}
\PYG{g+go}{  create\PYGZus{}atoms CPU = 0.032964 secs}
\PYG{g+go}{Neighbor list info ...}
\PYG{g+go}{  update every 20 steps, delay 0 steps, check no}
\PYG{g+go}{  max neighbors/atom: 2000, page size: 100000}
\PYG{g+go}{  master list distance cutoff = 2.8}
\PYG{g+go}{  ghost atom cutoff = 2.8}
\PYG{g+go}{  binsize = 1.4, bins = 12 12 12}
\PYG{g+go}{  1 neighbor lists, perpetual/occasional/extra = 1 0 0}
\PYG{g+go}{  (1) pair lj/cut, perpetual}
\PYG{g+go}{      attributes: half, newton on}
\PYG{g+go}{      pair build: half/bin/atomonly/newton}
\PYG{g+go}{      stencil: half/bin/3d/newton}
\PYG{g+go}{      bin: standard}
\PYG{g+go}{Setting up Verlet run ...}
\PYG{g+go}{  Unit style    : lj}
\PYG{g+go}{  Current step  : 0}
\PYG{g+go}{  Time step     : 0.005}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642== Invalid read of size 8}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    at 0x6653AB: LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::PairLJCut::compute(int, int) (pair\PYGZus{}lj\PYGZus{}cut.cpp:139)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    by 0x4CF0A1: LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Verlet::setup(int) (verlet.cpp:131)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    by 0x49DB41: LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Run::command(int, char**) (run.cpp:177)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    by 0x412589: void LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Input::command\PYGZus{}creator\PYGZlt{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Run\PYGZgt{}(LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::LAMMPS*, int, char**) (input.cpp:881)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    by 0x410AD2: LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Input::execute\PYGZus{}command() (input.cpp:864)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    by 0x4111FA: LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS::Input::file() (input.cpp:229)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==    by 0x409339: main (main.cpp:65)}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==  Address 0x0 is not stack\PYGZsq{}d, malloc\PYGZsq{}d or (recently) free\PYGZsq{}d}
\PYG{g+go}{==1933642==}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As you can see, the stack trace information is similar to that obtained
from GDB. In addition you get a more specific hint about what cause the
segmentation fault, i.e. that it is a NULL pointer dereference.  To find
out which pointer exactly was NULL, you need to use the debugger, though.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Error messages}
\label{\detokenize{Errors_messages:error-messages}}\label{\detokenize{Errors_messages::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is an alphabetic list of the ERROR messages LAMMPS prints out and
the reason why.  If the explanation here is not sufficient, the
documentation for the offending command may help.  Error messages also
list the source file and line number where the error was generated.
For example, a message like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ERROR: Illegal velocity command (velocity.cpp:78)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
means that line \#78 in the file src/velocity.cpp generated the error.
Looking in the source code may help you figure out what went wrong.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Doc page with {\hyperref[\detokenize{Errors_warnings::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{WARNING messages}}}}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{1\sphinxhyphen{}3 bond count is inconsistent}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An inconsistency was detected when computing the number of 1\sphinxhyphen{}3
neighbors for each atom.  This likely means something is wrong with
the bond topologies you have defined.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{1\sphinxhyphen{}4 bond count is inconsistent}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An inconsistency was detected when computing the number of 1\sphinxhyphen{}4
neighbors for each atom.  This likely means something is wrong with
the bond topologies you have defined.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Accelerator sharing is not currently supported on system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple MPI processes cannot share the accelerator on your
system. For NVIDIA GPUs, see the nvidia\sphinxhyphen{}smi command to change this
setting.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All angle coeffs are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All angle coefficients must be set in the data file or by the
angle\_coeff command before running a simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All atom IDs = 0 but atom\_modify id = yes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All atoms of a swapped type must have same charge.}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All atoms of a swapped type must have the same charge.}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All bond coeffs are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All bond coefficients must be set in the data file or by the
bond\_coeff command before running a simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All dihedral coeffs are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dihedral coefficients must be set in the data file or by the
dihedral\_coeff command before running a simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All improper coeffs are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All improper coefficients must be set in the data file or by the
improper\_coeff command before running a simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All masses are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom styles that define masses for each atom type, all masses must
be set in the data file or by the mass command before running a
simulation.  They must also be set before using the velocity
command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All mol IDs should be set for fix gcmc group atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The molecule flag is on, yet not all molecule ids in the fix group
have been set to non\sphinxhyphen{}zero positive values by the user. This is an
error since all atoms in the fix gcmc group are eligible for deletion,
rotation, and translation and therefore must have valid molecule ids.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All pair coeffs are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All pair coefficients must be set in the data file or by the
pair\_coeff command before running a simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All read\_dump x,y,z fields must be specified for scaled, triclinic coords}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For triclinic boxes and scaled coordinates you must specify all 3 of
the x,y,z fields, else LAMMPS cannot reconstruct the unscaled
coordinates.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All universe/uloop variables must have same \# of values}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{All variables in next command must be same style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle atom missing in delete\_bonds}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The delete\_bonds command cannot find one or more atoms in a particular
angle on a particular processor.  The pairwise cutoff is too short or
the atoms are too far apart to make a valid angle.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle atom missing in set command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The set command cannot find one or more atoms in a particular angle on
a particular processor.  The pairwise cutoff is too short or the atoms
are too far apart to make a valid angle.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle atoms \%d \%d \%d missing on proc \%d at step \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more of three atoms needed to compute a particular angle are
missing on this processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise
cutoff is set too short or the angle has blown apart and an atom is
too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle atoms missing on proc \%d at step \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more of three atoms needed to compute a particular angle are
missing on this processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise
cutoff is set too short or the angle has blown apart and an atom is
too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle coeff for hybrid has invalid style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Angle style hybrid uses another angle style as one of its
coefficients.  The angle style used in the angle\_coeff command or read
from a restart file is not recognized.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle coeffs are not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No angle coefficients have been assigned in the data file or via the
angle\_coeff command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle extent \textgreater{} half of periodic box length}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This error was detected by the neigh\_modify check yes setting.  It is
an error because the angle atoms are so far apart it is ambiguous how
it should be defined.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle potential must be defined for SHAKE}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When shaking angles, an angle\_style potential must be used.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle style hybrid cannot have hybrid as an argument}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle style hybrid cannot have none as an argument}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle style hybrid cannot use same angle style twice}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle table must range from 0 to 180 degrees}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle table parameters did not set N}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of angle table parameters must include N setting.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle\_coeff command before angle\_style is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coefficients cannot be set in the data file or via the angle\_coeff
command until an angle\_style has been assigned.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle\_coeff command before simulation box is defined}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot add atoms to fix move variable}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot append atoms to a triclinic box}}

Cartesian axes.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot balance in z dimension for 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change box ortho/triclinic with certain fixes defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because those fixes store the shape of the box.  You need to
use unfix to discard the fix, change the box, then redefine a new
fix.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change box ortho/triclinic with dumps defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because some dumps store the shape of the box.  You need to
use undump to discard the dump, change the box, then redefine a new
dump.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change box tilt factors for orthogonal box}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cannot use tilt factors unless the simulation box is non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change box to orthogonal when tilt is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change box z boundary to non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic for a 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change dump\_modify every for dump dcd}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change dump\_modify every for dump xtc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The frequency of writing dump xtc snapshots cannot be changed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change timestep once fix srd is setup}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

size.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change timestep with fix pour}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because fix pour pre\sphinxhyphen{}computes the time delay for particles to
fall out of the insertion volume due to gravity.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change to comm\_style brick from tiled layout}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change\_box after reading restart file with per\sphinxhyphen{}atom info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the restart file info cannot be migrated with the
atoms.  You can get around this by performing a 0\sphinxhyphen{}timestep run which
will assign the restart file info to actual atoms.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change\_box in xz or yz for 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot change\_box in z dimension for 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot clear group all}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This operation is not allowed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot close restart file \sphinxhyphen{} MPI error: \%s}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This error was generated by MPI when reading/writing an MPI\sphinxhyphen{}IO restart

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot compute initial g\_ewald\_disp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS failed to compute an initial guess for the PPPM\_disp g\_ewald\_6
factor that partitions the computation between real space and k\sphinxhyphen{}space
for Dispersion interactions.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot create an atom map unless atoms have IDs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simulation requires a mapping from global atom IDs to local atoms,
but the atoms that have been defined have no IDs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot create atoms with undefined lattice}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use the lattice command before using the create\_atoms
command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot create/grow a vector/array of pointers for \%s}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS code is making an illegal call to the templated memory
allocators, to create a vector or array of pointers.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot create\_atoms after reading restart file with per\sphinxhyphen{}atom info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom info was stored to be used when by a fix that you may
re\sphinxhyphen{}define.  If you add atoms before re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix, then there
will not be a correct amount of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom info.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot create\_box after simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A simulation box can only be defined once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot currently use pair reax with pair hybrid}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot currently use pppm/gpu with fix balance.}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot displace\_atoms after reading restart file with per\sphinxhyphen{}atom info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the restart file info cannot be migrated with the
atoms.  You can get around this by performing a 0\sphinxhyphen{}timestep run which
will assign the restart file info to actual atoms.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot do GCMC on atoms in atom\_modify first group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a restriction due to the way atoms are organized in a list to
enable the atom\_modify first command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot do atom/swap on atoms in atom\_modify first group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a restriction due to the way atoms are organized in a list to
enable the atom\_modify first command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot dump sort on atom IDs with no atom IDs defined}}

Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot dump sort when multiple dump files are written}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

no sorting is allowed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot embed Python when also extending Python with LAMMPS}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When running LAMMPS via Python through the LAMMPS library interface

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot evaporate atoms in atom\_modify first group}}

a list to enable the atom\_modify first command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot find specified group ID for shell particles}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot have both pair\_modify shift and tail set to yes}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot intersect groups using a dynamic group}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a multi\sphinxhyphen{}partition run, the master screen file cannot be opened.
Check that the directory you are running in allows for files to be
created.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot read from restart file \sphinxhyphen{} MPI error: \%s}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This error was generated by MPI when reading/writing an MPI\sphinxhyphen{}IO restart
file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot read\_data without add keyword after simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot read\_restart after simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The read\_restart command cannot be used after a read\_data,
read\_restart, or create\_box command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot redefine variable as a different style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable can be re\sphinxhyphen{}defined but only if it was
originally an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot replicate 2d simulation in z dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The replicate command cannot replicate a 2d simulation in the z
dimension.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot replicate with fixes that store atom quantities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Either fixes are defined that create and store atom\sphinxhyphen{}based vectors or a
restart file was read which included atom\sphinxhyphen{}based vectors for fixes.
The replicate command cannot duplicate that information for new atoms.
You should use the replicate command before fixes are applied to the
system.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot reset timestep with a dynamic region defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dynamic regions (see the region command) have a time dependence.
Thus you cannot change the timestep when one or more of these
are defined.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot reset timestep with a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent fix defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot reset the timestep when a fix that keeps track of elapsed
time is in place.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot run 2d simulation with non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic Z dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the boundary command to make the z dimension periodic in order to
run a 2d simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set bond topology types for atom style template}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bond, angle, etc types cannot be changed for this atom style since
they are static settings in the molecule template files.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set both respa pair and inner/middle/outer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the rRESPA integrator, you must compute pairwise potentials either
all together (pair), or in pieces (inner/middle/outer).  You can’t do
both.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set cutoff/multi before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set dpd/theta for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set dump\_modify flush for dump xtc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set mass for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This atom style does not support mass settings for each atom type.
Instead they are defined on a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom basis in the data file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set meso/cv for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set meso/e for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set meso/rho for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set non\sphinxhyphen{}zero image flag for non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set non\sphinxhyphen{}zero z velocity for 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set quaternion for atom that has none}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set quaternion with xy components for 2d system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set respa hybrid and any of pair/inner/middle/outer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the rRESPA integrator, you must compute pairwise potentials either
all together (pair), with different cutoff regions (inner/middle/outer),
or per hybrid sub\sphinxhyphen{}style (hybrid).  You cannot mix those.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set respa middle without inner/outer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the rRESPA integrator, you must define both a inner and outer
setting in order to use a middle setting.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set restart file size \sphinxhyphen{} MPI error: \%s}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This error was generated by MPI when reading/writing an MPI\sphinxhyphen{}IO restart
file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set smd/contact/radius for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set smd/mass/density for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set temperature for fix rigid/nph}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temp keyword cannot be specified.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set theta for atom that is not a line}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set this attribute for this atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The attribute being set does not exist for the defined atom style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot set variable z velocity for 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot skew triclinic box in z for 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot subtract groups using a dynamic group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This operation is not allowed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot union groups using a dynamic group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This operation is not allowed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use \sphinxhyphen{}kokkos on without KOKKOS installed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use \sphinxhyphen{}reorder after \sphinxhyphen{}partition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.  See page discussion of command\sphinxhyphen{}line switches.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use Ewald with 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace style ewald cannot be used in 2d simulations.  You can use
2d Ewald in a 3d simulation; see the kspace\_modify command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use Ewald/disp solver on system with no charge, dipole, or LJ particles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No atoms in system have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero charge or dipole, or are LJ
particles.  Change charges/dipoles or change options of the kspace
solver/pair style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use EwaldDisp with 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a current restriction of this command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use Kokkos pair style with rRESPA inner/middle}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use NEB unless atom map exists}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the atom\_modify command to create an atom map.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use NEB with a single replica}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use NEB with atom\_modify sort enabled}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is current restriction for NEB implemented in LAMMPS.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PPPM with 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace style pppm cannot be used in 2d simulations.  You can use
2d PPPM in a 3d simulation; see the kspace\_modify command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PPPMDisp with 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace style pppm/disp cannot be used in 2d simulations.  You can
use 2d pppm/disp in a 3d simulation; see the kspace\_modify command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PRD with a changing box}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current box dimensions are not copied between replicas

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PRD with a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent fix defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PRD alters the timestep in ways that will mess up these fixes.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PRD with a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent region defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PRD alters the timestep in ways that will mess up these regions.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PRD with atom\_modify sort enabled}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a current restriction of PRD.  You must turn off sorting,
which is enabled by default, via the atom\_modify command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use PRD with multi\sphinxhyphen{}processor replicas unless atom map exists}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use delete\_atoms bond yes with atom\_style template}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the bonds for that atom style are hardwired in the

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use delete\_bonds with non\sphinxhyphen{}molecular system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix TMD unless atom map exists}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using this fix requires the ability to lookup an atom index, which is
provided by an atom map.  An atom map does not exist (by default) for
non\sphinxhyphen{}molecular problems.  Using the atom\_modify map command will force
an atom map to be created.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix bond/break with non\sphinxhyphen{}molecular systems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only systems with bonds that can be changed can be used.  Atom\_style
template does not qualify.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix bond/create with non\sphinxhyphen{}molecular systems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

template does not qualify.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix bond/swap with non\sphinxhyphen{}molecular systems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only systems with bonds that can be changed can be used.  Atom\_style
template does not qualify.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix box/relax on a 2nd non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When specifying an off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal pressure component, the second of the two
dimensions must be periodic.  E.g. if the xy component is specified,
then the y dimension must be periodic.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix box/relax on a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When specifying a diagonal pressure component, the dimension must be
periodic.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix box/relax with both relaxation and scaling on a tilt factor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When specifying scaling on a tilt factor component, that component can not
also be controlled by the barostat. E.g. if scalexy yes is specified and
also keyword tri or xy, this is wrong.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix box/relax with tilt factor scaling on a 2nd non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When specifying scaling on a tilt factor component, the second of the two
dimensions must be periodic.  E.g. if the xy component is specified,
then the y dimension must be periodic.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix deform on a shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped boundary}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The x, y, z options cannot be applied to shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped
dimensions.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix deform tilt on a shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped 2nd dim}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapping will change the value
of the strain implied by the tilt factor.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use fix deform trate on a box with zero tilt}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The trate style alters the current strain.

then the y dimension must be periodic.

periodic.

unless you use the kspace\_modify command to define a 2d slab with a
non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic z dimension.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundaries with EwaldDisp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For kspace style ewald/disp, all 3 dimensions must have periodic
boundaries unless you use the kspace\_modify command to define a 2d
slab with a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic z dimension.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundaries with PPPM}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For kspace style pppm, all 3 dimensions must have periodic boundaries
unless you use the kspace\_modify command to define a 2d slab with a
non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic z dimension.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot use non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundaries with PPPMDisp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

boundaries unless you use the kspace\_modify command to define a 2d
slab with a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic z dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix balance shift string is invalid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The string can only contain the characters “x”, “y”, or “z”.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/break needs ghost atoms from further away}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the fix needs to walk bonds to a certain distance to
acquire needed info, The comm\_modify cutoff command can be used to
extend the communication range.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create angle type is invalid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create cutoff is longer than pairwise cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not allowed because bond creation is done using the
pairwise neighbor list.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create dihedral type is invalid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create improper type is invalid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create induced too many angles/dihedrals/impropers per atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the read\_data command for info on using the “extra/angle/per/atom”,
(or dihedral, improper) keywords to allow for additional
angles, dihedrals, and impropers to be formed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create needs ghost atoms from further away}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the fix needs to walk bonds to a certain distance to
acquire needed info, The comm\_modify cutoff command can be used to
extend the communication range.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Cannot use fix bond/react with non\sphinxhyphen{}molecular systems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only systems with bonds that can be changed can be used. Atom\_style
template does not qualify.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Invalid template atom ID in map file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom IDs in molecule templates range from 1 to the number of atoms in the template.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Rmax cutoff is longer than pairwise cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not allowed because bond creation is done using the pairwise
neighbor list.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Molecule template ID for fix bond/react does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A valid molecule template must have been created with the molecule
command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Reaction templates must contain the same number of atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There should be a one\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}one correspondence between atoms in the
pre\sphinxhyphen{}reacted and post\sphinxhyphen{}reacted templates, as specified by the map file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Unknown section in map file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Please ensure reaction map files are properly formatted.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Atom/Bond type affected by reaction too close to template edge}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means an atom which changes type or connectivity during the
reaction is too close to an ‘edge’ atom defined in the map
file.  This could cause incorrect assignment of bonds, angle, etc.
Generally, this means you must include more atoms in your templates,
such that there are at least two atoms between each atom involved in
the reaction and an edge atom.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Fix bond/react needs ghost atoms from farther away}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because a processor needs to map the entire unreacted
molecule template onto simulation atoms it knows about. The
comm\_modify cutoff command can be used to extend the communication
range.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: A deleted atom cannot remain bonded to an atom that is not deleted}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: First neighbors of chiral atoms must be of mutually different types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Chiral atoms must have exactly four first neighbors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Molecule template ‘Coords’ section required for chiralIDs keyword}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The coordinates of atoms in the pre\sphinxhyphen{}reacted template are used to determine
chirality.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react special bond generation overflow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of special bonds per\sphinxhyphen{}atom created by a reaction exceeds the
system setting. See the read\_data or create\_box command for how to
specify this value.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react topology/atom exceed system topology/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of bonds, angles etc per\sphinxhyphen{}atom created by a reaction exceeds
the system setting. See the read\_data or create\_box command for how to
specify this value.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/swap cannot use dihedral or improper styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles cannot be defined when using this fix.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/swap requires pair and bond styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/swap requires special\_bonds = 0,1,1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix box/relax generated negative box length}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pressure being applied is likely too large.  Try applying
it incrementally, to build to the high pressure.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix command cannot be used before a read\_data, read\_restart, or
create\_box command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix deform cannot use yz variable with xy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The yz setting cannot be a variable if xy deformation is also
specified.  This is because LAMMPS cannot determine if the yz setting
will induce a box flip which would be invalid if xy is also changing.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix deform is changing yz too much with xy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When both yz and xy are changing, it induces changes in xz if the
box must flip from one tilt extreme to another.  Thus it is not
allowed for yz to grow so much that a flip is induced.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix deform tilt factors require triclinic box}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cannot deform the tilt factors of a simulation box unless it
is a triclinic (non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal) box.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix deform volume setting is invalid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cannot use volume style unless other dimensions are being controlled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is done by including the PYTHON package before LAMMPS is built.
This is required to use python\sphinxhyphen{}style variables.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{LAMMPS unit\_style lj not supported by KIM models}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory. Check the input script or data file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{LJ6 off not supported in pair\_style buck/long/coul/long}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Label map is incomplete: all types must be assigned a unique type label}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a given type\sphinxhyphen{}kind (atom types, bond types, etc.) to be written to
the data file, all associated types must be assigned a type label, and
each type label can be assigned to only one numeric type.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Label wasn’t found in input script}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Labelmap command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The labelmap command cannot be used before a read\_data,
read\_restart, or create\_box command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lattice orient vectors are not orthogonal}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The three specified lattice orientation vectors must be mutually
orthogonal.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lattice orient vectors are not right\sphinxhyphen{}handed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The three specified lattice orientation vectors must create a
right\sphinxhyphen{}handed coordinate system such that a1 cross a2 = a3.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lattice primitive vectors are collinear}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified lattice primitive vectors do not for a unit cell with
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero volume.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lattice settings are not compatible with 2d simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more of the specified lattice vectors has a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero z
component.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lattice spacings are invalid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each x,y,z spacing must be \textgreater{} 0.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lattice style incompatible with simulation dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
2d simulation can use sq, sq2, or hex lattice.  3d simulation can use
sc, bcc, or fcc lattice.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Log of zero/negative value in variable formula}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lost atoms via balance: original \%ld current \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This should not occur.  Report the problem to the developers.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lost atoms: original \%ld current \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lost atoms are checked for each time thermo output is done.  See the
thermo\_modify lost command for options.  Lost atoms usually indicate
bad dynamics, e.g. atoms have been blown far out of the simulation
box, or moved further than one processor’s subdomain away before
reneighboring.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MEAM library error \%d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A call to the MEAM Fortran library returned an error.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MPI\_LMP\_BIGINT and bigint in lmptype.h are not compatible}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The size of the MPI datatype does not match the size of a bigint.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MPI\_LMP\_TAGINT and tagint in lmptype.h are not compatible}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The size of the MPI datatype does not match the size of a tagint.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MSM can only currently be used with comm\_style brick}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a current restriction in LAMMPS.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MSM grid is too large}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The global MSM grid is larger than OFFSET in one or more dimensions.
OFFSET is currently set to 16384.  You likely need to decrease the
requested accuracy.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MSM order must be 4, 6, 8, or 10}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a limitation of the MSM implementation in LAMMPS:
the MSM order can only be 4, 6, 8, or 10.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mass command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The mass command cannot be used before a read\_data, read\_restart, or
create\_box command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Matrix factorization to split dispersion coefficients failed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This should not normally happen.  Contact the developers.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Min\_style command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The min\_style command cannot be used before a read\_data, read\_restart,
or create\_box command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Minimization could not find thermo\_pe compute}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is created by the thermo command.  It must have been
explicitly deleted by a uncompute command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Minimize command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimize command cannot be used before a read\_data, read\_restart,
or create\_box command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mismatched brackets in variable}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mismatched compute in variable formula}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A compute is referenced incorrectly or a compute that produces per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
values is used in an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable formula.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mismatched fix in variable formula}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A fix is referenced incorrectly or a fix that produces per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
values is used in an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable formula.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mismatched parameter in MEAM library file: z!=lat}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The coordination number and lattice do not match, check that consistent values are given.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mismatched variable in variable formula}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A variable is referenced incorrectly or an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable that
produces per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values is used in an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable
formula.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Modulo 0 in variable formula}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule IDs too large for compute chunk/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The IDs must not be larger than can be stored in a 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit integer
since chunk IDs are 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit integers.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule auto special bond generation overflow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts exceed maxspecial setting for other atoms in system.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has angles but no nangles setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has body params but no setting for them}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has bonds but no nbonds setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has dihedrals but no ndihedrals setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has fragments but no nfragments setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has impropers but no nimpropers setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has no Body Doubles section}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has no Body Integers section}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has no Fragments section}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file has special flags but no bonds}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file needs both Special Bond sections}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file requires atom style body}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file shake flags not before shake atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The order of the two sections is important.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file shake flags not before shake bonds}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The order of the two sections is important.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file shake info is incomplete}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All 3 SHAKE sections are needed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file special list does not match special count}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of values in an atom’s special list does not match count.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file z center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass must be 0.0 for 2d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule file z coord must be 0.0 for 2d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule natoms must be 1 for body particle}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule sizescale must be 1.0 for body particle}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for atom\_style template does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for create\_atoms does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for fix deposit does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for fix gcmc does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for fix pour does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for fix rigid/small does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID for fix shake does not exist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template ID must be alphanumeric or underscore characters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule topology/atom exceeds system topology/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of bonds, angles, etc per\sphinxhyphen{}atom in the molecule exceeds the
system setting.  See the create\_box command for how to specify these
values.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule topology type exceeds system topology type}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of bond, angle, etc types in the molecule exceeds the
system setting.  See the create\_box command for how to specify these
values.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one fix deform}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one fix deform can be defined at a time.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one fix freeze}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one of these fixes can be defined, since the granular pair
potentials access it.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one fix shake}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one fix shake can be defined.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mu not allowed when not using semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand in fix atom/swap command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define angle\_style before Angle Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use an angle\_style command before reading a data file that
defines Angle Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define angle\_style before BondAngle Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use an angle\_style command before reading a data file that
defines Angle Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define angle\_style before BondBond Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use an angle\_style command before reading a data file that
defines Angle Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define bond\_style before Bond Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a bond\_style command before reading a data file that
defines Bond Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define dihedral\_style before AngleAngleTorsion Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a dihedral\_style command before reading a data file that
defines AngleAngleTorsion Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define dihedral\_style before AngleTorsion Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a dihedral\_style command before reading a data file that
defines AngleTorsion Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define dihedral\_style before BondBond13 Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a dihedral\_style command before reading a data file that
defines BondBond13 Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define dihedral\_style before Dihedral Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a dihedral\_style command before reading a data file that
defines Dihedral Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define dihedral\_style before EndBondTorsion Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a dihedral\_style command before reading a data file that
defines EndBondTorsion Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define dihedral\_style before MiddleBondTorsion Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a dihedral\_style command before reading a data file that
defines MiddleBondTorsion Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define improper\_style before AngleAngle Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use an improper\_style command before reading a data file that
defines AngleAngle Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define improper\_style before Improper Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use an improper\_style command before reading a data file that
defines Improper Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define pair\_style before Pair Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a pair\_style command before reading a data file that defines
Pair Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must define pair\_style before PairIJ Coeffs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must use a pair\_style command before reading a data file that defines
PairIJ Coeffs.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must have more than one processor partition to temper}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cannot use the temper command with only one processor partition.  Use
the \sphinxhyphen{}partition command\sphinxhyphen{}line option.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must not have multiple fixes change box parameter …}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Angle Type Labels before Angles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An Angle Type Labels section of a data file must come before the Angles section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atom Type Labels before Atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An Atom Type Labels section of a data file must come before the Atoms section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Angles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before an Angles section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Bodies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Bodies section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Bonds}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Bonds section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Dihedrals}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Dihedrals section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Ellipsoids}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Ellipsoids
section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Impropers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before an Impropers
section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Lines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Lines section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Triangles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Triangles section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Atoms before Velocities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Atoms section of a data file must come before a Velocities
section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Bond Type Labels before Bonds}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Bond Type Labels section of a data file must come before the Bonds section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Dihedral Type Labels before Dihedrals}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An Dihedral Type Labels section of a data file must come before the Dihedrals section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must read Improper Type Labels before Impropers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An Improper Type Labels section of a data file must come before the Impropers section.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must re\sphinxhyphen{}specify non\sphinxhyphen{}restarted pair style (xxx) after read\_restart}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair styles, that do not store their settings in a restart file,
it must be defined with a new ‘pair\_style’ command after read\_restart.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must set both respa inner and outer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cannot use just the inner or outer option with respa without using the
other.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must set number of threads via package omp command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because you are using the OPENMP package, set the number of threads
via its settings, not by the pair\_style snap nthreads setting.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrap piston boundary}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The boundary style of the face where the piston is applied must be of
type s (shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped).

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must specify a region in fix deposit}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The region keyword must be specified with this fix.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must specify a region in fix pour}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must specify at least 2 types in fix atom/swap command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kim\_style init’ command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kim\_style define’ command after simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kim\_style init’ command before ‘kim\_style define’}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kspace\_modify pressure/scalar no’ for rRESPA with kspace\_style MSM}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace scalar pressure option cannot (yet) be used with rRESPA.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kspace\_modify pressure/scalar no’ for tensor components with kspace\_style msm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Otherwise MSM will compute only a scalar pressure.  See the kspace\_modify
command for details on this setting.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kspace\_modify pressure/scalar no’ to obtain per\sphinxhyphen{}atom virial with kspace\_style MSM}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace scalar pressure option cannot be used to obtain per\sphinxhyphen{}atom virial.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kspace\_modify pressure/scalar no’ with GPU MSM Pair styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace scalar pressure option is not (yet) compatible with GPU MSM Pair styles.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use ‘kspace\_modify pressure/scalar no’ with kspace\_style msm/cg}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace scalar pressure option is not compatible with kspace\_style msm/cg.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use \sphinxhyphen{}in switch with multiple partitions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A multi\sphinxhyphen{}partition simulation cannot read the input script from stdin.
The \sphinxhyphen{}in command\sphinxhyphen{}line option must be used to specify a file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use Kokkos half/thread or full neighbor list with threads or GPUs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using Kokkos half\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor lists with threading is not allowed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use a block or cylinder region with fix pour}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use a block region with fix pour for 2d simulations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use a bond style with TIP4P potential}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
TIP4P potentials assume bond lengths in water are constrained
by a fix shake command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use a molecular atom style with fix poems molecule}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use a z\sphinxhyphen{}axis cylinder region with fix pour}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use an angle style with TIP4P potential}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
TIP4P potentials assume angles in water are constrained by a fix shake
command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use atom map style array with Kokkos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the atom\_modify map command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use atom style with molecule IDs with fix bond/swap}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use pair\_style comb or comb3 with fix qeq/comb}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use variable energy with fix addforce}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must define an energy variable when applying a dynamic
force during minimization.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Must use variable energy with fix efield}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You must define an energy when performing a minimization with a
variable E\sphinxhyphen{}field.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{NEB command before simulation box is defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{NEB requires damped dynamics minimizer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a different minimization style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{NEB requires use of fix neb}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{NL ramp in wall/piston only implemented in zlo for now}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ramp keyword can only be used for piston applied to face zlo.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Need nswaptypes mu values in fix atom/swap command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Needed bonus data not in data file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Some atom styles require bonus data.  See the read\_data page for
details.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Needed molecular topology not in data file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The header of the data file indicated bonds, angles, etc would be
included, but they are not present.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neigh\_modify exclude molecule requires atom attribute molecule}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neigh\_modify include group != atom\_modify first group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor delay must be 0 or multiple of every setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The delay and every parameters set via the neigh\_modify command are
inconsistent.  If the delay setting is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, then it must be a
multiple of the every setting.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor include group not allowed with ghost neighbors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a current restriction within LAMMPS.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor list overflow, boost neigh\_modify one}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are too many neighbors of a single atom.  Use the neigh\_modify
command to increase the max number of neighbors allowed for one atom.
You may also want to boost the page size.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor multi not yet enabled for ghost neighbors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a current restriction within LAMMPS.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor multi not yet enabled for granular}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor multi not yet enabled for rRESPA}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor page size must be \textgreater{}= 10x the one atom setting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is required to prevent wasting too much memory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{New atom IDs exceed maximum allowed ID}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Out of range atoms \sphinxhyphen{} cannot compute MSM}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more atoms are attempting to map their charge to a MSM grid point
that is not owned by a processor.  This is likely for one of two
reasons, both of them bad.  First, it may mean that an atom near the
boundary of a processor’s subdomain has moved more than 1/2 the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor skin distance}}}} without neighbor lists being
rebuilt and atoms being migrated to new processors.  This also means
you may be missing pairwise interactions that need to be computed.
The solution is to change the re\sphinxhyphen{}neighboring criteria via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command.  The safest settings are
“delay 0 every 1 check yes”.  Second, it may mean that an atom has
moved far outside a processor’s subdomain or even the entire
simulation box. This indicates bad physics, e.g. due to highly
overlapping atoms, too large a timestep, etc.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Out of range atoms \sphinxhyphen{} cannot compute PPPM}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more atoms are attempting to map their charge to a PPPM grid
point that is not owned by a processor.  This is likely for one of two
reasons, both of them bad.  First, it may mean that an atom near the
boundary of a processor’s subdomain has moved more than 1/2 the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor skin distance}}}} without neighbor lists being
rebuilt and atoms being migrated to new processors.  This also means
you may be missing pairwise interactions that need to be computed.
The solution is to change the re\sphinxhyphen{}neighboring criteria via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command.  The safest settings are
“delay 0 every 1 check yes”.  Second, it may mean that an atom has
moved far outside a processor’s subdomain or even the entire
simulation box. This indicates bad physics, e.g. due to highly
overlapping atoms, too large a timestep, etc.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Out of range atoms \sphinxhyphen{} cannot compute PPPMDisp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more atoms are attempting to map their charge to a PPPM grid
point that is not owned by a processor.  This is likely for one of two
reasons, both of them bad.  First, it may mean that an atom near the
boundary of a processor’s subdomain has moved more than 1/2 the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor skin distance}}}} without neighbor lists being
rebuilt and atoms being migrated to new processors.  This also means
you may be missing pairwise interactions that need to be computed.
The solution is to change the re\sphinxhyphen{}neighboring criteria via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command.  The safest settings are
“delay 0 every 1 check yes”.  Second, it may mean that an atom has
moved far outside a processor’s subdomain or even the entire
simulation box. This indicates bad physics, e.g. due to highly
overlapping atoms, too large a timestep, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar

how long the vector will grow to.  Contact the developers.

else the fix contribution to the pressure virial is incorrect.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{PPPMDisp can only currently be used with comm\_style brick}}

This is a current restriction in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
