\section{Warning messages}
\label{\detokenize{Errors_warnings:warning-messages}}\label{\detokenize{Errors_warnings::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is an alphabetic list of the WARNING messages LAMMPS prints out
and the reason why.  If the explanation here is not sufficient, the
documentation for the offending command may help.  Warning messages
also list the source file and line number where the warning was
generated.  For example, a message like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
WARNING: Bond atom missing in box size check (domain.cpp:187)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
means that line \#187 in the file src/domain.cpp generated the error.
Looking in the source code may help you figure out what went wrong.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Doc page with {\hyperref[\detokenize{Errors_messages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ERROR messages}}}}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Adjusting Coulombic cutoff for MSM, new cutoff = \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The adjust/cutoff command is turned on and the Coulombic cutoff has been
adjusted to match the user\sphinxhyphen{}specified accuracy.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle atoms missing at step \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more of three atoms needed to compute a particular angle are
missing on this processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise
cutoff is set too short or the angle has blown apart and an atom is
too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle style in data file differs from currently defined angle style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angles are defined but no angle style is set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains angles, but there are no angle forces computed
since there was no angle\_style command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atom style in data file differs from currently defined atom style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bond atom missing in box size check}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second atom needed to compute a particular bond is missing on this
processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise cutoff is set too
short or the bond has blown apart and an atom is too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bond atom missing in image check}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second atom in a particular bond is missing on this processor.
Typically this is because the pairwise cutoff is set too short or the
bond has blown apart and an atom is too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bond atoms missing at step \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second atom needed to compute a particular bond is missing on this
processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise cutoff is set too
short or the bond has blown apart and an atom is too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bond style in data file differs from currently defined bond style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bonds are defined but no bond style is set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains bonds, but there are no bond forces computed
since there was no bond\_style command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bond/angle/dihedral extent \textgreater{} half of periodic box length}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a restriction because LAMMPS can be confused about which image
of an atom in the bonded interaction is the correct one to use.
“Extent” in this context means the maximum end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end length of the
bond/angle/dihedral.  LAMMPS computes this by taking the maximum bond
length, multiplying by the number of bonds in the interaction (e.g. 3
for a dihedral) and adding a small amount of stretch.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Both groups in compute group/group have a net charge; the Kspace boundary correction to energy will be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Calling write\_dump before a full system init.}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The write\_dump command is used before the system has been fully
initialized as part of a ‘run’ or ‘minimize’ command. Not all dump
styles and features are fully supported at this point and thus the
command may fail or produce incomplete or incorrect output. Insert
a “run 0” command, if a full system init is required.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot count rigid body degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom before bodies are fully initialized}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means the temperature associated with the rigid bodies may be
incorrect on this timestep.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot count rigid body degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom before bodies are initialized}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means the temperature associated with the rigid bodies may be
incorrect on this timestep.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot include log terms without 1/r terms; setting flagHI to 1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cannot include log terms without 1/r terms; setting flagHI to 1.}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Charges are set, but coulombic solver is not used}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Charges did not converge at step \%ld: \%lg}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Communication cutoff is 0.0. No ghost atoms will be generated. Atoms may get lost}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The communication cutoff defaults to the maximum of what is inferred from
pair and bond styles (will be zero, if none are defined) and what is specified
via {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}} (defaults to 0.0).  If this results
to 0.0, no ghost atoms will be generated and LAMMPS may lose atoms or use
incorrect periodic images of atoms in interaction lists.  To avoid, either use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style zero}}}} with a suitable cutoff or use {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}}.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Communication cutoff is shorter than a bond length based estimate. This may lead to errors.}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since LAMMPS stores topology data with individual atoms, all atoms
comprising a bond, angle, dihedral or improper must be present on any
subdomain that “owns” the atom with the information, either as a
local or a ghost atom. The communication cutoff is what determines up
to what distance from a subdomain boundary ghost atoms are created.
The communication cutoff is by default the largest non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded cutoff
plus the neighbor skin distance, but for short or non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded cutoffs
and/or long bonds, this may not be sufficient. This warning indicates
that there is an increased risk of a simulation stopping unexpectedly
because of Bond/Angle/Dihedral/Improper atoms missing.  It can be
silenced by manually setting the communication cutoff via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}}.  However, since the
heuristic used to determine the estimate is not always accurate, it
is not changed automatically and the warning may be ignored depending
on the specific system being simulated.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Communication cutoff is too small for SNAP micro load balancing, increased to \%lf}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Compute cna/atom cutoff may be too large to find ghost atom neighbors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The neighbor cutoff used may not encompass enough ghost atoms
to perform this operation correctly.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Computing temperature of portions of rigid bodies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The group defined by the temperature compute does not encompass all
the atoms in one or more rigid bodies, so the change in
degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom for the atoms in those partial rigid bodies will
not be accounted for.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Create\_bonds max distance \textgreater{} minimum neighbor cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means atom pairs for some atom types may not be in the neighbor
list and thus no bond can be created between them.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Delete\_atoms cutoff \textgreater{} minimum neighbor cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means atom pairs for some atom types may not be in the neighbor
list and thus an atom in that pair cannot be deleted.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dihedral atoms missing at step \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more of 4 atoms needed to compute a particular dihedral are
missing on this processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise
cutoff is set too short or the dihedral has blown apart and an atom is
too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dihedral problem}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conformation of the 4 listed dihedral atoms is extreme; you may want
to check your simulation geometry.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dihedral problem: \%d \%ld \%d \%d \%d \%d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conformation of the 4 listed dihedral atoms is extreme; you may want
to check your simulation geometry.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dihedral style in data file differs from currently defined dihedral style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dihedrals are defined but no dihedral style is set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains dihedrals, but there are no dihedral forces computed
since there was no dihedral\_style command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dump dcd/xtc timestamp may be wrong with fix dt/reset}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the fix changes the timestep, the dump dcd file will not
reflect the change.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Energy due to X extra global DOFs will be included in minimizer energies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using fixes like box/relax, the potential energy used by the minimizer
is augmented by an additional energy provided by the fix. Thus the printed
converged energy may be different from the total potential energy.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Estimated error in splitting of dispersion coeffs is \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Error is greater than 0.0001 percent.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ewald/disp Newton solver failed, using old method to estimate g\_ewald}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory. Choosing a different cutoff value may help.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{FENE bond too long}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A FENE bond has stretched dangerously far.  It’s interaction strength
will be truncated to attempt to prevent the bond from blowing up.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{FENE bond too long: \%ld \%d \%d \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A FENE bond has stretched dangerously far.  It’s interaction strength
will be truncated to attempt to prevent the bond from blowing up.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{FENE bond too long: \%ld \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A FENE bond has stretched dangerously far.  It’s interaction strength
will be truncated to attempt to prevent the bond from blowing up.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix halt condition for fix\sphinxhyphen{}id \%s met on step \%ld with value \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix SRD walls overlap but fix srd overlap not set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You likely want to set this in your input script.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/create is used multiple times or with fix bond/break \sphinxhyphen{} may not work as expected}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using fix bond/create multiple times or in combination with
fix bond/break, the individual fix instances do not share information
about changes they made at the same time step and thus it may result
in unexpected behavior.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/react: Atom affected by reaction too close to template edge}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means an atom which changes type or connectivity during the
reaction is too close to an ‘edge’ atom defined in the superimpose
file. This could cause incorrect assignment of bonds, angle, etc.
Generally, this means you must include more atoms in your templates,
such that there are at least two atoms between each atom involved in
the reaction and an edge atom.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix bond/swap will ignore defined angles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the page for fix bond/swap for more info on this
restriction.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix deposit near setting \textless{} possible overlap separation \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This test is performed for finite size particles with a diameter, not
for point particles.  The near setting is smaller than the particle
diameter which can lead to overlaps.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix evaporate may delete atom with non\sphinxhyphen{}zero molecule ID}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is probably an error, since you should not delete only one atom
of a molecule.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix gcmc using full\_energy option}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix gcmc has automatically turned on the full\_energy option since it
is required for systems like the one specified by the user. User input
included one or more of the following: kspace, triclinic, a hybrid
pair style, an eam pair style, or no “single” function for the pair
style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix langevin gjf using random gaussians is not implemented with kokkos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This will most likely cause errors in kinetic fluctuations.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix property/atom mol or charge w/out ghost communication}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A model typically needs these properties defined for ghost atoms.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix qeq CG convergence failed (\%g) after \%d iterations at \%ld step}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix qeq has non\sphinxhyphen{}zero lower Taper radius cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Absolute value must be \textless{}= 0.01.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix qeq has very low Taper radius cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Value should typically be \textgreater{}= 5.0.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix qeq/dynamic tolerance may be too small for damped dynamics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix qeq/fire tolerance may be too small for damped fires}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix rattle should come after all other integration fixes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is designed to work after all other integration fixes change
atom positions.  Thus it should be the last integration fix specified.
If not, it will not satisfy the desired constraints as well as it
otherwise would.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix recenter should come after all other integration fixes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Other fixes may change the position of the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass, so
fix recenter should come last.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix srd SRD moves may trigger frequent reneighboring}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the SRD particles may move long distances.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix srd grid size \textgreater{} 1/4 of big particle diameter}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may cause accuracy problems.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix srd particle moved outside valid domain}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may indicate a problem with your simulation parameters.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix srd particles may move \textgreater{} big particle diameter}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may cause accuracy problems.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix srd viscosity \textless{} 0.0 due to low SRD density}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may cause accuracy problems.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fixes cannot send data in Kokkos communication, switching to classic communication}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is current restriction with Kokkos.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{For better accuracy use ‘pair\_modify table 0’}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user\sphinxhyphen{}specified force accuracy cannot be achieved unless the table
feature is disabled by using ‘pair\_modify table 0’.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Geometric mixing assumed for 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Group for fix\_modify temp != fix group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix\_modify command is specifying a temperature computation that
computes a temperature on a different group of atoms than the fix
itself operates on.  This is probably not what you want to do.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{H matrix size has been exceeded: m\_fill=\%d H.m=\%dn}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the size of the matrix.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ignoring unknown or incorrect info command flag}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.  An unknown argument was given to the info command.
Compare your input with the documentation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Improper atoms missing at step \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more of 4 atoms needed to compute a particular improper are
missing on this processor.  Typically this is because the pairwise
cutoff is set too short or the improper has blown apart and an atom is
too far away.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Improper problem: \%d \%ld \%d \%d \%d \%d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conformation of the 4 listed improper atoms is extreme; you may want
to check your simulation geometry.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Improper style in data file differs from currently defined improper style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Impropers are defined but no improper style is set}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains impropers, but there are no improper forces computed
since there was no improper\_style command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Inconsistent image flags}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The image flags for a pair on bonded atoms appear to be inconsistent.
Inconsistent means that when the coordinates of the two atoms are
unwrapped using the image flags, the two atoms are far apart.
Specifically they are further apart than half a periodic box length.
Or they are more than a box length apart in a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension.
This is usually due to the initial data file not having correct image
flags for the two atoms in a bond that straddles a periodic boundary.
They should be different by 1 in that case.  This is a warning because
inconsistent image flags will not cause problems for dynamics or most
LAMMPS simulations.  However they can cause problems when such atoms
are used with the fix rigid or replicate commands.  Note that if you
have an infinite periodic crystal with bonds then it is impossible to
have fully consistent image flags, since some bonds will cross
periodic boundaries and connect two atoms with the same image
flag.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Increasing communication cutoff for GPU style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair style has increased the communication cutoff to be consistent with
the communication cutoff requirements for this pair style when run on the GPU.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{KIM Model does not provide ‘energy’; Potential energy will be zero}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{KIM Model does not provide ‘forces’; Forces will be zero}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{KIM Model does not provide ‘particleEnergy’; energy per atom will be zero}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{KIM Model does not provide ‘particleVirial’; virial per atom will be zero}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspace\_modify slab param \textless{} 2.0 may cause unphysical behavior}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The kspace\_modify slab parameter should be larger to ensure periodic
grids padded with empty space do not overlap.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Less insertions than requested}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix pour command was unsuccessful at finding open space
for as many particles as it tried to insert.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Library error in lammps\_gather\_atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This library function cannot be used if atom IDs are not defined
or are not consecutively numbered.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Library error in lammps\_scatter\_atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This library function cannot be used if atom IDs are not defined or
are not consecutively numbered, or if no atom map is defined.  See the
atom\_modify command for details about atom maps.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Likewise 1\sphinxhyphen{}2 special neighbor interactions != 1.0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains bonds, but there is no bond style defined
and a 1\sphinxhyphen{}2 special neighbor scaling factor was not 1.0. This
means that pair style interactions may have scaled or missing
pairs in the neighbor list in expectation of interactions for
those pairs being computed from the bond style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Likewise 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 special neighbor interactions != 1.0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains angles, but there is no angle style defined
and a 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 special neighbor scaling factor was not 1.0. This
means that pair style interactions may have scaled or missing
pairs in the neighbor list in expectation of interactions for
those pairs being computed from the angle style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Likewise 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 special neighbor interactions != 1.0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The topology contains dihedrals, but there is no dihedral style defined
and a 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 special neighbor scaling factor was not 1.0. This
means that pair style interactions may have scaled or missing
pairs in the neighbor list in expectation of interactions for
those pairs being computed from the dihedral style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lost atoms via change\_box: original \%ld current \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The command options you have used caused atoms to be lost.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lost atoms via displace\_atoms: original \%ld current \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The command options you have used caused atoms to be lost.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lost atoms: original \%ld current \%ld}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lost atoms are checked for each time thermo output is done.  See the
thermo\_modify lost command for options.  Lost atoms usually indicate
bad dynamics, e.g. atoms have been blown far out of the simulation
box, or moved further than one processor’s subdomain away before
reneighboring.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{MSM mesh too small, increasing to 2 points in each direction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mismatch between velocity and compute groups}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature computation used by the velocity command will not be
on the same group of atoms that velocities are being set for.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Mixing forced for lj coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule attributes do not match system attributes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An attribute is specified (e.g. diameter, charge) that is
not defined for the specified atom style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule has bond topology but no special bond settings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means the bonded atoms will not be excluded in pairwise
interactions.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template for create\_atoms has multiple molecules}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The create\_atoms command will only create molecules of a single type,
i.e. the first molecule in the template.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template for fix gcmc has multiple molecules}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix gcmc command will only create molecules of a single type,
i.e. the first molecule in the template.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Molecule template for fix shake has multiple molecules}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix shake command will only recognize molecules of a single
type, i.e. the first molecule in the template.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute centro/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute centro/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute cluster/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute cluster/atom  more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute cna/atom defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute cna/atom  more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute contact/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute contact/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute coord/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute coord/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute damage/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute ke/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute dilatation/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute erotate/sphere/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute erorate/sphere/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute hexorder/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute hexorder/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute ke/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute ke/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute orientorder/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use compute orientorder/atom more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute plasticity/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute sna/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute sna/grid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute sna/grid/local}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute snad/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one compute snav/atom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one fix poems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use fix poems more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{More than one fix rigid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not efficient to use fix rigid more than once.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Neighbor exclusions used with KSpace solver may give inconsistent Coulombic energies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because excluding specific pair interactions also excludes
them from long\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions which may not be the desired effect.
The special\_bonds command handles this consistently by ensuring
excluded (or weighted) 1\sphinxhyphen{}2, 1\sphinxhyphen{}3, 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 interactions are treated
consistently by both the short\sphinxhyphen{}range pair style and the long\sphinxhyphen{}range
solver.  This is not done for exclusions of charged atom pairs via the
neigh\_modify exclude command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{New thermo\_style command, previous thermo\_modify settings will be lost}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a thermo\_style command is used after a thermo\_modify command, the
settings changed by the thermo\_modify command will be reset to their
default values.  This is because the thermo\_modify command acts on
the currently defined thermo style, and a thermo\_style command creates
a new style.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{No Kspace calculation with verlet/split}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second partition performs a kspace calculation so the kspace\_style
command must be used.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{No automatic unit conversion to XTC file format conventions possible for units lj}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means no scaling will be performed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{No fixes defined, atoms won’t move}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are not using a fix like nve, nvt, npt then atom velocities and
coordinates will not be updated during timestepping.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{No joints between rigid bodies, use fix rigid instead}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bodies defined by fix poems are not connected by joints.  POEMS
will integrate the body motion, but it would be more efficient to use
fix rigid.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Not using real units with pair reaxff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is most likely an error, unless you have created your own ReaxFF
parameter file in a different set of units.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Number of MSM mesh points changed to be a multiple of 2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
MSM requires that the number of grid points in each direction be a multiple
of two and the number of grid points in one or more directions have been
adjusted to meet this requirement.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS environment is not set.}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This environment variable must be set appropriately to use the
OPENMP package.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{One or more atoms are time integrated more than once}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is probably an error since you typically do not want to
advance the positions or velocities of an atom more than once
per timestep.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{One or more chunks do not contain all atoms in molecule}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may not be what you intended.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{One or more dynamic groups may not be updated at correct point in timestep}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If there are other fixes that act immediately after the initial stage
of time integration within a timestep (i.e. after atoms move), then
the command that sets up the dynamic group should appear after those
fixes.  This will ensure that dynamic group assignments are made
after all atoms have moved.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{One or more respa levels compute no forces}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is computationally inefficient.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair COMB charge \%.10f with force \%.10f hit max barrier}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Something is possibly wrong with your model.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair COMB charge \%.10f with force \%.10f hit min barrier}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Something is possibly wrong with your model.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair brownian needs newton pair on for momentum conservation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair dpd needs newton pair on for momentum conservation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair dsmc: num\_of\_collisions \textgreater{} number\_of\_A}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Collision model in DSMC is breaking down.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair dsmc: num\_of\_collisions \textgreater{} number\_of\_B}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Collision model in DSMC is breaking down.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair style in data file differs from currently defined pair style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair style restartinfo set but has no restart support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style has a bug, where it does not support reading and
writing information to a restart file, but does not set the member
variable “restartinfo” to 0 as required in that case.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Particle deposition was unsuccessful}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix deposit command was not able to insert as many atoms as
needed.  The requested volume fraction may be too high, or other atoms
may be in the insertion region.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Proc subdomain size \textless{} neighbor skin, could lead to lost atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The decomposition of the physical domain (likely due to load
balancing) has led to a processor’s subdomain being smaller than the
neighbor skin in one or more dimensions.  Since reneighboring is
triggered by atoms moving the skin distance, this may lead to lost
atoms, if an atom moves all the way across a neighboring processor’s
subdomain before reneighboring is triggered.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Reducing PPPM order b/c stencil extends beyond nearest neighbor processor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may lead to a larger grid than desired.  See the kspace\_modify overlap
command to prevent changing of the PPPM order.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Reducing PPPMDisp Coulomb order b/c stencil extends beyond neighbor processor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may lead to a larger grid than desired.  See the kspace\_modify overlap
command to prevent changing of the PPPM order.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Reducing PPPMDisp dispersion order b/c stencil extends beyond neighbor processor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may lead to a larger grid than desired.  See the kspace\_modify overlap
command to prevent changing of the PPPM order.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Replacing a fix, but new group != old group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ID and style of a fix match for a fix you are changing with a fix
command, but the new group you are specifying does not match the old
group.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Replicating in a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters for a replicate command will cause a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic
dimension to be replicated; this may cause unwanted behavior.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Resetting reneighboring criteria during PRD}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A PRD simulation requires that neigh\_modify settings be delay = 0,
every = 1, check = yes.  Since these settings were not in place,
LAMMPS changed them and will restore them to their original values
after the PRD simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Resetting reneighboring criteria during TAD}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A TAD simulation requires that neigh\_modify settings be delay = 0,
every = 1, check = yes.  Since these settings were not in place,
LAMMPS changed them and will restore them to their original values
after the PRD simulation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Resetting reneighboring criteria during minimization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimization requires that neigh\_modify settings be delay = 0, every =
1, check = yes.  Since these settings were not in place, LAMMPS
changed them and will restore them to their original values after the
minimization.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restart file used different \# of processors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The restart file was written out by a LAMMPS simulation running on a
different number of processors.  Due to round\sphinxhyphen{}off, the trajectories of
your restarted simulation may diverge a little more quickly than if
you ran on the same \# of processors.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restart file used different 3d processor grid}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The restart file was written out by a LAMMPS simulation running on a
different 3d grid of processors.  Due to round\sphinxhyphen{}off, the trajectories
of your restarted simulation may diverge a little more quickly than if
you ran on the same \# of processors.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restart file used different boundary settings, using restart file values}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Your input script cannot change these restart file settings.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restart file used different newton bond setting, using restart file value}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The restart file value will override the setting in the input script.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restart file used different newton pair setting, using input script value}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The input script value will override the setting in the restart file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restrain problem: \%d \%ld \%d \%d \%d \%d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conformation of the 4 listed dihedral atoms is extreme; you may want
to check your simulation geometry.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Running PRD with only one replica}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is allowed, but you will get no parallel speed\sphinxhyphen{}up.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{SRD bin shifting turned on due to small lamda}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is done to try to preserve accuracy.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{SRD bin size for fix srd differs from user request}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix SRD had to adjust the bin size to fit the simulation box.  See the
cubic keyword if you want this message to be an error vs warning.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{SRD bins for fix srd are not cubic enough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bin shape is not within tolerance of cubic.  See the cubic
keyword if you want this message to be an error vs warning.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{SRD particle \%d started inside big particle \%d on step \%ld bounce \%d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the inside keyword if you want this message to be an error vs
warning.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{SRD particle \%d started inside wall \%d on step \%ld bounce \%d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the inside keyword if you want this message to be an error vs
warning.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Shake determinant \textless{} 0.0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The determinant of the quadratic equation being solved for a single
cluster specified by the fix shake command is numerically suspect.  LAMMPS
will set it to 0.0 and continue.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Shell command ‘\%s’ failed with error ‘\%s’}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Shell command returned with non\sphinxhyphen{}zero status}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This may indicate the shell command did not operate as expected.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Should not allow rigid bodies to bounce off reflecting walls}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS allows this, but their dynamics are not computed correctly.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Should not use fix nve/limit with fix shake or fix rattle}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This will lead to invalid constraint forces in the SHAKE/RATTLE
computation.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Simulations might be very slow because of large number of structure factors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Slab correction not needed for MSM}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Slab correction is intended to be used with Ewald or PPPM and is not needed by MSM.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Specifying an ‘subset’ value of ‘0’ is equivalent to no ‘subset’ keyword}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{System is not charge neutral, net charge = \%g}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The total charge on all atoms on the system is not 0.0.
For some KSpace solvers this is only a warning.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Table inner cutoff \textgreater{}= outer cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You specified an inner cutoff for a Coulombic table that is longer
than the global cutoff.  Probably not what you wanted.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Temperature for MSST is not for group all}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
User\sphinxhyphen{}assigned temperature to MSST fix does not compute temperature for
all atoms.  Since MSST computes a global pressure, the kinetic energy
contribution from the temperature is assumed to also be for all atoms.
Thus the pressure used by MSST could be inaccurate.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Temperature for NPT is not for group all}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
User\sphinxhyphen{}assigned temperature to NPT fix does not compute temperature for
all atoms.  Since NPT computes a global pressure, the kinetic energy
contribution from the temperature is assumed to also be for all atoms.
Thus the pressure used by NPT could be inaccurate.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Temperature for fix modify is not for group all}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature compute is being used with a pressure calculation
which does operate on group all, so this may be inconsistent.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Temperature for thermo pressure is not for group all}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
User\sphinxhyphen{}assigned temperature to thermo via the thermo\_modify command does
not compute temperature for all atoms.  Since thermo computes a global
pressure, the kinetic energy contribution from the temperature is
assumed to also be for all atoms.  Thus the pressure printed by thermo
could be inaccurate.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{The fix ave/spatial command has been replaced by the more flexible fix ave/chunk and compute chunk/atom commands \textendash{} fix ave/spatial will be removed in the summer of 2015}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{The minimizer does not re\sphinxhyphen{}orient dipoles when using fix efield}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means that only the atom coordinates will be minimized,
not the orientation of the dipoles.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Too many common neighbors in CNA \%d times}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
More than the maximum \# of neighbors was found multiple times.  This
was unexpected.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Too many inner timesteps in fix ttm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Too many neighbors in CNA for \%d atoms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
More than the maximum \# of neighbors was found multiple times.  This
was unexpected.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Use special bonds = 0,1,1 with bond style fene}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most FENE models need this setting for the special\_bonds command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Use special bonds = 0,1,1 with bond style fene/expand}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most FENE models need this setting for the special\_bonds command.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using a many\sphinxhyphen{}body potential with bonds/angles/dihedrals and special\_bond exclusions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is likely not what you want to do.  The exclusion settings will
eliminate neighbors in the neighbor list, which the many\sphinxhyphen{}body potential
needs to calculated its terms correctly.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using compute temp/deform with inconsistent fix deform remap option}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix nvt/sllod assumes deforming atoms have a velocity profile provided
by “remap v” or “remap none” as a fix deform option.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using compute temp/deform with no fix deform defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is probably an error, since it makes little sense to use
compute temp/deform in this case.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using fix srd with box deformation but no SRD thermostat}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The deformation will heat the SRD particles so this can
be dangerous.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using kspace solver on system with no charge}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using largest cut\sphinxhyphen{}off for lj/long/dipole/long long long}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using largest cutoff for buck/long/coul/long}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using largest cutoff for lj/long/coul/long}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using largest cutoff for pair\_style lj/long/tip4p/long}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using package gpu without any pair style defined}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using pair potential shift with pair\_modify compute no}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The shift effects will thus not be computed.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using pair tail corrections with nonperiodic system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is probably a bogus thing to do, since tail corrections are
computed by integrating the density of a periodic system out to
infinity.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{Using pair tail corrections with pair\_modify compute no}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The tail corrections will thus not be computed.

\end{description}


\part{Programmer Guide}
\label{\detokenize{Manual:programmer-guide}}\label{\detokenize{Manual:programmer-documentation}}
\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{LAMMPS Library Interfaces}
\label{\detokenize{Library:lammps-library-interfaces}}\label{\detokenize{Library::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_library::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{library interface to LAMMPS}}}}
page, LAMMPS can be built as a library (static or shared), so that it
can be called by another code, used in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_couple::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coupled manner}}}} with other codes, or driven through a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python
script}}}}.  The LAMMPS standalone executable itself is
essentially a thin wrapper on top of the LAMMPS library, which creates a
LAMMPS instance, passes the input for processing to that instance, and
then exits.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most of the APIs described below are based on C language wrapper
functions in the files \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/library.h}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/library.cpp}}, but
it is also possible to use C++ directly.  The basic procedure is
always the same: you create one or more instances of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}}, pass commands as strings or
from files to that LAMMPS instance to execute calculations, and/or
call functions that read, manipulate, and update data from the active
class instances inside LAMMPS to do analysis or perform operations
that are not possible with existing input script commands.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{Library:thread-safety}}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Thread\sphinxhyphen{}safety}

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS was initially not conceived as a thread\sphinxhyphen{}safe program, but over
the years changes have been applied to replace operations that
collide with creating multiple LAMMPS instances from multiple\sphinxhyphen{}threads
of the same process with thread\sphinxhyphen{}safe alternatives.  This primarily
applies to the core LAMMPS code and less so on add\sphinxhyphen{}on packages,
especially when those packages require additional code in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lib}
folder, interface LAMMPS to Fortran libraries, or the code uses
static variables (like the COLVARS package).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Another major issue to deal with is to correctly handle MPI.
Creating a LAMMPS instance requires passing an MPI communicator, or
it assumes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_COMM\_WORLD}} communicator, which spans all MPI
processor ranks.  When creating multiple LAMMPS object instances
from different threads, this communicator has to be different for
each thread or else collisions can happen.  Or it has to be
guaranteed, that only one thread at a time is active.  MPI
communicators, however, are not a problem, if LAMMPS is compiled
with the MPI STUBS library, which implies that there is no MPI
communication and only 1 MPI rank.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\section{LAMMPS C Library API}
\label{\detokenize{Library:lammps-c-library-api}}\label{\detokenize{Library:lammps-c-api}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The C library interface is the most commonly used path to manage LAMMPS
instances from a compiled code and it is the basis for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Fortran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Fortran}}}} modules.  Almost all
functions of the C language API require an argument containing a
“handle” in the form of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void *}} type variable, which points to the
location of a LAMMPS class instance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{library.h}} header file by default does not include the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpi.h}}
header file and thus hides the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}} function which
requires the declaration of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_comm}} data type.  This is only
a problem when the communicator that would be passed is different from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_COMM\_WORLD}}.  Otherwise calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv418lammps_open_no_mpiiPPcPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_no\_mpi()}}}}}
will work just as well.  To make {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}} available,
you need to compile the code with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_LIB\_MPI}} or add the line
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#define LAMMPS\_LIB\_MPI}} before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#include "library.h"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please note the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpi.h}} file must usually be the same (and thus the
MPI library in use) for the LAMMPS code and library and the calling code.
The exception is when LAMMPS was compiled in serial mode using the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{STUBS}} MPI library.  In that case the calling code may be compiled
with a different MPI library so long as {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv418lammps_open_no_mpiiPPcPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_no\_mpi()}}}}}
is called to create a LAMMPS instance.  In that case each MPI rank will
run LAMMPS in serial mode.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Errors versus exceptions}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the LAMMPS executable encounters an error condition, it will abort
after printing an error message.  It does so by catching the
exceptions that LAMMPS could throw.  For a C library interface this
is usually not desirable since the calling code might lack the
ability to catch such exceptions.  Thus, the library functions will
catch those exceptions and return from the affected functions.  The
error status {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_utility:_CPPv416lammps_has_errorPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{can be queried}}}}} and an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_utility:_CPPv429lammps_get_last_error_messagePvPci}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{error message retrieved}}}}}.
This is, for example used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{LAMMPS python module}}}} and then a suitable Python exception is thrown.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Using the C library interface as a plugin}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rather than including the C library directly and link to the LAMMPS
library at compile time, you can use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammpsplugin.h}} header
file and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammpsplugin.c}} C code in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/COUPLE/plugin}} folder for an interface to LAMMPS that is
largely identical to the regular library interface, only that it will
load a LAMMPS shared library file at runtime.  This can be useful for
applications where the interface to LAMMPS would be an optional
feature.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No checks are made on the arguments of the function calls of the C
library interface.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{All} function arguments must be non\sphinxhyphen{}NULL unless
\sphinxstyleemphasis{explicitly} allowed, and must point to consistent and valid data.  Buffers
for storing returned data must be allocated to a suitable size.
Passing invalid or unsuitable information will likely cause crashes
or corrupt data.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Creating or deleting a LAMMPS object}
\label{\detokenize{Library_create:creating-or-deleting-a-lammps-object}}\label{\detokenize{Library_create::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section documents the following functions:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv418lammps_open_no_mpiiPPcPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_no\_mpi()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv419lammps_open_fortraniPPci}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_fortran()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv412lammps_closePv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_close()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv415lammps_mpi_initv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_mpi\_init()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv419lammps_mpi_finalizev}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_mpi\_finalize()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv422lammps_kokkos_finalizev}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_kokkos\_finalize()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv422lammps_python_finalizev}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_python\_finalize()}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv412lammps_errorPviPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_error()}}}}}

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv418lammps_open_no_mpiiPPcPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_no\_mpi()}}}}} functions
are used to create and initialize a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS()}} instance.  They
return a reference to this instance as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void *}} pointer to be used
as the “handle” argument in subsequent function calls until that
instance is destroyed by calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv412lammps_closePv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_close()}}}}}.  Here is a
simple example demonstrating its use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}library.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}stdio.h\PYGZgt{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{main}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{argc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{argv}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS library uses the MPI library it was compiled with and will
either run on all processors in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_COMM\_WORLD}} communicator or
on the set of processors in the communicator passed as the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{comm}}
argument of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}}.  This means the calling code can
run LAMMPS on all or a subset of processors.  For example, a wrapper
code might decide to alternate between LAMMPS and another code, allowing
them both to run on all the processors.  Or it might allocate part of
the processors to LAMMPS and the rest to the other code by creating a
custom communicator with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Comm\_split()}} and running both codes
concurrently before syncing them up periodically.  Or it might
instantiate multiple instances of LAMMPS to perform different
calculations and either alternate between them, run them concurrently on
split communicators, or run them one after the other.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}} function may be called multiple times for this
latter purpose.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv412lammps_closePv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_close()}}}}} function is used to shut down the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}} class pointed to by the handle
passed as an argument and free all its memory. This has to be called
for every instance created with one of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}}
functions.  It will, however, \sphinxstylestrong{not} call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Finalize()}}, since
that may only be called once.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv419lammps_mpi_finalizev}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_mpi\_finalize()}}}}} for
an alternative to invoking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Finalize()}} explicitly from the
calling program.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}} function creates a new {\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}} class instance while passing in a list of strings
as if they were {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{command\sphinxhyphen{}line arguments}}}} for the
LAMMPS executable, and an MPI communicator for LAMMPS to run under.
Since the list of arguments is \sphinxstylestrong{exactly} as when called from the
command line, the first argument would be the name of the executable and
thus is otherwise ignored.  However \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{argc}} may be set to 0 and then
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{argv}} may be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.  If MPI is not yet initialized, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Init()}}
will be called during creation of the LAMMPS class instance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If for some reason the creation or initialization of the LAMMPS instance
fails a null pointer is returned.

possible to provide the address of a pointer variable as final
argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{ptr}.

parallel and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Comm}} data type of the STUBS library would not

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MPI standard requires that any MPI application must call
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Init()}} exactly once before performing any other MPI function
calls.  This function checks, whether MPI is already initialized and
calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Init()}} in case it is not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shut down the MPI infrastructure.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 18Sep2020.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MPI standard requires that any MPI application calls
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Finalize()}} before exiting.  Even if a calling program does not
do any MPI calls, MPI is still initialized internally to avoid errors
accessing any MPI functions.  This function should then be called right
before exiting the program to wait until all (parallel) tasks are
completed and then MPI is cleanly shut down.  After calling this
function no more MPI calls may be made.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shut down the Kokkos library environment.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 2Jul2021.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Kokkos library may only be initialized once during the execution of
a process.  This is done automatically the first time Kokkos
functionality is used.  This requires that the Kokkos environment
must be explicitly shut down after any LAMMPS instance using it is
closed (to release associated resources).
After calling this function no Kokkos functionality may be used.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clear the embedded Python environment

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 20Sep2021.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function resets and clears an embedded Python environment
by calling the \sphinxhref{https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/init.html\#c.Py\_FinalizeEx}{Py\_Finalize() function}
of the embedded Python library, if enabled.
This call would free up all allocated resources and release
loaded shared objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, this is \sphinxstylestrong{not} done when a LAMMPS instance is deleted because
a) LAMMPS may have been used through the Python module and thus
the Python interpreter is external and not embedded into LAMMPS
and therefore may not be reset by LAMMPS b) some Python modules
and extensions, most notably NumPy, are not compatible with being
initialized multiple times, which would happen if additional
LAMMPS instances using Python would be created \sphinxstyleemphasis{after}
after calling Py\_Finalize().

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function can be called to explicitly clear the Python
environment in case it is safe to do so.

\end{description}

This function is a wrapper around functions in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Error}} to print an

The \sphinxstyleemphasis{error\_type} parameter selects which function to call.  It is a sum

match any valid combination of constants a warning is printed and the
function returns.

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Once a LAMMPS instance is created, there are multiple ways to “drive” a
simulation.  In most cases it is easiest to process single or multiple
LAMMPS commands like in an input file.  This can be done through reading
a file or passing single commands or lists of commands or blocks of
commands with the following functions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Via these functions, the calling code can have LAMMPS act on a series
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{input file commands}}}} that are either read from
a file or passed as strings.  For example, this allows setup of a
problem from an input script, and then running it in stages while
performing other operations in between or concurrently.  The caller
can interleave the LAMMPS function calls with operations it performs,
such as calls to extract information from or set information within
LAMMPS, or calls to another code’s library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Just as with {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{input script parsing}}}} comments can
be included in the file or strings, and expansion of variables with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$\{name\}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$(expression)}} syntax is performed.
Below is a short example using some of these functions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Process a single LAMMPS input command from a string.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function tells LAMMPS to execute the single command in the string
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cmd}.  The entire string is considered as command and need not have a
(final) newline character.  Newline characters in the body of the
string, however, will be treated as part of the command and will \sphinxstylestrong{not}
start a second command.  The function {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_execute:_CPPv422lammps_commands_stringPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_commands\_string()}}}}}
processes a string with multiple command lines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The function returns the name of the command on success or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} when
passing a string without a command.

\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{handle}} \textendash{} pointer to a previously created LAMMPS instance 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{cmd}} \textendash{} string with a single LAMMPS command 

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
string with parsed command name or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

Process a block of LAMMPS input commands from a single string.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function processes a multi\sphinxhyphen{}line string similar to a block of
commands from a file.  The string may have multiple lines (separated by
newline characters) and also single commands may be distributed over
multiple lines with continuation characters (’\&’).  Those lines are
combined by removing the ‘\&’ and the following newline character.  After
this processing the string is handed to LAMMPS for parsing and
executing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 21Nov2023: }The command is now able to process long strings with triple quotes and
loops using {\hyperref[\detokenize{jump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{jump SELF \textless{}label\textgreater{}}}}}.

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The library interface allows the extraction of different kinds of
information about the active simulation instance and also \sphinxhyphen{} in some
cases \sphinxhyphen{} to apply modifications to it.  This enables combining of a
LAMMPS simulation with other processing and simulation methods computed
by the calling code, or by another code that is coupled to LAMMPS via
the library interface.  In some cases the data returned is direct
reference to the original data inside LAMMPS, cast to a void pointer.
In that case the data needs to be cast to a suitable pointer for the
calling program to access it, and you may need to know the correct
dimensions and lengths.  This also means you can directly change those
value(s) from the calling program (e.g., to modify atom positions).  Of
course, changing values should be done with care.  When accessing per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
data, please note that these data are the per\sphinxhyphen{}processor \sphinxstylestrong{local} data and are
indexed accordingly. Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data can change sizes and ordering at
every neighbor list rebuild or atom sort event as atoms migrate between
subdomains and processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the total number of atoms in the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This number may be very large when running large simulations across
multiple processes.  Depending on compile time choices, LAMMPS may be
using either 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit or a 64\sphinxhyphen{}bit integer to store this number. For
portability this function returns thus a double precision
floating point number, which can represent up to a 53\sphinxhyphen{}bit signed
integer exactly (\(\approx 10^{16}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an alternative, you can use {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv421lammps_extract_globalPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_global()}}}}}
and cast the resulting pointer to an integer pointer of the correct
size and dereference it.  The size of that integer (in bytes) can be
queried by calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv422lammps_extract_settingPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_setting()}}}}} to return
the size of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bigint}} integer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 18Sep2020: }The type of the return value was changed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
to accommodate reporting atom counts for larger systems that would
overflow a 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit int without having to depend on a 64\sphinxhyphen{}bit bit
integer type definition.

\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{handle}} \textendash{} pointer to a previously created LAMMPS instance 

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
total number of atoms or 0 if value is too large 

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Jun2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function provides access to cached data from the last thermo output.
This differs from {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv417lammps_get_thermoPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_get\_thermo()}}}}} in that it does \sphinxstylestrong{not}
trigger an evaluation.  Instead it provides direct access to a read\sphinxhyphen{}only
location of the last thermo output data and the corresponding keyword
strings.  How to handle the return value depends on the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{what}
argument string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extract simulation box parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function (re\sphinxhyphen{})initializes the simulation box and boundary
information and then assign the designated data to the locations in the
pointers passed as arguments. Any argument (except the first) may be
a NULL pointer and then will not be assigned.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{handle}} \textendash{} pointer to a previously created LAMMPS instance 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{boxlo}} \textendash{} pointer to 3 doubles where the lower box boundary is stored 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{boxhi}} \textendash{} pointer to 3 doubles where the upper box boundary is stored 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{xy}} \textendash{} pointer to a double where the xy tilt factor is stored 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{yz}} \textendash{} pointer to a double where the yz tilt factor is stored

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function sets the simulation box dimensions (upper and lower bounds
and tilt factors) from the provided data and then re\sphinxhyphen{}initializes the box
information and all derived settings. It may only be called before atoms
are created.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get memory usage information

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 18Sep2020.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function will retrieve memory usage information for the current
LAMMPS instance or process.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meminfo} buffer will be filled with
3 different numbers (if supported by the operating system).  The first
is the tally (in MBytes) of all large memory allocations made by LAMMPS.
This is a lower boundary of how much memory is requested and does not
account for memory allocated on the stack or allocations via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new}}.
The second number is the current memory allocation of the current process
as returned by a memory allocation reporting in the system library.  The
third number is the maximum amount of RAM (not swap) used by the process
so far. If any of the two latter parameters is not supported by the operating
system it will be set to zero.

\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{handle}} \textendash{} pointer to a previously created LAMMPS instance 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{meminfo}} \textendash{} buffer with space for at least 3 double to store data in. 

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return current LAMMPS world communicator as integer

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 18Sep2020.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This will take the LAMMPS “world” communicator and convert it to an
integer using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Comm\_c2f()}}, so it is equivalent to the
corresponding MPI communicator in Fortran. This way it can be safely
passed around between different programming languages.  To convert it
to the C language representation use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_Comm\_f2c()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If LAMMPS was compiled with MPI\_STUBS, this function returns \sphinxhyphen{}1.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{See also}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv419lammps_open_fortraniPPci}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_fortran()}}}}}

\end{description}

\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{handle}} \textendash{} pointer to a previously created LAMMPS instance

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fortran representation of the LAMMPS world communicator 

\end{description}\end{quote}

\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 18Sep2020.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function returns an integer that encodes the data type of the global
property with the specified name. See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_LMP\_DATATYPE\_CONST}} for valid
values. Callers of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv421lammps_extract_globalPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_global()}}}}} can use this information
to then decide how to cast the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void *}} pointer and access the data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
integer constant encoding the data type of the property or \sphinxhyphen{}1 if not found. 

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Get pointer to internal global LAMMPS variables or arrays.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function returns a pointer to the location of some global property
stored in one of the constituent classes of a LAMMPS instance.  The
returned pointer is cast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void *}} and needs to be cast to a pointer
of the type that the entity represents. The pointers returned by this
function are generally persistent; therefore it is not necessary to call
the function again, unless a {\hyperref[\detokenize{clear::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{clear command}}}} command is issued which wipes
out and recreates the contents of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}} class.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please also see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv422lammps_extract_settingPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_setting()}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv417lammps_get_thermoPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_get\_thermo()}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv418lammps_extract_boxPvPdPdPdPdPdPiPi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_box()}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following tables list the supported names, their data types, length
of the data area, and a short description.  The data type can also be
queried through calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv430lammps_extract_global_datatypePvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_global\_datatype()}}}}}.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bigint}} type may be defined to be either an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}} or an
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int64\_t}}.  This is set at {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings:size}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{compile time}}}} of the LAMMPS
library and can be queried through calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv422lammps_extract_settingPvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_setting()}}}}}.
The function {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties:_CPPv430lammps_extract_global_datatypePvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_extract\_global\_datatype()}}}}} will directly

Get pointer to data from a LAMMPS compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function returns a pointer to the location of data provided by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute command}}}} instance identified by the compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  Computes may
provide global, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom, or local data, and those may be a scalar, a
vector, or an array or they may provide the information about the
dimensions of the respective data.  Since computes may provide multiple
kinds of data, it is required to set style and type flags representing
what specific data is desired.  This also determines to what kind of
pointer the returned pointer needs to be cast to access the data
correctly.  The function returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} if the compute ID is not found
or the requested data is not available or current. The following table
lists the available options.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the compute’s data is not computed for the current step, the
compute will be invoked.  LAMMPS cannot easily check at that time, if
it is valid to invoke a compute, so it may fail with an error.  The
caller has to check to avoid such an error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pointers returned by this function are generally not persistent
since the computed data may be re\sphinxhyphen{}distributed, re\sphinxhyphen{}allocated, and
re\sphinxhyphen{}ordered at every invocation. It is advisable to re\sphinxhyphen{}invoke this
function before the data is accessed, or make a copy if the data shall
be used after other LAMMPS commands have been issued.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{id}} \textendash{} string with ID of the compute 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{style}} \textendash{} constant indicating the style of data requested (global, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom, or local) 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{type}} \textendash{} constant indicating type of data (scalar, vector, or array) or size of rows or columns 

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
pointer (cast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void *}}) to the location of the requested data or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} if not found. 

\end{description}\end{quote}
