\sphinxAtStartPar
In the case of global data, this function returns a value of type
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{REAL(c\_double)}}. For per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local data, this function does not
return a value but instead associates the pointer on the left side of the
assignment to point to internal LAMMPS data. Pointers must be of the correct
type and kind to point to said data (i.e., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{REAL(c\_double)}}) and have
compatible rank.  The pointer being associated with LAMMPS data is type\sphinxhyphen{},
kind\sphinxhyphen{}, and rank\sphinxhyphen{}checked at run\sphinxhyphen{}time via an overloaded assignment operator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}
\PYG{k+kt}{REAL}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{c\PYGZus{}double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dr}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dx}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dy}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dz}
\PYG{c}{! more code to set up, etc.}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}fix george all recenter 2 2 2\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c}{! more code}
\PYG{n}{dr}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{extract\PYGZus{}fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}george\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{global}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{scalar}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{dx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{extract\PYGZus{}fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}george\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{global}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{dy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{extract\PYGZus{}fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}george\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{global}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{dz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{extract\PYGZus{}fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}george\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{global}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will extract the global scalar calculated by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_recenter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix recenter}}}} into the variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{dr} and the
three elements of the global vector calculated by fix recenter into the
variables \sphinxstyleemphasis{dx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dz}, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If asked for per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local data, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_fix()}} returns a
pointer to actual LAMMPS data.  The pointer returned will have the
appropriate size to match the internal data, and will be
type/kind/rank\sphinxhyphen{}checked at the time of the assignment. For example,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}
\PYG{k+kt}{REAL}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{c\PYGZus{}double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{DIMENSION}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{POINTER}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{r}
\PYG{c}{! more code to set up, etc.}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}fix state all store/state 0 x y z\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c}{! more code}
\PYG{n}{r}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{extract\PYGZus{}fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}state\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{k}{type}\PYG{p}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{k}{array}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will bind the pointer \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} to internal LAMMPS data representing the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
array computed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_store_state::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix store/state}}}} when three
inputs are specified. Similarly,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}
\PYG{k+kt}{REAL}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{c\PYGZus{}double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{DIMENSION}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{POINTER}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}
\PYG{c}{! more code to set up, etc.}

property/atom\sphinxhyphen{}based entities from all processes, in order by atom ID.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 22Dec2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This subroutine gathers data from all processes and stores them in a
one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional allocatable array. The array \sphinxstyleemphasis{data} will be
ordered by atom ID, which requires consecutive IDs (1 to \sphinxstyleemphasis{natoms}). If you
need a similar array but for non\sphinxhyphen{}consecutive atom IDs, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_scatter:_CPPv420lammps_gather_concatPvPKciiPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_gather\_concat()}}}}}; for a similar array but for a subset of

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{data} array will be ordered in groups of \sphinxstyleemphasis{count} values, sorted by atom
ID (e.g., if \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{data} is {[}x(1,1), x(2,1), x(3,1), x(1,2),
x(2,2), x(3,2), x(1,3), \(\dots\){]}); \sphinxstyleemphasis{data} must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ALLOCATABLE}} and
will be allocated to length (\sphinxstyleemphasis{count}\({}\times{}\)\sphinxstyleemphasis{natoms}), as
queried by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_natoms()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function will return an error if fix or compute data are requested and
the fix or compute ID given does not have per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data. See the note about
re\sphinxhyphen{}interpreting the vector as a matrix at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gather\_atoms()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is not compatible with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_BIGBIG}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Nov2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function performs the bit\sphinxhyphen{}shift, addition, and bit\sphinxhyphen{}wise OR operations
necessary to combine the values of three integers representing the image
flags in the \(x\)\sphinxhyphen{}, \(y\)\sphinxhyphen{}, and \(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}directions. Unless LAMMPS

signed integers \([-512,512)\). If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_BIGBIG}} was used when
compiling, then the return value is of kind \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int64\_t}} instead of
kind \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int}}, and the valid range for the individual image flags becomes
\([-1048576,1048575)\) (i.e., the range of a 21\sphinxhyphen{}bit signed integer).
There is no check on whether the arguments conform to these requirements;
values out of range will simply be wrapped back into the interval.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstylestrong{iy}\sphinxstyleemphasis{ {[}}\sphinxstyleemphasis{integer(c\_int)}\sphinxstyleemphasis{{]}} :: image flag in \(y\)\sphinxhyphen{}direction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{iz}\sphinxstyleemphasis{ {[}}\sphinxstyleemphasis{integer(c\_int)}\sphinxstyleemphasis{{]}} :: image flag in \(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}direction

is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int}} unless LAMMPS was built with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_BIGBIG}}, in which
case it is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int64\_t}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fact that the programmer does not know the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KIND}} parameter of the
return value until compile time means that it is impossible to define an

through its library interface to modify certain LAMMPS properties on

\PYG{k+kt}{    }\PYG{k}{CLASS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{INTENT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{INOUT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{caller}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{INTEGER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}bigint}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{INTENT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{IN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{timestep}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{INTEGER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}tagint}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{DIMENSION}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{INTENT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{IN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ids}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{REAL}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{c\PYGZus{}double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{DIMENSION}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{INTENT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{IN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{REAL}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{c\PYGZus{}double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{DIMENSION}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{INTENT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{OUT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kd}{::}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fexternal}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{END }\PYG{k}{SUBROUTINE }\PYG{n}{external\PYGZus{}callback}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_bigint}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int}} if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_SMALLSMALL}} was used and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int64\_t}} otherwise; and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_tagint}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int64\_t}} if
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_BIGBIG}} was used and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c\_int}} otherwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{caller} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_fix\_external\_callback()}} is unlimited
polymorphic (i.e., it can be any Fortran object you want to pass to the
calling function) and will be available as the first argument to the

a derived type and pass an instance of the derived type to \sphinxstyleemphasis{caller}.

The array \sphinxstyleemphasis{ids} is an array of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{nlocal} (as accessed from the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atom}} class or through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_global()}}). The arrays

transposed from what they would look like in C (see note about array index

simulation with the help of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_external::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix external}}}}. The
alternative is \sphinxstyleemphasis{array} mode, where one calls

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{IMPLICIT }\PYG{k}{NONE}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get pointer to the force array storage in a fix external instance with the
given ID.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 22Dec2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_external::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{external}}}} allows programs that are running LAMMPS
through its library interfaces to add or modify certain LAMMPS properties on
specific time steps, similar to the way other fixes do.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function provides access to the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom force storage in a fix
external instance with the given fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID to be added to the individual
atoms when using the “pf/array” mode.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fexternal} array can be
accessed like other “native” per\sphinxhyphen{}atom arrays accessible via the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_atom()}} function.  Please note that the array
stores the forces for \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} atoms for each MPI rank, in the order
determined by the neighbor list build.  Because the underlying data
structures can change as well as the order of atom as they migrate between
MPI processes because of the domain decomposition parallelization, this
function should be always called immediately before the forces are going to
be set to get an up\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}date pointer.  You can use, for example,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_setting()}} to obtain the number of local atoms \sphinxtitleref{nlocal} and
then assume the dimensions of the returned force array as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{REAL(c\_double) :: force(3,nlocal)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is an alternative to the callback mechanism in fix external
set up by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_fix\_external\_callback()}}. The main difference is that
this mechanism can be used when forces are to be pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed and the
control alternates between LAMMPS and the external driver, while the
callback mechanism can call an external subroutine to compute the force when
the fix is triggered and needs them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please see the documentation for {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_external::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix external}}}} for
more information about how to use the fix and how to couple it with an
external program.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{id}\sphinxstyleemphasis{ {[}}\sphinxstyleemphasis{character(len=*)}\sphinxstyleemphasis{{]}} :: ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_external::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix external}}}} instance

\sphinxlineitem{Call to}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_utility:_CPPv429lammps_fix_external_get_forcePvPKc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_fix\_external\_get\_force()}}}}}

command.  When running in parallel, it must be called from \sphinxstylestrong{all} MPI
processes with the \sphinxstylestrong{same} \sphinxstyleemphasis{idx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{val} parameters.  The variable
\sphinxstyleemphasis{val} is assumed to be extensive.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The index in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{idx} parameter is 1\sphinxhyphen{}based (i.e., the first element
is set with \sphinxstyleemphasis{idx}\({} = 1\), and the last element of the vector
with \sphinxstyleemphasis{idx}\({} = N\), where \(N\) is the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{length}
parameter of the call to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix\_external\_set\_vector\_length()}}).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please see the documentation for {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_external::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix external}}}} for

MPI ranks and is often recoverable, while a “2” indicates an abort that
would happen only in a single MPI rank and thus may not be recoverable, as
other MPI ranks may be waiting on the failing MPI rank(s) to send messages.

\section{LAMMPS C++ API}
\label{\detokenize{Library:lammps-cplusplus-api}}\label{\detokenize{Library:id2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is also possible to invoke the LAMMPS C++ API directly in your code.
It lacks some of the convenience of the C library API, but it allows
more direct access to simulation data and thus more low\sphinxhyphen{}level manipulations.
The following links provide some examples and references to the C++ API.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Using the C++ API directly}
\label{\detokenize{Cplusplus:using-the-c-api-directly}}\label{\detokenize{Cplusplus::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the C++ classes of the LAMMPS library is lacking some of the
convenience of the C library API, but it allows a more direct access to
simulation data and thus more low\sphinxhyphen{}level manipulations and tighter
integration of LAMMPS into another code.  While for the complete C
library API is provided in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{library.h}} header file, for using
the C++ API it is required to include the individual header files
defining the individual classes in use.  Typically the name of the
class and the name of the header follow some simple rule.  Examples
are given below.


\subsection{Creating or deleting a LAMMPS object}
\label{\detokenize{Cplusplus:creating-or-deleting-a-lammps-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the LAMMPS library interfaces, the core task is to create an
instance of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS\_NS::LAMMPS}}}}} class.  In C++ this can
be done directly through the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new}} operator.  All further operations
are then initiated through calling member functions of some of the
components of the LAMMPS class or accessing their data members.  The
destruction of the LAMMPS instance is correspondingly initiated by using
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delete}} operator.  Here is a simple example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}lammps.h\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}mpi.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}iostream\PYGZgt{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{main}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{argc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{argv}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// custom argument vector for LAMMPS library}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmpargv}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{liblammps}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZhy{}log}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{none}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmpargc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lmpargv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// explicitly initialize MPI}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}Init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{argc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{argv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// create LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{new}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lmpargc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{lmpargv}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}COMM\PYGZus{}WORLD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// output numerical version string}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{LAMMPS version ID: }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}ver}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{endl}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// delete LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{delete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// stop MPI environment}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This minimal example only requires to include the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps.h}} header
file since it only accesses a non\sphinxhyphen{}pointer member of the LAMMPS class.


\subsection{Executing LAMMPS commands}
\label{\detokenize{Cplusplus:executing-lammps-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Once a LAMMPS instance is created by your C++ code, you need to set up a
simulation and that is most conveniently done by “driving” it through
issuing commands like you would do when running a LAMMPS simulation from
an input script. Processing of input in LAMMPS is handled by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_input:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS5InputE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Input}}}}} class an instance of which is a
member of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}} class.  You have
two options: reading commands from a file, or executing a single
command from a string. See below for a small example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}lammps.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}input.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}mpi.h\PYGZgt{}}

\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}NS}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{main}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{argc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{argv}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmpargv}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{liblammps}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZhy{}log}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{none}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmpargc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lmpargv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}Init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{argc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{argv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{new}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lmpargc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{lmpargv}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}COMM\PYGZus{}WORLD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{input}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{in.melt}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{input}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{one}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{run 100 post no}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{delete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{Use Python with LAMMPS}
\label{\detokenize{Python_head:use-python-with-lammps}}\label{\detokenize{Python_head::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pages describe various ways that LAMMPS and Python can be used
together.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{Python_overview:overview}}\label{\detokenize{Python_overview::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS distribution includes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python}} directory with the Python
code needed to run LAMMPS from Python.  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python/lammps}} package
contains {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{the “lammps” Python module}}}} that wraps the
LAMMPS C\sphinxhyphen{}library interface.  This module makes it is possible to do the
following either from a Python script, or interactively from a Python
prompt:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
create one or more instances of LAMMPS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
invoke LAMMPS commands or read them from an input script

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
run LAMMPS incrementally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
extract LAMMPS results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
and modify internal LAMMPS data structures.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
From a Python script you can do this in serial or in parallel.  Running
Python interactively in parallel does not generally work, unless you
have a version of Python that extends Python to enable multiple
instances of Python to read what you type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To do all of this, you must build LAMMPS in {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_basics:exe}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{“shared” mode}}}}
and make certain that your Python interpreter can find the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}
Python package and the LAMMPS shared library file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Python wrapper for LAMMPS uses the \sphinxhref{https://docs.python.org/3/library/ctypes.html}{ctypes} package in
Python, which auto\sphinxhyphen{}generates the interface code needed between Python
and a set of C\sphinxhyphen{}style library functions.  Ctypes has been part of the
standard Python distribution since version 2.5.  You can check which
version of Python you have by simply typing “python” at a shell prompt.
Below is an example output for Python version 3.8.5.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }python
\PYG{g+go}{Python 3.8.5 (default, Aug 12 2020, 00:00:00)}
\PYG{g+go}{[GCC 10.2.1 20200723 (Red Hat 10.2.1\PYGZhy{}1)] on linux}
\PYG{g+go}{Type \PYGZdq{}help\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}copyright\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}credits\PYGZdq{} or \PYGZdq{}license\PYGZdq{} for more information.}
\PYG{g+go}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The options described in this section of the manual for using Python
with LAMMPS currently support either Python 2 or 3.  Specifically
version 2.7 or later and 3.6 or later.  Since the Python community no
longer maintains Python 2 (see \sphinxhref{https://www.python.org/doc/sunset-python-2/}{this notice}), we recommend use of
Python 3 with LAMMPS.  While Python 2 code should continue to work,
that is not something we can guarantee long\sphinxhyphen{}term.  If you notice
Python code in the LAMMPS distribution that is not compatible with
Python 3, please contact the LAMMPS developers or submit \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lammps/lammps/issues}{and issue
on GitHub}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS can work together with Python in three ways.  First, Python can
wrap LAMMPS through the its {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{library interface}}}}, so
that a Python script can create one or more instances of LAMMPS and
launch one or more simulations.  In Python terms, this is referred to as
“extending” Python with a LAMMPS module.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{python-invoke-lammps}.png}
\caption{Launching LAMMPS via Python}\label{\detokenize{Python_overview:id1}}\end{figure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Second, the lower\sphinxhyphen{}level Python interface in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps Python
class}}}}} can be used indirectly through the provided
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} wrapper classes, also written in Python.  These
wrappers try to simplify the usage of LAMMPS in Python by providing a
more object\sphinxhyphen{}based interface to common LAMMPS functionality.  They also
reduce the amount of code necessary to parameterize LAMMPS scripts
through Python and make variables and computes directly accessible.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{pylammps-invoke-lammps}.png}
\caption{Using the PyLammps / IPyLammps wrappers}\label{\detokenize{Python_overview:id2}}\end{figure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Third, LAMMPS can use the Python interpreter, so that a LAMMPS input
script or styles can invoke Python code directly, and pass information
back\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}forth between the input script and Python functions you write.
This Python code can also call back to LAMMPS to query or change its
attributes through the LAMMPS Python module mentioned above.  In Python
terms, this is called “embedding” Python into LAMMPS.  When used in this
mode, Python can perform script operations that the simple LAMMPS input
script syntax can not.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{lammps-invoke-python}.png}
\caption{Calling Python code from LAMMPS}\label{\detokenize{Python_overview:id3}}\end{figure}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Installation}
\label{\detokenize{Python_install:installation}}\label{\detokenize{Python_install::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS Python module enables calling the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library:lammps-c-api}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{LAMMPS C library API}}}} from Python by dynamically loading functions in the
LAMMPS shared library through the Python \sphinxhref{https://docs.python.org/3/library/ctypes.html}{ctypes}
module.  Because of the dynamic loading, it is required that LAMMPS is
compiled in {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_basics:exe}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{“shared” mode}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two components are necessary for Python to be able to invoke LAMMPS code:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS Python Package (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}) from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python}} folder

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS Shared Library (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps.so}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps.dylib}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps.dll}}) from the folder where you compiled LAMMPS.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Installing the LAMMPS Python Module and Shared Library}
\label{\detokenize{Python_install:installing-the-lammps-python-module-and-shared-library}}\label{\detokenize{Python_install:python-install-guides}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Making LAMMPS usable within Python and vice versa requires putting the
LAMMPS Python package (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}) into a location where the Python
interpreter can find it and installing the LAMMPS shared library into a
folder that the dynamic loader searches or inside of the installed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}} package folder.  There are multiple ways to achieve this.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install both components into a Python \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{site\sphinxhyphen{}packages}} folder, either
system\sphinxhyphen{}wide or in the corresponding user\sphinxhyphen{}specific folder. This way no
additional environment variables need to be set, but the shared
library is otherwise not accessible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do an installation into a virtual environment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Leave the files where they are in the source/development tree and
adjust some environment variables.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Python package}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compile LAMMPS with either {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_cmake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{CMake}}}} or the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_make::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{traditional make}}}} procedure in {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_basics:exe}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{shared
mode}}}}.  After compilation has finished, type (in the
compilation folder):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYGZhy{}python
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This will try to build a so\sphinxhyphen{}called (binary) wheel file, a
compressed binary python package and then install it with the
python package manager ‘pip’.  Installation will be attempted into
a system\sphinxhyphen{}wide \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{site\sphinxhyphen{}packages}} folder and if that fails into the
corresponding folder in the user’s home directory.  For a
system\sphinxhyphen{}wide installation you usually would have to gain superuser
privilege first, e.g. though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo}}


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabular}[t]{*{3}{\X{1}{3}}}
\sphinxtoprule
\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
File
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Location
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Notes
\\
\sphinxmidrule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS Python package
&\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$HOME/.local/lib/pythonX.Y/site\sphinxhyphen{}packages/lammps}}

\end{itemize}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X.Y}} depends on the installed Python version
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS shared library
&\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$HOME/.local/lib/pythonX.Y/site\sphinxhyphen{}packages/lammps}}

\end{itemize}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X.Y}} depends on the installed Python version
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabular}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a system\sphinxhyphen{}wide installation those folders would then become.


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering

\sphinxtoprule

File
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily
