Location
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Notes
\\
\sphinxmidrule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS Python package
&\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/usr/lib/pythonX.Y/site\sphinxhyphen{}packages/lammps}}

\end{itemize}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X.Y}} depends on the installed Python version
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS shared library
&\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/usr/lib/pythonX.Y/site\sphinxhyphen{}packages/lammps}}

\end{itemize}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X.Y}} depends on the installed Python version
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabular}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No environment variables need to be set for those, as those
folders are searched by default by Python or the LAMMPS Python
package.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 24Mar2022.}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If there is an existing installation of the LAMMPS python
module, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make install\sphinxhyphen{}python}} will try to update it.
However, that will fail if the older version of the module
was installed by LAMMPS versions until 17Feb2022.  Those
were using the distutils package, which does not create a
“manifest” that allows a clean uninstall.  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make
install\sphinxhyphen{}python}} command will always produce a
lammps\sphinxhyphen{}\textless{}version\textgreater{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textless{}python\textgreater{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textless{}abi\textgreater{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textless{}os\textgreater{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textless{}arch\textgreater{}.whl file (the
‘wheel’). And this file can be later installed directly with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python \sphinxhyphen{}m pip install \textless{}wheel file\textgreater{}.whl}} without having to
type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make install\sphinxhyphen{}python}} again and repeating the build
step, too.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the traditional make process you can override the python
version to version x.y when calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PYTHON=pythonX.Y}}.  For a CMake based compilation this choice
has to be made during the CMake configuration step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the default settings of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make install\sphinxhyphen{}python}} are not what you want,
you can invoke \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{install.py}} from the python directory manually as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }install.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}python\PYG{+w}{ }package\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}l\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}shared\PYG{+w}{ }library\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}version.h\PYG{+w}{ }file\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}n\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}} flag points to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}} Python package folder to be installed,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}l}} flag points to the LAMMPS shared library file to be installed,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}v}} flag points to the LAMMPS version header file to extract the version date,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}n}} instructs the script to only build a wheel file
but not attempt to install it.

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Virtual environment}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A virtual environment is a minimal Python installation inside of a
folder.  It allows isolating and customizing a Python environment
that is mostly independent from a user or system installation.
For the core Python environment, it uses symbolic links to the
system installation and thus it can be set up quickly and will not
take up much disk space.  This gives you the flexibility to
install (newer/different) versions of Python packages that would
potentially conflict with already installed system packages.  It
also does not requite any superuser privileges. See \sphinxhref{https://peps.python.org/pep-0405/}{PEP 405:
Python Virtual Environments} for more
information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a virtual environment in the folder \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$HOME/myenv}},
use the \sphinxhref{https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html}{venv} module as follows.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create virtual environment in folder \PYGZdl{}HOME/myenv}
python3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}HOME}/myenv
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Python versions prior 3.3 you can use \sphinxhref{https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/key\_projects/\#virtualenv}{virtualenv}
command instead of “python3 \sphinxhyphen{}m venv”.  This step has to be done
only once.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To activate the virtual environment type:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}HOME}/myenv/bin/activate
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This has to be done every time you log in or open a new terminal
window and after you turn off the virtual environment with the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deactivate}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using CMake to build LAMMPS, you need to set
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CMAKE\_INSTALL\_PREFIX}} to the value of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$VIRTUAL\_ENV}}
environment variable during the configuration step. For the
traditional make procedure, no additional steps are needed.
After compiling LAMMPS you can do a “Python package only”
installation with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make install\sphinxhyphen{}python}} and the LAMMPS Python
package and the shared library file are installed into the
following locations:


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabular}[t]{*{3}{\X{1}{3}}}
\sphinxtoprule
\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
File
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Location
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Notes
\\
\sphinxmidrule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS Python Module
&\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$VIRTUAL\_ENV/lib/pythonX.Y/site\sphinxhyphen{}packages/lammps}}

\end{itemize}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X.Y}} depends on the installed Python version
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS shared library
&\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$VIRTUAL\_ENV/lib/pythonX.Y/site\sphinxhyphen{}packages/lammps}}

\end{itemize}
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X.Y}} depends on the installed Python version
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabular}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{In place usage}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compile LAMMPS}}}} as usual in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_basics:exe}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{“shared” mode}}}} leave the shared library and Python
package inside the source/compilation folders. Instead of
copying the files where they can be found, you need to set the environment
variables \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PYTHONPATH}} (for the Python package) and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LD\_LIBRARY\_PATH}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DYLD\_LIBRARY\_PATH}} on macOS

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Bourne shells (bash, ksh and similar) the commands are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PYTHONPATH}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{PYTHONPATH}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}:\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{HOME}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}/lammps/python
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{LD\PYGZus{}LIBRARY\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{LD\PYGZus{}LIBRARY\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}:\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{HOME}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}/lammps/src
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the C\sphinxhyphen{}shells like csh or tcsh the commands are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{setenv }PYTHONPATH \PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{PYTHONPATH}\PYG{k}{\PYGZcb{}}:\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{HOME}\PYG{k}{\PYGZcb{}}/lammps/python
\PYG{n+nb}{setenv }LD\PYGZus{}LIBRARY\PYGZus{}PATH \PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{LD\PYGZus{}LIBRARY\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{k}{\PYGZcb{}}:\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{HOME}\PYG{k}{\PYGZcb{}}/lammps/src
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On macOS you may also need to set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DYLD\_LIBRARY\_PATH}} accordingly.
You can make those changes permanent by editing your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$HOME/.bashrc}}
or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$HOME/.login}} files, respectively.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PYTHONPATH}} needs to point to the parent folder that contains the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}} package!
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To verify if LAMMPS can be successfully started from Python, start the
Python interpreter, load the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}} Python module and create a
LAMMPS instance.  This should not generate an error message and produce
output similar to the following:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }python
\PYG{g+go}{Python 3.8.5 (default, Sep  5 2020, 10:50:12)}
\PYG{g+go}{[GCC 10.2.0] on linux}
\PYG{g+go}{Type \PYGZdq{}help\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}copyright\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}credits\PYGZdq{} or \PYGZdq{}license\PYGZdq{} for more information.}
\PYG{g+go}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} import lammps}
\PYG{g+go}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} lmp = lammps.lammps()}
\PYG{g+go}{LAMMPS (18 Sep 2020)}
\PYG{g+go}{using 1 OpenMP thread(s) per MPI task}
\PYG{g+go}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unless you opted for “In place use”, you will have to rerun the installation
any time you recompile LAMMPS to ensure the latest Python package and shared
library are installed and used.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want Python to be able to load different versions of the
LAMMPS shared library with different settings, you will need to
manually copy the files under different names
(e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps\_mpi.so}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps\_gpu.so}}) into the
appropriate folder as indicated above. You can then select the
desired library through the \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} argument of the LAMMPS object
constructor (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_create:python-create-lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Creating or deleting a LAMMPS object}}}}).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Extending Python to run in parallel}
\label{\detokenize{Python_install:extending-python-to-run-in-parallel}}\label{\detokenize{Python_install:python-install-mpi4py}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to run LAMMPS in parallel from Python, you need to extend
your Python with an interface to MPI.  This also allows you to
make MPI calls directly from Python in your script, if you desire.

\sphinxAtStartPar
We have tested this with \sphinxhref{https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/}{MPI for Python}
(aka mpi4py) and you will find installation instruction for it below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Installation of mpi4py (version 3.0.3 as of Sep 2020) can be done as
follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip}} into a local user folder with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }mpi4py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dnf}} into a system folder for RedHat/Fedora systems:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} for use with OpenMPI}
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }dnf\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }python3\PYGZhy{}mpi4py\PYGZhy{}openmpi
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} for use with MPICH}
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }dnf\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }python3\PYGZhy{}mpi4py\PYGZhy{}openmpi
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip}} into a virtual environment (see above):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}HOME}/myenv/activate
\PYG{g+gp+gpVirtualEnv}{(myenv)}\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }mpi4py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip}} into a system folder (not recommended):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }mpi4py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For more detailed installation instructions and additional options,
please see the \sphinxhref{https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/install.html}{mpi4py installation} page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpi4py}} and LAMMPS in parallel from Python, you \sphinxstylestrong{must} make
certain that \sphinxstylestrong{both} are using the \sphinxstylestrong{same} implementation and version
of MPI library.  If you only have one MPI library installed on your
system this is not an issue, but it can be if you have multiple MPI
installations (e.g. on an HPC cluster to be selected through environment
modules).  Your LAMMPS build is explicit about which MPI it is using,
since it is either detected during CMake configuration or in the
traditional make build system you specify the details in your low\sphinxhyphen{}level
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MAKE/Makefile.foo}} file. The installation process of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpi4py}}
uses the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpicc}} command to find information about the MPI it uses to
build against.  And it tries to load “libmpi.so” from the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LD\_LIBRARY\_PATH}}.  This may or may not find the MPI library that
LAMMPS is using.  If you have problems running both mpi4py and LAMMPS
together, this is an issue you may need to address, e.g. by loading the
module for different MPI installation so that mpi4py finds the right
one.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have successfully installed mpi4py, you should be able to run
Python and type

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{mpi4py}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{MPI}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
without error.  You should also be able to run Python in parallel
on a simple test script

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }python3\PYG{+w}{ }test.py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{test.py}} contains the lines

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{mpi4py}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{MPI}
\PYG{n}{comm} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MPI}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{COMM\PYGZus{}WORLD}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Proc }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}d}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ out of }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}d}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ procs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Get\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Get\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and see one line of output for each processor you run on.  Please note
that the order of the lines is not deterministic

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }python3\PYG{+w}{ }test.py
\PYG{g+go}{Proc 0 out of 4 procs}
\PYG{g+go}{Proc 1 out of 4 procs}
\PYG{g+go}{Proc 2 out of 4 procs}
\PYG{g+go}{Proc 3 out of 4 procs}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Run LAMMPS from Python}
\label{\detokenize{Python_run:run-lammps-from-python}}\label{\detokenize{Python_run::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After compiling the LAMMPS shared library and making it ready to use,
you can now write and run Python scripts that import the LAMMPS Python
module and launch LAMMPS simulations through Python scripts.
The following pages take you through the various steps necessary,
what functionality is available and give some examples how to use it.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Running LAMMPS and Python in serial}
\label{\detokenize{Python_launch:running-lammps-and-python-in-serial}}\label{\detokenize{Python_launch::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To run a LAMMPS in serial, type these lines into Python
interactively from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bench}} directory:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.lj}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or put the same lines in the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{test.py}} and run it as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python3\PYG{+w}{ }test.py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Either way, you should see the results of running the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{in.lj}} benchmark
on a single processor appear on the screen, the same as if you had
typed something like:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
lmp\PYGZus{}serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.lj
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Running LAMMPS and Python in parallel with MPI}
\label{\detokenize{Python_launch:running-lammps-and-python-in-parallel-with-mpi}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To run LAMMPS in parallel, assuming you have installed the
\sphinxhref{https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io}{mpi4py} package as discussed
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_install:python-install-mpi4py}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Extending Python to run in parallel}}}}, create a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{test.py}} file containing these lines:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{mpi4py}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{MPI}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.lj}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{me} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MPI}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{COMM\PYGZus{}WORLD}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Get\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{nprocs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MPI}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{COMM\PYGZus{}WORLD}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Get\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Proc }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}d}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ out of }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}d}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ procs has}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{me}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{nprocs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{MPI}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Finalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can run the script in parallel as:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }python3\PYG{+w}{ }test.py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and you should see the same output as if you had typed

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }lmp\PYGZus{}mpi\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.lj
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that without the mpi4py specific lines from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{test.py}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.lj}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
running the script with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mpirun}} on \(P\) processors would lead to
\(P\) independent simulations to run parallel, each with a single
processor. Therefore, if you use the mpi4py lines and you see multiple LAMMPS
single processor outputs, mpi4py is not working correctly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that once you import the mpi4py module, mpi4py initializes MPI
for you, and you can use MPI calls directly in your Python script, as
described in the mpi4py documentation.  The last line of your Python
script should be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI.finalize()}}, to ensure MPI is shut down
correctly.


\subsection{Running Python scripts}
\label{\detokenize{Python_launch:running-python-scripts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that any Python script (not just for LAMMPS) can be invoked in
one of several ways:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }script.py
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}i\PYG{+w}{ }script.py
./script.py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last command requires that the first line of the script be
something like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+ch}{\PYGZsh{}!/usr/bin/python}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
or

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+ch}{\PYGZsh{}!/usr/bin/env python}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the path in the first case needs to point to where you have Python
installed (the second option is workaround for when this may change),
and that you have made the script file executable:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
chmod\PYG{+w}{ }+x\PYG{+w}{ }script.py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Without the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}i}} flag, Python will exit when the script finishes.
With the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}i}} flag, you will be left in the Python interpreter when
the script finishes, so you can type subsequent commands.  As mentioned
above, you can only run Python interactively when running Python on a
single processor, not in parallel.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Creating or deleting a LAMMPS object}
\label{\detokenize{Python_create:creating-or-deleting-a-lammps-object}}\label{\detokenize{Python_create:python-create-lammps}}\label{\detokenize{Python_create::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With the Python interface the creation of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}} instance is included in the constructors for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} classes.
Internally it will call either {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv411lammps_openiPPc8MPI_CommPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open()}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_create:_CPPv418lammps_open_no_mpiiPPcPPv}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps\_open\_no\_mpi()}}}}} from the C
library API to create the class instance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All arguments are optional.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} argument allows loading a
LAMMPS shared library that is named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps\_machine.so}} instead of
the default name of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{liblammps.so}}.  In most cases the latter will be
installed or used.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ptr} argument is for use of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:module-lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} module from inside a LAMMPS instance, e.g. with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{python}}}} command, where a pointer to the already existing
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Classes_lammps:_CPPv4N9LAMMPS_NS6LAMMPSE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS}}}}} class instance can be passed
to the Python class and used instead of creating a new instance.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{comm} argument may be used in combination with the \sphinxhref{https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/}{mpi4py}
module to pass an MPI communicator to LAMMPS and thus it is possible
to run the Python module like the library interface on a subset of the
MPI ranks after splitting the communicator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are simple examples using all three Python interfaces:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{lammps API}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} NOTE: argv[0] is set by the lammps class constructor}
\PYG{n}{args} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}log}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{none}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmdargs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} get and print numerical version code}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{LAMMPS Version: }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{version}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} explicitly close and delete LAMMPS instance (optional)}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{PyLammps API}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} class is a wrapper around the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} class and all of its lower level functions.
By default, it will create a new instance of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} passing
along all arguments to the constructor of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} NOTE: argv[0] is set by the lammps class constructor}
\PYG{n}{args} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}log}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{none}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmdargs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} get and print numerical version code}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{LAMMPS Version: }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{version}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} explicitly close and delete LAMMPS instance (optional)}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} objects can also be created on top of an existing
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} object:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}
\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmdargs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create PyLammps instance using previously created LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful if you have to create the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}
instance is a specific way, but want to take advantage of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} interface.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{IPyLammps API}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} class is an extension of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} class. It has the same construction behavior. By
default, it will create a new instance of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:module-lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} passing
along all arguments to the constructor of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:module-lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{IPyLammps}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} NOTE: argv[0] is set by the lammps class constructor}
\PYG{n}{args} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}log}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{none}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{IPyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmdargs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} get and print numerical version code}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{LAMMPS Version: }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{version}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} explicitly close and delete LAMMPS instance (optional)}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also initialize IPyLammps on top of an existing {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:module-lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}} object:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{IPyLammps}
\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmdargs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create PyLammps instance using previously created LAMMPS instance}
\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful if you have to create the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}
instance is a specific way, but want to take advantage of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} interface.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In all of the above cases, same as with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library:lammps-c-api}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{C library API}}}}, this will use the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MPI\_COMM\_WORLD}} communicator for the MPI library that LAMMPS was
compiled with.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.close}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lmp.close()}}}}} call is
optional since the LAMMPS class instance will also be deleted
automatically during the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} class
destructor.  Instead of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.close}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lmp.close()}}}}}
it is also possible to call {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.finalize}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lmp.finalize()}}}}};
this will destruct the LAMMPS instance, but also finalized and release
the MPI and/or Kokkos environment if enabled and active.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that you can create multiple LAMMPS objects in your Python
script, and coordinate and run multiple simulations, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}
\PYG{n}{lmp1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp1}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.file1}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp2}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.file2}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Executing commands}
\label{\detokenize{Python_execute:executing-commands}}\label{\detokenize{Python_execute::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Once an instance of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} class is created, there are
multiple ways to “feed” it commands. In a way that is not very different from
running a LAMMPS input script, except that Python has many more facilities
for structured programming than the LAMMPS input script syntax. Furthermore
it is possible to “compute” what the next LAMMPS command should be.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{lammps API}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same as in the equivalent
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_execute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{C library functions}}}}, commands can be read from a file, a
single string, a list of strings and a block of commands in a single
multi\sphinxhyphen{}line string. They are processed under the same boundary conditions
as the C library counterparts.  The example below demonstrates the use
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps.file()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps.command()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps.commands\_list()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps.commands\_string()}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}
\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} read commands from file \PYGZsq{}in.melt\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{in.melt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} issue a single command}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{variable zpos index 1.0}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create 10 groups with 10 atoms each}
\PYG{n}{cmds} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{group g}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ id }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{:}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{format}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{commands\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmds}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} run commands from a multi\PYGZhy{}line string}
\PYG{n}{block} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{l+s+s2}{clear}
\PYG{l+s+s2}{region  box block 0 2 0 2 0 2}
\PYG{l+s+s2}{create\PYGZus{}box 1 box}
\PYG{l+s+s2}{create\PYGZus{}atoms 1 single 1.0 1.0 \PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}zpos\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{commands\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{PyLammps/IPyLammps API}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the lammps API, the PyLammps/IPyLammps APIs allow running LAMMPS
commands by calling equivalent member functions of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} instances.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For instance, the following LAMMPS command

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
can be executed using with the lammps API with the following Python code if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lmp}} is an
instance of {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}

\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{region box block 0 10 0 5 \PYGZhy{}0.5 0.5}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the PyLammps interface, any LAMMPS command can be split up into arbitrary parts.
These parts are then passed to a member function with the name of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{command}}}}.
For the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command that means the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region()}} method can be called.
The arguments of the command can be passed as one string, or
individually.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}

\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pass command parameters as one string}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{box block 0 10 0 5 \PYGZhy{}0.5 0.5}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} OR pass them individually}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{box block}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the latter example, all parameters except the first are Python floating\sphinxhyphen{}point literals. The
member function takes the entire parameter list and transparently merges it to a single command
string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The benefit of this approach is avoiding redundant command calls and easier
parameterization. In the lammps API parameterization needed to be done
manually by creating formatted command strings.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{region box block }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZpc{}f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{xhi}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ylo}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{yhi}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{zlo}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast, methods of PyLammps accept parameters directly and will convert
them automatically to a final command string.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{box block}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{xhi}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ylo}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{yhi}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{zlo}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using these facilities, the example shown for the lammps API can be rewritten as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}
\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} read commands from file \PYGZsq{}in.melt\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{in.melt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} issue a single command}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{zpos}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{index}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} create 10 groups with 10 atoms each}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
   \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{g}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{:}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{clear}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{box block}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}box}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{box}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}atoms}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{single}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdl{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}zpos\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{System properties}
\label{\detokenize{Python_properties:system-properties}}\label{\detokenize{Python_properties::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to what is described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{Library_properties::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{System properties}}}}, the instances of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} can be used to extract different kinds
of information about the active LAMMPS instance and also to modify some of it. The
main difference between the interfaces is how the information is exposed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
While the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}} is just a thin layer that wraps C API calls,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.IPyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IPyLammps}}}}} expose
information as objects and properties.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In some cases the data returned is a direct reference to the original data
inside LAMMPS cast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctypes}} pointers. Where possible, the wrappers will
determine the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctypes}} data type and cast pointers accordingly. If
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{numpy}} is installed arrays can also be extracted as numpy arrays, which
will access the C arrays directly and have the correct dimensions to protect
against invalid accesses.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When accessing per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data,
please note that this data is the per\sphinxhyphen{}processor local data and indexed
accordingly. These arrays can change sizes and order at every neighbor list
rebuild and atom sort event as atoms are migrating between subdomains.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{lammps API}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{lammps}

\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.sysinit}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{natoms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}natoms}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{running simulation with }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{natoms}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ atoms}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{run 1000 post no}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
   \PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{run 100 pre no post no}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
   \PYG{n}{pe} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}thermo}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pe}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
   \PYG{n}{ke} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}thermo}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ke}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
   \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{PE = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{KE = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Methods}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.version}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{version()}}}}}: return the numerical version id, e.g. LAMMPS 2 Sep 2015 \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} 20150902

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.get_thermo}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_thermo()}}}}}: return current value of a thermo keyword

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.last_thermo}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{last\_thermo()}}}}}: return a dictionary of the last thermodynamic output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.get_natoms}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_natoms()}}}}}: total \# of atoms as int

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.reset_box}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset\_box()}}}}}: reset the simulation box size

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.extract_setting}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_setting()}}}}}: return a global setting

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.extract_global}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_global()}}}}}: extract a global quantity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.extract_box}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract\_box()}}}}}: extract box info

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.create_atoms}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{create\_atoms()}}}}}: create N atoms with IDs, types, x, v, and image flags

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Properties}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps.last_thermo_step}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{last\_thermo\_step}}}}}: the last timestep thermodynamic output was computed

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{PyLammps/IPyLammps API}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the functions provided by {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.lammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lammps}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_module:lammps.PyLammps}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PyLammps}}}}} objects
have several properties which allow you to query the system state:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{L.system}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Is a dictionary describing the system such as the bounding box or number of atoms

\sphinxlineitem{L.system.xlo, L.system.xhi}
\sphinxAtStartPar
bounding box limits along x\sphinxhyphen{}axis

\sphinxlineitem{L.system.ylo, L.system.yhi}
\sphinxAtStartPar
bounding box limits along y\sphinxhyphen{}axis

\sphinxlineitem{L.system.zlo, L.system.zhi}
\sphinxAtStartPar
bounding box limits along z\sphinxhyphen{}axis

\sphinxlineitem{L.communication}
\sphinxAtStartPar
configuration of communication subsystem, such as the number of threads or processors

\sphinxlineitem{L.communication.nthreads}
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of threads used by each LAMMPS process

\sphinxlineitem{L.communication.nprocs}
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of MPI processes used by LAMMPS

\sphinxlineitem{L.fixes}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of fixes in the current system

\sphinxlineitem{L.computes}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of active computes in the current system

\sphinxlineitem{L.dump}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of active dumps in the current system

\sphinxlineitem{L.groups}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of groups present in the current system

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Retrieving the value of an arbitrary LAMMPS expressions}

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS expressions can be immediately evaluated by using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eval}} method. The
passed string parameter can be any expression containing global {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo command}}}} values,
variables, compute or fix data (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Output from LAMMPS (thermo, dumps, computes, fixes, variables)}}}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ke}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} kinetic energy}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pe}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} potential energy}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{v\PYGZus{}t/2.0}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}

\PYG{n}{L} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{PyLammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{in.sysinit}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{running simulation with }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{system}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{natoms}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ atoms}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{post no}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
   \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pre no post no}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
   \PYG{n}{pe} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pe}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
   \PYG{n}{ke} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ke}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
   \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{PE = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{KE = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
