\subsubsection{Writing coefficients to data files}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:writing-coefficients-to-data-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{write\_data()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{write\_data\_all()}} functions are optional and
write out the current state of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff
settings}}}} as “Pair Coeffs” or “PairIJ Coeffs” sections to a
data file when using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data command}}}}.  The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{write\_data()}} only writes out the diagonal elements of the pair
coefficient matrix, as that is required for the format of the “Pair
Coeffs” section.  It is called when the “pair” option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data command}}}} is “ii” (the default).  This is
suitable for force fields where \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal terms of the pair
coefficient matrix are generated from mixing.  If explicit settings for
off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal elements were made, LAMMPS will print a warning, as those
would be lost.  To avoid this, the “pair ij” option of {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}} can be used which will trigger calling the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{write\_data\_all()}} function instead, which will write out all settings
of the pair coefficient matrix (regardless of whether they were
originally created from mixing or not).

\sphinxAtStartPar
These data file output functions are only useful for true pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise
additive potentials, where the potential parameters can be entered
through \sphinxstyleemphasis{multiple} {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff commands}}}}.  Pair styles
that require a single “pair\_coeff * *” command line are not compatible
with reading their parameters from data files.  For pair styles like
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/gauss} that do support writing to data files, the potential
parameters will be read from the data file, if present, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff commands}}}} may not be needed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The member variable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{writedata}} should be set to 1 in the constructor,
if these functions are implemented (the default value is 0).

\subsubsection{Give access to internal data}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:give-access-to-internal-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The purpose of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}} function is to facilitate access to
internal data of the pair style by other parts of LAMMPS.  One possible
application is to use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}} to gradually change
potential parameters during a run.  Here, we implement access to the
pair coefficient matrix parameters.

Since the mercury potential, for which we have implemented the
born/gauss pair style, has a temperature dependent parameter “biga1”, we

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{biga1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZhy{}2.58717e\PYGZhy{}8*v\PYGZus{}temp+8.40841e\PYGZhy{}5}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m}{1.97475e\PYGZhy{}2}

\subsection{Case 2: a many\sphinxhyphen{}body potential}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:case-2-a-many-body-potential}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since there is a detailed description of the purpose and general layout
of a pair style in the previous case, we will focus on where the
implementation of a typical many\sphinxhyphen{}body potential \sphinxstyleemphasis{differs} from a
pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise additive potential.  We will use the implementation of the
Tersoff potential as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_tersoff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style tersoff}}}} as an
example.  The complete implementation can be found in the files
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_tersoff.cpp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_tersoff.h}} of
the LAMMPS source code.


\subsubsection{Constructor}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:constructor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the constructor, several {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify_pair::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style flags}}}} must
be set differently for many\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the potential is not pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise additive, so the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{single()}} function
cannot be used. This is indicated by setting the \sphinxtitleref{single\_enable}
member variable to 0 (default value is 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
many\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials are usually not written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  This is indicated by setting the member
variable \sphinxtitleref{restartinfo} to 0 (default is 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
many\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials typically read \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} parameters from a file which
stores parameters indexed with a string (e.g. the element).  For this,
only a single {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff * *}}}} command is allowed.
This requirement is set and checked for, when the member variable
\sphinxtitleref{one\_coeff} is set to 1 (default value is 0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
many\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials can produce incorrect results if pairs of atoms
are excluded from the neighbor list, e.g. explicitly by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify exclude}}}} or implicitly through
defining bonds, angles, etc. and having a {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds setting}}}} that is not “special\_bonds lj/coul 1.0 1.0 1.0”.
LAMMPS will check for this and print a suitable warning, when the
member variable \sphinxtitleref{manybody\_flag} is set to 1 (default value is 0).

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{PairTersoff}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{PairTersoff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Pair}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{single\PYGZus{}enable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{restartinfo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{one\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{manybody\PYGZus{}flag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Neighbor list request}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:neighbor-list-request}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For computing the three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions of the Tersoff potential a
“full” neighbor list (both atoms of a pair are listed in each other’s
neighbor list) is required.  By default a “half” neighbor list is
requested (each pair is listed only once).  The request is made in
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{init\_style()}} function.  A more in\sphinxhyphen{}depth discussion of neighbor
lists in LAMMPS and how to request them is in {\hyperref[\detokenize{Developer_notes:request-neighbor-list}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{this section of the
documentation}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{c+cm}{   init specific to this pair style}
\PYG{c+cm}{\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} */}

\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{PairTersoff::init\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{tag\PYGZus{}enable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{error}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{FLERR}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Pair style Tersoff requires newton pair on}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Computing forces from the neighbor list}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:computing-forces-from-the-neighbor-list}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computing forces for a many\sphinxhyphen{}body potential is usually more complex than
for a pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise additive potential and there are multiple components.
For Tersoff, there is a pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise additive two\sphinxhyphen{}body term (two nested
loops over indices \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}) and a three\sphinxhyphen{}body term (three nested
loops over indices \sphinxstyleemphasis{i}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{k}).  Since the neighbor list has
all neighbors up to the maximum cutoff (for the two\sphinxhyphen{}body term), but
the three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions have a significantly shorter cutoff,
a “short neighbor list” is also constructed at the same time while computing
the two\sphinxhyphen{}body term and looping over the neighbor list for the first time.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{rsq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutshortsq}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{neighshort}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{numshort}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{numshort}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxshort}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{maxshort}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxshort}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{grow}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{neighshort}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{maxshort}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{pair:neighshort}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the two\sphinxhyphen{}body term, only a half neighbor list would be needed, even
though we have requested a full list (for the three\sphinxhyphen{}body loops).
Rather than computing all interactions twice, we skip over half of
the entries.  This is done in a slightly complex way to make certain
the same choice is made across all subdomains and so that there is
no load imbalance introduced.

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{itag}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{jtag}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{continue}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{itag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{jtag}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{itag}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{jtag}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{continue}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{continue}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ztmp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ytmp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xtmp}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{continue}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Reading potential parameters}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:reading-potential-parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the Tersoff potential, the parameters are listed in a file and
associated with triples of elements.  Because we have set the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{one\_coeff}} flag to 1 in the constructor, there may only be a single
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff * *}}}} line in the input for this pair
style, and as a consequence the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coeff()}} function will only be called
once.  Thus, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coeff()}} function has to do three tasks, each of
which is delegated to a function in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairTersoff}} class:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
map elements to atom types.  Those follow the potential file name in the
command line arguments and are processed by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_element2type()}} function.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
read and parse the potential parameter file in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{read\_file()}} function.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Build data structures where the original and derived parameters are
indexed by all possible triples of atom types and thus can be looked
up quickly in the loops for the force computation

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{PairTersoff::coeff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{!}\PYG{n}{allocated}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{allocate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{map\PYGZus{}element2type}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// read potential file and initialize potential parameters}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{read\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{setup\PYGZus{}params}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Case 3: a potential requiring communication}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:case-3-a-potential-requiring-communication}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For some models, the interactions between atoms depends on properties of
their environment which have to be computed \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} the the forces can
be computed.  Since LAMMPS is designed to run in parallel using a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Developer_par_part::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{domain decomposition strategy}}}}, not all
information of the atoms may be directly available and thus
communication steps may be need to collect data from ghost atoms of
neighboring subdomains or send data to ghost atoms for application
during the pairwise computation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically, two communication patterns are needed: a “reverse
communication” and a “forward communication”.  The reverse communication
collects data added to “ghost” atoms from neighboring sub\sphinxhyphen{}domains and
sums it to their corresponding “local” atoms.  This communication is
only required and thus executed when the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Force::newton\_pair}} setting
is 1 (i.e. {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton on}}}}, the default).  The forward
communication is used to copy computed per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data from “local” atoms
to their corresponding “ghost” atoms in neighboring sub\sphinxhyphen{}domains.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For this we will look at how the embedding term of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{embedded
atom potential EAM}}}} is implemented in LAMMPS.  The complete
implementation of this pair style can be found in the files
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_eam.cpp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_eam.h}} of the
LAMMPS source code.


\subsubsection{Allocating additional per\sphinxhyphen{}atom storage}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:allocating-additional-per-atom-storage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
First suitable (local) per\sphinxhyphen{}atom arrays (\sphinxtitleref{rho}, \sphinxtitleref{fp}, \sphinxtitleref{numforce}) are
allocated. These have to be large enough to include ghost atoms, are not
used outside the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}} function and are re\sphinxhyphen{}initialized to zero
once per timestep.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{destroy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{rho}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{destroy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{fp}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{destroy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{numforce}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{rho}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{pair:rho}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{fp}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{pair:fp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{numforce}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{pair:numforce}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Reverse communication}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:reverse-communication}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Then a first loop over all pairs (\sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}) is performed, where data
is stored in the \sphinxtitleref{rho} array representing the electron density at the site of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i} contributed from all neighbors \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}.  Since the EAM pair style uses
a half neighbor list (for efficiency reasons), a reverse communication is
needed to collect the contributions to \sphinxtitleref{rho} from ghost atoms (only if
{\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton on}}}} is set for pair styles).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{newton\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{reverse\PYGZus{}comm}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{this}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To support the reverse communication, two functions must be defined:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pack\_reverse\_comm()}} that copies relevant data into a buffer for ghost
atoms and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unpack\_reverse\_comm()}} that takes the collected data and adds
it to the \sphinxtitleref{rho} array for the corresponding local atoms that match the
ghost atoms.  In order to allocate sufficiently sized buffers, a flag
must be set in the pair style constructor. Since in this case a single
double precision number is communicated per atom, the \sphinxtitleref{comm\_reverse}
member variable is set to 1 (default is 0 = no reverse communication).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{PairEAM::pack\PYGZus{}reverse\PYGZus{}comm}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{buf}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{last}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{last}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{buf}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rho}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{PairEAM::unpack\PYGZus{}reverse\PYGZus{}comm}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{list}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{buf}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{list}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{rho}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{buf}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Forward communication}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:forward-communication}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
From the density array \sphinxtitleref{rho}, the derivative of the embedding energy
\sphinxtitleref{fp} is computed. The computation is only done for “local” atoms, but
for the force computation, that property also is needed on ghost atoms.
For that a forward communication is needed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{forward\PYGZus{}comm}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{this}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to the reverse communication, this requires implementing a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pack\_forward\_comm()}} and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unpack\_forward\_comm()}} function.
Since there is one double precision number per atom that needs to be
communicated, we must set the \sphinxtitleref{comm\_forward} member variable to 1
(default is 0 = no forward communication).

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{list}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{buf}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fp}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{PairEAM::unpack\PYGZus{}forward\PYGZus{}comm}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{buf}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{Case 4: potentials without a compute() function}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:case-4-potentials-without-a-compute-function}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A small number of pair style classes do not implement a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}}
function, but instead use that of a different pair style.


\subsubsection{Embedded atom variants “eam/fs” and “eam/alloy”}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:embedded-atom-variants-eam-fs-and-eam-alloy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair styles {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{eam/fs and eam/alloy}}}} share the same
model and potential function as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{eam pair style}}}}.
They differ in the format of the potential files.  Pair style {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{eam}}}} supports only potential files for single elements.  For
multi\sphinxhyphen{}element systems, the mixed terms are computed from mixed
parameters.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{eam/fs} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{eam/alloy} pair styles, however,
\sphinxstylestrong{require} the use of a single potential file for all elements where
the mixed element potential is included in the tabulation.  That enables
more accurate models for alloys, since the mixed terms can be adjusted
for a better representation of material properties compared to terms
created from mixing of per\sphinxhyphen{}element terms in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairEAM}} class.

\sphinxAtStartPar
We take a closer at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{eam/alloy} pair style.  The complete
implementation is in the files \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_eam\_alloy.cpp}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_eam\_alloy.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairEAMAlloy}} class is derived from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairEAM}} and not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pair}}
and overrides only a small number of functions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{PairEAMAlloy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{virtual}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{public}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{PairEAM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{public}\PYG{o}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{PairEAMAlloy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{AIREBO and AIREBO\sphinxhyphen{}M potentials}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:airebo-and-airebo-m-potentials}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The AIREBO\sphinxhyphen{}M potential differs from the better known AIREBO potential in
that it use a Morse potential instead of a Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential for
non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded interactions.  Since this difference is very minimal compared
to the entire potential, both potentials are implemented in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairAIREBO}} class and which non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded potential is used is
determined by the value of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{morseflag}} flag, which would be set to
either 0 or 1.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{PairAIREBOMorse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{public}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{PairAIREBO}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{public}\PYG{o}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{PairAIREBOMorse}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{settings}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{override}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{morseflag}} variable defaults to 0 and is set to 1 in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairAIREBOMorse::settings()}} function which is called by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command.  This function delegates
all command line processing and setting of other parameters to the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairAIREBO::settings()}} function of the base class.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{PairAIREBOMorse::settings}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{PairAIREBO}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{settings}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{morseflag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The complete implementation is in the files
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_airebo.cpp}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_airebo.h}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_airebo\_morse.cpp}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MANYBODY/pair\_airebo\_morse.h}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_pair:bomont2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Bomont)} Bomont, Bretonnet, J. Chem. Phys. 124, 054504 (2006)

\subsection{Writing a new fix style}
\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_fix:writing-a-new-fix-style}}\label{\detokenize{Developer_write_fix::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writing fix styles is a flexible way of extending LAMMPS.  Users can
implement many things using fixes.  Some fix styles are only used
internally to support compute styles or pair styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
change particles attributes (positions, velocities, forces, etc.). Examples: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixNVE}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixFreeze}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
read or write data.  Example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixRestart}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
adding or modifying properties due to geometry. Example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixWall}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
interacting with other subsystems or external code: Examples: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixTTM}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixExternal}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixMDI}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
saving information for analysis or future use (previous positions,
for instance). Examples: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixAveTime}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixStoreState}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All fixes are derived from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Fix}} base class and must have a
constructor with the signature: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixPrintVel(class LAMMPS *, int, char **)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every fix must be registered in LAMMPS by writing the following lines
of code in the header before include guards:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{ifdef FIX\PYGZus{}CLASS}
\PYG{c+c1}{// clang\PYGZhy{}format off}
\PYG{n}{FixStyle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{vel}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{FixPrintVel}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// clang\PYGZhy{}format on}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{else}
\PYG{c+cm}{/* the definition of the FixPrintVel class comes here */}
\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{print/vel}} is the style name of your fix in the input script and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FixPrintVel}} is the name of the class. The header file would be called
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix\_print\_vel.h}} and the implementation file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix\_print\_vel.cpp}}.
These conventions allow LAMMPS to automatically integrate it into the
executable when compiling and associate your new fix class with the designated
keyword when it parses the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Let’s write a simple fix which will print the average velocity at the end
of each timestep. First of all, implement a constructor:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{FixPrintVel}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{FixPrintVel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{utils}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{missing\PYGZus{}cmd\PYGZus{}args}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{FLERR}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{fix print/vel}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{error}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{utils}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{inumeric}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{FLERR}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{error}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{FLERR}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Illegal fix print/vel nevery value: \PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nevery}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the constructor you should parse the fix arguments which are
specified in the script.  All fixes have pretty much the same syntax:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix \textless{}fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID\textgreater{} \textless{}fix group\textgreater{} \textless{}fix name\textgreater{} \textless{}fix arguments ...\textgreater{}}}. The first 3
parameters are parsed by Fix base class constructor, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}fix
arguments\textgreater{}}} should be parsed by you.  In our case, we need to specify
how often we want to print an average velocity. For instance, once in 50
timesteps: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix 1 print/vel 50}}. There is a special variable in the
Fix class called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nevery}} which specifies how often the method
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{end\_of\_step()}} is called.  Thus all we need to do is just set it up.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next method we need to implement is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{setmask()}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{FixPrintVel::setmask}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mask}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{mask}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{FixConst}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{END\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}STEP}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mask}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here the we specify which methods of the fix should be called during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Developer_flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{execution of a timestep}}}}.  The constant
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{END\_OF\_STEP}} corresponds to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{end\_of\_step()}} method.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{FixPrintVel::end\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}step}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// for add3, scale3}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{MathExtra}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nlocal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{nlocal}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{localAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{// 4th element for particles count}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{localAvgVel}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{add3}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{localAvgVel}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{particleInd}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{localAvgVel}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{localAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nlocal}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}Allreduce}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{localAvgVel}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}DOUBLE}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{MPI\PYGZus{}SUM}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{world}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{scale3}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{fmt}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{screen}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}, \PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}, \PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{globalAvgVel}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the code above, we use MathExtra routines defined in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{math\_extra.h}}.  There are bunch of math functions to work with
arrays of doubles as with math vectors.  It is also important to note
that LAMMPS code should always assume to be run in parallel and that
atom data is thus distributed across the MPI ranks.  Thus you can
only process data from local atoms directly and need to use MPI library
calls to combine or exchange data.  For serial execution, LAMMPS
comes bundled with the MPI STUBS library that contains the MPI library
function calls in dummy versions that only work for a single MPI rank.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this code we use an instance of Atom class. This object is stored
in the Pointers class (see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pointers.h}}) which is the base class of
the Fix base class. This object contains references to various class
instances (the original instances are created and held by the LAMMPS
class) with all global information about the simulation system.
Data from the Pointers class is available to all classes inherited from
it using protected inheritance. Hence when you write you own class,
which is going to use LAMMPS data, don’t forget to inherit from Pointers
or pass a Pointer to it to all functions that need access. When writing
fixes we inherit from class Fix which is inherited from Pointers so
there is no need to inherit from it directly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The code above computes average velocity for all particles in the
simulation.  Yet you have one unused parameter in fix call from the
script: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_name}}.  This parameter specifies the group of atoms
used in the fix. So we should compute the average for all particles in the
simulation only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_name == "all"}}, but it can be any group.
The group membership information of an atom is contained in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mask}
property of an atom and the bit corresponding to a given group is
stored in the groupbit variable which is defined in Fix base class:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nlocal}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{mask}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{groupbit}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// Do all job here}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Class Atom encapsulates atoms positions, velocities, forces, etc. Users
can access them using the particle index. Note, that particle indexes are
usually changed every few timesteps because of neighbor list rebuilds
and spatial sorting (to improve cache efficiency).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Let us consider another Fix example: We want to have a fix which stores
atoms position from the previous time step in your fix. The local atoms
indexes may not be valid on the next iteration. In order to handle
this situation there are several methods which should be implemented:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double memory\_usage()}}: return how much memory the fix uses (optional)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void grow\_arrays(int)}}: do reallocation of the per\sphinxhyphen{}particle arrays in your fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void copy\_arrays(int i, int j, int delflag)}}: copy i\sphinxhyphen{}th per\sphinxhyphen{}particle
information to j\sphinxhyphen{}th particle position. Used when atom sorting is performed.
if delflag is set and atom j owns a body, move the body information to atom i.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void set\_arrays(int i)}}: sets i\sphinxhyphen{}th particle related information to zero

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note, that if your class implements these methods, it must add calls of
add\_callback and delete\_callback to the constructor and destructor. Since we want
to store positions of atoms from the previous timestep, we need to add
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double** xold}} to the header file. Than add allocation code
to the constructor:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{FixSavePos}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{FixSavePos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{LAMMPS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{lmp}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{narg}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{nullptr}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{//...}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{FixSavePos:x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}callback}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{n}{FixSavePos}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{\PYGZti{}}\PYG{n}{FixSavePos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{delete\PYGZus{}callback}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{destroy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implement the aforementioned methods:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{FixSavePos::memory\PYGZus{}usage}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bytes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{bytes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bytes}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{FixSavePos::grow\PYGZus{}arrays}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memory}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{grow}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nmax}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{FixSavePos:xold}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{FixSavePos::copy\PYGZus{}arrays}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delflag}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memcpy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{FixSavePos::set\PYGZus{}arrays}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{memset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{xold}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Now, a little bit about memory allocation. We use the Memory class which
is just a bunch of template functions for allocating 1D and 2D
arrays. So you need to add include \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{memory.h}} to have access to them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finally, if you need to write/read some global information used in
your fix to the restart file, you might do it by setting the flag
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{restart\_global = 1}} in the constructor and implementing methods
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void write\_restart(FILE *fp)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void restart(char *buf)}}.
If, in addition, you want to write the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom property to restart
files then these additional settings and functions are needed:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a fix flag indicating this needs to be set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{restart\_peratom = 1;}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atom\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}add\_callback()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atom\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}delete\_callback()}} must be called
a second time with the final argument set to 1 instead of 0 (indicating
restart processing instead of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data memory management).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the functions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void pack\_restart(int i, double *buf)}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void unpack\_restart(int nlocal, int nth)}} need to be implemented

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\sphinxAtStartPar
This section documents how some of the code functionality within
LAMMPS works at a conceptual level.  Comments on code in source files
typically document what a variable stores, what a small section of
code does, or what a function does and its input/outputs.  The topics
on this page are intended to document code functionality at a higher level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Available topics are:

\item {}

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{Developer_notes:choosing-between-a-custom-atom-style-fix-property-atom-and-fix-store-atom}]{\sphinxcrossref{Choosing between a custom atom style, fix property/atom, and fix STORE/ATOM}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Developer_notes:fix-contributions-to-instantaneous-energy-virial-and-cumulative-energy}]{\sphinxcrossref{Fix contributions to instantaneous energy, virial, and cumulative energy}}}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{Developer_notes:kspace-pppm-fft-grids}]{\sphinxcrossref{KSpace PPPM FFT grids}}}
