\section{if command}
\label{\detokenize{if:if-command}}\label{\detokenize{if:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{if::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{if:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boolean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{elif}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boolean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{elif}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boolean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
boolean = a Boolean expression evaluated as TRUE or FALSE (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
then = required word

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
t1,t2,…,tN = one or more LAMMPS commands to execute if condition is met, each enclosed in quotes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
elif = optional word, can appear multiple times

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
f1,f2,…,fN = one or more LAMMPS commands to execute if elif condition is met, each enclosed in quotes (optional arguments)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
else = optional argument

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
e1,e2,…,eN = one or more LAMMPS commands to execute if no condition is met, each enclosed in quotes (optional arguments)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{if:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}steps\PYGZcb{} \PYGZgt{} 1000}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quit}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}myString\PYGZcb{} == a10}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quit}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}x \PYGZlt{}= \PYGZdl{}y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{print \PYGZsq{}X is smaller = \PYGZdl{}x\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{print \PYGZsq{}Y is smaller = \PYGZdl{}y\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{(\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}eng\PYGZcb{} \PYGZgt{} 0.0) || (\PYGZdl{}n \PYGZlt{} 1000)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{timestep 0.005}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{k}{elif}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}n}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{timestep 0.01}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{timestep 0.02}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{print \PYGZsq{}Max step reached\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}eng\PYGZcb{} \PYGZgt{} \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}eng\PYGZus{}previous\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{jump file1}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{jump file2}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{if:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command provides an if\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}else capability within an input
script.  A Boolean expression is evaluated and the result is TRUE or
FALSE.  Note that as in the examples above, the expression can contain
variables, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command, which
will be evaluated as part of the expression.  Thus a user\sphinxhyphen{}defined
formula that reflects the current state of the simulation can be used
to issue one or more new commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the result of the Boolean expression is TRUE, then one or more
commands (t1, t2, …, tN) are executed.  If it is FALSE, then Boolean
expressions associated with successive elif keywords are evaluated
until one is found to be true, in which case its commands (f1, f2,
…, fN) are executed.  If no Boolean expression is TRUE, then the
commands associated with the else keyword, namely (e1, e2, …, eN),
are executed.  The elif and else keywords and their associated
commands are optional.  If they are not specified and the initial
Boolean expression is FALSE, then no commands are executed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The syntax for Boolean expressions is described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each command (t1, f1, e1, etc.) can be any valid LAMMPS input script
command.  If the command is more than one word, it must enclosed in
quotes, so it will be treated as a single argument, as in the examples
above.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a command itself requires a quoted argument (e.g., a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{print::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{print}}}} command), then double and single quotes can be used
and nested in the usual manner, as in the examples above and below.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Commands parse}}}} page has more details on
using quotes in arguments.  Only one of level of nesting is allowed,
but that should be sufficient for most use cases.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that by using the line continuation character “\&”, the if command
can be spread across many lines, though it is still a single command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}a \PYGZlt{} \PYGZdl{}b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{print \PYGZsq{}Minimum value = \PYGZdl{}a\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{run 1000}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s}{print \PYGZdq{}Minimum value = \PYGZdl{}b\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{minimize 0.001 0.001 1000 10000}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if one of the commands to execute is {\hyperref[\detokenize{quit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{quit}}}}, as in
the first example above, then executing the command will cause LAMMPS
to halt.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that by jumping to a label in the same input script, the if
command can be used to break out of a loop.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable delete}}}} command for info on how to delete the associated
loop variable, so that it can be re\sphinxhyphen{}used later in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of a loop which checks every 1000 steps if the
system temperature has reached a certain value, and if so, breaks out
of the loop to finish the run.  Note that any variable could be
checked, so long as it is current on the timestep when the run
completes.  As explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} doc page,
this can be ensured by including the variable in thermodynamic output.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{label }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loop}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}myTemp\PYGZcb{} \PYGZlt{} 300.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{jump SELF break}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{next }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{SELF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}
\PYG{k}{label }\PYG{l+s+sc}{break}
\PYG{k}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ALL DONE}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of a double loop which uses the if and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{jump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{jump}}}} commands to break out of the inner loop when a
condition is met, then continues iterating through the outer loop.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{label       }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loopa}
\PYG{k}{variable    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{label     }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loopb}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{variable  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A,B = \PYGZdl{}a,\PYGZdl{}b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{l+m}{10000}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}b \PYGZgt{} 2}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{jump SELF break}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{next      }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{jump      }\PYG{l+s+sc}{in.script}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loopb}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{label       }\PYG{l+s+sc}{break}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{variable    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delete}
\PYG{k}{next        }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}
\PYG{k}{jump        }\PYG{l+s+sc}{SELF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loopa}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The Boolean expressions for the if and elif keywords have a C\sphinxhyphen{}like
syntax.  Note that each expression is a single argument within the if
command.  Thus if you want to include spaces in the expression for
clarity, you must enclose the entire expression in quotes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An expression is built out of numbers (which start with a digit or
period or minus sign) or strings (which start with a letter and can
contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, or forward slashes):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0.2, 100, 1.0e20, \PYGZhy{}15.4, ...
InP, myString, a123, ab\PYGZus{}23\PYGZus{}cd, lj/cut, ...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and Boolean operators:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
A == B, A != B, A \textless{} B, A \textless{}= B, A \textgreater{} B, A \textgreater{}= B, A \&\& B, A || B, A |\textasciicircum{} B, !A
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each A and B is a number or string or a variable reference like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$a}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$\{abc\}}}, or A or B can be another Boolean expression.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that all variables used will be substituted for before the
Boolean expression in evaluated.  A variable can produce a number,
like an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}}, or it can produce a
string, like an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{index\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Boolean operators \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{==}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}} can operate on a pair or strings
or numbers.  They cannot compare a number to a string.  All the other
Boolean operations can only operate on numbers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Expressions are evaluated left to right and have the usual C\sphinxhyphen{}style
precedence: the unary logical NOT operator \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!}} has the highest
precedence, the 4 relational operators \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}} are
next; the two remaining relational operators \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{==}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}} are next;
then the logical AND operator \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&\&}}; and finally the logical OR
operator \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{||}} and logical XOR (exclusive or) operator \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|\textasciicircum{}}} have
the lowest precedence.  Parenthesis can be used to group one or more
portions of an expression and/or enforce a different order of
evaluation than what would occur with the default precedence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the six relational operators (first six in list above) compare two
numbers, they return either a 1.0 or 0.0 depending on whether the
relationship between A and B is TRUE or FALSE.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the three logical operators (last three in list above) compare two numbers,
they also return either a 1.0 or 0.0 depending on whether the
relationship between A and B is TRUE or FALSE (or just A).  The
logical AND operator will return 1.0 if both its arguments are
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, else it returns 0.0.  The logical OR operator will return
1.0 if either of its arguments is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, else it returns 0.0.  The
logical XOR operator will return 1.0 if one of its arguments is zero
and the other non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, else it returns 0.0.  The logical NOT operator
returns 1.0 if its argument is 0.0, else it returns 0.0.  The 3
logical operators can only be used to operate on numbers, not on
strings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The overall Boolean expression produces a TRUE result if the numeric
result is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero.  If the result is zero, the expression result is
FALSE.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the Boolean expression is a single numeric value with no Boolean
operators, it will be FALSE if the value = 0.0, otherwise TRUE.  If
the Boolean expression is a single string, an error message will be
issued.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{improper\_coeff@\spxentry{improper\_coeff}}\ignorespaces 

\section{improper\_coeff command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:improper-coeff-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = numeric improper type (see asterisk form below), or type label

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = coefficients for one or more improper types

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{improper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{benzene}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{benzene}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the improper force field coefficients for one or more improper
types.  The number and meaning of the coefficients depends on the
improper style.  Improper coefficients can also be set in the data file
read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command or in a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N\) can be specified in one of two ways.  An explicit numeric
value can be used, as in the first example above.  Or \(N\) can be a
type label, which is an alphanumeric string defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} command or in a section of a data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For numeric values only, a wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used to set the
coefficients for multiple improper types.  This takes the form “*” or
“*n” or “n*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) = the number of improper types,
then an asterisk with no numeric values means all types from 1 to
\(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from 1 to n (inclusive).
A trailing asterisk means all types from n to \(N\) (inclusive).  A
middle asterisk means all types from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that using an improper\_coeff command can override a previous
setting for the same improper type.  For example, these commands set the
coeffs for all improper types, then overwrite the coeffs for just
improper type 2:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A line in a data file that specifies improper coefficients uses the
exact same format as the arguments of the improper\_coeff command in an
input script, except that wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisks should not be used since
coefficients for all \(N\) types must be listed in the file.  For
example, under the “Improper Coeffs” section of a data file, the line
that corresponds to the first example above would be listed as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
1 300.0 0.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_class2::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_style class2}}}} is an exception to
this rule, in that an additional argument is used in the input script
to allow specification of the cross\sphinxhyphen{}term coefficients.  See its doc
page for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The list of all improper styles defined in LAMMPS is given on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_style}}}} doc page.  They are also listed
in more compact form on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_bond:improper}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Commands improper}}}} doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On either of those pages, click on the style to display the formula it
computes and its coefficients as specified by the associated
improper\_coeff command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command must come after the simulation box is defined by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An improper style must be defined before any improper coefficients are
set, either in the input script or in a data file.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_style}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{improper_coeff:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{improper\_style@\spxentry{improper\_style}}\ignorespaces 

\section{improper\_style command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_style:improper-style-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_style:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_style::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_style:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvff} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_style:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvff}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_style:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the formula(s) LAMMPS uses to compute improper interactions
between quadruplets of atoms, which remain in force for the duration
of the simulation.  The list of improper quadruplets is read in by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command
from a data or restart file.  Note that the ordering of the 4 atoms in
an improper quadruplet determines the definition of the improper
angle used in the formula for each style.  See the doc pages of
individual styles for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Hybrid models where impropers are computed using different improper
potentials can be setup using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} improper style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients associated with an improper style can be specified in
a data or restart file or via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All improper potentials store their coefficient data in binary restart
files which means improper\_style and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} commands do not need to be
re\sphinxhyphen{}specified in an input script that restarts a simulation.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for details on how to do
this.  The one exception is that improper\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} only stores
the list of sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles in the restart file; improper coefficients need
to be re\sphinxhyphen{}specified.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When both an improper and pair style is defined, the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command often needs to be used to
turn off (or weight) the pairwise interaction that would otherwise
exist between a group of 4 bonded atoms.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an alphabetic list of improper styles defined in LAMMPS.
Click on the style to display the formula it computes and coefficients
specified by the associated {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Click on the style to display the formula it computes, any additional
arguments specified in the improper\_style command, and coefficients
specified by the associated {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are also additional accelerated pair styles included in the
LAMMPS distribution for faster performance on CPUs, GPUs, and KNLs.
The individual style names on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_bond:improper}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Commands improper}}}} page are followed by one or
more of (g,i,k,o,t) to indicate which accelerated styles exist.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_none::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{none}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} turn off improper interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{zero}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} topology but no interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} define multiple styles of improper interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{amoeba}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} AMOEBA out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane improper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_class2::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{class2}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} COMPASS (class 2) improper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_cossq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{cossq}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} improper with a cosine squared term

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_cvff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{cvff}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} CVFF improper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_distance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{distance}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} improper based on distance between atom planes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_distharm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{distharm}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} improper that is harmonic in the out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane distance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_fourier::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fourier}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} improper with multiple cosine terms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{harmonic}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} harmonic improper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{inversion/harmonic}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} harmonic improper with Wilson\sphinxhyphen{}Decius out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane definition

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_ring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ring}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} improper which prevents planar conformations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_umbrella::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{umbrella}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} DREIDING improper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{sqdistharm}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} improper that is harmonic in the square of the out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane distance

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_style:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Improper styles can only be set for atom\_style choices that allow
impropers to be defined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most improper styles are part of the MOLECULE package.  They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.  The doc pages for
individual improper potentials tell if it is part of a package.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}}

\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{include:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command opens a new input script file and begins reading LAMMPS
commands from that file.  When the new file is finished, the original
file is returned to.  Include files can be nested as deeply as
desired.  If input script A includes script B, and B includes A, then
LAMMPS could run for a long time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the filename is a variable (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}
command), different processor partitions can run different input
scripts.

\label{\detokenize{include:restrictions}}

none

\index{info@\spxentry{info}}\ignorespaces 

\section{info command}
\label{\detokenize{info:info-command}}\label{\detokenize{info:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{info::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{info:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = one or more of the following keywords: \sphinxstyleemphasis{out}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{system}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{memory}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{communication}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{computes}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dumps}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixes}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{groups}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{regions}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{variables}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{coeffs}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{styles}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{time}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{accelerator}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fft} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{configuration}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{out} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{screen}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{log}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} filename, \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{styles} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{compute}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{command}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dump}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{improper}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrate}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{minimize}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{info:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{system}
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{groups}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{computes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{variables}
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{log}
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{info.txt}
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{styles}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}
\PYG{k}{info}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{styles}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{styles}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{command}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{info:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Print out information about the current internal state of the running
LAMMPS process. This can be helpful when debugging or validating complex
input scripts.  Several output categories are available and one or more
output categories may be requested.  All category keywords take no
arguments, only \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{styles} take arguments as shown below.  The
keywords are cumulative, may be abbreviated, and unknown keywords are
ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} flag controls where the output is sent. It can only be sent
to one target. By default this is the screen, if it is active. The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{log} argument selects the log file instead. With the \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} option, followed by a filename, the output is written
to that file, which is either appended to or overwritten, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} flag activates printing all categories listed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{configuration} category prints some information about the
LAMMPS version as well as architecture and OS it is run on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{memory} category prints some information about the current
memory allocation of MPI rank 0 (this the amount of dynamically
allocated memory reported by LAMMPS classes). Where supported,
also some OS specific information about the size of the reserved
memory pool size (this is where malloc() and the new operator
request memory from) and the maximum resident set size is reported
(this is the maximum amount of physical memory occupied so far).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{system} category prints a general system overview listing.  This
includes the unit style, atom style, number of atoms, bonds, angles,
dihedrals, and impropers and the number of the respective types, box
dimensions and properties, force computing styles and more.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{communication} category prints a variety of information about
communication and parallelization: the MPI library version level,
the number of MPI ranks and OpenMP threads, the communication style
and layout, the processor grid dimensions, ghost atom communication
mode, cutoff, and related settings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{computes} category prints a list of all currently defined
computes, their IDs and styles and groups they operate on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dumps} category prints a list of all currently active dumps,
their IDs, styles, filenames, groups, and dump frequencies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixes} category prints a list of all currently defined fixes,
their IDs and styles and groups they operate on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{groups} category prints a list of all currently defined groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{regions} category prints a list of all currently defined regions,
their IDs and styles and whether “inside” or “outside” atoms are
selected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{variables} category prints a list of all currently defined
variables, their names, styles, definition and last computed value, if
available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coeffs} category prints a list for each defined force style
(pair, bond, angle, dihedral, improper) indicating which of the
corresponding coefficients have been set. This can be very helpful
to debug error messages like “All pair coeffs are not set”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{accelerator} category prints out information about compile time
settings of included accelerator support for the GPU, KOKKOS, INTEL,
and OPENMP packages.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fft} category prints out information about the included 3d\sphinxhyphen{}FFT
support.  This lists the 3d\sphinxhyphen{}FFT engine, FFT precision, FFT library
used by the FFT engine. If the KOKKOS package is included, the settings
used for the KOKKOS package are displayed as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{styles} category prints the list of styles available in the current
LAMMPS binary. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{styles} keyword without option is the same as using
the “all” option.  One of the following options may be used to control
which category of styles is printed out.  To select multiple categories,
the styles keyword needs to be used multiple times with the desired
categories:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
all

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
angle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
compute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dihedral

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
improper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
integrate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kspace

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
minimize

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{time} category prints the accumulated CPU and wall time for the
process that writes output (usually MPI rank 0).


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{info:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{info:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{print::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{print}}}}

\section{jump command}
\label{\detokenize{jump:jump-command}}\label{\detokenize{jump:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{jump::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}

\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{label}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{jump:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{newfile}
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{in.run2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{runloop}
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{SELF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{runloop}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{jump:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command closes the current input script file, opens the file with
the specified name, and begins reading LAMMPS commands from that file.
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{include::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{include}}}} command, the original file is not
returned to, although by using multiple jump commands it is possible
to chain from file to file or back to the original file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the word “SELF” is used for the filename, then the current input
script is re\sphinxhyphen{}opened and read again.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The SELF option is not guaranteed to work when the current input
script is being read through stdin (standard input), e.g.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
lmp\PYGZus{}g++\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.script
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
since the SELF option invokes the C\sphinxhyphen{}library rewind() call, which may
not be supported for stdin on some systems or by some MPI
implementations.  This can be worked around by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}in command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}}, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
lmp\PYGZus{}g++\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.script
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
or by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}var command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} to pass
the script name as a variable to the input script.  In the latter
case, a {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} called “fname” could be used in place
of SELF, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
lmp\PYGZus{}g++\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}var\PYG{+w}{ }fname\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.script\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{in}.script
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second argument to the jump command is optional.  If specified, it is
treated as a label and the new file is scanned (without executing
commands) until the label is found, and commands are executed from
that point forward.  This can be used to loop over a portion of the
input script, as in this example.  These commands perform 10 runs,
each of 10000 steps, and create 10 dump files named file.1, file.2,
etc.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{next::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{next}}}} command is used to exit the loop after 10
iterations.  When the “a” variable has been incremented for the tenth
time, it will cause the next jump command to be skipped.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{label }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loop}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file.}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}a}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}
\PYG{k}{undump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}
\PYG{k}{next }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{in.lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the jump \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} argument is a variable, the jump command can be
used to cause different processor partitions to run different input
scripts.  In this example, LAMMPS is run on 40 processors, with 4
partitions of 10 procs each.  An in.file containing the example
variable and jump command will cause each partition to run a different
simulation.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mpirun}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{40}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp\PYGZus{}ibm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{n}{x10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{in.file}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{world}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{script.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{script.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{script.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{script.4}
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}f}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of a loop which checks every 1000 steps if the
system temperature has reached a certain value, and if so, breaks out
of the loop to finish the run.  Note that any variable could be
checked, so long as it is current on the timestep when the run
completes.  As explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} doc page,
this can be ensured by including the variable in thermodynamic output.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{label }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loop}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}myTemp\PYGZcb{} \PYGZlt{} 300.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{jump SELF break}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{next }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}
\PYG{k}{jump }\PYG{l+s+sc}{SELF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}
\PYG{k}{label }\PYG{l+s+sc}{break}
\PYG{k}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ALL DONE}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of a double loop which uses the if and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{jump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{jump}}}} commands to break out of the inner loop when a
condition is met, then continues iterating through the outer loop.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{label       }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loopa}
\PYG{k}{variable    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{label     }\PYG{l+s+sc}{loopb}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{variable  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A,B = \PYGZdl{}a,\PYGZdl{}b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{l+m}{10000}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}b \PYGZgt{} 2}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{jump SELF break}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{next      }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{jump      }\PYG{l+s+sc}{in.script}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loopb}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{label       }\PYG{l+s+sc}{break}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{variable    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delete}
\PYG{k}{next        }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}
\PYG{k}{jump        }\PYG{l+s+sc}{SELF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{loopa}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{jump:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you jump to a file and it does not contain the specified label,
LAMMPS will come to the end of the file and exit.

\label{\detokenize{jump:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{include::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{include}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{label}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{next::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{next}}}}

none

\section{kim command}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:kim-command}}\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{sub\PYGZhy{}command}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

{\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands:query}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{query}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands:param}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{param}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands:property}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{property}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = arguments used by a particular sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim command} includes a set of sub\sphinxhyphen{}commands that allow LAMMPS
users to use interatomic models (IM) (potentials and force fields) and
their predictions for various physical properties archived in the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org}{Open Knowledgebase of Interatomic Models (OpenKIM)} repository.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using OpenKIM provides LAMMPS users with immediate access to a large
number of verified IMs and their predictions. OpenKIM IMs have
multiple benefits including \sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/overview/kim-features/}{reliability, reproducibility and
convenience}.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:im-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are two types of IMs archived in OpenKIM:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The first type is called a \sphinxstyleemphasis{KIM Portable Model} (PM).  A KIM PM is an
independent computer implementation of an IM written in one of the languages
supported by KIM (C, C++, Fortran) that conforms to the KIM Application
Programming Interface (\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/kim-api/}{KIM API}) Portable
Model Interface (PMI) standard.  A KIM PM will work seamlessly with any
simulation code that supports the KIM API/PMI standard (including LAMMPS; see
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/projects-using-kim/}{complete list of supported codes}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second type is called a \sphinxstyleemphasis{KIM Simulator Model} (SM).  A KIM SM is an IM
that is implemented natively within a simulation code (\sphinxstyleemphasis{simulator}) that
supports the KIM API Simulator Model Interface (SMI); in this case LAMMPS.  A
separate SM package is archived in OpenKIM for each parameterization of the
IM, which includes all of the necessary parameter files, LAMMPS commands, and
metadata (supported species, units, etc.) needed to run the IM in LAMMPS.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With these two IM types, OpenKIM can archive and test almost all IMs that can be
used by LAMMPS. (It is easy to contribute new IMs to OpenKIM, see the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/repository/adding-content/}{upload instructions}.)

\sphinxAtStartPar
OpenKIM IMs are uniquely identified by a
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/schema/kim-ids/}{KIM ID}.
The extended KIM ID consists of
a human\sphinxhyphen{}readable prefix identifying the type of IM, authors, publication year,
and supported species, separated by two underscores from the KIM ID itself,
which begins with an IM code
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{MO} for a KIM Portable Model, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{SM} for a KIM Simulator Model)
followed by a unique 12\sphinxhyphen{}digit code and a 3\sphinxhyphen{}digit version identifier.
By convention SM prefixes begin with \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sim\_} to readily identify them.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
SW\PYGZus{}StillingerWeber\PYGZus{}1985\PYGZus{}Si\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}405512056662\PYGZus{}005
Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}ReaxFF\PYGZus{}StrachanVanDuinChakraborty\PYGZus{}2003\PYGZus{}CHNO\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}107643900657\PYGZus{}001
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each OpenKIM IM has a dedicated “Model Page” on \sphinxhref{https://openkim.org}{OpenKIM}
providing all the information on the IM including a title, description,
authorship and citation information, test and verification check results,
visualizations of results, a wiki with documentation and user comments, and
access to raw files, and other information.
The URL for the Model Page is constructed from the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/schema/kim-ids/}{extended KIM ID} of the IM:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
https://openkim.org/id/extended\PYGZus{}KIM\PYGZus{}ID
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, for the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential listed above the Model Page is
located at:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxurl{https://openkim.org/id/SW\_StillingerWeber\_1985\_Si\_\_MO\_405512056662\_005}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/browse/models/by-species}{current list of KIM PMs and SMs archived in OpenKIM}.
This list is sorted by species and can be filtered to display only IMs for
certain species combinations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/usage/obtaining-models}{Obtaining KIM Models} to
learn how to install a pre\sphinxhyphen{}built binary of the OpenKIM Repository of Models.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is also possible to locally install IMs not archived in OpenKIM,
in which case their names do not have to conform to the KIM ID format.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Using OpenKIM IMs with LAMMPS (\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions})}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:using-openkim-ims-with-lammps-kim-init-kim-interactions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two sub\sphinxhyphen{}commands are employed when using OpenKIM IMs in LAMMPS, one to select
the IM and perform necessary initialization (\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init}), and the second to
set up the IM for use by executing any necessary LAMMPS commands
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions}).  Both are required.


\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unitarg}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{typeargs}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:typeargs-options}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
model = name of the KIM interatomic model (the KIM ID for models archived in
OpenKIM)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
user\_units = the LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} style assumed in the LAMMPS
input script

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
unitarg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{unit\_conversion\_mode} (optional)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
typeargs = atom type to species mapping (one entry per atom type) or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fixed\_types} for models with a preset fixed mapping

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SW\PYGZus{}StillingerWeber\PYGZus{}1985\PYGZus{}Si\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}405512056662\PYGZus{}005}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{metal}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}

\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}ReaxFF\PYGZus{}StrachanVanDuinChakraborty\PYGZus{}2003\PYGZus{}CHNO\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}107643900657\PYGZus{}001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{real}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}ReaxFF\PYGZus{}StrachanVanDuinChakraborty\PYGZus{}2003\PYGZus{}CHNO\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}107643900657\PYGZus{}001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{metal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unit\PYGZus{}conversion\PYGZus{}mode}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}

\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}IFF\PYGZus{}PCFF\PYGZus{}HeinzMishraLinEmami\PYGZus{}2015Ver1v5\PYGZus{}FccmetalsMineralsSolventsPolymers\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}039297821658\PYGZus{}000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{real}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixed\PYGZus{}types}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxstyleemphasis{examples/kim} directory for example input scripts that use KIM PMs
and KIM SMs.


\subsubsection{OpenKIM IM Initialization (\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init})}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:openkim-im-initialization-kim-init}}\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:kim-init}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim} command followed by \sphinxstyleemphasis{init} sub\sphinxhyphen{}command must be issued \sphinxstylestrong{before}
the simulation box is created (normally at the top of the file).  This command
sets the OpenKIM IM that will be used and may issue additional commands changing
LAMMPS default settings that are required for using the selected IM (such as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}).  If needed, those
settings can be overridden, however, typically a script containing a \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init}
command would not include \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The required arguments of \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} are the \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} name of the IM to be used
in the simulation (for an IM archived in OpenKIM this is its
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/schema/kim-ids/}{extended KIM ID}, and the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{user\_units}, which are the LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units style}}}} used in the input
script. (Any dimensioned numerical values in the input script and values read in
from files are expected to be in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{user\_units} system.)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The selected IM can be either a {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands:im-types}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{KIM PM or a KIM SM}}}}.  For a KIM
SM, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} command verifies that the SM is designed to work with LAMMPS
(and not another simulation code).  In addition, the LAMMPS version used for
defining the SM and the LAMMPS version being currently run are printed to help
diagnose any incompatible changes to input script or command syntax between the
two LAMMPS versions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Based on the selected model \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} may modify the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}.  Some SMs have requirements for this setting.
If this is the case, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style} will be set to the required style.
Otherwise, the value is left unchanged (which in the absence of an \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style}
command in the input script is the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{default atom\_style value}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regarding units, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} behaves in different ways depending on whether
or not \sphinxstyleemphasis{unit conversion mode} is activated as indicated by the optional
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unitarg} argument.
If unit conversion mode is \sphinxstylestrong{not} active, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{user\_units} must either match
the required units of the IM or the IM must be able to adjust its units to
match. (The latter is only possible with some KIM PMs; SMs can never adjust
their units.) If a match is possible, the LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command is
called to set the units to \sphinxstyleemphasis{user\_units}.  If the match fails, the simulation
is terminated with an error.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} command also sets the
default value for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{skin}}}} (extra distance beyond force
cutoff) as 2.0 Angstroms and sets the default value for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}} size as 1.0 femtosecond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of a LAMMPS script to compute the cohesive energy of a
face\sphinxhyphen{}centered cubic (fcc) lattice for the MEAM potential by Pascuet and
Fernandez (2015) for Al.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim          }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}MEAM\PYGZus{}PascuetFernandez\PYGZus{}2015\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}811588957187\PYGZus{}000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{metal}
\PYG{k}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}
\PYG{k}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.049}
\PYG{k}{region       }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{simbox}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\PYG{k}{create\PYGZus{}box   }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{simbox}
\PYG{k}{create\PYGZus{}atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{26.981539}
\PYG{k}{kim          }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{variable     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Ec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{pe/count}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{all}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{print}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Cohesive Energy = \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}Ec\PYGZcb{} eV}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The above script will end with an error in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} line if the IM is
changed to another potential for Al that does not work with \sphinxstyleemphasis{metal} units.  To
address this, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} offers the \sphinxstyleemphasis{unit\_conversion\_mode} as shown below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If unit conversion mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{is} active, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} calls the LAMMPS
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command to set the units to the IM’s required or preferred
units.  Conversion factors between the IM’s units and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{user\_units} are
defined for all {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{physical quantities}}}} (mass, distance, etc.).
(Note that converting to or from the “lj” unit style is not supported.)
These factors are stored as {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{internal style variables}}}} with the
following standard names:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}mass
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}time
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}energy
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}velocity
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}force
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}torque
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}temperature
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}pressure
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}viscosity
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}charge
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}dipole
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}efield
\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}density
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If desired, the input script can be designed to work with these conversion
factors so that the script will work without change with any OpenKIM IM.
(This approach is used in the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/evaluation/kim-tests/}{OpenKIM Testing Framework}.)

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, the script given above for the cohesive energy of fcc Al can be
rewritten to work with any IM regardless of units.  The following script
constructs an fcc lattice with a lattice parameter defined in meters, computes
the total energy, and prints the cohesive energy in Joules regardless of the
units of the IM.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim          }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}MEAM\PYGZus{}PascuetFernandez\PYGZus{}2015\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}811588957187\PYGZus{}000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unit\PYGZus{}conversion\PYGZus{}mode}
\PYG{k}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}
\PYG{k}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{4.049e\PYGZhy{}10*v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{region       }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{simbox}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\PYG{k}{create\PYGZus{}box   }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{simbox}
\PYG{k}{create\PYGZus{}atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{4.480134e\PYGZhy{}26*v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}mass}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{kim          }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}
\PYG{k}{neighbor}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{2e\PYGZhy{}10*v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bin}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{variable     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Ec\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}J}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{pe/count}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{all}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}energy}
\PYG{k}{print}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Cohesive Energy = \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}Ec\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}J\PYGZcb{} J}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note the multiplication by \sphinxtitleref{v\_\_u\_distance} and \sphinxtitleref{v\_\_u\_mass} to convert from SI
units (specified in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} command) to whatever units the IM uses (metal
in this case), and the division by \sphinxtitleref{v\_\_u\_energy} to convert from the IM’s energy
units to SI units (Joule).  This script will work correctly for any IM for Al
(KIM PM or SM) selected by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Care must be taken to apply unit conversion to dimensional variables read in
from a file.  For example, if a configuration of atoms is read in from a dump
file using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_dump}}}} command, the following can be done
to convert the box and all atomic positions to the correct units:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{change\PYGZus{}box }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{xy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{final}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{xy*v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{xz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{final}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{xz*v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{yz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{final}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{yz*v\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}u\PYGZus{}distance}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{n}{remap}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unit conversion will only work if the conversion factors are placed in all
appropriate places in the input script.  It is up to the user to do this
correctly.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{OpenKIM IM Execution (\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions})}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:openkim-im-execution-kim-interactions}}\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:interactions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second and final step in using an OpenKIM IM is to execute the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} command.  This command must be preceded by a \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init}
command and a command that defines the number of atom types \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} (such as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}).
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} command has one argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{typeargs}.  This argument
contains either a list of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} chemical species, which defines a mapping between
atom types in LAMMPS to the available species in the OpenKIM IM, or the keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fixed\_types} for models that have a preset fixed mapping (i.e.  the mapping
between LAMMPS atom types and chemical species is defined by the model and
cannot be changed).  In the latter case, the user must consult the model
documentation to see how many atom types there are and how they map to the
chemical species.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, consider an OpenKIM IM that supports Si and C species.  If the
LAMMPS simulation has four atom types, where the first three are Si, and the
fourth is C, the following \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} command would be used:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, for a model with a fixed mapping the command would be:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixed\PYGZus{}types}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} command performs all the necessary steps to set up the
OpenKIM IM selected in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} command.  The specific actions depend on
whether the IM is a KIM PM or a KIM SM.  For a KIM PM, a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kim::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style kim}}}} command is executed followed by the appropriate
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command.  For example, for the Ercolessi and Adams (1994) KIM PM
for Al set by the following commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EAM\PYGZus{}Dynamo\PYGZus{}ErcolessiAdams\PYGZus{}1994\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}123629422045\PYGZus{}005}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{metal}
\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{specification}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipped}
\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} command executes the following LAMMPS input commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{EAM\PYGZus{}Dynamo\PYGZus{}ErcolessiAdams\PYGZus{}1994\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}123629422045\PYGZus{}005}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a KIM SM, the generated input commands may be more complex and require that
LAMMPS is built with the required packages included for the type of potential
being used.  The set of commands to be executed is defined in the SM
specification file, which is part of the SM package.  For example, for the
Strachan et al.  (2003) ReaxFF SM set by the following commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sim\PYGZus{}LAMMPS\PYGZus{}ReaxFF\PYGZus{}StrachanVanDuinChakraborty\PYGZus{}2003\PYGZus{}CHNO\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}SM\PYGZus{}107643900657\PYGZus{}000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{real}
\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{specification}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipped}
\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{interactions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} command executes the following LAMMPS input commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lmp\PYGZus{}control}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{safezone}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mincap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ffield.reax.rdx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{reaxqeq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{param.qeq}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The files \sphinxstyleemphasis{lmp\_control}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.reax.rdx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{param.qeq} are specific to
the Strachan et al.  (2003) ReaxFF parameterization and are archived as part
of the SM package in OpenKIM.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters like cutoff radii and charge tolerances, which have an effect on
IM predictions, are also included in the SM definition ensuring
reproducibility.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} to select and set up an OpenKIM
IM, other LAMMPS commands for the same functions (such as pair\_style,
pair\_coeff, bond\_style, bond\_coeff, fixes related to charge equilibration,
etc.) should normally not appear in the input script.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} must be called each time after the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{change_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{change\_box}}}} command to provide the correct settings (it
should be called with the same {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands:typeargs-options}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{typeargs}}}} as the
first call.)  The reason is that changing a periodic boundary to a
non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic one, or in general, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{change\_box} command after the
interactions are set via \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} commands might
affect some of the settings.  For example, SM models containing Coulombic
terms in the interactions require different settings if a periodic boundary
changes to a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic one.  In other cases, the second call to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} does not affect any other settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Using OpenKIM Web Queries in LAMMPS (\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query})}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:using-openkim-web-queries-in-lammps-kim-query}}\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:query}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} command performs a web query to retrieve the predictions of an
IM set by \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} for material properties archived in
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org}{OpenKIM}.


\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:id5}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{query}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{formatarg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{query\PYGZus{}function}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{queryargs}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
variable(s) = single name or list of names of (string style) LAMMPS
variable(s) where a query result or parameter get result is stored.  Variables
that do not exist will be created by the command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
formatarg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{list} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{split} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{index} (optional)
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{list} = returns a single string with a list of space separated values
       (e.g. "1.0 2.0 3.0"), which is placed in a LAMMPS variable as
       defined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} argument. {[}default{]}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{split} = returns the values separately in new variables with names based
       on the prefix specified in \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} and a number appended to
       indicate which element in the list of values is in the variable
\sphinxstyleemphasis{index} = returns a variable style index that can be incremented via the
       next command.  This enables the construction of simple loops
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
query\_function = name of the OpenKIM web API query function to be used

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
queryargs = a series of \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword=value} pairs that represent the web query;
supported keywords depend on the query function

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:id6}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{query}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}lattice\PYGZus{}constant\PYGZus{}cubic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{crystal}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[fcc]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{species}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[Al]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[angstrom]}
\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{query}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}available\PYGZus{}models}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{species}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[Al]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{potential\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[eam]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result of the query is stored in one or more
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{string style variables}}}} as determined by the optional
\sphinxstyleemphasis{formatarg} argument.  For the “list”
setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{formatarg} (or if \sphinxstyleemphasis{formatarg} is not specified), the result is
returned as a space\sphinxhyphen{}separated list of values in \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{formatarg}
keyword “split” separates the result values into individual variables of the
form \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix\_I}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix} is set to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} argument
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{I} ranges from 1 to the number of returned values.  The number and order of
the returned values is determined by the type of query performed.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{formatarg} keyword “index” returns a {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable style index}}}}
that can be incremented via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{next::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{next}}}} command.  This enables the
construction of simple loops over the returned values by the type of query
performed.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} only supports queries that return a single result or an array of
values.  More complex queries that return a JSON structure are not currently
supported.  An attempt to use \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} in such cases will generate an
error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second required argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{query\_function} is the name of the query function
to be called (e.g.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{get\_lattice\_constant\_cubic}).  All following
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{arguments}}}} are parameters handed over to the web query in
the format \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword=value}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{value} is always an array of one or more
comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated items in brackets.  The list of supported keywords and the type
and format of their values depend on the query function used.  The current list
of query functions is available on the OpenKIM webpage at
\sphinxurl{https://openkim.org/doc/usage/kim-query}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All query functions, except \sphinxstyleemphasis{get\_available\_models}, require the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword, which identifies the IM whose predictions are being queried.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} automatically generates the \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword based on the IM set
in by \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init}, and it can be overwritten if specified as an argument to
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query}.  Where \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim init} is not specified, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword
must be provided as an argument to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each \sphinxstyleemphasis{query\_function} is associated with a default method (implemented as a
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/evaluation/kim-tests/}{KIM Test}) used to compute
this property.  In cases where there are multiple methods in OpenKIM for
computing a property, a \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} keyword can be provided to select the method
of choice.  See the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org/doc/usage/kim-query}{query documentation} to see which
methods are available for a given \sphinxstyleemphasis{query\_function}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{\sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} Usage Examples and Further Clarifications}
\label{\detokenize{kim_commands:kim-query-usage-examples-and-further-clarifications}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The data obtained by \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} commands can be used as part of the setup or
analysis phases of LAMMPS simulations.  Some examples are given below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Define an equilibrium fcc crystal}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{kim      }\PYG{l+s+s1}{init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EAM\PYGZus{}Dynamo\PYGZus{}ErcolessiAdams\PYGZus{}1994\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}123629422045\PYGZus{}005}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{metal}
\PYG{k}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}
\PYG{k}{kim      }\PYG{l+s+s1}{query}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}lattice\PYGZus{}constant\PYGZus{}cubic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{crystal}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[fcc]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{species}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[Al]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[angstrom]}
\PYG{k}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{a0}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{units}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{metal}
\PYG{k}{kim     }\PYG{l+s+s1}{query}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}lattice\PYGZus{}constant\PYGZus{}cubic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{crystal}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[fcc]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{species}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[Al]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[angstrom]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{[EAM\PYGZus{}Dynamo\PYGZus{}ErcolessiAdams\PYGZus{}1994\PYGZus{}Al\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}123629422045\PYGZus{}005]}
\PYG{k}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{a0}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query} command retrieves from \sphinxhref{https://openkim.org}{OpenKIM} the
equilibrium lattice constant predicted by the Ercolessi and Adams (1994)
potential for the fcc structure and places it in variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{a0}.  This variable
is then used on the next line to set up the crystal.  By using \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim query}, the
user is saved the trouble and possible error of tracking this value down, or of
having to perform an energy minimization to find the equilibrium lattice
constant.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
