\index{log@\spxentry{log}}\ignorespaces 

\section{log command}
\label{\detokenize{log:log-command}}\label{\detokenize{log:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{log::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{log:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{log}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of new logfile

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} if output should be appended to logfile (optional)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{log:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{log}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{log.equil}
\PYG{k}{log}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{log.equil}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{log:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command closes the current LAMMPS log file, opens a new file with
the specified name, and begins logging information to it.  If the
specified file name is \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}, then no new log file is opened.  If the
optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} is specified, then output will be appended
to an existing log file, instead of overwriting it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If multiple processor partitions are being used, the file name should
be a variable, so that different processors do not attempt to write to
the same log file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The file “log.lammps” is the default log file for a LAMMPS run.  The
name of the initial log file can also be set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}log command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{log:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{log:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{log:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default LAMMPS log file is named log.lammps

\index{mass@\spxentry{mass}}\ignorespaces 

\section{mass command}
\label{\detokenize{mass:mass-command}}\label{\detokenize{mass:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{mass::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{mass:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{I}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
I = atom type (see asterisk form below), or type label

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = mass

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{mass:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{62.5}
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{62.5}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\PYG{k}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.01}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{mass:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the mass for all atoms of one or more atom types.  Per\sphinxhyphen{}type mass
values can also be set in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} data file
using the “Masses” keyword.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for
what mass units to use.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The I index can be specified in one of several ways.  An explicit
numeric value can be used, as in the first example above.  Or I can be
a type label, which is an alphanumeric string defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} command or in a section of a data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, and which converts
internally to a numeric type. Or a wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used to
set the mass for multiple atom types.  This takes the form “*” or
“*n” or “n*” or “m*n”, where m and n are numbers.  If N = the
number of atom types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means
all types from 1 to N.  A leading asterisk means all types from 1 to n
(inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from n to N
(inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
A line in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data file}}}} that follows the “Masses”
keyword specifies mass using the same format as the arguments of the
mass command in an input script, except that no wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can
be used.  For example, under the “Masses” section of a data file, the
line that corresponds to the first example above would be listed as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
1 1.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the mass command can only be used if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} requires per\sphinxhyphen{}type atom mass to be set.
Currently, all but the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ellipsoid} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri} styles do.
They require mass to be set for individual particles, not types.
Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses are defined in the data file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, or set to default values by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command.  Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses can also be
set to new values by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set mass}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set density}}}}
commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style eam}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style bop}}}} commands define the masses of atom types in their
respective potential files, in which case the mass command is normally
not used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you define a {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid atom style}}}} which includes one
(or more) sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles which require per\sphinxhyphen{}type mass and one (or more)
sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles which require per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mass, then you must define both.
However, in this case the per\sphinxhyphen{}type mass will be ignored; only the
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mass will be used by LAMMPS.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{mass:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command must come after the simulation box is defined by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All masses must be defined before a simulation is run.  They must also
all be defined before a {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The mass assigned to any type or atom must be \textgreater{} 0.0.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{mass:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{mass:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{mdi@\spxentry{mdi}}\ignorespaces 

\section{mdi command}
\label{\detokenize{mdi:mdi-command}}\label{\detokenize{mdi:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{mdi::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{mdi:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{option}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
option = \sphinxstyleemphasis{engine} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{plugin} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{exit}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{engine} args = zero or more keyword/args pairs
  keywords = \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} args = N\_1 N\_2 ... N\_ntypes
      N\_1,N\_2,...N\_ntypes = chemical symbol for each of ntypes LAMMPS atom types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{plugin} args = name keyword value keyword value ...
  name = name of plugin library (e.g., \sphinxstyleemphasis{lammps} means a liblammps.so library will be loaded)
  keyword/value pairs in any order, some are required, some are optional
  keywords = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{infile} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{command}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi} value = args passed to MDI for driver to operate with plugins (required)
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{infile} value = filename the engine will read at start\sphinxhyphen{}up (optional)
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} value = aditional command\sphinxhyphen{}line args to pass to engine library when loaded (optional)
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{command} value = a LAMMPS input script command to execute (required)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} args = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{exit} args = none
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{mdi:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{engine}
\PYG{k}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{engine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{elements}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}
\PYG{k}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plugin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZhy{}role ENGINE \PYGZhy{}name lammps \PYGZhy{}method LINK}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{n}{infile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{in.aimd.engine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{extra}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZhy{}log log.aimd.engine.plugin}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{run 5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{connect}
\PYG{k}{mdi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{exit}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{mdi:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command implements operations within LAMMPS to use the \sphinxtitleref{MDI
Library \textless{}https://molssi\sphinxhyphen{}mdi.github.io/MDI\_Library/html/index.html\textgreater{}}
for coupling to other codes in a client/server protocol.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the Howto MDI doc page for a discussion of all the different ways
2 or more codes can interact via MDI.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples/mdi directory has examples which use LAMMPS in 4
different modes: as a driver using an engine as either a stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone
code or as a plugin, and as an engine operating as either a
stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone code or as a plugin.  The README file in that directory
shows how to launch and couple codes for all the 4 usage modes, and so
they communicate via the MDI library using either MPI or sockets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scripts in that directory illustrate the use of all the options
for this command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{engine} option enables LAMMPS to act as an MDI engine (server),
responding to requests from an MDI driver (client) code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{plugin} option enables LAMMPS to act as an MDI driver (client),
and load the MDI engine (server) code as a library plugin.  In this
case the MDI engine is a library plugin.  An MDI engine can also be a
stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone code, launched separately from LAMMPS, in which case the
mdi plugin command is not used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{exit} options are only used when LAMMPS is acting
as an MDI driver.  As explained below, these options are normally not
needed, except for a specific kind of use case.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi engine} command is used to make LAMMPS operate as an MDI
engine.  It is typically used in an input script after LAMMPS has
setup the system it is going to model consistent with what the driver
code expects.  Depending on when the driver code tells the LAMMPS
engine to exit, other commands can be executed after this command, but
typically it is used at the end of a LAMMPS input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To act as an MDI engine operating as an MD code (or surrogate QM
code), this is the list of standard MDI commands issued by a driver
code which LAMMPS currently recognizes.  Using standard commands
defined by the MDI library means that a driver code can work
interchangeably with LAMMPS or other MD codes or with QM codes which
support the MDI standard.  See more details about these commands in
the \sphinxhref{https://molssi-mdi.github.io/MDI\_Library/html/mdi\_standard.html}{MDI library documentation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These commands are valid at the @DEFAULT node defined by MDI.
Commands that start with “\textgreater{}” mean the driver is sending information to
LAMMPS.  Commands that start with “\textless{}” are requests by the driver for
LAMMPS to send it information.  Commands that start with an alphabetic
letter perform actions.  Commands that start with “@” are MDI “node”
commands, which are described further below.

Sends/request number of atoms in the system (1 value)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}NSTEPS
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send number of timesteps for next MD dynamics run via MD command
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textless{}PE
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Request potential energy of the system (1 value)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textless{}STRESS
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Request symmetric stress tensor (virial) of the system (9 values)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}TOLERANCE
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send 4 tolerance parameters for next MD minimization via OPTG command
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}TYPES or \textless{}TYPES
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send/request the LAMMPS atom type for each atom (N values)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}VELOCITIES or \textless{}VELOCITIES
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send/request the velocity of each atom (3N values)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
@INIT\_MD or @INIT\_OPTG
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Driver tells LAMMPS to start single\sphinxhyphen{}step dynamics or minimization (see below)
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
EXIT
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Driver tells LAMMPS to exit engine mode
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabular}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \textless{}ENERGY, \textless{}FORCES, \textless{}PE, and \textless{}STRESS commands trigger LAMMPS to
compute atomic interactions for the current configuration of atoms
and size/shape of the simulation box.  I.e. LAMMPS invokes its
pair, bond, angle, …, kspace styles.  If the driver is updating
the atom coordinates and/or box incrementally (as in an MD
simulation which the driver is managing), then the LAMMPS engine
will do the same, and only occasionally trigger neighbor list
builds.  If the change in atom positions is large (since the
previous \textgreater{}COORDS command), then LAMMPS will do a more expensive
operation to migrate atoms to new processors as needed and
re\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor.  If the \textgreater{}NATOMS or \textgreater{}TYPES or \textgreater{}ELEMENTS commands have
been sent (since the previous \textgreater{}COORDS command), then LAMMPS assumes
the system is new and re\sphinxhyphen{}initializes an entirely new simulation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \textgreater{}TYPES or \textgreater{}ELEMENTS commands are how the MDI driver tells the
LAMMPS engine which LAMMPS atom type to assign to each atom.  If
both the MDI driver and the LAMMPS engine are initialized so that
atom type values are consistent in both codes, then the \textgreater{}TYPES
command can be used.  If not, the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} keyword can
be used to specify what element each LAMMPS atom type corresponds
to.  This is specified by the chemical symbol of the element,
e.g. C or Al or Si.  A symbol must be specified for each of the
ntypes LAMMPS atom types.  Each LAMMPS type must map to a unique
element; two or more types cannot map to the same element.  Ntypes
is typically specified via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}
command or in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.  Once this has been done, the MDI driver can
send an \textgreater{}ELEMENTS command to the LAMMPS driver with the atomic
number of each atom and the LAMMPS engine will be able to map it to
a LAMMPS atom type.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MD and OPTG commands perform an entire MD simulation or energy
minimization (to convergence) with no communication from the driver
until the simulation is complete.  By contrast, the @INIT\_MD and
@INIT\_OPTG commands allow the driver to communicate with the engine at
each timestep of a dynamics run or iteration of a minimization; see
more info below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MD command performs a simulation using the most recent \textgreater{}NSTEPS
value.  The OPTG command performs a minimization using the 4
convergence parameters from the most recent \textgreater{}TOLERANCE command.  The 4
parameters sent are those used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}}
command in LAMMPS: etol, ftol, maxiter, and maxeval.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The mdi engine command also implements the following custom MDI
commands which are LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}specific.  These commands are also valid at
the @DEFAULT node defined by MDI:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Action

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}NBYTES

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send \# of datums in a subsequent command (1 value)

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}COMMAND

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send a LAMMPS input script command as a string (Nbytes in length)

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}COMMANDS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send multiple LAMMPS input script commands as a newline\sphinxhyphen{}separated string (Nbytes in length)

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}INFILE

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send filename of an input script to execute (filename Nbytes in length)

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\textless{}KE

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Request kinetic energy of the system (1 value)

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that other custom commands can easily be added if these are not
sufficient to support what a user\sphinxhyphen{}written driver code needs.  Code to
support new commands can be added to the MDI package within LAMMPS,
specifically to the src/MDI/mdi\_engine.cpp file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
MDI also defines a standard mechanism for the driver to request that
an MD engine (LAMMPS) perform a dynamics simulation one step at a time
or an energy minimization one iteration at a time.  This is so that
the driver can (optionally) communicate with LAMMPS at intermediate
points of the timestep or iteration by issuing MDI node commands which
start with “@”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To tell LAMMPS to run dynamics in single\sphinxhyphen{}step mode, the driver sends
as @INIT\_MD command followed by the these commands.  The driver
can interact with LAMMPS at 3 node locations within each
timestep: @COORDS, @FORCES, @ENDSTEP:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Action

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@COORDS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Proceed to next @COORDS node = post\sphinxhyphen{}integrate location in LAMMPS timestep

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@FORCES

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Proceed to next @FORCES node = post\sphinxhyphen{}force location in LAMMPS timestep

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@ENDSTEP

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Proceed to next @ENDSTEP node = end\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}step location in LAMMPS timestep

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@DEFAULT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Exit MD simulation, return to @DEFAULT node

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
EXIT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Driver tells LAMMPS to exit the MD simulation and engine mode

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To tell LAMMPS to run an energy minimization in single\sphinxhyphen{}iteration mode.
The driver can interact with LAMMPS at 2 node locations within each
iteration of the minimizer: @COORDS, @FORCES:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Action

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@COORDS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Proceed to next @COORDS node = min\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}force location in LAMMPS min iteration

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@FORCES

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Proceed to next @FORCES node = min\sphinxhyphen{}post\sphinxhyphen{}force location in LAMMPS min iteration

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
@DEFAULT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Exit minimization, return to @DEFAULT node

\end{itemize}

\item {} \begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
EXIT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Driver tells LAMMPS to exit the minimization and engine mode

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
While LAMMPS is at its @COORDS node, the following standard MDI
commands are supported, as documented above: \textgreater{}COORDS or \textless{}COORDS,
@COORDS, @FORCES, @ENDSTEP, @DEFAULT, EXIT.

\sphinxAtStartPar
While LAMMPS is at its @FORCES node, the following standard MDI
commands are supported, as documented above: \textless{}COORDS, \textless{}ENERGY, \textgreater{}FORCES
or \textgreater{}+FORCES or \textless{}FORCES, \textless{}KE, \textless{}PE, \textless{}STRESS, @COORDS, @FORCES, @ENDSTEP,
@DEFAULT, EXIT.

\sphinxAtStartPar
While LAMMPS is at its @ENDSTEP node, the following standard MDI
commands are supported, as documented above: \textless{}ENERGY, \textless{}FORCES, \textless{}KE,
\textless{}PE, \textless{}STRESS, @COORDS, @FORCES, @ENDSTEP, @DEFAULT, EXIT.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi plugin} command is used to make LAMMPS operate as an MDI
driver which loads an MDI engine as a plugin library.  It is typically
used in an input script after LAMMPS has setup the system it is going
to model consistent with the engine code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} argument specifies which plugin library to load.  A name
like “lammps” is converted to a filename liblammps.so.  The path for
where this file is located is specified by the \sphinxhyphen{}plugin\_path switch
within the \sphinxhyphen{}mdi command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch, which is specified when LAMMPS is
launched.  See the examples/mdi/README files for examples of how this
is done.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi} keyword is required and is used as the \sphinxhyphen{}mdi argument passed
to the library when it is launched.  The \sphinxhyphen{}role and \sphinxhyphen{}method settings
are required.  The \sphinxhyphen{}name setting can be anything you choose.  MDI
drivers and engines can query their names to verify they are values
they expect.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{infile} keyword is optional.  It sets the name of an input script
which the engine will open and process.  MDI will pass it as a
command\sphinxhyphen{}line argument to the library when it is launched.  The file
typically contains settings that an MD or QM code will use for its
calculations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keyword is optional.  It contains additional command\sphinxhyphen{}line
arguments which MDI will pass to the library when it is launched.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{command} keyword is required.  It specifies a LAMMPS input script
command (as a single argument in quotes if it is multiple words).
Once the plugin library is launched, LAMMPS will execute this command.
Other previously\sphinxhyphen{}defined commands in the input script, such as the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mdi/qm}}}} command, should perform MDI
communication with the engine, while the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{command} executes.
Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{command} is an {\hyperref[\detokenize{include::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{include}}}} command, then it
could specify a filename with multiple LAMMPS commands.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{command} is complete, LAMMPS will send an MDI EXIT
command to the plugin engine and the plugin will be removed.  The
“mdi plugin” command will then exit and the next command (if any)
in the LAMMPS input script will be processed.  A subsequent “mdi
plugin” command could then load the same or a different MDI
plugin if desired.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi connect} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi exit} commands are only used when LAMMPS is
operating as an MDI driver.  And when other LAMMPS command(s) which
send MDI commands and associated data to/from the MDI engine are not
able to initiate and terminate the connection to the engine code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The only current MDI driver command in LAMMPS is the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mdi/qm}}}} command.  If it is only used once in an input script
then it can initiate and terminate the connection, but if it is being
issued multiple times (e.g., in a loop that issues a {\hyperref[\detokenize{clear::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{clear}}}} command), then it cannot initiate or terminate the connection
multiple times.  Instead, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi connect} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdi exit} commands
should be used outside the loop to initiate or terminate the connection.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the examples/mdi/in.series.driver script for an example of how
this is done.  The LOOP in that script is reading a series of data
file configurations and passing them to an MDI engine (e.g., quantum
code) for energy and force evaluation.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{clear} command inside the
loop wipes out the current system so a new one can be defined.  This
operation also destroys all fixes.  So the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mdi/qm}}}} command is issued once per loop iteration.  Note that it
includes a “connect no” option which disables the initiate/terminate
logic within that fix.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{mdi:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is part of the MDI package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use LAMMPS in conjunction with other MDI\sphinxhyphen{}enabled atomistic codes,
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command should be used to specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{metal} units.  This will ensure the correct unit conversions between
LAMMPS and MDI units, which the other codes will also perform in their
preferred units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS can also be used as an MDI engine in other unit choices it
supports (e.g., \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj}), but then no unit conversion is performed.

\section{min\_modify command}
\label{\detokenize{min_modify:min-modify-command}}\label{\detokenize{min_modify:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{min_modify::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{min_modify:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be listed
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dmax} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha\_damp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrator} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{abcfire} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tmax}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dmax} value = max
    max = maximum distance for line search to move (distance units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{backtrack} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{forcezero} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_cubic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_none}
    backtrack,quadratic,forcezero,spin\_cubic,spin\_none = style of linesearch to use
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{two} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{inf} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{max}
    two = Euclidean two\sphinxhyphen{}norm (length of 3N vector)
    inf = max force component across all 3\sphinxhyphen{}vectors
    max = max force norm across all 3\sphinxhyphen{}vectors
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha\_damp} value = damping
    damping = fictitious magnetic damping for spin minimization (adim)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} value = factor
    factor = discretization factor for adaptive spin timestep (adim)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrator} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{eulerimplicit} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{verlet} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{leapfrog} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{eulerexplicit}
    time integration scheme for fire minimization
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{abcfire} value = yes or no (default no)
    yes = use ABC\sphinxhyphen{}FIRE variant of fire minimization style
    no  = use default FIRE variant of fire minimization style
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tmax} value = factor
    factor = maximum adaptive timestep for fire minimization (adim)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{min_modify:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{integrator}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{verlet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{min_modify:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command sets parameters that affect the energy minimization
algorithms selected by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}} command.  The
various settings may affect the convergence rate and overall number of
force evaluations required by a minimization, so users can experiment
with these parameters to tune their minimizations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sd} minimization styles have an outer iteration and an
inner iteration which is steps along a one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional line search in
a particular search direction.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dmax} parameter is how far any
atom can move in a single line search in any dimension (x, y, or z).
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} minimization styles, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dmax} setting
is how far any atom can move in a single iteration (timestep).  Thus a
value of 0.1 in real {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} means no atom will move
further than 0.1 Angstroms in a single outer iteration.  This prevents
highly overlapped atoms from being moved long distances (e.g. through
another atom) due to large forces.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The choice of line search algorithm for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sd} minimization
styles can be selected via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} keyword.  The default
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic} line search algorithm starts out using the robust
backtracking method described below. However, once the system gets
close to a local minimum and the linesearch steps get small, so that
the energy is approximately quadratic in the step length, it uses the
estimated location of zero gradient as the linesearch step, provided
the energy change is downhill.  This becomes more efficient than
backtracking for highly\sphinxhyphen{}converged relaxations. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{forcezero} line
search algorithm is similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic}.  It may be more
efficient than \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic} on some systems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The backtracking search is robust and should always find a local
energy minimum.  However, it will “converge” when it can no longer
reduce the energy of the system.  Individual atom forces may still be
larger than desired at this point, because the energy change is
measured as the difference of two large values (energy before and
energy after) and that difference may be smaller than machine epsilon
even if atoms could move in the gradient direction to reduce forces
further.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The choice of a norm can be modified for the min styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire/old}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} keyword.  The default \sphinxstyleemphasis{two} norm computes
the 2\sphinxhyphen{}norm (Euclidean length) of the global force vector:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}|| \vec{F} ||_{2} = \sqrt{\vec{F}_1^2+ \cdots + \vec{F}_N^2}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} norm computes the length of the 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector force
for each atom  (2\sphinxhyphen{}norm), and takes the maximum value of those across
all atoms
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}|| \vec{F} ||_{max} = {\rm max}\left(||\vec{F}_1||, \cdots, ||\vec{F}_N||\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{inf} norm takes the maximum component across the forces of
all atoms in the system:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}|| \vec{F} ||_{inf} = {\rm max}\left(|F_1^1|, |F_1^2|, |F_1^3| \cdots, |F_N^1|, |F_N^2|, |F_N^3|\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the min styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs}, the force
norm is replaced by the spin\sphinxhyphen{}torque norm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha\_damp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} only make sense when
a {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_spin}}}} command is declared.
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha\_damp} defines an analog of a magnetic damping.
It defines a relaxation rate toward an equilibrium for a given
magnetic system.
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} defines a discretization factor for the
adaptive timestep used in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin} minimization.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_spin}}}} for more information about those
quantities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The choice of a line search algorithm for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} styles can be specified via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} keyword.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_cubic} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_none} keywords only make sense when one of those two
minimization styles is declared.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_cubic} performs the line
search based on a cubic interpolation of the energy along the search
direction. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_none} keyword deactivates the line search
procedure.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_none} is a default value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} keyword for
both \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg}. Convergence of \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} can be
more robust if \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_cubic} line search is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Newton \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrator} used for \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} minimization can be selected to
be either the symplectic Euler (\sphinxstyleemphasis{eulerimplicit}), velocity Verlet (\sphinxstyleemphasis{verlet}), Leapfrog (\sphinxstyleemphasis{leapfrog}) or non\sphinxhyphen{}symplectic forward Euler
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{eulerexplicit} ). The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tmax} defines the maximum value for
the adaptive timestep during a \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} minimization. It is a
multiplication factor applied to the current {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}}
(not in time unit). For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tmax} = 4.0 with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}} of 2fs, means that the maximum value the timestep can reach
during a \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} minimization is 4fs.  Note that parameter defaults has
been chosen to be reliable in most cases, but one should consider
adjusting {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tmax} to optimize the
minimization for large or complex systems.  Other parameters of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} minimization can be tuned (\sphinxstyleemphasis{tmin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{delaystep}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dtgrow},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dtshrink}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha0}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{alphashrink}). Please refer to the
references describing the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire}.  An
additional stopping criteria \sphinxstyleemphasis{vdfmax} is used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} in order to
avoid unnecessary looping when it is reasonable to think the system will
not be relaxed further.  Note that in this case the system will NOT have
reached your minimization criteria. This could happen when the system
comes to be stuck in a local basin of the phase space.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{vdfmax} is the
maximum number of consecutive iterations with P(t) \textless{} 0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 8Feb2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{abcfire} keyword allows to activate the ABC\sphinxhyphen{}FIRE variant of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} minimization algorithm. ABC\sphinxhyphen{}FIRE introduces an additional factor
that modifies the bias and scaling of the velocities of the atoms during
the mixing step {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify:echeverrirestrepo}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Echeverri Restrepo)}}}}.  This
can lead to faster convergence of the minimizer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} is an optimized implementation of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire/old}. It can however behave similarly
to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire/old} style by using the following set of parameters:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{integrator}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eulerexplicit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delaystep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{dtgrow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dtshrink}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alpha0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alphashrink}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.99}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{vdfmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halfstepback}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{initialdelay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{min_modify:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For magnetic GNEB calculations, only \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_none} value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{line}
keyword can be used when minimization styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} are
employed.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb/spin}}}} for more explanation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{min_modify:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are dmax = 0.1, line = quadratic and norm = two.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} styles, the option
defaults are alpha\_damp = 1.0, discrete\_factor = 10.0, line =
spin\_none, and norm = euclidean.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} style, the option defaults are integrator =
eulerimplicit, tmax = 10.0, tmin = 0.02, delaystep = 20, dtgrow = 1.1,
dtshrink = 0.5, alpha0 = 0.25, alphashrink = 0.99, vdfmax = 2000,
halfstepback = yes and initialdelay = yes.

\section{min\_style spin command}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:min-style-spin-command}}\label{\detokenize{min_spin:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{min_spin::doc}}

\section{min\_style spin/cg command}

\section{min\_style spin/lbfgs command}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:min-style-spin-lbfgs-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:syntax}}

\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cg}
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lbfgs}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lbfgs}
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spin\PYGZus{}cubic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{discrete\PYGZus{}factor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a minimization algorithm to use when a {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}}
command is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin} defines a damped spin dynamics with an adaptive
timestep, according to:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{d \vec{s}_{i}}{dt} = \lambda\, \vec{s}_{i} \times\left( \vec{\omega}_{i} \times\vec{s}_{i} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\lambda\) a damping coefficient (similar to a magnetic
damping). \(\lambda\) can be defined by setting the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha\_damp} keyword with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimization procedure solves this equation using an
adaptive timestep. The value of this timestep is defined
by the largest precession frequency that has to be solved in the
system:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{\Delta t}_{\rm max} = \frac{2\pi}{\kappa \left|\vec{\omega}_{\rm max} \right|}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\left|\vec{\omega}_{\rm max}\right|\) the norm of the largest precession
frequency in the system (across all processes, and across all replicas if a
spin/neb calculation is performed).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\kappa\) defines a discretization factor \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} for
the definition of this timestep.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} can be defined with
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} defines an orthogonal spin optimization
(OSO) combined to a conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}} command can be used to
couple the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} to a line search procedure, and to modify the
discretization factor \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor}.
By default, style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} does not employ the line search procedure
and uses the adaptive time\sphinxhyphen{}step technique in the same way as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} defines an orthogonal spin optimization (OSO)
combined to a limited\sphinxhyphen{}memory Broyden\sphinxhyphen{}Fletcher\sphinxhyphen{}Goldfarb\sphinxhyphen{}Shanno (L\sphinxhyphen{}BFGS)
algorithm.  By default, style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} does not employ line search
procedure.  If the line search procedure is not used then the discrete
factor defines the maximum root mean squared rotation angle of spins by
equation \sphinxstyleemphasis{pi/(5*Kappa)}.  The default value for Kappa is 10.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spin\_cubic} line search option can improve the convergence of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} algorithm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}} command can be used to
activate the line search procedure, and to modify the
discretization factor \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For more information about styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs},
see their implementation reported in {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_spin:ivanov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ivanov)}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin} styles replace the force tolerance by a torque
tolerance. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} for more explanation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} styles can be used
for magnetic NEB calculations only if the line search procedure
is deactivated. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb/spin}}}} for more explanation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgps} styles are part of the SPIN
package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This minimization procedure is only applied to spin degrees of
freedom for a frozen lattice configuration.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{min_spin:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha\_damp} = 1.0, \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete\_factor} =
10.0, \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} = spin\_none and \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} = euclidean.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxalltt}

\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{min_style:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cg}
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fire}
\PYG{k}{min\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spin}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{min_style:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose a minimization algorithm to use when a {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg} is the Polak\sphinxhyphen{}Ribiere version of the conjugate gradient (CG)
algorithm.  At each iteration the force gradient is combined with the
previous iteration information to compute a new search direction
perpendicular (conjugate) to the previous search direction.  The PR
variant affects how the direction is chosen and how the CG method is
restarted when it ceases to make progress.  The PR variant is thought
to be the most effective CG choice for most problems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{hftn} is a Hessian\sphinxhyphen{}free truncated Newton algorithm.  At each
iteration a quadratic model of the energy potential is solved by a
conjugate gradient inner iteration.  The Hessian (second derivatives)
of the energy is not formed directly, but approximated in each
conjugate search direction by a finite difference directional
derivative.  When close to an energy minimum, the algorithm behaves
like a Newton method and exhibits a quadratic convergence rate to high
accuracy.  In most cases the behavior of \sphinxstyleemphasis{hftn} is similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg},
but it offers an alternative if \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg} seems to perform poorly.  This
style is not affected by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{sd} is a steepest descent algorithm.  At each iteration, the
search direction is set to the downhill direction corresponding to the
force vector (negative gradient of energy).  Typically, steepest
descent will not converge as quickly as CG, but may be more robust in
some situations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin} is a damped dynamics method described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style:sheppard}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sheppard)}}}}, where the damping parameter is related
to the projection of the velocity vector along the current force
vector for each atom.  The velocity of each atom is initialized to 0.0
by this style, at the beginning of a minimization.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} is a damped dynamics method described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style:bitzek}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bitzek)}}}}, which is similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin} but adds a variable timestep
and alters the projection operation to maintain components of the
velocity non\sphinxhyphen{}parallel to the current force vector.  The velocity of each
atom is initialized to 0.0 by this style, at the beginning of a
minimization.  This style correspond to an optimized version described
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style:guenole}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Guenole)}}}} that include different time integration
schemes and default parameters.  The default parameters can be modified
with the command {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_modify}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin} is a damped spin dynamics with an adaptive timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} uses an orthogonal spin optimization (OSO) combined to
a conjugate gradient (CG) approach to minimize spin configurations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} uses an orthogonal spin optimization (OSO) combined
to a limited\sphinxhyphen{}memory Broyden\sphinxhyphen{}Fletcher\sphinxhyphen{}Goldfarb\sphinxhyphen{}Shanno (LBFGS) approach
to minimize spin configurations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min/spin}}}} page for more information about
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin} or the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire} styles are useful in the context of
nudged elastic band (NEB) calculations via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/cg}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/lbfgs} styles are useful in the
context of magnetic geodesic nudged elastic band (GNEB) calculations via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb/spin}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The damped dynamic minimizers use whatever timestep you have
defined via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}} command.  Often they
will converge more quickly if you use a timestep about 10x larger
than you would normally use for dynamics simulations.
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire}, the default timestep is recommended to be equal to
the one you would normally use for dynamics simulations.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fire}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{hftn}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cg/kk} styles do not yet
support the use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_box_relax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix box/relax}}}} command
or minimizations involving the electron radius in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{eFF}}}} models.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.
