\section{read\_data command}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:read-data-command}}\label{\detokenize{read_data:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{read_data::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of data file to read in

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/atom/types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/bond/types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/angle/types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/dihedral/types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/improper/types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/bond/per/atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/angle/per/atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/dihedral/per/atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/improper/per/atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/special/per/atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{IDoffset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{IDoffset MOLoffset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{merge}
  append = add new atoms with atom IDs appended to current IDs
  IDoffset = add new atoms with atom IDs having IDoffset added
  MOLoffset = add new atoms with molecule IDs having MOLoffset added (only when molecule IDs are enabled)
  merge = add new atoms with their atom IDs (and molecule IDs) unchanged
\sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} args = toff boff aoff doff ioff
  toff = offset to add to atom types
  boff = offset to add to bond types
  aoff = offset to add to angle types
  doff = offset to add to dihedral types
  ioff = offset to add to improper types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} args = Sx Sy Sz
  Sx,Sy,Sz = distance to shift atoms when adding to system (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/atom/types} arg = \# of extra atom types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/bond/types} arg = \# of extra bond types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/angle/types} arg = \# of extra angle types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/dihedral/types} arg = \# of extra dihedral types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/improper/types} arg = \# of extra improper types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/bond/per/atom} arg = leave space for this many new bonds per atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/angle/per/atom} arg = leave space for this many new angles per atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/dihedral/per/atom} arg = leave space for this many new dihedrals per atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/improper/per/atom} arg = leave space for this many new impropers per atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/special/per/atom} arg = leave space for extra 1\sphinxhyphen{}2,1\sphinxhyphen{}3,1\sphinxhyphen{}4 interactions per atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{group} args = groupID
  groupID = add atoms in data file to this group
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} = ignore force field parameters
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} args = fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID header\sphinxhyphen{}string section\sphinxhyphen{}string
  fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of fix to process header lines and sections of data file
  header\sphinxhyphen{}string = header lines containing this string will be passed to fix
  section\sphinxhyphen{}string = section names with this string will be passed to fix
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{data.lj}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{run7}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{data.polymer.gz}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{data.protein}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mycmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{crossterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CMAP}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{data.water}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{offset}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{data.water}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{merge}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{group }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{solvent}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read in a data file containing information LAMMPS needs to run a
simulation.  The file can be ASCII text or a gzipped text file
(detected by a .gz suffix).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is one of 3 ways to specify the simulation box: see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
and commands for alternative methods.  It is also one of 3 ways to
specify initial atom coordinates: see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} and commands
for alternative methods.  Also see the explanation of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}restart command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} which can convert a
restart file to a data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can be used multiple times to add new atoms and their
properties to an existing system by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keywords.  However, it is important to understand that several
system parameters, like the number of types of different kinds and per
atom settings are \sphinxstylestrong{locked in} after the first \sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_data} command,
which means that no type ID (including its offset) may have a larger
value when processing additional data files than what is set by the
first data file and the corresponding \sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_data} command options.  See
more details on this situation below, which includes the use case for
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} keyword adds all the atoms in the data file to the
specified group\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  The group will be created if it does not already
exist.  This is useful if you are reading multiple data files and wish
to put sets of atoms into different groups so they can be operated on
later.  E.g. a group of added atoms can be moved to new positions via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms}}}} command.  Note that atoms
read from the data file are also always added to the “all” group.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} command discusses atom groups, as used in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} keyword tells read\_data to ignore force field parameters.
The various Coeff sections are still read and have to have the correct
number of lines, but they are not applied. This also allows to read a
data file without having any pair, bond, angle, dihedral or improper
styles defined, or to read a data file for a different force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} keyword is discussed below.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Reading multiple data files}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:reading-multiple-data-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The read\_data command can be used multiple times with the same or
different data files to build up a complex system from components
contained in individual data files.  For example one data file could
contain fluid in a confined domain; a second could contain wall atoms,
and the second file could be read a third time to create a wall on the
other side of the fluid.  The third set of atoms could be rotated to
an opposing direction using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms}}}}
command, after the third read\_data command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{add}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} keywords are
useful in this context.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a simulation box does not yet exist, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword cannot be
used; the read\_data command is being used for the first time.  If a
simulation box does exist, due to using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command, or a previous read\_data command, then the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add}
keyword must be used.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the first read\_data command defined an orthogonal or restricted
triclinic or general triclinic simulation box (see the sub\sphinxhyphen{}section
below on header keywords), then subsequent data files must define
the same kind of simulation box.  For orthogonal boxes, the new box
can be a different size; see the next Note.  For a restricted
triclinic box, the 3 new tilt factors (“xy xz yz” keyword) must
have the same values as in the original data file.  For a general
triclinic box, the new avec, bvec, cvec, and “abc origin” keywords
must have the same values in the original data file.  files.  Also
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword cannot be used in subsequent read\_data commands
for a general triclinic box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For orthogonal boxes, the simulation box size in the new data file
will be merged with the existing simulation box to create a large
enough box in each dimension to contain both the existing and new
atoms.  Each box dimension never shrinks due to this merge
operation, it only stays the same or grows.  Care must be used if
you are growing the existing simulation box in a periodic
dimension.  If there are existing atoms with bonds that straddle
that periodic boundary, then the atoms may become far apart if the
box size grows.  This will separate the atoms in the bond, which
can lead to “lost” bond atoms or bad dynamics.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The three choices for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} argument affect how the atom IDs and
molecule IDs of atoms in the data file are treated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} is specified, atoms in the data file are added to the
current system, with their atom IDs reset so that an atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID = M in
the data file becomes atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID = N+M, where N is the largest atom ID in
the current system.  This rule is applied to all occurrences of atom
IDs in the data file, e.g. in the Velocity or Bonds section. This is
also done for molecule IDs, if the atom style does support molecule
IDs or they are enabled via fix property/atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{IDoffset} is specified, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{IDoffset} is a numeric value is
given, e.g. 1000, so that an atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID = M in the data file becomes
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID = 1000+M. For systems with enabled molecule IDs, another
numerical argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{MOLoffset} is required representing the equivalent
offset for molecule IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{merge} is specified, the data file atoms are added to the current
system without changing their IDs.  They are assumed to merge (without
duplication) with the currently defined atoms.  It is up to you to
ensure there are no multiply defined atom IDs, as LAMMPS only performs
an incomplete check that this is the case by ensuring the resulting
max atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID \textgreater{}= the number of atoms. For molecule IDs, there is no
check done at all.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keywords can only be used if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add}
keyword is also specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} keyword adds the specified offset values to the atom
types, bond types, angle types, dihedral types, and improper types as
they are read from the data file.  E.g. if \sphinxstyleemphasis{toff} = 2, and the file
uses atom types 1,2,3, then the added atoms will have atom types
3,4,5.  These offsets apply to all occurrences of types in the data
file, e.g. for the Atoms or Masses or Pair Coeffs or Bond Coeffs
sections.  This makes it easy to use atoms and molecules and their
attributes from a data file in different simulations, where you want
their types (atom, bond, angle, etc) to be different depending on what
other types already exist.  All five offset values must be specified,
but individual values will be ignored if the data file does not use
that attribute (e.g. no bonds).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Offsets are \sphinxstylestrong{ignored} on lines using type labels, as the type
labels will determine the actual types directly depending on the
current {\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword can be used to specify an (Sx, Sy, Sz)
displacement applied to the coordinates of each atom.  Sz must be 0.0
for a 2d simulation.  This is a mechanism for adding structured
collections of atoms at different locations within the simulation box,
to build up a complex geometry.  It is up to you to ensure atoms do
not end up overlapping unphysically which would lead to bad dynamics.
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms}}}} command can be used
to move a subset of atoms after they have been read from a data file.
Likewise, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_atoms}}}} command can be used to
remove overlapping atoms.  Note that the shift values (Sx, Sy, Sz) are
also added to the simulation box information (xlo, xhi, ylo, yhi, zlo,
zhi) in the data file to shift its boundaries.  E.g. xlo\_new = xlo +
Sx, xhi\_new = xhi + Sx.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords can only be used the first time the read\_data
command is used.  They are useful if you intend to add new atom, bond,
angle, etc types later with additional read\_data commands.  This is
because the maximum number of allowed atom, bond, angle, etc types is
set by LAMMPS when the system is first initialized.  If you do not use
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords, then the number of these types will be limited
to what appears in the first data file you read.  For example, if the
first data file is a solid substrate of Si, it will likely specify a
single atom type.  If you read a second data file with a different
material (water molecules) that sit on top of the substrate, you will
want to use different atom types for those atoms.  You can only do
this if you set the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/atom/types} keyword to a sufficiently large
value when reading the substrate data file.  Note that use of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords also allows each data file to contain sections like
Masses or Pair Coeffs or Bond Coeffs which are sized appropriately for
the number of types in that data file.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} keyword is
used appropriately when each data file is read, the values in those
sections will be stored correctly in the larger data structures
allocated by the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords.  E.g. the substrate file
can list mass and pair coefficients for type 1 silicon atoms.  The
water file can list mass and pair coefficients for type 1 and type 2
hydrogen and oxygen atoms.  Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} keywords
will store those mass and pair coefficient values appropriately in
data structures that allow for 3 atom types (Si, H, O).  Of course,
you would still need to specify coefficients for H/Si and O/Si
interactions in your input script to have a complete pairwise
interaction model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An alternative to using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords with the read\_data
command, is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command to
initialize the simulation box and all the various type limits you need
via its \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} keywords.  Then use the read\_data command one or more
times to populate the system with atoms, bonds, angles, etc, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} keyword if desired to alter types used in the various data
files you read.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Format of a data file}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:format-of-a-data-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The structure of the data file is important, though many settings and
sections are optional or can come in any order.  See the examples
directory for sample data files for different problems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The file will be read line by line, but there is a limit of 254
characters per line and characters beyond that limit will be ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A data file has a header and a body.  The header appears first.  The
first line of the header and thus of the data file is \sphinxstyleemphasis{always} skipped;
it typically contains a description of the file or a comment from the
software that created the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Then lines are read one line at a time.  Lines can have a trailing
comment starting with ‘\#’ that is ignored.  There \sphinxstyleemphasis{must} be at least one
blank between any valid content and the comment. If a line is blank
(i.e. contains only white\sphinxhyphen{}space after comments are deleted), it is
skipped.  If the line contains a header keyword, the corresponding
value(s) is/are read from the line.  A line that is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} blank and does
\sphinxstyleemphasis{not} contain a header keyword begins the body of the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The body of the file contains zero or more sections.  The first line of
a section has only a keyword.  This line can have a trailing comment
starting with ‘\#’ that is either ignored or can be used to check for a
style match, as described below.  There must be a blank between the
keyword and any comment. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{next} line is \sphinxstyleemphasis{always} skipped.  The
remaining lines of the section contain values.  The number of lines
depends on the section keyword as described below.  Zero or more blank
lines can be used \sphinxstyleemphasis{between} sections.  Sections can appear in any order,
with a few exceptions as noted below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} can be used one or more times.  Each usage specifies
a fix that will be used to process a specific portion of the data
file.  Any header line containing \sphinxstyleemphasis{header\sphinxhyphen{}string} and any section that
is an exact match to \sphinxstyleemphasis{section\sphinxhyphen{}string} will be passed to the specified
fix.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} command for
an example of a fix that operates in this manner.  The doc page for
the fix defines the syntax of the header line(s) and section that it
reads from the data file.  Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{header\sphinxhyphen{}string} can be
specified as NULL, in which case no header lines are passed to the
fix.  This means the fix can infer the length of its Section from
standard header settings, such as the number of atoms.  Also the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{section\sphinxhyphen{}string} may be specified as NULL, and in that case the fix
ID is used as section name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The formatting of individual lines in the data file (indentation,
spacing between words and numbers) is not important except that header
and section keywords (e.g. atoms, xlo xhi, Masses, Bond Coeffs) must
be capitalized as shown and cannot have extra white\sphinxhyphen{}space between
their words \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. two spaces or a tab between the 2 words in “xlo
xhi” or the 2 words in “Bond Coeffs”, is not valid.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Format of the header of a data file}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:format-of-the-header-of-a-data-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the recognized header keywords.  Header lines can come in
any order.  Each keyword takes a single value unless noted in this
list.  The value(s) are read from the beginning of the line.
Thus the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{atoms} should be in a line like “1000 atoms”; the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo yhi} should be in a line like “\sphinxhyphen{}10.0 10.0 ylo yhi”; the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy xz yz} should be in a line like “0.0 5.0 6.0 xy xz yz”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All these settings have a default value of 0, except for the
simulation box size settings; their defaults are explained below.  A
keyword line need only appear if its value is different than the
default.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atoms} = \# of atoms in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bonds} = \# of bonds in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angles} = \# of angles in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedrals} = \# of dihedrals in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{impropers} = \# of impropers in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom types} = \# of atom types in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond types} = \# of bond types in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle types} = \# of angle types in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral types} = \# of dihedral types in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{improper types} = \# of improper types in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra bond per atom} = leave space for this many new bonds per atom (deprecated, use extra/bond/per/atom keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra angle per atom} = leave space for this many new angles per atom (deprecated, use extra/angle/per/atom keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra dihedral per atom} = leave space for this many new dihedrals per atom (deprecated, use extra/dihedral/per/atom keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra improper per atom} = leave space for this many new impropers per atom (deprecated, use extra/improper/per/atom keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra special per atom} = leave space for this many new special bonds per atom (deprecated, use extra/special/per/atom keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ellipsoids} = \# of ellipsoids in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lines} = \# of line segments in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{triangles} = \# of triangles in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bodies} = \# of bodies in system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo xhi} = simulation box boundaries in x dimension (2 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo yhi} = simulation box boundaries in y dimension (2 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo zhi} = simulation box boundaries in z dimension (2 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xy xz yz} = simulation box tilt factors for triclinic system (3 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{avec} = first edge vector of a general triclinic simulation box (3 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bvec} = second edge vector of a general triclinic simulation box (3 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cvec} = third edge vector of a general triclinic simulation box (3 values)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{abc origin} = origin of a general triclinic simulation box (3 values)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Header specification of the simulation box size and shape}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:header-specification-of-the-simulation-box-size-and-shape}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The last 8 keywords in the list of header keywords are for simulation
boxes of 3 kinds which LAMMPS supports:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
orthogonal box = faces are perpendicular to the xyz coordinate axes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
restricted triclinic box = a parallelepiped defined by 3 edge vectors oriented in a constrained manner

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
general triclinic box = a parallelepiped defined by 3 arbitrary edge vectors

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For restricted and general triclinic boxes, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_triclinic}}}} doc page for a fuller
description than is given here.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The units of the values for all 8 keywords in in distance units; see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all 3 kinds of simulation boxes, the system may be periodic or
non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic in any dimension; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}}
command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the simulation box is created by the read\_data command, it is
also partitioned into a regular 3d grid of subdomains, one per
processor, based on the number of processors being used and the
settings of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{processors::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{processors}}}} command.  For each kind
of simulation box the subdomains have the same shape as the simulation
box, i.e. smaller orthogonal bricks for orthogonal boxes, smaller
parallelepipeds for triclinic boxes.  The partitioning can later be
changed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix balance}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For an orthogonal box, only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo zhi}
keywords are used.  They define the extent of the simulation box in
each dimension so that the resulting edge vectors of an orthogonal box
are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{A} = (xhi\sphinxhyphen{}xlo,0,0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{B} = (0,yhi\sphinxhyphen{}ylo,0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{C} = (0,0,zhi\sphinxhyphen{}zlo)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The origin (lower left corner) of the orthogonal box is at
(xlo,ylo,zlo).  The default values for these 3 keywords are \sphinxhyphen{}0.5 and
0.5 for each lo/hi pair.  For a 2d simulation, the zlo and zhi values
must straddle zero.  The default zlo/zhi values do this, so that
keyword is not needed in 2d.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a restricted triclinic box, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy xz yz} keyword is used in
addition to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo zhi} keywords.  The three
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xy,xz,yz} values can be 0.0 or positive or negative, and are called
“tilt factors” because they are the amount of displacement applied to
edges of faces of an orthogonal box to transform it into a restricted
triclinic parallelepiped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_triclinic}}}} doc page discusses the
tilt factors in detail and explains that the resulting edge vectors of
a restricted triclinic box are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{A} = (xhi\sphinxhyphen{}xlo,0,0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{B} = (xy,yhi\sphinxhyphen{}ylo,0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{C} = (xz,yz,zhi\sphinxhyphen{}zlo)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This restricted form of edge vectors requires that \sphinxstylestrong{A} be in the
direction of the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis, \sphinxstylestrong{B} be in the xy plane with its y\sphinxhyphen{}component
in the +y direction, and \sphinxstylestrong{C} have its z\sphinxhyphen{}component in the +z
direction.  The origin (lower left corner) of the restricted triclinic
box is at (xlo,ylo,zlo).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a 2d simulation, the zlo and zhi values must straddle zero.  The
default zlo/zhi values do this, so that keyword is not needed in 2d.
The xz and yz values must also be zero in 2d.  The shape of the 2d
restricted triclinic simulation box is effectively a parallelogram.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When a restricted triclinic box is used, the simulation domain
should normally be periodic in any dimensions that tilt is applied
to, which is given by the second dimension of the tilt factor
(e.g. y for xy tilt).  This is so that pairs of atoms interacting
across that boundary will have one of them shifted by the tilt
factor.  Periodicity is set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}}
command which also describes the shifting by the tilt factor.  For
example, if the xy tilt factor is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, then the y dimension
should be periodic.  Similarly, the z dimension should be periodic
if xz or yz is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero.  LAMMPS does not require this periodicity,
but you may lose atoms if this is not the case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normally, the specified tilt factors (xy,xz,yz) should not skew the
simulation box by more than half the distance of the corresponding
parallel box length for computational efficiency.  For example, if
\(x_\text{lo} = 2\) and \(x_\text{hi} = 12\), then the
\(x\) box length is 10 and the \(xy\) tilt factor should be
between \(-5\) and \(5\).  LAMMPS will issue a warning if
this is not the case.  See the last sub\sphinxhyphen{}section of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_triclinic}}}} doc page for more details.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a simulation box is initially orthogonal, but will tilt during a
simulation, e.g. via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command,
then the box should be defined as restricted triclinic with all 3
tilt factors = 0.0.  Alternatively, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{change_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{change box}}}} command can be used to convert an orthogonal box to a
restricted triclinic box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a general triclinic box, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{avec}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bvec}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvec}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{abc
origin} keywords are used.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo zhi}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xy xz yz} keywords are NOT used.  The first 3 keywords define the 3
edge vectors \sphinxstylestrong{A}, \sphinxstylestrong{B}, \sphinxstylestrong{C} of the general triclinic box.  They
can be arbitrary vectors so long as they are distinct, non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, and
not co\sphinxhyphen{}planar.  They must also define a right\sphinxhyphen{}handed system such that
(\sphinxstylestrong{A} x \sphinxstylestrong{B}) points in the direction of \sphinxstylestrong{C}.  Note that a
left\sphinxhyphen{}handed system can be converted to a right\sphinxhyphen{}handed system by simply
swapping the order of any pair of the \sphinxstylestrong{A}, \sphinxstylestrong{B}, \sphinxstylestrong{C} vectors.
The origin of the box (origin of the 3 edge vectors) is set by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{abc origin} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default values for these 4 keywords are as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
avec = (1,0,0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bvec = (0,1,0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cvec = (0,0,1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
abc origin = (0,0,0) for 3d, (0,0,\sphinxhyphen{}0.5) for 2d

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For 2d simulations, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvec} = (0,0,1) is required, and the 3rd value of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{abc origin} must be \sphinxhyphen{}0.5.  These are the default values, so the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cvec} keyword is not needed in 2d.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS allows specification of general triclinic simulation boxes
as a convenience for users who may be converting data from
solid\sphinxhyphen{}state crystallographic representations or from DFT codes for
input to LAMMPS.  However, as explained on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_triclinic}}}} doc page, internally,
LAMMPS only uses restricted triclinic simulation boxes.  This means
the box and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom information (e.g. coordinates, velocities) in
the data file are converted (rotated) from general to restricted
triclinic form when the file is read.  Other sections of the data
file must also list their per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data appropriately if vector
quantities are specified. This requirement is explained below for
the relevant sections.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_triclinic}}}} doc page also discusses other LAMMPS commands
which can input/output general triclinic representations of the
simulation box and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following explanations apply to all 3 kinds of simulation boxes:
orthogonal, restricted triclinic, and general triclinic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the system is periodic (in a dimension), then atom coordinates can
be outside the bounds (in that dimension); they will be remapped (in a
periodic sense) back inside the box.  For triclinic boxes, periodicity
in x,y,z refers to the faces of the parallelepiped defined by the
\sphinxstylestrong{A},**B**,**C** edge vectors of the simulation box.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command doc page for a fuller discussion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} option is being used to add atoms to a
simulation box that already exists, this periodic remapping will be
performed using simulation box bounds that are the union of the
existing box and the box boundaries in the new data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the system is non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic (in a dimension), then an image flag for
that direction has no meaning, since there cannot be periodic images
without periodicity and the data file is therefore \sphinxhyphen{} technically speaking
\sphinxhyphen{} invalid.  This situation would happen when a data file was written
with periodic boundaries and then read back for non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundaries.
Accepting a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero image flag can lead to unexpected results for any
operations and computations in LAMMPS that internally use unwrapped
coordinates (for example computing the center of mass of a group of
atoms). Thus all non\sphinxhyphen{}zero image flags for non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimensions will
be be reset to zero on reading the data file and LAMMPS will print a
warning message, if that happens.  This is equivalent to wrapping atoms
individually back into the principal unit cell in that direction.  This
operation is equivalent to the behavior of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{change_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{change\_box command}}}} when used to change periodicity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If those atoms with non\sphinxhyphen{}zero image flags are involved in bonded
interactions, this reset can lead to undesired changes, when the image
flag values differ between the atoms, i.e. the bonded interaction
straddles domain boundaries.  For example a bond can become stretched
across the unit cell if one of its atoms is wrapped to one side of the
cell and the second atom to the other. In those cases the data file
needs to be pre\sphinxhyphen{}processed externally to become valid again.  This can be
done by first unwrapping coordinates and then wrapping entire molecules
instead of individual atoms back into the principal simulation cell and
finally expanding the cell dimensions in the non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic direction as
needed, so that the image flag would be zero.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the system is non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic (in a dimension), then all atoms in
the data file must have coordinates (in that dimension) that are
“greater than or equal to” the lo value and “less than or equal to”
the hi value.  If the non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension is of style “fixed”
(see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command), then the atom coords
must be strictly “less than” the hi value, due to the way LAMMPS
assign atoms to processors.  Note that you should not make the
lo/hi values radically smaller/larger than the extent of the atoms.
For example, if atoms extend from 0 to 50, you should not specify
the box bounds as \sphinxhyphen{}10000 and 10000 unless you also use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{processors::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{processors command}}}}.  This is because LAMMPS
uses the specified box size to layout the 3d grid of processors.  A
huge (mostly empty) box will be sub\sphinxhyphen{}optimal for performance when
using “fixed” boundary conditions (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command).  When using “shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrap” boundary conditions
(see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command), a huge (mostly empty)
box may cause a parallel simulation to lose atoms when LAMMPS
shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wraps the box around the atoms.  The read\_data command will
generate an error in this case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Meaning of other header keywords}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:meaning-of-other-header-keywords}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The “extra bond per atom” setting (angle, dihedral, improper) is only
needed if new bonds (angles, dihedrals, impropers) will be added to
the system when a simulation runs, e.g. by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_create::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
bond/create}}}} command. Using this header flag is
deprecated; please use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/bond/per/atom} keyword (and
correspondingly for angles, dihedrals and impropers) in the read\_data
command instead. Either will pre\sphinxhyphen{}allocate space in LAMMPS data
structures for storing the new bonds (angles, dihedrals, impropers).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “extra special per atom” setting is typically only needed if new
bonds/angles/etc will be added to the system, e.g. by using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_create::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/create}}}} command.  Or if entire new
molecules will be added to the system, e.g. by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
deposit}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pour::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix pour}}}} commands, which
will have more special 1\sphinxhyphen{}2,1\sphinxhyphen{}3,1\sphinxhyphen{}4 neighbors than any other molecules
defined in the data file.  Using this header flag is deprecated;
please use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/special/per/atom} keyword instead.  Using this
setting will pre\sphinxhyphen{}allocate space in the LAMMPS data structures for
storing these neighbors.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} doc pages for more discussion of
1\sphinxhyphen{}2,1\sphinxhyphen{}3,1\sphinxhyphen{}4 neighbors.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the “extra” settings are only applied in the first data file
read and when no simulation box has yet been created; as soon as
the simulation box is created (and read\_data implies that), these
settings are \sphinxstyleemphasis{locked} and cannot be changed anymore. Please see the
description of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword above for reading multiple data
files.  If they appear in later data files, they are ignored.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “ellipsoids” and “lines” and “triangles” and “bodies” settings are
only used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid or line or tri or body}}}} and specify how many of the atoms are finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
ellipsoids or lines or triangles or bodies; the remainder are point
particles.  See the discussion of ellipsoidflag and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ellipsoids}
section below.  See the discussion of lineflag and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Lines} section
below.  See the discussion of triangleflag and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Triangles} section
below.  See the discussion of bodyflag and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bodies} section below.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style template}}}}, the molecular topology
(bonds,angles,etc) is contained in the molecule templates read\sphinxhyphen{}in
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command.  This means you cannot
set the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bonds}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{angles}, etc header keywords in the data file,
nor can you define \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bonds}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Angles}, etc sections as discussed
below.  You can set the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond types}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle types}, etc header
keywords, though it is not necessary.  If specified, they must
match the maximum values defined in any of the template molecules.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Format of the body of a data file}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:format-of-the-body-of-a-data-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the section keywords for the body of the file.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms, Velocities, Masses, Ellipsoids, Lines, Triangles, Bodies} = atom\sphinxhyphen{}property sections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bonds, Angles, Dihedrals, Impropers} = molecular topology sections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atom Type Labels, Bond Type Labels, Angle Type Labels, Dihedral Type Labels, Improper Type Labels} = type label maps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair Coeffs, PairIJ Coeffs, Bond Coeffs, Angle Coeffs, Dihedral Coeffs,    Improper Coeffs} = force field sections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{BondBond Coeffs, BondAngle Coeffs, MiddleBondTorsion Coeffs,    EndBondTorsion Coeffs, AngleTorsion Coeffs, AngleAngleTorsion Coeffs,    BondBond13 Coeffs, AngleAngle Coeffs} = class 2 force field sections

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These keywords will check an appended comment for a match with the
currently defined style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms, Pair Coeffs, PairIJ Coeffs, Bond Coeffs, Angle Coeffs, Dihedral Coeffs, Improper Coeffs}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, these lines:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Atoms \PYGZsh{} sphere
Pair Coeffs \PYGZsh{} lj/cut
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will check if the currently\sphinxhyphen{}defined {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere}, and the current {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut}.
If not, LAMMPS will issue a warning to indicate that the data file
section likely does not contain the correct number or type of
parameters expected for the currently\sphinxhyphen{}defined style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each section is listed below in alphabetic order.  The format of each
section is described including the number of lines it must contain and
rules (if any) for where it can appear in the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any individual line in the various sections can have a trailing
comment starting with “\#” for annotation purposes. There must be at least
one blank between valid content and the comment. E.g. in the
Atoms section:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
10 1 17 \PYGZhy{}1.0 10.0 5.0 6.0   \PYGZsh{} salt ion
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle Coeffs} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per angle type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID coeffs

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID = angle type (1\PYGZhy{}N)
coeffs = list of coeffs
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
6 70 108.5 0 0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number and meaning of the coefficients are specific to the defined
angle style.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} commands for details.  Coefficients can
also be set via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command in the
input script.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angle Type Labels} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per angle type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID label

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID = angle type (1\PYGZhy{}N)
label = alphanumeric type label
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Define alphanumeric type labels for each numeric angle type.  These
can be used in the Angles section in place of a numeric type, but only
if the this section appears before the Angles section.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the
allowed syntax of type labels and a general discussion of how type
labels can be used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{AngleAngle Coeffs} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per improper type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID coeffs
\begin{sphinxalltt}
ID = improper type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
coeffs = list of coeffs (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}})
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{AngleAngleTorsion Coeffs} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per dihedral type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID coeffs
\begin{sphinxalltt}
ID = dihedral type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
coeffs = list of coeffs (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_coeff}}}})
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Angles} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per angle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID type atom1 atom2 atom3

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID = number of angle (1\PYGZhy{}Nangles)
type = angle type (1\PYGZhy{}Nangletype, or type label)
atom1,atom2,atom3 = IDs of 1st,2nd,3rd atom in angle
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
example:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
2 2 17 29 430
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The three atoms are ordered linearly within the angle.  Thus the central
atom (around which the angle is computed) is the atom2 in the list.
E.g. H,O,H for a water molecule.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Angles} section must appear
after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All values in this section must be integers (1, not 1.0).  However,
the type can be a numeric value or an alphanumeric label.  The latter
is only allowed if the type label has been defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} command or an Angle Type Labels section
earlier in the data file.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed syntax of type labels
and a general discussion of how type labels can be used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{AngleTorsion Coeffs} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per dihedral type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID coeffs
\begin{sphinxalltt}
ID = dihedral type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
coeffs = list of coeffs (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_coeff}}}})
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atom Type Labels} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per atom type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID label

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID = numeric atom type (1\PYGZhy{}N)
label = alphanumeric type label
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Define alphanumeric type labels for each numeric atom type.  These
can be used in the Atoms section in place of a numeric type, but only
if the Atom Type Labels section appears before the Atoms section.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the
allowed syntax of type labels and a general discussion of how type
labels can be used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: depends on atom style

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section must appear in the data file if natoms \textgreater{} 0 in the
header section.  The atoms can be listed in any order.  These are the
line formats for each {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} in LAMMPS.  As
discussed below, each line can optionally have 3 flags (nx,ny,nz)
appended to it, which indicate which image of a periodic simulation
box the atom is in.  These may be important to include for some kinds
of analysis.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For orthogonal and restricted and general triclinic simulation
boxes, the atom coordinates (x,y,z) listed in this section should
be inside the corresponding simulation box.  For restricted
triclinic boxes that means the parallelepiped defined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo
xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo zhi}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy xz yz}, keywords.  For general
triclinic boxes that means the parallelepiped defined by the 3 edge
vectors and origin specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{avec}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bvec}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvec}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{abc origin} header keywords.  See the discussion in the header
section above about how atom coordinates outside the simulation box
are (or are not) remapped to be inside the box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values have these meanings and units, listed alphabetically:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID = integer ID of atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}type = type of atom (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntype, or type label)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bodyflag = 1 for body particles, 0 for point particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ccN = chemical concentration for tDPD particles for each species (mole/volume units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cradius = contact radius for SMD particles (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cs\_re,cs\_im = real/imaginary parts of wave packet coefficients

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cv = heat capacity (need units) for SPH particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
density = density of particle (mass/distance\textasciicircum{}3 or mass/distance\textasciicircum{}2 or mass/distance units, depending on dimensionality of particle)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
diameter = diameter of spherical atom (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
edpd\_temp = temperature for eDPD particles (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
edpd\_cv = volumetric heat capacity for eDPD particles (energy/temperature/volume units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ellipsoidflag = 1 for ellipsoidal particles, 0 for point particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eradius = electron radius (or fixed\sphinxhyphen{}core radius)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
esph = energy (need units) for SPH particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
espin = electron spin (+1/\sphinxhyphen{}1), 0 = nuclei, 2 = fixed\sphinxhyphen{}core, 3 = pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}cores (i.e. ECP)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
etag = integer ID of electron that each wave packet belongs to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kradius = kernel radius for SMD particles (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lineflag = 1 for line segment particles, 0 for point or spherical particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mass = mass of particle (mass units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
molecule\sphinxhyphen{}ID = integer ID of molecule the atom belongs to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mux,muy,muz = components of dipole moment of atom (dipole units) (see general triclinic note below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
q = charge on atom (charge units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rho = density (need units) for SPH particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sp = magnitude of magnetic spin of atom (Bohr magnetons)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spx,spy,spz = components of magnetic spin of atom (unit vector) (see general triclinic note below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
template\sphinxhyphen{}atom = which atom within a template molecule the atom is

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
template\sphinxhyphen{}index = which molecule within the molecule template the atom is part of

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
theta = internal temperature of a DPD particle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
triangleflag = 1 for triangular particles, 0 for point or spherical particles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
volume = volume of Peridynamic particle (distance\textasciicircum{}3 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x,y,z = coordinates of atom (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x0,y0,z0 = original (strain\sphinxhyphen{}free) coordinates of atom (distance
units) (see general triclinic note below)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The units for these quantities depend on the unit style; see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For 2d simulations, the atom coordinate z must be specified as 0.0.
If the data file is created by another program, then z values for a 2d
simulation can be within epsilon of 0.0, and LAMMPS will force them to
zero.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the data file defines a general triclinic box, then the
following per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values in the list above are per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors
which imply an orientation: (mux,muy,muz) and (spx,spy,spz).  This
means they should be specified consistent with the general
triclinic box and its orientation relative to the standard x,y,z
coordinate axes.  For example a dipole moment vector which will be
in the +x direction once LAMMPS converts from a general to
restricted triclinic box, should be specified in the data file in
the direction of the \sphinxstylestrong{A} edge vector.  Likewise the (x0,y0,z0)
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom strain\sphinxhyphen{}free coordinates should be inside the general
triclinic simulation box as explained in the note above.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto triclinic}}}} doc page for more details.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID is used to identify the atom throughout the simulation and
in dump files.  Normally, it is a unique value from 1 to Natoms for
each atom.  Unique values larger than Natoms can be used, but they
will cause extra memory to be allocated on each processor, if an atom
map array is used, but not if an atom map hash is used; see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify}}}} command for details.  If an atom map is
not used (e.g. an atomic system with no bonds), and you don’t care if
unique atom IDs appear in dump files, then the atom\sphinxhyphen{}IDs can all be set
to 0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom\sphinxhyphen{}type can be a numeric value or an alphanumeric label.  The
latter is only allowed if the type label has been defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} command or an Atom Type Labels section
earlier in the data file.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed syntax of type labels
and a general discussion of how type labels can be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The molecule ID is a second identifier attached to an atom.  Normally, it
is a number from 1 to N, identifying which molecule the atom belongs
to.  It can be 0 if it is a non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded atom or if you don’t care to
keep track of molecule assignments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The diameter specifies the size of a finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particle.
It can be set to 0.0, which means that atom is a point particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ellipsoidflag, lineflag, triangleflag, and bodyflag determine
whether the particle is a finite\sphinxhyphen{}size ellipsoid or line or triangle or
body of finite size, or whether the particle is a point particle.
Additional attributes must be defined for each ellipsoid, line,
triangle, or body in the corresponding \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ellipsoids}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Lines},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Triangles}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bodies} section.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}index} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}atom} are only defined used by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style template}}}}.  In this case the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command is used to define a molecule template
which contains one or more molecules (as separate files).  If an atom
belongs to one of those molecules, its \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}index} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}atom}
are both set to positive integers; if not the values are both 0.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}index} is which molecule (1 to Nmols) the atom belongs to.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}atom} is which atom (1 to Natoms) within the molecule
the atom is.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some pair styles and fixes and computes that operate on finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
particles allow for a mixture of finite\sphinxhyphen{}size and point particles.  See
the doc pages of individual commands for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles, the density is used in conjunction with the
particle volume to set the mass of each particle as mass = density *
volume.  In this context, volume can be a 3d quantity (for spheres or
ellipsoids), a 2d quantity (for triangles), or a 1d quantity (for line
segments).  If the volume is 0.0, meaning a point particle, then the
density value is used as the mass.  One exception is for the body atom
style, in which case the mass of each particle (body or point
particle) is specified explicitly.  This is because the volume of the
body is unknown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for 2d simulations of spheres, this command will treat them
as spheres when converting density to mass.  However, they can also be
modeled as 2d discs (circles) if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set density/disc}}}}
command is used to reset their mass after the read\_data command is
used.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword can also be used with time integration fixes,
such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/sphere}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
nvt/sphere}}}} to time integrate their motion as 2d
discs (not 3d spheres), by changing their moment of inertia.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom\_style hybrid, following the 5 initial values
(ID,type,x,y,z), specific values for each sub\sphinxhyphen{}style must be listed.
The order of the sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles is the same as they were listed in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} command.  The specific values for each
sub\sphinxhyphen{}style are those that are not the 5 standard ones (ID,type,x,y,z).
For example, for the “charge” sub\sphinxhyphen{}style, a “q” value would appear.
For the “full” sub\sphinxhyphen{}style, a “molecule\sphinxhyphen{}ID” and “q” would appear.  These
are listed in the same order they appear as listed above.  Thus if

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZus{}style hybrid charge sphere
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
were used in the input script, each atom line would have these fields:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZhy{}ID atom\PYGZhy{}type x y z q diameter density
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if a non\sphinxhyphen{}standard value is defined by multiple sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles,
it only appears once in the atom line.  E.g. the atom line for
atom\_style hybrid dipole full would list “q” only once, with the
dipole sub\sphinxhyphen{}style fields; “q” does not appear with the full sub\sphinxhyphen{}style
fields.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZhy{}ID atom\PYGZhy{}type x y z q mux muy myz molecule\PYGZhy{}ID
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom lines specify the (x,y,z) coordinates of atoms.  These can be
inside or outside the simulation box.  When the data file is read,
LAMMPS wraps coordinates outside the box back into the box for
dimensions that are periodic.  As discussed above, if an atom is
outside the box in a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension, it will be lost.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS always stores atom coordinates as values which are inside the
simulation box.  It also stores 3 flags which indicate which image of
the simulation box (in each dimension) the atom would be in if its
coordinates were unwrapped across periodic boundaries.  An image flag
of 0 means the atom is still inside the box when unwrapped.  A value
of 2 means add 2 box lengths to get the unwrapped coordinate.  A value
of \sphinxhyphen{}1 means subtract 1 box length to get the unwrapped coordinate.
LAMMPS updates these flags as atoms cross periodic boundaries during
the simulation.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command can output atom
coordinates in wrapped or unwrapped form, as well as the 3 image
flags.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the data file, atom lines (all lines or none of them) can
optionally list 3 trailing integer values (nx,ny,nz), which are used
to initialize the atom’s image flags.  If nx,ny,nz values are not
listed in the data file, LAMMPS initializes them to 0.  Note that the
image flags are immediately updated if an atom’s coordinates need to
wrapped back into the simulation box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is only important to set image flags correctly in a data file if a
simulation model relies on unwrapped coordinates for some calculation;
otherwise they can be left unspecified.  Examples of LAMMPS commands
that use unwrapped coordinates internally are as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Atoms in a rigid body (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small}}}}) must have consistent image flags, so that
when the atoms are unwrapped, they are near each other, i.e. as a
single body.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the {\hyperref[\detokenize{replicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{replicate}}}} command is used to generate a larger
system, image flags must be consistent for bonded atoms when the bond
crosses a periodic boundary.  I.e. the values of the image flags
should be different by 1 (in the appropriate dimension) for the two
atoms in such a bond.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you plan to {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} image flags and perform post\sphinxhyphen{}analysis
that will unwrap atom coordinates, it may be important that a
continued run (restarted from a data file) begins with image flags
that are consistent with the previous run.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If your system is an infinite periodic crystal with bonds then
it is impossible to have fully consistent image flags.  This is because
some bonds will cross periodic boundaries and connect two atoms with the
same image flag.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom velocities and other atom quantities not defined above are set to
0.0 when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section is read.  Velocities can be set later by
a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Velocities} section in the data file or by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} command in the input script.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Bodies} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more lines per body

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
first line syntax: atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID Ninteger Ndouble

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Ninteger = \PYGZsh{} of integer quantities for this particle
Ndouble = \PYGZsh{} of floating\PYGZhy{}point quantities for this particle
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0 or more integer lines with total of Ninteger values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0 or more double lines with total of Ndouble values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
12 3 6
2 3 2
1.0 2.0 3.0 1.0 2.0 4.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
12 0 14
1.0 2.0 3.0 1.0 2.0 4.0 1.0
2.0 3.0 1.0 2.0 4.0 4.0 2.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bodies} section must appear if {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style body}}}}
is used and any atoms listed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section have a bodyflag =
1.  The number of bodies should be specified in the header section via
the “bodies” keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each body can have a variable number of integer and/or floating\sphinxhyphen{}point
values.  The number and meaning of the values is defined by the body
style, as described in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto body}}}} doc page.
The body style is given as an argument to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style body}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Ninteger and Ndouble values determine how many integer and
floating\sphinxhyphen{}point values are specified for this particle.  Ninteger and
Ndouble can be as large as needed and can be different for every body.
Integer values are then listed next on subsequent lines.  Lines are
read one at a time until Ninteger values are read.  Floating\sphinxhyphen{}point
values follow on subsequent lines, Again lines are read one at a time
until Ndouble values are read.  Note that if there are no values of a
particular type, no lines appear for that type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bodies} section must appear after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section.

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ellipsoids} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per ellipsoid

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID shapex shapey shapez quatw quati quatj quatk

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZhy{}ID = ID of atom which is an ellipsoid
shapex,shapey,shapez = 3 diameters of ellipsoid (distance units)
quatw,quati,quatj,quatk = quaternion components for orientation of atom
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
12 1 2 1 1 0 0 0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ellipsoids} section must appear if {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}} is used and any atoms are listed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section
with an ellipsoidflag = 1.  The number of ellipsoids should be
specified in the header section via the “ellipsoids” keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 3 shape values specify the 3 diameters or aspect ratios of a
finite\sphinxhyphen{}size ellipsoidal particle, when it is oriented along the 3
coordinate axes.  They must all be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatw}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{quati}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatj}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatk} set the orientation
of the atom as a quaternion (4\sphinxhyphen{}vector).  Note that the shape
attributes specify the aspect ratios of an ellipsoidal particle, which
is oriented by default with its x\sphinxhyphen{}axis along the simulation box’s
x\sphinxhyphen{}axis, and similarly for y and z.  If this body is rotated (via the
right\sphinxhyphen{}hand rule) by an angle theta around a unit vector (a,b,c), then
the quaternion that represents its new orientation is given by
(cos(theta/2), a*sin(theta/2), b*sin(theta/2), c*sin(theta/2)).  These
4 components are quatw, quati, quatj, and quatk as specified above.
LAMMPS normalizes each atom’s quaternion in case (a,b,c) is not
specified as a unit vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the data file defines a general triclinic box, then the quaternion
for each ellipsoid should be specified for its orientation relative to
the standard x,y,z coordinate axes.  When the system is converted to a
restricted triclinic box, the ellipsoid quaternions will be altered to
reflect the new orientation of the ellipsoid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ellipsoids} section must appear after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section.

one line per improper

ID = number of improper (1\PYGZhy{}Nimpropers)

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering of the 4 atoms determines the definition of the improper
angle used in the formula for each {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper style}}}}.  See the doc pages for individual styles for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All values in this section must be integers (1, not 1.0).  However,

earlier in the data file.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed syntax of type labels
and a general discussion of how type labels can be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Lines} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per line segment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID x1 y1 x2 y2

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZhy{}ID = ID of atom which is a line segment
x1,y1 = 1st end point
x2,y2 = 2nd end point
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
12 1.0 0.0 2.0 0.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Lines} section must appear if {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style line}}}}
is used and any atoms are listed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section with a
lineflag = 1.  The number of lines should be specified in the header
section via the “lines” keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 2 end points are the end points of the line segment.  They should
be values close to the center point of the line segment specified in
the Atoms section of the data file, even if individual end points are
outside the simulation box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering of the 2 points should be such that using a right\sphinxhyphen{}hand
rule to cross the line segment with a unit vector in the +z direction,
gives an “outward” normal vector perpendicular to the line segment.
I.e. normal = (c2\sphinxhyphen{}c1) x (0,0,1).  This orientation may be important
for defining some interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the data file defines a general triclinic box, then the x1,y1 and
x2,y2 values for each line segment should be specified for its
orientation relative to the standard x,y,z coordinate axes.  When the
system is converted to a restricted triclinic box, the x1,y1,x2,y2
values will be altered to reflect the new orientation of the line
segment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Lines} section must appear after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Masses} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per atom type

line syntax: ID mass

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID = atom type (1\PYGZhy{}N or atom type label)

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This defines the mass of each atom type.  This can also be set via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}} command in the input script.  This section cannot be
used for atom styles that define a mass for individual atoms \sphinxhyphen{}
e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using type labels instead of atom type numbers is only allowed if the
type label has been defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} command or
a Atom Type Labels section earlier in the data file.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed
syntax of type labels and a general discussion of how type labels can be
used.
