\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pair Coeffs} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per atom type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID coeffs

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID = atom type (1\PYGZhy{}N)
coeffs = list of coeffs
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
3 0.022 2.35197 0.022 2.35197
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number and meaning of the coefficients are specific to the defined
pair style.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} commands for details.  Since pair
coefficients for types I != J are not specified, these will be
generated automatically by the pair style’s mixing rule.  See the
individual pair\_style doc pages and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify mix}}}} command for details.  Pair coefficients can also be set
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command in the input script.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{PairIJ Coeffs} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per pair of atom types for all I,J with I \textless{}= J

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: ID1 ID2 coeffs

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID1 = atom type I = 1\PYGZhy{}N
ID2 = atom type J = I\PYGZhy{}N, with I \PYGZlt{}= J
coeffs = list of coeffs
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
3 3 0.022 2.35197 0.022 2.35197
3 5 0.022 2.35197 0.022 2.35197
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This section must have N*(N+1)/2 lines where N = \# of atom types.
The number and meaning of the coefficients are specific to the defined
pair style.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} commands for details.  Since pair
coefficients for types I != J are all specified, these values will
turn off the default mixing rule defined by the pair style.  See the
individual pair\_style doc pages and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify mix}}}} command for details.  Pair coefficients can also be set
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command in the input script.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Triangles} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per triangle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 x3 y3 z3

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZhy{}ID = ID of atom which is a line segment
x1,y1,z1 = 1st corner point
x2,y2,z2 = 2nd corner point
x3,y3,z3 = 3rd corner point
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
12 0.0 0.0 0.0 2.0 0.0 1.0 0.0 2.0 1.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Triangles} section must appear if {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tri}}}} is used and any atoms are listed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section
with a triangleflag = 1.  The number of lines should be specified in
the header section via the “triangles” keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 3 corner points are the corner points of the triangle.  They
should be values close to the center point of the triangle specified
in the Atoms section of the data file, even if individual corner
points are outside the simulation box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering of the 3 points should be such that using a right\sphinxhyphen{}hand
rule to go from point1 to point2 to point3 gives an “outward” normal
vector to the face of the triangle.  I.e. normal = (c2\sphinxhyphen{}c1) x (c3\sphinxhyphen{}c1).
This orientation may be important for defining some interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the data file defines a general triclinic box, then the x1,y1,z1
and x2,y2,z2 and x3,y3,z3 values for each triangle should be specified
for its orientation relative to the standard x,y,z coordinate axes.
When the system is converted to a restricted triclinic box, the
x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2,x3,y3,z3 values will be altered to reflect the new
orientation of the triangle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Triangles} section must appear after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Velocities} section:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: depends on atom style

\end{itemize}


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabulary}{\linewidth}[t]{TT}
\sphinxtoprule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
all styles except those listed
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID vx vy vz
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
electron
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID vx vy vz ervel
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
ellipsoid
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID vx vy vz lx ly lz
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
sphere
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID vx vy vz wx wy wz
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
hybrid
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID vx vy vz sub\sphinxhyphen{}style1 sub\sphinxhyphen{}style2 …
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabulary}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the keywords have these meanings:
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
vx,vy,vz = translational velocity of atom
lx,ly,lz = angular momentum of aspherical atom
wx,wy,wz = angular velocity of spherical atom
ervel = electron radial velocity (0 for fixed\PYGZhy{}core)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The velocity lines can appear in any order.  This section can only be
used after an \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section.  This is because the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Atoms} section
must have assigned a unique atom ID to each atom so that velocities
can be assigned to them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Vx, vy, vz, and ervel are in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} of velocity.  Lx, ly,
lz are in units of angular momentum (distance\sphinxhyphen{}velocity\sphinxhyphen{}mass).  Wx, Wy,
Wz are in units of angular velocity (radians/time).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the data file defines a general triclinic box, then each of the 3
vectors (translational velocity, angular momentum, angular velocity)
should be specified for the rotated coordinate axes of the general
triclinic box.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto triclinic}}}} doc
page for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom\_style hybrid, following the 4 initial values (ID,vx,vy,vz),
specific values for each sub\sphinxhyphen{}style must be listed.  The order of the
sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles is the same as they were listed in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} command.  The sub\sphinxhyphen{}style specific values
are those that are not the 5 standard ones (ID,vx,vy,vz).  For
example, for the “sphere” sub\sphinxhyphen{}style, “wx”, “wy”, “wz” values would
appear.  These are listed in the same order they appear as listed
above.  Thus if

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{atom\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{electron}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
were used in the input script, each velocity line would have these
fields:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
atom\PYGZhy{}ID vx vy vz ervel wx wy wz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Translational velocities can also be (re)set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} command in the input script.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{read_data:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To read gzipped data files, you must compile LAMMPS with the
\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_GZIP option.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build settings}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Label maps are currently not supported when using the KOKKOS package.

\section{read\_dump command}
\label{\detokenize{read_dump:read-dump-command}}\label{\detokenize{read_dump:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{read_dump::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{read_dump:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nstep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{field1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{field2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of dump file to read

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nstep = snapshot timestep to read from file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more fields may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
field = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ix} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x},\sphinxstyleemphasis{y},\sphinxstyleemphasis{z} = atom coordinates
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx},\sphinxstyleemphasis{vy},\sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} = velocity components
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} = charge
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ix},\sphinxstyleemphasis{iy},\sphinxstyleemphasis{iz} = image flags in each dimension
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx},\sphinxstyleemphasis{fy},\sphinxstyleemphasis{fz} = force components
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{timestep} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{replace} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{purge} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trim} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{label} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaled} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wrapped} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{format}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} value = Nfiles = how many parallel dump files exist
\sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = replace simulation box with dump box
\sphinxstyleemphasis{timestep} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = reset simulation timestep with dump timestep
\sphinxstyleemphasis{replace} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = overwrite atoms with dump atoms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{purge} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = delete all atoms before adding dump atoms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{trim} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = trim atoms not in dump snapshot
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{keep} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = add new dump atoms to system
\sphinxstyleemphasis{label} value = field column
  field = one of the listed fields or \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}
  column = label on corresponding column in dump file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scaled} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = coords in dump file are scaled/unscaled
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wrapped} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = coords in dump file are wrapped/unwrapped
\sphinxstyleemphasis{format} values = format of dump file, must be last keyword if used
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} = native LAMMPS dump file
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} = XYZ file
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{adios} {[}\sphinxstyleemphasis{timeout} value{]} = dump file written by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_adios::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump adios}}}} command
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{timeout} = specify waiting time for the arrival of the timestep when running concurrently.
              The value is a float number and is interpreted in seconds.
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} style path = VMD molfile plugin interface
    style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or others supported by molfile plugins
    path = optional path for location of molfile plugins
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{read_dump:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read atom information from a dump file to overwrite the current atom
coordinates, and optionally the atom velocities and image flags, the
simulation timestep, and the simulation box dimensions.  This is useful
for restarting a run from a particular snapshot in a dump file.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
commands for alternative methods to do this.  Also see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command for a means of reading multiple snapshots
from a dump file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that a simulation box must already be defined before using the
read\_dump command.  This can be done by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands.  The read\_dump command can
reset the simulation box dimensions, as explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that reading per\sphinxhyphen{}atom information from a dump snapshot is
limited to the atom coordinates, velocities and image flags, as
explained below.  Other atom properties, which may be necessary to run
a valid simulation, such as atom charge, or bond topology information
for a molecular system, are not read from (or may not even be contained
in) dump files.  Thus this auxiliary information should be defined in
the usual way, e.g. in a data file read in by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command, before using the read\_dump command, or by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}}
command, after the dump snapshot is read.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If the dump filename specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} ends with “.gz”, the dump
file is read in gzipped format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can read dump files that were written (in parallel) to multiple
files via the “\%” wild\sphinxhyphen{}card character in the dump file name.  If any
specified dump file name contains a “\%”, they must all contain it.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command for details.
The “\%” wild\sphinxhyphen{}card character is only supported by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} format
for dump files, described next.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If reading parallel dump files, you must also use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} keyword
to tell LAMMPS how many parallel files exist, via its specified
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfiles} value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of the dump file is selected through the \sphinxstyleemphasis{format} keyword.
If specified, it must be the last keyword used, since all remaining
arguments are passed on to the dump reader.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} format is
for native LAMMPS dump files, written with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump atom}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} format is for generic XYZ
formatted dump files.  These formats take no additional values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} format supports reading data through using the \sphinxhref{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd}{VMD}
molfile plugin interface. This dump reader format is only available,
if the MOLFILE package has been installed when compiling
LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} format takes one or two additional values.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{style}
value determines the file format to be used and can be any format that
the molfile plugins support, such as DCD or XYZ.  Note that DCD dump
files can be written by LAMMPS via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump dcd}}}} command.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{path} value specifies a list of directories which LAMMPS will
search for the molfile plugins appropriate to the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{style}.
The syntax of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{path} value is like other search paths: it can
contain multiple directories separated by a colon (or semicolon on
windows).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{path} keyword is optional and defaults to “.”,
i.e. the current directory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{adios} format supports reading data that was written by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_adios::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump adios}}}} command. The
entire dump is read in parallel across all the processes, dividing
the atoms evenly among the processes. The number of writers that
has written the dump file does not matter. Using the adios style for
dump and read\_dump is a convenient way to dump all atoms from \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
writers and read it back by \sphinxstyleemphasis{M} readers. If one is running two
LAMMPS instances concurrently where one dumps data and the other is
reading it with the rerun command, the timeout option can be specified
to wait on the reader side for the arrival of the requested step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for other dump format readers may be added in the future.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Global information is first read from the dump file, namely timestep
and box information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dump file is scanned for a snapshot with a timestamp that matches
the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nstep}.  This means the LAMMPS timestep the dump file
snapshot was written on for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{adios} formats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The list of timestamps available in an adios .bp file is stored in the
variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntimestep}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
console

\PYGZdl{} bpls dump.bp \PYGZhy{}d ntimestep
  uint64\PYGZus{}t  ntimestep  5*scalar
    (0)    0 50 100 150 200
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} formats do not store the timestep.
For these formats, timesteps are numbered logically, in a sequential
manner, starting from 0.  Thus to access the 10th snapshot in an \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mofile} formatted dump file, use \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nstep} = 9.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dimensions of the simulation box for the selected snapshot are
also read; see the \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} keyword discussion below.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{native}
format, an error is generated if the snapshot is for a triclinic box
and the current simulation box is orthogonal or vice versa.  A warning
will be generated if the snapshot box boundary conditions (periodic,
shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped, etc) do not match the current simulation boundary
conditions, but the boundary condition information in the snapshot is
otherwise ignored.  See the “boundary” command for more details. The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{adios} reader does the same as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} format reader.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} format, no information about the box is available, so
you must set the \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} flag to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.  See details below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} format, reading simulation box information is
typically supported, but the location of the simulation box origin is
lost and no explicit information about periodicity or
orthogonal/triclinic box shape is available.  The MOLFILE package
makes a best effort to guess based on heuristics, but this may not
always work perfectly.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom information from the dump file snapshot is then read from the
dump file snapshot.  This corresponds to the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{fields} listed
in the read\_dump command.  It is an error to specify a z\sphinxhyphen{}dimension
field, namely \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iz}, for a 2d simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For dump files in \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} format, each column of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data has a
text label listed in the file.  A matching label for each field must
appear, e.g. the label “vy” for the field \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
fields any of the following labels are considered a match:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
x, xs, xu, xsu for field \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}
y, ys, yu, ysu for field \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}
z, zs, zu, zsu for field \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The meaning of xs (scaled), xu (unwrapped), and xsu (scaled and
unwrapped) is explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command doc page.
These labels are searched for in the list of column labels in the dump
file, in order, until a match is found.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dump file must also contain atom IDs, with a column label of “id”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{keep}, as
discussed below, the dump file must contain atom types, with a column
label of “type”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a column label you want to read from the dump file is not a match
to a specified field, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{label} keyword can be used to specify the
specific column label from the dump file to associate with that field.
An example is if a time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged coordinate is written to the dump
file via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}} command.  The column
will then have a label corresponding to the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID rather than “x” or
“xs”.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{label} keyword can also be used to specify new column
labels for fields \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For dump files in \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} format, only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} fields are
supported.  The dump file does not store atom IDs, so these are
assigned consecutively to the atoms as they appear in the dump file,
starting from 1.  Thus you should ensure that order of atoms is
consistent from snapshot to snapshot in the XYZ dump file.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify sort}}}} command if the XYZ dump file
was written by LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For dump files in \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} format, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} fields can be specified.  However, not all molfile formats store
velocities, or their respective plugins may not support reading of
velocities.  The molfile dump files do not store atom IDs, so these
are assigned consecutively to the atoms as they appear in the dump
file, starting from 1.  Thus you should ensure that order of atoms are
consistent from snapshot to snapshot in the molfile dump file.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify sort}}}} command if the dump file
was written by LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{adios} format supports all fields that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} format supports
except for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} charge field.
The list of fields stored in an adios .bp file is recorded in the attributes
\sphinxstyleemphasis{columns} (array of short strings) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{columnstr} (space\sphinxhyphen{}separated single string).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
console

\PYGZdl{} bpls \PYGZhy{}la dump.bp column*
  string    columns            attr   = \PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}id\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}type\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}x\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}y\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}z\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}vx\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}vy\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}vz\PYGZdq{}\PYGZcb{}
  string    columnstr          attr   = \PYGZdq{}id type x y z vx vy vz \PYGZdq{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Information from the dump file snapshot is used to overwrite or
replace properties of the current system.  There are various options
for how this is done, determined by the specified fields and optional
keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 3Aug2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The timestep of the snapshot becomes the current timestep for the
simulation unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{timestep} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} value
(default setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}).  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}
command if you wish to change this to a different value after the dump
snapshot is read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} value, then the current
simulation box dimensions are replaced by the dump snapshot box
dimensions.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} value, the
current simulation box is unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{purge} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} value, then all
current atoms in the system are deleted before any of the operations
invoked by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{replace}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{trim}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keywords take place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{replace} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} value, then atoms
with IDs that are in both the current system and the dump snapshot
have their properties overwritten by field values.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{replace}
keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} value, atoms with IDs that are in
both the current system and the dump snapshot are not modified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{trim} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} value, then atoms with
IDs that are in the current system but not in the dump snapshot are
deleted.  These atoms are unaffected if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{trim} keyword is
specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} value (default), then
dump file atoms with IDs that are not in the current system are not
added to the system.  They are simply ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} value is specified, the atoms with new IDs are added to the
system but their atom IDs are not preserved.  Instead, after all the
atoms are added, new IDs are assigned to them in the same manner as is
described for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command.  Basically
the largest existing atom ID in the system is identified, and all the
added atoms are assigned IDs that consecutively follow the largest ID.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a \sphinxstyleemphasis{keep} value is specified, the atoms with new IDs are added to
the system and their atom IDs are preserved.  This may lead to
non\sphinxhyphen{}contiguous IDs for the combined system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that atoms added via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword will only have the
attributes read from the dump file due to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{field} arguments.  For
example, if \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} is not specified as a field, a
value of 0.0 is used for added atoms.  Added atoms must have an atom
type, so this value must appear in the dump file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any other attributes (e.g. charge or particle diameter for spherical
particles) will be set to default values, the same as if the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command were used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom coordinates read from the dump file are first converted into
unscaled coordinates, relative to the box dimensions of the snapshot.
These coordinates are then be assigned to an existing or new atom in
the current simulation.  The coordinates will then be remapped to the
simulation box, whether it is the original box or the dump snapshot
box.  If periodic boundary conditions apply, this means the atom will
be remapped back into the simulation box if necessary.  If shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrap
boundary conditions apply, the new coordinates may change the
simulation box dimensions.  If fixed boundary conditions apply, the
atom will be lost if it is outside the simulation box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{native} format dump files, the 3 xyz image flags for an atom in
the dump file are set to the corresponding values appearing in the
dump file if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ix}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iz} fields are specified.  If not
specified, the image flags for replaced atoms are not changed and
image flags for new atoms are set to default values.  If coordinates
read from the dump file are in unwrapped format (e.g. \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}) then the
image flags for read\sphinxhyphen{}in atoms are also set to default values.  The
remapping procedure described in the previous paragraph will then
change images flags for all atoms (old and new) if periodic boundary
conditions are applied to remap an atom back into the simulation box.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you get a warning about inconsistent image flags after
reading in a dump snapshot, it means one or more pairs of bonded atoms
now have inconsistent image flags.  As discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Errors_common::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Errors common}}}} page this may or may not cause problems
for subsequent simulations.  One way this can happen is if you read
image flag fields from the dump file but do not also use the dump file
box parameters.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS knows how to compute unscaled and remapped coordinates for the
snapshot column labels discussed above, e.g. \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xs}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xsu}.
If another column label is assigned to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} field via
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{label} keyword, e.g. for coordinates output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}} command, then LAMMPS needs to know whether
the coordinate information in the dump file is scaled and/or wrapped.
This can be set via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaled} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wrapped} keywords.  Note that
the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaled} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wrapped} keywords is ignored for fields
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{label} keyword is not used to assign a
column label to that field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scaled/unscaled and wrapped/unwrapped setting must be identical
for any of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} fields that are specified.  Thus you
cannot read \sphinxstyleemphasis{xs} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yu} from the dump file.  Also, if the dump file
coordinates are scaled and the simulation box is triclinic, then all 3
of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} fields must be specified, since they are all
needed to generate absolute, unscaled coordinates.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{read_dump:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To read gzipped dump files, you must compile LAMMPS with the
\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_GZIP option.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build settings}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} dump file formats are part of the MOLFILE package.
They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that packages.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To write and read adios .bp files, you must compile LAMMPS with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-adios}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{ADIOS}}}} package.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{read_dump:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_molfile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump molfile}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_adios::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump adios}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{read_dump:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are box = yes, timestep = yes, replace = yes, purge = no,
trim = no, add = no, scaled = no, wrapped = yes, and format = native.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{read\_restart@\spxentry{read\_restart}}\ignorespaces 

\section{read\_restart command}
\label{\detokenize{read_restart:read-restart-command}}\label{\detokenize{read_restart:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{read_restart::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{read_restart:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}restart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of binary restart file to read in

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{read_restart:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}restart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{save.10000}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}restart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restart.}\PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{read_restart:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read in a previously saved system configuration from a restart file.
This allows continuation of a previous run.  Details about what
information is stored (and not stored) in a restart file is given below.
Basically this operation will re\sphinxhyphen{}create the simulation box with all its
atoms and their attributes as well as some related global settings, at
the point in time it was written to the restart file by a previous
simulation.  The simulation box will be partitioned into a regular 3d
grid of rectangular bricks, one per processor, based on the number of
processors in the current simulation and the settings of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{processors::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{processors}}}} command.  The partitioning can later be
changed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix balance}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,deprecated}{Deprecated since version 23Jun2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom coordinates that are found to be outside the simulation box when
reading the restart will be remapped back into the box and their image
flags updated accordingly.  This previously required specifying the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} option, but that is no longer required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restart files are saved in binary format to enable exact restarts,
meaning that the trajectories of a restarted run will precisely match
those produced by the original run had it continued on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some information about a restart file can be gathered directly from the
command line when using LAMMPS with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options:restart2info}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{\sphinxhyphen{}restart2info}}}} command line flag.  On Unix\sphinxhyphen{}like operating systems (like
Linux or macOS), one can also {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools:magic}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{configure the “file” command line
program}}}} to display basic information about a restart file

\sphinxAtStartPar
The binary restart file format was not designed with backward, forward,
or cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform compatibility in mind, so the files are only expected
to be read correctly by the same LAMMPS executable on the same platform.
Changes to the architecture, compilation settings, or LAMMPS version can
render a restart file unreadable or it may read the data incorrectly.
If you want a more portable format, you can use the data file format as
created by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}} command.  Binary restart
files can also be converted into a data file from the command line by
the LAMMPS executable that wrote them using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options:restart2data}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{\sphinxhyphen{}restart2data}}}} command line flag.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Several things can prevent exact restarts due to round\sphinxhyphen{}off effects, in
which case the trajectories in the 2 runs will slowly diverge.  These
include running on a different number of processors or changing
certain settings such as those set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{processors::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{processors}}}} commands.  LAMMPS will issue a warning in
these cases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Certain fixes will not restart exactly, though they should provide
statistically similar results.  These include {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Certain pair styles will not restart exactly, though they should
provide statistically similar results.  This is because the forces
they compute depend on atom velocities, which are used at half\sphinxhyphen{}step
values every timestep when forces are computed.  When a run restarts,
forces are initially evaluated with a full\sphinxhyphen{}step velocity, which is
different than if the run had continued.  These pair styles include
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{granular pair styles}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair dpd}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lubricate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair lubricate}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a restarted run is immediately different than the run which
produced the restart file, it could be a LAMMPS bug, so consider
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Errors_bugs::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reporting it}}}} if you think the behavior is a bug.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because restart files are binary, they may not be portable to other
machines.  In this case, you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}restart command\sphinxhyphen{}line
switch}}}} to convert a restart file to a data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to how restart files are written (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}} commands), the restart
filename can contain two wild\sphinxhyphen{}card characters.  If a “*” appears in the
filename, the directory is searched for all filenames that match the
pattern where “*” is replaced with a timestep value.  The file with the
largest timestep value is read in.  Thus, this effectively means, read
the latest restart file.  It’s useful if you want your script to
continue a run from where it left off.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command
and its “upto” option for how to specify the run command so it does not
need to be changed either.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a “\%” character appears in the restart filename, LAMMPS expects a
set of multiple files to exist.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}} commands explain how such sets are
created.  Read\_restart will first read a filename where “\%” is
replaced by “base”.  This file tells LAMMPS how many processors
created the set and how many files are in it.  Read\_restart then reads
the additional files.  For example, if the restart file was specified
as save.\% when it was written, then read\_restart reads the files
save.base, save.0, save.1, … save.P\sphinxhyphen{}1, where P is the number of
processors that created the restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that P could be the total number of processors in the previous
simulation, or some subset of those processors, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} options were used when the restart file was written; see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}} commands
for details.  The processors in the current LAMMPS simulation share
the work of reading these files; each reads a roughly equal subset of
the files.  The number of processors which created the set can be
different the number of processors in the current LAMMPS simulation.
This can be a fast mode of input on parallel machines that support
parallel I/O.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is the list of information included in a restart file, which
means these quantities do not need to be re\sphinxhyphen{}specified in the input
script that reads the restart file, though you can redefine many of
these settings after the restart file is read.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton bond}}}} (see discussion of newton command below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify}}}} settings id, map, sort

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm style}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify}}}} settings mode, cutoff, vel

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep size}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep number}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
simulation box size and shape and {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} settings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom {\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} definitions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
per\sphinxhyphen{}type atom settings such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom attributes including their group assignments and molecular topology attributes (bonds, angles, etc)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
force field styles ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle}}}}, etc)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
force field coefficients ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle}}}}, etc) in some cases (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} settings, except the compute option

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is a list of information not stored in a restart file, which
means you must re\sphinxhyphen{}issue these commands in your input script, after
reading the restart file.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton pair}}}} (see discussion of newton command below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} commands (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} commands (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} commands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} commands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor list}}}} criteria including {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} settings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_modify}}}} settings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
info for {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}} output

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} command has two settings, one for pairwise
interactions, the other for bonded.  Both settings are stored in the
restart file.  For the bond setting, the value in the file will
overwrite the current value (at the time the read\_restart command is
issued) and warn if the two values are not the same and the current
value is not the default.  For the pair setting, the value in the file
will not overwrite the current value (so that you can override the
previous run’s value), but a warning is issued if the two values are
not the same and the current value is not the default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that some force field styles (pair, bond, angle, etc) do not
store their coefficient info in restart files.  Typically these are
many\sphinxhyphen{}body or tabulated potentials which read their parameters from
separate files.  In these cases you will need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, etc
commands in your restart input script.  The doc pages for individual
force field styles mention if this is the case.  This is also true of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}} (bond hybrid, angle hybrid, etc)
commands; they do not store coefficient info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As indicated in the above list, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} used for a
simulation are not stored in the restart file.  This means the new
input script should specify all fixes it will use.  However, note that
some fixes store an internal “state” which is written to the restart
file.  This allows the fix to continue on with its calculations in a
restarted simulation.  To re\sphinxhyphen{}enable such a fix, the fix command in the
new input script must be of the same style and use the same fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID as
was used in the input script that wrote the restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a match is found, LAMMPS prints a message indicating that the fix
is being re\sphinxhyphen{}enabled.  If no match is found before the first run or
minimization is performed by the new script, the “state” information
for the saved fix is discarded.  At the time the discard occurs,
LAMMPS will also print a list of fixes for which the information is
being discarded.  See the doc pages for individual fixes for info on
which ones can be restarted in this manner.  Note that fixes which are
created internally by other LAMMPS commands (computes, fixes, etc)
will have style names which are all\sphinxhyphen{}capitalized, and IDs which are
generated internally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Likewise, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{computes}}}} used for a simulation are not stored
in the restart file.  This means the new input script should specify
all computes it will use.  However, some computes create a fix
internally to store “state” information that persists from timestep to
timestep.  An example is the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_msd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute msd}}}} command
which uses a fix to store a reference coordinate for each atom, so
that a displacement can be calculated at any later time.  If the
compute command in the new input script uses the same compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID and
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID as was used in the input script that wrote the restart file,
then it will create the same fix in the restarted run.  This means the
re\sphinxhyphen{}created fix will be re\sphinxhyphen{}enabled with the stored state information as
described in the previous paragraph, so that the compute can continue
its calculations in a consistent manner.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are a handful of commands which can be used before or between
runs which may require a system initialization.  Examples include the
“balance”, “displace\_atoms”, “delete\_atoms”, “set” (some options),
and “velocity” (some options) commands.  This is because they can
migrate atoms to new processors.  Thus they will also discard unused
“state” information from fixes.  You will know the discard has
occurred because a list of discarded fixes will be printed to the
screen and log file, as explained above.  This means that if you wish
to retain that info in a restarted run, you must re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the
relevant fixes and computes (which create fixes) before those
commands are used.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some pair styles, like the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{granular pair styles}}}}, also
use a fix to store “state” information that persists from timestep to
timestep.  In the case of granular potentials, it is contact
information between pairs of touching particles.  This info will also
be re\sphinxhyphen{}enabled in the restart script, assuming you re\sphinxhyphen{}use the same
granular pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS allows bond interactions (angle, etc) to be turned off or
deleted in various ways, which can affect how their info is stored in
a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If bonds (angles, etc) have been turned off by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command, their info
will be written to a restart file as if they are turned on.  This means
they will need to be turned off again in a new run after the restart
file is read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bonds that are broken (e.g. by a bond\sphinxhyphen{}breaking potential) are written
to the restart file as broken bonds with a type of 0.  Thus these
bonds will still be broken when the restart file is read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bonds that have been broken by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_break::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/break}}}} command have disappeared from the system.  No
information about these bonds is written to the restart file.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{region command}
\label{\detokenize{region:region-command}}\label{\detokenize{region:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{region::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{region:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the region

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{block} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cone} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cylinder} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ellipsoid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{plane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{prism} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{intersect}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} = no args
\sphinxstyleemphasis{block} args = xlo xhi ylo yhi zlo zhi
  xlo,xhi,ylo,yhi,zlo,zhi = bounds of block in all dimensions (distance units)
  xlo,xhi,ylo,yhi,zlo,zhi can be a variable
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cone} args = dim c1 c2 radlo radhi lo hi
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} = axis of cone
  c1,c2 = coords of cone axis in other 2 dimensions (distance units)
  radlo,radhi = cone radii at lo and hi end (distance units)
  lo,hi = bounds of cone in dim (distance units)
  c1,c2,radlo,radhi,lo,hi can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cylinder} args = dim c1 c2 radius lo hi
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} = axis of cylinder
  c1,c2 = coords of cylinder axis in other 2 dimensions (distance units)
  radius = cylinder radius (distance units)
    c1,c2, and radius can be a variable (see below)
  lo,hi = bounds of cylinder in dim (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ellipsoid} args = x y z a b c
  x,y,z = center of ellipsoid (distance units)
  a,b,c = half the length of the principal axes of the ellipsoid (distance units)
    x,y,z,a,b and c can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{plane} args = px py pz nx ny nz
  px,py,pz = point on the plane (distance units)
  nx,ny,nz = direction normal to plane (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{prism} args = xlo xhi ylo yhi zlo zhi xy xz yz
  xlo,xhi,ylo,yhi,zlo,zhi = bounds of untilted prism (distance units)
  xy = distance to tilt y in x direction (distance units)
  xz = distance to tilt z in x direction (distance units)
  yz = distance to tilt z in y direction (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} args = x y z radius
  x,y,z = center of sphere (distance units)
  radius = radius of sphere (distance units)
    x,y,z, and radius can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{union} args = N reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID1 reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 ...
  N = \# of regions to follow, must be 2 or greater
  reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID1,reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID2, ... = IDs of regions to join together
\sphinxstyleemphasis{intersect} args = N reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID1 reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 ...
  N = \# of regions to follow, must be 2 or greater
  reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID1,reg\sphinxhyphen{}ID2, ... = IDs of regions to intersect
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{side} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{move} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{open}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{side} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{in} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{out}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{in} = the region is inside the specified geometry
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} = the region is outside the specified geometry
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} = the geometry is defined in lattice units
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} = the geometry is defined in simulation box units
\sphinxstyleemphasis{move} args = v\_x v\_y v\_z
  v\_x,v\_y,v\_z = equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables for x,y,z displacement of region over time (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} args = v\_theta Px Py Pz Rx Ry Rz
  v\_theta = equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable for rotaton of region over time (in radians)
  Px,Py,Pz = origin for axis of rotation (distance units)
  Rx,Ry,Rz = axis of rotation vector
\sphinxstyleemphasis{open} value = integer from 1\sphinxhyphen{}6 corresponding to face index (see below)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
accelerated styles (with same args) = \sphinxstyleemphasis{block/kk}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{INF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{INF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{INF}

\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cylinder}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EDGE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
