\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{set:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set one or more properties of one or more atoms.  Since atom
properties are initially assigned by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}}
commands, this command changes those assignments.  This can be useful
for overriding the default values assigned by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command (e.g. charge = 0.0).  It can
be useful for altering pairwise and molecular force interactions,
since force\sphinxhyphen{}field coefficients are defined in terms of types.  It can
be used to change the labeling of atoms by atom type or molecule ID
when they are output in {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} files.  It can also be useful
for debugging purposes; i.e. positioning an atom at a precise location
to compute subsequent forces or energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ID} arguments determine which atoms have
their properties reset.  The remaining keywords specify which
properties to reset and what the new values are.  Some strings like
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} can be used as a style and/or a keyword.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This section describes how to select which atoms to change
the properties of, via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ID} arguments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 28Mar2023: }Support for type labels was added for selecting atoms by type

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} selects all the atoms in a range of atom IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} selects all the atoms in a range of types or type
labels.  The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} selects atoms in one of two ways.  A range
of numeric atom types can be specified.  Or a single atom type label
can be specified, e.g. “C”.  The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} selects all the atoms in
a range of molecule IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In each of the range cases, the range can be specified as a single
numeric value, or a wildcard asterisk can be used to specify a range
of values.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “n*” or “m*n”.  For
example, for the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}, if N = the number of atom types, then
an asterisk with no numeric values means all types from 1 to N.  A
leading asterisk means all types from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing
asterisk means all types from n to N (inclusive).  A middle asterisk
means all types from m to n (inclusive).  For all the styles except
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, the lowest value for the wildcard is 1; for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} it is 0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} selects all the atoms in the specified group.  The
style \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} selects all the atoms in the specified geometric
region.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} commands
for details of how to specify a group or region.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This section describes the keyword options for which properties to
change, for the selected atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that except where explicitly prohibited below, all of the
keywords allow an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\sphinxhyphen{}style or atomfile\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} to be used as the specified value(s).  If the value is a
variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where name is the
variable name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated, and its
resulting per\sphinxhyphen{}atom value used to determine the value assigned to each
selected atom.  Note that the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom value from the variable will be
ignored for atoms that are not selected via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ID}
settings explained above.  A simple way to use per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from
the variable to reset a property for all atoms is to use style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}
with \sphinxstyleemphasis{ID} = “*”; this selects all atom IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  They can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent or
spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent set of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values.  As explained on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} doc page, atomfile\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can be
used in place of atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables, and thus as arguments to the
set command.  Atomfile\sphinxhyphen{}style variables read their per\sphinxhyphen{}atoms values
from a file.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style and atomfile\sphinxhyphen{}style variables return floating point
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values.  If the values are assigned to an integer variable,
such as the molecule ID, then the floating point value is truncated to
its integer portion, e.g. a value of 2.6 would become 2.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 28Mar2023: }Support for type labels was added for setting atom, bond, angle,
dihedral, and improper types

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} sets the atom type for all selected atoms.  A specified
value can be either a numeric atom type or an atom type label. When
using a numeric type, the specified value must be from 1 to ntypes,
where ntypes was set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command or
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom types} field in the header of the data file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.  When using a type label it must
have been defined previously.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed syntax of type labels
and a general discussion of how type labels can be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/fraction} sets the atom type for a fraction of the selected
atoms.  The actual number of atoms changed is not guaranteed
to be exactly the specified fraction (0 \textless{}= \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction} \textless{}= 1), but
should be statistically close.  Random numbers are used in such a way
that a particular atom is changed or not changed, regardless of how
many processors are being used.  This keyword does not allow use of an
atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/ratio} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/subset} also set the atom type for a
fraction of the selected atoms.  The actual number of atoms changed
will be exactly the requested number.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/ratio} the specified
fraction (0 \textless{}= \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction} \textless{}= 1) determines the number.  For
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type/subset}, the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nsubset} is the number.  An iterative
algorithm is used which ensures the correct number of atoms are
selected, in a perfectly random fashion.  Which atoms are selected
will change with the number of processors used.  These keywords do not
allow use of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} sets the molecule ID for all selected atoms.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} being used must support the use of
molecule IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} set the coordinates or
charge of all selected atoms.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge}, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} being used must support the use of atomic
charge. Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} set the velocities of all
selected atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} uses the specified x,y,z values as components of a
vector to set as the orientation of the dipole moment vectors of the
selected atoms.  The magnitude of the dipole moment is set by the
length of this orientation vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole/random} randomizes the orientation of the dipole
moment vectors for the selected atoms and sets the magnitude of each
to the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dlen} value.  For 2d systems, the z component of the
orientation is set to 0.0.  Random numbers are used in such a way that
the orientation of a particular atom is the same, regardless of how
many processors are being used.  This keyword does not allow use of an
atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/atom} uses the specified g value to set the magnitude of the
magnetic spin vectors, and the x,y,z values as components of a vector
to set as the orientation of the magnetic spin vectors of the selected
atoms.  This keyword was previously called \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/atom/random} randomizes the orientation of the magnetic spin
vectors for the selected atoms and sets the magnitude of each to the
specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dlen} value.  This keyword was previously called \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/random}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius/electron} uses the specified value to set the radius of
electrons or fixed cores.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/electron} sets the spin of an electron (+/\sphinxhyphen{} 1) or indicates
nuclei (=0), fixed\sphinxhyphen{}cores (=2), or pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}cores (= 3).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat} uses the specified values to create a quaternion
(4\sphinxhyphen{}vector) that represents the orientation of the selected atoms.  The
particles must define a quaternion for their orientation
(e.g. ellipsoids, triangles, body particles) as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} command.  Note that particles defined by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}} have 3 shape parameters.  The 3
values must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero for each particle set by this command.  They
are used to specify the aspect ratios of an ellipsoidal particle,
which is oriented by default with its x\sphinxhyphen{}axis along the simulation
box’s x\sphinxhyphen{}axis, and similarly for y and z.  If this body is rotated (via
the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand rule) by an angle theta around a unit rotation vector
(a,b,c), then the quaternion that represents its new orientation is
given by (cos(theta/2), a*sin(theta/2), b*sin(theta/2),
c*sin(theta/2)).  The theta and a,b,c values are the arguments to the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quat} keyword.  LAMMPS normalizes the quaternion in case (a,b,c) was
not specified as a unit vector.  For 2d systems, the a,b,c values are
ignored, since a rotation vector of (0,0,1) is the only valid choice.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat/random} randomizes the orientation of the quaternion for
the selected atoms.  The particles must define a quaternion for their
orientation (e.g. ellipsoids, triangles, body particles) as defined by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} command.  Random numbers are used in
such a way that the orientation of a particular atom is the same,
regardless of how many processors are being used.  For 2d systems,
only orientations in the xy plane are generated.  As with keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}, for ellipsoidal particles, the 3 shape values must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero
for each particle set by this command.  This keyword does not allow
use of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter} sets the size of the selected atoms.  The particles
must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} command.  The diameter of a particle can be set to 0.0,
which means they will be treated as point particles.  Note that this
command does not adjust the particle mass, even if it was defined with
a density, e.g. via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{shape} sets the size and shape of the selected atoms.  The
particles must be ellipsoids as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style
ellipsoid}}}} command.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sz} settings
are the 3 diameters of the ellipsoid in each direction.  All 3 can be
set to the same value, which means the ellipsoid is effectively a
sphere.  They can also all be set to 0.0 which means the particle will
be treated as a point particle.  Note that this command does not
adjust the particle mass, even if it was defined with a density,
e.g. via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{length} sets the length of selected atoms.  The particles
must be line segments as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style line}}}} command.  If the specified value is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero the line
segment is (re)set to a length = the specified value, centered around
the particle position, with an orientation along the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis.  If the
specified value is 0.0, the particle will become a point particle.
Note that this command does not adjust the particle mass, even if it
was defined with a density, e.g. via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} sets the size of selected atoms.  The particles must be
triangles as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tri}}}} command.
If the specified value is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero the triangle is (re)set to be an
equilateral triangle in the xy plane with side length = the specified
value, with a centroid at the particle position, with its base
parallel to the x axis, and the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis running from the center of the
base to the top point of the triangle.  If the specified value is 0.0,
the particle will become a point particle.  Note that this command
does not adjust the particle mass, even if it was defined with a
density, e.g. via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} sets the orientation of selected atoms.  The particles
must be line segments as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style line}}}} command.  The specified value is used to set the
orientation angle of the line segments with respect to the x axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta/random} randomizes the orientation of theta for the
selected atoms.  The particles must be line segments as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style line}}}} command.  Random numbers are used in
such a way that the orientation of a particular atom is the same,
regardless of how many processors are being used.  This keyword does
not allow use of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} sets the angular momentum of selected atoms.  The
particles must be ellipsoids as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style
ellipsoid}}}} command or triangles as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tri}}}} command.  The angular momentum
vector of the particles is set to the 3 specified components.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} sets the angular velocity of selected atoms.  The
particles must be spheres as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} command.  The angular velocity vector of the particles is
set to the 3 specified components.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{mass} sets the mass of all selected particles.  The particles
must have a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mass attribute, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} command.  See the “mass” command for how to set mass
values on a per\sphinxhyphen{}type basis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{density} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/disc} also sets the mass of all selected
particles, but in a different way.  The particles must have a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
mass attribute, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}
command.  If the atom has a radius attribute (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style
sphere}}}}) and its radius is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, its mass is set from
the density and particle volume for 3d systems (the input density is
assumed to be in mass/distance\textasciicircum{}3 units).  For 2d, the default is for
LAMMPS to model particles with a radius attribute as spheres.  However,
if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/disc} keyword is used, then they can be modeled as 2d
discs (circles).  Their mass is set from the density and particle area
(the input density is assumed to be in mass/distance\textasciicircum{}2 units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the atom has a shape attribute (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}}) and its 3 shape parameters are non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, then its mass is
set from the density and particle volume (the input density is assumed
to be in mass/distance\textasciicircum{}3 units).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/disc} keyword has no
effect; it does not (yet) treat 3d ellipsoids as 2d ellipses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the atom has a length attribute (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style line}}}}) and its length is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, then its mass is set from the
density and line segment length (the input density is assumed to be in
mass/distance units).  If the atom has an area attribute (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tri}}}}) and its area is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, then its
mass is set from the density and triangle area (the input density is
assumed to be in mass/distance\textasciicircum{}2 units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If none of these cases are valid, then the mass is set to the density
value directly (the input density is assumed to be in mass units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} sets the temperature of a finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particle.
Currently, only the GRANULAR package supports this attribute. The
temperature must be added using an instance of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} The values for the
temperature must be positive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} sets the volume of all selected particles.  Currently,
only the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style peri}}}} command defines particles
with a volume attribute.  Note that this command does not adjust the
particle mass.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{image} sets which image of the simulation box the atom is
considered to be in.  An image of 0 means it is inside the box as
defined.  A value of 2 means add 2 box lengths to get the true value.  A
value of \sphinxhyphen{}1 means subtract 1 box length to get the true value.  LAMMPS
updates these flags as atoms cross periodic boundaries during the
simulation.  The flags can be output with atom snapshots via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command.  If a value of NULL is specified for any of
nx,ny,nz, then the current image value for that dimension is unchanged.
For non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimensions only a value of 0 can be specified.  This
command can be useful after a system has been equilibrated and atoms
have diffused one or more box lengths in various directions.  This
command can then reset the image values for atoms so that they are
effectively inside the simulation box, e.g if a diffusion coefficient is
about to be measured via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_msd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute msd}}}} command.
Care should be taken not to reset the image flags of two atoms in a bond
to the same value if the bond straddles a periodic boundary (rather they
should be different by +/\sphinxhyphen{} 1).  This will not affect the dynamics of a
simulation, but may mess up analysis of the trajectories if a LAMMPS
diagnostic or your own analysis relies on the image flags to unwrap a
molecule which straddles the periodic box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{improper}, set the bond
type (angle type, etc) of all bonds (angles, etc) of selected atoms to
the specified value.  The value can be a numeric type from 1 to
nbondtypes (nangletypes, etc).  Or it can be a type label (bond type
label, angle type label, etc).  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed syntax of type labels
and a general discussion of how type labels can be used.  All atoms in
a particular bond (angle, etc) must be selected atoms in order for the
change to be made.  The value of nbondtypes (nangletypes, etc) was set
by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond types} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle types}, etc) field in the header of the
data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.  These
keywords do not allow use of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{rheo/rho} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rheo/status} set the density and the status of
rheo particles. In particular, one can only set the phase in the status
as described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RHEO howto page}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{sph/e}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sph/cv}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sph/rho} set the energy, heat capacity,
and density of smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) particles.  See
\sphinxhref{PDF/SPH\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using SPH in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{smd/mass/density} sets the mass of all selected particles, but
it is only applicable to the Smooth Mach Dynamics package MACHDYN.  It
assumes that the particle volume has already been correctly set and
calculates particle mass from the provided mass density value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{smd/contact/radius} only applies to simulations with the Smooth
Mach Dynamics package MACHDYN.  Itsets an interaction radius for
computing short\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions, e.g. repulsive forces to prevent
different individual physical bodies from penetrating each other. Note
that the SPH smoothing kernel diameter used for computing long range,
nonlocal interactions, is set using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/theta} sets the internal temperature of a DPD particle as
defined by the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}REACT package.  If the specified value is a number it
must be \textgreater{}= 0.0.  If the specified value is NULL, then the kinetic
temperature Tkin of each particle is computed as 3/2 k Tkin = KE = 1/2 m
v\textasciicircum{}2 = 1/2 m (vx*vx+vy*vy+vz*vz).  Each particle’s internal
temperature is set to Tkin.  If the specified value is an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
variable, then the variable is evaluated for each particle.  If a value
\textgreater{}= 0.0, the internal temperature is set to that value.  If it is \textless{} 0.0,
the computation of Tkin is performed and the internal temperature is set
to that value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd/temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd/cv} set the temperature and volumetric
heat capacity of an eDPD particle as defined by the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}MESO package.
Currently, only {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style edpd}}}} defines particles
with these attributes. The values for the temperature and heat capacity
must be positive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{cc} sets the chemical concentration of a tDPD particle for a
specified species as defined by the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}MESO package. Currently, only
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tdpd}}}} defines particles with this
attribute. An integer for “index” selects a chemical species (1 to
Nspecies) where Nspecies is set by the atom\_style command. The value for
the chemical concentration must be \textgreater{}= 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{epsilon} sets the dielectric constant of a particle, precisely
of the medium where the particle resides as defined by the DIELECTRIC
package. Currently, only {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style dielectric}}}}
defines particles with this attribute. The value for the dielectric
constant must be \textgreater{}= 0.0.  Note that the set command with this keyword
will rescale the particle charge accordingly so that the real charge
(e.g., as read from a data file) stays intact. To change the real
charges, one needs to use the set command with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge}
keyword. Care must be taken to ensure that the real and scaled charges,
and dielectric constants are consistent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name} refer to custom
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom integer and floating\sphinxhyphen{}point vectors or arrays that have been
added via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} command.
When that command is used specific names are given to each attribute
which are the “name” portion of these keywords.  For arrays \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name}, the column of the array must also be included following
the name in brackets: e.g. d2\_xyz{[}2{]}, i2\_mySpin{[}3{]}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{set:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot set an atom attribute (e.g. \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume}) if
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} does not have that attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command requires inter\sphinxhyphen{}processor communication to coordinate the
setting of bond types (angle types, etc).  This means that your system
must be ready to perform a simulation before using one of these
keywords (force fields set, atom mass set, etc).  This is not
necessary for other keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} style with the bond (angle, etc) keywords can give
unpredictable results if there are bonds (angles, etc) that straddle
periodic boundaries.  This is because the region may only extend up to
the boundary and partner atoms in the bond (angle, etc) may have
coordinates outside the simulation box if they are ghost atoms.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}

\index{shell@\spxentry{shell}}\ignorespaces 

\section{shell command}
\label{\detokenize{shell:shell-command}}\label{\detokenize{shell:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{shell::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{shell:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{command}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
command = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mkdir} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mv} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmdir} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{putenv} or arbitrary command
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cd} arg = dir
  dir = directory to change to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mkdir} args = dir1 dir2 ...
  dir1,dir2 = one or more directories to create
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mv} args = old new
  old = old filename
  new = new filename or destination folder
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rm} args = {[}\sphinxhyphen{}f{]} file1 file2 ...
  \sphinxhyphen{}f = turn off warnings (optional)
  file1,file2 = one or more filenames to delete
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rmdir} args = dir1 dir2 ...
  dir1,dir2 = one or more directories to delete
\sphinxstyleemphasis{putenv} args = var1=value1 var2=value2
  var=value = one of more definitions of environment variables
anything else is passed as a command to the shell for direct execution
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{shell:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sub1}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mkdir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tmp3}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rmdir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp2}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mv}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{log.lammps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hold}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{log.1}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TMP}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{file1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TMP}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{file2}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{putenv}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{LAMMPS\PYGZus{}POTENTIALS}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}setup}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file2}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}post\PYGZus{}process}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.out}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{shell:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Execute a shell command.  A few simple file\sphinxhyphen{}based shell commands are
supported directly, in Unix\sphinxhyphen{}style syntax.  Any command not listed
above is passed as\sphinxhyphen{}is to the C\sphinxhyphen{}library system() call, which invokes
the command in a shell.  To use the external executable instead of
the built\sphinxhyphen{}in version one needs to use a full path, for example
\sphinxstyleemphasis{/bin/rm} instead of \sphinxstyleemphasis{rm}.  The built\sphinxhyphen{}in commands will also work
on operating systems, that do not \sphinxhyphen{} by default \sphinxhyphen{} provide the
corresponding external executables (like \sphinxstyleemphasis{mkdir} on Windows).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command provides a ways to invoke custom commands or executables
from your input script.  For example, you can move files around in
preparation for the next section of the input script.  Or you can run a
program that pre\sphinxhyphen{}processes data for input into LAMMPS.  Or you can run a
program that post\sphinxhyphen{}processes LAMMPS output data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the exception of \sphinxstyleemphasis{cd}, all commands, including ones invoked via a
system() call, are executed by only a single processor, so that
files/directories are not being manipulated by multiple processors
concurrently which may result in unexpected errors or corrupted files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cd} command changes the current working directory similar to
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cd}} command.  All subsequent LAMMPS commands that read/write files
will use the new directory.  All processors execute this command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mkdir} command creates directories similar to the Unix \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mkdir \sphinxhyphen{}p}}
command.  That is, it will attempt to create the entire path of
subdirectories if they do not exist yet.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mv} command renames a file and/or moves it to a new directory.
It cannot rename files across filesystem boundaries or between drives.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rm} command deletes file similar to the Unix \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rm}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmdir} command deletes directories similar to Unix \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmdir}} command.
If a directory is not empty, its contents are also removed recursively
similar to the Unix \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rm \sphinxhyphen{}r}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{putenv} command defines or updates an environment variable directly.
Since this command does not pass through the shell, no shell variable
expansion or globbing is performed, only the usual substitution for
LAMMPS variables defined with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command is
performed.  The resulting string is then used literally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any other command is passed as\sphinxhyphen{}is to the shell along with its arguments as
one string, invoked by the C\sphinxhyphen{}library system() call.  For example,
these lines in your input script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{foo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file2}
\PYG{k}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}setup}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{foo}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
would be the same as invoking

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
my\PYGZus{}setup\PYG{+w}{ }file1\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }file2
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
from a command\sphinxhyphen{}line prompt.  The executable program “my\_setup” is run
with 3 arguments: file1 10 file2.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{shell:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS will do a best effort to detect errors and print suitable
warnings, but due to the nature of delegating commands to the C\sphinxhyphen{}library
system() call, this is not always reliable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{special\_bonds command}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:special-bonds-command}}\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{amber} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dreiding} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/coul} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{one/five}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{amber} values = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm} values = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dreiding} values = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} values = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/coul} values = w1,w2,w3
  w1,w2,w3 = weights (0.0 to 1.0) on pairwise Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones and Coulombic interactions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} values = w1,w2,w3
  w1,w2,w3 = weights (0.0 to 1.0) on pairwise Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul} values = w1,w2,w3
  w1,w2,w3 = weights (0.0 to 1.0) on pairwise Coulombic interactions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{one/five} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amber}
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charmm}
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fene}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set weighting coefficients for pairwise energy and force contributions
between pairs of atoms that are also permanently bonded to each other,
either directly or via one or two intermediate bonds.  These weighting
factors are used by nearly all {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair styles}}}} in
LAMMPS that compute simple pairwise interactions.  Permanent bonds
between atoms are specified by defining the bond topology in the data
file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.  Typically a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style}}}} command is also used to define a bond
potential.  The rationale for using these weighting factors is that
the interaction between a pair of bonded atoms is all (or mostly)
specified by the bond, angle, dihedral potentials, and thus the
non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones or Coulombic interaction between the pair of
atoms should be excluded (or reduced by a weighting factor).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These weighting factors are NOT used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair styles}}}} that compute many\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions, since the
“bonds” that result from such interactions are not permanent, but
are created and broken dynamically as atom conformations change.
Examples of pair styles in this category are EAM, MEAM,
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber, Tersoff, COMB, AIREBO, and ReaxFF.  In fact, it
generally makes no sense to define permanent bonds between atoms
that interact via these potentials, though such bonds may exist
elsewhere in your system, e.g. when using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style
hybrid}}}} command.  Thus LAMMPS ignores special\_bonds
settings when many\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials are calculated.  Please note,
that the existence of explicit bonds for atoms that are described
by a many\sphinxhyphen{}body potential will alter the neighbor list and thus can
render the computation of those interactions invalid, since those
pairs are not only used to determine direct pairwise interactions
but also neighbors of neighbors and more.  The recommended course
of action is to remove such bonds, or \sphinxhyphen{} if that is not possible \sphinxhyphen{}
use a special bonds setting of 1.0 1.0 1.0.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike some commands in LAMMPS, you cannot use this command
multiple times in an incremental fashion: e.g. to first set the LJ
settings and then the Coulombic ones.  Each time you use this
command it sets all the coefficients to default values and only
overrides the one you specify, so you should set all the options
you need each time you use it.  See more details at the bottom of
this page.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Coulomb factors are applied to any Coulomb (charge interaction)
term that the potential calculates.  The LJ factors are applied to the
remaining terms that the potential calculates, whether they represent
LJ interactions or not.  The weighting factors are a scaling
prefactor on the energy and force between the pair of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A value of 1.0 means include the full interaction without flagging the
pair as a “special pair”; a value of 0.0 means exclude the pair
completely from the neighbor list, except for pair styles that require a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace style}}}} and pair styles {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{amoeba}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hippo}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_thole::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thole}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coul/exclude}}}}, and pair styles that include
“coul/dsf” or “coul/wolf”.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To include pairs that would otherwise be excluded (so they are
included in the neighbor list for certain analysis compute styles),
you can use a very small but non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value like 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}100 instead of
0.0.  Due to using floating\sphinxhyphen{}point math, the computed force, energy,
and virial contributions from the pairs will be too small to cause
differences.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first of the 3 coefficients (LJ or Coulombic) is the weighting
factor on 1\sphinxhyphen{}2 atom pairs, which are pairs of atoms directly bonded to
each other.  The second coefficient is the weighting factor on 1\sphinxhyphen{}3
atom pairs which are those separated by 2 bonds (e.g. the two H atoms
in a water molecule).  The third coefficient is the weighting factor
on 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 atom pairs which are those separated by 3 bonds (e.g. the first
and fourth atoms in a dihedral interaction).  Thus if the 1\sphinxhyphen{}2
coefficient is set to 0.0, then the pairwise interaction is
effectively turned off for all pairs of atoms bonded to each other.
If it is set to 1.0, then that interaction will be at full strength.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For purposes of computing weighted pairwise interactions, 1\sphinxhyphen{}3
and 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 interactions are not defined from the list of angles or
dihedrals used by the simulation.  Rather, they are inferred
topologically from the set of bonds specified when the simulation is
defined from a data or restart file (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands).  Thus the set of
1\sphinxhyphen{}2,1\sphinxhyphen{}3,1\sphinxhyphen{}4 interactions that the weights apply to is the same whether
angle and dihedral potentials are computed or not, and remains the
same even if bonds are constrained, or turned off, or removed during a
simulation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two exceptions to this rule are (a) if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral}
keywords are set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} (see below), or (b) if the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{special}
option that re\sphinxhyphen{}computes the 1\sphinxhyphen{}2,1\sphinxhyphen{}3,1\sphinxhyphen{}4 topologies after bonds are
deleted; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command for more
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{amber} keyword sets the 3 coefficients to 0.0, 0.0, 0.5 for LJ
interactions and to 0.0, 0.0, 0.8333 for Coulombic interactions, which
is the default for a commonly used version of the AMBER force field,
where the last value is really 5/6.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds:cornell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Cornell)}}}} for a
description of the AMBER force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm} keyword sets the 3 coefficients to 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 for both
LJ and Coulombic interactions, which is the default for a commonly
used version of the CHARMM force field.  Note that in pair styles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/long} the 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 coefficients
are defined explicitly, and these pairwise contributions are computed
as part of the charmm dihedral style \sphinxhyphen{} see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_style}}}}
commands for more information.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds:mackerell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(MacKerell)}}}} for a
description of the CHARMM force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dreiding} keyword sets the 3 coefficients to 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 for both
LJ and Coulombic interactions, which is the default for the Dreiding
force field, as discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds:mayo}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Mayo)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} keyword sets the 3 coefficients to 0.0, 1.0, 1.0 for both
LJ and Coulombic interactions, which is consistent with a
coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained polymer model with {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_fene::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{FENE bonds}}}}.  See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds:kremer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kremer)}}}} for a description of FENE bonds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/coul}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul} keywords allow the 3 coefficients to
be set explicitly.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/coul} keyword sets both the LJ and
Coulombic coefficients to the same 3 values.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul}
keywords only set either the LJ or Coulombic coefficients.  Use both
of them if you wish to set the LJ coefficients to different values
than the Coulombic coefficients.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} keyword allows the 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 weighting factor to be ignored for
individual atom pairs if they are not listed as the first and last
atoms in any angle defined in the simulation or as 1,3 or 2,4 atoms in
any dihedral defined in the simulation.  For example, imagine the 1\sphinxhyphen{}3
weighting factor is set to 0.5 and you have a linear molecule with 4
atoms and bonds as follows: 1\sphinxhyphen{}2\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}4.  If your data file defines 1\sphinxhyphen{}2\sphinxhyphen{}3
as an angle, but does not define 2\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}4 as an angle or 1\sphinxhyphen{}2\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}4 as a
dihedral, then the pairwise interaction between atoms 1 and 3 will
always be weighted by 0.5, but different force fields use different
rules for weighting the pairwise interaction between atoms 2 and 4.
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} keyword is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the pairwise
interaction between atoms 2 and 4 will be unaffected (full weighting
of 1.0).  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} keyword is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} which is the
default, then the 2,4 interaction will also be weighted by 0.5.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} keyword allows the 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 weighting factor to be ignored
for individual atom pairs if they are not listed as the first and last
atoms in any dihedral defined in the simulation.  For example, imagine
the 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 weighting factor is set to 0.5 and you have a linear molecule
with 5 atoms and bonds as follows: 1\sphinxhyphen{}2\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}4\sphinxhyphen{}5.  If your data file
defines 1\sphinxhyphen{}2\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}4 as a dihedral, but does not define 2\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}4\sphinxhyphen{}5 as a
dihedral, then the pairwise interaction between atoms 1 and 4 will
always be weighted by 0.5, but different force fields use different
rules for weighting the pairwise interaction between atoms 2 and 5.
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} keyword is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the pairwise
interaction between atoms 2 and 5 will be unaffected (full weighting
of 1.0).  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} keyword is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} which is the
default, then the 2,5 interaction will also be weighted by 0.5.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{one/five} keyword enable calculation and storage of a list of 1\sphinxhyphen{}5
neighbors in the molecular topology for each atom.  It is required by
some pair styles, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style amoeba}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hippo}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS stores and maintains a data structure with a list of the
first, second, and third neighbors of each atom (within the bond
topology of the system).  If new bonds are created (or molecules
added containing atoms with more special neighbors), the size of
this list needs to grow.  Note that adding a single bond always
adds a new first neighbor but may also induce *many* new second
and third neighbors, depending on the molecular topology of your
system.  Using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/special/per/atom} keyword to either
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}
reserves empty space in the list for this N additional first,
second, or third neighbors to be added.  If you do not do this, you
may get an error when bonds (or molecules) are added.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you reuse this command in an input script, you should set all
the options you need each time.  This command cannot be used a second
time incrementally.  E.g. these two commands:
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
are not the same as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the first case you end up with (after the second command):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
LJ: 0.0 0.0 0.0
Coul: 0.0 0.0 1.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
while only in the second case do you get the desired settings of:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
LJ: 0.0 1.0 1.0
Coul: 0.0 0.0 1.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This happens because the LJ (and Coul) settings are reset to their
default values before modifying them, each time the \sphinxstyleemphasis{special\_bonds}
command is issued.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_create::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/create}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{special_bonds:default}}

All 3 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones and 3 Coulombic weighting coefficients = 0.0,
angle = no, dihedral = no.
