\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Vector Initialization}
\label{\detokenize{variable:vector-initialization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Jun2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Vector}\sphinxhyphen{}style variables only can be initialized with a special
syntax, instead of using a formula.  The syntax is a bracketed,
comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated syntax like the following:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myvec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[1},3.5,7,10.2\PYG{n}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 3rd argument formula is replaced by the vector values in brackets,
separated by commas.  This example creates a 4\sphinxhyphen{}length vector with
specific numeric values, each of which can be specified as an integer
or floating point value.  Note that while whitespace can be added
before or after individual values, no other mathematical operations
can be specified.  E.g. “3*10” or “3*v\_abc” are not valid vector
elements, nor is “10*{[}1,2,3,4{]}” valid for the entire vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike vector variables specified with formulas, this vector variable
is static; its length and values never changes.  Its values can be
used in other commands (including vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variables specified
with formulas) via the usual syntax for accessing individual vector
elements or the entire vector.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Immediate Evaluation of Variables}
\label{\detokenize{variable:immediate-evaluation-of-variables}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable to be evaluated immediately, it
may be the case that you do not need to define a variable at all.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Commands parse}}}} page for info on how to
use “immediate” variables in an input script, specified as \$(formula)
with parenthesis, where the formula has the same syntax as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables described on this page.  This effectively evaluates a
formula immediately without using the variable command to define a
named variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
More generally, there is a difference between referencing a variable
with a leading \$ sign (e.g. \$x or \$\{abc\}) versus with a leading “v\_”
(e.g. v\_x or v\_abc).  The former can be used in any input script
command, including a variable command.  The input script parser
evaluates the reference variable immediately and substitutes its value
into the command.  As explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Commands parse}}}} doc page, you can also use un\sphinxhyphen{}named “immediate”
variables for this purpose.  For example, a string like this
\$((xlo+xhi)/2+sqrt(v\_area)) in an input script command evaluates the
string between the parenthesis as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable formula.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Referencing a variable with a leading “v\_” is an optional or required
kind of argument for some commands (e.g. the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} commands) if you wish it to evaluate a variable
periodically during a run.  It can also be used in a variable formula
if you wish to reference a second variable.  The second variable will
be evaluated whenever the first variable is evaluated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, suppose you use this command in your input script to
define the variable “v” as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vol}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
before a run where the simulation box size changes.  You might think
this will assign the initial volume to the variable “v”.  That is not
the case.  Rather it assigns a formula which evaluates the volume
(using the thermo\_style keyword “vol”) to the variable “v”.  If you
use the variable “v” in some other command like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}} then the current volume of the box will be evaluated
continuously during the run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to store the initial volume of the system, you can do it
this way:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vol}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}v}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second command will force “v” to be evaluated (yielding the
initial volume) and assign that value to the variable “v0”.  Thus the
command

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}v0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
would print out both the current and initial volume periodically
during the run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that it is a mistake to enclose a variable formula in double
quotes if it contains variables preceded by \$ signs.  For example,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{vratio}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}vfinal\PYGZcb{}/\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}v0\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is because the quotes prevent variable substitution (explained on
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Commands parse}}}} doc page), and thus an error
will occur when the formula for “vratio” is evaluated later.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Variable Accuracy}
\label{\detokenize{variable:variable-accuracy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Obviously, LAMMPS attempts to evaluate variables which contain
formulas (\sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} style variables)
accurately whenever the evaluation is performed.  Depending on what is
included in the formula, this may require invoking a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}, either directly or indirectly via a thermo keyword, or
accessing a value previously calculated by a compute, or accessing a
value calculated and stored by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}}.  If the compute is
one that calculates the energy or pressure of the system, then the
corresponding energy or virial quantities need to be tallied during
the evaluation of the interatomic potentials (pair, bond, etc) on any
timestep that the variable needs the tallies.  An input script can
also request variables be evaluated before or after or in between
runs, e.g. by including them in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{print::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{print}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS keeps track of all of this as it performs a {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} simulation, as well as in between
simulations.  An error will be generated if you attempt to evaluate a
variable when LAMMPS knows it cannot produce accurate values.  For
example, if a {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command prints
a variable which accesses values stored by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}} command and the timesteps on which thermo output is
generated are not multiples of the averaging frequency used in the fix
command, then an error will occur.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, there are two special cases to be aware when a variable
requires invocation of a compute (directly or indirectly).  The first
is if the variable is evaluated before the first {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command in the input script.  In this case,
LAMMPS will generate an error.  This is because many computes require
initializations which have not yet taken place.  One example is the
calculation of degrees of freedom for temperature computes.  Another
example are the computes mentioned above which require tallying of
energy or virial quantities; these values are not tallied until the
first simulation begins.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second special case is when a variable that depends on a compute
is evaluated in between {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}}
commands.  It is possible for other input script commands issued
following the previous run, but before the variable is evaluated, to
change the system.  For example, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_atoms}}}}
command could be used to remove atoms.  Since the compute will not
re\sphinxhyphen{}initialize itself until the next simulation or it may depend on
energy/virial computations performed before the system was changed, it
will potentially generate an incorrect answer when evaluated.  Note
that LAMMPS will not generate an error in this case; the evaluated
variable may simply be incorrect.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The way to get around both of these special cases is to perform a
0\sphinxhyphen{}timestep run before evaluating the variable.  For example, these
commands

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} delete\PYGZus{}atoms random fraction 0.5 yes all NULL 49839}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} run 0 post no}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} this thermo keyword invokes a temperature compute}
\PYG{k}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Temperature of system = \PYGZdl{}t}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will generate an error if the “run 1000” command is the first
simulation in the input script.  If there were a previous run, these
commands will print the correct temperature of the system.  But if the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_atoms}}}} command is uncommented, the printed
temperature will be incorrect, because information stored by
temperature compute is no longer valid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both these issues are resolved, if the “run 0” command is uncommented.
This is because the “run 0” simulation will initialize (or
re\sphinxhyphen{}initialize) the temperature compute correctly.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{variable:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indexing any formula element by global atom ID, such as an atom value,
requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} to use a global mapping in
order to look up the vector indices.  By default, only atom styles
with molecular information create global maps.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify
map}}}} command can override the default, e.g. for
atomic\sphinxhyphen{}style atom styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All \sphinxstyleemphasis{universe}\sphinxhyphen{} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{uloop}\sphinxhyphen{}style variables defined in an input
script must have the same number of values.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{variable:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{next::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{next}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{jump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{jump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{include::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{include}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{temper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temper}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_print::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix print}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{print::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{print}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{variable:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{velocity@\spxentry{velocity}}\ignorespaces 

\section{velocity command}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:velocity-command}}\label{\detokenize{velocity:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{velocity::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of group of atoms whose velocity will be changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{create} args = temp seed
  temp = temperature value (temperature units)
  seed = random \# seed (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{set} args = vx vy vz
  vx,vy,vz = velocity value or NULL (velocity units)
  any of vx,vy,vz can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} arg = temp
  temp = temperature value (temperature units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} args = vdim vlo vhi dim clo chi
  vdim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}
  vlo,vhi = lower and upper velocity value (velocity units)
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
  clo,chi = lower and upper coordinate bound (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angular}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} = zero the linear momentum
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{angular} = zero the angular momentum
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sum} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rot} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{loop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sum} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mom} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rot} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value = temperature compute ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{loop} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{geom}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} value = fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of rigid body fix
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4928459}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{border}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mytemp}
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set or change the velocities of a group of atoms in one of several
styles.  For each style, there are required arguments and optional
keyword/value parameters.  Not all options are used by each style.
Each option has a default as listed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} style generates an ensemble of velocities using a random
number generator with the specified seed at the specified temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} style sets the velocities of all atoms in the group to the
specified values.  If any component is specified as NULL, then it is
not set.  Any of the vx,vy,vz velocity components can be specified as
an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value
is a variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where name is the
variable name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated, and its
value used to determine the velocity component.  Note that if a
variable is used, the velocity it calculates must be in box units, not
lattice units; see the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters or other parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus it is easy to specify a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
velocity field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} style computes the current temperature of the group of
atoms and then rescales the velocities to the specified temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} style is similar to that used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
temp/ramp}}}} command.  Velocities ramped uniformly
from vlo to vhi are applied to dimension vx, or vy, or vz.  The value
assigned to a particular atom depends on its relative coordinate value
(in dim) from clo to chi.  For the example above, an atom with
y\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate of 10 (1/4 of the way from 5 to 25), would be assigned a
x\sphinxhyphen{}velocity of 1.25 (1/4 of the way from 0.0 to 5.0).  Atoms outside
the coordinate bounds (less than 5 or greater than 25 in this case),
are assigned velocities equal to vlo or vhi (0.0 or 5.0 in this case).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} style adjusts the velocities of the group of atoms so that
the aggregate linear or angular momentum is zero.  No other changes
are made to the velocities of the atoms.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} option is
specified (see below), then the zeroing is performed on individual
rigid bodies, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid or fix rigid/small}}}} commands.  In other words, zero linear will set the
linear momentum of each rigid body to zero, and zero angular will set
the angular momentum of each rigid body to zero.  This is done by
adjusting the velocities of the atoms in each rigid body.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All temperatures specified in the velocity command are in temperature
units; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command.  The units of velocities and
coordinates depend on whether the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}, as discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all styles, no atoms are assigned z\sphinxhyphen{}component velocities if the
simulation is 2d; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword/value options are used in the following ways by the
various styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} keyword is used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{create}.  The ensemble of generated
velocities can be a \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform} distribution from some minimum to
maximum value, scaled to produce the requested temperature.  Or it can
be a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} distribution with a mean of 0.0 and a sigma scaled to
produce the requested temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sum} keyword is used by all styles, except \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero}.  The new
velocities will be added to the existing ones if sum = yes, or will
replace them if sum = no.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rot} keywords are used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{create}.  If mom = yes, the
linear momentum of the newly created ensemble of velocities is zeroed;
if rot = yes, the angular momentum is zeroed.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If specified, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword is used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} to
specify a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} that calculates temperature in a
desired way, e.g. by first subtracting out a velocity bias, as
discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} doc page.
If this keyword is not specified, \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} calculate
temperature using a compute that is defined internally as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{velocity\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where group\sphinxhyphen{}ID is the same ID used in the velocity command. i.e. the
group of atoms whose velocity is being altered.  This compute is
deleted when the velocity command is finished.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
temp}}}} command for details.  If the calculated
temperature should have degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom removed due to fix
constraints (e.g. SHAKE or rigid\sphinxhyphen{}body constraints), then the
appropriate fix command must be specified before the velocity command
is issued.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} setting is used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}, but only if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword is also used to specify a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} that calculates temperature in a desired way.
If the temperature compute also calculates a velocity bias, the bias
is subtracted from atom velocities before the \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}
operations are performed.  After the operations, the bias is added
back to the atom velocities.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for more discussion of temperature computes
with biases.  Note that the velocity bias is only applied to atoms in
the temperature compute specified with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, assume atoms are currently streaming in a flow
direction (which could be separately initialized with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp}
style), and you wish to initialize their thermal velocity to a desired
temperature.  In this context thermal velocity means the per\sphinxhyphen{}particle
velocity that remains when the streaming velocity is subtracted.  This
can be done using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} style with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword
specifying the ID of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/ramp}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/profile}}}} command, and the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword set to a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} value.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{loop} keyword is used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} in the following ways.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If loop = all, then each processor loops over all atoms in the
simulation to create velocities, but only stores velocities for atoms
it owns.  This can be a slow loop for a large simulation.  If atoms
were read from a data file, the velocity assigned to a particular atom
will be the same, independent of how many processors are being used.
This will not be the case if atoms were created using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command, since atom IDs will likely
be assigned to atoms differently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If loop = local, then each processor loops over only its atoms to
produce velocities.  The random number seed is adjusted to give a
different set of velocities on each processor.  This is a fast loop,
but the velocity assigned to a particular atom will depend on which
processor owns it.  Thus the results will always be different when a
simulation is run on a different number of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If loop = geom, then each processor loops over only its atoms.  For
each atom a unique random number seed is created, based on the atom’s
xyz coordinates.  A velocity is generated using that seed.  This is a
fast loop and the velocity assigned to a particular atom will be the
same, independent of how many processors are used.  However, the set
of generated velocities may be more correlated than if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{local} keywords are used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{loop geom} keyword will not necessarily assign
identical velocities for two simulations run on different machines.
This is because the computations based on xyz coordinates are
sensitive to tiny differences in the double\sphinxhyphen{}precision value for a
coordinate as stored on a particular machine.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} keyword only has meaning when used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} style.
It allows specification of a fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID for one of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rigid\sphinxhyphen{}body
fix}}}} variants which defines a set of rigid bodies.  The
zeroing of linear or angular momentum is then performed for each rigid
body defined by the fix, as described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword is used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp}.  If units = box,
the velocities and coordinates specified in the velocity command are
in the standard units described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command
(e.g. Angstroms/fs for real units).  If units = lattice, velocities
are in units of lattice spacings per time (e.g. spacings/fs) and
coordinates are in lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}}
command must have been previously used to define the lattice spacing.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assigning a temperature via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} style to a system with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rigid bodies}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{SHAKE constraints}}}} may not have the desired outcome for two reasons.  First,
the velocity command can be invoked before all of the relevant fixes
are created and initialized and the number of adjusted degrees of
freedom (DOFs) is known.  Thus it is not possible to compute the
target temperature correctly.  Second, the assigned velocities may be
partially canceled when constraints are first enforced, leading to a
different temperature than desired.  A workaround for this is to
perform a {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run 0}}}} command, which ensures all DOFs are
accounted for properly, and then rescale the temperature to the
desired value before performing a simulation.  For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12345}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{                             }\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} temperature may not be 300K}
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} now it should be}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{velocity:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are dist = uniform, sum = no, mom = yes, rot =
no, bias = no, loop = all, and units = lattice.  The temp and rigid
keywords are not defined by default.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{write\_coeff@\spxentry{write\_coeff}}\ignorespaces 

\section{write\_coeff command}
\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:write-coeff-command}}\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{write_coeff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}coeff }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{file}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of data file to write out

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}coeff }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{polymer.coeff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write a text format file with the currently defined force field
coefficients in a way, that it can be read by LAMMPS with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{include::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{include}}}} command. In combination with the nocoeff
option of {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}} this can be used to move
the Coeffs sections from a data file into a separate file.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The write\_coeff command is not yet fully implemented as
some pair styles do not output their coefficient information.
This means you will need to add/copy this information manually.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{write_coeff:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}}

\sphinxstepscope

\index{write\_data@\spxentry{write\_data}}\ignorespaces 

\section{write\_data command}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:write-data-command}}\label{\detokenize{write_data:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{write_data::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}data }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of data file to write out

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nofix} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nolabelmap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{triclinic/general} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} = do not write out force field info
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nofix} = do not write out extra sections read by fixes
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nolabelmap} = do not write out type labels
\sphinxstyleemphasis{triclinic/general} = write data file in general triclinic format
\sphinxstyleemphasis{types} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{numeric} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{labels}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ii} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ii} = write one line of pair coefficient info per atom type
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} = write one line of pair coefficient info per IJ atom type pair
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}data }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{data.polymer}
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}data }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{data.}\PYG{o}{*}
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}data }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{data.solid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{triclinic}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{general}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write a data file in text format of the current state of the
simulation.  Data files can be read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}
command to begin a simulation.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command
also describes their format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} files, the data filename can contain a “*”
wild\sphinxhyphen{}card character.  The “*” is replaced with the current timestep
value.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Data in Coeff sections}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The write\_data command may not always write all coefficient settings
to the corresponding Coeff sections of the data file.  This can have
one of multiple reasons.  1) The style may be a hybrid style. In that
case \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} coeff information is written.  2) A few styles may be
missing the code that would write those sections (This is rare these
days, but if you come across one, please notify the LAMMPS
developers).  3) Some pair styles require a single pair\_coeff
statement and those are not compatible with data files.  4) The
default for write\_data is to write a PairCoeff section, which has
only entries for atom types i == j. The remaining coefficients would
be inferred through the currently selected mixing rule.  If there has
been a pair\_coeff command with i != j, this setting would be lost.
LAMMPS will detect this and print a warning message unless \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair ij}
is appended to the write\_data command.  This will request writing a
PairIJCoeff section which has information for all pairs of atom types.
In cases where the coefficient data in the data file is incomplete,
you will need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify that information in your input script
that reads the data file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because a data file is in text format, if you use a data file written
out by this command to restart a simulation, the initial state of the
new run will be slightly different than the final state of the old run
(when the file was written) which was represented internally by LAMMPS
in binary format.  A new simulation which reads the data file will
thus typically diverge from a simulation that continued in the
original input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to do more exact restarts, using binary files, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands.  You can also convert
binary restart files to text data files, after a simulation has run,
using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}r command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only limited information about a simulation is stored in a data
file.  For example, no information about atom {\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{groups}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} are stored.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Binary restart files}}}}
store more information.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bond interactions (angle, etc) that have been turned off by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}}
command will be written to a data file as if they are turned on.  This
means they will need to be turned off again in a new run after the
data file is read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bonds that are broken (e.g. by a bond\sphinxhyphen{}breaking potential) are not
written to the data file.  Thus these bonds will not exist when the
data file is read.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} keyword means no force field parameters are
written to the data file. This can be helpful, for example, if you
want to make significant changes to the force field or if the force
field parameters are read in separately, e.g. from an include file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nofix} keyword means no extra sections read by fixes are
written to the data file (see the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command for details). For example, this option excludes
sections for user\sphinxhyphen{}created per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties from {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
property/atom}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nolabelmap} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} keywords refer to type labels that may be
defined for numeric atom types, bond types, angle types, etc.  The
label map can be defined in two ways, either by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{labelmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{labelmap}}}} command or in data files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command which have sections for Atom Type Labels, Bond
Type Labels, Angle Type Labels, etc.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto type labels}}}} doc page for the allowed syntax of type labels
and a general discussion of how type labels can be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nolabelmap} keyword means that even if type labels exist
for a given type\sphinxhyphen{}kind (Atoms, Bonds, Angles, etc.), type labels are
not written to the data file.  By default, they are written if they
exist.  A type label must be defined for every numeric type (within a
given type\sphinxhyphen{}kind) to be written to the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{triclinic/general} keyword will output a data file which
specifies a general triclinic simulation box as well as per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities consistent with the general triclinic box.  The latter means
that per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors, such as velocities and dipole moments will be
oriented consistent with the 3d rotation implied by the general
triclinic box (relative to the associated restricted triclinic box).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option can only be requested if the simulation box was initially
defined to be general triclinic.  If if was and the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{triclinic/general} keyword is not used, then the data file will
specify a restricted triclinic box, since that is the internal format
LAMMPS uses for both general and restricted triclinic simulations.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto triclinic}}}} doc page for more
explanation of how general triclinic simulation boxes are supported by
LAMMPS.  And see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} doc page for details
of how the format is altered for general triclinic data files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} keyword determines how atom types, bond types, angle
types, etc are written into these data file sections: Atoms, Bonds,
Angles, etc.  The default is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{numeric} setting, even if type label
maps exist.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{labels} setting is used, type labels will be
written to the data file, if the corresponding label map exists.  Note
that when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{types labels}, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nolabelmap} keyword cannot be
used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword lets you specify in what format the pair
coefficient information is written into the data file.  If the value
is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{ii}, then one line per atom type is written, to
specify the coefficients for each of the I=J interactions.  This means
that no cross\sphinxhyphen{}interactions for I != J will be specified in the data
file and the pair style will apply its mixing rule, as documented on
individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} doc pages.  Of course this
behavior can be overridden in the input script after reading the data
file, by specifying additional {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} commands
for any desired I,J pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the value is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}, then one line of coefficients is
written for all I,J pairs where I \textless{}= J.  These coefficients will
include any specific settings made in the input script up to that
point.  The presence of these I != J coefficients in the data file
will effectively turn off the default mixing rule for the pair style.
Again, the coefficient values in the data file can be overridden
in the input script after reading the data file, by specifying
additional {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} commands for any desired I,J
pairs.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command requires inter\sphinxhyphen{}processor communication to migrate atoms
before the data file is written.  This means that your system must be
ready to perform a simulation before using this command (force fields
setup, atom masses initialized, etc).


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{write_data:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are pair = ii and types = numeric.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{write\_dump@\spxentry{write\_dump}}\ignorespaces 

\section{write\_dump command}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{write_dump:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{args}

\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dump\sphinxhyphen{}modify\sphinxhyphen{}args = args for {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} (optional)

\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{.myforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myF[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sort}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}

\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{image}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{snap}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.jpg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{960}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{960}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{backcolor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{white}

\PYG{+w}{                }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myF[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                }\PYG{n}{modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sort}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                }\PYG{n}{compression\PYGZus{}level}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{15}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{write_dump:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a single snapshot of atom quantities to one or more files for the
current state of the system.  This is a one\sphinxhyphen{}time immediate operation,
in contrast to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command which will will set up a
dump style to write out snapshots periodically during a running
simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The syntax for this command is mostly identical to that of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} commands as if
they were concatenated together, with the following exceptions: There
is no need for a dump ID or dump frequency and the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{modify} is
added.  The latter is so that the full range of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} options can be specified for the single
snapshot, just as they can be for multiple snapshots.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{modify}
keyword separates the arguments that would normally be passed to the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dump} command from those that would be given the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dump\_modify}.  Both
support optional arguments and thus LAMMPS needs to be able to cleanly
separate the two sets of args.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if the specified filename uses wildcard characters “*” or
“\%”, as supported by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command, they will operate
in the same fashion to create the new filename(s).  Normally, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} files require a filename with a “*” character
for the timestep.  That is not the case for the write\_dump command; no
wildcard “*” character is necessary.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{write_dump:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All restrictions for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} commands apply to this command as well,
with the exception of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} filename not
requiring a wildcard “*” character, as noted above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since dumps are normally written during a {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}, the simulation has to be ready to run
before this command can be used.  Similarly, if the dump requires
information from a compute, fix, or variable, the information needs to
have been calculated for the current timestep (e.g. by a prior run),
else LAMMPS will generate an error message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, it is not possible to dump per\sphinxhyphen{}atom energy with this
command before a run has been performed, since no energies and forces
have yet been calculated.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} doc page
section on Variable Accuracy for more information on this topic.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{write_dump:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{write_dump:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The defaults are listed on the doc pages for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}
commands.

\index{write\_restart@\spxentry{write\_restart}}\ignorespaces 

\section{write\_restart command}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:write-restart-command}}\label{\detokenize{write_restart:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{write_restart::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}restart }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of file to write restart information to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} arg = Np
  Np = write one file for every this many processors
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} arg = Nf
  Nf = write this many files, one from each of Nf processors
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}restart }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{restart.equil}
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}restart }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{poly.}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write a binary restart file of the current state of the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
During a long simulation, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}} command is
typically used to output restart files periodically.  The
write\_restart command is useful after a minimization or whenever you
wish to write out a single current restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} files, the restart filename can contain
two wild\sphinxhyphen{}card characters.  If a “*” appears in the filename, it is
replaced with the current timestep value.  If a “\%” character appears
in the filename, then one file is written by each processor and the
“\%” character is replaced with the processor ID from 0 to P\sphinxhyphen{}1.  An
additional file with the “\%” replaced by “base” is also written, which
contains global information.  For example, the files written for
filename restart.\% would be restart.base, restart.0, restart.1, …
restart.P\sphinxhyphen{}1.  This creates smaller files and can be a fast mode of
output and subsequent input on parallel machines that support parallel
I/O.  The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} keywords discussed below can
alter the number of files written.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restart files can be read by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command to restart a simulation from a particular state.  Because the
file is binary (to enable exact restarts), it may not be readable on
another machine.  In this case, you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}r command\sphinxhyphen{}line
switch}}}} to convert a restart file to a data file.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Although the purpose of restart files is to enable restarting a
simulation from where it left off, not all information about a
simulation is stored in the file.  For example, the list of fixes
that were specified during the initial run is not stored, which
means the new input script must specify any fixes you want to use.
Even when restart information is stored in the file, as it is for
some fixes, commands may need to be re\sphinxhyphen{}specified in the new input
script, in order to re\sphinxhyphen{}use that information. Details are usually
given in the documentation of the respective command. Also, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for general information
about what is stored in a restart file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} keywords can be used in conjunction
with the “\%” wildcard character in the specified restart file name.
As explained above, the “\%” character causes the restart file to be
written in pieces, one piece for each of P processors.  By default P =
the number of processors the simulation is running on.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} keyword can be used to set P to a smaller value, which can
be more efficient when running on a large number of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} keyword sets P to the specified Nf value.  For example, if
Nf = 4, and the simulation is running on 100 processors, 4 files will
be written, by processors 0,25,50,75.  Each will collect information
from itself and the next 24 processors and write it to a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} keyword, the specified value of Np means write one
file for every Np processors.  For example, if Np = 4, every fourth
processor (0,4,8,12,etc) will collect information from itself and the
next 3 processors and write it to a restart file.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command requires inter\sphinxhyphen{}processor communication to migrate atoms
before the restart file is written.  This means that your system must
be ready to perform a simulation before using this command (force
fields setup, atom masses initialized, etc).


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{write_restart:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix accelerate/cos@\spxentry{fix accelerate/cos}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix accelerate/cos command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:fix-accelerate-cos-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accelerate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
accelerate/cos = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = amplitude of acceleration (in unit of velocity/time)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accelerate}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0e\PYGZhy{}7}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Give each atom a acceleration in x\sphinxhyphen{}direction based on its z coordinate.
The acceleration is a periodic function along the z\sphinxhyphen{}direction:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}a_{x}(z) = A \cos \left(\frac{2 \pi z}{l_{z}}\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(A\) is the acceleration amplitude, \(l_z\) is the
\(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}length of the simulation box.
At steady state, the acceleration generates a velocity profile:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}v_{x}(z) = V \cos \left(\frac{2 \pi z}{l_{z}}\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The generated velocity amplitude \(V\) is related to the
shear viscosity \(\eta\) by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}V = \frac{A \rho}{\eta}\left(\frac{l_{z}}{2 \pi}\right)^{2}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and it can be obtained from ensemble average of the velocity profile:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}V = \frac{\sum\limits_i 2 m_{i} v_{i, x} \cos \left(\frac{2 \pi z_i}{l_{z}}\right)}{\sum\limits_i m_{i}},\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(m_i\), \(v_{i,x}\), and \(z_i\) are the mass,
\(x\)\sphinxhyphen{}component velocity, and \(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate of a particle,
respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The velocity amplitude \(V\) can be calculated with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_viscosity_cos::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
viscosity/cos}}}}, which enables viscosity
calculation with periodic perturbation method, as described by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:hess2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Hess}}}}.  Because the applied acceleration drives the system
away from equilibration, the calculated shear viscosity is lower than
the intrinsic viscosity due to the shear\sphinxhyphen{}thinning effect.  Extrapolation
to zero acceleration should generally be performed to predict the
zero\sphinxhyphen{}shear viscosity.  As the shear stress decreases, the
signal\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}noise ratio decreases rapidly, and the simulation time must be
extended accordingly to get converged results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to get meaningful results, the group ID of this fix should be all.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to binary restart files.
None of the fix\_modify options are relevant to this fix.
No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for access by various
output commands.  No parameter of this fix can be used with the start/stop
keywords of the run command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during energy minimization.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MISC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since this fix depends on the \(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate of atoms, it cannot be used
in 2d simulations.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_viscosity_cos::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute viscosity/cos}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_accelerate_cos:hess2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Hess)} Hess, B. Journal of Chemical Physics 2002, 116 (1), 209\textendash{}217.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix acks2/reaxff@\spxentry{fix acks2/reaxff}}\ignorespaces 
\index{fix acks2/reaxff/kk@\spxentry{fix acks2/reaxff/kk}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix acks2/reaxff command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:fix-acks2-reaxff-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{acks2/reaxff/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acks2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cuthi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tolerance}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{params}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
acks2/reaxff = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = perform ACKS2 every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutlo,cuthi = lo and hi cutoff for Taper radius

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tolerance = precision to which charges will be equilibrated

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
params = reaxff or a filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keywords or keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} N = limit the number of iterations to \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acks2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acks2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{param.acks2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxiter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform the atom\sphinxhyphen{}condensed Kohn\textendash{}Sham DFT to second order (ACKS2) charge
equilibration method as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:verstraelen}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Verstraelen)}}}}.
ACKS2 impedes unphysical long\sphinxhyphen{}range charge transfer sometimes seen with
QEq (e.g., for dissociation of molecules), at increased computational
cost.  It is typically used in conjunction with the ReaxFF force field
model as implemented in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}}
command, but it can be used with any potential in LAMMPS, so long as it
defines and uses charges on each atom.  For more technical details about
the charge equilibration performed by fix acks2/reaxff, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:o-hearn}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(O’Hearn)}}}} paper.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ACKS2 method minimizes the electrostatic energy of the system by
adjusting the partial charge on individual atoms based on interactions
with their neighbors.  It requires some parameters for each atom type.
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{params} setting above is the word “reaxff”, then these are
extracted from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}} command and
the ReaxFF force field file it reads in.  If a file name is specified
for \sphinxstyleemphasis{params}, then the parameters are taken from the specified file
and the file must contain one line for each atom type.  The latter
form must be used when performing QeQ with a non\sphinxhyphen{}ReaxFF potential.
The lines should be formatted as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
bond\PYGZus{}softness
itype chi eta gamma bcut
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the first line is the global parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond\_softness}. The
remaining 1 to Ntypes lines include \sphinxstyleemphasis{itype}, the atom type from 1 to
Ntypes, \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi}, the electronegativity in eV, \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}, the self\sphinxhyphen{}Coulomb
potential in eV, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma}, the valence orbital exponent, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{bcut}, the
bond cutoff distance.  Note that these 4 quantities are also in the
ReaxFF potential file, except that eta is defined here as twice the eta
value in the ReaxFF file. Note that unlike the rest of LAMMPS, the units
of this fix are hard\sphinxhyphen{}coded to be \(\AA\), eV, and
electronic charge.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} keyword allows changing the max number
of iterations in the linear solver. The default value is 200.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to solve the self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent equations for electronegativity
equalization, LAMMPS imposes the additional constraint that all the
charges in the fix group must add up to zero.  The initial charge
assignments should also satisfy this constraint.  LAMMPS will print a
warning if that is not the case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This fix computes a global scalar (the number of
iterations) for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the REAXFF package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix does not correctly handle interactions involving multiple
periodic images of the same atom.  Hence, it should not be used for
periodic cell dimensions less than \(10~\AA\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix may be used in combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix efield}}}}
and will apply the external electric field during charge equilibration,
but there may be only one fix efield instance used, it may only use a
constant electric field, and the electric field vector may only have
components in non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic directions.

\section{fix adapt command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt:fix-adapt-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
adapt = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = adapt simulation settings every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more attribute/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
attribute = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} args = pstyle pparam I J v\_name
  pstyle = pair style name (e.g., lj/cut)
  pparam = parameter to adapt over time
  I,J = type pair(s) to set parameter for (integer or type label)
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates value of pparam
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} args = bstyle bparam I v\_name
  bstyle = bond style name (e.g., harmonic)
  bparam = parameter to adapt over time
  I = type bond to set parameter for (integer or type label)
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates value of bparam
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} args = astyle aparam I v\_name
  astyle = angle style name (e.g., harmonic)
  aparam = parameter to adapt over time
  I = type angle to set parameter for (integer or type label)
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates value of aparam
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} arg = v\_name
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates scale factor on \(k\)\sphinxhyphen{}space terms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} args = atomparam v\_name
  atomparam = \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter/disc} = parameter to adapt over time
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates value of atomparam
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mass}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = the variable value is the new setting
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = the variable value multiplies the original setting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = values will remain altered at the end of a run
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = reset altered values to their original values at the end of a run
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mass} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = mass is not altered by changes in diameter
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = mass is altered by changes in diameter
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change or adapt one or more specific simulation attributes or settings over
time as a simulation runs.  Pair potential and \(k\)\sphinxhyphen{}space and atom
attributes which can be varied by this fix are discussed below.  Many other
fixes can also be used to time\sphinxhyphen{}vary simulation parameters (e.g., the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command will change the simulation box
size/shape and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_move::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix move}}}} command will change atom
positions and velocities in a prescribed manner).  Also note that many commands
allow variables as arguments for specific parameters, if described in that
manner on their doc pages.  An equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable can calculate a
time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent quantity, so this is another way to vary a simulation parameter
over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \(N\) is specified as 0, the specified attributes are only changed
once, before the simulation begins.  This is all that is needed if the
associated variables are not time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent.  If \(N > 0\), then changes
are made every \(N\) steps during the simulation, presumably with a
variable that is time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} keyword, attributes changed by
this fix will or will not be reset back to their original values at
the end of a simulation.  Even if \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, a
restart file written during a simulation will contain the modified
settings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, which is the default, then
the value of the altered parameter will be whatever the variable
generates.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the value
of the altered parameter will be the initial value of that parameter
multiplied by whatever the variable generates (i.e., the variable is
now a “scale factor” applied in (presumably) a time\sphinxhyphen{}varying fashion to
the parameter).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that whether scale is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, internally, the parameters
themselves are actually altered by this fix.  Make sure you use the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reset yes} option if you want the parameters to be restored to their
initial values after the run.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword enables various parameters of potentials defined by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command to be changed, if the pair
style supports it.  Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} commands must be used in the usual manner
to specify these parameters initially; the fix adapt command simply
overrides the parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} argument is the name of the pair style.  If
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid or hybrid/overlay}}}} is used,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} should be a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style name.  If there are multiple
sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles using the same pair style, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} should be specified
as “style:N”, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is which instance of the pair style you wish to
adapt (e.g., the first or second).  For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} could be
specified as “soft” or “lubricate” or “lj/cut:1” or “lj/cut:2”.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pparam} argument is the name of the parameter to change.  This is the
current list of pair styles and parameters that can be varied by this
fix.  See the doc pages for individual pair styles and their energy
formulas for the meaning of these parameters:
