\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is easy to add new pairwise potentials and their parameters
to this list.  All it typically takes is adding an extract() method to
the pair\_*.cpp file associated with the potential.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some parameters are global settings for the pair style (e.g., the
viscosity setting “mu” for {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lubricate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lubricate}}}}).
Other parameters apply to atom type pairs within the pair style (e.g., the
prefactor \(a\) for {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style soft}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for many of the potentials, the parameter that can be varied
is effectively a prefactor on the entire energy expression for the
potential (e.g., the lj/cut epsilon).  The parameters listed as “scale”
are exactly that, since the energy expression for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coul/cut}}}} potential (for example) has no labeled
prefactor in its formula.  To apply an effective prefactor to some
potentials, multiple parameters need to be altered.  For example, the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Buckingham potential}}}} needs both the \(A\) and
\(C\) terms altered together.  To scale the Buckingham potential, you
should thus list the pair style twice, once for \(A\) and once for
\(C\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a type pair parameter is specified, the \(I\) and \(J\) settings
should be specified to indicate which type pairs to apply it to.  If a global
parameter is specified, the \(I\) and \(J\) settings still need to be
specified, but are ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff command}}}}, \(I\) and
\(J\) can be specified in one of several ways.  Explicit numeric values
can be used for each, as in the first example above.  Or, one or both of
the types in the I,J pair can be a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{type label}}}}.
LAMMPS sets the coefficients for the symmetric \(J,I\) interaction to
the same values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with
the \(I,J\) arguments to set the coefficients for multiple pairs of atom
types.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\)
is the number of atom types, then an asterisk with no numeric values
means all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from
1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from m to \(N\)
(inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).  For the asterisk syntax, note that only type pairs with
\(I \le J\) are considered; if asterisks imply type pairs where
\(J < I\), they are ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPORTANT NOTE: If {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid or hybrid/overlay}}}} is being used, then the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} will be a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style
name.  You must specify \(I,J\) arguments that correspond to type pair
values defined (via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command) for
that sub\sphinxhyphen{}style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} argument for keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} is the name of an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} which will be evaluated each time
this fix is invoked to set the parameter to a new value.  It should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can specify formulas with various mathematical functions, and
include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command keywords for the
simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed time.  Thus it is
easy to specify parameters that change as a function of time or span
consecutive runs in a continuous fashion.  For the latter, see the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command and the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{elaplong} keyword of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, these commands would change the prefactor coefficient of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style soft}}}} potential from 10.0 to 30.0 in a
linear fashion over the course of a simulation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prefactor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{10,30}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}prefactor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} keyword uses the specified variable to change the value of
a bond coefficient over time, very similar to how the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword
operates. The only difference is that now a bond coefficient for a
given bond type is adapted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with the
bond type argument to set the coefficients for multiple bond types.
This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is
the number of bond types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means
all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from
1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from m to
\(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} does not support bond\_style hybrid nor bond\_style
hybrid/overlay as bond styles. The bond styles that currently work
with fix\_adapt are

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} keyword uses the specified variable to change the value of
an angle coefficient over time, very similar to how the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword
operates. The only difference is that now an angle coefficient for a
given angle type is adapted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with the
angle type argument to set the coefficients for multiple angle types.
This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is
the number of angle types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means
all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from
1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from m to
\(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} does not support angle\_style hybrid nor angle\_style
hybrid/overlay as angle styles. The angle styles that currently work
with fix\_adapt are

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that internally, theta0 is stored in radians, so the variable
this fix uses to reset theta0 needs to generate values in radians.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} keyword used the specified variable as a scale factor on
the energy, forces, virial calculated by whatever \(k\)\sphinxhyphen{}space solver is
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command.  If the
variable has a value of 1.0, then the solver is unaltered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} keyword works this way whether the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword
is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword enables various atom properties to be changed.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aparam} argument is the name of the parameter to change.  This is the
current list of atom parameters that can be varied by this fix:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
charge = charge on particle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
diameter or diameter/disc = diameter of particle

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} argument of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword is the name of an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} which will be evaluated each
time this fix is invoked to set, or scale the parameter to a new
value.  It should be specified as v\_name, where name is the variable
name.  See the discussion above describing the formulas associated
with equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables.  The new value is assigned to the
corresponding attribute for all atoms in the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the atom parameter is \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter} and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom density and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
mass are defined for particles (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style granular}}}}), then the mass of each particle is, by default, also
changed when the diameter changes. The mass is set from the particle
volume for 3d systems (density is assumed to stay constant). For 2d,
the default is for LAMMPS to model particles with a radius attribute
as spheres. However, if the atom parameter is \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter/disc}, then the
mass is set from the particle area (the density is assumed to be in
mass/distance\(^2\) units). The mass of the particle may also be kept
constant if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mass} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}. This can be useful to account
for diameter changes that do not involve mass changes (e.g., thermal
expansion).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, these commands would shrink the diameter of all granular
particles in the “center” group from 1.0 to 0.1 in a linear fashion
over the course of a 1000\sphinxhyphen{}step simulation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{1.0,0.1}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{center}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diameter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}size}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be used in long simulations which are restarted one or
more times to continuously adapt simulation parameters, but it must be
done carefully.  There are two issues to consider.  The first is how
to adapt the parameters in a continuous manner from one simulation to
the next.  The second is how, if desired, to reset the parameters to
their original values at the end of the last restarted run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that all the parameters changed by this fix are written into a
restart file in their current changed state.  A new restarted
simulation does not know the original time=0 values, unless the
input script explicitly resets the parameters (after the restart file
is read) to the original values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that the time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent variable(s) used in the restart
script should typically be written as a function of time elapsed since
the original simulation began.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With this in mind, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} (the default)
in a restarted simulation, original parameters are not needed.  The
adapted parameters should seamlessly continue their variation relative
to the preceding simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the input script should
typically reset the parameters being adapted to their original values,
so that the scaling formula specified by the variable will operate
correctly.  An exception is if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword is being used with
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale yes}.  In this case, information is added to the restart file
so that per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties in the new run will automatically be
scaled relative to their original values.  This will only work if the
fix adapt command specified in the restart script has the same ID as
the one used in the original script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In a restarted run, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, and the
run ends in this script (as opposed to just writing more restart
files), parameters will be restored to the values they were at the
beginning of the run command in the restart script, which as
explained above, may or may not be the original values of the
parameters.  Again, an exception is if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword is being
used with \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset yes} (in all the runs). In that case, the original
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom parameters are stored in the restart file, and will be
restored when the restarted run finally completes.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword is used and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} keyword is
set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then this fix writes information to a restart file so
that in a restarted run scaling can continue in a seamless manner
and/or the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values can be restored, as explained above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to
this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter
of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy
minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rRESPA time integration}}}}, this fix changes
parameters on the outermost rRESPA level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are scale = no, reset = no, mass = yes.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix adapt/fep@\spxentry{fix adapt/fep}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix adapt/fep command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:fix-adapt-fep-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
adapt/fep = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = adapt simulation settings every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more attribute/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
attribute = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} args = pstyle pparam I J v\_name
  pstyle = pair style name (e.g., lj/cut)
  pparam = parameter to adapt over time
  I,J = type pair(s) to set parameter for (integer or type label)
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates value of pparam
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} arg = v\_name
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates scale factor on K\sphinxhyphen{}space terms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} args = aparam v\_name
  aparam = parameter to adapt over time
  I = type(s) to set parameter for (integer or type label)
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates value of aparam
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{after}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = the variable value is the new setting
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = the variable value multiplies the original setting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = values will remain altered at the end of a run
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = reset altered values to their original values at the end
  of a run
\sphinxstyleemphasis{after} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = parameters are adapted at timestep N
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = parameters are adapted one timestep after N
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}prefactor}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}prefactor}

Example input scripts available: examples/PACKAGES/fep


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change or adapt one or more specific simulation attributes or settings
over time as a simulation runs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is an enhanced version of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}} command
with two differences:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is possible to modify the charges of chosen atom types only,
instead of scaling all the charges in the system.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is a new option \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} for better compatibility with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This version is suited for free energy calculations using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_ti::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute ti}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_fep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute fep}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is specified as 0, the specified attributes are only changed
once, before the simulation begins.  This is all that is needed if the
associated variables are not time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} \textgreater{} 0, then changes
are made every \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} steps during the simulation, presumably with a
variable that is time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} keyword, attributes changed by
this fix will or will not be reset back to their original values at
the end of a simulation.  Even if \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, a
restart file written during a simulation will contain the modified
settings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, then the value the parameter is
set to will be whatever the variable generates.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}
keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the value of the altered parameter will
be the initial value of that parameter multiplied by whatever the
variable generates (i.e., the variable is now a “scale factor” applied
in (presumably) a time\sphinxhyphen{}varying fashion to the parameter).  Internally,
the parameters themselves are actually altered; make sure you use the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reset yes} option if you want the parameters to be restored to their
initial values after the run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the parameters are
changed one timestep after the multiple of N. In this manner, if a fix
such as “fix ave/time” is used to calculate averages at every N
timesteps, all the contributions to the average will be obtained with
the same values of the parameters.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword enables various parameters of potentials defined by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command to be changed, if the pair
style supports it.  Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} commands must be used in the usual manner
to specify these parameters initially; the fix adapt command simply
overrides the parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} argument is the name of the pair style.  If {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid or hybrid/overlay}}}} is used, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} should be
a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style name.  For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} could be specified as “soft”
or “lubricate”.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pparam} argument is the name of the parameter to
change.  This is the current list of pair styles and parameters that
can be varied by this fix.  See the doc pages for individual pair
styles and their energy formulas for the meaning of these parameters:

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is easy to add new potentials and their parameters to this
list.  All it typically takes is adding an extract() method to the
pair\_*.cpp file associated with the potential.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for many of the potentials, the parameter that can be varied
is effectively a prefactor on the entire energy expression for the
potential (e.g., the lj/cut epsilon).  The parameters listed as “scale”
are exactly that, since the energy expression for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coul/cut}}}} potential (for example) has no labeled
prefactor in its formula.  To apply an effective prefactor to some
potentials, multiple parameters need to be altered.  For example, the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Buckingham potential}}}} needs both the A and C terms
altered together.  To scale the Buckingham potential, you should thus
list the pair style twice, once for A and once for C.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a type pair parameter is specified, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{I} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{J} settings should
be specified to indicate which type pairs to apply it to.  If a global
parameter is specified, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{I} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{J} settings still need to be
specified, but are ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff command}}}}, \(I\) and
\(J\) can be specified in one of several ways.  Explicit numeric values
can be used for each, as in the first example above.  Or, one or both of
the types in the I,J pair can be a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{type label}}}}.
LAMMPS sets the coefficients for the symmetric \(J,I\) interaction to
the same values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with
the \(I,J\) arguments to set the coefficients for multiple pairs of atom
types.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is
the number of atom types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means
all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from 1 to n
(inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from m to \(N\)
(inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).  For the asterisk syntax, note that only type pairs with
\(I \le J\) are considered; if asterisks imply type pairs where
\(J < I\), they are ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPROTANT NOTE: If {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid or hybrid/overlay}}}} is
being used, then the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} will be a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style name.  You must specify
\(I,J\) arguments that correspond to type pair values defined (via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command) for that sub\sphinxhyphen{}style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} argument for keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} is the name of an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} which will be evaluated each time
this fix is invoked to set the parameter to a new value.  It should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can specify formulas with various mathematical functions,
and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command keywords for the
simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed time.  Thus it is
easy to specify parameters that change as a function of time or span
consecutive runs in a continuous fashion.  For the latter, see the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command and the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{elaplong} keyword of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, these commands would change the prefactor coefficient of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style soft}}}} potential from 10.0 to 30.0 in a
linear fashion over the course of a simulation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prefactor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{10,30}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}prefactor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} keyword used the specified variable as a scale factor on
the energy, forces, virial calculated by whatever \(k\)\sphinxhyphen{}space solver is
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command.  If the
variable has a value of 1.0, then the solver is unaltered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} keyword works this way whether the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword
is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword enables various atom properties to be changed.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aparam} argument is the name of the parameter to change.  This is the
current list of atom parameters that can be varied by this fix:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
charge = charge on particle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
diameter = diameter of particle

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(I\) argument indicates which atom types are affected. A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card
asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with the \(I\) argument
to set the coefficients for multiple atom types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} argument of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} keyword is the name of an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} which will be evaluated each time
this fix is invoked to set the parameter to a new value.  It should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  See the
discussion above describing the formulas associated with equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables.  The new value is assigned to the corresponding attribute
for all atoms in the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the atom parameter is \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter} and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom density and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
mass are defined for particles (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style granular}}}}),
then the mass of each particle is also changed when the diameter changes
(density is assumed to stay constant).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, these commands would shrink the diameter of all granular
particles in the “center” group from 1.0 to 0.1 in a linear fashion
over the course of a 1000\sphinxhyphen{}step simulation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{1.0,0.1}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{center}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diameter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}size}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rRESPA time integration}}}}, this fix changes
parameters on the outermost rRESPA level.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword “scale yes” is not supported for scaling per\sphinxhyphen{}atom parameters
diameter and change. You can use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}} for those.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_fep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute fep}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_ti::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute ti}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are scale = no, reset = no, after = no.

\index{fix add/heat@\spxentry{fix add/heat}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix add/heat command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:fix-add-heat-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
add/heat = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate} = rate of heat flow (energy/time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ttarget} \sphinxstyleemphasis{k}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ttarget} = target temperature (temperature units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{k} = prefactor (energy/(time*temperature) units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ttarget} \sphinxstyleemphasis{k}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ttarget} = target temperature (temperature units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{k} = prefactor (energy/(time*temperature\textasciicircum{}4) units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = sets current heat flow of particle
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = adds to current heat flow of particle
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constant}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}heat}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{overwrite}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix adds heat to particles with the temperature attribute every timestep
at a given rate. Note that this is an internal temperature of a particle intended
for use with non\sphinxhyphen{}atomistic models like the discrete element method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} style, heat is added at the specified rate. For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style,
heat is added at a rate of \(k (T_{target} - T)\) where \(k\) is the
specified prefactor, \(T_{target}\) is the specified target temperature, and
\(T\) is the temperature of the atom. This may be more representative of a
conductive process. For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} style, heat is added at a rate of
\(k (T_{target}^4 - T^4)\), akin to radiative heat transfer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The rate or temperature can be can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is a variable, it should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the
variable will be evaluated each time step, and its value will be used to
determine the rate of heat added.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters, time step, and elapsed time
to specify time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent heating.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates to specify spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent heating.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, this fix will set the total
heat flow on a particle every timestep, overwriting contributions from pair
styles or other fixes. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, this fix will add heat on
top of other contributions.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.
No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for access by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}. No parameter of this fix can be used
with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is
not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the GRANULAR package.  It is
only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store temperature and heat flow
as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} command or
included in certain atom styles, such as atom\_style rheo/thermal.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_heat_flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix heat/flow}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_add_heat:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}

\index{fix addforce@\spxentry{fix addforce}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix addforce command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:fix-addforce-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
addforce = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fx,fy,fz = force component values (force units)

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
any of fx,fy,fz can be a variable (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{every} value = Nevery
  Nevery = add force every this many time steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region atoms must be in to have added force
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} value = v\_name
  v\_name = variable with name that calculates the potential energy of each atom in the added force field
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{kick}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{kick}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}oscillate}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}push}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}espace}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add \((f_x,f_y,f_z)\) to the corresponding component of the force for each
atom in the group.  This command can be used to give an additional push to
atoms in a simulation, such as for a simulation of Poiseuille flow in
a channel.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the three quantities defining the force components, namely \(f_x\),
\(f_y\), and \(f_z\), can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is a variable, it should be specified
as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable
will be evaluated each time step, and its value(s) will be used to determine
the force component(s).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters, time step, and elapsed time.
Thus, it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus, it is easy to specify a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force
field with optional time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} keyword is used, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} setting determines how
often the forces are applied.  The default value is 1, for every
time step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the atom must also be in the
specified geometric {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} in order to have force added
to it.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Adding a force to atoms implies a change in their potential energy as
they move due to the applied force field.  For dynamics via the “run”
command, this energy can be optionally added to the system’s potential
energy for thermodynamic output (see below).  For energy minimization
via the “minimize” command, this energy must be added to the system’s
potential energy to formulate a self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent minimization problem
(see below).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is not allowed if the added force is a constant
vector \(\vec F = (f_x,f_y,f_z)\), with all components defined as numeric
constants and not as variables.  This is because LAMMPS can compute
the energy for each atom directly as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -\vec x \cdot \vec F = -(x f_x + y f_y + z f_z),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
so that \(-\vec\nabla E = \vec F\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is optional if the added force is defined with
one or more variables, and if you are performing dynamics via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  If the keyword is not used, LAMMPS will set
the energy to 0.0, which is typically fine for dynamics.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is required if the added force is defined with
one or more variables, and you are performing energy minimization via
the “minimize” command.  The keyword specifies the name of an
atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} which is used to compute the
energy of each atom as function of its position.  Like variables used
for \(f_x\), \(f_y\), \(f_z\), the energy variable is specified as
v\_name, where name is the variable name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is used during an energy
minimization, you must ensure that the formula defined for the
atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} is consistent with the force
variable formulas (i.e., that \(-\vec\nabla E = \vec F\)).
For example, if the force were a spring\sphinxhyphen{}like, \(\vec F = -k\vec x\), then
the energy formula should be \(E = \frac12 kx^2\).  If you do not do this
correctly, the minimization will not converge properly.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy inferred by the added force to
the global potential energy of the system as part of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for
this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.  Note that this
energy is a fictitious quantity but is needed so that the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command can include the forces added by
this fix in a consistent manner (i.e., there is a decrease in
potential energy when atoms move in the direction of the added force).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution due to the added forces on atoms to
both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of the system via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be
accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar and a global three\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the potential energy discussed above.
The vector is the total force on the group of atoms before the forces
on individual atoms are changed by the fix.  The scalar and vector
values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.  You should not
specify force components with a variable that has time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence for
use with a minimizer, since the minimizer increments the time step as
the iteration count during the minimization.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the fictitious potential energy associated with the
added forces to be included in the total potential energy of the
system (the quantity being minimized), you MUST enable the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_setforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix setforce}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_aveforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix aveforce}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addforce:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default for the every keyword is every = 1.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix addtorque@\spxentry{fix addtorque}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix addtorque command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:fix-addtorque-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addtorque}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ty}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tz}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
addtorque = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tx,Ty,Tz = torque component values (torque units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
any of Tx,Ty,Tz can be a variable (see below)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{kick}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bead}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addtorque}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{kick}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bead}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{addtorque}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}oscillate}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add a set of forces to each atom in
the group such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the components of the total torque applied on the group (around its
center of mass) are \(T_x\), \(T_y\), and \(T_z\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the group would move as a rigid body in the absence of other
forces.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can be used to drive a group of atoms into rotation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the three quantities defining the torque components can be specified
as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, namely \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tx},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ty}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tz}.  If the value is a variable, it should be specified as
v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable
will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine the
torque component.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent torque.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential “energy” inferred by the added torques
to the global potential energy of the system as part of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for
this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.  Note that this
is a fictitious quantity but is needed so that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command can include the forces added by this fix in a
consistent manner (i.e., there is a decrease in potential energy when
atoms move in the direction of the added forces).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by
this fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its torque. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar and a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector, which can be
accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar
is the potential energy discussed above.  The vector is the total
torque on the group of atoms before the forces on individual atoms are
changed by the fix.  The scalar and vector values calculated by this
fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the fictitious potential energy associated with the
added forces to be included in the total potential energy of the
system (the quantity being minimized), you MUST enable the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You should not specify force components with a variable that has
time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence for use with a minimizer, since the minimizer
increments the timestep as the iteration count during the
minimization.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for
more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_addtorque:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix alchemy@\spxentry{fix alchemy}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix alchemy command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:fix-alchemy-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alchemy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}name}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
alchemy = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
v\_name = variable with name that determines the \(\lambda_R\) value

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{trans}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alchemy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ramp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix command enables an “alchemical transformation” to be performed
between two systems, whereby one system slowly transforms into the other
over the course of a molecular dynamics run.  This is useful for
measuring thermodynamic differences between two different systems.  It
also allows transformations that are not easily possible with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style hybrid/scaled}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt/fep}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example inputs are included in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/alchemy}}
directory for (a) transforming a pure copper system into a
copper/aluminum bronze alloy and (b) transforming two water molecules
in a box of water into a hydronium and a hydroxyl ion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two systems must be defined as {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_replica::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{separate replica}}}} and run in separate partitions of processors using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}partition}}}} command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch.  Exactly two
partitions must be specified, and each partition must use the same number
of processors and the same domain decomposition.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the forces applied to the atoms are the same mix of the forces
from each partition and the simulation starts with the same atom
positions across both partitions, they will generate the same trajectory
of coordinates for each atom, and the same simulation box size and
shape.  The latter two conditions are \sphinxstyleemphasis{enforced} by this fix; it
exchanges coordinates and box information between the replicas.  This is
not strictly required, but since MD simulations are an example of a
chaotic system, even the tiniest random difference will eventually grow
exponentially into an unwanted divergence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Otherwise, the properties of each atom (type, charge, bond and angle
partners, etc.), as well as energy and forces between interacting atoms
(pair, bond, angle styles, etc.) can be different in the two systems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be initialized in the same input script by using commands which
only apply to one or the other replica.  The example scripts use a
world\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command along with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{if::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{if/then/else}}}} commands for this purpose.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{partition::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{partition}}}} command can also be used.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{create\PYGZus{}box }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{box}
\PYG{k}{create\PYGZus{}atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{alloy}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AlCu.eam.alloy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} replace 5\PYGZpc{} of copper with aluminum on the second partition only}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{world}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alloy}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}name\PYGZcb{} == alloy}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{then}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{set type 1 type/fraction 2 0.05 6745234}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both replicas must define an instance of this fix, but with a different
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} variable.  The named variable must be an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or
equivalent {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  The two variables should be
defined so that one ramps \sphinxstyleemphasis{down} from 1.0 to 0.0 for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} replica
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{R=0}) and the other ramps \sphinxstyleemphasis{up} from 0.0 to 1.0 for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{second}
replica (\sphinxstyleemphasis{R=1}).  A simple way is to do this is linearly, which can be
done using the ramp() function of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}
command.  You could also define a variable which returns a value between
0.0 and 1.0 as a non\sphinxhyphen{}linear function of the timestep.  Here is a linear
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{partition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{1.0,0.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{partition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,1.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alchemy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ramp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For an alchemical transformation, the two variables should sum to
exactly 1.0 at any timestep.  LAMMPS does \sphinxstyleemphasis{NOT} check that this is
the case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ramp()}} function to define the two variables, this fix
can easily be used across successive runs in the same input script by
ensuring each instance of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command specifies the
appropriate \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
At each timestep of an MD run, the two instances of this fix evaluate
their respective variables as a \(\lambda_R\) factor, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} = 0
or 1 for each replica.  The forces used by each system for the
propagation of their atoms is set to the sum of the forces for the two
systems, each scaled by their respective \(\lambda_R\) factor.  Thus,
during the MD run, the system will transform incrementally from the
first system to the second system.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As mentioned above, the coordinates of the atoms and box size/shape
must be exactly the same in the two replicas.  Therefore, it is
generally not a good idea to initialize the two replicas by reading
different data files or creating them individually from scratch.
Rather, a single system should be initialized and then desired
modifications applied to the system to either replica.  If your
input script somehow induces the two systems to become different
(e.g. by performing {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify sort}}}}
differently, or by adding or depositing a different number of atoms),
then LAMMPS will detect the mismatch and generate an error.  This is
done by ensuring that each step the number and ordering of atoms is
identical within each pair of processors in the two replicas.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix stores a global scalar (the current value of \(\lambda_R\))
and a global vector of length 3 which contains the potential energy of
the first partition, the second partition and the combined value,
respectively. The global scalar is unitless and “intensive”, the vector
is in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy units}}}} and “extensive”.  These values can be
used by any command that uses a global value from a fix as input.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output howto}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the REPLICA package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There may be only one instance of this fix in use at a time within
each replica.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure_alchemy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure/alchemy}}}} command,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}} command, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt_fep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt/fep}}}}
command, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/scaled}}}} command.


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_alchemy:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{fix amoeba/bitorsion@\spxentry{fix amoeba/bitorsion}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix amoeba/bitorsion command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion:fix-amoeba-bitorsion-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ameoba}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bitorsion}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filename}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
amoeba/bitorsion = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename = force\sphinxhyphen{}field file with AMOEBA bitorsion coefficients

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix            }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bitorsion}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bitorsion.ubiquitin.data}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{proteinX.data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bitorsions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{BiTorsions}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enables 5\sphinxhyphen{}body torsion/torsion interactions to be added
to simulations which use the AMOEBA and HIPPO force fields.  It
matches how the Tinker MD code computes its torsion/torsion
interactions for the AMOEBA and HIPPO force fields.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto amoeba}}}} doc page for more information about
the implementation of AMOEBA and HIPPO in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bitorsion interactions add additional potential energy contributions
to pairs of overlapping phi\sphinxhyphen{}psi dihedrals of amino\sphinxhyphen{}acids, which are
important to properly represent their conformational behavior.  Each
bitorsion interaction is thus defined for a 5\sphinxhyphen{}tuple of atoms
\(IJKLM\) with bonds between successive atoms in the list,
i.e. two overlapping dihedral interactions for atoms \(IJKL\) and
\(JKLM\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples/amoeba directory has a sample input script and data file
for ubiquitin, which illustrates use of the fix amoeba/bitorsion
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As in the example above, this fix should be used before reading a data
file that contains a listing of bitorsion interactions.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{filename} specified should contain the bitorsion parameters for the
AMOEBA or HIPPO force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command must
contain the topology of all the bitorsion interactions, similar to the
topology data for bonds, angles, dihedrals, etc.  Specifically it
should have a line like this in its header section:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
N bitorsions
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(N\) is the number of bitorsion 5\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.  It should
also have a section in the body of the data file like this with \(N\)
lines:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
BiTorsions

       1       1       8      10      12      18      20
       2       5      18      20      22      25      27
       [...]
       N       3     314     315     317      318    330
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first column is an index from 1 to \(N\) to enumerate the
bitorsion 5\sphinxhyphen{}atom tuples; it is ignored by LAMMPS.  The second column
is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} of the interaction; it is an index into the bitorsion
force field file.  The remaining 5 columns are the atom IDs of the
atoms (in order) for the 5\sphinxhyphen{}tuple \(IJKLM\), as described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bitorsions} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{BiTorsions} keywords for the header
and body sections match those specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command following the data file name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The data file should be generated by using the
tools/tinker/tinker2lmp.py conversion script which creates a LAMMPS
data file from Tinker input files, including its PRM file which
contains the parameters necessary for computing bitorsion
interactions.  The script must be invoked with the optional
“\sphinxhyphen{}bitorsion” flag to do this; see the example for the ubiquitin system
in the tools/tinker/README file.  The same conversion script also
creates the file of bitorsion coefficient data which is read by this
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential energy associated with bitorsion interactions can be
output as described below.  It can also be included in the total
potential energy of the system, as output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command, if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy}}}}
command is used, as in the example above.  See the note below about
how to include the bitorsion energy when performing an {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy
minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_bitorsion:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the list of bitorsion interactions to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy of the bitorsion interactions to
both the global potential energy and peratom potential energies of the
system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} or output
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pe_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pe/atom}}}} command.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy yes}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution due to the bitorsion interactions to
both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of the system via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be
accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial yes}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the potential
energy discussed above.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For energy minimization, if you want the potential energy
associated with the bitorsion terms forces to be included in the
total potential energy of the system (the quantity being
minimized), you MUST not disable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_pitorsion:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix            }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pitorsion}
