\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pitorsions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{PiTorsions}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_amoeba_pitorsion:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enables 6\sphinxhyphen{}body pitorsion interactions to be added to
simulations which use the AMOEBA and HIPPO force fields.  It matches
how the Tinker MD code computes its pitorsion interactions for the
AMOEBA and HIPPO force fields.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto amoeba}}}}
doc page for more information about the implementation of AMOEBA and HIPPO in
LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pitorsion interactions add additional potential energy contributions
to 6\sphinxhyphen{}tuples of atoms \(IJKLMN\) that have a bond between atoms
\(K\) and \(L\), where both \(K\) and \(L\) are additionally
bonded to exactly two other atoms. Namely, \(K\) is also bonded to
\(I\) and \(J\), and \(L\) is also bonded to \(M\) and
\(N\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples/amoeba directory has a sample input script and data file
for ubiquitin, which illustrates use of the fix amoeba/pitorsion
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As in the example above, this fix should be used before reading a data
file that contains a listing of pitorsion interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command must
contain the topology of all the pitorsion interactions, similar to the
topology data for bonds, angles, dihedrals, etc.  Specifically, it
should have two lines like these in its header section:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
M pitorsion types
N pitorsions
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(N\) is the number of pitorsion 6\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions and \(M\) is
the number of pitorsion types.  It should also have two sections in the body
of the data file like these with \(M\) and \(N\) lines each:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
PiTorsion Coeffs

       1 6.85
       2 10.2
       [...]
       M 6.85
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
PiTorsions

       1       1       2      4      3      20      21      24
       2       5      21     23     22      37      38      41
       [...]
       N       7      27     29     28      30      35      36
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For PiTorsion Coeffs, the first column is an index from 1 to \(M\)
to enumerate the pitorsion types.  The second column is the single
prefactor coefficient needed for each type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For PiTorsions, the first column is an index from 1 to \(N\) to
enumerate the pitorsion 6\sphinxhyphen{}atom tuples; it is ignored by LAMMPS.  The
second column is the “type” of the interaction; it is an index into
the PiTorsion Coeffs.  The remaining 6 columns are the atom IDs of the
atoms (in order) for the 6\sphinxhyphen{}tuple \(IJKLMN\), as described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pitorsion types} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pitorsions} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{PiTorsion
Coeffs} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{PiTorsions} keywords for the header and body sections of
the data file match those specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command following the data file name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The data file should be generated by using the
tools/tinker/tinker2lmp.py conversion script which creates a LAMMPS
data file from Tinker input files, including its PRM file which
contains the parameters necessary for computing pitorsion
interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential energy associated with pitorsion interactions can be
output as described below.  It can also be included in the total
potential energy of the system, as output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command, if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy}}}}
command is used, as in the example above.  See the note below about
how to include the pitorsion energy when performing an {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy
minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{fix append/atoms command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:fix-append-atoms-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{face}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
append/atoms = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
face = \sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{basis} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{size} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{freq} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{random} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{basis} values = M itype
  M = which basis atom
  itype = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N) to assign to this basis atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{size} args = Lz
  Lz = z size of lattice region appended in a single event(distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{freq} args = freq
  freq = the number of timesteps between append events
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} args = target damp seed extent
  target = target temperature for the region between zhi\sphinxhyphen{}extent and zhi (temperature units)
  damp = damping parameter (time units)
  seed = random number seed for langevin kicks
  extent = extent of thermostatted region (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{random} args = xmax ymax zmax seed
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{xmax}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ymax}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zmax} = maximum displacement in particular direction (distance units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} = random number seed for random displacement
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} = the wall position is defined in lattice units
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} = the wall position is defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{freq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{295}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{15.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{freq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{freq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix creates atoms on a lattice, appended on the zhi edge of the
system box.  This can be useful when a shock or wave is propagating
from zlo.  This allows the system to grow with time to accommodate an
expanding wave.  A simulation box must already exist, which is
typically created via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command.
Before using this command, a lattice must also be defined using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix will automatically freeze atoms on the zhi edge of the
system, so that overlaps are avoided when new atoms are appended.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{basis} keyword specifies an atom type that will be assigned to
specific basis atoms as they are created.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command for specifics on how basis atoms are
defined for the unit cell of the lattice.  By default, all created
atoms are assigned type = 1 unless this keyword specifies differently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{size} keyword defines the size in \(z\) of the chunk of material to
be added.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{random} keyword will give the atoms random displacements around
their lattice points to simulate some initial temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword will cause a region to be thermostatted with a
Langevin thermostat on the zhi boundary.  The size of the region is
measured from zhi and is set with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extent} argument.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define a wall position, but only when a numeric constant is used.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance units as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command (e.g., \(\AA\)
for units = real or metal.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in lattice spacings.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been previously used to
define the lattice spacings.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style is part of the SHOCK package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The boundary on which atoms are added with append/atoms must be
shrink/minimum.  The opposite boundary may be any boundary type other
than periodic.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_piston::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/piston}}}} command


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_append_atoms:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are size = 0.0, freq = 0, units = lattice.  All
added atoms are of type 1 unless the basis keyword is used.

\sphinxstepscope

\section{fix atc command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:fix-atc-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{parameter\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fixID = name of fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group = name of group fix is to be applied

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{two\_temperature} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hardy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{field}

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} = thermal coupling with fields: temperature
\sphinxstyleemphasis{two\_temperature} = electron\sphinxhyphen{}phonon coupling with field: temperature and electron\_temperature
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hardy} = on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly post\sphinxhyphen{}processing using kernel localization functions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{field} = on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly post\sphinxhyphen{}processing using mesh\sphinxhyphen{}based localization functions
\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
parameter\_file = name of the file with material parameters. Note: Neither hardy nor field requires a parameter file

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ar\PYGZus{}thermal.dat}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{two\PYGZus{}temperature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ar\PYGZus{}ttm.mat}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hardy}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{field}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is the beginning to creating a coupled FE/MD simulation and/or
an on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly estimation of continuum fields. The coupled versions of
this fix do Verlet integration and the post\sphinxhyphen{}processing does not. After
instantiating this fix, several other fix\_modify commands will be
needed to set up the problem (i.e., define the finite element mesh and
prescribe initial and boundary conditions).

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{atc_nanotube}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coupling example is typical, but non\sphinxhyphen{}exhaustive:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} ... commands to create and initialize the MD system}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} initial fix to designate coupling type and group to apply it to}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} tag group physics material\PYGZus{}file}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ar\PYGZus{}thermal.mat}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} create a uniform 12 x 2 x 2 mesh that covers region contain the group}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} nx ny nz region periodicity}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesh}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdRegion}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} specify the control method for the type of coupling}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} physics control\PYGZus{}type}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{control}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flux}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} specify the initial values for the empirical field \PYGZdq{}temperature\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} field node\PYGZus{}group value}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{initial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} create an output stream for nodal fields}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} filename output\PYGZus{}frequency}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{output}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc\PYGZus{}fe\PYGZus{}output}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}

\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
likewise for this post\sphinxhyphen{}processing example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} ... commands to create and initialize the MD system}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} initial fix to designate post\PYGZhy{}processing and the group to apply it to}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} no material file is allowed nor required}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hardy}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} for hardy fix, specific kernel function (function type and range) to \PYGZsh{} be used as a localization function}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{kernel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quartic\PYGZus{}sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} create a uniform 1 x 1 x 1 mesh that covers region contain the group}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} with periodicity this effectively creates a system average}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesh}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} change from default lagrangian map to eulerian}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} refreshed every 100 steps}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom\PYGZus{}element\PYGZus{}map}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eulerian}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} start with no field defined}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} add mass density, potential energy density, stress and temperature}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fields}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stress}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} create an output stream for nodal fields}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} filename output\PYGZus{}frequency}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{output}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvtFE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}

\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the mesh’s linear interpolation functions can be used as the localization function
by using the field option:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{field}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesh}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p}
\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note coupling and post\sphinxhyphen{}processing can be combined in the same simulations using separate fixes.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is not supported by
this fix, but this fix does add the kinetic energy imparted to atoms
by the momentum coupling mode of the AtC package to the global
potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options relevant to this
fix are listed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the energy
discussed in the previous paragraph.  The scalar value is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not
invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atc:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thermal and two\_temperature (coupling) types use a Verlet
time\sphinxhyphen{}integration algorithm. The hardy type does not contain its own
time\sphinxhyphen{}integrator and must be used with a separate fix that does contain
one (e.g., nve, nvt). In addition, currently:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the coupling is restricted to thermal physics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the FE computations are done in serial on each processor.

\end{itemize}

\index{fix atom/swap@\spxentry{fix atom/swap}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix atom/swap command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:fix-atom-swap-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{X}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom/swap = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = invoke this fix every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
X = number of swaps to attempt every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = scaling temperature of the MC swaps (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{types} values = two or more atom types (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} values = chemical potential of swap types (energy units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = no conservation of kinetic energy after atom swaps
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = kinetic energy is conserved after atom swaps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = particle type counts and fractions conserved
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand canonical ensemble, particle fractions not conserved
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region to use as an exchange/move volume
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{29494}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{types}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myFix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12345}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{298.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{my\PYGZus{}swap\PYGZus{}region}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{types}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{SGMC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{345}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{semi}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{grand}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{types}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs Monte Carlo swaps of atoms of one given atom type with
atoms of the other given atom types.  The specified scaling temperature
\sphinxstyleemphasis{T} is used in the Metropolis criterion dictating swap probabilities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform \sphinxstyleemphasis{X} swaps of atoms of one type with atoms of another type
according to a Monte Carlo probability. Swap candidates must be in the
fix group, must be in the region (if specified), and must be of one of
the listed types. Swaps are attempted between candidates that are chosen
randomly with equal probability among the candidate atoms. Swaps are not
attempted between atoms of the same type since nothing would happen.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All atoms in the simulation domain can be moved using regular time
integration displacements (e.g., via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}), resulting
in a hybrid MC+MD simulation. A smaller\sphinxhyphen{}than\sphinxhyphen{}usual timestep size may be
needed when running such a hybrid simulation, especially if the swapped
atoms are not well equilibrated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} keyword is required. At least two atom types must be
specified. If not using \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand}, exactly two atom types are
required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} keyword can be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} to turn off kinetic energy
conservation for swaps. The default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, which means that swapped
atoms have their velocities scaled by the ratio of the masses of the
swapped atom types. This ensures that the kinetic energy of each atom is
the same after the swap as it was before the swap, even though the atom
masses have changed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand} keyword can be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} to switch to the semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand
canonical ensemble as discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:sadigh}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sadigh)}}}}. This means
that the total number of each particle type does not need to be
conserved. The default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, which means that the only kind of swap
allowed exchanges an atom of one type with an atom of a different given
type. In other words, the relative mole fractions of the swapped atoms
remains constant. Whereas in the semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand canonical ensemble, the
composition of the system can change. Note that when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand},
atoms in the fix group whose type is not listed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} keyword
are ineligible for attempted conversion. An attempt is made to switch
the selected atom (if eligible) to one of the other listed types with
equal probability.  Acceptance of each attempt depends upon the
Metropolis criterion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} keyword allows users to specify chemical potentials. This is
required and allowed only when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand}.  All chemical
potentials are absolute, so there is one for each swap type listed
following the \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} keyword.  In semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand canonical ensemble
simulations the chemical composition of the system is controlled by the
difference in these values. So shifting all values by a constant amount
will have no effect on the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command may optionally use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword to define swap
volume.  The specified region must have been previously defined with a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  It must be defined with side = \sphinxstyleemphasis{in}.
Swap attempts occur only between atoms that are both within the
specified region. Swaps are not otherwise attempted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You should ensure you do not swap atoms belonging to a molecule, or
LAMMPS will eventually generate an error when it tries to find those
atoms.  LAMMPS will warn you if any of the atoms eligible for swapping
have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero molecule ID, but does not check for this at the time of
swapping.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If not using \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand} this fix checks to ensure all atoms of the
given types have the same atomic charge. LAMMPS does not enforce this in
general, but it is needed for this fix to simplify the swapping
procedure. Successful swaps will swap the atom type and charge of the
swapped atoms. Conversely, when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand}, it is assumed that
all the atom types involved in switches have the same charge. Otherwise,
charge would not be conserved. As a consequence, no checks on atomic
charges are performed, and successful switches update the atom type but
not the atom charge. While it is possible to use \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand} with
groups of atoms that have different charges, these charges will not be
changed when the atom types change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since this fix computes total potential energies before and after
proposed swaps, so even complicated potential energy calculations are
OK, including the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatics (\(k\)\sphinxhyphen{}space)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
many body pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hybrid pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eam pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
triclinic systems

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
need to include potential energy contributions from other fixes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some fixes have an associated potential energy. Examples of such fixes
include: {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{efield}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gravity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{gravity}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{addforce}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{langevin}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_restrain::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restrain}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/berendsen}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/rescale}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{wall fixes}}}}.  For that energy to be included in the
total potential energy of the system (the quantity used when
performing GCMC moves), you \sphinxstylestrong{must} enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for that fix.  The doc pages for
individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} commands specify if this should be done.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the fix to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This includes information about the random number generator
seed, the next timestep for MC exchanges, the number of exchange
attempts and successes, etc.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For this to work correctly, the timestep must \sphinxstylestrong{not} be changed
after reading the restart with {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}.  The fix will try to detect it and stop with an
error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global vector of length 2, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector values are
the following global cumulative quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
swap attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
swap accepts

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix cannot be used with systems that do not have per\sphinxhyphen{}type masses
(e.g. atom style sphere) since the implemented algorithm pre\sphinxhyphen{}computes
velocity rescaling factors from per\sphinxhyphen{}type masses and ignores any per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
masses, if present.  In case both, per\sphinxhyphen{}type and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses are
present, a warning is printed.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deposit}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_evaporate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix evaporate}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_atoms}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gcmc}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mol_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mol/swap}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sgcmc}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_atom_swap:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} = yes, \sphinxstyleemphasis{semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand} = no, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} = 0.0 for
all atom types.

\sphinxAtStartPar

L Zepeda\sphinxhyphen{}Ruiz, Phys. Rev. B, 85, 184203 (2012).

\index{fix ave/atom@\spxentry{fix ave/atom}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix ave/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom:fix-ave-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ave/atom = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of times to use input values for calculating averages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate averages every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more input values can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, c\_ID, c\_ID{[}i{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}i{]}, v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x,y,z,vx,vy,vz,fx,fy,fz = atom attribute (position, velocity, force component)
c\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}atom array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}atom array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by an atom\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[1]}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use one or more per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors as inputs every few timesteps, and
average them atom by atom over longer timescales.  The resulting
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom averages can be used by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}
such as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}}
commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with the command means only atoms within the group
have their averages computed.  Results are set to 0.0 for atoms not in
the group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each input value can be an atom attribute (position, velocity, force
component) or can be the result of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the evaluation of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  In the latter cases, the compute, fix, or
variable must produce a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector, not a global quantity or
local quantity.  If you wish to time\sphinxhyphen{}average global quantities from a
compute, fix, or variable, then see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each per\sphinxhyphen{}atom value of each input vector is averaged independently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Computes}}}} that produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors or arrays are
those which have the word \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} in their style name.  See the doc
pages for individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} to determine which ones produce
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors or arrays.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Variables}}}} of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}
are the only ones that can be used with this fix since they produce
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for values from a compute or fix, the bracketed index I can
be specified using a wildcard asterisk with the index to effectively
specify multiple values.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*” or
“m*n”.  If \(N\) is the size of the vector (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar) or the
number of columns in the array (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector), then an asterisk
with no numeric values means all indices from 1 to \(N\).  A leading
asterisk means all indices from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing
asterisk means all indices from m to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk
means all indices from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual columns of the array
had been listed one by one.  For example, these two fix ave/atom commands are
equivalent, since the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}}
command creates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with six columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{my\PYGZus{}stress}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stress}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                              }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[4]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                              }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[5]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}stress[6]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{every}\), \(N_\text{repeat}\), and \(N_\text{freq}\)
arguments specify on what timesteps the input values will be used in order to
contribute to the average.  The final averaged quantities are generated on
timesteps that are a multiple of \(N_\text{freq}\).  The average is over
\(N_\text{repeat}\) quantities, computed in the preceding portion of the
simulation every \(N_\text{every}\) timesteps.  \(N_\text{freq}\) must
be a multiple of \(N_\text{every}\) and \(N_\text{every}\) must be
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \(N_\text{repeat}\) is 1.  Also, the timesteps
contributing to the average value cannot overlap; that is,
\(N_\text{repeat} \times N_\text{every}\) cannot exceed \(N_\text{freq}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if \(N_\text{every}=2\), \(N_\text{repeat}=6\), and
\(N_\text{freq}=100\), then values on timesteps 90, 92, 94, 96, 98, and 100
will be used to compute the final average on time step 100.  Similarly for
timesteps 190, 192, 194, 196, 198, and 200 on time step 200, etc.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom attribute values (\sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}) are self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.  Note that other atom attributes can be used as
inputs to this fix by using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}} command and then
specifying an input value from that compute.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} attributes are values that are re\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped inside
the periodic box whenever an atom crosses a periodic boundary.  Thus, if
you time\sphinxhyphen{}average an atom that spends half of its time on either side of
the periodic box, you will get a value in the middle of the box.  If
this is not what you want, consider averaging unwrapped coordinates,
which can be provided by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}}
command via its \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yu}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zu} attributes.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed term is
appended, the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by the compute is used.  If a
bracketed term containing an index \(I\) is appended, the
\(I^\text{th}\) column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array calculated by the compute is
used.  Users can also write code for their own compute styles and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.  See the discussion above for how
\(I\) can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify
multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been previously
defined in the input script.  If no bracketed term is appended, the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
vector calculated by the fix is used.  If a bracketed term containing an index
\(I\) is appended, the \(I^\text{th}\) column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
calculated by the fix is used.  Note that some fixes only produce their values
on certain timesteps, which must be compatible with \(N_\text{every}\),
else an error will result.  Users can also write code for their own fix styles
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.  See the discussion above for how
\(I\) can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify
multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has
been previously defined in the input script as an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}}. Variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} can reference
thermodynamic keywords or invoke other computes, fixes, or variables
when they are evaluated, so this is a very general means of generating
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities to time average.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_atom:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.
No global scalar or vector quantities are stored by this fix for access by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector or array which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  A vector is produced if
only a single quantity is averaged by this fix.  If two or more
quantities are averaged, then an array of values is produced.  The
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values can only be accessed on timesteps that are multiples
of \(N_\text{freq}\) since that is when averaging is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\section{fix ave/chunk command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:fix-ave-chunk-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunkID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ave/chunk = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of times to use input values for calculating averages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate averages every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chunkID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more input values can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mass}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}, c\_ID, c\_ID{[}I{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}I{]}, v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
vx,vy,vz,fx,fy,fz,mass = atom attribute (velocity, force component, mass)
density/number, density/mass = number or mass density (per volume)
temp = temperature
c\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}atom array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}atom array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by an atom\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{format} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sample} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} = how output on \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} steps is normalized
  all = output is sum of atoms across all \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} samples, divided by atom count
  sample = output is sum of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} sample averages, divided by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}
  none = output is sum of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} sample sums, divided by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{running} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window M}
  one = output new average value every Nfreq steps
  running = output cumulative average of all previous Nfreq steps
  window M = output average of M most recent Nfreq steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} arg = bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of a temperature compute that removes a velocity bias for temperature calculation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} value = dof\_per\_atom
  dof\_per\_atom = define this many degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom per atom for temperature calculation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} value = dof\_per\_chunk
  dof\_per\_chunk = define this many degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom per chunk for temperature calculation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} arg = filename
  filename = file to write results to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{append} arg = filename
  filename = file to append results to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} arg = none = overwrite output file with only latest output
\sphinxstyleemphasis{format} arg = string
  string = C\sphinxhyphen{}style format string
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} arg = string
  string = text to print as 1st line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} arg = string
  string = text to print as 2nd line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} arg = string
  string = text to print as 3rd line of output file
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{binchunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{running}

\sphinxAtStartPar
