\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are trying to replace a deprecated fix ave/spatial command
with the newer, more flexible fix ave/chunk and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
chunk/atom}}}} commands, you simply need to split
the fix ave/spatial arguments across the two new commands.  For
example, this command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spatial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{norm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sample}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel.profile}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
could be replaced by:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{norm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sample}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel.profile}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use one or more per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors as inputs every few timesteps, sum
the values over the atoms in each chunk at each timestep, then average
the per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk values over longer timescales.  The resulting chunk
averages can be used by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} such
as {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}}, and can also be written to
a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LAMMPS, chunks are collections of atoms defined by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
chunk/atom}}}} command, which assigns each atom to a
single chunk (or no chunk).  The ID for this command is specified as
chunkID.  For example, a single chunk could be the atoms in a molecule
or atoms in a spatial bin.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} page and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto chunk}}}}
page for details of how chunks can be defined and examples of how they
can be used to measure properties of a system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}}
command defines spatial bins, the fix ave/chunk command performs a
similar computation as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/grid}}}} command.
However, the per\sphinxhyphen{}bin outputs from the fix ave/chunk command are
global; each processor stores a copy of the entire set of bin data.
By contrast, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/grid}}}} command uses a
distributed grid where each processor owns a subset of the bins.  Thus
it is more efficient to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/grid}}}}
command when the grid is large and a simulation is run on many
processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that only atoms in the specified group contribute to the summing
and averaging calculations.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command defines its own group as well as an
optional region.  Atoms will have a chunk ID = 0, meaning they belong
to no chunk, if they are not in that group or region.  Thus you can
specify the “all” group for this command if you simply want to use the
chunk definitions provided by chunkID.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each specified per\sphinxhyphen{}atom value can be an atom attribute (position,
velocity, force component), a number or mass density, a mass or
temperature, or the result of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the evaluation of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.
In the latter cases, the compute, fix, or variable must produce a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity, not a global quantity.  Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
property/atom}}}} command provides access to any
attribute defined and stored by atoms.  If you wish to time\sphinxhyphen{}average
global quantities from a compute, fix, or variable, then see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values of each input vector are summed and averaged
independently of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values in other input vectors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Computes}}}} that produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are those
which have the word \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} in their style name.  See the doc pages for
individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} to determine which ones produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Variables}}}} of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} are the only
ones that can be used with this fix since all other styles of variable
produce global quantities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for values from a compute or fix that produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
array (multiple values per atom), the bracketed index I can be
specified using a wildcard asterisk with the index to effectively
specify multiple values.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “n*”
or “m*n”.  If \(N\) = the size of the vector (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar) or the
number of columns in the array (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector), then an asterisk
with no numeric values means all indices from 1 to \(N\).  A leading
asterisk means all indices from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing
asterisk means all indices from m to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk
means all indices from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual columns of the array
had been listed one by one.  For example, these two fix ave/chunk commands are
equivalent, since the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}} command creates, in this case, a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
array with three columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myAng}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmomx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmomy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmomz}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myAng[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.angmom}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myAng[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myAng[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myAng[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.angmom}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix works by creating an array of size
\(N_\text{chunk} \times N_\text{values}\) on each processor.
\(N_\text{chunk}\) is the number of chunks, which is defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.
\(N_\text{values}\) is the number of input values specified.
Each processor loops over its atoms, tallying its values to the appropriate
chunk.  Then the entire array is summed across all processors.  This means
that using a large number of chunks will incur an overhead in memory and
computational cost (summing across processors), so be careful to
define a reasonable number of chunks.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{every}\), \(N_\text{repeat}\), and \(N_\text{freq}\)
arguments specify on what time steps the input values will be accessed and
contribute to the average.  The final averaged quantities are generated on time
steps that are a multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\).  The average is over
\(N_\text{repeat}\) quantities, computed in the preceding portion of the
simulation every \(N_\text{every}\) time steps.  \(N_\text{freq}\)
must be a multiple of \(N_\text{every}\) and \(N_\text{every}\) must be
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \(N_\text{repeat} = 1\).  Also, the time steps
contributing to the average value cannot overlap (i.e.,
\(N_\text{repeat} \times N_\text{every}\) cannot exceed \(N_\text{freq}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if \(N_\text{every}=2\), \(N_\text{repeat}=6\), and
\(N_\text{freq}=100\), then values on
time steps 90, 92, 94, 96, 98, 100 will be used to compute the final average
on time step 100.  Similarly for time steps 190, 192, 194, 196, 198, 200 on
time step 200, etc.  If \(N_\text{repeat}=1\) and
\(N_\text{freq} = 100\), then no time averaging is done; values are simply
generated on time steps 100, 200, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each input value can also be averaged over the atoms in each chunk.
The way the averaging is done across the \(N_\text{repeat}\) time steps to
produce output on the \(N_\text{freq}\) time steps, and across multiple
\(N_\text{freq}\) outputs, is determined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword
settings, as discussed below.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To perform per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk averaging within a \(N_\text{freq}\) time window,
the number of chunks \(N_\text{chunk}\) defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command must remain
constant.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{running} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window} then
\(N_\text{chunk}\) must remain constant for the duration of the
simulation.  This fix forces the chunk/atom compute specified by chunkID to
hold \(N_\text{chunk}\) constant for the appropriate time windows,
by not allowing it to re\sphinxhyphen{}calculate \(N_\text{chunk}\), which can also
affect how it assigns chunk IDs to atoms.  This is particularly important to
understand if the chunks defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command are spatial bins.  If its \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}, then the number of bins
\(N_\text{chunk}\) and size of each bin will be fixed over the
\(N_\text{freq}\) time window, which can affect which atoms are
discarded if the simulation box size changes.  If its \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword is set
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{reduced}, then the number of bins \(N_\text{chunk}\) will still be
fixed, but the size of each bin can vary at each time step if the
simulation box size changes (e.g., for an NPT simulation).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom attribute values (\sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mass}) are
self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.  As noted above, any other atom attributes can be
used as input values to this fix by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
property/atom}}}} command and then specifying an
input value from that compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number} value means the number density is computed for
each chunk (i.e., number/volume).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass} value means the
mass density is computed for each chunk (i.e., total\sphinxhyphen{}mass/volume).  The
output values are in units of 1/volume or mass density (mass/volume).  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command page for the definition of density
for each choice of units (e.g., g/cm\(^3\)).  If the chunks defined by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command are spatial
bins, the volume is the bin volume.  Otherwise, it is the volume of the
entire simulation box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value means the temperature is computed for each chunk,
by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{DOF}}{2} k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the chunk of atoms (sum of
\(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\)), DOF is the the total number of degrees of freedom
for all atoms in the chunk, \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, and
\(T\) is the absolute temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DOF is calculated as \(N\)*adof + cdof, where \(N\) is the
number of atoms in the chunk, adof is the number of degrees of freedom per
atom, and cdof is the number of degrees of freedom per chunk.  By default,
adof = 2 or 3 = dimensionality of system,
as set via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} command, and cdof = 0.0.
This gives the usual formula for temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that currently this temperature only includes translational
degrees of freedom for each atom.  No rotational degrees of freedom
are included for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles.  Also, no degrees of freedom
are subtracted for any velocity bias or constraints that are applied,
such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_partial::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/partial}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This is
because those degrees of freedom (e.g., a constrained bond) could apply
to sets of atoms that are both included and excluded from a specific
chunk, and hence the concept is somewhat ill\sphinxhyphen{}defined.  In some cases,
you can use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} keywords to adjust the calculated
degrees of freedom appropriately, as explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that a bias can be subtracted from atom velocities before
they are used in the above formula for KE, by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias}
keyword.  This allows, for example, a thermal temperature to be
computed after removal of a flow velocity profile.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk temperature calculated by this fix and the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/chunk}}}} command can be
different.  The compute calculates the temperature for each chunk for
a single snapshot.  This fix can do that but can also time average
those values over many snapshots, or it can compute a temperature as
if the atoms in the chunk on different time steps were collected
together as one set of atoms to calculate their temperature.  The
compute allows the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity of each chunk to be
subtracted before calculating the temperature; this fix does not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed integer is
appended, the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by the compute is used.  If a
bracketed integer is appended, the Ith column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
calculated by the compute is used.  Users can also write code for
their own compute styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.
See the discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard
asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed integer is
appended, the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by the fix is used.  If a
bracketed integer is appended, the Ith column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
calculated by the fix is used.  Note that some fixes only produce
their values on certain time steps, which must be compatible with
\(N_\text{every}\), else an error results.  Users can also write code for
their own fix styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.  See the
discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk
to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has
been previously defined in the input script.  Variables of style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} can reference thermodynamic keywords and various per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
attributes, or invoke other computes, fixes, or variables when they
are evaluated, so this is a very general means of generating per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities to average within chunks.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional optional keywords also affect the operation of this fix
and its outputs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} keyword affects how averaging is done for the per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk
values that are output every \(N_\text{freq}\) time steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}, which is the default, a chunk value is summed
over all atoms in all \(N_\text{repeat}\) samples, as is the count of
atoms in the chunk.  The averaged output value for the chunk on the
\(N_\text{freq}\) time steps is Total\sphinxhyphen{}sum / Total\sphinxhyphen{}count.  In other words it
is an average over atoms across the entire \(N_\text{freq}\) timescale.
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass} values, the volume (bin volume or
system volume) used in the final normalization will be the volume at
the final \(N_\text{freq}\) time step. For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values, degrees of
freedom and kinetic energy are summed separately across the entire
\(N_\text{freq}\) timescale, and the output value is calculated by dividing
those two sums.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{sample}, the chunk value is summed over
atoms for each sample, as is the count, and an “average sample value”
is computed for each sample (i.e., Sample\sphinxhyphen{}sum / Sample\sphinxhyphen{}count).  The
output value for the chunk on the \(N_\text{freq}\) time steps is the
average of the \(N_\text{repeat}\) “average sample values” (i.e., the sum
of \(N_\text{repeat}\) “average sample values” divided by
\(N_\text{repeat}\)).  In other words, it is an average of an average.
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass} values, the volume (bin volume or
system volume) used in the per\sphinxhyphen{}sample normalization will be the current volume
at each sampling step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}, a similar computation as for the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sample} setting is done, except the individual “average sample
values” are “summed sample values”.  A summed sample value is simply
the chunk value summed over atoms in the sample, without dividing by
the number of atoms in the sample.  The output value for the chunk on
the \(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps is the average of the
\(N_\text{repeat}\) “summed sample values” (i.e., the sum of
\(N_\text{repeat}\) “summed sample values” divided by
\(N_\text{repeat}\)).
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass} values, the
volume (bin volume or system volume) used in the per\sphinxhyphen{}sample sum
normalization will be the current volume at each sampling step.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword determines how the per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk values produced every
\(N_\text{freq}\) steps are averaged with values produced on previous steps
that were multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\), before they are accessed by
another output command or written to a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{one}, which is the default, then the chunk
values produced on timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are
independent of each other; they are output as\sphinxhyphen{}is without further averaging.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}, then the chunk values produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are summed and averaged
in a cumulative sense before being output.  Each output chunk value is thus
the average of the chunk value produced on that timestep with all
preceding values for the same chunk.  This running average begins when
the fix is defined; it can only be restarted by deleting the fix via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}} command, or re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix by re\sphinxhyphen{}specifying it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{window}, then the chunk values produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are summed and averaged
within a moving “window” of time, so that the last \(M\) values for the
same chunk are used to produce the output.  For example, if \(M = 3\) and
\(N_\text{freq} = 1000\), then the output on step 10000 will be the average
of the individual chunk values on time steps 8000, 9000, and 10000.  Outputs on
early steps will average over less than \(M\) values if they are not
available.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword specifies the ID of a temperature compute that
removes a “bias” velocity from each atom, specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID}.
It is only used when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value is calculated, to compute the
thermal temperature of each chunk after the translational kinetic
energy components have been altered in a prescribed way (e.g., to
remove a flow velocity profile).  See the doc pages for individual
computes that calculate a temperature to see which ones implement a bias.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} keywords define the values used in the degree of
freedom (DOF) formula described above for temperature calculation
for each chunk.  They are only used when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value is
calculated.  They can be used to calculate a more appropriate
temperature for some kinds of chunks.  Here are three examples:

\sphinxAtStartPar
If spatially binned chunks contain some number of water molecules and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} is used to make each molecule rigid, then
you could calculate a temperature with six degrees of freedom (DOF) (three
translational, three rotational) per molecule by setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} to 2.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_partial::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/partial}}}} is used with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword to only allow the \(x\) component of velocity to contribute
to the temperature, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} = 1.0 would be appropriate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If each chunk consists of a large molecule, with some number of its
bonds constrained by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or the entire molecule
by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small}}}}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} = 0.0 and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} could be
set to the remaining degrees of freedom for the entire molecule
(entire chunk in this case), that is, 6 for 3d or 3 for 2d for a rigid
molecule.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024: }new keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{append}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} keywords allow a filename to be specified.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} is used, then the filename is overwritten if it already exists.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} is used, then the filename is appended to if it already
exists, or created if it does not exist.  Every \(N_\text{freq}\)
timesteps, a section of chunk info will be written to a text file in the
following format.  A line with the timestep and number of chunks is
written.  Then one line per chunk is written, containing the chunk ID
\((1-N_\text{chunk}),\) an optional original ID value, optional
coordinate values for chunks that represent spatial bins, the number of
atoms in the chunk, and one or more calculated values.  More explanation
of the optional values is given below.  The number of values in each
line corresponds to the number of values specified in the fix ave/chunk
command.  The number of atoms and the value(s) are summed or average
quantities, as explained above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} keyword will continuously overwrite the output file
with the latest output, so that it only contains one timestep worth of
output.  This option can only be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave running} setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{format} keyword sets the numeric format of each value when it is
printed to a file via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword.  Note that all values are
floating point quantities.  The default format is \%g.  You can specify
a higher precision if desired (e.g., \%20.16g).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} keywords allow specification of
the strings that will be printed as the first three lines of the output
file, assuming the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword was used.  LAMMPS uses default
values for each of these, so they do not need to be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, these header lines are as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Chunk\PYGZhy{}averaged data for fix ID and group name
\PYGZsh{} Timestep Number\PYGZhy{}of\PYGZhy{}chunks
\PYGZsh{} Chunk (OrigID) (Coord1) (Coord2) (Coord3) Ncount value1 value2 ...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the first line, ID and name are replaced with the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID and group
name.  The second line describes the two values that are printed at
the first of each section of output.  In the third line the values are
replaced with the appropriate value names (e.g., \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx} or c\_myCompute{[}2{]}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The words in parenthesis only appear with corresponding columns if the
chunk style specified for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command supports them.  The OrigID column is
only used if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{compress} keyword was set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.  This means
that the original chunk IDs (e.g., molecule IDs) will have been
compressed to remove chunk IDs with no atoms assigned to them.  Thus a
compressed chunk ID of 3 may correspond to an original chunk ID or
molecule ID of 415.  The OrigID column will list 415 for the third chunk.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CoordN columns only appear if a \sphinxstyleemphasis{binning} style was used in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/1d},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/2d}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/3d} styles the column values are the center point
of the bin in the corresponding dimension.  Just Coord1 is used for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/1d}, Coord2 is added for \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/2d}, Coord3 is added for \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/3d}.
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/sphere}, just Coord1 is used, and it is the radial
coordinate.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/cylinder}, Coord1 and Coord2 are used.  Coord1
is the radial coordinate (away from the cylinder axis), and coord2 is
the coordinate along the cylinder axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword used in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom command}}}} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}, the coordinate values will be in distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.
If the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{reduced}, the
coordinate values will be in unitless reduced units (0\textendash{}1).  This is
not true for the Coord1 value of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/sphere} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/cylinder}
which both represent radial dimensions.  Those values are always in
distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global array of values which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The values can only be
accessed on timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\), since
that is when averaging is performed.  The global array has \# of rows =
the number of chunks \(N_\text{chunk}\), as calculated by the
specified {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.  The \#
of columns is \(M+1+N_\text{values}\), where \(M \in
\{1,\dotsc,4\}\), depending on whether the optional columns for OrigID
and CoordN are used, as explained above.  Following the optional
columns, the next column contains the count of atoms in the chunk, and
the remaining columns are the Nvalue quantities.  When the array is
accessed with a row \(I\) that exceeds the current number of chunks,
than a 0.0 is returned by the fix instead of an error, since the number
of chunks can vary as a simulation runs depending on how that value is
computed by the compute chunk/atom command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The array values calculated by this fix are treated as “intensive”,
since they are typically already normalized by the count of atoms in
each chunk.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/grid}}}}


\subsection{Default}

The option defaults are norm = all, ave = one, bias = none, no file
output, and title 1,2,3 = strings as described above.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix ave/correlate@\spxentry{fix ave/correlate}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix ave/correlate command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate:fix-ave-correlate-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ave/correlate = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of correlation time windows to accumulate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate time window averages every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more input values can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = c\_ID, c\_ID{[}N{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}N{]}, v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
c\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = global value calculated by an equal\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
v\PYGZus{}name[I] = Ith component of a vector\PYGZhy{}style variable with name, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefactor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{upper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lower} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/upper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/lower} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{full}
  auto = correlate each value with itself
  upper = correlate each value with each succeeding value
  lower = correlate each value with each preceding value
  auto/upper = auto + upper
  auto/lower = auto + lower
  full = correlate each value with every other value, including itself = auto + upper + lower
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}
  one = zero the correlation accumulation every Nfreq steps
  running = accumulate correlations continuously
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} args = Nstart
  Nstart = start accumulating correlations on this timestep
\sphinxstyleemphasis{prefactor} args = value
  value = prefactor to scale all the correlation data by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} arg = filename
  filename = name of file to output correlation data to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} arg = none = overwrite output file with only latest output
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} arg = string
  string = text to print as 1st line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} arg = string
  string = text to print as 2nd line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} arg = string
  string = text to print as 3rd line of output file
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp.correlate}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{running}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{title1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{My correlation data}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use one or more global scalar values as inputs every few timesteps,
calculate time correlations between them at varying time intervals,
and average the correlation data over longer timescales.  The resulting
correlation values can be time integrated by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}} or used by other
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} such as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}}, and can also be written to a file.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate/long}}}} command for an
alternate method for computing correlation functions efficiently over
very long time windows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with this command is ignored.  However, note that
specified values may represent calculations performed by computes and
fixes which store their own “group” definitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each listed value can be the result of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the evaluation of an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  In each case, the compute, fix, or variable
must produce a global quantity, not a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local quantity.  If
you wish to spatial\sphinxhyphen{} or time\sphinxhyphen{}average or histogram per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities
from a compute, fix, or variable, then see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}} commands.  If you wish to convert a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity into a single global value, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The input values must be all scalars.  What kinds of
correlations between input values are calculated is determined by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} keyword as discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Computes}}}} that produce global quantities are those which
do not have the word \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} in their style name.  Only a few
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} produce global quantities.  See the doc pages for
individual fixes for info on which ones produce such values.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Variables}}}} of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} are the only
ones that can be used with this fix.  Variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} cannot
be used, since they produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For input values from a compute or fix or variable , the bracketed
index I can be specified using a wildcard asterisk with the index to
effectively specify multiple values.  This takes the form “*” or
“*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the size of the vector, then an
asterisk with no numeric values means all indices from 1 to \(N\).  A
leading asterisk means all indices from 1 to n (inclusive).  A
trailing asterisk means all indices from m to \(N\) (inclusive).
A middle asterisk means all indices from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual elements of the
vector had been listed one by one.  For example, the following two fix
ave/correlate commands are equivalent, since the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} command creates a global vector with six values:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myPress}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[4]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[5]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myPress[6]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, only the wildcard forms “*n” or
“m*n” are allowed.  You must specify the upper bound, because
vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable lengths are not determined until the variable
is evaluated.  If n is specified larger than the vector length
turns out to be, zeroes are output for missing vector values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{every}\), \(N_\text{repeat}\), and \(N_\text{freq}\)
arguments specify on what timesteps the input values will be used to calculate
correlation data.  The input values are sampled every \(N_\text{every}\)
time steps.  The correlation data for the preceding samples is computed on
time steps that are a multiple of \(N_\text{freq}\).  Consider a set of
samples from some initial time up to an output timestep.  The initial time
could be the beginning of the simulation or the last output time; see the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave}
keyword for options.  For the set of samples, the correlation value
\(C_{ij}\) is calculated as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}C_{ij}(\Delta t) = \left\langle V_i(t) V_j(t+\Delta t)\right\rangle,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which is the correlation value between input values \(V_i\) and
\(V_j\), separated by time \(\Delta t\).  Note that the second value
\(V_j\) in the pair is always the one sampled at the later time.  The
average is an average over every pair of samples in the set that are separated
by time \(\Delta t\).  The maximum \(\Delta t\) used is of size
\((N_\text{repeat} - 1) N_\text{every}\).
Thus the correlation between a pair of input values yields
\(N_\text{repeat}\) correlation data:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}C_{ij}(0), C_{ij}(N_\text{every}), C_{ij}(2N_\text{every}), \dotsc,
  C_{ij}\bigl((N_\text{repeat}-1) N_\text{every}\bigr)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if \(N_\text{every}=5\), \(N_\text{repeat}=6\), and
\(N_\text{freq}=100\), then values on time steps
\(0, 5, 10, 15,\dotsc,100\) will be used to compute the final averages
on time step 100.  Six averages will be computed: \(C_{ij}(0)\),
\(C_{ij}(5)\), \(C_{ij}(10)\), \(C_{ij}(15)\), \(C_{ij}(20)\),
and \(C_{ij}(25)\).  \(C_{ij}(10)\) on time step 100 will
be the average of 19 samples, namely \(V_i(0) V_j(10)\),
\(V_i(5) V_j(15)\), \(V_i(10) V_j(20)\),
\(V_i(15) V_j(25), \dotsc,\)
\(V_i(85) V_j(95)\), and \(V_i(90) V_j(100)\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N_\text{freq}\) must be a multiple of \(N_\text{every}\);
\(N_\text{every}\) and \(N_\text{repeat}\) must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero.
Also, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} which is the default, then
\(N_\text{freq} \ge (N_\text{repeat} -1) N_\text{every}\) is required.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed term is
appended, the global scalar calculated by the compute is used.  If a
bracketed term is appended, the \(I^\text{th}\) element of the global
vector calculated by the compute is used.  See the discussion above for how
\(I\) can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify
multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that there is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command
that can sum per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities into a global scalar or vector which
can then be accessed by fix ave/correlate.  It can also be a compute defined
not in your input script, but by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}
or other fixes such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}.  See the doc pages for
these commands which give the IDs of these computes.  Users can also
write code for their own compute styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed term is
appended, the global scalar calculated by the fix is used.  If a
bracketed term is appended, the \(I^\text{th}\) element of the global
vector calculated by the fix is used.  See the discussion above for how
\(I\) can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify
multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that some fixes only produce their values on certain timesteps,
which must be compatible with \(N_\text{every}\), else an error will
result.  Users can also write code for their own fix styles and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  Only equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can be referenced; the latter requires a bracketed term to specify
the \(I^\text{th}\) element of the vector calculated by the variable.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for details. Note that variables of
style \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} define a formula which can reference individual atom
properties or thermodynamic keywords, or they can invoke other computes, fixes,
or variables when they are evaluated, so this is a very general means of
specifying quantities to time correlate.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional optional keywords also affect the operation of this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} keyword determines which pairs of input values are
correlated with each other.  For \(N\) input values \(V_i\),
with \(i \in \{1,\dotsc,N\}\), let the number of pairs be
\(N_\text{pair}\).  Note that the second value in the
pair, \(V_i(t) V_j(t+\Delta t)\), is always the one sampled at the later
time.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto} then each input value is correlated with
itself (i.e., \(C_{ii} = V_i^2\) for \(i \in \{1,\dotsc,N\}\),
so \(N_\text{pair} = N\)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{upper} then each input value is correlated with every
succeeding value (i.e., \(C_{ij} = V_i V_j\) for \(i < j\), so
\(N_\text{pair} = N (N-1)/2\)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{lower} then each input value is correlated with every
preceding value (i.e., \(C_{ij} = V_i V_j\) for \(i > j\), so
\(N_\text{pair} = N(N-1)/2\)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/upper} then each input value is correlated
with itself and every succeeding value (i.e., \(C_{ij} = V_i V_j\)
for \(i \ge j\), so \(N_\text{pair} = N(N+1)/2\)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/lower} then each input value is correlated
with itself and every preceding value (i.e., \(C_{ij} = V_i V_j\)
for \(i \le j\), so \(N_\text{pair} = N(N+1)/2\)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{full} then each input value is correlated with
itself and every other value (i.e., \(C_{ij} = V_i V_j\) for
\(\{i,j\} = \{1,N\}\), so \(N_\text{pair} = N^2\)).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword determines what happens to the accumulation of correlation
samples every \(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{one},
then the accumulation is restarted or zeroed every \(N_\text{freq}\)
timesteps.  Thus the outputs on successive \(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps are
essentially independent of each other.  The exception is that the
\(C_{ij}(0) = V_i(t) V_j(t)\) value at a time step \(t,\) where
\(t\) is a multiple of \(N_\text{freq}\), contributes to the
correlation output both at time \(t\) and at time \(t+N_\text{freq}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}, then the accumulation is never zeroed.
Thus the output of correlation data at any timestep is the average over samples
accumulated every \(N_\text{every}\) steps since the fix was defined.
It can only be restarted by deleting the fix via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}}
command, or by re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix by re\sphinxhyphen{}specifying it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} keyword specifies what time step the accumulation of
correlation samples will begin on.  The default is step 0.  Setting it
to a larger value can avoid adding non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrated data to the
correlation averages.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefactor} keyword specifies a constant which will be used as a multiplier
on the correlation data after it is averaged.  It is effectively a scale factor
on \(V_i V_j\), which can be used to account for the size of the time
window or other unit conversions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword allows a filename to be specified.  Every
\(N_\text{freq}\) steps, an array of correlation data is written to the
file.  The number of rows is \(N_\text{repeat}\), as described above.
The number of columns is \(N_\text{pair}+2\), also as described above.
Thus the file ends up to be a series of these array sections.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} keyword will continuously overwrite the output file
with the latest output, so that it only contains one timestep worth of
output.  This option can only be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave running} setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} keywords allow specification of
the strings that will be printed as the first three lines of the output file,
assuming the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword was used.  LAMMPS uses default values for each of
these, so they do not need to be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, these header lines are as follows:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\# Time\sphinxhyphen{}correlated data for fix ID
\# TimeStep Number\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}time\sphinxhyphen{}windows
\# Index TimeDelta Ncount valueI*valueJ valueI*valueJ ...
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the first line, ID is replaced with the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  The second line
describes the two values that are printed at the first of each section
of output.  In the third line the value pairs are replaced with the
appropriate fields from the fix ave/correlate command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Let \(S_{ij}\) be a set of time correlation data for input values
\(I\) and \(J\), namely the \(N_\text{repeat}\) values:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}S_{ij} = C_{ij}(0), C_{ij}(N_\text{every}), C_{ij}(2N_\text{every}),
 \dotsc, C_{ijI}\bigl((N_\text{repeat}-1) N_\text{every}\bigr)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As explained below, these data are output as one column of a global
array, which is effectively the correlation matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{trap} function defined for {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}}
can be used to perform a time integration of this vector of data,
using a trapezoidal rule.  This is useful for calculating various
quantities which can be derived from time correlation data.  If a
normalization factor is needed for the time integration, it can be
included in the variable formula or via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefactor} keyword.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global array of values which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The values can only be
accessed on timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) since that is
when averaging is performed.  The global array has \# of rows
\(N_\text{repeat}\) and \# of columns \(N_\text{pair}+2\).  The first
column has the time \(\Delta t\) (in time steps) between the pairs of input
values used to calculate the correlation, as described above.  The second
column has the number of samples contributing to the correlation average, as
described above.  The remaining Npair columns are for \(I,J\) pairs of the
\(N\) input values, as determined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} keyword, as described
above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto}, the \(N_\text{pair} = N\) columns are ordered:
\(C_{11}, C_{22}, \dotsc, C_{NN}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{upper}, the \(N_\text{pair} = N(N-1)/2\) columns are
ordered: \(C_{12}, C_{13}, \dotsc, C_{1N}, C_{23}, \dotsc, C_{2N},
C_{34}, \dotsc, C_{N-1,N}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lower}, the \(N_\text{pair} = N(N-1)/2\) columns are
ordered: \(C_{21}, C_{31}, C_{32}, C_{41}, C_{42}, C_{43I}, \dotsc,
C_{N1}, C_{N2}, \dotsc, C_{N,N-1}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/upper}, the \(N_\text{pair} = N(N+1)/2\) columns are
ordered: \(C_{11}, C_{12}, C_{13}, \dotsc, C_{1N}, C_{22}, C_{23},
\dotsc, C_{2N}, C_{33}, C_{34}, \dotsc, C_{N-1,N}, C_{NN}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/lower}, the \(N_\text{pair} = N(N+1)/2\) columns are
ordered: \(C_{11}, C_{21}, C_{22}, C_{31}, C_{32}, C_{33}, C_{41},
\dotsc, C_{44}, C_{N1}, C_{N2}, \dotsc, C_{N,N-1}, C_{NN}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{full}, the \(N_\text{pair} = N^2\) columns are ordered:
\(C_{11}, C_{12}, \dotsc, C_{1N}, C_{21}, C_{22}, \dotsc, C_{2N},
C_{31}, \dotsc, C_{3N}, \dotsc, C_{N1}, \dotsc, C_{N,N-1}, C_{NN}\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The array values calculated by this fix are treated as extensive.  If
you need to divide them by the number of atoms, you must do this in a
later processing step (e.g., when using them in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

none

\section{fix ave/correlate/long command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long:fix-ave-correlate-long-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{correlate}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = c\_ID, c\_ID{[}N{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}N{]}, v\_name, v\_name{[}I{]}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
c\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)

f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = global value calculated by an equal\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
v\PYGZus{}name[I] = Ith component of a vector\PYGZhy{}style variable with name, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ncorr} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nlen} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ncount}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{upper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lower} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/upper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto/lower} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{full}
  auto = correlate each value with itself
  upper = correlate each value with each succeeding value
  lower = correlate each value with each preceding value
  auto/upper = auto + upper
  auto/lower = auto + lower
  full = correlate each value with every other value, including itself = auto + upper + lower
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} args = Nstart
  Nstart = start accumulating correlations on this time step
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} arg = filename
  filename = name of file to output correlation data to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} arg = none = overwrite output file with only latest output
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} arg = string
  string = text to print as 1st line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} arg = string
  string = text to print as 2nd line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ncorr} arg = Ncorrelators
  Ncorrelators = number of correlators to store
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nlen} args = Nlen
  Nlen = length of each correlator
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ncount} args = Ncount
  Ncount = number of values over which successive correlators are averaged
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is similar in spirit and syntax to the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate}}}}.
However, this fix allows the efficient calculation of time correlation
functions on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly over extremely long time windows with little
additional CPU overhead, using a multiple\sphinxhyphen{}\(\tau\) method
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long:ramirez}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ramirez)}}}} that decreases the resolution of the stored
correlation function with time.  It is not a full drop\sphinxhyphen{}in replacement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with this command is ignored.  However, note that
specified values may represent calculations performed by computes and
fixes which store their own “group” definitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each listed value can be the result of a compute or fix or the
evaluation of an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable.  For
vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variables, the specified indices can include a wildcard
character.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate}}}} page
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} arguments specify on what time steps the input
values will be used to calculate correlation data and the frequency
with which the time correlation functions will be output to a file,
respectively.
Note that there is no \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} argument, unlike the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{ncorr}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nlen}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ncount} are unique to this
command and determine the number of correlation points calculated and
the memory and CPU overhead used by this calculation. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nlen} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ncount} determine the amount of averaging done at longer correlation
times.  The default values \sphinxstyleemphasis{nlen} = 16 and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ncount} = 2 ensure that the
systematic error of the multiple\sphinxhyphen{}\(\tau\) correlator is always below the
level of the statistical error of a typical simulation (which depends
on the ensemble size and the simulation length).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The maximum correlation time (in time steps) that can be reached is
given by the formula \((nlen-1) ncount^{(ncorr-1)}\).  Longer correlation
times are discarded and not calculated.  With the default values of
the parameters (\(ncorr=20\), \(nlen=16\) and \(ncount=2\)),
this corresponds to 7864320 time steps.  If longer correlation times are
needed, the value of ncorr should be increased. Using \(nlen=16\) and
\(ncount=2\), with \(ncorr=30\), the maximum number of steps that can
be correlated is 80530636808.  If \(ncorr=40\), correlation times in excess
of \(8\times 10^{12}\) time steps can be calculated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The total memory needed for each correlation pair is roughly
\(4 \times ncorr\times nlen \times 8\) bytes.
With the default values of the parameters, this corresponds to about 10 KB.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the meaning of the additional optional keywords, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate}}}} doc page.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate_long:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Contrary to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_correlate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/correlate}}}} this fix
does \sphinxstylestrong{not} provide access to its internal data to various output
options. Since this fix in intended for the calculation of time
correlation functions over very long MD simulations, the information
about this fix is written automatically to binary restart files, so
that the time correlation calculation can continue in subsequent
simulations. None of the fix\_modify options are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the start/stop keywords of
the run command. This fix is not invoked during energy minimization.
