\section{fix ave/grid command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:fix-ave-grid-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ave/grid = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of times to use input values for calculating averages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate averages every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nx, Ny, Nz = grid size in each dimension

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or per\sphinxhyphen{}grid input values can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom value = vx, vy, vz, fx, fy, fz, density/mass, density/number, mass, temp, c\_ID, c\_ID{[}I{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}I{]}, v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
vx,vy,vz,fx,fy,fz,mass = atom attribute (velocity, force component, mass)
density/number, density/mass = number or mass density (per volume)
temp = temperature
c\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}atom array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}atom array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = per\PYGZhy{}atom vector calculated by an atom\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
per\sphinxhyphen{}grid value = c\_ID:gname:dname, c\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}, f\_ID:gname:dname, f\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
gname = name of grid defined by compute or fix
dname = name of data field defined by compute or fix
c\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}grid vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}grid array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}grid vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}grid array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{discard} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{discard} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  yes = discard an atom outside grid in a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension
  no = remap an atom outside grid in a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimension to first or last grid cell
\sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sample} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} = how output on \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} steps is normalized
  all = output is sum of atoms across all \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} samples, divided by atom count
  sample = output is sum of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} sample averages, divided by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}
  none = output is sum of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} sample sums, divided by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{running} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window M}
  one = output new average value every Nfreq steps
  running = output cumulative average of all previous Nfreq steps
  window M = output average of M most recent Nfreq steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} arg = bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of a temperature compute that removes a velocity bias for temperature calculation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} value = dof\_per\_atom
  dof\_per\_atom = define this many degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom per atom for temperature calculation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} value = dof\_per\_grid\_cell
  dof\_per\_grid\_cell = add this many degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom per grid\_cell for temperature calculation
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myMSD[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}TTM}:grid:data
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overlay the 2d or 3d simulation box with a uniformly spaced 2d or 3d
grid and use it to either (a) time\sphinxhyphen{}average per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities for the
atoms in each grid cell, or to (b) time\sphinxhyphen{}average per\sphinxhyphen{}grid quantities
produced by other computes or fixes.  This fix operates in either
“per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode” (all input values are per\sphinxhyphen{}atom) or in “per\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode”
(all input values are per\sphinxhyphen{}grid).  You cannot use both per\sphinxhyphen{}atom and
per\sphinxhyphen{}grid inputs in the same command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The grid created by this command is distributed; each processor owns
the grid points that are within its subdomain.  This is similar to
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}} command when it uses chunks
from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command which
are 2d or 3d regular bins.  However, the per\sphinxhyphen{}bin outputs in that case
are global; each processor stores a copy of the entire set of bin
data.  Thus it more efficient to use the fix ave/grid command when the
grid is large and a simulation is run on many processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, only atoms in the specified group contribute to the
summing and averaging calculations.  For per\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode, the specified
group is ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{every}\), \(N_\text{repeat}\), and \(N_\text{freq}\)
arguments specify on what time steps the input values will be accessed and
contribute to the average.  The final averaged quantities are generated on time
steps that are a multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\).  The average is over
\(N_\text{repeat}\) quantities, computed in the preceding portion of the
simulation every \(N_\text{every}\) time steps.  \(N_\text{freq}\)
must be a multiple of \(N_\text{every}\) and \(N_\text{every}\) must be
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \(N_\text{repeat} = 1\).  Also, the time steps
contributing to the average value cannot overlap (i.e.,
\(N_\text{repeat} \times N_\text{every}\) cannot exceed \(N_\text{freq}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if \(N_\text{every}=2\), \(N_\text{repeat}=6\), and
\(N_\text{freq}=100\), then values on
time steps 90,92,94,96,98,100 will be used to compute the final average
on timestep 100.  Similarly for timesteps 190,192,194,196,198,200 on
timestep 200, etc.  If \(N_\text{repeat}=1\) and \(N_\text{freq} = 100\), then no time
averaging is done; values are simply generated on timesteps
100,200,etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, each input value can also be averaged over the atoms
in each grid cell.  The way the averaging is done across the \(N_\text{repeat}\)
timesteps to produce output on the \(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps, and across
multiple \(N_\text{freq}\) outputs, is determined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave}
keyword settings, as discussed below.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ny}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} arguments specify the size of the grid that
overlays the simulation box.  For 2d simulations, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} must be 1.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ny}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} values can be any positive integer.  The grid can be
very coarse compared to the particle count, or very fine.  If one or
more of the values = 1, then bins are 2d planes or 1d slices of the
simulation domain.  Note that if the total number of grid cells is
small, it may be more efficient to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}} command which can treat a grid defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command as a global
grid where each processor owns a copy of all the grid cells.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx}
= \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ny} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} = 1 is used, the same calculation would be more
efficiently performed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the simulation box size or shape changes during a simulation, the
grid always conforms to the size/shape of the current simulation box.
If one more dimensions have non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped boundary
conditions, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command, then
the grid will extend over the (dynamic) shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped extent in each
dimension.  If the box shape is triclinic, as explained in {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto
triclinic}}}}, then the grid is also triclinic; each
grid cell is a small triclinic cell with the same shape as the
simulation box.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In both per\sphinxhyphen{}atom and per\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode, input values from a compute or fix
that produces an array of values (multiple values per atom or per grid
point), the bracketed index I can be specified using a wildcard
asterisk with the index to effectively specify multiple values.  This
takes the form “*” or “*n” or “n*” or “m*n”.  If N = the number of
columns in the array (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector), then an asterisk with no
numeric values means all indices from 1 to N.  A leading asterisk
means all indices from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means
all indices from n to N (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all
indices from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual columns of the array
had been listed one by one.  E.g. if there were a compute fft/grid
command which produced 3 values for each grid point, these two fix
ave/grid commands would be equivalent:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myFFT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fft}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myFFT}:grid:data\PYG{n}{[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myFFT}:grid:data\PYG{n}{[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{][1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myFFT}:grid:data\PYG{n}{[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{][2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myFFT}:grid:data\PYG{n}{[3]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each specified per\sphinxhyphen{}atom value can be an atom attribute (velocity,
force component), a number or mass density, a mass or temperature, or
the result of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the
evaluation of an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  In the latter
cases, the compute, fix, or variable must produce a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity,
not a global quantity.  Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}} command provides access to any attribute
defined and stored by atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values of each input vector are summed and averaged
independently of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values in other input vectors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Computes}}}} that produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are those
which have the word \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} in their style name.  See the doc pages for
individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} to determine which ones produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Variables}}}} of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} are the only
ones that can be used with this fix since all other styles of variable
produce global quantities.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom attribute values (vx,vy,vz,fx,fy,fz,mass) are
self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.  As noted above, any other atom attributes can be
used as input values to this fix by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
property/atom}}}} command and then specifying an
input value from that compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number} value means the number density is computed for
each grid cell, i.e. number/volume.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass} value means
the mass density is computed for each grid/cell,
i.e. total\sphinxhyphen{}mass/volume.  The output values are in units of 1/volume or
density (mass/volume).  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command page for
the definition of density for each choice of units, e.g. gram/cm\textasciicircum{}3.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value computes the temperature for each grid cell, by the
formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{DOF}}{2} k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE = total kinetic energy of the atoms in the grid cell (
\(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\)), DOF = the total number of degrees of
freedom for all atoms in the grid cell, \(k_B\) = Boltzmann
constant, and \(T\) = temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DOF is calculated as N*adof + cdof, where N = number of atoms in
the grid cell, adof = degrees of freedom per atom, and cdof = degrees
of freedom per grid cell.  By default adof = 2 or 3 = dimensionality
of system, as set via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} command, and
cdof = 0.0.  This gives the usual formula for temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that currently this temperature only includes translational
degrees of freedom for each atom.  No rotational degrees of freedom
are included for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles.  Also no degrees of freedom
are subtracted for any velocity bias or constraints that are applied,
such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_partial::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/partial}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This is
because those degrees of freedom (e.g. a constrained bond) could apply
to sets of atoms that are both inside and outside a specific grid
cell, and hence the concept is somewhat ill\sphinxhyphen{}defined.  In some cases,
you can use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} keywords to adjust the calculated
degrees of freedom appropriately, as explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that a bias can be subtracted from atom velocities before
they are used in the above formula for KE, by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias}
keyword.  This allows, for example, a thermal temperature to be
computed after removal of a flow velocity profile.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid\sphinxhyphen{}cell temperature calculated by this fix and the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/chunk}}}} command (using bins)
can be different.  The compute calculates the temperature for each
chunk for a single snapshot.  This fix can do that but can also time
average those values over many snapshots, or it can compute a
temperature as if the atoms in the grid cell on different timesteps
were collected together as one set of atoms to calculate their
temperature.  The compute allows the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity of each
chunk to be subtracted before calculating the temperature; this fix
does not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed integer is
appended, the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by the compute is used.  If a
bracketed integer is appended, the Ith column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
calculated by the compute is used.  Users can also write code for
their own compute styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.  See
the discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard
asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If no bracketed integer is
appended, the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by the fix is used.  If a
bracketed integer is appended, the Ith column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
calculated by the fix is used.  Note that some fixes only produce
their values on certain timesteps, which must be compatible with
\(N_\text{every}\), else an error results.  Users can also write code for their
own fix styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.  See the
discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk
to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has
been previously defined in the input script.  Variables of style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} can reference thermodynamic keywords and various per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
attributes, or invoke other computes, fixes, or variables when they
are evaluated, so this is a very general means of generating per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities to average within grid cells.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Per\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The attributes that begin with \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} both take
colon\sphinxhyphen{}separated fields \sphinxstyleemphasis{gname} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dname}.  These refer to a grid
name and data field name which is defined by the compute or fix.  Note
that a compute or fix can define one or more grids (of different
sizes) and one or more data fields for each of those grids.  The sizes
of all grids used as values for one instance of this fix must be the
same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} attributes allow
per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vectors or arrays calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} to
be accessed.  The ID in the attribute should be replaced by the actual
ID of the compute that has been defined previously in the input
script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname} is used as a attribute, then the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector
calculated by the compute is accessed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} is
used, then I must be in the range from 1\sphinxhyphen{}M, which will access the Ith
column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array with M columns calculated by the compute.
See the discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard
asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} attributes allow
per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vectors or arrays calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} to be
output.  The ID in the attribute should be replaced by the actual ID
of the fix that has been defined previously in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname} is used as a attribute, then the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector
calculated by the fix is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} is used,
then I must be in the range from 1\sphinxhyphen{}M, which will print the Ith column
of the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid with M columns calculated by the fix.  See the
discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk
to effectively specify multiple values.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional optional keywords also affect the operation of this fix and
its outputs.  Some are only applicable to per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode.  Some are
applicable to both per\sphinxhyphen{}atom and per\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{discard} keyword is only applicable to per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode.  If a
dimension of the system is non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic, then grid cells will only
span the box dimension (fixed or shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrap boundaries as set by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary command}}}} command).  An atom may thus be slightly outside the
range of grid cells on a particular timestep.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{discard} is set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} (the default), then the atom will be assigned to the closest
grid cell (lowest or highest) in that dimension.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{discard} is set
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} the atom will be ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} keyword is only applicable to per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode.  In per\sphinxhyphen{}grid
mode, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} keyword setting is ignored.  The output grid value on
an \(N_\text{freq}\) timestep is the sum of the grid values in each of the
\(N_\text{repeat}\) samples, divided by \(N_\text{repeat}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
In per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} keyword affects how averaging is done for
the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid values that are output on an \(N_\text{freq}\) timestep. \(N_\text{repeat}\)
samples contribute to the output.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} keyword has 3 possible
settings: \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sample} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{All} is the default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the formulas that follow, SumI is the sum of a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom property
over the CountI atoms in a grid cell for a single sample I, where I
varies from 1 to N, and N = Nrepeat.  These formulas are used for any
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom input value listed above, except \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}.  Those input values are discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, for \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all} the output grid value on the \(N_\text{freq}\)
timestep is an average over atoms across the entire \(N_\text{freq}\) timescale:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output = (Sum1 + Sum2 + … + SumN) / (Count1 + Count2 + … + CountN)

\sphinxAtStartPar
In per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, for \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm sample} the output grid value on the
\(N_\text{freq}\) timestep is an average of an average:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output = (Sum1/Count1 + Sum2/Count2 + … + SumN/CountN) / Nrepeat

\sphinxAtStartPar
In per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, for \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm none} the output grid value on the
\(N_\text{freq}\) timestep is not normalized by the atom counts:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output = (Sum1 + Sum2 + … SumN) / Nrepeat

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass}, the output value is the same
as in the formulas above for \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm sample}, except that
the result is also divided by the grid cell volume.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all},
this will be the volume at the final \(N_\text{freq}\) timestep.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm
sample}, the divide\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}volume is done for each sample, using the grid
cell volume at the sample timestep.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm none}, the output is
the same as for \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}, the output temperature uses the formula for kinetic energy
KE listed above, and is normalized similarly to the formulas above for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm sample}, except for the way the degrees of
freedom (DOF) are calculated.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm none}, the output is the same
as for \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm all}, the DOF = \(N_\text{repeat} \times\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} plus \sphinxstyleemphasis{Count} times
\sphinxstyleemphasis{adof}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{Count} = (Count1 + Count2 + … + CountN).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} keywords are discussed below.  The output temperature is
computed with all atoms across all samples contributing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm sample}, the DOF for a single sample = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} plus \sphinxstyleemphasis{Count}
times \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{Count} = CountI for a single sample.  The output
temperature is the average of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nsample} temperatures calculated for
each sample.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finally, for all 3 \sphinxstyleemphasis{norm} settings the output count of atoms per grid
cell is:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output count = (Count1 + Count2 + … CountN) / Nrepeat

\sphinxAtStartPar
This count is the same for all per\sphinxhyphen{}atom input values, including
\sphinxstyleemphasis{density/number}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{density/mass}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword is applied to both per\sphinxhyphen{}atom and per\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode.  It
determines how the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid values produced once every \(N_\text{freq}\) steps
are averaged with values produced on previous steps that were
multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\), before they are accessed by another output
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{one}, which is the default, then the grid
values produced on \(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps are independent of each other;
they are output as\sphinxhyphen{}is without further averaging.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}, then the grid values produced on
\(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps are summed and averaged in a cumulative sense before
being output.  Each output grid value is thus the average of the grid
value produced on that timestep with all preceding values for the same
grid value.  This running average begins when the fix is defined; it
can only be restarted by deleting the fix via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}}
command, or re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix by re\sphinxhyphen{}specifying it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{window}, then the grid values produced on
\(N_\text{freq}\) timesteps are summed and averaged within a moving “window” of
time, so that the last M values for the same grid are used to produce
the output.  E.g. if M = 3 and Nfreq = 1000, then the grid value
output on step 10000 will be the average of the grid values on steps
8000,9000,10000.  Outputs on early steps will average over less than M
values if they are not available.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} keywords are only applicable to
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword specifies the ID of a temperature compute that
removes a “bias” velocity from each atom, specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID}.
It is only used when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value is calculated, to compute the
thermal temperature of each grid cell after the translational kinetic
energy components have been altered in a prescribed way, e.g.  to
remove a flow velocity profile.  See the doc pages for individual
computes that calculate a temperature to see which ones implement a
bias.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} keywords define the values used in the degree of
freedom (DOF) formula described above for temperature calculation for
each grid cell.  They are only used when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value is
calculated.  They can be used to calculate a more appropriate
temperature in some cases.  Here are 3 examples:

\sphinxAtStartPar
If grid cells contain some number of water molecules and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
shake}}}} is used to make each molecule rigid, then you could
calculate a temperature with 6 degrees of freedom (DOF) (3
translational, 3 rotational) per molecule by setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} to 2.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_partial::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/partial}}}} is used with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword to only allow the x component of velocity to contribute
to the temperature, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{adof} = 1.0 would be appropriate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using \sphinxstyleemphasis{cdof} = \sphinxhyphen{}2 or \sphinxhyphen{}3 (for 2d or 3d simulations) will subtract out 2
or 3 degrees of freedom for each grid cell, similar to how the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} command subtracts out 3 DOF for the
entire system.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array which has one column for each of
the specified input values.  The units for each column with be in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} for the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or per\sphinxhyphen{}grid quantity for the
corresponding input value.  If the fix is used in per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, it
also calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector with the count of atoms in each grid
cell.  The number of rows in the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array and number of values
in the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector (distributed across all processors) is Nx *
Ny * Nz.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For access by other commands, the name of the single grid produced by
this fix is “grid”.  The names of its two per\sphinxhyphen{}grid datums are “data”
for the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array and “count” for the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector (if using
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values).  Both datums can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output
commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mode, the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array values calculated by this fix are
treated as “intensive”, since they are typically already normalized by
the count of atoms in each grid cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_grid:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are discard = yes, norm = all, ave = one, and bias
= none.

\section{fix ave/histo command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:fix-ave-histo-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}}

\section{fix ave/histo/weight command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:fix-ave-histo-weight-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nbin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave/histo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave/histo/weight} = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of times to use input values for calculating histogram

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate histogram every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lo,hi = lo/hi bounds within which to histogram

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nbin = \# of histogram bins

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more input values can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, c\_ID, c\_ID{[}N{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}N{]}, v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x,y,z,vx,vy,vz,fx,fy,fz = atom attribute (position, velocity, force component)
c\PYGZus{}ID = scalar or vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of vector or Ith column of array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = scalar or vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of vector or Ith column of array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = value(s) calculated by an equal\PYGZhy{}style or vector\PYGZhy{}style or atom\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
v\PYGZus{}name[I] = value calculated by a vector\PYGZhy{}style variable with name, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kind} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalar} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector}
  scalar = all input values are scalars
  vector = all input values are vectors
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kind} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{global} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{peratom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} arg = filename
  filename = name of file to output histogram(s) to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{append} arg = filename
  filename = name of file to append histogram(s) to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{running} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window}
  one = output a new average value every Nfreq steps
  running = output cumulative average of all previous Nfreq steps
  window M = output average of M most recent Nfreq steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} args = Nstart
  Nstart = start averaging on this timestep
\sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ignore} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{end} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra}
  ignore = ignore values outside histogram lo/hi bounds
  end = count values outside histogram lo/hi bounds in end bins
  extra = create 2 extra bins for value outside histogram lo/hi bounds
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} arg = none = overwrite output file with only latest output
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} arg = string
  string = text to print as 1st line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} arg = string
  string = text to print as 2nd line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} arg = string
  string = text to print as 3rd line of output file, only for vector mode
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp.histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{running}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{title1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{My output values}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}press[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{18}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{running}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{beyond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{extra}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{weight}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}XRD[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}XRD[2]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use one or more values as inputs every few timesteps to create a
single histogram.  The histogram can then be averaged over longer
timescales.  The resulting histogram can be used by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output
commands}}}}, and can also be written to a file.  The fix
ave/histo/weight command has identical syntax to fix ave/histo, except
that exactly two values must be specified.  See details below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with this command is ignored for global and local
input values.  For per\sphinxhyphen{}atom input values, only atoms in the group
contribute to the histogram.  Note that regardless of the specified
group, specified values may represent calculations performed by
computes and fixes which store their own “group” definition.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A histogram is simply a count of the number of values that fall within
a histogram bin.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nbins} are defined, with even spacing between \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}.  Values that fall outside the lo/hi bounds can be treated in
different ways; see the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each input value can be an atom attribute (position, velocity, force
component) or can be the result of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the evaluation of an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  The set of input values can
be either all global, all per\sphinxhyphen{}atom, or all local quantities.  Inputs
of different kinds (e.g. global and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom) cannot be mixed.  Atom
attributes are per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector values.  See the page for individual
“compute” and “fix” commands to see what kinds of quantities they
generate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that a compute or fix can produce multiple kinds of data (global,
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom, local).  If LAMMPS cannot unambiguously determine which kind
of data to use, the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{kind} keyword discussed below can force
the desired disambiguation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the output of this command is a single histogram for all
input values combined together, not one histogram per input value.
See below for details on the format of the output of this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The input values must either be all scalars or all vectors (or
arrays), depending on the setting of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then the input values must be scalars, or vectors
with a bracketed term appended, indicating the Ith value of the vector
is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, then the input values must be vectors, or arrays
with a bracketed term appended, indicating the Ith column of the array
is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the fix ave/histo/weight command is used, exactly two values must
be specified.  If the values are vectors, they must be the same
length.  The first value (a scalar or vector) is what is histogrammed
into bins, in the same manner the fix ave/histo command operates.  The
second value (a scalar or vector) is used as a “weight”.  This means
that instead of each value tallying a “1” to its bin, the
corresponding weight is tallied.  For example, the \(N^\text{th}\) entry
(weight) in the second vector is tallied to the bin corresponding to the
\(N^\text{th}\) entry in the first vector.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For input values from a compute or fix or variable, the bracketed
index I can be specified using a wildcard asterisk with the index to
effectively specify multiple values.  This takes the form “*” or
“*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the size of the vector
(for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar) or the number of columns in the array
(for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector), then an asterisk with no numeric values means all
indices from 1 to \(N\).
A leading asterisk means all indices from 1 to n (inclusive).  A
trailing asterisk means all indices from m to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle
asterisk means all indices from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual elements of the
vector or columns of the array had been listed one by one.  For example, the
following two fix ave/histo commands are equivalent, since the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_com_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
com/chunk}}}} command creates a global array with three
columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myCOM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{com}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myCOM[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp1.com}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myCOM[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myCOM[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myCOM[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp2.com}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, only the wildcard forms “*n” or
“m*n” are allowed.  You must specify the upper bound, because
vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable lengths are not determined until the variable
is evaluated.  If n is specified larger than the vector length
turns out to be, zeroes are output for missing vector values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{every}\), \(N_\text{repeat}\), and \(N_\text{freq}\)
arguments specify on what time steps the input values will be used in order to
contribute to the histogram.  The final histogram is generated on time steps
that are multiple of \(N_\text{freq}\).  It is averaged over
\(N_\text{repeat}\) histograms, computed in the preceding portion of the
simulation every \(N_\text{every}\) time steps.
\(N_\text{freq}\) must be a multiple of \(N_\text{every}\) and
\(N_\text{every}\) must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \(N_\text{repeat}\) is 1.
Also, the time steps contributing to the histogram value cannot overlap
(i.e., \(N_\text{repeat}\times N_\text{every}\) cannot exceed
\(N_\text{freq}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if \(N_\text{every}=2\), \(N_\text{repeat}=6\), and
\(N_\text{freq}=100\), then input values on time steps 90, 92, 94, 96, 98,
and 100 will be used to compute the final histogram on timestep 100.
Similarly for timesteps 190, 192, 194, 196, 198, and 200 on timestep 200, etc.
If \(N_\text{repeat}=1\) and \(N_\text{freq} = 100\), then no time
averaging of the histogram is done; a histogram is simply generated on
timesteps 100, 200, etc.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom attribute values (\sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}) are self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.  Note that other atom attributes can be used as
inputs to this fix by using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}} command and then
specifying an input value from that compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then if
no bracketed term is appended, the global scalar calculated by the
compute is used.  If a bracketed term is appended, the Ith element of
the global vector calculated by the compute is used.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} =
vector, then if no bracketed term is appended, the global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
or local vector calculated by the compute is used.  If a bracketed
term is appended, the Ith column of the global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local
array calculated by the compute is used.  See the discussion above for
how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify
multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that there is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command
that can sum per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities into a global scalar or vector, which
can then be accessed by fix ave/histo.  It can also be a compute defined
not in your input script, but by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}
or other fixes such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}.  See the doc pages for
these commands which give the IDs of these computes.  Users can also
write code for their own compute styles and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then if
no bracketed term is appended, the global scalar calculated by the fix
is used.  If a bracketed term is appended, the Ith element of the
global vector calculated by the fix is used.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, then
if no bracketed term is appended, the global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local
vector calculated by the fix is used.  If a bracketed term is
appended, the \(I^\text{th}\) column of the global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local
array calculated by the fix is used.  See the discussion above for how
\(I\) can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify
multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that some fixes only produce their values on certain timesteps,
which must be compatible with \(N_\text{every}\), else an error will
result.  Users can also write code for their own fix styles and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has
been previously defined in the input script.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then
only equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can be used, which both
produce global values.  In this mode, a vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable requires
a bracketed term to specify the \(I^\text{th}\) element of the vector
calculated by the variable.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, then only vector\sphinxhyphen{}style or
atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can be used, which produce a global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
vector respectively.  The vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable must be used without a
bracketed term.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} define a
formula which can reference individual atom properties or
thermodynamic keywords, or they can invoke other computes, fixes, or
variables when they are evaluated, so this is a very general means of
specifying quantities to histogram.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional optional keywords also affect the operation of this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalar}, then all input values must
be global scalars, or elements of global vectors.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode}
keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector}, then all input values must be global or
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local vectors, or columns of global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local
arrays.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kind} keyword only needs to be used if any of the specified input
computes or fixes produce more than one kind of output (global,
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom, local).  If not, LAMMPS will determine the kind of data all
the inputs produce and verify it is all the same kind.  If not, an
error will be triggered.  If a compute or fix produces more than one
kind of output, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kind} keyword should be used to specify which
output will be used.  The other input arguments must still be
consistent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} keyword determines how input values that fall outside the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} bounds are treated.  Values such that \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} \(\le\) value
\(\le\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} are assigned to one bin.  Values on a bin boundary are
assigned to the lower of the two bins.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{ignore} then
values \(<\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and values \(>\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} are ignored (i.e., they are not
binned). If \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{end}, then values \(<\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} are counted in
the first bin and values \(>\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} are counted in the last bin.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{extend}, then two extra bins are created so that there
are \(N_\text{bins}+2\) total bins.  Values \(<\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} are counted in
the first bin and values \(>\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} are counted in the last bin
\((N_\text{bins}+2)\).  Values between
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} (inclusive) are counted in bins 2 through
\(N_\text{bins}+1\).  The “coordinate” stored and printed for these two
extra bins is \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword determines how the histogram produced every
\(N_\text{freq}\) steps are averaged with histograms produced on previous
steps that were multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\), before they are accessed by
another output command or written to a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{one}, then the histograms produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are independent of each
other; they are output as\sphinxhyphen{}is without further averaging.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}, then the histograms produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are summed and averaged
in a cumulative sense before being output.  Each bin value in the histogram
is thus the average of the bin value produced on that timestep with all
preceding values for the same bin.  This running average begins when the fix is
defined; it can only be restarted by deleting the fix via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}} command, or by re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix by re\sphinxhyphen{}specifying it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{window}, then the histograms produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are summed within a
moving “window” of time, so that the last \(M\) histograms are used to
produce the output (e.g., if \(M = 3\) and \(N_\text{freq} = 1000\),
then the output on step 10000 will be the combined histogram of the individual
histograms on steps 8000, 9000, and 10000.  Outputs on early steps will be sums
over less than \(M\) histograms if they are not available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} keyword specifies what timestep histogramming will begin
on.  The default is step 0.  Often input values can be 0.0 at time 0,
so setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} to a larger value can avoid including a 0.0 in
a running or windowed histogram.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024: }new keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{append}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} keywords allow a filename to be specified.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} is used, then the filename is overwritten if it already exists.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} is used, then the filename is appended to if it already
exists, or created if it does not exist.  Every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} steps, one
histogram is written to the file.  This includes a leading line that
contains the timestep, number of bins, the total count of values
contributing to the histogram, the count of values that were not
histogrammed (see the \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} keyword), the minimum value encountered,
and the maximum value encountered.  The min/max values include values
that were not histogrammed.  Following the leading line, one line per
bin is written into the file.  Each line contains the bin \#, the
coordinate for the center of the bin (between \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}), the
count of values in the bin, and the normalized count.  The normalized
count is the bin count divided by the total count (not including values
not histogrammed), so that the normalized values sum to 1.0 across all
bins.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} keyword will continuously overwrite the output file
with the latest output, so that it only contains one timestep worth of
output.  This option can only be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave running} setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} keywords allow specification of
the strings that will be printed as the first three lines of the output
file, assuming the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword was used.  LAMMPS uses default
values for each of these, so they do not need to be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, these header lines are as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Histogram for fix ID
\PYGZsh{} TimeStep Number\PYGZhy{}of\PYGZhy{}bins Total\PYGZhy{}counts Missing\PYGZhy{}counts Min\PYGZhy{}value Max\PYGZhy{}value
\PYGZsh{} Bin Coord Count Count/Total
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the first line, ID is replaced with the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  The second line
describes the six values that are printed at the first of each section
of output.  The third describes the four values printed for each bin in
the histogram.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_histo:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a global vector and global array which can be
accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The values
can only be accessed on timesteps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\)
since that is when a histogram is generated.  The global vector has four
values:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total counts in the histogram

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
values that were not histogrammed (see \sphinxstyleemphasis{beyond} keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min value of all input values, including ones not histogrammed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max value of all input values, including ones not histogrammed

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The global array has \(N_\text{bins}\) rows and three columns.  The
first column has the bin coordinate, the second column has the count of
values in that histogram bin, and the third column has the bin count
divided by the total count (not including missing counts), so that the
values in the third column sum to 1.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector and array values calculated by this fix are all treated as
intensive.  If this is not the case (e.g., due to histogramming
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom input values), then you will need to account for that when
interpreting the values produced by this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\section{fix ave/time command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time:fix-ave-time-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ave/time = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many time steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of times to use input values for calculating averages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate averages every this many time steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more input values can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = c\_ID, c\_ID{[}N{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}N{]}, v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
c\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar or vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector or Ith column of global array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar or vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector or Ith column of global array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\PYGZus{}name = value(s) calculated by an equal\PYGZhy{}style or vector\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
v\PYGZus{}name[I] = value calculated by a vector\PYGZhy{}style variable with name, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{format} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalar} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector}
  scalar = all input values are global scalars
  vector = all input values are global vectors or global arrays
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{running} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window M}
  one = output a new average value every Nfreq steps
  running = output cumulative average of all previous Nfreq steps
  window M = output average of M most recent Nfreq steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} args = Nstart
  Nstart = start averaging on this time step
\sphinxstyleemphasis{off} arg = M = do not average this value
  M = value \# from 1 to Nvalues
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} arg = filename
  filename = name of file to output time averages to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{append} arg = filename
  filename = name of file to append time averages to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} arg = none = overwrite output file with only latest output
\sphinxstyleemphasis{format} arg = string
  string = C\sphinxhyphen{}style format string
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} arg = string
  string = text to print as 1st line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} arg = string
  string = text to print as 2nd line of output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} arg = string
  string = text to print as 3rd line of output file, only for vector mode
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
