\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}indent[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp.indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{off}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use one or more global values as inputs every few time steps, and
average them over longer timescales.  The resulting averages can be
used by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} such as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}}, and can also be written to a
file.  Note that if no time averaging is done, this command can be
used as a convenient way to simply output one or more global values to
a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with this command is ignored.  However, note that
specified values may represent calculations performed by computes and
fixes which store their own “group” definitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each listed value can be the result of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the evaluation of an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  In each case, the compute, fix, or variable
must produce a global quantity, not a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local quantity.  If
you wish to spatial\sphinxhyphen{} or time\sphinxhyphen{}average or histogram per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities
from a compute, fix, or variable, then see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}},
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}} commands.  If you wish to sum a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity into a single global quantity, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Computes}}}} that produce global quantities are those which
do not have the word \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} in their style name.  Only a few
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} produce global quantities.  See the doc pages for
individual fixes for info on which ones produce such values.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Variables}}}} of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} are the only
ones that can be used with this fix.  Variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} cannot
be used, since they produce per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The input values must either be all scalars or all vectors depending
on the setting of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} keyword.  In both cases, the averaging is
performed independently on each input value (i.e., each input scalar
is averaged independently or each element of each input vector is
averaged independently).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then the input values must be scalars, or vectors
with a bracketed term appended, indicating the \(I^\text{th}\) value of the
vector is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, then the input values must be vectors, or arrays
with a bracketed term appended, indicating the Ith column of the array
is used.  All vectors must be the same length, which is the length of
the vector or number of rows in the array.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For input values from a compute or fix or variable, the bracketed
index I can be specified using a wildcard asterisk with the index to
effectively specify multiple values.  This takes the form “*” or
“*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the size of the vector (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} =
scalar) or the number of columns in the array (for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector),
then an asterisk with no numeric values means all indices from 1 to \(N\).
A leading asterisk means all indices from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing
asterisk means all indices from n to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk
means all indices from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual elements of the
vector or columns of the array had been listed one by one.  For example, the
following two fix ave/time commands are equivalent, since the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_rdf::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute rdf}}}} command creates, in this case, a global array with three
columns, each of length 50:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myRDF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myRDF[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp1.rdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myRDF[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myRDF[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myRDF[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp2.rdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, only the wildcard forms “*n” or
“m*n” are allowed.  You must specify the upper bound, because
vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable lengths are not determined until the variable
is evaluated.  If n is specified larger than the vector length
turns out to be, zeroes are output for missing vector values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{every}\), \(N_\text{repeat}\), and \(N_\text{freq}\)
arguments specify on what time steps the input values will be used in order to
contribute to the average.  The final averaged quantities are generated on
time steps that are a multiple of \(N_\text{freq}\).  The average is over
\(N_\text{repeat}\) quantities, computed in the preceding portion of the
simulation every \(N_\text{every}\) time steps.  \(N_\text{freq}\) must
be a multiple of \(N_\text{every}\) and \(N_\text{every}\) must be
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \(N_\text{repeat} = 1\). Also, the time steps
contributing to the average value cannot overlap (i.e.,
\(N_\text{repeat} \times N_\text{every}\) cannot exceed \(N_\text{freq}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if \(N_\text{every}=2\), \(N_\text{repeat}=6\), and
\(N_\text{freq}=100\), then values on time steps 90, 92, 94, 96, 98, and
100 will be used to compute the final average on time step 100.  Similarly for
time steps 190, 192, 194, 196, 198, and 200 on time step 200, etc.
If \(N_\text{repeat}=1\) and \(N_\text{freq} = 100\), then no time
averaging is done; values are simply generated on time steps
100, 200, etc.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then if
no bracketed term is appended, the global scalar calculated by the
compute is used.  If a bracketed term is appended, the Ith element of
the global vector calculated by the compute is used.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} =
vector, then if no bracketed term is appended, the global vector
calculated by the compute is used.  If a bracketed term is appended,
the Ith column of the global array calculated by the compute is used.
See the discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard
asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that there is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command
that can sum per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities into a global scalar or vector, which
can then be accessed by fix ave/time.  It can also be a compute defined
not in your input script, but by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} or other fixes such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}.  See the doc pages for
these commands which give the IDs of these computes.  Users can also
write code for their own compute styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then if
no bracketed term is appended, the global scalar calculated by the fix
is used.  If a bracketed term is appended, the Ith element of the
global vector calculated by the fix is used.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, then
if no bracketed term is appended, the global vector calculated by the
fix is used.  If a bracketed term is appended, the Ith column of the
global array calculated by the fix is used.  See the discussion above
for how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively
specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that some fixes only produce their values on certain time steps,
which must be compatible with \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}, else an error will result.
Users can also write code for their own fix styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has
been previously defined in the input script.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, then
only equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can be used, which both
produce global values.  In this mode, a vector\sphinxhyphen{}style variable requires
a bracketed term to specify the Ith element of the vector calculated
by the variable.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, then only a vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
variable can be used, without a bracketed term.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} define a formula
which can reference individual atom properties or thermodynamic
keywords, or they can invoke other computes, fixes, or variables when
they are evaluated, so this is a very general means of specifying
quantities to time average.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional optional keywords also affect the operation of this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalar}, then all input values must
be global scalars, or elements of global vectors.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode}
keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector}, then all input values must be global
vectors, or columns of global arrays.  They can also be global arrays,
which are converted into a series of global vectors (one per column),
as explained above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword determines how the values produced every
\(N_\text{freq}\) steps are averaged with values produced on previous steps
that were multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\), before they are accessed by
another output command or written to a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{one}, then the values produced on time steps
that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are independent of each other; they
are output as\sphinxhyphen{}is without further averaging.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}, then the values produced on
time steps that are multiples of \(N_\text{freq}\) are summed and averaged
in a cumulative sense before being output.  Each output value is thus the
average of the value produced on that time step with all preceding
values.  This running average begins when the fix is defined; it can
only be restarted by deleting the fix via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}}
command, or by re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix by re\sphinxhyphen{}specifying it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{window}, then the values produced on
time steps that are multiples of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} are summed and averaged within
a moving “window” of time, so that the last M values are used to
produce the output.  For example, if \(M = 3\) and
\(N_\text{freq} = 1000\), then the output on step 10000 will be the average
of the individual values on steps 8000, 9000, and 10000.  Outputs on early
steps will average over less than \(M\) values if they are not available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} keyword specifies what time step averaging will begin on.
The default is step 0.  Often input values can be 0.0 at time 0, so
setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} to a larger value can avoid including a 0.0 in a
running or windowed average.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} keyword can be used to flag any of the input values.  If a
value is flagged, it will not be time averaged.  Instead the most
recent input value will always be stored and output.  This is useful
if one of more of the inputs produced by a compute or fix or variable
are effectively constant or are simply current values (e.g., they are
being written to a file with other time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged values for purposes
of creating well\sphinxhyphen{}formatted output).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024: }new keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{append}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} keywords allow a filename to be specified.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} is used, then the filename is overwritten if it already exists.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} is used, then the filename is appended to if it already
exists, or created if it does not exist.  Every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} steps, one
quantity or vector of quantities is written to the file for each input
value specified in the fix ave/time command.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, this
means a single line is written each time output is performed.  Thus the
file ends up to be a series of lines, i.e. one column of numbers for
each input value.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector, an array of numbers is written
each time output is performed.  The number of rows is the length of the
input vectors, and the number of columns is the number of values.  Thus
the file ends up to be a series of these array sections.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the filename ends in ‘.yaml’ or ‘.yml’ then the output format
conforms to the \sphinxhref{https://yaml.org/}{YAML standard} which allows
easy import that data into tools and scripts that support reading YAML
files. The {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_structured_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{structured data Howto}}}} contains
examples for parsing and plotting such data with very little programming
effort in Python using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pyyaml}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pandas}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{matplotlib}
packages.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite} keyword will continuously overwrite the output file
with the latest output, so that it only contains one time step worth of
output.  This option can only be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave running} setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{format} keyword sets the numeric format of each value when it is
printed to a file via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword.  Note that all values are
floating point quantities.  The default format is \%g.  You can specify
a higher precision if desired (e.g., \%20.16g).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{title1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{title2} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} keywords allow specification of
the strings that will be printed as the first 2 or 3 lines of the
output file, assuming the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword was used.  LAMMPS uses
default values for each of these, so they do not need to be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, these header lines are as follows for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Time\PYGZhy{}averaged data for fix ID
\PYGZsh{} TimeStep value1 value2 ...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the first line, ID is replaced with the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  In the second line
the values are replaced with the appropriate fields from the fix
ave/time command.  There is no third line in the header of the file,
so the \sphinxstyleemphasis{title3} setting is ignored when \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, these header lines are as follows for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Time\PYGZhy{}averaged data for fix ID
\PYGZsh{} TimeStep Number\PYGZhy{}of\PYGZhy{}rows
\PYGZsh{} Row value1 value2 ...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the first line, ID is replaced with the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  The second line
describes the two values that are printed at the first of each section
of output.  In the third line the values are replaced with the
appropriate fields from the fix ave/time command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify colname}}}} option can be
used to change the name of the column in the output file.  When writing
a YAML format file this name will be in the list of keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a global scalar or global vector or global array
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
The values can only be accessed on time steps that are multiples of
\(N_\text{freq}\) since that is when averaging is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A scalar is produced if only a single input value is averaged and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar.  A vector is produced if multiple input values are
averaged for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = scalar, or a single input value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} =
vector.  In the first case, the length of the vector is the number of
inputs.  In the second case, the length of the vector is the same as
the length of the input vector.  An array is produced if multiple
input values are averaged and \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} = vector.  The global array has \#
of rows = length of the input vectors and \# of columns = number of
inputs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the fix produces a scalar or vector, then the scalar and each
element of the vector can be either “intensive” or “extensive”,
depending on whether the values contributing to the scalar or vector
element are “intensive” or “extensive”.  If the fix produces an array,
then all elements in the array must be the same, either “intensive” or
“extensive”.  If a compute or fix provides the value being time
averaged, then the compute or fix determines whether the value is
intensive or extensive; see the page for that compute or fix for
further info.  Values produced by a variable are treated as intensive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ave_time:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are mode = scalar, ave = one, start = 0, no file
output, format = \%g, title 1,2,3 = strings as described above, and no
off settings for any input values.

\section{fix aveforce command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce:fix-aveforce-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aveforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
aveforce = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fx,fy,fz = force component values (force units)

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
any of fx,fy,fz can be a variable (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region atoms must be in to have added force
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pressdown}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{topwall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aveforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bottomwall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aveforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bottomwall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aveforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}oscillate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply an additional external force to a group of atoms in such a way
that every atom experiences the same force.  This is useful for
pushing on wall or boundary atoms so that the structure of the wall
does not change over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The existing force is averaged for the group of atoms, component by
component.  The actual force on each atom is then set to the average
value plus the component specified in this command.  This means each
atom in the group receives the same force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz} values can be specified as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, which
means the force in that dimension is not changed.  Note that this is not the
same as specifying a 0.0 value, since that sets all forces to the same
average value without adding in any additional force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the three quantities defining the force components, namely \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.
If the value is a variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where
name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable will be
evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine the average
force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent average force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the atom must also be in the
specified geometric {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} in order to have force added
to it.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_aveforce:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global three\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  This is the total
force on the group of atoms before the forces on individual atoms are
changed by the fix.  The vector values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.  You should not
specify force components with a variable that has time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence for
use with a minimizer, since the minimizer increments the timestep as
the iteration count during the minimization.

\subsection{Related commands}

\section{fix balance command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_balance:fix-balance-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_balance:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_balance::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_balance:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{balance}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thresh}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
balance = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = perform dynamic load balancing every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thresh = imbalance threshold that must be exceeded to perform a re\sphinxhyphen{}balance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcb} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{report}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} args = dimstr Niter stopthresh
  dimstr = sequence of letters containing \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, each not more than once
  Niter = \# of times to iterate within each dimension of dimstr sequence
  stopthresh = stop balancing when this imbalance threshold is reached
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rcb} args = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{report} args = none
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{weight} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{out}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{weight} style args = use weighted particle counts for the balancing
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{neigh} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{time} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{store}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} args = Ngroup group1 weight1 group2 weight2 ...
      Ngroup = number of groups with assigned weights
      group1, group2, ... = group IDs
      weight1, weight2, ...   = corresponding weight factors
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{neigh} factor = compute weight based on number of neighbors
      factor = scaling factor (\textgreater{} 0)
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{time} factor = compute weight based on time spend computing
      factor = scaling factor (\textgreater{} 0)
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} name = take weight from atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable
      name = name of the atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{store} name = store weight in custom atom property defined by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} command
      name = atom property name (without d\_ prefix)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sort} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{out} arg = filename
  filename = write each processor\textquotesingle{}s subdomain to a file, at each re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{balance}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.05}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_balance:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command adjusts the size and shape of processor subdomains
within the simulation box, to attempt to balance the number of
particles and thus the computational cost (load) evenly across
processors.  The load balancing is “dynamic” in the sense that
re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing is performed periodically during the simulation.  To
perform “static” balancing, before or between runs, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{report} balance style only computes the load imbalance but
does not attempt any re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing.  This way the load imbalance
information can be used otherwise, for instance for stopping a
run with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_halt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix halt}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Load\sphinxhyphen{}balancing is typically most useful if the particles in the
simulation box have a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}varying density distribution or
where the computational cost varies significantly between different
atoms (e.g., a model of a vapor/liquid interface, or a solid with
an irregular\sphinxhyphen{}shaped geometry containing void regions, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid pair style simulations}}}} that combine
pair styles with different computational cost).  In these cases, the
LAMMPS default of dividing the simulation box volume into a
regular\sphinxhyphen{}spaced grid of 3d bricks, with one equal\sphinxhyphen{}volume subdomain
per processor, may assign numbers of particles per processor in a
way that the computational effort varies significantly.  This can
lead to poor performance when the simulation is run in parallel.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The balancing can be performed with or without per\sphinxhyphen{}particle weighting.
With no weighting, the balancing attempts to assign an equal number of
particles to each processor.  With weighting, the balancing attempts
to assign an equal aggregate computational weight to each processor,
which typically induces a different number of atoms assigned to each
processor.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The weighting options listed above are documented with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} command in {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance:weighted-balance}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{this section of the balance
command}}}} doc page.  That section
describes the various weighting options and gives a few examples of
how they can be used.  The weighting options are the same for both the
fix balance and {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{processors::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{processors}}}} command allows some control
over how the box volume is split across processors.  Specifically, for
a \(P_x \times P_y \times P_z\) grid of processors, it allows choices of
\(P_x\), \(P_y\), and \(P_z\) subject to the constraint that
\(P_x P_y P_z = P\), the total number of processors.
This is sufficient to achieve good load\sphinxhyphen{}balance for
some problems on some processor counts.  However, all the processor
subdomains will still have the same shape and the same volume.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On a particular time step, a load\sphinxhyphen{}balancing operation is only performed
if the current “imbalance factor” in particles owned by each processor
exceeds the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{thresh} parameter.  The imbalance factor is
defined as the maximum number of particles (or weight) owned by any
processor, divided by the average number of particles (or weight) per
processor.  Thus, an imbalance factor of 1.0 is perfect balance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, for 10000 particles running on 10 processors, if the
most heavily loaded processor has 1200 particles, then the imbalance factor is
1.2, meaning there is a 20\% imbalance.  Note that re\sphinxhyphen{}balances can be
forced even if the current balance is perfect (1.0) be specifying a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thresh} \textless{} 1.0.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command attempts to minimize the imbalance factor, as
defined above.  But depending on the method a perfect balance (1.0)
may not be achieved.  For example, “grid” methods (defined below) that
create a logical 3d grid cannot achieve perfect balance for many
irregular distributions of particles.  Likewise, if a portion of the
system is a perfect, non\sphinxhyphen{}rotated lattice (e.g., the initial system is
generated by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command with no
rotations), then “grid” methods may be unable to achieve exact balance.
This is because entire lattice planes will be owned or not owned by a single
processor.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The imbalance factor is also an estimate of the maximum speed\sphinxhyphen{}up
you can hope to achieve by running a perfectly balanced simulation
versus an imbalanced one.  In the example above, the 10000\sphinxhyphen{}particle
simulation could run up to 20\% faster if it were perfectly balanced,
versus when imbalanced.  However, computational cost is not strictly
proportional to particle count, and changing the relative size and
shape of processor subdomains may lead to additional computational
and communication overheads (e.g., in the PPPM solver used via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command).  Thus, you should benchmark
the run times of a simulation before and after balancing.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The method used to perform a load balance is specified by one of the
listed styles, which are described in detail below.  There are two kinds
of styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} style is a “grid” method which produces a logical 3d grid
of processors.  It operates by changing the cutting planes (or lines)
between processors in 3d (or 2d), to adjust the volume (area in 2d)
assigned to each processor, as in the following 2d diagram where
processor subdomains are shown and atoms are colored by the processor
that owns them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.320\linewidth]{{balance_uniform}.jpg}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.320\linewidth]{{balance_nonuniform}.jpg}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.320\linewidth]{{balance_rcb}.jpg}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The leftmost diagram is the default partitioning of the simulation box
across processors (one sub\sphinxhyphen{}box for each of 16 processors); the middle
diagram is after a “grid” method has been applied. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcb} style is a
“tiling” method which does not produce a logical 3d grid of processors.
Rather it tiles the simulation domain with rectangular sub\sphinxhyphen{}boxes of
varying size and shape in an irregular fashion so as to have equal
numbers of particles (or weight) in each sub\sphinxhyphen{}box, as in the rightmost
diagram above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “grid” methods can be used with either of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_style}}}} command options, \sphinxstyleemphasis{brick} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tiled}.  The
“tiling” methods can only be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_style tiled}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When a “grid” method is specified, the current domain partitioning can
be either a logical 3d grid or a tiled partitioning.  In the former
case, the current logical 3d grid is used as a starting point and
changes are made to improve the imbalance factor.  In the latter case,
the tiled partitioning is discarded and a logical 3d grid is created
with uniform spacing in all dimensions.  This is the starting point
for the balancing operation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When a “tiling” method is specified, the current domain partitioning
(“grid” or “tiled”) is ignored, and a new partitioning is computed
from scratch.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} is ignored.  However the impact of balancing on
different groups of atoms can be affected by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} weight
style as described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(N_\text{freq}\) setting determines how often a re\sphinxhyphen{}balance is
performed.  If \(N_\text{freq} > 0\), then re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing will occur every
\(N_\text{freq}\) steps.  Each time a re\sphinxhyphen{}balance occurs, a reneighboring is
triggered, so \(N_\text{freq}\) should not be too small.  If
\(N_\text{freq} = 0\), then re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing will be done every time
reneighboring normally occurs, as determined by the
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}}
command settings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On re\sphinxhyphen{}balance steps, re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing will only be attempted if the current
imbalance factor, as defined above, exceeds the \sphinxstyleemphasis{thresh} setting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} style invokes a “grid” method for balancing, as described
above.  It changes the positions of cutting planes between processors
in an iterative fashion, seeking to reduce the imbalance factor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dimstr} argument is a string of characters, each of which must be
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}.  Each character can appear zero or one time,
since there is no advantage to balancing on a dimension more than
once.  You should normally only list dimensions where you expect there
to be a density variation in the particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Balancing proceeds by adjusting the cutting planes in each of the
dimensions listed in \sphinxstyleemphasis{dimstr}, one dimension at a time.  For a single
dimension, the balancing operation (described below) is iterated on up
to \(N_\text{iter}\) times.  After each dimension finishes, the imbalance
factor is re\sphinxhyphen{}computed, and the balancing operation halts if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{stopthresh}
criterion is met.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A re\sphinxhyphen{}balance operation in a single dimension is performed using a
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent recursive multisectioning algorithm, where the
position of each cutting plane (line in 2d) in the dimension is
adjusted independently.  This is similar to a recursive bisectioning
for a single value, except that the bounds used for each bisectioning
take advantage of information from neighboring cuts if possible, as
well as counts of particles at the bounds on either side of each cuts,
which themselves were cuts in previous iterations.  The latter is used
to infer a density of particles near each of the current cuts.  At
each iteration, the count of particles on either side of each plane is
tallied.  If the counts do not match the target value for the plane,
the position of the cut is adjusted based on the local density.  The
low and high bounds are adjusted on each iteration, using new count
information, so that they become closer together over time.  Thus as
the recursion progresses, the count of particles on either side of the
plane gets closer to the target value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent part of this algorithm is often an advantage
when you re\sphinxhyphen{}balance a system that is already nearly balanced.  It
typically converges more quickly than the geometric bisectioning
algorithm used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} command.  However, if can
be a disadvantage if you attempt to re\sphinxhyphen{}balance a system that is far
from balanced, and converge more slowly.  In this case you probably
want to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}} command before starting a run,
so that you begin the run with a balanced system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Once the re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing is complete and final processor subdomains
assigned, particles migrate to their new owning processor as part of
the normal reneighboring procedure.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At each re\sphinxhyphen{}balance operation, the bisectioning for each cutting
plane (line in 2d) typically starts with low and high bounds separated
by the extent of a processor’s subdomain in one dimension.  The size
of this bracketing region shrinks based on the local density, as
described above, which should typically be 1/2 or more every
iteration.  Thus if \(N_\text{iter}\) is specified as 10, the cutting
plane will typically be positioned to better than 1 part in 1000 accuracy
(relative to the perfect target position).  For \(N_\text{iter} = 20\),
it will be accurate to better than 1 part in a million.  Thus there is no
need to set \(N_\text{iter}\) to a large value.  This is especially true
if you are re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing often enough that each time you expect only an
incremental adjustment in the cutting planes is necessary.  LAMMPS will
check if the threshold accuracy is reached (in a dimension) is less
iterations than \(N_\text{iter}\) and exit early.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcb} style invokes a “tiled” method for balancing, as described
above.  It performs a recursive coordinate bisectioning (RCB) of the
simulation domain. The basic idea is as follows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The simulation domain is cut into two boxes by an axis\sphinxhyphen{}aligned cut in
the longest dimension, leaving one new box on either side of the cut.
All the processors are also partitioned into two groups, half assigned
to the box on the lower side of the cut, and half to the box on the
upper side.  If the processor count is odd, one side gets an extra
processor.  The cut is positioned so that the number of atoms in the
lower box is exactly the number that the processors assigned to that
box should own for load balance to be perfect.  This also makes load
balance for the upper box perfect.  The positioning is done
iteratively, by a bisectioning method.  Note that counting atoms on
either side of the cut requires communication between all processors
at each iteration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
That is the procedure for the first cut.  Subsequent cuts are made
recursively, in exactly the same manner.  The subset of processors
assigned to each box make a new cut in the longest dimension of that
box, splitting the box, the subset of processors, and the atoms in
the box in two.  The recursion continues until every processor is
assigned a sub\sphinxhyphen{}box of the entire simulation domain, and owns the atoms
in that sub\sphinxhyphen{}box.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sort} keyword determines whether the communication of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
data to other processors during load\sphinxhyphen{}balancing will be random or
deterministic.  Random is generally faster; deterministic will ensure
the new ordering of atoms on each processor is the same each time the
same simulation is run.  This can be useful for debugging purposes.
Since the fix balance command is performed during timestepping, the
default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} so that sorting is not performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} keyword writes text to the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename} with the
results of each re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing operation.  The file contains the bounds
of the subdomain for each processor after the balancing operation
completes.  The format of the file is compatible with the
\sphinxhref{https://lammps.github.io/pizza}{Pizza.py} \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdump} tool which has support for manipulating and
visualizing mesh files.  An example is shown here for a balancing by four
processors for a 2d problem:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ITEM: TIMESTEP
0
ITEM: NUMBER OF NODES
16
ITEM: BOX BOUNDS
0 10
0 10
0 10
ITEM: NODES
1 1 0 0 0
2 1 5 0 0
3 1 5 5 0
4 1 0 5 0
5 1 5 0 0
6 1 10 0 0
7 1 10 5 0
8 1 5 5 0
9 1 0 5 0
10 1 5 5 0
11 1 5 10 0
12 1 10 5 0
13 1 5 5 0
14 1 10 5 0
15 1 10 10 0
16 1 5 10 0
ITEM: TIMESTEP
0
ITEM: NUMBER OF SQUARES
4
ITEM: SQUARES
1 1 1 2 3 4
2 1 5 6 7 8
3 1 9 10 11 12
4 1 13 14 15 16
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coordinates of all the vertices are listed in the NODES section, five
per processor.  Note that the four subdomains share vertices, so there
will be duplicate nodes in the list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “SQUARES” section lists the node IDs of the four vertices in a
rectangle for each processor (1 to 4).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a 3d problem, the syntax is similar but with eight vertices listed for
each processor instead of four, and “SQUARES” replaced by “CUBES”.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_balance:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which is the imbalance factor
after the most recent re\sphinxhyphen{}balance and a global vector of length 3 with
additional information about the most recent re\sphinxhyphen{}balancing.  The three
values in the vector are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max \# of particles per processor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total \# iterations performed in last re\sphinxhyphen{}balance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
imbalance factor right before the last re\sphinxhyphen{}balance was performed

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As explained above, the imbalance factor is the ratio of the maximum
number of particles (or total weight) on any processor to the average
number of particles (or total weight) per processor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These quantities can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar and vector values calculated
by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_balance:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For 2d simulations, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} style cannot be used, nor can \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
appear in \sphinxstyleemphasis{dimstr} for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Balancing through recursive bisectioning (\sphinxstyleemphasis{rcb} style) requires
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_style tiled}}}}.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{processors::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{processors}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{balance::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{balance}}}},

\index{fix bocs@\spxentry{fix bocs}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix bocs command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:fix-bocs-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bocs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bocs = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
two or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cgiso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values = Tstart Tstop Tdamp
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cgiso} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp basis\_set args
  basis\_set = \sphinxstyleemphasis{analytic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear\_spline} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic\_spline}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{analytic} args = V\_avg N\_particles N\_coeff Coeff\_1 Coeff\_2 ... Coeff\_N
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear\_spline} args = input\_filename
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic\_spline} args = input\_filename
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} value = N = length of thermostat chain (1 = single thermostat)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} value = N = length of thermostat on barostat (0 = no thermostat)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = add MTK adjustment term or not
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} value = M = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on thermostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} value = M = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on barostat
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bocs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cgiso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.986}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.986}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{analytic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{66476.015}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{968}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{245030.10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8962.20}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bocs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cgiso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.986}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.986}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cubic\PYGZus{}spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}Fv.dat}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}press}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These commands incorporate a pressure correction as described by
Dunn and Noid {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bocs:bocs-dunn1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dunn1)}}}} to the standard MTK
barostat by Martyna et al. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bocs:bocs-martyna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Martyna)}}}}.
The first half of the command mimics a standard {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}
command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bocs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tcoupl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cgiso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Pstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Pstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Pdamp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two differences are replacing \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} with \sphinxstyleemphasis{bocs}, and replacing
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}/etc. with \sphinxstyleemphasis{cgiso}.
The rest of the command details what form you would like to use for
the pressure correction equation. The choices are: \sphinxstyleemphasis{analytic}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear\_spline},
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic\_spline}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With either spline method, the only argument that needs to follow it
is the name of a file that contains the desired pressure correction
as a function of volume. The file must be formatted so each line has:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Volume\PYGZus{}i, PressureCorrection\PYGZus{}i
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note both the COMMA and the SPACE separating the volume’s
value and its corresponding pressure correction. The volumes in the file
must be uniformly spaced. Both the volumes and the pressure corrections
should be provided in the proper units (e.g., if you are using \sphinxstyleemphasis{units real},
the volumes should all be in \(\mathrm{\mathring{A}}^3\) and the pressure
corrections should all be in atm). Furthermore, the table should start/end at a
volume considerably smaller/larger than you expect your system to sample
during the simulation. If the system ever reaches a volume outside of the
range provided, the simulation will stop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the \sphinxstyleemphasis{analytic} option, the arguments are as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
... analytic V\PYGZus{}avg N\PYGZus{}particles N\PYGZus{}coeff Coeff\PYGZus{}1 Coeff\PYGZus{}2 ... Coeff\PYGZus{}N
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{V\_avg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Coeff\_i} should all be in the proper units (e.g., if you
are using \sphinxstyleemphasis{units real}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{V\_avg} should be in \(\mathrm{\mathring{A}^3}\)
and the coefficients should all be in
\(\mathrm{atm}\cdot\mathrm{\mathring{A}^3}\)).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the cumulative global energy change to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the fix continues in an uninterrupted
fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}
you have defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure, as described above.  For consistency, the group used by
this fix and by the compute should be the same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the BOCS package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As this is computing a (modified) pressure, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID should be \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pressure correction has only been tested for use with an isotropic
pressure coupling in 3 dimensions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, LAMMPS will still report the normal value for the pressure
if the pressure is printed via a \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo} command, or if the pressures
are written to a file every so often. In order to have LAMMPS report the
modified pressure, you must include the \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_modify} command given in
the examples. For the last argument in the command, you should put
XXXX\_press, where XXXX is the ID given to the fix bocs command (in the
example, the ID of the fix bocs command is 1).


\subsection{Further information}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bocs:further-information}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For more details about the pressure correction and the entire BOCS software
package, visit the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/noid-group/BOCS}{BOCS package on GitHub} and read the release
paper by Dunn et al. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bocs:bocs-dunn2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dunn2)}}}} .

\index{fix bond/break@\spxentry{fix bond/break}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix bond/break command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:fix-bond-break-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{break}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bondtype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bond/break = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = attempt bond breaking every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bondtype = type of bonds to break (integer or type label)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rmax = bond longer than Rmax can break (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{prob}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{prob} values = fraction seed
  fraction = break a bond with this probability if otherwise eligible
  seed = random number seed (positive integer)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{break}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{polymer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{break}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prob}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{49829}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Break bonds between pairs of atoms as a simulation runs according to
specified criteria.  This can be used to model the dissolution of a
polymer network due to stretching of the simulation box or other
deformations.  In this context, a bond means an interaction between a
pair of atoms computed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style}}}} command.
Once the bond is broken it will be permanently deleted, as will all
angle, dihedral, and improper interactions that bond is part of.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is different than a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise}}}} bond\sphinxhyphen{}order
potential such as Tersoff or AIREBO which infers bonds and many\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions based on the current geometry of a small cluster of atoms
and effectively creates and destroys bonds and higher\sphinxhyphen{}order many\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions from timestep to timestep as atoms move.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A check for possible bond breakage is performed every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}
timesteps.  If two bonded atoms \(i\) and \(j\) are farther than the
distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{Rmax} from each other, the bond is of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{bondtype}, and both
\(i\) and \(j\) are in the specified fix group, then the bond between
\(i\) and \(j\) is labeled as a “possible” bond to break.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If several bonds involving an atom are stretched, it may have multiple
possible bonds to break.  Every atom checks its list of possible bonds
to break and labels the longest such bond as its “sole” bond to break.
After this is done, if atom \(i\) is bonded to atom \(j\) in its sole
bond, and atom \(j\) is bonded to atom \(j\) in its sole bond, then the
bond between \(i\) and \(j\) is “eligible” to be broken.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these rules mean an atom will only be part of at most one
broken bond on a given time step.  It also means that if atom \(i\) chooses
atom \(j\) as its sole partner, but atom \(j\) chooses atom \(k\)
as its sole partner (because \(R_{jk} > R_{ij}\)), then this means atom
\(i\) will not be part of a broken bond on this time step, even if it has
other possible bond partners.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{prob} keyword can effect whether an eligible bond is actually
broken.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction} setting must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0.
A uniform random number between 0.0 and 1.0 is generated and the
eligible bond is only broken if the random number is less than \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When a bond is broken, data structures within LAMMPS that store bond
topologies are updated to reflect the breakage.  Likewise, if the bond
is part of a 3\sphinxhyphen{}body (angle) or 4\sphinxhyphen{}body (dihedral, improper)
interaction, that interaction is removed as well.  These changes
typically affect pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise interactions between atoms that used to be
part of bonds, angles, etc.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One data structure that is not updated when a bond breaks are
the molecule IDs stored by each atom.  Even though one molecule
becomes two molecules due to the broken bond, all atoms in both new
molecules retain their original molecule IDs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computationally, each time step this fix is invoked, it loops over all
the bonds in the system and computes distances between pairs of bonded
atoms.  It also communicates between neighboring processors to
coordinate which bonds are broken.  Moreover, if any bonds are broken,
neighbor lists must be immediately updated on the same time step.  This
is to ensure that any pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise interactions that should be turned “on”
due to a bond breaking, because they are no longer excluded by the
presence of the bond and the settings of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command, will be immediately
recognized.  All of these operations increase the cost of a time step.
Thus, you should be cautious about invoking this fix too frequently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can dump out snapshots of the current bond topology via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Breaking a bond typically alters the energy of a system.  You
should be careful not to choose bond breaking criteria that induce a
dramatic change in energy.  For example, if you define a very stiff
harmonic bond and break it when two atoms are separated by a distance
far from the equilibrium bond length, then the two atoms will be
dramatically released when the bond is broken.  More generally, you
may need to thermostat your system to compensate for energy changes
resulting from broken bonds (as well as angles, dihedrals, and impropers).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_broken_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto}}}} page on broken bonds for more
information on related features in LAMMPS.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes two statistics, which it stores in a global vector of
length 2. This vector can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector values calculated by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two quantities in the global vector are
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{(}{)}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of bonds broken on the most recent breakage time step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative number of bonds broken

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_create::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/create}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_react::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/react}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/swap}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_break:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are prob = 1.0.

\sphinxstepscope

\section{fix bond/create command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_create:fix-bond-create-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_create:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_create:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_create::doc}}

\section{fix bond/create/angle command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_create:fix-bond-create-angle-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_bond_create:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{itype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{jtype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rmin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bondtype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond/create} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond/create/angle}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = attempt bond creation every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
itype,jtype = atoms of itype can bond to atoms of jtype (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rmin = two atoms separated by less than Rmin can bond (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bondtype = type of created bonds (integer or type label)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{iparam} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{jparam} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{prob} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{atype} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dtype} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{itype} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aconstrain}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iparam} values = maxbond, newtype
  maxbond = max \# of bonds of bondtype the itype atom can have
  newtype = change the itype atom to this type when maxbonds exist (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{jparam} values = maxbond, newtype
  maxbond = max \# of bonds of bondtype the jtype atom can have
  newtype = change the jtype atom to this type when maxbonds exist (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{prob} values = fraction seed
  fraction = create a bond with this probability if otherwise eligible
  seed = random number seed (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atype} value = angletype
  angletype = type of created angles (integer or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dtype} value = dihedraltype
  dihedraltype = type of created dihedrals (integer or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{itype} value = impropertype
  impropertype = type of created impropers (integer or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aconstrain} value = amin amax
  amin = minimal angle at which new bonds can be created
  amax = maximal angle at which new bonds can be created
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
