\index{fix box/relax@\spxentry{fix box/relax}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix box/relax command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:fix-box-relax-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{relax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
box/relax = style name of this fix command
\begin{sphinxalltt}
one or more keyword value pairs may be appended
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vmax} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} value = Ptarget = desired pressure (pressure units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} value = Ptarget = desired pressure (pressure units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} value = reset reference cell every this many minimizer iterations
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{vmax} value = fraction = max allowed volume change in one iteration
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale yz with lz
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xz with lz
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xy with ly
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} values = x y z
    x,y,z = perform relaxation dilation/contraction around this point (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{relax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{water}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{relax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aniso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dilate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{partial}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{relax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tri}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{couple}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nreset}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply an external pressure or stress tensor to the simulation box
during an {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.  This allows the box
size and shape to vary during the iterations of the minimizer so that
the final configuration will be both an energy minimum for the
potential energy of the atoms, and the system pressure tensor will be
close to the specified external tensor.  Conceptually, specifying a
positive pressure is like squeezing on the simulation box; a negative
pressure typically allows the box to expand.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The external pressure tensor is specified using one or more of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple}
keywords.  These keywords give you the ability to specify all 6
components of an external stress tensor, and to couple various of
these components together so that the dimensions they represent are
varied together during the minimization.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Orthogonal simulation boxes have 3 adjustable dimensions (x,y,z).
Triclinic (non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal) simulation boxes have 6 adjustable
dimensions (x,y,z,xy,xz,yz).  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands
specify whether the simulation box is orthogonal or non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal
(triclinic) and explain the meaning of the xy,xz,yz tilt factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target pressures \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ptarget} for each of the 6 components of the
stress tensor can be specified independently via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} keywords, which correspond to the 6 simulation box
dimensions.  For example, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} keyword is used, the y\sphinxhyphen{}box length
will change during the minimization.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} keyword is used, the
xy tilt factor will change.  A box dimension will not change if that
component is not specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in order to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} keywords, the
simulation box must be triclinic, even if its initial tilt factors are
0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the size of the simulation box changes, all atoms are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled
to new positions, unless the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a
value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case only the atoms in the fix group are
re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled.  This can be useful for leaving the coordinates of atoms in
a solid substrate unchanged and controlling the pressure of a
surrounding fluid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} keywords control whether or
not the corresponding tilt factors are scaled with the associated box
dimensions when relaxing triclinic periodic cells.  The default
values \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} will turn on scaling, which corresponds to adjusting the
linear dimensions of the cell while preserving its shape.  Choosing
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no} ensures that the tilt factors are not scaled with the box
dimensions. See below for restrictions and default values in different
situations. In older versions of LAMMPS, scaling of tilt factors was
not performed. The old behavior can be recovered by setting all three
scale keywords to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} keyword specifies the fixed point for cell relaxation.
By default, it is the center of the box.  Whatever point is
chosen will not move during the simulation.  For example, if the lower
periodic boundaries pass through (0,0,0), and this point is provided
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint}, then the lower periodic boundaries will remain at
(0,0,0), while the upper periodic boundaries will move twice as
far. In all cases, the particle positions at each iteration are
unaffected by the chosen value, except that all particles are
displaced by the same amount, different on each iteration.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applying an external pressure to tilt dimensions \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}
can sometimes result in arbitrarily large values of the tilt factors,
i.e. a dramatically deformed simulation box.  This typically indicates
that there is something badly wrong with how the simulation was
constructed.  The two most common sources of this error are applying a
shear stress to a liquid system or specifying an external shear stress
tensor that exceeds the yield stress of the solid.  In either case the
minimization may converge to a bogus conformation or not converge at
all.  Also note that if the box shape tilts to an extreme shape,
LAMMPS will run less efficiently, due to the large volume of
communication needed to acquire ghost atoms around a processor’s
irregular\sphinxhyphen{}shaped subdomain.  For extreme values of tilt, LAMMPS may
also lose atoms and generate an error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Performing a minimization with this fix is not a mathematically
well\sphinxhyphen{}defined minimization problem.  This is because the objective
function being minimized changes if the box size/shape changes.  In
practice this means the minimizer can get “stuck” before you have
reached the desired tolerance.  The solution to this is to restart the
minimizer from the new adjusted box size/shape, since that creates a
new objective function valid for the new box size/shape.  Repeat as
necessary until the box size/shape has reached its new equilibrium.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keyword allows two or three of the diagonal components of
the pressure tensor to be “coupled” together.  The value specified
with the keyword determines which are coupled.  For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the stress tensor are coupled.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Xyz} means all 3 diagonal components are coupled.  Coupling means two
things: the instantaneous stress will be computed as an average of the
corresponding diagonal components, and the coupled box dimensions will
be changed together in lockstep, meaning coupled dimensions will be
dilated or contracted by the same percentage every timestep.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ptarget} values for any coupled dimensions must be identical.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Couple xyz} can be used for a 2d simulation; the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimension is
simply ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} keywords are simply shortcuts that are
equivalent to specifying several other keywords together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} means couple all 3 diagonal components together when
pressure is computed (hydrostatic pressure), and dilate/contract the
dimensions together.  Using “iso Ptarget” is the same as specifying
these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Ptarget y Ptarget z Ptarget couple xyz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions are controlled
independently using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pyy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the
stress tensor as the driving forces, and the specified scalar external
pressure.  Using “aniso Ptarget” is the same as specifying these 4
keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Ptarget y Ptarget z Ptarget couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} dimensions
are controlled independently using their individual stress components
as the driving forces, and the specified scalar pressure as the
external normal stress.  Using “tri Ptarget” is the same as specifying
these 7 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Ptarget y Ptarget z Ptarget xy 0.0 yz 0.0 xz 0.0 couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vmax} keyword can be used to limit the fractional change in the
volume of the simulation box that can occur in one iteration of the
minimizer.  If the pressure is not settling down during the
minimization this can be because the volume is fluctuating too much.
The specified fraction must be greater than 0.0 and should be \textless{}\textless{} 1.0.
A value of 0.001 means the volume cannot change by more than 1/10 of a
percent in one iteration when \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple xyz} has been specified.  For
any other case it means no linear dimension of the simulation box can
change by more than 1/10 of a percent.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
With this fix, the potential energy used by the minimizer is augmented
by an additional energy provided by the fix. The overall objective
function then is:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = U + P_t \left(V-V_0 \right) + E_{strain}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{U} is the system potential energy, \(P_t\) is the desired
hydrostatic pressure, \(V\) and \(V_0\) are the system and reference
volumes, respectively.  \(E_{strain}\) is the strain energy expression
proposed by Parrinello and Rahman {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_box_relax:parrinello1981}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Parrinello1981)}}}}.
Taking derivatives of \sphinxstyleemphasis{E} w.r.t. the box dimensions, and setting these
to zero, we find that at the minimum of the objective function, the
global system stress tensor \sphinxstylestrong{P} will satisfy the relation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf P = P_t \mathbf I + {\mathbf S_t} \left( \mathbf h_0^{-1} \right)^t \mathbf h_{0d}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstylestrong{I} is the identity matrix, \(\mathbf{h_0}\) is the box
dimension tensor of the reference cell, and :\(\mathbf{h_{0d}}\)
is the diagonal part of \(\mathbf{h_0}\). \(\mathbf{S_t}\)
is a symmetric stress tensor that is chosen by LAMMPS
so that the upper\sphinxhyphen{}triangular components of \sphinxstylestrong{P} equal the stress tensor
specified by the user.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This equation only applies when the box dimensions are equal to those
of the reference dimensions. If this is not the case, then the
converged stress tensor will not equal that specified by the user.  We
can resolve this problem by periodically resetting the reference
dimensions. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} controls how often this is done.  If
this keyword is not used, or is given a value of zero, then the
reference dimensions are set to those of the initial simulation domain
and are never changed. A value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} means that every \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep}
minimization steps, the reference dimensions are set to those of the
current simulation domain. Note that resetting the reference
dimensions changes the objective function and gradients, which
sometimes causes the minimization to fail. This can be resolved by
changing the value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset}, or simply continuing the minimization
from a restart file.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As normally computed, pressure includes a kinetic\sphinxhyphen{} energy or
temperature\sphinxhyphen{}dependent component; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} command.  However, atom velocities are
ignored during a minimization, and the applied pressure(s) specified
with this command are assumed to only be the virial component of the
pressure (the non\sphinxhyphen{}kinetic portion).  Thus if atoms have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero
temperature and you print the usual thermodynamic pressure, it may not
appear the system is converging to your specified pressure.  The
solution for this is to either (a) zero the velocities of all atoms
before performing the minimization, or (b) make sure you are
monitoring the pressure without its kinetic component.  The latter can
be done by outputting the pressure from the pressure compute this
command creates (see below) or a pressure compute you define yourself.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because pressure is often a very sensitive function of volume,
it can be difficult for the minimizer to equilibrate the system the
desired pressure with high precision, particularly for solids.  Some
techniques that seem to help are (a) use the “min\_modify line
quadratic” option when minimizing with box relaxations, (b) minimize
several times in succession if need be, to drive the pressure closer
to the target pressure, (c) relax the atom positions before relaxing
the box, and (d) relax the box to the target hydrostatic pressure
before relaxing to a target shear stress state. Also note that some
systems (e.g. liquids) will not sustain a non\sphinxhyphen{}hydrostatic applied
pressure, which means the minimizer will not converge.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure each timestep.  The
temperature is used to compute the kinetic contribution to the
pressure, even though this is subsequently ignored by default.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp” and “pressure”,
as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{virial}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the
IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is the same
as the fix group.  Also note that the pressure compute does not
include a kinetic component.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of this
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
or pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its temperature and pressure calculation, as described above.  Note
that as described above, if you assign a pressure compute to this fix
that includes a kinetic energy component it will affect the
minimization, most likely in an undesirable way.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If both the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keywords are used in a single
thermo\_modify command (or in two separate commands), then the order in
which the keywords are specified is important.  Note that a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pressure compute}}}} defines its own temperature compute as
an argument when it is specified.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword will override
this (for the pressure compute being used by fix box/relax), but only if the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword comes after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword
comes before the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword, then the new pressure compute
specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword will be unaffected by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}
setting.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}. The scalar is the pressure\sphinxhyphen{}volume
energy, plus the strain energy, if it exists, as described above.  The
energy values reported at the end of a minimization run under
“Minimization stats” include this energy, and so differ from what
LAMMPS normally reports as potential energy. This fix does not support
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option, because that would
result in double\sphinxhyphen{}counting of the fix energy in the minimization
energy. Instead, the fix energy can be explicitly added to the
potential energy using one of these two variants:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{emin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}1}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{emin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atoms}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}, but
not for the purpose of adding a contribution to the energy or forces
being minimized.  Instead it alters the simulation box geometry as
described above.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only dimensions that are available can be adjusted by this fix.
Non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic dimensions are not available.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, are
not available for 2D simulations. \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} are only
available if the simulation domain is non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands specify whether the
simulation box is orthogonal or non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal (triclinic) and explain
the meaning of the xy,xz,yz tilt factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz yes} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz yes} keyword/value pairs can not be used
for 2D simulations. \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz yes}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz yes}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy yes} options
can only be used if the second dimension in the keyword is periodic,
and if the tilt factor is not coupled to the barostat via keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are dilate = all, vmax = 0.0001, nreset = 0.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_box_relax:parrinello1981}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix brownian command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:fix-brownian-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian::doc}}

\section{fix brownian/sphere command}

\section{fix brownian/asphere command}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style\_name = \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp = temperature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number generator seed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rng} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r\_eigen} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t\_eigen} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotation\_temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{planar\_rotation}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rng} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform} = use uniform random number generator
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} = use gaussian random number generator
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} = turn off noise
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mux} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{muy} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{muz} for \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mux}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{muy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{muz} = update orientation of dipole having direction (\sphinxstyleemphasis{mux},*muy*,*muz*) in body frame of rigid body
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r\_eigen} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr2} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr3} for \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr2}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr3} = diagonal entries of body frame rotational friction tensor
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr} for \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{gr} = magnitude of the (isotropic) rotational friction tensor
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t\_eigen} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt2} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt3} for \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt2}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt3} = diagonal entries of body frame translational friction tensor
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt} for \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{gt} = magnitude of the (isotropic) translational friction tensor
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rotation\_temp} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{T} for \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{T} = rotation temperature, which can be different then \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} when out of equilibrium
\sphinxstyleemphasis{planar\_rotation} values = none (constrains rotational diffusion to be in xy plane if in 3D)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{brownian}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12908410}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{brownian}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1294019}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}r}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{brownian}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19581092}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}r}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{none}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{brownian}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1294019}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}t\PYGZus{}eigen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}r\PYGZus{}eigen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{brownian}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1294019}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}t\PYGZus{}eigen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}r\PYGZus{}eigen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform Brownian Dynamics time integration to update position, velocity,
dipole orientation (for spheres) and quaternion orientation (for
ellipsoids, with optional dipole update as well) of all particles in the
fix group in each timestep.  Brownian Dynamics uses Newton’s laws of
motion in the limit that inertial forces are negligible compared to
viscous forces. The stochastic equation of motion for the center of mass
positions is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}d\mathbf{r} = \boldsymbol{\gamma}_t^{-1}\mathbf{F}dt
+ \sqrt{2k_B T}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_t^{-1/2}d\mathbf{W}_t,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
in the lab\sphinxhyphen{}frame (i.e., \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}_t\) is not diagonal, but
only depends on orientation and so the noise is still additive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The rotational motion for the spherical and ellipsoidal particles is not
as simple an expression, but is chosen to replicate the Boltzmann
distribution for the case of conservative torques (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:ilie1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ilie)}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:delong1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Delong)}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian}, only the positions of the particles are
updated. This is therefore suitable for point particle simulations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere}, the positions of the particles are
updated, and a dipole slaved to the spherical orientation is also
updated. This style therefore requires the hybrid atom style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style dipole}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}. The equation of motion for the dipole is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\boldsymbol{\mu}(t+dt) = \frac{\boldsymbol{\mu}(t) + \boldsymbol{\omega} \times \boldsymbol{\mu}dt
}{|\boldsymbol{\mu}(t) + \boldsymbol{\omega} \times \boldsymbol{\mu}|}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which correctly reproduces a Boltzmann distribution of orientations and
rotational diffusion moments (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:ilie1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ilie)}}}}) when
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\boldsymbol{\omega} = \frac{\mathbf{T}}{\gamma_r} + \sqrt{\frac{2 k_B T_{rot}}{\gamma_r}\frac{d\mathbf{W}}{dt}},\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(d\mathbf{W}\) being a random number with zero mean and variance \(dt\)
and \(T_{rot}\) is \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotation\_temp}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}, the center of mass positions and the
quaternions of ellipsoidal particles are updated. This fix style is
suitable for equations of motion where the rotational and translational
friction tensors can be diagonalized in a certain (body) reference
frame. In this case, the rotational equation of motion is updated via
the quaternion
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{q}(t+dt) = \frac{\mathbf{q}(t) + d\mathbf{q}}{\lVert\mathbf{q}(t) + d\mathbf{q}\rVert}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which correctly reproduces a Boltzmann distribution of orientations and rotational
diffusion moments {[}see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:ilie1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ilie)}}}}{]} when the quaternion step is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}d\mathbf{q} = \boldsymbol{\Psi}\boldsymbol{\omega}dt\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}\) has rows \((-q_1,-q_2,-q_3)\),
\((q_0,-q_3,q_2)\), \((q_3,q_0,-q_1)\), and \((-q_2,q_1,q_0)\).
\(\boldsymbol{\omega}\) is evaluated in the body frame of reference where the
friction tensor is diagonal.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:delong1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Delong)}}}} for more details of
a similar algorithm.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This integrator does not by default assume a relationship between the
rotational and translational friction tensors, though such a
relationship should exist in the case of no\sphinxhyphen{}slip boundary conditions
between the particles and the surrounding (implicit) solvent. For example,
in the case of spherical particles, the condition
\(\gamma_t=3\gamma_r/\sigma^2\) must be explicitly accounted for
by setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} to 3x and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r} to x (where \(\sigma\)
is the sphere’s diameter). A similar (though more complex)
relationship holds for ellipsoids and rod\sphinxhyphen{}like particles. The
translational diffusion and rotational diffusion are given by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/gamma\_t} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotation\_temp/gamma\_r}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Temperature computation using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}
will not correctly compute the temperature of these overdamped dynamics
since we are explicitly neglecting inertial effects.  Furthermore,
this time integrator does not add the stochastic terms or viscous
terms to the force and/or torques.  Rather, they are just added in to
the equations of motion to update the degrees of freedom.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rng} keyword is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform} value, then the noise
is generated from a uniform distribution (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:dunweg7}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dunweg)}}}} for why this works). This is the same method
of noise generation as used in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_langevin}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rng} keyword is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} value, then the noise
is generated from a Gaussian distribution. Typically this added
complexity is unnecessary, and one should be fine using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform}
value for reasons argued in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_brownian:dunweg7}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dunweg)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rng} keyword is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} value, then the noise
terms are set to zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} keyword sets the (isotropic) translational viscous damping.
Required for (and only compatible with) \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere}.
The units of \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} are mass/time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r} keyword sets the (isotropic) rotational viscous damping.
Required for (and only compatible with) \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere}.
The units of \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r} are mass*length**2/time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r\_eigen}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t\_eigen} keywords are the eigenvalues of
the rotational and viscous damping tensors (having the same units as
their isotropic counterparts). Required for (and only compatible with)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}. For a 2D system, the first two values of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r\_eigen} must be \sphinxstyleemphasis{inf} (only rotation in \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}\textendash{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{y} plane), and the third
value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t\_eigen} must be \sphinxstyleemphasis{inf} (only diffusion in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}\textendash{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{y} plane).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} keyword is used, then the dipole moments of the particles
are updated as described above. Only compatible with \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}
(as \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} updates dipoles automatically).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotation\_temp} keyword is used, then the rotational diffusion
will be occur at this prescribed temperature instead of \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}. Only
compatible with \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{planar\_rotation} keyword is used, then rotation is constrained
to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}\textendash{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} plane in a 3D simulation. Only compatible with
\sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere} in 3D.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere}, the components \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t\_eigen} = (x,x,x) and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r\_eigen} = (y,y,y), the dynamics will replicate those of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} style with \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} = x and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_r} = y.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/sphere} fix requires that atoms store torque and
angular velocity (omega) as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} command.  The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/asphere} fix requires that
atoms store torque and quaternions as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style
ellipsoid}}}} command.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} keyword is used, they
must also store a dipole moment as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style
dipole}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the BROWNIAN package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_propel_self::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix propel/self}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/sphere}}}},


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_brownian:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default for \sphinxstyleemphasis{rng} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{uniform}. The default for the rotational and
translational friction tensors are the identity tensor.

\section{fix charge/regulation command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:fix-charge-regulation-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cation\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{anion\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{s}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
charge/regulation = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cation\_type = atom type of free cations (integer or type label)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
anion\_type = atom type of free anions (integer or type label)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pH}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pKa}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pKb}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pIp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pIm}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pKs}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{acid\_type}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{base\_type}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lunit\_nm}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tempfixid}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nevery}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{rxd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tag}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{group}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{onlysalt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcmoves}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pH} value = pH of the solution (can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pKa} value = acid dissociation constant (in the \sphinxhyphen{}log10 representation)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pKb} value = base dissociation constant (in the \sphinxhyphen{}log10 representation)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pIp} value = activity (effective concentration) of free cations (in the \sphinxhyphen{}log10 representation)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pIm} value = activity (effective concentration) of free anions (in the \sphinxhyphen{}log10 representation)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pKs} value = solvent self\sphinxhyphen{}dissociation constant (in the \sphinxhyphen{}log10 representation)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{acid\_type} = atom type of acid groups (integer or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{base\_type}  = atom type of base groups (integer or type label)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lunit\_nm} value = unit length used by LAMMPS (\# in the units of nanometers)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value = temperature
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tempfixid} value = fix ID of temperature thermostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nevery} value = invoke this fix every nevery steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nmc} value = number of charge regulation MC moves to attempt every nevery steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rxd} value = cutoff distance for acid/base reaction
\sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} value = random \# seed (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tag} value = yes or no (yes: The code assign unique tags to inserted ions; no: The tag of all inserted ions is "0")
\sphinxstyleemphasis{group} value = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID, inserted ions are assigned to group group\sphinxhyphen{}ID. Can be used multiple times to assign inserted ions to multiple groups.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{onlysalt} values = flag charge\_cation charge\_anion.
   flag = yes or no (yes: the fix performs only ion insertion/deletion, no: perform acid/base dissociation and ion insertion/deletion)
   charge\_cation, charge\_anion = value of cation/anion charge, must be an integer (only specify if flag = yes)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcmoves} values = pmcA pmcB pmcI \sphinxhyphen{}  MC move fractions for acid ionization (pmcA), base ionization (pmcB) and free ion exchange (pmcI)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{chareg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acid\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nmc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{123}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tempfixid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fT}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{chareg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{onlysalt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{123}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{OH}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{chareg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{OH}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{onlysalt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{123}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs Monte Carlo (MC) sampling of charge regulation and
exchange of ions with a reservoir as discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:curk1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Curk1)}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:curk2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Curk2)}}}}.  The implemented method is largely analogous
to the grand\sphinxhyphen{}reaction ensemble method in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:landsgesell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Landsgesell)}}}}.  The implementation is parallelized, compatible with
existing LAMMPS functionalities, and applicable to any system utilizing
discrete, ionizable groups or surface sites.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically, the fix implements the following three types of MC moves,
which discretely change the charge state of individual particles and
insert ions into the systems: \(\mathrm{A} \rightleftharpoons
\mathrm{A}^-+\mathrm{X}^+\), \(\mathrm{B} \rightleftharpoons
\mathrm{B}^++\mathrm{X}^-\), and \(\emptyset \rightleftharpoons
Z^-\mathrm{X}^{Z^+}+Z^+\mathrm{X}^{-Z^-}\).  In the former two types of
reactions, Monte Carlo moves alter the charge value of specific atoms
(\(\mathrm{A}\), \(\mathrm{B}\)) and simultaneously insert a
counterion to preserve the charge neutrality of the system, modeling the
dissociation/association process.  The last type of reaction performs
grand canonical MC exchange of ion pairs with a (fictitious) reservoir.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In our implementation “acid” refers to particles that can attain charge
\(q=\{0,-1\}\) and “base” to particles with \(q=\{0,1\}\),
whereas the MC exchange of free ions allows any integer charge values of
\({Z^+}\) and \({Z^-}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here we provide several practical examples for modeling charge
regulation effects in solvated systems.  An acid ionization reaction
(\(\mathrm{A} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{A}^-+\mathrm{H}^+\)) can be
defined via a single line in the input file

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{acid\PYGZus{}reaction}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acid\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the fix attempts to charge \(\mathrm{A}\) (discharge
\(\mathrm{A}^-\)) to \(\mathrm{A}^-\) (\(\mathrm{A}\)) and
insert (delete) a proton (atom type 2). Besides, the fix implements
self\sphinxhyphen{}ionization reaction of water \(\emptyset \rightleftharpoons
\mathrm{H}^++\mathrm{OH}^-\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, this approach is highly inefficient at \(\mathrm{pH}
\approx 7\) when the concentration of both protons and hydroxyl ions is
low, resulting in a relatively low acceptance rate of MC moves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A more efficient way is to allow salt ions to participate in ionization
reactions, which can be easily achieved via

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{acid\PYGZus{}reaction2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acid\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where particles of atom type 4 and 5 are the salt cations and anions,
both at activity (effective concentration) of \(10^{-2}\) mol/l, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:curk1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Curk1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:landsgesell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Landsgesell)}}}} for more
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
We could have simultaneously added a base ionization reaction
(\(\mathrm{B} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{B}^++\mathrm{OH}^-\))

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{acid\PYGZus{}base\PYGZus{}reaction}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acid\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the fix will attempt to charge \(\mathrm{B}\) (discharge
\(\mathrm{B}^+\)) to \(\mathrm{B}^+\) (\(\mathrm{B}\)) and
insert (delete) a hydroxyl ion \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) of atom type 3.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dissociated ions and salt ions can be combined into a single particle
type, which reduces the number of necessary MC moves and increases
sampling performance, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:curk1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Curk1)}}}}. The
\(\mathrm{H}^+\) and monovalent salt cation (\(\mathrm{S}^+\))
are combined into a single particle type, \(\mathrm{X}^+ =
\{\mathrm{H}^+, \mathrm{S}^+\}\). In this case “pIp” refers to the
effective concentration of the combined cation type \(\mathrm{X}^+\)
and its value is determined by \(10^{-\mathrm{pIp}} =
10^{-\mathrm{pH}} + 10^{-\mathrm{pSp}}\), where
\(10^{-\mathrm{pSp}}\) is the effective concentration of salt
cations. For example, at pH=7 and pSp=6 we would find pIp\textasciitilde{}5.958 and the
command that performs reactions with combined ions could read,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{acid\PYGZus{}reaction\PYGZus{}combined}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acid\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pKa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.958}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.958}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If neither the acid or the base type is specified, for example,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{salt\PYGZus{}reaction}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charge}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{regulation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pIm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the fix simply inserts or deletes an ion pair of a free cation (atom
type 4) and a free anion (atom type 5) as done in a conventional
grand\sphinxhyphen{}canonical MC simulation. Multivalent ions can be inserted
(deleted) by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{onlysalt} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is compatible with LAMMPS packages such as MOLECULE or
RIGID. The acid and base particles can be part of larger molecules or
rigid bodies. Free ions that are inserted to or deleted from the system
must be defined as single particles (no bonded interactions allowed) and
cannot be part of larger molecules or rigid bodies. If an atom style
with molecule IDs is used, all inserted ions have a molecule ID equal to
zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that LAMMPS implicitly assumes a constant number of particles
(degrees of freedom). Since using this fix alters the total number of
particles during the simulation, any thermostat used by LAMMPS, such as
NVT or Langevin, must use a dynamic calculation of system
temperature. This can be achieved by specifying a dynamic temperature
compute (e.g. dtemp) and using it with the desired thermostat, e.g. a
Langevin thermostat:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dtemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dtemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamic}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dof}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{123}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dtemp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The units of pH, pKa, pKb, pIp, pIm are considered to be in the
standard \sphinxhyphen{}log10 representation assuming reference concentration
\(\rho_0 = \mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}\).  For example, in the dilute
ideal solution limit, the concentration of free cations will be
\(c_\mathrm{I} = 10^{-\mathrm{pIp}}\mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}\). To
perform the internal unit conversion, the the value of the LAMMPS unit
length must be specified in nanometers via \sphinxstyleemphasis{lunit\_nm}. The default value
is set to the Bjerrum length in water at room temperature (0.71 nm),
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lunit\_nm} = 0.71.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature used in MC acceptance probability is set by \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}. This
temperature should be the same as the temperature set by the molecular
dynamics thermostat. For most purposes, it is probably best to use
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tempfixid} keyword which dynamically sets the temperature equal to the
chosen MD thermostat temperature, in the example above we assumed the
thermostat fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID is \sphinxstyleemphasis{fT}. The inserted particles attain a random
velocity corresponding to the specified temperature. Using \sphinxstyleemphasis{tempfixid}
overrides any fixed temperature set by \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rxd} keyword can be used to restrict the inserted/deleted
counterions to a specific radial distance from an acid or base particle
that is currently participating in a reaction. This can be used to
simulate more realist reaction dynamics. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{rxd} = 0 or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rxd} \textgreater{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{L} /
2, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{L} is the smallest box dimension, the radial restriction is
automatically turned off and free ion can be inserted or deleted
anywhere in the simulation box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tag yes} is used, every inserted atom gets a unique tag ID,
otherwise, the tag of every inserted atom is set to 0. \sphinxstyleemphasis{tag yes} might
cause an integer overflow in very long simulations since the tags are
unique to every particle and thus increase with every successful
particle insertion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcmoves} keyword sets the relative probability of attempting the
three types of MC moves (reactions): acid charging, base charging, and
ion pair exchange.  The fix only attempts to perform particle charging
MC moves if \sphinxstyleemphasis{acid\_type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{base\_type} is defined. Otherwise fix only
performs free ion insertion/deletion. For example, if \sphinxstyleemphasis{acid\_type} is not
defined, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcA} is automatically set to 0. The vector \sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcmoves} is
automatically normalized, for example, if set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcmoves} 0 0.33 0.33,
the vector would be normalized to {[}0,0.5,0.5{]}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{only\_salt} option can be used to perform multivalent
grand\sphinxhyphen{}canonical ion\sphinxhyphen{}exchange moves. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{only\_salt yes} is used, no
charge exchange is performed, only ion insertion/deletion (\sphinxstyleemphasis{pmcmoves} is
set to {[}0,0,1{]}), but ions can be multivalent. In the example above, an
MC move would consist of three ion insertion/deletion to preserve the
charge neutrality of the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} keyword can be used to add inserted particles to a specific
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID. All inserted particles are automatically added to group \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}.


\subsection{Output}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:output}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global vector of length 8, which can be accessed by
various output commands. The vector values are the following global
quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative MC attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative MC successes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current \# of neutral acid atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current \# of \sphinxhyphen{}1 charged acid atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current \# of neutral base atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current \# of +1 charged base atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current \# of free cations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current \# of free anions

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package. It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}, used must contain the charge
property and have per atom type masses, for example, the style could be
\sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{full}. Only usable for 3D simulations.  Atoms specified as
free ions cannot be part of rigid bodies or molecules and cannot have
bonding interactions.  The scheme is limited to integer charges, any
atoms with non\sphinxhyphen{}integer charges will not be considered by the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All interaction potentials used must be continuous, otherwise the MD
integration and the particle exchange MC moves do not correspond to the
same equilibrium ensemble. For example, if an lj/cut pair style is used,
the LJ potential must be shifted so that it vanishes at the cutoff. This
can be easily achieved using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
command, i.e., by using: \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_modify shift yes}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Region restrictions are not yet implemented.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gcmc}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atom/swap}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
pH = 7.0; pKa = 100.0; pKb = 100.0; pIp = 5.0; pIm = 5.0; pKs = 14.0;
acid\_type = \sphinxhyphen{}1; base\_type = \sphinxhyphen{}1; lunit\_nm = 0.71; temp = 1.0; nevery =
100; nmc = 100; rxd = 0; seed = 0; tag = no; onlysalt = no, pmcmoves =
{[}1/3, 1/3, 1/3{]}, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = all


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:curk1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Curk1)} T. Curk, J. Yuan, and E. Luijten, “Accelerated simulation method for charge regulation effects”, JCP 156 (2022).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:curk2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Curk2)} T. Curk and E. Luijten, “Charge\sphinxhyphen{}regulation effects in nanoparticle self\sphinxhyphen{}assembly”, PRL 126 (2021)

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_charge_regulation:landsgesell}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Landsgesell)} J. Landsgesell, P. Hebbeker, O. Rud, R. Lunkad, P. Kosovan, and C. Holm, “Grand\sphinxhyphen{}reaction method for simulations of ionization equilibria coupled to ion partitioning”, Macromolecules 53, 3007\sphinxhyphen{}3020 (2020).

\index{fix cmap@\spxentry{fix cmap}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix cmap command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:fix-cmap-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filename}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cmap = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename = force\sphinxhyphen{}field file with CMAP coefficients

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix            }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myCMAP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cmap36.data}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{proteinX.data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myCMAP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{crossterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CMAP}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myCMAP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enables CMAP 5\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions to be added to
simulations which use the CHARMM force field.  These are relevant for
any CHARMM model of a peptide or protein sequences that is 3 or more
amino\sphinxhyphen{}acid residues long; see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_cmap:buck}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Buck)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_cmap:brooks2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Brooks)}}}} for details, including the analytic energy expressions for
CMAP interactions.  The CMAP 5\sphinxhyphen{}body terms add additional potential
energy contributions to pairs of overlapping phi\sphinxhyphen{}psi dihedrals of
amino\sphinxhyphen{}acids, which are important to properly represent their
conformational behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples/cmap directory has a sample input script and data file
for a small peptide, that illustrates use of the fix cmap command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As in the example above, this fix should be used before reading a data
file that contains a listing of CMAP interactions.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename}
specified should contain the CMAP parameters for a particular version
of the CHARMM force field.  Two such files are including in the
lammps/potentials directory: charmm22.cmap and charmm36.cmap.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The data file read by the “read\_data” must contain the topology of all
the CMAP interactions, similar to the topology data for bonds, angles,
dihedrals, etc.  Specially it should have a line like this in its
header section:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
N crossterms
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where N is the number of CMAP 5\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.  It should also
have a section in the body of the data file like this with N lines:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
CMAP

       1       1       8      10      12      18      20
       2       5      18      20      22      25      27
       [...]
       N       3     314     315     317      318    330
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first column is an index from 1 to N to enumerate the CMAP 5\sphinxhyphen{}atom
tuples; it is ignored by LAMMPS.  The second column is the “type” of
the interaction; it is an index into the CMAP force field file.  The
remaining 5 columns are the atom IDs of the atoms in the two 4\sphinxhyphen{}atom
dihedrals that overlap to create the CMAP interaction.  Note that the
“crossterm” and “CMAP” keywords for the header and body sections match
those specified in the read\_data command following the data file name;
see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} page for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A data file containing CMAP 5\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions can be generated from
a PDB file using the charmm2lammps.pl script in the tools/ch2lmp
directory of the LAMMPS distribution.  The script must be invoked with
the optional “\sphinxhyphen{}cmap” flag to do this; see the tools/ch2lmp/README file
for more information.  The same conversion script also creates the
file of CMAP coefficient data which is read by this command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential energy associated with CMAP interactions can be output
as described below.  It can also be included in the total potential
energy of the system, as output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command, if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy}}}}
command is used, as in the example above.  See the note below about
how to include the CMAP energy when performing an {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy
minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the list of CMAP cross\sphinxhyphen{}terms to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command
for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a
restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy of the CMAP interactions to both
the global potential energy and peratom potential energies of the
system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} or
output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pe_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pe/atom}}}} command.  The
default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy yes}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution due to the CMAP interactions to both
the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of the system via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be
accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial yes}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the potential
energy discussed above.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For energy minimization, if you want the potential energy
associated with the CMAP terms forces to be included in the total
potential energy of the system (the quantity being minimized), you
MUST not disable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option
for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To function as expected this fix command must be issued \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command but \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the MOLECULE
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:buck}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Buck)} Buck, Bouguet\sphinxhyphen{}Bonnet, Pastor, MacKerell Jr., Biophys J, 90, L36
(2006).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_cmap:brooks2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Brooks)} Brooks, Brooks, MacKerell Jr., J Comput Chem, 30, 1545 (2009).
