\index{fix colvars@\spxentry{fix colvars}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix colvars command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:fix-colvars-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{configfile}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ID}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“colvars” = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{configfile} = configuration file for Colvars (use “\sphinxstyleemphasis{none}” to provide it inline)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{output} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{input} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{output} value = state filename/prefix for Colvars (default: "out")
\sphinxstyleemphasis{input} value = input state filename/prefix for Colvars (optional, default: "NULL")
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} value = "yes" or "no" (default: "yes")
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} value = fix ID of thermostat applied to relevant atoms (default: "NULL")
\sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} value = seed for random number generator (default: 1966)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Create the fix using a config file, set prefix for its output files}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{colvars.inp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{output}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{JOB}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Communicate the LAMMPS target temperature to the Colvars module}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tstat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NPT}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Add a new restraint specific to this LAMMPS run}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{l+s}{harmonic \PYGZob{}}
\PYG{l+s}{    name restraint}
\PYG{l+s}{    colvars distance1 distance2}
\PYG{l+s}{    centers \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}ref1\PYGZcb{} \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}ref2\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{l+s}{    forceConstant \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}kappa\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix interfaces LAMMPS to the collective variables \sphinxhref{https://colvars.github.io}{Colvars} library, which allows to accelerate
sampling of rare events and the computation of free energy surfaces
and potentials of mean force (PMFs) for any set of collective
variables using a variety of sampling methods (e.g. umbrella\sphinxhyphen{}sampling,
metadynamics, ABF…).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This documentation describes only the “fix colvars” command itself in a
LAMMPS script.  The Colvars library is fully documented in the included
\sphinxhref{PDF/colvars-refman-lammps.pdf}{PDF manual} or in the webpage
\sphinxurl{https://colvars.github.io/colvars-refman-lammps/colvars-refman-lammps.html}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Colvars library is developed at \sphinxhref{https://github.com/colvars/colvars}{https://github.com/Colvars/colvars}.  A detailed discussion of its
implementation is in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_colvars:fiorin}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fiorin)}}}}; additional citations for
specific features are printed at runtime if these features are used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are example scripts on the \sphinxhref{https://colvars.github.io}{Colvars website} as well as in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/colvars}} directory in the LAMMPS source tree.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The only required argument to the fix is the name of the Colvars
configuration file.  The contents of this file are independent from the
MD engine in which the Colvars library has been integrated, save for the
units that are specific to each engine.  In LAMMPS, the units used by
Colvars are consistent with those specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version Colvars\_2023\sphinxhyphen{}06\sphinxhyphen{}04: }The special value “\sphinxstyleemphasis{none}” (lowercase) initializes an empty Colvars
module, which allows loading configuration dynamically using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} (see below).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} entry is ignored.  “fix colvars” will always apply to the
entire system, but specific atoms will be selected based on selection
keywords in the Colvars configuration file or files.  There is no need
to define multiple “fix colvars” instances and it is not allowed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “output” keyword allows to specify the prefix of output files
generated by Colvars, for example “\sphinxstyleemphasis{output}.colvars.traj” or
“output.pmf”.  Supplying an empty string suppresses any file output from
Colvars to file, except for data saved into the LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart}}}} files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “input” keyword allows to specify an optional state file that
contains the restart information needed to continue a previous
simulation state.  However, because “fix colvars” records its state in
LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart}}}} files, this is usually not needed
when using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} keyword controls whether wrapped or unwrapped coordinates
are passed to the Colvars library for calculation of the collective
variables and the resulting forces.  The default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, i.e. the
image flags are used to reconstruct the absolute atom positions.
Setting this to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} will use the current local coordinates that are
wrapped back into the simulation cell at each re\sphinxhyphen{}neighboring step
instead.  For information about when and how this affects results,
please see
\sphinxurl{https://colvars.github.io/colvars-refman-lammps/colvars-refman-lammps.html\#sec:colvar\_atom\_groups\_wrapping}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} keyword can be either “NULL” or the label of a
thermostatting fix that thermostats all atoms in the fix colvars
group. This will be used to provide the colvars module with the current
thermostat target temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} keyword contains the seed for the random number generator
that will be used in the colvars module.


\subsection{Restarting}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:restarting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the current state of the Colvars module into
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This is in addition to the
text\sphinxhyphen{}mode “.colvars.state” state file that is written by the Colvars
module itself.  The information contained in both files is identical,
and the binary LAMMPS restart file is also used by fix colvars when
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} is called in a LAMMPS script.  In
that case, there is typically no need to specify the \sphinxstyleemphasis{input} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As long as LAMMPS binary restarts will be used to continue a simulation,
it is safe to delete the “.colvars.state” files to save space.  However,
when a LAMMPS simulation is restarted using {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, the Colvars state file must be available and loaded via
the “input” keyword or via a “fix\_modify Colvars load” command (see
below).

\sphinxAtStartPar
When restarting, the fix and the Colvars module should be created and
configured using the original configuration file(s).


\subsection{Output}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:output}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the energy due to
all external potentials defined in the Colvars configuration.  The
scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aside from the state information in a “.colvars.state” file, other
\sphinxhref{https://colvars.github.io/colvars-refman-lammps/colvars-refman-lammps.html\#sec:colvars\_output}{output files}
are produced by Colvars depending on the type of simulation.  For this
reason, the “output” keyword is required for fix colvars.


\subsection{Controlling Colvars via \sphinxtitleref{fix\_modify}}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:controlling-colvars-via-fix-modify}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version Colvars\_2023\sphinxhyphen{}06\sphinxhyphen{}04.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command may be used on “fix colvars”
in either one of two ways:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{(}{)}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Provide updated values for the fix parameters, such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{output},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{input}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed}.  Additionally, the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is supported by this fix
to add the energy change from the biasing force added by Colvars to the
global potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic
output}}}} (the default is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}).  For example, in a multi\sphinxhyphen{}step LAMMPS script involving
multiple thermostats (e.g. fix nvt followed by fix npt), Colvars can
read a new thermostat’s target temperature like this:

\end{enumerate}
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NVT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{configfile}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{output}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equil1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tstat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NVT}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{NUMSTEPS}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{k}{unfix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{nvt}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NPT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tstat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NPT}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{output}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equil2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{quote}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{(}{)}%
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call one of the scripting functions provided by the Colvars module
itself (a full list is available in the Colvars doc).  The arguments
to these functions are provided as strings and passed to Colvars.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS variables referenced by their string representation
“\$\{variable\}” will be expanded immediately.  Note also that this
variable expansion \sphinxstyleemphasis{will also happen within quotes}, similar to what
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi}}}} command provides.  This feature makes it
possible to use the values of certain LAMMPS variables in Colvars
configuration strings.  For example, to synchronize the LAMMPS and
Colvars dump frequencies:

\end{enumerate}
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{freq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myDump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{zstd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{freq}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.atom.zstd}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Colvars}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{colvarsTrajFrequency \PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}freq\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Although it is possible to use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} at any
time, its results will only reflect the state of the Colvars module
at the end of the most recent “run” or “minimize” command.  Any new
configuration added via “fix\_modify Colvars configfile” or
“fix\_modify Colvars config” will only be loaded when the simulation
resumes.  Configuration files or strings will be parsed in the same
sequence as they were provided in the LAMMPS script.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is provided by the COLVARS package and is only available if
LAMMPS was built with that package (default in most builds).  Some of
the features also require code available from the LEPTON package.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There can only be one Colvars instance defined at a time.  Since the
interface communicates only the minimum required amount of information,
and the Colvars module itself can handle an arbitrary number of
collective variables, this is not a limitation of functionality.

\label{\detokenize{fix_colvars:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix smd}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_plumed::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix plumed}}}}

\section{fix controller command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_controller:fix-controller-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_controller:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_controller::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_controller:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{controller}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Kp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ki}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Kd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pvar}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{setpoint}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvar}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
controller = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = invoke controller every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
alpha = coupling constant for PID equation (see units discussion below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kp = proportional gain in PID equation (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ki = integral gain in PID equation (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kd = derivative gain in PID equation (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pvar = process variable of form c\_ID, c\_ID{[}I{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}I{]}, or v\_name

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
c\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector calculated by a compute with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID = global scalar calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith component of global vector calculated by a fix with ID
v\PYGZus{}name = value calculated by an equal\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
setpoint = desired value of process variable (same units as process variable)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cvar = name of control variable

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_controller:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{controller}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}thermo\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tcontrol}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{controller}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}pxxwall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.01325}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xwall}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{controller}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}avpe}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{3.785}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tcontrol}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_controller:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix enables control of a LAMMPS simulation using a control loop
feedback mechanism known as a proportional\sphinxhyphen{}integral\sphinxhyphen{}derivative (PID)
controller.  The basic idea is to define a “process variable” which is
a quantity that can be monitored during a running simulation.  A
desired target value is chosen for the process variable.  A “control
variable” is also defined which is an adjustable attribute of the
running simulation, which the process variable will respond to.  The
PID controller continuously adjusts the control variable based on the
difference between the process variable and the target.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are examples of ways in which this fix can be used.  The
examples/pid directory contains a script that implements the simple
thermostat.


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabulary}{\linewidth}[t]{TTT}
\sphinxtoprule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
Goal
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
process variable
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
control variable
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simple thermostat
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
instantaneous T
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermostat target T
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find melting temperature
&
\sphinxAtStartPar
average PE per atom
&
\sphinxAtStartPar

\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar

&

\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For this fix to work, the control variable must actually induce
a change in a running LAMMPS simulation.  Typically this will only
occur if there is some other command (e.g. a thermostat fix) which
uses the control variable as an input parameter.  This could be done
directly or indirectly, e.g. the other command uses a variable as
input whose formula uses the control variable.  The other command
should alter its behavior dynamically as the variable changes.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If there is a command you think could be used in this fashion,
but does not currently allow a variable as an input parameter, please
notify the LAMMPS developers.  It is often not difficult to enable a
command to use a variable as an input parameter.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with this command is ignored.  However, note that
the process variable may be defined by calculations performed by
computes and fixes which store their own “group” definitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The PID controller is invoked once each \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The PID controller is implemented as a discretized version of
the following dynamic equation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{dc}{dt}  = -\alpha (K_p e + K_i \int_0^t e \, dt + K_d \frac{de}{dt} )\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{c} is the continuous time analog of the control variable,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{e} =\sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{setpoint} is the error in the process variable, and
\(\alpha\), \(K_p\), \(K_i\) , and \(K_d\) are constants
set by the corresponding
keywords described above. The discretized version of this equation is:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}c_n  = c_{n-1} -\alpha \left( K_p \tau e_n + K_i \tau^2 \sum_{i=1}^n e_i + K_d (e_n - e_{n-1}) \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\tau = \mathtt{Nevery} \cdot \mathtt{timestep}\) is the time
interval between updates,
and the subscripted variables indicate the values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{c} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{e} at
successive updates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From the first equation, it is clear that if the three gain values
\(K_p\), \(K_i\), \(K_d\) are dimensionless constants,
then \(\alpha\) must have
units of {[}unit \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvar}{]}/{[}unit \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar}{]}/{[}unit time{]} e.g. {[} eV/K/ps
{]}. The advantage of this unit scheme is that the value of the
constants should be invariant under a change of either the MD timestep
size or the value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}. Similarly, if the LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unit style}}}} is changed, it should only be necessary to change
the value of \(\alpha\) to reflect this, while leaving \(K_p\),
\(K_i\), and \(K_d\) unaltered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When choosing the values of the four constants, it is best to first
pick a value and sign for \(\alpha\) that is consistent with the
magnitudes and signs of \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvar}.  The magnitude of \(K_p\)
should then be tested over a large positive range keeping \(K_i = K_d =0\).
A good value for \(K_p\) will produce a fast response in \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar},
without overshooting the \sphinxstyleemphasis{setpoint}.  For many applications, proportional
feedback is sufficient, and so \(K_i = K_d =0\) can be used. In cases
where there is a substantial lag time in the response of \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} to a change
in \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvar}, this can be counteracted by increasing \(K_d\). In situations
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} plateaus without reaching \sphinxstyleemphasis{setpoint}, this can be
counteracted by increasing \(K_i\).  In the language of Charles Dickens,
\(K_p\) represents the error of the present, \(K_i\) the error of
the past, and \(K_d\) the error yet to come.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because this fix updates \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvar}, but does not initialize its value,
the initial value \(c_0\) is that assigned by the user in the input script via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} command.  This value is
used (by every other LAMMPS command that uses the variable) until this
fix performs its first update of \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvar} after \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} timesteps.  On
the first update, the value of the derivative term is set to zero,
because the value of \(e_{n-1}\) is not yet defined.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The process variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} can be specified as the output of a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or the evaluation of a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  In each case, the compute, fix, or variable
must produce a global quantity, not a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local quantity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script and which generates a global
scalar or vector.  See the individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} doc page
for details.  If no bracketed integer is appended, the scalar
calculated by the compute is used.  If a bracketed integer is
appended, the Ith value of the vector calculated by the compute is
used.  Users can also write code for their own compute styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script and which generates a global
scalar or vector.  See the individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} page for
details.  Note that some fixes only produce their values on certain
timesteps, which must be compatible with when fix controller
references the values, or else an error results.  If no bracketed integer
is appended, the scalar calculated by the fix is used.  If a bracketed
integer is appended, the Ith value of the vector calculated by the fix
is used.  Users can also write code for their own fix style and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script.  Only equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables
can be referenced.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for
details.  Note that variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} define a formula which
can reference individual atom properties or thermodynamic keywords, or
they can invoke other computes, fixes, or variables when they are
evaluated, so this is a very general means of specifying the process
variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target value \sphinxstyleemphasis{setpoint} for the process variable must be a numeric
value, in whatever units \sphinxstyleemphasis{pvar} is defined for.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The control variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvar} must be the name of an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} previously defined in the input script.  Note
that it is not specified with a “v\_” prefix, just the name of the
variable.  It must be an internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, because this fix
updates its value directly.  Note that other commands can use an
equal\sphinxhyphen{}style versus internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable interchangeably.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_controller:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, no information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a global vector with 3 values which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The values can be
accessed on any timestep, though they are only updated on timesteps
that are a multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The three values are the most recent updates made to the control
variable by each of the 3 terms in the PID equation above.  The first
value is the proportional term, the second is the integral term, the
third is the derivative term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The units of the vector values will be whatever units the control
variable is in.  The vector values calculated by this fix are
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\section{fix damping/cundall command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:fix-damping-cundall-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damping}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cundall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}l}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damping/cundall = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gamma\_l = linear damping coefficient (dimensionless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gamma\_a = angular damping coefficient (dimensionless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type ratio} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name}
    type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
    ratio = factor to scale the damping coefficients by
    v\_name = reference to atom style variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{name}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damping}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cundall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damping}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cundall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damping}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cundall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}radscale}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add damping force and torque to finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particles in the group
following the model of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:cundall1987}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Cundall, 1987}}}}, as implemented in other
granular physics code (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:yadedem}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Yade\sphinxhyphen{}DEM}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:pfc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{PFC}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The damping is constructed to always have negative mechanical power with respect
to the current velocity/angular velocity to ensure dissipation of kinetic energy.
If used without additional thermostatting (to add kinetic energy to the system),
it has the effect of slowly (or rapidly) freezing the system; hence it can also
be used as a simple energy minimization technique.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The magnitude of the damping force/torque \(F_d\)/\(T_d\) is a fraction
\(\gamma \in [0;1]\) of the current force/torque \(F\)/\(T\) on the
particle. Damping is applied component\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}component in each direction
\(k\in\{x, y, z\}\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{F_d}_k = - \gamma_l \, F_k \, \mathrm{sign}(F_k v_k)\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{T_d}_k = - \gamma_a \, T_k \, \mathrm{sign}(T_k \omega_k)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The larger the coefficients, the faster the kinetic energy is reduced.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} is used, \(\gamma_l\) and \(\gamma_a\)
can be scaled up or down by the specified factor for atoms.  This factor can be
set for different atom types and thus the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} keyword used multiple times
followed by the atom type and the associated scale factor.  Alternately the
scaling factor can be computed for each atom (e.g. based on its radius) by
using an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The damping force/torque is computed based on the force/torque at the moment
this fix is invoked. Any force/torque added after this fix, e.g., by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addtorque::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addtorque}}}}
will not be damped. When performing simulations with gravity, invoking
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gravity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gravity}}}} after this fix will maintain the specified
gravitational acceleration.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This scheme is dependent on the coordinates system and does not correspond to
realistic physical processes. It is constructed for numerical convenience and
efficacy.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This non\sphinxhyphen{}viscous damping presents the following advantages:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damping is independent of velocity, equally damping regions with
distinct natural frequencies,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damping affects acceleration and vanishes for steady uniform motion
of the particles,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damping parameter \(\gamma\) is dimensionless and does not
require scaling.

\end{enumerate}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_damping_cundall:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter
of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is modifying forces/torques.  Default is the outermost
level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces/torques due to this fix are imposed during an energy
minimization, invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.  This
fix should only be used with damped dynamics minimizers that allow for
non\sphinxhyphen{}conservative forces.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}} command
for details.

\section{fix deform command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:fix-deform-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{deform/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{parameter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = perform box deformation every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more parameter/args sequences may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
parameter = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} args = style value(s)
    style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean}
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} values = lo hi
        lo hi = box boundaries at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} values = dlo dhi
        dlo dhi = change in box boundaries at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} values = factor
        factor = multiplicative factor for change in box length at end of run
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} value = V
        V = change box length at this velocity (distance/time units),
            effectively an engineering strain rate
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} value = R
        R = engineering strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} value = R
        R = true strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} value = none = adjust this dim to preserve volume of system
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} values = A Tp
        A = amplitude of oscillation (distance units)
        Tp = period of oscillation (time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} values = v\_name1 v\_name2
        v\_name1 = variable with name1 for box length change as function of time
        v\_name2 = variable with name2 for change rate as function of time

  \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} args = style value
    style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} value = tilt
        tilt = tilt factor at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} value = dtilt
        dtilt = change in tilt factor at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} value = V
        V = change tilt factor at this velocity (distance/time units),
            effectively an engineering shear strain rate
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} value = R
        R = engineering shear strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} value = R
        R = true shear strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} values = A Tp
        A = amplitude of oscillation (distance units)
        Tp = period of oscillation (time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} values = v\_name1 v\_name2
        v\_name1 = variable with name1 for tilt change as function of time
        v\_name2 = variable with name2 for change rate as function of time
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vol/balance/p} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{max/rate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize/pressure}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}
  x = remap coords of atoms in group into deforming box
  v = remap velocities of atoms in group when they cross periodic boundaries
  none = no remapping of x or v
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  allow or disallow box flips when it becomes highly skewed
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  lattice = distances are defined in lattice units
  box = distances are defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{trate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volume}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volume}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the volume and/or shape of the simulation box during a dynamics
run.  Orthogonal simulation boxes have 3 adjustable parameters
(x,y,z).  Triclinic (non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal) simulation boxes have 6
adjustable parameters (x,y,z,xy,xz,yz).  Any or all of them can be
adjusted independently and simultaneously.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform/pressure}}}} command extends
this command with additional keywords and arguments.  The rest of this
page explains the options common to both commands.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
deform/pressure}}}} page explains the options
available ONLY with the fix deform/pressure command.  Note that a
simulation can define only a single deformation command: fix deform or
fix deform/pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both these fixes can be used to perform non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD)
simulations of a continuously strained system.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
nvt/sllod}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}} commands for more details.  Note that
simulation of a continuously extended system (extensional flow) can be
modeled using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-uef}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{UEF package}}}} and its {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
commands}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Inconsistent trajectories due to image flags}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When running long simulations while shearing the box or using a high
shearing rate, it is possible that the image flags used for storing
unwrapped atom positions will “wrap around”.  When LAMMPS is compiled
with the default settings, case image flags are limited to a range of
\(-512 \le i \le 511\), which will overflow when atoms starting
at zero image flag value have passed through a periodic box dimension
more than 512 times.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Changing the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings:size}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{size of LAMMPS integer types}}}} to the
“bigbig” setting can make this overflow much less likely, since it
increases the image flag value range to \(- 1,048,576 \le i \le
1\,048\,575\)
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} parameters, the associated dimension cannot be
shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} parameters, the associated
second dimension cannot be shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped.  Dimensions not varied by
this command can be periodic or non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  Dimensions
corresponding to unspecified parameters can also be controlled by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The size and shape of the simulation box at the beginning of the
simulation run were either specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command used to setup the simulation initially if it
is the first run, or they are the values from the end of the previous
run.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands specify
whether the simulation box is orthogonal or non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal (triclinic)
and explain the meaning of the xy,xz,yz tilt factors.  If fix deform
changes the xy,xz,yz tilt factors, then the simulation box must be
triclinic, even if its initial tilt factors are 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As described below, the desired simulation box size and shape at the
end of the run are determined by the parameters of the fix deform
command.  Every Nth timestep during the run, the simulation box is
expanded, contracted, or tilted to ramped values between the initial
and final values.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} parameters, this is the meaning of their
styles and values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{final}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} styles all change
the specified dimension of the box via “constant displacement” which
is effectively a “constant engineering strain rate”.  This means the
box dimension changes linearly with time from its initial to final
value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{final}, the final lo and hi box boundaries of a dimension
are specified.  The values can be in lattice or box distance units.
See the discussion of the units keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}, plus or minus changes in the lo/hi box boundaries
of a dimension are specified.  The values can be in lattice or box
distance units.  See the discussion of the units keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}, a multiplicative factor to apply to the box length
of a dimension is specified.  For example, if the initial box length
is 10, and the factor is 1.1, then the final box length will be 11.  A
factor less than 1.0 means compression.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}, a velocity at which the box length changes is
specified in units of distance/time.  This is effectively a “constant
engineering strain rate”, where rate = V/L0 and L0 is the initial box
length.  The distance can be in lattice or box distance units.  See
the discussion of the units keyword below.  For example, if the
initial box length is 100 Angstroms, and V is 10 Angstroms/ps, then
after 10 ps, the box length will have doubled.  After 20 ps, it
will have tripled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} style changes a dimension of the box at a “constant
engineering strain rate”.  The units of the specified strain rate are
1/time.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for the time units
associated with different choices of simulation units,
e.g. picoseconds for “metal” units).  Tensile strain is unitless and
is defined as delta/L0, where L0 is the original box length and delta
is the change relative to the original length.  The box length L as a
function of time will change as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
L(t) = L0 (1 + erate*dt)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where dt is the elapsed time (in time units).  Thus if \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} R is
specified as 0.1 and time units are picoseconds, this means the box
length will increase by 10\% of its original length every picosecond.
I.e. strain after 1 ps = 0.1, strain after 2 ps = 0.2, etc.  R =
\sphinxhyphen{}0.01 means the box length will shrink by 1\% of its original length
every picosecond.  Note that for an “engineering” rate the change is
based on the original box length, so running with R = 1 for 10
picoseconds expands the box length by a factor of 11 (strain of 10),
which is different that what the \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} style would induce.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} style changes a dimension of the box at a “constant true
strain rate”.  Note that this is not an “engineering strain rate”, as
the other styles are.  Rather, for a “true” rate, the rate of change
is constant, which means the box dimension changes non\sphinxhyphen{}linearly with
time from its initial to final value.  The units of the specified
strain rate are 1/time.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for the
time units associated with different choices of simulation units,
e.g. picoseconds for “metal” units).  Tensile strain is unitless and
is defined as delta/L0, where L0 is the original box length and delta
is the change relative to the original length.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The box length L as a function of time will change as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
L(t) = L0 exp(trate*dt)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where dt is the elapsed time (in time units).  Thus if \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} R is
specified as ln(1.1) and time units are picoseconds, this means the
box length will increase by 10\% of its current (not original) length
every picosecond.  I.e. strain after 1 ps = 0.1, strain after 2 ps
= 0.21, etc.  R = ln(2) or ln(3) means the box length will double or
triple every picosecond.  R = ln(0.99) means the box length will
shrink by 1\% of its current length every picosecond.  Note that for a
“true” rate the change is continuous and based on the current length,
so running with R = ln(2) for 10 picoseconds does not expand the box
length by a factor of 11 as it would with \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate}, but by a factor of
1024 since the box length will double every picosecond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that to change the volume (or cross\sphinxhyphen{}sectional area) of the
simulation box at a constant rate, you can change multiple dimensions
via \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate}.  E.g. to double the box volume in a picosecond
picosecond, you could set “x erate M”, “y erate M”, “z erate M”, with
M = pow(2,1/3) \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = 0.26, since if each box dimension grows by 26\%,
the box volume doubles.  Or you could set “x trate M”, “y trate M”, “z
trate M”, with M = ln(1.26) = 0.231, and the box volume would double
every picosecond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} style changes the specified dimension in such a way that
the box volume remains constant while other box dimensions are changed
explicitly via the styles discussed above.  For example, “x scale 1.1
y scale 1.1 z volume” will shrink the z box length as the x,y box
lengths increase, to keep the volume constant (product of x,y,z
lengths).  If “x scale 1.1 z volume” is specified and parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} is
unspecified, then the z box length will shrink as x increases to keep
the product of x,z lengths constant.  If “x scale 1.1 y volume z
volume” is specified, then both the y,z box lengths will shrink as x
increases to keep the volume constant (product of x,y,z lengths).  In
this case, the y,z box lengths shrink so as to keep their relative
aspect ratio constant.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For solids or liquids, note that when one dimension of the box is
expanded via fix deform (i.e. tensile strain), it may be physically
undesirable to hold the other 2 box lengths constant (unspecified by
fix deform) since that implies a density change.  Using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume}
style for those 2 dimensions to keep the box volume constant may make
more physical sense, but may also not be correct for materials and
potentials whose Poisson ratio is not 0.5.  An alternative is to use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt aniso}}}} with zero applied pressure on those 2
dimensions, so that they respond to the tensile strain dynamically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style oscillates the specified box length dimension
sinusoidally with the specified amplitude and period.  I.e. the box
length L as a function of time is given by
\begin{sphinxalltt}
L(t) = L0 + A sin(2*pi t/Tp)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where L0 is its initial length.  If the amplitude A is a positive
number the box initially expands, then contracts, etc.  If A is
negative then the box initially contracts, then expands, etc.  The
amplitude can be in lattice or box distance units.  See the discussion
of the units keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style changes the specified box length dimension by
evaluating a variable, which presumably is a function of time.  The
variable with \sphinxstyleemphasis{name1} must be an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} and should calculate a change in box length in units of
distance.  Note that this distance is in box units, not lattice units;
see the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword below.  The formula
associated with variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{name1} can reference the current timestep.
Note that it should return the “change” in box length, not the
absolute box length.  This means it should evaluate to 0.0 when
invoked on the initial timestep of the run following the definition of
fix deform.  It should evaluate to a value \textgreater{} 0.0 to dilate the box at
future times, or a value \textless{} 0.0 to compress the box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{name2} must also be an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} and should calculate the rate of box length change, in
units of distance/time, i.e. the time\sphinxhyphen{}derivative of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{name1}
variable.  This quantity is used internally by LAMMPS to reset atom
velocities when they cross periodic boundaries.  It is computed
internally for the other styles, but you must provide it when using an
arbitrary variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style to perform the same
box deformation as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style formula listed above, where we
assume that the current timestep = 0.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Tp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{displace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}A * sin(2*PI * step*dt/v\PYGZus{}Tp)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{rate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2*PI*v\PYGZus{}A/v\PYGZus{}Tp * cos(2*PI * step*dt/v\PYGZus{}Tp)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}displace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} styles, the box length is expanded or compressed around its
mid point.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} parameters, this is the meaning of their
styles and values.  Note that changing the tilt factors of a triclinic
box does not change its volume.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{final}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} styles all change the shear
strain at a “constant engineering shear strain rate”.  This means the
tilt factor changes linearly with time from its initial to final
value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{final}, the final tilt factor is specified.  The value
can be in lattice or box distance units.  See the discussion of the
units keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}, a plus or minus change in the tilt factor is
specified.  The value can be in lattice or box distance units.  See
the discussion of the units keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}, a velocity at which the tilt factor changes is
specified in units of distance/time.  This is effectively an
“engineering shear strain rate”, where rate = V/L0 and L0 is the
initial box length perpendicular to the direction of shear.  The
distance can be in lattice or box distance units.  See the discussion
of the units keyword below.  For example, if the initial tilt factor
is 5 Angstroms, and the V is 10 Angstroms/ps, then after 1 ps, the
tilt factor will be 15 Angstroms.  After 2 ps, it will be 25
Angstroms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} style changes a tilt factor at a “constant engineering
shear strain rate”.  The units of the specified shear strain rate are
1/time.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for the time units
associated with different choices of simulation units,
e.g. picoseconds for “metal” units).  Shear strain is unitless and is
defined as offset/length, where length is the box length perpendicular
to the shear direction (e.g. y box length for xy deformation) and
offset is the displacement distance in the shear direction (e.g. x
direction for xy deformation) from the unstrained orientation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The tilt factor T as a function of time will change as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
T(t) = T0 + L0*erate*dt
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where T0 is the initial tilt factor, L0 is the original length of the
box perpendicular to the shear direction (e.g. y box length for xy
deformation), and dt is the elapsed time (in time units).  Thus if
\sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} R is specified as 0.1 and time units are picoseconds, this
means the shear strain will increase by 0.1 every picosecond.  I.e. if
the xy shear strain was initially 0.0, then strain after 1 ps = 0.1,
strain after 2 ps = 0.2, etc.  Thus the tilt factor would be 0.0 at
time 0, 0.1*ybox at 1 ps, 0.2*ybox at 2 ps, etc, where ybox is the
original y box length.  R = 1 or 2 means the tilt factor will increase
by 1 or 2 every picosecond.  R = \sphinxhyphen{}0.01 means a decrease in shear
strain by 0.01 every picosecond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} style changes a tilt factor at a “constant true shear
strain rate”.  Note that this is not an “engineering shear strain
rate”, as the other styles are.  Rather, for a “true” rate, the rate
of change is constant, which means the tilt factor changes
non\sphinxhyphen{}linearly with time from its initial to final value.  The units of
the specified shear strain rate are 1/time.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for the time units associated with
different choices of simulation units, e.g. picoseconds for “metal”
units).  Shear strain is unitless and is defined as offset/length,
where length is the box length perpendicular to the shear direction
(e.g. y box length for xy deformation) and offset is the displacement
distance in the shear direction (e.g. x direction for xy deformation)
from the unstrained orientation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The tilt factor T as a function of time will change as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
T(t) = T0 exp(trate*dt)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where T0 is the initial tilt factor and dt is the elapsed time (in
time units).  Thus if \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} R is specified as ln(1.1) and time units
are picoseconds, this means the shear strain or tilt factor will
increase by 10\% every picosecond.  I.e. if the xy shear strain was
initially 0.1, then strain after 1 ps = 0.11, strain after 2 ps =
0.121, etc.  R = ln(2) or ln(3) means the tilt factor will double or
triple every picosecond.  R = ln(0.99) means the tilt factor will
shrink by 1\% every picosecond.  Note that the change is continuous, so
running with R = ln(2) for 10 picoseconds does not change the tilt
factor by a factor of 10, but by a factor of 1024 since it doubles
every picosecond.  Note that the initial tilt factor must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero
to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that shear strain is defined as the tilt factor divided by the
perpendicular box length.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} styles control the
tilt factor, but assume the perpendicular box length remains constant.
If this is not the case (e.g. it changes due to another fix deform
parameter), then this effect on the shear strain is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style oscillates the specified tilt factor sinusoidally
with the specified amplitude and period.  I.e. the tilt factor T as a
function of time is given by
\begin{sphinxalltt}
T(t) = T0 + A sin(2*pi t/Tp)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where T0 is its initial value.  If the amplitude A is a positive
number the tilt factor initially becomes more positive, then more
negative, etc.  If A is negative then the tilt factor initially
becomes more negative, then more positive, etc.  The amplitude can be
in lattice or box distance units.  See the discussion of the units
keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style changes the specified tilt factor by evaluating a
variable, which presumably is a function of time.  The variable with
\sphinxstyleemphasis{name1} must be an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} and should
calculate a change in tilt in units of distance.  Note that this
distance is in box units, not lattice units; see the discussion of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword below.  The formula associated with variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{name1}
can reference the current timestep.  Note that it should return the
“change” in tilt factor, not the absolute tilt factor.  This means it
should evaluate to 0.0 when invoked on the initial timestep of the run
following the definition of fix deform.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{name2} must also be an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} and should calculate the rate of tilt change, in units of
distance/time, i.e. the time\sphinxhyphen{}derivative of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{name1} variable.  This
quantity is used internally by LAMMPS to reset atom velocities when
they cross periodic boundaries.  It is computed internally for the
other styles, but you must provide it when using an arbitrary
variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style to perform the same
box deformation as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style formula listed above, where we
assume that the current timestep = 0.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Tp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{displace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}A * sin(2*PI * step*dt/v\PYGZus{}Tp)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{rate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2*PI*v\PYGZus{}A/v\PYGZus{}Tp * cos(2*PI * step*dt/v\PYGZus{}Tp)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}displace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the tilt styles change the xy, xz, yz tilt factors during a
simulation.  In LAMMPS, tilt factors (xy,xz,yz) for triclinic boxes
are normally bounded by half the distance of the parallel box length.
See the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword below, to allow this bound to
be exceeded, if desired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if xlo = 2 and xhi = 12, then the x box length is 10 and
the xy tilt factor must be between \sphinxhyphen{}5 and 5.  Similarly, both xz and
yz must be between \sphinxhyphen{}(xhi\sphinxhyphen{}xlo)/2 and +(yhi\sphinxhyphen{}ylo)/2.  Note that this is
not a limitation, since if the maximum tilt factor is 5 (as in this
example), then configurations with tilt = …, \sphinxhyphen{}15, \sphinxhyphen{}5, 5, 15, 25,
… are all equivalent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To obey this constraint and allow for large shear deformations to be
applied via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} parameters, the following
algorithm is used.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{prd} is the associated parallel box length (10
in the example above), then if the tilt factor exceeds the accepted
range of \sphinxhyphen{}5 to 5 during the simulation, then the box is flipped to the
other limit (an equivalent box) and the simulation continues.  Thus
for this example, if the initial xy tilt factor was 0.0 and “xy final
100.0” was specified, then during the simulation the xy tilt factor
would increase from 0.0 to 5.0, the box would be flipped so that the
tilt factor becomes \sphinxhyphen{}5.0, the tilt factor would increase from \sphinxhyphen{}5.0 to
5.0, the box would be flipped again, etc.  The flip occurs 10 times
and the final tilt factor at the end of the simulation would be 0.0.
During each flip event, atoms are remapped into the new box in the
appropriate manner.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The one exception to this rule is if the first dimension in the tilt
factor (x for xy) is non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  In that case, the limits on the
tilt factor are not enforced, since flipping the box in that dimension
does not change the atom positions due to non\sphinxhyphen{}periodicity.  In this
mode, if you tilt the system to extreme angles, the simulation will
simply become inefficient due to the highly skewed simulation box.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Each time the box size or shape is changed, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} keyword
determines whether atom positions are remapped to the new box.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} (the default), atoms in the fix group are
remapped; otherwise they are not.  Note that their velocities are not
changed, just their positions are altered.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{v},
then any atom in the fix group that crosses a periodic boundary will
have a delta added to its velocity equal to the difference in
velocities between the lo and hi boundaries.  Note that this velocity
difference can include tilt components, e.g. a delta in the x velocity
when an atom crosses the y periodic boundary.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} is set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{none}, then neither of these remappings take place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Conceptually, setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} forces the atoms to deform via an
affine transformation that exactly matches the box deformation.  This
setting is typically appropriate for solids.  Note that though the
atoms are effectively “moving” with the box over time, it is not due
to their having a velocity that tracks the box change, but only due to
the remapping.  By contrast, setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{v} is typically
appropriate for fluids, where you want the atoms to respond to the
change in box size/shape on their own and acquire a velocity that
matches the box change, so that their motion will naturally track the
box without explicit remapping of their coordinates.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD) simulations are performed using
this fix, the option “remap v” should normally be used.  This is
because {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}} adjusts the atom positions
and velocities to induce a velocity profile that matches the changing
box size/shape.  Thus atom coordinates should NOT be remapped by fix
deform, but velocities SHOULD be when atoms cross periodic boundaries,
since that is consistent with maintaining the velocity profile already
created by fix nvt/sllod.  LAMMPS will warn you if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} setting
is not consistent with fix nvt/sllod.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD) simulations using “remap v” it is
usually desirable that the fluid (or flowing material,
e.g. granular particles) stream with a velocity profile consistent
with the deforming box.  As mentioned above, using a thermostat
such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lavgevin}}}} (with a bias provided by {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}}), will typically accomplish that.  If you do
not use a thermostat, then there is no driving force pushing the
atoms to flow in a manner consistent with the deforming box.
E.g. for a shearing system the box deformation velocity may vary
from 0 at the bottom to 10 at the top of the box.  But the stream
velocity profile of the atoms may vary from \sphinxhyphen{}5 at the bottom to +5
at the top.  You can monitor these effects using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
ave/chunk}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/profile}}}} commands.  One way to induce atoms to
stream consistent with the box deformation is to give them an
initial velocity profile, via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity ramp}}}}
command, that matches the box deformation rate.  This also
typically helps the system come to equilibrium more quickly, even
if a thermostat is used.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}} is defined for rigid bodies, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, then the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass coordinates of rigid
bodies will be remapped to the changing simulation box.  This will
be done regardless of whether atoms in the rigid bodies are in the
fix deform group or not.  The velocity of the centers of mass are
not remapped even if \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{v}, since {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
nvt/sllod}}}} does not currently do anything special
for rigid particles.  If you wish to perform a NEMD simulation of
rigid particles, you can either thermostat them independently or
include a background fluid and thermostat the fluid via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
nvt/sllod}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword allows the tilt factors for a triclinic box to
exceed half the distance of the parallel box length, as discussed
above.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the bound is enforced by
flipping the box when it is exceeded.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, the tilt will continue to change without flipping.  Note that if
you apply large deformations, this means the box shape can tilt
dramatically LAMMPS will run less efficiently, due to the large volume
of communication needed to acquire ghost atoms around a processor’s
irregular\sphinxhyphen{}shaped subdomain.  For extreme values of tilt, LAMMPS may
also lose atoms and generate an error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define various arguments.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance
units as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command, e.g. Angstroms for
units = real or metal.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are
in lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have
been previously used to define the lattice spacing.  Note that the
units choice also affects the \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} style parameters since it is
defined in terms of distance/time.  Also note that the units keyword
does not affect the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style.  You should use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlat},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ylat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlat} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
command if you want to include lattice spacings in a variable formula.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix will restore the initial box settings from {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}, which allows the fix to be properly continue
deformation, when using the start/stop options of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by
this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can perform deformation over multiple runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot apply x, y, or z deformations to a dimension that is
shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot apply xy, yz, or xz deformations to a second dimension (y
in xy) that is shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}}
command.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform/pressure}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{change_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{change\_box}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are remap = x, flip = yes, and units = lattice.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix deform/pressure@\spxentry{fix deform/pressure}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix deform/pressure command}
