\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:fix-deform-pressure-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID deform/pressure N parameter style args ... keyword value ...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
deform/pressure = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = perform box deformation every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more parameter/args sequences may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
parameter = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} args = style value(s)
    style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean}
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} values = lo hi
        lo hi = box boundaries at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} values = dlo dhi
        dlo dhi = change in box boundaries at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} values = factor
        factor = multiplicative factor for change in box length at end of run
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} value = V
        V = change box length at this velocity (distance/time units),
            effectively an engineering strain rate
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} value = R
        R = engineering strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} value = R
        R = true strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} value = none = adjust this dim to preserve volume of system
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} values = A Tp
        A = amplitude of oscillation (distance units)
        Tp = period of oscillation (time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} values = v\_name1 v\_name2
        v\_name1 = variable with name1 for box length change as function of time
        v\_name2 = variable with name2 for change rate as function of time
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} values = target gain
        target = target pressure (pressure units)
        gain = proportional gain constant (1/(time * pressure) or 1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} values = target gain
        target = target pressure (pressure units)
        gain = proportional gain constant (1/(time * pressure) or 1/time units)

  \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} args = style value
    style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate/rescale}
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{final} value = tilt
        tilt = tilt factor at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} value = dtilt
        dtilt = change in tilt factor at end of run (distance units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} value = V
        V = change tilt factor at this velocity (distance/time units),
            effectively an engineering shear strain rate
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} value = R
        R = engineering shear strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate/rescale} value = R
        R = engineering shear strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} value = R
        R = true shear strain rate (1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} values = A Tp
        A = amplitude of oscillation (distance units)
        Tp = period of oscillation (time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} values = v\_name1 v\_name2
        v\_name1 = variable with name1 for tilt change as function of time
        v\_name2 = variable with name2 for change rate as function of time
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} values = target gain
        target = target pressure (pressure units)
        gain = proportional gain constant (1/(time * pressure) or 1/time units)
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate/rescale} value = R
        R = engineering shear strain rate (1/time units)

  \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} = style value
    style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure}
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} value = none = isotropically adjust system to preserve volume of system
      \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} values = target gain
        target = target mean pressure (pressure units)
        gain = proportional gain constant (1/(time * pressure) or 1/time units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vol/balance/p} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{max/rate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize/pressure}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{remap} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}
  x = remap coords of atoms in group into deforming box
  v = remap velocities of atoms in group when they cross periodic boundaries
  none = no remapping of x or v
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  allow or disallow box flips when it becomes highly skewed
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  lattice = distances are defined in lattice units
  box = distances are defined in simulation box units
\sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
  couple pressure values of various dimensions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vol/balance/p} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  Modifies the behavior of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} option to try and balance pressures
\sphinxstyleemphasis{max/rate} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate}
  rate = maximum strain rate for pressure control
\sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize/pressure} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  Modifies pressure controls such that the deviation in pressure is normalized by the target pressure
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{trate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volume}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volume}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vol}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{balance}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deform}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{trate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is an extension of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}
command, which allows all of its options to be used as well as new
pressure\sphinxhyphen{}based controls implemented by this command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All arguments described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} doc page
also apply to this fix unless otherwise noted below.  The rest of this
page explains the arguments specific to this fix only.  Note that a
simulation can define only a single deformation command: fix deform or
fix deform/pressure.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Inconsistent trajectories due to image flags}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When running long simulations while shearing the box or using a high
shearing rate, it is possible that the image flags used for storing
unwrapped atom positions will “wrap around”.  When LAMMPS is compiled
with the default settings, case image flags are limited to a range of
\(-512 \le i \le 511\), which will overflow when atoms starting
at zero image flag value have passed through a periodic box dimension
more than 512 times.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Changing the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings:size}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{size of LAMMPS integer types}}}} to the
“bigbig” setting can make this overflow much less likely, since it
increases the image flag value range to \(- 1,048,576 \le i \le
1\,048\,575\)
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} parameters, this is the meaning of the
styles and values provided by this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} style adjusts a dimension’s box length to control the
corresponding component of the pressure tensor. This option attempts to
maintain a specified target pressure using a linear controller where the
box length \(L\) evolves according to the equation
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{d L(t)}{dt} = L(t) k (P_t - P)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k\) is a proportional gain constant, \(P_t\) is the target
pressure, and \(P\) is the current pressure along that dimension. This
approach is similar to the method used to control the pressure by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_press_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix press/berendsen}}}}. The target pressure
accepts either a constant numeric value or a LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output:variable}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{variable}}}}.
Notably, this variable can be a function of time or other components of
the pressure tensor. By default, \(k\) has units of 1/(time * pressure)
although this will change if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize/pressure} option is set as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-normalize}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{discussed below}}}}. There is no proven method
to choosing an appropriate value of \(k\) as it will depend on the
specific details of a simulation. Testing different values is recommended.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, there is no limit on the resulting strain rate in any dimension.
A maximum limit can be applied using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-max-rate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{max/rate}}}}
option. Akin to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt and nph}}}}, pressures in different
dimensions can be coupled using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-couple}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{couple}}}} option.
This means the instantaneous pressure along coupled dimensions are averaged
and the box strains identically along the coupled dimensions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} style changes a dimension’s box length to maintain
a constant mean pressure defined as the trace of the pressure tensor.
This option has identical arguments to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} style and a similar
functional equation, except the current and target pressures refer to the
mean trace of the pressure tensor. All options for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} style
also apply to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} style except for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-couple}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{couple}}}} option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that while this style can be identical to coupled \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} styles,
it is generally not the same. For instance in 2D, a coupled \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure}
style in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} dimensions would be equivalent to using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} style with identical settings in each dimension. However,
it would not be the same if settings (e.g. gain constants) were used in
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} dimensions or if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} command was only applied
along one dimension.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} parameters, this is the meaning of the
styles and values provided by this fix.  Note that changing the
tilt factors of a triclinic box does not change its volume.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} style adjusts a tilt factor to control the corresponding
off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal component of the pressure tensor. This option attempts to
maintain a specified target value using a linear controller where the
tilt factor T evolves according to the equation
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{d T(t)}{dt} = L(t) k (P - P_t)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k\) is a proportional gain constant, \(P_t\) is the
target pressure, \(P\) is the current pressure, and \(L\) is
the perpendicular box length. The target pressure accepts either a
constant numeric value or a LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output:variable}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{variable}}}}. Notably, this variable can be a function of time or other
components of the pressure tensor. By default, \(k\) has units of
1/(time * pressure) although this will change if the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize/pessure} option is set as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-normalize}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{discussed below}}}}.  There is no proven method to choosing an
appropriate value of \(k\) as it will depend on the specific
details of a simulation and testing different values is
recommended. One can also apply a maximum limit to the magnitude of
the applied strain using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-max-rate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{max/rate}}}} option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate/rescale} style operates similarly to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} style with
a specified strain rate in units of 1/time. The difference is that
the change in the tilt factor will depend on the current length of
the box perpendicular to the shear direction, \sphinxstyleemphasis{L}, instead of the
original length, \sphinxstyleemphasis{L0}. The tilt factor T as a function of time will
change as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T(t) = T(t-1) + L \cdot \mathrm{erate} \cdot \Delta t\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where T(t\sphinxhyphen{}1) is the tilt factor on the previous timestep and
\(\Delta t\) is the timestep size. This option may be useful
in scenarios where \sphinxstyleemphasis{L} changes in time.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} parameter provides an additional control over the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} box lengths by isotropically dilating or contracting the box
to either maintain a fixed mean pressure or volume. This isotropic
scaling is applied after the box is deformed by the above \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} styles, acting as a second deformation
step. This parameter will change the overall strain rate in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions.  This parameter can only be used in
combination with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} commands: \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{trate}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle}. This is the meaning of its styles
and values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} style isotropically scales box lengths to maintain a constant
box volume in response to deformation from other parameters. This style
may be useful in scenarios where one wants to apply a constant deviatoric
pressure using \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} styles in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions (
deforming the shape of the box), while maintaining a constant volume.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} style isotropically scales box lengths in an attempt to
maintain a target mean pressure (the trace of the pressure tensor) of the
system. This is accomplished by isotropically scaling all box lengths
\(L\) by an additional factor of \(k (P_t - P_m)\) where \(k\)
is the proportional gain constant, \(P_t\) is the target pressure, and
\(P_m\) is the current mean pressure. This style may be useful in
scenarios where one wants to apply a constant deviatoric strain rate
using various strain\sphinxhyphen{}based styles (e.g. \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate}) along the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
dimensions (deforming the shape of the box), while maintaining a mean pressure.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional keywords provided by this fix are described below.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-normalize}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize/pressure} keyword changes how box dimensions evolve when
using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} deformation styles. If the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{deform/normalize} value is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the deviation from the
target pressure is normalized by the absolute value of the target
pressure such that the proportional gain constant scales a percentage
error and has units of 1/time. If the target pressure is ever zero, this
will produce an error unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{max/rate} keyword is defined,
described below, which will cap the divergence.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-max-rate}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{max/rate} keyword sets an upper threshold, \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate}, that limits the
maximum magnitude of the instantaneous strain rate applied in any dimension.
This keyword only applies to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/mean} options. If
a pressure\sphinxhyphen{}controlled rate is used for both \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} and either \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, then this threshold will apply separately to each individual controller
such that the cumulative strain rate on a box dimension may be up to twice
the value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate}.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-couple}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keyword allows two or three of the diagonal components of
the pressure tensor to be “coupled” together for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} option.
The value specified with the keyword determines which are coupled. For
example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the stress tensor
are coupled. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Xyz} means all 3 diagonal components are coupled. Coupling
means two things: the instantaneous stress will be computed as an average
of the corresponding diagonal components, and the coupled box dimensions
will be changed together in lockstep, meaning coupled dimensions will be
dilated or contracted by the same percentage every timestep. If a \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure}
style is defined for more than one coupled dimension, the target pressures
and gain constants must be identical. Alternatively, if a \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure}
style is only defined for one of the coupled dimensions, its settings are
copied to other dimensions with undefined styles. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Couple xyz} can be used
for a 2d simulation; the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimension is simply ignored.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:deform-balance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vol/balance/p} keyword modifies the behavior of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} style when
applied to two of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions. Instead of straining
the two dimensions in lockstep, the two dimensions are allowed to
separately dilate or contract in a manner to maintain a constant
volume while simultaneously trying to keep the pressure along each
dimension equal using a method described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:huang2014}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Huang2014)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If any pressure controls are used, this fix computes a temperature and
pressure each timestep. To do this, the fix creates its own computes
of style “temp” and “pressure”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the IDs of the
new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is the same
as the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the
attributes of this fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this
temperature or pressure during thermodynamic output via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the
appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID. It also means that changing attributes of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix will restore the initial box settings from {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}, which allows the fix to be properly continue
deformation, when using the start/stop options of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If any pressure controls are used, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are supported by this fix, unlike in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be
used in its temperature and pressure calculations.  If you do this,
note that the kinetic energy derived from the compute temperature
should be consistent with the virial term computed using all atoms for
the pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to compute
temperature on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can perform deformation over multiple runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot apply x, y, or z deformations to a dimension that is
shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot apply xy, yz, or xz deformations to a second dimension (y
in xy) that is shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}}
command.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{change_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{change\_box}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are normalize/pressure = no.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_deform_pressure:huang2014}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Huang2014)} X. Huang, “Exploring critical\sphinxhyphen{}state behavior using DEM”, Doctoral dissertation, Imperial College. (2014). \sphinxurl{https://doi.org/10.25560/25316}

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix deposit@\spxentry{fix deposit}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix deposit command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:fix-deposit-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deposit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
deposit = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = \# of atoms or molecules to insert

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label) to assign to inserted atoms (offset for molecule insertion)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
M = insert a single atom or molecule every M steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{global} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{near} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{attempt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{target} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfrac} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{shake} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{orient} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region to use as insertion volume
\sphinxstyleemphasis{var} value = name = variable name to evaluate for test of atom creation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{set} values = dim name
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
  name = name of variable to set with x, y, or z atom position
\sphinxstyleemphasis{id} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{next}
  max = atom ID for new atom(s) is max ID of all current atoms plus one
  next = atom ID for new atom(s) increments by one for every deposition
\sphinxstyleemphasis{global} values = lo hi
  lo,hi = put new atom/molecule a distance lo\sphinxhyphen{}hi above all other atoms (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{local} values = lo hi delta
  lo,hi = put new atom/molecule a distance lo\sphinxhyphen{}hi above any nearby atom beneath it (distance units)
  delta = lateral distance within which a neighbor is considered "nearby" (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{near} value = R
  R = only insert atom/molecule if further than R from existing particles (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} values = xmid ymid zmid sigma
  xmid,ymid,zmid = center of the gaussian distribution (distance units)
  sigma = width of gaussian distribution (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{attempt} value = Q
  Q = attempt a single insertion up to Q times
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rate} value = V
  V = z velocity (y in 2d) at which insertion volume moves (velocity units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vx} values = vxlo vxhi
  vxlo,vxhi = range of x velocities for inserted atom/molecule (velocity units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vy} values = vylo vyhi
  vylo,vyhi = range of y velocities for inserted atom/molecule (velocity units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} values = vzlo vzhi
  vzlo,vzhi = range of z velocities for inserted atom/molecule (velocity units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{target} values = tx ty tz
  tx,ty,tz = location of target point (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} value = template\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  template\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of molecule template specified in a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command
\sphinxstyleemphasis{molfrac} values = f1 f2 ... fN
  f1 to fN = relative probability of creating each of N molecules in template\sphinxhyphen{}ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} value = fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small}}}} command
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shake} value = fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} command
\sphinxstyleemphasis{orient} values = rx ry rz
  rx,ry,rz = vector to randomly rotate an inserted molecule around
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  lattice = the geometry is defined in lattice units
  box = the geometry is defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deposit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{29494}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myblock}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{newatoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deposit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12345}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{disk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{near}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.8}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sputter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deposit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12235}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{insert}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deposit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{777}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{disk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Au}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sputter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deposit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Au}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12235}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Insert a single atom or molecule into the simulation domain every M
timesteps until N atoms or molecules have been inserted.  This is
useful for simulating deposition onto a surface.  For the remainder of
this doc page, a single inserted atom or molecule is referred to as a
“particle”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If inserted particles are individual atoms, they are assigned the
specified atom type.  If they are molecules, the type of each atom in
the inserted molecule is specified in the file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command, and those values are added to the
specified atom type.  E.g. if the file specifies atom types 1,2,3, and
those are the atom types you want for inserted molecules, then specify
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = 0.  If you specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = 2, the in the inserted molecule
will have atom types 3,4,5.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All atoms in the inserted particle are assigned to two groups: the
default group “all” and the group specified in the fix deposit command
(which can also be “all”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are computing temperature values which include inserted
particles, you will want to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify dynamic/dof yes}}}} option, which ensures the current number of atoms is
used as a normalizing factor each time the temperature is computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Care must be taken that inserted particles are not too near existing
atoms, using the options described below.  When inserting particles
above a surface in a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic box (see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command), the possibility of a particle
escaping the surface and flying upward should be considered, since the
particle may be lost or the box size may grow infinitely large.  A
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/reflect}}}} command can be used to
prevent this behavior.  Note that if a shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrap boundary is used,
it is OK to insert the new particle outside the box, however the box
will immediately be expanded to include the new particle. When
simulating a sputtering experiment it is probably more realistic to
ignore those atoms using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}}
command with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lost ignore} option and a fixed
{\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix deposit command must use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword to define an
insertion volume.  The specified region must have been previously
defined with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  It must be defined with
side = \sphinxstyleemphasis{in}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS checks that the specified region is wholly inside the
simulation box.  It can do this correctly for orthonormal simulation
boxes.  However for {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{triclinic boxes}}}}, it only
tests against the larger orthonormal box that bounds the tilted
simulation box.  If the specified region includes volume outside the
tilted box, then an insertion will likely fail, leading to a “lost
atoms” error.  Thus for triclinic boxes you should ensure the
specified region is wholly inside the simulation box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The locations of inserted particles are taken from uniform distributed
random numbers, unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} keyword is used. Then the
individual coordinates are taken from a gaussian distribution of
width \sphinxstyleemphasis{sigma} centered on \sphinxstyleemphasis{xmid,ymid,zmid}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Individual atoms are inserted, unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used.  It
specifies a \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}ID} previously defined using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command, which reads files that define one or
more molecules.  The coordinates, atom types, charges, etc, as well as
any bond/angle/etc and special neighbor information for the molecule
can be specified in the molecule file.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command for details.  The only settings
required to be in each file are the coordinates and types of atoms in
the molecule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the molecule template contains more than one molecule, the relative
probability of depositing each molecule can be specified by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{molfrac} keyword.  N relative probabilities, each from 0.0 to 1.0, are
specified, where N is the number of molecules in the template.  Each
time a molecule is deposited, a random number is used to sample from
the list of relative probabilities.  The N values must sum to 1.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to insert molecules via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword, that will be
treated as rigid bodies, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} keyword, specifying as its
value the ID of a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small}}}}
command which also appears in your input script.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish the new rigid molecules (and other rigid molecules) to be
thermostatted correctly via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small/nvt}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small/npt}}}}, then you need to use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify dynamic/dof yes}}}} command for the rigid
fix.  This is to inform that fix that the molecule count will vary
dynamically.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to insert molecules via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword, that will have
their bonds or angles constrained via SHAKE, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shake} keyword,
specifying as its value the ID of a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} command which also appears in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each timestep a particle is inserted, the coordinates for its atoms
are chosen as follows.  For insertion of individual atoms, the
“position” referred to in the following description is the coordinate
of the atom.  For insertion of molecule, the “position” is the
geometric center of the molecule; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} doc
page for details.  A random rotation of the molecule around its center
point is performed, which determines the coordinates all the
individual atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A random position within the region insertion volume is generated.  If
neither the \sphinxstyleemphasis{global} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} keyword is used, the random position
is the trial position.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{global} keyword is used, the random
x,y values are used, but the z position of the new particle is set
above the highest current atom in the simulation by a distance
randomly chosen between lo/hi.  (For a 2d simulation, this is done for
the y position.)  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} keyword is used, the z position is
set a distance between lo/hi above the highest current atom in the
simulation that is “nearby” the chosen x,y position.  In this context,
“nearby” means the lateral distance (in x,y) between the new and old
particles is less than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Once a trial x,y,z position has been selected, the insertion is only
performed if both the \sphinxstyleemphasis{near} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} keywords are satisfied (see below).
If either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{near} or the \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} keyword is not satisfied, a new random
position within the insertion volume is chosen and another trial is made.
Up to Q attempts are made.  If one or more particle insertions are not
successful, LAMMPS prints a warning message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{near} keyword ensures that no current atom in the simulation is within
a distance R of any atom in the new particle, including the effect of
periodic boundary conditions if applicable.  Note that the default value
for R is 0.0, which will allow atoms to strongly overlap if you are
inserting where other atoms are present.  This distance test is performed
independently for each atom in an inserted molecule, based on the randomly
rotated configuration of the molecule.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are inserting finite size particles or a molecule or
rigid body consisting of finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles, then you should
typically set R larger than the distance at which any inserted
particle may overlap with either a previously inserted particle or an
existing particle.  LAMMPS will issue a warning if R is smaller than
this value, based on the radii of existing and inserted particles.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 21Nov2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} keywords can be used together to provide a criterion
for accepting or rejecting the addition of an individual atom, based on its
coordinates.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} keyword is the name of an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} that should evaluate to a zero or
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value based on one or two or three variables that will store the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} coordinates of an atom (one variable per coordinate).  If
used, these other variables must be {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}} defined in the input script; their initial numeric value can be
anything. They must be internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables, because this command
resets their values directly.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} keyword is used to identify the
names of these other variables, one variable for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate of a
created atom, one for \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and one for \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}.  When an atom is created, its
\((x,y,z)\) coordinates become the values for any \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} variable that
is defined.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{var} variable is then evaluated.  If the returned value
is 0.0, the atom is not created.  If it is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, the atom is created.
For an example of how to use these keywords, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rate} option moves the insertion volume in the z direction (3d)
or y direction (2d).  This enables particles to be inserted from a
successively higher height over time.  Note that this parameter is
ignored if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{global} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} keywords are used, since those
options choose a z\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate for insertion independently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vx, vy, and vz components of velocity for the inserted particle
are set by sampling a uniform distribution between the bounds set by
the values specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz} keywords. Note that
normally, new particles should be a assigned a negative vertical
velocity so that they move towards the surface.  For molecules, the
same velocity is given to every particle (no rotation or bond vibration).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{target} option is used, the velocity vector of the inserted
particle is changed so that it points from the insertion position
towards the specified target point.  The magnitude of the velocity is
unchanged.  This can be useful, for example, for simulating a
sputtering process.  E.g. the target point can be far away, so that
all incident particles strike the surface as if they are in an
incident beam of particles at a prescribed angle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{orient} keyword is only used when molecules are deposited.  By
default, each molecule is inserted at a random orientation.  If this
keyword is specified, then (rx,ry,rz) is used as an orientation
vector, and each inserted molecule is rotated around that vector with
a random value from zero to 2*PI.  For a 2d simulation, rx = ry = 0.0
is required, since rotations can only be performed around the z axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} keyword determines how atom IDs and molecule IDs are assigned
to newly deposited particles.  Molecule IDs are only assigned if
molecules are being inserted.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} setting, the atom and
molecule IDs of all current atoms are checked.  Atoms in the new
particle are assigned IDs starting with the current maximum plus one.
If a molecule is inserted it is assigned an ID = current maximum plus
one.  This means that if particles leave the system, the new IDs may
replace the lost ones.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{next} setting, the maximum ID of any
atom and molecule is stored at the time the fix is defined.  Each time
a new particle is added, this value is incremented to assign IDs to
the new atom(s) or molecule.  Thus atom and molecule IDs for deposited
particles will be consecutive even if particles leave the system over
time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
for the other deposition parameters.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard
distance units as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command,
e.g. Angstroms for units = real or metal.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the
distance units are in lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}}
command must have been previously used to define the lattice spacing.
Note that the units choice affects all the keyword values that have
units of distance or velocity.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are monitoring the temperature of a system where the atom
count is changing due to adding particles, you typically should use
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify dynamic/dof yes}}}} command
for the temperature compute you are using.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the deposition to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This includes information about how many
particles have been deposited, the random number generator seed, the
next timestep for deposition, etc.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For this to work correctly, the timestep must \sphinxstylestrong{not} be changed
after reading the restart with {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}.
The fix will try to detect it and stop with an error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.  This fix computes a global scalar, which can be accessed by various
output commands.  The scalar is the cumulative number of insertions.  The
scalar value calculated by this fix is “intensive”.  No parameter of this
fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified insertion region cannot be a “dynamic” region, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pour::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix pour}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_deposit:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Insertions are performed for individual atoms, i.e. no \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} setting
is defined.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used, the default for \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfrac}
is an equal probabilities for all molecules in the template.
Additional option defaults are id = max, delta = 0.0, near = 0.0,
attempt = 10, rate = 0.0, vx = 0.0 0.0, vy = 0.0 0.0, vz = 0.0 0.0,
and units = lattice.

\section{fix dpd/energy command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:fix-dpd-energy-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/energy/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{energy}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dpd/energy = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{energy}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant energy dissipative particle dynamics (DPD\sphinxhyphen{}E)
integration.  This fix updates the internal energies for particles in
the group at each timestep.  It must be used in conjunction with a
deterministic integrator (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}) that updates
the particle positions and velocities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/energy}, the particle internal temperature is related to
the particle internal energy through a mesoparticle equation of state.
An additional fix must be specified that defines the equation of state
for each particle, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_eos_cv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix eos/cv}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix must be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/fdt/energy}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that numerous variants of DPD can be specified by choosing an
appropriate combination of the integrator and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/fdt/energy}}}} command.  DPD under isoenergetic conditions
can be specified by using fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/energy}, fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve} and pair\_style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/fdt/energy}.  DPD under isoenthalpic conditions can
be specified by using fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/energy}, fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} and pair\_style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/fdt/energy}.  Examples of each DPD variant are provided in the
examples/PACKAGES/dpd\sphinxhyphen{}react directory.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}REACT package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix must be used with an additional fix that specifies time
integration, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/energy} requires the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd} {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}
to be used in order to properly account for the particle internal
energies and temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/energy} must be used with an additional fix that specifies the
mesoparticle equation of state for each particle.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_eos_cv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix eos/cv}}}}

\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_energy:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{fix edpd/source command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:fix-edpd-source-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source::doc}}

\section{fix tdpd/source command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:fix-tdpd-source-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{edpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tdpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc\PYGZus{}index}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
edpd/source or tdpd/source = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
index (only specified for tdpd/source) = index of chemical species (1 to Nspecies)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cuboid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} args = cx cy cz radius source
  cx,cy,cz = x,y,z center of spherical domain (distance units)
  radius = radius of a spherical domain (distance units)
  source = heat source or concentration source (flux units, see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cuboid} values = cx cy cz dLx dLy dLz source
  cx,cy,cz = x,y,z center of a cuboid domain (distance units)
  dLx,dLy,dLz = x,y,z side length of a cuboid domain (distance units)
  source = heat source or concentration source (flux units, see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} values = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID source
  region = ID of region for heat or concentration source
  source = heat source or concentration source (flux units, see below)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{edpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{edpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cuboid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tdpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tdpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cuboid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tdpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{lower}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd/source} adds a heat source as an external heat flux to each
atom in a spherical or cuboid domain, where the \sphinxstyleemphasis{source} is in units
of energy/time.  Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd/source} adds an external concentration
source of the chemical species specified by \sphinxstyleemphasis{index} as an external
concentration flux for each atom in a spherical or cuboid domain,
where the \sphinxstyleemphasis{source} is in units of mole/volume/time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can be used to give an additional heat/concentration
source term to atoms in a simulation, such as for a simulation of a
heat conduction with a source term (see Fig.12 in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:li2014b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2014)}}}})
or diffusion with a source term (see Fig.1 in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_dpd_source:li2015b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2015)}}}}), as
an analog of a periodic Poiseuille flow problem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,deprecated}{Deprecated since version 15Jun2023: }The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cuboid} keywords will be removed in a future version
of LAMMPS.  The same functionality and more can be achieved with a region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} keyword is used, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cx, cy, cz, radius} values define
a spherical domain to apply the source flux to.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cuboid} keyword is used, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cx, cy, cz, dLx, dLy, dLz} define
a cuboid domain to apply the source flux to.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region\sphinxhyphen{}ID} selects which
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} to apply the source flux to.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
No information of these fixes is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to these fixes.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by
these fixes for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of these fixes can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords
of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  These fixes are not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\section{fix drag command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:fix-drag-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_drag::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fmag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delta}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
drag = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x,y,z = coord to drag atoms towards

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fmag = magnitude of force to apply to each atom (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
delta = cutoff distance inside of which force         is not applied (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{center}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{small\PYGZhy{}molecule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a force to each atom in a group to drag it towards the point
(x,y,z).  The magnitude of the force is specified by fmag.  If an atom
is closer than a distance delta to the point, then the force is not
applied.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the x,y,z values can be specified as NULL which means do not
include that dimension in the distance calculation or force
application.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can be used to steer one or more atoms to a new location
in the simulation.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  This is the total
force on the group of atoms by the drag force.  The vector values
calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_self::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/self}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_rg::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/rg}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix smd}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drag:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{fix drude command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:fix-drude-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_drude::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
drude = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flag1 flag2 … flagN = Drude flag for each atom type (1 to N) in the system

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{D}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{D}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{D}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input scripts available: examples/PACKAGES/drude


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assign each atom type in the system to be one of 3 kinds of atoms
within the Drude polarization model. This fix is designed to be used
with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermalized Drude oscillator model}}}}.
Polarizable models in LAMMPS are described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_polarizable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto polarizable}}}} doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The three possible types can be designated with an integer (0,1,2)
or capital letter (N,C,D):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0 or N = non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atom (not part of Drude model)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 or C = Drude core

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2 or D = Drude electron

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix should be invoked before any other commands that implement
the Drude oscillator model, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_tgnh_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix tgnvt/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude_transform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude/transform}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_thole::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style thole}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_tgnh_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix tgnvt/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude_transform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude/transform}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_thole::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style thole}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_drude:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix drude/transform/direct@\spxentry{fix drude/transform/direct}}\ignorespaces
