\section{fix electron/stopping command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:fix-electron-stopping-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping::doc}}

\section{fix electron/stopping/fit command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:fix-electron-stopping-fit-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{electron/stopping} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{electron/stopping/fit}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{electron/stopping} args = Ecut file keyword value ...
  Ecut  = minimum kinetic energy for electronic stopping (energy units)
  file  = name of the file containing the electronic stopping power table

\sphinxstyleemphasis{electron/stopping/fit} args = Ecut c1 c2 ...
  Ecut  = minimum kinetic energy for electronic stopping (energy units)
  c1 c2 = linear and quadratic coefficients for the fitted quadratic polynomial
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args for style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{electron/stopping}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{minneigh}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
      region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = region whose atoms will be affected by this fix
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{minneigh} value = minneigh
      minneigh = minimum number of neighbors an atom to have stopping applied
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{el}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{electron}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stopping}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{elstop}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{table.txt}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{el}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{electron}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stopping}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{elstop}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{table.txt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{minneigh}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{el}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mygroup}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{electron}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stopping}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{elstop}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{table.txt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bulk}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{electron}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stopping}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.63}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.3e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0e\PYGZhy{}8}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{electron}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stopping}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.49}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.8e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9.0e\PYGZhy{}8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.57}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.2e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0e\PYGZhy{}8}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements inelastic energy loss for fast projectiles in solids. It
applies a friction force to fast moving atoms to slow them down due to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:elstopping}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{electronic stopping}}}} (energy lost via electronic collisions per
unit of distance). This fix should be used for simulation of irradiation
damage or ion implantation, where the ions can lose noticeable amounts of
energy from electron excitations. If the electronic stopping power is not
considered, the simulated range of the ions can be severely overestimated
({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:nordlund98}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Nordlund98}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:nordlund95}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Nordlund95}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The electronic stopping is implemented by applying a friction force
to each atom as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{F}_i = \vec{F}^0_i - \frac{\vec{v}_i}{\|\vec{v}_i\|} \cdot S_e\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\vec{F}_i\) is the resulting total force on the atom.
\(\vec{F}^0_i\) is the original force applied to the atom, \(\vec{v}_i\) is
its velocity and \(S_e\) is the stopping power of the ion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to electronic stopping, atomic cascades and irradiation
simulations require the use of an adaptive timestep (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_dt_reset::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix dt/reset}}}}) and the repulsive ZBL potential (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zbl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ZBL}}}} potential) or similar. Without these settings the
interaction between the ion and the target atoms will be faulty. It is also
common to use in such simulations a thermostat ({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_nvt}}}}) in
the borders of the simulation cell.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix removes energy from fast projectiles without depositing it as a
heat to the simulation cell. Such implementation might lead to the unphysical
results when the amount of energy deposited to the electronic system is large,
e.g. simulations of Swift Heavy Ions (energy per nucleon of 100 keV/amu or
higher) or multiple projectiles. You could compensate energy loss by coupling
bulk atoms with some thermostat or control heat transfer between electronic and
atomic subsystems with the two\sphinxhyphen{}temperature model ({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ttm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_ttm}}}}).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
At low velocities the electronic stopping is negligible. The electronic
friction is not applied to atoms whose kinetic energy is smaller than \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ecut},
or smaller than the lowest energy value given in the table in \sphinxstyleemphasis{file}.
Electronic stopping should be applied only when a projectile reaches bulk
material. This fix scans neighbor list and excludes atoms with fewer than
\sphinxstyleemphasis{minneigh} neighbors (by default one). If the pair potential cutoff is large,
minneigh should be increased, though not above the number of nearest neighbors
in bulk material. An alternative is to disable the check for neighbors by
setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{minneigh} to zero and using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword. This is necessary
when running simulations of cluster bombardment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the atom must also be in the specified
geometric {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} in order to have electronic stopping applied to
it. This is useful if the position of the bulk material is fixed. By default
the electronic stopping is applied everywhere in the simulation cell.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The energy ranges and stopping powers are read from the file \sphinxstyleemphasis{file}.
Lines starting with \sphinxstyleemphasis{\#} and empty lines are ignored. Otherwise each
line must contain exactly \sphinxstylestrong{N+1} numbers, where \sphinxstylestrong{N} is the number of atom
types in the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first column is the energy for which the stopping powers on that
line apply. The energies must be sorted from the smallest to the largest.
The other columns are the stopping powers \(S_e\) for each atom type,
in ascending order, in force {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}. The stopping powers for
intermediate energy values are calculated with linear interpolation between
2 nearest points.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} This is a comment
\PYGZsh{}       atom\PYGZhy{}1    atom\PYGZhy{}2
\PYGZsh{} eV    eV/Ang    eV/Ang  \PYGZsh{} units metal
 10        0        0
250       60       80
750      100      150
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If an atom which would have electronic stopping applied to it has a
kinetic energy higher than the largest energy given in \sphinxstyleemphasis{file}, LAMMPS
will exit with an error message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The stopping power depends on the energy of the ion and the target
material. The electronic stopping table can be obtained from
scientific publications, experimental databases or by using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:srim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{SRIM}}}} software. Other programs such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:casp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{CasP}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:pass}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{PASS}}}} can calculate the energy deposited as a function
of the impact parameter of the ion; these results can be used
to derive the stopping power.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{electron/stopping/fit} calculates the electronic stopping power
and cumulative energy lost to the electron gas via a quadratic functional
and applies a drag force to the classical equations\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}motion for all
atoms moving above some minimum cutoff velocity (i.e., kinetic energy).
These coefficients can be determined by fitting a quadratic polynomial to
electronic stopping data predicted by, for example, SRIM or TD\sphinxhyphen{}DFT. Multiple
‘Ecut c1 c2’ values can be provided for multi\sphinxhyphen{}species simulations in the order
of the atom types. There is an examples/PACKAGES/electron\_stopping/ directory,
which illustrates uses of this command. Details of this implementation are
further described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:stewart2018}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Stewart2018}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:lee2020}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Lee2020}}}}.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are not supported.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar, which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}. The scalar is the total energy
loss from electronic stopping applied by this fix since the start of
the latest run. It is considered “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command have no effect
on this fix.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package. It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_electron_stopping:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default is no limitation by region, and minneigh = 1.

\section{fix enforce2d command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d:fix-enforce2d-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d::doc}}

Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{enforce2d/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{enforce2d}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{enforce2d}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_enforce2d:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero out the z\sphinxhyphen{}dimension velocity and force on each atom in the group.
This is useful when running a 2d simulation to ensure that atoms do
not move from their initial z coordinate.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar

by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the

\subsection{Syntax}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_cv:examples}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_cv:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/cv} applies a mesoparticle equation of state to relate the
particle internal energy (\(u_i\)) to the particle internal temperature
(\(\theta_i\)).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/cv} mesoparticle equation of state requires
the constant\sphinxhyphen{}volume heat capacity, and is defined as follows:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}u_{i} = u^{mech}_{i} + u^{cond}_{i} = C_{V} \theta_{i}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(C_V\) is the constant\sphinxhyphen{}volume heat capacity, \(u^{cond}\)
is the internal conductive energy, and \(u^{mech}\) is the internal
mechanical energy.  Note that alternative definitions of the mesoparticle
equation of state are possible.

\section{fix eos/table command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table:fix-eos-table-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eos/table = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} = method of interpolation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = filename containing the tabulated equation of state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = use N values in \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} tables

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = name of table keyword corresponding to table file

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eos}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eos.table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{KEYWORD}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/table} applies a tabulated mesoparticle equation of state to
relate the particle internal energy (u\_i) to the particle internal
temperature (dpdTheta\_i).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/table} creates interpolation tables of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} from
internal energy values listed in a file as a function of internal
temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interpolation tables are created by fitting cubic splines to the
file values and interpolating energy values at each of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} internal
temperatures, and vice versa.  During a simulation, these tables are
used to interpolate internal energy or temperature values as needed.
The interpolation is done with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style, the internal temperature is used to find 2
surrounding table values from which an internal energy is computed by
linear interpolation, and vice versa.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filename specifies a file containing tabulated internal
temperature and internal energy values.  The keyword specifies a
section of the file.  The format of this file is described below.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is as follows (without the
parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} EOS TABLE                (one or more comment or blank lines)

KEYWORD                    (keyword is first text on line)
N 500                      (N  parameter)
                           (blank)
1   1.00 0.000             (index, internal temperature, internal energy)
2   1.02 0.001
...
500 10.0 0.500
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which
identifies the section.  The line can contain additional text, but the
initial text must match the argument specified in the fix command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next line lists the number of table entries.  The parameter “N” is
required and its value is the number of table entries that follow.
Note that this may be different than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_eos_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix eos/table}}}} command.  Let Ntable = \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} in the fix
command, and Nfile = “N” in the tabulated file.  What LAMMPS does is a
preliminary interpolation by creating splines using the Nfile
tabulated values as nodal points.  It uses these to interpolate as
needed to generate energy and temperature values at Ntable different
points.  The resulting tables of length Ntable are then used as
described above, when computing energy and temperature relationships.
This means that if you want the interpolation tables of length Ntable
to match exactly what is in the tabulated file (with effectively no
preliminary interpolation), you should set Ntable = Nfile.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines list the tabulated values.
On each line, the first value is the index from 1 to N, the second value is
the internal temperature (in temperature units), the third value is the
internal energy (in energy units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the internal temperature and internal energy values must
increase from one line to the next.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one file can contain many sections, each with a tabulated
potential.  LAMMPS reads the file section by section until it finds
one that matches the specified keyword.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}REACT package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command also requires use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style dpd}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equation of state must be a monotonically increasing function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An error will occur if the internal temperature or internal energies
are not within the table cutoffs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shardlow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shardlow}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_fdt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair dpd/fdt}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Examples}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table_rx:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/table/rx} applies a tabulated mesoparticle equation
of state to relate the concentration\sphinxhyphen{}dependent particle internal
energy (\(u_i\)) to the particle internal temperature (\(\theta_i\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The concentration\sphinxhyphen{}dependent particle internal energy (\(u_i\)) is
computed according to the following relation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U_{i} = \displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^{m} c_{i,j}(u_{j} + \Delta H_{f,j}) + \frac{3k_{B}T}{2} + Nk_{B}T \\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the number of species, \(c_{i,j}\) is the
concentration of species \sphinxstyleemphasis{j} in particle \sphinxstyleemphasis{i}, \(u_j\) is the
internal energy of species j, \(\Delta H_{f,j} is the heat of
formation of species *j*, N is the number of molecules represented
by the coarse-grained particle, :math:`k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant,
and \(T\) is the temperature of the system.  Additionally, it is
possible to modify the concentration\sphinxhyphen{}dependent particle internal
energy relation by adding an energy correction, temperature\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
correction, and/or a molecule\sphinxhyphen{}dependent correction.  An energy
correction can be specified as a constant (in energy units).  A
temperature correction can be specified by multiplying a temperature
correction coefficient by the internal temperature.  A molecular
correction can be specified by by multiplying a molecule correction
coefficient by the average number of product gas particles in the
coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grain particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/table/rx} creates interpolation tables of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} from \sphinxstyleemphasis{m}
internal energy values of each species \(u_j\) listed in a file as a
function of internal temperature.  During a simulation, these tables
are used to interpolate internal energy or temperature values as needed.
The interpolation is done with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style,
the internal temperature is used to find 2 surrounding table values from
which an internal energy is computed by linear interpolation.  A secant
solver is used to determine the internal temperature from the internal energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first filename specifies a file containing tabulated internal
temperature and \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} internal energy values for each species \(u_j\).
The keyword specifies a section of the file.  The format of this
file is described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second filename specifies a file containing heat of formation
\(\Delta H_{f,j}\) for each species.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In cases where the coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grain particle represents a single molecular
species (i.e., no reactions occur and fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{rx} is not present in the
input file), fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/table/rx} can be applied in a similar manner to
fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{eos/table} within a non\sphinxhyphen{}reactive DPD simulation.  In this case,
the heat of formation filename is replaced with the heat of formation
value for the single species.  Additionally, the energy correction and
temperature correction coefficients may also be specified as fix
arguments.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is as follows (without the
parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} EOS TABLE                (one or more comment or blank lines)

KEYWORD                    (keyword is first text on line)
N 500 h2 no2 n2 ... no     (N  parameter species1 species2 ... speciesN)
                           (blank)
1   1.00 0.000 ... 0.0000  (index, internal temperature, internal energy of species 1, ..., internal energy of species m)
2   1.02 0.001 ... 0.0002
...
500 10.0 0.500 ... 1.0000
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which
identifies the section.  The line can contain additional text, but the
initial text must match the argument specified in the fix command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next line lists the number of table entries and the species names
that correspond with all the species listed in the reaction equations
through the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix rx} command.
The parameter “N” is required and its value is the number of table
entries that follow.  Let Nfile = “N” in the tabulated file.
What LAMMPS does is a preliminary interpolation by creating splines
using the Nfile tabulated values as nodal points.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines list the tabulated values.
On each line, the first value is the index from 1 to N, the second value is
the internal temperature (in temperature units), the third value until
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{m+3} value are the internal energies of the m species (in energy units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that all internal temperature and internal energy values must
increase from one line to the next.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one file can contain many sections, each with a tabulated
potential.  LAMMPS reads the file section by section until it finds
one that matches the specified keyword.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a heat of formation file is as follows (without the
parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} HEAT OF FORMATION TABLE  (one or more comment or blank lines)

                           (blank)
h2      0.00               (species name, heat of formation)
no2     0.34
n2      0.00
...
no      0.93
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the species can be listed in any order.  The tag that is
used as the species name must correspond with the tags used to define
the reactions with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rx::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rx}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, corrections to the EOS can be included by specifying
three additional columns that correspond to the energy correction,
the temperature correction coefficient and molecule correction
coefficient.  In this case, the format of the file is as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} HEAT OF FORMATION TABLE     (one or more comment or blank lines)

                              (blank)
h2      0.00 1.23 0.025  0.0  (species name, heat of formation, energy correction, temperature correction coefficient, molecule correction coefficient)
no2     0.34 0.00 0.000 \PYGZhy{}1.76
n2      0.00 0.00 0.000 \PYGZhy{}1.76
...
no      0.93 0.00 0.000 \PYGZhy{}1.76
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_eos_table_rx:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rx::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rx}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_fdt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair dpd/fdt}}}}

\index{fix evaporate@\spxentry{fix evaporate}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix evaporate command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:fix-evaporate-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{evaporate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
evaporate = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = delete atoms every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
M = number of atoms to delete each time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region within which to perform deletions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for choosing atoms to delete

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{molecule}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{molecule} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{solvent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{evaporate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{surface}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{49892}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{solvent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{evaporate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{surface}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{38277}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molecule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove M atoms from the simulation every N steps.  This can be used,
for example, to model evaporation of solvent particles or molecules
(i.e. drying) of a system.  Every N steps, the number of atoms in the
fix group and within the specified region are counted.  M of these are
chosen at random and deleted.  If there are less than M eligible
particles, then all of them are deleted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the setting for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{molecule} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, then only single
atoms are deleted.  In this case, you should ensure you do not delete
only a portion of a molecule (only some of its atoms), or LAMMPS will
soon generate an error when it tries to find those atoms.  LAMMPS will
warn you if any of the atoms eligible for deletion have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero
molecule ID, but does not check for this at the time of deletion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the setting for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{molecule} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then when an atom
is chosen for deletion, the entire molecule it is part of is deleted.
The count of deleted atoms is incremented by the number of atoms in
the molecule, which may make it exceed \sphinxstyleemphasis{M}.  If the molecule ID of the
chosen atom is 0, then it is assumed to not be part of a molecule, and
just the single atom is deleted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, if you wish to delete 10 water molecules every \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
steps, you should set \sphinxstyleemphasis{M} to 30.  If only the water’s oxygen atoms
were in the fix group, then two hydrogen atoms would be deleted when
an oxygen atom is selected for deletion, whether the hydrogen atoms
are inside the evaporation region or not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that neighbor lists are re\sphinxhyphen{}built on timesteps that atoms are
removed.  Thus you should not remove atoms too frequently or you will
incur overhead due to the cost of building neighbor lists.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are monitoring the temperature of a system where the atom
count is changing due to evaporation, you typically should use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify dynamic/dof yes}}}} command for the
temperature compute you are using.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar, which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the cumulative
number of deleted atoms.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is
“intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
None


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deposit}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_evaporate:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are molecule = no.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix external@\spxentry{fix external}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix external command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:fix-external-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_external:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_external::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{external}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
external = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pf/callback} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pf/array}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pf/callback} args = Ncall Napply
  Ncall = make callback every Ncall steps
  Napply = apply callback forces every Napply steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pf/array} args = Napply
  Napply = apply array forces every Napply steps
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{external}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{callback}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{external}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{callback}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{external}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix allows external programs that are running LAMMPS through its
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_library::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{library interface}}}} to modify certain LAMMPS
properties on specific timesteps, similar to the way other fixes do.
The external driver can be a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_library::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{C/C++ or Fortran program}}}} or a {\hyperref[\detokenize{Python_head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python script}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If mode is \sphinxstyleemphasis{pf/callback} then the fix will make a callback every
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ncall} timesteps or minimization iterations to the external program.
The external program computes forces on atoms by setting values in an
array owned by the fix.  The fix then adds these forces to each atom
in the group, once every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Napply} steps, similar to the way the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}} command works.  Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ncall} \textgreater{}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Napply}, the force values produced by one callback will persist, and
be used multiple times to update atom forces.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback function “foo” is invoked by the fix as:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{foo}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bigint}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{timestep}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nlocal}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tagint}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{ids}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{fexternal}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The arguments are as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ptr} = pointer provided by and simply passed back to external driver

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{timestep} = current LAMMPS timestep

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nlocal} = \# of atoms on this processor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ids} = list of atom IDs on this processor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} = coordinates of atoms on this processor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fexternal} = forces to add to atoms on this processor

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{timestep} is a “bigint” which is defined in src/lmptype.h,
typically as a 64\sphinxhyphen{}bit integer. And \sphinxstyleemphasis{ids} is a pointer to type “tagint”
which is typically a 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit integer unless LAMMPS is compiled with
\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_BIGBIG. For more info please see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings:size}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{build settings}}}} section of the manual.  Finally, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fexternal} are the forces
returned by the driver program.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix has a set\_callback() method which the external driver can call
to pass a pointer to its foo() function.  See the
couple/lammps\_quest/lmpqst.cpp file in the LAMMPS distribution for an
example of how this is done.  This sample application performs
classical MD using quantum forces computed by a density functional
code \sphinxhref{https://dft.sandia.gov/Quest}{Quest}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If mode is \sphinxstyleemphasis{pf/array} then the fix simply stores force values in an
array.  The fix adds these forces to each atom in the group, once
every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Napply} steps, similar to the way the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}} command works.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The name of the public force array provided by the FixExternal
class is

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{fexternal}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is allocated by the FixExternal class as an (N,3) array where N is
the number of atoms owned by a processor.  The 3 corresponds to the
fx, fy, fz components of force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is up to the external program to set the values in this array to
the desired quantities, as often as desired.  For example, the driver
program might perform an MD run in stages of 1000 timesteps each.  In
between calls to the LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command, it could retrieve
atom coordinates from LAMMPS, compute forces, set values in fexternal,
etc.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
To use this fix during energy minimization, the energy corresponding
to the added forces must also be set so as to be consistent with the
added forces.  Otherwise the minimization will not converge correctly.
Correspondingly, the global virial needs to be updated to be use this
fix with variable cell calculations (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_box_relax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix box/relax}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be done from the external driver by calling these public
methods of the FixExternal class:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{set\PYGZus{}energy\PYGZus{}global}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eng}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{set\PYGZus{}virial\PYGZus{}global}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{virial}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{eng} is the potential energy, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} an array of the 6
stress tensor components.  Eng is an extensive quantity,
meaning it should be the sum over per\sphinxhyphen{}atom energies of all affected
atoms.  It should also be provided in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy units}}}}
consistent with the simulation.  See the details below for how to
ensure this energy setting is used appropriately in a minimization.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional public methods that the caller can use to update system
properties are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{set\PYGZus{}energy\PYGZus{}peratom}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{eng}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{set\PYGZus{}virial\PYGZus{}peratom}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{virial}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{set\PYGZus{}vector\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{set\PYGZus{}vector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{idx}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{val}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These allow to set per\sphinxhyphen{}atom energy contributions, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress
contributions, the length and individual values of a global vector
of properties that the caller code may want to communicate  to LAMMPS
(e.g. for use in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}} or in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}} or for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{custom thermo output}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy set by the external driver to
both the global potential energy and peratom potential energies of the
system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} or output
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pe_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pe/atom}}}} command.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy yes}}}}.
Note that this energy may be a fictitious quantity but it is needed so
that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command can include the forces
added by this fix in a consistent manner.  I.e. there is a decrease in
potential energy when atoms move in the direction of the added force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution computed by the external program to
both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of the system via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be
accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial yes}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the potential
energy discussed above.  The scalar stored by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the fictitious potential energy associated with the
added forces to be included in the total potential energy of the
system (the quantity being minimized), you MUST not disable the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_external:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{fix ffl@\spxentry{fix ffl}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix ffl command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:fix-ffl-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{id\PYGZhy{}group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ffl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tau}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[flip}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{type]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ffl = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tau = thermostat parameter (positive real)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart, Tstop = temperature ramp during the run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for generating noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one more value may be appended

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
flip\PYGZhy{}type  = determines the flipping type, can be chosen between rescale \PYGZhy{} no\PYGZus{}flip \PYGZhy{} hard \PYGZhy{} soft, if no flip type is given, rescale will be chosen by default
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ffl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31415}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ffl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9265}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a Fast\sphinxhyphen{}Forward Langevin Equation (FFL) thermostat as described
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ffl:hijazi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Hijazi)}}}}. Contrary to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}, this fix performs both
thermostatting and evolution of the Hamiltonian equations of motion, so it
should not be used together with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} \textendash{} at least not
on the same atom groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The time\sphinxhyphen{}evolution of a single particle undergoing Langevin dynamics is described
by the equations
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac {dq}{dt} = \frac{p}{m},\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac {dp}{dt} = -\gamma p + W + F,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(F\) is the physical force, \(\gamma\) is the friction coefficient, and \(W\) is a
Gaussian random force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The friction coefficient is the inverse of the thermostat parameter : \(\gamma = 1/\tau\), with \(\tau\) the thermostat parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{tau}.
The thermostat parameter is given in the time units, \(\gamma\) is in inverse time units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equilibrium sampling a temperature T is obtained by specifying the
target value as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} arguments, so that the internal
constants depending on the temperature are computed automatically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The random number \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} must be a positive integer.  A Marsaglia random
number generator is used.  Each processor uses the input seed to
generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random numbers.
Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two runs on
different numbers of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The flipping type \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip\sphinxhyphen{}type} can be chosen between 4 types described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ffl:hijazi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Hijazi)}}}}. The flipping operation occurs during the thermostatting
step and it flips the momenta of the atoms. If no\_flip is chosen, no flip
will be executed and the integration will be the same as a standard
Langevin thermostat {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ffl:bussi3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bussi)}}}}. The other flipping types are : rescale \sphinxhyphen{} hard \sphinxhyphen{} soft.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The instantaneous values of the extended variables are written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the
random number generator is not saved in restart files, this means you
cannot do “exact” restarts with this fix, where the simulation
continues on the same as if no restart had taken place. However, in a
statistical sense, a restarted simulation should produce the same
behavior.  Note however that you should use a different seed each time
you restart, otherwise the same sequence of random numbers will be
used each time, which might lead to stochastic synchronization and
subtle artifacts in the sampling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to perform constant\sphinxhyphen{}pressure simulations please use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_press_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix press/berendsen}}}}, rather than
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, to avoid duplicate integration of the
equations of motion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ffl:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/tstat}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gld}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gle}}}}

\section{fix filter/corotate command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:fix-filter-corotate-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{corotate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more constraint/value pairs are appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
constraint = \sphinxstyleemphasis{b} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{a} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{t} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{m}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{b} values = one or more bond types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{a} values = one or more angle types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{t} values = one or more atom types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{m} value = one or more mass values
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{timestep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}
\PYG{k}{run\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{respa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kspace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{corotate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{corotate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements a corotational filter for a mollified impulse
method. In biomolecular simulations, it allows the usage of larger
timesteps for long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatic interactions.  For details, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:fath2017}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fath)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} for a biomolecular
simulation with high\sphinxhyphen{}frequency covalent bonds, the outer time\sphinxhyphen{}step is
restricted to below \textasciitilde{} 4fs due to resonance problems. This fix filters
the outer stage of the respa and thus a larger (outer) time\sphinxhyphen{}step can
be used. Since in large biomolecular simulations the computation of
the long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatic contributions poses a major bottleneck,
this can significantly accelerate the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filter computes a cluster decomposition of the molecular structure
following the criteria indicated by the options a, b, t and m. This
process is similar to the approach in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}},
however, the clusters are not kept constrained. Instead, the position
is slightly modified only for the computation of long\sphinxhyphen{}range forces. A
good cluster decomposition constitutes in building clusters which
contain the fastest covalent bonds inside clusters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the clusters are chosen suitably, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} is stable for outer timesteps of at least 8fs.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about these fixes is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to these fixes.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are
stored by these fixes for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter of these fixes can be used
with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  These
fixes are not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package. It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, it does not support {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule templates}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:related-commands}}

\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{fix flow/gauss@\spxentry{fix flow/gauss}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix flow/gauss command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:fix-flow-gauss-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flow}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gauss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xflag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yflag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zflag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flow/gauss = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
xflag,yflag,zflag = 0 or 1

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0 = do not conserve current in this dimension
1 = conserve current in this dimension
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not compute work done by this fix
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = compute work done by this fix
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{GD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flow}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gauss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{GD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flow}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gauss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements the Gaussian dynamics (GD) method to simulate a
system at constant mass flux {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:strong}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Strong)}}}}. GD is a
nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulation method that can be used
to study fluid flows through pores, pipes, and channels. In its
original implementation GD was used to compute the pressure required
to achieve a fixed mass flux through an opening.  The flux can be
conserved in any combination of the directions, x, y, or z, using
xflag,yflag,zflag. This fix does not initialize a net flux through a
system, it only conserves the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass momentum that is present
when the fix is declared in the input script. Use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} command to generate an initial center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
momentum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
GD applies an external fluctuating gravitational field that acts as a
driving force to keep the system away from equilibrium. To maintain
steady state, a profile\sphinxhyphen{}unbiased thermostat must be implemented to
dissipate the heat that is added by the driving force. {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Compute
temp/profile}}}} can be used to implement a
profile\sphinxhyphen{}unbiased thermostat.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A common use of this fix is to compute a pressure drop across a pipe,
pore, or membrane. The pressure profile can be computed in LAMMPS with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
ave/chunk}}}}, or with the hardy method in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}}. Note that the simple {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}} method is only accurate away from
inhomogeneities in the fluid, such as fixed wall atoms. Further, the
computed pressure profile must be corrected for the acceleration
applied by GD before computing a pressure drop or comparing it to
other methods, such as the pump method {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:zhu}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Zhu)}}}}. The
pressure correction is discussed and described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:strong}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Strong)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a complete example including the considerations discussed
above, see the examples/PACKAGES/flow\_gauss directory.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the flux of the atoms in group\sphinxhyphen{}ID will be conserved. If the
velocities of the group\sphinxhyphen{}ID atoms are coupled to the velocities of
other atoms in the simulation, the flux will not be conserved. For
example, in a simulation with fluid atoms and harmonically constrained
wall atoms, if a single thermostat is applied to group \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}, the
fluid atom velocities will be coupled to the wall atom velocities, and
the flux will not be conserved. This issue can be avoided by
thermostatting the fluid and wall groups separately.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Adding an acceleration to atoms does work on the system. This added
energy can be optionally subtracted from the potential energy for the
thermodynamic output (see below) to check that the timestep is small
enough to conserve energy. Since the applied acceleration is
fluctuating in time, the work cannot be computed from a potential. As
a result, computing the work is slightly more computationally
expensive than usual, so it is not performed by default. To invoke the
work calculation, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword. The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option also invokes the work
calculation, and overrides an \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy no} setting here. If neither
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_modify energy yes} are set, the global scalar
computed by the fix will return zero.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to check energy conservation, any other fixes that do
work on the system must have \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_modify energy yes} set as well. This
includes thermostat fixes and any constraints that hold the positions
of wall atoms fixed, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_self::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/self}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this fix is used in a simulation with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rRESPA}}}}
integrator, the applied acceleration must be computed and applied at
the same rRESPA level as the interactions between the flowing fluid
and the obstacle.  The rRESPA level at which the acceleration is
applied can be changed using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option discussed below. If the flowing fluid and the obstacle
interact through multiple interactions that are computed at different
rRESPA levels, then there must be a separate flow/gauss fix for each
level. For example, if the flowing fluid and obstacle interact through
pairwise and long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulomb interactions, which are computed at
rRESPA levels 3 and 4, respectively, then there must be two separate
flow/gauss fixes, one that specifies \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_modify respa 3} and one with
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_modify respa 4}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy added by the fix to the global
potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows the user to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rRESPA}}}} integrator the fix computes and adds the external
acceleration. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar and a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the negative of the work done on the
system, see the discussion above.  It is only calculated if the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is enabled or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy yes}}}} is set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector is the total force that this fix applied to the group of
atoms on the current timestep.  The scalar and vector values
calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/profile}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_flow_gauss:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} keyword is energy = no.

\section{fix freeze command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:fix-freeze-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{freeze/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{freeze}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
freeze = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero out the force and torque on a granular particle.  This is useful
for preventing certain particles from moving in a simulation.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{granular pair styles}}}} also detect if this fix has been
defined and compute interactions between frozen and non\sphinxhyphen{}frozen
particles appropriately, as if the frozen particle has infinite mass.
A similar functionality for normal (point) particles can be obtained
using {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_setforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix setforce}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  This is the total
force on the group of atoms before the forces on individual atoms are
changed by the fix.  The vector values calculated by this fix are
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_freeze:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the GRANULAR package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There can only be a single freeze fix defined.  This is because other
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{granular pair styles}}}} treat frozen particles
differently and need to be able to reference a single group to which
this fix is applied.
