\section{fix gcmc command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:fix-gcmc-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gcmc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{X}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{displace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gcmc = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = invoke this fix every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
X = average number of GCMC exchanges to attempt every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
M = average number of MC moves to attempt every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label) for inserted atoms (must be 0 if mol keyword used)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = temperature of the ideal gas reservoir (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mu = chemical potential of the ideal gas reservoir (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
displace = maximum Monte Carlo translation distance (length units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxangle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fugacity\_coeff}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{group}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{grouptype}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intra\_energy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tfac\_insert}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap\_cutoff}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} value = template\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    template\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of molecule template specified in a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mcmoves} values = Patomtrans Pmoltrans Pmolrotate
    Patomtrans = proportion of atom translation MC moves
    Pmoltrans = proportion of molecule translation MC moves
    Pmolrotate = proportion of molecule rotation MC moves
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} value = fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small}}}} command
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{shake} value = fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} command
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region where GCMC exchanges and MC moves are allowed
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxangle} value = maximum molecular rotation angle (degrees)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} value = pressure of the gas reservoir (pressure units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{fugacity\_coeff} value = fugacity coefficient of the gas reservoir (unitless)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} = compute the entire system energy when performing GCMC exchanges and MC moves
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} value = charge of inserted atoms (charge units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} value = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID for inserted atoms (string)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{grouptype} values = type group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label)
    group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID for inserted atoms (string)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{intra\_energy} value = intramolecular energy (energy units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tfac\_insert} value = scale up/down temperature of inserted atoms (unitless)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap\_cutoff} value = maximum pair distance for overlap rejection (distance units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} value = Maximum number of molecules allowed in the system
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} value = Minimum number of molecules allowed in the system
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) exchanges of atoms or
molecules with an imaginary ideal gas reservoir at the specified T and
chemical potential (mu) as discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc:frenkel2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Frenkel)}}}}.  It
also attempts Monte Carlo (MC) moves (translations and molecule rotations)
within the simulation cell or region.  If used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
command, simulations in the grand canonical ensemble (muVT, constant
chemical potential, constant volume, and constant temperature) can be
performed.  Specific uses include computing isotherms in microporous
materials, or computing vapor\sphinxhyphen{}liquid coexistence curves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every N timesteps the fix attempts both GCMC exchanges (insertions or
deletions) and MC moves of gas atoms or molecules.  On those timesteps, the
average number of attempted GCMC exchanges is X, while the average number
of attempted MC moves is M.  For GCMC exchanges of either molecular or
atomic gasses, these exchanges can be either deletions or insertions, with
equal probability.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The possible choices for MC moves are translation of an atom, translation
of a molecule, and rotation of a molecule.  The relative amounts of each are
determined by the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{mcmoves} keyword (see below).  The default
behavior is as follows. If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used, only molecule
translations and molecule rotations are performed with equal probability.
Conversely, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is not used, only atom translations are
performed.  M should typically be chosen to be approximately equal to the
expected number of gas atoms or molecules of the given type within the
simulation cell or region, which will result in roughly one MC move per
atom or molecule per MC cycle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All inserted particles are always added to two groups: the default group
“all” and the fix group specified in the fix command.  In addition,
particles are also added to any groups specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{grouptype} keywords.  If inserted particles are individual atoms, they are
assigned the atom type given by the type argument.  If they are molecules,
the type argument has no effect and must be set to zero. Instead, the type
of each atom in the inserted molecule is specified in the file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Care should be taken to apply fix gcmc only to
a group that contains only those atoms and molecules
that you wish to manipulate using Monte Carlo.
Hence it is generally not a good idea to specify
the default group “all” in the fix command, although it is allowed.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix cannot be used to perform GCMC insertions of gas atoms or
molecules other than the exchanged type, but GCMC deletions,
and MC translations, and rotations can be performed on any atom/molecule in
the fix group.  All atoms in the simulation cell can be moved using
regular time integration translations, e.g. via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}},
resulting in a hybrid GCMC+MD simulation. A smaller\sphinxhyphen{}than\sphinxhyphen{}usual
timestep size may be needed when running such a hybrid simulation,
especially if the inserted molecules are not well equilibrated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command may optionally use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword to define an
exchange and move volume.  The specified region must have been
previously defined with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  It must be
defined with side = \sphinxstyleemphasis{in}.  Insertion attempts occur only within the
specified region. For non\sphinxhyphen{}rectangular regions, random trial points are
generated within the rectangular bounding box until a point is found
that lies inside the region. If no valid point is generated after 1000
trials, no insertion is performed, but it is counted as an attempted
insertion.  Move and deletion attempt candidates are selected from gas
atoms or molecules within the region. If there are no candidates, no
move or deletion is performed, but it is counted as an attempt move or
deletion. If an attempted move places the atom or molecule
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass outside the specified region, a new attempted move is
generated. This process is repeated until the atom or molecule
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass is inside the specified region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, the temperature of the imaginary
reservoir, T, should be set to be equivalent to the target temperature
used in fix nvt. Otherwise, the imaginary reservoir will not be in
thermal equilibrium with the simulation cell. Also, it is important that
the temperature used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix nvt} is dynamically updated, which can be
achieved as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mdtemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mdatoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mdtemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamic}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dof}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mdnvt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mdatoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mdnvt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdtemp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that neighbor lists are re\sphinxhyphen{}built every timestep that this fix is
invoked, so you should not set N to be too small.  However, periodic
rebuilds are necessary in order to avoid dangerous rebuilds and missed
interactions. Specifically, avoid performing so many MC translations
per timestep that atoms can move beyond the neighbor list skin
distance. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When an atom or molecule is to be inserted, its coordinates are chosen
at a random position within the current simulation cell or region, and
new atom velocities are randomly chosen from the specified temperature
distribution given by T. The effective temperature for new atom
velocities can be increased or decreased using the optional keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tfac\_insert} (see below). Relative coordinates for atoms in a
molecule are taken from the template molecule provided by the
user. The center of mass of the molecule is placed at the insertion
point. The orientation of the molecule is chosen at random by rotating
about this point.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Individual atoms are inserted, unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used.  It
specifies a \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}ID} previously defined using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command, which reads a file that defines the
molecule.  The coordinates, atom types, charges, etc., as well as any
bonding and special neighbor information for the molecule can
be specified in the molecule file.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}}
command for details.  The only settings required to be in this file
are the coordinates and types of atoms in the molecule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When not using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword, you should ensure you do not delete
atoms that are bonded to other atoms, or LAMMPS will soon generate an
error when it tries to find bonded neighbors.  LAMMPS will warn you if
any of the atoms eligible for deletion have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero molecule ID,
but does not check for this at the time of deletion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to insert molecules using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword that will be
treated as rigid bodies, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} keyword, specifying as its
value the ID of a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small}}}} command
which also appears in your input script.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish the new rigid molecules (and other rigid molecules) to be
thermostatted correctly via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small/nvt}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/small/npt}}}}, then you need to use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify dynamic/dof yes}}}} command for the rigid
fix.  This is to inform that fix that the molecule count will vary
dynamically.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to insert molecules via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword, that will have
their bonds or angles constrained via SHAKE, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shake} keyword,
specifying as its value the ID of a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} command which also appears in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optionally, users may specify the relative amounts of different MC
moves using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mcmoves} keyword. The values \sphinxstyleemphasis{Patomtrans},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pmoltrans}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pmolrotate} specify the average proportion of
atom translations, molecule translations, and molecule rotations,
respectively. The values must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative integers or real
numbers, with at least one non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value. For example, (10,30,0)
would result in 25\% of the MC moves being atomic translations, 75\%
molecular translations, and no molecular rotations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optionally, users may specify the maximum rotation angle for molecular
rotations using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxangle} keyword and specifying the angle in
degrees. Rotations are performed by generating a random point on the
unit sphere and a random rotation angle on the range
{[}0,maxangle). The molecule is then rotated by that angle about an
axis passing through the molecule center of mass. The axis is parallel
to the unit vector defined by the point on the unit sphere.  The same
procedure is used for randomly rotating molecules when they are
inserted, except that the maximum angle is 360 degrees.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that fix gcmc does not use configurational bias MC or any other
kind of sampling of intramolecular degrees of freedom.  Inserted
molecules can have different orientations, but they will all have the
same intramolecular configuration, which was specified in the molecule
command input.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For atomic gasses, inserted atoms have the specified atom type, but
deleted atoms are any atoms that have been inserted or that already
belong to the fix group. For molecular gasses, exchanged
molecules use the same atom types as in the template molecule supplied
by the user.  In both cases, exchanged atoms/molecules are assigned to
two groups: the default group “all” and the fix group
(which can also be “all”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The chemical potential is a user\sphinxhyphen{}specified input parameter defined
as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mu = \mu^{id} + \mu^{ex}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second term mu\_ex is the excess chemical potential due to
energetic interactions and is formally zero for the fictitious gas
reservoir but is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero for interacting systems. So, while the
chemical potential of the reservoir and the simulation cell are equal,
mu\_ex is not, and as a result, the densities of the two are generally
quite different.  The first term mu\_id is the ideal gas contribution
to the chemical potential.  mu\_id can be related to the density or
pressure of the fictitious gas reservoir by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mu^{id}  = & k T \ln{\rho \Lambda^3} \\
          = & k T \ln{\frac{\phi P \Lambda^3}{k_B T}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, \(T\) is the user\sphinxhyphen{}specified
temperature, \(\rho\) is the number density, \sphinxstyleemphasis{P} is the pressure,
and \(\phi\) is the fugacity coefficient.  The constant
\(\Lambda\) is required for dimensional consistency.  For all unit
styles except \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} it is defined as the thermal de Broglie wavelength
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Lambda = \sqrt{ \frac{h^2}{2 \pi m k_B T}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{h} is Planck’s constant, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the mass of the exchanged atom
or molecule.  For unit style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj}, \(\Lambda\) is simply set to
unity. Note that prior to March 2017, \(\Lambda\) for unit style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj}
was calculated using the above formula with \sphinxstyleemphasis{h} set to the rather specific
value of 0.18292026.  Chemical potential under the old definition can
be converted to an equivalent value under the new definition by
subtracting \(3 k T \ln(\Lambda_{old})\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an alternative to specifying mu directly, the ideal gas reservoir
can be defined by its pressure \sphinxstyleemphasis{P} using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} keyword, in
which case the user\sphinxhyphen{}specified chemical potential is ignored. The user
may also specify the fugacity coefficient \(\phi\) using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fugacity\_coeff} keyword, which defaults to unity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option means that the fix calculates the total
potential energy of the entire simulated system, instead of just
the energy of the part that is changed. The total system
energy before and after the proposed GCMC exchange or MC move
is then used in the
Metropolis criterion to determine whether or not to accept the
proposed change. By default, this option is off,
in which case only
partial energies are computed to determine the energy difference
due to the proposed change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option is needed for systems with complicated
potential energy calculations, including the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatics (kspace)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
many\sphinxhyphen{}body pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hybrid pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eam pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tail corrections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
need to include potential energy contributions from other fixes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In these cases, LAMMPS will automatically apply the \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy}
keyword and issue a warning message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option also includes
the intramolecular energy of inserted and deleted molecules, whereas
this energy is not included when \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} is not used. If this
is not desired, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{intra\_energy} keyword can be used to define an
amount of energy that is subtracted from the final energy when a
molecule is inserted, and subtracted from the initial energy when a molecule
is deleted. For molecules that have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero intramolecular energy,
this will ensure roughly the same behavior whether or not the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Inserted atoms and molecules are assigned random velocities based on
the specified temperature \(T\). Because the relative velocity of all
atoms in the molecule is zero, this may result in inserted molecules
that are systematically too cold. In addition, the intramolecular
potential energy of the inserted molecule may cause the kinetic energy
of the molecule to quickly increase or decrease after insertion.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tfac\_insert} keyword allows the user to counteract these effects by
changing the temperature used to assign velocities to inserted atoms
and molecules by a constant factor. For a particular application, some
experimentation may be required to find a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{tfac\_insert} that
results in inserted molecules that equilibrate quickly to the correct
temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some fixes have an associated potential energy. Examples of such fixes
include: {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{efield}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gravity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{gravity}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{addforce}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{langevin}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_restrain::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restrain}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/berendsen}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/rescale}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{wall fixes}}}}.  For that energy to be included in the
total potential energy of the system (the quantity used when performing
GCMC exchange and MC moves), you MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for that fix.  The doc pages for
individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} commands specify if this should be done.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} option to insert atoms with a user\sphinxhyphen{}specified point
charge. Note that doing so will cause the system to become non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral.
LAMMPS issues a warning when using long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatics (kspace)
with non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral systems. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_group_group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute group/group}}}} documentation for more details about simulating
non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral systems with kspace on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of this fix typically will cause the number of atoms to fluctuate,
therefore, you will want to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify dynamic/dof}}}} command to ensure that the current number of atoms is
used as a normalizing factor each time temperature is computed. A simple
example of this is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{thermo\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamic}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dof}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A more complicated example is listed earlier on this page
in the context of NVT dynamics.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the density of the cell is initially very small or zero, and
increases to a much larger density after a period of equilibration,
then certain quantities that are only calculated once at the start
(kspace parameters) may no longer be accurate.  The solution is to
start a new simulation after the equilibrium density has been
reached.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With some pair\_styles, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Buckingham}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Born\sphinxhyphen{}Mayer\sphinxhyphen{}Huggins}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ReaxFF}}}},
two atoms placed close to each other may have an arbitrary large,
negative potential energy due to the functional form of the potential.
While these unphysical configurations are inaccessible to typical
dynamical trajectories, they can be generated by Monte Carlo moves. The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap\_cutoff} keyword suppresses these moves by effectively assigning
an infinite positive energy to all new configurations that place any
pair of atoms closer than the specified overlap cutoff distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} keywords allow for the restriction of the number of
atoms in the simulation. They automatically reject all insertion or
deletion moves that would take the system beyond the set boundaries.
Should the system already be beyond the boundary, only moves that bring
the system closer to the bounds may be accepted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} keyword adds all inserted atoms to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}}
of the group\sphinxhyphen{}ID value. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{grouptype} keyword adds all inserted atoms
of the specified type to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} of the group\sphinxhyphen{}ID value.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the fix to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This includes information about the random number
generator seed, the next timestep for MC exchanges, the number of MC
step attempts and successes etc.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an
input script that reads a restart file, so that the operation of the
fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For this to work correctly, the timestep must \sphinxstylestrong{not} be changed
after reading the restart with {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}.
The fix will try to detect it and stop with an error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to
this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global vector of length 8, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector values are
the following global cumulative quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
translation attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
translation successes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
insertion attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
insertion successes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
deletion attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
deletion successes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rotation attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rotation successes

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style requires an {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} with per atom
type masses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not set “neigh\_modify once yes” or else this fix will never be
called.  Reneighboring is \sphinxstylestrong{required}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only usable for 3D simulations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be run in parallel, but aspects of the GCMC part will not
scale well in parallel.  Currently, molecule translations and rotations
are not supported with more than one MPI process.  It is still possible
to do parallel molecule exchange without translation and rotation moves
by setting MC moves to zero and/or by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mcmoves} keyword with
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pmoltrans} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pmolrotate} = 0 .

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using fix gcmc in combination with fix shake or fix rigid, only
GCMC exchange moves are supported, so the argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{M} must be zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using fix gcmc in combination with fix rigid, deletion of the last
remaining molecule is not allowed for technical reasons, and so the
molecule count will never drop below 1, regardless of the specified
chemical potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that very lengthy simulations involving insertions/deletions of
billions of gas molecules may run out of atom or molecule IDs and
trigger an error, so it is better to run multiple shorter\sphinxhyphen{}duration
simulations. Likewise, very large molecules have not been tested and
may turn out to be problematic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of multiple fix gcmc commands in the same input script can be
problematic if using a template molecule. The issue is that the
user\sphinxhyphen{}referenced template molecule in the second fix gcmc command may
no longer exist since it might have been deleted by the first fix gcmc
command. An existing template molecule will need to be referenced by
the user for each subsequent fix gcmc command.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atom/swap}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deposit}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_evaporate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix evaporate}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_atoms}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are mol = no, maxangle = 10, overlap\_cutoff = 0.0,
fugacity\_coeff = 1.0, intra\_energy = 0.0, tfac\_insert = 1.0.
(Patomtrans, Pmoltrans, Pmolrotate) = (1, 0, 0) for mol = no and
(0, 1, 1) for mol = yes. full\_energy = no,
except for the situations where full\_energy is required, as
listed above.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_gcmc:frenkel2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Frenkel)} Frenkel and Smit, Understanding Molecular Simulation,
Academic Press, London, 2002.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix gld@\spxentry{fix gld}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix gld command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:fix-gld-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gld::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gld}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N\PYGZus{}k}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{series}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tau\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}N\PYGZus{}k}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tau\PYGZus{}N\PYGZus{}k}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gld = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N\_k = number of terms in the Prony series representation of the memory kernel

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
series = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pprony} is presently the only available option

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_k = the weight of the kth term in the Prony series (mass per time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tau\_k = the time constant of the kth term in the Prony series (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{frozen} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{frozen} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = initialize extended variables using values drawn from equilibrium distribution at Tstart
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = initialize extended variables to zero (i.e., from equilibrium distribution at zero temperature)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not set total random force to zero
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = set total random force to zero
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gld}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{82885}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pprony}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{frozen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{rouse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gld}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.355}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.355}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48823}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pprony}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{107.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.02415}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{186.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.04294}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{428.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.09661}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1714}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.38643}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies Generalized Langevin Dynamics to a group of atoms, as
described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld:baczewski}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baczewski)}}}}.  This is intended to model the
effect of an implicit solvent with a temporally non\sphinxhyphen{}local dissipative
force and a colored Gaussian random force, consistent with the
Fluctuation\sphinxhyphen{}Dissipation Theorem.  The functional form of the memory
kernel associated with the temporally non\sphinxhyphen{}local force is constrained
to be a Prony series.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
While this fix bears many similarities to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}, it has one significant
difference. Namely, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gld}}}} performs time integration,
whereas {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} does NOT. To this end, the
specification of another fix to perform time integration, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, is NOT necessary.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With this fix active, the force on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}th atom is given as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{\bf F}_{j}(t) = & {\bf F}^C_j(t)-\int \limits_{0}^{t} \Gamma_j(t-s) {\bf v}_j(s)~\text{d}s + {\bf F}^R_j(t) \\
\Gamma_j(t-s) = & \sum \limits_{k=1}^{N_k} \frac{c_k}{\tau_k} e^{-(t-s)/\tau_k} \\
\langle{\bf F}^R_j(t),{\bf F}^R_j(s)\rangle = & \text{k$_\text{B}$T} ~\Gamma_j(t-s)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, the first term is representative of all conservative (pairwise,
bonded, etc) forces external to this fix, the second is the temporally
non\sphinxhyphen{}local dissipative force given as a Prony series, and the third is
the colored Gaussian random force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Prony series form of the memory kernel is chosen to enable an
extended variable formalism, with a number of exemplary mathematical
features discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld:baczewski}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baczewski)}}}}. In particular, \(3N_k\)
extended variables are added to each atom, which effect the action of
the memory kernel without having to explicitly evaluate the integral
over time in the second term of the force. This also has the benefit
of requiring the generation of uncorrelated random forces, rather than
correlated random forces as specified in the third term of the force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Presently, the Prony series coefficients are limited to being greater
than or equal to zero, and the time constants are limited to being
greater than zero. To this end, the value of series MUST be set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pprony}, for now. Future updates will allow for negative coefficients
and other representations of the memory kernel. It is with these
updates in mind that the series option was included.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The units of the Prony series coefficients are chosen to be mass per
time to ensure that the numerical integration scheme stably approaches
the Newtonian and Langevin limits. Details of these limits, and the
associated numerical concerns are discussed in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld:baczewski}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baczewski)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The desired temperature at each timestep is ramped from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} over the course of the next run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The random \# \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} must be a positive integer. A Marsaglia random
number generator is used. Each processor uses the input seed to
generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random
numbers. Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two
runs on different numbers of processors.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword/value option pairs are used in the following ways.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{frozen} can be used to specify how the extended variables
associated with the GLD memory kernel are initialized. Specifying no
(the default), the initial values are drawn at random from an
equilibrium distribution at \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart}, consistent with the
Fluctuation\sphinxhyphen{}Dissipation Theorem. Specifying yes, initializes the
extended variables to zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} can be used to eliminate drift due to the
thermostat. Because the random forces on different atoms are
independent, they do not sum exactly to zero. As a result, this fix
applies a small random force to the entire system, and the
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of the system undergoes a slow random walk. If the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the total random force is set exactly
to zero by subtracting off an equal part of it from each atom in the
group. As a result, the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of a system with zero initial
momentum will not drift over time.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The instantaneous values of the extended variables are written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the random
number generator is not saved in restart files, this means you cannot
do “exact” restarts with this fix, where the simulation continues on
the same as if no restart had taken place. However, in a statistical
sense, a restarted simulation should produce the same behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gld:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix gle command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:fix-gle-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gle::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{id\PYGZhy{}group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ns}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Amatrix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[noneq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cmatrix]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[every}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stride]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gle = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ns = number of additional fictitious momenta

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart, Tstop = temperature ramp during the run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Amatrix = file to read the drift matrix A from

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for generating noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{noneq} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{every}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{noneq} Cmatrix  = file to read the non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium covariance matrix from
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} stride   = apply the GLE once every time steps. Reduces the accuracy
      of the integration of the GLE, but has *no effect* on the accuracy of equilibrium
      sampling. It might change sampling properties when used together with \sphinxstyleemphasis{noneq}.
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31415}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smart.A}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31415}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qt}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{n}{k.A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{noneq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qt}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{n}{k.C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE) thermostat as described
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gle:ceriotti}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ceriotti)}}}}. The formalism allows one to obtain a number
of different effects ranging from efficient sampling of all
vibrational modes in the system to inexpensive (approximate)
modelling of nuclear quantum effects. Contrary to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}, this fix performs both
thermostatting and evolution of the Hamiltonian equations of motion, so it
should not be used together with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} \textendash{} at least not
on the same atom groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each degree of freedom in the thermostatted group is supplemented
with Ns additional degrees of freedom s, and the equations of motion
become

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
dq/dt=p/m
d(p,s)/dt=(F,0) \PYGZhy{} A(p,s) + B dW/dt
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where F is the physical force, A is the drift matrix (that generalizes
the friction in Langevin dynamics), B is the diffusion term and dW/dt
un\sphinxhyphen{}correlated Gaussian random forces. The A matrix couples the physical
(q,p) dynamics with that of the additional degrees of freedom,
and makes it possible to obtain effectively a history\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
noise and friction kernel.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The drift matrix should be given as an external file \sphinxstyleemphasis{Afile},
as a (Ns+1 x Ns+1) matrix in inverse time units. Matrices that are
optimal for a given application and the system of choice can be
obtained from {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gle:gle4md}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(GLE4MD)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equilibrium sampling a temperature T is obtained by specifying the
target value as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} arguments, so that the diffusion
matrix that gives canonical sampling for a given A is computed automatically.
However, the GLE framework also allow for non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium sampling, that
can be used for instance to model inexpensively zero\sphinxhyphen{}point energy
effects {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gle:ceriotti2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ceriotti2)}}}}. This is achieved specifying the \sphinxstyleemphasis{noneq}
keyword followed by the name of the file that contains the static covariance
matrix for the non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium dynamics.  Please note, that the covariance
matrix is expected to be given in \sphinxstylestrong{temperature units}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since integrating GLE dynamics can be costly when used together with
simple potentials, one can use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} optional keyword to
apply the Langevin terms only once every several MD steps, in a
multiple time\sphinxhyphen{}step fashion. This should be used with care when doing
non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium sampling, but should have no effect on equilibrium
averages when using canonical sampling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The random number \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} must be a positive integer.  A Marsaglia random
number generator is used.  Each processor uses the input seed to
generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random numbers.
Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two runs on
different numbers of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note also that the Generalized Langevin Dynamics scheme that is
implemented by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gld}}}} scheme is closely related
to the present one. In fact, it should be always possible to cast the
Prony series form of the memory kernel used by GLD into an appropriate
input matrix for {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gle}}}}. While the GLE scheme is more
general, the form used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gld}}}} can be more directly
related to the representation of an implicit solvent environment.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The instantaneous values of the extended variables are written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the
random number generator is not saved in restart files, this means you
cannot do “exact” restarts with this fix, where the simulation
continues on the same as if no restart had taken place. However, in a
statistical sense, a restarted simulation should produce the same
behavior.  Note however that you should use a different seed each time
you restart, otherwise the same sequence of random numbers will be
used each time, which might lead to stochastic synchronization and
subtle artifacts in the sampling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The GLE thermostat in its current implementation should not be used
with rigid bodies, SHAKE or RATTLE. It is expected that all the
thermostatted degrees of freedom are fully flexible, and the sampled
ensemble will not be correct otherwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to perform constant\sphinxhyphen{}pressure simulations please use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_press_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix press/berendsen}}}}, rather than
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, to avoid duplicate integration of the
equations of motion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gle:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/tstat}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gld::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gld}}}}

\section{fix gravity command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:fix-gravity-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{gravity/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gravity/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gravity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{magnitude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gravity = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
magnitude = size of acceleration (force/mass units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
magnitude can be a variable (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{chute} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spherical} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gradient} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{chute} args = angle
  angle = angle in +x away from \sphinxhyphen{}z or \sphinxhyphen{}y axis in 3d/2d (in degrees)
  angle can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spherical} args = phi theta
  phi = azimuthal angle from +x axis (in degrees)
  theta = angle from +z or +y axis in 3d/2d (in degrees)
  phi or theta can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} args = x y z
  x y z = vector direction to apply the acceleration
  x or y or z can be a variable (see below)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gravity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gravity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}increase}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gravity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spherical}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{180.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gravity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spherical}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}phi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}theta}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gravity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Impose an additional acceleration on each particle in the group.  This
fix is typically used with granular systems to include a “gravity”
term acting on the macroscopic particles.  More generally, it can
represent any kind of driving field, e.g. a pressure gradient inducing
a Poiseuille flow in a fluid.  Note that this fix operates differently
than the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}} command.  The addforce fix
adds the same force to each atom, independent of its mass.  This
command imparts the same acceleration to each atom (force/mass).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{magnitude} of the acceleration is specified in force/mass units.
For granular systems (LJ units) this is typically 1.0.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{chute} is typically used for simulations of chute flow where
the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} is the chute angle, with flow occurring in the +x
direction.  For 3d systems, the tilt is away from the z axis; for 2d
systems, the tilt is away from the y axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spherical} allows an arbitrary 3d direction to be specified for
the acceleration vector.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Phi} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} are defined in the usual
spherical coordinates.  Thus for acceleration acting in the \sphinxhyphen{}z
direction, \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} would be 180.0 (or \sphinxhyphen{}180.0).  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Theta} = 90.0 and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{phi} = \sphinxhyphen{}90.0 would mean acceleration acts in the \sphinxhyphen{}y direction.  For
2d systems, \sphinxstyleemphasis{phi} is ignored and \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} is an angle in the xy plane
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} = 0.0 is the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} imposes an acceleration in the vector direction given
by (x,y,z).  Only the direction of the vector is important; it’s
length is ignored.  For 2d systems, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} component is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the quantities \sphinxstyleemphasis{magnitude}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{phi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{z} which define the gravitational magnitude and direction, can be
specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is
a variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where name is the
variable name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated each
timestep, and its value used to determine the quantity.  You should
ensure that the variable calculates a result in the appropriate units,
e.g. force/mass or degrees.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent gravitational
field.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the gravitational potential energy of the system to
the global potential energy of the system as part of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for
this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  This scalar is the
gravitational potential energy of the particles in the defined field,
namely mass * (g dot x) for each particles, where x and mass are the
particles position and mass, and g is the gravitational field.  The
scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_gravity:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix grem@\spxentry{fix grem}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix grem command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:fix-grem-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_grem::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{grem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lambda}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermostat}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
grem = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lambda = intercept parameter of linear effective temperature function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eta = slope parameter of linear effective temperature function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
H0 = shift parameter of linear effective temperature function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermostat\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat or barostat used in simulation

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix             }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fxgREM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{grem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{400}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{30000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fxnpt}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fxgREM\PYGZus{}press}

\PYG{k}{fix             }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fxgREM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{grem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{502}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.15}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{80000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fxnvt}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements the molecular dynamics version of the generalized
replica exchange method (gREM) originally developed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_grem:kim2010}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kim)}}}},
which uses non\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann ensembles to sample over first order phase
transitions. The is done by defining replicas with an enthalpy
dependent effective temperature
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T_{eff} = \lambda + \eta (H - H_0)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\eta\) negative and steep enough to only intersect the
characteristic microcanonical temperature (Ts) of the system once,
ensuring a unimodal enthalpy distribution in that replica.
\(\lambda\) is the intercept and effects the generalized ensemble
similar to how temperature effects a Boltzmann ensemble. \(H_0\)
is a reference enthalpy, and is typically set as the lowest desired
sampled enthalpy.  Further explanation can be found in our recent
papers {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_grem:malolepsza}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Malolepsza)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires a Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat fix reference passed to the
grem as \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermostat\sphinxhyphen{}ID}. Two distinct temperatures exist in this
generalized ensemble, the effective temperature defined above, and a
kinetic temperature that controls the velocity distribution of
particles as usual. Either constant volume or constant pressure
algorithms can be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix enforces a generalized ensemble in a single replica
only. Typically, this ideology is combined with replica exchange with
replicas differing by \(\lambda\) only for simplicity, but this is not
required. A multi\sphinxhyphen{}replica simulation can be run within the LAMMPS
environment using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{temper_grem::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temper/grem}}}} command. This
utilizes LAMMPS partition mode and requires the number of available
processors be on the order of the number of desired replicas. A
100\sphinxhyphen{}replica simulation would require at least 100 processors (1 per
world at minimum). If many replicas are needed on a small number of
processors, multi\sphinxhyphen{}replica runs can be run outside of LAMMPS.  An
example of this can be found in examples/PACKAGES/grem and has no
limit on the number of replicas per processor. However, this is very
inefficient and error prone and should be avoided if possible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In general, defining the generalized ensembles is unique for every
system. When starting a many\sphinxhyphen{}replica simulation without any knowledge
of the underlying microcanonical temperature, there are several tricks
we have utilized to optimize the process.  Choosing a less\sphinxhyphen{}steep
\(\eta\) yields broader distributions, requiring fewer replicas to
map the microcanonical temperature.  While this likely struggles from
the same sampling problems gREM was built to avoid, it provides quick
insight to Ts.  Initially using an evenly\sphinxhyphen{}spaced \(\lambda\)
distribution identifies regions where small changes in enthalpy lead
to large temperature changes. Replicas are easily added where needed.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} option is supported
by this fix to add the rescaled kinetic pressure as part of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the effective
temperature \(T_{eff}\).  The scalar value calculated by this
fix is “intensive”.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the REPLICA package. It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_grem:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{temper_grem::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temper/grem}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}}


\subsection{Default}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
