\index{fix halt@\spxentry{fix halt}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix halt command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:fix-halt-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_halt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{operator}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{avalue}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
halt = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = check halt condition every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
attribute = \sphinxstyleemphasis{bondmax} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tlimit} or v\_name
\begin{sphinxalltt}
bondmax = length of longest bond in the system (in length units)
tlimit = elapsed CPU time (in seconds)
diskfree = free disk space (in MBytes)
v\_name = name of {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
operator = “\textless{}” or “\textless{}=” or “\textgreater{}” or “\textgreater{}=” or “==” or “!=” or “|\textasciicircum{}”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
avalue = numeric value to compare attribute to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{error} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{message} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{path}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{error} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{hard} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{soft} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{continue}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{message} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{path} value = path to check for free space (may be in quotes)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bondmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}myCheck}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{!}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{error}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diskfree}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{dump storage/.}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check a condition every N steps during a simulation run.  N must be \textgreater{}=1.
If the condition is met, exit the run.  In this context a “run” can be
dynamics or minimization iterations, as specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified group\sphinxhyphen{}ID is ignored by this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{attribute} can be one of the options listed above, namely
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bondmax}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tlimit}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{diskfree}, or an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} referenced as \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name}, where “name” is the name of a
variable that has been defined previously in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bondmax} attribute will loop over all bonds in the system,
compute their current lengths, and set \sphinxstyleemphasis{attribute} to the longest bond
distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tlimit} attribute queries the elapsed CPU time (in seconds) since
the current run began, and sets \sphinxstyleemphasis{attribute} to that value.  This is an
alternative way to limit the length of a simulation run, similar to
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{timer::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timer}}}} timeout command.  There are two differences in
using this method versus the timer command option.  The first is that
the clock starts at the beginning of the current run (not when the
timer or fix command is specified), so that any setup time for the run
is not included in the elapsed time.  The second is that the timer
invocation and syncing across all processors (via MPI\_Allreduce) is
not performed once every \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} steps by this command.  Instead it is
performed (typically) only a small number of times and the elapsed
times are used to predict when the end\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}run will be.  Both of
these attributes can be useful when performing benchmark calculations
for a desired length of time with minimal overhead.  For example, if
a run is performing 1000s of timesteps/sec, the overhead for syncing
the timer frequently across a large number of processors may be
non\sphinxhyphen{}negligible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{diskfree} attribute will check for available disk space (in
MBytes) on supported operating systems. By default it will
check the file system of the current working directory.  This
can be changed with the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{path} keyword, which will take
the path to a file or folder on the file system to be checked
as argument.  This path must be given with single or double quotes,
if it contains blanks or other special characters (like \$).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables evaluate to a numeric value.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for a description.  They calculate
formulas which can involve mathematical operations, atom properties,
group properties, thermodynamic properties, global values calculated
by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}}, or references to other
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}}.  Thus they are a very general means of
computing some attribute of the current system.  For example, the
following “bondmax” variable will calculate the same quantity as the
hstyle = bondmax option.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute         }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bdist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}
\PYG{k}{compute         }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reduce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}bdist}
\PYG{k}{variable        }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bondmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}bmax}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus these two versions of a fix halt command will do the same thing:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bondmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}bondmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The version with “bondmax” will just run somewhat faster, due to less
overhead in computing bond lengths and not storing them in a separate
compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A variable can be used to implement a large variety of conditions,
including to stop when a specific file exists.  Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{exit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{EXIT}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}exit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{!}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{error}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{soft}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Will stop the current run command when a file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXIT}} is created
in the current working directory.  The condition can be cleared
by removing the file through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{shell::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{shell}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The choice of operators listed above are the usual comparison
operators.  The XOR operation (exclusive or) is also included as “|\textasciicircum{}”.
In this context, XOR means that if either the attribute or avalue is
0.0 and the other is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, then the result is “true”.  Otherwise
it is “false”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{avalue} must be a numeric value.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{error} keyword determines how the current run is halted.
If its value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{hard}, then LAMMPS will stop with an error message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If its value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{soft}, LAMMPS will exit the current run, but continue
to execute subsequent commands in the input script.  However,
additional {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} commands will be
skipped.  For example, this allows a script to output the current
state of the system, e.g. via a {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_dump}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If its value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{continue}, the behavior is the same as for \sphinxstyleemphasis{soft},
except subsequent {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} commands
are executed.  This allows your script to remedy the condition that
triggered the halt, if necessary.  Note that you may wish use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}} command on the fix halt ID, so that the same
condition is not immediately triggered in a subsequent run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{message} keyword determines whether a message is printed
to the screen and logfile when the halt condition is triggered.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{message} is set to yes, a one line message with the values that
triggered the halt is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{message} is set to no, no message
is printed; the run simply exits.  The latter may be desirable for
post\sphinxhyphen{}processing tools that extract thermodynamic information from log
files.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{diskfree} attribute is currently only supported on Linux, macOS, and *BSD.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_halt:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are error = soft, message = yes, and path = “.”.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix heat@\spxentry{fix heat}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix heat command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat:fix-heat-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_heat:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_heat::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eflux}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
heat = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = add/subtract heat every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eflux = rate of heat addition or subtraction (energy/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eflux can be a variable (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region atoms must be in to have added force
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{qin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{qin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}flux}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{qout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add non\sphinxhyphen{}translational kinetic energy (heat) to a group of atoms in a
manner that conserves their aggregate momentum.  Two of these fixes
can be used to establish a temperature gradient across a simulation
domain by adding heat (energy) to one group of atoms (hot reservoir)
and subtracting heat from another (cold reservoir).  E.g. a simulation
sampling from the McDLT ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the atom must be in both the group
and the specified geometric {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} in order to have
energy added or subtracted to it.  If not specified, then the atoms in
the group are affected wherever they may move to.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Heat addition/subtraction is performed every N timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} parameter can be specified as a numeric constant or as an
equal\sphinxhyphen{} or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is a
variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} is the variable
name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated each timestep, and
its current value(s) used to determine the flux.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} is a numeric constant or equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable which evaluates
to a scalar value, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} determines the change in aggregate energy
of the entire group of atoms per unit time, e.g. in eV/ps for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{metal units}}}}.  In this case it is an “extensive” quantity,
meaning its magnitude should be scaled with the number of atoms in the
group.  Note that since \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} also has per\sphinxhyphen{}time units (i.e. it is a
flux), this means that a larger value of N will add/subtract a larger
amount of energy each time the fix is invoked.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The heat\sphinxhyphen{}exchange (HEX) algorithm implemented by this fix is
known to exhibit a pronounced energy drift. An improved algorithm
(eHEX) is available as a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ehex::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ehex}}}} command and might be
preferable if energy conservation is important.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} is specified as an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable (see below), then
the variable computes one value per atom.  In this case, each value is
the energy flux for a single atom, again in units of energy per unit
time.  In this case, each value is an “intensive” quantity, which need
not be scaled with the number of atoms in the group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent flux.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus it is easy to specify a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent flux
with optional time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence as well.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If heat is subtracted from the system too aggressively so that
the group’s kinetic energy would go to zero, or any individual atom’s
kinetic energy would go to zero for the case where \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} is an
atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, then LAMMPS will halt with an error message.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix heat is different from a thermostat such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}} in that energy is
added/subtracted continually.  Thus if there is not another mechanism
in place to counterbalance this effect, the entire system will heat or
cool continuously.  You can use multiple heat fixes so that the net
energy change is 0.0 or use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}} to drain
energy from the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix does not change the coordinates of its atoms; it only scales
their velocities.  Thus you must still use an integration fix
(e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}) on the affected atoms.  This fix should
not normally be used on atoms that have their temperature controlled
by another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} fix.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  This scalar is the most recent
value by which velocities were scaled.  The scalar value calculated by
this fix is “intensive”.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{eflux} is specified as an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
variable, this fix computes the average value by which the velocities
were scaled for all of the atoms that had their velocities scaled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\section{fix heat/flow command}

  \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = cp1 ... cpN

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat_flow:examples}}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_heat_flow:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform plain time integration to update temperature for atoms in the
group each timestep. The specific heat of atoms can be defined using either
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} keywords. For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant}, the specific heat
is a constant value \sphinxstyleemphasis{cp} for all atoms. For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} different values
of the specific heat are defined, one for each of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} types of atoms.

\section{fix hyper/global command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:fix-hyper-global-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hyper}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{global}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutbond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qfactor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Vmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tequil}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hyper/global = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutbond = max distance at which a pair of atoms is considered bonded (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qfactor = max strain at which bias potential goes to 0.0 (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Vmax = height of bias potential (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is meant to be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} command to
perform a bond\sphinxhyphen{}boost global hyperdynamics (GHD) simulation.  The role
of this fix is to a select a single pair of atoms in the system at
each timestep to add a global bias potential to, which will alter the
dynamics of the system in a manner that effectively accelerates time.
This is in contrast to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix hyper/local}}}}
command, which can be user to perform a local hyperdynamics (LHD)
simulation, by adding a local bias potential to multiple pairs of
atoms at each timestep.  GHD can time accelerate a small simulation
with up to a few 100 atoms.  For larger systems, LHD is needed to
achieve good time acceleration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a system that undergoes rare transition events, where one or more
atoms move over an energy barrier to a new potential energy basin, the
effect of the bias potential is to induce more rapid transitions.
This can lead to a dramatic speed\sphinxhyphen{}up in the rate at which events
occurs, without altering their relative frequencies, thus leading to
an overall increase in the elapsed real time of the simulation as
compared to running for the same number of timesteps with normal MD.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} page for a more general discussion of
hyperdynamics and citations that explain both GHD and LHD.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equations and logic used by this fix and described here to perform
GHD follow the description given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:voter2013ghd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Voter2013)}}}}.  The
bond\sphinxhyphen{}boost form of a bias potential for HD is due to Miron and
Fichthorn as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:mironghd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Miron)}}}}.  In LAMMPS we use a
simplified version of bond\sphinxhyphen{}boost GHD where a single bond in the system
is biased at any one timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bonds are defined between each pair of atoms \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}, whose \(R^0_{ij}\)
distance is less than \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutbond}, when the system is in a quenched state
(minimum) energy.  Note that these are not “bonds” in a covalent
sense.  A bond is simply any pair of atoms that meet the distance
criterion.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Cutbond} is an argument to this fix; it is discussed
below.  A bond is only formed if one or both of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} atoms are in
the specified group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The current strain of bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} (when running dynamics) is defined as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_{ij} = \frac{R_{ij} - R^0_{ij}}{R^0_{ij}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(R_{ij}\) is the current distance between atoms \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j},
and \(R^0_{ij}\) is the equilibrium distance in the quenched state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bias energy \(V_{ij}\) of any bond between atoms \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}
is defined as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}V_{ij} = V^{max} \cdot \left( 1 - \left(\frac{E_{ij}}{q}\right)^2 \right) \textrm{ for } \left|E_{ij}\right| < qfactor \textrm{ or } 0 \textrm{ otherwise}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the prefactor \(V^{max}\) and the cutoff \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} are arguments to
this fix; they are discussed below.  This functional form is an
inverse parabola centered at 0.0 with height \(V^{max}\) and
which goes to 0.0 at +/\sphinxhyphen{} qfactor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Let \(E^{max}\) be the maximum of \(\left| E_{ij} \right|\)
for all \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} bonds in the system on a
given timestep.  On that step, \(V_{ij}\) is added as a bias potential
to only the single bond with strain \(E^{max}\), call it
\(V^{max}_{ij}\).  Note that \(V^{max}_{ij}\) will be 0.0
if \(E^{max} >= \textrm{qfactor}\) on that timestep.  Also note
that \(V^{max}_{ij}\) is added to the normal interatomic potential
that is computed between all atoms in the system at every step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The derivative of \(V^{max}_{ij}\) with respect to the position of
each atom in the \(E^{max}\) bond gives a bias force
\(F^{max}_{ij}\) acting on the bond as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F^{max}_{ij} = - \frac{dV^{max}_{ij}}{dE_{ij}} = \frac{2 V^{max} E-{ij}}{\textrm{qfactor}^2}   \textrm{ for } \left|E_{ij}\right| < \textrm{qfactor} \textrm{ or } 0 \textrm{ otherwise}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which can be decomposed into an equal and opposite force acting on
only the two \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} atoms in the \(E^{max}\) bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The time boost factor for the system is given each timestep I by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}B_i = e^{\beta V^{max}_{ij}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\beta = \frac{1}{kT_{equil}}\), and \(T_{equil}\) is the
temperature of the system and an argument to this fix.  Note that
\(B_i >= 1\) at every step.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To run a GHD simulation, the input script must also use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
langevin}}}} command to thermostat the atoms at the same
\(T_{equil}\) as specified by this fix, so that the system is
running constant\sphinxhyphen{}temperature (NVT) dynamics.  LAMMPS does not check
that this is done.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The elapsed time \(t_{hyper}\) for a GHD simulation running for \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps is simply
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}t_{hyper} = \sum_{i=1,N} B-i \cdot dt\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} is the timestep size defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}}
command.  The effective time acceleration due to GHD is thus t\_hyper /
N*dt, where N*dt is elapsed time for a normal MD run of N timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in GHD, the boost factor varies from timestep to timestep.
Likewise, which bond has \(E^{max}\) strain and thus which pair of
atoms the bias potential is added to, will also vary from timestep to timestep.
This is in contrast to local hyperdynamics (LHD) where the boost
factor is an input parameter; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix hyper/local}}}} page for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is additional information on the input parameters for GHD.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutbond} argument is the cutoff distance for defining bonds between
pairs of nearby atoms.  A pair of \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} atoms in their equilibrium,
minimum\sphinxhyphen{}energy configuration, which are separated by a distance
\(R_{ij} < cutbond\), are flagged as a bonded pair.  Setting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cubond} to be \textasciitilde{}25\% larger than the nearest\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor distance in a
crystalline lattice is a typical choice for solids, so that bonds exist
only between nearest neighbor pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} argument is the limiting strain at which the bias
potential goes to 0.0.  It is dimensionless, so a value of 0.3 means a
bond distance can be up to 30\% larger or 30\% smaller than the
equilibrium (quenched) \(R^0_{ij}\) distance and the two atoms in
the bond could still experience a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero bias force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} is set too large, then transitions from one energy basin
to another are affected because the bias potential is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero at the
transition state (e.g. saddle point).  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} is set too small
than little boost is achieved because the \(E_{ij}\) strain of some bond in
the system will (nearly) always exceed \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor}.  A value of 0.3 for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} is typically reasonable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} argument is the prefactor on the bias potential.  Ideally,
tt should be set to a value slightly less than the smallest barrier
height for an event to occur.  Otherwise the applied bias potential
may be large enough (when added to the interatomic potential) to
produce a local energy basin with a maxima in the center.  This can
produce artificial energy minima in the same basin that trap an atom.
Or if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} is even larger, it may induce an atom(s) to rapidly
transition to another energy basin.  Both cases are “bad dynamics”
which violate the assumptions of GHD that guarantee an accelerated
time\sphinxhyphen{}accurate trajectory of the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} is set too small, the GHD simulation will run
correctly.  There will just be fewer events because the hyper time
(t\_hyper equation above) will be shorter.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have no physical intuition as to the smallest barrier
height in your system, a reasonable strategy to determine the largest
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} you can use for a GHD model, is to run a sequence of
simulations with smaller and smaller \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} values, until the event
rate does not change (as a function of hyper time).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tequil} argument is the temperature at which the system is
simulated; see the comment above about the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} thermostatting.  It is also part of the beta term in the
exponential factor that determines how much boost is achieved as a
function of the bias potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In general, the lower the value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tequil} and the higher the value
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax}, the more time boost will be achievable by the GHD
algorithm.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy of the bias potential to the global
potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar and global vector of length 12,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the magnitude of the bias potential
(energy units) applied on the current timestep.  The vector stores the
following quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
boost factor on this step (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max strain \(E_{ij}\) of any bond on this step (absolute value, unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID of first atom in the max\sphinxhyphen{}strain bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID of second atom in the max\sphinxhyphen{}strain bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average \# of bonds/atom on this step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fraction of timesteps where the biased bond has bias = 0.0 during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fraction of timesteps where the biased bond has negative strain during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max drift distance of any atom during this run (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max bond length during this run (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative hyper time since fix was defined (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative count of event timesteps since fix was defined

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative count of atoms in events since fix was defined

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 5 quantities are for the current timestep.  Quantities 6\sphinxhyphen{}9
are for the current hyper run.  They are reset each time a new hyper
run is performed.  Quantities 19\sphinxhyphen{}12 are cumulative across multiple
runs (since the point in the input script the fix was defined).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 8, drift is the distance an atom moves between two quenched
states when the second quench determines an event has occurred.  Atoms
involved in an event will typically move the greatest distance since
others typically remain near their original quenched position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 11, events are checked for by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} command
once every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevent} timesteps.  This value is the count of those
timesteps on which one (or more) events was detected.  It is NOT the
number of distinct events, since more than one event may occur in the
same \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevent} time window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 12, each time the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} command checks for an
event, it invokes a compute to flag zero or more atoms as
participating in one or more events.  E.g. atoms that have displaced
more than some distance from the previous quench state.  Value 11 is
the cumulative count of the number of atoms participating in any of
the events that were found.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar and vector values calculated by this fix are all
“intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the REPLICA
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_global:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix hyper/local}}}}


\subsection{Default}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{fix hyper/local@\spxentry{fix hyper/local}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix hyper/local command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:fix-hyper-local-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_local::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hyper}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutbond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qfactor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Vmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tequil}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Dcut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Btarget}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hyper/local = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutbond = max distance at which a pair of atoms is considered bonded (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qfactor = max strain at which bias potential goes to 0.0 (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Vmax = estimated height of bias potential (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tequil = equilibration temperature (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dcut = minimum distance between boosted bonds (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
alpha = boostostat relaxation time (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Btarget = desired time boost factor (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{bound} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{check/ghost} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{check/bias}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bound} value = Bfrac
  Bfrac =  \sphinxhyphen{}1 or a value \textgreater{}= 0.0
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} value = Rfreq
  Rfreq = \sphinxhyphen{}1 or 0 or timestep value \textgreater{} 0
\sphinxstyleemphasis{check/ghost} values = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{check/bias} values = Nevery error/warn/ignore
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hyper}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bound}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reset}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is meant to be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} command to
perform a bond\sphinxhyphen{}boost local hyperdynamics (LHD) simulation.  The role
of this fix is to a select multiple pairs of atoms in the system at
each timestep to add a local bias potential to, which will alter the
dynamics of the system in a manner that effectively accelerates time.
This is in contrast to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_global::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix hyper/global}}}}
command, which can be user to perform a global hyperdynamics (GHD)
simulation, by adding a global bias potential to a single pair of
atoms at each timestep.  GHD can time accelerate a small simulation
with up to a few 100 atoms.  For larger systems, LHD is needed to
achieve good time acceleration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a system that undergoes rare transition events, where one or more
atoms move over an energy barrier to a new potential energy basin, the
effect of the bias potential is to induce more rapid transitions.
This can lead to a dramatic speed\sphinxhyphen{}up in the rate at which events
occurs, without altering their relative frequencies, thus leading to
an overall increase in the elapsed real time of the simulation as
compared to running for the same number of timesteps with normal MD.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} page for a more general discussion of
hyperdynamics and citations that explain both GHD and LHD.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equations and logic used by this fix and described here to perform
LHD follow the description given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:voter2013lhd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Voter2013)}}}}.  The
bond\sphinxhyphen{}boost form of a bias potential for HD is due to Miron and
Fichthorn as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:mironlhd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Miron)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To understand this description, you should first read the description
of the GHD algorithm on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_global::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix hyper/global}}}}
doc page.  This description of LHD builds on the GHD description.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The definition of bonds and \(E_{ij}\) are the same for GHD and LHD.
The formulas for \(V^{max}_{ij}\) and \(F^{max}_{ij}\) are also
the same except for a prefactor \(C_{ij}\), explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bias energy \(V_{ij}\) applied to a bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} with maximum strain is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}V^{max}_{ij} = C_{ij} \cdot V^{max} \cdot \left(1 - \left(\frac{E_{ij}}{q}\right)^2\right) \textrm{ for } \left|E_{ij}\right| < qfactor \textrm{ or } 0 \textrm{ otherwise}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The derivative of \(V^{max}_{ij}\) with respect to the position of
each atom in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} bond gives a bias force \(F^{max}_{ij}\) acting
on the bond as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F^{max}_{ij} = - \frac{dV^{max}_{ij}}{dE_{ij}} = 2 C_{ij} V^{max} \frac{E_{ij}}{qfactor^2} \textrm{ for } \left|E_{ij}\right| < qfactor \textrm{ or } 0 \textrm{ otherwise}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which can be decomposed into an equal and opposite force acting on
only the two atoms \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j} in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The key difference is that in GHD a bias energy and force is added (on
a particular timestep) to only one bond (pair of atoms) in the system,
which is the bond with maximum strain \(E^{max}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LHD, a bias energy and force can be added to multiple bonds
separated by the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} distance or more.  A bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} is
biased if it is the maximum strain bond within its local
“neighborhood”, which is defined as the bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} plus any neighbor
bonds within a distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} from \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}.  The “distance” between bond
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} and bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{kl} is the minimum distance between any of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ik}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{il},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{jk}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{jl} pairs of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a large system, multiple bonds will typically meet this
requirement, and thus a bias potential \(V^{max}_{ij}\) will be
applied to many bonds on the same timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LHD, all bonds store a \(C_{ij}\) prefactor which appears in
the \(V^{max}_{ij}\) and \(F^{max}_{ij}equations above.  Note
that the :math:`C_{ij}\) factor scales the strength of the bias energy
and forces whenever bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} is the maximum strain bond in its neighborhood.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_{ij}\) is initialized to 1.0 when a bond between the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} atoms
is first defined.  The specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} factor is then used to adjust the
\(C_{ij}\) prefactors for each bond every timestep in the following manner.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An instantaneous boost factor \(B_{ij}\) is computed each timestep
for each bond, as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}B_{ij} = e^{\beta V^{max}_{kl}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(V^{max}_{kl}\) is the bias energy of the maxstrain bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{kl}
within bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}‘s neighborhood, \(\beta = \frac{1}{kT_{equil}}\),
and \(T_{equil}\) is the temperature of the system and an argument
to this fix.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To run an LHD simulation, the input script must also use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} command to thermostat the atoms at
the same \(T_{equil}\) as specified by this fix, so that the
system is running constant\sphinxhyphen{}temperature (NVT) dynamics.  LAMMPS does
not check that this is done.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}== \sphinxstyleemphasis{kl}, then bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} is a biased bond on that
timestep, otherwise it is not.  But regardless, the boost factor
\(B_{ij}\) can be thought of an estimate of time boost currently
being applied within a local region centered on bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}.  For LHD,
we want this to be the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} value everywhere in the
simulation domain.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To accomplish this, if \(B_{ij} < B_{target}\), the \(C_{ij}\)
prefactor for bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{ij} is incremented on the current timestep by an
amount proportional to the inverse of the specified \(\alpha\) and
the difference (\(B_{ij} - B_{target}\)).  Conversely if
\(B_{ij} > B_{target}\), \(C_{ij}\) is decremented by the same
amount.  This procedure is termed “boostostatting” in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:voter2013lhd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Voter2013)}}}}.  It drives all of the individual \(C_{ij}\) to
values such that when \(V^{max}_{ij}\) is applied as a bias to bond
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ij}, the resulting boost factor \(B_{ij}\) will be close to
\(B_{target}\) on average.  Thus the LHD time acceleration factor
for the overall system is effectively \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in LHD, the boost factor \(B_{target}\) is specified by the user.
This is in contrast to global hyperdynamics (GHD) where the boost
factor varies each timestep and is computed as a function of \(V_{max}\),
\(E_{max}\), and \(T_{equil}\); see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_global::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix hyper/global}}}} page for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is additional information on the input parameters for LHD.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutbond}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tequil} arguments have the
same meaning as for GHD.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} argument is slightly different.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} parameters are unique to LHD.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutbond} argument is the cutoff distance for defining bonds
between pairs of nearby atoms.  A pair of I,J atoms in their
equilibrium, minimum\sphinxhyphen{}energy configuration, which are separated by a
distance \(R_{ij} < cutbond\), are flagged as a bonded pair.  Setting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cubond} to be \textasciitilde{}25\% larger than the nearest\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor distance in a
crystalline lattice is a typical choice for solids, so that bonds
exist only between nearest neighbor pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} argument is the limiting strain at which the bias
potential goes to 0.0.  It is dimensionless, so a value of 0.3 means a
bond distance can be up to 30\% larger or 30\% smaller than the
equilibrium (quenched) \(R^0_{ij}\) distance and the two atoms in the bond
could still experience a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero bias force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} is set too large, then transitions from one energy basin
to another are affected because the bias potential is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero at the
transition state (e.g. saddle point).  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} is set too small
than little boost can be achieved because the \(E_{ij}\) strain of
some bond in
the system will (nearly) always exceed \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor}.  A value of 0.3 for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} is typically a reasonable value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} argument is a fixed prefactor on the bias potential.  There
is a also a dynamic prefactor \(C_{ij}\), driven by the choice of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} as discussed above.  The product of these should be a value less than
the smallest barrier height for an event to occur.  Otherwise the
applied bias potential may be large enough (when added to the
interatomic potential) to produce a local energy basin with a maxima
in the center.  This can produce artificial energy minima in the same
basin that trap an atom.  Or if \(C_{ij} \cdot V^{max}\) is even
larger, it may
induce an atom(s) to rapidly transition to another energy basin.  Both
cases are “bad dynamics” which violate the assumptions of LHD that
guarantee an accelerated time\sphinxhyphen{}accurate trajectory of the system.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It may seem that \(V^{max}\) can be set to any value, and
\(C_{ij}\) will compensate to reduce the overall prefactor
if necessary.  However the \(C_{ij}\) are initialized to 1.0
and the boostostatting procedure typically operates slowly enough
that there can be a time period of bad dynamics if \(V^{max}\)
is set too large.  A better strategy is to set \(V^{max}\) to the
slightly smaller than the lowest barrier height for an event (the same
as for GHD), so that the \(C_{ij}\) remain near unity.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tequil} argument is the temperature at which the system is
simulated; see the comment above about the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} thermostatting.  It is also part of the beta term in the
exponential factor that determines how much boost is achieved as a
function of the bias potential.  See the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget}
argument below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed above, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} argument is the distance required
between two locally maxstrain bonds for them to both be selected as
biased bonds on the same timestep.  Computationally, the larger \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut}
is, the more work (computation and communication) must be done each
timestep within the LHD algorithm.  And the fewer bonds can be
simultaneously biased, which may mean the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} time
acceleration cannot be achieved.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Physically \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} should be a long enough distance that biasing two
pairs of atoms that close together will not influence the dynamics of
each pair.  E.g. something like 2x the cutoff of the interatomic
potential.  In practice a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} value of \textasciitilde{}10 Angstroms seems to work
well for many solid\sphinxhyphen{}state systems.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You should ensure that ghost atom communication is performed for
a distance of at least \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} + \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutevent} = the distance one or more
atoms move (between quenched states) to be considered an “event”.  It
is an argument to the “compute event/displace” command used to detect
events.  By default the ghost communication distance is set by the
pair\_style cutoff, which will typically be \textless{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut}.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}} command should be used to override the ghost
cutoff explicitly, e.g.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{comm\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this fix does not know the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutevent} parameter, but uses
half the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutbond} parameter as an estimate to warn if the ghost
cutoff is not long enough.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As described above the \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} argument is a prefactor in the
boostostat update equation for each bond’s \(C_{ij}\) prefactor.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Alpha} is specified in time units, similar to other thermostat or barostat
damping parameters.  It is roughly the physical time it will take the
boostostat to adjust a \(C_{ij}\) value from a too high (or too low)
value to a correct one.  An \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} setting of a few ps is typically good for
solid\sphinxhyphen{}state systems.  Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} argument here is the
inverse of the alpha parameter discussed in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:voter2013lhd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Voter2013)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} argument is the desired time boost factor (a value \textgreater{} 1)
that all the atoms in the system will experience.  The elapsed time
t\_hyper for an LHD simulation running for \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} timesteps is simply
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}t_{hyper} = B_{target} \cdot N \cdot dt\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} is the timestep size defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}}
command.  The effective time acceleration due to LHD is thus
\(\frac{t_{hyper}}{N\cdot dt} = B_{target}\), where \(N\cdot dt\)
is the elapsed time for a normal MD run of N timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You cannot choose an arbitrarily large setting for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget}.  The
maximum value you should choose is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}B_{target} = e^{\beta V_{small}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(V_{small}\) is the smallest event barrier height in your
system, \(\beta = \frac{1}{kT_{equil}}\), and \(T_{equil}\)
is the specified temperature of the system
(both by this fix and the Langevin thermostat).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} is set smaller than this, the LHD simulation
will run correctly.  There will just be fewer events because the hyper
time (t\_hyper equation above) will be shorter.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have no physical intuition as to the smallest barrier
height in your system, a reasonable strategy to determine the largest
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} you can use for an LHD model, is to run a sequence of
simulations with smaller and smaller \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} values, until the event
rate does not change (as a function of hyper time).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is additional information on the optional keywords for this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bound} keyword turns on min/max bounds for bias coefficients
\(C_{ij}\) for all bonds.  \(C_{ij}\) is a prefactor for each bond on
the bias potential of maximum strength \(V^{max}\).  Depending on the
choice of \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax}, the boostostatting can cause
individual \(C_{ij}\) values to fluctuate.  If the fluctuations are too
large \(C_{ij} \cdot V^{max}\) can exceed low barrier heights and induce
bad event dynamics.  Bounding the \(C_{ij}\) values is a way to prevent
this.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bfrac} is set to \sphinxhyphen{}1 or any negative value (the default) then no
bounds are enforced on \(C_{ij}\) values (except they must always
be \textgreater{}= 0.0).  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bfrac} setting \textgreater{}= 0.0
sets a lower bound of 1.0 \sphinxhyphen{} Bfrac and upper bound of 1.0 + Bfrac on each
\(C_{ij}\) value.  Note that all \(C_{ij}\) values are initialized
to 1.0 when a bond is created for the first time.  Thus \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bfrac} limits the
bias potential height to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} +/\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bfrac}*\sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} keyword allow \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} to be adjusted dynamically depending on the
average value of all \(C_{ij}\) prefactors.  This can be useful if you
are unsure what value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} will match the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget} boost for the
system.  The \(C_{ij}\) values will then adjust in aggregate (up or down)
so that \(C_{ij} \cdot V^{max}\) produces a boost of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Btarget}, but this
may conflict with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bound} keyword settings.  By using \sphinxstyleemphasis{bound} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset}
together, \(V^{max}\) itself can be reset, and desired bounds still applied
to the \(C_{ij}\) values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A setting for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Rfreq} of \sphinxhyphen{}1 (the default) means \sphinxstyleemphasis{Vmax} never changes.
A setting of 0 means \(V^{max}\) is adjusted every time an event occurs and
bond pairs are recalculated.  A setting of N \textgreater{} 0 timesteps means
\(V^{max}\) is adjusted on the first time an event occurs on a timestep \textgreater{}=
N steps after the previous adjustment.  The adjustment to \(V^{max}\) is
computed as follows.  The current average of all \(C_{ij} \cdot V^{max}\)
values is computed and the \(V^{max}\) is reset to that value.  All
\(C_{ij}\) values are changed to new prefactors such the new
\(C_{ij} \cdot V^{max}\) is the same as it was previously.  If the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bound} keyword was used, those bounds are enforced on the new \(C_{ij}\)
values.  Henceforth, new bonds are assigned a \(C_{ij} = 1.0\), which
means their bias potential magnitude is the new \(V^{max}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{check/ghost} keyword turns on extra computation each timestep to
compute statistics about ghost atoms used to determine which bonds to
bias.  The output of these stats are the vector values 14 and 15,
described below.  If this keyword is not enabled, the output
of the stats will be zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{check/bias} keyword turns on extra computation and communication
to check if any biased bonds are closer than \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} to each other,
which should not be the case if LHD is operating correctly.  Thus it
is a debugging check.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} setting determines how often the
check is made.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{error}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{warn}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ignore} setting determines
what is done if the count of too\sphinxhyphen{}close bonds is not zero.  Either the
code will exit, or issue a warning, or silently tally the count.  The
count can be output as vector value 17, as described below.  If this
keyword is not enabled, the output of that statistic will be 0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that both of these computations are costly, hence they are only
enabled by these keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_hyper_local:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy of the bias potential to the global
potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar and global vector of length 28,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the magnitude of the bias potential
(energy units) applied on the current timestep, summed over all biased
bonds.  The vector stores the following quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average boost for all bonds on this step (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of biased bonds on this step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max strain \(E_{ij}\) of any bond on this step (absolute value, unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value of \(V^{max}\) on this step (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average bias coeff for all bonds on this step (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min bias coeff for all bonds on this step (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max bias coeff for all bonds on this step (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average \# of bonds/atom on this step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average neighbor bonds/bond on this step within \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average boost for all bonds during this run (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average \# of biased bonds/step during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fraction of biased bonds with no bias during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fraction of biased bonds with negative strain during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max bond length during this run (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average bias coeff for all bonds during this run (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min bias coeff for any bond during this run (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max bias coeff for any bond during this run (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max drift distance of any bond atom during this run (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max distance from proc subbox of any ghost atom with maxstrain \textless{} qfactor during this run (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max distance outside my box of any ghost atom with any maxstrain during this run (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
count of ghost atoms that could not be found on reneighbor steps during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
count of bias overlaps (\textless{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut}) found during this run

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative hyper time since fix created (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative count of event timesteps since fix created

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative count of atoms in events since fix created

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cumulative \# of new bonds formed since fix created

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average boost for biased bonds on this step (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of bonds with absolute strain \textgreater{}= q on this step

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quantities 1\sphinxhyphen{}9 are for the current timestep.  Quantities 10\sphinxhyphen{}22
are for the current hyper run.  They are reset each time a new
hyper run is performed.  Quantities 23\sphinxhyphen{}26 are cumulative across
multiple runs (since the point in the input script the fix was
defined).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 10, each bond instantaneous boost factor is given by the
equation for \(B_{ij}\) above.  The total system boost (average across all
bonds) fluctuates, but should average to a value close to the
specified \(B_{target}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 12, the numerator is a count of all biased bonds on each
timestep whose bias energy = 0.0 due to \(E_{ij} >= qfactor\).  The
denominator is the count of all biased bonds on all timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 13, the numerator is a count of all biased bonds on each
timestep with negative strain.  The denominator is the count of all
biased bonds on all timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Values 18\sphinxhyphen{}22 are mostly useful for debugging and diagnostic purposes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 18, drift is the distance an atom moves between two quenched
states when the second quench determines an event has occurred.  Atoms
involved in an event will typically move the greatest distance since
others typically remain near their original quenched position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For values 19\sphinxhyphen{}21, neighbor atoms in the full neighbor list with cutoff
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} may be ghost atoms outside a processor’s sub\sphinxhyphen{}box.  Before the
next event occurs they may move further than \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} away from the
sub\sphinxhyphen{}box boundary.  Value 19 is the furthest (from the sub\sphinxhyphen{}box) any
ghost atom in the neighbor list with maxstrain \textless{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor} was
accessed during the run.  Value 20 is the same except that the ghost
atom’s maxstrain may be \textgreater{}= \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfactor}, which may mean it is about to
participate in an event.  Value 21 is a count of how many ghost atoms
could not be found on reneighbor steps, presumably because they moved
too far away due to their participation in an event (which will likely
be detected at the next quench).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typical values for 19 and 20 should be slightly larger than \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut},
which accounts for ghost atoms initially at a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} distance moving
thermally before the next event takes place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for values 19 and 20 to be computed, the optional keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{check/ghost} must be specified.  Otherwise these values will be zero.
This is because computing them incurs overhead, so the values are only
computed if requested.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Value 21 should be zero or small.  As explained above a small count
likely means some ghost atoms were participating in their own events
and moved a longer distance.  If the value is large, it likely means
the communication cutoff for ghosts is too close to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} leading to
many not\sphinxhyphen{}found ghost atoms before the next event.  This may lead to a
reduced number of bonds being selected for biasing, since the code
assumes those atoms are part of highly strained bonds.  As explained
above, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}} command can be used
to set a longer cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 22, no two bonds should be biased if they are within a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} distance of each other.  This value should be zero, indicating
that no pair of biased bonds are closer than \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dcut} from each other.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for value 22 to be computed, the optional keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{check/bias} must be specified and it determines how often this check
is performed.  This is because performing the check incurs overhead,
so if only computed as often as requested.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result at the end of the run is the cumulative total from every
timestep the check was made.  Note that the value is a count of atoms
in bonds which found other atoms in bonds too close, so it is almost
always an over\sphinxhyphen{}count of the number of too\sphinxhyphen{}close bonds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Value 23 is simply the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{boost} factor times the number of
timesteps times the timestep size.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 24, events are checked for by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} command
once every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevent} timesteps.  This value is the count of those
timesteps on which one (or more) events was detected.  It is NOT the
number of distinct events, since more than one event may occur in the
same \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevent} time window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For value 25, each time the {\hyperref[\detokenize{hyper::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hyper}}}} command checks for an
event, it invokes a compute to flag zero or more atoms as
participating in one or more events.  E.g. atoms that have displaced
more than some distance from the previous quench state.  Value 25 is
the cumulative count of the number of atoms participating in any of
the events that were found.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Value 26 tallies the number of new bonds created by the bond reset
operation.  Bonds between a specific I,J pair of atoms may persist for
the entire hyperdynamics simulation if neither I or J are involved in
an event.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Value 27 computes the average boost for biased bonds only on this step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Value 28 is the count of bonds with an absolute value of strain \textgreater{}= q
on this step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value and vector values are all “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes a local vector of length the number of bonds
currently in the system.  The value for each bond is its \(C_{ij}\)
prefactor (bias coefficient).  These values can be can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  A particularly useful one is the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}} command which can be used to
histogram the Cij values to see if they are distributed reasonably
close to 1.0, which indicates a good choice of \(V^{max}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The local values calculated by this fix are unitless.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.
