\section{fix imd command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:fix-imd-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_imd::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{imd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{trate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{port}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
imd = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
port = port number on which the fix listens for an IMD client

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fscale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nowait}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
  off = coordinates are wrapped back into the principal unit cell (default)
  on = "unwrapped" coordinates using the image flags used
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fscale} arg = factor
  factor = floating point number to scale IMD forces (default: 1.0)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} arg = transmission rate of coordinate data sets (default: 1)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nowait} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
  off = LAMMPS waits to be connected to an IMD client before continuing (default)
  on = LAMMPS listens for an IMD client, but continues with the run
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{vmd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{imd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5678}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{comm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{imd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8888}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{trate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unwrap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fscale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements the “Interactive MD” (IMD) protocol which allows
realtime visualization and manipulation of MD simulations through the
IMD protocol, as initially implemented in VMD and NAMD.  Specifically
it allows LAMMPS to connect an IMD client, for example the \sphinxhref{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd}{VMD visualization program}, so that it can monitor the progress of the
simulation and interactively apply forces to selected atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If LAMMPS is compiled with the pre\sphinxhyphen{}processor flag \sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_ASYNC\_IMD
then fix imd will use POSIX threads to spawn a IMD communication
thread on MPI rank 0 in order to offload data reading and writing
from the main execution thread and potentially lower the inferred
latencies for slow communication links. This feature has only been
tested under linux.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The source code for this fix includes code developed by the Theoretical
and Computational Biophysics Group in the Beckman Institute for Advanced
Science and Technology at the University of Illinois at
Urbana\sphinxhyphen{}Champaign.  We thank them for providing a software interface that
allows codes like LAMMPS to hook to \sphinxhref{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd}{VMD}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upon initialization of the fix, it will open a communication port on
the node with MPI task 0 and wait for an incoming connection.  As soon
as an IMD client is connected, the simulation will continue and the
fix will send the current coordinates of the fix’s group to the IMD
client at every trate MD step. When using r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA, trate applies to
the steps of the outmost RESPA level.  During a run with an active IMD
connection also the IMD client can request to apply forces to selected
atoms of the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The port number selected must be an available network port number.  On
many machines, port numbers \textless{} 1024 are reserved for accounts with
system manager privilege and specific applications. If multiple imd
fixes would be active at the same time, each needs to use a different
port number.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nowait} keyword controls the behavior of the fix when no IMD
client is connected. With the default setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}, LAMMPS will
wait until a connection is made before continuing with the
execution. Setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{nowait} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} will have the LAMMPS code be ready
to connect to a client, but continue with the simulation. This can for
example be used to monitor the progress of an ongoing calculation
without the need to be permanently connected or having to download a
trajectory file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{trate} keyword allows to select how often the coordinate data is
sent to the IMD client. It can also be changed on request of the IMD
client through an IMD protocol message.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} keyword allows
to send “unwrapped” coordinates to the IMD client that undo the
wrapping back of coordinates into the principle unit cell, as done by
default in LAMMPS.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fscale} keyword allows to apply a scaling
factor to forces transmitted by the IMD client. The IMD protocols
stipulates that forces are transferred in kcal/mol/Angstrom under the
assumption that coordinates are given in Angstrom. For LAMMPS runs
with different units or as a measure to tweak the forces generated by
the manipulation of the IMD client, this option allows to make
adjustments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To connect VMD to a listening LAMMPS simulation on the same machine
with fix imd enabled, one needs to start VMD and load a coordinate or
topology file that matches the fix group.  When the VMD command
prompts appears, one types the command line:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
imd connect localhost 5678
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This assumes that \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix imd} was started with 5678 as a port
number for the IMD protocol.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The steps to do interactive manipulation of a running simulation in
VMD are the following:

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the Mouse menu of the VMD Main window, select “Mouse \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Force \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}
Atom”.  You may alternately select “Residue”, or “Fragment” to apply
forces to whole residues or fragments. Your mouse can now be used to
apply forces to your simulation. Click on an atom, residue, or fragment
and drag to apply a force. Click quickly without moving the mouse to
turn the force off. You can also use a variety of 3D position trackers
to apply forces to your simulation. Game controllers or haptic devices
with force\sphinxhyphen{}feedback such as the Novint Falcon or Sensable PHANTOM allow
you to feel the resistance due to inertia or interactions with neighbors
that the atoms experience you are trying to move, as if they were real
objects. See the \sphinxhref{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd/imd/}{VMD IMD Homepage} for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If IMD control messages are received, a line of text describing the
message and its effect will be printed to the LAMMPS output screen, if
screen output is active.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.  No global scalar or vector or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities
are stored by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter of this fix can be used with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not
invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_imd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MISC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When used in combination with VMD, a topology or coordinate file has
to be loaded, which matches (in number and ordering of atoms) the
group the fix is applied to. The fix internally sorts atom IDs by
ascending integer value; in VMD (and thus the IMD protocol) those will
be assigned 0\sphinxhyphen{}based consecutive index numbers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using multiple active IMD connections at the same time, each
needs to use a different port number.

\index{fix indent@\spxentry{fix indent}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix indent command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:fix-indent-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_indent::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{K}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
indent = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K = force constant for indenter surface (force/distance\textasciicircum{}2 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gstyle = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cylinder} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cone} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{plane}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere} args = x y z R
  x, y, z = position of center of indenter (distance units)
  R = sphere radius of indenter (distance units)
  any of x, y, z, R can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cylinder} args = dim c1 c2 R
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} = axis of cylinder
  c1, c2 = coords of cylinder axis in other 2 dimensions (distance units)
  R = cylinder radius of indenter (distance units)
  any of c1,c2,R can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cone} args = dim c1 c2 radlo radhi lo hi
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} = axis of cone
  c1, c2 = coords of cone axis in other 2 dimensions (distance units)
  radlo,radhi = cone radii at lo and hi end (distance units)
  lo,hi = bounds of cone in dim (distance units)
  any of c1, c2, radlo, radhi, lo, hi can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{plane} args = dim pos side
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} = plane perpendicular to this dimension
  pos = position of plane in dimension x, y, or z (distance units)
  pos can be a variable (see below)
  side = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{side} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{side} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{in} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{out}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{in} = the indenter acts on particles inside the sphere or cylinder or cone
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} = the indenter acts on particles outside the sphere or cylinder or cone
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  lattice = the geometry is defined in lattice units
  box = the geometry is defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{15.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}radius}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{side}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{in}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cylinder}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Insert an indenter within a simulation box.  The indenter repels all
atoms in the group that touch it, so it can be used to push into a
material or as an obstacle in a flow.  Alternatively, it can be used as a
constraining wall around a simulation; see the discussion of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{side} keyword below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gstyle} keyword selects the geometry of the indenter and it can
either have the value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cylinder}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cone}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{plane}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A spherical indenter (\sphinxstyleemphasis{gstyle} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere}) exerts a force of magnitude
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F(r) = - K \left( r - R \right)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
on each atom where \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} is the specified force constant, \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} is the
distance from the atom to the center of the indenter, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} is the
radius of the indenter.  The force is repulsive and F(r) = 0 for \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} \textgreater{}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{R}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A cylindrical indenter (\sphinxstyleemphasis{gstyle} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cylinder}) follows the same formula
for the force as a sphere, except that \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} is defined the distance
from the atom to the center axis of the cylinder.  The cylinder extends
infinitely along its axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17April2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A conical indenter (\sphinxstyleemphasis{gstyle} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cone}) is similar to a cylindrical indenter
except that it has a finite length (between \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}), and that two
different radii (one at each end, \sphinxstyleemphasis{radlo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{radhi}) can be defined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Spherical, cylindrical, and conical indenters account for periodic
boundaries in two ways.  First, the center point of a spherical
indenter (x,y,z) or axis of a cylindrical/conical indenter (c1,c2) is
remapped back into the simulation box, if the box is periodic in a
particular dimension.  This occurs every timestep if the indenter
geometry is specified with a variable (see below), e.g. it is moving
over time.  Second, the calculation of distance to the indenter center
or axis accounts for periodic boundaries.  Both of these mean that an
indenter can effectively move through and straddle one or more
periodic boundaries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A planar indenter (\sphinxstyleemphasis{gstyle} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{plane}) behaves like an axis\sphinxhyphen{}aligned
infinite\sphinxhyphen{}extent wall with the same force expression on atoms in the
system as before, but where \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} is the position of the plane and \sphinxstyleemphasis{r\sphinxhyphen{}R}
is the distance of an from the plane.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{side} parameter of the
plane is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} then it will indent from the lo end of the
simulation box, meaning that atoms with a coordinate less than the
plane’s current position will be pushed towards the hi end of the box
and atoms with a coordinate higher than the plane’s current position
will feel no force.  Vice versa if \sphinxstyleemphasis{side} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the 4 quantities defining a spherical indenter’s geometry can
be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, namely \sphinxstyleemphasis{x},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}.  For a cylindrical indenter, any of the 3
quantities \sphinxstyleemphasis{c1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{c2}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}, can be a variable.  For a conical
indenter, any of the 6 quantities \sphinxstyleemphasis{c1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{c2}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{radlo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{radhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo},
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} can be a variable.  For a planar indenter, the single value
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pos} can be a variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If any of these values is a variable, it should be specified as
v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable
will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to define the
indenter geometry.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various
mathematical functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
command keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and
elapsed time.  Thus it is easy to specify indenter properties that
change as a function of time or span consecutive runs in a continuous
fashion.  For the latter, see the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{elaplong} keyword of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if a spherical indenter’s x\sphinxhyphen{}position is specified as v\_x,
then this variable definition will keep it’s center at a relative
position in the simulation box, 1/4 of the way from the left edge to
the right edge, even if the box size changes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{xlo + 0.25*lx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly, either of these variable definitions will move the indenter
from an initial position at 2.5 at a constant velocity of 5:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2.5 + 5*elaplong*dt}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdisplace}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{2.5,5}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a spherical indenter’s radius is specified as v\_r, then these
variable definitions will grow the size of the indenter at a specified
rate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{r0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{rate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{r}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}r0 + step*dt*v\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{side} keyword is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{out}, which is the default,
then particles outside the indenter are pushed away from its outer
surface, as described above.  This only applies to spherical,
cylindrical, and conical indenters.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{side} keyword is
specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{in}, the action of the indenter is reversed.  Particles
inside the indenter are pushed away from its inner surface.  In other
words, the indenter is now a containing wall that traps the particles
inside it.  If the radius shrinks over time, it will squeeze the
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define the indenter geometry.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard
distance units as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command,
e.g. Angstroms for units = real or metal.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the
distance units are in lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}}
command must have been previously used to define the lattice spacing.
The (x,y,z) coords of the indenter position are scaled by the x,y,z
lattice spacings respectively.  The radius of a spherical or
cylindrical indenter is scaled by the x lattice spacing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the units keyword only affects indenter geometry parameters
specified directly with numbers, not those specified as variables.  In
the latter case, you should use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlat} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command if you want to include
lattice spacings in a variable formula.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The force constant \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} is not affected by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword.  It is
always in force/distance\textasciicircum{}2 units where force and distance are defined
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command.  If you wish K to be scaled by
the lattice spacing, you can define K with a variable whose formula
contains \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlat} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{k}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xlat}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xlat}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}k}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy of interaction between atoms and the
indenter to the global potential energy of the system as part of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for
this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}. The energy of
each particle interacting with the indenter is K/3 (r \sphinxhyphen{} R)\textasciicircum{}3.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar energy and a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector of
forces (on the indenter), which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar and vector values
calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.  Note that if you
define the indenter geometry with a variable using a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
formula, LAMMPS uses the iteration count in the minimizer as the
timestep.  But it is almost certainly a bad idea to have the indenter
change its position or size during a minimization.  LAMMPS does not
check if you have done this.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the atom/indenter interaction energy to be included in
the total potential energy of the system (the quantity being
minimized), you must enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_indent:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are side = out and units = lattice.

\section{fix ipi command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:fix-ipi-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ipi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{address}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{port}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[unix]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[reset]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ipi = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
address = internet address (FQDN or IP), or UNIX socket name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
port = port number (ignored for UNIX sockets)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{unix} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unix} args = none = use a unix socket
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} args = none = reset electrostatics at each call
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ipi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{my.server.com}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12345}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ipi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mysocket}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{666}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reset}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix enables LAMMPS to be run as a client for the i\sphinxhyphen{}PI Python
wrapper {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ipi:ipihome}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(IPI)}}}}. i\sphinxhyphen{}PI is a universal force engine,
designed to perform advanced molecular simulations, with a special
focus on path integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) simulation.
The philosophy behind i\sphinxhyphen{}PI is to separate the evaluation of the
energy and forces, which is delegated to the client, and the evolution
of the dynamics, that is the responsibility of i\sphinxhyphen{}PI. This approach also
simplifies combining energies computed from different codes, which
can for instance be useful to mix first\sphinxhyphen{}principles calculations,
empirical force fields or machine\sphinxhyphen{}learning potentials.
The following publication {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ipi:ipicpc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(IPI\sphinxhyphen{}CPC\sphinxhyphen{}2014)}}}} discusses the
overall implementation of i\sphinxhyphen{}PI, and focuses on path\sphinxhyphen{}integral techniques,
while a later release {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ipi:ipicpc2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(IPI\sphinxhyphen{}CPC\sphinxhyphen{}2019)}}}} introduces several
additional features and simulation schemes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The communication between i\sphinxhyphen{}PI and LAMMPS takes place using sockets,
and is reduced to the bare minimum. All the parameters of the dynamics
are specified in the input of i\sphinxhyphen{}PI, and all the parameters of the force
field must be specified as LAMMPS inputs, preceding the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix ipi} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The server address must be specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{address} argument, and
can be either the IP address, the fully\sphinxhyphen{}qualified name of the server,
or the name of a UNIX socket for local, faster communication. In the
case of internet sockets, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{port} argument specifies the port
number on which i\sphinxhyphen{}PI is listening, while the \sphinxstyleemphasis{unix} optional switch
specifies that the socket is a UNIX socket.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that there is no check of data integrity, or that the atomic
configurations make sense. It is assumed that the species in the i\sphinxhyphen{}PI
input are listed in the same order as in the data file of LAMMPS. The
initial configuration is ignored, as it will be substituted with the
coordinates received from i\sphinxhyphen{}PI before forces are ever evaluated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A note of caution when using potentials that contain long\sphinxhyphen{}range
electrostatics, or that contain parameters that depend on box size:
all of these options will be initialized based on the cell size in the
LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}side initial configuration and kept constant during the run.
This is required to e.g. obtain reproducible and conserved forces.
If the cell varies too wildly, it may be advisable to re\sphinxhyphen{}initialize
these interactions at each call. This behavior can be requested by
setting the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reset} switch.


\subsection{Obtaining i\sphinxhyphen{}PI}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:obtaining-i-pi}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are the commands to set up a virtual environment and install
i\sphinxhyphen{}PI into it with all its dependencies via the PyPI repository and
the pip package manager.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }ipienv
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }ipienv/bin/activate
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }ipi
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no restart information associated with this fix, since all
the dynamical parameters are dealt with by i\sphinxhyphen{}PI.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_ipi:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using this fix on anything other than all atoms requires particular
care, since i\sphinxhyphen{}PI will know nothing on atoms that are not those whose
coordinates are transferred. However, one could use this strategy to
define an external potential acting on the atoms that are moved by
i\sphinxhyphen{}PI.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since the i\sphinxhyphen{}PI code uses atomic units internally, this fix needs to
convert LAMMPS data to and from its {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{specified units}}}}
accordingly when communicating with i\sphinxhyphen{}PI.  This is not possible for
reduced units (“units lj”) and thus \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix ipi} will stop with an error in
this case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MISC package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.
Because of the use of UNIX domain sockets, this fix will only
work in a UNIX environment.

\section{fix langevin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:fix-langevin-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
langevin = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart can be a variable (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp = damping parameter (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or factor
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not thermostat rotational degrees of freedom via the angular momentum
  factor = do thermostat rotational degrees of freedom via the angular momentum and apply numeric scale factor as discussed below
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vfull} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vhalf}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = use standard formulation
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{vfull} = use Gronbech\sphinxhyphen{}Jensen/Farago formulation
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{vhalf} = use 2GJ formulation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not thermostat rotational degrees of freedom via the angular velocity
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = do thermostat rotational degrees of freedom via the angular velocity
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} values = type ratio
  type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
  ratio = factor by which to scale the damping coefficient
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not tally the energy added/subtracted to atoms
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = do tally the energy added/subtracted to atoms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not set total random force to zero
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = set total random force to zero
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{699483}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48279}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48279}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.333}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a Langevin thermostat as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin:schneider1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Schneider)}}}}
to a group of atoms which models an interaction with a background
implicit solvent.  Used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, this command
performs Brownian dynamics (BD), since the total force on each atom
will have the form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F = & F_c + F_f + F_r \\
F_f = & - \frac{m}{\mathrm{damp}} v \\
F_r \propto & \sqrt{\frac{k_B T m}{dt~\mathrm{damp}}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_c\) is the conservative force computed via the usual
inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style}}}}, etc).  The \(F_f\) and \(F_r\)
terms are added by this fix on a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle basis.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/tstat}}}} command for a thermostatting
option that adds similar terms on a pairwise basis to pairs of
interacting particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_f\) is a frictional drag or viscous damping term proportional to
the particle’s velocity.  The proportionality constant for each atom is
computed as \(\frac{m}{\mathrm{damp}}\), where \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the mass of the
particle and damp is the damping factor specified by the user.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_r\) is a force due to solvent atoms at a temperature \(T\)
randomly bumping into the particle.  As derived from the
fluctuation/dissipation theorem, its magnitude as shown above is
proportional to \(\sqrt{\frac{k_B T m}{dt~\mathrm{damp}}}\), where
\(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, \(T\) is the desired temperature,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the mass of the particle, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} is the timestep size, and damp is
the damping factor.  Random numbers are used to randomize the direction
and magnitude of this force as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin:dunweg1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dunweg)}}}},
where a uniform random number is used (instead of a Gaussian random
number) for speed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that unless you use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} keywords, the
thermostat effect of this fix is applied to only the translational
degrees of freedom for the particles, which is an important
consideration for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles, which have rotational degrees
of freedom, are being thermostatted.  The translational degrees of
freedom can also have a bias velocity removed from them before
thermostatting takes place; see the description below.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command which performs Nose/Hoover
thermostatting AND time integration, this fix does NOT perform time
integration.  It only modifies forces to effect thermostatting.  Thus
you must use a separate time integration fix, like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} to actually update the velocities and positions of atoms
using the modified forces.  Likewise, this fix should not normally be
used on atoms that also have their temperature controlled by another
fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for
a discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The desired temperature at each timestep is a ramped value during the
run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  In this case, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} setting is
ignored.  If the value is a variable, it should be specified as
v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable
will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine the
target temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus it is easy to specify a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
temperature with optional time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp} parameter is specified in time units and determines how
rapidly the temperature is relaxed.  For example, a value of 100.0 means
to relax the temperature in a timespan of (roughly) 100 time units
(\(\tau\) or fs or ps \sphinxhyphen{} see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).  The
damp factor can be thought of as inversely related to the viscosity of
the solvent.  I.e. a small relaxation time implies a high\sphinxhyphen{}viscosity
solvent and vice versa.  See the discussion about \(\gamma\) and
viscosity in the documentation for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}}
command for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The random \# \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} must be a positive integer.  A Marsaglia random
number generator is used.  Each processor uses the input seed to
generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random numbers.
Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two runs on
different numbers of processors.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword/value option pairs are used in the following ways.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} keywords enable thermostatting of
rotational degrees of freedom in addition to the usual translational
degrees of freedom.  This can only be done for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A simulation using atom\_style sphere defines an omega for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
spheres.  A simulation using atom\_style ellipsoid defines a finite
size and shape for aspherical particles and an angular momentum.
The Langevin formulas for thermostatting the rotational degrees of
freedom are the same as those above, where force is replaced by
torque, m is replaced by the moment of inertia I, and v is replaced by
omega (which is derived from the angular momentum in the case of
aspherical particles).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The rotational temperature of the particles can be monitored by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/sphere}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
temp/asphere}}}} commands with their rotate
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} keyword there is also a scale factor of
\(\frac{10.0}{3.0}\) that is applied as a multiplier on the
\(F_f\) (damping) term in the equation above and of
\(\sqrt{\frac{10.0}{3.0}}\) as a multiplier on the \(F_r\) term.
This does not affect the thermostatting behavior of the Langevin
formalism but ensures that the randomized rotational diffusivity of
spherical particles is correct.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} keyword a similar scale factor is needed which is
\(\frac{10.0}{3.0}\) for spherical particles, but is anisotropic for
aspherical particles (e.g. ellipsoids).  Currently LAMMPS only applies
an isotropic scale factor, and you can choose its magnitude as the
specified value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} keyword.  If your aspherical particles
are (nearly) spherical than a value of \(\frac{10.0}{3.0} =
3.\overline{3}\) is a good choice.  If they are highly aspherical, a
value of 1.0 is as good a choice as any, since the effects on rotational
diffusivity of the particles will be incorrect regardless.  Note that
for any reasonable scale factor, the thermostatting effect of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} keyword on the rotational temperature of the aspherical
particles should still be valid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} allows the damp factor to be scaled up or down by
the specified factor for atoms of that type.  This can be useful when
different atom types have different sizes or masses.  It can be used
multiple times to adjust damp for several atom types.  Note that
specifying a ratio of 2 increases the relaxation time which is
equivalent to the solvent’s viscosity acting on particles with
\(\frac{1}{2}\) the diameter.  This is the opposite effect of scale
factors used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}} command, since the
damp factor in fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin} is inversely related to the \(\gamma\)
factor in fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{viscous}.  Also note that the damping factor in fix
\sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin} includes the particle mass in Ff, unlike fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{viscous}.
Thus the mass and size of different atom types should be accounted for
in the choice of ratio values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} enables the calculation of the cumulative energy
added/subtracted to the atoms as they are thermostatted.  Effectively
it is the energy exchanged between the infinite thermal reservoir and
the particles.  As described below, this energy can then be printed
out or added to the potential energy of the system to monitor energy
conservation.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This accumulated energy does NOT include kinetic energy removed
by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} flag. LAMMPS will print a warning when both options are
active.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} can be used to eliminate drift due to the
thermostat. Because the random forces on different atoms are
independent, they do not sum exactly to zero.  As a result, this fix
applies a small random force to the entire system, and the
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of the system undergoes a slow random walk.  If the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the total random force is set exactly
to zero by subtracting off an equal part of it from each atom in the
group.  As a result, the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of a system with zero initial
momentum will not drift over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} can be used to run the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin:gronbech-jensen}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Gronbech\sphinxhyphen{}Jensen/Farago}}}} time\sphinxhyphen{}discretization of the Langevin model.  As
described in the papers cited below, the purpose of this method is to
enable longer timesteps to be used (up to the numerical stability
limit of the integrator), while still producing the correct Boltzmann
distribution of atom positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The current implementation provides the user with the option to output
the velocity in one of two forms: \sphinxstyleemphasis{vfull} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vhalf}, which replaces
the outdated option \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} option \sphinxstyleemphasis{vfull} outputs the
on\sphinxhyphen{}site velocity given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin:gronbech-jensen}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Gronbech\sphinxhyphen{}Jensen/Farago}}}}; this velocity is shown to be systematically lower
than the target temperature by a small amount, which grows
quadratically with the timestep.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} option \sphinxstyleemphasis{vhalf} outputs the
2GJ half\sphinxhyphen{}step velocity given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin:id1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Gronbech Jensen/Gronbech\sphinxhyphen{}Jensen}}}}; for linear systems, this velocity is shown to not
have any statistical errors for any stable time step.  An overview of
statistically correct Boltzmann and Maxwell\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann sampling of true
on\sphinxhyphen{}site and true half\sphinxhyphen{}step velocities is given in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin:id2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Gronbech\sphinxhyphen{}Jensen}}}}.  Regardless of the choice
of output velocity, the sampling of the configurational distribution
of atom positions is the same, and linearly consistent with the target
temperature.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the random number generator
is not saved in restart files, this means you cannot do “exact”
restarts with this fix, where the simulation continues on the same as
if no restart had taken place.  However, in a statistical sense, a
restarted simulation should produce the same behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}
you have defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure, as described above.  For consistency, the group used by
this fix and by the compute should be the same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}, but only if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} keyword to set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} page for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.
Note that calculation of this quantity also requires setting the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} do not choose damp=dt/2. \sphinxstyleemphasis{gjf} is not compatible
with run\_style respa.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/tstat}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are angmom = no, omega = no, scale = 1.0 for all
types, tally = no, zero = no, gjf = no.

\index{fix langevin/drude@\spxentry{fix langevin/drude}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix langevin/drude command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:fix-langevin-drude-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tcom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp\PYGZus{}com}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed\PYGZus{}com}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tdrude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp\PYGZus{}drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed\PYGZus{}drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
langevin/drude = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tcom = desired temperature of the centers of mass (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp\_com = damping parameter for the thermostat on centers of mass (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed\_com = random number seed to use for white noise of the thermostat on centers of mass (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tdrude = desired temperature of the Drude oscillators (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp\_drude = damping parameter for the thermostat on Drude oscillators (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed\_drude = random number seed to use for white noise of the thermostat on Drude oscillators (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not set total random force on centers of mass to zero
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = set total random force on centers of mass to zero
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19377}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{83451}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{298.15}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19377}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{83451}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input scripts available: examples/PACKAGES/drude


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply two Langevin thermostats as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:jiang1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jiang1)}}}} for
thermalizing the reduced degrees of freedom of Drude oscillators.
This link describes how to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermalized Drude oscillator model}}}} in LAMMPS and polarizable models in LAMMPS
are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_polarizable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto polarizable}}}} doc
page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Drude oscillators are a way to simulate polarizables atoms, by
splitting them into a core and a Drude particle bound by a harmonic
bond.  The thermalization works by transforming the particles degrees
of freedom by these equations.  In these equations upper case denotes
atomic or center of mass values and lower case denotes Drude particle
or dipole values. Primes denote the transformed (reduced) values,
while bare letters denote the original values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Velocities:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}V' = \frac {M\, V + m\, v} {M'}\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}v' = v - V\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Masses:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}M' = M + m\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}m' = \frac {M\, m } {M'}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Langevin forces are computed as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F' = - \frac {M'} {\mathtt{damp_com}}\, V' + F_r'\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f' = - \frac {m'} {\mathtt{damp_drude}}\, v' + f_r'\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_r'\) is a random force proportional to
\(\sqrt { \frac {2\, k_B \mathtt{Tcom}\, m'}                  {\mathrm dt\, \mathtt{damp_com} }         }\).
\(f_r'\) is a random force proportional to
\(\sqrt { \frac {2\, k_B \mathtt{Tdrude}\, m'}                  {\mathrm dt\, \mathtt{damp_drude} }         }\).
Then the real forces acting on the particles are computed from the inverse
transform:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F = \frac M {M'}\, F' - f'\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f = \frac m {M'}\, F' + f'\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also thermostats non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atoms in the group at
temperature \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tcom}, as if they had a massless Drude partner.  The
Drude particles themselves need not be in the group. The center of
mass and the dipole are thermostatted iff the core atom is in the
group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the thermostat effect of this fix is applied to only the
translational degrees of freedom of the particles, which is an
important consideration if finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles, which have
rotational degrees of freedom, are being thermostatted. The
translational degrees of freedom can also have a bias velocity removed
from them before thermostatting takes place; see the description below.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} command, this fix does
NOT perform time integration. It only modifies forces to effect
thermostatting. Thus you must use a separate time integration fix, like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} to actually update the
velocities and positions of atoms using the modified forces.
Likewise, this fix should not normally be used on atoms that also have
their temperature controlled by another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires each atom know whether it is a Drude particle or
not.  You must therefore use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude}}}} command to
specify the Drude status of each atom type.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
only the Drude core atoms need to be in the group specified for
this fix. A Drude electron will be transformed together with its cores
even if it is not itself in the group.  It is safe to include Drude
electrons or non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atoms in the group. The non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable
atoms will simply be thermostatted as if they had a massless Drude
partner (electron).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ghost atoms need to know their velocity for this fix to act
correctly.  You must use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify}}}} command to
enable this, e.g.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{comm\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tcom} is the target temperature of the centers of mass, which would
be used to thermostat the non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atoms.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdrude} is the
(normally low) target temperature of the core\sphinxhyphen{}Drude particle pairs
(dipoles).  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tcom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdrude} can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is a variable, it should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name. In this case,
the variable will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to
determine the target temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: The temperature thermostatting the core\sphinxhyphen{}Drude particle pairs
should be chosen low enough, so as to mimic as closely as possible the
self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent minimization. It must however be high enough, so that
the dipoles can follow the local electric field exerted by the
neighboring atoms. The optimal value probably depends on the
temperature of the centers of mass and on the mass of the Drude
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{damp\_com} is the characteristic time for reaching thermal equilibrium
of the centers of mass.  For example, a value of 100.0 means to relax
the temperature of the centers of mass in a timespan of (roughly) 100
time units (tau or fs or ps \sphinxhyphen{} see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}
command).  \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp\_drude} is the characteristic time for reaching
thermal equilibrium of the dipoles. It is typically a few timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed\_com} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed\_drude} are positive integers. They set
the seeds of the Marsaglia random number generators used for
generating the random forces on centers of mass and on the
dipoles. Each processor uses the input seed to generate its own unique
seed and its own stream of random numbers.  Thus the dynamics of the
system will not be identical on two runs on different numbers of
processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} can be used to eliminate drift due to the
thermostat on centers of mass. Because the random forces on different
centers of mass are independent, they do not sum exactly to zero.  As
a result, this fix applies a small random force to the entire system,
and the momentum of the total center of mass of the system undergoes a
slow random walk.  If the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the total
random force on the centers of mass is set exactly to zero by
subtracting off an equal part of it from each center of mass in the
group. As a result, the total center of mass of a system with zero
initial momentum will not drift over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual temperatures of cores and Drude particles, in
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass and relative coordinates, respectively, can be
calculated using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/drude}}}}
command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Usage example for rigid bodies in the NPT ensemble:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{comm\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{TEMP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{drude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1256}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{13977}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NPH}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ATOMS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rigid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{nph}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molecule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NVE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{DRUDES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{TDRUDE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{drude}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cpu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{etotal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ebond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ecoul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{elong}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}TDRUDE[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}TDRUDE[2]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Comments:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Drude particles should not be in the rigid group, otherwise the Drude
oscillators will be frozen and the system will lose its
polarizability.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zero yes} avoids a drift of the center of mass of
the system, but is a bit slower.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use two different random seeds to avoid unphysical correlations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Temperature is controlled by the fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin/drude}, so the
time\sphinxhyphen{}integration fixes do not thermostat.  Don’t forget to
time\sphinxhyphen{}integrate both cores and Drude particles.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pressure is time\sphinxhyphen{}integrated only once by using \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve} for Drude
particles and \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} for atoms/cores (or vice versa). Do not use \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph}
for both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperatures of cores and Drude particles are calculated by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/drude}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Contrary to the alternative thermostatting using Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat
fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude_transform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude/transform}}}}, the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_modify} command is not required here, because the fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph}
computes the global pressure even if its group is \sphinxstyleemphasis{ATOMS}. This is
what we want. If we thermostatted \sphinxstyleemphasis{ATOMS} using \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt}, the pressure
should be the global one, but the temperature should be only that of
the cores. That’s why the command \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_modify} should be called in
that case.

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the random number generator
is not saved in restart files, this means you cannot do “exact”
restarts with this fix, where the simulation continues on the same as
if no restart had taken place.  However, in a statistical sense, a
restarted simulation should produce the same behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}
you have defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure, as described above. For consistency, the group used by the
compute should include the group of this fix and the Drude particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude}}}},
