\section{fix langevin/eff command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:fix-langevin-eff-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
langevin/eff = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp = damping parameter (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zero}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} values = type ratio
    type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
    ratio = factor by which to scale the damping coefficient
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not tally the energy added/subtracted to atoms
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = do tally the energy added/subtracted to atoms
\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zero} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do not set total random force to zero
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = set total random force to zero
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{699483}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48279}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a Langevin thermostat as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:schneider2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Schneider)}}}}
to a group of nuclei and electrons in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}} model.  Used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/eff}}}},
this command performs Brownian dynamics (BD), since the total force on
each atom will have the form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F   = & F_c + F_f + F_r \\
F_f = & - \frac{m}{\mathrm{damp}} v \\
F_r \propto &  \sqrt{\frac{k_B T m}{dt~\mathrm{damp}}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_c\) is the conservative force computed via the usual
inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}}).
The \(F_f\) and \(F_r\) terms are added by this fix on a
per\sphinxhyphen{}particle basis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this fix is exactly like that described by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} command, except that the
thermostatting is also applied to the radial electron velocity for
electron particles.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_eff:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the random number generator is not
saved in restart files, this means you cannot do “exact” restarts with
this fix, where the simulation continues on the same as if no restart
had taken place.  However, in a statistical sense, a restarted
simulation should produce the same behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}
you have defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure, as described above.  For consistency, the group used by
this fix and by the compute should be the same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}, but only if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} keyword to set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} page for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.
Note that calculation of this quantity also requires setting the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tally} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{fix langevin/spin@\spxentry{fix langevin/spin}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix langevin/spin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:fix-langevin-spin-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tdamp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
langevin/spin = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = desired temperature of the bath (temperature units, K in metal units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tdamp = transverse magnetic damping parameter (adim)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{21}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a Langevin thermostat as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:mayergoyz1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Mayergoyz)}}}} to the
magnetic spins associated to the atoms.
Used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/spin}}}}, this command performs
Brownian dynamics (BD).
A random torque and a transverse dissipation are applied to each spin i according to
the following stochastic differential equation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} \frac{d \vec{s}_{i}}{dt} = \frac{1}{\left(1+\lambda^2 \right)} \left( \left(
 \vec{\omega}_{i} +\vec{\eta} \right) \times \vec{s}_{i} + \lambda\, \vec{s}_{i}
\times\left( \vec{\omega}_{i} \times\vec{s}_{i} \right) \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\lambda\) the transverse damping, and \(\eta\) a random vector.
This equation is referred to as the stochastic Landau\sphinxhyphen{}Lifshitz (sLL)
equation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The components of \(\eta\) are drawn from a Gaussian probability
law. Their amplitude is defined as a proportion of the temperature of
the external thermostat T (in K in metal units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
More details about this implementation are reported in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:tranchida2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: due to the form of the sLL equation, this fix has to be defined just
before the nve/spin fix (and after all other magnetic fixes).
As an example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{precession}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zeeman}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{21}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{moving}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
is correct, but defining a force/spin command after the langevin/spin command
would give an error message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: The random \# \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} must be a positive integer.  A Marsaglia random
number generator is used.  Each processor uses the input seed to
generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random numbers.
Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two runs on
different numbers of processors.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the random number generator
is not saved in restart files, this means you cannot do “exact”
restarts with this fix, where the simulation continues on the same as
if no restart had taken place.  However, in a statistical sense, a
restarted simulation should produce the same behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin/spin} fix is part of the SPIN package.  This style is
only enabled if LAMMPS was built with this package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The numerical integration has to be performed with \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix nve/spin}
when \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix langevin/spin} is enabled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix has to be the last defined magnetic fix before the time
integration fix (e.g. \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix nve/spin}).


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/spin}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_precession_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix precession/spin}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_langevin_spin:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{fix lb/fluid@\spxentry{fix lb/fluid}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix lb/fluid command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:fix-lb-fluid-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{viscosity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lb/fluid = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nevery = update the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid every this many timesteps (should normally be 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
viscosity = the fluid viscosity (units of mass/(time*length)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
density = the fluid density.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{noise} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{stencil} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_restart} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{write\_restart} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zwall\_velocity} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressurebcx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bodyforce} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{D3Q19} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dumpxdmf} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{linearInit} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dof} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleGamma} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{a0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{npits} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dx} values = dx\_LB = the lattice spacing.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dm} values = dm\_LB = the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann mass unit.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{noise} values = Temperature seed
    Temperature = fluid temperature.
    seed = random number generator seed (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{stencil} values = 2 (trilinear stencil, the default), 3 (3\sphinxhyphen{}point immersed boundary stencil), or 4 (4\sphinxhyphen{}point Keys\textquotesingle{} interpolation stencil)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_restart} values = restart file = name of the restart file to use to restart a fluid run.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{write\_restart} values = N = write a restart file every N MD timesteps.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zwall\_velocity} values = velocity\_bottom velocity\_top = velocities along the y\sphinxhyphen{}direction of the bottom and top walls (located at z=zmin and z=zmax).
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pressurebcx} values = pgradav = imposes a pressure jump at the (periodic) x\sphinxhyphen{}boundary of pgradav*Lx*1000.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bodyforce} values = bodyforcex bodyforcey bodyforcez = the x,y and z components of a constant body force added to the fluid.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{D3Q19} values = none (used to switch from the default D3Q15, 15 velocity lattice, to the D3Q19, 19 velocity lattice).
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dumpxdmf} values = N file timeI
    N = output the force and torque every N timesteps
    file = output file name
    timeI = 1 (use simulation time to index xdmf file), 0 (use output frame number to index xdmf file)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linearInit} values = none = initialize density and velocity using linear interpolation (default is uniform density, no velocities)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dof} values = dof = specify the number of degrees of freedom for temperature calculation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleGamma} values = type gammaFactor
    type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}N)
    gammaFactor = factor to scale the \sphinxstyleemphasis{setGamma} gamma value by, for the specified atom type.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{a0} values = a\_0\_real = the square of the speed of sound in the fluid.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{npits} values = npits h\_p l\_p l\_pp l\_e
    npits = number of pit regions
    h\_p = z\sphinxhyphen{}height of pit regions (floor to bottom of slit)
    l\_p = x\sphinxhyphen{}length of pit regions
    l\_pp = x\sphinxhyphen{}length of slit regions between consecutive pits
    l\_e = x\sphinxhyphen{}length of slit regions at ends
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wp} values = w\_p = y\sphinxhyphen{}width of slit regions (defaults to full width if not present or if sw active)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} values = none  (turns on y\sphinxhyphen{}sidewalls (in xz plane) if npits option active)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0009982071}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0009982071}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{noise}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2761}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dumpxdmf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fflow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressurebcx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npits}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{40}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 24Mar2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implement a lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid on a uniform mesh covering the
LAMMPS simulation domain.  Note that this fix was updated in 2022 and is
not backward compatible with the previous version.  If you need the
previous version, please download an older version of LAMMPS.  The MD
particles described by \sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} apply a velocity dependent force to
the fluid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann algorithm solves for the fluid motion governed by
the Navier Stokes equations,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\partial_t \rho + \partial_{\beta}\left(\rho u_{\beta}\right)= & 0 \\
\partial_t\left(\rho u_{\alpha}\right) + \partial_{\beta}\left(\rho u_{\alpha} u_{\beta}\right) = & \partial_{\beta}\sigma_{\alpha \beta} + F_{\alpha} + \partial_{\beta}\left(\eta_{\alpha \beta \gamma \nu}\partial_{\gamma} u_{\nu}\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\eta_{\alpha \beta \gamma \nu} = \eta\left[\delta_{\alpha \gamma}\delta_{\beta \nu} + \delta_{\alpha \nu}\delta_{\beta \gamma} - \frac{2}{3}\delta_{\alpha \beta}\delta_{\gamma \nu}\right] + \Lambda \delta_{\alpha \beta}\delta_{\gamma \nu}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\rho\) is the fluid density, \sphinxstyleemphasis{u} is the local
fluid velocity, \(\sigma\) is the stress tensor, \sphinxstyleemphasis{F} is a local external
force, and \(\eta\) and \(\Lambda\) are the shear and bulk viscosities
respectively.  Here, we have implemented
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\sigma_{\alpha \beta} = -P_{\alpha \beta} = -\rho a_0 \delta_{\alpha \beta}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(a_0\) set to \(\frac{1}{3} \frac{dx}{dt}^2\) by default.
You should not normally need to change this default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The algorithm involves tracking the time evolution of a set of partial
distribution functions which evolve according to a velocity discretized
version of the Boltzmann equation,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\left(\partial_t + e_{i\alpha}\partial_{\alpha}\right)f_i = -\frac{1}{\tau}\left(f_i - f_i^{eq}\right) + W_i\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the first term on the right hand side represents a single time
relaxation towards the equilibrium distribution function, and
\(\tau\) is a parameter physically related to the viscosity.  On a
technical note, we have implemented a 15 velocity model (D3Q15) as
default; however, the user can switch to a 19 velocity model (D3Q19)
through the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{D3Q19} keyword.  Physical variables are then
defined in terms of moments of the distribution functions,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\rho = & \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i} f_i \\
\rho u_{\alpha} = & \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i} f_i e_{i\alpha}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Full details of the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann algorithm used can be found in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:fluid-denniston}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Denniston et al.}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fluid is coupled to the MD particles described by \sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} through
a velocity dependent force.  The contribution to the fluid force on a
given lattice mesh site j due to MD particle \(\alpha\) is
calculated as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{\bf F}_{j \alpha} = \gamma \left({\bf v}_n - {\bf u}_f \right) \zeta_{j\alpha}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{v}_n\) is the velocity of the MD particle,
\(\mathbf{u}_f\) is the fluid velocity interpolated to the particle
location, and \(\gamma\) is the force coupling constant.  This
force, as with most forces in LAMMPS, and hence the velocities, are
calculated at the half\sphinxhyphen{}time step. \(\zeta\) is a weight assigned to
the grid point, obtained by distributing the particle to the nearest
lattice sites.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The force coupling constant, \(\gamma\), is calculated
according to
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\gamma = \frac{2m_um_v}{m_u+m_v}\left(\frac{1}{\Delta t}\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, \(m_v\) is the mass of the MD particle, \(m_u\) is a
representative fluid mass at the particle location, and \(\Delta t\)
is the time step.  The fluid mass \(m_u\) that the MD particle
interacts with is calculated internally.  This coupling is chosen to
constrain the particle and associated fluid velocity to match at the end
of the time step.  As with other constraints, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{shake}}}}, this constraint can remove degrees of freedom from the
simulation which are accounted for internally in the algorithm.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
While this fix applies the force of the particles on the fluid, it
does not apply the force of the fluid to the particles.  There is
only one option to include this hydrodynamic force on the particles,
and that is through the use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lb/viscous}}}}
fix.  This fix adds the hydrodynamic force to the total force acting
on the particles, after which any of the built\sphinxhyphen{}in LAMMPS integrators
can be used to integrate the particle motion.  If the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lb/viscous}}}} fix is NOT used to add the
hydrodynamic force to the total force acting on the particles, this
physically corresponds to a situation in which an infinitely massive
particle is moving through the fluid (since collisions between the
particle and the fluid do not act to change the particle’s velocity).
In this case, setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleGamma} to \sphinxhyphen{}1 for the corresponding
particle type will explicitly take this limit (of infinite particle
mass) in computing the force coupling for the fluid force.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Physical parameters describing the fluid are specified through
\sphinxstyleemphasis{viscosity} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{density}.  These parameters should all be given in
terms of the mass, distance, and time units chosen for the main LAMMPS
run, as they are scaled by the LB timestep, lattice spacing, and mass
unit, inside the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dx} keyword allows the user to specify a value for the LB grid
spacing and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dm} keyword allows the user to specify the LB mass
unit.  Inside the fix, parameters are scaled by the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann
timestep, \(dt_{LB}\), grid spacing, \(dx_{LB}\), and mass unit,
\(dm_{LB}\).  \(dt_{LB}\) is set equal to
\(\mathrm{nevery}\cdot dt_{MD}\), where \(dt_{MD}\) is the MD
timestep.  By default, \(dm_{LB}\) is set equal to 1.0, and
\(dx_{LB}\) is chosen so that \(\frac{\tau}{dt} = \frac{3\eta
dt}{\rho dx^2}\) is approximately equal to 1.
\begin{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Care must be taken when choosing both a value for \(dx_{LB}\),
and a simulation domain size.  This fix uses the same subdivision of
the simulation domain among processors as the main LAMMPS program.  In
order to uniformly cover the simulation domain with lattice sites, the
lengths of the individual LAMMPS subdomains must all be evenly
divisible by \(dx_{LB}\).  If the simulation domain size is cubic,
with equal lengths in all dimensions, and the default value for
\(dx_{LB}\) is used, this will automatically be satisfied.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{noise} keyword is used, followed by a positive temperature
value, and a positive integer random number seed, the thermal LB algorithm
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:adhikari}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Adhikari et al.}}}} is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{stencil} is used, the value sets the number of
interpolation points used in each direction.  For this, the user has the
choice between a trilinear stencil (\sphinxstyleemphasis{stencil} 2), which provides a
support of 8 lattice sites, or the 3\sphinxhyphen{}point immersed boundary method
stencil (\sphinxstyleemphasis{stencil} 3), which provides a support of 27 lattice sites, or
the 4\sphinxhyphen{}point Keys’ interpolation stencil (stencil 4), which provides a
support of 64 lattice sites.  The trilinear stencil is the default as it
is better suited for simulation of objects close to walls or other
objects, due to its smaller support.  The 3\sphinxhyphen{}point stencil provides
smoother motion of the lattice and is suitable for particles not likely
to be to close to walls or other objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{write\_restart} is used, followed by a positive integer,
N, a binary restart file is printed every N LB timesteps.  This restart
file only contains information about the fluid.  Therefore, a LAMMPS
restart file should also be written in order to print out full details
of the simulation.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When a large number of lattice grid points are used, the restart
files may become quite large.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to restart the fluid portion of the simulation, the keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_restart} is specified, followed by the name of the binary
lb\_fluid restart file to be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{zwall\_velocity} keyword is used y\sphinxhyphen{}velocities are assigned to
the lower and upper walls.  This keyword requires the presence of
walls in the z\sphinxhyphen{}direction.  This is set by assigning fixed boundary
conditions in the z\sphinxhyphen{}direction.  If fixed boundary conditions are
present in the z\sphinxhyphen{}direction, and this keyword is not used, the walls
are assumed to be stationary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressurebcx} keyword is used, a pressure jump (implemented by a
step jump in density) is imposed at the (periodic) x\sphinxhyphen{}boundary.  The
value set specifies what would be the resulting equilibrium average
pressure gradient in the x\sphinxhyphen{}direction if the system had a constant
cross\sphinxhyphen{}section (i.e. resistance to flow).  It is converted to a pressure
jump by multiplication by the system size in the x\sphinxhyphen{}direction.  As this
value should normally be quite small, it is also assumed to be scaled
by 1000.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bodyforce} keyword is used, a constant body force is added to
the fluid, defined by it’s x, y and z components.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{D3Q19} is used, the 19 velocity (D3Q19) lattice is
used by the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann algorithm.  By default, the 15 velocity
(D3Q15) lattice is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dumpxdmf} keyword is used, followed by a positive integer, N,
and a file name, the fluid densities and velocities at each lattice site
are output to an xdmf file every N timesteps.  This is a binary file
format that can be read by visualization packages such as \sphinxhref{https://www.paraview.org/}{Paraview} .  The xdmf file format contains a time
index for each frame dump and the value timeI = 1 uses simulation time
while 0 uses the output frame number to index xdmf file.  The later can
be useful if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_vtk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump vtk}}}} command is used to output
the particle positions at the same timesteps and you want to visualize
both the fluid and particle data together in \sphinxhref{https://www.paraview.org/}{Paraview} .

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleGamma} keyword allows the user to scale the \(\gamma\)
value by a factor, gammaFactor, for a given atom type.  Setting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleGamma} to \sphinxhyphen{}1 for the corresponding particle type will explicitly
take the limit of infinite particle mass in computing the force coupling
for the fluid force (see note above).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{a0} keyword is used, the value specified is used for the square
of the speed of sound in the fluid.  If this keyword is not present, the
speed of sound squared is set equal to
\(\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{dx_{LB}}{dt_{LB}}\right)^2\).  Setting
\(a0 > (\frac{dx_{LB}}{dt_{LB}})^2\) is not allowed, as this may
lead to instabilities.  As the speed of sound should usually be much
larger than any fluid velocity of interest, its value does not normally
have a significant impact on the results.  As such, it is usually best
to use the default for this option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{npits} keyword (followed by integer arguments: npits, h\_p, l\_p,
l\_pp, l\_e) sets the fluid domain to the pits geometry.  These arguments
should only be used if you actually want something more complex than a
rectangular/cubic geometry.  The npits value sets the number of pits
regions (arranged along x).  The remaining arguments are sizes measured
in multiples of dx\_lb: h\_p is the z\sphinxhyphen{}height of the pit regions, l\_p is
the x\sphinxhyphen{}length of the pit regions, l\_pp is the length of the region
between consecutive pits (referred to as a “slit” region), and l\_e is
the x\sphinxhyphen{}length of the slit regions at each end of the channel.  The pit
geometry must fill the system in the x\sphinxhyphen{}direction but can be longer, in
which case it is truncated (which enables asymmetric entrance/exit end
sections).  The additional \sphinxstyleemphasis{wp} keyword allows the width (in
y\sphinxhyphen{}direction) of the pit to be specified (the default is full width) and
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} keyword indicates that there should be sidewalls in the
y\sphinxhyphen{}direction (default is periodic in y\sphinxhyphen{}direction).  These parameters are
illustrated below:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
For further details, as well as descriptions and results of several test
runs, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:fluid-denniston}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Denniston et al.}}}}.  Please include a
citation to this paper if the lb\_fluid fix is used in work contributing
to published research.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Due to the large size of the fluid data, this fix writes it’s own
binary restart files, if requested, independent of the main LAMMPS
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}; no information about \sphinxstyleemphasis{lb\_fluid}
is written to the main LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the current
temperature of the group of particles described by \sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} along with
the fluid constrained to move with them. The temperature is computed via
the kinetic energy of the group and fluid constrained to move with them
and the total number of degrees of freedom (calculated internally).  If
the particles are not integrated independently (such as via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
NVE}}}}) but have additional constraints imposed on them (such as
via integration using {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}) the degrees of
freedom removed from these additional constraints will not be properly
accounted for.  In this case, the user can specify the total degrees of
freedom independently using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dof} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix also computes a global array of values which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  There are 5 entries in
the array.  The first entry is the temperature of the fluid, the second
entry is the total mass of the fluid plus particles, the third through
fifth entries give the x, y, and z total momentum of the fluid plus
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the LATBOLTZ package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can only be used with an orthogonal simulation domain.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The boundary conditions for the fluid are specified independently to the
particles.  However, these should normally be specified consistently via
the main LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command (p p p, p p f, and p
f f are the only consistent possibilities).  Shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped boundary
conditions are not permitted with this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix must be used before any of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/viscous}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/momentum}}}} as the
fluid needs to be initialized before any of these routines try to access
its properties.  In addition, in order for the hydrodynamic forces to be
added to the particles, this fix must be used in conjunction with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lb/viscous}}}} fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix needs to be used in conjunction with a standard LAMMPS
integrator such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix NVE}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/viscous}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/momentum}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dx} is chosen such that \(\frac{\tau}{dt_{LB}} = \frac{3\eta dt_{LB}}{\rho dx_{LB}^2}\) is approximately equal to 1.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dm} is set equal to 1.0.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{a0} is set equal to \(\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{dx_{LB}}{dt_{LB}}\right)^2\).
The trilinear stencil is used as the default interpolation method.
The D3Q15 lattice is used for the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann algorithm.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:fluid-denniston}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Denniston et al.)} Denniston, C., Afrasiabian, N., Cole\sphinxhyphen{}Andre, M.G., Mackay, F. E., Ollila, S.T.T., and Whitehead, T., LAMMPS lb/fluid fix version 2: Improved Hydrodynamic Forces Implemented into LAMMPS through a lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid, Computer Physics Communications 275 (2022) \sphinxhref{https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpc.2022.108318}{108318} .

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:mackay2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Mackay and Denniston)} Mackay, F. E., and Denniston, C., Coupling MD particles to a lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid through the use of conservative forces, J. Comput. Phys. 237 (2013) 289\sphinxhyphen{}298.

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid:adhikari}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Adhikari et al.)} Adhikari, R., Stratford, K.,  Cates, M. E., and Wagner, A. J., Fluctuating lattice Boltzmann, Europhys. Lett. 71 (2005) 473\sphinxhyphen{}479.

\index{fix lb/momentum@\spxentry{fix lb/momentum}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix lb/momentum command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:fix-lb-momentum-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{momentum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lb/momentum = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nevery = adjust the momentum every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} values = xflag yflag zflag
  xflag,yflag,zflag = 0/1 to exclude/include each dimension.
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{momentum}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{momentum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is based on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix momentum}}}} command, and
was created to be used in place of that command, when a
lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid is present.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero the total linear momentum of the system, including both the atoms
specified by group\sphinxhyphen{}ID and the lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid every nevery
timesteps.  If there are no atoms specified by group\sphinxhyphen{}ID only the fluid momentum is affected.  This is accomplished by adjusting the particle velocities
and the fluid velocities at each lattice site.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix only considers the linear momentum of the system.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the subtraction is performed for each dimension.  This can
be changed by specifying the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}, along with a set of
three flags set to 0/1 in order to exclude/ include the corresponding
dimension.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Can only be used if a lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid has been created via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}} command, and must come after this
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the LATBOLTZ package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix momentum}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_momentum:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zeros the total system linear momentum in each dimension.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix lb/viscous@\spxentry{fix lb/viscous}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix lb/viscous command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:fix-lb-viscous-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{viscous}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lb/viscous = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{viscous}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is similar to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}} command, and
is to be used in place of that command when a lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid
is present using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}}.  This should be used in conjunction with one of the built\sphinxhyphen{}in LAMMPS integrators, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix NVE}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix adds a viscous force to each atom to cause it move with the same velocity as the fluid (an equal and opposite force is applied to the fluid via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}}).  When {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}} is called with the noise option, the atoms will also experience random forces which will thermalize them to the same temperature as the fluid.  In this way, the combination of this fix with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}} and a LAMMPS integrator like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix NVE}}}} is analogous to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} except here the fluid is explicit.  The temperature of the particles can be monitored via the scalar output of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For details of this fix, as well as descriptions and results of several
test runs, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:fluid-denniston2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Denniston et al.}}}}.  Please include a citation to
this paper if this fix is used in work contributing to published
research.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As described in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}} documentation:

\sphinxAtStartPar
“No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.  This fix should only
be used with damped dynamics minimizers that allow for
non\sphinxhyphen{}conservative forces.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{min_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{min\_style}}}} command
for details.”


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lb_viscous:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the LATBOLTZ package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Can only be used if a lattice\sphinxhyphen{}Boltzmann fluid has been created via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lb_fluid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lb/fluid}}}} command, and must come after this
command.

\section{fix lineforce command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lineforce:fix-lineforce-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lineforce:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_lineforce::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lineforce:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lineforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lineforce = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x y z = direction of line as a 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lineforce:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{hold}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lineforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_lineforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjust the forces on each atom in the group so that only the component
of force along the linear direction specified by the vector (x,y,z)
remains.  This is done by subtracting out components of force in the
plane perpendicular to the line.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the initial velocity of the atom is 0.0 (or along the line), then
it should continue to move along the line thereafter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_manifoldforce:examples}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_manifoldforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix subtracts each time step from the force the component along
the normal of the specified {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_manifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{manifold}}}}.  This can be
used in combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} to remove overlap
between particles while keeping them (roughly) constrained to the
given manifold, e.g. to set up a run with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/manifold/rattle}}}}.  I have found that
only \sphinxstyleemphasis{hftn} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{quickmin} with a very small time step perform
adequately though.

\index{fix mdi/qm@\spxentry{fix mdi/qm}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix mdi/qm command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:fix-mdi-qm-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{qm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{s}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{s}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mdi/qm = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mc}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  yes = request virial tensor from server code
  no = do not request virial tensor from server code
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  yes = add returned value from server code to LAMMPS quantities
  no = do not add returned values to LAMMPS quantities
\sphinxstyleemphasis{every} args = Nevery
  Nevery = request values from server code once every Nevery steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  yes = perform a one\sphinxhyphen{}time connection to the MDI engine code
  no = do not perform the connection operation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} args = N\_1 N\_2 ... N\_ntypes
  N\_1,N\_2,...N\_ntypes = chemical symbol for each of ntypes LAMMPS atom types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mc} args = mcfixID
  mcfixID = ID of a Monte Carlo fix designed to work with this fix
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{qm}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{qm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{virial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{qm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{every}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{elements}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Aug2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enables LAMMPS to act as a client with another server
code that will compute the total energy, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom forces, and total
virial for atom conformations and simulation box size/shapes that
LAMMPS sends it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typically the server code will be a quantum mechanics (QM) code, hence
the name of the fix.  However this is not required, the server code
could be another classical molecular dynamics code or LAMMPS itself.
The server code must support use of the \sphinxhref{https://molssi-mdi.github.io/MDI\_Library/html/index.html}{MDI Library} as
explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typically, to use this fix, the input script should not define any
other classical force field components, e.g. a pair style, bond style,
etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are example use cases for this fix, discussed further below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
perform an ab initio MD (AIMD) simulation with quantum forces

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
perform an energy minimization with quantum forces

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
perform a nudged elastic band (NEB) calculation with quantum forces

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
perform a QM calculation for a series of independent systems which
LAMMPS reads or generates once

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
run a classical MD simulation and calculate QM energy/forces once
every N steps on the current configuration

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
More generally any command which calculates per\sphinxhyphen{}atom forces can instead
use quantum forces by defining this fix.  Examples are the Monte Carlo
commands {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gcmc}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atom/swap}}}}, as well as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_born_matrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute born/matrix}}}} command.  The only requirement is that internally
the command invokes the post\_force() method of fixes such as this one,
which will trigger the quantum calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The code coupling performed by this command is done via the \sphinxhref{https://molssi-mdi.github.io/MDI\_Library/html/index.html}{MDI
Library}.
LAMMPS runs as an MDI driver (client), and sends MDI commands to an
external MDI engine code (server), e.g. a QM code which has support
for MDI.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto mdi}}}} page for more
information about how LAMMPS can operate as either an MDI driver or
engine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/mdi}} directory contains input scripts using this fix in
the various use cases discussed below.  In each case, two instances of
LAMMPS are used, once as an MDI driver, once as an MDI engine (surrogate
for a QM code).  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/mdi/README}} file explains how to launch
two codes so that they communicate via the MDI library using either MPI
or sockets.  Any QM code that supports MDI could be used in place of
LAMMPS acting as a QM surrogate.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto mdi}}}}
page for a current list (March 2022) of such QM codes.  The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM}} directory has examples for coupling LAMMPS to 3 QM
codes either via this fix or the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mdi/qmmm}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that an engine code can support MDI in either or both of two modes.
It can be used as a stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone code, launched at the same time as
LAMMPS.  Or it can be used as a plugin library, which LAMMPS loads.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi plugin}}}} command for how to trigger LAMMPS to load a
plugin library.  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/mdi/README}} file and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM/QM\sphinxhyphen{}code/README}} files explain how to launch the two
codes in either mode.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} keyword setting of yes or no determines whether LAMMPS
will request the QM code to also compute and return the QM
contribution to a stress tensor for the system which LAMMPS will
convert to a 6\sphinxhyphen{}element symmetric virial tensor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} determines whether the
energy and forces and virial returned by the QM code will be added to
the LAMMPS internal energy and forces and virial or not.  If the
setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} then the default {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial}}}} settings are also set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no} and your input scripts should not set them to yes.  See more
details on these fix\_modify settings below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whatever the setting for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword, the QM energy, forces, and
virial will be stored by the fix, so they can be accessed by other
commands.  See details below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} keyword determines how often the QM code will be invoked
during a dynamics run with the current LAMMPS simulation box and
configuration of atoms.  The QM code will be called once every
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} timesteps.  By default \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} = 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} keyword determines whether this fix performs a one\sphinxhyphen{}time
connection to the QM code.  The default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.  The only time a \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
is needed is if this command is used multiple times in an input script
and the MDI coupling is between two stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone codes (not plugin mode).
E.g. if it used inside a loop which also uses the {\hyperref[\detokenize{clear::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{clear}}}}
command to destroy the system (including this fix).  See the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/mdi/in.series.driver}} script as an example of this, where
LAMMPS is using the QM code to compute energy and forces for a series of
system configurations.  In this use case \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect no} is used along with
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi connect and exit}}}} command to one\sphinxhyphen{}time
initiate/terminate the connection outside the loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} keyword allows specification of what element each
LAMMPS atom type corresponds to.  This is specified by the chemical
symbol of the element, e.g. C or Al or Si.  A symbol must be specified
for each of the ntypes LAMMPS atom types.  Multiple LAMMPS types can
represent the same element.  Ntypes is typically specified via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command or in the data file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this keyword is specified, then this fix will send the MDI
“\textgreater{}ELEMENTS” command to the engine, to ensure the two codes are
consistent in their definition of atomic species.  If this keyword is
not specified, then this fix will send the MDI \textgreater{}TYPES command to the
engine.  This is fine if both the LAMMPS driver and the MDI engine are
initialized so that the atom type values are consistent in both codes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mc} keyword enables this fix to be used with a Monte Carlo (MC)
fix to calculate before/after quantum energies as part of the MC
accept/reject criterion.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gcmc}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
atom/swap}}}} commands can be used in this manner.
Specify the ID of the MC fix following the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mc} keyword.  This allows
the two fixes to coordinate when MC events are being calculated versus
MD timesteps between the MC events.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The following 3 example use cases are illustrated in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/mdi}} directory.  See its README file for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
(1) To run an ab initio MD (AIMD) dynamics simulation, or an energy
minimization with QM forces, or a multi\sphinxhyphen{}replica NEB calculation, use
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add yes} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{every 1} (the defaults).  This is so that every time
LAMMPS needs energy and forces, the QM code will be invoked.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both LAMMPS and the QM code should define the same system (simulation
box, atoms and their types) in their respective input scripts.  Note
that on this scenario, it may not be necessary for LAMMPS to define a
pair style or use a neighbor list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS will then perform the timestepping or minimization iterations
for the simulation.  At the point in each timestep or iteration when
LAMMPS needs the force on each atom, it communicates with the engine
code.  It sends the current simulation box size and shape (if they
change dynamically, e.g. during an NPT simulation), and the current
atom coordinates.  The engine code computes quantum forces on each
atom and the total energy of the system and returns them to LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if the AIMD simulation is an NPT or NPH model, or the energy
minimization includes {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_box_relax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix box relax}}}} to
equilibrate the box size/shape, then LAMMPS computes a pressure.  This
means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} keyword should be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} so that the QM
contribution to the pressure can be included.

\sphinxAtStartPar
(2) To run dynamics with a LAMMPS interatomic potential, and evaluate
the QM energy and forces once every 1000 steps, use \sphinxstyleemphasis{add no} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{every 1000}.  This could be useful for using an MD run to generate
randomized configurations which are then passed to the QM code to
produce training data for a machine learning potential.  A {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump
custom}}}} command could be invoked every 1000 steps to dump the
atom coordinates and QM forces to a file.  Likewise the QM energy and
virial could be output with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
(3) To do a QM evaluation of energy and forces for a series of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
independent systems (simulation box and atoms), use \sphinxstyleemphasis{add no} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{every 1}.  Write a LAMMPS input script which loops over the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
systems.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_multiple::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto multiple}}}} doc page for
details on looping and removing old systems.  The series of systems
could be initialized by reading them from data files with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} commands.  Or, for example, by using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} , {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_atoms}}}}, and/or {\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms
random}}}} commands to generate a series of different
systems.  At the end of the loop perform {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run 0}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_dump}}}} commands to invoke the QM code and
output the QM energy and forces.  As in (2) this be useful to produce
QM data for training a machine learning potential.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy computed by the QM code to the
global potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic
output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy yes}}}}, unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword is
set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, in which case the default setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution computed by the QM code to the global
pressure of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
virial yes}}}}, unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, in
which case the default setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the energy
returned by the QM code.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes a global vector with of length 6 which contains
the symmetric virial tensor values returned by the QM code.  It can
likewise be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering of values in the symmetric virial tensor is as follows:
vxx, vyy, vzz, vxy, vxz, vyz.  The values will be in pressure
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes a peratom array with 3 columns which contains
the peratom forces returned by the QM code.  It can likewise be
accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Assuming the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} (the default), the forces
computed by the QM code are used during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the potential energy associated with the QM forces to
be included in the total potential energy of the system (the
quantity being minimized), you MUST not disable the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix, which
means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} keyword should also be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} (the default).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MDI package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use LAMMPS as an MDI driver in conjunction with other MDI\sphinxhyphen{}enabled
codes (MD or QM codes), the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command should be used
to specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{metal} units.  This will ensure the correct unit
conversions between LAMMPS and MDI units.  The other code will also
perform similar unit conversions into its preferred units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS can also be used as an MDI driver in other unit choices it
supports, e.g. \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj}, but then no unit conversion to MDI units is
performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this fix is used in conjunction with a QM code that does not support
periodic boundary conditions (more specifically, a QM code that does not
support the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}CELL}} MDI command), the LAMMPS system must be fully
non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  I.e. no dimension of the system can be periodic.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi plugin}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi engine}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mdi/qmmm}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default for the optional keywords are virial = no, add = yes,
every = 1, connect = yes.

\sphinxstepscope

\section{fix mdi/qmmm command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:fix-mdi-qmmm-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{qmmm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{s}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{s}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mdi/qmmm = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  yes = request virial tensor from server code
  no = do not request virial tensor from server code
\sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
  yes = perform a one\sphinxhyphen{}time connection to the MDI engine code
  no = do not perform the connection operation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} args = N\_1 N\_2 ... N\_ntypes
  N\_1,N\_2,...N\_ntypes = chemical symbol for each of ntypes LAMMPS atom types
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
