\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enables LAMMPS to act as a client with another server code
to perform a coupled QM/MM (quantum\sphinxhyphen{}mechanics/molecular\sphinxhyphen{}mechanics)
simulation.  LAMMPS will perform classical MD (molecular mechanics
or MM) for the (typically larger) MM portion of the system.  A quantum
mechanics code will calculate quantum energy and forces for the QM
portion of the system.  The two codes work together to calculate the
energy and forces due to the cross interactions between QM and MM atoms.
The QM server code must support use of the \sphinxhref{https://molssi-mdi.github.io/MDI\_Library/html/index.html}{MDI Library} as
explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The partitioning of the system between QM and MM atoms is as follows.
Atoms in the specified group are QM atoms; the remaining atoms are MM
atoms.  The input script should thus define this partitioning.
See additional information below about other requirements for an input
script to use this fix and perform a QM/MM simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The code coupling performed by this command is done via the \sphinxhref{https://molssi-mdi.github.io/MDI\_Library/html/index.html}{MDI
Library}.
LAMMPS runs as an MDI driver (client), and sends MDI commands to an
external MDI engine code (server), in this case a QM code which has
support for MDI.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto mdi}}}} page for more
information about how LAMMPS can operate as either an MDI driver or
engine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM}} directory has sub\sphinxhyphen{}directories with example
input scripts using this fix in tandem with different QM codes.  The
README files in the sub\sphinxhyphen{}directories explain how to download and build
the various QM codes.  They also explain how to launch LAMMPS and the QM
code so that they communicate via the MDI library using either MPI or
sockets.  Any QM code that supports MDI could be used in addition to
those discussed in the sub\sphinxhyphen{}directories.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto mdi}}}} page for a current list (March 2022) of such QM codes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that an engine code can support MDI in either or both of two modes.
It can be used as a stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone code, launched at the same time as
LAMMPS.  Or it can be used as a plugin library, which LAMMPS loads.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi plugin}}}} command for how to trigger LAMMPS to load a
plugin library.  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM}} sub\sphinxhyphen{}directory README files
explains how to launch the two codes in either mode.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} setting determines which QM/MM coupling algorithm is used.
LAMMPS currently supports \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential} algorithms, based
on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mode} setting.  Both algorithms should give reasonably
accurate results, but some QM codes support only one of the two modes.
E.g. in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM}} directory, PySCF supports only \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct},
NWChem supports only \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential}, and LATTE currently supports
neither, so it cannot be used for QM/MM simulations using this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct} option passes the coordinates and charges of each MM atom
to the quantum code, in addition to the coordinates of each QM atom.
The quantum code returns forces on each QM atom as well as forces on
each MM atom.  The latter is effectively the force on MM atoms due to
the QM atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The input script for performing a \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct} mode QM/MM simulation should
do the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
delete all bonds (angles, dihedrals, etc) between QM atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
set the charge on each QM atom to zero

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
define no bonds (angles, dihedrals, etc) which involve both QM and MM atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
define a force field (pair, bonds, angles, optional kspace) for the entire system

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first two bullet can be performed using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third bullet is required to have a consistent model, but is not
checked by LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fourth bullet implies that non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic interactions
(e.g. van der Waals) between QM/QM and QM/MM pairs of atoms are
computed by LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM/PySCF/in.*}} files for examples of input
scripts for QM/MM simulations using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct} mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential} option passes the coordinates of each QM atom and a
Coulomb potential for each QM atom to the quantum code.  The latter is
calculated by performing a Coulombics\sphinxhyphen{}only calculation for the entire
system, subtracting all QM/QM pairwise Coulombic terms, and dividing
the Coulomb energy on each QM atom by the charge of the QM atom.  The
potential value represents the Coulombic influence of all the MM atoms
on each QM atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quantum code returns forces and charge on each QM atom.  The new
charges on the QM atom are used to re\sphinxhyphen{}calculate the MM force field,
resulting in altered forces on the MM atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The input script for performing a \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential} mode QM/MM simulation
should do the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
delete all bonds (angles, dihedrals, etc) between QM atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
define a hybrid pair style which includes a Coulomb\sphinxhyphen{}only pair sub\sphinxhyphen{}style

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
define no bonds (angles, dihedrals, etc) which involve both QM and MM atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
define a force field (pair, bonds, angles, optional kspace) for the entire system

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first operation can be performed using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command.  See the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM/NWChem/in.*}} files
for examples of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second operation is necessary so that this fix can calculate the
Coulomb potential for the QM atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third bullet is required to have a consistent model, but is not
checked by LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fourth bullet implies that non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic interactions
(e.g. van der Waals) between QM/QM and QM/MM pairs of atoms are computed
by LAMMPS.  However, some QM codes do not want the MM code (LAMMPS) to
compute QM/QM van der Waals interactions.  NWChem is an example.  In
this case, the coefficients for those interactions need to be turned
off, which typically requires the atom types for the QM atoms be
different than those for the MM atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/QUANTUM/NWChem/in.*}} files for examples of input
scripts for QM/MM simulations using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential} mode.  Those scripts
also illustrate how to turn off QM/QM van der Waals interactions.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} keyword setting of yes or no determines whether LAMMPS
will request the QM code to also compute and return the QM
contribution to a stress tensor for the system which LAMMPS will
convert to a 6\sphinxhyphen{}element symmetric virial tensor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{connect} keyword determines whether this fix performs a one\sphinxhyphen{}time
connection to the QM code.  The default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.  The only time a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no} is needed is if this command is used multiple times in an input
script.  E.g. if it used inside a loop which also uses the {\hyperref[\detokenize{clear::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{clear}}}} command to destroy the system (including this fix).  As
example would be a script which loop over a series of independent QM/MM
simulations, e.g. each with their own data file.  In this use case
\sphinxstyleemphasis{connect no} could be used along with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi connect and exit}}}} command to one\sphinxhyphen{}time initiate/terminate the connection outside
the loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{elements} keyword allows specification of what element each
LAMMPS atom type corresponds to.  This is specified by the chemical
symbol of the element, e.g. C or Al or Si.  A symbol must be specified
for each of the ntypes LAMMPS atom types.  Multiple LAMMPS types can
represent the same element.  Ntypes is typically specified via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}} command or in the data file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this keyword is specified, then this fix will send the MDI
“\textgreater{}ELEMENTS” command to the engine, to insure the two codes are
consistent in their definition of atomic species.  If this keyword is
not specified, then this fix will send the MDI \textgreater{}TYPES command to the
engine.  This is fine if both the LAMMPS driver and the MDI engine are
initialized so that the atom type values are consistent in both codes.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

The ordering of values in the symmetric virial tensor is as follows:

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes a peratom array with 3 columns which contains
the peratom forces returned by the QM code.  It can likewise be
accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  Note that
for \sphinxstyleemphasis{direct} mode this will be quantum forces on both QM and MM atoms.
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential} mode it will only be quantum forces on QM atoms; the
forces for MM atoms will be zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces computed by the QM code are used during an energy
minimization, invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the potential energy associated with the QM forces to
be included in the total potential energy of the system (the
quantity being minimized), you MUST not disable the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is part of the MDI package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use LAMMPS as an MDI driver in conjunction with other MDI\sphinxhyphen{}enabled
codes (MD or QM codes), the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command should be used
to specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{metal} units.  This will ensure the correct unit
conversions between LAMMPS and MDI units.  The other code will also
perform similar unit conversions into its preferred units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this fix is used in conjunction with a QM code that does not support
periodic boundary conditions (more specifically, a QM code that does not
support the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}CELL}} MDI command), the LAMMPS system must be fully
non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  I.e. no dimension of the system can be periodic.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi plugin}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mdi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mdi engine}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mdi_qm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mdi/qm}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mdi_qmmm:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default for the optional keywords are virial = no and connect = yes.

\index{fix meso/move@\spxentry{fix meso/move}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix meso/move command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:fix-meso-move-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meso}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
meso/move = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} args = Vx Vy Vz
  Vx,Vy,Vz = components of velocity vector (velocity units), any component can be specified as NULL
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} args = Ax Ay Az period
  Ax,Ay,Az = components of amplitude vector (distance units), any component can be specified as NULL
  period = period of oscillation (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} args = Px Py Pz Rx Ry Rz period
  Px,Py,Pz = origin point of axis of rotation (distance units)
  Rx,Ry,Rz = axis of rotation vector
  period = period of rotation (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} args = v\_dx v\_dy v\_dz v\_vx v\_vy v\_vz
  v\_dx,v\_dy,v\_dz = 3 variable names that calculate x,y,z displacement as function of time, any component can be specified as NULL
  v\_vx,v\_vy,v\_vz = 3 variable names that calculate x,y,z velocity as function of time, any component can be specified as NULL
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meso}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meso}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rotate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meso}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}myx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}myy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}VX}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}VY}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform updates of position, velocity, internal energy and local
density for mesoscopic particles in the group each timestep using the
specified settings or formulas, without regard to forces on the
particles. This can be useful for boundary, solid bodies or other
particles, whose movement can influence nearby particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this fix is exactly like that described by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_move::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix move}}}} command, except that particles’ density,
internal energy and extrapolated velocity are also updated.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The particles affected by this fix should not be time integrated by
other fixes (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sph}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph_stationary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
sph/stationary}}}}), since that will change their
positions and velocities twice.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As particles move due to this fix, they will pass through periodic
boundaries and be remapped to the other side of the simulation box,
just as they would during normal time integration (e.g. via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sph}}}} command).  It is up to you to decide
whether periodic boundaries are appropriate with the kind of
particle motion you are prescribing with this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed below, particles are moved relative to their initial
position at the time the fix is specified.  These initial coordinates
are stored by the fix in “unwrapped” form, by using the image flags
associated with each particle.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command
for a discussion of “unwrapped” coordinates.  See the Atoms section of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command for a discussion of image flags
and how they are set for each particle.  You can reset the image flags
(e.g. to 0) before invoking this fix by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set image}}}}
command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style moves particles at a constant velocity, so that their
position \sphinxstyleemphasis{X} = (x,y,z) as a function of time is given in vector
notation as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
X(t) = X0 + V * delta
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{X0} = (x0,y0,z0) is their position at the time the fix is
specified, \sphinxstyleemphasis{V} is the specified velocity vector with components
(Vx,Vy,Vz), and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the time elapsed since the fix was
specified.  This style also sets the velocity of each particle to V =
(Vx,Vy,Vz).  If any of the velocity components is specified as NULL,
then the position and velocity of that component is time integrated
the same as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sph}}}} command would perform, using
the corresponding force component on the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style is identical to using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
style with an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} that uses the
vdisplace() function.  E.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{V}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdisplace}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,\PYGZdl{}V}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}V}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style moves particles in an oscillatory fashion, so that
their position \sphinxstyleemphasis{X} = (x,y,z) as a function of time is given in vector
notation as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
X(t) = X0 + A sin(omega*delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{X0} = (x0,y0,z0) is their position at the time the fix is
specified, \sphinxstyleemphasis{A} is the specified amplitude vector with components
(Ax,Ay,Az), \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} is 2 PI / \sphinxstyleemphasis{period}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the time
elapsed since the fix was specified.  This style also sets the
velocity of each particle to the time derivative of this expression.
If any of the amplitude components is specified as NULL, then the
position and velocity of that component is time integrated the same as
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sph}}}} command would perform, using the
corresponding force component on the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style is identical to using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
style with {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}} that use the
swiggle() and cwiggle() functions.  E.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{omega}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{PI}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}T}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{swiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,\PYGZdl{}A,\PYGZdl{}T}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}omega}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}A\PYGZhy{}cwiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,\PYGZdl{}A,\PYGZdl{}T}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} style rotates particles around a rotation axis \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} =
(Rx,Ry,Rz) that goes through a point \sphinxstyleemphasis{P} = (Px,Py,Pz).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{period} of
the rotation is also specified.  The direction of rotation for the
particles around the rotation axis is consistent with the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand
rule: if your right\sphinxhyphen{}hand thumb points along \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}, then your fingers wrap
around the axis in the direction of rotation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style also sets the velocity of each particle to (omega cross
Rperp) where omega is its angular velocity around the rotation axis and
Rperp is a perpendicular vector from the rotation axis to the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style allows the position and velocity components of
each particle to be set by formulas specified via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command.  Each of the 6 variables is
specified as an argument to the fix as v\_name, where name is the
variable name that is defined elsewhere in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each variable must be of either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} style.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Equal}\sphinxhyphen{}style variables compute a single numeric quantity, that can be
a function of the timestep as well as of other simulation values.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atom}\sphinxhyphen{}style variables compute a numeric quantity for each particle, that
can be a function per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities, such as the particle’s position, as
well as of the timestep and other simulation values.  Note that this
fix stores the original coordinates of each particle (see note below) so
that per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity can be used in an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable formula.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 3 variables (v\_dx,v\_dy,v\_dz) specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
style are used to calculate a displacement from the particle’s original
position at the time the fix was specified.  The second 3 variables
(v\_vx,v\_vy,v\_vz) specified are used to compute a velocity for each
particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the 6 variables can be specified as NULL.  If both the
displacement and velocity variables for a particular x,y,z component
are specified as NULL, then the position and velocity of that
component is time integrated the same as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sph}}}}
command would perform, using the corresponding force component on the
particle.  If only the velocity variable for a component is specified
as NULL, then the displacement variable will be used to set the
position of the particle, and its velocity component will not be
changed. If only the displacement variable for a component is
specified as NULL, then the velocity variable will be used to set the
velocity of the particle, and the position of the particle will be
time integrated using that velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} velocity and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} amplitude and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate}
origin.  This setting is ignored for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
value selects standard units as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}
command, e.g. velocity in Angstroms/fs and amplitude and position
in Angstroms for units = real.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the velocity
units are in lattice spacings per time and the amplitude and position
are in lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have
been previously used to define the lattice spacing.  Each of these 3
quantities may be dependent on the x,y,z dimension, since the lattice
spacings can be different in x,y,z.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the original coordinates of moving particles to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, as well as the initial timestep, so that
the motion can be continuous in a restarted simulation.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the move positions are a function of the current
timestep and the initial timestep, you cannot reset the timestep to a
different value after reading a restart file, if you expect a fix move
command to work in an uninterrupted fashion.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The number of columns for each
atom is 3, and the columns store the original unwrapped x,y,z coords
of each particle.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values can be accessed on any timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}SMOOTH package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store density and internal energy as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sph}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be mesoscopic SPH/SDPD particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is incompatible with deformation controls that remap velocity,
for instance the \sphinxstyleemphasis{remap v} option of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_move::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix move}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sph::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix sph}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_meso_move:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default is units = lattice.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{fix\_modify AtC commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_modify_atc_commands:fix-modify-atc-commands}}\label{\detokenize{fix_modify_atc_commands::doc}}
\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix\_modify AtC add\_molecule@\spxentry{fix\_modify AtC add\_molecule}}\ignorespaces 

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC add\_molecule command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_add_molecule:fix-modify-atc-add-molecule-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_add_molecule:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_add_molecule::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_add_molecule:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}molecule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{tag}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
add\_molecule = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{small} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{large} = can be \sphinxstyleemphasis{small} if molecule size \textless{} cutoff radius, must be \sphinxstyleemphasis{large} otherwise

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tag = tag for tracking a molecule

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} = LAMMPS defined group\sphinxhyphen{}ID

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_add_molecule:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{group }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{WATERGROUP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom\_weight = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
method = \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{element} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_in}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} \textless{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID\textgreater{} \textless{}value\textgreater{}: atoms in specified group are assigned the constant value given

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}: volume per atom for specified lattice type (e.g. fcc) and parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{element}: element volume divided among atoms within element

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region}: volume per atom determined based on the atom count in the MD regions and their volumes. Note: meaningful only if atoms completely fill all the regions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{group}: volume per atom determined based on the atom count in a group and its volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{node}: (undocumented)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{node\_element}: (undocumented)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_in}\textless{}filename\textgreater{}: list of values for atoms are read\sphinxhyphen{}in from specified file

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:fix-modify-atc-boundary-dynamics-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boundary\PYGZus{}dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{on}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{damped\PYGZus{}harmonic}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{prescribed}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{coupled}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{none}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
boundary\_dynamics = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{damped\_harmonic} \sphinxstyleemphasis{prescribed} \sphinxstyleemphasis{coupled} \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets different schemes for controlling boundary atoms.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} will integrate
the boundary atoms using the velocity\sphinxhyphen{}verlet algorithm.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{damped\_harmonic}
uses a mass/spring/dashpot for the boundary atoms with added arguments
of the damping and spring constants followed by the ratio of the
boundary type mass to the desired mass.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{prescribed} forces the boundary
atoms to follow the finite element displacement.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{coupled} does the same.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Boundary atoms must be specified.  When using swaps between internal and
boundary atoms, the initial configuration must have already correctly
partitioned the two.

\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:related-atc-commands}}\begin{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{atc_boundary_dynamics:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{prescribed on}

useful for fully overlapping simulations.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_localized_lambda:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Turns the localization algorithms \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} for control algorithms
to restrict the influence of FE coupling or boundary conditions to a
region near the boundary of the MD region.  Control algorithms will not
affect atoms in elements not possessing faces on the boundary of the
region.  Flux\sphinxhyphen{}based control is localized via row\sphinxhyphen{}sum lumping while
quantity control is done by solving a truncated matrix equation.

None.

\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_momentum:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{control}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{momentum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{glc\PYGZus{}velocity}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_momentum:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The general version of \sphinxstyleemphasis{control} sets the numerical parameters for the
matrix solvers used in the specified control algorithm.  Many solution
approaches require iterative solvers, and these methods enable users to
provide the maximum number of iterations and the relative tolerance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{control momentum} version sets the momentum exchange mechanism from
the finite elements to the atoms, managed through a control algorithm.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} computes a scale factor for each atom to match the finite
element temperature.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{hoover} is a Gaussian least\sphinxhyphen{}constraint isokinetic
thermostat enforces that the nodal restricted atomic temperature matches
the finite element temperature.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{flux} is a similar mode, but rather
adds energy to the atoms based on conservation of energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{correction\_max\_iterations} sets the maximum number of iterations to
compute the second order in time correction term for lambda with the
fractional step method. The method uses the same tolerance as the
controller’s matrix solver.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_momentum:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only for be used with the specific controllers \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{momentum}.
They are ignored if a lumped solution is requested.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{control momentum} is only for be used with specific transfers: elastic
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} not valid with time filtering activated


\subsubsection{Related AtC commands}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_momentum:related-atc-commands}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_control_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify AtC control thermal}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_momentum:default}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{max\_iterations} is the number of rows in the matrix.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance} is 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}10.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_control_thermal:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The general version of \sphinxstyleemphasis{control} sets the numerical parameters for the
matrix solvers used in the specified control algorithm.  Many solution
approaches require iterative solvers, and these methods enable users to
provide the maximum number of iterations and the relative tolerance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{control thermal} version sets the energy exchange mechanism from
the finite elements to the atoms, managed through a control algorithm.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} computes a scale factor for each atom to match the finite
element temperature.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{hoover} is a Gaussian least\sphinxhyphen{}constraint isokinetic
thermostat enforces that the nodal restricted atomic temperature matches
the finite element temperature.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{flux} is a similar mode, but rather
adds energy to the atoms based on conservation of energy. \sphinxstyleemphasis{hoover} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flux} allow the prescription of sources or fixed temperatures on the
atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{correction\_max\_iterations} sets the maximum number of iterations to
compute the second order in time correction term for lambda with the
fractional step method. The method uses the same tolerance as the

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC decomposition command}

\label{\detokenize{atc_decomposition:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{decomposition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type =  \sphinxstyleemphasis{replicated\_memory} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{distributed\_memory}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_decomposition:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_decomposition:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command for assigning the distribution of work and memory for parallel
runs.  With \sphinxstyleemphasis{replicated\_memory} the nodal information is replicated on
each processor, and with \sphinxstyleemphasis{distributed\_memory} only the owned nodal
information kept on each processor.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{replicated\_memory} option
is most appropriate for simulations were the number of nodes is much
smaller than the number of atoms.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC fe\_md\_boundary command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary:fix-modify-atc-fe-md-boundary-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fe\PYGZus{}md\PYGZus{}boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{faceset}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{interpolate}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}boundary}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fe\_md\_boundary = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{faceset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{interpolate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_boundary}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fe\PYGZus{}md\PYGZus{}boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{interpolate}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifies different methods for computing fluxes between between the MD
and FE integration regions.  Faceset defines a faceset separating the MD
and FE regions and uses finite element face quadrature to compute the
flux.  Interpolate uses a reconstruction scheme to approximate the flux,
which is more robust but less accurate if the MD/FE boundary does
correspond to a faceset.  No boundary results in no fluxes between the
systems being computed.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fe_md_boundary:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{faceset} is used, all the AtC non\sphinxhyphen{}boundary atoms must lie within and
completely fill the domain enclosed by the faceset.

\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fix_flux:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix\PYGZus{}flux}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{faceSet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fix_flux:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command for fixing normal fluxes e.g. heat\_flux. This command only
prescribes the normal component of the physical flux, e.g. heat (energy)
flux. The units are in AtC units, i.e. derived from the LAMMPS length,
time, and mass scales.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_fix_flux:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only normal fluxes (Neumann data) can be prescribed.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC computes command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes:fix-modify-atc-computes-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{computes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{delete}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{per}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{volume}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{number}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
computes = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} = add or delete the calculation of an equivalent continuum field for the specified per\sphinxhyphen{}atom compute as volume or number density quantity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom compute; fields can be calculated for all per\sphinxhyphen{}atom computes available in LAMMPS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{volume} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{number} = select whether the created field is a per\sphinxhyphen{}unit\sphinxhyphen{}volume quantity or a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity as weighted by kernel functions

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{virial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stress}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{computes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{virial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volume}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{computes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{virial}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{centrosymmetry}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{centro}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{computes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{centrosymmetry}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{number}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculates continuum fields corresponding to specified per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{computes}}}} created by LAMMPS.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc hardy}}}}.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom compute
must be specified before the corresponding continuum field can be
requested.

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC fields command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:fix-modify-atc-fields-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fields}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{none}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fields}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{delete}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{list\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}fields}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fields = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} = output all or no fields

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} = add or delete the listed output fields

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
list\_of\_fields = one or more of the fields listed below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
density : mass per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
displacement : displacement vector

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
momentum : momentum per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
velocity : defined by momentum divided by density

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
projected\_velocity : simple kernel estimation of atomic velocities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature : temperature derived from the relative atomic kinetic energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic\_temperature : temperature derived from the full kinetic energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number\_density : simple kernel estimation of number of atoms per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stress : Cauchy stress tensor for eulerian analysis (atom\_element\_map), or first Piola\sphinxhyphen{}Kirchhoff stress tensor for lagrangian analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
transformed\_stress : first Piola\sphinxhyphen{}Kirchhoff stress tensor for eulerian analysis (atom\_element\_map), or Cauchy stress tensor for lagrangian analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
heat\_flux : spatial heat flux vector for eulerian, or referential heat flux vector for lagrangian

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
potential\_energy : potential energy per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic\_energy : kinetic energy per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermal\_energy : thermal energy (kinetic energy \sphinxhyphen{} continuum kinetic energy) per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
internal\_energy : total internal energy (potential + thermal) per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
energy : total energy (potential + kinetic) per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number\_density : number of atoms per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eshelby\_stress : configurational stress (energy\sphinxhyphen{}momentum) tensor defined by {\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:eshelby1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Eshelby)}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vacancy\_concentration : volume fraction of vacancy content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type\_concentration : volume fraction of a specific atom type

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fields}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{temperature}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allows modification of the fields calculated and output by the AtC
transfer class.  The commands are cumulative, e.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fields}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{none}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fields}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{temperature}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will only output the velocity and temperature fields.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc hardy}}}}.  Currently, the stress
and heat flux formulas are only correct for central force potentials,
e.g. Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones and EAM but not Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify AtC rates}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_hardy_computes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify AtC computes}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, no fields are output.

\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_kernel:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the localization kernel type and parameters for {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc hardy}}}}.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_kernel:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc hardy}}}}.  For bar kernel types,
half\sphinxhyphen{}width oriented along x\sphinxhyphen{}direction.  For cylinder kernel types,
cylindrical axis is assumed to be in z\sphinxhyphen{}direction.

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC on\_the\_fly command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:fix-modify-atc-on-the-fly-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}the\PYGZus{}fly}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{kernel}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{on}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{off}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
on\_the\_fly = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kernel} = specifies on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly calculation of \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kernel} matrix elements

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = activate or discontinue on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly mode

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}the\PYGZus{}fly}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}the\PYGZus{}fly}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kernel}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}the\PYGZus{}fly}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kernel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{off}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overrides normal mode of pre\sphinxhyphen{}calculating and storing bond pair\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}node a
nd kernel atom\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}node matrices. If activated, it will calculate elements
of these matrices during repeated calls of field computations
(i.e. “on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly”) and not store them for future use.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} flag is
optional \sphinxhyphen{} if omitted, on\_the\_fly will be activated for the specified
matrix.  Can be deactivated using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} flag.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc hardy}}}}.


\subsubsection{Related AtC commands}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:related-atc-commands}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc:atc-fix-modify}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{fix\_modify AtC command overview}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_on_the_fly:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly calculation is not active (i.e. off). However,
THE code does a memory allocation check to determine if it can store all
needed bond and kernel matrix elements. If this allocation fails,
on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly will be activated.

\sphinxstepscope

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC rates command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:fix-modify-atc-rates-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rates}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{delete}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{list\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}fields}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rates = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{add} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} = select whether to add or delete calculation of rates for the listed output fields

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
list\_of\_fields = one or more of the fields listed below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
density : mass per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
displacement : displacement vector

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
momentum : momentum per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
velocity : defined by momentum divided by density

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
projected\_velocity : simple kernel estimation of atomic velocities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature : temperature derived from the relative atomic kinetic energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic\_temperature : temperature derived from the full kinetic energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number\_density : simple kernel estimation of number of atoms per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stress : Cauchy stress tensor for eulerian analysis (atom\_element\_map), or first Piola\sphinxhyphen{}Kirchhoff stress tensor for lagrangian analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
transformed\_stress : first Piola\sphinxhyphen{}Kirchhoff stress tensor for eulerian analysis (atom\_element\_map), or Cauchy stress tensor for lagrangian analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
heat\_flux : spatial heat flux vector for eulerian, or referential heat flux vector for lagrangian

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
potential\_energy : potential energy per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic\_energy : kinetic energy per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermal\_energy : thermal energy (kinetic energy \sphinxhyphen{} continuum kinetic energy) per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
internal\_energy : total internal energy (potential + thermal) per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
energy : total energy (potential + kinetic) per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number\_density : number of atoms per unit volume

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eshelby\_stress : configurational stress (energy\sphinxhyphen{}momentum) tensor defined by {\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:eshelby2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Eshelby)}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vacancy\_concentration : volume fraction of vacancy content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type\_concentration : volume fraction of a specific atom type

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rates}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{stress}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rates}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stress}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requests calculation and output of rates (time derivatives) of the
fields from the AtC transfer class.  For Eulerian analysis (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_atom_element_map::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify AtC atom\_element\_map}}}}) these
rates are the partial time derivatives of the nodal fields, not the full
(material) time derivatives.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc hardy}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_hardy_fields::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify AtC fields}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atc_hardy_gradients::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify AtC fields}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{atc_hardy_rates:default}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_element_set:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{internal\PYGZus{}element\PYGZus{}set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{element\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
internal\_element\_set = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element\_set\_name = name of element set defining internal region, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_element_set:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{internal\PYGZus{}element\PYGZus{}set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myElementSet}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{internal\PYGZus{}element\PYGZus{}set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{off}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_element_set:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enables AtC to base the region for internal atoms to be an element
set. If no ghost atoms are used, all the AtC atoms must be constrained
to remain in this element set by the user, e.g., with walls. If boundary
atoms are used in conjunction with Eulerian atom maps AtC will partition
all atoms of a boundary or internal type to be of type internal if they
are in the internal region or to be of type boundary otherwise.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_element_set:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If boundary atoms are used in conjunction with Eulerian atom maps, the
Eulerian reset frequency must be an integer multiple of the Lammps
reneighbor frequency.

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC internal\_quadrature command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_quadrature:fix-modify-atc-internal-quadrature-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_quadrature:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_quadrature::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_quadrature:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{internal\PYGZus{}quadrature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{on}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{off}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[region]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
internal\_quadrature = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
on or off = select whether internal quadrature is enabled or not

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region = treat finite elements as within MD region (optional)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_quadrature:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_internal_quadrature:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command to use or not use atomic quadrature on internal elements fully
filled with atoms. By turning the internal quadrature off these elements
do not contribute to the governing PDE and the fields at the internal
nodes follow the weighted averages of the atomic data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional region tag specifies which finite element nodes will be treated
as being within the MD region. This option is only valid with
internal\_quadrature off.

sets the zero point for the potential energy density using the value

if no value is provided, or values provided within the specified

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

units for mass, length and time and are defined by the PDE being solved,

\label{\detokenize{atc_temperature_definition:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature\PYGZus{}definition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{kinetic}\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{n}{total}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature\_definition = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_temperature_definition:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the definition for the atomic temperature used to create the
finite element temperature.  The kinetic option is based only on the
kinetic energy of the atoms while the total option uses the total energy
(kinetic + potential) of an atom.


\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_temperature_definition:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is only valid when using thermal coupling.  Also, while not
a formal restriction, the user should ensure that associating a
potential energy with each atom makes physical sense for the total
option to be meaningful.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{fix\_modify AtC time\_integration command}
\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration:fix-modify-atc-time-integration-command}}\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration::doc}}

\subsubsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixID}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{time\PYGZus{}integration}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{descriptor}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AtC fixID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atc}}}} instance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
time\_integration = name of the AtC sub\sphinxhyphen{}command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
descriptor =  \sphinxstyleemphasis{gear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fractional\_step} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{verlet}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{AtC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{time\PYGZus{}integration}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fractional\PYGZus{}step}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command to select the thermal or momentum time integration.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Options for thermal time integration:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{gear}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
atomic velocity update with second order Verlet, nodal temperature update
with third or fourth order Gear, thermostats based on controlling power

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{fractional\_step}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
atomic velocity update with second order Verlet, mixed nodal temperature
update, 3/4 Gear for continuum and 2 Verlet for atomic contributions,
thermostats based on controlling discrete energy changes

\end{description}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Options for momentum time integration:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{verlet}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
atomic velocity update with second order Verlet, nodal temperature update
with second order Verlet, kinetostats based on controlling force

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{fractional\_step}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
atomic velocity update with second order Verlet, mixed nodal momentum
update, second order Verlet for continuum and exact second order Verlet for
atomic contributions, kinetostats based on controlling discrete
momentum changes

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{gear}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
atomic velocity update with second order Verlet, nodal temperature update
with third or fourth order Gear, kinetostats based on controlling power.

\end{description}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{atc_time_integration:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
None.
