\section{fix mol/swap command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:fix-mol-swap-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{X}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{itype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{jtype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atom/swap = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = invoke this fix every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
X = number of swaps to attempt every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
itype,jtype = two atom types (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label) to swap with each other

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = scaling temperature of the MC swaps (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = no conservation of kinetic energy after atom swaps
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = kinetic energy is conserved after atom swaps
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{29494}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mySwap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{482798}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{B}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mySwap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{B}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{482798}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs Monte Carlo swaps of two specified atom types within
a randomly selected molecule.  Two possible use cases are as follows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
First, consider a mixture of some molecules with atoms of itype and
other molecules with atoms of jtype.  The fix will select a random
molecule and attempt to swap all the itype atoms to jtype for the
first kind of molecule, or all the jtype atoms to itype for the second
kind.  Because the swap will only take place if it is energetically
favorable, the fix can be used to determine the miscibility of 2
different kinds of molecules much more quickly than just dynamics
would do it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Second, consider diblock co\sphinxhyphen{}polymers with two types of monomers itype
and jtype.  The fix will select a random molecule and attempt to do a
itype \textless{}\textendash{}\textgreater{} jtype swap of all those monomers within the molecule.  Thus
the fix can be used to find the energetically favorable fractions of
two flavors of diblock co\sphinxhyphen{}polymers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Intra\sphinxhyphen{}molecular swaps of atom types are attempted every N timesteps.  On
that timestep, X swaps are attempted.  For each attempt a single
molecule ID is randomly selected.  The range of possible molecule IDs
from loID to hiID is pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed before each run begins.  The
loID/hiID is set for the molecule with the smallest/largest ID which
has any itype or jtype atoms in it.  Note that if you define a system
with many molecule IDs between loID and hiID which have no itype or
jtype atoms, then the fix will be inefficient at performing swaps.
Also note that if atoms with molecule ID = 0 exist, they are not
considered molecules by this fix; they are assumed to be solvent atoms
or molecules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Candidate atoms for swapping must also be in the fix group.  Atoms
within the selected molecule which are not itype or jtype are ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When an atom is swapped from itype to jtype (or vice versa), if
charges are defined, the charge values for itype versus jtype atoms
are also swapped.  This requires that all itype atoms in the system
have the same charge value.  Likewise all jtype atoms in the system
must have the same charge value.  If this is not the case, LAMMPS
issues a warning that it cannot swap charge values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} keyword is set to yes, which is the default, and the
masses of itype and jtype atoms are different, then when a swap
occurs, the velocity of the swapped atom is rescaled by the sqrt of
the mass ratio, so as to conserve the kinetic energy of the atom.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential energy of the entire system is computed before and after
each swap is performed within a single molecule.  The specified
temperature T is used in the Metropolis criterion to accept or reject
the attempted swap.  If the swap is rejected all swapped values are
reversed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential energy calculations can include systems and models with
the following features:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
manybody pair styles, including EAM

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hybrid pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatics (kspace)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
triclinic systems

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
potential energy contributions from other fixes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the last bullet point, fixes can have an associated potential
energy. Examples of such fixes include: {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{efield}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gravity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{gravity}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{addforce}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{langevin}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_restrain::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restrain}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/berendsen}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/rescale}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{wall fixes}}}}.  For that
energy to be included in the total potential energy of the system (the
quantity used for the swap accept/reject decision), you MUST enable
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for that fix.  The
doc pages for individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} commands specify if this
should be done.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One comment on computational efficiency.  If the cutoff lengths
defined for the pair style are different for itype versus jtype
atoms (for any of their interactions with any other atom type), then
a new neighbor list needs to be generated for every attempted swap.
This is potentially expensive if N is small or X is large.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the fix to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This includes information about the random number
generator seed, the next timestep for MC exchanges, the number of
exchange attempts and successes etc.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an
input script that reads a restart file, so that the operation of the
fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For this to work correctly, the timestep must \sphinxstylestrong{not} be changed
after reading the restart with {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}.
The fix will try to detect it and stop with an error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global vector of length 2, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector values are
the following global cumulative quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
swap attempts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
swap accepts

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atom/swap}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gcmc}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mol_swap:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default is ke = yes.

\sphinxstepscope

momentum = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = adjust the momentum every this many timesteps
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID momentum/chunk N chunkID keyword values ...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
momentum/chunk = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = adjust the momentum per chunk every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chunkID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command

\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value settings may be appended to each of the fix commands:

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angular} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} values = xflag yflag zflag
  xflag,yflag,zflag = 0/1 to exclude/include each dimension
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angular} values = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} values = none
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_momentum:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix momentum zeroes the linear and/or angular momentum of the group of
atoms every N timesteps by adjusting the velocities of the atoms.
Fix momentum/chunk works equivalently, but operates on a per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk basis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One (or both) of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angular} keywords \sphinxstylestrong{must} be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} keyword is used, the linear momentum is zeroed by
subtracting the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity of the group or chunk from each
atom.  This does not change the relative velocity of any pair of atoms.
One or more dimensions can be excluded from this operation by setting
the corresponding flag to 0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angular} keyword is used, the angular momentum is zeroed by
subtracting a rotational component from each atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can be used to ensure the entire collection of atoms (or
a subset of them) does not drift or rotate during the simulation due
to random perturbations (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}
thermostatting).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} keyword enables conserving the kinetic energy of the group
or chunk of atoms by rescaling the velocities after the momentum was removed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} command can be used to create
initial velocities with zero aggregate linear and/or angular momentum.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_momentum:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by
this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\section{fix move command}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_move:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
move = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{transrot} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} args = Vx Vy Vz
  Vx,Vy,Vz = components of velocity vector (velocity units), any component can be specified as NULL
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} args = Ax Ay Az period
  Ax,Ay,Az = components of amplitude vector (distance units), any component can be specified as NULL
  period = period of oscillation (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} args = Px Py Pz Rx Ry Rz period
  Px,Py,Pz = origin point of axis of rotation (distance units)
  Rx,Ry,Rz = axis of rotation vector
  period = period of rotation (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{transrot} args = Vx Vy Vz Px Py Pz Rx Ry Rz period
  Vx,Vy,Vz = components of velocity vector (velocity units)
  Px,Py,Pz = origin point of axis of rotation (distance units)
  Rx,Ry,Rz = axis of rotation vector
  period = period of rotation (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} args = v\_dx v\_dy v\_dz v\_vx v\_vy v\_vz
  v\_dx,v\_dy,v\_dz = 3 variable names that calculate x,y,z displacement as function of time, any component can be specified as NULL
  v\_vx,v\_vy,v\_vz = 3 variable names that calculate x,y,z velocity as function of time, any component can be specified as NULL
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_move:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform updates of position and velocity for atoms in the group each
timestep using the specified settings or formulas, without regard to
forces on the atoms.  This can be useful for boundary or other atoms,
whose movement can influence nearby atoms.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The atoms affected by this fix should not normally be time integrated
by other fixes (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}), since that will change their positions and velocities
twice.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As atoms move due to this fix, they will pass through periodic
boundaries and be remapped to the other side of the simulation box,
just as they would during normal time integration (e.g. via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command).  It is up to you to decide whether
periodic boundaries are appropriate with the kind of atom motion you
are prescribing with this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed below, atoms are moved relative to their initial
position at the time the fix is specified.  These initial coordinates
are stored by the fix in “unwrapped” form, by using the image flags
associated with each atom.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command
for a discussion of “unwrapped” coordinates.  See the Atoms section
of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command for a discussion of image
flags and how they are set for each atom.  You can reset the image
flags (e.g. to 0) before invoking this fix by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set
image}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style moves atoms at a constant velocity, so that their
position \sphinxstyleemphasis{X} = (x,y,z) as a function of time is given in vector
notation as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
X(t) = X0 + V * delta
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{X0} = (x0,y0,z0) is their position at the time the fix is
specified, \sphinxstyleemphasis{V} is the specified velocity vector with components
(Vx,Vy,Vz), and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the time elapsed since the fix was
specified.  This style also sets the velocity of each atom to V =
(Vx,Vy,Vz).  If any of the velocity components is specified as NULL,
then the position and velocity of that component is time integrated
the same as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command would perform, using
the corresponding force component on the atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style is identical to using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
style with an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} that uses the
vdisplace() function.  E.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{V}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdisplace}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,\PYGZdl{}V}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}V}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style moves atoms in an oscillatory fashion, so that
their position \sphinxstyleemphasis{X} = (x,y,z) as a function of time is given in vector
notation as
\begin{sphinxalltt}
X(t) = X0 + A sin(omega*delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{X0} = (x0,y0,z0) is their position at the time the fix is
specified, \sphinxstyleemphasis{A} is the specified amplitude vector with components
(Ax,Ay,Az), \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} is 2 PI / \sphinxstyleemphasis{period}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the time elapsed
since the fix was specified.  This style also sets the velocity of each
atom to the time derivative of this expression.  If any of the amplitude
components is specified as NULL, then the position and velocity of that
component is time integrated the same as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}
command would perform, using the corresponding force component on the
atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} style is identical to using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
style with {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}} that use the
swiggle() and cwiggle() functions.  E.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{omega}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{PI}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}T}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{swiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,\PYGZdl{}A,\PYGZdl{}T}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}omega}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}A\PYGZhy{}cwiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,\PYGZdl{}A,\PYGZdl{}T}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{v\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}v}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} style rotates atoms around a rotation axis \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} = (Rx,Ry,Rz)
that goes through a point \sphinxstyleemphasis{P} = (Px,Py,Pz).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{period} of the
rotation is also specified.  The direction of rotation for the atoms
around the rotation axis is consistent with the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand rule: if your
right\sphinxhyphen{}hand thumb points along \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}, then your fingers wrap around the
axis in the direction of rotation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style also sets the velocity of each atom to (omega cross Rperp)
where omega is its angular velocity around the rotation axis and Rperp
is a perpendicular vector from the rotation axis to the atom.  If the
defined {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} assigns an angular velocity or
angular momentum or orientation to each atom ({\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom styles}}}} sphere, ellipsoid, line, tri, body), then
those properties are also updated appropriately to correspond to the
atom’s motion and rotation over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{transrot} style combines the effects of \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} so
that it is possible to prescribe a rotating group of atoms that also
moves at a constant velocity.  The arguments are for the translation
first and then for the rotation.  Since the rotation affects all
coordinate components, it is not possible to set any of the
translation vector components to NULL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style allows the position and velocity components of
each atom to be set by formulas specified via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command.  Each of the 6 variables is
specified as an argument to the fix as v\_name, where name is the
variable name that is defined elsewhere in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each variable must be of either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} style.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Equal}\sphinxhyphen{}style variables compute a single numeric quantity, that can be
a function of the timestep as well as of other simulation values.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Atom}\sphinxhyphen{}style variables compute a numeric quantity for each atom, that
can be a function per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities, such as the atom’s position, as
well as of the timestep and other simulation values.  Note that this fix
stores the original coordinates of each atom (see note below) so that
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity can be used in an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable formula.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 3 variables (v\_dx,v\_dy,v\_dz) specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable}
style are used to calculate a displacement from the atom’s original
position at the time the fix was specified.  The second 3 variables
(v\_vx,v\_vy,v\_vz) specified are used to compute a velocity for each
atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the 6 variables can be specified as NULL.  If both the
displacement and velocity variables for a particular x,y,z component
are specified as NULL, then the position and velocity of that
component is time integrated the same as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}
command would perform, using the corresponding force component on the
atom.  If only the velocity variable for a component is specified as
NULL, then the displacement variable will be used to set the position
of the atom, and its velocity component will not be changed.  If only
the displacement variable for a component is specified as NULL, then
the velocity variable will be used to set the velocity of the atom,
and the position of the atom will be time integrated using that
velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} velocity and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} amplitude and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate}
origin.  This setting is ignored for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{variable} style.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
value selects standard units as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}
command, e.g. velocity in Angstroms/fs and amplitude and position
in Angstroms for units = real.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the velocity
units are in lattice spacings per time and the amplitude and position
are in lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have
been previously used to define the lattice spacing.  Each of these 3
quantities may be dependent on the x,y,z dimension, since the lattice
spacings can be different in x,y,z.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_move:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the original coordinates of moving atoms to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}, as well as the initial timestep, so that the
motion can be continuous in a restarted simulation.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the move positions are a function of the current
timestep and the initial timestep, you cannot reset the timestep to a
different value after reading a restart file, if you expect a fix move
command to work in an uninterrupted fashion.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The number of columns for each
atom is 3, and the columns store the original unwrapped x,y,z coords of
each atom.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values can be accessed on any timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rRESPA time integration}}}}, this fix adjusts the
position and velocity of atoms on the outermost rRESPA level.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_move:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_move:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_move:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default is units = lattice.

\index{fix msst@\spxentry{fix msst}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix msst command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:fix-msst-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_msst::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shockvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
msst = style name of this fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dir = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
shockvel = shock velocity (strictly positive, distance/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dftb}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{q} value = cell mass\sphinxhyphen{}like parameter (mass\textasciicircum{}2/distance\textasciicircum{}4 units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} value = artificial viscosity (mass/length/time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} value = initial pressure in the shock equations (pressure units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} value = initial simulation cell volume in the shock equations (distance\textasciicircum{}3 units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{e0} value = initial total energy (energy units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} value = reduction in initial temperature (unitless fraction between 0.0 and 1.0)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dftb} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} for whether using MSST in conjunction with DFTB+
\sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} value = scale factor for improved energy conservation
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{q}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{q}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e4}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{v0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.3419}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m}{03}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{p0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.7797}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m}{03}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{9.72360}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m}{02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tscale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{q}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dftb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command performs the Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Scale Shock Technique (MSST)
integration to update positions and velocities each timestep to mimic
a compressive shock wave passing over the system. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst:reed}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Reed)}}}}
for a detailed description of this method.  The MSST varies the cell
volume and temperature in such a way as to restrain the system to the
shock Hugoniot and the Rayleigh line. These restraints correspond to
the macroscopic conservation laws dictated by a shock
front. \sphinxstyleemphasis{shockvel} determines the steady shock velocity that will be
simulated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To perform a simulation, choose a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} that provides volume
compression on the timescale of 100 fs to 1 ps.  If the volume is not
compressing, either the shock speed is chosen to be below the material
sound speed or \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} has been chosen inaccurately.  Volume compression
at the start can be sped up by using a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale}. Use
the smallest value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} that results in compression.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Under some special high\sphinxhyphen{}symmetry conditions, the pressure (volume)
and/or temperature of the system may oscillate for many cycles even
with an appropriate choice of mass\sphinxhyphen{}like parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}. Such
oscillations have physical significance in some cases.  The optional
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} keyword adds an artificial viscosity that helps break the system
symmetry to equilibrate to the shock Hugoniot and Rayleigh line more
rapidly in such cases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} is a factor between 0 and 1 that determines what
fraction of thermal kinetic energy is converted to compressive strain
kinetic energy at the start of the simulation.  Setting this parameter
to a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value may assist in compression at the start of
simulations where it is slow to occur.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0},or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} are not supplied, these quantities will
be calculated on the first step, after the energy specified by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} is removed.  The value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0} is not used in the dynamical
equations, but is used in calculating the deviation from the Hugoniot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} is a scaling term that can be added to the MSST
ionic equations of motion to account for drift in the conserved
quantity during long timescale simulations, similar to a Berendsen
thermostat. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst:reed}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Reed)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst:goldman2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Goldman)}}}} for more
details.  The value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.
A value of 0.0 means no contribution, a value of 1.0 means a full
contribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Values of shockvel less than a critical value determined by the
material response will not have compressive solutions. This will be
reflected in lack of significant change of the volume in the MSST.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all pressure styles, the simulation box stays orthogonal in shape.
Parrinello\sphinxhyphen{}Rahman boundary conditions (tilted box) are supported by
LAMMPS, but are not implemented for MSST.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure and potential energy each
timestep. To do this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp”
“pressure”, and “pe”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}MSST\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}MSST\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}MSST\PYGZus{}temp}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}MSST\PYGZus{}pe}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pe}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the IDs of the
new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + “\_MSST\_temp” or “MSST\_press” or
“\_MSST\_pe”.  The group for the new computes is “all”.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dftb} keyword is to allow this fix to be used when LAMMPS is
being driven by DFTB+, a density\sphinxhyphen{}functional tight\sphinxhyphen{}binding code. If the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dftb} is used with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, then the MSST equations
are altered to account for the electron entropy contribution to the
Hugonio relations and total energy.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst:reed2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Reed2)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst:goldman2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Goldman)}}}} for details on this contribution.  In this case,
you must define a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_external::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix external}}}} command in your
input script, which is used to callback to DFTB+ during the LAMMPS
timestepping.  DFTB+ will communicate its info to LAMMPS via that fix.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of all internal variables to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The progress of the MSST can be monitored by printing the global
scalar and global vector quantities computed by the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As mentioned above, the scalar is the cumulative energy change due to
the fix.  By monitoring the thermodynamic \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve} output, this can
be used to test if the MD timestep is sufficiently small for accurate
integration of the dynamic equations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The global vector contains four values in the following order.  The
vector values output by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{[}\sphinxstyleemphasis{dhugoniot}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{drayleigh}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_speed},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_position}{]}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dhugoniot} is the departure from the Hugoniot (temperature units).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{drayleigh} is the departure from the Rayleigh line (pressure units).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_speed} is the laboratory\sphinxhyphen{}frame Lagrangian speed (particle velocity) of the computational cell (velocity units).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_position} is the computational cell position in the reference frame moving at the shock speed. This is usually a good estimate of distance of the computational cell behind the shock front.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To print these quantities to the log file with descriptive column
headers, the following LAMMPS commands are suggested:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix              }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{msst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dhug}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}msst[1]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dray}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}msst[2]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{lgr\PYGZus{}vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}msst[3]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{lgr\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}msst[4]}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pzz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{econserve}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}dhug}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}dray}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}lgr\PYGZus{}vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}lgr\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}msst}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style is part of the SHOCK package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All cell dimensions must be periodic. This fix can not be used with a
triclinic cell.  The MSST fix has been tested only for the group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
all.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nphug::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nphug}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_msst:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are q = 10, mu = 0, tscale = 0.01, dftb = no,
beta = 0.0.  Note that p0, v0, and e0 are calculated on the first
timestep.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_mvv_dpd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform time integration using the modified velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet (MVV)
algorithm to update position and velocity (fix mvv/dpd), or position,
velocity and temperature (fix mvv/edpd), or position, velocity and
concentration (fix mvv/tdpd) for particles in the group each timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The modified velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet (MVV) algorithm aims to improve the
stability of the time integrator by using an extrapolated version of
the velocity for the force evaluation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}v(t+\frac{\Delta t}{2}) = & v(t) + \frac{\Delta t}{2}\cdot a(t) \\
r(t+\Delta t) = & r(t) + \Delta t\cdot v(t+\frac{\Delta t}{2}) \\
a(t+\Delta t) = & \frac{1}{m}\cdot F\left[ r(t+\Delta t), v(t) +\lambda \cdot \Delta t\cdot a(t)\right] \\
v(t+\Delta t) = & v(t+\frac{\Delta t}{2}) + \frac{\Delta t}{2}\cdot a(t+\Delta t)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the parameter \(\lambda\) depends on the
specific choice of DPD parameters, and needs to be tuned on a
case\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}case basis.  Specification of a \sphinxstyleemphasis{lambda} value is optional.
If specified, the setting must be from 0.0 to 1.0.  If not specified,
a default value of 0.5 is used, which effectively reproduces the
standard velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet (VV) scheme.  For more details, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mvv_dpd:groot2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Groot}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{mvv/dpd} updates the position and velocity of each atom.  It can be
used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style mdpd}}}} command or other
pair styles such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair dpd}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{mvv/edpd} updates the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom temperature, in addition to position
and velocity, and must be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style edpd}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{mvv/tdpd} updates the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom chemical concentration, in addition
to position and velocity, and must be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style
tdpd}}}} command.

\section{fix neb command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb:fix-neb-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_neb:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_neb::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Kspring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
neb = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kspring = spring constant for parallel nudging force (force/distance units or force units, see parallel keyword)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{parallel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{perp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{end}

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{parallel} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{neigh} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ideal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{neigh} = parallel nudging force based on distance to neighbor replicas (Kspring = force/distance units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ideal} = parallel nudging force based on interpolated ideal position (Kspring = force units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} = parallel nudging force based on interpolated ideal position before climbing, then interpolated ideal energy whilst climbing (Kspring = force units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{perp} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring2}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring2} = spring constant for perpendicular nudging force (force/distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{end} values = estyle Kspring3
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst/middle}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} = apply force to first replica
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} = apply force to last replica
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst} = apply force to last replica and set its target energy to that of first replica
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst/middle} = same as \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst} plus prevent middle replicas having lower energy than first replica
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring3} = spring constant for target energy term (1/distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{active}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{perp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{last}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{perp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ideal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{last}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{efirst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add nudging forces to atoms in the group for a multi\sphinxhyphen{}replica
simulation run via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb}}}} command to perform a nudged
elastic band (NEB) calculation for finding the transition state.
Hi\sphinxhyphen{}level explanations of NEB are given with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb}}}} command
and on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_replica::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto replica}}}} doc page.  The fix neb
command must be used with the “neb” command and defines how
inter\sphinxhyphen{}replica nudging forces are computed.  A NEB calculation is
divided in two stages. In the first stage n replicas are relaxed
toward a MEP until convergence.  In the second stage, the climbing
image scheme (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb:henkelman2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henkelman2)}}}}) is enabled, so that the
replica having the highest energy relaxes toward the saddle point
(i.e. the point of highest energy along the MEP), and a second
relaxation is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A key purpose of the nudging forces is to keep the replicas equally
spaced.  During the NEB calculation, the \(3N\)\sphinxhyphen{}length vector of
interatomic force \(F_i = -\nabla V\) for each replica \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} is
altered.  For all intermediate replicas (i.e. for \(1 < i < N\),
except the climbing replica) the force vector becomes:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_i = -\nabla V + (\nabla V \cdot T') T' + F_\parallel + F_\perp\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
T’ is the unit “tangent” vector for replica \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and is a function of
\(R_i, R_{i-1}, R_{i+1}\), and the potential energy of the 3
replicas; it points roughly in the direction of \(R_{i+i} -
R_{i-1}\); see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb:henkelman1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henkelman1)}}}} paper for details.
\(R_i\) are the atomic coordinates of replica \sphinxstyleemphasis{i}; \(R_{i-1}\)
and \(R_{i+1}\) are the coordinates of its neighbor replicas.  The
term \(\nabla V \cdot T'\) is used to remove the component of the
gradient parallel to the path which would tend to distribute the replica
unevenly along the path.  \(F_\parallel\) is an artificial nudging
force which is applied only in the tangent direction and which maintains
the equal spacing between replicas (see below for more information).
\(F_\perp\) is an optional artificial spring which is applied in a
direction perpendicular to the tangent direction and which prevent the
paths from forming acute kinks (see below for more information).

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the second stage of the NEB calculation, the interatomic force \(F_i\)
for the climbing replica (the replica of highest energy after the
first stage) is changed to:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_i = -\nabla V + 2 (\nabla V \cdot T') T' + F_\perp\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the relaxation procedure is continued to a new converged MEP.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{parallel} specifies how the parallel nudging force is
computed.  With a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{neigh}, the parallel nudging force is
computed as in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb:henkelman1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henkelman1)}}}} by connecting each
intermediate replica with the previous and the next image:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_\parallel = Kspring \cdot \left(\left|R_{i+1} - R_i\right| - \left|R_i - R_{i-1}\right|\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in this case the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring} is in
force/distance units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{ideal}, the spring force is computed as suggested in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb:weinane}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(WeinanE)}}}}
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_\parallel = -Kspring \cdot (RD - RD_{ideal}) / (2 \cdot meanDist)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{RD} is the “reaction coordinate” see {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb}}}} section,
and \(RD_{ideal}\) is the ideal \sphinxstyleemphasis{RD} for which all the images are
equally spaced.  I.e. \(RD_{ideal} = (i-1) \cdot meanDist\) when the
climbing replica is off, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} is the replica number).  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{meanDist} is the average distance between replicas.  Note that in this
case the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring} is in force units. When the climbing
replica is on, \(RD_{ideal}\) and \(meanDist\) are calculated
separately each side of the climbing image. Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ideal} form
of nudging can often be more effective at keeping the replicas equally
spaced before climbing, then equally spaced either side of the climbing
image whilst climbing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} the spring force is computed as for \sphinxstyleemphasis{ideal} when
the climbing replica is off, promoting equidistance. When the climbing
replica is on, the spring force is computed to promote equidistant
absolute differences in energy, rather than distance, each side of the
climbing image:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_\parallel = -Kspring \cdot (ED - ED_{ideal}) / (2 \cdot meanEDist)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{ED} is the cumulative sum of absolute energy differences:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}ED = \sum_{i<N} \left|E(R_{i+1}) - E(R_i)\right|,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{meanEdist} is the average absolute energy difference between replicas
up to the climbing image or from the climbing image to the final image,
for images before or after the climbing image
respectively. \(ED_{ideal}\) is the corresponding cumulative sum of
average absolute energy differences in each case, in close analogy to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ideal}. This form of nudging is to aid schemes which integrate forces
along, or near to, NEB pathways such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pafi::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_pafi}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{perp} specifies if and how a perpendicular nudging force is
computed.  It adds a spring force perpendicular to the path in order to
prevent the path from becoming too strongly kinked.  It can
significantly improve the convergence of the NEB calculation when the
resolution is poor.  I.e. when few replicas are used; see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb:maras1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Maras)}}}} for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The perpendicular spring force is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_\perp = K_{spring2} \cdot F(R_{i-1},R_i,R_{i+1}) (R_{i+1} + R_{i-1} - 2 R_i)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring2} is the specified value.  \(F(R_{i-1}, R_i,
R_{i+1})\) is a smooth scalar function of the angle \(R_{i-1} R_i
R_{i+1}\).  It is equal to 0.0 when the path is straight and is equal to
1 when the angle \(R_{i-1} R_i R_{i+1}\) is acute.
\(F(R_{i-1}, R_i, R_{i+1})\) is defined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb:jonsson}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jonsson)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring2} is set to 0.0 (the default) then no perpendicular spring
force is added.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, no additional forces act on the first and last replicas
during the NEB relaxation, so these replicas simply relax toward their
respective local minima.  By using the key word \sphinxstyleemphasis{end}, additional forces
can be applied to the first and/or last replicas, to enable them to
relax toward a MEP while constraining their energy E to the target
energy ETarget.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \(E_{Target} > E\), the interatomic force \(F_i\) for the
specified replica becomes:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_i & = -\nabla V + (\nabla V \cdot T' + (E - E_{Target}) \cdot K_{spring3}) T', \qquad  \textrm{when} \quad \nabla V \cdot T' < 0 \\
F_i & = -\nabla V + (\nabla V \cdot T' + (E_{Target} - E) \cdot K_{spring3}) T', \qquad \textrm{when} \quad \nabla V  \cdot T' > 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The “spring” constant on the difference in energies is the specified
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Kspring3} value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{first}, the force is applied to the first
replica.  When \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{last}, the force is applied to
the last replica.  Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{end} keyword can be used twice to add
forces to both the first and last replicas.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For both these \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} settings, the target energy \sphinxstyleemphasis{ETarget} is set
to the initial energy of the replica (at the start of the NEB
calculation).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst/middle},
force is applied to the last replica, but the target energy \sphinxstyleemphasis{ETarget} is
continuously set to the energy of the first replica, as it evolves
during the NEB relaxation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The difference between these two \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} options is as follows.  When
\sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} is specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst}, no change is made to the
inter\sphinxhyphen{}replica force applied to the intermediate replicas (neither first
or last).  If the initial path is too far from the MEP, an intermediate
replica may relax “faster” and reach a lower energy than the last
replica.  In this case the intermediate replica will be relaxing toward
its own local minima.  This behavior can be prevented by specifying
\sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} as \sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst/middle} which will alter the inter\sphinxhyphen{}replica
force applied to intermediate replicas by removing the contribution of
the gradient to the inter\sphinxhyphen{}replica force.  This will only be done if a
particular intermediate replica has a lower energy than the first
replica.  This should effectively prevent the intermediate replicas from
over\sphinxhyphen{}relaxing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After converging a NEB calculation using an \sphinxstyleemphasis{estyle} of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{last/efirst/middle}, you should check that all intermediate replicas
have a larger energy than the first replica. If this is not the case,
the path is probably not a MEP.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finally, note that the last replica may never reach the target energy
if it is stuck in a local minima which has a larger energy than the
target energy.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by
this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
as invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb}}}} command.

\section{fix neb/spin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:fix-neb-spin-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Kspring}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
neb/spin = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Kspring = spring constant for parallel nudging force
(force/distance units or force units, see parallel keyword)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add nudging forces to spins in the group for a multi\sphinxhyphen{}replica
simulation run via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neb_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb/spin}}}} command to perform a
geodesic nudged elastic band (GNEB) calculation for finding the
transition state.
Hi\sphinxhyphen{}level explanations of GNEB are given with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neb_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb/spin}}}} command and on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_replica::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto replica}}}} doc page.
The fix neb/spin command must be used with the “neb/spin” command and
defines how inter\sphinxhyphen{}replica nudging forces are computed.  A GNEB
calculation is divided in two stages. In the first stage n replicas
are relaxed toward a MEP until convergence.  In the second stage, the
climbing image scheme is enabled, so that the replica having the highest
energy relaxes toward the saddle point (i.e. the point of highest energy
along the MEP), and a second relaxation is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The nudging forces are calculated as explained in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:bessarabb}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bessarab)}}}}).
See this reference for more explanation about their expression.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_neb_spin:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
as invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neb_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neb/spin}}}} command.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style\_name = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nvt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ptemp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{update}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values = Tstart Tstop Tdamp
    Tstart,Tstop = external temperature at start/end of run
    Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
    Pstart,Pstop = scalar external pressure at start/end of run (pressure units)
    Pdamp = pressure damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
    Pstart,Pstop = external stress tensor component at start/end of run (pressure units)
    Pdamp = stress damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} value = N
    N = length of thermostat chain (1 = single thermostat)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} value = N
    N length of thermostat chain on barostat (0 = no thermostat)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = add in MTK adjustment term or not
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} value = M
    M = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on thermostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} value = M
    M = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on barostat thermostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} value = reset reference cell every this many timesteps
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} value = Df
    Df = drag factor added to barostat/thermostat (0.0 = no drag)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ptemp} value = Ttarget
    Ttarget = target temperature for barostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} value = dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = only dilate atoms in this group due to barostat volume changes
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xy with ly
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale yz with lz
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xz with lz
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = allow or disallow box flips when it becomes highly skewed
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} values = x y z
    x,y,z = perform barostat dilation/contraction around this point (distance units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole/dlm}
    dipole = update dipole orientation (only for sphere variants)
    dipole/dlm = use DLM integrator to update dipole orientation (only for sphere variants)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
