\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These commands perform time integration on Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover style
non\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian equations of motion which are designed to generate
positions and velocities sampled from the canonical (nvt),
isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric (npt), and isenthalpic (nph) ensembles.  This
updates the position and velocity for atoms in the group each
timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostatting and barostatting is achieved by adding some dynamic
variables which are coupled to the particle velocities
(thermostatting) and simulation domain dimensions (barostatting).  In
addition to basic thermostatting and barostatting, these fixes can
also create a chain of thermostats coupled to the particle thermostat,
and another chain of thermostats coupled to the barostat
variables. The barostat can be coupled to the overall box volume, or
to individual dimensions, including the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} tilt
dimensions. The external pressure of the barostat can be specified as
either a scalar pressure (isobaric ensemble) or as components of a
symmetric stress tensor (constant stress ensemble).  When used
correctly, the time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged temperature and stress tensor of the
particles will match the target values specified by Tstart/Tstop and
Pstart/Pstop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equations of motion used are those of Shinoda et al in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-shinoda}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Shinoda)}}}}, which combine the hydrostatic equations of
Martyna, Tobias and Klein in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-martyna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Martyna)}}}} with the strain
energy proposed by Parrinello and Rahman in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-parrinello}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Parrinello)}}}}.  The time integration schemes closely
follow the time\sphinxhyphen{}reversible measure\sphinxhyphen{}preserving Verlet and rRESPA
integrators derived by Tuckerman et al in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-tuckerman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tuckerman)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat parameters for fix styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{nvt} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} are specified
using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword.  Other thermostat\sphinxhyphen{}related keywords are
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag}, which are discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to only the translational degrees of freedom
for the particles.  The translational degrees of freedom can also have
a bias velocity removed before thermostatting takes place; see the
description below.  The desired temperature at each timestep is a
ramped value during the run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp}
parameter is specified in time units and determines how rapidly the
temperature is relaxed.  For example, a value of 10.0 means to relax
the temperature in a timespan of (roughly) 10 time units (e.g. \(\tau\)
or fs or ps \sphinxhyphen{} see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).  The atoms in the
fix group are the only ones whose velocities and positions are updated
by the velocity/position update portion of the integration.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat will not work well for arbitrary values
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp}.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} is too small, the temperature can fluctuate
wildly; if it is too large, the temperature will take a very long time
to equilibrate.  A good choice for many models is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} of around
100 timesteps.  Note that this is NOT the same as 100 time units for
most {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} settings. A simple way to ensure this, is
via using an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{immediate variable}}}} expression accessing
the thermo property ‘dt’, which is the length of the time step. Example:
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nv}{100.0*dt}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The barostat parameters for fix styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} is specified
using one or more of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keywords.  These keywords give you the
ability to specify all 6 components of an external stress tensor, and
to couple various of these components together so that the dimensions
they represent are varied together during a constant\sphinxhyphen{}pressure
simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other barostat\sphinxhyphen{}related keywords are \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate}, which are discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Orthogonal simulation boxes have 3 adjustable dimensions (x,y,z).
Triclinic (non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal) simulation boxes have 6 adjustable
dimensions (x,y,z,xy,xz,yz).  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands
specify whether the simulation box is orthogonal or non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal
(triclinic) and explain the meaning of the xy,xz,yz tilt factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target pressures for each of the 6 components of the stress tensor
can be specified independently via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}
keywords, which correspond to the 6 simulation box dimensions.  For
each component, the external pressure or tensor component at each
timestep is a ramped value during the run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}.
If a target pressure is specified for a component, then the
corresponding box dimension will change during a simulation.  For
example, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} keyword is used, the y\sphinxhyphen{}box length will change.  If
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} keyword is used, the xy tilt factor will change.  A box
dimension will not change if that component is not specified, although
you have the option to change that dimension via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in order to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} keywords, the
simulation box must be triclinic, even if its initial tilt factors are
0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all barostat keywords, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} parameter operates like the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} parameter, determining the time scale on which pressure is
relaxed.  For example, a value of 10.0 means to relax the pressure in
a timespan of (roughly) 10 time units (e.g. \(\tau\) or fs or ps
\sphinxhyphen{} see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover barostat will not work well for arbitrary values
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is too small, the pressure and volume can
fluctuate wildly; if it is too large, the pressure will take a very
long time to equilibrate.  A good choice for many models is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}
of around 1000 timesteps.  However, note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is specified in
time units, and that timesteps are NOT the same as time units for most
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The relaxation rate of the barostat is set by its inertia \(W\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}W = (N + 1) k_B T_{\rm target} P_{\rm damp}^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(N\) is the number of atoms, \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant,
and \(T_{\rm target}\) is the target temperature of the barostat {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-martyna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Martyna)}}}}.
If a thermostat is defined, \(T_{\rm target}\) is the target temperature
of the thermostat. If a thermostat is not defined, \(T_{\rm target}\)
is set to the current temperature of the system when the barostat is initialized.
If this temperature is too low the simulation will quit with an error.
Note: in previous versions of LAMMPS, \(T_{\rm target}\) would default to
a value of 1.0 for \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} units and 300.0 otherwise if the system had a temperature
of exactly zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a thermostat is not specified by this fix, \(T_{\rm target}\) can be
manually specified using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ptemp} parameter. This may be useful if the
barostat is initialized when the current temperature does not reflect the
steady state temperature of the system. This keyword may also be useful in
athermal simulations where the temperature is not well defined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what atoms are in the fix group (the only atoms which
are time integrated), a global pressure or stress tensor is computed
for all atoms.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation box is
changed, all atoms are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} for a group that
represents a subset of the atoms.  This can be useful, for example, to
leave the coordinates of atoms in a solid substrate unchanged and
controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.  This option should
be used with care, since it can be unphysical to dilate some atoms and
not others, because it can introduce large, instantaneous
displacements between a pair of atoms (one dilated, one not) that are
far from the dilation origin.  Also note that for atoms not in the fix
group, a separate time integration fix like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} can be used on them, independent of whether they
are dilated or not.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keyword allows two or three of the diagonal components of
the pressure tensor to be “coupled” together.  The value specified
with the keyword determines which are coupled.  For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the stress tensor are coupled.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Xyz} means all 3 diagonal components are coupled.  Coupling means two
things: the instantaneous stress will be computed as an average of the
corresponding diagonal components, and the coupled box dimensions will
be changed together in lockstep, meaning coupled dimensions will be
dilated or contracted by the same percentage every timestep.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} parameters for any coupled dimensions must
be identical.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Couple xyz} can be used for a 2d simulation; the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
dimension is simply ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} keywords are simply shortcuts that are
equivalent to specifying several other keywords together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} means couple all 3 diagonal components together when
pressure is computed (hydrostatic pressure), and dilate/contract the
dimensions together.  Using “iso Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as
specifying these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple xyz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions are controlled
independently using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pyy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the
stress tensor as the driving forces, and the specified scalar external
pressure.  Using “aniso Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as specifying
these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} dimensions
are controlled independently using their individual stress components
as the driving forces, and the specified scalar pressure as the
external normal stress.  Using “tri Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as
specifying these 7 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
xy 0.0 0.0 Pdamp
yz 0.0 0.0 Pdamp
xz 0.0 0.0 Pdamp
couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In some cases (e.g. for solids) the pressure (volume) and/or
temperature of the system can oscillate undesirably when a Nose/Hoover
barostat and thermostat is applied.  The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} keyword will
damp these oscillations, although it alters the Nose/Hoover equations.
A value of 0.0 (no drag) leaves the Nose/Hoover formalism unchanged.
A non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value adds a drag term; the larger the value specified, the
greater the damping effect.  Performing a short run and monitoring the
pressure and temperature is the best way to determine if the drag term
is working.  Typically a value between 0.2 to 2.0 is sufficient to
damp oscillations after a few periods. Note that use of the drag
keyword will interfere with energy conservation and will also change
the distribution of positions and velocities so that they do not
correspond to the nominal NVT, NPT, or NPH ensembles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An alternative way to control initial oscillations is to use chain
thermostats. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} determines the number of thermostats
in the particle thermostat. A value of 1 corresponds to the original
Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} specifies the number of
thermostats in the chain thermostatting the barostat degrees of
freedom. A value of 0 corresponds to no thermostatting of the
barostat variables.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} keyword controls whether or not the correction terms due to
Martyna, Tuckerman, and Klein are included in the equations of motion
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-martyna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Martyna)}}}}.  Specifying \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} reproduces the original
Hoover barostat, whose volume probability distribution function
differs from the true NPT and NPH ensembles by a factor of 1/V.  Hence
using \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} is more correct, but in many cases the difference is
negligible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} can be used to improve the accuracy of integration
scheme at little extra cost.  The initial and final updates of the
thermostat variables are broken up into \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} sub\sphinxhyphen{}steps, each of
length \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop}. This corresponds to using a first\sphinxhyphen{}order
Suzuki\sphinxhyphen{}Yoshida scheme {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-tuckerman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tuckerman)}}}}.  The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop}
does the same thing for the barostat thermostat.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} controls how often the reference dimensions used
to define the strain energy are reset.  If this keyword is not used,
or is given a value of zero, then the reference dimensions are set to
those of the initial simulation domain and are never changed. If the
simulation domain changes significantly during the simulation, then
the final average pressure tensor will differ significantly from the
specified values of the external stress tensor.  A value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep}
means that every \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} timesteps, the reference dimensions are set
to those of the current simulation domain.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} keywords control whether or
not the corresponding tilt factors are scaled with the associated box
dimensions when barostatting triclinic periodic cells.  The default
values \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} will turn on scaling, which corresponds to adjusting the
linear dimensions of the cell while preserving its shape.  Choosing
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no} ensures that the tilt factors are not scaled with the box
dimensions. See below for restrictions and default values in different
situations. In older versions of LAMMPS, scaling of tilt factors was
not performed. The old behavior can be recovered by setting all three
scale keywords to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword allows the tilt factors for a triclinic box to
exceed half the distance of the parallel box length, as discussed
below.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the bound is enforced by
flipping the box when it is exceeded.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, the tilt will continue to change without flipping.  Note that if
applied stress induces large deformations (e.g. in a liquid), this
means the box shape can tilt dramatically and LAMMPS will run less
efficiently, due to the large volume of communication needed to
acquire ghost atoms around a processor’s irregular\sphinxhyphen{}shaped subdomain.
For extreme values of tilt, LAMMPS may also lose atoms and generate an
error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} keyword specifies the fixed point for barostat volume
changes. By default, it is the center of the box.  Whatever point is
chosen will not move during the simulation.  For example, if the lower
periodic boundaries pass through (0,0,0), and this point is provided
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint}, then the lower periodic boundaries will remain at
(0,0,0), while the upper periodic boundaries will move twice as
far. In all cases, the particle trajectories are unaffected by the
chosen value, except for a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent constant translation of
positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} keyword is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} value, then the
orientation of the dipole moment of each particle is also updated
during the time integration.  This option should be used for models
where a dipole moment is assigned to finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles,
e.g. spheroids via use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style hybrid sphere dipole}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default dipole orientation integrator can be changed to the
Dullweber\sphinxhyphen{}Leimkuhler\sphinxhyphen{}McLachlan integration scheme
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-dullweber}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dullweber)}}}} when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} with the value
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole/dlm}. This integrator is symplectic and time\sphinxhyphen{}reversible,
giving better energy conservation and allows slightly longer timesteps
at only a small additional computational cost.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a barostat coupled to tilt dimensions \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} can
sometimes result in arbitrarily large values of the tilt dimensions,
i.e. a dramatically deformed simulation box.  LAMMPS allows the tilt
factors to grow a small amount beyond the normal limit of half the box
length (0.6 times the box length), and then performs a box “flip” to
an equivalent periodic cell.  See the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword
above, to allow this bound to be exceeded, if desired.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The flip operation is described in more detail in the page for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}.  Both the barostat dynamics and the atom
trajectories are unaffected by this operation.  However, if a tilt
factor is incremented by a large amount (1.5 times the box length) on
a single timestep, LAMMPS can not accommodate this event and will
terminate the simulation with an error. This error typically indicates
that there is something badly wrong with how the simulation was
constructed, such as specifying values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart} that are too far
from the current stress value, or specifying a timestep that is too
large. Triclinic barostatting should be used with care. This also is
true for other barostat styles, although they tend to be more
forgiving of insults. In particular, it is important to recognize that
equilibrium liquids can not support a shear stress and that
equilibrium solids can not support shear stresses that exceed the
yield stress.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One exception to this rule is if the first dimension in the tilt factor
(x for xy) is non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  In that case, the limits on the tilt
factor are not enforced, since flipping the box in that dimension does
not change the atom positions due to non\sphinxhyphen{}periodicity.  In this mode,
if you tilt the system to extreme angles, the simulation will simply
become inefficient due to the highly skewed simulation box.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}} command
which performs thermostatting but NO time integration, these fixes
perform thermostatting/barostatting AND time integration.  Thus you
should not use any other time integration fix, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} on atoms to which this fix is applied.  Likewise,
fix nvt and fix npt should not normally be used on atoms that also
have their temperature controlled by another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}
commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_barostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto barostat}}}} doc pages for a discussion of different
ways to compute temperature and perform thermostatting and
barostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the thermostat and barostat fixes create their own computes of
style “temp” and “pressure”, as if one of these sets of commands had
been issued:

\sphinxAtStartPar
For fix nvt:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For fix npt and fix nph:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For fix nvt, the group for the new temperature compute is the same as
the fix group.  For fix npt and fix nph, the group for both the new
temperature and pressure compute is “all” since pressure is computed
for the entire system.  In the case of fix nph, the temperature
compute is not used for thermostatting, but just for a kinetic\sphinxhyphen{}energy
contribution to the pressure.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}
commands for details.  Note that the IDs of the new computes are the
fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID + underscore + “press”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of these
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.  Or you can print this
temperature or pressure during thermodynamic output via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate
compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can be used with either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{verlet} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{integrators}}}}. When using one of the barostat fixes
with \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa}, LAMMPS uses an integrator constructed
according to the following factorization of the Liouville propagator
(for two rRESPA levels):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L \Delta t \right) = & \hat{E}
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}baro} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}part} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 2} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(2)} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right) \\
&\times \left[
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(1)} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 1} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_1 \frac{\Delta t}{n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 1} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(1)} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\right]^n \\
&\times
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(2)} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 2} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}part} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}baro} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right) \\
&+ \mathcal{O} \left(\Delta t^3 \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This factorization differs somewhat from that of Tuckerman et al, in
that the barostat is only updated at the outermost rRESPA level,
whereas Tuckerman’s factorization requires splitting the pressure into
pieces corresponding to the forces computed at each rRESPA level. In
theory, the latter method will exhibit better numerical stability. In
practice, because Pdamp is normally chosen to be a large multiple of
the outermost rRESPA timestep, the barostat dynamics are not the
limiting factor for numerical stability. Both factorizations are
time\sphinxhyphen{}reversible and can be shown to preserve the phase space measure
of the underlying non\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian equations of motion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation has been shown to conserve linear momentum
up to machine precision under NVT dynamics. Under NPT dynamics,
for a system with zero initial total linear momentum, the total
momentum fluctuates close to zero. It may occasionally undergo brief
excursions to non\sphinxhyphen{}negligible values, before returning close to zero.
Over long simulations, this has the effect of causing the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
to undergo a slow random walk. This can be mitigated by resetting
the momentum at infrequent intervals using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix momentum}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix npt and fix nph commands can be used with rigid bodies or
mixtures of rigid bodies and non\sphinxhyphen{}rigid particles (e.g. solvent).  But
there are also {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/npt}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid/nph}}}} commands, which are typically a more natural
choice.  See the page for those commands for more discussion of
the various ways to do this.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes writes the state of all the thermostat and barostat
variables to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by these fixes.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its thermostatting or barostatting procedure, as described above.
If you do this, note that the kinetic energy derived from the compute
temperature should be consistent with the virial term computed using
all atoms for the pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to
compute temperature on a subset of atoms.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If both the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keywords are used in a single
thermo\_modify command (or in two separate commands), then the order in
which the keywords are specified is important.  Note that a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pressure compute}}}} defines its own temperature compute as
an argument when it is specified.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword will override
this (for the pressure compute being used by fix npt), but only if the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword comes after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword
comes before the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword, then the new pressure compute
specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword will be unaffected by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}
setting.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by these fixes, via
either thermostatting and/or barostatting, is included in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} page for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute also compute a global vector of quantities, which
can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The
vector values are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector stores internal Nose/Hoover thermostat and barostat
variables.  The number and meaning of the vector values depends on
which fix is used and the settings for keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain},
which specify the number of Nose/Hoover chains for the thermostat and
barostat.  If no thermostatting is done, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} is 0.  If no
barostatting is done, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} is 0.  In the following list,
“ndof” is 0, 1, 3, or 6, and is the number of degrees of freedom in
the barostat.  Its value is 0 if no barostat is used, else its value
is 6 if any off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal stress tensor component is barostatted, else
its value is 1 if \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple xyz} is used or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple xy} for a 2d
simulation, otherwise its value is 3.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The order of values in the global vector and their meaning is as
follows.  The notation means there are tchain values for eta, followed
by tchain for eta\_dot, followed by ndof for omega, etc:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eta{[}tchain{]} = particle thermostat displacements (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eta\_dot{[}tchain{]} = particle thermostat velocities (1/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
omega{[}ndof{]} = barostat displacements (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
omega\_dot{[}ndof{]} = barostat velocities (1/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
etap{[}pchain{]} = barostat thermostat displacements (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
etap\_dot{[}pchain{]} = barostat thermostat velocities (1/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_eta{[}tchain{]} = potential energy of each particle thermostat displacement (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KE\_eta\_dot{[}tchain{]} = kinetic energy of each particle thermostat velocity (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_omega{[}ndof{]} = potential energy of each barostat displacement (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KE\_omega\_dot{[}ndof{]} = kinetic energy of each barostat velocity (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_etap{[}pchain{]} = potential energy of each barostat thermostat displacement (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KE\_etap\_dot{[}pchain{]} = kinetic energy of each barostat thermostat velocity (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_strain{[}1{]} = scalar strain energy (energy units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can ramp their external temperature and pressure over
multiple runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of
how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{X}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} cannot be barostatted if the associated dimension is not
periodic.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} can only be barostatted if the
simulation domain is triclinic and the second dimension in the keyword
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{y} dimension in \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}) is periodic.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, cannot be
barostatted for 2D simulations.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands specify whether the simulation box is orthogonal or
non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal (triclinic) and explain the meaning of the xy,xz,yz
tilt factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword, the final Tstop cannot be 0.0 since it would
make the external T = 0.0 at some timestep during the simulation which
is not allowed in the Nose/Hoover formulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz yes} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz yes} keyword/value pairs can not be used
for 2D simulations. \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz yes}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz yes}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy yes} options
can only be used if the second dimension in the keyword is periodic,
and if the tilt factor is not coupled to the barostat via keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can be used with dynamic groups as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} command.  Likewise they can be used with groups to
which atoms are added or deleted over time, e.g. a deposition
simulation.  However, the conservation properties of the thermostat
and barostat are defined for systems with a static set of atoms.  You
may observe odd behavior if the atoms in a group vary dramatically
over time or the atom count becomes very small.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are tchain = 3, pchain = 3, mtk = yes, tloop = 1,
ploop = 1, nreset = 0, drag = 0.0, dilate = all, couple = none,
flip = yes, scaleyz = scalexz = scalexy = yes if periodic in second
dimension and not coupled to barostat, otherwise no.

\section{fix nph/eff command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_eff:fix-nph-eff-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_eff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style\_name = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nvt/eff} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt/eff} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph/eff}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
one or more keyword value pairs may be appended
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values = Tstart Tstop Tdamp
    Tstart,Tstop = external temperature at start/end of run
    Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
    Pstart,Pstop = scalar external pressure at start/end of run (pressure units)
    Pdamp = pressure damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
    Pstart,Pstop = external stress tensor component at start/end of run (pressure units)
    Pdamp = stress damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} value = length of thermostat chain (1 = single thermostat)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} values = length of thermostat chain on barostat (0 = no thermostat)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = add in MTK adjustment term or not
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} value = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on thermostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} value = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on barostat thermostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} value = reset reference cell every this many timesteps
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} value = drag factor added to barostat/thermostat (0.0 = no drag)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These commands perform time integration on Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover style
non\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian equations of motion for nuclei and electrons in the
group for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}} model.  The fixes
are designed to generate positions and velocities sampled from the
canonical (nvt), isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric (npt), and isenthalpic (nph)
ensembles.  This is achieved by adding some dynamic variables which
are coupled to the particle velocities (thermostatting) and simulation
domain dimensions (barostatting).  In addition to basic thermostatting
and barostatting, these fixes can also create a chain of thermostats
coupled to the particle thermostat, and another chain of thermostats
coupled to the barostat variables. The barostat can be coupled to the
overall box volume, or to individual dimensions, including the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} tilt dimensions. The external pressure of the barostat
can be specified as either a scalar pressure (isobaric ensemble) or as
components of a symmetric stress tensor (constant stress ensemble).
When used correctly, the time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged temperature and stress tensor
of the particles will match the target values specified by
Tstart/Tstop and Pstart/Pstop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of these fixes is exactly like that described by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt, npt, and nph}}}} commands, except that the radius
and radial velocity of electrons are also updated.  Likewise the
temperature and pressure calculated by the fix, using the computes it
creates (as discussed in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt, npt, and nph}}}}
doc page), are performed with computes that include the eFF contribution
to the temperature or kinetic energy from the electron radial velocity.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
there are two different pressures that can be reported for eFF
when defining the pair\_style (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair eff/cut}}}} to
understand these settings), one (default) that considers electrons do
not contribute radial virial components (i.e. electrons treated as
incompressible ‘rigid’ spheres) and one that does.  The radial
electronic contributions to the virials are only tallied if the
flexible pressure option is set, and this will affect both global and
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities.  In principle, the true pressure of a system is
somewhere in between the rigid and the flexible eFF pressures, but,
for most cases, the difference between these two pressures will not be
significant over long\sphinxhyphen{}term averaged runs (i.e. even though the energy
partitioning changes, the total energy remains similar).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
currently, there is no available option for the user to set or
create temperature distributions that include the radial electronic
degrees of freedom with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} command, so the
the user must allow for these degrees of freedom to equilibrate
(i.e. equi\sphinxhyphen{}partitioning of energy) through time integration.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_eff:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the page for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt, npt, and nph}}}} commands
for details.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_eff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EFF package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other restriction discussed on the page for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt, npt, and nph}}}} commands also apply.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature for systems (regions or groups) with only
electrons and no nuclei is 0.0 (i.e. not defined) in the current
temperature calculations, a practical example would be a uniform
electron gas or a very hot plasma, where electrons remain delocalized
from the nuclei.  This is because, even though electron virials are
included in the temperature calculation, these are averaged over the
nuclear degrees of freedom only.  In such cases a corrective term must
be added to the pressure to get the correct kinetic contribution.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can be used to simulate non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium molecular dynamics
(NEMD) under diagonal flow fields, including uniaxial and bi\sphinxhyphen{}axial flow.
Simulations under continuous extensional flow may be carried out for an
indefinite amount of time.  It is an implementation of the boundary
conditions from {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:dobson}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dobson)}}}}, and also uses numerical
lattice reduction as was proposed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:hunt}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Hunt)}}}}. The lattice
reduction algorithm is from {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:semaev}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Semaev)}}}}. The fix is
intended for simulations of homogeneous flows, and integrates the SLLOD
equations of motion, originally proposed by Hoover and Ladd (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:sllod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans and Morriss)}}}}).  Additional detail about this
implementation can be found in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:nicholson}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Nicholson and Rutledge)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that NEMD simulations of a continuously strained system can be
performed using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}}
commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The applied flow field is set by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{erate} keyword. The values
\sphinxstyleemphasis{edot\_x} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{edot\_y} correspond to the strain rates in the xx and yy
directions.  It is implicitly assumed that the flow field is
traceless, and therefore the strain rate in the zz direction is eqal
to \sphinxhyphen{}(\sphinxstyleemphasis{edot\_x} + \sphinxstyleemphasis{edot\_y}).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Due to an instability in the SLLOD equations under extension,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix momentum}}}} should be used to regularly reset the
linear momentum.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The boundary conditions require a simulation box that does not have a
consistent alignment relative to the applied flow field. Since LAMMPS
utilizes an upper\sphinxhyphen{}triangular simulation box, it is not possible to
express the evolving simulation box in the same coordinate system as the
flow field.  These fixes keep track of two coordinate systems: the flow
frame, and the upper triangular LAMMPS frame. The coordinate systems are
related to each other through the QR decomposition, as is illustrated in
the image below.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{uef_frames}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
During most molecular dynamics operations, the system is represented
in the LAMMPS frame. Only when the positions and velocities are
updated is the system rotated to the flow frame, and it is rotated
back to the LAMMPS frame immediately afterwards. For this reason, all
vector\sphinxhyphen{}valued quantities (except for the tensors from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure/uef}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/uef}}}}) will be computed in the
LAMMPS frame. Rotationally invariant scalar quantities like the
temperature and hydrostatic pressure are frame\sphinxhyphen{}invariant and will be
computed correctly. Additionally, the system is in the LAMMPS frame
during all of the output steps, and therefore trajectory files made
using the dump command will be in the LAMMPS frame unless the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump cfg/uef}}}} command is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Temperature control is achieved with the default Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover style
thermostat documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}.  When this fix is
active, only the peculiar velocity of each atom is stored, defined as
the velocity relative to the streaming velocity. This is in contrast to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}}, which uses a lab\sphinxhyphen{}frame velocity,
and removes the contribution from the streaming velocity in order to
compute the temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pressure control is achieved using the default Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover barostat
documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}. There are two ways to control the
pressure using this fix. The first method involves using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ext}
keyword along with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} pressure style. With this method, the
pressure is controlled by scaling the simulation box isotropically to
achieve the average pressure only in the directions specified by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ext}.  For example, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ext} value is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, the average
pressure (Pxx+Pyy)/2 will be controlled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This example command will control the total hydrostatic pressure under
uniaxial tension:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ext}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xyz}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This example command will control the average stress in compression
directions, which would typically correspond to free surfaces under
drawing with uniaxial tension:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ext}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xy}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second method for pressure control involves setting the normal
stresses using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and/or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} keywords. When using this
method, the same pressure must be specified via \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}
for all dimensions controlled. Any choice of pressure conditions that
would cause LAMMPS to compute a deviatoric stress are not permissible
and will result in an error. Additionally, all dimensions with
controlled stress must have the same applied strain rate. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ext}
keyword must be set to the default value (\sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}) when using this
method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, the following commands will work:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following commands will not work:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{f6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{erate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, they create their own computes of style “temp/uef” and
“pressure/uef”, as if one of these two sets of commands had been
issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/uef}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
pressure/uef}}}} commands for details.  Note that
the IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or
fix\_ID + underscore + “press”.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix writes the state of all the thermostat and barostat variables,
as well as the cumulative strain applied, to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info
on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a restart file,
so that the operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not necessary to set the \sphinxstyleemphasis{strain} keyword when resuming a
run from a restart file. Only for resuming from data files, which do
not contain the cumulative applied strain, will this keyword be
necessary.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options. The temperature and pressure computes used must be
of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/uef} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure/uef}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute the same global scalar and vector quantities as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt andnpt}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are part of the UEF package. They are only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Due to requirements of the boundary conditions, when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{strain}
keyword is set to zero (or unset), the initial simulation box must be
cubic and have style triclinic. If the box is initially of type ortho,
use {\hyperref[\detokenize{change_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{change\_box}}}} before invoking the fix.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/uef}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure/uef}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump cfg/uef}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nh_uef:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default keyword values specific to these fixes are exy = xyz, strain
= 0 0.  The remaining defaults are the same as for {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt or npt}}}} except tchain = 1.  The reason for this change is given in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}}.

\section{fix nonaffine/displacement command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement:fix-nonaffine-displacement-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group nonaffine/displacement style args reference/style nstep keyword values
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nonaffine/displacement = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nevery = calculate nonaffine displacement every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2min} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrated}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d2min} args = cutoff args
  cutoff = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} args = none, cutoffs determined by atom types
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} args = none, cutoffs determined based on atom diameters (atom style sphere)
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmax}, cutoff set by a constant numeric value \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmax} (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{integrated} args = none
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
reference/style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixed} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fixed} = use a fixed reference frame at \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{update} = update the reference frame every \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} timesteps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} = update the reference frame \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} timesteps before calculating the nonaffine displacement
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{z/min} values = zmin
  zmin = minimum coordination number to calculate D2min
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nonaffine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{displacement}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{integrated}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{update}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nonaffine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{displacement}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d2min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nonaffine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{displacement}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d2min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{offset}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes different metrics of the nonaffine displacement of
particles. The first metric, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2min} calculates the \(D^2_\mathrm{min}\)
nonaffine displacement by Falk and Langer in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nonaffine_displacement:d2min-falk}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Falk)}}}}.
For each atom, the fix computes the two tensors
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}X = \sum_{\mathrm{neighbors}} \vec{r} \left(\vec{r}_{0} \right)^T\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Y = \sum_{\mathrm{neighbors}} \vec{r}_0 \left(\vec{r}_{0} \right)^T\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the neighbors include all other atoms within the distance criterion
set by the cutoff option, discussed below, \(\vec{r}\) is the current
displacement between particles, and \(\vec{r}_0\) is the reference
displacement. A deformation gradient tensor is then calculated as
\(F = X Y^{-1}\) from which
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}D^2_\mathrm{min} = \sum_{\mathrm{neighbors}} \left| \vec{r} - F \vec{r}_0 \right|^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and a strain tensor is calculated \(E = F F^{T} - I\) where \(I\)
is the identity tensor. This calculation is only performed on timesteps that
are a multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nevery} (including timestep zero). Data accessed before
this occurs will simply be zeroed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For particles with low coordination numbers, calculations of \(D^2_\mathrm{min}\)
may not be accurate. An optional minimum coordination number can be defined using
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z/min} keyword. If any particle has fewer than the specified number of particles
in the cutoff distance or in contact, the above calculations will be skipped and the
corresponding peratom array entries will be zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrated} style simply integrates the velocity of particles
every timestep to calculate a displacement. This style only works if
used in conjunction with another fix that deforms the box and displaces
atom positions such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} with remap x,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_press_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix press/berendsen}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nh}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both of these methods require defining a reference state. With the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixed} reference
style, the user picks a specific timestep \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} at which particle positions are saved.
If peratom data is accessed from this compute prior to this timestep, it will simply be
zeroed. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} reference style implies the reference state will be updated every
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} timesteps. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} reference will update the reference state \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep}
timesteps before a multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nevery} timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a peratom array with 3 columns, which can be accessed
by indices 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 using any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from a fix
as input.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrated} style, the three columns are the nonaffine
displacements in the x, y, and z directions. For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2min} style,
the three columns are the calculated \(\sqrt{D^2_\mathrm{min}}\), the
volumetric strain, and the deviatoric strain.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nph_asphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NPH integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity each timestep for aspherical or
ellipsoidal particles in the group using a Nose/Hoover pressure
barostat.  P is pressure; H is enthalpy.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the isenthalpic ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command, which assumes
point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the barostat are specified by keywords
and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command.  See,
for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The particles in the fix group are the only ones whose velocities and
positions are updated by the velocity/position update portion of the
NPH integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what particles are in the fix group, a global pressure is
computed for all particles.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation
box is changed, all particles are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case
only the particles in the fix group are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled.  The latter can be
useful for leaving the coordinates of particles in a solid substrate
unchanged and controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp/asphere” and
“pressure”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/asphere}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the
IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is “all”
since pressure is computed for the entire system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of this
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
or pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nph_asphere:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the Nose/Hoover barostat to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its thermostatting or barostatting procedure.  If you do this, note
that the kinetic energy derived from the compute temperature should be
consistent with the virial term computed using all atoms for the
pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to compute temperature
on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of
quantities as does the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target pressure over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nph_asphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular momentum and a
quaternion as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size.  They cannot be point
particles, but they can be aspherical or spherical as defined by their
shape attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
