\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nph_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NPH integration to update position, velocity, and
angular velocity each timestep for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particles in
the group using a Nose/Hoover pressure barostat.  P is pressure; H is
enthalpy.  This creates a system trajectory consistent with the
isenthalpic ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command, which assumes
point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is used, then each particle is treated as a 2d
disc (circle) instead of as a sphere.  This is only possible for 2d
simulations, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.
The only difference between discs and spheres in this context is their
moment of inertia, as used in the time integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the barostat are specified by keywords
and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command.  See,
for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The particles in the fix group are the only ones whose velocities and
positions are updated by the velocity/position update portion of the
NPH integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what particles are in the fix group, a global pressure is
computed for all particles.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation
box is changed, all particles are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case
only the particles in the fix group are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled.  The latter can be
useful for leaving the coordinates of particles in a solid substrate
unchanged and controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp/sphere” and
“pressure”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/sphere}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the
IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is “all”
since pressure is computed for the entire system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of this
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
or pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\label{\detokenize{fix_nph_sphere:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the Nose/Hoover barostat to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its thermostatting or barostatting procedure.  If you do this, note
that the kinetic energy derived from the compute temperature should be
consistent with the virial term computed using all atoms for the
pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to compute temperature
on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of
quantities as does the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target pressure over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nph_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular velocity (omega)
and a radius as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres.  They cannot
be point particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is only allowed for 2d simulations, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.

\section{fix nphug command}

Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{nphug/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nphug:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nphug}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command
\begin{sphinxalltt}
one or more keyword value pairs may be appended
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values = Value1 Value2 Tdamp
    Value1, Value2 = Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover target temperatures, ignored by Hugoniostat
    Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
    Pstart,Pstop = scalar external pressures, must be equal (pressure units)
    Pdamp = pressure damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
    Pstart,Pstop = external stress tensor components, must be equal (pressure units)
    Pdamp = stress damping parameter (time units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} value = length of thermostat chain (1 = single thermostat)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} values = length of thermostat chain on barostat (0 = no thermostat)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = add in MTK adjustment term or not
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} value = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on thermostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} value = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on barostat thermostat
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} value = reset reference cell every this many timesteps
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} value = drag factor added to barostat/thermostat (0.0 = no drag)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale yz with lz
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xz with lz
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xy with ly
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nphug:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is a variant of the Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} fix style.
It performs time integration of the Hugoniostat equations
of motion developed by Ravelo et al. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nphug:ravelo1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ravelo)}}}}.
These equations compress the system to a state with average
axial stress or pressure equal to the specified target value
and that satisfies the Rankine\sphinxhyphen{}Hugoniot (RH)
jump conditions for steady shocks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The compression can be performed
either
hydrostatically (using keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}) or uniaxially
(using keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}).  In the hydrostatic case,
the cell dimensions change dynamically so that the average axial stress
in all three directions converges towards the specified target value.
In the uniaxial case, the chosen cell dimension changes dynamically
so that the average
axial stress in that direction converges towards the target value. The
other two cell dimensions are kept fixed (zero lateral strain).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This leads to the following additional restrictions on the keywords:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
One and only one of the following keywords should be used: \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified initial and final target pressures must be the same.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} may not be used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The only admissible value for the couple keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}, which has the same effect as keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword must be used to specify the time constant for kinetic energy relaxation, but initial and final target temperature values are ignored.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Essentially, a Hugoniostat simulation is an NPT simulation in which the
user\sphinxhyphen{}specified target temperature is replaced with a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
target temperature Tt obtained from the following equation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T_t - T = \frac{\left(\frac{1}{2}\left(P + P_0\right)\left(V_0 - V\right) + E_0 - E\right)}{N_{dof} k_B } = \Delta\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(T\) and \(T_t\) are the instantaneous and target
temperatures, \sphinxstyleemphasis{P} and \(P_0\) are the instantaneous and reference
pressures or axial stresses, depending on whether hydrostatic or
uniaxial compression is being performed, \sphinxstyleemphasis{V} and \(V_0\) are the
instantaneous and reference volumes, \sphinxstyleemphasis{E} and \(E_0\) are the
instantaneous and reference internal energy (potential plus kinetic),
\(N_{dof}\) is the number of degrees of freedom used in the
definition of temperature, and \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann
constant. \(\Delta\) is the negative deviation of the instantaneous
temperature from the target temperature.  When the system reaches a
stable equilibrium, the value of \(\Delta\) should fluctuate about
zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values of \(E_0\), \(V_0\), and \(P_0\) are the
instantaneous values at the start of the simulation. These can be
overridden using the fix\_modify keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} described
below.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}} command
which performs thermostatting but NO time integration, this fix
performs thermostatting/barostatting AND time integration.  Thus you
should not use any other time integration fix, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} on atoms to which this fix is applied.  Likewise,
this fix should not be used on atoms that have their temperature
controlled by another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure at each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp” and “pressure”,
as if one of these two sets of commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the
IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”.  The group for
the new computes is “all” since pressure is computed for the entire
system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of this
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
or pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nphug:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the values of \(E_0\), \(V_0\), and \(P_0\),
as well as the state of all the thermostat and barostat variables to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input
script that reads a restart file, so that the operation of the fix
continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} keywords can be
used to define the values of \(E_0\), \(V_0\), and
\(P_0\). Note the the values for \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} are extensive, and so
must correspond to the total energy and volume of the entire system, not
energy and volume per atom. If any of these quantities are not
specified, then the instantaneous value in the system at the start of
the simulation is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used in its
thermostatting or barostatting procedure, as described above.  If you
do this, note that the kinetic energy derived from the compute
temperature should be consistent with the virial term computed using
all atoms for the pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to
compute temperature on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.  Note that this energy is *not* included in
the definition of internal energy E when calculating the value of
Delta in the above equation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes a global vector of quantities, which can be
accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar
The vector values are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector stores three quantities unique to this fix (\(\Delta\),
Us, and up), followed by all the internal Nose/Hoover thermostat and
barostat variables defined for {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}. Delta is the
deviation of the temperature from the target temperature, given by the
above equation.  Us and up are the shock and particle velocity
corresponding to a steady shock calculated from the RH
conditions. They have units of distance/time.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_asphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NPT integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity each timestep for aspherical or
ellipsoidal particles in the group using a Nose/Hoover temperature
thermostat and Nose/Hoover pressure barostat.  P is pressure; T is
temperature.  This creates a system trajectory consistent with the
isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to both the translational and rotational
degrees of freedom for the aspherical particles, assuming a compute is
used which calculates a temperature that includes the rotational
degrees of freedom (see below).  The translational degrees of freedom
can also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the thermostat and barostat are
specified by keywords and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command.  See, for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The particles in the fix group are the only ones whose velocities and
positions are updated by the velocity/position update portion of the
NPT integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what particles are in the fix group, a global pressure is
computed for all particles.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation
box is changed, all particles are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case
only the particles in the fix group are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled.  The latter can be
useful for leaving the coordinates of particles in a solid substrate
unchanged and controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp/asphere” and
“pressure”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/asphere}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the
IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is “all”
since pressure is computed for the entire system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of this
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
or pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_asphere:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the Nose/Hoover thermostat and barostat
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its thermostatting or barostatting procedure.  If you do this, note
that the kinetic energy derived from the compute temperature should be
consistent with the virial term computed using all atoms for the
pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to compute temperature
on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of
quantities as does the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature and pressure over multiple
runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do
this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_asphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular momentum and a
quaternion as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size.  They cannot be point
particles, but they can be aspherical or spherical as defined by their
shape attribute.

\section{fix npt/body command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:fix-npt-body-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
npt/body = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
additional thermostat and barostat related keyword/value pairs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command can be appended

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{water}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aniso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dilate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{partial}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NPT integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity each timestep for body
particles in the group using a Nose/Hoover temperature
thermostat and Nose/Hoover pressure barostat.  P is pressure; T is
temperature.  This creates a system trajectory consistent with the
isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to both the translational and rotational
degrees of freedom for the body particles, assuming a compute is
used which calculates a temperature that includes the rotational
degrees of freedom (see below).  The translational degrees of freedom
can also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the thermostat and barostat are
specified by keywords and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command.  See, for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The particles in the fix group are the only ones whose velocities and
positions are updated by the velocity/position update portion of the
NPT integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what particles are in the fix group, a global pressure is
computed for all particles.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation
box is changed, all particles are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case
only the particles in the fix group are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled.  The latter can be
useful for leaving the coordinates of particles in a solid substrate
unchanged and controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp/body” and
“pressure”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/body}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note that the
IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is “all”
since pressure is computed for the entire system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of this
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
or pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the Nose/Hoover thermostat and barostat
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its thermostatting or barostatting procedure.  If you do this, note
that the kinetic energy derived from the compute temperature should be
consistent with the virial term computed using all atoms for the
pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to compute temperature
on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of
quantities as does the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature and pressure over multiple
runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do
this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the BODY package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular momentum and a
quaternion as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style body}}}}
command.

\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_body:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve\_body}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt\_body}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
