\section{fix npt/cauchy command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:fix-npt-cauchy-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style\_name = \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt/cauchy}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{continue} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values = Tstart Tstop Tdamp
  Tstart,Tstop = external temperature at start/end of run
  Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
  Pstart,Pstop = scalar external pressure at start/end of run (pressure units)
  Pdamp = pressure damping parameter (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
  Pstart,Pstop = external stress tensor component at start/end of run (pressure units)
  Pdamp = stress damping parameter (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} value = N
  N = length of thermostat chain (1 = single thermostat)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} values = N
  N length of thermostat chain on barostat (0 = no thermostat)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = add in MTK adjustment term or not
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} value = M
  M = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on thermostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop} value = M
  M = number of sub\sphinxhyphen{}cycles to perform on barostat thermostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} value = reset reference cell every this many timesteps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} value = Df
  Df = drag factor added to barostat/thermostat (0.0 = no drag)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} value = dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = only dilate atoms in this group due to barostat volume changes
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xy with ly
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale yz with lz
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = scale xz with lz
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = allow or disallow box flips when it becomes highly skewed
\sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} value = strength of Cauchy stress control parameter
\sphinxstyleemphasis{continue} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = whether of not to continue from a previous run
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} values = x y z
  x,y,z = perform barostat dilation/contraction around this point (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{water}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cauchy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command performs time integration on Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover style
non\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian equations of motion which are designed to generate
positions and velocities sampled from the isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric (npt)
ensembles.  This updates the position and velocity for atoms in the
group each timestep and the box dimensions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostatting and barostatting is achieved by adding some dynamic
variables which are coupled to the particle velocities
(thermostatting) and simulation domain dimensions (barostatting).  In
addition to basic thermostatting and barostatting, this fix can
also create a chain of thermostats coupled to the particle thermostat,
and another chain of thermostats coupled to the barostat
variables. The barostat can be coupled to the overall box volume, or
to individual dimensions, including the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} tilt
dimensions. The external pressure of the barostat can be specified as
either a scalar pressure (isobaric ensemble) or as components of a
symmetric stress tensor (constant stress ensemble).  When used
correctly, the time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged temperature and stress tensor of the
particles will match the target values specified by Tstart/Tstop and
Pstart/Pstop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equations of motion used are those of Shinoda et al in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:nc-shinoda}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Shinoda)}}}}, which combine the hydrostatic equations of
Martyna, Tobias and Klein in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:nc-martyna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Martyna)}}}} with the strain
energy proposed by Parrinello and Rahman in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:nc-parrinello}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Parrinello)}}}}.  The time integration schemes closely
follow the time\sphinxhyphen{}reversible measure\sphinxhyphen{}preserving Verlet and rRESPA
integrators derived by Tuckerman et al in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:nc-tuckerman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tuckerman)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat parameters are specified using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword.
Other thermostat\sphinxhyphen{}related keywords are \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag},
which are discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to only the translational degrees of freedom
for the particles.  The translational degrees of freedom can also have
a bias velocity removed before thermostatting takes place; see the
description below.  The desired temperature at each timestep is a
ramped value during the run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp}
parameter is specified in time units and determines how rapidly the
temperature is relaxed.  For example, a value of 10.0 means to relax
the temperature in a timespan of (roughly) 10 time units (e.g. \(\tau\)
or fs or ps \sphinxhyphen{} see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).  The atoms in the
fix group are the only ones whose velocities and positions are updated
by the velocity/position update portion of the integration.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat will not work well for arbitrary values
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp}.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} is too small, the temperature can fluctuate
wildly; if it is too large, the temperature will take a very long time
to equilibrate.  A good choice for many models is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} of around
100 timesteps.  Note that this is NOT the same as 100 time units for
most {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The barostat parameters are specified using one or more of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keywords.
These keywords give you the ability to specify all 6 components of an
external stress tensor, and to couple various of these components
together so that the dimensions they represent are varied together
during a constant\sphinxhyphen{}pressure simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other barostat\sphinxhyphen{}related keywords are \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate}, which are discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Orthogonal simulation boxes have 3 adjustable dimensions (x,y,z).
Triclinic (non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal) simulation boxes have 6 adjustable
dimensions (x,y,z,xy,xz,yz).  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands
specify whether the simulation box is orthogonal or non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal
(triclinic) and explain the meaning of the xy,xz,yz tilt factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target pressures for each of the 6 components of the stress tensor
can be specified independently via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}
keywords, which correspond to the 6 simulation box dimensions.  For
each component, the external pressure or tensor component at each
timestep is a ramped value during the run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}.
If a target pressure is specified for a component, then the
corresponding box dimension will change during a simulation.  For
example, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} keyword is used, the y\sphinxhyphen{}box length will change.  If
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} keyword is used, the xy tilt factor will change.  A box
dimension will not change if that component is not specified, although
you have the option to change that dimension via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in order to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} keywords, the
simulation box must be triclinic, even if its initial tilt factors are
0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all barostat keywords, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} parameter operates like the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} parameter, determining the time scale on which pressure is
relaxed.  For example, a value of 10.0 means to relax the pressure in
a timespan of (roughly) 10 time units (e.g. \(\tau\) or fs or ps
\sphinxhyphen{} see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover barostat will not work well for arbitrary values
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is too small, the pressure and volume can
fluctuate wildly; if it is too large, the pressure will take a very
long time to equilibrate.  A good choice for many models is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}
of around 1000 timesteps.  However, note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is specified in
time units, and that timesteps are NOT the same as time units for most
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what atoms are in the fix group (the only atoms which
are time integrated), a global pressure or stress tensor is computed
for all atoms.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation box is
changed, all atoms are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} for a group that
represents a subset of the atoms.  This can be useful, for example, to
leave the coordinates of atoms in a solid substrate unchanged and
controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.  This option should
be used with care, since it can be unphysical to dilate some atoms and
not others, because it can introduce large, instantaneous
displacements between a pair of atoms (one dilated, one not) that are
far from the dilation origin.  Also note that for atoms not in the fix
group, a separate time integration fix like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} can be used on them, independent of whether they
are dilated or not.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keyword allows two or three of the diagonal components of
the pressure tensor to be “coupled” together.  The value specified
with the keyword determines which are coupled.  For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the stress tensor are coupled.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Xyz} means all 3 diagonal components are coupled.  Coupling means two
things: the instantaneous stress will be computed as an average of the
corresponding diagonal components, and the coupled box dimensions will
be changed together in lockstep, meaning coupled dimensions will be
dilated or contracted by the same percentage every timestep.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} parameters for any coupled dimensions must
be identical.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Couple xyz} can be used for a 2d simulation; the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
dimension is simply ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} keywords are simply shortcuts that are
equivalent to specifying several other keywords together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} means couple all 3 diagonal components together when
pressure is computed (hydrostatic pressure), and dilate/contract the
dimensions together.  Using “iso Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as
specifying these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple xyz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions are controlled
independently using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pyy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the
stress tensor as the driving forces, and the specified scalar external
pressure.  Using “aniso Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as specifying
these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} dimensions
are controlled independently using their individual stress components
as the driving forces, and the specified scalar pressure as the
external normal stress.  Using “tri Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as
specifying these 7 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
xy 0.0 0.0 Pdamp
yz 0.0 0.0 Pdamp
xz 0.0 0.0 Pdamp
couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In some cases (e.g. for solids) the pressure (volume) and/or
temperature of the system can oscillate undesirably when a Nose/Hoover
barostat and thermostat is applied.  The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag} keyword will
damp these oscillations, although it alters the Nose/Hoover equations.
A value of 0.0 (no drag) leaves the Nose/Hoover formalism unchanged.
A non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value adds a drag term; the larger the value specified, the
greater the damping effect.  Performing a short run and monitoring the
pressure and temperature is the best way to determine if the drag term
is working.  Typically a value between 0.2 to 2.0 is sufficient to
damp oscillations after a few periods. Note that use of the drag
keyword will interfere with energy conservation and will also change
the distribution of positions and velocities so that they do not
correspond to the nominal NVT, NPT, or NPH ensembles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An alternative way to control initial oscillations is to use chain
thermostats. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} determines the number of thermostats
in the particle thermostat. A value of 1 corresponds to the original
Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} specifies the number of
thermostats in the chain thermostatting the barostat degrees of
freedom. A value of 0 corresponds to no thermostatting of the
barostat variables.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mtk} keyword controls whether or not the correction terms due to
Martyna, Tuckerman, and Klein are included in the equations of motion
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:nc-martyna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Martyna)}}}}.  Specifying \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} reproduces the original
Hoover barostat, whose volume probability distribution function
differs from the true NPT and NPH ensembles by a factor of 1/V.  Hence
using \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} is more correct, but in many cases the difference is
negligible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} can be used to improve the accuracy of integration
scheme at little extra cost.  The initial and final updates of the
thermostat variables are broken up into \sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop} sub\sphinxhyphen{}steps, each of
length \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{tloop}. This corresponds to using a first\sphinxhyphen{}order
Suzuki\sphinxhyphen{}Yoshida scheme {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:nc-tuckerman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tuckerman)}}}}.  The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{ploop}
does the same thing for the barostat thermostat.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{nreset} controls how often the reference dimensions used
to define the strain energy are reset.  If this keyword is not used,
or is given a value of zero, then the reference dimensions are set to
those of the initial simulation domain and are never changed. If the
simulation domain changes significantly during the simulation, then
the final average pressure tensor will differ significantly from the
specified values of the external stress tensor.  A value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep}
means that every \sphinxstyleemphasis{nstep} timesteps, the reference dimensions are set
to those of the current simulation domain.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy} keywords control whether or
not the corresponding tilt factors are scaled with the associated box
dimensions when barostatting triclinic periodic cells.  The default
values \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} will turn on scaling, which corresponds to adjusting the
linear dimensions of the cell while preserving its shape.  Choosing
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no} ensures that the tilt factors are not scaled with the box
dimensions. See below for restrictions and default values in different
situations. In older versions of LAMMPS, scaling of tilt factors was
not performed. The old behavior can be recovered by setting all three
scale keywords to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword allows the tilt factors for a triclinic box to
exceed half the distance of the parallel box length, as discussed
below.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the bound is enforced by
flipping the box when it is exceeded.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, the tilt will continue to change without flipping.  Note that if
applied stress induces large deformations (e.g. in a liquid), this
means the box shape can tilt dramatically and LAMMPS will run less
efficiently, due to the large volume of communication needed to
acquire ghost atoms around a processor’s irregular\sphinxhyphen{}shaped subdomain.
For extreme values of tilt, LAMMPS may also lose atoms and generate an
error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint} keyword specifies the fixed point for barostat volume
changes. By default, it is the center of the box.  Whatever point is
chosen will not move during the simulation.  For example, if the lower
periodic boundaries pass through (0,0,0), and this point is provided
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixedpoint}, then the lower periodic boundaries will remain at
(0,0,0), while the upper periodic boundaries will move twice as
far. In all cases, the particle trajectories are unaffected by the
chosen value, except for a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent constant translation of
positions.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a barostat coupled to tilt dimensions \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} can
sometimes result in arbitrarily large values of the tilt dimensions,
i.e. a dramatically deformed simulation box.  LAMMPS allows the tilt
factors to grow a small amount beyond the normal limit of half the box
length (0.6 times the box length), and then performs a box “flip” to
an equivalent periodic cell.  See the discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword
above, to allow this bound to be exceeded, if desired.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The flip operation is described in more detail in the page for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}.  Both the barostat dynamics and the atom
trajectories are unaffected by this operation.  However, if a tilt
factor is incremented by a large amount (1.5 times the box length) on
a single timestep, LAMMPS can not accommodate this event and will
terminate the simulation with an error. This error typically indicates
that there is something badly wrong with how the simulation was
constructed, such as specifying values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart} that are too far
from the current stress value, or specifying a timestep that is too
large. Triclinic barostatting should be used with care. This also is
true for other barostat styles, although they tend to be more
forgiving of insults. In particular, it is important to recognize that
equilibrium liquids can not support a shear stress and that
equilibrium solids can not support shear stresses that exceed the
yield stress.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One exception to this rule is if the first dimension in the tilt factor
(x for xy) is non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  In that case, the limits on the tilt
factor are not enforced, since flipping the box in that dimension does
not change the atom positions due to non\sphinxhyphen{}periodicity.  In this mode,
if you tilt the system to extreme angles, the simulation will simply
become inefficient due to the highly skewed simulation box.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}} command
which performs thermostatting but NO time integration, this fix
performs thermostatting/barostatting AND time integration.  Thus you
should not use any other time integration fix, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} on atoms to which this fix is applied.  Likewise,
fix npt/cauchy should not normally be used on atoms that also
have their temperature controlled by another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}
commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_barostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto barostat}}}} doc pages for a discussion of different
ways to compute temperature and perform thermostatting and
barostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix compute a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp” and “pressure”,
as if one of these sets of commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group for both the new temperature and pressure compute is “all”
since pressure is computed for the entire system.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}
commands for details.  Note that the IDs of the new computes are the
fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp” or fix\_ID + underscore + “press”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the attributes of these
fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.  Or you can print this
temperature or pressure during thermodynamic output via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate
compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be used with either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{verlet} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{integrators}}}}. When using this fix
with \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa}, LAMMPS uses an integrator constructed
according to the following factorization of the Liouville propagator
(for two rRESPA levels):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L \Delta t \right) = & \hat{E}
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}baro} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}part} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 2} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(2)} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right) \\
&\times \left[
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(1)} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 1} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_1 \frac{\Delta t}{n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 1} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(1)} \frac{\Delta t}{2n} \right)
\right]^n \\
&\times
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{2}^{(2)} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\epsilon , 2} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}part} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right)
\exp \left(\mathrm{i} L_{\rm T\textrm{-}baro} \frac{\Delta t}{2} \right) \\
&+ \mathcal{O} \left(\Delta t^3 \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This factorization differs somewhat from that of Tuckerman et al, in
that the barostat is only updated at the outermost rRESPA level,
whereas Tuckerman’s factorization requires splitting the pressure into
pieces corresponding to the forces computed at each rRESPA level. In
theory, the latter method will exhibit better numerical stability. In
practice, because Pdamp is normally chosen to be a large multiple of
the outermost rRESPA timestep, the barostat dynamics are not the
limiting factor for numerical stability. Both factorizations are
time\sphinxhyphen{}reversible and can be shown to preserve the phase space measure
of the underlying non\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian equations of motion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Under NPT dynamics, for a system with zero initial total linear
momentum, the total momentum fluctuates close to zero.  It may occasionally
undergo brief excursions to non\sphinxhyphen{}negligible values, before returning close
to zero.  Over long simulations, this has the effect of causing the
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass to undergo a slow random walk. This can be mitigated by
resetting the momentum at infrequent intervals using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix momentum}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of all the thermostat and barostat
variables to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its thermostatting or barostatting procedure, as described above.
If you do this, note that the kinetic energy derived from the compute
temperature should be consistent with the virial term computed using
all atoms for the pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to
compute temperature on a subset of atoms.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If both the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keywords are used in a single
thermo\_modify command (or in two separate commands), then the order
in which the keywords are specified is important.  Note that a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pressure compute}}}} defines its own
temperature compute as an argument when it is specified.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword will override this (for the pressure compute being
used by fix npt), but only if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword comes after the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{press} keyword.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword comes before the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press}
keyword, then the new pressure compute specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{press}
keyword will be unaffected by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} setting.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix, due to
thermostatting and/or barostatting, is included in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} page for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes a global vector of quantities, which can be
accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  Rhe vector
values are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector stores internal Nose/Hoover thermostat and barostat
variables.  The number and meaning of the vector values depends on
which fix is used and the settings for keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain},
which specify the number of Nose/Hoover chains for the thermostat and
barostat.  If no thermostatting is done, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{tchain} is 0.  If no
barostatting is done, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} is 0.  In the following list,
“ndof” is 0, 1, 3, or 6, and is the number of degrees of freedom in
the barostat.  Its value is 0 if no barostat is used, else its value
is 6 if any off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal stress tensor component is barostatted, else
its value is 1 if \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple xyz} is used or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple xy} for a 2d
simulation, otherwise its value is 3.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The order of values in the global vector and their meaning is as
follows.  The notation means there are tchain values for eta, followed
by tchain for eta\_dot, followed by ndof for omega, etc:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eta{[}tchain{]} = particle thermostat displacements (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eta\_dot{[}tchain{]} = particle thermostat velocities (1/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
omega{[}ndof{]} = barostat displacements (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
omega\_dot{[}ndof{]} = barostat velocities (1/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
etap{[}pchain{]} = barostat thermostat displacements (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
etap\_dot{[}pchain{]} = barostat thermostat velocities (1/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_eta{[}tchain{]} = potential energy of each particle thermostat displacement (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KE\_eta\_dot{[}tchain{]} = kinetic energy of each particle thermostat velocity (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_omega{[}ndof{]} = potential energy of each barostat displacement (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KE\_omega\_dot{[}ndof{]} = kinetic energy of each barostat velocity (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_etap{[}pchain{]} = potential energy of each barostat thermostat displacement (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KE\_etap\_dot{[}pchain{]} = kinetic energy of each barostat thermostat velocity (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PE\_strain{[}1{]} = scalar strain energy (energy units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its external temperature and pressure over
multiple runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of
how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{X}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} cannot be barostatted if the associated dimension is not
periodic.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} can only be barostatted if the
simulation domain is triclinic and the second dimension in the keyword
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{y} dimension in \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}) is periodic.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, cannot be
barostatted for 2D simulations.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read data}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands specify whether the simulation box is orthogonal or
non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal (triclinic) and explain the meaning of the xy,xz,yz
tilt factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword, the final Tstop cannot be 0.0 since it would
make the external T = 0.0 at some timestep during the simulation which
is not allowed in the Nose/Hoover formulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz yes} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz yes} keyword/value pairs can not be used
for 2D simulations. \sphinxstyleemphasis{scaleyz yes}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexz yes}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{scalexy yes} options
can only be used if the second dimension in the keyword is periodic,
and if the tilt factor is not coupled to the barostat via keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tri}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} keyword modifies the barostat as per Miller et
al. (Miller)\_”\#nc\sphinxhyphen{}Miller” so that the Cauchy stress is controlled.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} is the non\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional parameter, typically set to 0.001 or
0.01 that determines how aggressively the algorithm drives the system
towards the set Cauchy stresses.  Larger values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} will modify
the system more quickly, but can lead to instabilities.  Smaller
values will lead to longer convergence time.  Since \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} also
influences how much the stress fluctuations deviate from the
equilibrium fluctuations, it should be set as small as possible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{continue} value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} indicates that the fix is subsequent to a
previous run with the npt/cauchy fix, and the intention is to continue
from the converged stress state at the end of the previous run.  This
may be required, for example, when implementing a multi\sphinxhyphen{}step loading/unloading
sequence over several fixes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} to zero is not permitted.  To “turn off” the
cauchystat control and thus restore the equilibrium stress
fluctuations, two subsequent fixes should be used.  In the first, fix
npt/cauchy is used and the simulation box equilibrates to the
correct shape for the desired stresses.  In the second,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} is used instead which uses the
original Parrinello\sphinxhyphen{}Rahman algorithm, but now with the corrected
simulation box shape from using fix npt/cauchy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be used with dynamic groups as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} command.  Likewise it can be used with groups to
which atoms are added or deleted over time, e.g. a deposition
simulation.  However, the conservation properties of the thermostat
and barostat are defined for systems with a static set of atoms.  You
may observe odd behavior if the atoms in a group vary dramatically
over time or the atom count becomes very small.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_cauchy:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are tchain = 3, pchain = 3, mtk = yes, tloop =
ploop = 1, nreset = 0, drag = 0.0, dilate = all, couple = none,
cauchystat = no,
scaleyz = scalexz = scalexy = yes if periodic in second dimension and
not coupled to barostat, otherwise no.

\section{fix npt/sphere command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:fix-npt-sphere-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt/sphere/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}

npt/sphere = style name of this fix command
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{itemize}

NOTE: additional thermostat and barostat and dipole related keyword/value pairs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command can be appended

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NPT integration to update position, velocity, and
angular velocity each timestep for finite\sphinxhyphen{}sizex spherical particles in
the group using a Nose/Hoover temperature thermostat and Nose/Hoover
pressure barostat.  P is pressure; T is temperature.  This creates a
system trajectory consistent with the isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to both the translational and rotational
degrees of freedom for the spherical particles, assuming a compute is
used which calculates a temperature that includes the rotational
degrees of freedom (see below).  The translational degrees of freedom
can also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is used, then each particle is treated as a 2d
disc (circle) instead of as a sphere.  This is only possible for 2d
simulations, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.
The only difference between discs and spheres in this context is their
moment of inertia, as used in the time integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the thermostat and barostat are
specified by keywords and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command.  See, for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The particles in the fix group are the only ones whose velocities and
positions are updated by the velocity/position update portion of the
NPT integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what particles are in the fix group, a global pressure is
computed for all particles.  Similarly, when the size of the simulation
box is changed, all particles are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case
only the particles in the fix group are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled.  The latter can be
useful for leaving the coordinates of particles in a solid substrate
unchanged and controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature and pressure each timestep.  To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “temp/sphere” and
“pressure”, as if these commands had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/sphere}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands for details.  Note
that the IDs of the new computes are the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp”
or fix\_ID
+ underscore + “press”, and the group for the new computes is “all”
since pressure is computed for the entire system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these are NOT the computes used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}.  This means you can change the
attributes of this fix’s temperature or pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this
temperature or pressure during thermodynamic output via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the
appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  It also means that changing attributes of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the Nose/Hoover thermostat and barostat
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} options are
supported by this fix.  You can use them to assign a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used in its
thermostatting or barostatting procedure.  If you do this, note that
the kinetic energy derived from the compute temperature should be
consistent with the virial term computed using all atoms for the
pressure.  LAMMPS will warn you if you choose to compute temperature
on a subset of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of
quantities as does the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature and pressure over multiple
runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do
this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular velocity (omega)
and a radius as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres.  They cannot
be point particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is only allowed for 2d simulations, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.

\label{\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere:related-commands}}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve\_sphere}}}},}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix numdiff command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff:fix-numdiff-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numdiff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delta}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numdiff = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = calculate force by finite difference every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
delta = size of atom displacements (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{movegroup}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numdiff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate forces through finite difference calculations of energy
versus position.  These forces can be compared to analytic forces
computed by pair styles, bond styles, etc.  This can be useful for
debugging or other purposes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified with the command means only atoms within the group
have their averages computed.  Results are set to 0.0 for atoms not in
the group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs a loop over all atoms in the group.  For each atom
and each component of force it adds \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} to the position, and
computes the new energy of the entire system.  It then subtracts
\sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} from the original position and again computes the new energy
of the system.  It then restores the original position.  That
component of force is calculated as the difference in energy divided
by two times \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important to choose a suitable value for delta, the magnitude of
atom displacements that are used to generate finite difference
approximations to the exact forces.  For typical systems, a value in
the range of 1 part in 1e4 to 1e5 of the typical separation distance
between atoms in the liquid or solid state will be sufficient.
However, the best value will depend on a multitude of factors
including the stiffness of the interatomic potential, the thermodynamic
state of the material being probed, and so on. The only way to be sure
that you have made a good choice is to do a sensitivity study on a
representative atomic configuration, sweeping over a wide range of
values of delta.  If delta is too small, the output forces will vary
erratically due to truncation effects. If delta is increased beyond a
certain point, the output forces will start to vary smoothly with
delta, due to growing contributions from higher order derivatives. In
between these two limits, the numerical force values should be largely
independent of delta.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The cost of each energy evaluation is essentially the cost of an MD
timestep.  Thus invoking this fix once for a 3d system has a cost
of 6N timesteps, where N is the total number of atoms in the system.
So this fix can be very expensive to use for large systems.
One expedient alternative is to define the fix for a group containing
only a few atoms.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} argument specifies on what timesteps the force will
be used calculated by finite difference.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} argument specifies the size of the displacement each
atom will undergo.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_numdiff_virial:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Feb2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the virial stress tensor through a finite difference calculation of
energy versus strain.  These values can be compared to the analytic virial
tensor computed by pair styles, bond styles, etc.  This can be useful for
debugging or other purposes. The specified group must be “all”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix applies linear strain fields of magnitude \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} to all the
atoms relative to a point at the center of the box.  The
strain fields are in six different directions, corresponding to the
six Cartesian components of the stress tensor defined by LAMMPS.
For each direction it applies the strain field in both the positive
and negative senses, and the new energy of the entire system
is calculated after each. The difference in these two energies
divided by two times \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}, approximates the corresponding
component of the virial stress tensor, after applying
a suitable unit conversion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important to choose a suitable value for delta, the magnitude of
strains that are used to generate finite difference
approximations to the exact virial stress.  For typical systems, a value in
the range of 1 part in 1e5 to 1e6 will be sufficient.
However, the best value will depend on a multitude of factors
including the stiffness of the interatomic potential, the thermodynamic
state of the material being probed, and so on. The only way to be sure
that you have made a good choice is to do a sensitivity study on a
representative atomic configuration, sweeping over a wide range of
values of delta.  If delta is too small, the output values will vary
erratically due to truncation effects. If delta is increased beyond a
certain point, the output values will start to vary smoothly with
delta, due to growing contributions from higher order derivatives. In
between these two limits, the numerical virial values should be largely
independent of delta.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} argument specifies on what timesteps the force will
be used calculated by finite difference.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} argument specifies the size of the displacement each
atom will undergo.

No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a global vector which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}, which stores the components of
the virial stress tensor as calculated by finite difference.  The
global vector can only be accessed on timesteps that are multiples
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} since that is when the finite difference virial is
calculated. See the examples in \sphinxstyleemphasis{examples/numdiff} directory
to see how this fix can be used to directly compare with
the analytic virial stress tensor computed by LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The order of the virial stress tensor components is \sphinxstyleemphasis{xx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zz},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, consistent with Voigt notation. Note that
the vector produced by {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}
uses a different ordering, with \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} swapped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by this compute are
“intensive”.  The vector values will be in pressure
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy
minimization}}}}.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform plain time integration to update position and velocity for
atoms in the group each timestep.  This creates a system trajectory
consistent with the microcanonical ensemble (NVE) provided there
are (full) periodic boundary conditions and no other “manipulations”
of the system (e.g. fixes that modify forces or velocities).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix invokes the velocity form of the
Stoermer\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet time integration algorithm (velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet). Other
time integration options can be invoked using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_asphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity for aspherical particles in the
group each timestep.  V is volume; E is energy.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the microcanonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_asphere_noforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform updates of position and orientation, but not velocity or
angular momentum for atoms in the group each timestep.  In other
words, the force and torque on the atoms is ignored and their velocity
and angular momentum are not updated.  The atom velocities and
angular momenta are used to update their positions and orientation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful as an implicit time integrator for Fast Lubrication
Dynamics, since the velocity and angular momentum are updated by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lubricateU::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lubricuteU}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular momentum and a
quaternion as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size.  They cannot be point
particles, but they can be aspherical or spherical as defined by their
shape attribute.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_awpmd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position and velocity for
nuclei and electrons in the group for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_awpmd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Antisymmetrized Wave Packet Molecular Dynamics}}}} model.  V is volume; E is energy.
This creates a system trajectory consistent with the microcanonical
ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this fix is exactly like that described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, except that the width and width\sphinxhyphen{}velocity of
the electron wave functions are also updated.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_body:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity for body particles in the group each
timestep.  V is volume; E is energy.  This creates a system trajectory
consistent with the microcanonical ensemble.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto body}}}} page for more details on using body
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\section{fix nve/bpm/sphere command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:fix-nve-bpm-sphere-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/bpm/sphere = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} value = none = treat particles as 2d discs, not spheres
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{disc}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position, velocity, angular
velocity, and quaternion orientation for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical
particles in the group each timestep.  V is volume; E is energy.  This
creates a system trajectory consistent with the microcanonical
ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.
It also differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/sphere}}}}
command which assumes finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheroid particles which do not
store a quaternion.  It thus does not update a particle’s orientation
or quaternion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is used, then each particle is treated as a 2d
disc (circle) instead of as a sphere.  This is only possible for 2d
simulations, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.
The only difference between discs and spheres in this context is their
moment of inertia, as used in the time integration.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by
this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the BPM package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque, angular velocity (omega), a
radius, and a quaternion as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style bpm/sphere}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres with
quaternions.  They cannot be point particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is only allowed for 2d simulations, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix nve/dot command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:fix-nve-dot-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dot}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/dot = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dot}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a rigid\sphinxhyphen{}body integrator as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:davidchack4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Davidchack)}}}}
to a group of atoms, but without Langevin dynamics.
This command performs Molecular dynamics (MD)
via a velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet algorithm and an evolution operator that rotates
the quaternion degrees of freedom, similar to the scheme outlined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:miller4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Miller)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is the equivalent of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}}
without damping and noise and can be used to determine the stability range
in a NVE ensemble prior to using the Langevin\sphinxhyphen{}type DOTC\sphinxhyphen{}integrator
(see also {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}}).
The command is equivalent to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}.
The particles are always considered to have a finite size.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An example input file can be found in /examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/duplex1/.
Further details of the implementation and stability of the integrator are contained in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:henrich4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henrich)}}}}.
The preprint version of the article can be found \sphinxhref{PDF/CG-DNA.pdf}{here}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-cg-dna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{CG\sphinxhyphen{}DNA}}}} package and the MOLECULE and ASPHERE package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:davidchack4}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Davidchack)} R.L Davidchack, T.E. Ouldridge, and M.V. Tretyakov. J. Chem. Phys. 142, 144114 (2015).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:miller4}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Miller)} T. F. Miller III, M. Eleftheriou, P. Pattnaik, A. Ndirango, G. J. Martyna, J. Chem. Phys., 116, 8649\sphinxhyphen{}8659 (2002).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dot:henrich4}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Henrich)} O. Henrich, Y. A. Gutierrez\sphinxhyphen{}Fosado, T. Curk, T. E. Ouldridge, Eur. Phys. J. E 41, 57 (2018).
