\section{fix nve/dotc/langevin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:fix-nve-dotc-langevin-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dotc}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/dotc/langevin = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp = damping parameter (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} value = factor
  factor = do thermostat rotational degrees of freedom via the angular momentum and apply numeric scale factor as discussed below
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dotc}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.03}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{457145}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dotc}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{78.9375}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{457145}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a rigid\sphinxhyphen{}body Langevin\sphinxhyphen{}type integrator of the kind “Langevin C”
as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:davidchack5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Davidchack)}}}}
to a group of atoms, which models an interaction with an implicit background
solvent.  This command performs Brownian dynamics (BD)
via a technique that splits the integration into a deterministic Hamiltonian
part and the Ornstein\sphinxhyphen{}Uhlenbeck process for noise and damping.
The quaternion degrees of freedom are updated though an evolution
operator which performs a rotation in quaternion space, preserves
the quaternion norm and is akin to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:miller5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Miller)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In terms of syntax this command has been closely modelled on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} option. But it combines
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} in
one single command. The main feature is improved stability
over the standard integrator, permitting slightly larger timestep sizes.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} this command performs
also time integration of the translational and quaternion degrees of freedom.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The total force on each atom will have the form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F =   & F_c + F_f + F_r \\
F_f = & - \frac{m}{\mathrm{damp}} v \\
F_r \propto & \sqrt{\frac{k_B T m}{dt~\mathrm{damp}}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_c\) is the conservative force computed via the usual
inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style}}}}, etc). The \(F_f\) and \(F_r\)
terms are implicitly taken into account by this fix on a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle
basis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_f\) is a frictional drag or viscous damping term proportional to
the particle’s velocity.  The proportionality constant for each atom is
computed as \(\frac{m}{\mathrm{damp}}\), where \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the mass of
the particle and damp is the damping factor specified by the user.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F_r\) is a force due to solvent atoms at a temperature \(T\)
randomly bumping into the particle.  As derived from the
fluctuation/dissipation theorem, its magnitude as shown above is
proportional to \(\sqrt{\frac{k_B T m}{dt~\mathrm{damp}}}\), where
\(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, \(T\) is the desired temperature,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the mass of the particle, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} is the timestep size, and damp is
the damping factor.  Random numbers are used to randomize the direction
and magnitude of this force as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:dunweg5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dunweg)}}}},
where a uniform random number is used (instead of a Gaussian random
number) for speed.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} have to be constant values, i.e. they cannot
be variables. If used together with the oxDNA force field for
coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained simulation of DNA please note that T = 0.1 in oxDNA units
corresponds to T = 300 K.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp} parameter is specified in time units and determines how
rapidly the temperature is relaxed.  For example, a value of 0.03
means to relax the temperature in a timespan of (roughly) 0.03 time
units \(\tau\) (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).
The damp factor can be thought of as inversely related to the
viscosity of the solvent, i.e. a small relaxation time implies a
high\sphinxhyphen{}viscosity solvent and vice versa.  See the discussion about gamma
and viscosity in the documentation for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscous::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscous}}}} command for more details.
Note that the value 78.9375 in the second example above corresponds
to a diffusion constant, which is about an order of magnitude larger
than realistic ones. This has been used to sample configurations faster
in Brownian dynamics simulations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The random \# \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} must be a positive integer. A Marsaglia random
number generator is used.  Each processor uses the input seed to
generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random numbers.
Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two runs on
different numbers of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword/value option has to be used in the following way:

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix has to be used together with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} keyword. The
particles are always considered to have a finite size.
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} enables thermostatting of the rotational degrees of
freedom in addition to the usual translational degrees of freedom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scale factor after the \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmom} keyword gives the ratio of the
rotational to the translational friction coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An example input file can be found in examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/duplex2/.
Further details of the implementation and stability of the integrators are contained in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:henrich5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henrich)}}}}.
The preprint version of the article can be found \sphinxhref{PDF/CG-DNA.pdf}{here}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details:pkg-cg-dna}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{CG\sphinxhyphen{}DNA}}}} package and the MOLECULE and ASPHERE package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix nve/eff command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff:fix-nve-eff-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/eff = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position and velocity for
nuclei and electrons in the group for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}} model.  V is volume; E is energy.  This creates a
system trajectory consistent with the microcanonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this fix is exactly like that described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, except that the radius and radial velocity
of electrons are also updated.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_eff:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\index{fix nve/limit@\spxentry{fix nve/limit}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix nve/limit command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:fix-nve-limit-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xmax}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
xmax = maximum distance an atom can move in one timestep (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE updates of position and velocity for atoms in the
group each timestep.  A limit is imposed on the maximum distance an
atom can move in one timestep.  This is useful when starting a
simulation with a configuration containing highly overlapped atoms.
Normally this would generate huge forces which would blow atoms out of
the simulation box, causing LAMMPS to stop with an error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using this fix can overcome that problem.  Forces on atoms must still
be computable (which typically means two atoms must have a separation
distance \textgreater{} 0.0).  But large velocities generated by large forces are
reset to a value that corresponds to a displacement of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{xmax}
in a single timestep.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Xmax} is specified in distance units; see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command for details.  The value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{xmax} should be
consistent with the neighbor skin distance and the frequency of
neighbor list re\sphinxhyphen{}building, so that pairwise interactions are not
missed on successive timesteps as atoms move.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} commands
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if a velocity reset occurs the integrator will not conserve
energy.  On steps where no velocity resets occur, this integrator is
exactly like the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command.  Since forces are
unaltered, pressures computed by thermodynamic output will still be
very large for overlapped configurations.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You should not use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} in conjunction
with this fix.  That is because fix shake applies constraint forces
based on the predicted positions of atoms after the next timestep.
It has no way of knowing the timestep may change due to this fix,
which will cause the constraint forces to be invalid.  A better
strategy is to turn off fix shake when performing initial dynamics
that need this fix, then turn fix shake on when doing normal dynamics
with a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size timestep.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the count of how
many updates of atom’s velocity/position were limited by the maximum
distance criterion.  This should be roughly the number of atoms so
affected, except that updates occur at both the beginning and end of a
timestep in a velocity Verlet timestepping algorithm.  This is a
cumulative quantity for the current run, but is re\sphinxhyphen{}initialized to zero
each time a run is performed.  The scalar value calculated by this fix
is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/noforce}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style soft}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_limit:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\subsection{Syntax}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{line}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}

\item {}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_line:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{line}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_line:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity for line segment particles in the
group each timestep.  V is volume; E is energy.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the microcanonical ensemble.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_spherical::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto spherical}}}} page for an overview of using line
segment particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_line:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}

are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix nve/manifold/rattle command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:fix-nve-manifold-rattle-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{manifold}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rattle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{manifold}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{manifold}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/manifold/rattle = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tol = tolerance to which Newton iteration must converge

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
maxit = maximum number of iterations to perform

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
manifold = name of the manifold

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
manifold\sphinxhyphen{}args = parameters for the manifold

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{every}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} values = N
    N = print info about iteration every N steps. N = 0 means no output
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{manifold}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rattle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1e\PYGZhy{}4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{manifold}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rattle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1e\PYGZhy{}8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ellipsoid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{every}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position and velocity for
atoms constrained to a curved surface (manifold) in the group each
timestep. The constraint is handled by RATTLE {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:andersen1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Andersen)}}}}
written out for the special case of single\sphinxhyphen{}particle constraints as
explained in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle:paquay2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Paquay)}}}}.  V is volume; E is energy. This way,
the dynamics of particles constrained to curved surfaces can be
studied. If combined with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}, this
generates Brownian motion of particles constrained to a curved
surface. For a list of currently supported manifolds and their
parameters, see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_manifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto manifold}}}} doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the particles must initially be close to the manifold in
question. If not, RATTLE will not be able to iterate until the
constraint is satisfied, and an error is generated. For simple
manifolds this can be achieved with \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{create\_atoms}
commands, but for more complex surfaces it might be more useful to
write a script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The manifold args may be equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables, like so:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{R}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ramp(5.0,3.0)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{shrink\PYGZus{}sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{manifold}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rattle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1e\PYGZhy{}4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}R}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this case, the manifold parameter will change in time according to
the variable.  This is not a problem for the time integrator as long
as the change of the manifold is slow with respect to the dynamics of
the particles.  Note that if the manifold has to exert work on the
particles because of these changes, the total energy might not be
conserved.

\section{fix nve/noforce command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce:fix-nve-noforce-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/noforce = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{noforce}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_noforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform updates of position, but not velocity for atoms in the group
each timestep.  In other words, the force on the atoms is ignored and
their velocity is not updated.  The atom velocities are used to update
their positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be useful for wall atoms, when you set their velocities, and
want the wall to move (or stay stationary) in a prescribed fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can also be accomplished via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_setforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix setforce}}}}
command, but with fix nve/noforce, the forces on the wall atoms are
unchanged, and can thus be printed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command or
queried with an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} that uses the
fcm() group function to compute the total force on the group of atoms.

\section{fix nve/sphere command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:fix-nve-sphere-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve/sphere/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve/sphere/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/sphere = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{update} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole/dlm}
  dipole = update orientation of dipole moment during integration
  dipole/dlm = use DLM integrator to update dipole orientation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} value = none = treat particles as 2d discs, not spheres
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{update}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dipole}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{disc}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{update}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dlm}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position, velocity, and
angular velocity for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particles in the group each
timestep.  V is volume; E is energy.  This creates a system trajectory
consistent with the microcanonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} keyword is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} value, then the
orientation of the dipole moment of each particle is also updated
during the time integration.  This option should be used for models
where a dipole moment is assigned to finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles,
e.g. spheroids via use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style hybrid sphere dipole}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default dipole orientation integrator can be changed to the
Dullweber\sphinxhyphen{}Leimkuhler\sphinxhyphen{}McLachlan integration scheme
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh:nh-dullweber}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dullweber)}}}} when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{update} with the value
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole/dlm}. This integrator is symplectic and time\sphinxhyphen{}reversible,
giving better energy conservation and allows slightly longer timesteps
at only a small additional computational cost.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is used, then each particle is treated as a 2d
disc (circle) instead of as a sphere.  This is only possible for 2d
simulations, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.
The only difference between discs and spheres in this context is their
moment of inertia, as used in the time integration.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are

No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular velocity (omega)
and a radius as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}
command.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} keyword is used, then they must also store a
dipole moment as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style dipole}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres.  They cannot
be point particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is only allowed for 2d simulations, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.

\index{fix nve/spin@\spxentry{fix nve/spin}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix nve/spin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:fix-nve-spin-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nve/spin = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{moving} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{frozen}
  moving = integrate both spin and atomic degress of freedom
  frozen = integrate spins on a fixed lattice
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{moving}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{frozen}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a symplectic integration for the spin or spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} keyword defines if the spins are integrated on a lattice
of fixed atoms (lattice = frozen), or if atoms are moving
(lattice = moving).
The first case corresponds to a spin dynamics calculation, and
the second to a spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice calculation.
By default a spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice integration is performed (lattice = moving).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve/spin} fix applies a Suzuki\sphinxhyphen{}Trotter decomposition to
the equations of motion of the spin lattice system, following the scheme:

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{fix_integration_spin_stdecomposition}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
according to the implementation reported in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:omelyan1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Omelyan)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A sectoring method enables this scheme for parallel calculations.
The implementation of this sectoring algorithm is reported
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:tranchida1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the SPIN
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use the spin algorithm, it is necessary to define a map with
the atom\_modify command. Typically, by adding the command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{atom\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{map}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{array}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
before you create the simulation box. Note that the keyword “hash”
instead of “array” is also valid.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style spin}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default is lattice = moving.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:omelyan1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Omelyan)} Omelyan, Mryglod, and Folk. Phys. Rev. Lett.
86(5), 898. (2001).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_spin:tranchida1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Tranchida)} Tranchida, Plimpton, Thibaudeau and Thompson,

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_tri:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVE integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular momentum for triangular particles in the
group each timestep.  V is volume; E is energy.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the microcanonical ensemble.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_spherical::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto spherical}}}} page for an overview of
using triangular particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_tri:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{fix_nve_tri:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that particles be triangles as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tri}}}} command.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvk}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

nvk = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvk:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant kinetic energy integration using the Gaussian
thermostat to update position and velocity for atoms in the group each
timestep.  V is volume; K is kinetic energy. This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the isokinetic ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equations of motion used are those of Minary et al in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvk:nvk-minary}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Minary)}}}}, a variant of those initially given by Zhang in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvk:nvk-zhang}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Zhang)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The kinetic energy will be held constant at its value given when fix
nvk is initiated. If a different kinetic energy is desired, the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} command should be used to change the kinetic
energy prior to this fix.

by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvk:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Gaussian thermostat only works when it is applied to all atoms in
the simulation box. Therefore, the group must be set to all.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix has not yet been implemented to work with the RESPA integrator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{fix nvt/asphere command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:fix-nvt-asphere-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{nvt/asphere/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nvt/asphere = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
additional thermostat related keyword/value pairs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command can be appended

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nvt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVT integration to update position, velocity,
orientation, and angular velocity each timestep for aspherical or
ellipsoidal particles in the group using a Nose/Hoover temperature
thermostat.  V is volume; T is temperature.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the canonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to both the translational and rotational
degrees of freedom for the aspherical particles, assuming a compute is
used which calculates a temperature that includes the rotational
degrees of freedom (see below).  The translational degrees of freedom
can also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the thermostat are specified by
keywords and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
command.  See, for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag}
keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature each timestep.  To do this, the fix
creates its own compute of style “temp/asphere”, as if this command
had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{asphere}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/asphere}}}} command for
details.  Note that the ID of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID +
underscore + “temp”, and the group for the new compute is the same as
the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}.
This means you can change the attributes of this fix’s temperature
(e.g. its degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom) via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} will have no
effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the Nose/Hoover thermostat to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an
input script that reads a restart file, so that the operation of the
fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have
defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of
quantities as does the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular momentum and a
quaternion as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size.  They cannot be point
particles, but they can be aspherical or spherical as defined by their
shape attribute.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_asphere:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve\_asphere}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt\_asphere}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}

Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.

Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.

hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_manifold_rattle:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix combines the RATTLE\sphinxhyphen{}based {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_manifold_rattle:andersen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Andersen)}}}} time
integrator of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/manifold/rattle}}}}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_manifold_rattle:paquay3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Paquay)}}}} with a Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover\sphinxhyphen{}chain thermostat to sample the
canonical ensemble of particles constrained to a curved surface
(manifold). This sampling does suffer from discretization bias of
O(dt).  For a list of currently supported manifolds and their
parameters, see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_manifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto manifold}}}} doc page.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVT integration to update positions and velocities
each timestep for atoms in the group using a Nose/Hoover temperature
thermostat.  V is volume; T is temperature.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the canonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This thermostat is used for a simulation box that is changing size
and/or shape, for example in a non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD) simulation.
The size/shape change is induced by use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command, so each point in the simulation box can be
thought of as having a “streaming” velocity.  This position\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
streaming velocity is subtracted from each atom’s actual velocity to
yield a thermal velocity which is used for temperature computation and
thermostatting.  For example, if the box is being sheared in x,
relative to y, then points at the bottom of the box (low y) have a
small x velocity, while points at the top of the box (hi y) have a
large x velocity.  These velocities do not contribute to the thermal
“temperature” of the atom.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Fix deform}}}} has an option for remapping either
atom coordinates or velocities to the changing simulation box.  To use
fix nvt/sllod, fix deform should NOT remap atom positions, because fix
nvt/sllod adjusts the atom positions and velocities to create a
velocity profile that matches the changing box size/shape.  Fix deform
SHOULD remap atom velocities when atoms cross periodic boundaries
since that is consistent with maintaining the velocity profile created
by fix nvt/sllod.  LAMMPS will give an error if this setting is not
consistent.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SLLOD equations of motion, originally proposed by Hoover and Ladd
(see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:evans3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans and Morriss)}}}}), were proven to be equivalent
to Newton’s equations of motion for shear flow by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:evans3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans and
Morriss)}}}}. They were later shown to generate the desired
velocity gradient and the correct production of work by stresses for all
forms of homogeneous flow by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:daivis}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Daivis and Todd)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 8Feb2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the default (\sphinxstyleemphasis{psllod} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}), the LAMMPS implementation adheres to
the standard SLLOD equations of motion, as defined by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:evans3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans and
Morriss)}}}}.  The option \sphinxstyleemphasis{psllod} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} invokes the slightly
different SLLOD variant first introduced by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:tuckerman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tuckerman et al.)}}}} as g\sphinxhyphen{}SLLOD and later by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:edwards}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Edwards)}}}} as
p\sphinxhyphen{}SLLOD.  In all cases, the equations of motion are coupled to a
Nose/Hoover chain thermostat in a velocity Verlet formulation, closely
following the implementation used for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A recent (2017) book by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod:todd-sllod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Todd and Daivis)}}}}
discusses use of the SLLOD method and non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD)
thermostatting generally, for both simple and complex fluids,
e.g. molecular systems.  The latter can be tricky to do correctly.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the thermostat are specified by
keywords and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
command.  See, for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag}
keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature each timestep.  To do this, the fix
creates its own compute of style “temp/deform”, as if this command had
been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{deform}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}} command for
details.  Note that the ID of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID +
underscore + “temp”, and the group for the new compute is the same as
the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}.  This means you can change the attributes of this fix’s
temperature (e.g. its degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom) via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature during
thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}}
command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  It also means that changing
attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used

atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a

velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual

a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should

\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVT integration to update positions and velocities each
timestep for nuclei and electrons in the group for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron
force field}}}} model, using a Nose/Hoover temperature
thermostat.  V is volume; T is temperature.  This creates a system
trajectory consistent with the canonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this fix is exactly like that described by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}} command, except that the radius and
radial velocity of electrons are also updated and thermostatted.
Likewise the temperature calculated by the fix, using the compute it
creates (as discussed in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt, npt, and nph}}}} doc
page), is performed with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform/eff}}}} command that includes the eFF contribution to
the temperature from the electron radial velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes the same global scalar and global vector of

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform constant NVT integration to update position, velocity, and
angular velocity each timestep for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particles in
the group using a Nose/Hoover temperature thermostat.  V is volume; T
is temperature.  This creates a system trajectory consistent with the
canonical ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix differs from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command, which
assumes point particles and only updates their position and velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to both the translational and rotational
degrees of freedom for the spherical particles, assuming a compute is
used which calculates a temperature that includes the rotational
degrees of freedom (see below).  The translational degrees of freedom
can also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is used, then each particle is treated as a 2d
disc (circle) instead of as a sphere.  This is only possible for 2d
simulations, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.
The only difference between discs and spheres in this context is their
moment of inertia, as used in the time integration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional parameters affecting the thermostat are specified by
keywords and values documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}
command.  See, for example, discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{drag}
keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature each timestep.  To do this, the fix
creates its own compute of style “temp/sphere”, as if this command
had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/sphere}}}} command for
details.  Note that the ID of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID +
underscore + “temp”, and the group for the new compute is the same as
the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}.  This means you can change the attributes of this fix’s
temperature (e.g. its degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom) via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature during
thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}}
command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  It also means that changing
attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_nvt_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular velocity (omega)
and a radius as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres.  They cannot
be point particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{disc} keyword is only allowed for 2d simulations, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} keyword.

\section{fix oneway command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_oneway:fix-oneway-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_oneway:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_oneway::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_oneway:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oneway}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{direction}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
oneway = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = apply this fix every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region where fix is active

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
direction = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{\sphinxhyphen{}x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{\sphinxhyphen{}y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{\sphinxhyphen{}z} = coordinate and direction of the oneway constraint

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_oneway:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oneway}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{semi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{x}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oneway}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{z}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oneway}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_oneway:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enforce that particles in the group and in a given region can only
move in one direction.  This is done by reversing a particle’s
velocity component, if it has the wrong sign in the specified
dimension.  The effect is that the particle moves in one direction
only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be used, for example, as a simple model of a semi\sphinxhyphen{}permeable
membrane, or as an implementation of Maxwell’s demon.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orient}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nstats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cuthi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file1}

\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
