\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{gb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orient}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.032008}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.75}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xi.vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chi.vec}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{gb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orient}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{bcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.882}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.75}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ngb.left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ngb.right}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix applies an orientation\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force to atoms near a planar
grain boundary which can be used to induce grain boundary migration
(in the direction perpendicular to the grain boundary plane).  The
motivation and explanation of this force and its application are
described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient:janssens}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Janssens)}}}}. The adaptation to bcc crystals
is described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient:wicaksono1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Wicaksono1)}}}}. The computed force is only
applied to atoms in the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The basic idea is that atoms in one grain (on one side of the
boundary) have a potential energy dE added to them.  Atoms in the
other grain have 0.0 potential energy added.  Atoms near the boundary
(whose neighbor environment is intermediate between the two grain
orientations) have an energy between 0.0 and dE added.  This creates
an effective driving force to reduce the potential energy of atoms
near the boundary by pushing them towards one of the grain
orientations.  For dir = 1 and dE \textgreater{} 0, the boundary will thus move so
that the grain described by file0 grows and the grain described by
file1 shrinks.  Thus this fix is designed for simulations of two\sphinxhyphen{}grain
systems, either with one grain boundary and free surfaces parallel to
the boundary, or a system with periodic boundary conditions and two
equal and opposite grain boundaries.  In either case, the entire
system can displace during the simulation, and such motion should be
accounted for in measuring the grain boundary velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential energy added to atom I is given by these formulas
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} \xi_{i} = & \sum_{j=1}^{12} \left| \mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{j}^{\rm I} \right| \qquad\qquad\left(1\right) \\
 \\
\xi_{\rm IJ} = & \sum_{j=1}^{12} \left| \mathbf{r}_{j}^{\rm J} - \mathbf{r}_{j}^{\rm I} \right| \qquad\qquad\left(2\right)\\
\\
\xi_{\rm low}  = & {\rm cutlo} \, \xi_{\rm IJ}  \qquad\qquad\qquad\left(3\right)\\
\xi_{\rm high}  = & {\rm cuthi} \, \xi_{\rm IJ} \qquad\qquad\qquad\left(4\right) \\
\\
\omega_{i} = & \frac{\pi}{2} \frac{\xi_{i} - \xi_{\rm low}}{\xi_{\rm high} - \xi_{\rm low}} \qquad\qquad\left(5\right)\\
\\
u_{i}  = & 0 \quad\quad\qquad\qquad\qquad \textrm{ for } \qquad \xi_{i} < \xi_{\rm low}\\
       = & {\rm dE}\,\frac{1 - \cos(2 \omega_{i})}{2}
 \qquad \mathrm{ for }\qquad \xi_{\rm low} < \xi_{i} < \xi_{\rm high}  \quad \left(6\right) \\
       = & {\rm dE} \quad\qquad\qquad\qquad\textrm{ for } \qquad \xi_{\rm high} < \xi_{i}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which are fully explained in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient:janssens}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Janssens)}}}}.  For fcc crystals
this order parameter Xi for atom I in equation (1) is a sum over the
12 nearest neighbors of atom I. For bcc crystals it is the
corresponding sum of the 8 nearest neighbors. Rj is the vector from
atom I to its neighbor J, and RIj is a vector in the reference
(perfect) crystal.  That is, if dir = 0/1, then RIj is a vector to an
atom coord from file 0/1.  Equation (2) gives the expected value of
the order parameter XiIJ in the other grain.  Hi and lo cutoffs are
defined in equations (3) and (4), using the input parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutlo}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cuthi} as thresholds to avoid adding grain boundary energy when
the deviation in the order parameter from 0 or 1 is small (e.g. due to
thermal fluctuations in a perfect crystal).  The added potential
energy Ui for atom I is given in equation (6) where it is interpolated
between 0 and dE using the two threshold Xi values and the Wi value of
equation (5).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The derivative of this energy expression gives the force on each atom
which thus depends on the orientation of its neighbors relative to the
2 grain orientations.  Only atoms near the grain boundary feel a net
force which tends to drive them to one of the two grain orientations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In equation (1), the reference vector used for each neighbor is the
reference vector closest to the actual neighbor position.  This means
it is possible two different neighbors will use the same reference
vector.  In such cases, the atom in question is far from a perfect
orientation and will likely receive the full dE addition, so the
effect of duplicate reference vector usage is small.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dir} parameter determines which grain wants to grow at the
expense of the other.  A value of 0 means the first grain will shrink;
a value of 1 means it will grow.  This assumes that \sphinxstyleemphasis{dE} is positive.
The reverse will be true if \sphinxstyleemphasis{dE} is negative.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{alat} parameter is the cubic lattice constant for the fcc or bcc
material and is only used to compute a cutoff distance of 1.57 * alat
/ sqrt(2) for finding the 12 or 8 nearest neighbors of each atom
(which should be valid for an fcc or bcc crystal).  A longer/shorter
cutoff can be imposed by adjusting \sphinxstyleemphasis{alat}.  If a particular atom has
less than 12 or 8 neighbors within the cutoff, the order parameter of
equation (1) is effectively multiplied by 12 or 8 divided by the
actual number of neighbors within the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dE} parameter is the maximum amount of additional energy added to
each atom in the grain which wants to shrink.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutlo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cuthi} parameters are used to reduce the force added
to bulk atoms in each grain far away from the boundary.  An atom in
the bulk surrounded by neighbors at the ideal grain orientation would
compute an order parameter of 0 or 1 and have no force added.
However, thermal vibrations in the solid will cause the order
parameters to be greater than 0 or less than 1.  The cutoff parameters
mask this effect, allowing forces to only be added to atoms with
order\sphinxhyphen{}parameters between the cutoff values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{File0} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{file1} are filenames for the two grains which each
contain 6 vectors (6 lines with 3 values per line) which specify the
grain orientations.  Each vector is a displacement from a central atom
(0,0,0) to a nearest neighbor atom in an fcc lattice at the proper
orientation.  The vector lengths should all be identical since an fcc
lattice has a coordination number of 12.  Only 6 are listed due to
symmetry, so the list must include one from each pair of
equal\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}opposite neighbors.  A pair of orientation files for a
Sigma=5 tilt boundary are shown below. A tutorial that can help for
writing the orientation files is given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient:wicaksono2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Wicaksono2)}}}}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy of atom interactions with the
grain boundary driving force to the global potential energy of the
system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The
default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by
these fixes. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator a fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix calculates a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the potential
energy change due to this fix.  The scalar value calculated by this
fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The array stores the
order parameter Xi and normalized order parameter (0 to 1) for each
atom.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values can be accessed on any timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are part of the ORIENT package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes should only be used with fcc or bcc lattices.

\section{fix orient/eco command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:fix-orient-eco-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_orient_eco::doc}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID orient/eco u0 eta cutoff orientationsFile
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
u0 = energy added to each atom (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eta = cutoff value (usually 0.25)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = cutoff radius for orientation parameter calculation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
orientationsFile = file that specifies orientation of each grain

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{gb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orient}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eco}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.08}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.524}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sigma5.ori}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix applies a synthetic driving force to a grain boundary which
can be used for the investigation of grain boundary motion. The
affiliation of atoms to either of the two grains forming the grain
boundary is determined from an orientation\sphinxhyphen{}dependent order parameter
as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:ulomek}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ulomek)}}}}. The potential energy of
atoms is either increased by an amount of 0.5*\sphinxstyleemphasis{u0} or \sphinxhyphen{}0.5*\sphinxstyleemphasis{u0}
according to the orientation of the surrounding crystal. This creates
a potential energy gradient which pushes atoms near the grain boundary
to orient according to the energetically favorable grain
orientation. This fix is designed for applications in bicrystal system
with one grain boundary and open ends, or two opposite grain
boundaries in a periodic system. In either case, the entire system can
experience a displacement during the simulation which needs to be
accounted for in the evaluation of the grain boundary velocity. While
the basic method is described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:ulomek}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ulomek)}}}}, the
implementation follows the efficient implementation from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:schratt}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Schratt \& Mohles)}}}}. The synthetic potential energy
added to an atom j is given by the following formulas
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}w(|\vec{r}_{jk}|) = w_{jk} & = \left\{\begin{array}{lc} \frac{|\vec{r}_{jk}|^{4}}{r_{\mathrm{cut}}^{4}}
  -2\frac{|\vec{r}_{jk}|^{2}}{r_{\mathrm{cut}}^{2}}+1, & |\vec{r}_{jk}|<r_{\mathrm{cut}} \\
   0, & |\vec{r}_{jk}|\ge r_{\mathrm{cut}}
   \end{array}\right. \\
\chi_{j} & = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{3}\left\lbrack\left\vert\psi_{l}^{\mathrm{I}}(\vec{r}_{j})\right\vert^{2}-\left\vert\psi_{l}^{\mathrm{II}}(\vec{r}_{j})\right\vert^{2}\right\rbrack \\
\psi_{l}^{\mathrm{X}}(\vec{r}_{j}) & = \sum_{k\in\mathit{\Gamma}_{j}}w_{jk}\exp\left(\mathrm{i}\vec{r}_{jk}\cdot\vec{q}_{l}^{\mathrm{X}}\right) \\
u(\chi_{j}) & = \frac{u_{0}}{2}\left\{\begin{array}{lc}
1, & \chi_{j}\ge\eta\\
\sin\left(\frac{\pi\chi_{j}}{2\eta}\right), &  -\eta<\chi_{j}<\eta\\
-1, & \chi_{j}\le-\eta
\end{array}\right.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which are fully explained in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:ulomek}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ulomek)}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:schratt}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Schratt \& Mohles)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The force on each atom is the negative gradient of the synthetic
potential energy. It depends on the surrounding of this atom. An atom
far from the grain boundary does not experience a synthetic force as
its surrounding is that of an oriented single crystal and thermal
fluctuations are masked by the parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}. Near the grain
boundary however, the gradient is nonzero and synthetic force terms
are computed.  The orientationsFile specifies the perfect oriented
crystal basis vectors for the two adjoining crystals. The first three
lines (line=row vector) for the energetically penalized and the last
three lines for the energetically favored grain assuming \sphinxstyleemphasis{u0} is
positive. For negative \sphinxstyleemphasis{u0}, this is reversed. With the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}
parameter, the size of the region around each atom which is used in
the order parameter computation is defined. The cutoff must be smaller
than the interaction range of the MD potential. It should at least
include the nearest neighbor shell. For high temperatures or low angle
grain boundaries, it might be beneficial to increase the cutoff in
order to get a more precise identification of the atoms
surrounding. However, computation time will increase as more atoms are
considered in the order parameter and force computation.  It is also
worth noting that the cutoff radius must not exceed the communication
distance for ghost atoms in LAMMPS. With orientationsFile, the 6
oriented crystal basis vectors is specified. Each line of the input
file contains the three components of a primitive lattice vector
oriented according to the grain orientation in the simulation box. The
first (last) three lines correspond to the primitive lattice vectors
of the first (second) grain. An example for a
\(\Sigma\langle001\rangle\) mis\sphinxhyphen{}orientation is given at the end.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If no synthetic energy difference between the grains is created,
\(u0=0\), the force computation is omitted. In this case, still,
the order parameter of the driving force is computed and can be used
to track the grain boundary motion throughout the simulation.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_orient_eco:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy of atom interactions with the
grain boundary driving force to the global potential energy of the
system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The
default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with 2 columns, which can be
accessed by indices 1\sphinxhyphen{}1 by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from
a fix as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first column is the order parameter for each atom; the second is
the thermal masking value for each atom.  Both are described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the start/stop keywords of
the run command. This fix is not invoked during energy minimization.

\index{fix pafi@\spxentry{fix pafi}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix pafi command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:fix-pafi-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pafi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tdamp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pafi = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}} that holds data used by this fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Temp = desired temperature (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tdamp = damping parameter (time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{overdamped} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{com}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overdamped} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or 1 or 0
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or 1 = Brownian (overdamped) integration in hyperplane
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or 0 = Langevin integration in hyperplane
\sphinxstyleemphasis{com} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or 1 or 0
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or 1 = zero linear momentum, fixing center or mass (recommended)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or 0 = do not zero linear momentum, allowing center of mass drift
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}ny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}nz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}dnx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}dny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}dnz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}ddnx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}ddny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}ddnz}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{post}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{hp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pafi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pa}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{434}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{overdamped}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform Brownian or Langevin integration whilst constraining the system to lie
in some hyperplane, which is expected to be the tangent plane to some reference
pathway in a solid state system. The instantaneous value of a modified force
projection is also calculated, whose time integral can be shown to be equal to
the true free energy gradient along the minimum free energy path local to the reference pathway.
A detailed discussion of the projection technique can be found in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pafi:swinburne}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Swinburne)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be used with LAMMPS as demonstrated in examples/PACKAGES/pafi,
though it is primarily intended to be coupled with the PAFI C++ code, developed
at \sphinxurl{https://github.com/tomswinburne/pafi},
which distributes multiple LAMMPS workers in parallel to compute and collate
hyperplane\sphinxhyphen{}constrained averages, allowing the calculation of free energy barriers and pathways.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}} must be provided with 9 fields per atom coordinate,
which in order are the x,y,z coordinates of a configuration on the reference path,
the x,y,z coordinates of the path tangent (derivative of path position with path coordinate)
and the x,y,z coordinates of the change in tangent (derivative of path tangent with path coordinate).

\sphinxAtStartPar
A 4\sphinxhyphen{}element vector is also calculated by this fix. The 4 components are the
modified projected force, its square, the expected projection of the minimum
free energy path tangent on the reference path tangent and the minimum image
distance between the current configuration and the reference configuration,
projected along the path tangent. This latter value should be essentially zero.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When com=yes/1, which is recommended, the provided tangent vector must also
have zero center of mass. This can be achieved by subtracting from each
coordinate of the path tangent the average x,y,z value. The PAFI C++ code
(see above) can generate these paths for use in LAMMPS.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When overdamped=yes/1, the Tdamp parameter should be around 5\sphinxhyphen{}10 times smaller
than that used in typical Langevin integration.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} for typical values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a global vector each timestep which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pafi:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are com = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, overdamped = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}

\index{fix pair@\spxentry{fix pair}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix pair command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:fix-pair-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pair::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pair = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = invoke this fix once every N timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pstyle = name of pair style to extract info from (e.g. eam)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more name/flag pairs can be listed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
name = name of quantity the pair style allows extraction of

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flag = 1 if pair style needs to be triggered to produce data for name, 0 if not

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{request}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rho}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{request}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uind}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uinp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extract per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities from a pair style and store them in this
fix so they can be accessed by other LAMMPS commands, e.g. by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} command or by another {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are example use cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
extract per\sphinxhyphen{}atom density from {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style eam}}}} to a dump file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
extract induced dipoles from {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style amoeba}}}} to a dump file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
extract accuracy metrics from a machine\sphinxhyphen{}learned potential to trigger output when
a condition is met (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify skip}}}} command)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} argument determines how often the fix is invoked.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} argument is the name of the pair style.  It can be a
sub\sphinxhyphen{}style used in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}} command.  If
there are multiple sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles using the same pair style, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle}
should be specified as “style:N”, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is the number of the
instance of the pair style you wish monitor (e.g., the first or second).
For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle} could be specified as “pace/extrapolation” or
“amoeba” or “eam:1” or “eam:2”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more \sphinxstyleemphasis{name/flag} pairs of arguments follow.  Each \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} is a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity which the pair style must recognize as an extraction
request.  See the doc pages for individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_styles}}}} to see what fix pair requests (if any) they support.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag} setting determines whether this fix will also trigger the
pair style to compute the named quantity so it can be extracted.  If the
quantity is always computed by the pair style, no trigger is needed;
specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag} = 0.  If the quantity is not always computed
(e.g. because it is expensive to calculate), then specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag} = 1.
This will trigger the quantity to be calculated only on timesteps it is
needed.  Again, see the doc pages for individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_styles}}}} to determine which fix pair requests (if any) need to be
triggered with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag} = 1 setting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data extracted from the pair style is stored by this fix
as either a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector or array.  If there is only one \sphinxstyleemphasis{name}
argument specified and the pair style computes a single value for each
atom, then this fix stores it as a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector.  Otherwise a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array is created, with its data in the order of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{name}
arguments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style amoeba}}}} allows extraction of
two named quantities: “uind” and “uinp”, both of which are 3\sphinxhyphen{}vectors for
each atom, i.e. dipole moments. In the example below a 6\sphinxhyphen{}column per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
array will be created.  Columns 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 will store the “uind” values;
columns 4\sphinxhyphen{}6 will store the “uinp” values.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ex}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uind}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uinp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As explained above, this fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector or array which
can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  If
an array is produced, the number of columns is the sum of the number
of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities produced by each \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} argument requested from
the pair style.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pair:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pair::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pair}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{fix phonon@\spxentry{fix phonon}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix phonon command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:fix-phonon-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{phonon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Noutput}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nwait}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{map\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
phonon = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = measure the Green’s function every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Noutput = output the dynamical matrix every this many measurements

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nwait = wait this many timesteps before measuring

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
map\_file = \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{GAMMA}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} is the file that contains the mapping info between atom ID and the lattice indices.
\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{GAMMA} flags to treate the whole simulation box as a unit cell, so that the mapping
info can be generated internally. In this case, dynamical matrix at only the gamma\sphinxhyphen{}point
will/can be evaluated.
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
prefix = prefix for output files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or none keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sysdim} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nasr}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sysdim} value = d
  d = dimension of the system, usually the same as the MD model dimension
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nasr} value = n
  n = number of iterations to enforce the acoustic sum rule
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:examples}}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{phonon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{map.in}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{LJ1D}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sysdim}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the dynamical matrix from molecular dynamics simulations
based on fluctuation\sphinxhyphen{}dissipation theory for a group of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider a crystal with \(N\) unit cells in three dimensions labeled
\(l = (l_1, l_2, l_3)\) where \(l_i\) are integers.  Each unit cell is
defined by three linearly independent vectors \(\mathbf{a}_1\),
\(\mathbf{a}_2\), \(\mathbf{a}_3\) forming a parallelepiped,
containing \(K\) basis atoms labeled \(k\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Based on fluctuation\sphinxhyphen{}dissipation theory, the force constant
coefficients of the system in reciprocal space are given by
({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_phonon:campana}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Campana}}}} , {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_phonon:kong}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Kong}}}})
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{\Phi}_{k\alpha,k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q}) = k_B T \mathbf{G}^{-1}_{k\alpha,k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{G}\) is the Green’s functions coefficients given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{G}_{k\alpha,k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q}) = \left< \mathbf{u}_{k\alpha}(\mathbf{q}) \bullet \mathbf{u}_{k^\prime \beta}^*(\mathbf{q}) \right>\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\left< \ldots \right>\) denotes the ensemble average, and
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{u}_{k\alpha}(\mathbf{q}) = \sum_l \mathbf{u}_{l k \alpha} \exp{(i\mathbf{qr}_l)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
is the \(\alpha\) component of the atomic displacement for the \(k\)
th atom in the unit cell in reciprocal space at \(\mathbf{q}\). In
practice, the Green’s functions coefficients can also be measured
according to the following formula,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{G}_{k\alpha,k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q}) =
\left< \mathbf{R}_{k \alpha}(\mathbf{q}) \bullet \mathbf{R}^*_{k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q}) \right>
- \left<\mathbf{R}\right>_{k \alpha}(\mathbf{q}) \bullet \left<\mathbf{R}\right>^*_{k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{R}\) is the instantaneous positions of atoms, and
\(\left<\mathbf{R}\right>\) is the averaged atomic positions. It
gives essentially the same results as the displacement method and is
easier to implement in an MD code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Once the force constant matrix is known, the dynamical matrix
\(\mathbf{D}\) can then be obtained by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{D}_{k\alpha, k^\prime\beta}(\mathbf{q}) =
(m_k m_{k^\prime})^{-\frac{1}{2}} \mathbf{\Phi}_{k \alpha, k^\prime \beta}(\mathbf{q})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
whose eigenvalues are exactly the phonon frequencies at \(\mathbf{q}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix uses positions of atoms in the specified group and calculates
two\sphinxhyphen{}point correlations.  To achieve this. the positions of the atoms
are examined every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} steps and are Fourier\sphinxhyphen{}transformed into
reciprocal space, where the averaging process and correlation
computation is then done.  After every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Noutput} measurements, the
matrix \(\mathbf{G}(\mathbf{q})\) is calculated and inverted to
obtain the elastic stiffness coefficients.  The dynamical matrices are
then constructed and written to \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix}.bin.timestep files in binary
format and to the file \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix}.log for each wave\sphinxhyphen{}vector
\(\mathbf{q}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
A detailed description of this method can be found in
({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_phonon:kong2011}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Kong2011}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sysdim} keyword is optional.  If specified with a value smaller
than the dimensionality of the LAMMPS simulation, its value is used
for the dynamical matrix calculation.  For example, using LAMMPS to
model a 2D or 3D system, the phonon dispersion of a 1D atomic chain
can be computed using \sphinxstyleemphasis{sysdim} = 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nasr} keyword is optional.  An iterative procedure is employed to
enforce the acoustic sum rule on \(\Phi\) at \(\Gamma\), and the number
provided by keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{nasr} gives the total number of iterations. For a
system whose unit cell has only one atom, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nasr} = 1 is sufficient;
for other systems, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nasr} = 10 is typically sufficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{map\_file} contains the mapping information between the lattice
indices and the atom IDs, which tells the code which atom sits at
which lattice point; the lattice indices start from 0. An auxiliary
code, \sphinxhref{https://code.google.com/p/latgen}{latgen}, can be employed to
generate the compatible map file for various crystals.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In case one simulates a non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic system, where the whole simulation
box is treated as a unit cell, one can set \sphinxstyleemphasis{map\_file} as \sphinxstyleemphasis{GAMMA}, so
that the mapping info will be generated internally and a file is not
needed. In this case, the dynamical matrix at only the gamma\sphinxhyphen{}point
will/can be evaluated. Please keep in mind that fix\sphinxhyphen{}phonon is designed
for cyrstals, it will be inefficient and even degrade the performance
of LAMMPS in case the unit cell is too large.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The calculated dynamical matrix elements are written out in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2/mass}}}} units.  The coordinates for \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}
points in the log file is in the units of the basis vectors of the
corresponding reciprocal lattice.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix. You can use it to change the temperature compute from thermo\_temp
to the one that reflects the true temperature of atoms in the group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No global scalar or vector or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this
fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead, this fix outputs its initialization information (including
mapping information) and the calculated dynamical matrices to the file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix}.log, with the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix}.  The dynamical matrices are
also written to files \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix}.bin.timestep in binary format.  These
can be read by the post\sphinxhyphen{}processing tool in tools/phonon to compute the
phonon density of states and/or phonon dispersion curves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords
of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix assumes a crystalline system with periodical lattice. The
temperature of the system should not exceed the melting temperature to
keep the system in its solid state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the PHONON package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  This fix also requires LAMMPS to be built
with 3d\sphinxhyphen{}FFT support which is included in the KSPACE package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_msd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute msd}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dynamical_matrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dynamical\_matrix}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_phonon:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are sysdim = the same dimension as specified by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dimension}}}} command, and nasr = 20.

\section{fix pimd/langevin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:fix-pimd-langevin-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd::doc}}

\section{fix pimd/nvt command}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keywords for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{keywords} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nhc}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{method} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmpimd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cmd}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass} value = scaling factor on mass
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sp} value = scaling factor on Planck constant
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value = temperature (temperature units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nhc} value = Nc = number of chains in Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover thermostat
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keywords for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{keywords} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrator} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermostat} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tau} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{barostat} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{taup} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixcom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{method} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmpimd} (default) or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{integrator} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{obabo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{baoab}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{physical} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{normal}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass} value = scaling factor on mass
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} value = temperature (temperature unit)
   temperature = target temperature of the thermostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermostat} values = style seed
   style value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{PILE\_L}
   seed = random number generator seed
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tau} value = thermostat damping parameter (time unit)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} value = scaling factor of the damping times of non\sphinxhyphen{}centroid modes of PILE\_L thermostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} values = pressure (pressure unit)
  pressure = scalar external pressure of the barostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{barostat} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{BZP} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{MTTK}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{taup} value = barostat damping parameter (time unit)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fixcom} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} values = epsilon sigma mass planck mvv2e
   epsilon = energy scale for reduced units (energy units)
   sigma = length scale for reduced units (length units)
   mass = mass scale for reduced units (mass units)
   planck = Planck\textquotesingle{}s constant for other unit style
   mvv2e = mass * velocity\textasciicircum{}2 to energy conversion factor for other unit style
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix pimd was renamed to fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} and fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} was added.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fix commands perform quantum molecular dynamics simulations based
on the Feynman path\sphinxhyphen{}integral to include effects of tunneling and
zero\sphinxhyphen{}point motion.  In this formalism, the isomorphism of a quantum
partition function for the original system to a classical partition
function for a ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer system is exploited, to efficiently sample
configurations from the canonical ensemble {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:feynman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Feynman)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The classical partition function and its components are given
by the following equations:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Z = & \int d{\bf q} d{\bf p} \cdot \textrm{exp} [ -\beta H_{eff} ] \\
H_{eff} = & \bigg(\sum_{i=1}^P \frac{p_i^2}{2M_i}\bigg) + V_{eff} \\
V_{eff} = & \sum_{i=1}^P \bigg[ \frac{mP}{2\beta^2 \hbar^2} (q_i - q_{i+1})^2 + \frac{1}{P} V(q_i)\bigg]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(M_i\) is the fictitious mass of the \(i\)\sphinxhyphen{}th mode, and m is the actual mass of the atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interested user is referred to any of the numerous references on
this methodology, but briefly, each quantum particle in a path integral
simulation is represented by a ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer of P quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads, labeled
from 1 to P.  During the simulation, each quasi\sphinxhyphen{}bead interacts with
beads on the other ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymers with the same imaginary time index (the
second term in the effective potential above).  The quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads also
interact with the two neighboring quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads through the spring
potential in imaginary\sphinxhyphen{}time space (first term in effective potential).
To sample the canonical ensemble, any thermostat can be applied.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} applies a Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover massive chain thermostat
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:pimd-tuckerman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tuckerman)}}}}.  With the massive chain
algorithm, a chain of NH thermostats is coupled to each degree of
freedom for each quasi\sphinxhyphen{}bead.  The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} sets the target
temperature for the system and the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{nhc} sets the number \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nc} of
thermostats in each chain.  For example, for a simulation of N particles
with P beads in each ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer, the total number of NH thermostats
would be 3 x N x P x Nc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} implements a Langevin thermostat in the normal mode
representation, and also provides a barostat to sample the NPH/NPT ensembles.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both these \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} styles implement a complete velocity\sphinxhyphen{}verlet integrator
combined with a thermostat, so no other time integration fix should be used.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} keyword determines what style of PIMD is performed.  A
value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd} is standard PIMD.  A value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmpimd} is for
normal\sphinxhyphen{}mode PIMD.  A value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{cmd} is for centroid molecular dynamics
(CMD).  The difference between the styles is as follows.
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In standard PIMD, the value used for a bead’s fictitious mass is
arbitrary.  A common choice is to use \(M_i = m/P\), which results in the
mass of the entire ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer being equal to the real quantum
particle.  But it can be difficult to efficiently integrate the
equations of motion for the stiff harmonic interactions in the ring
polymers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A useful way to resolve this issue is to integrate the equations of
motion in a normal mode representation, using Normal Mode
Path\sphinxhyphen{}Integral Molecular Dynamics (NMPIMD) {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:cao1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Cao1)}}}}.  In
NMPIMD, the NH chains are attached to each normal mode of the
ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer and the fictitious mass of each mode is chosen as Mk =
the eigenvalue of the Kth normal mode for k \textgreater{} 0. The k = 0 mode,
referred to as the zero\sphinxhyphen{}frequency mode or centroid, corresponds to
overall translation of the ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer and is assigned the mass of
the real particle.
\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Motion of the centroid can be effectively uncoupled from the other
normal modes by scaling the fictitious masses to achieve a partial
adiabatic separation.  This is called a Centroid Molecular Dynamics
(CMD) approximation {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:cao2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Cao2)}}}}.  The time\sphinxhyphen{}evolution (and
resulting dynamics) of the quantum particles can be used to obtain
centroid time correlation functions, which can be further used to
obtain the true quantum correlation function for the original system.
The CMD method also uses normal modes to evolve the system, except
only the k \textgreater{} 0 modes are thermostatted, not the centroid degrees of
freedom.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 21Nov2023: }Mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd} added to fix pimd/langevin.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix pimd/langevin supports the \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} values \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmpimd} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd}. The default value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmpimd}.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmpimd}, the normal mode representation is used to integrate the equations of motion.
The exact solution of harmonic oscillator is used to propagate the free ring polymer part of the Hamiltonian.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{method} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd}, the Cartesian representation is used to integrate the equations of motion.
The harmonic force is added to the total force of the system, and the numerical integrator is used to propagate the Hamiltonian.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{integrator} specifies the Trotter splitting method used by \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/langevin}.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hbond_dreiding:liu}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Liu)}}}} for a discussion on the OBABO and BAOAB splitting schemes. Typically
either of the two should work fine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass} sets a further scaling factor for the fictitious
masses of beads, which can be used for the Partial Adiabatic CMD
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:hone}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Hone)}}}}, or to be set as P, which results in the fictitious
masses to be equal to the real particle masses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/langevin} determines the mode of fictitious
mass preconditioning. There are two options: \sphinxstyleemphasis{physical} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{normal}. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{physical}, then the physical mass of the particles are used (and then multiplied by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass}). If \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{normal}, then the physical mass is first multiplied by the
eigenvalue of each normal mode, and then multiplied by \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass}. More precisely, the
fictitious mass of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/langevin} is determined by two factors: \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmass}.
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{physical}, then the fictitious mass is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}M_i = \mathrm{fmass} \times m\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{normal}, then the fictitious mass is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}M_i = \mathrm{fmass} \times \lambda_i \times m\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\lambda_i\) is the eigenvalue of the \(i\)\sphinxhyphen{}th normal mode.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fictitious mass is only used in the momentum of the equation of motion
(\(\mathbf{p}_i=M_i\mathbf{v}_i\)), and not used in the spring elastic energy
(\(\sum_{i=1}^P \frac{1}{2}m\omega_P^2(q_i - q_{i+1})^2\), \(m\) is always the
actual mass of the particles).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{sp} is a scaling factor on Planck’s constant, which can
be useful for debugging or other purposes.  The default value of 1.0
is appropriate for most situations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} determines which ensemble is it
going to sample. The value can be \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve} (microcanonical), \sphinxstyleemphasis{nvt} (canonical), \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} (isoenthalpic),
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} (isothermal\sphinxhyphen{}isobaric).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} specifies temperature parameter for fix styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. It should read
a positive floating\sphinxhyphen{}point number.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For pimd simulations, a temperature values should be specified even for nve ensemble. Temperature will make a difference
for nve pimd, since the spring elastic frequency between the beads will be affected by the temperature.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermostat} reads \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} of thermostat for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} can only
be \sphinxstyleemphasis{PILE\_L} (path integral Langevin equation local thermostat, as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gle:ceriotti2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ceriotti}}}}), and \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} should a positive integer number, which serves as the seed of the pseudo random number generator.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} uses the stochastic PILE\_L thermostat to control temperature. This thermostat works on the normal modes
of the ring polymer. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tau} parameter controls the centroid mode, and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} parameter controls the non\sphinxhyphen{}centroid modes.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tau} specifies the thermostat damping time parameter for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. It is in time unit. It only works on the centroid mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale} specifies a scaling parameter for the damping times of the non\sphinxhyphen{}centroid modes for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. The default
damping time of the non\sphinxhyphen{}centroid mode \(i\) is \(\frac{P}{\beta\hbar}\sqrt{\lambda_i\times\mathrm{fmass}}\) (\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{physical}) or  \(\frac{P}{\beta\hbar}\sqrt{\mathrm{fmass}}\) (\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmmode} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{normal}). The damping times of all non\sphinxhyphen{}centroid modes are the default values divided by \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The barostat parameters for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} with \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} ensemble is specified using one of \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}
keywords. A \sphinxstyleemphasis{pressure} value should be given with pressure unit. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} means couple all 3 diagonal components together when pressure is computed (hydrostatic pressure), and dilate/contract the dimensions together. The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} means x, y, and z dimensions are controlled independently using the Pxx, Pyy, and Pzz components of the stress tensor as the driving forces, and the specified scalar external pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{barostat} reads \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} of barostat for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} can
be \sphinxstyleemphasis{BZP} (Bussi\sphinxhyphen{}Zykova\sphinxhyphen{}Parrinello, as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:bussi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Bussi}}}}) or \sphinxstyleemphasis{MTTK} (Martyna\sphinxhyphen{}Tuckerman\sphinxhyphen{}Tobias\sphinxhyphen{}Klein, as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:martyna3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Martyna1}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:martyna4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Martyna2}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{taup} specifies the barostat damping time parameter for fix style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. It is in time unit.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixcom} specifies whether the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of the extended ring\sphinxhyphen{}polymer system is fixed during the pimd simulation.
Once \sphinxstyleemphasis{fixcom} is set to be \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity will be distracted from the centroid\sphinxhyphen{}mode velocities in each step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} should be used if {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj units}}}} is used for \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/langevin}. Typically one may want to use
reduced units to run the simulation, and then convert the results into some physical units (for example, {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{metal units}}}}). In this case, the 5 quantities in the physical mass units are needed: epsilon (energy scale), sigma (length scale), mass, Planck’s constant, mvv2e (mass * velocity\textasciicircum{}2 to energy conversion factor). Planck’s constant and mvv2e can be found in src/update.cpp. If there is no need to convert reduced units to physical units, you can omit the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj} and these five values will be set to 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The PIMD algorithm in LAMMPS is implemented as a hyper\sphinxhyphen{}parallel scheme
as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:calhoun}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Calhoun}}}}.  In LAMMPS this is done by using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_replica::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{multi\sphinxhyphen{}replica feature}}}} in LAMMPS, where each
quasi\sphinxhyphen{}particle system is stored and simulated on a separate partition
of processors.  The following diagram illustrates this approach.  The
original system with 2 ring polymers is shown in red.  Since each ring
has 4 quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads (imaginary time slices), there are 4 replicas of the
system, each running on one of the 4 partitions of processors.  Each
replica (shown in green) owns one quasi\sphinxhyphen{}bead in each ring.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{pimd}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To run a PIMD simulation with M quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads in each ring polymer using
N MPI tasks for each partition’s domain\sphinxhyphen{}decomposition, you would use P
= MxN processors (cores) and run the simulation as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
mpirun\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}np\PYG{+w}{ }P\PYG{+w}{ }lmp\PYGZus{}mpi\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}partition\PYG{+w}{ }MxN\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}in\PYG{+w}{ }script
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in the LAMMPS input script for a multi\sphinxhyphen{}partition simulation,
it is often very useful to define a {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{uloop\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} such as

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ibead}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uloop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pad}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where M is the number of quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads (partitions) used in the
calculation.  The uloop variable can then be used to manage I/O
related tasks for each of the partitions, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dcd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dcd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{system\PYGZus{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{ibead}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{n}{.dcd}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{ibead}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{n}{.xyz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fz}
\PYG{k}{restart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{system\PYGZus{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{ibead}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{n}{.restart1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{system\PYGZus{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{ibead}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{n}{.restart2}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}restart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{system\PYGZus{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{ibead}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{n}{.restart2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} dumps the Cartesian coordinates, but dumps the velocities and
forces in the normal mode representation. If the Cartesian velocities and forces are
needed, it is easy to perform the transformation when doing post\sphinxhyphen{}processing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is recommended to dump the image flags (\sphinxstyleemphasis{ix iy iz}) for fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin}. It
will be useful if you want to calculate some estimators during post\sphinxhyphen{}processing.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Major differences of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/nvt} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/langevin} are:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/nvt} includes Cartesian pimd, normal mode pimd, and centroid md. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/langevin} only intends to support normal mode pimd, as it is commonly enough for thermodynamic sampling.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/nvt} uses Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover chain thermostat. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/langevin} uses Langevin thermostat.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/langevin} provides barostat, so the npt ensemble can be sampled. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/nvt} only support nvt ensemble.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/langevin} provides several quantum estimators in output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/langevin} allows multiple processes for each bead. For \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/nvt}, there is a large chance that multi\sphinxhyphen{}process tasks for each bead may fail.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The dump of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/nvt} are all Cartesian. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Fix pimd/langevin} dumps normal\sphinxhyphen{}mode velocities and forces, and Cartesian coordinates.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Initially, the inter\sphinxhyphen{}replica communication and normal mode transformation parts of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/langevin} are written based on
those of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix pimd/nvt}, but are significantly revised.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} writes the state of the Nose/Hoover thermostat over all
quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify
a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that the
operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} writes the state of the barostat overall beads to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}. Since it uses a stochastic thermostat,
the state of the thermostat is not written. However, the state of the system
can be restored by reading the restart file, except that it will re\sphinxhyphen{}initialize
the random number generator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to fix pimd/nvt.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} computes a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector, which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The three quantities in
the global vector are:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the total spring energy of the quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the current temperature of the classical system of ring polymers,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the current value of the scalar virial estimator for the kinetic
energy of the quantum system {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pimd:herman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Herman)}}}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} are “extensive”, except for the
temperature, which is “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} computes a global vector of quantities, which
can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}. Note that
it outputs multiple log files, and different log files contain information
about different beads or modes (see detailed explanations below). If \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble}
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nvt}, the vector has 10 values:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic energy of the normal mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring elastic energy of the normal mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
potential energy of the bead

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total energy of all beads (conserved if \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
primitive kinetic energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
virial energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
centroid\sphinxhyphen{}virial energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
primitive pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermodynamic pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
centroid\sphinxhyphen{}virial pressure estimator

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 3 are different for different log files, and the others are the same for different log files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{npt}, the vector stores internal variables of the barostat. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} is used,
the vector has 15 values:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic energy of the normal mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring elastic energy of the normal mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
potential energy of the bead

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total energy of all beads (conserved if \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
primitive kinetic energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
virial energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
centroid\sphinxhyphen{}virial energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
primitive pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermodynamic pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
centroid\sphinxhyphen{}virial pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat velocity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat kinetic energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat potential energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat cell Jacobian

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enthalpy of the extended system (sum of 4, 12, 13, and 14; conserved if \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph})

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} is used for the barostat, the vector has 17 values:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic energy of the normal mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring elastic energy of the normal mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
potential energy of the bead

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total energy of all beads (conserved if \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
primitive kinetic energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
virial energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
centroid\sphinxhyphen{}virial energy estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
primitive pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thermodynamic pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
centroid\sphinxhyphen{}virial pressure estimator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x component of barostat velocity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
y component of barostat velocity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
z component of barostat velocity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat kinetic energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat potential energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barostat cell Jacobian

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enthalpy of the extended system (sum of 4, 14, 15, and 16; conserved if \sphinxstyleemphasis{ensemble} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph})

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords
of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are part of the REPLICA package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} cannot be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj units}}}}.
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/langevin} can be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj units}}}}. See the above part for how to use it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A PIMD simulation can be initialized with a single data file read via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.  However, this means all
quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads in a ring polymer will have identical positions and
velocities, resulting in identical trajectories for all quasi\sphinxhyphen{}beads.  To
avoid this, users can simply initialize velocities with different random
number seeds assigned to each partition, as defined by the uloop
variable, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1234}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{ibead}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_pimd:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults for fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{pimd/nvt} are method = pimd, fmass = 1.0, sp
= 1.0, temp = 300.0, and nhc = 2.

\sphinxstylestrong{(Cao1)} J. Cao and B. Berne, J Chem Phys, 99, 2902 (1993).

\sphinxstylestrong{(Cao2)} J. Cao and G. Voth, J Chem Phys, 100, 5093 (1994).

\index{fix planeforce@\spxentry{fix planeforce}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix planeforce command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:fix-planeforce-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{planeforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
planeforce = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x y z = 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector that is normal to the plane

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{hold}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{planeforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjust the forces on each atom in the group so that only the
components of force in the plane specified by the normal vector
(x,y,z) remain.  This is done by subtracting out the component of
force perpendicular to the plane.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the initial velocity of the atom is 0.0 (or in the plane), then it
should continue to move in the plane thereafter.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_lineforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix lineforce}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_planeforce:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none
