\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjust the pressure of the system by using a Langevin stochastic barostat
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:gronbech}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Gronbech)}}}}, which rescales the system volume and
(optionally) the atoms coordinates within the simulation box every
timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Langevin barostat couple each direction \sphinxstyleemphasis{L} with a pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}particle that obeys
the Langevin equation such as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_P = & \frac{N k_B T_{target}}{V} + \frac{1}{V d}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \vec r_i \cdot \vec f_i - P_{target} \\
Q\ddot{L} + \alpha{}\dot{L} = & f_P + \beta(t)\\
L^{n+1} = & L^{n} + bdt\dot{L}^{n} \frac{bdt^{2}}{2Q} \\
\dot{L}^{n+1} = & \alpha\dot{L}^{n} + \frac{dt}{2Q}\left(a f^{n}_{P} + f^{n+1}_{P}\right) + \frac{b}{Q}\beta^{n+1} \\
a = & \frac{1-\frac{\alpha{}dt}{2Q}}{1+\frac{\alpha{}dt}{2Q}} \\
b = & \frac{1}{1+\frac{\alpha{}dt}{2Q}} \\
\left< \beta(t)\beta(t') \right> = & 2\alpha k_B Tdt\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where \(dt\) is the timestep \(\dot{L}\) and \(\ddot{L}\) the first
and second derivatives of the coupled direction with regard to time,
\(\alpha\) is a friction coefficient, \(\beta\) is a random gaussian
variable and \(Q\) the effective mass of the coupled pseudoparticle. The
two first terms on the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand side of the first equation are the virial
expression of the canonical pressure. It is to be noted that the temperature
used to compute the pressure is not based on the atom velocities but rather on
the canonical
target temperature directly. This temperature is specified using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}
keyword parameter and should be close to the expected target temperature of the
system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regardless of what atoms are in the fix group, a global pressure is
computed for all atoms. Similarly, when the size of the simulation
box is changed, all atoms are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled to new positions, unless the
keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} is specified with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{partial}, in which case
only the atoms in the fix group are re\sphinxhyphen{}scaled. The latter can be
useful for leaving the coordinates of atoms in a solid substrate
unchanged and controlling the pressure of a surrounding fluid.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} commands which
perform Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover barostatting AND time integration, this fix does NOT
perform time integration of the atoms but only of the barostat coupled
coordinate. It then only modifies the box size and atom coordinates to
effect barostatting. Thus you must use a separate time integration fix,
like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} to actually update
the positions and velocities of atoms.  This fix can be used in conjunction
with thermostatting fixes to control the temperature, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_barostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto barostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to perform barostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The barostat is specified using one or more of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} \sphinxstyleemphasis{x},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keywords.  These keywords give you the
ability to specify the 3 diagonal components of an external stress tensor, and
to couple various of these components together so that the dimensions they
represent are varied together during a constant\sphinxhyphen{}pressure simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target pressures for each of the 6 diagonal components of the stress tensor
can be specified independently via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}, keywords, which
correspond to the 3 simulation box dimensions, and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}
keywords which corresponds to the 3 simulation box tilt factors. For each
component, the external pressure or tensor component at each timestep is a
ramped value during the run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}. If a target pressure is
specified for a component, then the corresponding box dimension will change
during a simulation.  For example, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} keyword is used, the y\sphinxhyphen{}box length
will change.  A box dimension will not change if that component is not
specified, although you have the option to change that dimension via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} parameter can be seen in the same way as a Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover parameter as
it is used to compute the mass of the fictitious particle. Without friction,
the barostat can be compared to a single particle Nose\sphinxhyphen{}Hoover barostat and
should follow a similar decay in time. The mass of the barostat is
linked to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} by the relation
\(Q=(N_{at}+1)\cdot{}k_BT_{target}\cdot{}P_{damp}^2\). Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}
should be expressed in time units.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As for Berendsen barostat, a Langevin barostat will not work well for
arbitrary values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is too small, the pressure and
volume can fluctuate wildly; if it is too large, the pressure will take a
very long time to equilibrate.  A good choice for many models is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}
of around 1000 timesteps.  However, note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is specified in time
units, and that timesteps are NOT the same as time units for most
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword sets the temperature to use in the equation of motion of the
barostat. This value is used to compute the value of the force \(f_P\) in
the equation of motion. It is important to note that this value is not the
instantaneous temperature but a target temperature that ramps from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}. Also the required argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} sets the seed for the random
number generator used in the generation of the random forces.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} keyword allows two or three of the diagonal components of
the pressure tensor to be “coupled” together.  The value specified
with the keyword determines which are coupled.  For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
means the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the stress tensor are coupled.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Xyz} means all 3 diagonal components are coupled.  Coupling means two
things: the instantaneous stress will be computed as an average of the
corresponding diagonal components, and the coupled box dimensions will
be changed together in lockstep, meaning coupled dimensions will be
dilated or contracted by the same percentage every timestep.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstart}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pstop}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} parameters for any coupled dimensions must
be identical.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Couple xyz} can be used for a 2d simulation; the \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
dimension is simply ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} keywords are simply shortcuts that are
equivalent to specifying several other keywords together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} means couple all 3 diagonal components together when
pressure is computed (hydrostatic pressure), and dilate/contract the
dimensions together.  Using “iso Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as
specifying these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple xyz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} means \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions are controlled
independently using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pxx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pyy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pzz} components of the
stress tensor as the driving forces, and the specified scalar external
pressure.  Using “aniso Pstart Pstop Pdamp” is the same as specifying
these 4 keywords:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} is the same as \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} but also adds the control on the
shear pressure coupled with the tilt factors.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x Pstart Pstop Pdamp
y Pstart Pstop Pdamp
z Pstart Pstop Pdamp
xy Pstart Pstop Pdamp
xz Pstart Pstop Pdamp
yz Pstart Pstop Pdamp
couple none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} keyword allows the tilt factors for a triclinic box to
exceed half the distance of the parallel box length, as discussed
below.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the bound is enforced by
flipping the box when it is exceeded.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} value is set to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, the tilt will continue to change without flipping.  Note that if
applied stress induces large deformations (e.g. in a liquid), this
means the box shape can tilt dramatically and LAMMPS will run less
efficiently, due to the large volume of communication needed to
acquire ghost atoms around a processor’s irregular\sphinxhyphen{}shaped subdomain.
For extreme values of tilt, LAMMPS may also lose atoms and generate an
error.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{friction} keyword sets the friction parameter \(\alpha\) in the
equations of motion of the barostat. For each barostat direction, the value of
\(\alpha\) depends on both \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{friction}. The value given as a
parameter is the Langevin characteristic time
\(\tau_{L}=\frac{Q}{\alpha}\) in time units. The langevin time can be understood as a
decorrelation time for the pressure. A long Langevin time value will make the
barostat act as an underdamped oscillator while a short value will make it
act as an overdamped oscillator. The ideal configuration would be to find
the critical parameter of the barostat. Empirically this is observed to
occur for \(\tau_{L}\approx{}P_{damp}\).  For this reason, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{friction}
keyword is not used, the default value \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp} is used for each barostat direction.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes pressure each timestep. To do
this, the fix creates its own computes of style “pressure”,
as if this command had been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{virial}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The kinetic contribution to the pressure is taken as the ensemble value
\(\frac{Nk_bT}{V}\) and computed by the fix itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} command for details.  Note
that the IDs of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “press” and the
group for the new computes is the same as the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press}. This
means you can change the attributes of this fix’s pressure via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature or
pressure during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID. It also means that
changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_press} will have no effect on
this fix.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{press} option is
supported by this fix.  You can use it to assign a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} you have defined to this fix which will be used
in its pressure calculations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for access by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target pressure and temperature over multiple runs, using
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this. It is recommended that
the ramped temperature is the same as the effective temperature of the
thermostatted system. That is, if the system’s temperature is ramped by other
commands, it is recommended to do the same with this pressure control.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any dimension being adjusted by this fix must be periodic.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_press_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix press/berendsen}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} = all, \sphinxstyleemphasis{flip} = yes, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{friction} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pdamp}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_press_langevin:gronbech}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{fix print@\spxentry{fix print}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix print command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:fix-print-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_print:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_print::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
print = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = print every N steps; N can be a variable (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
string = text string to print with optional variable names

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{screen} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{title}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} value = filename
\sphinxstyleemphasis{append} value = filename
\sphinxstyleemphasis{screen} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{title} value = string
  string =  text to print as 1st line of output file
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{extra}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Coords of marker atom = \PYGZdl{}x \PYGZdl{}y \PYGZdl{}z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{extra}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Coords of marker atom = \PYGZdl{}x \PYGZdl{}y \PYGZdl{}z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coord.txt}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Print a text string every N steps during a simulation run.  This can
be used for diagnostic purposes or as a debugging tool to monitor some
quantity during a run.  The text string must be a single argument, so
it should be enclosed in single or double quotes if it is more than
one word.  If it contains variables it must be enclosed in double
quotes to ensure they are not evaluated when the input script line is
read, but will instead be evaluated each time the string is printed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Jun2023: }support for vector style variables

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command for a description of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{equal} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} style variables which are typically the most
useful ones to use with the print command.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{} and vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can calculate formulas involving mathematical operations,
atom properties, group properties, thermodynamic properties, global
values calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}},
or references to other {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}}.  Vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables are printed in a bracketed, comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated format,
e.g. {[}1,2,3,4{]} or {[}12.5,2,4.6,10.1{]}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Commands parse}}}} doc
page, the text string can use “immediate” variables, specified as
\$(formula) with parenthesis, where the numeric formula has the same
syntax as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} doc page.  This is a convenient way to evaluate a
formula immediately without using the variable command to define a
named variable and then use that variable in the text string.  The
formula can include a trailing colon and format string which
determines the precision with which the numeric value is output.
This is also explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Commands_parse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Commands parse}}}} doc page.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of a numeric value, N can be specified as an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variable}}}}, which should be specified as v\_name, where name
is the variable name.  In this case, the variable is evaluated at the
beginning of a run to determine the \sphinxstylestrong{next} timestep at which the
string will be written out.  On that timestep, the variable will be
evaluated again to determine the next timestep, etc.  Thus the
variable should return timestep values.  See the stagger() and
logfreq() and stride() math functions for {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}}, as examples of useful functions to use in this
context. For example, the following commands will print output at
timesteps 10,20,30,100,200,300,1000,2000,etc:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable        }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{s}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{logfreq}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{10,3,10}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{extra}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{print}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}s}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Coords of marker atom = \PYGZdl{}x \PYGZdl{}y \PYGZdl{}z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified group\sphinxhyphen{}ID is ignored by this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{append} keyword is used, a filename is specified to
which the output generated by this fix will be written.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} is
used, then the filename is overwritten if it already exists.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{append} is used, then the filename is appended to if it already
exists, or created if it does not exist.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{screen} keyword is used, output by this fix to the screen and
logfile can be turned on or off as desired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{title} keyword allow specification of the string that will be
printed as the first line of the output file, assuming the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file}
keyword was used.  By default, the title line is as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Fix print output for fix ID
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where ID is replaced with the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by
this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{print::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{print}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_print:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are no file output, screen = yes, and title string
as described above.

\index{fix propel/self@\spxentry{fix propel/self}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix propel/self command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self:fix-propel-self-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{propel}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{magnitude}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
propel/self = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
magnitude = magnitude of self\sphinxhyphen{}propulsion force

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or one keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{qvector}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qvector} value = direction of force in ellipsoid frame
 \sphinxstyleemphasis{sx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sz} = components of \sphinxstyleemphasis{qvector}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{active}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{propel}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{40.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{active}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{propel}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{active}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{propel}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{15.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qvector}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add a force to each atom in the group due to a self\sphinxhyphen{}propulsion force. The
force is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_i = f_P e_i\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} is the particle the force is being applied to, \(f_P\)
is the magnitude of the force, and \(e_i\) is the vector direction
of the force. The specification of \(e_i\) is based on which of the
three keywords (\sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}) one selects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole}, \(e_i\) is just equal to
the dipole vectors of the atoms in the group. Therefore, if the dipoles
are not unit vectors, the \(e_i\) will not be unit vectors.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If another command changes the magnitude of the dipole, this force will
change accordingly (since \(|e_i|\) will change, which is physically
equivalent to re\sphinxhyphen{}scaling \(f_P\) while keeping \(|e_i|\) constant),
and no warning will be provided by LAMMPS. This is almost never what you
want, so ensure you are not changing dipole magnitudes with another LAMMPS
fix or pair style. Furthermore, self\sphinxhyphen{}propulsion forces (almost) always
set \(e_i\)  to be a unit vector for all times, so it’s best to set
all the dipole magnitudes to 1.0 unless you have a good reason not to
(see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} command on how to do this).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity}, \(e_i\) points in the direction
of the current velocity (a unit\sphinxhyphen{}vector). This can be interpreted as a
velocity\sphinxhyphen{}dependent friction, as proposed by e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_propel_self:erdmann1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Erdmann)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}, \(e_i\) points in the direction of a unit
vector, oriented in the coordinate frame of the ellipsoidal particles,
which defaults to point along the x\sphinxhyphen{}direction. This default behavior
can be changed by via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatvec} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatvec} keyword specifies the direction of self\sphinxhyphen{}propulsion
via a unit vector (sx,sy,sz). The arguments \sphinxstyleemphasis{sx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sz}, are
defined within the coordinate frame of the atom’s
ellipsoid. For instance, for an ellipsoid with long axis along
its x\sphinxhyphen{}direction, if one wanted the self\sphinxhyphen{}propulsion force to also
be along this axis, set \sphinxstyleemphasis{sx} equal to 1 and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sz} both equal
to zero. This keyword may only be specified for mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In using keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatvec}, the three arguments \sphinxstyleemphasis{sx},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sz} will be automatically normalized to components
of a unit vector internally to avoid users having to explicitly
do so themselves. Therefore, in mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}, the vectors \(e_i\)
will always be of unit length.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Along with adding a force contribution, this fix can also
contribute to the virial (pressure) of the system, defined as
\(f_P \sum_i <e_i . r_i>/(d V)\), where \(r_i\) is the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrapped} coordinate of particle i in the case of periodic
boundary conditions. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_propel_self:winkler1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Winkler)}}}} for a
discussion of this active pressure contribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For modes \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}, this fix is by default
included in pressure computations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity}, this fix is by default not included
in pressure computations.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast to equilibrium systems, pressure of active systems
in general depends on the geometry of the container.
The active pressure contribution as calculated in this fix
is only valid for certain boundary conditions (spherical
walls, rectangular walls, or periodic boundary conditions).
For other geometries, the pressure must be measured via
explicit calculation of the force per unit area on a wall,
and so one must not calculate it using this fix.
(Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} as described below
to turn off the virial contribution of this fix). Again,
see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_propel_self:winkler1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Winkler)}}}} for discussion of why this
is the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Furthermore, when dealing with active systems, the temperature
is no longer well defined. Therefore, one should ensure that
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} flag is used in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} command (turning
off temperature contributions).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_propel_self:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by this
fix to add the contribution due to the added forces on atoms to the
system’s virial as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.
The default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial yes} for keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{quat}. The
default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial no} for keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.


\subsection{Restrictions}

With keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole}, this fix only works when the DIPOLE package is enabled.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the BROWNIAN package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}}

\section{fix property/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:fix-property-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{property/atom/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{name1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{name2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
property/atom = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
name1,name2,… = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmass} or i\_name or d\_name or i2\_name or d2\_name
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} = molecule IDs
\sphinxstyleemphasis{q} = charge
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rmass} = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mass
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} = internal temperature of atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{heatflow} = internal heat flow of atom
i\_name = new integer vector referenced by name
d\_name = new floating\sphinxhyphen{}point vector referenced by name
i2\_name = new integer array referenced by name
   i2\_name arg = N = number of columns in the array
d2\_name = new floating\sphinxhyphen{}point array referenced by name
   d2\_name arg = N = number of columns in the array
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero of more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ghost}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ghost} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} for whether ghost atom info in communicated
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i\PYGZus{}myflag1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i\PYGZus{}myflag2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d2\PYGZus{}sxyz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ghost}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create one or more additional per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors or arrays to store
information about atoms and to use during a simulation.  The specified
\sphinxstyleemphasis{group\sphinxhyphen{}ID} is ignored by this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The atom style used for a simulation defines a set of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
properties, as explained on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} doc pages.  The latter command defines
these properties for each atom in the system when a data file is read.
This fix augments the set of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties with new custom
ones. This can be useful in several scenarios.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the atom style does not define molecule IDs, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom charge,
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom mass, internal temperature, or internal heat flow, they can
be added using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmass}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{heatflow}
keywords.  This could be useful to define “molecules” to use as rigid
bodies with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}} command, or to carry
around an extra flag with atoms (stored as a molecule ID) that can be
used by various commands like {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} to group atoms without having to use the group
command (which is limited to a total of 32 groups including \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}).
For finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles, an internal temperature and heat flow can
be used to model heat conduction as in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{GRANULAR package}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Another application is to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmass} flag in order to have
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses instead of per\sphinxhyphen{}type masses.  This could be used to
study isotope effects with partial isotope substitution. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom:isotopes}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{See
below}}}} for an example of simulating a mixture of light and
heavy water with the TIP4P water potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An alternative to using fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{property/atom} for these examples is to
use an atom style that does define molecule IDs or charge or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
mass (indirectly via diameter and density) or to use a hybrid atom
style that combines two or more atom styles to provide the union of
all their atom properties. However, this has two practical drawbacks:
first, it typically necessitates changing the format of the Atoms
section in the data file and second, it may define additional
properties that are not needed such as bond lists, which incurs some
overhead when there are no bonds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the future, we may add additional existing per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties to
fix property/atom, similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmass}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature},
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{heatflow} which “turn\sphinxhyphen{}on” specific properties defined by some atom
styles, so they can be easily used by atom styles that do not define
them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
More generally, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name} options allow one or more
new custom per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors to be defined.  Likewise the \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name} options allow one or more custom per\sphinxhyphen{}atom arrays to be
defined.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name} options take an argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
which specifies the number of columns in the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array, i.e. the
number of attributes associated with each atom.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} \textgreater{}= 1 is required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each name must be unique and can use alphanumeric or underscore
characters.  These vectors and arrays can store whatever values you
decide are useful in your simulation.  As explained below there are
several ways to initialize, access, and output these values, via input
script commands, data files, and in new code you add to LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is effectively a simple way to add per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties to a model
without needing to write code for a new {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}}
that defines the properties.  Note however that implementing a new
atom style allows new atom properties to be more tightly and
seamlessly integrated with the rest of the code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new atom properties encode values that migrate with atoms to new
processors and are written to restart files.  If you want the new
properties to also be defined for ghost atoms, then use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ghost}
keyword with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}.  This will invoke extra communication
when ghost atoms are created (at every re\sphinxhyphen{}neighboring) to ensure the
new properties are also defined for the ghost atoms.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Properties on ghost atoms}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmass} names, you most likely want
to set \sphinxstyleemphasis{ghost} yes, since these properties are stored with ghost
atoms if you use an {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}} that defines
them.  Many LAMMPS operations that use molecule IDs or charge, such
as neighbor lists and pair styles, will expect ghost atoms to have
these values.  LAMMPS will issue a warning it you define those
vectors but do not set \sphinxstyleemphasis{ghost} yes.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Limitations on ghost atom properties}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified properties for ghost atoms are not updated every
timestep, but only once every few steps when neighbor lists are
re\sphinxhyphen{}built.  Thus the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ghost} keyword is suitable for static
properties, like molecule IDs, but not for dynamic properties that
change every step.  For the latter, the code you add to LAMMPS to
change the properties will also need to communicate their new
values to/from ghost atoms, an operation that can be invoked from
within a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} that you write.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is one of a small number that can be defined in an input
script before the simulation box is created or atoms are defined.
This is so it can be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command as described next.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties that are defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} are initialized when atoms are created, e.g. by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_atoms}}}}
commands.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties defined by this fix are not.  So
you need to initialize them explicitly.  One way to do this is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, using its \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} keyword and
passing it the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID of this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus these commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}flag}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{data.txt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Molecules}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
would allow a data file to have a section like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Molecules

1 4 1.5
2 4 3.0
3 10 1.0
4 10 1.0
5 10 1.0
...
N 763 4.5
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where N is the number of atoms, the first field on each line is the
atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID, the next two are a molecule\sphinxhyphen{}ID and a floating point value
that will be stored in a new property called “flag”.  If a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
array was specified in the fix property/atom command then the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
values for that array must be specified consecutively for that
property on each line.  Note that the order of values on each line
corresponds to the order of custom names in the fix property/atom
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the the lines of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties can be listed in any
order.  Also note that all the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties specified by the
fix ID (prop in this case) must be included on each line in the
specified data file section (Molecules in this case).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Another way of initializing the new properties is via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} command.  For example, if you wanted molecules defined for
every set of 10 atoms, based on their atom\sphinxhyphen{}IDs, these commands could
be used:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cluster}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{id\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{n+nv}{/10}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}cluster}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} will create values for atoms
with IDs 31,32,33,…40 that are 4.0,4.1,4.2,…,4.9.  When the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} commands assigns them to the molecule ID for each
atom, they will be truncated to an integer value, so atoms 31\sphinxhyphen{}40 will
all be assigned a molecule ID of 4.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atomfile\sphinxhyphen{}style variables}}}} can also be used
in place of atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables, which means in this case that the
molecule IDs could be read\sphinxhyphen{}in from a separate file and assigned by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} command.  This allows you to initialize new per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
properties in a completely general fashion.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
For new atom properties specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name}, or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name}, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
property/atom}}}} commands can access their
values.  This means that the values can be used accessed by fixes like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}}, accessed by other computes like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}}, or used in {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, these commands will output both the instantaneous and
time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged values of two new properties to a custom dump file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myprops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i\PYGZus{}flag1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}flag2}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i\PYGZus{}flag1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}flag2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[2]}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i\PYGZus{}flag1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}flag2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}1[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}1[2]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to add new {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair styles}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{computes}}}} that use the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties
defined by this fix, see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Modify atom}}}} doc page
which has details on how the custom properties of this fix can be
accessed from added classes.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:isotopes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of using per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses with TIP4P water to study
isotope effects. When setting up simulations with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_tip4p::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{TIP4P pair
styles}}}} for water, you have to provide exactly one atom
type each to identify the water oxygen and hydrogen atoms. Since the
atom mass is normally tied to the atom type, this makes it impossible
to study multiple isotopes in the same simulation.  With \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix
property/atom rmass} however, the per\sphinxhyphen{}type masses are replaced by
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses. Asumming you have a working input deck for regular
TIP4P water, where water oxygen is atom type 1 and water hydrogen is
atom type 2, the following lines of input script convert this to using
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom masses:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Isotopes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rmass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ghost}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{15.9994}
\PYG{k}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.008}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When writing out the system data with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}} command, there will be a new section named with the
fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID (i.e. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Isotopes} in this case). Alternatively, you can take an
existing data file and just add this \sphinxstyleemphasis{Isotopes} section with one line
per atom containing atom\sphinxhyphen{}ID and mass. Either way, the extended data
file can be read back with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Isotopes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rmass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ghost}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{read\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tip4p}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{isotopes.data}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Isotopes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Isotopes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please note that the first \sphinxstyleemphasis{Isotopes} refers to the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID and the
second to the name of the section. The following input script code
will now change the first 100 water molecules in this example to heavy
water:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{group }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{hwat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2:300:3}
\PYG{k}{group }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{hwat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3:300:3}
\PYG{k}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{group }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{hwat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0141018}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values it stores to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, so that the values can be restored when a simulation
is restarted.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for
info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a
restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When reading data from a restart file, this fix command has to be
specified \sphinxstylestrong{after} the \sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_restart} command and \sphinxstylestrong{exactly} the
same was in the input script that created the restart file.  LAMMPS
will only check whether a fix is of the same style and has the same
fix ID and in case of a match will then try to initialize the fix
with the data stored in the binary restart file.  If the names and
associated date types in the new fix property/atom command do not
match the old one exactly, data can be corrupted or LAMMPS may crash.
If the fix is specified \sphinxstylestrong{before} the \sphinxstyleemphasis{read\_restart} command its
data will not be restored.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to
this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter
of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy
minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_property_atom:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default keyword value is ghost = no.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix python/invoke@\spxentry{fix python/invoke}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix python/invoke command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:fix-python-invoke-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{python}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{invoke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{callback}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{function\PYGZus{}name}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are ignored by this fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
python/invoke = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = execute every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
callback = \sphinxstyleemphasis{post\_force} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{end\_of\_step}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{post\_force} = callback after force computations on atoms every N time steps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{end\_of\_step} = callback after every N time steps
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{python}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{post\PYGZus{}force\PYGZus{}callback}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{here}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{l+s}{from lammps import lammps}

\PYG{l+s}{def post\PYGZus{}force\PYGZus{}callback(lammps\PYGZus{}ptr, vflag):}
\PYG{l+s}{    lmp = lammps(ptr=lammps\PYGZus{}ptr)}
\PYG{l+s}{    \PYGZsh{} access LAMMPS state using Python interface}
\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{k}{python}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}step\PYGZus{}callback}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{here}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{l+s}{def end\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}step\PYGZus{}callback(lammps\PYGZus{}ptr):}
\PYG{l+s}{    lmp = lammps(ptr=lammps\PYGZus{}ptr)}
\PYG{l+s}{    \PYGZsh{} access LAMMPS state using Python interface}
\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pf}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{python}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{invoke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{post\PYGZus{}force}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{post\PYGZus{}force\PYGZus{}callback}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{eos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{python}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{invoke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{end\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}step\PYGZus{}callback}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix allows you to call a Python function during a simulation run.
The callback is either executed after forces have been applied to atoms
or at the end of every N time steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback functions must be declared in the global scope of the
active Python interpreter. This can either be done by defining it
inline using the python command or by importing functions from other
Python modules. If LAMMPS is driven using the library interface from
Python, functions defined in the driving Python interpreter can also
be executed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each callback is given a pointer object as first argument. This can be
used to initialize an instance of the lammps Python interface, which
gives access to the LAMMPS state from Python.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
While you can access the state of LAMMPS via library functions
from these callbacks, trying to execute input script commands will in the best
case not work or in the worst case result in undefined behavior.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the PYTHON package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Building LAMMPS with the PYTHON package will link LAMMPS with the
Python library on your system.  Settings to enable this are in the
lib/python/Makefile.lammps file.  See the lib/python/README file for
information on those settings.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_invoke:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{python command}}}}

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix python/move@\spxentry{fix python/move}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix python/move command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move:fix-python-move-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{python}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pymodule.CLASS}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
pymodule.CLASS = use class \sphinxstylestrong{CLASS} in module/file \sphinxstylestrong{pymodule} to compute how to move atoms


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{python}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{py\PYGZus{}nve.NVE}
\PYG{k}{fix  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{python}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{py\PYGZus{}nve.NVE\PYGZus{}OPT}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{python/move} fix style provides a way to define ways how particles
are moved during an MD run from python script code, that is loaded from
a file into LAMMPS and executed at the various steps where other fixes
can be executed. This python script must contain specific python class
definitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This allows to implement complex position updates and also modified
time integration methods. Due to python being an interpreted language,
however, the performance of this fix can be moderately to significantly
slower than the corresponding C++ code. For specific cases, this
performance penalty can be limited through effective use of NumPy.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The python module file has to start with the following code:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}future\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{print\PYGZus{}function}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{lammps}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{ctypes}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{traceback}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{LAMMPSFix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{object}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{all}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lmp} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lammps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}name} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}name}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{LAMMPSFixMove}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{LAMMPSFix}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{all}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb}{super}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{LAMMPSFixMove}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ptr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{initial\PYGZus{}integrate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{vflag}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{final\PYGZus{}integrate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{initial\PYGZus{}integrate\PYGZus{}respa}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{vflag}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ilevel}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{iloop}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{final\PYGZus{}integrate\PYGZus{}respa}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ilevel}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{iloop}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{reset\PYGZus{}dt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{pass}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any classes implementing new atom motion functionality have to be
derived from the \sphinxstylestrong{LAMMPSFixMove} class, overriding the available
methods as needed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples for how to do this are in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{examples/python} folder.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_python_move:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}

\sphinxAtStartPar
