\index{fix qbmsst@\spxentry{fix qbmsst}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix qbmsst command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:fix-qbmsst-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qbmsst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shockvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qbmsst = style name of this fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dir = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
shockvel = shock velocity (strictly positive, velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{T\_init}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{q} value = cell mass\sphinxhyphen{}like parameter (mass\textasciicircum{}2/distance\textasciicircum{}4 units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} value = artificial viscosity (mass/distance/time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{p0} value = initial pressure in the shock equations (pressure units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} value = initial simulation cell volume in the shock equations (distance\textasciicircum{}3 units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{e0} value = initial total energy (energy units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} value = reduction in initial temperature (unitless fraction between 0.0 and 1.0)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{damp} value = damping parameter (time units) inverse of friction \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} value = random number seed (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} value = upper cutoff frequency of the vibration spectrum (1/time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} value = number of frequency bins (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} value = coupling constant between the shock system and the quantum thermal bath (positive unitless)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} value = the quantum temperature is updated every beta time steps (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{T\_init} value = quantum temperature for the initial state (temperature units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} (liquid methane modeled with the REAX force field, real units)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qbmsst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.122}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{q}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tscale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{35082}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N\PYGZus{}f}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{400}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{110}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} (quartz modeled with the BKS force field, metal units)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qbmsst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{72}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{q}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{40}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tscale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{damp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{47508}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{120.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N\PYGZus{}f}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two example input scripts are given, including shocked
\(\alpha\textrm{-quartz}\) and shocked liquid methane.  The input
script first equilibrates an initial state with the quantum thermal
bath at the target temperature and then applies \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix qbmsst} to simulate
shock compression with quantum nuclear correction.  The following two
figures plot relevant quantities for shocked
\(\alpha\textrm{-quartz}\).

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{qbmsst_init}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Figure 1. Classical temperature
\(T_{cl} = \sum \frac{m_iv_i^2}{3Nk_B}\) vs. time for coupling the
\(\alpha\textrm{-quartz}\) initial state with the quantum thermal
bath at target quantum temperature \(T^{qm} = 300 K\). The NpH
ensemble is used for time integration while QTB provides the colored
random force. \(T^{cl}\) converges at the timescale of \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp}
which is set to be 1 ps.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{qbmsst_shock}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Figure 2. Quantum temperature and pressure vs. time for simulating
shocked \(\alpha\textrm{-quartz}\) with \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix qbmsst}. The shock
propagates along the z direction. Restart of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix qbmsst} command
is demonstrated in the example input script. Thermodynamic quantities
stay continuous before and after the restart.


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command performs the Quantum\sphinxhyphen{}Bath coupled Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Scale Shock
Technique (QBMSST) integration. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:qi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Qi)}}}} for a detailed
description of this method.  QBMSST provides description of the
thermodynamics and kinetics of shock processes while incorporating
quantum nuclear effects.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{shockvel} setting determines the steady
shock velocity that will be simulated along direction \sphinxstyleemphasis{dir}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quantum nuclear effects {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{(fix qtb)}}}} can be crucial
especially when the temperature of the initial state is below the
classical limit or there is a great change in the zero point energies
between the initial and final states. Theoretical post processing
quantum corrections of shock compressed water and methane have been
reported as much as 30\% of the temperatures {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:goldman1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Goldman)}}}}.  A
self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent method that couples the shock to a quantum thermal
bath described by a colored noise Langevin thermostat has been
developed by Qi et al {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:qi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Qi)}}}} and applied to shocked methane.  The
onset of chemistry is reported to be at a pressure on the shock
Hugoniot that is 40\% lower than observed with classical molecular
dynamics.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is highly recommended that the system be already in an equilibrium
state with a quantum thermal bath at temperature of \sphinxstyleemphasis{T\_init}.  The fix
command {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qtb}}}} at constant temperature \sphinxstyleemphasis{T\_init} could
be used before applying this command to introduce self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent
quantum nuclear effects into the initial state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} are described
in the command {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix msst}}}}. The values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{e0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{p0}, or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v0} will be calculated on the first step if not specified.  The
parameter of \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} are described in the command
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qtb}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix qbmsst} command couples the shock system to a quantum thermal
bath with a rate that is proportional to the change of the total
energy of the shock system, \(E^{tot} - E^{tot}_0\).
Here \(E^{etot}\) consists of both the system energy and a thermal
term, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:qi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Qi)}}}}, and \(E^{tot}_0 = e0\) is the
initial total energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} (\(\eta\)) parameter is a unitless coupling constant
between the shock system and the quantum thermal bath. A small \(\eta\)
value cannot adjust the quantum temperature fast enough during the
temperature ramping period of shock compression while large \(\eta\)
leads to big temperature oscillation. A value of \(\eta\) between 0.3 and
1 is usually appropriate for simulating most systems under shock
compression. We observe that different values of \(\eta\) lead to almost
the same final thermodynamic state behind the shock, as expected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quantum temperature is updated every \sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} (\(\beta\)) steps
with an integration time interval \(\beta\) times longer than the
simulation time step. In that case, \(E^{tot}\) is taken as its
average over the past \(\beta\) steps. The temperature of the quantum
thermal bath \(T^{qm}\) changes dynamically according to
the following equation where \(\Delta_t\) is the MD time step and
\(\gamma\) is the friction constant which is equal to the inverse
of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp} parameter.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{dT^{qm}}{dt} = \gamma\eta\sum^\beta_{l=1}\frac{E^{tot}(t-l\Delta t) - E^{tot}_0}{3\beta N k_B}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{T\_init} is the initial temperature of the quantum
thermal bath and the system before shock loading.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all pressure styles, the simulation box stays orthorhombic in
shape. Parrinello\sphinxhyphen{}Rahman boundary conditions (tilted box) are
supported by LAMMPS, but are not implemented for QBMSST.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the state of the random number generator is not written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, this fix cannot be restarted
“exactly” in an uninterrupted fashion. However, in a statistical
sense, a restarted simulation should produce similar behaviors of the
system as if it is not interrupted.  To achieve such a restart, one
should write explicitly the same value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{beta} and set \sphinxstyleemphasis{tscale} = 0 if the system
is compressed during the first run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The progress of the QBMSST can be monitored by printing the global
scalar and global vector quantities computed by the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As mentioned above, the scalar is the cumulative energy change due to
the fix.  By monitoring the thermodynamic \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve} output, this can
be used to test if the MD timestep is sufficiently small for accurate
integration of the dynamic equations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The global vector contains five values in the following order.  The
vector values output by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{[}\sphinxstyleemphasis{dhugoniot}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{drayleigh}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_speed}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_position},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quantum\_temperature}{]}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dhugoniot} is the departure from the Hugoniot (temperature units).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{drayleigh} is the departure from the Rayleigh line (pressure units).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_speed} is the laboratory\sphinxhyphen{}frame Lagrangian speed (particle velocity) of the computational cell (velocity units).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lagrangian\_position} is the computational cell position in the reference frame moving at the shock speed. This is the distance of the computational cell behind the shock front.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quantum\_temperature} is the temperature of the quantum thermal bath \(T^{qm}\).

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To print these quantities to the log file with descriptive column
headers, the following LAMMPS commands are suggested.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix             fix\PYGZus{}id all msst z
variable        dhug    equal f\PYGZus{}fix\PYGZus{}id[1]
variable        dray    equal f\PYGZus{}fix\PYGZus{}id[2]
variable        lgr\PYGZus{}vel equal f\PYGZus{}fix\PYGZus{}id[3]
variable        lgr\PYGZus{}pos equal f\PYGZus{}fix\PYGZus{}id[4]
variable        T\PYGZus{}qm    equal f\PYGZus{}fix\PYGZus{}id[5]
thermo\PYGZus{}style    custom  step temp ke pe lz pzz econserve v\PYGZus{}dhug v\PYGZus{}dray v\PYGZus{}lgr\PYGZus{}vel v\PYGZus{}lgr\PYGZus{}pos v\PYGZus{}T\PYGZus{}qm f\PYGZus{}fix\PYGZus{}id
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is worth noting that the temp keyword for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command prints the instantaneous classical temperature
\(T^{cl}\) as described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qtb}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style is part of the QTB package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All cell dimensions must be periodic. This fix can not be used with a
triclinic cell.  The QBMSST fix has been tested only for the group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
all.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qtb}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_msst::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix msst}}}}

\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qbmsst:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are q = 10, mu = 0, tscale = 0.01, damp = 1, seed
= 880302, f\_max = 200.0, N\_f = 100, eta = 1.0, beta = 100, and
T\_init=300.0. e0, p0, and v0 are calculated on the first step.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tolerance}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxiter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/point} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/shielded} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/slater} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/fire}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = perform charge equilibration every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for charge\sphinxhyphen{}charge interactions (distance unit)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tolerance = precision to which charges will be equilibrated

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
maxiter = maximum iterations to perform charge equilibration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qfile = a filename with QEq parameters or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/streitz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qdamp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qstep} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{warn}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} value = Slater type orbital exponent (qeq/slater only)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qdamp} value = damping factor for damped dynamics charge solver (qeq/dynamic and qeq/fire only)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qstep} value = time step size for damped dynamics charge solver (qeq/dynamic and qeq/fire only)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{warn} value = do (=yes) or do not (=no) print a warning when the maximum number of iterations is reached
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{point}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{param.qeq1}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{qeq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shielded}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{param.qeq2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{slater}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{params}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{qeq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dynamic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}qeq}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fire}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}qeq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qdamp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qstep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform the charge equilibration (QEq) method as described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:rappe1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Rappe and Goddard)}}}} and formulated in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:nakano1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Nakano)}}}} (also known as the matrix inversion method) and in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:rick1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Rick and Stuart)}}}} (also known as the extended Lagrangian
method) based on the electronegativity equilization principle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can be used with any {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style}}}} in
LAMMPS, so long as per\sphinxhyphen{}atom charges are defined.  The most typical
use\sphinxhyphen{}case is in conjunction with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style}}}} that
performs charge equilibration periodically (e.g. every timestep), such
as the ReaxFF or Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire potential.  But these fixes can also
be used with potentials that normally assume per\sphinxhyphen{}atom charges are fixed,
e.g. a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Buckingham}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{LJ/Coulombic}}}}
potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the charge equilibration calculation is effectively independent
of the pair style, these fixes can also be used to perform a one\sphinxhyphen{}time
assignment of charges to atoms.  For example, you could define the QEq
fix, perform a zero\sphinxhyphen{}timestep run via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command
without any pair style defined which would set per\sphinxhyphen{}atom charges (based
on the current atom configuration), then remove the fix via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}} command before performing further dynamics.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computing and using charge values different from published
values defined for a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}charge potential like Buckingham or CHARMM
or AMBER, can have a strong effect on energies and forces, and
produces a different model than the published versions.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/comb}}}} command must still be used to
perform charge equilibration with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{COMB potential}}}}.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/reaxff}}}} command can be
used to perform charge equilibration with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ReaxFF force
field}}}}, although fix qeq/shielded yields the same
results as fix qeq/reaxff if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance}
are the same.  Eventually the fix qeq/reaxff command will be
deprecated.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The QEq method minimizes the electrostatic energy of the system (or
equalizes the derivative of energy with respect to charge of all the
atoms) by adjusting the partial charge on individual atoms based on
interactions with their neighbors within \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}.  It requires a few
parameters in the appropriate units for each atom type which are read
from a file specified by \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile}.  The file has the following format

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
1 chi eta gamma zeta qcore
2 chi eta gamma zeta qcore
...
Ntype chi eta gamma zeta qcore
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There have to be parameters given for every atom type. Wildcard entries
are possible using the same type range syntax as for “coeff” commands
(i.e., n*m, n*, *m, *). Later entries will overwrite previous ones.
Empty lines or any text following the pound sign (\#) are ignored.
Each line starts with the atom type followed by five parameters.
Only a subset of the parameters is used by each QEq style as described
below, thus the others can be set to 0.0 if desired, but all five
entries per line are required.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{chi} = electronegativity in energy units

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} = self\sphinxhyphen{}Coulomb potential in energy units

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma} = shielded Coulomb constant defined by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:vanduin}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{ReaxFF force field}}}} in distance units

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zeta} = Slater type orbital exponent defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:streitz1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire}}}} potential in reverse distance units

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qcore} = charge of the nucleus defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:streitz1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire potential}}}} potential in charge units

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix qeq styles will print a warning if the charges are not
equilibrated within \sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance} by \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} steps, unless the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{warn} keyword is used with “no” as argument.  This latter option
may be useful for testing and benchmarking purposes, as it allows
to use a fixed number of QEq iterations when \sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance} is set
to a small enough value to always reach the \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} limit.  Turning
off warnings will avoid the excessive output in that case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/point} style describes partial charges on atoms as point
charges.  Interaction between a pair of charged particles is 1/r,
which is the simplest description of the interaction between charges.
Only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} parameters from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile} file are used.
Note that Coulomb catastrophe can occur if repulsion between the pair
of charged particles is too weak.  This style solves partial charges
on atoms via the matrix inversion method.  A tolerance of 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}6 is
usually a good number.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/shielded} style describes partial charges on atoms also as
point charges, but uses a shielded Coulomb potential to describe the
interaction between a pair of charged particles.  Interaction through
the shielded Coulomb is given by equation (13) of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:vanduin}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{ReaxFF force
field}}}} paper.  The shielding accounts for charge overlap
between charged particles at small separation.  This style is the same
as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/reaxff}}}}, and can be used with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}}.  Only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma} parameters from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile} file are used. When using the string
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} as filename, these parameters are extracted directly from an
active \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} pair style.  This style solves partial charges on atoms
via the matrix inversion method.  A tolerance of 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}6 is usually a
good number.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/slater} style describes partial charges on atoms as spherical
charge densities centered around atoms via the Slater 1\sphinxstyleemphasis{s} orbital, so
that the interaction between a pair of charged particles is the product
of two Slater 1\sphinxstyleemphasis{s} orbitals.  The expression for the Slater 1\sphinxstyleemphasis{s}
orbital is given under equation (6) of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:streitz1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire}}}} paper.  Only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zeta}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{qcore}
parameters from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile} file are used. When using the string
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/streitz} as filename, these parameters are extracted directly from
an active \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/streitz} pair style.  This style solves partial charges
on atoms via the matrix inversion method.  A tolerance of 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}6 is
usually a good number.  Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} can be used to change the Slater
type orbital exponent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic} style describes partial charges on atoms as point
charges that interact through 1/r, but the extended Lagrangian method is
used to solve partial charges on atoms.  Only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}
parameters from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile} file are used.  Note that Coulomb
catastrophe can occur if repulsion between the pair of charged particles
is too weak.  A tolerance of 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}3 is usually a good number.  Keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qdamp} can be used to change the damping factor, while keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{qstep}
can be used to change the time step size.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq:shan}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{*qeq/fire*}}}} style describes the same charge model
and charge solver as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic} style, but employs a FIRE
minimization algorithm to solve for equilibrium charges.  Keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qdamp} can be used to change the damping factor, while keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{qstep}
can be used to change the time step size.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/point}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/shielded}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/slater} describe
different charge models, whereas the matrix inversion method and the
extended Lagrangian method (\sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/fire}) are
different solvers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/point}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/fire} styles all
describe charges as point charges that interact through 1/r
relationship, but solve partial charges on atoms using different
solvers.  These three styles should yield comparable results if the QEq
parameters and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance} are the same.
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/point} is typically faster, \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic} scales better on
larger sizes, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/fire} is faster than \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/dynamic}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to solve the self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent equations for electronegativity
equalization, LAMMPS imposes the additional constraint that all the
charges in the fix group must add up to zero.  The initial charge
assignments should also satisfy this constraint.  LAMMPS will print a
warning if that is not the case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Developing QEq parameters (chi, eta, gamma, zeta, and qcore) is
non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial.  Charges on atoms are not guaranteed to equilibrate with
arbitrary choices of these parameters.  We do not develop these QEq
parameters.  See the examples/qeq directory for some examples.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\section{fix qeq/comb command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:fix-qeq-comb-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/comb/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{comb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{precision}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qeq/comb = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = perform charge equilibration every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
precision = convergence criterion for charge equilibration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{file}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} value = filename
  filename = name of file to write QEQ equilibration info to
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform charge equilibration (QeQ) in conjunction with the COMB
(Charge\sphinxhyphen{}Optimized Many\sphinxhyphen{}Body) potential as described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:comb-1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(COMB\_1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:comb-2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(COMB\_2)}}}}.  It performs the charge
equilibration portion of the calculation using the so\sphinxhyphen{}called QEq
method, whereby the charge on each atom is adjusted to minimize the
energy of the system.  This fix can only be used with the COMB
potential; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/reaxff}}}} command for a QeQ
calculation that can be used with any potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only charges on the atoms in the specified group are equilibrated.
The fix relies on the pair style (COMB in this case) to calculate the
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom electronegativity (effective force on the charges).  An
electronegativity equalization calculation (or QEq) is performed in an
iterative fashion, which in parallel requires communication at each
iteration for processors to exchange charge information about nearby
atoms with each other.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:rappe-and-goddard}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Rappe\_and\_Goddard}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:rick-and-stuart}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Rick\_and\_Stuart}}}} for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
During a run, charge equilibration is performed every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} time
steps.  Charge equilibration is also always enforced on the first step
of each run.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{precision} argument controls the tolerance for the
difference in electronegativity for all atoms during charge
equilibration.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Precision} is a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off between the cost of
performing charge equilibration (more iterations) and accuracy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword is used, then information about each
equilibration calculation is written to the specified file.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to solve the self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent equations for electronegativity
equalization, LAMMPS imposes the additional constraint that all the
charges in the fix group must add up to zero.  The initial charge
assignments should also satisfy this constraint.  LAMMPS will print a
warning if that is not the case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is performing charge equilibration. Default is
the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector stores the gradient
of the charge on each atom.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values be accessed on any
timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/reaxff/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/reaxff/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cuthi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tolerance}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{params}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qeq/reaxff = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = perform QEq every this many steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutlo,cuthi = lo and hi cutoff for Taper radius

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dual} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nowarn}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dual} = process S and T matrix in parallel (only for qeq/reaxff/omp)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} N = limit the number of iterations to \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{nowarn} = do not print a warning message if the maximum number of iterations was reached
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{param.qeq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxiter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform the charge equilibration (QEq) method as described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:rappe2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Rappe and Goddard)}}}} and formulated in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:nakano2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Nakano)}}}}.  It is typically used in conjunction with the ReaxFF force
field model as implemented in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}}
command, but it can be used with any potential in LAMMPS, so long as it
defines and uses charges on each atom.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/comb}}}} command should be used to perform charge equilibration
with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{COMB potential}}}}.  For more technical details
about the charge equilibration performed by fix qeq/reaxff, see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:qeq-aktulga}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Aktulga)}}}} paper.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The QEq method minimizes the electrostatic energy of the system by
adjusting the partial charge on individual atoms based on interactions
with their neighbors.  It requires some parameters for each atom type.
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{params} setting above is the word “reaxff”, then these are
extracted from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}} command and
the ReaxFF force field file it reads in.  If a file name is specified
for \sphinxstyleemphasis{params}, then the parameters are taken from the specified file
and the file must contain one line for each atom type.  The latter
form must be used when performing QeQ with a non\sphinxhyphen{}ReaxFF potential.
Each line should be formatted as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
itype chi eta gamma
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{itype} is the atom type from 1 to Ntypes, \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi} denotes the
electronegativity in eV, \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} denotes the self\sphinxhyphen{}Coulomb
potential in eV, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma} denotes the valence orbital
exponent.  Note that these 3 quantities are also in the ReaxFF
potential file, except that eta is defined here as twice the eta value
in the ReaxFF file. Note that unlike the rest of LAMMPS, the units
of this fix are hard\sphinxhyphen{}coded to be A, eV, and electronic charge.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{dual} keyword allows to perform the optimization
of the S and T matrices in parallel. This is only supported for
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/reaxff/omp} style. Otherwise they are processed separately.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeq/reaxff/kk} style always solves the S and T matrices in
parallel.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} keyword allows changing the max number
of iterations in the linear solver. The default value is 200.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nowarn} keyword silences the warning message printed
when the maximum number of iterations was reached.  This can be
useful for comparing serial and parallel results where having the
same fixed number of QEq iterations is desired, which can be achieved
by using a very small tolerance and setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxiter} to the desired
number of iterations.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to solve the self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent equations for electronegativity
equalization, LAMMPS imposes the additional constraint that all the
charges in the fix group must add up to zero.  The initial charge
assignments should also satisfy this constraint.  LAMMPS will print a
warning if that is not the case.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This fix computes a global scalar (the number of
iterations) for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the REAXFF package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix does not correctly handle interactions involving multiple
periodic images of the same atom.  Hence, it should not be used for
periodic cell dimensions less than 10 Angstroms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix may be used in combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix efield}}}}
and will apply the external electric field during charge equilibration,
but there may be only one fix efield instance used and the electric field
vector may only have components in non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic directions. Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can be used for electric field vector components without any further
settings. Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can be used for spatially\sphinxhyphen{}varying electric field
vector components, but the resulting electric potential must be specified
as an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potential} keyword for \sphinxtitleref{fix efield}.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qmmm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix provides functionality to enable a quantum
mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) coupling of LAMMPS to a quantum
mechanical code.  The current implementation only supports an ONIOM
style mechanical coupling to the \sphinxhref{https://www.quantum-espresso.org}{Quantum ESPRESSO} plane
wave DFT package.  Electrostatic coupling is in preparation and the
interface has been written in a manner that coupling to other QM codes
should be possible without changes to LAMMPS itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interface code for this is in the lib/qmmm directory of the LAMMPS
distribution and is being made available at this early stage of
development in order to encourage contributions for interfaces to
other QM codes.  This will allow the LAMMPS side of the implementation
to be adapted if necessary before being finalized.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Details about how to use this fix are currently documented in the
description of the QM/MM interface code itself in lib/qmmm/README.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qmmm:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global scalar or vector or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities are stored by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter of this fix can be used
with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This
fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qmmm:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the QMMM package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. It also requires building a
library provided with LAMMPS.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix is only functional when LAMMPS is built as a library and
linked with a compatible QM program and a QM/MM front end into a QM/MM
executable.  See the lib/qmmm/README file for details.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qtb:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command performs the quantum thermal bath scheme proposed by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb:dammak}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Dammak)}}}} to include self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent quantum nuclear effects,
when used in conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Classical molecular dynamics simulation does not include any quantum
nuclear effect. Quantum treatment of the vibrational modes will
introduce zero point energy into the system, alter the energy power
spectrum and bias the heat capacity from the classical limit. Missing
all the quantum nuclear effects, classical MD cannot model systems at
temperatures lower than their classical limits. This effect is
especially important for materials with a large population of hydrogen
atoms and thus higher classical limits.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The equation of motion implemented by this command follows a Langevin
form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}m_i a_i = f_i + R_i - m_i\gamma v_i\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here \(m_i, a_i, f_i, R_i, \gamma, \textrm{and} v_i\)
represent in this order mass, acceleration, force exerted by all other atoms, random
force, frictional coefficient (the inverse of damping parameter damp),
and velocity. The random force \(R_i\) is “colored” so
that any vibrational mode with frequency \(\omega\) will have a
temperature\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive energy \(\theta(\omega,T)\) which
resembles the energy expectation for a quantum harmonic oscillator
with the same natural frequency:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\theta(\omega T) = \frac{\hbar}{2} + \hbar\omega \left[\exp(\frac{\hbar\omega}{k_B T})-1 \right]^{-1}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To efficiently generate the random forces, we employ the method
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qtb:barrat}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Barrat)}}}}, that circumvents the need to generate all
random forces for all times before the simulation. The memory
requirement of this approach is less demanding and independent
of the simulation duration. Since the total random force \(R_{tot}\)
does not necessarily vanish for a finite number of atoms,
\(R_i\) is replaced by \(R_i - \frac{R_{tot}}{N_{tot}}\)
to avoid collective motion of the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} parameter sets the target quantum temperature. LAMMPS will
still have an output temperature in its thermo style. That is the
instantaneous classical temperature \(T^{cl}\) derived from
the atom velocities at thermal equilibrium. A non\sphinxhyphen{}zero
\(T^{cl}\) will be present even when the quantum
temperature approaches zero. This is associated with zero\sphinxhyphen{}point energy
at low temperatures.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T^{cl} = \sum \frac{m_i v_i^2}{3 N k_B}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{damp} parameter is specified in time units, and it equals the
inverse of the frictional coefficient \(\gamma\). \(\gamma\)
should be as small as possible but slightly larger than the timescale
of anharmonic coupling in the system which is about 10 ps to 100
ps. When \(\gamma\) is too large, it gives an energy spectrum that
differs from the desired Bose\sphinxhyphen{}Einstein spectrum. When \(\gamma\)
is too small, the quantum thermal bath coupling to the system will be
less significant than anharmonic effects, reducing to a classical
limit. We find that setting \(\gamma\) between 5 THz and 1 THz
could be appropriate depending on the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The random number \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} is a positive integer used to initiate a
Marsaglia random number generator. Each processor uses the input seed
to generate its own unique seed and its own stream of random
numbers. Thus the dynamics of the system will not be identical on two
runs on different numbers of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} parameter truncate the noise frequency domain so that
vibrational modes with frequencies higher than \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} will not be
modulated. If we denote \(\Delta t\) as the time interval for the
MD integration, \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} is always reset by the code to make
\(\alpha = (int)(2\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} \(\Delta t)^{-1}\) a
positive integer and print out relative information. An appropriate
value for the cutoff frequency \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} would be around 2\textasciitilde{}3 \(f_D\),
where \(f_D\) is the Debye frequency.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} parameter is the frequency grid size, the number of points
from 0 to \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} in the frequency domain that will be
sampled. 3*2\sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} per\sphinxhyphen{}atom random numbers are required
in the random force generation and there could be as many atoms as in
the whole simulation that can migrate into every individual
processor. A larger \sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} provides a more accurate sampling of the
spectrum while consumes more memory.  With fixed \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_max} and
\(\gamma\), \sphinxstyleemphasis{N\_f} should be big enough to converge the classical
temperature \(T^{cl}\) as a function of target quantum bath
temperature. Memory usage per processor could be from 10 to 100
MBytes.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command which performs
Nose/Hoover thermostatting AND time integration, this fix does NOT
perform time integration. It only modifies forces to a colored
thermostat. Thus you must use a separate time integration fix, like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}} to actually
update the velocities and positions of atoms (as shown in the
examples). Likewise, this fix should not normally be used with
other fixes or commands that also specify system temperatures ,
e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qtb:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Because the state of the random number generator is not
saved in restart files, this means you cannot do “exact” restarts with
this fix. However, in a statistical sense, a restarted simulation
should produce similar behaviors of the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_qtb:default}}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_reaxff_bonds:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write out the bond information computed by the ReaxFF potential specified
by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}} in the exact same format as the
original stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone ReaxFF code of Adri van Duin.  The bond information
is written to \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename} on timesteps that are multiples of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery},
including timestep 0.  For time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged chemical species analysis,
please see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix reaxff/species}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified group\sphinxhyphen{}ID is ignored by this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of the output file should be reasonably self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.
The meaning of the column header abbreviations is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
id = atom id

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type = atom type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nb = number of bonds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
id\_1 = atom id of first bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
id\_nb = atom id of Nth bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mol = molecule id

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bo\_1 = bond order of first bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bo\_nb = bond order of Nth bond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
abo = atom bond order (sum of all bonds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nlp = number of lone pairs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
q = atomic charge

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the filename ends with “.gz”, the output file is written in gzipped
format.  A gzipped dump file will be about 3x smaller than the text
version, but will also take longer to write.

\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{species}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filename}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
reaxff/species = style name of this command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = sample bond\sphinxhyphen{}order every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of bond\sphinxhyphen{}order samples used for calculating averages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate average bond\sphinxhyphen{}order every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename = name of output file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{element} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{position} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete\_rate\_limit}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} value = I J Cutoff
  I, J = atom types (see asterisk form below)
  Cutoff = Bond\sphinxhyphen{}order cutoff value for this pair of atom types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{element} value = Element1, Element2, ...
\sphinxstyleemphasis{position} value = posfreq filepos
  posfreq = write position files every this many timestep
  filepos = name of position output file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} value = filedel keyword value
  filedel = name of delete species output file
  keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{specieslist} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{masslimit}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{specieslist} value = Nspecies Species1 Species2 ...
      Nspecies = number of species in list
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{masslimit} value = massmin massmax
      massmin = minimum molecular weight of species to delete
      massmax = maximum molecular weight of species to delete
\sphinxstyleemphasis{delete\_rate\_limit} value = Nlimit Nsteps
      Nlimit = maximum number of deletions allowed to occur within interval
      Nsteps = the interval (number of timesteps) over which to count deletions
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write out the chemical species information computed by the ReaxFF
potential specified by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}}.
Bond\sphinxhyphen{}order values (either averaged or instantaneous, depending on
value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}) are used to determine chemical bonds.  Every
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} timesteps, chemical species information is written to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{filename} as a two line output.  The first line is a header
containing labels. The second line consists of the following:
timestep, total number of molecules, total number of distinct species,
number of molecules of each species.  In this context, “species” means
a unique molecule.  The chemical formula of each species is given in
the first line.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to compute averaged data, it is required that there are no
neighbor list rebuilds for at least Nrepeat*Nevery steps preceding
each \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} step.  For that reason, fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff/species} may
change your neighbor list settings.  Reneighboring will occur no
more frequently than every Nrepeat*Nevery timesteps, and will
occur less frequently if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} is not a multiple of
Nrepeat*Nevery.  There will be a warning message showing the new
settings.  Having a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} setting that is larger than what is
required for correct computation of the ReaxFF force field
interactions, in combination with certain \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}
settings, can thus lead to incorrect results.  For typical ReaxFF
calculations, reneighboring only every 100 steps is already quite a
low frequency.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the filename ends with “.gz”, the output file is written in gzipped
format.  A gzipped dump file will be about 3x smaller than the text version,
but will also take longer to write.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Jun2023: }Support for wildcards added

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} can be assigned to change the minimum
bond\sphinxhyphen{}order values used in identifying chemical bonds between pairs of
atoms.  Bond\sphinxhyphen{}order cutoffs should be carefully chosen, as bond\sphinxhyphen{}order
cutoffs that are too small may include too many bonds (which will result
in an error), while cutoffs that are too large will result in fragmented
molecules.  The default cutoff of 0.3 usually gives good results.  A
wildcard asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with the I,J
arguments to set the bond\sphinxhyphen{}order cutoff for multiple pairs of atom types.
This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “n*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is
the number of atom types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means
all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from
1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from n to
\(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{element} can be used to specify the chemical
symbol printed for each LAMMPS atom type. The number of symbols must
match the number of LAMMPS atom types and each symbol must consist of
1 or 2 alphanumeric characters. By default, these symbols are the same
as the chemical identity of each LAMMPS atom type, as specified by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ReaxFF pair\_coeff}}}} command and the ReaxFF force
field file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{position} writes center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass positions of
each identified molecules to file \sphinxstyleemphasis{filepos} every \sphinxstyleemphasis{posfreq} timesteps.
The first line contains information on timestep, total number of
molecules, total number of distinct species, and box dimensions.  The
second line is a header containing labels.  From the third line
downward, each molecule writes a line of output containing the
following information: molecule ID, number of atoms in this molecule,
chemical formula, total charge, and center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass xyz positions of
this molecule.  The xyz positions are in fractional coordinates
relative to the box dimensions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{position}, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{filepos} is the name of the output
file.  It can contain the wildcard character “*”.  If the “*”
character appears in \sphinxstyleemphasis{filepos}, then one file per snapshot is written
at \sphinxstyleemphasis{posfreq} and the “*” character is replaced with the timestep
value.  For example, AuO.pos.* becomes AuO.pos.0, AuO.pos.1000, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Aug2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete} enables the periodic removal of molecules
from the system {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species:delete}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Gissinger)}}}}.  Criteria for deletion can
be either a list of specific chemical formulae or a range of molecular
weights.  Molecules are deleted every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} timesteps, and bond
connectivity is determined using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} keywords.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{filedel} argument is the name of the output file that records the species
that are removed from the system.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{specieslist} keyword permits
specific chemical species to be deleted.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nspecies} argument specifies
how many species are eligible for deletion and is followed by a list of
chemical formulae, whose strings are compared to species identified by this
fix.  For example, “specieslist 2 CO CO2” deletes molecules that are
identified as “CO” and “CO2” in the species output file.  When using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{specieslist} keyword, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{filedel} file has the following format: the
first line lists the chemical formulae eligible for deletion, and each
additional line contains the timestep on which a molecule deletion occurs
and the number of each species deleted on that timestep.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{masslimit}
keyword permits deletion of molecules with molecular weights between
\sphinxstyleemphasis{massmin} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{massmax}.  When using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{masslimit} keyword, each line of
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{filedel} file contains the timestep on which deletions occurs,
followed by how many of each species are deleted (with quantities preceding
chemical formulae).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{specieslist} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{masslimit} keywords cannot both
be used in the same \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff/species} fix.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete\_rate\_limit} keyword
can enforce an upper limit on the overall rate of molecule deletion.  The
number of deletion occurrences is limited to Nlimit within an interval of
Nsteps timesteps.  Nlimit can be specified with an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  When using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{delete\_rate\_limit} keyword, no
deletions are permitted to occur within the first Nsteps timesteps of the
first run (after reading a either a data or restart file).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} arguments specify on what
timesteps the bond\sphinxhyphen{}order values are sampled to get the average bond
order.  The species analysis is performed using the average bond\sphinxhyphen{}order
on timesteps that are a multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq}.  The average is over
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} bond\sphinxhyphen{}order samples, computed in the preceding portion of the
simulation every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} timesteps.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} must be a multiple of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} is 1.
Also, the timesteps
contributing to the average bond\sphinxhyphen{}order cannot overlap,
i.e. Nrepeat*Nevery can not exceed Nfreq.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if Nevery=2, Nrepeat=6, and Nfreq=100, then bond\sphinxhyphen{}order
values on timesteps 90,92,94,96,98,100 will be used to compute the
average bond\sphinxhyphen{}order for the species analysis output on timestep 100.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes both a global vector of length 2 and a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector,
either of which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
The values in the global vector are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 2 values in the global vector are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total number of molecules

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total number of distinct species

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector stores the molecule ID for each atom as identified
by the fix.  If an atom is not in a molecule, its ID will be 0.
For atoms in the same molecule, the molecule ID for all of them
will be the same and will be equal to the smallest atom ID of
any atom in the molecule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The “fix reaxff/species” requires that {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}} is used.
This fix is part of the REAXFF package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To write gzipped species files, you must compile LAMMPS with the \sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_GZIP option.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style reaxff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_reaxff_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix reaxff/bonds}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_reaxff_species:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default values for bond\sphinxhyphen{}order cutoffs are 0.3 for all I\sphinxhyphen{}J pairs.
The default element symbols are taken from the ReaxFF pair\_coeff command.
Position files are not written by default.
