\index{fix recenter@\spxentry{fix recenter}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix recenter command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:fix-recenter-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{recenter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
recenter = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x,y,z = constrain center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass to these coords (distance units),         any coord can also be NULL or INIT (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} value = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = group of atoms whose coords are shifted
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{recenter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{recenter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{INIT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{INIT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{recenter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{INIT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Constrain the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass position of a group of atoms by adjusting
the coordinates of the atoms every timestep.  This is simply a small
shift that does not alter the dynamics of the system or change the
relative coordinates of any pair of atoms in the group.  This can be
used to ensure the entire collection of atoms (or a portion of them)
do not drift during the simulation due to random perturbations
(e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} thermostatting).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Distance units for the x,y,z values are determined by the setting of
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword, as discussed below.  One or more x,y,z values can
also be specified as NULL, which means exclude that dimension from
this operation.  Or it can be specified as INIT which means to
constrain the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass to its initial value at the beginning of
the run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass (COM) is computed for the group specified by the
fix.  If the current COM is different than the specified x,y,z, then a
group of atoms has their coordinates shifted by the difference.  By
default the shifted group is also the group specified by the fix.  A
different group can be shifted by using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword.  For
example, the COM could be computed on a protein to keep it in the
center of the simulation box.  But the entire system (protein + water)
could be shifted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}, then the distance units of
x,y,z are defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. Angstroms
for \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} units.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in
lattice spacings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been
previously used to define the lattice spacing.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction} value
means a fractional distance between the lo/hi box boundaries, e.g. 0.5
= middle of the box.  The default is to use lattice units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}} command can be used to create
velocities with zero aggregate linear and/or angular momentum.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs its operations at the same point in the
timestep as other time integration fixes, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}.
Thus fix recenter should normally be the last such fix specified in
the input script, since the adjustments it makes to atom coordinates
should come after the changes made by time integration.  LAMMPS will
warn you if your fixes are not ordered this way.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use this fix on a small group of atoms (e.g. a molecule
in solvent) without using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword to adjust the positions
of all atoms in the system, then the results can be unpredictable.
For example, if the molecule is pushed consistently in one direction
by a flowing solvent, its velocity will increase.  But its coordinates
will be re\sphinxhyphen{}centered, meaning it is moved back towards the force.  Thus
over time, the velocity and effective temperature of the molecule
could become very large, though it won’t actually be moving due to the
re\sphinxhyphen{}centering.  If you are thermostatting the entire system, then the
solvent would be cooled to compensate.  A better solution for this
simulation scenario is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring}}}} command
to tether the molecule in place.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the distance the
group is moved by fix recenter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The 3 quantities in the
vector are xyz components of displacement applied to the group of
atoms by the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar and vector values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix should not be used with an x,y,z setting that causes a large
shift in the system on the first timestep, due to the requested COM
being very different from the initial COM.  This could cause atoms to
be lost, especially in parallel.  Instead, use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{displace_atoms::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{displace\_atoms}}}} command, which can be used to
move atoms a large distance.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_momentum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix momentum}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_recenter:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are shift = fix group\sphinxhyphen{}ID, and units = lattice.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{fix restrain@\spxentry{fix restrain}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix restrain command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain:fix-restrain-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
restrain = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lbound} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} args = atom1 atom2 Kstart Kstop r0start (r0stop)
  atom1,atom2 = IDs of two atoms in bond
  Kstart,Kstop = restraint coefficients at start/end of run (energy units)
  r0start = equilibrium bond distance at start of run (distance units)
  r0stop = equilibrium bond distance at end of run (optional) (distance units). If not
    specified it is assumed to be equal to r0start
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lbound} args = atom1 atom2 Kstart Kstop r0start (r0stop)
  atom1,atom2 = IDs of two atoms in bond
  Kstart,Kstop = restraint coefficients at start/end of run (energy units)
  r0start = equilibrium bond distance at start of run (distance units)
  r0stop = equilibrium bond distance at end of run (optional) (distance units). If not
    specified it is assumed to be equal to r0start
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} args = atom1 atom2 atom3 Kstart Kstop theta0
  atom1,atom2,atom3 = IDs of three atoms in angle, atom2 = middle atom
  Kstart,Kstop = restraint coefficients at start/end of run (energy units)
  theta0 = equilibrium angle theta (degrees)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} args = atom1 atom2 atom3 atom4 Kstart Kstop phi0 keyword/value
  atom1,atom2,atom3,atom4 = IDs of 4 atoms in dihedral in linear order
  Kstart,Kstop = restraint coefficients at start/end of run (energy units)
  phi0 = equilibrium dihedral angle phi (degrees)
  keyword/value = optional keyword value pairs. supported keyword/value pairs:
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{mult} n = dihedral multiplicity n (integer \textgreater{}= 0, default = 1)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{holdem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{45}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.75}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{holdem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lbound}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{45}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.75}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{holdem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{120.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{holdem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{45}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{48}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.75}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{120.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{texas\PYGZus{}holdem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{120.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{120.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restrain the motion of the specified sets of atoms by making them part
of a bond or angle or dihedral interaction whose strength can vary
over time during a simulation.  This is functionally similar to
creating a bond or angle or dihedral for the same atoms in a data
file, as specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, albeit
with a time\sphinxhyphen{}varying prefactor coefficient, and except for exclusion
rules, as explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the purpose of force field parameter\sphinxhyphen{}fitting or mapping a molecular
potential energy surface, this fix reduces the hassle and risk
associated with modifying data files.  In other words, use this fix to
temporarily force a molecule to adopt a particular conformation.  To
create a permanent bond or angle or dihedral, you should modify the
data file.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adding a bond/angle/dihedral with this command does not apply
the exclusion rules and weighting factors specified by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command to atoms in the restraint
that are now bonded (1\sphinxhyphen{}2,1\sphinxhyphen{}3,1\sphinxhyphen{}4 neighbors) as a result.  If they are
close enough to interact in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} sense
(non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded interaction), then the bond/angle/dihedral restraint
interaction will simply be superposed on top of that interaction.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group\sphinxhyphen{}ID specified by this fix is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second example above applies a restraint to hold the dihedral
angle formed by atoms 1, 2, 3, and 4 near 120 degrees using a constant
restraint coefficient.  The fourth example applies similar restraints
to multiple dihedral angles using a restraint coefficient that
increases from 0.0 to 2000.0 over the course of the run.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adding a force to atoms implies a change in their potential
energy as they move due to the applied force field.  For dynamics via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command, this energy can be added to the system’s
potential energy for thermodynamic output (see below).  For energy
minimization via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command, this energy
must be added to the system’s potential energy to formulate a
self\sphinxhyphen{}consistent minimization problem (see below).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order for a restraint to be effective, the restraint force must
typically be significantly larger than the forces associated with
conventional force field terms.  If the restraint is applied during a
dynamics run (as opposed to during an energy minimization), a large
restraint coefficient can significantly reduce the stable timestep
size, especially if the atoms are initially far from the preferred
conformation.  You may need to experiment to determine what value of \(K\)
works best for a given application.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the case of finding a minimum energy structure for a single
molecule with particular restraints (e.g. for fitting force field
parameters or constructing a potential energy surface), commands such
as the following may be useful:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} minimize molecule energy with restraints}
\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{600.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8675309}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{NVE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nve}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{TFIX}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{600.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24601}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{REST}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{angle1}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{angle2}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{REST}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{TFIX}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{langevin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24601}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{REST}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{angle1}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dihedral}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{angle2}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{fix\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{REST}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{energy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10000}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} sanity check for convergence}
\PYG{k}{minimize}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1e\PYGZhy{}9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100000}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} report unrestrained energies}
\PYG{k}{unfix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{REST}
\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} keyword applies a bond restraint to the specified atoms
using the same functional form used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style harmonic}}}} command.  The potential associated with
the restraint is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the following coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) and \(r_0\) are specified with the fix.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor
is included in \(K\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lbound} keyword applies a lower bound bond restraint to the specified atoms
using the same functional form used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style harmonic}}}} command if the distance between
the atoms is smaller than the equilibrium bond distance and 0 otherwise. The potential associated with
the restraint is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_0)^2 ,if\;r < r_0\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 0 \qquad\quad\quad ,if\;r \ge r_0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the following coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) and \(r_0\) are specified with the fix.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor
is included in \(K\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} keyword applies an angle restraint to the specified atoms
using the same functional form used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style harmonic}}}} command.  The potential associated with
the restraint is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the following coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) and \(\theta_0\) are specified with the fix.
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} keyword applies a dihedral restraint to the specified
atoms using a simplified form of the function used by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_charmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_style charmm}}}} command.  The potential
associated with the restraint is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K [ 1 + \cos (n \phi - d) ]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the following coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) (multiplicity, \textgreater{}= 0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(d\) (degrees) = \(\phi_0 + 180\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) and \(\phi_0\) are specified with the fix.  Note that the value of the
dihedral multiplicity \(n\) is set by default to 1. You can use the
optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{mult} keyword to set it to a different positive integer.
Also note that the energy will be a minimum when the
current dihedral angle \(\phi\) is equal to \(\phi_0\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_restrain:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy associated with this fix to the
global potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic
output}}}} The default setting for this fix is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the fictitious potential energy associated with the
added forces to be included in the total potential energy of the
system (the quantity being minimized), you MUST enable the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar and a global vector of length 3,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
The scalar is the total potential energy for \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} the restraints as
discussed above. The vector values are the sum of contributions to the
following individual categories:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bond energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
angle energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dihedral energy

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar and vector values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix rheo command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:fix-rheo-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID rheo cut kstyle zmin keyword values...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rheo = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cut = cutoff for the kernel (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kstyle = \sphinxstyleemphasis{quintic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{RK0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{RK1} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{RK2}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zmin = minimal number of neighbors for reproducing kernels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} \begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{interface/reconstruct} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{surface/detection} or}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/sum} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{density} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{self/mass} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{speed/sound}

\end{description}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} values = none, turns on thermal evolution
\sphinxstyleemphasis{interface/reconstruct} values = none, reconstructs interfaces with solid particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{surface/detection} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sdstyle} \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit} \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit/splash}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{sdstyle} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{coordination} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{divergence}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit} = threshold for surface particles
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit/splash} = threshold for splash particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} values = none, turns on velocity shifting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/sum} values = none, uses the kernel to compute the density of particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{self/mass} values = none, a particle uses its own mass in a rho summation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{density} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho01}, ... \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho0N} (density)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{speed/sound} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cs0}, ... \sphinxstyleemphasis{csN} (velocity)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quintic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{speed}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sound}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RK1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{surface}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coordination}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{40}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform time integration for RHEO particles, updating positions, velocities,
and densities. For an overview of other features available in the RHEO package,
see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{the RHEO howto}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The type of kernel is specified using \sphinxstyleemphasis{kstyle} and the cutoff is \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}. Four
kernels are currently available. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{quintic} kernel is a standard quintic
spline function commonly used in SPH. The other options, \sphinxstyleemphasis{RK0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{RK1}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{RK2}, are zeroth, first, and second order reproducing. To generate a
reproducing kernel, a particle must have sufficient neighbors inside the
kernel cutoff distance (a coordination number) to accurately calculate
moments. This threshold is set by \sphinxstyleemphasis{zmin}. If reproducing kernels are
requested but a particle has fewer neighbors, then it will revert to a
non\sphinxhyphen{}reproducing quintic kernel until it gains more neighbors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To model temperature evolution, one must specify the \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} keyword,
define a separate instance of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}},
and use atom style rheo/thermal.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the density of solid RHEO particles does not evolve and forces
with fluid particles are calculated using the current velocity of the solid
particle. If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{interface/reconstruct} keyword is used, then the density
and velocity of solid particles are alternatively reconstructed for every
fluid\sphinxhyphen{}solid interaction to ensure no\sphinxhyphen{}slip and pressure\sphinxhyphen{}balanced boundaries.
This is done by estimating the location of the fluid\sphinxhyphen{}solid interface and
extrapolating fluid particle properties across the interface to calculate a
temporary apparent density and velocity for a solid particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A modified form of Fickian particle shifting can be enabled with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword. This effectively shifts particle positions to generate a
more uniform spatial distribution. Shifting currently does not consider the
type of a particle and therefore may be inappropriate in systems consisting
of multiple fluid phases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In systems with free surfaces, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{surface/detection} keyword can be used
to classify the location of particles as being within the bulk fluid, on a
free surface, or isolated from other particles in a splash or droplet.
Shifting is then disabled in the normal direction away from the free surface
to prevent particles from diffusing away. Surface detection can also be used
to control surface\sphinxhyphen{}nucleated effects like oxidation when used in combination
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/oxidation}}}}. Surface detection is not
performed on solid bodies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{surface/detection} keyword takes three arguments: \sphinxstyleemphasis{sdstyle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit/splash}. The first, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sdstyle}, specifies whether surface particles
are identified using a coordination number (\sphinxstyleemphasis{coordination}) or the divergence
of the local particle positions (\sphinxstyleemphasis{divergence}). The threshold value for a
surface particle for either of these criteria is set by the numerical value
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit}. Additionally, if a particle’s coordination number is too low,
i.e. if it has separated off from the bulk in a droplet, it is not possible
to define surfaces and the particle is classified as a splash. The coordination
threshold for this classification is set by the numerical value of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{limit/splash}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, RHEO integrates particles’ densities using a mass diffusion
equation. Alternatively, one can update densities every timestep by performing
a kernel summation of the masses of neighboring particles by specifying the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/sum}
keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{self/mass} keyword modifies the behavior of the density summation in \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/sum}.
Typically, the density \(\rho\) of a particle is calculated as the sum over neighbors
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\rho_i = \sum_{j} W_{ij} M_j\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(W_{ij}\) is the kernel, and \(M_j\) is the mass of particle \(j\).
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{self/mass} keyword augments this expression by replacing \(M_j\) with
\(M_i\). This may be useful in simulations of multiple fluid phases with large
differences in density, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo:fix-rheo-hu}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Hu)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{density} keyword is used to specify the equilibrium density of each of the N
particle types. It must be followed by N numerical values specifying each type’s
equilibrium density \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho0}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{speed/sound} keyword is used to specify the speed of sound of each of the
N particle types. It must be followed by N numerical values specifying each type’s
speed of sound \sphinxstyleemphasis{cs}.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix must be used with atom style rheo or rheo/thermal. This fix must
be used in conjunction with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/pressure}}}}.
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/viscosity}}}}. If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermal} setting
is used, there must also be an instance of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}}. The fix group must be set to all.
Only one instance of fix rheo may be defined and it  must be defined prior
to all other RHEO fixes in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the RHEO package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was built
with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/viscosity}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/pressure}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair rheo}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_rheo_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute rheo/property/atom}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rho0} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cs} are set to 1.0 for all atom types.

\index{fix rheo/oxidation@\spxentry{fix rheo/oxidation}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix rheo/oxidation command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation:fix-rheo-oxidation-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID rheo/oxidation cut btype rsurf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rheo/oxidation = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cut = maximum bond length (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
btype = type of bonds created

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rsurf = distance from surface to create bonds (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{oxidation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{oxidation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix dynamically creates bonds on the surface of fluids to
represent physical processes such as oxidation. It is intended
for use with bond style {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond rheo/shell}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every timestep, particles check neighbors within a distance of \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}.
This distance must be smaller than the kernel length defined in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}}. Bonds of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} are created between
a fluid particle and either a fluid or solid neighbor. The fluid particles
must also be on the fluid surface, or within a distance of \sphinxstyleemphasis{rsurf} from
the surface. This process is further described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation:howto-rheo-clemmer2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Clemmer)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If used in conjunction with solid bodies, such as those generated
by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{react} option of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}},
it is recommended to use a {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid bond style}}}}
with different bond types for solid and oxide bonds.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}

\section{fix rheo/pressure command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure:fix-rheo-pressure-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID rheo/pressure type1 pstyle1 args1 ... typeN pstyleN argsN
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rheo/pressure = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
types = lists of types (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pstyle = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{taitwater} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} args = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{taitwater} args = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic} args = cubic prefactor \(A_3\) (pressure/density\textasciicircum{}2)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix defines a pressure equation of state for RHEO particles. One can
define different equations of state for different atom types. An equation
must be specified for every atom type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One first defines the atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{types}. A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used in place
of or in conjunction with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} argument to set the coefficients for
multiple pairs of atom types.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*”
or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the number of atom types, then an asterisk with
no numeric values means all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk
means all types from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types
from m to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} definition is followed by the pressure style, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pstyle}. Current
options \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{taitwater}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic}. Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} is a linear
equation of state with a particle pressure \(P\) calculated as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}P = c (\rho - \rho_0)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(c\) is the speed of sound, \(\rho_0\) is the equilibrium density,
and \(\rho\) is the current density of a particle. The numerical values of
\(c\) and \(\rho_0\) are set in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}}. Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic}
is a cubic equation of state which has an extra argument \(A_3\),
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}P = c ((\rho - \rho_0) + A_3 (\rho - \rho_0)^3) .\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{taitwater} is Tait’s equation of state:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}P = \frac{c^2 \rho_0}{7} \biggl[\left(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0}\right)^{7} - 1\biggr].\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix must be used with an atom style that includes density
such as atom\_style rheo or rheo/thermal. This fix must be used in
conjunction with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}}. The fix group must be

\section{fix rheo/thermal command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal:fix-rheo-thermal-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

attribute = \sphinxstyleemphasis{conductivity} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{specific/heat} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{latent/heat} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tfreeze} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{react}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{conductivity} args = types style args
  types = lists of types (see below)
  style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} arg = conductivity (power/temperature)

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{conductivity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constant}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{conductivity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constant}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{specific}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{heat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constant}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs time integration of temperature for atom style rheo/thermal.
In addition, it defines multiple thermal properties of particles and handles
melting/solidification, if applicable. For more details on phase transitions
in RHEO, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{the RHEO howto}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the temperature of a particle is always derived from the energy.
This implies the \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} attribute of {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{the set command}}}} does
not affect particles. Instead, one should use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sph/e} attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each atom type, one can define expressions for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{conductivity},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{specific/heat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{latent/heat}, and critical temperature (\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tfreeze}).
The conductivity and specific heat must be defined for all atom types.
The latent heat and critical temperature are optional. However, a
critical temperature must be defined to specify a latent heat.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note, if shifting is turned on in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}}, the gradient
of the energy is used to shift energies. This may be inappropriate in systems
with multiple atom types with different specific heats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each property, one must first define a list of atom types. A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card
asterisk can be used in place of or in conjunction with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} argument
to set the coefficients for multiple pairs of atom types.  This takes the
form “*” or “*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the number of atom
types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means all types from 1 to
\(N\).  A leading asterisk means all types from 1 to n (inclusive).
A trailing asterisk means all types from m to \(N\) (inclusive).  A
middle asterisk means all types from m to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} definition for each property is followed by the style. Currently,
the only option is \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant}. Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} simply applies a constant value
of respective property to each particle of the assigned type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{react} keyword controls whether bonds are created/deleted when particles
transition between a fluid and solid state. This option only applies to atom
types that have a defined value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tfreeze}. When a fluid particle’s
temperature drops below \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tfreeze}, bonds of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} are created between
nearby solid particles within a distance of \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}. The particle’s status also
swaps to a solid state. When a solid particle’s temperature rises above
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tfreeze}, all bonds of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} are broken and the particle’s status swaps
to a fluid state.

\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity:fix-rheo-viscosity-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity:syntax}}

fix ID group\PYGZhy{}ID rheo/viscosity type1 pstyle1 args1 ... typeN pstyleN argsN

\item {}

\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} = viscosity

\sphinxstyleemphasis{power} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gd0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{K}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{n}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} = viscosity
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{gd0} = critical strain rate
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} = consistency index
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} = power\sphinxhyphen{}law exponent
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix defines a viscosity for RHEO particles. One can define different
viscosities for different atom types, but a viscosity must be specified for
every atom type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One first defines the atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{types}. A wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used in place
of or in conjunction with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} argument to set the coefficients for
multiple pairs of atom types.  This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “m*”
or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the number of atom types, then an asterisk with
no numeric values means all types from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk
means all types from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types
from m to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} definition is followed by the viscosity style, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vstyle}. Two
options are available, \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{power}. Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{constant} simply
applies a constant value of the viscosity \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta} to each particle of the
assigned type. Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{power} is a Hershchel\sphinxhyphen{}Bulkley constitutive equation
for the stress \(\tau\)
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\tau = \left(\frac{\tau_0}{\dot{\gamma}} + K \dot{\gamma}^{n - 1}\right) \dot{\gamma}, \tau \ge \tau_0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\dot{\gamma}\) is the strain rate and \(\tau_0\) is the critical
yield stress, below which \(\dot{\gamma} = 0.0\). To avoid divergences, this
expression is regularized by defining a critical strain rate \sphinxstyleemphasis{gd0}. If the local
strain rate on a particle falls below this limit, a constant viscosity of \sphinxstyleemphasis{eta}
is assigned. This implies a value of
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\tau_0 = \eta \dot{\gamma}_0 - K \dot{\gamma}_0^N\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix rhok command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok:fix-rhok-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rhok}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{K}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nx, ny, nz = k\sphinxhyphen{}vector of collective density field

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K = spring constant of bias potential

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a = anchor point of bias potential

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bias}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rhok}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{npt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.0}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} output of 4 values from fix rhok: U\PYGZus{}bias rho\PYGZus{}k\PYGZus{}RE  rho\PYGZus{}k\PYGZus{}IM  \PYGZbs{}|rho\PYGZus{}k\PYGZbs{}|}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pzz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}bias}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}bias[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}bias[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}bias[3]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix applies a force to atoms given by the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U  = &  \frac{1}{2} K (|\rho_{\vec{k}}| - a)^2 \\
\rho_{\vec{k}}  = & \sum_j^N \exp(-i\vec{k} \cdot \vec{r}_j )/\sqrt{N} \\
\vec{k}  = & (2\pi n_x /L_x , 2\pi n_y  /L_y , 2\pi n_z/L_z )\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rhok:pedersen}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pedersen)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This field, which biases configurations with long\sphinxhyphen{}range order, can be
used to study crystal\sphinxhyphen{}liquid interfaces and determine melting
temperatures {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rhok:pedersen}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pedersen)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An example of using the interface pinning method is located in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{examples/PACKAGES/rhok} directory.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rhok:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the potential energy calculated by the fix to the
global potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic
output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the potential
energy discussed in the preceding paragraph.  The scalar stored by
this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rigid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bodystyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/nve} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/nvt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/npt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/nph} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/small} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/nve/small} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/nvt/small} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/npt/small} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rigid/nph/small}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bodystyle = \sphinxstyleemphasis{single} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{molecule} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{group}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{single} args = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{molecule} args = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_propname} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_varname}
  i\_propname = a custom integer vector defined via fix property/atom
  v\_varname  = an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style or atomfile\sphinxhyphen{}style variable
\sphinxstyleemphasis{group} args = N groupID1 groupID2 ...
  N = \# of groups
  groupID1, groupID2, ... = list of N group IDs
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{reinit} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp}  or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tparam} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{force} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{torque} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{infile} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gravity}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{langevin} values = Tstart Tstop Tperiod seed
  Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/stop of run (temperature units)
  Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)
  seed = random number seed to use for white noise (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reinit} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} values = Tstart Tstop Tdamp
  Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/stop of run (temperature units)
  Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} value = template\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  template\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of molecule template specified in a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command
\sphinxstyleemphasis{iso} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{aniso} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
  Pstart,Pstop = scalar external pressure at start/end of run (pressure units)
  Pdamp = pressure damping parameter (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} values = Pstart Pstop Pdamp
  Pstart,Pstop = external stress tensor component at start/end of run (pressure units)
  Pdamp = stress damping parameter (time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tparam} values = Tchain Titer Torder
  Tchain = length of Nose/Hoover thermostat chain
  Titer = number of thermostat iterations performed
  Torder = 3 or 5 = Yoshida\sphinxhyphen{}Suzuki integration parameters
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pchain} values = Pchain
  Pchain = length of the Nose/Hoover thermostat chain coupled with the barostat
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dilate} value = dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  dilate\sphinxhyphen{}group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = only dilate atoms in this group due to barostat volume changes
\sphinxstyleemphasis{force} values = M xflag yflag zflag
  M = which rigid body from 1\sphinxhyphen{}Nbody (see asterisk form below)
  xflag,yflag,zflag = off/on if component of center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass force is active
\sphinxstyleemphasis{torque} values = M xflag yflag zflag
  M = which rigid body from 1\sphinxhyphen{}Nbody (see asterisk form below)
  xflag,yflag,zflag = off/on if component of center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass torque is active
\sphinxstyleemphasis{infile} filename
  filename = file with per\sphinxhyphen{}body values of mass, center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass, moments of inertia
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gravity} values = gravity\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  gravity\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of fix gravity command to add gravitational forces
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
