\section{fix rx command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rx:fix-rx-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rx:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rx:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_rx::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{rx/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rx:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{localTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{matrix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{solver}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{minSteps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rx = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = filename containing the reaction kinetic equations and Arrhenius parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
localTemp = \sphinxstyleemphasis{none,lucy} = no local temperature averaging or local temperature defined through Lucy weighting function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
matrix = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sparse, dense} format for the stoichiometric matrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
solver = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lammps\_rk4,rkf45} = rk4 is an explicit fourth order Runge\sphinxhyphen{}Kutta method; rkf45 is an adaptive fourth\sphinxhyphen{}order Runge\sphinxhyphen{}Kutta\sphinxhyphen{}Fehlberg method

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
minSteps = \# of steps for rk4 solver or minimum \# of steps for rkf45 (rk4 or rkf45)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
maxSteps = maximum number of steps for the rkf45 solver (rkf45 only)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
relTol = relative tolerance for the rkf45 solver (rkf45 only)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
absTol = absolute tolerance for the rkf45 solver (rkf45 only)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
diag   = Diagnostics frequency for the rkf45 solver (optional, rkf45 only)

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_rx:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{rx} solves the reaction kinetic ODEs for a given reaction set that is
defined within the file associated with this command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a general reaction such that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nu_{A}A + \nu_{B}B \rightarrow \nu_{C}C\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
the reaction rate equation is defined to be of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}r = k(T)[A]^{\nu_{A}}[B]^{\nu_{B}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the current implementation, the exponents are defined to be equal
to the stoichiometric coefficients.  A given reaction set consisting
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} reaction equations will contain a total of \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} species.  A set
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} ordinary differential equations (ODEs) that describe the change
in concentration of a given species as a function of time are then
constructed based on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} reaction rate equations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ODE systems are solved over the full DPD timestep \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} using either a fourth
order Runge\sphinxhyphen{}Kutta \sphinxstyleemphasis{rk4} method with a fixed step\sphinxhyphen{}size \sphinxstyleemphasis{h}, specified
by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lammps\_rk4} keyword, or a fourth order Runge\sphinxhyphen{}Kutta\sphinxhyphen{}Fehlberg (rkf45) method
with an adaptive step\sphinxhyphen{}size for \sphinxstyleemphasis{h}. The number of ODE steps per DPD timestep
for the rk4 method is optionally specified immediately after the rk4
keyword. The ODE step\sphinxhyphen{}size is set as \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt/num\_steps}. Smaller
step\sphinxhyphen{}sizes tend to yield more accurate results but there is not
control on the error. For error control, use the rkf45 ODE solver.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The rkf45 method adjusts the step\sphinxhyphen{}size so that the local truncation error is held
within the specified absolute and relative tolerances. The initial step\sphinxhyphen{}size \sphinxstyleemphasis{h0}
can be specified by the user or estimated internally. It is recommended that the user
specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{h0} since this will generally reduced the number of ODE integration steps
required. \sphinxstyleemphasis{h0} is defined as \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt / min\_steps} if min\_steps \textgreater{}= 1. If min\_steps == 0,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{h0} is estimated such that an explicit Euler method would likely produce
an acceptable solution. This is generally overly conservative for the fourth\sphinxhyphen{}order
method and users are advised to specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{h0} as some fraction of the DPD timestep.
For small DPD timesteps, only one step may be necessary depending upon the tolerances.
Note that more than min\_steps ODE steps may be taken depending upon the ODE stiffness
but no more than max\_steps will be taken. If max\_steps is reached, an error warning
is printed and the simulation is stopped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After each ODE step, the solution error \sphinxstyleemphasis{e} is tested and weighted using the absTol
and relTol values. The error vector is weighted as \sphinxstyleemphasis{e} / (relTol * |\sphinxstyleemphasis{u}| + absTol)
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{u} is the solution vector. If the norm of the error is \textless{}= 1, the solution is
accepted, \sphinxstyleemphasis{h} is increased by a proportional amount, and the next ODE step is begun.
Otherwise, \sphinxstyleemphasis{h} is shrunk and the ODE step is repeated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Run\sphinxhyphen{}time diagnostics are available for the rkf45 ODE solver. The frequency
(in timesteps) that diagnostics are reported is controlled by the last (optional)
12th argument. A negative frequency means that diagnostics are reported once at the
end of each run. A positive value N means that the diagnostics are reported once
per N timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The diagnostics report the average \# of integrator steps and RHS function evaluations
and run\sphinxhyphen{}time per ODE as well as the average/RMS/min/max per process. If the
reporting frequency is 1, the RMS/min/max per ODE are also reported. The per ODE
statistics can be used to adjust the tolerance and min/max step parameters. The
statistics per MPI process can be useful to examine any load imbalance caused by the
adaptive ODE solver. (Some DPD particles can take longer to solve than others. This
can lead to an imbalance across the MPI processes.)


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The filename specifies a file that contains the entire set of reaction
kinetic equations and corresponding Arrhenius parameters.  The format of
this file is described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no restriction on the total number or reaction equations that
are specified.  The species names are arbitrary string names that are
associated with the species concentrations.  Each species in a given
reaction must be preceded by it’s stoichiometric coefficient.  The
only delimiters that are recognized between the species are either a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{+} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{=} character.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{=} character corresponds to an
irreversible reaction.  After specifying the reaction, the reaction
rate constant is determined through the temperature dependent
Arrhenius equation:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}k = AT^{n}e^{\frac{-E_{a}}{k_{B}T}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{A} is the Arrhenius factor in time units or concentration/time
units, \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} is the unitless exponent of the temperature dependence, and
\(E_a\) is the activation energy in energy units.  The temperature
dependence can be removed by specifying the exponent as zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The internal temperature of the coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained particles can be used
in constructing the reaction rate constants at every DPD timestep by
specifying the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}.  Alternatively, the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{lucy} can
be specified to compute a local\sphinxhyphen{}average particle internal temperature
for use in the reaction rate constant expressions.  The local\sphinxhyphen{}average
particle internal temperature is defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\theta_i^{-1} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}\omega_{Lucy}\left(r_{ij}\right)\theta_j^{-1}}{\sum_{j=1}\omega_{Lucy}\left(r_{ij}\right)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the Lucy function is expressed as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\omega_{Lucy}\left(r_{ij}\right) = \left( 1 + \frac{3r_{ij}}{r_c} \right) \left( 1 - \frac{r_{ij}}{r_c} \right)^3\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The self\sphinxhyphen{}particle interaction is included in the above equation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The stoichiometric coefficients for the reaction mechanism are stored
in either a sparse or dense matrix format. The dense matrix should only be
used for small reaction mechanisms. The sparse matrix should be used when there
are many reactions (e.g., more than 5). This allows the number of reactions and
species to grow while keeping the computational cost tractable. The matrix
format can be specified as using either the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sparse} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dense} keywords.
If all stoichiometric coefficients for a reaction are small integers (whole
numbers \textless{}= 3), a fast exponential function is used. This can save significant
computational time so users are encouraged to use integer coefficients
where possible.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is as follows (without the
parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Rxn equations and parameters                                               (one or more comment or blank lines)

1.0 hcn + 1.0 no2 = 1.0  no + 0.5 n2  + 0.5 h2 + 1.0 co   2.49E+01 0.0 1.34  (rxn equation, A, n, Ea)
1.0 hcn + 1.0  no = 1.0  co + 1.0 n2  + 0.5 h2            2.16E+00 0.0 1.52
...
1.0  no + 1.0  co = 0.5  n2 + 1.0 co2                     1.66E+06 0.0 0.69
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines list the N reaction
equations.  Each species within the reaction equation is specified
through its stoichiometric coefficient and a species tag.  Reactant
species are specified on the left\sphinxhyphen{}hand side of the equation and
product species are specified on the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand side of the equation.
After specifying the reactant and product species, the final three
arguments of each line represent the Arrhenius parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{A}, the
temperature exponent \sphinxstyleemphasis{n}, and the activation energy \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ea}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the species tags that are defined in the reaction equations
are used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_eos_table_rx::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix eos/table/rx}}}} command to
define the thermodynamic properties of each species.  Furthermore, the
number of species molecules (i.e., concentration) can be specified
either with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} command using the “d\_” prefix or by
reading directly the concentrations from a data file.  For the latter
case, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command with the fix keyword
should be specified, where the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID will be the “fix rx\textasciigrave{}ID with a \textless{}SPECIES”\textgreater{}\textasciigrave{}\_ suffix, e.g.

\sphinxAtStartPar
fix          foo all rx reaction.file …
read\_data    data.dpd fix foo\_SPECIES NULL Species


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}REACT package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

This command also requires use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style dpd}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can only be used with a constant energy or constant
enthalpy DPD simulation.

\section{fix saed/vtk command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_saed_vtk:fix-saed-vtk-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_saed_vtk:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_saed_vtk::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_saed_vtk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saed}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{vtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nevery}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nrepeat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nfreak}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
saed/vtk = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nevery = use input values every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nrepeat = \# of times to use input values for calculating averages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nfreq = calculate averages every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_ID = saed compute ID
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overwrite}:l
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{running} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window M}
    one = output a new average value every Nfreq steps
    running = output cumulative average of all previous Nfreq steps
    window M = output average of M most recent Nfreq steps
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} args = Nstart
    Nstart = start averaging on this timestep
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} arg = filename
    filename = name of file to output time averages to
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_saed_vtk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time average computed intensities from {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute saed}}}} and
write output to a file in the third generation vtk image data format for
visualization directly in parallelized visualization software packages
like ParaView and VisIt. Note that if no time averaging is done, this
command can be used as a convenient way to simply output diffraction
intensities at a single snapshot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To produce output in the image data vtk format ghost data is added
outside the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kmax} range assigned in the compute saed. The ghost data is
assigned a value of \sphinxhyphen{}1 and can be removed setting a minimum isovolume
of 0 within the visualization software. SAED images can be created by
visualizing a spherical slice of the data that is centered at
R\_Ewald*{[}h k l{]}/norm({[}h k l{]}), where R\_Ewald=1/lambda.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The group specified within this command is ignored. However, note that
specified values may represent calculations performed by saed computes
which store their own “group” definitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix saed/vtk is designed to work only with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute saed}}}}
values, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0251}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{saed}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{vtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al2O3\PYGZus{}001.saed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} arguments specify on what
timesteps the input values will be used in order to contribute to the
average.  The final averaged quantities are generated on timesteps
that are a multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq}.  The average is over \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat}
quantities, computed in the preceding portion of the simulation every
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} timesteps.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} must be a multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nevery} must be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero even if \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nrepeat} is 1.
Also, the timesteps
contributing to the average value cannot overlap,
i.e. Nrepeat*Nevery can not exceed Nfreq.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if Nevery=2, Nrepeat=6, and Nfreq=100, then values on
timesteps 90,92,94,96,98,100 will be used to compute the final average
on timestep 100.  Similarly for timesteps 190,192,194,196,198,200 on
timestep 200, etc.  If Nrepeat=1 and Nfreq = 100, then no time
averaging is done; values are simply generated on timesteps
100,200,etc.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The output for fix ave/time/saed is a file written with the third generation
vtk image data formatting.  The filename assigned by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword is
appended with \_N.vtk where N is an index (0,1,2…) to account for multiple
diffraction intensity outputs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default the header contains the following information (with example data):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} vtk DataFile Version 3.0 c\PYGZus{}SAED
Image data set
ASCII
DATASET STRUCTURED\PYGZus{}POINTS
DIMENSIONS 337 219 209
ASPECT\PYGZus{}RATIO 0.00507953 0.00785161 0.00821458
ORIGIN \PYGZhy{}0.853361 \PYGZhy{}0.855826 \PYGZhy{}0.854316
POINT\PYGZus{}DATA 15424827
SCALARS intensity float
LOOKUP\PYGZus{}TABLE default
...data
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this example, kspace is sampled across a 337 x 219 x 209 point mesh
where the mesh spacing is approximately 0.005, 0.007, and 0.008
inv(length) units in the k1, k2, and k3 directions, respectively.
The data is shifted by \sphinxhyphen{}0.85, \sphinxhyphen{}0.85, \sphinxhyphen{}0.85 inv(length) units so that
the origin will lie at 0, 0, 0.   Here, 15,424,827 kspace points are
sampled in total.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional optional keywords also affect the operation of this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} keyword determines how the values produced every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq}
steps are averaged with values produced on previous steps that were
multiples of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq}, before they are accessed by another output
command or written to a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{one}, then the values produced on timesteps
that are multiples of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} are independent of each other; they are
output as\sphinxhyphen{}is without further averaging.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{running}, then the values produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} are summed and averaged in a
cumulative sense before being output.  Each output value is thus the
average of the value produced on that timestep with all preceding
values.  This running average begins when the fix is defined; it can
only be restarted by deleting the fix via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{unfix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{unfix}}}}
command, or by re\sphinxhyphen{}defining the fix by re\sphinxhyphen{}specifying it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave} setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{window}, then the values produced on
timesteps that are multiples of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq} are summed and averaged within
a moving “window” of time, so that the last M values are used to
produce the output.  E.g. if M = 3 and Nfreq = 1000, then the output
on step 10000 will be the average of the individual values on steps
8000,9000,10000.  Outputs on early steps will average over less than M
values if they are not available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} keyword specifies what timestep averaging will begin on.
The default is step 0.  Often input values can be 0.0 at time 0, so
setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} to a larger value can avoid including a 0.0 in a
running or windowed average.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword allows a filename to be specified.  Every \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfreq}
steps, the vector of saed intensity data is written to a new file using
the third generation vtk format.  The base of each file is assigned by
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file} keyword and this string is appended with \_N.vtk where N is
an index (0,1,2…) to account for situations with multiple diffraction
intensity outputs.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_saed_vtk:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the DIFFRACTION package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Related commands}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_saed}}}}

Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{setforce/kk}


\section{fix setforce/spin command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_setforce:fix-setforce-spin-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_setforce:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{setforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
setforce = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fx,fy,fz = force component values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
any of fx,fy,fz can be a variable (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region atoms must be in to have added force
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_setforce:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{freeze}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{indenter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{setforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{edge}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{setforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{edge}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{setforce}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{edge}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{setforce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}oscillate}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_setforce:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set each component of force on each atom in the group to the specified
values fx,fy,fz.  This erases all previously computed forces on the
atom, though additional fixes could add new forces.  This command can
be used to freeze certain atoms in the simulation by zeroing their
force, either for running dynamics or performing an energy
minimization.  For dynamics, this assumes their initial velocity is
also zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the fx,fy,fz values can be specified as NULL which means do not
alter the force component in that dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the 3 quantities defining the force components can be specified
as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, namely \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}.  If the value is a variable, it should be specified as
v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable
will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine the
force component.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus it is easy to specify a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force
field with optional time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the atom must also be in the
specified geometric {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} in order to have force added
to it.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin} suffix sets the components of the magnetic precession
vectors instead of the mechanical forces. This also erases all
previously computed magnetic precession vectors on the atom, though
additional magnetic fixes could add new forces.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can be used to freeze the magnetic moment of certain
atoms in the simulation by zeroing their precession vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All options defined above remain valid, they just apply to the magnetic
precession vectors instead of the forces.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The region keyword is supported by Kokkos, but a Kokkos\sphinxhyphen{}enabled
region must be used. See the region {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command for
more information.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_setforce:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by
this fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is setting the forces to the desired values; on all
other levels, the force is set to 0.0 for the atoms in the fix group,
so that setforce values are not counted multiple times. Default is to
to override forces at the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  This is the total
force on the group of atoms before the forces on individual atoms are
changed by the fix.  The vector values calculated by this fix are
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command, but you cannot set
forces to any value besides zero when performing a minimization.  Use
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix addforce}}}} command if you want to apply a
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero force to atoms during a minimization.

package}}}} page for more info.

\index{fix sgcmc@\spxentry{fix sgcmc}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix sgcmc command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:fix-sgcmc-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sgcmc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{every\PYGZus{}nsteps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{swap\PYGZus{}fraction}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{deltamu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sgcmc = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
every\_nsteps = number of MD steps between MC cycles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
swap\_fraction = fraction of a full MC cycle carried out at each call (a value of 1.0 will perform as many trial moves as there are atoms)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature = temperature that enters Boltzmann factor in Metropolis criterion (usually the same as MD temperature)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
deltamu = \sphinxtitleref{N\sphinxhyphen{}1} chemical potential differences \(\mu_1-\mu_2, \ldots, \mu_1-\mu_N\) (\sphinxtitleref{N} is the number of atom types)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to fix definition line:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{variance} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{randseed} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_moves} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_size}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{variance} kappa conc1 {[}conc2{]} ... {[}concN{]}
    kappa = variance constraint parameter
    \sphinxtitleref{c\_2}, \sphinxtitleref{c\_3},..., \sphinxtitleref{c\_N} = \sphinxtitleref{N\sphinxhyphen{}1} target concentration fractions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{randseed} N
    N = seed for pseudo random number generator
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_moves} N
    N = number of times sampling window is moved during one MC cycle
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_size} frac
    frac = size of sampling window (must be between 0.5 and 1.0)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sgcmc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{400.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.55}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{vc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sgcmc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{700.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{randseed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{324234}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{variance}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.05}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sgcmc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{700.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{window\PYGZus{}moves}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 22Dec2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command allows to carry out parallel hybrid molecular
dynamics/Monte Carlo (MD/MC) simulations using the algorithms described
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sadigh1)}}}}.  Simulations can be carried out in either
the semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand canonical (SGC) or variance constrained semi\sphinxhyphen{}grand
canonical (VC\sphinxhyphen{}SGC) ensemble {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sadigh2)}}}}. Only atom type
swaps are performed by the SGCMC fix. Relaxations are accounted for by
the molecular dynamics integration steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be used with standard multi\sphinxhyphen{}element EAM potentials
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair styles eam/alloy or eam/fs}}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SGCMC fix can handle Finnis/Sinclair type EAM potentials where
\(\rho(r)\) is atom\sphinxhyphen{}type specific, such that different elements can
contribute differently to the total electron density at an atomic site
depending on the identity of the element at that atomic site.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If this fix is applied, the regular MD simulation will be interrupted in
defined intervals to carry out a fraction of a Monte Carlo (MC)
cycle. The interval is set using the parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{every\_nsteps} which
determines how many MD integrator steps are taken between subsequent
calls to the MC routine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is possible to carry out pure lattice MC simulations by setting
\sphinxstyleemphasis{every\_nsteps} to 1 and not defining an integration fix such as NVE,
NPT etc.  In that case, the particles will not move and only the MC
routine will be called to perform atom type swaps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{swap\_fraction} determines how many MC trial steps are carried
out every time the MC routine is entered. It is measured in units of full MC
cycles where one full cycle, \sphinxstyleemphasis{swap\_fraction=1}, corresponds to as many MC
trial steps as there are atoms.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} specifies the temperature that is used
to evaluate the Metropolis acceptance criterion. While it usually
should be set to the same value as the MD temperature there are cases
when it can be useful to use two different values for at least part of
the simulation, e.g., to speed up equilibration at low temperatures.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{deltamu} is used to set the chemical potential differences
in the SGC MC algorithm (see Eq. 16 in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Sadigh1}}}}).
The \sphinxtitleref{N\sphinxhyphen{}1} differences are defined as \(\mu_1-\mu_2, \ldots, \mu_1-\mu_N\),
where \sphinxtitleref{N} is the number of atom types.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The variance\sphinxhyphen{}constrained SGC MC algorithm is activated if the keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{variance} is used. In that case the fix parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{deltamu} determines
the effective average constraint in the parallel VC\sphinxhyphen{}SGC MC algorithm
(parameter \(\delta\mu_0\) in Eq. (20) of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Sadigh1}}}}). The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{kappa} specifies the variance constraint
(see Eqs. (20\sphinxhyphen{}21) in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Sadigh1}}}}).
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{conc} sets the \sphinxtitleref{N\sphinxhyphen{}1} target atomic concentration
fractions (parameter \(c_0\) in Eqs.  (20\sphinxhyphen{}21) of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Sadigh1}}}})
\(0 \le c_2, \ldots, c_N \le 1\), with
\(c_1 = 1 - \Sigma_{i=2}^N c_i\).
When the simulation includes \sphinxtitleref{N} atom types (elements),
\sphinxtitleref{N\sphinxhyphen{}1} concentration values must be specified.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
There are several technical parameters that can be set via optional flags.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{randseed} is expected to be a positive integer number and is used
to initialize the random number generator on each processor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_size} controls the size of the sampling window in a parallel MC
simulation. The size has to lie between 0.5 and 1.0. Normally, this
parameter should be left unspecified which instructs the code to choose
the optimal window size automatically (see Sect. III.B and Figure 6 in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Sadigh1}}}} for details).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of times the window is moved during a MC cycle is set using
the parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_moves} (see Sect. III.B in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:sadigh1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Sadigh1}}}} for details).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to restart files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MC routine keeps track of the global concentration(s) as well as the
number of accepted and rejected trial swaps during each MC step. These
values are provided by the sgcmc fix in the form of a global vector that
can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}
components of the vector represent the following quantities:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 = The absolute number of accepted trial swaps during the last MC step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2 = The absolute number of rejected trial swaps during the last MC step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3 = Current global concentration \sphinxtitleref{c\_1} (= number of atoms of type 1 / total number of atoms)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
4 = Current global concentration \sphinxtitleref{c\_2} (= number of atoms of type 2 / total number of atoms)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N+2 = Current global concentration \sphinxtitleref{c\_N} (= number of atoms of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} / total number of atoms)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by this fix are “intensive”.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package. It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style requires an {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} with per atom
type masses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
At present the fix provides optimized subroutines for EAM type
potentials (see above) that calculate potential energy changes due to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{local} atom type swaps very efficiently.  Other potentials are
supported by using the generic potential functions. This, however, will
lead to exceedingly slow simulations since it implies that the
energy of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{entire} system is recomputed at each MC trial step.  If
other potentials are to be used it is strongly recommended to modify and
optimize the existing generic potential functions for this purpose.
Also, the generic energy calculation can not be used for parallel
execution i.e. it only works with a single MPI process.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sgcmc:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional parameters default to the following values:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{randseed} = 324234

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_moves} = 8

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{window\_size} = automatic

\end{itemize}

\section{fix shake command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:fix-shake-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{shake/kk}


\section{fix rattle command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:fix-rattle-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = shake or rattle = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tol = accuracy tolerance of SHAKE solution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
iter = max \# of iterations in each SHAKE solution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = print SHAKE statistics every this many timesteps (0 = never)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more constraint/value pairs are appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
constraint = \sphinxstyleemphasis{b} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{a} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{t} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{m}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{b} values = one or more bond types (may use type labels)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{a} values = one or more angle types  (may use type labels)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{t} values = one or more atom types (may use type labels)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{m} value = one or more mass values
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kbond}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} value = template\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  template\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of molecule template specified in a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command
\sphinxstyleemphasis{kbond} value = force constant
  force constant = force constant used to apply a restraint force when used during minimization
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sub}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rattle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{sub}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rattle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myMol}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply bond and angle constraints to specified bonds and angles in the
simulation by either the SHAKE or RATTLE algorithms.  This typically
enables a longer timestep.  The SHAKE or RATTLE constraint algorithms,
however, can \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} be applied during molecular dynamics runs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes may now also be used during minimization.  In that case the
constraints are \sphinxstyleemphasis{approximated} by strong harmonic restraints.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SHAKE vs RATTLE:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SHAKE algorithm was invented for schemes such as standard Verlet
timestepping, where only the coordinates are integrated and the
velocities are approximated as finite differences to the trajectories
({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake:ryckaert}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ryckaert et al. (1977)}}}}).  If the velocities are
integrated explicitly, as with velocity Verlet which is what LAMMPS
uses as an integration method, a second set of constraining forces is
required in order to eliminate velocity components along the bonds
({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake:andersen3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Andersen (1983)}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to formulate individual constraints for SHAKE and RATTLE,
focus on a single molecule whose bonds are constrained.  Let Ri and Vi
be the position and velocity of atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} at time \sphinxstyleemphasis{n}, for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i} =1,…,\sphinxstyleemphasis{N}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is the number of sites of our reference
molecule. The distance vector between sites \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j} is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf r^{n+1}_{ij} = \mathbf r^n_j - \mathbf r^n_i\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The constraints can then be formulated as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf r^{n+1}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf r^{n+1}_{ij} &= d^2_{ij} \quad \text{and} \\
\mathbf v^{n+1}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf r^{n+1}_{ij} &= 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The SHAKE algorithm satisfies the first condition, i.e. the sites at
time \sphinxstyleemphasis{n+1} will have the desired separations Dij immediately after the
coordinates are integrated.  If we also enforce the second condition,
the velocity components along the bonds will vanish.  RATTLE satisfies
both conditions.  As implemented in LAMMPS, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix rattle} uses fix shake
for satisfying the coordinate constraints. Therefore the settings and
optional keywords are the same for both fixes, and all the information
below about SHAKE is also relevant for RATTLE.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SHAKE:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each timestep the specified bonds and angles are reset to their
equilibrium lengths and angular values via the SHAKE algorithm
({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake:ryckaert}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ryckaert et al. (1977)}}}}).  This is done by applying an
additional constraint force so that the new positions preserve the
desired atom separations.  The equations for the additional force are
solved via an iterative method that typically converges to an accurate
solution in a few iterations.  The desired tolerance (e.g. 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}4 = 1
part in 10000) and maximum \# of iterations are specified as arguments.
Setting the N argument will print statistics to the screen and log
file about regarding the lengths of bonds and angles that are being
constrained.  Small delta values mean SHAKE is doing a good job.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LAMMPS, only small clusters of atoms can be constrained.  This is
so the constraint calculation for a cluster can be performed by a
single processor, to enable good parallel performance.  A cluster is
defined as a central atom connected to others in the cluster by
constrained bonds.  LAMMPS allows for the following kinds of clusters
to be constrained: one central atom bonded to 1 or 2 or 3 atoms, or
one central atom bonded to 2 others and the angle between the three atoms
also constrained.  This means water molecules or CH2 or CH3 groups may
be constrained, but not all the C\sphinxhyphen{}C backbone bonds of a long polymer
chain.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{b} constraint lists bond types that will be constrained.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{t}
constraint lists atom types.  All bonds connected to an atom of the
specified type will be constrained.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} constraint lists atom
masses.  All bonds connected to atoms of the specified masses will be
constrained (within a fudge factor of MASSDELTA specified in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/RIGID/fix\_shake.cpp}}).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{a} constraint lists angle types.  If
both bonds in the angle are constrained then the angle will also be
constrained if its type is in the list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The types may be given as type labels \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} if there is no atom, bond,
or angle type label named \sphinxstyleemphasis{b}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{a}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{t}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} defined in the
simulation.  If that is the case, type labels cannot be used as
constraint type index with these two fixes, because the type labels
would be incorrectly treated as a new type of constraint instead.
Thus, LAMMPS will print a warning and type label handling is disabled
and numeric types must be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all constraints, a particular bond is only constrained if \sphinxstyleemphasis{both}
atoms in the bond are in the group specified with the SHAKE fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom removed by SHAKE bonds and angles are accounted
for in temperature and pressure computations.  Similarly, the SHAKE
contribution to the pressure of the system (virial) is also accounted
for.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command works by using the current forces on atoms to calculate
an additional constraint force which when added will leave the atoms
in positions that satisfy the SHAKE constraints (e.g. bond length)
after the next time integration step.  If you define fixes
(e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix efield}}}}) that add additional force to
the atoms after \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix shake} operates, then this fix will not take them
into account and the time integration will typically not satisfy the
SHAKE constraints.  The solution for this is to make sure that fix
shake is defined in your input script after any other fixes which add
or change forces (to atoms that \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix shake} operates on).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword should be used when other commands, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
deposit}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_pour::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix pour}}}}, add molecules
on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly during a simulation, and you wish to constrain the new
molecules via SHAKE.  You specify a \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}ID} previously defined
using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command, which reads a file that
defines the molecule.  You must use the same \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}ID} that the
command adding molecules uses.  The coordinates, atom types, special
bond restrictions, and SHAKE info can be specified in the molecule file.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command for details.  The only
settings required to be in this file (by this command) are the SHAKE
info of atoms in the molecule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kbond} keyword sets the restraint force constant when \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix shake}
or fix rattle are used during minimization.  In that case the constraint
algorithms are \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} applied and restraint forces are used instead to
maintain the geometries similar to the constraints.  How well the
geometries are maintained and how quickly a minimization converges,
depends largely on the force constant \sphinxstyleemphasis{kbond}: larger values will reduce
the deviation from the desired geometry, but can also lead to slower
convergence of the minimization or lead to instabilities depending on
the minimization algorithm requiring to reduce the value of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}}.  Even though the restraints will not
preserve the bond lengths and angles as closely as the constraints
during the MD, they are generally close enough so that the constraints
will be fulfilled to the desired accuracy within a few MD steps
following the minimization. The default value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{kbond} depends on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} setting and is 1.0e6*k\_B.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RATTLE:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The velocity constraints lead to a linear system of equations which
can be solved analytically.  The implementation of the algorithm in
LAMMPS closely follows ({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake:andersen3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Andersen (1983)}}}}).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix rattle} command modifies forces and velocities and thus
should be defined after all other integration fixes in your input
script.  If you define other fixes that modify velocities or forces
after \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix rattle} operates, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix rattle} will not take them
into account and the overall time integration will typically not
satisfy the RATTLE constraints.  You can check whether the
constraints work correctly by setting the value of RATTLE\_DEBUG in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/RIGID/fix\_rattle.cpp}} to 1 and recompiling LAMMPS.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about these fixes is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{shake} and fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{rattle} behave differently during a minimization
in comparison to a molecular dynamics run:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When used during a minimization, the SHAKE or RATTLE constraint
algorithms themselves are \sphinxstylestrong{not} applied.  Instead the constraints
are replaced by harmonic restraint forces.  The energy and virial
contributions due to the restraint forces are tallied into global and
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom accumulators. The total restraint energy is also accessible
as a global scalar property of the fix.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
During molecular dynamics runs, however, the fixes do apply the
requested SHAKE or RATTLE constraint algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
these fixes to add the contribution due to the added constraint forces
on atoms to both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of the system
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be
accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The  default  setting  for  this  fix  is  {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify  virial  yes}}}}.  No global  or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom  quantities are  stored by  these
fixes for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} during
an  MD  run.   No  parameter  of  these  fixes  can  be  used  with  the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are part of the RIGID package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For computational efficiency, there can only be one shake or rattle
fix defined in a simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use a tolerance that is too large or a max\sphinxhyphen{}iteration count that
is too small, the constraints will not be enforced very strongly,
which can lead to poor energy conservation.  You can test for this in
your system by running a constant NVE simulation with a particular set
of SHAKE parameters and monitoring the energy versus time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
SHAKE or RATTLE should not be used to constrain an angle at 180 degrees
(e.g. a linear CO2 molecule).  This causes a divergence when solving the
constraint equations numerically.  You can use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid or fix
rigid/small}}}} instead to make a linear molecule rigid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When used during minimization choosing a too large value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kbond}
can make minimization very inefficient and also cause stability problems
with some minimization algorithms.  Sometimes those can be avoided by
reducing the {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ehex::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ehex}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_manifold_rattle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/manifold/rattle}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shake:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
kbond = 1.0e9*k\_B

\sphinxstylestrong{(Ryckaert)} J.\sphinxhyphen{}P. Ryckaert, G. Ciccotti and H. J. C. Berendsen,
J of Comp Phys, 23, 327\sphinxhyphen{}341 (1977).

\section{fix shardlow command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:fix-shardlow-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{shardlow/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shardlow}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
shardlow = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shardlow}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifies that the Shardlow splitting algorithm (SSA) is to be used to
integrate the DPD equations of motion.  The SSA splits the integration
into a stochastic and deterministic integration step.  The fix
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shardlow} performs the stochastic integration step and must be used in
conjunction with a deterministic integrator (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}}).  The stochastic integration of
the dissipative and random forces is performed prior to the
deterministic integration of the conservative force. Further details
regarding the method are provided in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shardlow:lisal}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lisal)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shardlow:larentzos1sh}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Larentzos1)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{shardlow} must be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/fdt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/fdt/energy}}}} command
to properly initialize the fluctuation\sphinxhyphen{}dissipation theorem parameter(s)
sigma (and kappa, if necessary).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that numerous variants of DPD can be specified by choosing an
appropriate combination of the integrator and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/fdt}}}} command.  DPD under isothermal conditions can be specified
by using fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{shardlow}, fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve} and pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/fdt}.  DPD
under isoenergetic conditions can be specified by using fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{shardlow},
fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nve} and pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/fdt/energy}.  DPD under isobaric
conditions can be specified by using fix shardlow, fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} and
pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/fdt}.  DPD under isoenthalpic conditions can be
specified by using fix shardlow, fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{nph} and pair\_style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/fdt/energy}.  Examples of each DPD variant are provided in the
examples/PACKAGES/dpd\sphinxhyphen{}react directory.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}REACT package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is currently limited to orthogonal simulation cell
geometries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix must be used with an additional fix that specifies time
integration, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Shardlow splitting algorithm requires the sizes of the subdomain
lengths to be larger than twice the cutoff+skin.  Generally, the
domain decomposition is dependent on the number of processors
requested.

\label{\detokenize{fix_shardlow:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_fdt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/fdt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_eos_cv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix eos/cv}}}}
