\index{fix smd@\spxentry{fix smd}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix smd command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:fix-smd-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
smd  = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfor} to select constant velocity or constant force SMD
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cvel} values = K vel
  K = spring constant (force/distance units)
  vel = velocity of pulling (distance/time units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cfor} values = force
  force = pulling force (force units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} values = x y z R0
  x,y,z = point to which spring is tethered
  R0 = distance of end of spring from tether point (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} values = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 x y z R0
  group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 = 2nd group to couple to fix group with a spring
  x,y,z = direction of spring, automatically computed with \textquotesingle{}auto\textquotesingle{}
  R0 = distance of end of spring (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pull}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.00005}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pull}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.0001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{stretch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0.0001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{couple}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pull}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cterm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cfor}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements several options of steered MD (SMD) as reviewed in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd:izrailev}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Izrailev)}}}}, which allows to induce conformational
changes in systems and to compute the potential of mean force (PMF)
along the assumed reaction coordinate {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd:park}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Park)}}}} based on
Jarzynski’s equality {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd:jarzynski}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jarzynski)}}}}.  This fix borrows
a lot from {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_setforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix setforce}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can apply a moving spring force to a group of atoms (\sphinxstyleemphasis{tether}
style) or between two groups of atoms (\sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} style).  The spring
can then be used in either constant velocity (\sphinxstyleemphasis{cvel}) mode or in
constant force (\sphinxstyleemphasis{cfor}) mode to induce transitions in your systems.
When running in \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} style, you may need some way to fix some
other part of the system (e.g. via {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_self::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/self}}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} style attaches a spring between a point at a distance of
R0 away from a fixed point \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} and the center of mass of the fix
group of atoms.  A restoring force of magnitude K (R \sphinxhyphen{} R0) Mi / M is
applied to each atom in the group where \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} is the spring constant, Mi
is the mass of the atom, and M is the total mass of all atoms in the
group.  Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} thus represents the total force on the group of
atoms, not a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvel} mode the distance R is incremented or decremented
monotonously according to the pulling (or pushing) velocity.
In \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfor} mode a constant force is added and the actual distance
in direction of the spring is recorded.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} style links two groups of atoms together.  The first
group is the fix group; the second is specified by group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2.  The
groups are coupled together by a spring that is at equilibrium when
the two groups are displaced by a vector in direction \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} with
respect to each other and at a distance R0 from that displacement.
Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} only provides a direction and will be internally
normalized. But since it represents the \sphinxstyleemphasis{absolute} displacement of
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 relative to the fix group, (1,1,0) is a different spring
than (\sphinxhyphen{}1,\sphinxhyphen{}1,0).  For each vector component, the displacement can be
described with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto} parameter. In this case the direction is
re\sphinxhyphen{}computed in every step, which can be useful for steering a local
process where the whole object undergoes some other change.  When the
relative positions and distance between the two groups are not in
equilibrium, the same spring force described above is applied to atoms
in each of the two groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For both the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} styles, any of the x,y,z values can
be specified as NULL which means do not include that dimension in the
distance calculation or force application.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For constant velocity pulling (\sphinxstyleemphasis{cvel} mode), the running integral
over the pulling force in direction of the spring is recorded and
can then later be used to compute the potential of mean force (PMF)
by averaging over multiple independent trajectories along the same
pulling path.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix stores the direction of the spring, current pulling target
distance and the running PMF to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to
re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that
the operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution due to the added forces on atoms to
both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of the system via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be
accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default
setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a vector list of 7 quantities, which can be accessed
by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The quantities in
the vector are in this order: the x\sphinxhyphen{}, y\sphinxhyphen{}, and z\sphinxhyphen{}component of the
pulling force, the total force in direction of the pull, the
equilibrium distance of the spring, the distance between the two
reference points, and finally the accumulated PMF (the sum of pulling
forces times displacement).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The force is the total force on the group of atoms by the spring.  In
the case of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} style, it is the force on the fix group
(group\sphinxhyphen{}ID) or the negative of the force on the second group
(group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2).  The vector values calculated by this fix are
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drag}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_self::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/self}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_rg::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/rg}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_colvars::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix colvars}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_plumed::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix plumed}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{fix smd/adjust\_dt command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_adjust_dt:fix-smd-adjust-dt-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_adjust_dt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_adjust_dt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adjust\PYGZus{}dt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{arg}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
smd/adjust\_dt = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{s\_fact}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{s\_fact} = safety factor
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_adjust_dt:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adjust\PYGZus{}dt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_adjust_dt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix calculates a new stable time increment for use with the SMD
time integrators.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The stable time increment is based on multiple conditions. For the SPH
pair styles, a CFL criterion (Courant, Friedrichs \& Lewy, 1928) is
evaluated, which determines the speed of sound cannot propagate
further than a typical spacing between particles within a single time
step to ensure no information is lost. For the contact pair styles, a
linear analysis of the pair potential determines a stable maximum time
step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix inquires the minimum stable time increment across all
particles contained in the group for which this fix is defined. An
additional safety factor \sphinxstyleemphasis{s\_fact} is applied to the time increment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to use Smooth Mach
Dynamics in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, no part of MACHDYN supports restarting nor minimization.

\section{fix smd/integrate\_ulsph command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_integrate_ulsph:fix-smd-integrate-ulsph-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_integrate_ulsph:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_integrate_ulsph::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_integrate_ulsph:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{integrate\PYGZus{}ulsph}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
smd/integrate\_ulsph = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = adjust\_radius or limit\_velocity

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{adjust\_radius values = adjust\_radius\_factor min\_nn max\_nn}
\sphinxAtStartPar
adjust\_radius\_factor = factor which scale the smooth/kernel radius
min\_nn = minimum number of neighbors
max\_nn = maximum number of neighbors

\sphinxlineitem{limit\_velocity values = max\_velocity}
\sphinxAtStartPar
max\_velocity = maximum allowed velocity.

\end{description}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_integrate_ulsph:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{integrate\PYGZus{}ulsph}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adjust\PYGZus{}radius}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{integrate\PYGZus{}ulsph}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{limit\PYGZus{}velocity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_integrate_ulsph:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix performs explicit time integration for particles which
interact with the updated Lagrangian SPH pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth Mach
Dynamics in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{adjust\_radius} keyword activates dynamic adjustment of the
per\sphinxhyphen{}particle SPH smoothing kernel radius such that the number of
neighbors per particles remains within the interval \sphinxstyleemphasis{min\_nn} to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{max\_nn}. The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{adjust\_radius\_factor} determines the amount
of adjustment per timestep. Typical values are \sphinxstyleemphasis{adjust\_radius\_factor}
=1.02, \sphinxstyleemphasis{min\_nn} =15, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{max\_nn} =20.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit\_velocity} keyword will control the velocity, scaling the norm of
the velocity vector to max\_vel in case it exceeds this velocity limit.

\section{fix smd/move\_tri\_surf command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface:fix-smd-move-tri-surf-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move\PYGZus{}tri\PYGZus{}surf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
smd/move\_tri\_surf keyword = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{*LINEAR} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{*WIGGLE} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{*ROTATE}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{*LINEAR} args = Vx Vy Vz
   Vx,Vy,Vz = components of velocity vector (velocity units), any component can be specified as NULL
\sphinxstyleemphasis{*WIGGLE} args = Vx Vy Vz max\_travel
   vx,vy,vz = components of velocity vector (velocity units), any component can be specified as NULL
   max\_travel = wiggle amplitude
\sphinxstyleemphasis{*ROTATE} args = Px Py Pz Rx Ry Rz period
   Px,Py,Pz = origin point of axis of rotation (distance units)
   Rx,Ry,Rz = axis of rotation vector
   period = period of rotation (time units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{tool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move\PYGZus{}tri\PYGZus{}surf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{LINEAR}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{tool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move\PYGZus{}tri\PYGZus{}surf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{WIGGLE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{tool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{move\PYGZus{}tri\PYGZus{}surf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{ROTATE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix applies only to rigid surfaces read from .STL files via fix
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{smd/wall\_surface}}}} .  It updates position
and velocity for the particles in the group each timestep without
regard to forces on the particles.  The rigid surfaces can thus be
moved along simple trajectories during the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{*LINEAR} style moves particles with the specified constant velocity
vector V = (Vx,Vy,Vz). This style also sets the velocity of each particle
to V = (Vx,Vy,Vz).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{*WIGGLE} style moves particles in an oscillatory fashion.
Particles are moved along (vx, vy, vz) with constant velocity until a
displacement of max\_travel is reached. Then, the velocity vector is
reversed. This process is repeated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{*ROTATE} style rotates particles around a rotation axis R =
(Rx,Ry,Rz) that goes through a point P = (Px,Py,Pz). The period of the
rotation is also specified. This style also sets the velocity of each
particle to (omega cross Rperp) where omega is its angular velocity
around the rotation axis and Rperp is a perpendicular vector from the
rotation axis to the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth Mach
Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, no part of MACHDYN supports restarting nor
minimization. This fix has no outputs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MACHDYN package.  It is only enabled if

\index{fix smd/setvel@\spxentry{fix smd/setvel}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix smd/setvel command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel:fix-smd-setvel-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{setvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
smd/setvel = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vx,vy,vz = velocity component values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
any of vx,vy,vz can be a variable (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region particles must be in to have their velocities set
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top\PYGZus{}velocity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top\PYGZus{}group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{setvel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set each component of velocity on each particle in the group to the specified
values vx,vy,vz, regardless of the forces acting on the particle.  This command can
be used to impose velocity boundary conditions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the vx,vy,vz values can be specified as NULL which means do not
alter the velocity component in that dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is indented to be used together with a time integration fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of the 3 quantities defining the velocity components can be specified
as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, namely \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}.  If the value is a variable, it should be specified as
v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the variable
will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine the
force component.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent velocity field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify the same formulas as equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables but can also include per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values, such as atom
coordinates.  Thus it is easy to specify a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}dependent velocity
field with optional time\sphinxhyphen{}dependence as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword is used, the particle must also be in the
specified geometric {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} in order to have its velocity set by this command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_setvel:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, no part of MACHDYN supports restarting nor minimization
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}vector of forces, which can be accessed

force on the group of atoms.  The vector values calculated by this fix
are “extensive”.

No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\section{fix smd/wall\_surface command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:fix-smd-wall-surface-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{wall\PYGZus{}surface}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
smd/wall\_surface = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{file}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file} = file name of a triangular mesh in stl format
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type = particle type to be given to the new particles created by this fix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mol\sphinxhyphen{}ID = molecule\sphinxhyphen{}ID to be given to the new particles created by this fix (must be \textgreater{}= 65535)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{stl\PYGZus{}surf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{wall\PYGZus{}surface}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tool.stl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{65535}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix creates reads a triangulated surface from a file in .STL
format.  For each triangle, a new particle is created which stores the
barycenter of the triangle and the vertex positions.  The radius of
the new particle is that of the minimum circle which encompasses the
triangle vertices.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The triangulated surface can be used as a complex rigid wall via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_smd_triangulated_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{smd/tri\_surface}}}} pair style.  It
is possible to move the triangulated surface via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{smd/move\_tri\_surf}}}} fix style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Immediately after a .STL file has been read, the simulation needs to
be run for 0 timesteps in order to properly register the new particles
in the system. See the “funnel\_flow” example in the MACHDYN examples
directory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to use Smooth Mach
Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, no part of MACHDYN supports restarting nor
minimization. This fix has no outputs.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MACHDYN package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The molecule ID given to the particles created by this fix have to be
equal to or larger than 65535.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Within each .STL file, only a single triangulated object must be
present, even though the STL format allows for the possibility of
multiple objects in one file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_smd_triangle_vertices::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{smd/triangle\_mesh\_vertices}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd_move_triangulated_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{smd/move\_tri\_surf}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_smd_triangulated_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{smd/tri\_surface}}}}

none

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_sph:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform time integration to update position, velocity, internal energy
and local density for atoms in the group each timestep. This fix is
needed to time\sphinxhyphen{}integrate SPH systems where particles carry internal
variables such as internal energy.  SPH stands for Smoothed Particle
Hydrodynamics.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/SPH\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using SPH in
LAMMPS.

are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.

but not position or velocity for atoms in the group each timestep.

fixed boundary particles which constrain a fluid to a given region in
space.  SPH stands for Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics.

LAMMPS.

\section{fix spring command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:fix-spring-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} values = K x y z R0
  K = spring constant (force/distance units)
  x,y,z = point to which spring is tethered
  R0 = equilibrium distance from tether point (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} values = group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 K x y z R0
  group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 = 2nd group to couple to fix group with a spring
  K = spring constant (force/distance units)
  x,y,z = direction of spring
  R0 = equilibrium distance of spring (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ligand}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ligand}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ligand}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bilayer1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{couple}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bilayer2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{longitudinal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pore}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{couple}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ion}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{radial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pore}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{couple}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ion}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a spring force to a group of atoms or between two groups of
atoms.  This is useful for applying an umbrella force to a small
molecule or lightly tethering a large group of atoms (e.g. all the
solvent or a large molecule) to the center of the simulation box so
that it does not wander away over the course of a long simulation.  It
can also be used to hold the centers of mass of two groups of atoms at
a given distance or orientation with respect to each other.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} style attaches a spring between a fixed point \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} and
the center of mass of the fix group of atoms.  The equilibrium
position of the spring is R0.  At each timestep the distance R from
the center of mass of the group of atoms to the tethering point is
computed, taking account of wrap\sphinxhyphen{}around in a periodic simulation box.
A restoring force of magnitude K (R \sphinxhyphen{} R0) Mi / M is applied to each
atom in the group where \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} is the spring constant, Mi is the mass of
the atom, and M is the total mass of all atoms in the group.  Note
that \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} thus represents the spring constant for the total force on
the group of atoms, not for a spring applied to each atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} style links two groups of atoms together.  The first
group is the fix group; the second is specified by group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2.  The
groups are coupled together by a spring that is at equilibrium when
the two groups are displaced by a vector \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} with respect to each
other and at a distance R0 from that displacement.  Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z}
is the equilibrium displacement of group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2 relative to the fix
group.  Thus (1,1,0) is a different spring than (\sphinxhyphen{}1,\sphinxhyphen{}1,0).  When the
relative positions and distance between the two groups are not in
equilibrium, the same spring force described above is applied to atoms
in each of the two groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For both the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tether} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} styles, any of the x,y,z values can
be specified as NULL which means do not include that dimension in the
distance calculation or force application.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first example above pulls the ligand towards the point (0,0,0).
The second example holds the ligand near the surface of a sphere of
radius 5 around the point (0,0,0).  The third example holds the ligand
a distance 3 away from the z=2 plane (on either side).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fourth example holds 2 bilayers a distance 10 apart in z.  For the
last two examples, imagine a pore (a slab of atoms with a cylindrical
hole cut out) oriented with the pore axis along z, and an ion moving
within the pore.  The fifth example holds the ion a distance of \sphinxhyphen{}20
below the z = 0 center plane of the pore (umbrella sampling).  The
last example holds the ion a distance 5 away from the pore axis
(assuming the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of the pore in x,y is the pore axis).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The center of mass of a group of atoms is calculated in
“unwrapped” coordinates using atom image flags, which means that the
group can straddle a periodic boundary.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc
page for a discussion of unwrapped coordinates.  It also means that a
spring connecting two groups or a group and the tether point can cross
a periodic boundary and its length be calculated correctly.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy stored in the spring to the global
potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}. The default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the spring energy
= 0.5 * K * r\textasciicircum{}2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix also computes global 4\sphinxhyphen{}vector which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The first 3 quantities
in the vector are xyz components of the total force added to the group
of atoms by the spring.  In the case of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{couple} style, it is the
force on the fix group (group\sphinxhyphen{}ID) or the negative of the force on the
second group (group\sphinxhyphen{}ID2).  The fourth quantity in the vector is the
magnitude of the force added by the spring, as a positive value if
(r\sphinxhyphen{}R0) \textgreater{} 0 and a negative value if (r\sphinxhyphen{}R0) \textless{} 0.  This sign convention
can be useful when using the spring force to compute a potential of
mean force (PMF).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar and vector values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the spring energy to be included in the total
potential energy of the system (the quantity being minimized), you
MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this
fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drag}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_self::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/self}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_spring_rg::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix spring/rg}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix smd}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring:default}}

\section{fix spring/chunk command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk:fix-spring-chunk-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{K}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunkID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring/chunk = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K = spring constant for each chunk (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chunkID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
comID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_com_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute com/chunk}}}} command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{restrain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunkID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a spring force to the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass (COM) of chunks of atoms as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.
Chunks can be molecules or spatial bins or other groupings of atoms.
This is a way of tethering each chunk to its initial COM coordinates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{chunkID} is the ID of a compute chunk/atom command defined in the
input script.  It is used to define the chunks.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{comID} is the ID
of a compute com/chunk command defined in the input script.  It is
used to compute the COMs of each chunk.

\sphinxAtStartPar
At the beginning of the first {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command after this fix is defined, the
initial COM of each chunk is calculated and stored as R0m, where M is
the chunk number.  Thereafter, at every timestep (or minimization
iteration), the current COM of each chunk is calculated as Rm.  A
restoring force of magnitude K (Rm \sphinxhyphen{} R0m) Mi / Mm is applied to each
atom in each chunk where \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} is the specified spring constant, Mi is
the mass of the atom, and Mm is the total mass of all atoms in the
chunk.  Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} thus represents the spring constant for the
total force on each chunk of atoms, not for a spring applied to each
atom.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_chunk:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the locations of the initial per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk center of mass
coordinates to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to
re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that
the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.  Since this fix depends
on an instance of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}}
it will check when reading the restart if the chunk still exists and
will define the same number of chunks. The restart data is only applied
when the number of chunks matches. Otherwise the center of mass
coordinates are recomputed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy stored in all the springs to the global
potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the energy of all
the springs, i.e. 0.5 * K * r\textasciicircum{}2 per\sphinxhyphen{}spring.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the spring energies to be included in the total
potential energy of the system (the quantity being minimized), you
MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this
fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{fix spring/rg command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg:fix-spring-rg-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{K}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RG0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring/rg = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K = harmonic force constant (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RG0 = target radius of gyration to constrain to (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
if RG0 = NULL, use the current RG as the target value
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{protein}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{micelle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a harmonic restraining force to atoms in the group to affect
their central moment about the center of mass (radius of gyration).
This fix is useful to encourage a protein or polymer to fold/unfold
and also when sampling along the radius of gyration as a reaction
coordinate (i.e. for protein folding).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The radius of gyration is defined as RG in the first formula.  The
energy of the constraint and associated force on each atom is given by
the second and third formulas, when the group is at a different RG
than the target value RG0.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{R_G}^2 & = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i}^{N}{m_{i}\left( x_{i} -
\frac{1}{M}\sum_{j}^{N}{m_{j}x_{j}} \right)^{2}} \\
E & = K\left( R_G - R_{G0} \right)^{2} \\
F_{i} & = 2K\frac{m_{i}}{M}\left( 1-\frac{R_{G0}}{R_G}
\right)\left( x_{i} - \frac{1}{M}\sum_{j}^{N}{m_{j}x_{j}} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The (\(x_i\) \sphinxhyphen{} center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass) term is computed taking into account
periodic boundary conditions, \(m_i\) is the mass of the atom, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{M} is the mass of the entire group.  Note that K is thus a force constant
for the aggregate force on the group of atoms, not a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \(R_{G0}\) is specified as NULL, then the RG of the group is computed at
the time the fix is specified, and that value is used as the target.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_rg:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the currently used reference RG (\(R_{G0}\)) to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input
script that reads a restart file, so that the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the reference
radius of gyration \(R_{G0}\) used by the fix.  energy change due to
this fix.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\section{fix spring/self command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:fix-spring-self-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{K}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dir}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spring/self = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K = spring constant (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dir = xyz, xy, xz, yz, x, y, or z (optional, default: xyz)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{tether}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary\PYGZhy{}atoms}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{zrest}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{move}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{self}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply a spring force independently to each atom in the group to tether
it to its initial position.  The initial position for each atom is its
location at the time the fix command was issued.  At each timestep,
the magnitude of the force on each atom is \sphinxhyphen{}Kr, where r is the
displacement of the atom from its current position to its initial
position.  The distance r correctly takes into account any crossings
of periodic boundary by the atom since it was in its initial
position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the (optional) dir flag, one can select in which direction the
spring force is applied. By default, the restraint is applied in all
directions, but it can be limited to the xy\sphinxhyphen{}, xz\sphinxhyphen{}, yz\sphinxhyphen{}plane and the
x\sphinxhyphen{}, y\sphinxhyphen{}, or z\sphinxhyphen{}direction, thus restraining the atoms to a line or a
plane, respectively.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_spring_self:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the original coordinates of tethered atoms to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so that the spring effect will
be the same in a restarted simulation.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an
input script that reads a restart file, so that the operation of the
fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy stored in the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom springs to the
global potential energy of the system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic
output}}}}.  The default setting for this fix is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by
this fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is an energy which is
the sum of the spring energy for each atom, where the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom energy
is 0.5 * K * r\textasciicircum{}2.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is
“extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom spring energy to be included in the
total potential energy of the system (the quantity being minimized),
you MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for
this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
