\section{fix srd command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:fix-srd-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_srd::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{groupbig}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tsrd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hgrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
srd = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = reset SRD particle velocities every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
groupbig\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of group of large particles that SRDs interact with

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tsrd = temperature of SRD particles (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hgrid = grid spacing for SRD grouping (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lamda} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{collision} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{inside} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{exact} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bounce} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{search} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lamda} value = mean free path of SRD particles (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{collision} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{noslip} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{slip} = collision model
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = whether big particles may overlap
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inside} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{error} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{warn} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ignore} = how SRD particles which end up inside a big particle are treated
\sphinxstyleemphasis{exact} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} value = rfactor = scale collision radius by this factor
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bounce} value = Nbounce = max \# of collisions an SRD particle can undergo in one timestep
\sphinxstyleemphasis{search} value = sgrid = grid spacing for collision partner searching (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic} values = style tolerance
  style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{error} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{warn}
  tolerance = fractional difference allowed (0 \textless{}= tol \textless{}= 1)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} values = flag shiftseed
  flag = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{possible} = SRD bin shifting for better statistics
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = perform bin shifting each time SRD velocities are rescaled
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = no shifting
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{possible} = shift depending on mean free path and bin size
  shiftseed = random \# seed (positive integer)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = thermostat SRD particles or not
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{collide} = rescaling of SRD velocities
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} = rescale during velocity rotation and collisions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = no rescaling
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} = rescale during velocity rotation, but not collisions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{collide} = rescale during collisions, but not velocity rotation
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{big}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{482984}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{big}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{482984}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{collision}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{slip}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{search}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat a group of particles as stochastic rotation dynamics (SRD)
particles that serve as a background solvent when interacting with big
(colloidal) particles in groupbig\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  The SRD formalism is described
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd:hecht}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Hecht)}}}}.  The same methodology is also called
multi\sphinxhyphen{}particle collision dynamics (MPCD) in the literature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The key idea behind using SRD particles as a cheap coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained
solvent is that SRD particles do not interact with each other, but
only with the solute particles, which in LAMMPS can be spheroids,
ellipsoids, or line segments, or triangles, or rigid bodies containing
multiple spheroids or ellipsoids or line segments or triangles.  The
collision and rotation properties of the model imbue the SRD particles
with fluid\sphinxhyphen{}like properties, including an effective viscosity.  Thus
simulations with large solute particles can be run more quickly, to
measure solute properties like diffusivity and viscosity in a
background fluid.  The usual LAMMPS fixes for such simulations, such
as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_viscosity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix viscosity}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}}, can be
used in conjunction with the SRD model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These 3 papers give more details on how the SRD model is implemented
in LAMMPS.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd:petersen1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Petersen)}}}} describes pure SRD fluid
systems.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd:bolintineanu1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bolintineanu1)}}}} describes models
where pure SRD fluids interact with boundary walls.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd:bolintineanu2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bolintineanu2)}}}} describes mixture models where
large colloidal particles are solvated by an SRD fluid.  See the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/srd}} directory for sample input scripts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix does two things:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It advects the SRD particles, performing collisions between SRD
and big particles or walls every timestep, imparting force and torque
to the big particles.  Collisions also change the position and
velocity of SRD particles.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It resets the velocity distribution of SRD particles via random
rotations every N timesteps.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
SRD particles have a mass, temperature, characteristic timestep
\(dt_{SRD}\), and mean free path between collisions
(\(\lambda\)).  The fundamental equation relating these 4 quantities
is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\lambda = dt_{SRD} \sqrt{\frac{k_B T_{SRD}}{m}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The mass \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} of SRD particles is set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}} command
elsewhere in the input script.  The SRD timestep \(dt_{SRD}\) is N
times the step \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}} command.
Big particles move in the normal way via a time integration {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} with a short timestep dt.  SRD particles advect with a large
timestep \(dt_{SRD} \ge dt\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lamda} keyword is not specified, the SRD temperature
\(T_{SRD}\) is used in the above formula to compute \(\lambda\).
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lamda} keyword is specified, then the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd} setting is ignored
and the above equation is used to compute the SRD temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The characteristic length scale for the SRD fluid is set by \sphinxstyleemphasis{hgrid}
which is used to bin SRD particles for purposes of resetting their
velocities.  Normally hgrid is set to be 1/4 of the big particle
diameter or smaller, to adequately resolve fluid properties around the
big particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\lambda\) cannot be smaller than 0.6 * hgrid, else an error is
generated (unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword is used, see below).  The
velocities of SRD particles are bounded by Vmax, which is set so that an
SRD particle will not advect further than \(D_{max} = 4 \lambda\) in
\(dt_{SRD}\).  This means that roughly speaking, \(D_{max}\)
should not be larger than a big particle diameter, else SRDs may pass
through big particles without colliding.  A warning is generated if this
is the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Collisions between SRD particles and big particles or walls are
modeled as a lightweight SRD point particle hitting a heavy big
particle of given diameter or a wall at a point on its surface and
bouncing off with a new velocity.  The collision changes the momentum
of the SRD particle.  It imparts a force and torque to the big
particle.  It imparts a force to a wall.  Static or moving SRD walls
are setup via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/srd}}}} command.  For the
remainder of this doc page, a collision of an SRD particle with a wall
can be viewed as a collision with a big particle of infinite radius
and mass.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{collision} keyword sets the style of collisions.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{slip}
style means that the tangential component of the SRD particle momentum
is preserved.  Thus a force is imparted to a big particle, but no
torque.  The normal component of the new SRD velocity is sampled from
a Gaussian distribution at temperature \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{noslip} style, both the normal and tangential components of
the new SRD velocity are sampled from a Gaussian distribution at
temperature \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd}.  Additionally, a new tangential direction for the
SRD velocity is chosen randomly.  This collision style imparts torque
to a big particle.  Thus a time integrator {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} that rotates
the big particles appropriately should be used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} keyword should be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} if two (or more) big
particles can ever overlap.  This depends on the pair potential
interaction used for big\sphinxhyphen{}big interactions, or could be the case if
multiple big particles are held together as rigid bodies via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}} command.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
and big particles do in fact overlap, then SRD/big collisions can
generate an error if an SRD ends up inside two (or more) big particles
at once.  How this error is treated is determined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inside}
keyword.  Running with \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} allows for faster collision
checking, so it should only be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} if needed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{inside} keyword determines how a collision is treated if the
computation determines that the timestep started with the SRD particle
already inside a big particle.  If the setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{error} then this
generates an error message and LAMMPS stops.  If the setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{warn}
then this generates a warning message and the code continues.  If the
setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{ignore} then no message is generated.  One of the output
quantities logged by the fix (see below) tallies the number of such
events, so it can be monitored.  Note that once an SRD particle is
inside a big particle, it may remain there for several steps until it
drifts outside the big particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{exact} keyword determines how accurately collisions are computed.
A setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} computes the time and position of each collision as
SRD and big particles move together.  A setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} estimates the
position of each collision based on the end\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}timestep positions of
the SRD and big particle.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} is set to yes, the setting of
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{exact} keyword is ignored since time\sphinxhyphen{}accurate collisions are
needed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} keyword scales the effective size of big particles.  If
big particles will overlap as they undergo dynamics, then this keyword
can be used to scale down their effective collision radius by an
amount \sphinxstyleemphasis{rfactor}, so that SRD particle will only collide with one big
particle at a time.  For example, in a Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones system at a
temperature of 1.0 (in reduced LJ units), the minimum separation
between two big particles is as small as about 0.88 sigma.  Thus an
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rfactor} value of 0.85 should prevent dual collisions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bounce} keyword can be used to limit the maximum number of
collisions an SRD particle undergoes in a single timestep as it
bounces between nearby big particles.  Note that if the limit is
reached, the SRD can be left inside a big particle.  A setting of 0 is
the same as no limit.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
There are 2 kinds of bins created and maintained when running an SRD
simulation.  The first are “SRD bins” which are used to bin SRD
particles and reset their velocities, as discussed above.  The second
are “search bins” which are used to identify SRD/big particle
collisions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{search} keyword can be used to choose a search bin size for
identifying SRD/big particle collisions.  The default is to use the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hgrid} parameter for SRD bins as the search bin size.  Choosing a
smaller or large value may be more efficient, depending on the
problem.  But, in a statistical sense, it should not change the
simulation results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic} keyword can be used to generate an error or warning when
the bin size chosen by LAMMPS creates SRD bins that are non\sphinxhyphen{}cubic or
different than the requested value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{hgrid} by a specified
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance}.  Note that using non\sphinxhyphen{}cubic SRD bins can lead to
undetermined behavior when rotating the velocities of SRD particles,
hence LAMMPS tries to protect you from this problem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS attempts to set the SRD bin size to exactly \sphinxstyleemphasis{hgrid}.  However,
there must be an integer number of bins in each dimension of the
simulation box.  Thus the actual bin size will depend on the size and
shape of the overall simulation box.  The actual bin size is printed
as part of the SRD output when a simulation begins.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the actual bin size in non\sphinxhyphen{}cubic by an amount exceeding the
tolerance, an error or warning is printed, depending on the style of
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cubic} keyword.  Likewise, if the actual bin size differs from
the requested \sphinxstyleemphasis{hgrid} value by an amount exceeding the tolerance, then
an error or warning is printed.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tolerance} is a fractional
difference.  E.g. a tolerance setting of 0.01 on the shape means that
if the ratio of any 2 bin dimensions exceeds (1 +/\sphinxhyphen{} tolerance) then an
error or warning is generated.  Similarly, if the ratio of any bin
dimension with \sphinxstyleemphasis{hgrid} exceeds (1 +/\sphinxhyphen{} tolerance), then an error or
warning is generated.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fix srd command can be used with simulations where the size and/or
shape of the simulation box changes.  This can be due to non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic
boundary conditions or the use of fixes such as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/srd}}}} commands
to impose a shear on an SRD fluid or an interaction with an external
wall.  If the box size changes then the size of SRD bins must be
recalculated every reneighboring.  This is not necessary if only the
box shape changes.  This re\sphinxhyphen{}binning is always done so as to fit an
integer number of bins in the current box dimension, whether it be a
fixed, shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped, or periodic boundary, as set by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command.  If the box size or shape changes,
then the size of the search bins must be recalculated every
reneighboring.  Note that changing the SRD bin size may alter the
properties of the SRD fluid, such as its viscosity.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} keyword determines whether the coordinates of SRD particles
are randomly shifted when binned for purposes of rotating their
velocities.  When no shifting is performed, SRD particles are binned and
the velocity distribution of the set of SRD particles in each bin is
adjusted via a rotation operator.  This is a statistically valid
operation if SRD particles move sufficiently far between successive
rotations.  This is determined by their mean\sphinxhyphen{}free path \(\lambda\).
If \(\lambda\) is less than 0.6 of the SRD bin size, then shifting
is required.  A shift means that all of the SRD particles are shifted by
a vector whose coordinates are chosen randomly in the range {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1/2 bin
size, 1/2 bin size{]}.  Note that all particles are shifted by the same
vector.  The specified random number \sphinxstyleemphasis{shiftseed} is used to generate
these vectors.  This operation sufficiently randomizes which SRD
particles are in the same bin, even if \(lambda\) is small.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} flag is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, then no shifting is performed, but
bin data will be communicated if bins overlap processor boundaries.  An
error will be generated if \(\lambda < 0.6\) of the SRD bin size.
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} flag is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{possible}, then shifting is performed
only if \(\lambda < 0.6\) of the SRD bin size.  A warning is
generated to let you know this is occurring.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift} flag is set
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} then shifting is performed regardless of the magnitude of
\(\lambda\).  Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shiftseed} is not used if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift}
flag is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, but must still be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that shifting of SRD coordinates requires extra communication,
hence it should not normally be enabled unless required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} keyword will thermostat the SRD particles to the specified
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd}.  This is done every N timesteps, during the velocity rotation
operation, by rescaling the thermal velocity of particles in each SRD
bin to the desired temperature.  If there is a streaming velocity
associated with the system, e.g. due to use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command to perform a simulation undergoing
shear, then that is also accounted for.  The mean velocity of each bin
of SRD particles is set to the position\sphinxhyphen{}dependent streaming velocity,
based on the coordinates of the center of the SRD bin.  Note that
collisions of SRD particles with big particles or walls has a
thermostatting effect on the colliding particles, so it may not be
necessary to thermostat the SRD particles on a bin by bin basis in
that case.  Also note that for streaming simulations, if no
thermostatting is performed (the default), then it may take a long
time for the SRD fluid to come to equilibrium with a velocity profile
that matches the simulation box deformation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} keyword enables rescaling of an SRD particle’s velocity
if it would travel more than 4 mean\sphinxhyphen{}free paths in an SRD timestep.  If
an SRD particle exceeds this velocity it is possible it will be lost
when migrating to other processors or that collisions with big
particles will be missed, either of which will generate errors.  Thus
the safest mode is to run with rescaling enabled.  However rescaling
removes kinetic energy from the system (the particle’s velocity is
reduced).  The latter will not typically be a problem if
thermostatting is enabled via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tstat} keyword or if SRD collisions
with big particles or walls effectively thermostat the system.  If you
wish to turn off rescaling (on is the default), e.g. for a pure SRD
system with no thermostatting so that the temperature does not decline
over time, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rescale} keyword can be used.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} value turns
rescaling off during collisions and the per\sphinxhyphen{}bin velocity rotation
operation.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{collide} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} values turn it on for
one of the operations and off for the other.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is normally used for simulations with a huge number of
SRD particles relative to the number of big particles, e.g. 100 to 1.
In this scenario, computations that involve only big particles
(neighbor list creation, communication, time integration) can slow
down dramatically due to the large number of background SRD particles.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Three other input script commands will largely overcome this effect,
speeding up an SRD simulation by a significant amount.  These are the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify first}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify include}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify group}}}}
commands.  Each takes a group\sphinxhyphen{}ID as an argument, which in this case
should be the group\sphinxhyphen{}ID of the big solute particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additionally, when a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} for big/big particle
interactions is specified, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command
should be used to turn off big/SRD interactions, e.g. by setting their
epsilon or cutoff length to 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “delete\_atoms overlap” command may be useful in setting up an SRD
simulation to ensure there are no initial overlaps between big and SRD
particles.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix tabulates several SRD statistics which are stored in a vector
of length 12, which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector values calculated by this fix
are “intensive”, meaning they do not scale with the size of the
simulation.  Technically, the first 8 do scale with the size of the
simulation, but treating them as intensive means they are not scaled
when printed as part of thermodynamic output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the 12 quantities.  All are values for the current timestep,
except for quantity 5 and the last three, each of which are
cumulative quantities since the beginning of the run.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{(}{)}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of SRD/big collision checks performed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of SRDs which had a collision

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of SRD/big collisions (including multiple bounces)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of SRD particles inside a big particle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of SRD particles whose velocity was rescaled to be \textless{} Vmax

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of bins for collision searching

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of bins for SRD velocity rotation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of bins in which SRD temperature was computed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SRD temperature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of SRD particles which have undergone max \# of bounces

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max \# of bounces any SRD particle has had in a single step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# of reneighborings due to SRD particles moving too far

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the SRD package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/srd}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_srd:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lamda} (\(\lambda\)) is inferred from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd},
collision = noslip, overlap = no, inside = error, exact = yes, radius =
1.0, bounce = 0, search = hgrid, cubic = error 0.01, shift = no, tstat =
no, and rescale = yes.

Chem Phys, 132, 174106 (2010).

\index{fix store/force@\spxentry{fix store/force}}\ignorespaces 

\section{fix store/force command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force:fix-store-force-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{force}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
store/force = style name of this fix command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{force}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Store the forces on atoms in the group at the point during each timestep
when the fix is invoked, as described below.  This is useful for storing
forces before constraints or other boundary conditions are computed
which modify the forces, so that unmodified forces can be {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{written
to a dump file}}}} or accessed by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} that use per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is invoked at the point in the velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet timestepping
immediately after {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{long\sphinxhyphen{}range}}}}
forces have been calculated.  It is the point in the timestep when
various fixes that compute constraint forces are calculated and
potentially modify the force on each atom.  Examples of such fixes are
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_indent::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
indent}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The order in which various fixes are applied which operate at the
same point during the timestep, is the same as the order they are
specified in the input script.  Thus normally, if you want to store
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom forces due to force field interactions, before constraints
are applied, you should list this fix first within that set of fixes,
i.e. before other fixes that apply constraints.  However, if you wish
to include certain constraints (e.g. fix shake) in the stored force,
then it could be specified after some fixes and before others.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_force:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are
relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The number of columns for each
atom is 3, and the columns store the x,y,z forces on each atom.  The
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values be accessed on any timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

none

\section{fix store/state command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state:fix-store-state-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
store/state = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = store atom attributes every N steps, N = 0 for initial store only

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
input = one or more atom attributes

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = id, mol, type, mass,
                      x, y, z, xs, ys, zs, xu, yu, zu, xsu, ysu, zsu, ix, iy, iz,
                      vx, vy, vz, fx, fy, fz,
                      q, mux, muy, muz, mu,
                      radius, diameter, omegax, omegay, omegaz,
                      angmomx, angmomy, angmomz, tqx, tqy, tqz,
                      c\PYGZus{}ID, c\PYGZus{}ID[I], f\PYGZus{}ID, f\PYGZus{}ID[I], v\PYGZus{}name,
                      d\PYGZus{}name, i\PYGZus{}name, i2\PYGZus{}name[I], d2\PYGZus{}name[I],
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
id = atom ID
mol = molecule ID
type = atom type
mass = atom mass
x,y,z = unscaled atom coordinates
xs,ys,zs = scaled atom coordinates
xu,yu,zu = unwrapped atom coordinates
xsu,ysu,zsu = scaled unwrapped atom coordinates
ix,iy,iz = box image that the atom is in
vx,vy,vz = atom velocities
fx,fy,fz = forces on atoms
q = atom charge
mux,muy,muz = orientation of dipolar atom
mu = magnitued of dipole moment of atom
radius,diameter = radius.diameter of spherical particle
omegax,omegay,omegaz = angular velocity of spherical particle
angmomx,angmomy,angmomz = angular momentum of aspherical particle
tqx,tqy,tqz = torque on finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by a compute with ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID{[}I{]}} = Ith column of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array calculated by a compute with ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by a fix with ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID{[}I{]}} = Ith column of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array calculated by a fix with ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name} = custom integer vector with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name} = custom floating point vector with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name{[}I{]}} = Ith column of custom integer array with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name{[}I{]}} = Ith column of custom floating\sphinxhyphen{}point array with name
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{com}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{com} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{com}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a fix that stores attributes for each atom in the group at the
time the fix is defined.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is 0, then the values are never
updated, so this is a way of archiving an atom attribute at a given
time for future use in a calculation or output.  See the discussion of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} that take fixes as inputs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is not zero, then the attributes will be updated every \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
steps.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Actually, only atom attributes specified by keywords like \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} are initially stored immediately at the point in
your input script when the fix is defined.  Attributes specified by a
compute, fix, or variable are not initially stored until the first run
following the fix definition begins.  This is because calculating
those attributes may require quantities that are not defined in
between runs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The list of possible attributes is the same as that used by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command, which describes their meaning.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{com} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} then the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yu}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zu}
inputs store the position of each atom relative to the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
of the group of atoms, instead of storing the absolute position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The requested values are stored in a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector or array as
discussed below.  Zeroes are stored for atoms not in the specified
group.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_store_state:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values it stores to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, so that the values can be restored when a simulation
is restarted.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for
info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a
restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When reading data from a restart file, this fix command has to be specified
\sphinxstylestrong{exactly} the same way as before. LAMMPS will only check whether a
fix is of the same style and has the same fix ID and in case of a match
will then try to initialize the fix with the data stored in the binary
restart file.  If the fix store/state command does not match exactly,
data can be corrupted or LAMMPS may crash.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a single input is specified, this fix produces a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector.
If multiple inputs are specified, a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array is produced where
the number of columns for each atom is the number of inputs.  These
can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values be accessed on any timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/atom}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}

\section{fix temp/berendsen command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:fix-temp-berendsen-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/berendsen/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{berendsen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tdamp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/berendsen = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Tstart can be a variable (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tdamp = temperature damping parameter (time units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{berendsen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reset the temperature of a group of atoms by using a Berendsen
thermostat {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:berendsen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Berendsen)}}}}, which rescales their velocities
every timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to only the translational degrees of freedom
for the particles, which is an important consideration for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
particles which have rotational degrees of freedom are being
thermostatted with this fix.  The translational degrees of freedom can
also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The desired temperature at each timestep is a ramped value during the
run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} parameter is specified in
time units and determines how rapidly the temperature is relaxed.  For
example, a value of 100.0 means to relax the temperature in a timespan
of (roughly) 100 time units (tau or fs or ps \sphinxhyphen{} see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.
In this case, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} setting is ignored.  If the value is a
variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where name is the variable
name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated each timestep, and
its value used to determine the target temperature.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This thermostat will generate an error if the current
temperature is zero at the end of a timestep.  It cannot rescale a
zero temperature.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent temperature.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command which performs
Nose/Hoover thermostatting AND time integration, this fix does NOT
perform time integration.  It only modifies velocities to effect
thermostatting.  Thus you must use a separate time integration fix,
like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} to actually update the positions of atoms
using the modified velocities.  Likewise, this fix should not normally
be used on atoms that also have their temperature controlled by
another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature each timestep.  To do this, the fix
creates its own compute of style “temp”, as if this command had been
issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} command for details.  Note
that the ID of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp”,
and the group for the new compute is the same as the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}.
This means you can change the attributes of this fix’s temperature
(e.g. its degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom) via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} will have no
effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the cumulative global energy change to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to
re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a restart file,
so that the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}
you have defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure, as described above.  For consistency, the group used by
this fix and by the compute should be the same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can be used with dynamic groups as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{group}}}} command.  Likewise it can be used with groups to
which atoms are added or deleted over time, e.g. a deposition
simulation.  However, the conservation properties of the thermostat
and barostat are defined for systems with a static set of atoms.  You
may observe odd behavior if the atoms in a group vary dramatically
over time or the atom count becomes very small.

\section{fix temp/csvr command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:fix-temp-csvr-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr::doc}}

\section{fix temp/csld command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:fix-temp-csld-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{csvr}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tdamp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{csld}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tdamp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Tstart can be a variable (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:examples}}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{csvr}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{54324}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{csld}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{123321}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjust the temperature with a canonical sampling thermostat that uses
global velocity rescaling with Hamiltonian dynamics (\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/csvr})
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:bussi1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bussi1)}}}}, or Langevin dynamics (\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/csld})
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_csvr:bussi2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bussi2)}}}}.  In the case of \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/csvr} the thermostat is
similar to the empirical Berendsen thermostat in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{temp/berendsen}}}}, but chooses the actual
scaling factor from a suitably chosen (gaussian) distribution rather
than having it determined from the time constant directly. In the case
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/csld} the velocities are updated to a linear combination of
the current velocities with a gaussian distribution of velocities at
the desired temperature.  Both thermostats are applied every timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermostat is applied to only the translational degrees of freedom
for the particles, which is an important consideration for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
particles which have rotational degrees of freedom are being
thermostatted with these fixes.  The translational degrees of freedom
can also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The desired temperature at each timestep is a ramped value during the
run from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tdamp} parameter is specified in
time units and determines how rapidly the temperature is relaxed.  For
example, a value of 100.0 means to relax the temperature in a timespan
of (roughly) 100 time units (tau or fs or ps \sphinxhyphen{} see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.
In this case, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} setting is ignored.  If the value is a
variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where name is the variable
name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated each timestep, and
its value used to determine the target temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent temperature.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command which performs
Nose/Hoover thermostatting AND time integration, these fixes do NOT
perform time integration. They only modify velocities to effect
thermostatting.  Thus you must use a separate time integration fix,
like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} to actually update the positions of atoms
using the modified velocities.  Likewise, these fixes should not
normally be used on atoms that also have their temperature controlled
by another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute a temperature each timestep.  To do this, the fix
creates its own compute of style “temp”, as if this command had been
issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} command for details.  Note
that the ID of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp”,
and the group for the new compute is the same as the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}.
This means you can change the attributes of this fix’s temperature
(e.g. its degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom) via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature
during thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.
It also means that changing attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} will have no
effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An important feature of these thermostats is that they have an
associated effective energy that is a constant of motion.  The
effective energy is the total energy (kinetic + potential) plus the
accumulated kinetic energy changes due to the thermostat. The latter
quantity is the global scalar computed by these fixes. This feature is
useful to check the integration of the equations of motion against
discretization errors. In other words, the conservation of the
effective energy can be used to choose an appropriate integration
{\hyperref[\detokenize{timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{timestep}}}}. This is similar to the usual paradigm of
checking the conservation of the total energy in the microcanonical
ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes compute a global scalar which can be accessed by various

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes can ramp their target temperature over multiple runs,
using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes are not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\section{fix temp/rescale command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:fix-temp-rescale-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp/rescale/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rescale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{window}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fraction}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/rescale = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = perform rescaling every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run (temperature units)

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Tstart can be a variable (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
window = only rescale if temperature is outside this window (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fraction = rescale to target temperature by this fraction

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rescale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rescale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rescale}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reset the temperature of a group of atoms by explicitly rescaling
their velocities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The rescaling is applied to only the translational degrees of freedom
for the particles, which is an important consideration if finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
particles which have rotational degrees of freedom are being
thermostatted with this fix.  The translational degrees of freedom can
also have a bias velocity removed from them before thermostatting
takes place; see the description below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rescaling is performed every N timesteps.  The target temperature is a
ramped value between the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} temperatures at the
beginning and end of the run.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This thermostat will generate an error if the current
temperature is zero at the end of a timestep it is invoked on.  It
cannot rescale a zero temperature.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} can be specified as an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.
In this case, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop} setting is ignored.  If the value is a
variable, it should be specified as v\_name, where name is the variable
name.  In this case, the variable will be evaluated each timestep, and
its value used to determine the target temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables can specify formulas with various mathematical
functions, and include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command
keywords for the simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed
time.  Thus it is easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rescaling is only performed if the difference between the current and
desired temperatures is greater than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{window} value.  The amount
of rescaling that is applied is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction} (from 0.0 to 1.0) of the
difference between the actual and desired temperature.  E.g. if
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fraction} = 1.0, the temperature is reset to exactly the desired
value.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} command which performs
Nose/Hoover thermostatting AND time integration, this fix does NOT
perform time integration.  It only modifies velocities to effect
thermostatting.  Thus you must use a separate time integration fix,
like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} to actually update the positions of atoms
using the modified velocities.  Likewise, this fix should not normally
be used on atoms that also have their temperature controlled by
another fix \sphinxhyphen{} e.g. by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} commands.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a temperature each timestep.  To do this, the fix
creates its own compute of style “temp”, as if one of this command had
been issued:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fix\PYGZhy{}ID\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} for details.  Note that the
ID of the new compute is the fix\sphinxhyphen{}ID + underscore + “temp”, and the
group for the new compute is the same as the fix group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this is NOT the compute used by thermodynamic output (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command) with ID =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp}.  This means you can change the attributes of this fix’s
temperature (e.g. its degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom) via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command or print this temperature during
thermodynamic output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}}
command using the appropriate compute\sphinxhyphen{}ID.  It also means that changing
attributes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{thermo\_temp} will have no effect on this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like other fixes that perform thermostatting, this fix can be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} that remove a “bias” from the
atom velocities.  E.g. to apply the thermostat only to atoms within a
spatial {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}}, or to remove the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity from a group of atoms, or to remove the x\sphinxhyphen{}component of
velocity from the calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not done by default, but only if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} command is used to assign a temperature compute to this
fix that includes such a bias term.  See the doc pages for individual
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp commands}}}} to determine which ones include
a bias.  In this case, the thermostat works in the following manner:
bias is removed from each atom, thermostatting is performed on the
remaining thermal degrees of freedom, and the bias is added back in.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the cumulative global energy change to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that
reads a restart file, so that the fix continues in an uninterrupted
fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} option is supported by this
fix.  You can use it to assign a temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}
you have defined to this fix which will be used in its thermostatting
procedure, as described above.  For consistency, the group used by
this fix and by the compute should be the same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cumulative energy change in the system imposed by this fix is
included in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}} keywords
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecouple} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{econserve}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}
doc page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar which can be accessed by various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar is the same
cumulative energy change due to this fix described in the previous
paragraph.  The scalar value calculated by this fix is “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can ramp its target temperature over multiple runs, using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\subsection{Syntax}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rescale}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{window}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fraction}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/rescale/eff = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = perform rescaling every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale_eff:examples}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reset the temperature of a group of nuclei and electrons in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}} model by explicitly rescaling
their velocities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this fix is exactly like that described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}} command, except that the rescaling
is also applied to the radial electron velocity for electron
particles.
