\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bound the simulation domain on one or more of its faces with a flat
wall that interacts with the atoms in the group by generating a force
on the atom in a direction perpendicular to the wall.  The energy of
wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions depends on the style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj93}, the energy E is given by the 9\sphinxhyphen{}3 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \left[ \frac{2}{15} \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{9} -
                      \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^3 \right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj126}, the energy E is given by the 12\sphinxhyphen{}6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
                      \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj1043}, the energy E is given by the 10\sphinxhyphen{}4\sphinxhyphen{}3 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 2 \pi \epsilon \left[ \frac{2}{5} \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{10} -
                      \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^4 -
                      \frac{\sqrt(2)\sigma^3}{3\left(r+\left(0.61/\sqrt(2)\right)\sigma\right)^3}\right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/colloid}, the energy E is given by an integrated form
of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_colloid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style colloid}}}} potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = & \epsilon \left[ \frac{\sigma^{6}}{7560}
\left(\frac{6R-D}{D^{7}} + \frac{D+8R}{(D+2R)^{7}} \right) \right. \\
 & \left. - \frac{1}{6} \left(\frac{2R(D+R) + D(D+2R)
 \left[ \ln D - \ln (D+2R) \right]}{D(D+2R)} \right) \right] \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/harmonic}, the energy E is given by a repulsive\sphinxhyphen{}only harmonic
spring potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \quad (r - r_c)^2 \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/morse}, the energy E is given by a Morse potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = D_0 \left[ e^{- 2 \alpha (r - r_0)} - 2 e^{- \alpha (r - r_0)} \right]
    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lepton}, the energy E is provided as an Lepton
expression string using “r” as the distance variable.  The \sphinxhref{https://simtk.org/projects/lepton}{Lepton
library}, that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lepton}
style interfaces with, evaluates this expression string at run time to
compute the wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle energy.  It also creates an analytical
representation of the first derivative of this expression with respect
to “r” and then uses that to compute the force between the wall and
atoms in the fix group.  The Lepton expression must be either enclosed
in quotes or must not contain any whitespace so that LAMMPS recognizes
it as a single keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optionally, the expression may use “rc” to refer to the cutoff distance
for the given wall.  Further constants in the expression can be defined
in the same string as additional expressions separated by semicolons.
The expression “k*(r\sphinxhyphen{}rc)\textasciicircum{}2;k=100.0” represents a repulsive\sphinxhyphen{}only harmonic
spring as in fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/harmonic} with a force constant \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} (same as
\(\epsilon\) above) of 100 energy units.  More details on the Lepton
expression strings are given below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/table}, the energy E and forces are determined from
interpolation tables listed in one or more files as a function of
distance.  The interpolation tables are used to evaluate energy and
forces between particles and the wall similar to how analytic formulas
are used for the other wall styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interpolation tables are created as a pre\sphinxhyphen{}computation by fitting
cubic splines to the file values and interpolating energy and force
values at each of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} distances.  During a simulation, the tables are
used to interpolate energy and force values as needed for each wall and
particle separated by a distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}.  The interpolation is done in
one of two styles: \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spline}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style, the distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} is used to find the 2
surrounding table values from which an energy or force is computed by
linear interpolation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spline} style, cubic spline coefficients are computed and
stored for each of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} values in the table, one set of splines for
energy, another for force.  Note that these splines are different than
the ones used to pre\sphinxhyphen{}compute the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} values.  Those splines were fit
to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfile} values in the tabulated file, where often \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nfile} \textless{}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{N}.  The distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} is used to find the appropriate set of spline
coefficients which are used to evaluate a cubic polynomial which
computes the energy or force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each wall a filename and a keyword must be provided as in the
examples above.  The filename specifies a file containing tabulated
energy and force values.  The keyword specifies a section of the file.
The format of this file is described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In all cases, \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} is the distance from the particle to the wall at
position \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord}, and \(r_c\) is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} distance at which the
particle and wall no longer interact.  The energy of the wall
potential is shifted so that the wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interaction energy is
0.0 at the cutoff distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Up to 6 walls or faces can be specified in a single command: \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi}.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} face interacts with
particles near the lower side of the simulation box in that dimension.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} face interacts with particles near the upper side of the
simulation box in that dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The position of each wall can be specified in one of 3 ways: as the
EDGE of the simulation box, as a constant value, or as a variable.  If
EDGE is used, then the corresponding boundary of the current
simulation box is used.  If a numeric constant is specified then the
wall is placed at that position in the appropriate dimension (x, y, or
z).  In both the EDGE and constant cases, the wall will never move.
If the wall position is a variable, it should be specified as v\_name,
where name is an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} name.  In this
case the variable is evaluated each timestep and the result becomes
the current position of the reflecting wall.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables
can specify formulas with various mathematical functions, and include
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command keywords for the simulation
box parameters and timestep and elapsed time.  Thus it is easy to
specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent wall position.  See examples below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj93} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj126} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj1043} styles,
\(\epsilon\) and \(\sigma\) are the usual Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
parameters, which determine the strength and size of the particle as it
interacts with the wall.  Epsilon has energy units.  Note that this
\(\epsilon\) and \(\sigma\) may be different than any
\(\epsilon\) or \(\sigma\) values defined for a pair style that
computes particle\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj93} interaction is derived by integrating over a 3d
half\sphinxhyphen{}lattice of Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones 12/6 particles.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj126}
interaction is effectively a harder, more repulsive wall interaction.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj1043} interaction is yet a different form of wall
interaction, described in Magda et al in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall:magda}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Magda)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/colloid} style, \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} is the radius of the colloid particle,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{D} is the distance from the surface of the colloid particle to the wall
(r\sphinxhyphen{}R), and \(\sigma\) is the size of a constituent LJ particle
inside the colloid particle and wall.  Note that the cutoff distance Rc
in this case is the distance from the colloid particle center to the
wall.  The prefactor \(\epsilon\) can be thought of as an effective
Hamaker constant with energy units for the strength of the colloid\sphinxhyphen{}wall
interaction.  More specifically, the \(\epsilon\) prefactor is
\(4\pi^2 \rho_{wall} \rho_{colloid} \epsilon \sigma^6\), where
\(\epsilon\) and \(\sigma\) are the LJ parameters for the
constituent LJ particles. \(\rho_{wall}\) and \(\rho_{colloid}\)
are the number density of the constituent particles, in the wall and
colloid respectively, in units of 1/volume.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/colloid} interaction is derived by integrating over
constituent LJ particles of size \(\sigma\) within the colloid
particle and a 3d half\sphinxhyphen{}lattice of Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones 12/6 particles of size
\(\sigma\) in the wall.  As mentioned in the preceding paragraph,
the density of particles in the wall and colloid can be different, as
specified by the \(\epsilon\) prefactor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/harmonic} style, \(\epsilon\) is effectively the spring
constant K, and has units (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2).  The input parameter
\(\sigma\) is ignored.  The minimum energy position of the harmonic
spring is at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}.  This is a repulsive\sphinxhyphen{}only spring since the
interaction is truncated at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/morse} style, the three parameters are in this order:
\(D_0\) the depth of the potential, \(\alpha\) the width
parameter, and \(r_0\) the location of the minimum.  \(D_0\) has
energy units, \(\alpha\) inverse distance units, and \(r_0\)
distance units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For any wall that supports them, the \(\epsilon\) and/or
\(\sigma\) and/or \(\alpha\) parameter can be specified as an
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}}, in which case it should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  As with a
variable wall position, the variable is evaluated each timestep and the
result becomes the current epsilon or sigma of the wall.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can specify formulas with various mathematical functions, and
include {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command keywords for the
simulation box parameters and timestep and elapsed time.  Thus it is
easy to specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent wall interaction.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For all of the styles, you must ensure that r is always \textgreater{} 0 for
all particles in the group, or LAMMPS will generate an error.  This
means you cannot start your simulation with particles at the wall
position \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord} (r = 0) or with particles on the wrong side of the
wall (r \textless{} 0).  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj93} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj126} styles, the energy
of the wall/particle interaction (and hence the force on the particle)
blows up as r \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} 0.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/colloid} style is even more
restrictive, since the energy blows up as D = r\sphinxhyphen{}R \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} 0.  This means
the finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles of radius R must be a distance larger than R
from the wall position \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} style is a softer
potential and does not blow up as r \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} 0, but you must use a large
enough \(\epsilon\) that particles always reamin on the correct side of
the wall (r \textgreater{} 0).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define a wall position, but only when a numeric constant or
variable is used.  It is not relevant when EDGE is used to specify a
face position.  In the variable case, the variable is assumed to
produce a value compatible with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} setting you specify.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance units as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command, e.g. Angstroms for units = real or metal.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in lattice spacings.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been previously used to
define the lattice spacings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fld} keyword can be used with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} setting to invoke the wall
constraint before pairwise interactions are computed.  This allows an
implicit FLD model using {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lubricateU::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lubricateU}}}}
to include the wall force in its calculations.  If the setting is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no},
wall forces are imposed after pairwise interactions, in the usual
manner.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pbc} keyword can be used with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} setting to allow walls to be
specified in a periodic dimension.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}}
command for options on simulation box boundaries.  The default for \sphinxstyleemphasis{pbc}
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, which means the system must be non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic when using a wall.
But you may wish to use a periodic box.  E.g. to allow some particles to
interact with the wall via the fix group\sphinxhyphen{}ID, and others to pass through
it and wrap around a periodic box.  In this case you should ensure that
the wall is sufficiently far enough away from the box boundary.  If you
do not, then particles may interact with both the wall and with periodic
images on the other side of the box, which is probably not what you
want.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are examples of variable definitions that move the wall position
in a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent fashion using equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}}.  The wall interaction parameters (epsilon,
sigma) could be varied with additional variable definitions.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0,10}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdisplace}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0,20}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{swiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,5.0,3.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cwiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,5.0,3.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp(lo,hi)} function adjusts the wall position linearly from \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} over the course of a run.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vdisplace(c0,velocity)} function does
something similar using the equation \sphinxstyleemphasis{position = c0 + velocity*delta},
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the elapsed time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{swiggle(c0,A,period)} function causes the wall position to
oscillate sinusoidally according to this equation, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega = 2 PI
/ period}:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = c0 + A sin(omega*delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cwiggle(c0,A,period)} function causes the wall position to
oscillate sinusoidally according to this equation, which will have an
initial wall velocity of 0.0, and thus may impose a gentler
perturbation on the particles:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = c0 + A (1 \sphinxhyphen{} cos(omega*delta))
\end{sphinxalltt}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\label{\detokenize{fix_wall:lepton-expression-syntax-and-features}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numbers may be given in either decimal or exponential form.  All of the
following are valid numbers: \sphinxtitleref{5}, \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}3.1}, \sphinxtitleref{1e6}, and \sphinxtitleref{3.12e\sphinxhyphen{}2}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an extension to the standard Lepton syntax, it is also possible to
use LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}} in the format “v\_name”.  Before
evaluating the expression, “v\_name” will be replaced with the value of
the variable “name”.  This is compatible with all kinds of scalar
variables, but not with vectors, arrays, local, or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
variables.  If necessary, a custom scalar variable needs to be defined
that can access the desired (single) item from a non\sphinxhyphen{}scalar variable.
As an example, the following lines will instruct LAMMPS to ramp
the force constant for a harmonic bond from 100.0 to 200.0 during the
next run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fconst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{100.0, 200}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}fconst * (r\PYGZca{}2)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An expression may be followed by definitions for intermediate values that appear in the
expression. A semicolon “;” is used as a delimiter between value definitions. For example,
the expression:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
is exactly equivalent to

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The definition of an intermediate value may itself involve other
intermediate values. Whitespace and quotation characters (’\textquotesingle{}’ and ‘”’)
are ignored.  All uses of a value must appear \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} that value’s
definition.  For efficiency reasons, the expression string is parsed,
optimized, and then stored in an internal, pre\sphinxhyphen{}parsed representation for
evaluation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluating a Lepton expression is typically between 2.5 and 5 times
slower than the corresponding compiled and optimized C++ code.  If
additional speed or GPU acceleration (via GPU or KOKKOS) is required,
the interaction can be represented as a table.  Suitable table files
can be created either internally using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_write}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_write}}}} command or through the Python scripts
in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools:tabulate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{tools/tabulate}}}} folder.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Table file format}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall:table-file-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Suitable tables for use with fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/table} can be created by the
Python code in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/tabulate}} folder of the LAMMPS source code
distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is as follows (without the parenthesized
comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Tabulated wall potential UNITS: real

HARMONIC                       (keyword is the first text on a line)
N 100 FP 200 200
                               (blank line)
1  0.04    1568.16    792.00   (index, distance to wall, energy, force)
2  0.08    1536.64    784.00
3  0.12    1505.44    776.00
...
99  3.96      0.16      8.00
100  4.00     0         0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which identifies
the section.  The line can contain additional text, but the initial text
must match the argument specified in the fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/table} command.  The
next line lists (in any order) one or more parameters for the table.
Each parameter is a keyword followed by one or more numeric values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter “N” is required and its value is the number of table
entries that follow.  Note that this may be different than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
specified in the fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/table} command.  Let Ntable = \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} in the fix
command, and Nfile = “N” in the tabulated file.  What LAMMPS does is a
preliminary interpolation by creating splines using the Nfile tabulated
values as nodal points.  It uses these to interpolate as needed to
generate energy and force values at Ntable different points.  The
resulting tables of length Ntable are then used as described above, when
computing energy and force for wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions.  This means that
if you want the interpolation tables of length Ntable to match exactly
what is in the tabulated file (with effectively no preliminary
interpolation), you should set Ntable = Nfile.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy of interaction between atoms and all the
specified walls to the global potential energy of the system as part
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting
for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution due to the interaction between atoms
and all the specified walls to both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
stress of the system via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former can be accessed by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for
this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar energy and a global vector of forces,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
Note that the scalar energy is the sum of interactions with all defined
walls.  If you want the energy on a per\sphinxhyphen{}wall basis, you need to use
multiple fix wall commands.  The length of the vector is equal to the
number of walls defined by the fix.  Each vector value is the normal
force on a specific wall.  Note that an outward force on a wall will be
a negative value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} walls and a positive value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} walls.
The scalar and vector values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the atom/wall interaction energy to be included in
the total potential energy of the system (the quantity being
minimized), you MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy}
option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\section{fix wall/body/polygon command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:fix-wall-body-polygon-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{polygon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{k\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wallstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/body/polygon = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
k\_n = normal repulsion strength (force/distance or pressure units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_n = normal damping coefficient (force/distance or pressure units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_t = tangential damping coefficient (force/distance or pressure units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wallstyle = \sphinxstyleemphasis{xplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yplane} args = lo hi
  lo,hi = position of lower and upper plane (distance units), either can be NULL)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} args = radius
  radius = cylinder radius (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} values = dim amplitude period
  dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
  amplitude = size of oscillation (distance units)
  period = time of oscillation (time units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{polygon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xplane}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is for use with 2d models of body particles of style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rounded/polygon}.  It bounds the simulation domain with wall(s).  All
particles in the group interact with the wall when they are close
enough to touch it.  The nature of the interaction between the wall
and the polygon particles is the same as that between the polygon
particles themselves, which is similar to a Hookean potential.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto body}}}} page for more details on using
body particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{k\_n}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_n}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_t} have the same meaning and units as
those specified with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_body_rounded_polygon::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style body/rounded/polygon}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wallstyle} can be planar or cylindrical.  The 2 planar options
specify a pair of walls in a dimension.  Wall positions are given by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}.  Either of the values can be specified as NULL if a
single wall is desired.  For a \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} wallstyle, the cylinder’s
axis is at x = y = 0.0, and the radius of the cylinder is specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optionally, the wall can be moving, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} keyword is
appended.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} keyword, the wall oscillates sinusoidally, similar to
the oscillations of particles which can be specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_move::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix move}}}} command.  This is useful in packing simulations of
particles.  The arguments to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} keyword specify a dimension
for the motion, as well as it’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{amplitude} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{period}.  Note that
if the dimension is in the plane of the wall, this is effectively a
shearing motion.  If the dimension is perpendicular to the wall, it is
more of a shaking motion.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} wall can only be wiggled in
the z dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each timestep, the position of a wiggled wall in the appropriate \sphinxstyleemphasis{dim}
is set according to this equation:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = coord + A \sphinxhyphen{} A cos (omega * delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord} is the specified initial position of the wall, \sphinxstyleemphasis{A} is
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{amplitude}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} is 2 PI / \sphinxstyleemphasis{period}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the time
elapsed since the fix was specified.  The velocity of the wall is set
to the derivative of this expression.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored by this fix for
access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  No parameter
of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_body_polygon:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the BODY package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any dimension (xy) that has a wall must be non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.

\sphinxAtStartPar

to the derivative of this expression.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_ees:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/ees} bounds the simulation domain on one or more of its
faces with a flat wall that interacts with the ellipsoidal atoms in
the group by generating a force on the atom in a direction
perpendicular to the wall and a torque parallel with the wall.  The
energy of wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions E is given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \left[ \frac{2 \sigma_{LJ}^{12} \left(7 r^5+14 r^3
\sigma_{n}^2+3 r \sigma_{n}^4\right) }{945
\left(r^2-\sigma_{n}^2\right)^7} -\frac{ \sigma_{LJ}^6 \left(2 r
\sigma_{n}^3+\sigma_{n}^2 \left(r^2-\sigma_{n}^2\right)\log{
\left[\frac{r-\sigma_{n}}{r+\sigma_{n}}\right]}\right) }{12
\sigma_{n}^5 \left(r^2-\sigma_{n}^2\right)} \right]\qquad \sigma_n
< r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduced by Babadi and Ejtehadi in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_ees:babadiejtehadi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Babadi2)}}}}. Here, \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} is the distance from the particle to the
wall at position \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord}, and Rc is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} distance at which
the particle and wall no longer interact. Also, \(\sigma_n\) is
the distance between center of ellipsoid and the nearest point of its
surface to the wall as shown below.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{fix_wall_ees_image}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Details of using this command and specifications are the same as
fix/wall command. You can also find an example in USER/ees/ under
examples/ directory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The prefactor \(\epsilon\) can be thought of as an
effective Hamaker constant with energy units for the strength of the
ellipsoid\sphinxhyphen{}wall interaction.  More specifically, the \(\epsilon\)
prefactor is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}8 \pi^2 \quad \rho_{wall} \quad \rho_{ellipsoid} \quad \epsilon
\quad \sigma_a \quad \sigma_b \quad \sigma_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\epsilon\) is the LJ energy parameter for the constituent
LJ particles and \(\sigma_a\), \(\sigma_b\), and
\(\sigma_c\) are the radii of the ellipsoidal
particles. \(\rho_{wall}\) and \(\rho_{ellipsoid}\) are the
number density of the constituent particles, in the wall and ellipsoid
respectively, in units of 1/volume.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You must ensure that r is always bigger than \(\sigma_n\) for
all particles in the group, or LAMMPS will generate an error.  This
means you cannot start your simulation with particles touching the wall
position \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord} (\(r = \sigma_n\)) or with particles penetrating
the wall (\(0 =< r < \sigma_n\)) or with particles on the wrong
side of the wall (\(r < 0\)).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/region/ees} treats the surface of the geometric region defined
by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region\sphinxhyphen{}ID} as a bounding wall which interacts with nearby
ellipsoidal particles according to the EES potential introduced above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other details of this command are the same as for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
wall/region}}}} command.  One may also find an example
of using this fix in the examples/PACKAGES/ees/ directory.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_ees:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about these fixes are written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
these fixes to add the energy of interaction between atoms and all the
specified walls or region wall to the global potential energy of the
system as part of {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The
default settings for these fixes are {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by
these fixes. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}} integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the
outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These fixes computes a global scalar and a global vector of forces,
which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall}}}} command for a
description of the scalar and vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of these fixes can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to these fixes are imposed during an energy
minimization, invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the atom/wall interaction energy to be included in
the total potential energy of the system (the quantity being
minimized), you MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy}
option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_flow:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix implements flow boundary conditions (FBC) introduced in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_flow:fbc-pavlov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pavlov1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_flow:fbc-pavlov2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pavlov2)}}}}.
The goal is to generate a stationary flow with a shifted Maxwell
velocity distribution:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_a(v_a) \propto \exp{\left(-\frac{m (v_a-v_{\text{flow}})^2}{2 kB T}\right)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(v_a\) is the component of velocity along the specified
\sphinxstyleemphasis{axis} argument (a = x,y,z), \(v_{\text{flow}}\) is the flow
velocity specified as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{vflow} argument, \sphinxstyleemphasis{T} is the specified flow
temperature, \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} is the particle mass, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{kB} is the Boltzmann
constant.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is achieved by defining a series of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} transparent walls along
the flow \sphinxstyleemphasis{axis} direction.  Each wall is at the specified position
listed in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{coords} argument.  Note that an additional transparent
wall is defined by the code at the boundary of the (periodic)
simulation domain in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{axis} direction.  So there are effectively
N+1 walls.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each time a particle in the specified group passes through one of the
transparent walls, its velocity is re\sphinxhyphen{}assigned.  Particles not in the
group do not interact with the wall. This can be used, for example, to
add obstacles composed of atoms, or to simulate a solution of complex
molecules in a one\sphinxhyphen{}atom liquid (note that the fix has been tested for
one\sphinxhyphen{}atom systems only).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Conceptually, the velocity re\sphinxhyphen{}assignment represents creation of a new
particle within the system with simultaneous removal of the particle
which passed through the wall.  The velocity components in directions
parallel to the wall are re\sphinxhyphen{}assigned according to the standard Maxwell
velocity distribution for the specified temperature \sphinxstyleemphasis{T}.  The velocity
component perpendicular to the wall is re\sphinxhyphen{}assigned according to the
shifted Maxwell distribution defined above:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_{\text{a generated}}(v_a) \propto v_a f_a(v_a)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It can be shown that for an ideal\sphinxhyphen{}gas scenario this procedure makes
the velocity distribution of particles between walls exactly as
desired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since in most cases simulated systems are not an ideal gas, multiple
walls can be defined, since a single wall may not be sufficient for
maintaining a stationary flow without “congestion” which can manifest
itself as regions in the flow with increased particle density located
upstream from static obstacles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the same reason, the actual temperature and velocity of the
generated flow may differ from what is requested.  The degree of
discrepancy is determined by how different from an ideal gas the
simulated system is.  Therefore, a calibration procedure may be
required for such a system as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_flow:fbc-pavlov2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pavlov)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the interactions between particles on different sides of a
transparent wall are not disabled or neglected.  Likewise particle
positions are not altered by the velocity reassignment.  This removes
the need to modify the force field to work correctly in cases when a
particle is close to a wall.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if particle positions were uniformly redistributed across
the surface of a wall, two particles could end up too close to each
other, potentially causing the simulation to explode.  However due to
this compromise, some collective phenomena such as regions with
increased/decreased density or collective movements are not fully
removed when particles cross a wall.  This unwanted consequence can
also be potentially mitigated by using more multiple walls.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the specified flow has a high velocity, a lost atoms error can
occur (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Errors_messages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{error messages}}}}).  If this
happens, you should ensure the checks for neighbor list rebuilds,
set via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command, are as
conservative as possible (every timestep if needed).  Those are the
default settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_flow:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall\_flow} is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Flow boundary conditions should not be used with rigid bodies such as
those defined by a “fix rigid” command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix can only be used with periodic boundary conditions along the
flow axis. The size of the box in this direction must not change. Also,
the fix is designed to work only in an orthogonal simulation box.

\subsection{Default}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default for the units keyword is lattice.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{fix wall/gran command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran:fix-wall-gran-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/gran/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gran}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fstyle\PYGZus{}params}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wallstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/gran = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fstyle = style of force interactions between particles and wall

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible choices: hooke, hooke/history, hertz/history, granular
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fstyle\_params = parameters associated with force interaction style
\begin{sphinxalltt}
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke/history}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hertz/history}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle\_params} are:
      Kn = elastic constant for normal particle repulsion (force/distance units or pressure units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      Kt = elastic constant for tangential contact (force/distance units or pressure units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      gamma\_n = damping coefficient for collisions in normal direction (1/time units or 1/time\sphinxhyphen{}distance units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      gamma\_t = damping coefficient for collisions in tangential direction (1/time units or 1/time\sphinxhyphen{}distance units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      xmu = static yield criterion (unitless value between 0.0 and 1.0e4)
      dampflag = 0 or 1 if tangential damping force is excluded or included
      optional keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit\_damping}, limit damping to prevent attractive interaction
\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{granular}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle\_params} are set using the same syntax as for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wallstyle = \sphinxstyleemphasis{xplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yplane} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zplane} args = lo hi
  lo,hi = position of lower and upper plane (distance units), either can be NULL)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} args = radius
  radius = cylinder radius (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{shear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{contacts} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
 \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} values = dim amplitude period
   dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
   amplitude = size of oscillation (distance units)
   period = time of oscillation (time units)
 \sphinxstyleemphasis{shear} values = dim vshear
   dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
   vshear = magnitude of shear velocity (velocity units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{contacts} value = none
   generate contact information for each particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} value = temperature
   specify temperature of wall
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bound the simulation domain of a granular system with a frictional
wall.  All particles in the group interact with the wall when they are
close enough to touch it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The nature of the wall/particle interactions are determined by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle} setting.  It can be any of the styles defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}} or the more general
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} commands.  Currently the
options are \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke/history}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hertz/history} for the
former, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{granular} with all the possible options of the associated
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command for the latter.  The equation for the force
between the wall and particles touching it is the same as the
corresponding equation on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} doc pages, in the limit of
one of the two particles going to infinite radius and mass (flat wall).
Specifically, delta = radius \sphinxhyphen{} r = overlap of particle with wall, m\_eff
= mass of particle, and the effective radius of contact = RiRj/Ri+Rj is
set to the radius of the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kn}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_n}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xmu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dampflag},
and the optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit\_damping}
have the same meaning and units as those specified with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}} commands.  This means a NULL can be
used for either \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} as described on that page.  If a
NULL is used for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt}, then a default value is used where \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt} = 2/7
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Kn}.  If a NULL is used for \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t}, then a default value is used
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} = 1/2 \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_n}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All the model choices for cohesion, tangential friction, rolling
friction and twisting friction supported by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} through its \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command are also
supported for walls. These are discussed in greater detail on the doc
page for {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle} \sphinxstyleemphasis{granular} is specified, the associated \sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle\_params} are taken as
those for a wall/particle interaction. For example, for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hertz/material} normal
contact model with \(E = 960\) and \(\nu = 0.2\), the effective Young’s
modulus for a wall/particle interaction is computed as
\(E_{eff} = \frac{960}{2(1-0.2^2)} = 500\). Any pair coefficients defined by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} are not taken into consideration. To
model different wall/particle interactions for particles of different material
types, the user may define multiple fix wall/gran commands operating on separate
groups (e.g. based on particle type) each with a different wall/particle effective
Young’s modulus.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that you can choose a different force styles and/or different
values for the wall/particle coefficients than for particle/particle
interactions.  E.g. if you wish to model the wall as a different
material.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed on the page for {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}},
versions of LAMMPS before 9Jan09 used a different equation for
Hertzian interactions.  This means Hertizian wall/particle
interactions have also changed.  They now include a sqrt(radius) term
which was not present before.  Also the previous versions used Kn and
Kt from the pairwise interaction and hardwired dampflag to 1, rather
than letting them be specified directly.  This means you can set the
values of the wall/particle coefficients appropriately in the current
code to reproduce the results of a previous Hertzian monodisperse
calculation.  For example, for the common case of a monodisperse
system with particles of diameter 1, Kn, Kt, gamma\_n, and gamma\_s
should be set sqrt(2.0) larger than they were previously.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The effective mass \sphinxstyleemphasis{m\_eff} in the formulas listed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} page is the mass of the particle for
particle/wall interactions (mass of wall is infinite).  If the
particle is part of a rigid body, its mass is replaced by the mass of
the rigid body in those formulas.  This is determined by searching for
a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}} command (or its variants).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wallstyle} can be planar or cylindrical.  The 3 planar options
specify a pair of walls in a dimension.  Wall positions are given by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi}.  Either of the values can be specified as NULL if a
single wall is desired.  For a \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} wallstyle, the cylinder’s
axis is at x = y = 0.0, and the radius of the cylinder is specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optionally, the wall can be moving, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{shear}
keywords are appended.  Both keywords cannot be used together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} keyword, the wall oscillates sinusoidally, similar to
the oscillations of particles which can be specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_move::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix move}}}} command.  This is useful in packing simulations of
granular particles.  The arguments to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wiggle} keyword specify a
dimension for the motion, as well as it’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{amplitude} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{period}.
Note that if the dimension is in the plane of the wall, this is
effectively a shearing motion.  If the dimension is perpendicular to
the wall, it is more of a shaking motion.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} wall can only
be wiggled in the z dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each timestep, the position of a wiggled wall in the appropriate \sphinxstyleemphasis{dim}
is set according to this equation:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = coord + A \sphinxhyphen{} A cos (omega * delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord} is the specified initial position of the wall, \sphinxstyleemphasis{A} is
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{amplitude}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} is 2 PI / \sphinxstyleemphasis{period}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the time
elapsed since the fix was specified.  The velocity of the wall is set
to the derivative of this expression.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shear} keyword, the wall moves continuously in the specified
dimension with velocity \sphinxstyleemphasis{vshear}.  The dimension must be tangential to
walls with a planar \sphinxstyleemphasis{wallstyle}, e.g. in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} directions for
an \sphinxstyleemphasis{xplane} wall.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{zcylinder} walls, a dimension of \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} means the
cylinder is moving in the z\sphinxhyphen{}direction along it’s axis.  A dimension of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} means the cylinder is spinning around the z\sphinxhyphen{}axis, either in
the clockwise direction for \sphinxstyleemphasis{vshear} \textgreater{} 0 or counter\sphinxhyphen{}clockwise for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vshear} \textless{} 0.  In this case, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vshear} is the tangential velocity of
the wall at whatever \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} has been defined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} keyword is used to assign a temperature to the wall.
The following value can either be a numeric value or an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is a variable, it should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the
variable will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine
the temperature. This option must be used in conjunction with a heat
conduction model defined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} to store temperature and a
heat flow, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_heat_flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix heat/flow}}}} to integrate heat
flow.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the shear friction state of atoms interacting with the
wall to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so that a simulation can
continue correctly if granular potentials with shear “history” effects
are being used.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for
info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a
restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contacts}} option is used, this fix generates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
with 8 columns as output, containing the contact information for owned
particles (nlocal on each processor). All columns in this per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array will
be zero if no contact has occurred.  The values of these columns are listed in
the following table:

\subsection{Restrictions}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the GRANULAR package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any dimension (xyz) that has a granular wall must be non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.

\section{fix wall/gran/region command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region:fix-wall-gran-region-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gran}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fstyle\PYGZus{}params}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wallstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{regionID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/region = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fstyle = style of force interactions between particles and wall

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible choices: hooke, hooke/history, hertz/history, granular
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fstyle\_params = parameters associated with force interaction style
\begin{sphinxalltt}
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke/history}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{hertz/history}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle\_params} are:
      Kn = elastic constant for normal particle repulsion (force/distance units or pressure units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      Kt = elastic constant for tangential contact (force/distance units or pressure units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      gamma\_n = damping coefficient for collisions in normal direction (1/time units or 1/time\sphinxhyphen{}distance units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      gamma\_t = damping coefficient for collisions in tangential direction (1/time units or 1/time\sphinxhyphen{}distance units \sphinxhyphen{} see discussion below)
      xmu = static yield criterion (unitless value between 0.0 and 1.0e4)
      dampflag = 0 or 1 if tangential damping force is excluded or included
\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{granular}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle\_params} are set using the same syntax as for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wallstyle = region (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/gran}}}} for options for other kinds of walls)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = region whose boundary will act as wall

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{contacts} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{contacts} value = none
   generate contact information for each particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} value = temperature
   specify temperature of wall
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
