\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat the surface of the geometric region defined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region\sphinxhyphen{}ID}
as a bounding frictional wall which interacts with nearby finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
granular particles when they are close enough to touch the wall.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/region}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/gran}}}} commands for related kinds of walls for
non\sphinxhyphen{}granular particles and simpler wall geometries, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are snapshots of example models using this command.  Corresponding
input scripts can be found in examples/granregion.  Movies of these
simulations are \sphinxhref{https://www.lammps.org/movies.html\#granregion}{here on the Movies page}
of the LAMMPS website.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.480\linewidth]{{gran_funnel}.png}  \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.480\linewidth]{{gran_mixer}.png}




\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The distance between a particle and the region boundary is the
distance to the nearest point on the region surface.  The force the
wall exerts on the particle is along the direction between that point
and the particle center, which is the direction normal to the surface
at that point.  Note that if the region surface is comprised of
multiple “faces”, then each face can exert a force on the particle if
it is close enough.  E.g. for {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region\_style block}}}}, a
particle in the interior, near a corner of the block, could feel wall
forces from 1, 2, or 3 faces of the block.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regions are defined using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  Note that
the region volume can be interior or exterior to the bounding surface,
which will determine in which direction the surface interacts with
particles, i.e. the direction of the surface normal. The exception to
this is if one or more \sphinxstyleemphasis{open} options are specified for the region
command, in which case particles interact with both the interior and
exterior surfaces of regions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regions can either be primitive shapes (block, sphere, cylinder, etc)
or combinations of primitive shapes specified via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{intersect} region styles.  These latter styles can be used to
construct particle containers with complex shapes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regions can also move dynamically via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command
keywords (move) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate}, or change their shape by use of variables
as inputs to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  If such a region is used
with this fix, then the region surface will move in time in the
corresponding manner.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command doc page,
regions in LAMMPS do not get wrapped across periodic boundaries.  It
is up to you to ensure that the region location with respect to
periodic or non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundaries is specified appropriately via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} commands when using
a region as a wall that bounds particle motion.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For primitive regions with sharp corners and/or edges (e.g. a
block or cylinder), wall/particle forces are computed accurately for
both interior and exterior regions.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{intersect}
regions, additional sharp corners and edges may be present due to the
intersection of the surfaces of 2 or more primitive volumes.  These
corners and edges can be of two types: concave or convex.  Concave
points/edges are like the corners of a cube as seen by particles in
the interior of a cube.  Wall/particle forces around these features
are computed correctly.  Convex points/edges are like the corners of a
cube as seen by particles exterior to the cube, i.e. the points jut
into the volume where particles are present.  LAMMPS does NOT compute
the location of these convex points directly, and hence wall/particle
forces in the cutoff volume around these points suffer from
inaccuracies.  The basic problem is that the outward normal of the
surface is not continuous at these points.  This can cause particles
to feel no force (they don’t “see” the wall) when in one location,
then move a distance epsilon, and suddenly feel a large force because
they now “see” the wall.  In a worst\sphinxhyphen{}case scenario, this can blow
particles out of the simulation box.  Thus, as a general rule you
should not use the fix wall/gran/region command with \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{interesect} regions that have convex points or edges resulting from
the union/intersection (convex points/edges in the union/intersection
due to a single sub\sphinxhyphen{}region are still OK).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly, you should not define \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{intersert} regions
for use with this command that share an overlapping common face that
is part of the overall outer boundary (interior boundary is OK), even
if the face is smooth.  E.g. two regions of style block in a \sphinxstyleemphasis{union}
region, where the two blocks overlap on one or more of their faces.
This is because LAMMPS discards points that are part of multiple
sub\sphinxhyphen{}regions when calculating wall/particle interactions, to avoid
double\sphinxhyphen{}counting the interaction.  Having two coincident faces could
cause the face to become invisible to the particles.  The solution is
to make the two faces differ by epsilon in their position.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The nature of the wall/particle interactions are determined by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fstyle} setting.  It can be any of the styles defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}} or the more general
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} commands.  Currently the
options are \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{hooke/history}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hertz/history} for the
former, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{granular} with all the possible options of the associated
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command for the latter.  The equation for the force
between the wall and particles touching it is the same as the
corresponding equation on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} doc pages, but the effective
radius is calculated using the radius of the particle and the radius of
curvature of the wall at the contact point.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically, delta = radius \sphinxhyphen{} r = overlap of particle with wall,
m\_eff = mass of particle, and RiRj/Ri+Rj is the effective radius, with
Rj replaced by the radius of curvature of the wall at the contact
point.  The radius of curvature can be negative for a concave wall
section, e.g. the interior of cylinder.  For a flat wall, delta =
radius \sphinxhyphen{} r = overlap of particle with wall, m\_eff = mass of particle,
and the effective radius of contact is just the radius of the
particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kn}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_n}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xmu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dampflag},
and the optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{limit\_damping}
have the same meaning and units as those specified with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gran/*}}}} commands.  This means a NULL can be
used for either \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} as described on that page.  If a
NULL is used for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt}, then a default value is used where \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kt} = 2/7
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Kn}.  If a NULL is used for \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t}, then a default value is used
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_t} = 1/2 \sphinxstyleemphasis{gamma\_n}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All the model choices for cohesion, tangential friction, rolling
friction and twisting friction supported by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}} through its \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command are also
supported for walls. These are discussed in greater detail on the doc
page for {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that you can choose a different force styles and/or different
values for the 6 wall/particle coefficients than for particle/particle
interactions.  E.g. if you wish to model the wall as a different
material.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} keyword is used to assign a temperature to the wall.
The following value can either be a numeric value or an equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}.  If the value is a variable, it should be
specified as v\_name, where name is the variable name.  In this case, the
variable will be evaluated each timestep, and its value used to determine
the temperature. This option must be used in conjunction with a heat
conduction model defined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_granular::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style granular}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} to store temperature and a
heat flow, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_heat_flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix heat/flow}}}} to integrate heat
flow.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/gran}}}} command, this fix writes
the shear friction state of atoms interacting with the wall to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so that a simulation can continue
correctly if granular potentials with shear “history” effects are
being used.  This fix also includes info about a moving region in the
restart file.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for
info on how to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a
restart file, so that the operation of the fix continues in an
uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Information about region definitions is NOT included in restart
files, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} doc page.
So you must re\sphinxhyphen{}define your region and if it is a moving region, define
its motion attributes in a way that is consistent with the simulation
that wrote the restart file.  In particular, if you want to change the
region motion attributes (e.g. its velocity), then you should ensure
the position/orientation of the region at the initial restart timestep
is the same as it was on the timestep the restart file was written.
If this is not possible, you may need to ignore info in the restart
file by defining a new fix wall/gran/region command in your restart
script, e.g. with a different fix ID.  Or if you want to keep the
shear history info but discard the region motion information, you can
use the same fix ID for fix wall/gran/region, but assign it a region
with a different region ID.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contacts}} option is used, this fix generates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array
with 8 columns as output, containing the contact information for owned
particles (nlocal on each processor). All columns in this per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array will
be zero if no contact has occurred. The values of these columns are listed in
the following table:

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_gran_region:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the GRANULAR package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\section{fix wall/piston command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston:fix-wall-piston-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{piston}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{face}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/piston = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
face = \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{pos} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pos} args = z
  z = z coordinate at which the piston begins (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} args = vz
  vz = final velocity of the piston (velocity units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} = use a linear velocity ramp from 0 to vz
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} args = target damp seed extent
  target = target velocity for region immediately ahead of the piston
  damp = damping parameter (time units)
  seed = random number seed for langevin kicks
  extent = extent of thermostatted region (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} = the wall position is defined in lattice units
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} = the wall position is defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{xwalls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{piston}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zlo}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{walls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{piston}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{piston}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bound the simulation with a moving wall which reflect particles in the
specified group and drive the system with an effective infinite\sphinxhyphen{}mass
piston capable of driving shock waves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A momentum mirror technique is used, which means that if an atom (or
the wall) moves such that an atom is outside the wall on a timestep by
a distance delta (e.g. due to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}), then it is put
back inside the face by the same delta, and the velocity relative to
the moving wall is flipped in z.  For instance, a stationary particle
hit with a piston wall with velocity vz, will end the timestep with a
velocity of 2*vz.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently the \sphinxstyleemphasis{face} keyword can only be \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo}.  This creates a piston
moving in the positive z direction.  Particles with z coordinate less
than the wall position are reflected to a z coordinate greater than
the wall position.  If the piston velocity is vpz and the particle
velocity before reflection is vzi, the particle velocity after
reflection is \sphinxhyphen{}vzi + 2*vpz.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The initial position of the wall can be specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pos} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The final velocity of the wall can be specified by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} keyword

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} keyword will cause the wall/piston to adjust the velocity
linearly from zero velocity to \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel} over the course of the run. If
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp} keyword is omitted then the wall/piston moves at a constant
velocity defined by \sphinxstyleemphasis{vel}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp} keyword will cause the region immediately in front of the
wall/piston to be thermostatted with a Langevin thermostat.  This
region moves with the piston.  The damping and kicking are measured in
the reference frame of the piston.  So, a temperature of zero would
mean all particles were moving at exactly the speed of the
wall/piston.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define a wall position, but only when a numeric constant is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance units as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command, e.g. Angstroms for units = real or metal.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in lattice spacings.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been previously used to
define the lattice spacings.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.  No global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities are stored
by this fix for access by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_piston:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style is part of the SHOCK package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The face that has the wall/piston must be boundary type ‘s’
(shrink\sphinxhyphen{}wrapped). The opposing face can be
any boundary type other than periodic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A wall/piston should not be used with rigid bodies such as those
defined by a “fix rigid” command.  This is because the wall/piston
displaces atoms directly rather than exerting a force on them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword defaults are pos = 0, vel = 0, units = lattice.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bound the simulation with one or more walls which reflect particles
in the specified group when they attempt to move through them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reflection means that if an atom moves outside the wall on a timestep
by a distance delta (e.g. due to {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}}), then it is
put back inside the face by the same delta, and the sign of the
corresponding component of its velocity is flipped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When used in conjunction with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style verlet}}}}, the resultant time\sphinxhyphen{}integration
algorithm is equivalent to the primitive splitting algorithm (PSA)
described by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect:bond1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Bond}}}}.  Because each reflection event
divides the corresponding timestep asymmetrically, energy conservation
is only satisfied to O(dt), rather than to O(dt\textasciicircum{}2) as it would be for
velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Verlet integration without reflective walls.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Up to 6 walls or faces can be specified in a single command: \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi}.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} face reflects particles
that move to a coordinate less than the wall position, back in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} direction.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} face reflects particles that move to a
coordinate higher than the wall position, back in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The position of each wall can be specified in one of 3 ways: as the
EDGE of the simulation box, as a constant value, or as a variable.  If
EDGE is used, then the corresponding boundary of the current
simulation box is used.  If a numeric constant is specified then the
wall is placed at that position in the appropriate dimension (x, y, or
z).  In both the EDGE and constant cases, the wall will never move.
If the wall position is a variable, it should be specified as v\_name,
where name is an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} name.  In this
case the variable is evaluated each timestep and the result becomes
the current position of the reflecting wall.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables
can specify formulas with various mathematical functions, and include
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command keywords for the simulation
box parameters and timestep and elapsed time.  Thus it is easy to
specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent wall position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define a wall position, but only when a numeric constant or
variable is used.  It is not relevant when EDGE is used to specify a
face position.  In the variable case, the variable is assumed to
produce a value compatible with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} setting you specify.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance units as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command, e.g. Angstroms for units = real or metal.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in lattice spacings.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been previously used to
define the lattice spacings.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are examples of variable definitions that move the wall position
in a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent fashion using equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0,10}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ramp}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdisplace}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0,20}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}linear}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{swiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,5.0,3.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}wiggle}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cwiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,5.0,3.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}wiggle}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp(lo,hi)} function adjusts the wall position linearly from \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} over the course of a run.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vdisplace(c0,velocity)} function does
something similar using the equation \sphinxstyleemphasis{position = c0 + velocity*delta},
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the elapsed time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{swiggle(c0,A,period)} function causes the wall position to
oscillate sinusoidally according to this equation, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega = 2 PI
/ period}:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = c0 + A sin(omega*delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cwiggle(c0,A,period)} function causes the wall position to
oscillate sinusoidally according to this equation, which will have an
initial wall velocity of 0.0, and thus may impose a gentler
perturbation on the particles:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = c0 + A (1 \sphinxhyphen{} cos(omega*delta))
\end{sphinxalltt}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any dimension (xyz) that has a reflecting wall must be non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reflecting wall should not be used with rigid bodies such as those
defined by a “fix rigid” command.  This is because the wall/reflect
displaces atoms directly rather than exerts a force on them.  For
rigid bodies, use a soft wall instead, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/lj93}}}}.  LAMMPS will flag the use of a rigid fix with fix
wall/reflect with a warning, but will not generate an error.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/lj93}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_oneway::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix oneway}}}}

\section{fix wall/reflect/stochastic command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:fix-wall-reflect-stochastic-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stochastic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rstyle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{face}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/reflect/stochastic = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rstyle = diffusive or maxwell or ccl

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random seed for stochasticity (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more face/args pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
face = \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
args = pos temp velx vely velz accomx accomy accomz
  pos = EDGE or constant
    EDGE = current lo or hi edge of simulation box
    constant = number like 0.0 or 30.0 (distance units)
  temp = wall temperature (temperature units)
  velx,vely,velz = wall velocity in x,y,z directions (velocity units)
  accomx,accomy,accomz = accommodation coeffs in x,y,z directions (unitless)
    not specified for rstyle = diffusive
    single accom coeff specified for rstyle maxwell
    all 3 coeffs specified for rstyle cll
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} = the wall position is defined in lattice units
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} = the wall position is defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{zwalls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stochastic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diffusive}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{23424}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EDGE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EDGE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ywalls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stochastic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxwell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{345533}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ylo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{xwalls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{reflect}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stochastic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cercignanilampis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2308}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EDGE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bound the simulation with one or more walls which reflect particles
in the specified group when they attempt to move through them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reflection means that if an atom moves outside the wall on a timestep
(e.g. due to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve}}}} command), then it is put back
inside the wall with a changed velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix models treats the wall as a moving solid boundary with a
finite temperature, which can exchange energy with particles that
collide with it.  This is different than the simpler {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/reflect}}}} command which models mirror
reflection.  For this fix, the post collision velocity of each
particle is treated stochastically.  The randomness can come from many
sources: thermal motion of the wall atoms, surface roughness, etc.
Three stochastic reflection models are currently implemented.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For rstyle \sphinxstyleemphasis{diffusive}, particles are reflected diffusively. Their
velocity distribution corresponds to an equilibrium distribution of
particles at the wall temperature.  No accommodation coefficients
are specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For rstyle \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxwell}, particle reflection is Maxwellian which means
partially diffusive and partially specular ({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:maxwell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Maxwell}}}}).  A
single accommodation coeff is specified which must be between 0.0 and
1.0 inclusive.  It determines the fraction of the collision which is
diffusive versus specular.  An accommodation coefficient of 1.0 is fully
diffusive; a coefficient of 0.0 is fully specular.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For rstyle \sphinxstyleemphasis{cll}, particle collisions are computed by the
Cercignani/Lampis model.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:cl}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{CL}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:to}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{To}}}} for details.
Three accommodations coefficient are specified.  Each must be between
0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.  Two are velocity accommodation coefficients;
one is a normal kinetic energy accommodation.  The normal coeff is the
one corresponding to the normal of the wall itself.  For example if
the wall is \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{accomx} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{accomz} are the tangential
velocity accommodation coefficients, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{accomy} is the normal
kinetic energy accommodation coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the distance units used to
define a wall position.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance units
as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command, e.g. Angstroms for units
= real or metal.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in
lattice spacings. The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been
previously used to define the lattice spacings.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix has the same limitations as the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/reflect}}}} command.  Any dimension (xyz) that
has a wall must be non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.  It should not be used with rigid
bodies such as those defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}
command.  The wall velocity must lie on the same plane as the wall
itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}FIX package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix wall/reflect}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_reflect_stochastic:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default for the units keyword is lattice.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

(1867).

\section{fix wall/region command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region:fix-wall-region-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{region\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/region = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = region whose boundary will act as wall

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj93} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj126} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj1043} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{colloid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args for styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj93} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj126} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj1043} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{colloid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} =
\begin{sphinxalltt}
epsilon = strength factor for wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interaction (energy or energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2 units)
sigma = size factor for wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interaction (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} =

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
D\PYGZus{}0 = depth of the potential (energy units)
alpha = width parameter (1/distance units)
r\PYGZus{}0 = distance of the potential minimum from wall position (distance units)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = distance from wall at which wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interaction is cut off (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mySphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj93}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mySphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wall}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{box\PYGZus{}top}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{morse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat the surface of the geometric region defined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region\sphinxhyphen{}ID}
as a bounding wall which interacts with nearby particles according to
the specified style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The distance between a particle and the surface is the distance to the
nearest point on the surface and the force the wall exerts on the
particle is along the direction between that point and the particle,
which is the direction normal to the surface at that point.  Note that
if the region surface is comprised of multiple “faces”, then each face
can exert a force on the particle if it is close enough.  E.g. for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region\_style block}}}}, a particle in the interior, near a
corner of the block, could feel wall forces from 1, 2, or 3 faces of
the block.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regions are defined using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  Note that
the region volume can be interior or exterior to the bounding surface,
which will determine in which direction the surface interacts with
particles, i.e. the direction of the surface normal.  The surface of
the region only exerts forces on particles “inside” the region; if a
particle is “outside” the region it will generate an error, because it
has moved through the wall.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regions can either be primitive shapes (block, sphere, cylinder, etc)
or combinations of primitive shapes specified via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{intersect} region styles.  These latter styles can be used to
construct particle containers with complex shapes.  Regions can also
change over time via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command keywords (move)
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate}.  If such a region is used with this fix, then the of
region surface will move over time in the corresponding manner.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command doc page,
regions in LAMMPS do not get wrapped across periodic boundaries.  It
is up to you to ensure that periodic or non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundaries are
specified appropriately via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command when
using a region as a wall that bounds particle motion.  This also means
that if you embed a region in your simulation box and want it to
repulse particles from its surface (using the “side out” option in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command), that its repulsive force will not be
felt across a periodic boundary.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For primitive regions with sharp corners and/or edges (e.g. a
block or cylinder), wall/particle forces are computed accurately for
both interior and exterior regions.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{intersect}
regions, additional sharp corners and edges may be present due to the
intersection of the surfaces of 2 or more primitive volumes.  These
corners and edges can be of two types: concave or convex.  Concave
points/edges are like the corners of a cube as seen by particles in
the interior of a cube.  Wall/particle forces around these features
are computed correctly.  Convex points/edges are like the corners of a
cube as seen by particles exterior to the cube, i.e. the points jut
into the volume where particles are present.  LAMMPS does NOT compute
the location of these convex points directly, and hence wall/particle
forces in the cutoff volume around these points suffer from
inaccuracies.  The basic problem is that the outward normal of the
surface is not continuous at these points.  This can cause particles
to feel no force (they don’t “see” the wall) when in one location,
then move a distance epsilon, and suddenly feel a large force because
they now “see” the wall.  In a worst\sphinxhyphen{}case scenario, this can blow
particles out of the simulation box.  Thus, as a general rule you
should not use the fix wall/gran/region command with \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{interesect} regions that have convex points or edges resulting from
the union/intersection (convex points/edges in the union/intersection
due to a single sub\sphinxhyphen{}region are still OK).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly, you should not define \sphinxstyleemphasis{union} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{intersert} regions
for use with this command that share an overlapping common face that
is part of the overall outer boundary (interior boundary is OK), even
if the face is smooth.  E.g. two regions of style block in a \sphinxstyleemphasis{union}
region, where the two blocks overlap on one or more of their faces.
This is because LAMMPS discards points that are part of multiple
sub\sphinxhyphen{}regions when calculating wall/particle interactions, to avoid
double\sphinxhyphen{}counting the interaction.  Having two coincident faces could
cause the face to become invisible to the particles.  The solution is
to make the two faces differ by epsilon in their position.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The energy of wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle interactions depends on the specified
style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj93}, the energy E is given by the 9/3 potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \left[ \frac{2}{15} \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{9} -
                      \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^3 \right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj126}, the energy E is given by the 12/6 potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
                      \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/lj1043}, the energy E is given by the 10/4/3 potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 2 \pi \epsilon \left[ \frac{2}{5} \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{10} -
                      \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^4 -
                      \frac{\sqrt(2)\sigma^3}{3\left(r+\left(0.61/\sqrt(2)\right)\sigma\right)^3}\right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{colloid}, the energy E is given by an integrated form of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_colloid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style colloid}}}} potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = & \epsilon \left[ \frac{\sigma^{6}}{7560}
\left(\frac{6R-D}{D^{7}} + \frac{D+8R}{(D+2R)^{7}} \right) \right. \\
 & \left. - \frac{1}{6} \left(\frac{2R(D+R) + D(D+2R)
 \left[ \ln D - \ln (D+2R) \right]}{D(D+2R)} \right) \right] \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/harmonic}, the energy E is given by a harmonic spring
potential (the distance parameter is ignored):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \quad (r - r_c)^2 \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{wall/morse}, the energy E is given by the Morse potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = D_0 \left[ e^{- 2 \alpha (r - r_0)} - 2 e^{- \alpha (r - r_0)} \right]
    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike other styles, this requires three parameters (\(D_0\),
\(\alpha\), and \(r_0\) in this order) instead of two like
for the other wall styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In all cases, \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} is the distance from the particle to the region
surface, and Rc is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} distance at which the particle and
surface no longer interact.  The cutoff is always the last argument.
The energy of the wall potential is shifted so that the wall\sphinxhyphen{}particle
interaction energy is 0.0 at the cutoff distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a full description of these wall styles, see fix\_style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{wall}}}}


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_region:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option is supported by
this fix to add the energy of interaction between atoms and the region
wall to the global potential energy of the system as part of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The default setting for
this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify energy no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} option is supported by
this fix to add the contribution due to the interaction between atoms
and the region wall to both the global pressure and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom stress of
the system via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}} commands.  The former
can be accessed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermodynamic output}}}}.  The
default setting for this fix is {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify virial no}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{respa} option is supported by this
fix. This allows to set at which level of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{r\sphinxhyphen{}RESPA}}}}
integrator the fix is adding its forces. Default is the outermost level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global scalar energy and a global 3\sphinxhyphen{}length vector
of forces, which can be accessed by various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The scalar energy is the sum of energy interactions
for all particles interacting with the wall represented by the region
surface.  The 3 vector quantities are the x,y,z components of the
total force acting on the wall due to the particles.  The scalar and
vector values calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces due to this fix are imposed during an energy minimization,
invoked by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the atom/wall interaction energy to be included in the
total potential energy of the system (the quantity being
minimized), you MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for this fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\section{fix wall/srd command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd:fix-wall-srd-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{face}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{arg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wall/srd = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more face/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
face = \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo},\sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo},\sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo} arg = EDGE or constant or variable
  EDGE = current lo edge of simulation box
  constant = number like 0.0 or \sphinxhyphen{}30.0 (distance units)
  variable = {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} like v\_x or v\_wiggle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi},\sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi},\sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi} arg = EDGE or constant or variable
  EDGE = current hi edge of simulation box
  constant = number like 50.0 or 100.3 (distance units)
  variable = {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} like v\_x or v\_wiggle
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} = the wall position is defined in lattice units
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} = the wall position is defined in simulation box units
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{walls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ylo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{top}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}pressdown}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bound the simulation with one or more walls which interact with
stochastic reaction dynamics (SRD) particles as slip (smooth) or
no\sphinxhyphen{}slip (rough) flat surfaces.  The wall interaction is actually
invoked via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix srd}}}} command, only on the group of
SRD particles it defines, so the group setting for the fix wall/srd
command is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A particle/wall collision occurs if an SRD particle moves outside the
wall on a timestep.  This alters the position and velocity of the SRD
particle and imparts a force to the wall.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{collision} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd} settings specified via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix srd}}}} command affect the SRD/wall collisions.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{slip}
setting for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{collision} keyword means that the tangential
component of the SRD particle momentum is preserved.  Thus only a
normal force is imparted to the wall.  The normal component of the new
SRD velocity is sampled from a Gaussian distribution at temperature
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a \sphinxstyleemphasis{noslip} setting of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{collision} keyword, both the normal and
tangential components of the new SRD velocity are sampled from a
Gaussian distribution at temperature \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tsrd}.  Additionally, a new
tangential direction for the SRD velocity is chosen randomly.  This
collision style imparts both a normal and tangential force to the
wall.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Up to 6 walls or faces can be specified in a single command: \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yhi}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zlo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zhi}.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} face reflects particles
that move to a coordinate less than the wall position, back in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} direction.  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} face reflects particles that move to a
coordinate higher than the wall position, back in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The position of each wall can be specified in one of 3 ways: as the
EDGE of the simulation box, as a constant value, or as a variable.  If
EDGE is used, then the corresponding boundary of the current
simulation box is used.  If a numeric constant is specified then the
wall is placed at that position in the appropriate dimension (x, y, or
z).  In both the EDGE and constant cases, the wall will never move.
If the wall position is a variable, it should be specified as v\_name,
where name is an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} name.  In this
case the variable is evaluated each timestep and the result becomes
the current position of the reflecting wall.  Equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variables
can specify formulas with various mathematical functions, and include
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command keywords for the simulation
box parameters and timestep and elapsed time.  Thus it is easy to
specify a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent wall position.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the trajectory of the SRD particle is tracked as it
collides with the wall, you must ensure that r = distance of the
particle from the wall, is always \textgreater{} 0 for SRD particles, or LAMMPS
will generate an error.  This means you cannot start your simulation
with SRD particles at the wall position \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord} (r = 0) or with
particles on the wrong side of the wall (r \textless{} 0).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have 2 or more walls that come together at an edge or
corner (e.g. walls in the x and y dimensions), then be sure to set the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{overlap} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix srd}}}} command,
since the walls effectively overlap when SRD particles collide with
them.  LAMMPS will issue a warning if you do not do this.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The walls of this fix only interact with SRD particles, as
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_srd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix srd}}}} command.  If you are simulating
a mixture containing other kinds of particles, then you should
typically use {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{another wall command}}}} to act on the other
particles.  Since SRD particles will be colliding both with the walls
and the other particles, it is important to ensure that the other
particle’s finite extent does not overlap an SRD wall.  If you do not
do this, you may generate errors when SRD particles end up “inside”
another particle or a wall at the beginning of a collision step.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
to define a wall position, but only when a numeric constant is used.
It is not relevant when EDGE or a variable is used to specify a face
position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value selects standard distance units as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command, e.g. Angstroms for units = real or metal.
A \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in lattice spacings.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}} command must have been previously used to
define the lattice spacings.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are examples of variable definitions that move the wall position
in a time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent fashion using equal\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0,10}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ramp}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdisplace}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0,20}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}linear}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{swiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,5.0,3.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}wiggle}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{wiggle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cwiggle}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{0.0,5.0,3.0}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wall}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{srd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}wiggle}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ramp(lo,hi)} function adjusts the wall position linearly from \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo}
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} over the course of a run.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vdisplace(c0,velocity)} function
does something similar using the equation \sphinxstyleemphasis{position = c0 +
velocity*delta}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} is the elapsed time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{swiggle(c0,A,period)} function causes the wall position to
oscillate sinusoidally according to this equation, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega = 2 PI
/ period}:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = c0 + A sin(omega*delta)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cwiggle(c0,A,period)} function causes the wall position to
oscillate sinusoidally according to this equation, which will have an
initial wall velocity of 0.0, and thus may impose a gentler
perturbation on the particles:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
position = c0 + A (1 \sphinxhyphen{} cos(omega*delta))
\end{sphinxalltt}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No information about this fix is written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options
are relevant to this fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global array of values which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The number of rows in
the array is equal to the number of walls defined by the fix.  The
number of columns is 3, for the x,y,z components of force on each
wall.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that an outward normal force on a wall will be a negative value
for \sphinxstyleemphasis{lo} walls and a positive value for \sphinxstyleemphasis{hi} walls.  The array values
calculated by this fix are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{fix_wall_srd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any dimension (xyz) that has an SRD wall must be non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic.

\section{fix widom command}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:fix-widom-command}}\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{fix_widom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{widom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
widom = style name of this fix command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = invoke this fix every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
M = number of Widom insertions to attempt every N steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type = atom type (1\sphinxhyphen{}Ntypes or type label) for inserted atoms (must be 0 if mol keyword used)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = temperature of the system (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intra\_energy}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} value = template\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    template\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of molecule template specified in a separate {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} value = region\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region where Widom insertions are allowed
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} = compute the entire system energy when performing Widom insertions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} value = charge of inserted atoms (charge units)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{intra\_energy} value = intramolecular energy (energy units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{gas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{widom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19494}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{water}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{widom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{29494}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h2omol}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{full\PYGZus{}energy}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Li}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ion}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{widom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Li}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19494}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix performs Widom insertions of atoms or molecules at the given
temperature as discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_widom:frenkel1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Frenkel)}}}}. Specific uses
include computation of Henry constants of small molecules in microporous
materials or amorphous systems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every N timesteps the fix attempts M number of Widom insertions of atoms
or molecules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used, only molecule insertions are performed.
Conversely, if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is not used, only atom insertions are
performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command may optionally use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{region} keyword to define an
insertion volume.  The specified region must have been previously
defined with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region}}}} command.  It must be defined with
side = \sphinxstyleemphasis{in}.  Insertion attempts occur only within the specified
region. For non\sphinxhyphen{}rectangular regions, random trial points are generated
within the rectangular bounding box until a point is found that lies
inside the region. If no valid point is generated after 1000 trials, no
insertion is performed. If an attempted insertion places the atom or
molecule center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass outside the specified region, a new attempted
insertion is generated. This process is repeated until the atom or
molecule center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass is inside the specified region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that neighbor lists are re\sphinxhyphen{}built every timestep that this fix is
invoked, so you should not set N to be too small. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When an atom or molecule is to be inserted, its coordinates are chosen
at a random position within the current simulation cell or region.
Relative coordinates for atoms in a molecule are taken from the
template molecule provided by the user. The center of mass of the
molecule is placed at the insertion point. The orientation of the
molecule is chosen at random by rotating about this point.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Individual atoms are inserted, unless the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used.  It
specifies a \sphinxstyleemphasis{template\sphinxhyphen{}ID} previously defined using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command, which reads a file that defines the molecule.  The
coordinates, atom types, charges, etc., as well as any bonding and
special neighbor information for the molecule can be specified in the
molecule file.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{molecule::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{molecule}}}} command for details.
The only settings required to be in this file are the coordinates and
types of atoms in the molecule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that fix widom does not use configurational bias MC or any other
kind of sampling of intramolecular degrees of freedom.  Inserted
molecules can have different orientations, but they will all have the
same intramolecular configuration, which was specified in the molecule
command input.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For atoms, inserted particles have the specified atom type.  For
molecules, they use the same atom types as in the template molecule
supplied by the user.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The excess chemical potential mu\_ex is defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mu_{ex} = -kT \ln(<\exp(-(U_{N+1}-U_{N})/{k_B T})>)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, \(T\) is the
user\sphinxhyphen{}specified temperature, \(U_N\) and \(U_{N+1}\) is the
potential energy of the system with \(N\) and \(N+1\) particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option means that the fix calculates the total
potential energy of the entire simulated system, instead of just the
energy of the part that is changed. By default, this option is off, in
which case only partial energies are computed to determine the energy
difference due to the proposed change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option is needed for systems with complicated
potential energy calculations, including the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatics (kspace)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
many\sphinxhyphen{}body pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hybrid pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eam pair styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tail corrections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
need to include potential energy contributions from other fixes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In these cases, LAMMPS will automatically apply the \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy}
keyword and issue a warning message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} keyword is used, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} option also includes
the intramolecular energy of inserted and deleted molecules, whereas
this energy is not included when \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy} is not used. If this is
not desired, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{intra\_energy} keyword can be used to define an amount
of energy that is subtracted from the final energy when a molecule is
inserted, and subtracted from the initial energy when a molecule is
deleted. For molecules that have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero intramolecular energy, this
will ensure roughly the same behavior whether or not the \sphinxstyleemphasis{full\_energy}
option is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some fixes have an associated potential energy. Examples of such fixes
include: {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_efield::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{efield}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gravity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{gravity}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_addforce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{addforce}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_restrain::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restrain}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_wall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{wall fixes}}}}.  For that energy to be included in the
total potential energy of the system (the quantity used when performing
Widom insertions), you MUST enable the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy} option for that fix.  The doc pages for individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} commands specify if this should be done.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{charge} option to insert atoms with a user\sphinxhyphen{}specified point
charge. Note that doing so will cause the system to become non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral.
LAMMPS issues a warning when using long\sphinxhyphen{}range electrostatics (kspace)
with non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral systems. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_group_group::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute group/group}}}} documentation for more details about simulating
non\sphinxhyphen{}neutral systems with kspace on.


\subsection{Restart, fix\_modify, output, run start/stop, minimize info}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:restart-fix-modify-output-run-start-stop-minimize-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix writes the state of the fix to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  This includes information about the random number
generator seed, the next timestep for Widom insertions etc.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command for info on how to
re\sphinxhyphen{}specify a fix in an input script that reads a restart file, so that
the operation of the fix continues in an uninterrupted fashion.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For this to work correctly, the timestep must \sphinxstylestrong{not} be changed
after reading the restart with {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}.  The fix will try to detect it and stop with an
error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify}}}} options are relevant to this
fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix computes a global vector of length 3, which can be accessed by
various {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  The vector values are
the following global cumulative quantities:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average excess chemical potential on each timestep

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
average difference in potential energy on each timestep

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
volume of the insertion region

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values calculated by this fix are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No parameter of this fix can be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start/stop} keywords of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command.  This fix is not invoked during
{\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{energy minimization}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MC package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS was
built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not set “neigh\_modify once yes” or else this fix will never be
called.  Reneighboring is \sphinxstylestrong{required}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix style requires an {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style}}}} with per atom
type masses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Can be run in parallel, but some aspects of the insertion procedure
will not scale well in parallel. Only usable for 3D simulations.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_gcmc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix gcmc}}}}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_atom_swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix atom/swap}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deposit::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deposit}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_evaporate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix evaporate}}}},


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{fix_widom:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are mol = no, intra\_energy = 0.0 and full\_energy =
no, except for the situations where full\_energy is required, as listed
above.
