\section{compute ackland/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:compute-ackland-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ackland}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ackland/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{legacy}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{legacy} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = use (\sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}) or do not use (\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}) legacy Ackland algorithm implementation
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ackland}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ackland}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{legacy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Defines a computation that calculates the local lattice structure
according to the formulation given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:ackland}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ackland)}}}}.
Historically, LAMMPS had two, slightly different implementations of
the algorithm from the paper. With the \sphinxstyleemphasis{legacy} keyword, it is
possible to switch between the pre\sphinxhyphen{}2015 (\sphinxstyleemphasis{legacy yes}) and post\sphinxhyphen{}2015
implementation (\sphinxstyleemphasis{legacy no}). The post\sphinxhyphen{}2015 variant is the default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_centro_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{centro\sphinxhyphen{}symmetry parameter}}}} this method is stable against
temperature boost, because it is based not on the distance between
particles but the angles.  Therefore statistical fluctuations are
averaged out a little more.  A comparison with the Common Neighbor
Analysis metric is made in the paper.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is a number which is mapped to the following different
lattice structures:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0 = UNKNOWN

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 = BCC

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2 = FCC

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3 = HCP

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
4 = ICO

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The neighbor list needed to compute this quantity is constructed each
time the calculation is performed (i.e. each time a snapshot of atoms
is dumped).  Thus it can be inefficient to compute/dump this quantity
too frequently or to have multiple compute/dump commands, each of
which computes this quantity.\sphinxhyphen{}


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector, which can be accessed by
any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from a compute as input.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of
LAMMPS output options.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}COMPUTE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector values will be unitless since they are the
integers defined above.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_centro_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute centro/atom}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{legacy} defaults to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{compute adf command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:compute-adf-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_adf::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nbin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{itype1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{jtype1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ktype1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rjinner1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rjouter1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rkinner1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rkouter1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
adf = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nbin = number of ADF bins

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
itypeN = central atom type for Nth ADF histogram (see asterisk form below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
jtypeN = J atom type for Nth ADF histogram (see asterisk form below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ktypeN = K atom type for Nth ADF histogram (see asterisk form below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RjinnerN = inner radius of J atom shell for Nth ADF histogram (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RjouterN = outer radius of J atom shell for Nth ADF histogram (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RkinnerN = inner radius of K atom shell for Nth ADF histogram (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RkouterN = outer radius of K atom shell for Nth ADF histogram (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or one keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ordinate}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ordinate} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{degree} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{radian} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine}
  Choose the ordinate parameter for the histogram
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{32}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                       }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{32}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{32}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates one or more angular distribution functions
(ADF) for a group of particles.  Each ADF is calculated in histogram form
by measuring the angle formed by a central atom and two neighbor atoms and
binning these angles into \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nbin} bins.
Only neighbors for which \sphinxstyleemphasis{Rinner} \textless{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{R} \textless{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Router} are counted, where
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Rinner} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Router} are specified separately for the first and second
neighbor atom in each requested ADF.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have a bonded system, then the settings of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command can remove pairwise
interactions between atoms in the same bond, angle, or dihedral.  This
is the default setting for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}}
command, and means those pairwise interactions do not appear in the
neighbor list.  Because this fix uses a neighbor list, it also means
those pairs will not be included in the ADF. This does not apply when
using long\sphinxhyphen{}range coulomb interactions (\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/msm},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/wolf} or similar.  One way to get around this would be to set
special\_bond scaling factors to very tiny numbers that are not exactly
zero (e.g. 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}50). Another workaround is to write a dump file, and
use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command to compute the ADF for snapshots in
the dump file.  The rerun script can use a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command that includes all pairs in
the neighbor list.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you request any outer cutoff \sphinxstyleemphasis{Router} \textgreater{} force cutoff, or if no
pair style is defined,  e.g. the {\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command is being used to
post\sphinxhyphen{}process a dump file of snapshots you must ensure ghost atom information
out to the largest value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Router} + \sphinxstyleemphasis{skin} is communicated, via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}} command, else the ADF computation
cannot be performed, and LAMMPS will give an error message.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{skin} value
is what is specified with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN},\sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN},\sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN} settings can be specified in one of two
ways.  An explicit numeric value can be used, as in the first example
above.  Or a wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk can be used to specify a range of atom
types as in the second example above.
This takes the form “*” or “*n” or “n*” or “m*n”.  If N = the
number of atom types, then an asterisk with no numeric values means
all types from 1 to N.  A leading asterisk means all types from 1 to n
(inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from n to N
(inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN} are single values, as in the first example
above, this means that the ADF is computed where atoms of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN}
are the central atom, and neighbor atoms of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN}
are forming the angle.  If any of \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN}
represent a range of values via
the wild\sphinxhyphen{}card asterisk, as in the second example above, this means that the
ADF is computed where atoms of any of the range of types represented
by \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN} are the central atom, and the angle is formed by two neighbors,
one neighbor in the range of types represented by \sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN} and another neighbor
in the range of types represented by \sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If no \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN} settings are specified, then
LAMMPS will generate a single ADF for all atoms in the group.
The inner cutoff is set to zero and the outer cutoff is set
to the force cutoff. If no pair\_style is specified, there is no
force cutoff and LAMMPS will give an error message. Note that
in most cases, generating an ADF for all atoms is not a good thing.
Such an ADF is both uninformative and
extremely expensive to compute.  For example, with liquid water
with a 10 A force cutoff, there are 80,000 angles per atom.
In addition, most of the interesting angular structure occurs for
neighbors that are the closest to the central atom, involving
just a few dozen angles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Angles for each ADF are generated by double\sphinxhyphen{}looping over the list of
neighbors of each central atom I,
just as they would be in the force calculation for
a three\sphinxhyphen{}body potential such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber}}}}.
The angle formed by central atom I and neighbor atoms J and K is included in an
ADF if the following criteria are met:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atoms I,J,K are all in the specified compute group

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the distance between atoms I,J is between Rjinner and Rjouter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the distance between atoms I,K is between Rkinner and Rkouter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the type of the I atom matches itypeN (one or a range of types)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
atoms I,J,K are distinct

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the type of the J atom matches jtypeN (one or a range of types)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the type of the K atom matches ktypeN (one or a range of types)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each unique angle satisfying the above criteria is counted only once, regardless
of whether either or both of the neighbor atoms making up the
angle appear in both the J and K lists.
It is OK if a particular angle is included in more than
one individual histogram, due to the way the \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN}
arguments are specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first ADF value for a bin is calculated from the histogram count by
dividing by the total number of triples satisfying the criteria,
so that the integral of the ADF w.r.t. angle is 1, i.e. the ADF
is a probability density function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second ADF value is reported as a cumulative sum of
all bins up to the current bins, averaged
over atoms of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN}. It represents the
number of angles per central atom with angle less
than or equal to the angle of the current bin,
analogous to the coordination
number radial distribution function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ordinate} optional keyword determines
whether the bins are of uniform angular size from zero
to 180 (\sphinxstyleemphasis{degree}), zero to Pi (\sphinxstyleemphasis{radian}), or the
cosine of the angle uniform in the range {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1,1{]} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine}).
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine} has the advantage of eliminating the \sphinxstyleemphasis{acos()} function
call, which speeds up the compute by 2\sphinxhyphen{}3x, and it is also preferred
on physical grounds, because the for uniformly distributed particles
in 3D, the angular probability density w.r.t dtheta is
sin(theta)/2, while for d(cos(theta)), it is 1/2,
Regardless of which ordinate is chosen, the first column of ADF
values is normalized w.r.t. the range of that ordinate, so that
the integral is 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest way to output the results of the compute adf calculation
to a file is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}} command, for
example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myADF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{32}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myADF[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.adf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global array with the number of rows =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nbins} and the number of columns = \(1 + 2 \times\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ntriples}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ntriples}
is the number of I,J,K triples specified.  The first column has the bin
coordinate (angle\sphinxhyphen{}related ordinate at midpoint of bin). Each subsequent column has
the two ADF values for a specific set of (\sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN},\sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN},\sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN})
interactions, as described above.  These values can be used
by any command that uses a global values from a compute as input.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of
LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The array values calculated by this compute are all “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first column of array values is the angle\sphinxhyphen{}related ordinate, either
the angle in degrees or radians, or the cosine of the angle.  Each
subsequent pair of columns gives the first and second kinds of ADF
for a specific set of (\sphinxstyleemphasis{itypeN},\sphinxstyleemphasis{jtypeN},\sphinxstyleemphasis{ktypeN}). The values
in the first ADF column are normalized numbers \(\ge 0.0\),
whose integral w.r.t. the ordinate is 1,
i.e. the first ADF is a normalized probability distribution.
The values in the second ADF column are also numbers \(\ge 0.0\).
They are the cumulative density distribution of angles per atom.
By definition, this ADF is monotonically increasing from zero to
a maximum value equal to the average total number of
angles per atom satisfying the ADF criteria.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}COMPUTE package.  It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the ADF is not computed for distances longer than the
largest force cutoff, since the neighbor list creation will only contain
pairs up to that distance (plus neighbor list skin).  If you use outer
cutoffs larger than that, you must use {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor style ‘bin’ or
‘nsq’}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want an ADF for a larger outer cutoff, you can also use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command to post\sphinxhyphen{}process a dump file, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair
style zero}}}} and set the force cutoff to be larger in the
rerun script.  Note that in the rerun context, the force cutoff is
arbitrary and with pair style zero you are not computing any forces, and
since you are not running dynamics you are not changing the model that
generated the trajectory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ADF is not computed for neighbors outside the force cutoff,
since processors (in parallel) don’t know about atom coordinates for
atoms further away than that distance.  If you want an ADF for larger
distances, you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command to post\sphinxhyphen{}process
a dump file and set the cutoff for the potential to be longer in the
rerun script.  Note that in the rerun context, the force cutoff is
arbitrary, since you are not running dynamics and thus are not changing
your model.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_rdf::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute rdf}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_adf:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword default is ordinate = degree.

\sphinxstepscope

\section{compute angle command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:compute-angle-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_angle::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
angle = style name of this compute command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that extracts the angle energy calculated by each of the
angle sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles used in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style hybrid}}}} command.
These values are made accessible for output or further processing by other
commands.  The group specified for this command is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is useful when using {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style hybrid}}}} if
you want to know the portion of the total energy contributed by one or more of
the hybrid sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global vector of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is the number
of sub\_styles defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style hybrid}}}} command,
which can be accessed by indices 1 through \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}.  These values can be used by
any command that uses global scalar or vector values from a compute as input.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values are “extensive” and will be in energy
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pe}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pair::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pair}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{compute angle/local command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:compute-angle-local-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
angle/local = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more values may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{eng} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} = tabulate angles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{eng} = tabulate angle energies
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} = equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable with name (see below)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/args pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{set}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{set} args = theta name
  theta = only currently allowed arg
  name = name of variable to set with theta
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eng}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}cos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates properties of individual angle
interactions.  The number of datums generated, aggregated across all
processors, equals the number of angles in the system, modified by the
group parameter as explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} is the angle for the three atoms in the interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{eng} is the interaction energy for the angle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} can be used together with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} keyword to
compute a user\sphinxhyphen{}specified function of the angle theta.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{name}
specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} value is the name of an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} which should evaluate a formula based on a
variable which will store the angle theta.  This other variable must
be an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} defined in the input
script; its initial numeric value can be anything.  It must be an
internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, because this command resets its value
directly.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} keyword is used to identify the name of this
other variable associated with theta.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the value of theta for each angle which stored in the
internal variable is in radians, not degrees.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, these commands can be added to the bench/in.rhodo
script to compute the cosine and cosine\sphinxhyphen{}squared of every angle in the
system and output the statistics in various ways:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{v\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cossq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{v\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{v\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{n+nv}{)}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atype}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eng}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}cos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}cossq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reduce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}3[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.histo}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command will output the potential energy
(\(\phi\)), the angle (\(\theta\)), \(\cos(\theta\)), and
\(\cos^2(\theta)\) for every angle \(\theta\) in the system.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command will print the
average of those quantities via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}}
command with thermo output.  And the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}}
command will histogram the \(\cos(\theta)\) values and write them to a
file.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The local data stored by this command is generated by looping over all
the atoms owned on a processor and their angles.  An angle will only
be included if all three atoms in the angle are in the specified compute
group.  Any angles that have been broken (see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style}}}} command) by setting their angle type to
0 are not included.  Angles that have been turned off (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} commands) by
setting their angle type negative are written into the file, but their
energy will be 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that as atoms migrate from processor to processor, there will be
no consistent ordering of the entries within the local vector or array
from one timestep to the next.  The only consistency that is
guaranteed is that the ordering on a particular timestep will be the
same for local vectors or arrays generated by other compute commands.
For example, angle output from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/local}}}} command can be combined
with data from this command and output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}}
command in a consistent way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of how to do this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom3}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{theta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eng}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[4]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[2]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a local vector or local array depending on the
number of values.  The length of the vector or number of rows in the
array is the number of angles.  If a single value is specified, a
local vector is produced.  If two or more values are specified, a
local array is produced where the number of columns = the number of
values.  The vector or array can be accessed by any command that uses
local values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output for \sphinxstyleemphasis{theta} will be in degrees.  The output for \sphinxstyleemphasis{eng} will
be in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angle_local:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{compute angmom/chunk@\spxentry{compute angmom/chunk}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute angmom/chunk command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:compute-angmom-chunk-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunkID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
angmom/chunk = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chunkID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molchunk}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the angular momentum of multiple
chunks of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LAMMPS, chunks are collections of atoms defined by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command, which assigns each atom
to a single chunk (or no chunk).  The ID for this command is specified
as chunkID.  For example, a single chunk could be the atoms in a
molecule or atoms in a spatial bin.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto chunk}}}}
doc pages for details of how chunks can be defined and examples of how
they can be used to measure properties of a system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates the 3 components of the angular momentum
vector for each chunk, due to the velocity/momentum of the individual
atoms in the chunk around the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass of the chunk.  The
calculation includes all effects due to atoms passing through periodic
boundaries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that only atoms in the specified group contribute to the
calculation.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command
defines its own group; atoms will have a chunk ID = 0 if they are not
in that group, signifying they are not assigned to a chunk, and will
thus also not contribute to this calculation.  You can specify the
“all” group for this command if you simply want to include atoms with
non\sphinxhyphen{}zero chunk IDs.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The coordinates of an atom contribute to the chunk’s angular
momentum in “unwrapped” form, by using the image flags associated with
each atom.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command for a discussion
of “unwrapped” coordinates.  See the Atoms section of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command for a discussion of image flags and
how they are set for each atom.  You can reset the image flags
(e.g. to 0) before invoking this compute by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set image}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest way to output the results of the compute angmom/chunk
calculation to a file is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}}
command, for example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molecule}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myChunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{angmom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc1}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myChunk[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global array where the number of rows = the
number of chunks \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nchunk} as calculated by the specified {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.  The number of columns = 3 for the three
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}) components of the angular momentum for each chunk.
These values can be accessed by any command that uses global array
values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The array values are “intensive”.  The array values will be in
mass\sphinxhyphen{}velocity\sphinxhyphen{}distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable angmom() function}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_angmom_chunk:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{compute ave/sphere/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:compute-ave-sphere-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{ave/sphere/atom/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ave/sphere/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} value = distance cutoff
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{comm\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 7Jan2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the local mass density and
temperature for each atom based on its neighbors inside a spherical
cutoff.  If an atom has \(M\) neighbors, then its local mass density is
calculated as the sum of its mass and its \(M\) neighbor masses, divided
by the volume of the cutoff sphere (or circle in 2d).  The local
temperature of the atom is calculated as the temperature of the
collection of \(M+1\) atoms, after subtracting the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity
of the \(M+1\) atoms from each of the \(M+1\) atom’s velocities.  This
is effectively the thermal velocity of the neighborhood of the central
atom, similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_com::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/com}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} defines the distance cutoff used when
searching for neighbors. The default value is the cutoff specified by
the pair style. If no pair style is defined, then a cutoff must be
defined using this keyword. If the specified cutoff is larger than
that of the pair\_style plus neighbor skin (or no pair style is
defined), the \sphinxstyleemphasis{comm\_modify cutoff} option must also be set to match
that of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The neighbor list needed to compute this quantity is constructed each
time the calculation is performed (i.e. each time a snapshot of atoms
is dumped).  Thus it can be inefficient to compute/dump this quantity
too frequently.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have a bonded system, then the settings of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command can remove pairwise
interactions between atoms in the same bond, angle, or dihedral.
This is the default setting for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command, and means those pairwise interactions do
not appear in the neighbor list.  Because this compute uses the
neighbor list, it also means those pairs will not be included in
the order parameter.  This difficulty can be circumvented by
writing a dump file, and using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command to
compute the order parameter for snapshots in the dump file.  The
rerun script can use a {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command
that includes all pairs in the neighbor list.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with two columns: mass
density in density {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} and temperature in temperature
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These values can be accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values
from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}}
doc page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}COMPUTE package.  It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute requires {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor styles ‘bin’ or ‘nsq’}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ave_sphere_atom:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} = pair style cutoff.

\section{compute basal/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:compute-basal-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{basal}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
basal/atom = style name of this compute command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{basal}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Defines a computation that calculates the hexagonal close\sphinxhyphen{}packed “c”
lattice vector for each atom in the group.  It does this by
calculating the normal unit vector to the basal plane for each atom.
The results enable efficient identification and characterization of
twins and grains in hexagonal close\sphinxhyphen{}packed structures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output of the compute is thus the 3 components of a unit vector
associated with each atom.  The components are set to 0.0 for
atoms not in the group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Details of the calculation are given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:barrett}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Barrett)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The neighbor list needed to compute this quantity is constructed each
time the calculation is performed (i.e. each time a snapshot of atoms
is dumped).  Thus it can be inefficient to compute/dump this quantity
too frequently or to have multiple compute/dump commands, each of
which computes this quantity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An example input script that uses this compute is provided
in examples/PACKAGES/basal.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with three columns, which can be
accessed by indices 1\textendash{}3 by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from
a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector values are unitless since the three columns represent
components of a unit vector.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}COMPUTE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output of this compute will be meaningless unless the atoms are on
(or near) hcp lattice sites, since the calculation assumes a
well\sphinxhyphen{}defined basal plane.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_centro_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute centro/atom}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_ackland_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute ackland/atom}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{compute_basal_atom:barrett}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{compute body/local@\spxentry{compute body/local}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute body/local command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local:compute-body-local-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
body/local = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keywords may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{integer}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{id} = atom ID of the body particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = atom type of the body particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{integer} = 1,2,3,etc = index of fields defined by body style
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates properties of individual body
sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles.  The number of data generated, aggregated across all
processors, equals the number of body sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles plus the number of
non\sphinxhyphen{}body particles in the system, modified by the group parameter as
explained below.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto body}}}} page for
more details on using body particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The local data stored by this command is generated by looping over all
the atoms.  An atom will only be included if it is in the group.  If
the atom is a body particle, then its \(N\) sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles will be looped
over, and it will contribute \(N\) data to the count of data.  If it
is not a body particle, it will contribute 1 datum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For both body particles and non\sphinxhyphen{}body particles, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} keyword
will store the ID of the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For both body particles and non\sphinxhyphen{}body particles, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} keyword
will store the type of the particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{integer} keywords mean different things for body and non\sphinxhyphen{}body
particles.  If the atom is not a body particle, only its \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}
coordinates can be referenced, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{integer} keywords 1,2,3.
Note that this means that if you want to access more fields than this
for body particles, then you cannot include non\sphinxhyphen{}body particles in the
group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a body particle, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{integer} keywords refer to fields calculated
by the body style for each sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle.  The body style, as specified
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style body}}}}, determines how many fields
exist and what they are.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_body::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_body}}}} doc
page for details of the different styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of how to output body information using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command with this compute.  If fields 1, 2, and 3 for the
body sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles are (\sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}) coordinates, then the dump file will be
formatted similar to the output of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump atom or custom}}}}
command.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}

\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_body_local:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a local vector or local array depending on the
number of keywords.  The length of the vector or number of rows in the
array is the number of data as described above.  If a single keyword
is specified, a local vector is produced.  If two or more keywords are
specified, a local array is produced where the number of columns = the
number of keywords.  The vector or array can be accessed by any
command that uses local values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

The {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} for output values depend on the body style.

\section{compute bond command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond:compute-bond-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_bond:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_bond::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond:syntax}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bond = style name of this compute command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that extracts the bond energy calculated by each
of the bond sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles used in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style hybrid}}}} command.  These values are made accessible
for output or further processing by other commands.  The group
specified for this command is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is useful when using {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style hybrid}}}}
if you want to know the portion of the total energy contributed by one
or more of the hybrid sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global vector of length \(N\), where \(N\)
is the number of sub\_styles defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style hybrid}}}} command,
which can be accessed by indices 1 through \(N\).
These values can be used by any command that uses global scalar or
vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector values are “extensive” and will be in energy
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\section{compute bond/local command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local:compute-bond-local-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bond/local = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more values may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{engpot} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{force} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{engvib} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{engrot} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{engtrans} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{velvib} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bN}

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} = bond distance
\sphinxstyleemphasis{engpot} = bond potential energy
\sphinxstyleemphasis{force} = bond force

\sphinxstyleemphasis{dx},\sphinxstyleemphasis{dy},\sphinxstyleemphasis{dz} = components of pairwise distance
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fx},\sphinxstyleemphasis{fy},\sphinxstyleemphasis{fz} = components of bond force
\sphinxstyleemphasis{engvib} = bond kinetic energy of vibration
\sphinxstyleemphasis{engrot} = bond kinetic energy of rotation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{engtrans} = bond kinetic energy of translation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} = magnitude of bond angular velocity
\sphinxstyleemphasis{velvib} = vibrational velocity along the bond length
\sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} = equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable with name (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bN} = bond style specific quantities for allowed N values
\end{sphinxalltt}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/args pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{set}

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{set} args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} name
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} = only currently allowed arg
  name = name of variable to set with distance (dist)
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{engpot}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{engpot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{force}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b2}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}distsq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates properties of individual bond
interactions.  The number of datums generated, aggregated across all
processors, equals the number of bonds in the system, modified by the
group parameter as explained below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All these properties are computed for the pair of atoms in a bond,
whether the two atoms represent a simple diatomic molecule, or are part
of some larger molecule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} is the current length of the bond.
The values \sphinxstyleemphasis{dx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dz} are the xyz components of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{distance} between the pair of atoms. This value is always the
distance from the atom of lower to the one with the higher id.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{engpot} is the potential energy for the bond,
based on the current separation of the pair of atoms in the bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{force} is the magnitude of the force acting between the
pair of atoms in the bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz} are the xyz components of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{force} between the pair of atoms in the bond. For bond styles that apply
non\sphinxhyphen{}central forces, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style bpm/rotational}}}}, these values only include the \((x,y,z)\)
components of the normal force component.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The remaining properties are all computed for motion of the two atoms
relative to the center of mass (COM) velocity of the two atoms in the
bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{engvib} is the vibrational kinetic energy of the two atoms
in the bond, which is simply \(\frac12 m_1 v_1^2 + \frac12 m_2 v_2^2,\)
where \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) are the magnitude of the velocity of the two
atoms along the bond direction, after the COM velocity has been subtracted from
each.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{engrot} is the rotational kinetic energy of the two atoms
in the bond, which is simply \(\frac12 m_1 v_1^2 + \frac12 m_2 v_2^2,\)
where \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) are the magnitude of the velocity of the two
atoms perpendicular to the bond direction, after the COM velocity has been
subtracted from each.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{engtrans} is the translational kinetic energy associated
with the motion of the COM of the system itself, namely \(\frac12(m_1+m_2)
V_{\mathrm{cm}}^2\), where \sphinxtitleref{Vcm} = magnitude of the velocity of the COM.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these three kinetic energy terms are simply a partitioning of
the summed kinetic energy of the two atoms themselves.  That is, the total
kinetic energy is
\(\frac12 m_1 v_1^2 + \frac12 m_2 v_2^2\) = engvib + engrot + engtrans,
where \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) are the magnitude of the velocities of the
two atoms, without any adjustment for the COM velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} is the magnitude of the angular velocity of the
two atoms around their COM position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{velvib} is the magnitude of the relative velocity of the
two atoms in the bond towards each other.  A negative value means the
two atoms are moving toward each other; a positive value means they are
moving apart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} can be used together with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} keyword to
compute a user\sphinxhyphen{}specified function of the bond distance.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{name}
specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} value is the name of an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{equal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} which should evaluate a formula based on a
variable which will store the bond distance.  This other variable must
be an {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} defined in the input
script; its initial numeric value can be anything.  It must be an
internal\sphinxhyphen{}style variable, because this command resets its value
directly.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{set} keyword is used to identify the name of this
other variable associated with theta.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, these commands can be added to the bench/in.rhodo
script to compute the length\(^2\) of every bond in the system and
output the statistics in various ways:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{internal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dsq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}d}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}d}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{btype}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{engpot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}dsq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reduce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}3[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{histo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.histo}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command will output the energy, length,
and length\(^2\) for every bond in the system.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command will print the average of
those quantities via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command
with thermo output, and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}}
command will histogram the length\(^2\) values and write them to a file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A bond style may define additional bond quantities which can be
accessed as \sphinxstyleemphasis{b1} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{bN}, where N is defined by the bond style.  Most
bond styles do not define any additional quantities, so N = 0.  An
example of ones that do are the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bpm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{BPM bond styles}}}}
which store the reference state between two particles. See
individual bond styles for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using \sphinxstyleemphasis{bN} with bond style \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid}, the output will be the Nth
quantity from the sub\sphinxhyphen{}style that computes the bonded interaction
(based on bond type).  If that sub\sphinxhyphen{}style does not define a \sphinxstyleemphasis{bN},
the output will be 0.0.  The maximum allowed N is the maximum number
of quantities provided by any sub\sphinxhyphen{}style.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The local data stored by this command is generated by looping over all
the atoms owned on a processor and their bonds.  A bond will only be
included if both atoms in the bond are in the specified compute group.
Any bonds that have been broken (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style}}}}
command) by setting their bond type to 0 are not included.  Bonds that
have been turned off (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} commands) by setting their bond type
negative are written into the file, but their energy will be 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that as atoms migrate from processor to processor, there will be
no consistent ordering of the entries within the local vector or array
from one timestep to the next.  The only consistency that is
guaranteed is that the ordering on a particular timestep will be the
same for local vectors or arrays generated by other compute commands.
For example, bond output from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/local}}}} command can be combined
with data from this command and output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}}
command in a consistent way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of how to do this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{btype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom2}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{engpot}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_bond_local:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a local vector or local array depending on the
number of values.  The length of the vector or number of rows in the
array is the number of bonds.  If a single value is specified, a local
vector is produced.  If two or more values are specified, a local
array is produced where the number of columns = the number of values.
The vector or array can be accessed by any command that uses local
values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output for \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist} will be in distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}. The
output for \sphinxstyleemphasis{velvib} will be in velocity {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}. The output
for \sphinxstyleemphasis{omega} will be in velocity/distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}. The
output for \sphinxstyleemphasis{engtrans}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{engvib}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{engrot}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{engpot} will be in
energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}. The output for \sphinxstyleemphasis{force} will be in force
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\section{compute born/matrix command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_born_matrix:compute-born-matrix-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_born_matrix:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_born_matrix::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_born_matrix:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{born}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{matrix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords or keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}

  \sphinxstyleemphasis{numdiff} values = delta virial\sphinxhyphen{}ID
    delta = magnitude of strain (dimensionless)
    virial\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of pressure compute for virial (string)
    (\sphinxstyleemphasis{numdiff} cannot be used with any other keyword)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} = compute pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise contributions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} = compute bonding contributions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} = compute angle contributions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} = compute dihedral contributions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{improper} = compute improper contributions

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_born_matrix:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{born}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{matrix}
