\section{compute pressure command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:compute-pressure-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pressure = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of compute that calculates temperature, can be NULL if not needed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{improper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair/hybrid}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermo\PYGZus{}temp}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the pressure of the entire system
of atoms.  The specified group must be “all”.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}} command if you want per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
pressure (stress).  These per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values could be summed for a group
of atoms via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pressure is computed by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}P = \frac{N k_B T}{V} + \frac{1}{V d}\sum_{i=1}^{N'} \vec r_i \cdot \vec f_i\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is the number of atoms in the system (see discussion of DOF
below), \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, \(T\) is the
temperature, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d} is the dimensionality of the system (2 for 2d, 3 for
3d), and \sphinxstyleemphasis{V} is the system volume (or area in 2d).  The second term is
the virial, equal to \(-dU/dV\), computed for all pairwise as well
as 2\sphinxhyphen{}body, 3\sphinxhyphen{}body, 4\sphinxhyphen{}body, many\sphinxhyphen{}body, and long\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions, where
\(\vec r_i\) and \(\vec f_i\) are the position and force vector
of atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i}, and the dot indicates the dot product (scalar product).
This is computed in parallel for each subdomain and then summed over
all parallel processes. Thus \(N'\) necessarily includes atoms from
neighboring subdomains (so\sphinxhyphen{}called ghost atoms) and the position and
force vectors of ghost atoms are thus included in the summation.  Only
when running in serial and without periodic boundary conditions is
\(N' = N\) the number of atoms in the system.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Fixes}}}}
that impose constraints (e.g., the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} command)
may also contribute to the virial term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric pressure tensor, stored as a 6\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also
calculated by this compute.  The six components of the vector are
ordered \(xx,\) \(yy,\) \(zz,\) \(xy,\) \(xz,\)
\(yz.\) The equation for the \((I,J)\) components (where
\(I\) and \(J\) are \(x\), \(y\), or \(z\)) is
similar to the above formula, except that the first term uses
components related to the kinetic energy tensor and the second term
uses components of the virial tensor:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}P_{IJ} = \frac{1}{V}\sum_{k=1}^{N} m_k v_{k_I} v_{k_J} +
\frac{1}{V}\sum_{k=1}^{N'} r_{k_I} f_{k_J}.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If no extra keywords are listed, the entire equations above are
calculated.  This includes a kinetic energy (temperature) term and the
virial as the sum of pair, bond, angle, dihedral, improper, kspace
(long\sphinxhyphen{}range), and fix contributions to the force on each atom.  If any
extra keywords are listed, then only those components are summed to
compute temperature or ke and/or the virial.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial} keyword means
include all terms except the kinetic energy \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair/hybrid} keyword means to only include contribution
from a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style in a \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/overlay} pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Details of how LAMMPS computes the virial efficiently for the entire
system, including for many\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials and accounting for the
effects of periodic boundary conditions are discussed in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure:thompson1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Thompson)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature and kinetic energy tensor are not calculated by this
compute, but rather by the temperature compute specified with the
command.  See the doc pages for individual compute temp variants for an
explanation of how they calculate temperature and a symmetric tensor
(6\sphinxhyphen{}element vector) whose components are twice that of the traditional KE
tensor.  That tensor is what appears in the pressure tensor formula
above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the kinetic energy is not included in the pressure, than the
temperature compute is not used and can be specified as NULL.  Normally
the temperature compute used by compute pressure should calculate the
temperature of all atoms for consistency with the virial term, but any
compute style that calculates temperature can be used (e.g., one that
excludes frozen atoms or other degrees of freedom).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if desired the specified temperature compute can be one that
subtracts off a bias to calculate a temperature using only the thermal
velocity of the atoms (e.g., by subtracting a background streaming
velocity).  See the doc pages for individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute commands}}}} to determine which ones include a bias.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note that the \(N\) in the first formula above is really
degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom divided by \(d\) = dimensionality, where the
DOF value is calculated by the temperature compute.  See the various
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temperature}}}} styles for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A compute of this style with the ID of thermo\_press is created when
LAMMPS starts up, as if this command were in the input script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{thermo\PYGZus{}press}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pressure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermo\PYGZus{}temp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where thermo\_temp is the ID of a similarly defined compute of style
“temp”.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command for more details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the pressure) and a global
vector of length 6 (pressure tensor), which can be accessed by indices
1\textendash{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses global scalar
or vector values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering of values in the symmetric pressure tensor is as follows:
\(p_{xx},\) \(p_{yy},\) \(p_{zz},\) \(p_{xy},\)
\(p_{xz},\) \(p_{yz}.\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar and vector values calculated by this compute are “intensive”.
The scalar and vector values will be in pressure {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}},

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure_alchemy:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a compute style that makes the “mixed” system pressure available
for a system that uses the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_alchemy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix alchemy}}}} command to
transform one topology to another.  This can be used in combination with
either {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify press}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify
press}}}} to output and access a pressure consistent with the
simulated combined two topology system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual pressure is determined with {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}} commands that are internally used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_alchemy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
alchemy}}}} for each topology individually and then combined.
This command just extracts the information from the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/alchemy}} folder contains an example input for this command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto
output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\section{compute pressure/uef command}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of compute that calculates temperature, can be NULL if not needed

\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords may be appended

keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ke} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dihedral} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{improper} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kspace} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{virial}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure_uef:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is used to compute the pressure tensor in
the reference frame of the applied flow field when
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/uef}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/uef}}}} is used.
It is not necessary to use this command to compute the scalar
value of the pressure. A {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}
may be used for that purpose.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keywords and output information are documented in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_pressure}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_pressure_uef:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the UEF package. It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page
for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can only be used when {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/uef}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/uef}}}} is active.

will be accurate only when the compute specified by \sphinxstyleemphasis{temp\sphinxhyphen{}ID} is a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/uef}}}}.

\section{compute property/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_atom:compute-property-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_atom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
property/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
input = one or more atom attributes

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = id, mol, proc, type, mass,
                      x, y, z, xs, ys, zs, xu, yu, zu, ix, iy, iz,
                      vx, vy, vz, fx, fy, fz,
                      q, mux, muy, muz, mu,
                      spx, spy, spz, sp, fmx, fmy, fmz,
                      nbonds,
                      radius, diameter, omegax, omegay, omegaz,
                      temperature, heatflow,
                      angmomx, angmomy, angmomz,
                      shapex, shapey, shapez,
                      quatw, quati, quatj, quatk, tqx, tqy, tqz,
                      end1x, end1y, end1z, end2x, end2y, end2z,
                      corner1x, corner1y, corner1z,
                      corner2x, corner2y, corner2z,
                      corner3x, corner3y, corner3z,
                      i\PYGZus{}name, d\PYGZus{}name, i2\PYGZus{}name[I], d2\PYGZus{}name[I],
                      vfrac, s0, espin, eradius, ervel, erforce,
                      rho, drho, e, de, cv, buckling,
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{id} = atom ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mol} = molecule ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{proc} = ID of processor that owns atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = atom type
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mass} = atom mass
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} = unscaled atom coordinates
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xs,ys,zs} = scaled atom coordinates
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xu,yu,zu} = unwrapped atom coordinates
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ix,iy,iz} = box image that the atom is in
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vx,vy,vz} = atom velocities
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fx,fy,fz} = forces on atoms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{q} = atom charge
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mux,muy,muz} = orientation of dipole moment of atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} = magnitude of dipole moment of atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spx, spy, spz} = direction of the atomic magnetic spin
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sp} = magintude of atomic magnetic spin moment
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fmx, fmy, fmz} = magnetic force
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nbonds} = number of bonds assigned to an atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{radius,diameter} = radius,diameter of spherical particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{omegax,omegay,omegaz} = angular velocity of spherical particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{temperature} = internal temperature of spherical particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{heatflow} = internal heat flow of spherical particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angmomx,angmomy,angmomz} = angular momentum of aspherical particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shapex,shapey,shapez} = 3 diameters of aspherical particle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quatw,quati,quatj,quatk} = quaternion components for aspherical or body particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tqx,tqy,tqz} = torque on finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{end12x, end12y, end12z} = end points of line segment
\sphinxstyleemphasis{corner123x, corner123y, corner123z} = corner points of triangle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name} = custom integer vector with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name} = custom floating point vector with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name{[}I{]}} = Ith column of custom integer array with name
\sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name{[}I{]}} = Ith column of custom floating\sphinxhyphen{}point array with name
\end{sphinxalltt}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
PERI package per\PYGZhy{}atom properties:
vfrac = volume fraction
s0 = max stretch of any bond a particle is part of
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
EFF and AWPMD package per\PYGZhy{}atom properties:
espin = electron spin
eradius = electron radius
ervel = electron radial velocity
erforce = electron radial force
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
SPH package per\PYGZhy{}atom properties:
rho = density of SPH particles
drho = change in density
e = energy
de = change in thermal energy
cv = heat capacity
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mux}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iz}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spz}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i\PYGZus{}myFlag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}Sxyz[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d\PYGZus{}Sxyz[3]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that simply stores atom attributes for each atom
in the group.  This is useful so that the values can be used by other
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} that take computes as inputs.
See for example, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
ave/atom}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_histo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/histo}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The list of possible attributes is essentially the same as that used
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command, which describes their
meaning, with some additional quantities that are only defined for
certain {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom styles}}}}.  The goal of this augmented
list gives an input script access to any per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity stored by
LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values are stored in a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector or array as discussed
below.  Zeroes are stored for atoms not in the specified group or for
quantities that are not defined for a particular particle in the group
(e.g., \sphinxstyleemphasis{shapex} if the particle is not an ellipsoid).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Attributes \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name} refer to custom
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom integer and floating\sphinxhyphen{}point vectors or arrays that have been
added via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}} command.
When that command is used specific names are given to each attribute
which are the “name” portion of these attributes.  For arrays
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name}, the column of the array must also be included
following the name in brackets (e.g., d2\_xyz{[}2{]} or i2\_mySpin{[}3{]}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The additional quantities only accessible via this command, and not
directly via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command, are as follows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nbonds} is available for all molecular atom styles and refers to the
number of explicit bonds assigned to an atom.  Note that if the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton bond}}}} command is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{on}, which is the
default, then every bond in the system is assigned to only one of the
two atoms in the bond.  Thus a bond between atoms \(I\) and \(J\) may
be tallied for either atom \(I\) or atom \(J\).
If {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton bond off}}}} is set, it will be tallied with both atom
\(I\) and atom \(J\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quantities \sphinxstyleemphasis{shapex}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{shapey}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{shapez} are defined for ellipsoidal
particles and define the 3d shape of each particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quantities \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatw}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{quati}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatj}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{quatk} are defined for
ellipsoidal particles and body particles and store the 4\sphinxhyphen{}vector quaternion
representing the orientation of each particle.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}}
command for an explanation of the quaternion vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{End1x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{end1y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{end1z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{end2x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{end2y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{end2z}, are defined for line
segment particles and define the end points of each line segment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Corner1x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner1y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner1z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner2x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner2y},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{corner2z}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner3x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner3y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{corner3z}, are defined for
triangular particles and define the corner points of each triangle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition, the various per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities listed above for specific
packages are only accessible by this command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 15Sep2022: }The \sphinxstyleemphasis{espin} property was previously called \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin}.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array depending
on the number of input values.  If a single input is specified, a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector is produced.  If two or more inputs are specified, a
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array is produced where the number of columns = the number of
inputs.  The vector or array can be accessed by any command that uses
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array values will be in whatever {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} the
corresponding attribute is in (e.g., velocity units for \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, charge
units for \sphinxstyleemphasis{q}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the spin quantities, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sp} is in the units of the Bohr magneton;
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spz} are unitless quantities; and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{fmz}
are given in rad/THz.

\section{compute property/chunk command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:compute-property-chunk-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunkID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
property/chunk = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chunkID = ID of {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command that defines the chunks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
input1,etc = one or more attributes
\begin{sphinxalltt}
attributes = count, id, coord1, coord2, coord3
  count = \# of atoms in chunk
  id = original chunk IDs before compression by {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}}
  coord123 = coordinates for spatial bins calculated by {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bin2d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{count}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myChunks}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coord1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that stores the specified attributes of chunks of
atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LAMMPS, chunks are collections of atoms defined by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
chunk/atom}}}} command, which assigns each atom to a
single chunk (or no chunk).  The ID for this command is specified as
chunkID.  For example, a single chunk could be the atoms in a molecule
or atoms in a spatial bin.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto chunk}}}} doc pages
for details of how chunks can be defined and examples of how they can
be used to measure properties of a system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates and stores the specified attributes of chunks
as global data so they can be accessed by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}} and used in conjunction with other commands that
generate per\sphinxhyphen{}chunk data, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_com_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute com/chunk}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_msd_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute msd/chunk}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that only atoms in the specified group contribute to the
calculation of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{count} attribute.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command defines its own group; atoms will have a
chunk ID = 0 if they are not in that group, signifying they are not
assigned to a chunk, and will thus also not contribute to this
calculation.  You can specify the “all” group for this command if you
simply want to include atoms with non\sphinxhyphen{}zero chunk IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{count} attribute is the number of atoms in the chunk.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} attribute stores the original chunk ID for each chunk.  It
can only be used if the \sphinxstyleemphasis{compress} keyword was set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command referenced by
chunkID.  This means that the original chunk IDs (e.g., molecule IDs)
will have been compressed to remove chunk IDs with no atoms assigned
to them.  Thus a compressed chunk ID of 3 may correspond to an
original chunk ID (molecule ID in this case) of 415.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{id}
attribute will then be 415 for the third chunk.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coordN} attributes can only be used if a \sphinxstyleemphasis{binning} style was used

\sphinxAtStartPar
in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command
referenced by chunkID.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/1d}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/2d}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/3d} styles
the attribute is the center point of the bin in the corresponding
dimension.  Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/1d} only defines a \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord1} attribute.  Style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/2d} adds a \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord2} attribute.  Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin/3d} adds a \sphinxstyleemphasis{coord3}
attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword used in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom command}}}} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice}, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{coordN} attributes will be in distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  If the value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{reduced}, the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coordN} attributes will be in unitless reduced units (0\sphinxhyphen{}1).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest way to output the results of the compute property/chunk
calculation to a file is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_time::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/time}}}}
command, for example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molecule}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myChunk1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{count}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myChunk2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{com}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{chunk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cc1}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ave}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myChunk1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myChunk2[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vector}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global vector or global array depending on
the number of input values.  The length of the vector or number of
rows in the array is the number of chunks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global vector or global array where the
number of rows = the number of chunks \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nchunk} as calculated by the
specified {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_chunk_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute chunk/atom}}}} command.  If a
single input is specified, a global vector is produced.  If two or
more inputs are specified, a global array is produced where the number
of columns = the number of inputs.  The vector or array can be
accessed by any command that uses global values from a compute as
input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an
overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array values are “intensive”.  The values will be
unitless or in the units discussed above.

none

\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_chunk:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{compute property/grid@\spxentry{compute property/grid}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute property/grid command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:compute-property-grid-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
property/grid = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nx, Ny, Nz = grid size in each dimension

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
input1,etc = one or more attributes

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
attributes = id, ix, iy, iz, x, y, z, xs, ys, zs, xc, yc, zc, xsc, ysc, zsc
  id = ID of grid cell, x fastest, y next, z slowest
  proc = processor ID (0 to Nprocs\PYGZhy{}1) which owns the grid cell
  ix,iy,iz = grid indices in each dimension (1 to N inclusive)
  x,y,z = coords of lower left corner of grid cell
  xs,ys,zs = scaled coords of lower left corner of grid cell (0.0 to 1.0)
  xc,yc,zc = coords of center point of grid cell
  xsc,ysc,zsc = scaled coords of center point of grid cell (0.0 to 1.0)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iz}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zc}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that stores the specified attributes of a
distributed grid.  In LAMMPS, distributed grids are regular 2d or 3d
grids which overlay a 2d or 3d simulation domain.  Each processor owns
the grid cells whose center points lie within its subdomain.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto grid}}}} doc page for details of how distributed
grids can be defined by various commands and referenced.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute stores the specified attributes of grids as per\sphinxhyphen{}grid data
so they can be accessed by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}
such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump grid}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ny}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} define the size of the grid.  For a 2d simulation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} must be 1.  When this compute is used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump grid}}}},
to output per\sphinxhyphen{}grid values from other computes of fixes, the grid size
specified for this command must be consistent with the grid sizes
used by the other commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} attribute is the grid ID for each grid cell.  For a global
grid of size Nx by Ny by Nz (in 3d simulations) the grid IDs range
from 1 to Nx*Ny*Nz.  They are ordered with the X index of the 3d grid
varying fastest, then Y, then Z slowest.  For 2d grids (in 2d
simulations), the grid IDs range from 1 to Nx*Ny, with X varying
fastest and Y slowest.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 21Nov2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{proc} attribute is the ID of the processor which owns the grid
cell.  Processor IDs range from 0 to Nprocs \sphinxhyphen{} 1, where Nprocs is the
number of processors the simulation is running on.  Each grid cell is
owned by a single processor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ix}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iz} attributes are the indices of a grid cell in
each dimension.  They range from 1 to Nx inclusive in the X dimension,
and similar for Y and Z.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} attributes are the coordinates of the lower left
corner point of each grid cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xs}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ys}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zs} attributes are also coordinates of the lower left
corner point of each grid cell, except in scaled coordinates, where
the lower\sphinxhyphen{}left corner of the entire simulation box is (0,0,0) and the
upper right corner is (1,1,1).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zc} attributes are the coordinates of the center
point of each grid cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xsc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ysc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zsc} attributes are also coordinates of the center
point each grid cell, except in scaled coordinates, where the
lower\sphinxhyphen{}left corner of the entire simulation box is (0,0,0) and the upper
right corner is (1,1,1).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{triclinic simulation boxes}}}}, the grid
point coordinates for (x,y,z) and (xc,yc,zc) will reflect the
triclinic geometry.  For (xs,yz,zs) and (xsc,ysc,zsc), the coordinates
are the same for orthogonal versus triclinic boxes.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector or array depending on the
number of input values.  The length of the vector or number of array
rows (distributed across all processors) is Nx * Ny * Nz.  For access
by other commands, the name of the single grid produced by this
command is “grid”.  The name of its per\sphinxhyphen{}grid data is “data”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The (x,y,z) and (xc,yc,zc) coordinates are in distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For 2d simulations, the attributes which refer to
the Z dimension cannot be used.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump grid}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_grid:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{compute property/local@\spxentry{compute property/local}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute property/local command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:compute-property-local-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
property/local = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more attributes of the same type (neighbor, pair, bond, angle,
dihedral, or improper) may be appended

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = natom1, natom2, ntype1, ntype2,
                      patom1, patom2, ptype1, ptype2,
                      batom1, batom2, btype,
                      aatom1, aatom2, aatom3, atype,
                      datom1, datom2, datom3, datom4, dtype,
                      iatom1, iatom2, iatom3, iatom4, itype
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Neighbor attributes

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
natom1, natom2 = store IDs of two atoms in each pair (within neighbor cutoff)
ntype1, ntype2 = store types of two atoms in each pair (within neighbor cutoff)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair attributes

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
patom1, patom2 = store IDs of two atoms in each pair (within force cutoff)
ptype1, ptype2 = store types of two atoms in each pair (within force cutoff)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bond attributes

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
batom1, batom2 = store IDs of two atoms in each bond
btype = store bond type of each bond
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Angle attributes

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
aatom1, aatom2, aatom3 = store IDs of three atoms in each angle
atype = store angle type of each angle
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dihedral attributes

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
datom1, datom2, datom3, datom4 = store IDs of 4 atoms in each dihedral
dtype = store dihedral type of each dihedral
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Improper attributes

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
iatom1, iatom2, iatom3, iatom4 = store IDs of 4 atoms in each improper
itype = store improper type of each improper
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/arg pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} arg = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{btype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom2}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aatom2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that stores the specified attributes as local
data so it can be accessed by other {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{output commands}}}}.  If the input attributes refer to bond information,
then the number of datums generated, aggregated across all processors,
equals the number of bonds in the system.  Ditto for pairs, angles,
etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If multiple attributes are specified then they must all generate the
same amount of information, so that the resulting local array has the
same number of rows for each column.  This means that only bond
attributes can be specified together, or angle attributes, etc.  Bond
and angle attributes cannot be mixed in the same compute
property/local command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the inputs are pair attributes, the local data is generated by
looping over the pairwise neighbor list.  Info about an individual
pairwise interaction will only be included if both atoms in the pair
are in the specified compute group.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{natom1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{natom2}, all
atom pairs in the neighbor list are considered (out to the neighbor
cutoff = force cutoff + {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor skin}}}}).  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{patom1}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{patom2}, the distance between the atoms must be less than the
force cutoff distance for that pair to be included, as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}
commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} keyword determines how the force cutoff distance
for an interaction is determined for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{patom1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{patom2}
attributes.  For the default setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}, the pairwise cutoff
defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command for the types of
the two atoms is used.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} setting, the sum of the radii
of the two particles is used as a cutoff.  For example, this is
appropriate for granular particles which only interact when they are
overlapping, as computed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gran::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{granular pair styles}}}}.
Note that if a granular model defines atom types such that all
particles of a specific type are monodisperse (same diameter), then
the two settings are effectively identical.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the inputs are bond, angle, etc attributes, the local data is
generated by looping over all the atoms owned on a processor and
extracting bond, angle, etc info.  For bonds, info about an individual
bond will only be included if both atoms in the bond are in the
specified compute group.  Likewise for angles, dihedrals, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For bonds and angles, a bonds/angles that have been broken by setting
their bond/angle type to 0 will not be included.  Bonds/angles that
have been turned off (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} commands) by setting their
bond/angle type negative are written into the file.  This is
consistent with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute bond/local}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_angle_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute angle/local}}}} commands

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that as atoms migrate from processor to processor, there will be
no consistent ordering of the entries within the local vector or array
from one timestep to the next.  The only consistency that is
guaranteed is that the ordering on a particular timestep will be the
same for local vectors or arrays generated by other compute commands.
For example, output from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute bond/local}}}} command can be combined with bond atom indices
from this command and output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command
in a consistent way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{natom1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{natom2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{patom1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{patom2} attributes refer
to the atom IDs of the two atoms in each pairwise interaction computed
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntype1} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ntype2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ptype1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ptype2} attributes refer to the atom types
of the two atoms in each pairwise interaction.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For pairs, if two atoms \(I,J\) are involved in 1\textendash{}2, 1\textendash{}3, 1\textendash{}4
interactions within the molecular topology, their pairwise interaction
may be turned off, and thus they may not appear in the neighbor list,
and will not be part of the local data created by this command.  More
specifically, this may be true of \(I,J\) pairs with a weighting factor
of 0.0; pairs with a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero weighting factor are included.  The
weighting factors for 1\textendash{}2, 1\textendash{}3, and 1\textendash{}4 pairwise interactions are set
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{batom1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{batom2} attributes refer to the atom IDs of the 2
atoms in each {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond}}}}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} attribute refers to
the type of the bond, from 1 to Nbtypes = \# of bond types.  The number
of bond types is defined in the data file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The attributes that start with “a”, “d”, and “i” refer to similar values
for {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angles}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedrals}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{impropers}}}}.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a local vector or local array depending on the
number of input values.  The length of the vector or number of rows in
the array is the number of bonds, angles, etc.  If a single input is
specified, a local vector is produced.  If two or more inputs are
specified, a local array is produced where the number of columns = the
number of inputs.  The vector or array can be accessed by any command
that uses local values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto
output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array values will be integers that correspond to the
specified attribute.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_reduce::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute reduce}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_property_local:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword default is cutoff = type.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{compute ptm/atom@\spxentry{compute ptm/atom}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute ptm/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:compute-ptm-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ptm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{structures}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{group2}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ptm/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
structures = \sphinxstyleemphasis{default} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or any hyphen\sphinxhyphen{}separated combination of \sphinxstyleemphasis{fcc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{hcp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bcc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ico}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcub}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dhex}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{graphene} = structure types to search for

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
threshold = lattice distortion threshold (RMSD)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group2\sphinxhyphen{}ID determines which group is used for neighbor selection (optional, default “all”)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ptm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{default}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ptm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{hcp}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{dcub}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{dhex}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.15}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ptm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that determines the local lattice structure
around an atom using the PTM (Polyhedral Template Matching) method.
The PTM method is described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:larsen}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Larsen)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, there are seven lattice structures PTM recognizes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fcc = 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hcp = 2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bcc = 3

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ico (icosahedral) = 4

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sc (simple cubic) = 5

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dcub (diamond cubic) = 6

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dhex (diamond hexagonal) = 7

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
graphene = 8

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value of the PTM structure will be 0 for unknown types and \(-1\) for
atoms not in the specified compute group.  The choice of structures to search
for can be specified using the “structures” argument, which is a
hyphen\sphinxhyphen{}separated list of structure keywords.
Two convenient pre\sphinxhyphen{}set options are provided:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
default: fcc\sphinxhyphen{}hcp\sphinxhyphen{}bcc\sphinxhyphen{}ico

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
all: fcc\sphinxhyphen{}hcp\sphinxhyphen{}bcc\sphinxhyphen{}ico\sphinxhyphen{}sc\sphinxhyphen{}dcub\sphinxhyphen{}dhex\sphinxhyphen{}graphene

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ‘default’ setting detects the same structures as the Common Neighbor Analysis method.
The ‘all’ setting searches for all structure types.  A performance penalty is
incurred for the diamond and graphene structures, so it is not recommended to use this option if
it is known that the simulation does not contain these structures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
PTM identifies structures using two steps.  First, a graph isomorphism test is used
to identify potential structure matches.  Next, the deviation is computed between the
local structure (in the simulation) and a template of the ideal lattice structure.
The deviation is calculated as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{RMSD}(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v})
 = \min_{s, \mathbf{Q}} \sqrt{\frac{1}{N} \sum\limits_{i=1}^{N}
{\left\lVert s[\vec{u}_i - \mathbf{\bar{u}}]
              - \mathbf{Q} \cdot \vec{v}_i \right\rVert}^2}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, \(\vec u\) and \(\vec v\) contain the coordinates of the local
and ideal structures respectively, \(s\) is a scale factor, and
\(\mathbf Q\) is a rotation.  The best match is identified by the lowest
RMSD value, using the optimal scaling, rotation, and correspondence between the
points.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{threshold} keyword sets an upper limit on the maximum permitted deviation
before a local structure is identified as disordered.  Typical values are in
the range 0.1\textendash{}0.15, but larger values may be desirable at higher temperatures.
A value of 0 is equivalent to infinity and can be used if no threshold is
desired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The neighbor list needed to compute this quantity is constructed each
time the calculation is performed (e.g., each time a snapshot of atoms
is dumped).  Thus it can be inefficient to compute/dump this quantity
too frequently or to have multiple compute/dump commands, each with a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ptm/atom} style. By default the compute processes \sphinxstylestrong{all} neighbors
unless the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{group2\sphinxhyphen{}ID} argument is given, then only members
of that group are considered as neighbors.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_ptm_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array, which can be accessed by
any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from a compute as input.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of
LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Results are stored in the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array in the following order:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rmsd

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
interatomic distance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qw

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qx

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
qz

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The type is a number from \(-1\) to 8. The rmsd is a positive real number.
The interatomic distance is computed from the scale factor in the RMSD equation.
The \((qw,qx,qy,qz)\) parameters represent the orientation of the local
structure in quaternion form.  The reference coordinates for each template
(from which the orientation is determined) can be found in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ptm\_constants.h} file in the PTM source directory.
For atoms that are not within the compute group\sphinxhyphen{}ID, all values are set to zero.

This fix is part of the PTM package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{compute rattlers/atom command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:compute-rattlers-atom-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
compute ID group\PYGZhy{}ID rattlers/atom cutoff zmin ntries
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rattlers/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} = cutoffs determined based on atom types
\sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} = cutoffs determined based on atom diameters (atom style sphere)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zmin = minimum coordination for a non\sphinxhyphen{}rattler atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ntries = maximum number of iterations to remove rattlers

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rattlers}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a compute that identifies rattlers in a system. Rattlers are often
identified in granular or glassy packings as under\sphinxhyphen{}coordinated atoms that
do not have the required number of contacts to constrain their translational
degrees of freedom. Such atoms are not considered rigid and can often freely
rattle around in the system. This compute identifies rattlers which can be
helpful for excluding them from analysis or providing extra damping forces
to accelerate relaxation processes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rattlers are identified using an interactive approach. The coordination
number of all atoms is first calculated.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} settings
are used to select whether interaction cutoffs are determined by atom
types or by the sum of atomic radii (atom style sphere), respectively.
Rattlers are then identified as atoms with a coordination number less
than \sphinxstyleemphasis{zmin} and are removed from consideration. Atomic coordination
numbers are then recalculated, excluding previously identified rattlers,
to identify a new set of rattlers. This process is iterated up to a maximum
of \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntries} or until no new rattlers are identified and the remaining
atoms form a stable network of contacts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In dense homogeneous systems where the average atom coordination number
is expected to be larger than \sphinxstyleemphasis{zmin}, this process usually only takes a few
iterations and a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntries} around ten may be sufficient. In systems
with significant heterogeneity or average coordination numbers less than
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zmin}, an appropriate value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntries} depends heavily on the specific
system. For instance, a linear chain of N rattler atoms with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{zmin} of 2
would take N/2 iterations to identify that all the atoms are rattlers.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector and a global scalar. The vector
designates which atoms are rattlers, indicated by a value 1. Non\sphinxhyphen{}rattlers
have a value of 0. The global scalar returns the total number of rattlers
in the system. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an
overview of LAMMPS output options.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}COMPUTE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} cutoff option requires that atoms store a radius as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} or similar commands.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_coord_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute coord/atom}}}}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_contact_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute contact/atom}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_rattlers_atom:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none
