\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_saed:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates electron diffraction intensity as
described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed:saed-coleman}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Coleman)}}}} on a mesh of reciprocal lattice nodes
defined by the entire simulation domain (or manually) using simulated
radiation of wavelength lambda.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The electron diffraction intensity I at each reciprocal lattice point
is computed from the structure factor F using the equations:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}I = & \frac{F^{*}F}{N} \\
F(\mathbf{k}) = & \sum_{j=1}^{N}f_j(\theta)exp(2\pi i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{r}_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, K is the location of the reciprocal lattice node, \(r_j\) is the
position of each atom, \(f_j\) are atomic scattering factors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Diffraction intensities are calculated on a three\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional mesh of
reciprocal lattice nodes. The mesh spacing is defined either (a)  by
the entire simulation domain or (b) manually using selected values as
shown in the 2D diagram below.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.75]{{saed_mesh}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a mesh defined by the simulation domain, a rectilinear grid is
constructed with spacing \sphinxstyleemphasis{c}*inv(A) along each reciprocal lattice
axis. Where A are the vectors corresponding to the edges of the
simulation cell. If one or two directions has non\sphinxhyphen{}periodic boundary
conditions, then the spacing in these directions is defined from the
average of the (inversed) box lengths with periodic boundary conditions.
Meshes defined by the simulation domain must contain at least one periodic
boundary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{manual} flag is included, the mesh of reciprocal lattice nodes
will defined using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{c} values for the spacing along each reciprocal
lattice axis. Note that manual mapping of the reciprocal space mesh is
good for comparing diffraction results from  multiple simulations; however
it can reduce the likelihood that Bragg reflections will be satisfied
unless small spacing parameters (\(<0.05~\AA^-1\))
are implemented.  Meshes with manual spacing do not require a periodic
boundary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The limits of the reciprocal lattice mesh are determined by the use of
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kmax}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Zone}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dR\_Ewald} parameters.  The rectilinear mesh
created about the origin of reciprocal space is terminated at the
boundary of a sphere of radius \sphinxstyleemphasis{Kmax} centered at the origin.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Zone} parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{z1} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{z2} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{z3} = 0 are used, diffraction intensities are
computed throughout the entire spherical volume \sphinxhyphen{} note this can
greatly increase the cost of computation.  Otherwise, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Zone}
parameters will denote the \(z1=h\), \(z2=k\), and \(z3=\ell\)
(in a global sense) zone axis of an intersecting Ewald sphere.  Diffraction
intensities will only be computed at the intersection of the reciprocal lattice
mesh and a \sphinxstyleemphasis{dR\_Ewald} thick surface of the Ewald sphere.  See the
example 3D intensity data and the intersection of a {[}010{]} zone axis
in the below image.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.75]{{saed_ewald_intersect}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The atomic scattering factors, fj, accounts for the reduction in
diffraction intensity due to Compton scattering.  Compute saed uses
analytical approximations of the atomic scattering factors that vary
for each atom type (type1 type2 … typeN) and angle of diffraction.
The analytic approximation is computed using the formula
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed:brown}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Brown)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_j\left ( \frac{sin(\theta)}{\lambda} \right )=\sum_{i}^{5}
a_i exp\left ( -b_i \frac{sin^{2}(\theta)}{\lambda^{2}} \right )\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coefficients parameterized by {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed:fox}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fox)}}}} are assigned for each
atom type designating the chemical symbol and charge of each atom
type. Valid chemical symbols for compute saed are:

\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_saed:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global vector.  The length of the vector is
the number of reciprocal lattice nodes that are explored by the mesh.
The entries of the global vector are the computed diffraction
intensities as described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector can be accessed by any command that uses global values from
a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All array values calculated by this compute are “intensive”.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_saed:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the DIFFRACTION package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The compute\_saed command does not work for triclinic cells.

0.01.

\section{compute sans command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:compute-sans-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_sans::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sans}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sans = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kmax = maximum wave vector magnitude to explore (inverse length units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{qmin} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{qmax} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nq} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dR\_Ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxdeg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{logdist} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lengthpath}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qmin} value = minimum wave vector magnitude to calculate (inverse length units)
               (default: 1.0 Å⁻\(\sp{\text{1}}\))
\sphinxstyleemphasis{qmax} value = maximum wave vector magnitude to calculate (inverse length units)
               (default: 30.0 Å⁻\(\sp{\text{1}}\))
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nq} value = number of wave vectors distributed between qmin and qmax
             (default: 100)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dR\_Ewald} value = thickness of Ewald sphere slice around target q values
                   (inverse length units)
                   (default: 0.2 Å⁻\(\sp{\text{1}}\))
\sphinxstyleemphasis{maxdeg} value = maximum degeneracy allowed for wave vector selection
                 (default: varies)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{logdist} = flag to use logarithmic distribution of wave vectors instead
            of linear distribution
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lengthpath} file = path to file containing custom neutron scattering lengths
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sans}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qmin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sans}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dR\PYGZus{}Ewald}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.15}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{logdist}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sans}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lengthpath}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scattering\PYGZus{}lengths.txt}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates small\sphinxhyphen{}angle neutron scattering (SANS)
intensity as a function of wave vector magnitude (q), based on the atomic
structure of the system. This computation is particularly useful for
comparing molecular dynamics simulations with neutron diffraction
experiments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SANS intensity I(q) at each wave vector magnitude is computed from
the structure factor F(q) using:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}I(q) = \frac{1}{N} \left| \sum_{i}^{N} b_i exp(2\pi i \mathbf{q} \cdot \mathbf{r}_i) \right|^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where N is the number of atoms in the group, \(\mathbf{r}_i\) is the
position of atom i, \(b_i\) is the neutron scattering length for atom
type i, and \(\mathbf{q}\) is the scattering wave vector with magnitude q.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Wave Vector Generation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The compute generates a set of wave vectors distributed within reciprocal
space. By default, wave vectors are distributed linearly between \sphinxstyleemphasis{qmin}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{qmax} in steps determined by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nq}. If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{logdist} flag is specified,
wave vectors are instead distributed on a logarithmic scale, which is often
more suitable for exploring a wide range of length scales.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{kmax} determines the maximum distance explored from the
origin of reciprocal space in units of inverse length. Wave vectors are
selected to lie approximately at the specified q magnitudes, within a
tolerance defined by \sphinxstyleemphasis{dR\_Ewald} (the thickness of the Ewald sphere slice).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Scattering Lengths}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, scattering lengths are set to 1.0 for all atom types, which
gives an unweighted calculation. For comparison with actual neutron
scattering experiments, custom neutron scattering lengths can be provided
via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lengthpath} keyword, which specifies a file containing scattering
length values for each atom type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scattering lengths file should contain one line per atom type with the
format:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
type\PYGZus{}number scattering\PYGZus{}length
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where type\_number is the LAMMPS atom type (starting from 1) and
scattering\_length is the neutron scattering length in inverse length
units (typically in fm or 10⁻\(\sp{\text{1}}\)\(\sp{\text{5}}\) m for neutrons).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Degeneracy and Ewald Sphere}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dR\_Ewald} parameter controls how many wave vectors are selected
around each target q value. A smaller value results in fewer selected
wave vectors but more precise targeting of specific q values. A larger
value samples a thicker sphere in reciprocal space around each q value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxdeg} parameter can be used to limit the degeneracy (number of
equivalent wave vectors) selected for each q value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parallel Calculation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute uses MPI to efficiently distribute the scattering calculation
across multiple processors. The cos and sin components of the structure
factor are accumulated separately on each processor and then reduced
globally before computing the final intensity.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global array with dimensions of Nq rows and
3 columns. Each row contains:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column 1: Index (i) of the wave vector

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column 2: Wave vector magnitude (q) in inverse length units

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column 3: Normalized SANS intensity I(q)/N

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The array can be accessed by any command that uses global values from
a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All array values calculated by this compute are “intensive”.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the DIFFRACTION package. It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The compute\_sans command does not work for triclinic cells.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The compute\_sans command only works with 3\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional systems.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_saed::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute saed}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_xrd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute xrd}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_sans:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are qmin = 1.0, qmax = 30.0, Nq = 100, dR\_Ewald = 0.2,
logdist = off (linear distribution)

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
slcsa/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
twojmax = band limit for bispectrum components (non\sphinxhyphen{}negative integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nclasses = number of crystal structures used in the database for the classifier SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
db\_mean\_descriptor\_file = file name of file containing the database mean descriptor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lda\_file = file name of file containing the linear discriminant analysis matrix for dimension reduction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lr\_decision\_file = file name of file containing the scaling matrix for logistic regression classification

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lr\_bias\_file = file name of file containing the bias vector for logistic regression classification

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
maha\_file = file name of file containing for each crystal structure: the Mahalanobis distance threshold for sanity check purposes, the average reduced descriptor and the inverse of the corresponding covariance matrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_ID{[}*{]} = compute ID of previously required \sphinxstyleemphasis{compute sna/atom} command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slcsa_atom:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.99363}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rmin0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nnn}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wmode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.3}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{b2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{slcsa}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mean\PYGZus{}descriptors.dat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lda\PYGZus{}scalings.dat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lr\PYGZus{}decision.dat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lr\PYGZus{}bias.dat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maha\PYGZus{}thresholds.dat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}b1[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slcsa_atom:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that performs the Supervised Learning Crystal
Structure Analysis (SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA) from {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_slcsa_atom:lafourcade2023-1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lafourcade)}}}}
for each atom in the group. The SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA tool takes as an input a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
descriptor (bispectrum) that is computed through the \sphinxstyleemphasis{compute sna/atom}
command and then proceeds to a dimension reduction step followed by a
logistic regression in order to assign a probable crystal structure to
each atom in the group. The SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA tool is pre\sphinxhyphen{}trained on a database
containing \(C\) distinct crystal structures from which a crystal
structure classifier is derived and a tutorial to build such a tool is
available at \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lafourcadep/SL-CSA}{SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first step of the SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA tool consists in performing a dimension
reduction of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom descriptor \(\mathbf{B}^i \in
\mathbb{R}^{D}\) through the Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) method,
leading to a new projected descriptor
\(\mathbf{x}^i=\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{LDA}(\mathbf{B}^i):\mathbb{R}^D
\rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{d=C-1}\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{x}^i = \mathbf{C}^T_\mathrm{LDA} \cdot (\mathbf{B}^i - \mu^\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{db})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{C}^T_\mathrm{LDA} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times d}\) is
the reduction coefficients matrix of the LDA model read in file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lda\_file}, \(\mathbf{B}^i \in \mathbb{R}^{D}\) is the bispectrum of
atom \(i\) and \(\mu^\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{db} \in \mathbb{R}^{D}\)
is the average descriptor of the entire database. The latter is computed
from the average descriptors of each crystal structure read from the
file \sphinxstyleemphasis{mean\_descriptors\_file}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new projected descriptor with dimension \(d=C-1\) allows for a
good separation of different crystal structures fingerprints in the
latent space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Once the dimension reduction step is performed by means of LDA, the new
descriptor \(\mathbf{x}^i \in \mathbb{R}^{d=C-1}\) is taken as an
input for performing a multinomial logistic regression (LR) which
provides a score vector
\(\mathbf{s}^i=\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{LR}(\mathbf{x}^i):\mathbb{R}^d
\rightarrow \mathbb{R}^C\) defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{s}^i = \mathbf{b}_\mathrm{LR} + \mathbf{D}_\mathrm{LR} \cdot {\mathbf{x}^i}^T\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\mathbf{b}_\mathrm{LR} \in \mathbb{R}^C\) and
\(\mathbf{D}_\mathrm{LR} \in \mathbb{R}^{C \times d}\) the bias
vector and decision matrix of the LR model after training both read in
files \sphinxstyleemphasis{lr\_fil1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lr\_file2} respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finally, a probability vector
\(\mathbf{p}^i=\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{LR}(\mathbf{x}^i):\mathbb{R}^d
\rightarrow \mathbb{R}^C\) is defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{p}^i = \frac{\mathrm{exp}(\mathbf{s}^i)}{\sum\limits_{j} \mathrm{exp}(s^i_j) }\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
from which the crystal structure assigned to each atom with descriptor
\(\mathbf{B}^i\) and projected descriptor \(\mathbf{x}^i\) is
computed as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{argmax} of the probability vector
\(\mathbf{p}^i\). Since the logistic regression step systematically
attributes a crystal structure to each atom, a sanity check is needed to
avoid misclassification. To this end, a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom Mahalanobis distance to
each crystal structure \sphinxstyleemphasis{CS} present in the database is computed:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}d_\mathrm{Mahalanobis}^{i \rightarrow \mathrm{CS}} = \sqrt{(\mathbf{x}^i - \mathbf{\mu}^\mathbf{x}_\mathrm{CS})^\mathrm{T} \cdot \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}_\mathrm{CS} \cdot (\mathbf{x}^i - \mathbf{\mu}^\mathbf{x}_\mathrm{CS}) }\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{\mu}^\mathbf{x}_\mathrm{CS} \in \mathbb{R}^{d}\) is
the average projected descriptor of crystal structure \sphinxstyleemphasis{CS} in the
database and where \(\mathbf{\Sigma}_\mathrm{CS} \in \mathbb{R}^{d
\times d}\) is the corresponding covariance matrix. Finally, if the
Mahalanobis distance to crystal structure \sphinxstyleemphasis{CS} for atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} is greater
than the pre\sphinxhyphen{}determined threshold, no crystal structure is assigned to
atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i}. The Mahalanobis distance thresholds are read in file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{maha\_file} while the covariance matrices are read in file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{covmat\_file}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lafourcadep/SL-CSA}{SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA} framework provides
an automatic computation of the different matrices and thresholds
required for a proper classification and writes down all the required
files for calling the \sphinxstyleemphasis{compute slcsa/atom} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{compute slcsa/atom} command requires that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_sna_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
sna/atom}}}} command is called before as it takes the
resulting per\sphinxhyphen{}atom bispectrum as an input. In addition, it is crucial
that the value \sphinxstyleemphasis{twojmax} is set to the same value of the value \sphinxstyleemphasis{twojmax}
used in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{compute sna/atom} command, as well as that the value
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nclasses} is set to the number of crystal structures used in the
database to train the SL\sphinxhyphen{}CSA tool.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slcsa_atom:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, this compute computes the Mahalanobis distances to the
different crystal structures present in the database in addition to
assigning a crystal structure for each atom as a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector, which
can be accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}atom values from a compute
as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an
overview of LAMMPS output options.

\section{compute slice command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slice:compute-slice-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_slice:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_slice::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slice:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nskip}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{input2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
slice = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nstart = starting index within input vector(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nstop = stopping index within input vector(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nskip = extract every Nskip elements from input vector(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
input = c\_ID, c\_ID{[}N{]}, f\_ID, f\_ID{[}N{]}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
c\PYGZus{}ID = global vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of global array calculated by a compute with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID = global vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of global array calculated by a fix with ID
v\PYGZus{}name = vector calculated by an vector\PYGZhy{}style variable with name
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slice:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}msdmol[4]}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{301}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{400}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}msdmol[4]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}myVec}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slice:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a calculation that “slices” one or more vector inputs into
smaller vectors, one per listed input.  The inputs can be global
quantities; they cannot be per\sphinxhyphen{}atom or local quantities.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Computes}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} and vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}} can generate such global quantities.  The
group specified with this command is ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values extracted from the input vector(s) are determined by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nstart}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nstop}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nskip} parameters.  The elements of an input
vector of length N are indexed from 1 to N.  Starting at element
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nstart}, every Mth element is extracted, where M = \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nskip}, until
element \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nstop} is reached.  The extracted quantities are stored as a
vector, which is typically shorter than the input vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each listed input is operated on independently to produce one output
vector.  Each listed input must be a global vector or column of a
global array calculated by another {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If an input value begins with “c\_”, a compute ID must follow which has
been previously defined in the input script and which generates a
global vector or array.  See the individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} doc
page for details.  If no bracketed integer is appended, the vector
calculated by the compute is used.  If a bracketed integer is
appended, the Ith column of the array calculated by the compute is
used.  Users can also write code for their own compute styles and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value begins with “f\_”, a fix ID must follow which has been
previously defined in the input script and which generates a global
vector or array.  See the individual {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} page for
details.  Note that some fixes only produce their values on certain
timesteps, which must be compatible with when compute slice references
the values, else an error results.  If no bracketed integer is
appended, the vector calculated by the fix is used.  If a bracketed
integer is appended, the Ith column of the array calculated by the fix
is used.  Users can also write code for their own fix style and {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{add them to LAMMPS}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If an input value begins with “v\_”, a variable name must follow which
has been previously defined in the input script.  Only vector\sphinxhyphen{}style
variables can be referenced.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} command
for details.  Note that variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{vector} define a formula
which can reference individual atom properties or thermodynamic
keywords, or they can invoke other computes, fixes, or variables when
they are evaluated, so this is a very general means of specifying
quantities to slice.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a single input is specified this compute produces a global vector,
even if the length of the vector is 1.  If multiple inputs are
specified, then a global array of values is produced, with the number
of columns equal to the number of inputs specified.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_slice:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global vector if a single input value is
specified or a global array with N columns where N is the number of
inputs.  The length of the vector or the number of rows in the array
is equal to the number of values extracted from each input vector.
These values can be used by any command that uses global vector or
array values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array values calculated by this compute are simply
copies of values generated by computes or fixes or variables that are
input vectors to this compute.  If there is a single input vector of
intensive and/or extensive values, then each value in the vector of
values calculated by this compute will be “intensive” or “extensive”,
depending on the corresponding input value.  If there are multiple
input vectors, and all the values in them are intensive, then the
array values calculated by this compute are “intensive”.  If there are
multiple input vectors, and any value in them is extensive, then the
array values calculated by this compute are “extensive”.  Values
produced by a variable are treated as intensive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array values will be in whatever {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} the
input quantities are in.

none
\end{quote}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_contact_radius:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation which outputs the contact radius, i.e., the
radius used to prevent particles from penetrating each other.  The
contact radius is used only to prevent particles belonging to
different physical bodies from penetrating each other. It is used by
the contact pair styles, e.g., smd/hertz and smd/tri\_surface.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value of the contact radius will be 0.0 for particles not in the
specified compute group.

\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_contact_radius:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector, which can be accessed
by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values from a compute as input.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of
LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector values will be in distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_hourglass_error:examples}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_hourglass_error:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation which outputs the error of the approximated
relative separation with respect to the actual relative separation of
the particles i and j. Ideally, if the deformation gradient is exact,
and there exists a unique mapping between all particles’ positions
within the neighborhood of the central node and the deformation
gradient, the approximated relative separation will coincide with the
actual relative separation of the particles i and j in the deformed
configuration.  This compute is only really useful for debugging the
hourglass control mechanism which is part of the Total\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrangian SPH
pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to use Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Output Info:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector, which can be accessed
by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values from a compute as input.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of
LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector values will are dimensionless. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_rho:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the per\sphinxhyphen{}particle mass density.
The mass density is the mass of a particle which is constant during
the course of a simulation, divided by its volume, which can change
due to mechanical deformation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to use Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_defgrad:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the deformation gradient.  It is
only meaningful for particles which interact according to the
Total\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrangian SPH pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to use Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_defgrad:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute outputs a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector of vectors (tensors),
which can be accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values
from a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc
page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector values will be given dimensionless. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector has 10 entries. The first
nine entries correspond to the xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz
components of the asymmetric deformation gradient tensor. The tenth
entry is the determinant of the deformation gradient.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_dt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that outputs the CFL\sphinxhyphen{}stable time increment per
particle.  This time increment is essentially given by the speed of
sound, divided by the SPH smoothing length.  Because both the speed of
sound and the smoothing length typically change during the course of a
simulation, the stable time increment needs to be re\sphinxhyphen{}computed every
time step.  This calculation is performed automatically in the
relevant SPH pair styles and this compute only serves to make the
stable time increment accessible for output purposes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_dt:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector, which can be accessed
by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values from a compute as input.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of
LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values will be given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} of time.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_dt:restrictions}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_shape:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that outputs the current shape of the volume
associated with a particle as a rotated ellipsoid.  It is only
meaningful for particles which interact according to the
Total\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrangian SPH pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to use Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_shape:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector of vectors, which can be
accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values from a compute
as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an
overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector has 7 entries. The first three entries
correspond to the lengths of the ellipsoid’s axes and have units of
length.  These axis values are computed as the contact radius times the
xx, yy, or zz components of the Green\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrange strain tensor
associated with the particle.  The next 4 values are quaternions
(order: q, x, y, z) which describe the spatial rotation of the
particle relative to its initial state.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_shape:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the MACHDYN package.  It is only enabled if

\sphinxAtStartPar
This quantity will be computed only for particles which interact with
the Total\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrangian SPH pair style.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_stress:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that outputs the Cauchy stress tensor for
particles interacting via the Total\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrangian SPH pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_tlsph_stress:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector of vectors (tensors),
which can be accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values
from a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc
page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values will be given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} of pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector has 7 entries. The first six entries
correspond to the xx, yy, zz, xy, xz and yz components of the
symmetric Cauchy stress tensor. The seventh entry is the second
invariant of the stress tensor, i.e., the von Mises equivalent stress.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_triangle_vertices:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that returns the coordinates of the vertices
corresponding to the triangle\sphinxhyphen{}elements of a mesh created by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix smd/wall\_surface}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_triangle_vertices:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute returns a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector of vectors, which can be
accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values from a compute
as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an
overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector has nine entries, (x1/y1/z1), (x2/y2/z2), and
(x3/y3/z3) corresponding to the first, second, and third vertex of
each triangle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is only meaningful to use this compute for a group of particles
which is created via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_smd_wall_surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix smd/wall\_surface}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output of this compute can be used with the dump2vtk\_tris tool to
generate a VTK representation of the smd/wall\_surface mesh for
visualization purposes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values will be given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} of distance.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_ulsph_stress:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that outputs the Cauchy stress tensor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{this PDF guide} to using Smooth
Mach Dynamics in LAMMPS.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_smd_ulsph_stress:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector of vectors (tensors),
which can be accessed by any command that uses per\sphinxhyphen{}particle values
from a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} doc
page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values will be given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} of pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}particle vector has 7 entries. The first six entries
correspond to the xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz components of the symmetric
Cauchy stress tensor. The seventh entry is the second invariant of the
stress tensor, i.e., the von Mises equivalent stress.

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{snap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rcutfac}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rfac0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{twojmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{R\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{R\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{w\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{w\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rcutfac}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rfac0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{twojmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{R\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{R\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{w\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{w\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{grid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ny}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rcutfac}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rfac0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{twojmax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{R\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{R\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{w\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{w\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}

\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sna/atom = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rcutfac = scale factor applied to all cutoff radii (positive real)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rfac0 = parameter in distance to angle conversion (0 \textless{} rcutfac \textless{} 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
twojmax = band limit for bispectrum components (non\sphinxhyphen{}negative integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
R\_1, R\_2,… = list of cutoff radii, one for each type (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
w\_1, w\_2,… = list of neighbor weights, one for each type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nx, ny, nz = number of grid points in x, y, and z directions (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rmin0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{switchflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bzeroflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadraticflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{chem} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bnormflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wselfallflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bikflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{switchinnerflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sinner} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dinner} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dgradflag} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nnn} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wmode} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rmin0} value = parameter in distance to angle conversion (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{switchflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = do not use switching function
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = use switching function
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bzeroflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = do not subtract B0
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = subtract B0
\sphinxstyleemphasis{quadraticflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = do not generate quadratic terms
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = generate quadratic terms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{chem} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelements} \sphinxstyleemphasis{elementlist}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelements} = number of SNAP elements
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{elementlist} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntypes} integers in range {[}0, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelements})
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bnormflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = do not normalize
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = normalize bispectrum components
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wselfallflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = self\sphinxhyphen{}contribution only for element of central atom
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = self\sphinxhyphen{}contribution for all elements
\sphinxstyleemphasis{switchinnerflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = do not use inner switching function
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = use inner switching function
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sinner} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sinnerlist}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{sinnerlist} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntypes} values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sinner} (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dinner} values = \sphinxstyleemphasis{dinnerlist}
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{dinnerlist} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ntypes} values of \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dinner} (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bikflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} (only implemented for compute snap)
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = descriptors are summed over atoms of each type
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = descriptors are listed separately for each atom
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dgradflag} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} (only implemented for compute snap)
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = descriptor gradients are summed over atoms of each type
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = descriptor gradients are listed separately for each atom pair
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
additional keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nnn} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{wmode} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nnn} value = number of considered nearest neighbors to compute the bispectrum over a target specific number of neighbors (only implemented for compute sna/atom)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{wmode} value = weight function for finding optimal cutoff to match the target number of neighbors (required if nnn used, only implemented for compute sna/atom)
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{0} = heavyside weight function
   \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} = hyperbolic tangent weight function
\sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} value = transition interval centered at cutoff distance for hyperbolic tangent weight function (ignored if wmode=0, required if wmode=1, only implemented for compute sna/atom)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}
