\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_deform:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{deform}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_deform:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
atoms, after subtracting out a streaming velocity induced by the
simulation box changing size and/or shape, for example in a
non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD) simulation.  The size/shape change is
induced by use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command.  A compute
of this style is created by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod}}}}
command to compute the thermal temperature of atoms for thermostatting
purposes.  A compute of this style can also be used by any command
that computes a temperature (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The deformation fix changes the box size and/or shape over time, so
each atom in the simulation box can be thought of as having a
“streaming” velocity.  For example, if the box is being sheared in \sphinxstyleemphasis{x},
relative to \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, then atoms at the bottom of the box (low \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}) have a
small \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} velocity, while atoms at the top of the box (high \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}) have a
large \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} velocity.  This position\sphinxhyphen{}dependent streaming velocity is
subtracted from each atom’s actual velocity to yield a thermal
velocity, which is then used to compute the temperature.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Fix deform}}}} has an option for remapping either
atom coordinates or velocities to the changing simulation box.  When
using this compute in conjunction with a deforming box, fix deform
should NOT remap atom positions, but rather should let atoms respond
to the changing box by adjusting their own velocities (or let
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} remap the atom velocities; see its remap
option).  If fix deform does remap atom positions, then they appear to
move with the box but their velocity is not changed, and thus they do
NOT have the streaming velocity assumed by this compute.  LAMMPS will
warn you if fix deform is defined and its remap setting is not
consistent with this compute.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After the streaming velocity has been subtracted from each atom, the
temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{dim}}{2} N k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\), dim = 2 or 3 is the dimensionality of the
simulation, \(N\) is the number of atoms in the group, \(k_B\)
is the Boltzmann constant, and \(T\) is the temperature.  Note that
\(v\) in the kinetic energy formula is the atom’s velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also calculated
by this compute for use in the computation of a pressure tensor by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}} command.  The formula for
the components of the tensor is the same as the above expression for
\(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2 factor is NOT included and
the \(v_i^2\) is replaced by \(v_{i,x} v_{i,y}\) for the
\(xy\) component, and so on.  Note that because it lacks the 1/2
factor, these tensor components are twice those of the traditional
kinetic energy tensor.  The six components of the vector are ordered
\(xx\), \(yy\), \(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\),
\(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be
constant for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The removal of the box deformation velocity component by this fix is
essentially computing the temperature after a “bias” has been removed
from the velocity of the atoms.  If this compute is used with a fix
command that performs thermostatting then this bias will be subtracted
from each atom, thermostatting of the remaining thermal velocity will
be performed, and the bias will be added back in.  Thermostatting
fixes that work in this way include {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature calculated by this compute is only accurate if
the atoms are indeed moving with a stream velocity profile that
matches the box deformation.  If not, then the compute will subtract
off an incorrect stream velocity, yielding a bogus thermal
temperature.  You should \sphinxstylestrong{not} assume that your atoms are streaming at
the same rate the box is deforming.  Rather, you should monitor their
velocity profiles (e.g., via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/chunk}}}}
command).  You can also compare the results of this compute to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/profile}}}}, which actually
calculates the stream profile before subtracting it.  If the two computes do
not give roughly the same temperature, then your atoms are not streaming
consistent with the box deformation.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}}
command for more details on ways to get atoms to stream consistently with
the box deformation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that
constrain molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups of
atoms that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If
needed, the subtracted degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom can be altered using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{compute temp/deform/eff command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_deform_eff:compute-temp-deform-eff-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_deform_eff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_deform_eff::doc}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_deform_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
nuclei and electrons in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}}
model, after subtracting out a streaming velocity induced by the
simulation box changing size and/or shape, for example in a
non\sphinxhyphen{}equilibrium MD (NEMD) simulation.  The size/shape change is
induced by use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix deform}}}} command.  A
compute of this style is created by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sllod_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sllod/eff}}}} command to compute the thermal temperature of
atoms for thermostatting purposes.  A compute of this style can also
be used by any command that computes a temperature (e.g.,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/eff}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The calculation performed by this compute is exactly like that
described by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}}
command, except that the formulas for the temperature (scalar) and
diagonal components of the symmetric tensor (vector) include the
radial electron velocity contributions, as discussed by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/eff}}}} command.  Note that only
the translational degrees of freedom for each nuclei or electron are
affected by the streaming velocity adjustment.  The radial velocity
component of the electrons is not affected.

vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\section{compute temp/drude command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:compute-temp-drude-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{drude}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/drude = style name of this compute command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input scripts available: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/drude}}.


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperatures of core\textendash{}Drude
pairs. This compute is designed to be used with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermalized Drude oscillator model}}}}.
Polarizable models in LAMMPS
are described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_polarizable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto polarizable}}}} doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Drude oscillators consist of a core particle and a Drude particle
connected by a harmonic bond, and the relative motion of these Drude
oscillators is usually maintained cold by a specific thermostat that
acts on the relative motion of the core\textendash{}Drude particle
pairs. Therefore, because LAMMPS considers Drude particles as normal
atoms in its default temperature compute ({\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}
command), the reduced temperature of the core\textendash{}Drude particle pairs is not
calculated correctly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By contrast, this compute calculates the temperature of the cores
using center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocities of the core\textendash{}Drude pairs, and the
reduced temperature of the Drude particles using the relative
velocities of the Drude particles with respect to their cores.
Non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atoms are considered as cores.  Their velocities
contribute to the temperature of the cores.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6, which can be accessed by indices 1\textendash{}6, whose components
are
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature of the centers of mass (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature of the dipoles (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of degrees of freedom of the centers of mass

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of degrees of freedom of the dipoles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic energy of the centers of mass (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kinetic energy of the dipoles (energy units)

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These values can be used by any command that uses global scalar or
vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both the scalar value and the first two values of the vector
calculated by this compute are “intensive”.  The other four vector values
are “extensive”.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of degrees of freedom contributing to the temperature is
assumed to be constant for the duration of the run unless the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix\_modify command}}}} sets the option \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic/dof
yes}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_drude:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin/drude}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude_transform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude/transform}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_thole::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style thole}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}

\section{compute temp/eff command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:compute-temp-eff-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/eff = style name of this compute command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mobile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
nuclei and electrons in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}}
model.  A compute of this style can be used by commands that compute a
temperature (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/eff}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{dim}}{2} N k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\) for nuclei and sum of
\(\frac12 (m v^2 + \frac34 m s^2\)) for electrons, where \(s\)
includes the radial electron velocity contributions), dim = 2 or 3 is the
dimensionality of the simulation, \(N\) is the number of atoms (only total
number of nuclei in the eFF (see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_eff}}}}
command) in the group, \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant, and \(T\) is
the absolute temperature.  This expression is summed over all nuclear and
electronic degrees of freedom, essentially by setting the kinetic contribution
to the heat capacity to \(\frac32 k\) (where only nuclei contribute). This
subtlety is valid for temperatures well below the Fermi temperature, which for
densities two to five times the density of liquid hydrogen ranges from
86,000 to 170,000 K.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For eFF models, in order to override the default temperature
reported by LAMMPS in the thermodynamic quantities reported via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo}}}} command, the user should apply a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}} command, as shown in the following
example:
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute         }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{effTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{etotal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pe}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ke}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{press}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{effTemp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A six\sphinxhyphen{}component kinetic energy tensor is also calculated by this compute
for use in the computation of a pressure tensor.  The formula for the
components of the tensor is the same as the above formula, except that
\(v^2\) is replaced by \(v_x v_y\) for the \(xy\) component, etc.
For the eFF, again, the radial electronic velocities are also considered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be
constant for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that
constrain molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups of
atoms that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If
needed, the subtracted degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom can be altered using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”, meaning it
is independent of the number of atoms in the simulation.  The vector
values are “extensive”, meaning they scale with the number of atoms in
the simulation.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EFF package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_partial::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/partial}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/region}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_eff:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\section{compute temp/partial command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:compute-temp-partial-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{partial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xflag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yflag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zflag}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/partial = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
xflag,yflag,zflag = 0/1 for whether to exclude/include this dimension

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{newT}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{partial}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
atoms, after excluding one or more velocity components.  A compute of
this style can be used by any command that computes a temperature
(e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{dim}}{2} N k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\)), dim = 2 or 3 is the dimensionality of the simulation,
\(N\) is the number of atoms in the group, \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann
constant, and \(T\) = temperature.  The calculation of KE excludes the
\(x\), \(y\), or \(z\) dimensions if \sphinxstyleemphasis{xflag}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yflag}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zflag}
is 0.  The dim parameter is adjusted to give the correct number of
degrees of freedom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also calculated
by this compute for use in the computation of a pressure tensor by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}} command.  The formula for
the components of the tensor is the same as the above expression for
\(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2 factor is NOT included and
the \(v_i^2\) is replaced by \(v_{i,x} v_{i,y}\) for the
\(xy\) component, and so on.  Note that because it lacks the 1/2
factor, these tensor components are twice those of the traditional
kinetic energy tensor.  The six components of the vector are ordered
\(xx\), \(yy\), \(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\),
\(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be
constant for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The removal of velocity components by this fix is essentially
computing the temperature after a “bias” has been removed from the
velocity of the atoms.  If this compute is used with a fix command
that performs thermostatting then this bias will be subtracted from
each atom, thermostatting of the remaining thermal velocity will be
performed, and the bias will be added back in.  Thermostatting fixes
that work in this way include {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that
constrain molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups of
atoms that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If
needed, the subtracted degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom can be altered using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by
indices 1\textendash{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses
global scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_partial:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/region}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{x} arg = Nx
\sphinxstyleemphasis{y} arg = Ny
\sphinxstyleemphasis{z} arg = Nz
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xy} args = Nx Ny
\sphinxstyleemphasis{yz} args = Ny Nz
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xz} args = Nx Nz

  Nx, Ny, Nz = number of velocity bins in \sphinxstyleemphasis{x}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} dimensions

\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{profile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{profile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bin}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
atoms, after subtracting out a spatially\sphinxhyphen{}averaged center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass
velocity field, before computing the kinetic energy.  This can be
useful for thermostatting a collection of atoms undergoing a complex
flow (e.g. via a profile\sphinxhyphen{}unbiased thermostat (PUT) as described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:evans1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans)}}}}).  A compute of this style can be used by any command
that computes a temperature (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xflag}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yflag}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zflag} settings determine which components of
average velocity are subtracted out.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{binstyle} setting and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ny}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz} arguments determine how bins
are setup to perform spatial averaging.  “Bins” can be 1d slabs, 2d pencils,
or 3d bricks depending on which \sphinxstyleemphasis{binstyle} is used.  The simulation box is
partitioned conceptually into \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx} \(\times\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ny} \(\times\) \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nz}
bins.  Depending on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{binstyle}, you may only specify one or two of these
values; the others are effectively set to 1 (no binning in that dimension).
For non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal (triclinic) simulation boxes, the bins are “tilted” slabs or
pencils or bricks that are parallel to the tilted faces of the box.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{region prism}}}} command for a discussion of the geometry of tilted
boxes in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When a temperature is computed, the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity for the
set of atoms that are both in the compute group and in the same
spatial bin is calculated.  This bias velocity is then subtracted from
the velocities of individual atoms in the bin to yield a thermal
velocity for each atom.  Note that if there is only one atom in the
bin, its thermal velocity will thus be 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After the spatially\sphinxhyphen{}averaged velocity field has been subtracted from
each atom, the temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \left( \frac{\text{dim}}{N} - N_s N_x N_y N_z
                      - \text{extra} \right) \frac{k_B T}{2},\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\); dim = 2 or 3 is the dimensionality of the simulation;
\(N_s =\) 0, 1, 2, or 3 for streaming velocity subtracted in 0, 1, 2, or 3
dimensions, respectively; \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} is the number of  extra degrees of freedom;
\sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is the number of atoms in the group; \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant,
and \(T\) is the absolute temperature.  The \(N_s N_x N_y N_z\) term is
the number of degrees of freedom subtracted to adjust for the removal of the
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity in each direction of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Nx*Ny*Nz} bins, as
discussed in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:evans1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans)}}}} paper.  The extra term defaults to
\(\text{dim} - N_s\) and accounts for overall conservation of
center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity across the group in directions where streaming velocity
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} subtracted. This can be altered using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} keyword is used with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{tensor} value, which is the
default, then a symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is
also calculated by this compute for use in the computation of a
pressure tensor by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}}
command.  The formula for the components of the tensor is the same as
the above expression for \(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2
factor is NOT included and the \(v_i^2\) is replaced by
\(v_{i,x} v_{i,y}\) for the \(xy\) component, and so on.  Note
that because it lacks the 1/2 factor, these tensor components are
twice those of the traditional kinetic energy tensor.  The six
components of the vector are ordered \(xx\), \(yy\),
\(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\), \(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} keyword is used with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin} value, the count of atoms
and computed temperature for each bin are stored for output, as an
array of values, as described below.  The temperature of each bin is
calculated as described above, where the bias velocity is subtracted
and only the remaining thermal velocity of atoms in the bin
contributes to the temperature.  See the note below for how the
temperature is normalized by the degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom of atoms in the
bin.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be
constant for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The removal of the spatially\sphinxhyphen{}averaged velocity field by this fix is
essentially computing the temperature after a “bias” has been removed
from the velocity of the atoms.  If this compute is used with a fix
command that performs thermostatting then this bias will be subtracted
from each atom, thermostatting of the remaining thermal velocity will
be performed, and the bias will be added back in.  Thermostatting
fixes that work in this way include {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that constrain
molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups of atoms
that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If needed, the
subtracted degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom can be altered using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} keyword with a value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin}, the
calculated temperature for each bin includes the degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom
adjustment described in the preceding paragraph for fixes that
constrain molecular motion, as well as the adjustment due to
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option (which defaults to \sphinxstyleemphasis{dim} \sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ns} as described above),
by fractionally applying them based on the fraction of atoms in each
bin. As a result, the bin degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom summed over all bins exactly
equals the degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom used in the scalar temperature calculation,
\(\Sigma N_{\text{DOF}_i} = N_\text{DOF}\) and the corresponding
relation for temperature is also satisfied
(\(\Sigma N_{\text{DOF}_i} T_i = N_\text{DOF} T\)).
These relations will break down in cases for which the adjustment
exceeds the actual number of degrees of freedom in a bin. This could happen
if a bin is empty or in situations in which rigid molecules
are non\sphinxhyphen{}uniformly distributed, in which case the reported
temperature within a bin may not be accurate.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.  Using this compute in conjunction with a
thermostatting fix, as explained there, will effectively implement a
profile\sphinxhyphen{}unbiased thermostat (PUT), as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:evans1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Evans)}}}}.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature).  Depending
on the setting of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} keyword, it also calculates a global
vector or array.  For \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{tensor}, it calculates a vector of
length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by indices 1\textendash{}6.
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{out} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin} it calculates a global array which has 2 columns and
\(N\) rows, where \(N\) is the number of bins.  The first
column contains the number of atoms in that bin.  The second contains
the temperature of that bin, calculated as described above.  The
ordering of rows in the array is as follows.  Bins in \(x\) vary
fastest, then \(y\), then \(z\).  Thus for a \(10\times
10\times 10\) 3d array of bins, there will be 1000 rows.  The bin with
indices \((i_x,i_y,i_z) = (2,3,4)\) would map to row \(M =
10^2(i_z-1) + 10(i_y-1) + i_x = 322\), where the rows are numbered from
1 to 1000 and the bin indices are numbered from 1 to 10 in each
dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These values can be used by any command that uses global scalar or
vector or array values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output
options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.  The array values are “intensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value us in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The first column of array
values are counts; the values in the second column will be in
temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You should not use too large a velocity\sphinxhyphen{}binning grid, especially in
3d.  In the current implementation, the binned velocity averages are
summed across all processors, so this will be inefficient if the grid
is too large, and the operation is performed every timestep, as it
will be for most thermostats.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/ramp}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_deform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/deform}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_profile:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option default is out = tensor.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{compute temp/ramp command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:compute-temp-ramp-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vdim}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vlo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vhi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{clo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/ramp = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vdim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vlo,vhi = subtract velocities between vlo and vhi (velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dim = \sphinxstyleemphasis{x} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{y} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{z}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
clo,chi = lower and upper bound of domain to subtract from (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{units}

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{units} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box}
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2nd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{middle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lattice}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of atoms,
after subtracting out an ramped velocity profile before computing the kinetic
energy.  A compute of this style can be used by any command that computes a
temperature (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The meaning of the arguments for this command which define the
velocity ramp are the same as for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{velocity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{velocity ramp}}}}
command which was presumably used to impose the velocity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After the ramp velocity has been subtracted from the specified
dimension for each atom, the temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{dim}}{2} N k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\)), dim = 2 or 3 is the dimensionality of the simulation,
\(N\) is the number of atoms in the group, \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann
constant, and \(T\) is the absolute temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{units} keyword determines the meaning of the distance units used
for coordinates (\sphinxstyleemphasis{clo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{chi}) and velocities (\sphinxstyleemphasis{vlo}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vhi}).  A \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value
selects standard distance units as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}
command (e.g., \(\AA\) for units = real or metal).  A
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lattice} value means the distance units are in lattice spacings (i.e.,
velocity in lattice spacings per unit time).  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{lattice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lattice}}}}
command must have been previously used to define the lattice spacing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also calculated
by this compute for use in the computation of a pressure tensor by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}} command.  The formula for
the components of the tensor is the same as the above expression for
\(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2 factor is NOT included and
the \(v_i^2\) is replaced by \(v_{i,x} v_{i,y}\) for the
\(xy\) component, and so on.  Note that because it lacks the 1/2
factor, these tensor components are twice those of the traditional
kinetic energy tensor.  The six components of the vector are ordered
\(xx\), \(yy\), \(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\),
\(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be constant
for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The removal of the ramped velocity component by this fix is
essentially computing the temperature after a “bias” has been removed
from the velocity of the atoms.  If this compute is used with a fix
command that performs thermostatting then this bias will be subtracted
from each atom, thermostatting of the remaining thermal velocity will
be performed, and the bias will be added back in.  Thermostatting
fixes that work in this way include {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that
constrain molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups of
atoms that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If
needed, the subtracted degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom can be altered using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by
indices 1\textendash{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses
global scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_ramp:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}},

\index{compute temp/region@\spxentry{compute temp/region}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute temp/region command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:compute-temp-region-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{region\PYGZhy{}ID}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/region = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
region\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of region to use for choosing atoms

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{k}{region }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{boundary}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of atoms in a
geometric region.  This can be useful for thermostatting one portion of the
simulation box.  For example, a McDLT simulation where one side is cooled, and
the other side is heated.  A compute of this style can be used by any command
that computes a temperature (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that a \sphinxstyleemphasis{region}\sphinxhyphen{}style temperature can be used to thermostat with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}, but should probably not be used with
Nose\textendash{}Hoover style fixes ({\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}},
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nph}}}}) if the degrees of freedom included in the computed
temperature vary with time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{dim}}{2} N k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE = is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\)), dim = 2 or 3 is the dimensionality of the simulation,
\(N\) is the  number of atoms in both the group and region, \(k_B\) is
the Boltzmann constant, and \(T\) temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also calculated
by this compute for use in the computation of a pressure tensor by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}} command.  The formula for
the components of the tensor is the same as the above expression for
\(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2 factor is NOT included and
the \(v_i^2\) is replaced by \(v_{i,x} v_{i,y}\) for the
\(xy\) component, and so on.  Note that because it lacks the 1/2
factor, these tensor components are twice those of the traditional
kinetic energy tensor.  The six components of the vector are ordered
\(xx\), \(yy\), \(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\),
\(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is calculated each
time the temperature is evaluated since it is assumed atoms can
enter/leave the region.  Thus there is no need to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic}
option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command for this
compute style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The removal of atoms outside the region by this fix is essentially
computing the temperature after a “bias” has been removed, which in
this case is the velocity of any atoms outside the region.  If this
compute is used with a fix command that performs thermostatting then
this bias will be subtracted from each atom, thermostatting of the
remaining thermal velocity will be performed, and the bias will be
added back in.  Thermostatting fixes that work in this way include
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.  This means that when this compute
is used to calculate the temperature for any of the thermostatting
fixes via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix modify temp}}}} command, the thermostat
will operate only on atoms that are currently in the geometric region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike other compute styles that calculate temperature, this compute
does not subtract out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that constrain
motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This is because those degrees of freedom (e.g., a
constrained bond) could apply to sets of atoms that straddle the
region boundary, and hence the concept is somewhat ill\sphinxhyphen{}defined.  If
needed the number of subtracted degrees of freedom can be set
explicitly using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by
indices 1\textendash{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses
global scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressure}}}}

\index{compute temp/region/eff@\spxentry{compute temp/region/eff}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute temp/region/eff command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:compute-temp-region-eff-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{ID}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/region/eff = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{eff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boundary}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
nuclei and electrons in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{electron force field}}}}
model, within a geometric region using the electron force field.
A compute of this style can be used by commands that compute a
temperature (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The operation of this compute is exactly like that described by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_region::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/region}}}} command, except that
the formulas for the temperature (scalar) and diagonal components of
the symmetric tensor (vector) include the radial electron velocity
contributions, as discussed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_eff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/eff}}}} command.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by
indices 1\textendash{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses
global scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_region_eff:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EFF package.  It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\index{compute temp/rotate@\spxentry{compute temp/rotate}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute temp/rotate command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:compute-temp-rotate-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rotate}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/rotate = style name of this compute command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Tbead}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{bead}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rotate}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
atoms, after subtracting out the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity and angular velocity
of the group.  This is useful if the group is expected to have a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero net
velocity and/or global rotation motion for some reason.  A compute of this
style can be used by any command that computes a temperature
(e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
After the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity and angular velocity has been subtracted from
each atom, the temperature is calculated by the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{KE} = \frac{\text{dim}}{2} N k_B T,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where KE is the total kinetic energy of the group of atoms (sum of
\(\frac12 m v^2\)), dim = 2 or 3 is the dimensionality of the simulation,
\(N\) is the number of atoms in the group, \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann
constant, and \(T\) is the absolute temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also calculated
by this compute for use in the computation of a pressure tensor by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}} command.  The formula for
the components of the tensor is the same as the above expression for
\(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2 factor is NOT included and
the \(v_i^2\) is replaced by \(v_{i,x} v_{i,y}\) for the
\(xy\) component, and so on.  Note that because it lacks the 1/2
factor, these tensor components are twice those of the traditional
kinetic energy tensor.  The six components of the vector are ordered
\(xx\), \(yy\), \(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\),
\(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be
constant for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The removal of the center\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}mass velocity and angular velocity by this fix is
essentially computing the temperature after a “bias” has been removed from the
velocity of the atoms.  If this compute is used with a fix command
that performs thermostatting then this bias will be subtracted from
each atom, thermostatting of the remaining thermal velocity will be
performed, and the bias will be added back in.  Thermostatting fixes
that work in this way include {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_rescale::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/rescale}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_temp_berendsen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix temp/berendsen}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes that
constrain molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups of
atoms that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If
needed, the subtracted degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom can be altered using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by
indices 1\sphinxhyphen{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses global
scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto
output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}COMPUTE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_rotate:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{compute temp/sphere@\spxentry{compute temp/sphere}}\ignorespaces 

\section{compute temp/sphere command}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:compute-temp-sphere-command}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID, group\sphinxhyphen{}ID are documented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temp/sphere = style name of this compute command

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dof}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} value = bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID
  bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of a temperature compute that removes a velocity bias
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dof} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate}
  all = compute temperature of translational and rotational degrees of freedom
  rotate = compute temperature of just rotational degrees of freedom
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mobile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bias}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tempCOM}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myTemp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mobile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dof}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rotate}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a computation that calculates the temperature of a group of
spherical particles, including a contribution from both their
translational and rotational kinetic energy.  This differs from the
usual {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} command, which assumes point
particles with only translational kinetic energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both point and finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles can be included in the group.
Point particles do not rotate, so they have only three translational
degrees of freedom.  For 3d spherical particles, each has six degrees of
freedom (three translational, three rotational).  For 2d spherical particles,
each has three degrees of freedom (two translational, one rotational).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This choice for degrees of freedom (DOF) assumes that all finite\sphinxhyphen{}size
spherical particles in your model will freely rotate, sampling all
their rotational DOF.  It is possible to use a combination of
interaction potentials and fixes that induce no torque or otherwise
constrain some of all of your particles so that this is not the case.
Then there are less DOF and you should use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify
extra/dof}}}} command to adjust the DOF accordingly.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The translational kinetic energy is computed the same as is described
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}} command.  The rotational
kinetic energy is computed as \(\frac12 I \omega^2\), where \(I\) is
the moment of inertia for a sphere and \(\omega\) is the particle’s angular
velocity.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{dimension::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{2d models}}}}, particles are treated as
spheres, not disks, meaning their moment of inertia will be the same
as in 3d.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A kinetic energy tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also
calculated by this compute.  The formula for the components of the
tensor is the same as the above formulas, except that \(v^2\) and
\(\omega^2\) are replaced by \(v_x v_y\) and \(\omega_x
\omega_y\) for the \(xy\) component.  The six components of the
vector are ordered \(xx\), \(yy\), \(zz\), \(xy\),
\(xz\), \(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
A symmetric tensor, stored as a six\sphinxhyphen{}element vector, is also calculated
by this compute for use in the computation of a pressure tensor by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pressue}}}} command.  The formula for
the components of the tensor is the same as the above expression for
\(E_\mathrm{kin}\), except that the 1/2 factor is NOT included and
the \(v_i^2\) and \(\omega^2\) are replaced by \(v_x v_y\)
and \(\omega_x \omega_y\) for the \(xy\) component, and so on.
Note that because it lacks the 1/2 factor, these tensor components are
twice those of the traditional kinetic energy tensor.  The six
components of the vector are ordered \(xx\), \(yy\),
\(zz\), \(xy\), \(xz\), \(yz\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms contributing to the temperature is assumed to be
constant for the duration of the run; use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dynamic} option of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}} command if this is not the case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute subtracts out translational degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom due to fixes
that constrain molecular motion, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rigid}}}}.  This means the temperature of groups
of atoms that include these constraints will be computed correctly.  If
needed, the subtracted degrees of freedom can be altered using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{extra/dof} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute\_modify}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_thermostat::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto thermostat}}}} page for a
discussion of different ways to compute temperature and perform
thermostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword/value option pairs are used in the following ways.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} keyword, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias\sphinxhyphen{}ID} refers to the ID of a temperature
compute that removes a “bias” velocity from each atom.  This allows
compute temp/sphere to compute its thermal temperature after the
translational kinetic energy components have been altered in a
prescribed way (e.g., to remove a flow velocity profile).  Thermostats
that use this compute will work with this bias term.  See the doc
pages for individual computes that calculate a temperature and the doc
pages for fixes that perform thermostatting for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dof} keyword, a setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} calculates a temperature
that includes both translational and rotational degrees of freedom.
A setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{rotate} calculates a temperature that includes only
rotational degrees of freedom.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Output info}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:output-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compute calculates a global scalar (the temperature) and a global
vector of length 6 (symmetric tensor), which can be accessed by
indices 1\textendash{}6.  These values can be used by any command that uses
global scalar or vector values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value calculated by this compute is “intensive”.  The
vector values are “extensive”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar value is in temperature {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  The vector
values are in energy {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix requires that atoms store torque and angular velocity (omega)
and a radius as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All particles in the group must be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres, or point
particles with radius = 0.0.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/asphere}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are no bias and dof = all.
