\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bop:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bop}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{CdTe\PYGZus{}bop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Te}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{save}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{CdTe.bop.table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Te}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Te}
\PYG{k}{comm\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{14.70}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bop:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bop} pair style computes Bond\sphinxhyphen{}Order Potentials (BOP) based on
quantum mechanical theory incorporating both \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) bonding.
By analytically deriving the BOP from quantum mechanical theory its
transferability to different phases can approach that of quantum
mechanical methods.  This potential is similar to the original BOP
developed by Pettifor ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:pettifor-1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Pettifor\_1}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:pettifor-2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Pettifor\_2}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:pettifor-3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Pettifor\_3}}}}) and later updated
by Murdick, Zhou, and Ward ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:murdick}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Murdick}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:ward}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ward}}}}).
Currently, BOP potential files for these systems are provided with
LAMMPS: AlCu, CCu, CdTe, CdTeSe, CdZnTe, CuH, GaAs.  A system with
only a subset of these elements, including a single element (e.g. C or
Cu or Al or Ga or Zn or CdZn), can also be modeled by using the
appropriate alloy file and assigning all atom types to the
single element or subset of elements via the pair\_coeff command, as
discussed below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The BOP potential consists of three terms:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{j=i_1}^{i_N} \phi_{ij} \left( r_{ij} \right) - \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{j=i_1}^{i_N} \beta_{\sigma,ij} \left( r_{ij} \right) \cdot \Theta_{\sigma,ij} - \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{j=i_1}^{i_N} \beta_{\pi,ij} \left( r_{ij} \right) \cdot \Theta_{\pi,ij} + U_{prom}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\phi_{ij}(r_{ij})\) is a short\sphinxhyphen{}range two\sphinxhyphen{}body function
representing the repulsion between a pair of ion cores,
\(\beta_{\sigma,ij}(r_{ij})\) and \(\beta_{\sigma,ij}(r_{ij})\)
are respectively sigma and \(\pi\) bond integrals, \(\Theta_{\sigma,ij}\)
and \(\Theta_{\pi,ij}\) are \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\)
bond\sphinxhyphen{}orders, and U\_prom is the promotion energy for sp\sphinxhyphen{}valent systems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The detailed formulas for this potential are given in Ward
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:ward}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ward}}}}); here we provide only a brief description.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The repulsive energy \(\phi_{ij}(r_{ij})\) and the bond integrals
\(\beta_{\sigma,ij}(r_{ij})\) and \(\beta_{\phi,ij}(r_{ij})\) are functions of the
interatomic distance \(r_{ij}\) between atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}.  Each of these
potentials has a smooth cutoff at a radius of \(r_{cut,ij}\).  These
smooth cutoffs ensure stable behavior at situations with high sampling
near the cutoff such as melts and surfaces.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bond\sphinxhyphen{}orders can be viewed as environment\sphinxhyphen{}dependent local variables
that are ij bond specific.  The maximum value of the \(\sigma\)
bond\sphinxhyphen{}order (\(\Theta_{\sigma}\) is 1, while that of the \(\pi\)
bond\sphinxhyphen{}order (\(\Theta_{\pi}\)) is 2, attributing to a maximum value
of the total bond\sphinxhyphen{}order (\(\Theta_{\sigma}+\Theta_{\pi}\)) of 3.
The \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) bond\sphinxhyphen{}orders reflect the ubiquitous
single\sphinxhyphen{}, double\sphinxhyphen{}, and triple\sphinxhyphen{} bond behavior of chemistry. Their
analytical expressions can be derived from tight\sphinxhyphen{} binding theory by
recursively expanding an inter\sphinxhyphen{}site Green’s function as a continued
fraction. To accurately represent the bonding with a computationally
efficient potential formulation suitable for MD simulations, the derived
BOP only takes (and retains) the first two levels of the recursive
representations for both the \(\sigma\) and the \(\pi\) bond\sphinxhyphen{}orders. Bond\sphinxhyphen{}order
terms can be understood in terms of molecular orbital hopping paths
based upon the Cyrot\sphinxhyphen{}Lackmann theorem ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:pettifor-1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Pettifor\_1}}}}).
The \(\sigma\) bond\sphinxhyphen{}order with a half\sphinxhyphen{}full valence shell is used to
interpolate the bond\sphinxhyphen{}order expression that incorporated explicit valance
band filling.  This \(\pi\) bond\sphinxhyphen{}order expression also contains also contains
a three\sphinxhyphen{}member ring term that allows implementation of an asymmetric
density of states, which helps to either stabilize or destabilize
close\sphinxhyphen{}packed structures.  The \(\pi\) bond\sphinxhyphen{}order includes hopping paths of
length 4.  This enables the incorporation of dihedral angles effects.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that unlike for other potentials, cutoffs for BOP
potentials are not set in the pair\_style or pair\_coeff command; they
are specified in the BOP potential files themselves.  Likewise, the
BOP potential files list atomic masses; thus you do not need to use
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}} command to specify them.  Note that for BOP
potentials with hydrogen, you will likely want to set the mass of H
atoms to be 10x or 20x larger to avoid having to use a tiny timestep.
You can do this by using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}} command after using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command to read the BOP potential
file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
One option can be specified as a keyword with the pair\_style command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{save} keyword gives you the option to calculate in advance and
store a set of distances, angles, and derivatives of angles.  The
default is to not do this, but to calculate them on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly each time
they are needed.  The former may be faster, but takes more memory.
The latter requires less memory, but may be slower.  It is best to
test this option to optimize the speed of BOP for your particular
system configuration.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bop} style which
specifies a BOP potential file, with parameters for all needed
elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying
N additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command,
where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of BOP elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine the CdTe.bop file has BOP values for Cd
and Te.  If your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you want the
first 3 to be Cd, and the fourth to be Te, you would use the following
pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CdTe}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Te}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Cd arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the Cd
element in the BOP file.  The final Te argument maps LAMMPS atom type
4 to the Te element in the BOP file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
BOP files in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potentials} directory of the LAMMPS distribution
have a “.bop” suffix.  The potentials are in tabulated form containing
pre\sphinxhyphen{}tabulated pair functions for phi\_ij(r\_ij), beta\_(sigma,ij)(r\_ij),
and beta\_pi,ij)(r\_ij).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters/coefficients format for the different kinds of BOP
files are given below with variables matching the formulation of Ward
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:ward}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ward}}}}) and Zhou ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:zhou1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Zhou}}}}). Each header line containing a
“:” is preceded by a blank line.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No angular table file format}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters/coefficients format for the BOP potentials input file
containing pre\sphinxhyphen{}tabulated functions of g is given below with variables
matching the formulation of Ward ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:ward}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ward}}}}).  This format also
assumes the angular functions have the formulation of ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:ward}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ward}}}}).
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: \# elements N

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first line is followed by N lines containing the atomic
number, mass, and element symbol of each element.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following the definition of the elements several global variables for
the tabulated functions are given.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: nr, nBOt (nr is the number of divisions the radius is broken
into for function tables and MUST be a factor of 5; nBOt is the number
of divisions for the tabulated values of THETA\_(S,ij)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: delta\_1\sphinxhyphen{}delta\_7 (if all are not used in the particular

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
formulation, set unused values to 0.0)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following this N lines for e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_N containing p\_pi.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 3: p\_pi (for e\_1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 4: p\_pi (for e\_2 and continues to e\_N)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains several pair constants for the number of
interaction types e\_i\sphinxhyphen{}e\_j, with i=1\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N, j=i\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: r\_cut (for e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1 interactions)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: c\_sigma, a\_sigma, c\_pi, a\_pi

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 3: delta\_sigma, delta\_pi

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 4: f\_sigma, k\_sigma, delta\_3 (This delta\_3 is similar to that of
the previous section but is interaction type dependent)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains a line for each three body interaction type
e\_j\sphinxhyphen{}e\_i\sphinxhyphen{}e\_k with i=0\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N, j=0\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N, k=j\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: g\_(sigma0), g\_(sigma1), g\_(sigma2) (These are coefficients for
g\_(sigma,jik)(THETA\_ijk) for e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1 interaction. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bop:ward}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ward}}}}
contains the full expressions for the constants as functions of
b\_(sigma,ijk), p\_(sigma,ijk), u\_(sigma,ijk))

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: g\_(sigma0), g\_(sigma1), g\_(sigma2) (for e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_2)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains a block for each interaction type for the
phi\_ij(r\_ij).  Each block has nr entries with 5 entries per line.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: phi(r1), phi(r2), phi(r3), phi(r4), phi(r5) (for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1
interaction type)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: phi(r6), phi(r7), phi(r8), phi(r9), phi(r10) (this continues
until nr)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line nr/5\_1: phi(r1), phi(r2), phi(r3), phi(r4), phi(r5), (for the
e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1 interaction type)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains a block for each interaction type for the
beta\_(sigma,ij)(r\_ij).  Each block has nr entries with 5 entries per
line.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: beta\_sigma(r1), beta\_sigma(r2), beta\_sigma(r3), beta\_sigma(r4),
beta\_sigma(r5) (for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1 interaction type)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: beta\_sigma(r6), beta\_sigma(r7), beta\_sigma(r8), beta\_sigma(r9),
beta\_sigma(r10) (this continues until nr)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line nr/5+1: beta\_sigma(r1), beta\_sigma(r2), beta\_sigma(r3),
beta\_sigma(r4), beta\_sigma(r5) (for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_2 interaction type)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains a block for each interaction type for
beta\_(pi,ij)(r\_ij).  Each block has nr entries with 5 entries per line.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: beta\_pi(r1), beta\_pi(r2), beta\_pi(r3), beta\_pi(r4), beta\_pi(r5)
(for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_1 interaction type)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: beta\_pi(r6), beta\_pi(r7), beta\_pi(r8), beta\_pi(r9),
beta\_pi(r10) (this continues until nr)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line nr/5+1: beta\_pi(r1), beta\_pi(r2), beta\_pi(r3), beta\_pi(r4),
beta\_pi(r5) (for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_2 interaction type)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains a block for each interaction type for the
THETA\_(S,ij)((THETA\_(sigma,ij))\textasciicircum{}(1/2), f\_(sigma,ij)).  Each block has
nBOt entries with 5 entries per line.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: THETA\_(S,ij)(r1), THETA\_(S,ij)(r2), THETA\_(S,ij)(r3),
THETA\_(S,ij)(r4), THETA\_(S,ij)(r5) (for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_2 interaction type)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: THETA\_(S,ij)(r6), THETA\_(S,ij)(r7), THETA\_(S,ij)(r8),
THETA\_(S,ij)(r9), THETA\_(S,ij)(r10) (this continues until nBOt)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line nBOt/5+1: THETA\_(S,ij)(r1), THETA\_(S,ij)(r2), THETA\_(S,ij)(r3),
THETA\_(S,ij)(r4), THETA\_(S,ij)(r5) (for the e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_2 interaction type)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section contains a block of N lines for e\_1\sphinxhyphen{}e\_N
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: delta\textasciicircum{}mu (for e\_1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: delta\textasciicircum{}mu (for e\_2 and repeats to e\_N)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last section contains more constants for e\_i\sphinxhyphen{}e\_j interactions with
i=0\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N, j=i\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}N
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 1: (A\_ij)\textasciicircum{}(mu*nu) (for e1\sphinxhyphen{}e1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line 2: (A\_ij)\textasciicircum{}(mu*nu) (for e1\sphinxhyphen{}e2 and repeats as above)

\end{itemize}

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bop:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mix, shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bop:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the MANYBODY package.  They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair potentials require the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newtion}}}} setting to be
“on” for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style bop is not compatible with being used as a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style with
doc:\sphinxtitleref{hybrid pair styles \textless{}pair\_hybrid\textgreater{}}. Pair style bop is also not
compatible with {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{multi\sphinxhyphen{}cutoff neighbor lists}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{multi\sphinxhyphen{}cutoff communitcation}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The .bop.table potential files provided with LAMMPS (see the
potentials directory) are parameterized for metal {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.
You can use the BOP potential with any LAMMPS units, but you would need
to create your own BOP potential file with coefficients listed in the
appropriate units if your simulation does not use “metal” units.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{born} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/msm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/wolf}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/msm} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/wolf} args = alpha cutoff (cutoff2)
  alpha = damping parameter (inverse distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/dsf} args = alpha cutoff (cutoff2)
  alpha = damping parameter (inverse distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{born} style computes the Born\sphinxhyphen{}Mayer\sphinxhyphen{}Huggins or Tosi/Fumi
potential described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born:fumitosi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fumi and Tosi)}}}}, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = A \exp \left(\frac{\sigma - r}{\rho} \right) -
\frac{C}{r^6} + \frac{D}{r^8} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\sigma\) is an interaction\sphinxhyphen{}dependent length parameter,
\(\rho\) is an ionic\sphinxhyphen{}pair dependent length parameter, and
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/msm} add a Coulombic term as
described for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/cut}}}} pair styles.  An additional
damping factor is applied to the Coulombic term so it can be used in
conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command and its
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} of \sphinxstyleemphasis{msm} option.  The Coulombic cutoff specified for
this style means that pairwise interactions within this distance are
computed directly; interactions outside that distance are computed in
reciprocal space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If one cutoff is specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/msm} style, it is used for both the A,C,D and Coulombic
terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, the first is used as the cutoff
for the A,C,D terms, and the second is the cutoff for the Coulombic
term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/wolf} style adds a Coulombic term as described for the
Wolf potential in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coul/wolf}}}} pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/dsf} style computes the Coulomb contribution with the
damped shifted force model as in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coul/dsf}}}} style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these potentials are related to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Buckingham potential}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\rho\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C (energy units * distance units\textasciicircum{}6)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
D (energy units * distance units\textasciicircum{}8)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second coefficient, rho, must be greater than zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global A,C,D
cutoff specified in the pair\_style command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/wolf} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/dsf} no
Coulombic cutoff can be specified for an individual I,J type pair.
All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff specified in the
pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option
for the energy of the exp(), 1/r\textasciicircum{}6, and 1/r\textasciicircum{}8 portion of the pair
interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long} pair style supports the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option to tabulate the
short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles support the pair\_modify tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range
tail corrections to energy and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thess styles writes thei information to binary {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{restart}}}}
files, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long} style is part of the KSPACE package.  It is only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/dsf} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/wolf} pair styles are part of the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with
that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page
for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{pair\_style born/gauss command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:pair-style-born-gauss-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{born}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gauss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
born/gauss = name of the pair style

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{born}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{gauss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.2464e13}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.48}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.042644277}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.44}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.56}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/gauss} computes pairwise interactions from a combination of a Born\sphinxhyphen{}Mayer
repulsive term and a Gaussian attractive term according to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:bomont}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bomont)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = A_0 \exp \left( -\alpha r \right) - A_1 \exp\left[ -\beta \left(r - r_0 \right)^2 \right]
    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (1/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_1\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\beta\) (1/(distance units)\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global cutoff is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_born_gauss:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all I,J
pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table options are not relevant for
this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\section{pair\_style bpm/spring command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:pair-style-bpm-spring-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spring}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spring}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpm/spring} computes pairwise forces with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F = k (r - r_c)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k\) is a stiffness and \(r_c\) is the cutoff length.
An additional damping force is also applied to interacting
particles. The force is proportional to the difference in the
normal velocity of particles
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_D = - \gamma w (\hat{r} \bullet \vec{v})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\gamma\) is the damping strength, \(\hat{r}\) is the
radial normal vector, \(\vec{v}\) is the velocity difference
between the two particles, and \(w\) is a smoothing factor.
This smoothing factor is constructed such that damping forces go to zero
as particles come out of contact to avoid discontinuities. It is
given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}w = 1.0 - \left( \frac{r}{r_c} \right)^8 .\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is designed for use in a spring\sphinxhyphen{}based bonded particle
model.  It mirrors the construction of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bpm/spring}}}} bond style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair interaction is always applied to pairs of non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded particles
that are within the interaction distance. For pairs of bonded particles
that are within the interaction distance, there is the option to either
include this pair interaction and overlay the pair force over the bond
force or to exclude this pair interaction such that the two particles
only interact via the bond force. See discussion of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair}
option for BPM bond styles and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}}
command in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bpm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{how to}}}} page on BPMs for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k\)             (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\)           (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)        (force/velocity units)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the A coefficient and cutoff
distance for this pair style can be mixed.  A is always mixed via a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric} rule.  The cutoff is mixed according to the pair\_modify
mix value.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the
“pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option, since the pair interaction goes to 0.0 at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and tail options are not
relevant for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\label{\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the BPM package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\section{pair\_style brownian command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:pair-style-brownian-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/omp}


\section{pair\_style brownian/poly command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:pair-style-brownian-poly-command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/poly/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flaglog}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flagfld}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutinner}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flagHI}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flagVF}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/poly}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mu = dynamic viscosity (dynamic viscosity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flaglog = 0/1 log terms in the lubrication approximation on/off

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flagfld = 0/1 to include/exclude Fast Lubrication Dynamics effects

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutinner = inner cutoff distance (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = outer cutoff for interactions (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
t\_target = target temp of the system (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = seed for the random number generator (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flagHI (optional) = 0/1 to include/exclude 1/r hydrodynamic interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flagVF (optional) = 0/1 to include/exclude volume fraction corrections in the long\sphinxhyphen{}range isotropic terms

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{brownian}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5878567}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} (assuming radius = 1)}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.8}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{brownian/poly} compute Brownian forces and
torques on finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particles.  The former requires
monodisperse spherical particles; the latter allows for polydisperse
spherical particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are designed to be used with either the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lubricate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lubricate}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lubricateU::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style
lubricateU}}}} commands to provide thermostatting when
dissipative lubrication forces are acting.  Thus the parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flaglog}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{flagfld}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutinner}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} should be specified
consistent with the settings in the lubrication pair styles.  For
details, refer to either of the lubrication pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{t\_target} setting is used to specify the target temperature of
the system.  The random number \sphinxstyleemphasis{seed} is used to generate random
numbers for the thermostatting procedure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{flagHI} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{flagVF} settings are optional.  Neither should be
used, or both must be defined.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutinner (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two coefficients are optional.  If neither is specified, the two
cutoffs specified in the pair\_style command are used.  Otherwise both
must be specified.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the two cutoff distances for these
pair styles can be mixed.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See
the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for these pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_brownian:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles are part of the COLLOID package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only spherical monodisperse particles are allowed for pair\_style
brownian.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only spherical particles are allowed for pair\_style brownian/poly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are only compatible with the following wall fixes:
doc:\sphinxtitleref{fix wall/lj93, fix wall/lj126, fix wall/lj1043, fix wall/colloid,
fix wall/harmonic, fix wall/lepton, fix wall/morse, fix wall/table
\textless{}fix\_wall\textgreater{}}.

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/msm}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{buck} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for Buckingham interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/cut} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Buckingham (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Buckingham (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/msm} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Buckingham (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck} style computes a Buckingham potential (exp/6 instead of
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones 12/6) given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = A e^{-r / \rho} - \frac{C}{r^6} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\rho\) is an ionic\sphinxhyphen{}pair dependent length parameter, and
\(r_c\) is the cutoff on both terms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/msm} add a
Coulombic term as described for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/cut}}}} pair styles.
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{buc/coul/msm}, an additional damping factor
is applied to the Coulombic term so it can be used in conjunction with
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm}
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{msm} option.  The Coulombic cutoff specified for this style means
that pairwise interactions within this distance are computed directly;
interactions outside that distance are computed in reciprocal space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If one cutoff is specified for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/cut} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/msm} styles, it is used for both the
A,C and Coulombic terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, the first is
used as the cutoff for the A,C terms, and the second is the cutoff for
the Coulombic term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these potentials are related to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Born\sphinxhyphen{}Mayer\sphinxhyphen{}Huggins potential}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For all these pair styles, the terms with A and C are always
cutoff.  The additional Coulombic term can be cutoff or long\sphinxhyphen{}range (no
cutoff) depending on whether the style name includes coul/cut or
coul/long or coul/msm.  If you wish the C/r\textasciicircum{}6 term to be long\sphinxhyphen{}range
(no cutoff), then see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck_long::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck/long/coul/long}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\rho\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C (energy\sphinxhyphen{}distance\textasciicircum{}6 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second coefficient, \(\rho\), must be greater than zero.
The coefficients A, \(\rho\), and C can be written as analytical expressions
of \(\epsilon\) and \(\sigma\), in analogy to the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck:khrapak}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Khrapak)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global
A,C and Coulombic cutoffs are used.  If only one cutoff is specified,
it is used as the cutoff for both A,C and Coulombic interactions for
this type pair.  If both coefficients are specified, they are used as
the A,C and Coulombic cutoffs for this type pair.  You cannot specify
2 cutoffs for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck}, since it has no Coulombic terms.
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long} only the LJ cutoff can be specified since a
Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J type pair.
All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff specified in the
pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option
for the energy of the exp() and 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long} pair style supports the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option to tabulate the
short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles support the pair\_modify tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range
tail corrections to energy and pressure for the A,C terms in the
pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long} style is part of the KSPACE package.  They are
only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\section{pair\_style buck6d/coul/gauss/long command}

\subsection{Syntax}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d/coul/gauss} styles evaluate vdW and Coulomb
interactions following the MOF\sphinxhyphen{}FF force field after
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss:schmid}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Schmid)}}}}. The vdW term of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d} styles
computes a dispersion damped Buckingham potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = A e^{-\kappa r} - \frac{C}{r^6} \cdot \frac{1}{1 + D r^{14}} \qquad r < r_c \\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where A and C are a force constant, \(\kappa\) is an ionic\sphinxhyphen{}pair dependent
reciprocal length parameter, D is a dispersion correction parameter,
and the cutoff \(r_c\) truncates the interaction distance.
The first term in the potential corresponds to the Buckingham
repulsion term and the second term to the dispersion attraction with
a damping correction analog to the Grimme correction used in DFT.
The latter corrects for artifacts occurring at short distances which
become an issue for soft vdW potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d} styles include a smoothing function which is invoked
according to the global smoothing parameter within the specified
cutoff.  Hereby a parameter of i.e. 0.9 invokes the smoothing
within 90\% of the cutoff.  No smoothing is applied at a value
of 1.0. For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{gauss/dsf} style this smoothing is only applicable
for the dispersion damped Buckingham potential. For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{gauss/long}
styles the smoothing function can also be invoked for the real
space coulomb interactions which enforce continuous energies and
forces at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d/coul/gauss/dsf} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d/coul/gauss/long}
evaluate a Coulomb potential using spherical Gaussian type charge
distributions which effectively dampen electrostatic interactions
for high charges at close distances.  The electrostatic potential
is thus evaluated as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C_{q_i q_j}}{\epsilon r_{ij}}\,\, \textrm{erf}\left(\alpha_{ij} r_{ij}\right)\quad\quad\quad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where C is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\)
are the charges on the two atoms, epsilon is the dielectric constant which
can be set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command, \(\alpha\)
is the ion pair dependent damping parameter and erf() is the
error\sphinxhyphen{}function.  The cutoff \(r_c\) truncates the interaction distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d/coul/gauss/dsf} computes the Coulomb interaction
via the damped shifted force model described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss:fennell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fennell)}}}}
approximating an Ewald sum similar to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair coul/dsf}}}}
styles. In \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck6d/coul/gauss/long} an additional damping factor is
applied to the Coulombic term so it can be used in conjunction with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm}
options. The Coulombic cutoff in this case separates the real and
reciprocal space evaluation of the Ewald sum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If one cutoff is specified it is used for both the vdW and Coulomb
terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, the first is used as the cutoff
for the vdW terms, and the second is the cutoff for the Coulombic term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\rho\) (distance\textasciicircum{}\sphinxhyphen{}1 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C (energy\sphinxhyphen{}distance\textasciicircum{}6 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
D (distance\textasciicircum{}14 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (distance\textasciicircum{}\sphinxhyphen{}1 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second coefficient, \(\rho\), must be greater than zero. The
latter coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global vdW cutoff
is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy. Instead the smoothing function should be applied
by setting the global smoothing parameter to a value \textless{} 1.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles are part of the MOFFF package.  They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}

\section{pair\_style buck/long/coul/long command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long:pair-style-buck-long-coul-long-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/long/coul/long/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{buck}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flag\PYGZus{}buck}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flag\PYGZus{}coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{cutoff2}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flag\_buck = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use Kspace long\sphinxhyphen{}range summation for the dispersion term 1/r\textasciicircum{}6
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cut} = use a cutoff
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flag\_coul = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use Kspace long\sphinxhyphen{}range summation for the Coulombic term 1/r
\sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = omit the Coulombic term
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for Buckingham (and Coulombic if only 1 cutoff) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/long/coul/long} style computes a Buckingham potential (exp/6
instead of Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones 12/6) and Coulombic potential, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = & A e^{-r / \rho} - \frac{C}{r^6} \qquad r < r_c \\
E = & \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.  If one cutoff is specified in the pair\_style
command, it is used for both the Buckingham and Coulombic terms.  If
two cutoffs are specified, they are used as cutoffs for the Buckingham
and Coulombic terms respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The purpose of this pair style is to capture long\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions
resulting from both attractive 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 Buckingham and Coulombic 1/r
interactions.  This is done by use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_buck} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul}
settings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck_long:ismail}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ismail}}}} paper has more details on when it is
appropriate to include long\sphinxhyphen{}range 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 interactions, using this
potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_buck} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, no cutoff is used on the Buckingham
1/r\textasciicircum{}6 dispersion term.  The long\sphinxhyphen{}range portion can be calculated by
using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style ewald/disp or pppm/disp}}}}
commands.  The specified Buckingham cutoff then determines which
portion of the Buckingham interactions are computed directly by the
pair potential versus which part is computed in reciprocal space via
the Kspace style.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_buck} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}, the Buckingham
interactions are simply cutoff, as with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, no cutoff is used on the Coulombic
interactions.  The long\sphinxhyphen{}range portion can calculated by using any of
several {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command options such as
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald}.  Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_buck} is also set to long, then
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald/disp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm/disp} Kspace style needs to be used to
perform the long\sphinxhyphen{}range calculations for both the Buckingham and
Coulombic interactions.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}, Coulombic
interactions are not computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rho (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C (energy\sphinxhyphen{}distance\textasciicircum{}6 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second coefficient, rho, must be greater than zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global
Buckingham and Coulombic cutoffs specified in the pair\_style command
are used.  If only one cutoff is specified, it is used as the cutoff
for both Buckingham and Coulombic interactions for this type pair.  If
both coefficients are specified, they are used as the Buckingham and
Coulombic cutoffs for this type pair.  Note that if you are using
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_buck} set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, you cannot specify a Buckingham cutoff for
an atom type pair, since only one global Buckingham cutoff is allowed.
Similarly, if you are using \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul} set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, you cannot
specify a Coulombic cutoff for an atom type pair, since only one
global Coulombic cutoff is allowed.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_buck_long:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the exp() and 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 portion of the pair
interaction, assuming \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_buck} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the Buckingham portion of the pair
interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and
table/disp options since they can tabulate the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of
the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic and dispersion interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer}
keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command, meaning the
pairwise forces can be partitioned by distance at different levels of
the rRESPA hierarchy.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for
details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_charmm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm/implicit} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/msm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/charmmfsh} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/long}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm} args = inner outer (inner2) (outer2)
  inner, outer = global switching cutoffs for Lennard Jones (and Coulombic if only 2 args)
  inner2, outer2 = global switching cutoffs for Coulombic (optional)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm/implicit} args = inner outer (inner2) (outer2)
  inner, outer = global switching cutoffs for LJ (and Coulombic if only 2 args)
  inner2, outer2 = global switching cutoffs for Coulombic (optional)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/long} args = inner outer (cutoff)
  inner, outer = global switching cutoffs for LJ (and Coulombic if only 2 args)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional, outer is Coulombic cutoff if only 2 args)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/msm} args = inner outer (cutoff)
  inner, outer = global switching cutoffs for LJ (and Coulombic if only 2 args)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional, outer is Coulombic cutoff if only 2 args)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/charmmfsh} args = inner outer (cutoff)
  inner, outer = global cutoffs for LJ (and Coulombic if only 2 args)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional, outer is Coulombic cutoff if only 2 args)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/long} args = inner outer (cutoff)
  inner, outer = global cutoffs for LJ (and Coulombic if only 2 args)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional, outer is Coulombic cutoff if only 2 args)
\end{sphinxalltt}
