\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_charmm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles compute Lennard Jones (LJ) and Coulombic
interactions with additional switching or shifting functions that ramp
the energy and/or force smoothly to zero between an inner and outer
cutoff.  They implement the widely used CHARMM force field, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bioFF::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto discussion on biomolecular force fields}}}} for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm} (not \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmmfsw} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmmfsh}) in their
name are the older, original LAMMPS implementations.  They compute the
LJ and Coulombic interactions with an energy switching function which
ramps the energy smoothly to zero between the inner and outer cutoff.
This can cause irregularities in pairwise forces (due to the discontinuous
second derivative of energy at the boundaries of the switching region),
which in some cases can result in detectable artifacts in an MD simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The newer styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmmfsw} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmmfsh} in their name replace
the energy switching with force switching (fsw) and force shifting
(fsh) functions, for LJ and Coulombic interactions respectively.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The newer \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmmfsw} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmmfsh} styles were released in
March 2017.  We recommend they be used instead of the older \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm}
styles.  This includes the newer {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_charmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_style charmmfsw}}}} command.  Eventually code from the new
styles will propagate into the related pair styles (e.g. implicit,
accelerator, free energy variants).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The newest CHARMM pair styles reset the Coulombic energy
conversion factor used internally in the code, from the LAMMPS value
to the CHARMM value, as if it were effectively a parameter of the
force field.  This is because the CHARMM code uses a slightly
different value for the this conversion factor in {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{real units}}}} (kcal/mol), namely CHARMM = 332.0716, LAMMPS =
332.06371.  This is to enable more precise agreement by LAMMPS with
the CHARMM force field energies and forces, when using one of these
two CHARMM pair styles.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm styles}, both the LJ and
Coulombic terms require an inner and outer cutoff. They can be the
same for both formulas or different depending on whether 2 or 4
arguments are used in the pair\_style command.  For the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/charmmfsh} style, the LJ term requires both an
inner and outer cutoff, while the Coulombic term requires only one
cutoff.  If the Coulombic cutoff is not specified (2 instead of 3
arguments), the LJ outer cutoff is used for the Coulombic cutoff.  In
all cases where an inner and outer cutoff are specified, the inner
cutoff distance must be less than the outer cutoff.  It is typical to
make the difference between the inner and outer cutoffs about 2.0
Angstroms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm/implicit} computes the same formulas as
style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm} except that an additional 1/r term is
included in the Coulombic formula.  The Coulombic energy thus varies
as 1/r\textasciicircum{}2.  This is effectively a distance\sphinxhyphen{}dependent dielectric term
which is a simple model for an implicit solvent with additional
screening.  It is designed for use in a simulation of an unsolvated
biomolecule (no explicit water molecules).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/msm} compute the same
formulas as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/charmm} and style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/long} computes the same formulas as style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/charmmfsh}, except that an additional damping
factor is applied to the Coulombic term, so it can be used in
conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command and its
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{msm} option.  Only one Coulombic cutoff is
specified for these styles; if only 2 arguments are used in the
pair\_style command, then the outer LJ cutoff is used as the single
Coulombic cutoff.  The Coulombic cutoff specified for these styles
means that pairwise interactions within this distance are computed
directly; interactions outside that distance are computed in
reciprocal space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{14}\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma_{14}\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma\) is defined in the LJ formula as the zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing
distance for the potential, not as the energy minimum at \(2^{1/6} \sigma\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If they are specified, they
are used in the LJ formula between two atoms of these types which are
also first and fourth atoms in any dihedral.  No cutoffs are specified
because the CHARMM force field does not allow varying cutoffs for
individual atom pairs; all pairs use the global cutoff(s) specified in
the pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_charmm:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon, sigma, epsilon\_14,
and sigma\_14 coefficients for all of the lj/charmm pair styles can be
mixed.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{arithmetic} to coincide with the
usual settings for the CHARMM force field.  See the “pair\_modify”
command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option, since the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
portion of the pair interaction is smoothed to 0.0 at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/long} styles support
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option since they can
tabulate the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic
interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail
corrections to energy and pressure, since the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of
the pair interaction is smoothed to 0.0 at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw} pair styles write their
information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and
pair\_coeff commands do not need to be specified in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmm/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/charmmfsw/coul/long} pair styles
support the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command, meaning the pairwise forces
can be partitioned by distance at different levels of the rRESPA
hierarchy.  The other styles only support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of
run\_style respa.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for
details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_charmm:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All the styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/charmm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/charmmfsh} styles are part
of the MOLECULE package.  All the styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} style are
part of the KSPACE package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built
with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_class2:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/long}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for class 2 interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/cut} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for class 2 (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/long} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for class 2 (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{class2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_class2:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2} styles compute a 6/9 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \left[ 2 \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^9 -
  3 \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
\qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/cut} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/long} styles add a
Coulombic term as described for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/cut}}}} pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_class2:pair-sun}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sun)}}}} for a description of the COMPASS class2 force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff1 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global
class 2 and Coulombic cutoffs are used.  If only one cutoff is
specified, it is used as the cutoff for both class 2 and Coulombic
interactions for this type pair.  If both coefficients are specified,
they are used as the class 2 and Coulombic cutoffs for this type pair.
You cannot specify 2 cutoffs for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2}, since it has no
Coulombic terms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/long} only the class 2 cutoff can be specified
since a Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J
type pair.  All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff
specified in the pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
If the pair\_coeff command is not used to define coefficients for a
particular I != J type pair, the mixing rule for \(\epsilon\) and
\(\sigma\) for all class2 potentials is to use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sixthpower}
formulas documented by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} command.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify mix}}}} setting is thus ignored for
class2 potentials for epsilon and sigma.  However it is still followed
for mixing the cutoff distance.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
A version of these styles with a soft core, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/soft}, suitable for use in
free energy calculations, is part of the FEP package and is documented with
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}} styles. The version with soft core is
only available if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_class2:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the lj/class2 pair styles can be mixed.
Epsilon and sigma are always mixed with the value \sphinxstyleemphasis{sixthpower}.  The
cutoff distance is mixed by whatever option is set by the pair\_modify
command (default = geometric).  See the “pair\_modify” command for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the lj/class2 pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option for the energy of the
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/long} pair style does not support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option since a tabulation
capability has not yet been added to this potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the lj/class2 pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range
tail correction to the energy and pressure of the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the lj/class2 pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do
not need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/class2/coul/long} pair styles support the use of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command, meaning the pairwise forces can be
partitioned by distance at different levels of the rRESPA hierarchy.
The other styles only support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of run\_style respa.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles are part of the CLASS2 package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}}

\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:pair-style-colloid-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid::doc}}

\subsection{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{colloid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{144}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{75.398}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{9.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{39.478}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{colloid} computes pairwise interactions between large colloidal
particles and small solvent particles using 3 formulas.  A colloidal
particle has a size \textgreater{} sigma; a solvent particle is the usual
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones particle of size sigma.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The colloid\sphinxhyphen{}colloid interaction energy is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} U_A = & - \frac{A_{cc}}{6} \left[
 \frac{2 a_1 a_2}{r^2-\left(a_1+a_2\right)^2}
 + \frac{2 a_1 a_2}{r^2 - \left(a_1 - a_2\right)^2}
   + \mathrm{ln}
     \left(
\frac{r^2-\left(a_1+a_2\right)^2}{r^2-\left(a_1-a_2\right)^2}
 \right)
\right] \\
  & \\
  U_R = & \frac{A_{cc}}{37800}  \frac{\sigma^6}{r}
  \biggl[ \frac{r^2-7r\left(a_1+a_2\right)+6\left(a_1^2+7a_1a_2+a_2^2\right)}
{\left(r-a_1-a_2\right)^7} \\
 &\qquad              +\frac{r^2+7r\left(a_1+a_2\right)+6\left(a_1^2+7a_1a_2+a_2^2\right)}
{\left(r+a_1+a_2\right)^7}  \\
&\qquad               -\frac{r^2+7r\left(a_1-a_2\right)+6\left(a_1^2-7a_1a_2+a_2^2\right)}
{\left(r+a_1-a_2\right)^7} \\
&\qquad       \left.  -\frac{r^2-7r\left(a_1-a_2\right)+6\left(a_1^2-7a_1a_2+a_2^2\right)}
{\left(r-a_1+a_2\right)^7}
\right]  \\
& \\
U = & U_A + U_R, \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(A_{cc}\) is the Hamaker constant, \(a_1\) and \(a_2\) are the
radii of the two colloidal particles, and \(r_c\) is the cutoff.  This
equation results from describing each colloidal particle as an
integrated collection of Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones particles of size sigma and is
derived in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_colloid:everaers1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Everaers)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The colloid\sphinxhyphen{}solvent interaction energy is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U = \frac{2 ~ a^3 ~ \sigma^3 ~ A_{cs}}{9 \left( a^2 - r^2 \right)^3}
\left[ 1 - \frac{\left(5 ~ a^6+45~a^4~r^2+63~a^2~r^4+15~r^6\right) \sigma^6}
{15 \left(a-r\right)^6 \left( a+r \right)^6} \right], \quad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(A_{cs}\) is the Hamaker constant, \sphinxstyleemphasis{a} is the radius of the colloidal
particle, and \(r_c\) is the cutoff.  This formula is derived from the
colloid\sphinxhyphen{}colloid interaction, letting one of the particle sizes go to
zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The solvent\sphinxhyphen{}solvent interaction energy is given by the usual
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U = \frac{A_{ss}}{36} \left[ \left( \frac{\sigma}{r}
     \right)^{12} - \left( \frac{ \sigma}{r} \right)^6 \right], \quad
     r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(A_{ss}\) set appropriately, which results from letting both
particle sizes go to zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When used in combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style yukawa/colloid}}}}, the two terms become the so\sphinxhyphen{}called DLVO potential,
which combines electrostatic repulsion and van der Waals attraction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
d1 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
d2 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A is the Hamaker energy prefactor and should typically be set as
follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_{cc}\) = colloid/colloid = \(4 \pi^2 = 39.5\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_{cs}\) = colloid/solvent = \(\sqrt{A_{cc} A_{ss}}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_{ss}\) = solvent/solvent = 144 (assuming epsilon = 1, so that 144/36 = 4)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) is the size of the solvent particle or the constituent
particles integrated over in the colloidal particle and should typically
be set as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma_{cc}\) = colloid/colloid = 1.0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma_{cs}\) = colloid/solvent = arithmetic mixing between colloid \(\sigma\) and solvent \(\sigma\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma_{ss}\) = solvent/solvent = 1.0 or whatever size the solvent particle is

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus typically \(\sigma_{cs} = 1.0\), unless the solvent particle’s size !=
1.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
D1 and d2 are particle diameters, so that d1 = 2*a1 and d2 = 2*a2 in
the formulas above.  Both d1 and d2 must be values \textgreater{}= 0.  If d1 \textgreater{} 0
and d2 \textgreater{} 0, then the pair interacts via the colloid\sphinxhyphen{}colloid formula
above.  If d1 = 0 and d2 = 0, then the pair interacts via the
solvent\sphinxhyphen{}solvent formula.  I.e. a d value of 0 is a Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
particle of size \(\sigma\).  If either d1 = 0 or d2 = 0 and the other is
larger, then the pair interacts via the colloid\sphinxhyphen{}solvent formula.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the diameter of a particular particle type may appear in
multiple pair\_coeff commands, as it interacts with other particle
types.  You should ensure the particle diameter is specified
consistently each time it appears.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global cutoff
specified in the pair\_style command is used.  However, you typically
want different cutoffs for interactions between different particle
sizes.  E.g. if colloidal particles of diameter 10 are used with
solvent particles of diameter 1, then a solvent\sphinxhyphen{}solvent cutoff of 2.5
would correspond to a colloid\sphinxhyphen{}colloid cutoff of 25.  A good
rule\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}thumb is to use a colloid\sphinxhyphen{}solvent cutoff that is half the big
diameter + 4 times the small diameter.  I.e. 9 = 5 + 4 for the
colloid\sphinxhyphen{}solvent cutoff in this case.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using pair\_style colloid for a mixture with 2 (or more)
widely different particles sizes (e.g. sigma=10 colloids in a
background sigma=1 LJ fluid), you will likely want to use these
commands for efficiency: {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor multi}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify multi}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the A, sigma, d1, and d2
coefficients and cutoff distance for this pair style can be mixed.  A
is an energy value mixed like a LJ epsilon.  D1 and d2 are distance
values and are mixed like sigma.  The default mix value is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the COLLOID package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Normally, this pair style should be used with finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles
which have a diameter, e.g. see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} command.  However, this is not a requirement,
since the only definition of particle size is via the pair\_coeff
parameters for each type.  In other words, the physical radius of the
particle is ignored.  Thus you should ensure that the d1,d2 parameters
you specify are consistent with the physical size of the particles of
that type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}particle polydispersity is not yet supported by this pair style;
only per\sphinxhyphen{}type polydispersity is enabled via the pair\_coeff parameters.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_colloid:everaers1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Everaers)} Everaers, Ejtehadi, Phys Rev E, 67, 041710 (2003).

\sphinxstepscope

\section{pair\_style comb command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:pair-style-comb-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_comb::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb/omp}


\section{pair\_style comb3 command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:pair-style-comb3-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comb}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comb3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{polar}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{polar} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{polar\_on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{polar\_off} = whether or not to include atomic polarization
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comb}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{ffield.comb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{ffield.comb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Hf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{comb3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{polar\PYGZus{}off}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{ffield.comb3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb} computes the second generation variable charge COMB
(Charge\sphinxhyphen{}Optimized Many\sphinxhyphen{}Body) potential.  Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3} computes the
third\sphinxhyphen{}generation COMB potential.  These COMB potentials are described
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_comb:comb}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(COMB)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_comb:comb3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(COMB3)}}}}.  Briefly, the
total energy \(E_T\) of a system of atoms is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_T  = & \sum_i [ E_i^{self} (q_i) + \sum_{j>i} [E_{ij}^{short} (r_{ij}, q_i, q_j) + E_{ij}^{Coul} (r_{ij}, q_i, q_j)] + \\
       & E^{polar} (q_i, r_{ij}) + E^{vdW} (r_{ij}) + E^{barr} (q_i) + E^{corr} (r_{ij}, \theta_{jik})]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(E_i^{self}\) is the self\sphinxhyphen{}energy of atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} (including
atomic ionization energies and electron affinities),
\(E_{ij}^{short}\) is the bond\sphinxhyphen{}order potential between atoms \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{j}, \(E_{ij}^{Coul}\) is the Coulomb interactions,
\(E^{polar}\) is the polarization term for organic systems (style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3} only), \(E^{vdW}\) is the van der Waals energy (style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3} only), \(E^{barr}\) is a charge barrier function, and
\(E^{corr}\) are angular correction terms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The COMB potentials (styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3}) are variable charge
potentials.  The equilibrium charge on each atom is calculated by the
electronegativity equalization (QEq) method.  See {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_comb:rick2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Rick}}}} for
further details.  This is implemented by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/comb}}}} command, which should normally be
specified in the input script when running a model with the COMB
potential.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/comb}}}} command has options
that determine how often charge equilibration is performed, its
convergence criterion, and which atoms are included in the
calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3}
styles which specifies the COMB potential file with parameters for all
needed elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying
N additional arguments after the potential file in the pair\_coeff
command, where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if your LAMMPS simulation of a Si/SiO2/
HfO2 interface has 4 atom types, and you want the first and
last to be Si, the second to be Hf, and the third to be O, and you would
use the following pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{ffield.comb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Hf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first two arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom
types.  The first and last Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1 and 4
to the Si element in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb} file.  The second Hf argument
maps LAMMPS atom type 2 to the Hf element, and the third O argument
maps LAMMPS atom type 3 to the O element in the potential file.  If a
mapping value is specified as NULL, the mapping is not performed.
This can be used when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb} potential is used as part of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values are placeholders for atom types
that will be used with other potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb}, the provided potential file \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb} contains
all currently\sphinxhyphen{}available second generation COMB parameterizations: for Si,
Cu, Hf, Ti, O, their oxides and Zr, Zn and U metals.  For style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3}, the potential file \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb3} contains all
currently\sphinxhyphen{}available third generation COMB parameterizations: O, Cu, N, C,
H, Ti, Zn and Zr.  The status of the optimization of the compounds, for
example Cu2O, TiN and hydrocarbons, are given in the
following table:

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3}, in addition to ffield.comb3, a special parameter
file, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lib.comb3}, that is exclusively used for C/O/H systems, will be
automatically loaded if carbon atom is detected in LAMMPS input
structure.  This file must be in your working directory or in the
directories listed in the environment variable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LAMMPS\_POTENTIALS}}, as
described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{polar} indicates whether the force field includes
the atomic polarization.  Since the equilibration of the polarization
has not yet been implemented, it can only set polar\_off at present.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can not use potential file \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb} with style \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb3},
nor file \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb3} with style \sphinxstyleemphasis{comb}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS as
described above from values in the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style, pair\_coeff, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/comb}}}} commands in an input script that reads a
restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the MANYBODY package.  It is only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The COMB potentials in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.comb3} files provided
with LAMMPS (see the potentials directory) are parameterized for metal
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  You can use the COMB potential with any LAMMPS
units, but you would need to create your own COMB potential file with
coefficients listed in the appropriate units if your simulation
does not use “metal” units.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_comb:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_comb::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/comb}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{pair\_style cosine/squared@\spxentry{pair\_style cosine/squared}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style cosine/squared command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:pair-style-cosine-squared-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cosine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{squared}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for cosine\sphinxhyphen{}squared interactions (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{I}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{J}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sigma}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{I}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{J}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{I}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{J}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wca}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{I}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{J}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eps}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wca}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
I, J = a particle type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eps = interaction strength, i.e. the depth of the potential minimum (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sigma = distance of the potential minimum from 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = the cutoff distance for this pair type, if different from global (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wca = if specified a Weeks\sphinxhyphen{}Chandler\sphinxhyphen{}Andersen potential (with eps strength and minimum at sigma) is added, otherwise not

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cosine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{squared}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wca}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wca}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/squared} computes a potential of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E =
\begin{cases}
-\epsilon& \quad r < \sigma \\
-\epsilon\cos\left(\frac{\pi\left(r - \sigma\right)}{2\left(r_c - \sigma\right)}\right)^2&\quad \sigma \leq r < r_c \\
0& \quad r \geq r_c
\end{cases}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
between two point particles, where (\(\sigma, -\epsilon\)) is the
location of the (rightmost) minimum of the potential, as explained in
the syntax section above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential was first used in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:ckd}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Cooke)}}}} for a coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained lipid
membrane model.  It is generally very useful as a non\sphinxhyphen{}specific
interaction potential because it is fully adjustable in depth and width
while joining the minimum at (sigma, \sphinxhyphen{}epsilon) and zero at (cutoff, 0)
smoothly, requiring no shifting and causing no related artifacts, tail
energy calculations etc. This evidently requires \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} to be larger
than \sphinxstyleemphasis{sigma}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{wca} option is used then a Weeks\sphinxhyphen{}Chandler\sphinxhyphen{}Andersen potential
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_cosine_squared:wca}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Weeks)}}}} is added to the above specified cosine\sphinxhyphen{}squared potential,
specifically the following:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
                      2\left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 + 1\right]
                      , \quad r < \sigma\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In this case, and this case only, the \(\sigma\) parameter can be equal to
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} (\(\sigma =\) cutoff) which will result in ONLY the WCA potential
being used (and print a warning), so the minimum will be attained at
(sigma, 0). This is a convenience feature that enables a purely
repulsive potential to be used without a need to define an additional
pair style and use the hybrid styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} style computes the standard Coulombic interaction
potential given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where C is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, Qi and Qj are the charges on
the two atoms, and \(\epsilon\) is the dielectric constant which can be set
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command.  The cutoff \(r_c\) truncates
the interaction distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut/global} computes the same Coulombic interactions
as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} except that it allows only a single global cutoff
and thus makes it compatible for use in combination with long\sphinxhyphen{}range
coulomb styles in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid pair styles}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/debye} adds an additional exp() damping factor to the
Coulombic term, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \exp(- \kappa r) \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\kappa\) is the Debye length.  This potential is another way to
mimic the screening effect of a polar solvent.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/dsf} computes Coulombic interactions via the damped
shifted force model described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul:fennell1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Fennell}}}}, given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = q_iq_j \left[ \frac{\mbox{erfc} (\alpha r)}{r} -  \frac{\mbox{erfc} (\alpha r_c)}{r_c} +
\left( \frac{\mbox{erfc} (\alpha r_c)}{r_c^2} +  \frac{2\alpha}{\sqrt{\pi}}\frac{\exp (-\alpha^2    r^2_c)}{r_c} \right)(r-r_c) \right] \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\alpha\) is the damping parameter and \sphinxstyleemphasis{erfc()} is the
complementary error\sphinxhyphen{}function. The potential corrects issues in the Wolf
model (described below) to provide consistent forces and energies (the
Wolf potential is not differentiable at the cutoff) and smooth decay to
zero.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/wolf} computes Coulombic interactions via the Wolf
summation method, described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul:wolf1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Wolf}}}}, given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_i = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{j \neq i}
\frac{q_i q_j {\rm erfc}(\alpha r_{ij})}{r_{ij}} +
\frac{1}{2} \sum_{j \neq i}
\frac{q_i q_j {\rm erf}(\alpha r_{ij})}{r_{ij}} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\alpha\) is the damping parameter, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{erf()} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{erfc()}
are error\sphinxhyphen{}function and complementary error\sphinxhyphen{}function terms.  This
potential is essentially a short\sphinxhyphen{}range, spherically\sphinxhyphen{}truncated,
charge\sphinxhyphen{}neutralized, shifted, pairwise \sphinxstyleemphasis{1/r} summation.  With a
manipulation of adding and subtracting a self term (for i = j) to the
first and second term on the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand\sphinxhyphen{}side, respectively, and a small
enough \(\alpha\) damping parameter, the second term shrinks and the
potential becomes a rapidly\sphinxhyphen{}converging real\sphinxhyphen{}space summation.  With a
long enough cutoff and small enough \(\alpha\) parameter, the energy
and forces calculated by the Wolf summation method approach those of the
Ewald sum.  So it is a means of getting effective long\sphinxhyphen{}range
interactions with a short\sphinxhyphen{}range potential.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/streitz} is the Coulomb pair interaction defined as part of
the Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire potential, as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul:streitz2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{this paper}}}}, in which charge distribution about an atom is modeled as a
Slater 1\sphinxstyleemphasis{s} orbital.  More details can be found in the referenced
paper.  To fully reproduce the published Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire potential,
which is a variable charge potential, style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/streitz} must be used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style eam/alloy}}}} (or some other short\sphinxhyphen{}range
potential that has been parameterized appropriately) via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}} command.  Likewise,
charge equilibration must be performed via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/slater}}}} command. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{streitz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wolf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.31}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{alloy}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{streitz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AlO.streitz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{alloy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AlO.eam.alloy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Al}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{qeq}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{slater}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{streitz}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{wolf} in the coul/streitz command denotes computing
Coulombic interactions via Wolf summation.  An additional damping
parameter is required for the Wolf summation, as described for the
coul/wolf potential above.  Alternatively, Coulombic interactions can
be computed via an Ewald summation.  For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{streitz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ewald}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{alloy}
\PYG{k}{kspace\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ewald}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1e\PYGZhy{}6}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} does not need a damping parameter, but a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} must be defined, which can be style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm}.  The Ewald method was used in Streitz and
Mintmire’s original paper, but a Wolf summation offers a speed\sphinxhyphen{}up in
some cases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the fix qeq/slater command, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile} can be a filename that
contains QEq parameters as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq}}}}
command doc page.  Alternatively \sphinxstyleemphasis{qfile} can be replaced by
“coul/streitz”, in which case the fix will extract QEq parameters from
the coul/streitz pair style itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the examples/strietz directory for an example input script that
uses the Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire potential.  The potentials directory has the
AlO.eam.alloy and AlO.streitz potential files used by the example.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the Streiz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire potential is generally used for oxides,
but there is no conceptual problem with extending it to nitrides and
carbides (such as SiC, TiN).  Pair coul/strietz used by itself or with
any other pair style such as EAM, MEAM, Tersoff, or LJ in
hybrid/overlay mode.  To do this, you would need to provide a
Streitz\sphinxhyphen{}Mintmire parameterization for the material being modeled.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/exclude} computes Coulombic interactions like \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut}
but \sphinxstylestrong{only} applies them to excluded pairs using a scaling factor
of \(\gamma - 1.0\) with \(\gamma\) being the factor assigned
to that excluded pair via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds coul}}}}
setting. With this it is possible to treat Coulomb interactions for
molecular systems with {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace style scafacos}}}},
which always computes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{full} Coulomb interactions without exclusions.
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/exclude} will then \sphinxstyleemphasis{subtract} the excluded interactions
accordingly. So to achieve the same forces as with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair\_style lj/cut/coul/long 12.0}}
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kspace\_style pppm 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}6}}, one would use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair\_style hybrid/overlay lj/cut 12.0 coul/exclude 12.0}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kspace\_style scafacos p3m 1.0e\sphinxhyphen{}6}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/msm} compute the same Coulombic
interactions as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} except that an additional damping
factor is applied so it can be used in conjunction with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm}
option.  The Coulombic cutoff specified for this style means that
pairwise interactions within this distance are computed directly;
interactions outside that distance are computed in reciprocal space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p/cut} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p/long} implement the Coulomb part of
the TIP4P water model of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul:jorgensen3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jorgensen)}}}}, which introduces
a massless site located a short distance away from the oxygen atom
along the bisector of the HOH angle.  The atomic types of the oxygen and
hydrogen atoms, the bond and angle types for OH and HOH interactions,
and the distance to the massless charge site are specified as
pair\_style arguments.  Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p/cut} uses a global cutoff for
Coulomb interactions; style \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p/long} is for use with a long\sphinxhyphen{}range
Coulombic solver (Ewald or PPPM).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each TIP4P water molecule in your system, the atom IDs for
the O and 2 H atoms must be consecutive, with the O atom first.  This
is to enable LAMMPS to “find” the 2 H atoms associated with each O
atom.  For example, if the atom ID of an O atom in a TIP4P water
molecule is 500, then its 2 H atoms must have IDs 501 and 502.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If using type labels, the type labels must be defined before calling
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_tip4p::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto tip4p}}}} page for more information
on how to use the TIP4P pair styles and lists of parameters to set.
Note that the neighbor list cutoff for Coulomb interactions is
effectively extended by a distance 2*qdist when using the TIP4P pair
style, to account for the offset distance of the fictitious charges on
O atoms in water molecules.  Thus it is typically best in an
efficiency sense to use a LJ cutoff \textgreater{}= Coulombic cutoff + 2*qdist, to
shrink the size of the neighbor list.  This leads to slightly larger
cost for the long\sphinxhyphen{}range calculation, so you can test the trade\sphinxhyphen{}off for
your model.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that these potentials are designed to be combined with other pair
potentials via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}}
command.  This is because they have no repulsive core.  Hence if they
are used by themselves, there will be no repulsion to keep two
oppositely charged particles from moving arbitrarily close to each
other.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/debye} the cutoff coefficient is optional.
If it is not used (as in some of the examples above), the default
global value specified in the pair\_style command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut/global}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/msm} no cutoff can be
specified for an individual I,J type pair via the pair\_coeff command.
All type pairs use the same global Coulomb cutoff specified in the
pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the cutoff distance for the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} style can be mixed.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.
See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option is not relevant
for these pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
table option for tabulation of the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the
long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/msm}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/streitz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p/long} styles are
part of the KSPACE package.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut/global}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/exclude} styles are
part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p/cut} style is part of the MOLECULE
package.  A pair style is only enabled if LAMMPS was built with its
corresponding package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul:related-commands}}

\section{pair\_style coul/diel command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:pair-style-coul-diel-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/diel/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{diel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{diel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{78}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.375}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.112}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/diel} computes a Coulomb correction for implicit solvent
ion interactions in which the dielectric permittivity is distance dependent.
The dielectric permittivity \(\epsilon_D(r)\) connects to limiting regimes:
One limit is defined by a small dielectric permittivity (close to vacuum)
at or close to contact separation between the ions. At larger separations
the dielectric permittivity reaches a bulk value used in the regular Coulomb
interaction coul/long or coul/cut.
The transition is modeled by a hyperbolic function which is incorporated
in the Coulomb correction term for small ion separations as follows
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E  = & \frac{Cq_iq_j}{\epsilon r} \left( \frac{\epsilon}{\epsilon_D(r)}-1\right)                       \qquad r < r_c \\
\epsilon_D(r)  = & \frac{5.2+\epsilon}{2} +  \frac{\epsilon-5.2}{2}\tanh\left(\frac{r-r_{me}}{\sigma_e}\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_{me}\) is the inflection point of \(\epsilon_D(r)\) and \(\sigma_e\) is a slope
defining length scale. C is the same Coulomb conversion factor as in the
pair\_styles coul/cut, coul/long, and coul/debye. In this way the Coulomb
interaction between ions is corrected at small distances r. The lower
limit of \(\epsilon_D(r \to 0) = 5.2\) due to dielectric saturation {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:stiles}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Stiles)}}}}
while the Coulomb interaction reaches its bulk limit by setting
\(\epsilon_D(r \to \infty) = \epsilon\), the bulk value of the solvent which is 78
for water at 298K.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples of the use of this type of Coulomb interaction include implicit
solvent simulations of salt ions
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:lenart1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lenart)}}}} and of ionic surfactants {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:jusufi1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jusufi)}}}}.
Note that this potential is only reasonable for implicit solvent simulations
and in combination with coul/cut or coul/long. It is also usually combined
with gauss/cut, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:lenart1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lenart)}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:jusufi1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jusufi)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (no units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_{me}\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma_e\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The global cutoff (\(r_c\)) specified in the pair\_style command is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_diel:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support parameter mixing. Coefficients must
be given explicitly for each type of particle pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the Gauss\sphinxhyphen{}potential portion of the pair
interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\section{pair\_style coul/shield command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:pair-style-coul-shield-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_shield::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shield}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tap\PYGZus{}flag}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tap\_flag = 0/1 to turn off/on the taper function

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shield}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.70}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/shield} computes a Coulomb interaction for boron and
nitrogen atoms located in different layers of hexagonal boron
nitride. This potential is designed be used in combination with
the pair style {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ilp_graphene_hbn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ilp/graphene/hbn}}}}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential is intended for electrostatic interactions between
two different layers of hexagonal boron nitride. Therefore, to avoid
interaction within the same layers, each layer should have a separate
molecule id and is recommended to use the “full” atom style, so that
charge and molecule ID information is included.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E      = & \frac{1}{2} \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} V_{ij} \\
V_{ij} = & {\rm Tap}(r_{ij})\frac{\kappa q_i q_j}{\sqrt[3]{r_{ij}^3+(1/\lambda_{ij})^3}}\\
{\rm Tap}(r_{ij}) = & 20\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^7 -
                       70\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^6 +
                       84\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^5 -
                       35\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^4 + 1\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where Tap(\(r_{ij}\)) is the taper function which provides a continuous cutoff
(up to third derivative) for inter\sphinxhyphen{}atomic separations larger than \(r_c\)
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:leven3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Leven1)}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:leven4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Leven2)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:maaravi1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Maaravi)}}}}.
Here \(\lambda\) is the shielding parameter that
eliminates the short\sphinxhyphen{}range singularity of the classical mono\sphinxhyphen{}polar
electrostatic interaction expression {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_shield:maaravi1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Maaravi)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The shielding parameter \(\lambda\) (1/distance units) must be defined for
each pair of atom types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as
in the example above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The global cutoff (\(r_c\)) specified in the pair\_style command is used.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_slater:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/slater/*} compute electrostatic interactions in mesoscopic models
which employ potentials without explicit excluded\sphinxhyphen{}volume interactions.
The goal is to prevent artificial ionic pair formation by including a charge
distribution in the Coulomb potential, following the formulation of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_slater:melchor}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Melchor)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E  =  \frac{Cq_iq_j}{\epsilon r} \left( 1- \left( 1 + \frac{r_{ij}}{\lambda} exp\left( -2r_{ij}/\lambda \right) \right) \right)                       \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_c\) is the cutoff distance and \(\lambda\) is the decay length of the charge.
C is the same Coulomb conversion factor as in the pair\_styles coul/cut and coul/long. In this way the Coulomb
interaction between ions is corrected at small distances r.
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/slater/cut} style, the potential energy for distances larger than the cutoff is zero,
while for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/slater/long}, the long\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions are computed either by the Ewald or the PPPM technique.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Phenomena that can be captured at a mesoscopic level using this type of electrostatic
interactions include the formation of polyelectrolyte\sphinxhyphen{}surfactant aggregates,
charge stabilization of colloidal suspensions, and the formation of
complexes driven by charged species in biological systems. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_slater:vaiwala}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Vaiwala)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoff distance is optional. If it is not used,
the default global value specified in the pair\_style command is used.
For each pair of atom types, a specific cutoff distance can be defined via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The global decay length of the charge (\(\lambda\)) specified in the pair\_style command is used for all pairs.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the cutoff distance for the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/slater} styles can be mixed.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.
