for these pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\section{pair\_style coul/tt command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:pair-style-coul-tt-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:syntax}}

\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input scripts available: examples/PACKAGES/drude


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/tt} pair style is meant to be used with force fields that
include explicit polarization through Drude dipoles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/tt} pair style should be used as a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style within in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}} command, in conjunction with a
main pair style including Coulomb interactions and \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} pair style,
or with \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long} pair style that is equivalent to the combination
of preceding two.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/tt} pair styles compute the charge\sphinxhyphen{}dipole Coulomb interaction damped
at short distances by a function
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_{n,ij}(r) = 1 - c_{ij} \cdot e^{-b_{ij} r} \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(b_{ij} r)^k}{k!}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function results from an adaptation to the Coulomb interaction {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:salanne1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Salanne)}}}} of the damping function originally proposed
by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:tangtoennies1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Tang Toennies}}}} for van der Waals interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The polynomial takes the degree 4 for damping the Coulomb interaction.
The parameters \(b_{ij}\) and \(c_{ij}\) could be determined from
first\sphinxhyphen{}principle calculations for small, mainly mono\sphinxhyphen{}atomic, ions {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:salanne1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Salanne)}}}}, or else treated as empirical for large molecules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In pair styles with Drude induced dipoles, this damping function is typically
applied to the interactions between a Drude charge (either \(q_{D,i}\) on
a Drude particle or \(-q_{D,i}\) on the respective
Drude core)) and a charge on a non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atom, \(q_{j}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Tang\sphinxhyphen{}Toennies function could also be used to damp electrostatic
interactions between the (non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable part of the) charge of a core,
\(q_{i}-q_{D,i}\), and the Drude charge of another, \(-q_{D,j}\).
The \(b_{ij}\) and \(c_{ij}\) are equal  to \(b_{ji}\) and
\(c_{ji}\) in the case of core\sphinxhyphen{}core interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/tt}, the following coefficients must be defined for
each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command
as in the example above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(b_{ij}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(c_{ij}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
degree of polynomial (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last two coefficients are optional.  If not specified the global
degree of the polynomial or the global cutoff specified in the pair\_style
command are used. In order to specify a cutoff (forth argument), the degree of
the polynomial (third argument) must also be specified.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/tt} pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients
for all I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_coul_tt:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the DRUDE package. They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair\_style should currently not be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_charmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{charmm dihedral
style}}}} if the latter has non\sphinxhyphen{}zero 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 weighting
factors. This is because the \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/tt} pair style does not know which
pairs are 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 partners of which dihedrals.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/dsf/cs} args = alpha cutoff (cutoff2)
  alpha = damping parameter (inverse distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulombic (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{born/coul/long/cs} args = cutoff (cutoff2)

\sphinxstyleemphasis{buck/coul/long/cs} args = cutoff (cutoff2)

\sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} args = cutoff

\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long/cs} args = cutoff (cutoff2)

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_cs:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are designed to be used with the adiabatic
core/shell model of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_cs:mitchellfincham3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Mitchell and Fincham)}}}}.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_coreshell::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto coreshell}}}} page for an overview of
the model as implemented in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All the styles are identical to the corresponding pair style without
the “/cs” in the name:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style born/coul/dsf}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style born/coul/long}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_born::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style born/coul/wolf}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck/coul/long}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style coul/long}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style coul/wolf}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/cut/coul/long}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_class2::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/class2/coul/long}}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
except that they correctly treat the special case where the distance
between two charged core and shell atoms in the same core/shell pair
approach r = 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a “/long” in the name are used with a long\sphinxhyphen{}range solver
for Coulombic interactions via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}}
command.  They require special treatment of the short\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic
interactions within the cor/shell model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically, the short\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulomb interaction between a core and
its shell should be turned off using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command by setting the 1\sphinxhyphen{}2 weight
to 0.0, which works because the core and shell atoms are bonded to
each other.  This induces a long\sphinxhyphen{}range correction approximation which
fails at small distances (\textasciitilde{}\textless{} 10e\sphinxhyphen{}8). Therefore, the Coulomb term which
is used to calculate the correction factor is extended by a minimal
distance (r\_min = 1.0\sphinxhyphen{}6) when the interaction between a core/shell
pair is treated, as follows
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon (r + r_{min})} \qquad r \rightarrow 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where C is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\)
are the charges on the core and shell, epsilon is the dielectric
constant and \(r_{min}\) is the minimal distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For styles that are not used with a long\sphinxhyphen{}range solver, i.e. those with
“/dsf” or “/wolf” in the name, the only correction is the addition of
a minimal distance to avoid the possible r = 0.0 case for a core/shell
pair.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dielectric:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All these pair styles are derived from the corresponding pair styles
without the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dielectric} suffix. In addition to computing atom forces
and energies, these pair styles compute the electric field vector at
each atom, which are intended to be used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_polarize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix polarize}}}} commands to compute induced charges at interfaces
between two regions of different dielectric constant.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles should be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style dielectric}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles lj/cut/coul/long/dielectric, lj/cut/coul/msm/dielectric, and
lj/long/coul/long/dielectric should be used with their kspace style
counterparts, namely, pppm/dielectric, pppm/disp/dielectric, and
msm/dielectric, respectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dielectric:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distances for this pair style can be mixed.  The default mix
algorithm is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}”
command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}

\sphinxAtStartPar

if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dipole:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{cutoff2}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{cutoff2}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{cutoff2}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dipole}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flag\PYGZus{}lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flag\PYGZus{}coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{cutoff2}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic and dipole (optional) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flag\_lj = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use long\sphinxhyphen{}range damping on dispersion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cut} = use a cutoff on dispersion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term
\sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = omit disperion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term entirely
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
flag\_coul = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use long\sphinxhyphen{}range damping on Coulombic 1/r and point\sphinxhyphen{}dipole terms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = omit Coulombic and point\sphinxhyphen{}dipole terms entirely
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dipole:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/dipole/cut} computes interactions between pairs of
particles that each have a charge and/or a point dipole moment.  In
addition to the usual Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interaction between the particles
(Elj) the charge\sphinxhyphen{}charge (Eqq), charge\sphinxhyphen{}dipole (Eqp), and dipole\sphinxhyphen{}dipole
(Epp) interactions are computed by these formulas for the energy (E),
force (F), and torque (T) between particles I and J.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_{LJ}  = & 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
                     \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right] \\
E_{qq}  = & \frac{q_i q_j}{r} \\
E_{qp}  = & \frac{q}{r^3} (p \bullet \vec{r}) \\
E_{pp}  = & \frac{1}{r^3} (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{p}_j) -
          \frac{3}{r^5} (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r}) (\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r}) \\
          & \\
F_{qq}  = & \frac{q_i q_j}{r^3} \vec{r} \\
F_{qp}  = & -\frac{q}{r^3} \vec{p} + \frac{3q}{r^5}
          (\vec{p} \bullet \vec{r}) \vec{r} \\
F_{pp}  = & \frac{3}{r^5} (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{p}_j) \vec{r} -
          \frac{15}{r^7} (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r})
          (\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r}) \vec{r} +
          \frac{3}{r^5} \left[ (\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r}) \vec{p}_i +
          (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r}) \vec{p}_j \right] \\
          & \\
T_{pq} = T_{ij}  = & \frac{q_j}{r^3} (\vec{p}_i \times \vec{r}) \\
T_{qp} = T_{ji}  = & - \frac{q_i}{r^3} (\vec{p}_j \times \vec{r}) \\
T_{pp} = T_{ij}  = & -\frac{1}{r^3} (\vec{p}_i \times \vec{p}_j) +
                   \frac{3}{r^5} (\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r})
                   (\vec{p}_i \times \vec{r}) \\
T_{pp} = T_{ji}  = & -\frac{1}{r^3} (\vec{p}_j \times \vec{p}_i) +
                   \frac{3}{r^5} (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r})
                   (\vec{p}_j \times \vec{r})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(q_i\) and \(q_j\) are the charges on the two
particles, \(\vec{p}_i\) and \(\vec{p}_j\) are the dipole
moment vectors of the two particles, r is their separation distance,
and the vector r = Ri \sphinxhyphen{} Rj is the separation vector between the two
particles.  Note that Eqq and Fqq are simply Coulombic energy and
force, Fij = \sphinxhyphen{}Fji as symmetric forces, and Tij != \sphinxhyphen{}Tji since the
torques do not act symmetrically.  These formulas are discussed in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:allen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(AllenTildesley)}}}} and in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:toukmaji2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Toukmaji)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also note, that in the code, all of these terms (except Elj) have a
\(C/\epsilon\) prefactor, the same as the Coulombic term in the
LJ + Coulombic pair styles discussed {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{here}}}}.  C is an
energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant and \(\epsilon\) is the dielectric constant
which can be set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command.  The
same is true of the equations that follow for other dipole pair
styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/sf/dipole/sf} computes “shifted\sphinxhyphen{}force” interactions between
pairs of particles that each have a charge and/or a point dipole
moment. In general, a shifted\sphinxhyphen{}force potential is a (slightly) modified
potential containing extra terms that make both the energy and its
derivative go to zero at the cutoff distance; this removes
(cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}related) problems in energy conservation and any numerical
instability in the equations of motion {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:allen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(AllenTildesley)}}}}. Shifted\sphinxhyphen{}force interactions for the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones (E\_LJ),
charge\sphinxhyphen{}charge (Eqq), charge\sphinxhyphen{}dipole (Eqp), dipole\sphinxhyphen{}charge (Epq) and
dipole\sphinxhyphen{}dipole (Epp) potentials are computed by these formulas for the
energy (E), force (F), and torque (T) between particles I and J:
\begin{align*}\!\begin{aligned}
E_{LJ}  = &  4\epsilon \left\{ \left[ \left( \frac{\sigma}{r} \right)^{\!12} -
\left( \frac{\sigma}{r} \right)^{\!6}  \right] +
\left[ 6\left( \frac{\sigma}{r_c} \right)^{\!12} -
3\left(\frac{\sigma}{r_c}\right)^{\!6}\right]\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2}
- 7\left( \frac{\sigma}{r_c} \right)^{\!12} +
4\left( \frac{\sigma}{r_c} \right)^{\!6}\right\} \\
E_{qq}  = & \frac{q_i q_j}{r}\left(1-\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} \\
E_{pq}  = & E_{ji} = -\frac{q}{r^3} \left[ 1 -
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} +
2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3}\right] (\vec{p}\bullet\vec{r}) \\
E_{qp}  = & E_{ij} = \frac{q}{r^3} \left[ 1 -
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} +
2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3}\right] (\vec{p}\bullet\vec{r}) \\
E_{pp} = & \left[1-4\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3} +
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right]\left[\frac{1}{r^3}
(\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{p}_j) - \frac{3}{r^5}
(\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r}) (\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r})\right] \\
         & \\\\
F_{LJ}  = & \left\{\left[48\epsilon \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{\!12} -
24\epsilon \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{\!6} \right]\frac{1}{r^2} -
\left[48\epsilon \left(\frac{\sigma}{r_c}\right)^{\!12} - 24\epsilon
\left(\frac{\sigma}{r_c}\right)^{\!6} \right]\frac{1}{r_c^2}\right\}\vec{r}\\
F_{qq}  = & \frac{q_i q_j}{r}\left(\frac{1}{r^2} -
\frac{1}{r_c^2}\right)\vec{r} \\
F_{pq} = & F_{ij } =  -\frac{3q}{r^5} \left[ 1 -
\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2}\right](\vec{p}\bullet\vec{r})\vec{r} +
\frac{q}{r^3}\left[1-3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} +
2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3}\right] \vec{p} \\
F_{qp} = & F_{ij}  = \frac{3q}{r^5} \left[ 1 -
\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2}\right] (\vec{p}\bullet\vec{r})\vec{r} -
\frac{q}{r^3}\left[1-3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} +
2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3}\right] \vec{p} \\
F_{pp}  = &\frac{3}{r^5}\Bigg\{\left[1-\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right]
\left[(\vec{p}_i\bullet\vec{p}_j) - \frac{3}{r^2} (\vec{p}_i\bullet\vec{r})
(\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r})\right] \vec{r} + \\
  & \left[1 -
4\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3}+3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right]
\left[ (\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r}) \vec{p}_i + (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r})
\vec{p}_j -\frac{2}{r^2} (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r})
(\vec{p}_j \bullet \vec{r})\vec{r}\right] \Bigg\}\\
\end{aligned}\end{align*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} T_{pq} = T_{ij}  = & \frac{q_j}{r^3} \left[ 1 -
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} +
2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3}\right] (\vec{p}_i\times\vec{r}) \\
T_{qp} = T_{ji}  = & - \frac{q_i}{r^3} \left[ 1 -
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!2} +
2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3} \right] (\vec{p}_j\times\vec{r}) \\
T_{pp} = T_{ij}  = & -\frac{1}{r^3}\left[1-4\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3} +
e3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right] (\vec{p}_i \times \vec{p}_j) + \\
                   & \frac{3}{r^5}\left[1-4\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3} +
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right] (\vec{p}_j\bullet\vec{r})
(\vec{p}_i \times \vec{r}) \\
T_{pp} = T_{ji} = & -\frac{1}{r^3}\left[1-4\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3} +
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right](\vec{p}_j \times \vec{p}_i) + \\
                   & \frac{3}{r^5}\left[1-4\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!3} +
3\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^{\!4}\right] (\vec{p}_i \bullet \vec{r})
(\vec{p}_j \times \vec{r})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\epsilon\) and \(\sigma\) are the standard LJ
parameters, \(r_c\) is the cutoff, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\) are
the charges on the two particles, \(\vec{p}_i\) and
\(\vec{p}_j\) are the dipole moment vectors of the two particles,
r is their separation distance, and the vector r = Ri \sphinxhyphen{} Rj is the
separation vector between the two particles.  Note that Eqq and Fqq
are simply Coulombic energy and force, Fij = \sphinxhyphen{}Fji as symmetric forces,
and Tij != \sphinxhyphen{}Tji since the torques do not act symmetrically.  The
shifted\sphinxhyphen{}force formula for the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential is reported in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:stoddard}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Stoddard)}}}}.  The original (non\sphinxhyphen{}shifted) formulas for
the electrostatic potentials, forces and torques can be found in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:price2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Price)}}}}. The shifted\sphinxhyphen{}force electrostatic potentials
have been obtained by applying equation 5.13 of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:allen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(AllenTildesley)}}}}. The formulas for the corresponding forces and torques have
been obtained by applying the ‘chain rule’ as in appendix C.3 of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:allen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(AllenTildesley)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If one cutoff is specified in the pair\_style command, it is used for
both the LJ and Coulombic (q,p) terms.  If two cutoffs are specified,
they are used as cutoffs for the LJ and Coulombic (q,p) terms
respectively. This pair style also supports an optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale}
keyword as part of a pair\_coeff statement, where the interactions can
be scaled according to this factor. This scale factor is also made
available for use with fix adapt.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/dipole/long} computes the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of
point\sphinxhyphen{}dipole interactions as discussed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dipole:toukmaji2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Toukmaji)}}}}. Dipole\sphinxhyphen{}dipole, dipole\sphinxhyphen{}charge, and charge\sphinxhyphen{}charge
interactions are all supported, along with the standard 12/6
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions, which are computed with a cutoff.  A
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} must be defined to use this pair
style.  If only dipoles (not point charges) are included in the model,
the kspace style can be one of these 3 options, all of which compute
the long\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of dipole\sphinxhyphen{}dipole interactions.  If the model
includes point charges (in addition to dipoles), then only the first
of these kspace styles can be used:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style ewald/disp}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style ewald/dipole}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style pppm/dipole}}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/dipole/long} has the same functionality as style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/dipole/long}, except it also has an option to compute 12/6
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions for use with a long\sphinxhyphen{}range dispersion kspace
style.  This is done by setting its \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} argument to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}.  For
long\sphinxhyphen{}range LJ interactions, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style ewald/disp}}}} command must be used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above,
or in the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by
mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff1 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global LJ
and Coulombic cutoffs specified in the pair\_style command are used.  If
only one cutoff is specified, it is used as the cutoff for both LJ and
Coulombic interactions for this type pair.  If both coefficients are
specified, they are used as the LJ and Coulombic cutoffs for this type
pair.  When using a long\sphinxhyphen{}rang Coulomb solver, only a global Coulomb
cutoff may be used and only the LJ cutoff may be changed with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.  When using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/dipole/long} pair style with \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} setting, only a
single global cutoff may be provided and no cutoff for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for systems using these pair styles, typically particles
should be able to exert torque on each other via their dipole moments
so that the particle and its dipole moment can rotate.  This requires
they not be point particles, but finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres.  Thus you should
use a command like {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style hybrid sphere dipole}}}}
to use particles with both attributes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment for each particle
can be defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}} command or in the “Atoms”
section of the data file read in by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rotating finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles have 6 degrees of freedom (DOFs),
translation and rotational.  You can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/sphere}}}} command to monitor a temperature which includes
all these DOFs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles with dipole moments should be integrated using
one of these options:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/sphere update dipole}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/sphere update dipole}}}} plus {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin omega yes}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sphere update dipole}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_npt_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/sphere update dipole}}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In all cases the “update dipole” setting ensures the dipole moments
are also rotated when the finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres rotate.  The 2nd and 3rd
bullets perform thermostatting; in the case of a Langevin thermostat
the “omega yes” option also thermostats the rotational degrees of
freedom (if desired).  The 4th bullet performs thermostatting and
barostatting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dipole:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distances for this pair style can be mixed.  The default
mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the A, sigma, d1, and d2
coefficients and cutoff distance for this pair style can be mixed.  A
is an energy value mixed like a LJ epsilon.  D1 and d2 are distance
values and are mixed like sigma.  The default mix value is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair
interaction; such energy goes to zero at the cutoff by construction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dipole:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/dipole/cut}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/dipole/long}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/dipole/long},
and lj/sf/dipole/sf* styles are part of the DIPOLE package.  They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using dipole pair styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{electron} {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} is not currently supported.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dipole:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/sphere}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nvt_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/sphere}}}}

\section{pair\_style dpd command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:pair-style-dpd-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-8}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-7}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-6}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-5}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-4}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/omp}


\section{pair\_style dpd/tstat command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:pair-style-dpd-tstat-command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tstat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Tstop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = temperature (temperature units) (dpd only)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tstart,Tstop = desired temperature at start/end of run (temperature units) (dpd/tstat only)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for DPD interactions (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tstat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{34387}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tstat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd} computes a force field for dissipative particle dynamics
(DPD) following the exposition in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd:groot1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Groot)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat} invokes a DPD thermostat on pairwise interactions,
which is equivalent to the non\sphinxhyphen{}conservative portion of the DPD force
field.  This pairwise thermostat can be used in conjunction with any
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style}}}}, and instead of per\sphinxhyphen{}particle thermostats
like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or ensemble thermostats like
Nose Hoover as implemented by {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt}}}}.  To use
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat} as a thermostat for another pair style, use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}} command to compute both
the desired pair interaction and the thermostat for each pair of
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd}, the force on atom I due to atom J is given as a sum
of 3 terms
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{f}  = & (F^C + F^D + F^R) \hat{r_{ij}} \qquad \qquad r < r_c \\
F^C      = & A w(r) \\
F^D      = & - \gamma w^2(r) (\hat{r_{ij}} \bullet \vec{v}_{ij}) \\
F^R      = & \sigma w(r) \alpha (\Delta t)^{-1/2} \\
w(r)     = & 1 - \frac{r}{r_c}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(F^C\) is a conservative force, \(F^D\) is a dissipative
force, and \(F^R\) is a random force.  \(\hat{r_{ij}}\) is a
unit vector in the direction \(r_i - r_j\), \(\vec{v}_{ij}\) is
the vector difference in velocities of the two atoms \(\vec{v}_i -
\vec{v}_j\), \(\alpha\) is a Gaussian random number with zero mean
and unit variance, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} is the timestep size, and \(w(r)\) is a
weighting factor that varies between 0 and 1.  \(r_c\) is the
pairwise cutoff.  \(\sigma\) is set equal to \(\sqrt{2 k_B T
\gamma}\), where \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant and \sphinxstyleemphasis{T} is the
temperature parameter in the pair\_style command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat}, the force on atom I due to atom J is the same as
the above equation, except that the conservative \(F^C\) term is
dropped.  Also, during the run, \sphinxstyleemphasis{T} is set each timestep to a ramped
value from \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstart} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Tstop}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd}, the pairwise energy associated with style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd} is only
due to the conservative force term \(F^C\), and is shifted to be
zero at the cutoff distance \(r_c\).  The pairwise virial is
calculated using all 3 terms.  For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat} there is no
pairwise energy, but the last two terms of the formula make a
contribution to the virial.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd}, the following coefficients must be defined for each
pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in
the examples above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoff coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global DPD
cutoff is used.  Note that sigma is set equal to sqrt(2 T gamma),
where T is the temperature set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}}
command so it does not need to be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat}, the coefficients defined for each pair of
atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoff coefficient is optional.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu} suffix are implemented based on
the work of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd:afshar}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Afshar)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd:phillips}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Phillips)}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are modeling DPD polymer chains, you may want to use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_srp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style srp}}}} command in conjunction with these pair
styles.  It is a soft segmental repulsive potential (SRP) that can
prevent DPD polymer chains from crossing each other.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The virial calculation for pressure when using these pair styles
includes all the components of force listed above, including the
random force.  Since the random force depends on random numbers,
everything that changes the order of atoms in the neighbor list
(e.g. different number of MPI ranks or a different neighbor list
skin distance) will also change the sequence in which the random
numbers are applied and thus the individual forces and therefore
also the virial/pressure.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For more consistent time integration and force computation you may
consider using {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mvv_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mvv/dpd}}}} instead of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
nve}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the pair interaction.  Note that as
discussed above, the energy due to the conservative \(F^C\) term is already
shifted to be 0.0 at the cutoff distance \(r_c\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for these pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.  Note that the
user\sphinxhyphen{}specified random number seed is stored in the restart file, so when
a simulation is restarted, each processor will re\sphinxhyphen{}initialize its random
number generator the same way it did initially.  This means the random
forces will be random, but will not be the same as they would have been
if the original simulation had continued past the restart time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/tstat} style can ramp its target temperature over multiple
runs, using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{stop} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do
this.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles are part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}BASIC package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default frequency for rebuilding neighbor lists is every 10 steps
(see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command). This may be too
infrequent for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd} simulations since particles move rapidly and
can overlap by large amounts.  If this setting yields a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero number
of “dangerous” reneighborings (printed at the end of a simulation), you
should experiment with forcing reneighboring more often and see if
system energies/trajectories change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles requires you to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify vel yes}}}} command so that velocities are stored by ghost atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles will not restart exactly when using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command, though they should provide
statistically similar results.  This is because the forces they compute
depend on atom velocities.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for more details.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_ext::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd/ext}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}},

\section{pair\_style dpd/coul/slater/long command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:pair-style-dpd-coul-slater-long-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/coul/slater/long/gpu}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{slater}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{T}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff\PYGZus{}DPD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lambda}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff\PYGZus{}coul}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
T = temperature (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random \# seed (positive integer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lambda = decay length of the charge (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:examples}}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{slater}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{34387}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{78.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.5}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} not charged by default}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{78.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 27June2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/coul/slater/long} computes a force field for dissipative
particle dynamics (DPD) following the exposition in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:groot5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Groot)}}}}.  It also allows for the use of charged particles in the
model by adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic term to the DPD interactions.
The short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the Coulombics is calculated by this pair
style.  The long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombics are computed by use of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command, e.g. using the Ewald or
PPPM styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Coulombic forces in mesoscopic models such as DPD employ potentials
without explicit excluded\sphinxhyphen{}volume interactions.  The goal is to prevent
artificial ionic pair formation by including a charge distribution in
the Coulomb potential, following the formulation in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:melchor1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Melchor1)}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is effectively the combination of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_slater::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style
coul/slater/long}}}} commands, but should be more
efficient (especially on GPUs) than using {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style
hybrid/overlay dpd coul/slater/long}}}}. That is
particularly true for the GPU package version of the pair style since
this version is compatible with computing neighbor lists on the GPU
instead of the CPU as is required for hybrid styles.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the charged DPD model, the force on bead I due to bead J is given
as a sum of 4 terms:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{f}  = & (F^C + F^D + F^R + F^E) \hat{r_{ij}} \\
F^C      = & A w(r) \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad r < r_{DPD} \\
F^D      = & - \gamma w^2(r) (\hat{r_{ij}} \bullet \vec{v}_{ij}) \qquad \qquad r < r_{DPD} \\
F^R      = & \sigma w(r) \alpha (\Delta t)^{-1/2} \qquad \qquad \qquad r < r_{DPD} \\
w(r)     = & 1 - \frac{r}{r_{DPD}} \\
F^E      = & \frac{C q_iq_j}{\epsilon r^2} \left( 1- exp\left( \frac{2r_{ij}}{\lambda} \right) \left( 1 + \frac{2r_{ij}}{\lambda} \left( 1 + \frac{r_{ij}}{\lambda} \right)\right) \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(F^C\) is a conservative force, \(F^D\) is a
dissipative force, \(F^R\) is a random force, and \(F^E\) is
an electrostatic force.  \(\hat{r_{ij}}\) is a unit vector in the
direction \(r_i - r_j\), \(\vec{v}_{ij}\) is the vector
difference in velocities of the two atoms \(\vec{v}_i -
\vec{v}_j\), \(\alpha\) is a Gaussian random number with zero mean
and unit variance, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dt} is the timestep size, and \(w(r)\) is a
weighting factor that varies between 0 and 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) is set equal to \(\sqrt{2 k_B T \gamma}\), where
\(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant and \sphinxstyleemphasis{T} is the temperature
parameter in the pair\_style command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_{DPD}\) is the pairwise cutoff for the first 3 DPD terms in
the formula as specified by \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff\_DPD}.  For the \(F^E\) term,
pairwise interactions within the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff\_coul} distance are
computed directly; interactions beyond that distance are computed in
reciprocal space.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{C} is the same Coulomb conversion factor used in
the Coulombic formulas described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coul}}}}
doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following parameters must be defined for each pair of atoms types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
is\_charged (optional boolean, default = no)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{is\_charged} parameter is optional and can be specified as \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Yes} should be used for interactions between two types of
charged particles.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{No} is the default and should be used for
interactions between two types of particles when one or both are
uncharged.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.  Note that the
user\sphinxhyphen{}specified random number seed is stored in the restart file, so
when a simulation is restarted, each processor will re\sphinxhyphen{}initialize its
random number generator the same way it did initially.  This means the
random forces will be random, but will not be the same as they would
have been if the original simulation had continued past the restart
time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}BASIC package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default frequency for rebuilding neighbor lists is every 10 steps
(see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command). This may be too
infrequent since particles move rapidly and can overlap by large
amounts.  If this setting yields a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero number of “dangerous”
reneighborings (printed at the end of a simulation), you should
experiment with forcing reneighboring more often and see if system
energies/trajectories change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires use of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify vel yes}}}} command so that velocities are stored by ghost atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style also requires use of a long\sphinxhyphen{}range solvers from the
KSPACE package.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style will not restart exactly when using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command, though they should provide
statistically similar results.  This is because the forces they compute
depend on atom velocities.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style dpd}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul_slater::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style coul/slater/long}}}},


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_coul_slater_long:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the pair\_coeff command, the default is is\_charged = no.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_ext:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext} computes an extended force field for dissipative
particle dynamics (DPD) following the exposition in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_ext:groot}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Groot)}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd_ext:junghans}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Junghans)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat} invokes an extended DPD thermostat on pairwise
interactions, equivalent to the non\sphinxhyphen{}conservative portion of the extended
DPD force field. To use \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat} as a thermostat for another pair
style, use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}} command to
compute both the desired pair interaction and the thermostat for each
pair of particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext}, the force on atom I due to atom J is given as
a sum of 3 terms
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{f}  = & f^C + f^D + f^R \qquad \qquad r < r_c \\
f^C      = & A_{ij} w(r) \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij} \\
f^D      = & - \gamma_{\parallel} w_{\parallel}^2(r) (\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{ij}) \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij}  - \gamma_{\perp} w_{\perp}^2 (r) ( \mathbf{I} - \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij} \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij}^{\rm T} ) \mathbf{v}_{ij} \\
f^R      = & \sigma_{\parallel} w_{\parallel}(r) \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{\Delta t}} \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij}  + \sigma_{\perp} w_{\perp} (r) ( \mathbf{I} - \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij} \hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij}^{\rm T} ) \frac{\mathbf{\xi}_{ij}}{\sqrt{\Delta t}}\\
w(r)     = & 1 - r/r_c \\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{f}^C\) is a conservative force, \(\mathbf{f}^D\)
is a dissipative force, and \(\mathbf{f}^R\) is a random
force. \(A_{ij}\) is the maximum repulsion between the two atoms,
\(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij}\) is a unit vector in the direction
\(\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\), \(\mathbf{v}_{ij} =
\mathbf{v}_i - \mathbf{v}_j\) is the vector difference in velocities of
the two atoms, \(\alpha\) and \(\mathbf{\xi}_{ij}\) are Gaussian
random numbers with zero mean and unit variance, \(\Delta t\) is the
timestep, \(w (r) = 1 - r / r_c\) is a weight function for the
conservative interactions that varies between 0 and 1, \(r_c\) is
the corresponding cutoff, \(w_{\alpha} ( r ) = ( 1 - r / \bar{r}_c
)^{s_{\alpha}}\), \(\alpha \equiv ( \parallel, \perp )\), are weight
functions with coefficients \(s_\alpha\) that vary between 0 and 1,
\(\bar{r}_c\) is the corresponding cutoff, \(\mathbf{I}\) is the
unit matrix, \(\sigma_{\alpha} = \sqrt{2 k_B T \gamma_{\alpha}}\),
where \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) is the
temperature in the pair\_style command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat}, the force on atom I due to atom J is
the same as the above equation, except that the conservative
\(\mathbf{f}^C\) term is dropped. Also, during the run, T is set
each timestep to a ramped value from Tstart to Tstop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext}, the pairwise energy associated with style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext} is only due to the conservative force term
\(\mathbf{f}^C\), and is shifted to be zero at the cutoff distance
\(r_c\). The pairwise virial is calculated using all three
terms. There is no pairwise energy for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat}, but the
last two terms of the formula contribute the virial.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat}, the force on atom I due to atom J is the
same as the above equation, except that the conservative
\(\mathbf{f}^C\) term is dropped.  Also, during the run, T is set
each timestep to a ramped value from Tstart to Tstop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext}, the pairwise energy associated with style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext} is only due to the conservative force term
\(\mathbf{f}^C\), and is shifted to be zero at the cutoff distance
\(r_c\). The pairwise virial is calculated using all three
terms. There is no pairwise energy for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat}, but the
last two terms of the formula contribute the virial.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext}, the following coefficients must be defined for
each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command
as in the examples above:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_{\parallel}\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_{\perp}\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(s_{\parallel}\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(s_{\perp}\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional. If not specified, the global DPD
cutoff is used. Note that \(\sigma\)’s are set equal to
\(\sqrt{2 k_B T \gamma}\), where \(T\) is the temperature set by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command so it does not need to be
specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat}, the coefficients defined for each pair of
atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_{\parallel}\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_{\perp}\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(s_{\parallel}\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(s_{\perp}\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are modeling DPD polymer chains, you may want to use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_srp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style srp}}}} command in conjunction with these pair
styles.  It is a soft segmental repulsive potential (SRP) that can
prevent DPD polymer chains from crossing each other.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The virial calculation for pressure when using these pair styles
includes all the components of force listed above, including the
random force.  Since the random force depends on random numbers,
everything that changes the order of atoms in the neighbor list
(e.g. different number of MPI ranks or a different neighbor list
skin distance) will also change the sequence in which the random
numbers are applied and thus the individual forces and therefore
also the virial/pressure.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For more consistent time integration and force computation you may
consider using {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_mvv_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix mvv/dpd}}}} instead of {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
nve}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext} does not support mixing. Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the pair interaction. Note that as
discussed above, the energy due to the conservative \(\mathbf{f}^C\)
term is already shifted to be zero at the cutoff distance \(r_c\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant for
the style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext} does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to
energy and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair styles can only be used via the pair keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command. They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer}keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext/tstat} can ramp its target temperature over multiple
runs, using the start and stop keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}}
command. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} command for details of how to do this.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_dpd_ext:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles are part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}BASIC package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default frequency for rebuilding neighbor lists is every 10 steps
(see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neigh_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neigh\_modify}}}} command). This may be too
infrequent for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{dpd/ext} simulations since particles move rapidly
and can overlap by large amounts. If this setting yields a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero
number of say\{dangerous\} reneighborings (printed at the end of a
simulation), you should experiment with forcing reneighboring more often
and see if system energies/trajectories change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair styles require to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify vel yes}}}} command so that velocities are stored by ghost atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair styles will not restart exactly when using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} command, though they should provide
statistically similar results. This is because the forces they compute
depend on atom velocities. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
command for more details.

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
