\index{pair\_style kim@\spxentry{pair\_style kim}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style kim command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:pair-style-kim-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_kim::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{model}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
model = name of a KIM model (the KIM ID for models archived in OpenKIM)


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{kim }\PYG{l+s+s1}{SW\PYGZus{}StillingerWeber\PYGZus{}1985\PYGZus{}Si\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}MO\PYGZus{}405512056662\PYGZus{}005}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is a wrapper on the
\sphinxhref{https://openkim.org}{Open Knowledgebase of Interatomic Models (OpenKIM)}
repository of interatomic potentials to enable their use in LAMMPS scripts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The preferred interface for using interatomic models archived in
OpenKIM is the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim command}}}} interface. That
interface supports both “KIM Portable Models” (PMs) that conform to the
KIM API Portable Model Interface (PMI) and can be used by any
simulation code that conforms to the KIM API/PMI, and
“KIM Simulator Models” (SMs) that are natively implemented within a single
simulation code (like LAMMPS) and can only be used with it.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style kim} command is limited to KIM PMs. It is
used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim command}}}} interface as needed.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style kim} is called by \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim interactions} as needed,
it is not recommended to be directly used in input scripts.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} is the name of the KIM PM.
For potentials archived in OpenKIM
this is the extended KIM ID (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim command}}}}
for details). LAMMPS can invoke any KIM PM, however there can
be incompatibilities (for example due to unit matching issues).
In the event of an incompatibility, the code will terminate with
an error message. Check both the LAMMPS and KIM log files for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim} style, which
specifies the mapping of LAMMPS atom types to the species supported by
the KIM PM.  This is done by specifying \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} additional arguments
after the * * in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is the number of
LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of KIM elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, consider a KIM PM that supports Si and C species.
If the LAMMPS simulation has four atom types, where the first three are Si,
and the fourth is C, the following \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command would be used:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first two arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1, 2, and 3 to Si as
defined within KIM PM.  The final C argument maps LAMMPS atom type 4 to C.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the usual LAMMPS error messages, the KIM library itself
may generate errors, which should be printed to the screen.  In this
case it is also useful to check the \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim.log} file for additional error
information.  The file \sphinxstyleemphasis{kim.log} should be generated in the same
directory where LAMMPS is running.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To download, build, and install the KIM library on your system, see
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lib/kim/README} file.  Once you have done this and built LAMMPS
with the KIM package installed you can run the example input scripts
in \sphinxstyleemphasis{examples/kim}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mix, shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since KIM stores the potential parameters.
Thus, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in
an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the KIM package. See details on
restrictions in {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim command}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This current version of pair\_style kim is compatible with the
kim\sphinxhyphen{}api package version 2.0.0 and higher.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{kim_commands::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kim command}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kim:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{pair\_style kolmogorov/crespi/full@\spxentry{pair\_style kolmogorov/crespi/full}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style kolmogorov/crespi/full command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:pair-style-kolmogorov-crespi-full-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{full}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tap\PYGZus{}flag}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tap\_flag = 0/1 to turn off/on the taper function

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{full}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{none}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{full}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CH.KC}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{full}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{                    }\PYG{n}{CH.rebo}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{full}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CH\PYGZus{}taper.KC}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kolmogorov/crespi/full} style computes the Kolmogorov\sphinxhyphen{}Crespi (KC)
interaction potential as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:kolmogorov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kolmogorov)}}}}.
No simplification is made,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} E  = & \frac{1}{2} \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} V_{ij} \\
 V_{ij}  = & e^{-\lambda (r_{ij} -z_0)} \left [ C + f(\rho_{ij}) + f(\rho_{ji}) \right ] - A \left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{z_0}\right )^{-6} \\
\rho_{ij}^2 = & r_{ij}^2 - ({\bf r}_{ij}\cdot {\bf n}_{i})^2 \\
\rho_{ji}^2 = & r_{ij}^2 - ({\bf r}_{ij}\cdot  {\bf n}_{j})^2 \\
f(\rho) & =  e^{-(\rho/\delta)^2} \sum_{n=0}^2 C_{2n} { (\rho/\delta) }^{2n}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important to have a sufficiently large cutoff to ensure smooth
forces and to include all the pairs to build the neighbor list for
calculating the normals.  Energies are shifted so that they go
continuously to zero at the cutoff assuming that the exponential part of
\(V_{ij}\) (first term) decays sufficiently fast.  This shift is achieved by
the last term in the equation for \(V_{ij}\) above. This is essential only
when the tapper function is turned off. The formula of taper function
can be found in pair style {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ilp_graphene_hbn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{ilp/graphene/hbn}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential (ILP) is intended for interlayer interactions between two
different layers of graphene. To perform a realistic simulation, this potential
must be used in combination with intralayer potential, such as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_airebo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{AIREBO}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_tersoff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Tersoff}}}} potential.
To keep the intralayer properties unaffected, the interlayer interaction
within the same layers should be avoided. Hence, each atom has to have a layer
identifier such that atoms residing on the same layer interact via the
appropriate intralayer potential and atoms residing on different layers
interact via the ILP. Here, the molecule id is chosen as the layer identifier,
thus a data file with the “full” atom style is required to use this potential.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter file (e.g. CH.KC), is intended for use with \sphinxstyleemphasis{metal}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}, with energies in meV. Two additional parameters, \sphinxstyleemphasis{S},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcut} are included in the parameter file. \sphinxstyleemphasis{S} is designed to
facilitate scaling of energies. \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcut} is designed to build the neighbor
list for calculating the normals for each atom pair.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two new sets of parameters of KC potential for hydrocarbons, CH.KC
(without the taper function) and CH\_taper.KC (with the taper function)
are presented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:ouyang3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouyang1)}}}}.  The energy for the KC potential
with the taper function goes continuously to zero at the cutoff.  The
parameters in both CH.KC and CH\_taper.KC provide a good description in
both short\sphinxhyphen{} and long\sphinxhyphen{}range interaction regimes. While the original
parameters (CC.KC) published in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:kolmogorov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kolmogorov)}}}} are only
suitable for long\sphinxhyphen{}range interaction regime.  This feature is essential
for simulations in high pressure regime (i.e., the interlayer distance
is smaller than the equilibrium distance).  The benchmark tests and
comparison of these parameters can be found in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:ouyang3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouyang1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:ouyang4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouyang2)}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential must be used in combination with hybrid/overlay.
Other interactions can be set to zero using pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style tallies a breakdown of the total interlayer potential
energy into sub\sphinxhyphen{}categories, which can be accessed via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pair::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pair}}}} command as a vector of values of length 2.
The 2 values correspond to the following sub\sphinxhyphen{}categories:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{E\_vdW} = vdW (attractive) energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{E\_Rep} = Repulsive energy

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To print these quantities to the log file (with descriptive column
headings) the following commands could be included in an input script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{full}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Evdw}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}0[1]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Erep}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}0[2]}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{epair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}Erep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}Evdw}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the pair\_modify mix, shift, table,
and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write their information to binary restart
files, since it is stored in potential files. Thus, you need to
re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the INTERLAYER package.  It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the newton setting to be \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} for pair
interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CH.KC potential file provided with LAMMPS (see the potentials
folder) is parameterized for metal units.  You can use this pair style
with any LAMMPS units, but you would need to create your own custom
CH.KC potential file with all coefficients converted to the appropriate
units.

\section{pair\_style kolmogorov/crespi/z command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:pair-style-kolmogorov-crespi-z-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CC.KC}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{14.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{n}{CH.rebo}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kolmogorov}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{crespi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CC.KC}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{kolmogorov/crespi/z} style computes the Kolmogorov\sphinxhyphen{}Crespi interaction
potential as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:kc05}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kolmogorov)}}}}. An important simplification is made,
which is to take all normals along the z\sphinxhyphen{}axis.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E  = & \frac{1}{2} \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} V_{ij} \\
V_{ij}  = & e^{-\lambda(r_{ij} -z_0)} \left[ C + f(\rho_{ij}) + f(\rho_{ji}) \right] - A \left( \frac{r_{ij}}{z_0}\right)^{-6} + A \left( \frac{\textrm{cutoff}}{z_0}\right)^{-6} \\
\rho_{ij}^2 = & \rho_{ji}^2  =  x_{ij}^2 + y_{ij}^2 \qquad \qquad (\mathbf{n}_i \equiv \mathbf{\hat{z}}) \\
f(\rho)  = &  e^{-(\rho/\delta)^2} \sum_{n=0}^2 C_{2n} \left( \rho/\delta \right)^{2n}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important to have a sufficiently large cutoff to ensure smooth forces.
Energies are shifted so that they go continuously to zero at the cutoff assuming
that the exponential part of \(V_{ij}\) (first term) decays sufficiently fast.
This shift is achieved by the last term in the equation for \(V_{ij}\) above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential is intended for interactions between two layers of graphene.
Therefore, to avoid interaction between layers in multi\sphinxhyphen{}layered materials,
each layer should have a separate atom type and interactions should only
be computed between atom types of neighboring layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter file (e.g. CC.KC), is intended for use with metal
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}, with energies in meV. An additional parameter, \sphinxstyleemphasis{S},
is available to facilitate scaling of energies in accordance with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:vanwijk}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(vanWijk)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential must be used in combination with hybrid/overlay.
Other interactions can be set to zero using pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\label{\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_z:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_none::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_none}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_drip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style drip}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ilp_graphene_hbn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style ilp/graphene/hbn}}}}.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_kolmogorov_crespi_full::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style kolmogorov/crespi/full}}}},

\index{pair\_style lcbop@\spxentry{pair\_style lcbop}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style lcbop command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:pair-style-lcbop-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lcbop}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lcbop}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{..}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{potentials}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{C.lcbop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lcbop} pair style computes the long\sphinxhyphen{}range bond\sphinxhyphen{}order potential
for carbon (LCBOP) of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lcbop:los}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Los and Fasolino)}}}}.  See section II in
that paper for the analytic equations associated with the potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lcbop} style which
specifies an LCBOP potential file with parameters for specific
elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N
additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command,
where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of LCBOP elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, if your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atom types and you want
the first 3 to be C you would use the following pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C.lcbop}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first C argument maps LAMMPS atom type 1 to the C element in the
LCBOP file. If a mapping value is specified as NULL, the mapping is
not performed.  This can be used when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{lcbop} potential is used as
part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values are placeholders for
atom types that will be used with other potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters/coefficients for the LCBOP potential as applied to C
are listed in the C.lcbop file to agree with the original {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lcbop:los}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Los and Fasolino)}}}} paper.  Thus the parameters are specific to this
potential and the way it was fit, so modifying the file should be done
carefully.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mix, shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MANYBODY package.  It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair potential requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be
“on” for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C.lcbop}} potential file provided with LAMMPS (see the potentials
directory) is parameterized for {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{metal units}}}}.  You can use
the LCBOP potential with any LAMMPS units, but you would need to
create your own LCBOP potential file with coefficients listed in the
appropriate units if your simulation does not use “metal” units.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_airebo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_airebo}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lcbop:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{pair\_style lebedeva/z@\spxentry{pair\_style lebedeva/z}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style lebedeva/z command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:pair-style-lebedeva-z-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lebedeva}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lebedeva}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{none}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lebedeva}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CC.Lebedeva}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lebedeva}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{14.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{CH.rebo}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lebedeva}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CC.Lebedeva}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lebedeva/z} pair style computes the Lebedeva interaction potential
as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:leb01}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lebedeva1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:leb02}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lebedeva2)}}}}.  An important simplification is made, which is to take all
normals along the z\sphinxhyphen{}axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Lebedeva potential is intended for the description of the interlayer
interaction between graphene layers.  To perform a realistic simulation,
this potential must be used in combination with an intralayer potential
such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_airebo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{AIREBO}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_tersoff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Tersoff}}}}
facilitated by using pair style {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid/overlay}}}}.  To
keep the intralayer properties unaffected, the interlayer interaction
within the same layers should be avoided.  This can be achieved by
assigning different atom types to atoms of different layers (e.g. 1 and
2 in the examples above).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other interactions can be set to zero using pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E       = & \frac{1}{2} \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} V_{ij}\\
V_{ij}  = & B e^{-\alpha(r_{ij} - z_0)} \\
          & + C(1 + D_1\rho^2_{ij} + D_2\rho^4_{ij}) e^{-\lambda_1\rho^2_{ij}} e^{-\lambda_2 (z^2_{ij} - z^2_0)} \\
          & - A \left(\frac{z_0}{r_ij}\right)^6 + A \left( \frac{z_0}{r_c} \right)^6 \\
\rho^2_{ij} = & x^2_{ij} + y^2_{ij} \qquad (\mathbf{n_i} \equiv \mathbf{\hat{z}})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important to have a sufficiently large cutoff to ensure smooth forces.
Energies are shifted so that they go continuously to zero at the cutoff assuming
that the exponential part of \(V_{ij}\) (first term) decays sufficiently fast.
This shift is achieved by the last term in the equation for \(V_{ij}\) above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The provided parameter file (CC.Lebedeva) contains two sets of parameters.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The first set (element name “C”) is suitable for normal conditions and
is taken from {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:popov}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Popov1)}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second set (element name “C1”) is suitable for high\sphinxhyphen{}pressure
conditions and is taken from {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lebedeva_z:koziol}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Koziol1)}}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both sets contain an additional parameter, \sphinxstyleemphasis{S}, that can be used to
facilitate scaling of energies and is set to 1.0 by default.

\section{pair\_style lepton command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:pair-style-lepton-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:index-5}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:index-4}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul/comp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere/comp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for the interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul} args = cutoff keyword
  cutoff = global cutoff for the interactions (distance units)
  zero or more keywords may be appended
  keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{msm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dispersion} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tip4p}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for the interactions (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k*((r\PYGZhy{}r0)\PYGZca{}2*step(r0\PYGZhy{}r)); k=200; r0=1.5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{4.0*eps*((sig/r)\PYGZca{}12 \PYGZhy{} (sig/r)\PYGZca{}6);eps=1.0;sig=1.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.12246204830937}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{eps*(2.0*(sig/r)\PYGZca{}9 \PYGZhy{} 3.0*(sig/r)\PYGZca{}6);eps=1.0;sig=1.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{zbl(13,6,r)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{(1.0\PYGZhy{}switch)*zbl(6,6,r)\PYGZhy{}switch*4.0*eps*((sig/r)\PYGZca{}6);switch=0.5*(tanh(10.0*(r\PYGZhy{}sig))+1.0);eps=0.05;sig=3.20723}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{qi*qj/r}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{lj+coul; lj=4.0*eps*((sig/r)\PYGZca{}12 \PYGZhy{} (sig/r)\PYGZca{}6); eps=1.0; sig=1.0; coul=qi*qj/r}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pppm}
\PYG{k}{kspace\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pppm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0e\PYGZhy{}4}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{qi*qj/r*erfc(alpha*r); alpha=1.067}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{4.0*eps*((sig/r)\PYGZca{}12 \PYGZhy{} (sig/r)\PYGZca{}6); eps=1.0; sig=2.0*sqrt(radi*radj)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 8Feb2023: }added pair styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 15Jun2023: }added pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} compute pairwise
interactions between particles which depend on the distance and have a
cutoff.  The potential function must be provided as an expression string
using “r” as the distance variable.  With pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul} one
may additionally reference the charges of the two atoms of the pair with
“qi” and “qj”, respectively.  With pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} one may
instead reference the radii of the two atoms of the pair with “radi” and
“radj”, respectively; this is half of the diameter that can be set in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data files}}}} or the {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set command}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that further constants in the expressions can be defined in the
same string as additional expressions separated by semicolons as shown
in the examples above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression \sphinxtitleref{“200.0*(r\sphinxhyphen{}1.5)\textasciicircum{}2”} represents a harmonic potential
around the pairwise distance \(r_0\) of 1.5 distance units and a
force constant \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} of 200.0 energy units:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U_{ij} = K (r-r_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression \sphinxtitleref{“qi*qj/r”} represents a regular Coulombic potential with cutoff:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U_{ij} = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression \sphinxtitleref{“200.0*(r\sphinxhyphen{}(radi+radj)\textasciicircum{}2”} represents a harmonic potential
that has the equilibrium distance chosen so that the radii of the two
atoms touch:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U_{ij} = K (r-(r_i+r_j))^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://simtk.org/projects/lepton}{Lepton library}, that the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} pair style interfaces with, evaluates this expression string at
run time to compute the pairwise energy.  It also creates an analytical
representation of the first derivative of this expression with respect
to “r” and then uses that to compute the force between the pairs of
particles within the given cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above,
or in the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lepton expression (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Lepton expression must be either enclosed in quotes or must not
contain any whitespace so that LAMMPS recognizes it as a single keyword.
More on valid Lepton expressions below.  The last coefficient is
optional; it allows to set the cutoff for a pair of atom types to a
different value than the global cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} only the “lj” values of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings apply in case the interacting pair is also
connected with a bond.  The potential energy will \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} be added to the
“evdwl” property.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul} only the “coul” values of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings apply in case the
interacting pair is also connected with a bond.  The potential energy
will \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} be added to the “ecoul” property.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} only the “lj” values of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings apply in case the
interacting pair is also connected with a bond.  The potential energy
will \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} be added to the “evdwl” property.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the functions listed below, both pair styles support in
addition a custom “zbl(zi,zj,r)” function which computes the
Ziegler\sphinxhyphen{}Biersack\sphinxhyphen{}Littmark (ZBL) screened nuclear repulsion for
describing high\sphinxhyphen{}energy collisions between atoms.  For details of the
function please see the documentation for {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zbl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style zbl}}}}. The arguments of the function are the atomic numbers of
atom i (zi), atom j (zj) and the distance r.  Please see the examples
above.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numbers may be given in either decimal or exponential form.  All of the
following are valid numbers: \sphinxtitleref{5}, \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}3.1}, \sphinxtitleref{1e6}, and \sphinxtitleref{3.12e\sphinxhyphen{}2}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an extension to the standard Lepton syntax, it is also possible to
use LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}} in the format “v\_name”.  Before
evaluating the expression, “v\_name” will be replaced with the value of
the variable “name”.  This is compatible with all kinds of scalar
variables, but not with vectors, arrays, local, or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
variables.  If necessary, a custom scalar variable needs to be defined
that can access the desired (single) item from a non\sphinxhyphen{}scalar variable.
As an example, the following lines will instruct LAMMPS to ramp
the force constant for a harmonic bond from 100.0 to 200.0 during the
next run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fconst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{100.0, 200}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}fconst * (r\PYGZca{}2)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An expression may be followed by definitions for intermediate values that appear in the
expression. A semicolon “;” is used as a delimiter between value definitions. For example,
the expression:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
is exactly equivalent to

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The definition of an intermediate value may itself involve other
intermediate values. Whitespace and quotation characters (’\textquotesingle{}’ and ‘”’)
are ignored.  All uses of a value must appear \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} that value’s
definition.  For efficiency reasons, the expression string is parsed,
optimized, and then stored in an internal, pre\sphinxhyphen{}parsed representation for
evaluation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluating a Lepton expression is typically between 2.5 and 5 times
slower than the corresponding compiled and optimized C++ code.  If
additional speed or GPU acceleration (via GPU or KOKKOS) is required,
the interaction can be represented as a table.  Suitable table files
can be created either internally using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_write}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_write}}}} command or through the Python scripts
in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools:tabulate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{tools/tabulate}}}} folder.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} do not support
mixing.  Thus, expressions for \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} I,J pairs must be specified
explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify shift}}}}
option for shifting the potential energy of the pair interaction so that
it is 0 at the cutoff, pair styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} do \sphinxstyleemphasis{not}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify table}}}} options are not relevant for
the these pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify tail}}}} option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy
and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lepton:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the LEPTON package and only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with this package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/coul} requires that atom atoms have a charge
property, e.g. via {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style charge}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/sphere} requires that atom atoms have a radius
property, e.g. via {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}.

\section{pair\_style line/lj command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:pair-style-line-lj-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:syntax}}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for interactions (distance units)


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.12}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{line/lj} treats particles which are line segments as a set of
small spherical particles that tile the line segment length as explained
below.  Interactions between two line segments, each with N1 and N2
spherical particles, are calculated as the pairwise sum of N1*N2
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions.  Interactions between a line segment with N
spherical particles and a point particle are treated as the pairwise sum
of N Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/cut}}}} page for the definition of Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The set of non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping spherical sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles that represent a
line segment are generated in the following manner.  Their size is a
function of the line segment length and the specified sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle
size for that particle type.  If a line segment has a length L and is
of type I, then the number of spheres N that represent the segment is
calculated as N = L/sizeI, rounded up to an integer value.  Thus if L
is not evenly divisible by sizeI, N is incremented to include one
extra sphere.  The centers of the spheres are spaced equally along the
line segment.  Imagine N+1 equally\sphinxhyphen{}space points, which include the 2
end points of the segment.  The sphere centers are halfway between
each pair of points.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The LJ interaction between 2 spheres on different line segments (or a
sphere on a line segment and a point particles) is computed with
sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle \(\epsilon\), \(\sigma\), and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} values that
are set by the pair\_coeff command, as described below.  If the distance
between the 2 spheres is greater than the sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle cutoff, there is
no interaction.  This means that some pairs of sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles on 2 line
segments may interact, but others may not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For purposes of creating the neighbor list for pairs of interacting
line segments or lines/point particles, a regular particle\sphinxhyphen{}particle
cutoff is used, as defined by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} setting above in the
pair\_style command or overridden with an optional argument in the
pair\_coeff command for a type pair as discussed below.  The distance
between the centers of 2 line segments, or the center of a line
segment and a point particle, must be less than this distance (plus
the neighbor skin; see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} command), for
the pair of particles to be included in the neighbor list.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This means that a too\sphinxhyphen{}short value for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} setting can
exclude a pair of particles from the neighbor list even if pairs of
their sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle spheres would interact, based on the sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle
cutoff specified in the pair\_coeff command.  E.g. sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles at the
ends of the line segments that are close to each other.  Which may not
be what you want, since it means the ends of 2 line segments could
pass through each other.  It is up to you to specify a \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff}
setting that is consistent with the length of the line segments you
are using and the sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle cutoff settings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{line/lj}, the following coefficients must be defined for
each pair of atom types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command
as in the examples above, or in the data file or restart files read by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sizeI (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sizeJ (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
subcutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sizeI} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sizeJ} coefficients are the sub\sphinxhyphen{}particle sizes for
line particles of type I and type J.  They are used to define the N
sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles per segment as described above.  These coefficients are
actually stored on a per\sphinxhyphen{}type basis.  Thus if there are multiple
pair\_coeff commands that involve type I, as either the first or
second atom type, you should use consistent values for sizeI or sizeJ
in all of them.  If you do not do this, the last value specified for
sizeI will apply to all segments of type I.  If typeI or typeJ refers
to point particles, the corresponding sizeI or sizeJ is ignored; it
can be set to 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(\epsilon\), \(\sigma\), and \sphinxstyleemphasis{subcutoff} coefficients are
used to compute an LJ interactions between a pair of sub\sphinxhyphen{}particles on 2
line segments (of type I and J), or between a sub particle/point
particle pair.  As discussed above, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{subcutoff} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} params
are different.  The latter is only used for building the neighbor list
when the distance between centers of two line segments or one segment
and a point particle is calculated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cutoff} coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global
cutoff is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, coefficients must be specified.
No default mixing rules are used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_line_lj:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Defining particles to be line segments so they participate in
line/line or line/particle interactions requires the use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style line}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{pair\_style list@\spxentry{pair\_style list}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style list command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:pair-style-list-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_list:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_list::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{list}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{listfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
listfile = name of file with list of pairwise interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = optional flag \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocheck} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{check} (default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{check})

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{list}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{restraints.txt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1225}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{list}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair\PYGZus{}list.txt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{list}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{list} computes interactions between explicitly listed pairs of
atoms with the option to select functional form and parameters for each
individual pair.  Because the parameters are set in the list file, the
pair\_coeff command has no parameters (but still needs to be provided).
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{check} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocheck} keywords enable/disable tests that checks
whether all listed pairs of atom IDs were present and the interactions
computed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocheck} is set and either atom ID is not present, the
interaction is skipped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can be thought of as a hybrid between bonded,
non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded, and restraint interactions.  It will typically be used as an
additional interaction within the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/overlay} pair style.  It
currently supports three interaction styles: a 12\sphinxhyphen{}6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones, a
Morse and a harmonic potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of the list file is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one line per pair of atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
empty lines will be ignored

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
comment text starts with a ‘\#’ character

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
line syntax: \sphinxstyleemphasis{ID1 ID2 style coeffs cutoff}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ID1 = atom ID of first atom
ID2 = atom ID of second atom
style = style of interaction
coeffs = list of coeffs
cutoff = cutoff for interaction (optional)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoff parameter is optional for all but the \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} interactions.
If it is not specified, the global cutoff is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} this is a comment

15 259 lj126     1.0 1.0      50.0
15 603 morse    10.0 1.2 2.0  10.0 \PYGZsh{} and another comment
18 470 harmonic 50.0 1.2       5.0
19 332 quartic  10.0 5.0 \PYGZhy{}1.2 1.2
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj126} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} - \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right] \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = D_0 \left[ 1 - e^{-\alpha (r - r_0)} \right]^2 \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(D_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (1/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_0)^2 \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_0)^2 (r - r_0 -b_1) (r - r_0 - b_2) \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the coefficients:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(b_1\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(b_2\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mixing since all parameters are
explicit for each pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option is supported by this
pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and tail options are not
relevant for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not use a neighbor list and instead identifies
atoms by their IDs.  This has two consequences: 1) The cutoff has to be
chosen sufficiently large, so that the second atom of a pair has to be a
ghost atom on the same node on which the first atom is local; otherwise
the interaction will be skipped.  You can use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{check} option to
detect, if interactions are missing.  2) Unlike other pair styles in
LAMMPS, an atom I will not interact with multiple images of atom J
(assuming the images are within the cutoff distance), but only with the
closest image.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the MISC package. It is only enabled if LAMMPS is
build with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page on for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/cut}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_morse::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style morse}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style harmonic}}}}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_quartic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style quartic}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_list:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstepscope

\section{pair\_style lj/cut command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:pair-style-lj-cut-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:index-5}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:index-4}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/opt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for Lennard Jones interactions (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.8}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} styles compute the standard 12/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential,
given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
    \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]   \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/cut/coul}}}} styles to add a Coulombic
pairwise interaction and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/cut/tip4p}}}} styles to
add the TIP4P water model.


\subsection{Coefficients}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LJ cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global
LJ cutoff specified in the pair\_style command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma\) is defined in the LJ formula as the
zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing distance for the potential, \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} as the energy minimum at
\(r_0 = 2^{\frac{1}{6}} \sigma\).  The \_same\_ potential function becomes:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)^{12} -
     2 \left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)^6 \right]  \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the minimum as reference width. In the literature both
formulations are used, but the describe the same potential, only the
\(\sigma\) value must be computed by \(\sigma = r_0 /
2^{\frac{1}{6}}\) for use with LAMMPS, if this latter formulation is
used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
A version of these styles with a soft core, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/soft}, suitable
for use in free energy calculations, is part of the FEP package and
is documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}}
styles.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the lj/cut pair styles can be mixed.
The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option for the energy of the
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range
tail correction to the energy and pressure for the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do
not need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command,
meaning the pairwise forces can be partitioned by distance at different
levels of the rRESPA hierarchy.  The other styles only support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of run\_style respa.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}}
command for details.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj96:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj96/cut} style compute a 9/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential, instead
of the standard 12/6 potential, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{9} -
\left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
                    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global LJ
cutoff specified in the pair\_style command is used.

\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:pair-style-lj-cubic-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:syntax}}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cubic} style computes a truncated LJ interaction potential
whose energy and force are continuous everywhere.  Inside the
inflection point the interaction is identical to the standard 12/6
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones}}}} potential.  The LJ function outside the
inflection point is replaced with a cubic function of distance. The
energy, force, and second derivative are continuous at the inflection
point.  The cubic coefficient A3 is chosen so that both energy and
force go to zero at the cutoff distance.  Outside the cutoff distance
the energy and force are zero.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = u_{LJ}(r) \qquad r \leq r_s \\
  & = u_{LJ}(r_s) + (r-r_s) u'_{LJ}(r_s) - \frac{1}{6} A_3 (r-r_s)^3 \qquad r_s < r \leq r_c \\
  & = 0 \qquad r > r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The location of the inflection point \(r_s\) is defined
by the LJ diameter, \(r_s/\sigma = (26/7)^{1/6}\). The cutoff distance
is defined by \(r_c/r_s = 67/48\) or \(r_c/\sigma = 1.737...\)
The analytic expression for the
the cubic coefficient
\(A_3 r_{min}^3/\epsilon = 27.93...\) is given in the paper by
Holian and Ravelo {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:holian}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Holian)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential is commonly used to study the shock mechanics of FCC
solids, as in Ravelo et al. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:ravelo2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ravelo)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above,
or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma\) is defined in the LJ formula as the
zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing distance for the potential, not as the energy minimum,
which is located at \(r_{min} = 2^{\frac{1}{6}} \sigma\). In the
above example, \(\sigma = 0.8908987\), so \(r_{min} = 1.0\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cubic:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the lj/cut pair styles can be mixed.
The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command

\sphinxAtStartPar
The lj/cubic pair style does not support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option,
since pair interaction is already smoothed to 0.0 at the
cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The lj/cubic pair style does not support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail
corrections to energy and pressure, since there are no corrections for
a potential that goes to 0.0 at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The lj/cubic pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do
not need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The lj/cubic pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair}
keyword of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not
support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.
