\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/debye} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/dsf} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/msm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/wolf}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/cut} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/debye} args = kappa cutoff (cutoff2)
  kappa = inverse of the Debye length (inverse distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/dsf} args = alpha cutoff (cutoff2)
  alpha = damping parameter (inverse distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/msm} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/wolf} args = alpha cutoff (cutoff2)
  alpha = damping parameter (inverse distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 2 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul} styles compute the standard 12/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential,
given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
    \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
                    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/cut} adds a Coulombic pairwise interaction given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(C\) is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\)
are the charges on the two atoms, and \(\epsilon\) is the dielectric
constant which can be set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command.
If one cutoff is specified in the pair\_style command, it is used for
both the LJ and Coulombic terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, they are
used as cutoffs for the LJ and Coulombic terms respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/debye} adds an additional exp() damping factor
to the Coulombic term, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \exp(- \kappa r) \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\kappa\) is the inverse of the Debye length.  This potential
is another way to mimic the screening effect of a polar solvent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/dsf} computes the Coulombic term via the damped
shifted force model described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:fennell2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Fennell}}}}, given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E =
 q_iq_j \left[ \frac{\mbox{erfc} (\alpha r)}{r} -  \frac{\mbox{erfc} (\alpha r_c)}{r_c} +
\left( \frac{\mbox{erfc} (\alpha r_c)}{r_c^2} +  \frac{2\alpha}{\sqrt{\pi}}\frac{\exp (-\alpha^2    r^2_c)}{r_c} \right)(r-r_c) \right] \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\alpha\) is the damping parameter and erfc() is the complementary
error\sphinxhyphen{}function. This potential is essentially a short\sphinxhyphen{}range,
spherically\sphinxhyphen{}truncated, charge\sphinxhyphen{}neutralized, shifted, pairwise \sphinxstyleemphasis{1/r}
summation.  The potential is based on Wolf summation, proposed as an
alternative to Ewald summation for condensed phase systems where
charge screening causes electrostatic interactions to become
effectively short\sphinxhyphen{}ranged. In order for the electrostatic sum to be
absolutely convergent, charge neutralization within the cutoff radius
is enforced by shifting the potential through placement of image
charges on the cutoff sphere. Convergence can often be improved by
setting \(\alpha\) to a small non\sphinxhyphen{}zero value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/msm} compute the same
Coulombic interactions as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/cut} except that an
additional damping factor is applied to the Coulombic term so it can
be used in conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}}
command and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} option.  The Coulombic cutoff
specified for this style means that pairwise interactions within this
distance are computed directly; interactions outside that distance are
computed in reciprocal space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/wolf} adds a Coulombic pairwise interaction via the Wolf
summation method, described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:wolf3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Wolf}}}}, given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_i = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{j \neq i}
\frac{q_i q_j {\rm erfc}(\alpha r_{ij})}{r_{ij}} +
\frac{1}{2} \sum_{j \neq i}
\frac{q_i q_j {\rm erf}(\alpha r_{ij})}{r_{ij}} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\alpha\) is the damping parameter, and erfc() is the
complementary error\sphinxhyphen{}function terms.  This potential is essentially a
short\sphinxhyphen{}range, spherically\sphinxhyphen{}truncated, charge\sphinxhyphen{}neutralized, shifted,
pairwise \sphinxstyleemphasis{1/r} summation.  With a manipulation of adding and subtracting
a self term (for i = j) to the first and second term on the
right\sphinxhyphen{}hand\sphinxhyphen{}side, respectively, and a small enough \(\alpha\) damping
parameter, the second term shrinks and the potential becomes a
rapidly\sphinxhyphen{}converging real\sphinxhyphen{}space summation.  With a long enough cutoff and
small enough \(\alpha\) parameter, the energy and forces calculated by the
Wolf summation method approach those of the Ewald sum.  So it is a means
of getting effective long\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions with a short\sphinxhyphen{}range
potential.


\subsection{Coefficients}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For all of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul} pair styles, the following coefficients must
be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as
described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff1 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma\) is defined in the LJ formula as the zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing
distance for the potential, not as the energy minimum at \(2^{\frac{1}{6}} \sigma\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global
LJ and Coulombic cutoffs specified in the pair\_style command are used.
If only one cutoff is specified, it is used as the cutoff for both LJ
and Coulombic interactions for this type pair.  If both coefficients
are specified, they are used as the LJ and Coulombic cutoffs for this
type pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/msm} only the LJ cutoff can be
specified since a Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J
type pair.  All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff specified in
the pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
A version of these styles with a soft core, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/soft}and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long/soft}, suitable for use in free energy calculations, is
part of the FEP package and is documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}} styles.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the lj/cut pair styles can be mixed.
The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option for the energy of the
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option since they can tabulate
the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range
tail correction to the energy and pressure for the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do
not need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} pair styles support the use of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command, meaning the pairwise forces can be
partitioned by distance at different levels of the rRESPA hierarchy.
The other styles only support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of run\_style respa.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_coul:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/msm} styles are part of the KSPACE package.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/debye}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/dsf}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/wolf} styles are part
of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.

These styles are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with those respective
packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for
more info.

\section{pair\_style lj/cut/sphere command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:pair-style-lj-cut-sphere-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variant: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Jun2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} style compute the standard 12/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential,
given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r}\right)^{12} -
    \left(\frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r}\right)^6 \right]  \qquad  r < r_c * \sigma_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff ratio.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the same potential function used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/cut}}}} pair style, but the \(\sigma_{ij}\) parameter is not
set as a per\sphinxhyphen{}type parameter via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff command}}}}.  Instead it is calculated individually for each pair
using the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom diameter attribute of {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} for the two atoms as \(\sigma_{i}\) and
\(\sigma_{j}\); \(\sigma_{ij}\) is then computed by the mixing
rule for pair coefficients as set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify mix}}}} command (defaults to geometric mixing).  The cutoff is
not specified as a distance, but as ratio that is internally
multiplied by \(\sigma_{ij}\) to obtain the actual cutoff for each
pair of atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma_{ij}\) is defined in the LJ formula above as the
zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing distance for the potential, \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} as the energy minimum which
is at \(2^{\frac{1}{6}} \sigma_{ij}\).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Notes on cutoffs, neighbor lists, and efficiency}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If your system is mildly polydisperse, meaning the ratio of the
diameter of the largest particle to the smallest is less than 2.0,
then the neighbor lists built by the code should be reasonably
efficient.  Which means they will not contain too many particle
pairs that do not interact.  However, if your system is highly
polydisperse (ratio \textgreater{} 2.0), the neighbor list build and force
computations may be inefficient.  There are two ways to try and
speed up the simulations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first is to assign atoms to different atom types so that atoms of
each type are similar in size.  E.g. if particle diameters range from
1 to 5 use 4 atom types, ensuring atoms of type 1 have diameters from
1.0\sphinxhyphen{}2.0, type 2 from 2.0\sphinxhyphen{}3.0, etc.  This will reduce the number of
non\sphinxhyphen{}interacting pairs in the neighbor lists and thus reduce the time
spent on computing pairwise interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor multi}}}} command
which enabled a different algorithm for building neighbor lists.  This
will also require that you assign multiple atom types according to
diameters, but will in addition use a more efficient size\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
strategy to construct the neighbor lists and thus reduce the time
spent on building neighbor lists.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are example input script commands using both ideas for a
highly polydisperse system:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{n}{lj}
\PYG{n}{atom\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{n}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.8442}
\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}
\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}box}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}atoms}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{ create atoms with random diameters from bimodal distribution}
\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{switch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{345634}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}switch}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.75}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{normal}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.075}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{325}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}switch}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.7}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{normal}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{453}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diameter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}diam}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{ assign type 2 to atoms with diameter \PYGZgt{} 0.6}
\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{radius}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}
\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}
\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}

\PYG{n}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.5}
\PYG{n}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}

\PYG{n}{neighbor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{multi}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using multiple atom types speeds up the calculation for this example
by more than a factor of 2, and using the multi\sphinxhyphen{}style neighbor list
build causes an additional speedup of about 20 percent.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Coefficients}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LJ cutoff ratio (unitless) (optional)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global LJ
cutoff ratio specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style command}}}} is
used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a repulsive only LJ interaction is desired, the coefficient for the cutoff
ratio should be set to the minimum of the LJ potential using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$(2.0\textasciicircum{}(1.0/6.0))}}

Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon coefficients and cutoff
ratio for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} pair style can be mixed.  The default mixing
style is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify command}}}}
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify shift}}}}
option for the energy of the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} pair style does \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to
the energy and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not
need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} pair style is only enabled if LAMMPS was built with the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page
for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/sphere} pair style does not support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sixthpower} mixing rule.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/cut} args = otype htype btype atype qdist cutoff (cutoff2)
  otype,htype = atom types (numeric or type label) for TIP4P O and H
  btype,atype = bond and angle types (numeric or type label) for TIP4P waters
  qdist = distance from O atom to massless charge (distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long} args = otype htype btype atype qdist cutoff (cutoff2)
  otype,htype = atom types (numeric or type label) for TIP4P O and H
  btype,atype = bond and angle types (numeric or type label) for TIP4P waters
  qdist = distance from O atom to massless charge (distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p} styles implement the TIP4P water model of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p:jorgensen2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jorgensen)}}}} and similar models, which introduce a
massless site M located a short distance away from the oxygen atom along
the bisector of the HOH angle.  The atomic types of the oxygen and
hydrogen atoms, the bond and angle types for OH and HOH interactions,
and the distance to the massless charge site are specified as pair\_style
arguments and are used to identify the TIP4P\sphinxhyphen{}like molecules and
determine the position of the M site from the positions of the hydrogen
and oxygen atoms of the water molecules.  The M site location is used
for all Coulomb interactions instead of the oxygen atom location, also
with all other atom types, while the location of the oxygen atom is used
for the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions.  Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/cut} uses a
cutoff for Coulomb interactions; style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long} is for use
with a long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic solver (Ewald or PPPM).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each TIP4P water molecule in your system, the atom IDs for
the O and 2 H atoms must be consecutive, with the O atom first.  This
is to enable LAMMPS to “find” the 2 H atoms associated with each O
atom.  For example, if the atom ID of an O atom in a TIP4P water
molecule is 500, then its 2 H atoms must have IDs 501 and 502.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If using type labels, the type labels must be defined before calling
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_tip4p::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto tip4p}}}} page for more information
on how to use the TIP4P pair styles and lists of parameters to set.
Note that the neighbor list cutoff for Coulomb interactions is
effectively extended by a distance 2*qdist when using the TIP4P pair
style, to account for the offset distance of the fictitious charges on
O atoms in water molecules.  Thus it is typically best in an
efficiency sense to use a LJ cutoff \textgreater{}= Coulombic cutoff + 2*qdist, to
shrink the size of the neighbor list.  This leads to slightly larger
cost for the long\sphinxhyphen{}range calculation, so you can test the trade\sphinxhyphen{}off for
your model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p} styles compute the standard 12/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential,
given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
    \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
                    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
They add Coulombic pairwise interactions given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(C\) is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\)
are the charges on the two atoms, and \(\epsilon\) is the dielectric
constant which can be set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command.
If one cutoff is specified in the pair\_style command, it is used for
both the LJ and Coulombic terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, they are
used as cutoffs for the LJ and Coulombic terms respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long} compute the same
Coulombic interactions as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/cut} except that an
additional damping factor is applied to the Coulombic term so it can
be used in conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}}
command and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} option.  The Coulombic cutoff
specified for this style means that pairwise interactions within this
distance are computed directly; interactions outside that distance are
computed in reciprocal space.


\subsection{Coefficients}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p:coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For all of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles, the following coefficients must
be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as
described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LJ cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma\) is defined in the LJ formula as the zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing
distance for the potential, not as the energy minimum at \(2^{\frac{1}{6}} \sigma\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global
LJ cutoff specified in the pair\_style command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/cut} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long} only the LJ cutoff can be
specified since a Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J
type pair. All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff specified in
the pair\_style command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because of how these pair styles implement the coulomb interactions
by implicitly defining a fourth site for the negative charge
of the TIP4P and similar water models, special care must be taken
when using these pair styles with other computations that also use
charges.  Unless they are specially set up to also handle the implicit
definition of the 4th site, results are likely incorrect.  Example:
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_dipole_chunk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute dipole/chunk}}}}.  For the same
reason, when using one of these pair styles with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style  hybrid}}}}, \sphinxstylestrong{all} coulomb interactions
should be handled by a single sub\sphinxhyphen{}style with TIP4P support. All other
instances and styles will “see” the M point charges at the position
of the Oxygen atom and thus compute incorrect forces and energies.
LAMMPS will print a warning when it detects one of these issues.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
A version of these styles with a soft core, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long/soft}, suitable
for use in free energy calculations, is part of the FEP package and
is documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}}
styles.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the lj/cut pair styles can be mixed.
The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option for the energy of the
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option since they can tabulate
the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range
tail correction to the energy and pressure for the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do
not need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/coul/long} pair styles support the use of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command, meaning the pairwise forces can be
partitioned by distance at different levels of the rRESPA hierarchy.
The other styles only support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of run\_style respa.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/long} styles are part of the
KSPACE package. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/tip4p/cut} style is part of the MOLECULE
package. These styles are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with those
packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for
more info.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_expand:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/expand} computes a LJ interaction with a distance shifted by
delta which can be useful when particles are of different sizes, since
it is different that using different sigma values in a standard LJ
formula:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r - \Delta}\right)^{12} -
  \left(\frac{\sigma}{r - \Delta}\right)^6 \right]
  \qquad r < r_c + \Delta\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff which does not include the \(\Delta\)
distance.  I.e. the actual force cutoff is the sum of \(r_c +
\Delta\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/expand} pair styles, the following coefficients must
be defined for each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data file or
restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as described
below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(\Delta\) values can be positive or negative.  The last
coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global LJ cutoff is
used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/expand/coul/long} only the LJ cutoff can be specified since a
Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J type pair.
All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff specified in the
pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}

produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_expand:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon, sigma, and shift
coefficients and cutoff distance for this pair style can be mixed.
Shift is always mixed via an \sphinxstyleemphasis{arithmetic} rule.  The other
coefficients are mixed according to the pair\_modify mix value.  The
default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail
option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail correction to the energy and
pressure of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_expand_sphere:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Jun2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/expand/sphere} style compute a 12/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential with
a distance shifted by \(\Delta = \frac{1}{2} (d_i + d_j)\), the
average diameter of both atoms.  This can be used to model particles of
different sizes but same interactions, which is different from using
different sigma values as in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style lj/cut/sphere}}}}.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r - \Delta}\right)^{12} -
  \left(\frac{\sigma}{r - \Delta}\right)^6 \right]
  \qquad r < r_c + \Delta\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff which does not include the distance \(\Delta\).
I.e. the actual force cutoff is the sum \(r_c + \Delta\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the same potential function used by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{lj/expand}}}} pair style, but the \(\Delta\) parameter is not
set as a per\sphinxhyphen{}type parameter via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff command}}}}.  Instead it is calculated individually for each pair
using the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom diameter attribute of {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}} for the two atoms as the average diameter, \(\Delta = \frac{1}{2} (d_i + d_j)\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(\sigma\) is defined in the LJ formula above as the
zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing distance for the potential, \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} as the energy minimum which
is at \(2^{\frac{1}{6}} \sigma\).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Notes on cutoffs, neighbor lists, and efficiency}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If your system is mildly polydisperse, meaning the ratio of the
diameter of the largest particle to the smallest is less than 2.0,
then the neighbor lists built by the code should be reasonably
efficient.  Which means they will not contain too many particle
pairs that do not interact.  However, if your system is highly
polydisperse (ratio \textgreater{} 2.0), the neighbor list build and force
computations may be inefficient.  There are two ways to try and
speed up the simulations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first is to assign atoms to different atom types so that atoms of
each type are similar in size.  E.g. if particle diameters range from
1 to 5 use 4 atom types, ensuring atoms of type 1 have diameters from
1.0\sphinxhyphen{}2.0, type 2 from 2.0\sphinxhyphen{}3.0, etc.  This will reduce the number of
non\sphinxhyphen{}interacting pairs in the neighbor lists and thus reduce the time
spent on computing pairwise interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second is to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor multi}}}} command
which enabled a different algorithm for building neighbor lists.  This
will also require that you assign multiple atom types according to
diameters, but will in addition use a more efficient size\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
strategy to construct the neighbor lists and thus reduce the time
spent on building neighbor lists.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are example input script commands using the first option for a
highly polydisperse system:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{n}{lj}
\PYG{n}{atom\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{sphere}
\PYG{n}{lattice}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{n}{fcc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.8442}
\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{block}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}
\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}box}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}
\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}atoms}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{box}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{ create atoms with random diameters from bimodal distribution}
\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{switch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{345634}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}switch}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.75}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{normal}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.04}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{325}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}switch}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.7}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{normal}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{453}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diameter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}diam}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{ assign type 2 to atoms with diameter \PYGZgt{} 0.35}
\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{radius}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.35}
\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{variable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}
\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{group}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{large}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}

\PYG{n}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{expand}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sphere}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}
\PYG{n}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}

\PYG{n}{neighbor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bin}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using multiple atom types speeds up the calculation for this example
by more than 30 percent, but using the multi\sphinxhyphen{}style neighbor list does
not provide a speedup.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Coefficients}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_expand_sphere:coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LJ cutoff (distance units) (optional)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global LJ
cutoff specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style command}}}} is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon, sigma, and cutoff

option for the energy of the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/expand/sphere} pair style does \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to
the energy and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/expand/sphere} pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not
need to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\section{pair\_style lj/long/tip4p/long command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_long:pair-style-lj-long-tip4p-long-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_long:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/tip4p/long}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/coul/long} args = flag\_lj flag\_coul cutoff (cutoff2)
  flag\_lj = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use Kspace long\sphinxhyphen{}range summation for dispersion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut} = use a cutoff on dispersion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = omit disperion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term entirely
  flag\_coul = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use Kspace long\sphinxhyphen{}range summation for Coulombic 1/r term
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = omit Coulombic term
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/tip4p/long} args = flag\_lj flag\_coul otype htype btype atype qdist cutoff (cutoff2)
  flag\_lj = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use Kspace long\sphinxhyphen{}range summation for dispersion 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 term
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut} = use a cutoff
  flag\_coul = \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{long} = use Kspace long\sphinxhyphen{}range summation for Coulombic 1/r term
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} = omit Coulombic term
  otype,htype = atom types (numeric or type label) for TIP4P O and H
  btype,atype = bond and angle types (numeric or type label) for TIP4P waters
  qdist = distance from O atom to massless charge (distance units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_long:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/coul/long} computes the standard 12/6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} -
                    \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right]
                    \qquad r < r_c \\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\epsilon\) and \(\sigma\) being the usual Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
potential parameters, plus the Coulomb potential, given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where C is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\) are the charges on
the two atoms, \(\epsilon\) is the dielectric constant which can be set by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command, and \(r_c\) is the cutoff.  If
one cutoff is specified in the pair\_style command, it is used for both
the LJ and Coulombic terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, they are
used as cutoffs for the LJ and Coulombic terms respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The purpose of this pair style is to capture long\sphinxhyphen{}range interactions
resulting from both attractive 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones and Coulombic 1/r
interactions.  This is done by use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul}
settings.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_long:veld2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{In ‘t Veld}}}} paper has more details on when it is
appropriate to include long\sphinxhyphen{}range 1/r\textasciicircum{}6 interactions, using this
potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/tip4p/long} implements the TIP4P water model of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_long:jorgensen4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jorgensen)}}}}, which introduces a massless site located a
short distance away from the oxygen atom along the bisector of the HOH
angle.  The atomic types of the oxygen and hydrogen atoms, the bond
and angle types for OH and HOH interactions, and the distance to the
massless charge site are specified as pair\_style arguments.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each TIP4P water molecule in your system, the atom IDs for
the O and 2 H atoms must be consecutive, with the O atom first.  This
is to enable LAMMPS to “find” the 2 H atoms associated with each O
atom.  For example, if the atom ID of an O atom in a TIP4P water
molecule is 500, then its 2 H atoms must have IDs 501 and 502.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If using type labels, the type labels must be defined before calling
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_tip4p::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto tip4p}}}} page for more
information on how to use the TIP4P pair style.  Note that the
neighbor list cutoff for Coulomb interactions is effectively extended
by a distance 2*qdist when using the TIP4P pair style, to account for
the offset distance of the fictitious charges on O atoms in water
molecules.  Thus it is typically best in an efficiency sense to use a
LJ cutoff \textgreater{}= Coulombic cutoff + 2*qdist, to shrink the size of the
neighbor list.  This leads to slightly larger cost for the long\sphinxhyphen{}range
calculation, so you can test the trade\sphinxhyphen{}off for your model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, no cutoff is used on the LJ 1/r\textasciicircum{}6
dispersion term.  The long\sphinxhyphen{}range portion can be calculated by using
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style ewald/disp or pppm/disp}}}} commands.
The specified LJ cutoff then determines which portion of the LJ
interactions are computed directly by the pair potential versus which
part is computed in reciprocal space via the Kspace style.  If
\sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}, the LJ interactions are simply cutoff, as
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/cut}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, no cutoff is used on the Coulombic
interactions.  The long\sphinxhyphen{}range portion can calculated by using any of
several {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}} command options such as
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald}.  Note that if \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} is also set to long, then
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald/disp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm/disp} Kspace style needs to be used to
perform the long\sphinxhyphen{}range calculations for both the LJ and Coulombic
interactions.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul} is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{off}, Coulombic interactions
are not computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff1 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that sigma is defined in the LJ formula as the zero\sphinxhyphen{}crossing
distance for the potential, not as the energy minimum at 2\textasciicircum{}(1/6)
sigma.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global
LJ and Coulombic cutoffs specified in the pair\_style command are used.
If only one cutoff is specified, it is used as the cutoff for both LJ
and Coulombic interactions for this type pair.  If both coefficients
are specified, they are used as the LJ and Coulombic cutoffs for this
type pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if you are using \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, you
cannot specify a LJ cutoff for an atom type pair, since only one
global LJ cutoff is allowed.  Similarly, if you are using \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_coul}
set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{long}, you cannot specify a Coulombic cutoff for an atom type
pair, since only one global Coulombic cutoff is allowed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/long/tip4p/long} only the LJ cutoff can be specified
since a Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J
type pair.  All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff
specified in the pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
A version of these styles with a soft core, \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/soft}, suitable for use in
free energy calculations, is part of the FEP package and is documented with
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}} styles. The version with soft core is
only available if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_lj_long:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the lj/long pair styles can be mixed.
The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command
for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair
interaction, assuming \sphinxstyleemphasis{flag\_lj} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{cut}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and
table/disp options since they can tabulate the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of
the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic and dispersion interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thes pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail correction to the
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the energy and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair lj/long/coul/long styles support the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}}
command, meaning the pairwise forces can be partitioned by distance at
different levels of the rRESPA hierarchy.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

These styles are part of the KSPACE package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.
