\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam:description}}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The behavior of the MEAM potential for alloy systems has changed
as of November 2010; see description below of the mixture\_ref\_t
parameter
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} computes non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded interactions for a variety of
materials using the modified embedded\sphinxhyphen{}atom method (MEAM) {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:baskes}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baskes)}}}}.  Conceptually, it is an extension to the original {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{EAM
method}}}} which adds angular forces.  It is thus suitable for
modeling metals and alloys with fcc, bcc, hcp and diamond cubic
structures, as well as materials with covalent interactions like silicon
and carbon.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} pair style is a translation of the original Fortran version
to C++. It is functionally equivalent but more efficient and has
additional features. The Fortran version of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} pair style has
been removed from LAMMPS after the 12 December 2018 release.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/ms} uses the multi\sphinxhyphen{}state MEAM (MS\sphinxhyphen{}MEAM) method
according to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:baskes2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baskes2)}}}}, which is an extension to MEAM.
This pair style is mostly equivalent to \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} and differs only
where noted in the documentation below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the MEAM formulation, the total energy E of a system of atoms is
given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \sum_i \left\{ F_i(\bar{\rho}_i)
    + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i \neq j} \phi_{ij} (r_{ij}) \right\}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{F} is the embedding energy which is a function of the atomic
electron density \(\rho\), and \(\phi\) is a pair potential
interaction.  The pair interaction is summed over all neighbors J of
atom I within the cutoff distance.  As with EAM, the multi\sphinxhyphen{}body nature
of the MEAM potential is a result of the embedding energy term.  Details
of the computation of the embedding and pair energies, as implemented in
LAMMPS, are given in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:gullet}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Gullet)}}}} and references therein.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The various parameters in the MEAM formulas are listed in two files
which are specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.
These are ASCII text files in a format consistent with other MD codes
that implement MEAM potentials, such as the serial DYNAMO code and
Warp.  Several MEAM potential files with parameters for different
materials are included in the “potentials” directory of the LAMMPS
distribution with a “.meam” suffix.  All of these are parameterized in
terms of LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{metal units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that unlike for other potentials, cutoffs for MEAM potentials are
not set in the pair\_style or pair\_coeff command; they are specified in
the MEAM potential files themselves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} style which
specifies two MEAM files and the element(s) to extract information
for.  The MEAM elements are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying
N additional arguments after the second filename in the pair\_coeff
command, where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
MEAM library file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Element1, Element2, …

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
MEAM parameter file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of MEAM elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials/library.meam}} file has generic MEAM
settings for a variety of elements.  The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials/SiC.meam}} file
has specific parameter settings for a Si and C alloy system.  If your
LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you want the first 3 to be Si,
and the fourth to be C, you would use the following pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{library.meam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sic.meam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first filename is the element library file. The list of elements following
it extracts lines from the library file and assigns numeric indices to these
elements. The second filename is the alloy parameter file, which refers to
elements using the numeric indices assigned before.
The arguments after the parameter file map LAMMPS atom types to elements, i.e.
LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the MEAM Si element.  The final C argument maps
LAMMPS atom type 4 to the MEAM C element.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the second filename is specified as NULL, no parameter file is read,
which simply means the generic parameters in the library file are
used.  Use of the NULL specification for the parameter file is
discouraged for systems with more than a single element type
(e.g. alloys), since the parameter file is expected to set element
interaction terms that are not captured by the information in the
library file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a mapping value is specified as NULL, the mapping is not performed.
This can be used when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} potential is used as part of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values are placeholders for atom types
that will be used with other potentials.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the second filename is NULL, the element names between the two
filenames can appear in any order, e.g. “Si C” or “C Si” in the
example above.  However, if the second filename is \sphinxstylestrong{not} NULL (as in the
example above), it contains settings that are indexed \sphinxstylestrong{by numbers}
for the elements that precede it.  Thus you need to ensure that you list
the elements between the filenames in an order consistent with how the
values in the second filename are indexed.  See details below on the
syntax for settings in the second file.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MEAM library file provided with LAMMPS has the name
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials/library.meam}}.  It is the “meamf” file used by other MD
codes.  Aside from blank and comment lines (starting with \# which can
appear anywhere), it is formatted as a series of entries, each of which
has 19 parameters and can span multiple lines:

\sphinxAtStartPar
elt, lat, z, ielement, atwt, alpha, b0, b1, b2, b3, alat, esub, asub,
t0, t1, t2, t3, rozero, ibar

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{elt} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lat} parameters are text strings, such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{elt} = Si or
Cu and \sphinxstyleemphasis{lat} = dia or fcc.  Because the library file is used by Fortran
MD codes, these strings may be enclosed in single quotes, but this is
not required.  The other numeric parameters match values in the
formulas above.  The value of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{elt} string is what is used in the
pair\_coeff command to identify which settings from the library file
you wish to read in.  There can be multiple entries in the library
file with the same \sphinxstyleemphasis{elt} value; LAMMPS reads the first matching entry it
finds and ignores the rest.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other parameters in the MEAM library file correspond to single\sphinxhyphen{}element
potential parameters:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
lat      = lattice structure of reference configuration
z        = number of nearest neighbors in the reference structure
ielement = atomic number
atwt     = atomic weight
alat     = lattice constant of reference structure
esub     = energy per atom (eV) in the reference structure at equilibrium
asub     = "A" parameter for MEAM (see e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:baskes}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baskes)}}}})
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{b0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{b1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{b2}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{b3}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{t0}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{t1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{t2}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{t3} parameters correspond to the
standard MEAM parameters in the literature {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:baskes}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Baskes)}}}} (the b
parameters are the standard beta parameters). Note that only parameters
normalized to \sphinxstyleemphasis{t0 = 1.0} are supported.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rozero} parameter is
an element\sphinxhyphen{}dependent density scaling that weights the reference
background density (see e.g. equation 4.5 in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:gullet}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Gullet)}}}}) and
is typically 1.0 for single\sphinxhyphen{}element systems.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ibar} parameter
selects the form of the function G(Gamma) used to compute the electron
density; options are

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
 0 =\PYGZgt{} G = sqrt(1+Gamma)
 1 =\PYGZgt{} G = exp(Gamma/2)
 2 =\PYGZgt{} not implemented
 3 =\PYGZgt{} G = 2/(1+exp(\PYGZhy{}Gamma))
 4 =\PYGZgt{} G = sqrt(1+Gamma)
\PYGZhy{}5 =\PYGZgt{} G = +\PYGZhy{}sqrt(abs(1+Gamma))
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If used, the MEAM parameter file contains settings that override or
complement the library file settings.  Examples of such parameter
files are in the potentials directory with a “.meam” suffix.  Their
format is the same as is read by other Fortran MD codes.  Aside from
blank and comment lines (start with \# which can appear anywhere), each
line has one of the following forms.  Each line can also have a
trailing comment (starting with \#) which is ignored.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
keyword = value
keyword(I) = value
keyword(I,J) = value
keyword(I,J,K) = value
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The indices I, J, K correspond to the elements selected from the
MEAM library file numbered in the order of how those elements were
selected starting from 1. Thus for the example given before

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{library.meam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sic.meam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
an index of 1 would refer to Si and an index of 2 to C.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The recognized keywords for the parameter file are as follows:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
rc          = cutoff radius for cutoff function; default = 4.0
delr        = length of smoothing distance for cutoff function; default = 0.1
rho0(I)     = relative density for element I (overwrites value
              read from meamf file)
Ec(I,J)     = cohesive energy of reference structure for I\sphinxhyphen{}J mixture
delta(I,J)  = heat of formation for I\sphinxhyphen{}J alloy; if Ec\_IJ is input as
              zero, then LAMMPS sets Ec\_IJ = (Ec\_II + Ec\_JJ)/2 \sphinxhyphen{} delta\_IJ
alpha(I,J)  = alpha parameter for pair potential between I and J (can
              be computed from bulk modulus of reference structure)
re(I,J)     = equilibrium distance between I and J in the reference
              structure
Cmax(I,J,K) = Cmax screening parameter when I\sphinxhyphen{}J pair is screened
              by K (I\textless{}=J); default = 2.8
Cmin(I,J,K) = Cmin screening parameter when I\sphinxhyphen{}J pair is screened
              by K (I\textless{}=J); default = 2.0
lattce(I,J) = lattice structure of I\sphinxhyphen{}J reference structure:
                fcc = face centered cubic
                bcc = body centered cubic
                hcp = hexagonal close\sphinxhyphen{}packed
                dim = dimer
                dia = diamond (interlaced fcc for alloy)
                dia3= diamond structure with primary 1NN and secondary 3NN interaction
                b1  = rock salt (NaCl structure)
                c11 = MoSi2 structure
                l12 = Cu3Au structure (lower case L, followed by 12)
                b2  = CsCl structure (interpenetrating simple cubic)
                ch4 = methane\sphinxhyphen{}like structure, only for binary system
                lin = linear structure (180 degree angle)
                zig = zigzag structure with a uniform angle
                tri = H2O\sphinxhyphen{}like structure that has an angle
                sc  = simple cubic
nn2(I,J)    = turn on second\sphinxhyphen{}nearest neighbor MEAM formulation for
              I\sphinxhyphen{}J pair (see for example {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:lee}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lee)}}}}).
                0 = second\sphinxhyphen{}nearest neighbor formulation off
                1 = second\sphinxhyphen{}nearest neighbor formulation on
                default = 0
attrac(I,J) = additional cubic attraction term in Rose energy I\sphinxhyphen{}J pair potential
                default = 0
repuls(I,J) = additional cubic repulsive term in Rose energy I\sphinxhyphen{}J pair potential
                default = 0
zbl(I,J)    = blend the MEAM I\sphinxhyphen{}J pair potential with the ZBL potential for small
              atom separations {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:zbl}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(ZBL)}}}}
                default = 1
theta(I,J)  = angle between three atoms in line, zigzag, and trimer reference structures in degrees
                default = 180
gsmooth\_factor  = factor determining the length of the G\sphinxhyphen{}function smoothing
                  region; only significant for ibar=0 or ibar=4.
                      99.0 = short smoothing region, sharp step
                      0.5  = long smoothing region, smooth step
                      default = 99.0
augt1           = integer flag for whether to augment t1 parameter by
                  3/5*t3 to account for old vs. new meam formulations;
                    0 = don\textquotesingle{}t augment t1
                    1 = augment t1
                    default = 1
ialloy          = integer flag to use alternative averaging rule for t parameters,
                  for comparison with the DYNAMO MEAM code
                    0 = standard averaging (matches ialloy=0 in DYNAMO)
                    1 = alternative averaging (matches ialloy=1 in DYNAMO)
                    2 = no averaging of t (use single\sphinxhyphen{}element values)
                    default = 0
mixture\_ref\_t   = integer flag to use mixture average of t to compute the background
                  reference density for alloys, instead of the single\sphinxhyphen{}element values
                  (see description and warning elsewhere in this doc page)
                    0 = do not use mixture averaging for t in the reference density
                    1 = use mixture averaging for t in the reference density
                    default = 0
erose\_form      = integer value to select the form of the Rose energy function
                  (see description below).
                    default = 0
emb\_lin\_neg     = integer value to select embedding function for negative densities
                    0 = F(rho)=0
                    1 = F(rho) = \sphinxhyphen{}asub*esub*rho (linear in rho, matches DYNAMO)
                    default = 0
bkgd\_dyn        = integer value to select background density formula
                    0 = rho\_bkgd = rho\_ref\_meam(a) (as in the reference structure)
                    1 = rho\_bkgd = rho0\_meam(a)*Z\_meam(a) (matches DYNAMO)
                    default = 0
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Rc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{delr}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{re} are in distance units (Angstroms in the case of metal
units).  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ec} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} are in energy units (eV in the case of metal
units).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each keyword represents a quantity which is either a scalar, vector,
2d array, or 3d array and must be specified with the correct
corresponding array syntax.  The indices I,J,K each run from 1 to N
where N is the number of MEAM elements being used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus these lines

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
rho0(2) = 2.25
alpha(1,2) = 4.37
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
set \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho0} for the second element to the value 2.25 and set \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha} for the
alloy interaction between elements 1 and 2 to 4.37.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{augt1} parameter is related to modifications in the MEAM
formulation of the partial electron density function.  In recent
literature, an extra term is included in the expression for the
third\sphinxhyphen{}order density in order to make the densities orthogonal (see for
example {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:wang2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Wang)}}}}, equation 3d); this term is included in the
MEAM implementation in LAMMPS.  However, in earlier published work
this term was not included when deriving parameters, including most of
those provided in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{library.meam}} file included with LAMMPS, and to
account for this difference the parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{t1} must be augmented by
3/5**t3*.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{augt1} = 1, the default, this augmentation is done
automatically.  When parameter values are fit using the modified
density function, as in more recent literature, augt1 should be set to
0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mixture\_ref\_t} parameter is available to match results with those
of previous versions of LAMMPS (before January 2011).  Newer versions
of LAMMPS, by default, use the single\sphinxhyphen{}element values of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{t}
parameters to compute the background reference density.  This is the
proper way to compute these parameters.  Earlier versions of LAMMPS
used an alloy mixture averaged value of \sphinxstyleemphasis{t} to compute the background
reference density.  Setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{mixture\_ref\_t} = 1 gives the old behavior.
WARNING: using \sphinxstyleemphasis{mixture\_ref\_t} = 1 will give results that are demonstrably
incorrect for second\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor MEAM, and non\sphinxhyphen{}standard for
first\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor MEAM; this option is included only for matching with
previous versions of LAMMPS and should be avoided if possible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{attrac} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{repuls}, along with the integer selection
parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{erose\_form}, can be used to modify the Rose energy function
used to compute the pair potential.  This function gives the energy of
the reference state as a function of interatomic spacing.  The form of
this function is:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
astar = alpha * (r/re \sphinxhyphen{} 1.d0)
if erose\_form = 0: erose = \sphinxhyphen{}Ec*(1+astar+a3*(astar**3)/(r/re))*exp(\sphinxhyphen{}astar)
if erose\_form = 1: erose = \sphinxhyphen{}Ec*(1+astar+(\sphinxhyphen{}attrac+repuls/r)*(astar**3))*exp(\sphinxhyphen{}astar)
if erose\_form = 2: erose = \sphinxhyphen{}Ec*(1 +astar + a3*(astar**3))*exp(\sphinxhyphen{}astar)
a3 = repuls, astar \textless{} 0
a3 = attrac, astar \textgreater{}= 0
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most published MEAM parameter sets use the default values \sphinxstyleemphasis{attrac} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{repulse} = 0.
Setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{repuls} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{attrac} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta} corresponds to the form used in several
recent published MEAM parameter sets, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:valone}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Valone)}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Then using \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/ms} pair style the multi\sphinxhyphen{}state MEAM (MS\sphinxhyphen{}MEAM) method is
activated.  This requires 6 extra parameters in the MEAM library file,
resulting in 25 parameters ordered that are ordered like this:

\sphinxAtStartPar
elt, lat, z, ielement, atwt, alpha, b0, b1, b2, b3, b1m, b2m, b3m, alat, esub, asub,
t0, t1, t2, t3, t1m, t2m, t3m, rozero, ibar

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 6 extra MS\sphinxhyphen{}MEAM parameters are \sphinxstyleemphasis{b1m, b2m, b3m, t1m, t2m, t3m}.
In the LAMMPS \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} folder, compatible files have an “.msmeam” extension.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default form of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{erose} expression in LAMMPS was corrected
in March 2009.  The current version is correct, but may show different
behavior compared with earlier versions of LAMMPS with the attrac
and/or repuls parameters are non\sphinxhyphen{}zero.  To obtain the previous default
form, use \sphinxstyleemphasis{erose\_form} = 1 (this form does not seem to appear in the
literature).  An alternative form (see e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam:lee2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lee2)}}}}) is
available using \sphinxstyleemphasis{erose\_form} = 2.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS with
user\sphinxhyphen{}specifiable parameters as described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shift}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{table}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tail} options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}},
since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/ms} pair styles are provided in the MEAM
package. They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The maximum number of elements that can be read from the MEAM library
file is determined at compile time. The default is 8.  If you need
support for more elements, you have to change the the constant ‘MAXELT’
at the beginning of the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/MEAM/meam.h}} and update/recompile
LAMMPS.  There is no limit on the number of atoms types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_eam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style eam}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_spline::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style meam/spline}}}}

\section{pair\_style meam/spline command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:pair-style-meam-spline-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spline}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spline}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti.meam.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti.meam.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline} style computes pairwise interactions for metals
using a variant of modified embedded\sphinxhyphen{}atom method (MEAM) potentials
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:lenosky1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lenosky)}}}}.  For a single species (“old\sphinxhyphen{}style”) MEAM,
the total energy E is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & =\sum_{i<j}\phi(r_{ij})+\sum_{i}U(n_{i}) \\
n_{i} & =\sum_{j}\rho(r_{ij})+\sum_{\substack{j<k,\\j,k\neq i}}f(r_{ij})f(r_{ik})g[\cos(\theta_{jik})]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\rho_i\) is the density at atom I, \(\theta_{jik}\) is
the angle between atoms J, I, and K centered on atom I. The five
functions \(\phi, U, \rho, f,\) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{g} are represented by cubic splines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline} style also supports a new style multicomponent
modified embedded\sphinxhyphen{}atom method (MEAM) potential {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:zhang4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Zhang)}}}}, where
the total energy E is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E &= \sum_{i<j}\phi_{ij}(r_{ij})+\sum_{i}U_i(n_{i}) \\
n_{i} & = \sum_{j\ne i}\rho_j(r_{ij})+\sum_{\substack{j<k,\\j,k\neq i}}f_{j}(r_{ij})f_{k}(r_{ik})g_{jk}[\cos(\theta_{jik})]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the five functions \(\phi, U, \rho, f,\) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{g} depend on the
chemistry of the atoms in the interaction.  In particular, if there are
N different chemistries, there are N different \sphinxstyleemphasis{U}, \(\rho\), and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{f} functions, while there are N(N+1)/2 different \(\phi\) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{g}
functions.  The new style multicomponent MEAM potential files are
indicated by the second line in the file starts with “meam/spline”
followed by the number of elements and the name of each element.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoffs and the coefficients for these spline functions are listed
in a parameter file which is specified by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.  Parameter files for different
elements are included in the “potentials” directory of the LAMMPS
distribution and have a “.meam.spline” file suffix.  All of these
files are parameterized in terms of LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{metal units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that unlike for other potentials, cutoffs for spline\sphinxhyphen{}based MEAM
potentials are not set in the pair\_style or pair\_coeff command; they
are specified in the potential files themselves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the EAM pair style, which retrieves the atomic mass from the
potential file, the spline\sphinxhyphen{}based MEAM potentials do not include mass
information; thus you need to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}} command to
specify it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline} style
which specifies a potential file with parameters for all needed
elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N
additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command,
where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of spline\sphinxhyphen{}based MEAM elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine the Ti.meam.spline file has values for Ti (old style).
In that case your LAMMPS simulation may only have one atom type which has
to be mapped to the Ti element as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti.meam.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * and there may be only one element
following or NULL. Systems where there would be multiple atom types
assigned to the same element are \sphinxstylestrong{not} supported by this pair style
due to limitations in its implementation.  If a mapping value is
specified as NULL, the mapping is not performed.  This can be used when
a \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline} potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.
The NULL values are placeholders for atom types that will be used with
other potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An example with a two component spline (new style) is TiO.meam.spline, where
the command

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TiO.meam.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will map the first atom type to Ti and the second atom type to O. Note
in this case that the species names need to match exactly with the
names of the elements in the TiO.meam.spline file; otherwise an
error will be raised. This behavior is different than the old style
MEAM files.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline} pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in an external
potential parameter file.  Thus, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style
and pair\_coeff commands in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/spline} pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mapping multiple atom types to the same element.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is only enabled if LAMMPS was built with the MANYBODY
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.

\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style meam}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_spline:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\index{pair\_style meam/sw/spline@\spxentry{pair\_style meam/sw/spline}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style meam/sw/spline command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:pair-style-meam-sw-spline-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spline}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{meam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spline}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti.meam.sw.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti.meam.sw.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/sw/spline} style computes pairwise interactions for metals
using a variant of modified embedded\sphinxhyphen{}atom method (MEAM) potentials
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:lenosky2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lenosky)}}}} with an additional Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber (SW) term
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:stillinger1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Stillinger)}}}} in the energy.  This form of the potential
was first proposed by Nicklas, Fellinger, and Park
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:nicklas}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Nicklas)}}}}.  We refer to it as MEAM+SW.  The total energy E
is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = E_{MEAM} + E_{SW} \\
E_{MEAM} & =  \sum _{IJ} \phi (r_{IJ}) + \sum _{I} U(\rho _I) \\
E_{SW} & =  \sum _{I} \sum _{JK} F(r_{IJ}) \, F(r_{IK}) \, G(\cos(\theta _{JIK})) \\
\rho _I & = \sum _J \rho(r_{IJ}) + \sum _{JK} f(r_{IJ}) \, f(r_{IK}) \, g(\cos(\theta _{JIK}))\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\rho_I\) is the density at atom I, \(\theta_{JIK}\) is
the angle between atoms J, I, and K centered on atom I. The seven
functions \(\phi, F, G, U, \rho, f,\) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{g} are represented by
cubic splines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoffs and the coefficients for these spline functions are listed
in a parameter file which is specified by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.  Parameter files for different
elements are included in the “potentials” directory of the LAMMPS
distribution and have a “.meam.sw.spline” file suffix.  All of these
files are parameterized in terms of LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{metal units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that unlike for other potentials, cutoffs for spline\sphinxhyphen{}based
MEAM+SW potentials are not set in the pair\_style or pair\_coeff
command; they are specified in the potential files themselves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the EAM pair style, which retrieves the atomic mass from the
potential file, the spline\sphinxhyphen{}based MEAM+SW potentials do not include
mass information; thus you need to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{mass::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{mass}}}} command to
specify it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the meam/sw/spline style
which specifies a potential file with parameters for all needed
elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N
additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command,
where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of spline\sphinxhyphen{}based MEAM+SW elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine the Ti.meam.sw.spline file has values for Ti.
If your LAMMPS simulation has 3 atoms types and they are all to be
treated with this potential, you would use the following pair\_coeff
command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti.meam.sw.spline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ti}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The three Ti arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the Ti element
in the potential file. If a mapping value is specified as NULL, the
mapping is not performed. This can be used when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/sw/spline}
potential is used as part of the hybrid pair style. The NULL values
are placeholders for atom types that will be used with other
potentials.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/sw/spline} style currently supports only
single\sphinxhyphen{}element MEAM+SW potentials.  It may be extended for alloy
systems in the future.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input scripts that use this pair style are provided
in the examples/PACKAGES/meam\_sw\_spline directory.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair style does not support multiple element types or mixing.
It has been designed for pure elements only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/sw/spline} pair style does not write its information to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in an external
potential parameter file.  Thus, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style
and pair\_coeff commands in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{meam/sw/spline} pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair}
keyword of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not
support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is only enabled if LAMMPS was built with the MANYBODY
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style meam}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_meam_spline::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style meam/spline}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:lenosky2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Lenosky)} Lenosky, Sadigh, Alonso, Bulatov, de la Rubia, Kim, Voter,
Kress, Modell. Simul. Mater. Sci. Eng. 8, 825 (2000).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:stillinger1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Stillinger)} Stillinger, Weber, Phys. Rev. B 31, 5262 (1985).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_meam_sw_spline:nicklas}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Nicklas)}
The spline\sphinxhyphen{}based MEAM+SW format was first devised and used to develop
potentials for bcc transition metals by Jeremy Nicklas, Michael Fellinger,
and Hyoungki Park at The Ohio State University.

\index{pair\_style mesocnt@\spxentry{pair\_style mesocnt}}\ignorespaces 
\index{pair\_style mesocnt/viscous@\spxentry{pair\_style mesocnt/viscous}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style mesocnt command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:pair-style-mesocnt-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt::doc}}

\section{pair\_style mesocnt/viscous command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:pair-style-mesocnt-viscous-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neigh\PYGZus{}cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neigh\PYGZus{}mode}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt/viscous}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
neigh\_cutoff = neighbor list cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{chain} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} (optional)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
neigh\_mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{topology} (optional)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C\PYGZus{}10\PYGZus{}10.mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{viscous}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{60.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{topology}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C\PYGZus{}10\PYGZus{}10.mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.001}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} implements a mesoscopic potential for the interaction
of carbon nanotubes (CNTs), or other quasi\sphinxhyphen{}1D objects such as other
kinds of nanotubes or nanowires. In this potential, CNTs are modelled
as chains of cylindrical segments in which each infinitesimal surface
element interacts with all other CNT surface elements with the
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones (LJ) term adopted from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_airebo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{airebo}}}}
style. The interaction energy is then computed by integrating over the
surfaces of all interacting CNTs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In LAMMPS, cylindrical segments are represented by bonds. Each segment
is defined by its two end points (“nodes”) which correspond to atoms
in LAMMPS. For the exact functional form of the potential and
implementation details, the reader is referred to the original papers
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:volkov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Volkov1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:volkov2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Volkov2)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential supports two modes, \sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{chain}. By default,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{chain} mode is enabled.  In \sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} mode, interactions are
pair\sphinxhyphen{}wise between all neighboring segments based on a segment\sphinxhyphen{}segment
approach (keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} in pair\_style command).  In \sphinxstyleemphasis{chain} mode,
interactions are calculated between each segment and infinitely or
semi\sphinxhyphen{}infinitely long CNTs as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:volkov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Volkov1)}}}}.
Chains of segments are converted to these (semi\sphinxhyphen{})infinite CNTs bases
on an approximate chain approach outlined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:volkov2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Volkov2)}}}}. Hence, interactions are calculated on a segment\sphinxhyphen{}chain
basis (keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{chain} in the pair\_style command).  Using \sphinxstyleemphasis{chain} mode
allows to simplify the computation of the interactions significantly
and reduces the computational times to the same order of magnitude as
for regular bead spring models where beads interact with the standard
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_lj/cut}}}} potential. However, this method is only
valid when the curvature of the CNTs in the system is small.  When
CNTs are buckled (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_mesocnt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_mesocnt}}}}), local
curvature can be very high and the pair\_style automatically switches
to \sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} mode for interactions involving buckled CNTs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential further implements two different neighbor list
construction modes. Mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} uses atom and mol IDs to construct
neighbor lists while \sphinxstyleemphasis{topology} modes uses only the bond topology of
the system. While \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} mode requires bonded atoms to have consecutive
LAMMPS atom IDs and atoms in different CNTs to have different LAMMPS
molecule IDs, \sphinxstyleemphasis{topology} mode has no such requirement. Using \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} mode
is faster and is enabled by default.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Neighbor \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} mode requires all CNTs in the system to have distinct
LAMMPS molecule IDs and bonded atoms to have consecutive LAMMPS atom
IDs. If this is not possible (e.g. in simulations of CNT rings),
\sphinxstyleemphasis{topology} mode needs to be enabled in the pair\_style command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the LJ interactions described above, style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt/viscous} explicitly models friction between neighboring
segments. Friction forces are a function of the relative velocity
between a segment and its neighboring approximate chain (even in
\sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} mode) and only act along the axes of the interacting segment
and chain. In this potential, friction forces acting per unit length
of a nanotube segment are modelled as a shifted logistic function:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F^{\text{FRICTION}}(v) / L = \frac{F^{\text{max}}}{1 +
\exp(-k(v-v_0))} - \frac{F^{\text{max}}}{1 + \exp(k v_0)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In the pair\_style command, the modes described above can be toggled
using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{segment} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{chain} keywords.  The neighbor list cutoff
defines the cutoff within which atoms are included in the neighbor
list for constructing neighboring CNT chains.  This is different from
the potential cutoff, which is directly calculated from parameters
specified in the potential file. We recommend using a neighbor list
cutoff of at least 3 times the maximum segment length used in the
simulation to ensure proper neighbor chain construction.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CNT ends are treated differently by all \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} styles. Atoms on
CNT ends need to be assigned different LAMMPS atom types than atoms
not on CNT ends.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} requires tabulated data provided in a single ASCII
text file, as well as a list of integers corresponding to all LAMMPS
atom types representing CNT ends:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N\) CNT end atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if your LAMMPS simulation of (10, 10) nanotubes has 4
atom types where atom types 1 and 3 are assigned to ‘inner’ nodes and
atom types 2 and 4 are assigned to CNT end nodes, the pair\_coeff
command would be:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C\PYGZus{}10\PYGZus{}10.mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Likewise, style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt/viscous} also requires the same information
as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt}, with the addition of 3 parameters for the viscous
friction forces as listed above:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(F^{\text{max}}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(v_0\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N\) CNT end atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the same example system as with style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} with the
addition of friction, the pair\_coeff command is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C\PYGZus{}10\PYGZus{}10.mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.03}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Potential files for CNTs can be readily generated using the freely
available code provided on

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
https://github.com/phankl/cntpot
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the same approach, it should also be possible to generate
potential files for other 1D systems mentioned above.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because of their size, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} style potential files are not
bundled with LAMMPS.  When compiling LAMMPS from source code, the
file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C\_10\_10.mesocnt}} should be downloaded separately from
\sphinxurl{https://download.lammps.org/potentials/C\_10\_10.mesocnt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first line of the potential file provides a time stamp and
general information. The second line lists four integers giving the
number of data points provided in the subsequent four data
tables. The third line lists four floating point numbers: the CNT
radius R, the LJ parameter sigma and two numerical parameters
delta1 and delta2. These four parameters are given in
Angstroms. This is followed by four data tables each separated by a
single empty line. The first two tables have two columns and list
the parameters uInfParallel and Gamma respectively.  The last two
tables have three columns giving data on a quadratic array and list
the parameters Phi and uSemiParallel respectively.  uInfParallel
and uSemiParallel are given in eV/Angstrom, Phi is given in eV and
Gamma is unitless.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a simulation produces many warnings about segment\sphinxhyphen{}chain
interactions falling outside the interpolation range, we recommend
generating a potential file with lower values of delta1 and delta2.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles does not support mixing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary
restart files}}}}, since it is stored in tabulated potential
files.  Thus, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff
commands in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These styles are part of the MESONT package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles require the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be
“on” for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles require all 3 {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds lj}}}}
settings to be non\sphinxhyphen{}zero for proper neighbor list construction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt/viscous} requires you to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify
vel yes}}}} command so that velocities are stored by ghost
atoms.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_mesocnt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style mesocnt}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_mesocnt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style mesocnt}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesocnt:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = chain, neigh\_mode = id


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd} args = cutoff seed
  cutoff = global cutoff for eDPD interactions (distance units)
  seed = random \# seed (integer) (if \textless{}= 0, eDPD will use current time as the seed)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd} args = T cutoff seed
  T = temperature (temperature units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for mDPD interactions (distance units)
  seed = random \# seed (integer) (if \textless{}= 0, mDPD will use current time as the seed)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} args =
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd} args = T cutoff seed
  T = temperature (temperature units)
  cutoff = global cutoff for tDPD interactions (distance units)
  seed = random \# seed (integer) (if \textless{}= 0, tDPD will use current time as the seed)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd} style computes the pairwise interactions and heat fluxes
for eDPD particles following the formulations in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2014-jcp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2014\_JCP)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2015-cc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Li2015\_CC}}}}. The time
evolution of an eDPD particle is governed by the conservation of
momentum and energy given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathbf{r}_i}{\mathrm{d} t^2}=
\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathbf{v}_i}{\mathrm{d} t}
=\mathbf{F}_{i}=\sum_{i\neq j}(\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{C}+\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{D}+\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{R}) \\
C_v\frac{\mathrm{d} T_i}{\mathrm{d} t}= q_{i} = \sum_{i\neq j}(q_{ij}^{C}+q_{ij}^{V}+q_{ij}^{R}),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the three components of \(F_{i}\) including the conservative
force \(F_{ij}^C\), dissipative force \(F_{ij}^D\) and random
force \(F_{ij}^R\) are expressed as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{C} & = \alpha_{ij}{\omega_{C}}(r_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{D} & = -\gamma {\omega_{D}}(r_{ij})(\mathbf{e}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{R} & = \sigma {\omega_{R}}(r_{ij}){\xi_{ij}}\Delta t^{-1/2} \mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\omega_{C}(r) & = 1 - r/r_c \\
\alpha_{ij} & = A\cdot k_B(T_i + T_j)/2 \\
\omega_{D}(r) & = \omega^2_{R}(r) = (1-r/r_c)^s \\
\sigma_{ij}^2 & = 4\gamma k_B T_i T_j/(T_i + T_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
in which the exponent of the weighting function \sphinxstyleemphasis{s} can be defined as a
temperature\sphinxhyphen{}dependent variable. The heat flux between particles
accounting for the collisional heat flux \(q^C\), viscous heat flux
\(q^V\), and random heat flux \(q^R\) are given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}q_i^C & = \sum_{j \ne i} k_{ij} \omega_{CT}(r_{ij}) \left( \frac{1}{T_i} - \frac{1}{T_j} \right) \\
q_i^V & = \frac{1}{2 C_v}\sum_{j \ne i}{ \left\{ \omega_D(r_{ij})\left[\gamma_{ij} \left( \mathbf{e}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{ij} \right)^2 - \frac{\left( \sigma _{ij} \right)^2}{m}\right] - \sigma _{ij} \omega_R(r_{ij})\left( \mathbf{e}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{ij} \right){\xi_{ij}} \right\} } \\
q_i^R & = \sum_{j \ne i} \beta _{ij} \omega_{RT}(r_{ij}) d {t^{ - 1/2}} \xi_{ij}^e \\
\omega_{CT}(r) & =\omega_{RT}^2(r)=\left(1-r/r_{ct}\right)^{s_T} \\
k_{ij} & =C_v^2\kappa(T_i + T_j)^2/4k_B \\
\beta_{ij}^2 & = 2k_Bk_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the mesoscopic heat friction \(\kappa\) is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\kappa  = \frac{315k_B\upsilon }{2\pi \rho C_v r_{ct}^5}\frac{1}{Pr},\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\upsilon\) being the kinematic viscosity. For more details,
see Eq.(15) in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2014-jcp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2014\_JCP)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined in eDPD system for each
pair of atom types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in
the examples above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
power\_f (positive real)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kappa (thermal conductivity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
power\_T (positive real)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff\_T (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optional keyword = power or kappa

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{power} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kappa} is optional. Both “power” and “kappa”
require 4 parameters \(c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4\) showing the temperature
dependence of the exponent \(s(T) = \mathrm{power}_f ( 1+c_1
(T-1) + c_2 (T-1)^2 + c_3 (T-1)^3 + c_4 (T-1)^4 )\) and of the mesoscopic
heat friction \(s_T(T) = \kappa (1 + c_1 (T-1) + c_2 (T-1)^2 + c_3
(T-1)^3 + c_4 (T-1)^4)\).  If the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{power} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{kappa} is not
specified, the eDPD system will use constant power\_f and
\(\kappa\), which is independent to temperature changes.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} style computes the local particle mass density
\(\rho\) for mDPD particles by kernel function interpolation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd} style computes the many\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions between mDPD
particles following the formulations in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2013-pof}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2013\_POF)}}}}. The dissipative and random forces are in
the form same as the classical DPD, but the conservative force is
local density dependent, which are given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{F}_{ij}^C & = Aw_c(r_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij} + B(\rho_i+\rho_j)w_d(r_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{D} & = -\gamma {\omega_{D}}(r_{ij})(\mathbf{e}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{R} & = \sigma {\omega_{R}}(r_{ij}){\xi_{ij}}\Delta t^{-1/2} \mathbf{e}_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the first term in \(F_C\) with a negative coefficient \(A
< 0\) stands for an attractive force within an interaction range
\(r_c\), and the second term with \(B > 0\) is the
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent repulsive force within an interaction range
\(r_d\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
B (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff\_c (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff\_d (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd} style computes the pairwise interactions and chemical
concentration fluxes for tDPD particles following the formulations in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2015-jcp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2015\_JCP)}}}}.  The time evolution of a tDPD particle is
governed by the conservation of momentum and concentration given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathbf{r}_i}{\mathrm{d} t^2} & = \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathbf{v}_i}{\mathrm{d} t}=\mathbf{F}_{i}=\sum_{i\neq j}(\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{C}+\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{D}+\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{R}) \\
\frac{\mathrm{d} C_{i}}{\mathrm{d} t} & = Q_{i} = \sum_{i\neq j}(Q_{ij}^{D}+Q_{ij}^{R}) + Q_{i}^{S}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the three components of \(F_{i}\) including the conservative
force \(F_{ij}^C\), dissipative force \(F_{ij}^C\) and random
force \(F_{ij}^C\) are expressed as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{C} & = A{\omega_{C}}(r_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{D} & = -\gamma {\omega_{D}}(r_{ij})(\mathbf{e}_{ij} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{ij})\mathbf{e}_{ij}  \\
\mathbf{F}_{ij}^{R} & = \sigma {\omega_{R}}(r_{ij}){\xi_{ij}}\Delta t^{-1/2} \mathbf{e}_{ij} \\
\omega_{C}(r) & = 1 - r/r_c \\
\omega_{D}(r) & = \omega^2_{R}(r) = (1-r/r_c)^{\rm power_f} \\
\sigma^2 = 2\gamma k_B T\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The concentration flux between two tDPD particles includes the Fickian
flux \(Q_{ij}^D\) and random flux \(Q_{ij}^R\), which are given
by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q_{ij}^D & = -\kappa_{ij} w_{DC}(r_{ij}) \left( C_i - C_j \right) \\
Q_{ij}^R & = \epsilon_{ij}\left( C_i + C_j \right) w_{RC}(r_{ij}) \xi_{ij} \\
w_{DC}(r_{ij}) & =w^2_{RC}(r_{ij}) = (1 - r/r_{cc})^{\rm power_{cc}} \\
\epsilon_{ij}^2 & = m_s^2\kappa_{ij}\rho\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the parameters kappa and epsilon determine the strength of the
Fickian and random fluxes. \(m_s\) is the mass of a single solute
molecule.  In general, \(m_s\) is much smaller than the mass of a
tDPD particle \sphinxstyleemphasis{m}. For more details, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2015-jcp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2015\_JCP)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\) (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
power\_f (positive real)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff\_CC (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\kappa_i\) (diffusivity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_i\) (diffusivity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
power\_cc\_i (positive real)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last 3 values must be repeated Nspecies times, so that values for
each of the Nspecies chemical species are specified, as indicated by
the “I” suffix.  In the first pair\_coeff example above for pair\_style
tdpd, Nspecies = 1.  In the second example, Nspecies = 2, so 3
additional coeffs are specified (for species 2).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Example scripts}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:example-scripts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are example scripts for using all these pair styles in
examples/PACKAGES/mesodpd.  The example for an eDPD simulation models heat
conduction with source terms analog of periodic Poiseuille flow
problem. The setup follows Fig.12 in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2014-jcp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2014\_JCP)}}}}. The
output of the short eDPD simulation (about 2 minutes on a single core)
gives a temperature and density profiles as

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{examples_edpd}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The example for a mDPD simulation models the oscillations of a liquid
droplet started from a liquid film. The mDPD parameters are adopted
from {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2013-pof}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2013\_POF)}}}}.  The short mDPD run (about 2 minutes
on a single core) generates a particle trajectory which can
be visualized as follows.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{examples_mdpd_first}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{examples_mdpd_last}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first image is the initial state of the simulation.  If you
click it a GIF movie should play in your browser.  The second image
is the final state of the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The example for a tDPD simulation computes the effective diffusion
coefficient of a tDPD system using a method analogous to the periodic
Poiseuille flow.  The tDPD system is specified with two chemical
species, and the setup follows Fig.1 in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:li2015-jcp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Li2015\_JCP)}}}}. The output of the short tDPD simulation
(about one and a half minutes on a single core) gives the
concentration profiles of the two chemical species as

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{examples_tdpd}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd} do not support
mixing. Thus, coefficients for all I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd} do not support
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd} do not write
information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}. Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{edpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mdpd/rhosum} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tdpd} are part of
the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}MESO package. They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with
that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for
more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mesodpd:related-commands}}

\section{pair\_style mgpt command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:pair-style-mgpt-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:syntax}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:examples}}
