\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mgpt}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ta6.8x.mgpt.parmin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ta6.8x.mgpt.potin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Omega}
\PYG{n}{cp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/lammps/potentials/Ta6.8x.mgpt.parmin\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{parmin}
\PYG{n}{cp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/lammps/potentials/Ta6.8x.mgpt.potin\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{potin}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{parmin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{potin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Omega}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volpress}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nbody}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1234}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{precision}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{double}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{parmin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{potin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Omega}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volpress}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nbody}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Within DFT quantum mechanics, generalized pseudopotential theory (GPT)
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:moriarty1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moriarty1}}}}) provides a first\sphinxhyphen{}principles approach to
multi\sphinxhyphen{}ion interatomic potentials in d\sphinxhyphen{}band transition metals, with a
volume\sphinxhyphen{}dependent, real\sphinxhyphen{}space total\sphinxhyphen{}energy functional for the N\sphinxhyphen{}ion
elemental bulk material in the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_{\rm tot}({\bf R}_1 \ldots {\bf R}_N) = NE_{\rm vol}(\Omega )
+ \frac{1}{2} \sum _{i,j} \mbox{}^\prime \ v_2(ij;\Omega )
+ \frac{1}{6} \sum _{i,j,k} \mbox{}^\prime \ v_3(ijk;\Omega )
+ \frac{1}{24} \sum _{i,j,k,l} \mbox{}^\prime \ v_4(ijkl;\Omega )\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the prime on each summation sign indicates the exclusion of all
self\sphinxhyphen{}interaction terms from the summation.  The leading volume term
E\_vol as well as the two\sphinxhyphen{}ion central\sphinxhyphen{}force pair potential v\_2 and the
three\sphinxhyphen{} and four\sphinxhyphen{}ion angular\sphinxhyphen{}force potentials, v\_3 and v\_4, depend
explicitly on the atomic volume Omega, but are structure independent
and transferable to all bulk ion configurations, either ordered or
disordered, and with of without the presence of point and line
defects.  The simplified model GPT or MGPT ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:moriarty2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moriarty2}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:moriarty3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moriarty3}}}}), which retains the form of E\_tot and permits
more efficient large\sphinxhyphen{}scale atomistic simulations, derives from the GPT
through a series of systematic approximations applied to E\_vol and the
potentials v\_n that are valid for mid\sphinxhyphen{}period transition metals with
nearly half\sphinxhyphen{}filled d bands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both analytic ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:moriarty2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moriarty2}}}}) and matrix
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:moriarty3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moriarty3}}}}) representations of MGPT have been developed.
In the more general matrix representation, which can also be applied
to f\sphinxhyphen{}band actinide metals and permits both canonical and non\sphinxhyphen{}canonical
d/f bands, the multi\sphinxhyphen{}ion potentials are evaluated on the fly during a
simulation through d\sphinxhyphen{} or f\sphinxhyphen{}state matrix multiplication, and the forces
that move the ions are determined analytically.  Fast matrix\sphinxhyphen{}MGPT
algorithms have been developed independently by Glosli
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:glosli}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Glosli}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:moriarty3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Moriarty3}}}}) and by Oppelstrup
({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mgpt:oppelstrup}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Oppelstrup}}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mgpt} pair style calculates forces, energies, and the total
energy per atom, E\_tot/N, using the Oppelstrup matrix\sphinxhyphen{}MGPT algorithm.
Input potential and control data are entered through the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.  Each material treated requires
input parmin and potin potential files, as shown in the above
examples, as well as specification by the user of the initial atomic
volume Omega through pair\_coeff.  At the beginning of a time step in
any simulation, the total volume of the simulation cell V should
always be equal to Omega*N, where N is the number of metal ions
present, taking into account the presence of any vacancies and/or
interstitials in the case of a solid.  In a constant\sphinxhyphen{}volume
simulation, which is the normal mode of operation for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mgpt} pair
style, Omega, V and N all remain constant throughout the simulation
and thus are equal to their initial values.  In a constant\sphinxhyphen{}stress
simulation, the cell volume V will change (slowly) as the simulation
proceeds.  After each time step, the atomic volume should be updated
by the code as Omega = V/N.  In addition, the volume term E\_vol and
the potentials v\_2, v\_3 and v\_4 have to be removed at the end of the
time step, and then respecified at the new value of Omega.  In all
simulations, Omega must remain within the defined volume range for
E\_vol and the potentials for the given material.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default option volpress yes in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}
command includes all volume derivatives of E\_tot required to calculate
the stress tensor and pressure correctly.  The option volpress no
disregards the pressure contribution resulting from the volume term
E\_vol, and can be used for testing and analysis purposes.  The
additional optional variable nbody controls the specific terms in
E\_tot that are calculated.  The default option and the normal option
for mid\sphinxhyphen{}period transition and actinide metals is nbody 1234 for which
all four terms in E\_tot are retained.  The option nbody 12, for
example, retains only the volume term and the two\sphinxhyphen{}ion pair potential
term and can be used for GPT series\sphinxhyphen{}end transition metals that can be
well described without v\_3 and v\_4.  The nbody option can also be used
to test or analyze the contribution of any of the four terms in E\_tot
to a given calculated property.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mgpt} pair style makes extensive use of matrix algebra and
includes optimized kernels for the BlueGene/Q architecture and the
Intel/AMD (x86) architectures.  When compiled with the appropriate
compiler and compiler switches (\sphinxhyphen{}msse3 on x86, and using the IBM XL
compiler on BG/Q), these optimized routines are used automatically.
For BG/Q machines, building with the default Makefile for that
architecture (e.g., “make bgq”) should enable the optimized algebra
routines.  For x\sphinxhyphen{}86 machines, there is a provided Makefile.mgptfast
which enables the fast algebra routines, i.e. build LAMMPS with “make
mgptfast”.  The user will be informed in the output files of the
matrix kernels in use. To further improve speed, on x86 the option
precision single can be added to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}
command line, which improves speed (up to a factor of two) at the cost
of doing matrix calculations with 7 digit precision instead of the
default 16. For consistency the default option can be specified
explicitly by the option precision double.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All remaining potential and control data are contained with the parmin
and potin files, including cutoffs, atomic mass, and other basic MGPT
variables.  Specific MGPT potential data for the transition metals
tantalum (Ta4 and Ta6.8x potentials), molybdenum (Mo5.2 potentials),
and vanadium (V6.1 potentials) are contained in the LAMMPS potentials
directory.  The stored files are, respectively, Ta4.mgpt.parmin,
Ta4.mgpt.potin, Ta6.8x.mgpt.parmin, Ta6.8x.mgpt.potin,
Mo5.2.mgpt.parmin, Mo5.2.mgpt.potin, V6.1.mgpt.parmin, and
V6.1.mgpt.potin .  Useful corresponding informational “README” files
on the Ta4, Ta6.8x, Mo5.2 and V6.1 potentials are also included in the
potentials directory.  These latter files indicate the volume mesh and
range for each potential and give appropriate references for the
potentials.  It is expected that MGPT potentials for additional
materials will be added over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Useful example MGPT scripts are given in the examples/PACKAGES/mgpt
directory.  These scripts show the necessary steps to perform
constant\sphinxhyphen{}volume calculations and simulations.  It is strongly
recommended that the user work through and understand these examples
before proceeding to more complex simulations.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For good performance, LAMMPS should be built with the compiler
flags “\sphinxhyphen{}O3 \sphinxhyphen{}msse3 \sphinxhyphen{}funroll\sphinxhyphen{}loops” when including this pair style.  The
src/MAKE/OPTIONS/Makefile.mgptfast is an example machine Makefile with
these options included as part of a standard MPI build.  Note that it
as provided, it will build with whatever low\sphinxhyphen{}level compiler (g++, icc,
etc) is the default for your MPI installation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mix, shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
needs to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MGPT package and is only enabled
if LAMMPS is built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MGPT potentials require the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newtion}}}} setting to be
“on” for pair style interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The stored parmin and potin potential files provided with LAMMPS in
the “potentials” directory are written in Rydberg atomic units, with
energies in Rydbergs and distances in Bohr radii. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mgpt} pair
style converts Rydbergs to Hartrees to make the potential files
compatible with LAMMPS electron {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The form of E\_tot used in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mgpt} pair style is only appropriate
for elemental bulk solids and liquids.  This includes solids with
point and extended defects such as vacancies, interstitials, grain
boundaries and dislocations.  Alloys and free surfaces, however,
require significant modifications, which are not included in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{mgpt} pair style.  Likewise, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style is not allowed,
where MGPT would be used for some atoms but not for others.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Electron\sphinxhyphen{}thermal effects are not included in the standard MGPT
potentials provided in the “potentials” directory, where the
potentials have been constructed at zero electron temperature.
Physically, electron\sphinxhyphen{}thermal effects may be important in 3d (e.g., V)
and 4d (e.g., Mo) transition metals at high temperatures near melt and
above.  It is expected that temperature\sphinxhyphen{}dependent MGPT potentials for
such cases will be added over time.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mgpt:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}

The options defaults for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command are
volpress yes, nbody 1234, and precision double.

\section{pair\_style mie/cut command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:pair-style-mie-cut-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mie::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{mie/cut/gpu}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mie}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for mie/cut interactions (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mie}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.72}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.40}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{23.00}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.66}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.30}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.55}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.65}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.00}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.46}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.32}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16.90}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.31}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mie/cut} style computes the Mie potential, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E =  C \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{\gamma_{rep}} - \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{\gamma_{att}} \right]
                      \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff and C is a function that depends on the repulsive and
attractive exponents, given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}C = \left(\frac{\gamma_{rep}}{\gamma_{rep}-\gamma_{att}}\right) \left(\frac{\gamma_{rep}}{\gamma_{att}}\right)^{\left(\frac{\gamma_{att}}{\gamma_{rep}-\gamma_{att}}\right)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that for 12/6 exponents, C is equal to 4 and the formula is the
same as the standard Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
epsilon (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sigma (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gammaR

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gammaA

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global
cutoff specified in the pair\_style command is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of the mie/cut pair styles can be mixed.
If not explicitly defined, both the repulsive and attractive gamma
exponents for different atoms will be calculated following the same
mixing rule defined for distances.  The default mix value is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}. See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail
option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail correction to the energy and
pressure of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer}
keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command, meaning the
pairwise forces can be partitioned by distance at different levels of
the rRESPA hierarchy.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for
details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\label{\detokenize{pair_mie:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{pair\_style mliap command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:pair-style-mliap-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliap/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or two keyword/value pairs must be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{unified}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{model} values = style filename
  style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nn} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy}
  filename = name of file containing model definitions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor} values = style filename
  style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sna} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{so3} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace}
  filename = name of file containing descriptor definitions
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unified} values = filename ghostneigh\_flag
  filename = name of file containing serialized unified Python object
  ghostneigh\_flag = 0/1 to turn off/on inclusion of ghost neighbors in neighbors list
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{InP.mliap.model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{descriptor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sna}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{InP.mliap.descriptor}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quadratic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{W.mliap.model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{descriptor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sna}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{W.mliap.descriptor}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nn}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si.nn.mliap.model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{descriptor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{so3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si.nn.mliap.descriptor}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliappy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ACE\PYGZus{}NN\PYGZus{}Pytorch.pt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{descriptor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ccs\PYGZus{}single\PYGZus{}element.yace}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unified}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mliap\PYGZus{}unified\PYGZus{}lj\PYGZus{}Ar.pkl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{In}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{P}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliap} provides a general interface to families of
machine\sphinxhyphen{}learning interatomic potentials.  It allows separate definitions
of the interatomic potential functional form (\sphinxstyleemphasis{model}) and the geometric
quantities that characterize the atomic positions (\sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
By defining \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor} separately, it is possible to use
many different models with a given descriptor, or many different
descriptors with a given model.  The pair style currently supports \sphinxstyleemphasis{sna},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{so3} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptor styles, but it is straightforward to add new
descriptor styles.  By using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{unified} keyword, it is possible to
define a Python model that combines functionalities of both \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SNAP descriptor style \sphinxstyleemphasis{sna} is the same as that used by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_snap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style snap}}}}, including the linear, quadratic, and
chem variants.  The available models are \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{nn},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy} style can be used to couple python models,
e.g. PyTorch neural network energy models, and requires building LAMMPS
with the PYTHON package (see below).  In order to train a model, it is
useful to know the gradient or derivative of energy, force, and stress
w.r.t. model parameters. This information can be accessed using the
related {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_mliap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute mliap}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 2Jun2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The descriptor style \sphinxstyleemphasis{so3} is a descriptor that is derived from the
the smooth SO(3) power spectrum with the explicit inclusion of a radial
basis {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mliap:bartok2013}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Bartok)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mliap:zagaceta2020}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Zagaceta)}}}}.
The available models are \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{nn}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The descriptor style \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} is a class of highly general atomic
descriptors, atomic cluster expansion descriptors (ACE) from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pace:drautz19}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Drautz)}}}}, that include a radial basis, an angular
basis, and bases for other variables (such as chemical species) if
relevant. In descriptor style \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace}, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptors may be
defined up to an arbitrary body order. This descriptor style is the same
as that used in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style pace}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
pace}}}}.  The available models with \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} in ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP are
\sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptors and models require
building LAMMPS with the ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE package (see below).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy}
model style may be used with \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptors, but it requires that
LAMMPS is also built with the PYTHON package.  As with other model
styles, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy} model style can be used to couple arbitrary python
models that use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptors such as Pytorch NNs.  Note that
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ALL} mliap model styles with \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptors require that descriptors
and hyperparameters are supplied in a \sphinxtitleref{.yace} or \sphinxtitleref{.ace} file, similar to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pace}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliap} command must be followed by two keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{model}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor} in either order, or the one keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{unified}.  A
single \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command is also required.  The first 2 arguments
must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.  This is followed by
a list of N arguments that specify the mapping of MLIAP element names to
LAMMPS atom types, where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword is followed by the model style. This is followed by
a single argument specifying the model filename containing the
parameters for a set of elements.  The model filename usually ends in
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{.mliap.model} extension.  It may contain parameters for many
elements. The only requirement is that it contain at least those element
names appearing in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The top of the model file can contain any number of blank and comment
lines (start with \#), but follows a strict format after that. The first
non\sphinxhyphen{}blank non\sphinxhyphen{}comment line must contain two integers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nelems  = Number of elements

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nparams = Number of parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{quadratic}, this is followed by
one block for each of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelem} elements.  Each block consists of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nparams} parameters, one per line.  Note that this format is similar,
but not identical to that used for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_snap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style snap}}}} coefficient file.  Specifically, the line containing the
element weight and radius is omitted, since these are handled by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{nn} (neural networks), the model file can
contain blank and comment lines (start with \#) anywhere. The second
non\sphinxhyphen{}blank non\sphinxhyphen{}comment line must contain the string NET, followed by two
integers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ndescriptors = Number of descriptors

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nlayers      = Number of layers (including the hidden layers and the output layer)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and followed by a sequence of a string and an integer for each layer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Activation function (linear, sigmoid, tanh or relu)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nnodes = Number of nodes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is followed by one block for each of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelem} elements. Each
block consists of \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale0} minimum value, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale1} (maximum \sphinxhyphen{} minimum)
value, in order to normalize the descriptors, followed by \sphinxstyleemphasis{nparams}
parameters, including \sphinxstyleemphasis{bias} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{weights} of the model, starting with
the first node of the first layer and so on, with a maximum of 30 values
per line.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The detail of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nn} module implementation can be found at {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mliap:yanxon2020}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Yanxon)}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Notes on mliappy models}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} keyword is \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy}, if the filename ends in ‘.pt’,
or ‘.pth’, it will be loaded using pytorch; otherwise, it will be
loaded as a pickle file.  To load a model from memory (i.e. an
existing python object), specify the filename as “LATER”, and then
call \sphinxtitleref{lammps.mliap.load\_model(model)} from python before using the
pair style.  When using LAMMPS via the library mode, you will need to
call \sphinxtitleref{lammps.mliappy.activate\_mliappy(lmp)} on the active LAMMPS
object before the pair style is defined.  This call locates and loads
the mliap\sphinxhyphen{}specific python module that is built into LAMMPS.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor} keyword is followed by a descriptor style, and additional arguments.
Currently three descriptor styles are available: \sphinxstyleemphasis{sna}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{so3}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace}.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{sna} indicates the bispectrum component descriptors used by the Spectral
Neighbor Analysis Potential (SNAP) potentials of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_snap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style snap}}}}.  A single additional argument specifies the descriptor
filename containing the parameters and setting used by the SNAP
descriptor.  The descriptor filename usually ends in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{.mliap.descriptor} extension.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{so3} indicated the power spectrum component descriptors. A single additional
argument specifies the descriptor filename containing the parameters and setting.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} indicates the atomic cluster expansion (ACE) descriptors. A single
additional argument specifies the filename containing parameters, settings, and
definitions of the ace descriptors (through tabulated basis function indices and
corresponding generalized Clebsch\sphinxhyphen{}Gordan coefficients) in the ctilde file format,
e.g. in the potential file format with \sphinxtitleref{*.ace} or \sphinxtitleref{*.yace} extensions from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style pace}}}}. Note that unlike the potential file, the
Clebsch\sphinxhyphen{}Gordan coefficients in the descriptor file supplied should \sphinxstyleemphasis{NOT} be
multiplied by linear or square root embedding terms.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SNAP descriptor file closely follows the format of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_snap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style snap}}}} parameter file.  The file can contain
blank and comment lines (start with \#) anywhere. Each non\sphinxhyphen{}blank
non\sphinxhyphen{}comment line must contain one keyword/value pair. The required
keywords are \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcutfac} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{twojmax}. There are many optional keywords
that are described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_snap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style snap}}}} doc page.
In addition, the SNAP descriptor file must contain the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelems},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{elems}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{radelems}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{welems} keywords.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelems} keyword
specifies the number of elements provided in the other three keywords.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{elems} keyword is followed by a list of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelems} element names that
must include the element names appearing in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command,
but can contain other names too.  Similarly, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{radelems} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{welems}
keywords are followed by lists of \sphinxstyleemphasis{nelems} numbers giving the element
radius and element weight of each element. Obviously, the order in which
the elements are listed must be consistent for all three keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SO3 descriptor file is similar to the SNAP descriptor except that it
contains a few more arguments (e.g., \sphinxstyleemphasis{nmax} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{alpha}). The preparation
of SO3 descriptor and model files can be done with the
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/qzhu2017/PyXtal\_FF}{Pyxtal\_FF} package.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ACE descriptor file differs from the SNAP and SO3 files. It more
closely resembles the potential file format for linear or square\sphinxhyphen{}root
embedding ACE potentials used in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style pace}}}}.
As noted above, the key difference is that the Clebsch\sphinxhyphen{}Gordan
coefficients in the descriptor file with \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliap descriptor ace} are
\sphinxstyleemphasis{NOT} multiplied by linear or square root embedding terms.  In other
words,the model is separated from the descriptor definitions and
hyperparameters.  In {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style pace}}}}, they are
combined.  The ACE descriptor files required by \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliap} are generated
automatically in \sphinxhref{https://github.com/FitSNAP/FitSNAP}{FitSNAP} during
linear, pytorch, etc. ACE model fitting. Additional tools are provided
there to prepare \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptor files and hyperparameters before model
fitting.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptor files can also be extracted from ACE
model fits in \sphinxhref{https://github.com/ICAMS/python-ace}{python\sphinxhyphen{}ace.}.  It
is important to note that order of the types listed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} must match the order of the elements/types listed in the
ACE descriptor file for all \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliap} styles when using \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for these \sphinxstyleemphasis{model} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{descriptor} files.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To significantly reduce SO3 descriptor/force calculation time,
some properties are pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed and reused during the calculation.
These can consume a significant amount of RAM for simulations of
larger systems since their size depends on the total number of
neighbors per MPI process.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Nov2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{unified} keyword is followed by an argument specifying the
filename containing the serialized unified Python object and the “ghostneigh” toggle
(0/1) to disable/enable the construction of neighbors lists including
neighbors of ghost atoms. If the filename ends in ‘.pt’, or ‘.pth’, it will be loaded
using pytorch; otherwise, it will be loaded as a pickle file.
If ghostneigh is enabled, it is recommended to set {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify}}}}
cutoff manually, such as in the following example.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ninteractions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{cutdist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.5}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{skin}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{commcut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}ninteractions\PYGZcb{}*\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}cutdist\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{n+nv}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{skin}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{neighbor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{skin}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bin}
\PYG{k}{comm\PYGZus{}modify}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{commcut}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To load a model from memory
(i.e. an existing python object), call \sphinxtitleref{lammps.mliap.load\_unified(unified)}
from python, and then specify the filename as “EXISTS”. When using LAMMPS via
the library mode, you will need to call \sphinxtitleref{lammps.mliappy.activate\_mliappy(lmp)}
on the active LAMMPS object before the pair style is defined. This call locates
and loads the mliap\sphinxhyphen{}specific python module that is built into LAMMPS.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS with
user\sphinxhyphen{}specifiable parameters as described above.  You never need to
specify a pair\_coeff command with I != J arguments for this style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_mliap:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. In addition, building LAMMPS with
the ML\sphinxhyphen{}IAP package requires building LAMMPS with the ML\sphinxhyphen{}SNAP package.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mliappy} model requires building LAMMPS with the PYTHON package.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ace} descriptor requires building LAMMPS with the ML\sphinxhyphen{}PACE package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info. Note
that \sphinxtitleref{pair\_mliap/kk} acceleration will \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} invoke the \sphinxtitleref{kk}
accelerated variants of SNAP or ACE descriptors.

\section{pair\_style momb command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_momb:pair-style-momb-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_momb:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_momb::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_momb:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{momb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{s6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
s6 = global scaling factor of the exchange\sphinxhyphen{}correlation functional used (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
d = damping scaling factor of Grimme’s method (unitless)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_momb:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{momb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.75}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{charmm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{momb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.75}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{morse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.5}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{momb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.2847}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.361}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_momb:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{momb} computes pairwise van der Waals (vdW) and short\sphinxhyphen{}range
interactions using the Morse potential and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_momb:grimme}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Grimme)}}}} method
implemented in the Many\sphinxhyphen{}Body Metal\sphinxhyphen{}Organic (MOMB) force field
described comprehensively in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_momb:fichthorn}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fichthorn)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_momb:zhou5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Zhou)}}}}. Grimme’s method is widely used to correct for
dispersion in density functional theory calculations.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} E & = D_0 [\exp^{-2 \alpha (r-r_0)} - 2\exp^{-\alpha (r-r_0)}] - s_6 \frac{C_6}{r^6} f_{damp}(r,R_r) \\
f_{damp}(r,R_r) & = \frac{1}{1 + \exp^{-d(r/R_r - 1)}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{momb} pair style, the following coefficients must be defined
for each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}
command as in the examples above, or in the data file or restart files
read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(D_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (1/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_6\) (energy*distance\textasciicircum{}6 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_r\) (distance units, typically sum of atomic vdW radii)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/opt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/kk}


\section{pair\_style morse/smooth/linear command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_morse:pair-style-morse-smooth-linear-command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/smooth/linear/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_morse:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/smooth/linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/soft}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for Morse interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/smooth/linear} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for Morse interactions (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_morse:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{morse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{morse}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{smooth}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_morse:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = D_0 \left[ e^{- 2 \alpha (r - r_0)} - 2 e^{- \alpha (r - r_0)} \right]
    \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(D_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (1/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global morse
cutoff is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/smooth/linear} variant is similar to the lj/smooth/linear
variant in that it adds to the potential a shift and a linear term
so that both, potential energy and force, go to zero at the cut\sphinxhyphen{}off:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\phi\left(r\right) & =  D_0 \left[ e^{- 2 \alpha (r - r_0)} - 2 e^{- \alpha (r - r_0)} \right] \qquad r < r_c \\
E\left(r\right) & =  \phi\left(r\right)  - \phi\left(r_c\right) - \left(r - r_c\right) \left.\frac{d\phi}{d r} \right|_{r=r_c}       \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The syntax of the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands are the same for
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/smooth/linear} styles.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
A version of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} style with a soft core, \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/soft},
suitable for use in free energy calculations, is part of the FEP
package and is documented with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_fep_soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style */soft}}}} styles. The version with soft core is only available if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_morse:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
None of these pair styles support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of these pair styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table options are not relevant for
the Morse pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of these pair styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of these pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

built with the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\label{\detokenize{pair_morse:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{pair\_style multi/lucy@\spxentry{pair\_style multi/lucy}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style multi/lucy command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:pair-style-multi-lucy-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{multi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lucy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lookup} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} = method of interpolation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = use N values in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lookup}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} tables

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{multi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lucy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{multibody.table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ENTRY1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{multi/lucy} computes a density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force following from
the many\sphinxhyphen{}body form described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:moore1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Moore)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:warren1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Warren)}}}} as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_{i}^{DD}(\rho_i,\rho_j,r_{ij}) = \frac{1}{2} \omega_{DD}\left(r_{ij}\right)
\left[A\left(\rho_i\right) + A\left(\rho_j\right)\right]e_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which consists of a density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent function, \(A(\rho)\), and a
radial\sphinxhyphen{}dependent weight function, \(\omega_{DD}(r_{ij})\).  The
radial\sphinxhyphen{}dependent weight function, \(\omega_{DD}(r_{ij})\), is taken
as the Lucy function:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\omega_{DD}\left(r_{ij}\right) = \left(1+\frac{3r_{ij}}{r_{cut}}\right)\left(1+\frac{r_{ij}}{r_{cut}}\right)^3\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy for a given particle is given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}u_{i}^{DD}\left(\rho_{i}\right) = \frac{\pi r_{cut}^4}{84} \int_{\rho_0}^{\rho_i} A\left(\rho'\right) d\rho'\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the supporting information of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:brennan1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Brennan)}}}} or the
publication by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:moore1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Moore)}}}} for more details on the functional
form.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An interpolation table is used to evaluate the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy
(\(\int A(\rho') d\rho'\)) and force (\(A(\rho')\)).  Note that
the prefactor to the energy is computed after the interpolation, thus
the \(\int A(\rho') d \rho'\) will have units of energy / length\textasciicircum{}4.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interpolation table is created as a pre\sphinxhyphen{}computation by fitting
cubic splines to the file values and interpolating the
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force at each of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} densities.  During a
simulation, the tables are used to interpolate the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
energy and force as needed for each pair of particles separated by a
distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}.  The interpolation is done in one of 2 styles: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lookup}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lookup} style, the density is used to find the nearest table
entry, which is the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style, the density is used to find the 2 surrounding
table values from which the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force are
computed by linear interpolation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filename specifies a file containing the tabulated
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force.  The keyword specifies a section
of the file.  The cutoff is an optional coefficient.  If not
specified, the outer cutoff in the table itself (see below) will be
used to build an interpolation table that extend to the largest
tabulated distance.  If specified, only file values up to the cutoff
are used to create the interpolation table.  The format of this file
is described below.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is a series of one or more sections,
defined as follows (without the parenthesized comments):
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\# Density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent function (one or more comment or blank lines)

DD\sphinxhyphen{}FUNCTION                (keyword is first text on line)
N 500 R 1.0 10.0           (N, R, RSQ parameters)
                           (blank)
1 1.0 25.5 102.34          (index, density, energy/r\textasciicircum{}4, force)
2 1.02 23.4 98.5
...
500 10.0 0.001 0.003
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which
identifies the section.  The line can contain additional text, but the
initial text must match the argument specified in the pair\_coeff
command.  The next line lists (in any order) one or more parameters
for the table.  Each parameter is a keyword followed by one or more
numeric values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter “N” is required and its value is the number of table
entries that follow.  Note that this may be different than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style multi/lucy}}}} command.
Let Ntable = \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} in the pair\_style command, and Nfile = “N” in the
tabulated file.  What LAMMPS does is a preliminary interpolation by
creating splines using the Nfile tabulated values as nodal points.  It
uses these to interpolate the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force at
Ntable different points.  The resulting tables of length Ntable are
then used as described above, when computing the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
energy and force.  This means that if you want the interpolation
tables of length Ntable to match exactly what is in the tabulated file
(with effectively no preliminary interpolation), you should set Ntable
= Nfile, and use the “RSQ” parameter.  This is because the internal
table abscissa is always RSQ (separation distance squared), for
efficient lookup.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All other parameters are optional.  If “R” or “RSQ” does
not appear, then the distances in each line of the table are used
as\sphinxhyphen{}is to perform spline interpolation.  In this case, the table values
can be spaced in \sphinxstyleemphasis{density} uniformly or however you wish to position table
values in regions of large gradients.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If used, the parameters “R” or “RSQ” are followed by 2 values \sphinxstyleemphasis{rlo} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rhi}.  If specified, the density associated with each
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force value is computed from these 2 values
(at high accuracy), rather than using the (low\sphinxhyphen{}accuracy) value listed in
each line of the table.  The density values in the table file are
ignored in this case.  For “R”, distances uniformly spaced between \sphinxstyleemphasis{rlo}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rhi} are computed; for “RSQ”, squared distances uniformly spaced
between \sphinxstyleemphasis{rlo*rlo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rhi*rhi} are computed.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use “R” or “RSQ”, the tabulated distance values in the file
are effectively ignored, and replaced by new values as described in
the previous paragraph.  If the density value in the table is not
very close to the new value (i.e. round\sphinxhyphen{}off difference), then you
will be assigning density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force values to a
different density, which is probably not what you want.  LAMMPS will
warn if this is occurring.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines list the tabulated values.
On each line, the first value is the index from 1 to N, the second value is
r (in density units), the third value is the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent function value
(in energy units / length\textasciicircum{}4), and the fourth is the force (in force units).  The
density values must increase from one line to the next.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one file can contain many sections, each with a tabulated
potential.  LAMMPS reads the file section by section until it finds
one that matches the specified keyword.

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift, table, and tail options are
not relevant for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes the settings for the “pair\_style multi/lucy” command
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so a pair\_style command does
not need to specified in an input script that reads a restart file.
However, the coefficient information is not stored in the restart

\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{multi}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lucy}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{multibody.table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ENTRY1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h2o}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{fluid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy_rx:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{multi/lucy/rx} is used in reaction DPD simulations, where the
coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained (CG) particles are composed of \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} species whose
reaction rate kinetics are determined from a set of \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} reaction rate
equations through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rx::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rx}}}} command.  The species of
one CG particle can interact with a species in a neighboring CG
particle through a site\sphinxhyphen{}site interaction potential model.  Style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{multi/lucy/rx} computes the site\sphinxhyphen{}site density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent force
following from the many\sphinxhyphen{}body form described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy_rx:moore2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Moore)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy_rx:warren2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Warren)}}}} as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_{i}^{DD}(\rho_i,\rho_j,r_{ij}) = \frac{1}{2} \omega_{DD}\left(r_{ij}\right)
\left[A\left(\rho_i\right) + A\left(\rho_j\right)\right]e_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which consists of a density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent function, \(A(\rho)\), and a
radial\sphinxhyphen{}dependent weight function, \(\omega_{DD}(r_{ij})\).  The
radial\sphinxhyphen{}dependent weight function, \(\omega_{DD}(r_{ij})\), is taken
as the Lucy function:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\omega_{DD}\left(r_{ij}\right) = \left(1+\frac{3r_{ij}}{r_{cut}}\right)\left(1+\frac{r_{ij}}{r_{cut}}\right)^3\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy for a given particle is given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}u_{i}^{DD}\left(\rho_{i}\right) = \frac{\pi r_{cut}^4}{84} \int_{\rho_0}^{\rho_i} A\left(\rho'\right) d\rho'\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the supporting information of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy_rx:brennan2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Brennan)}}}} or the
publication by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy_rx:moore2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Moore)}}}} for more details on the functional
form.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An interpolation table is used to evaluate the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy
(\(\int A(\rho') d \rho'\)) and force (\(A(\rho')\)).  Note that
the prefactor to the energy is computed after the interpolation, thus
the \(\int A(\rho') d\rho'\) will have units of energy / length\textasciicircum{}4.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interpolation table is created as a pre\sphinxhyphen{}computation by fitting
cubic splines to the file values and interpolating the
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force at each of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} densities.  During a
simulation, the tables are used to interpolate the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
energy and force as needed for each pair of particles separated by a
distance \sphinxstyleemphasis{R}.  The interpolation is done in one of 2 styles: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lookup}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{lookup} style, the density is used to find the nearest table
entry, which is the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style, the density is used to find the 2 surrounding
table values from which the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force are
computed by linear interpolation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
species1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
species2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filename specifies a file containing the tabulated
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force.  The keyword specifies a section
of the file.  The cutoff is an optional coefficient.  If not
specified, the outer cutoff in the table itself (see below) will be
used to build an interpolation table that extend to the largest
tabulated distance.  If specified, only file values up to the cutoff
are used to create the interpolation table.  The format of this file
is described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The species tags define the site\sphinxhyphen{}site interaction potential between
two species contained within two different particles.  The species
tags must either correspond to the species defined in the reaction
kinetics files specified with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rx::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rx}}}} command or they
must correspond to the tag “1fluid”, signifying interaction with a
product species mixture determined through a one\sphinxhyphen{}fluid approximation.
The interaction potential is weighted by the geometric average of
either the mole fraction concentrations or the number of molecules
associated with the interacting coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained particles (see the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fractional} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{molecular} weighting pair style options). The coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained potential is
stored before and after the reaction kinetics solver is applied, where
the difference is defined to be the internal chemical energy (uChem).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is a series of one or more sections,
defined as follows (without the parenthesized comments):
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\# Density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent function (one or more comment or blank lines)

DD\sphinxhyphen{}FUNCTION                (keyword is first text on line)
N 500 R 1.0 10.0           (N, R, RSQ parameters)
                           (blank)
1 1.0 25.5 102.34          (index, density, energy/r\textasciicircum{}4, force)
2 1.02 23.4 98.5
...
500 10.0 0.001 0.003
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which
identifies the section.  The line can contain additional text, but the
initial text must match the argument specified in the pair\_coeff
command.  The next line lists (in any order) one or more parameters
for the table.  Each parameter is a keyword followed by one or more
numeric values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter “N” is required and its value is the number of table
entries that follow.  Note that this may be different than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_multi_lucy_rx::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style multi/lucy/rx}}}}
command.  Let Ntable = \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} in the pair\_style command, and Nfile = “N”
in the tabulated file.  What LAMMPS does is a preliminary
interpolation by creating splines using the Nfile tabulated values as
nodal points.  It uses these to interpolate the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent
energy and force at Ntable different points.  The resulting tables of
length Ntable are then used as described above, when computing the
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force.  This means that if you want the
interpolation tables of length Ntable to match exactly what is in the
tabulated file (with effectively no preliminary interpolation), you
should set Ntable = Nfile, and use the “RSQ” parameter.  This is
because the internal table abscissa is always RSQ (separation distance
squared), for efficient lookup.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All other parameters are optional.  If “R” or “RSQ” does not appear,
then the distances in each line of the table are used as\sphinxhyphen{}is to perform
spline interpolation.  In this case, the table values can be spaced in
\sphinxstyleemphasis{density} uniformly or however you wish to position table values in
regions of large gradients.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If used, the parameters “R” or “RSQ” are followed by 2 values \sphinxstyleemphasis{rlo}
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rhi}.  If specified, the density associated with each
density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force value is computed from these 2
values (at high accuracy), rather than using the (low\sphinxhyphen{}accuracy) value
listed in each line of the table.  The density values in the table
file are ignored in this case.  For “R”, distances uniformly spaced
between \sphinxstyleemphasis{rlo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rhi} are computed; for “RSQ”, squared distances
uniformly spaced between \sphinxstyleemphasis{rlo*rlo} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rhi*rhi} are computed.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use “R” or “RSQ”, the tabulated distance values in the
file are effectively ignored, and replaced by new values as described
in the previous paragraph.  If the density value in the table is not
very close to the new value (i.e. round\sphinxhyphen{}off difference), then you will
be assigning density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent energy and force values to a different
density, which is probably not what you want.  LAMMPS will warn if
this is occurring.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines list the tabulated values.
On each line, the first value is the index from 1 to N, the second value is
r (in density units), the third value is the density\sphinxhyphen{}dependent function
value (in energy units / length\textasciicircum{}4), and the fourth is the force (in force
units).  The density values must increase from one line to the next.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one file can contain many sections, each with a tabulated
potential.  LAMMPS reads the file section by section until it finds
one that matches the specified keyword.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

This pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift, table, and tail options are
not relevant for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes the settings for the “pair\_style multi/lucy/rx” command
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so a pair\_style command does
not need to specified in an input script that reads a restart file.
However, the coefficient information is not stored in the restart

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the

\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\section{pair\_style nb3b/harmonic command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b:pair-style-nb3b-harmonic-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b::doc}}

\section{pair\_style nb3b/screened command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b:pair-style-nb3b-screened-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b:examples}}
