\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiOH.nb3b.screened}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nb3b:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nb3b/harmonic} computes a non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded 3\sphinxhyphen{}body harmonic potential for the
energy E of a system of atoms as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium value of the angle and \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} is a
prefactor. Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \sphinxstyleemphasis{K}. The form
of the potential is identical to that used in angle\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic},
but in this case, the atoms do not need to be explicitly bonded.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nb3b/screened} adds an additional exponentially decaying factor to
the harmonic term, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2 \exp \left(- \frac{r_{ij}}{\rho_{ij}} - \frac{r_{ik}}{\rho_{ik}} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\rho_ij\) and \(\rho_ik\) are the screening factors along
the two bonds. Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \sphinxstyleemphasis{K}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with these styles which
specifies a potential file with parameters for specified elements.
These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N additional
arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command, where N is the
number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine a file SiC.nb3b.harmonic has potential values
for Si and C.  If your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you
want the first 3 to be Si, and the fourth to be C, you would use the
following pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiC.nb3b.harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the Si
element in the potential file.  The final C argument maps LAMMPS atom
type 4 to the C element in the potential file.  If a mapping value is
specified as NULL, the mapping is not performed.  This can be used
when the potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The
NULL values are placeholders for atom types that will be used with
other potentials. Two examples of pair\_coeff command for use with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nb3b}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{MgOH.nb3b.harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Mg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Three\sphinxhyphen{}body non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded harmonic files in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potentials} directory of
the LAMMPS distribution have a “.nb3b.harmonic” suffix.  Lines that
are not blank or comments (starting with \#) define parameters for a
triplet of elements.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each entry has six arguments. The first three are atom types as
referenced in the LAMMPS input file. The first argument specifies the
central atom. The fourth argument indicates the \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} parameter. The
fifth argument indicates \(\theta_0\). The sixth argument indicates a
separation cutoff in Angstroms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a given entry, if the second and third arguments are identical,
then the entry is for a cutoff for the distance between types 1 and 2
(values for \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} and \(\theta_0\) are irrelevant in this case).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a given entry, if the first three arguments are all different, then
the entry is for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} and \(\theta_0\) parameters (the cutoff in
this case is irrelevant).

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is required that the potential file contains entries for \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}
permutations of the elements listed in the pair\_coeff command.
If certain combinations are not parameterized the corresponding
parameters should be set to zero. The potential file can also
contain entries for additional elements which are not used in
a particular simulation; LAMMPS ignores those entries.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/split} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/long}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for Pair interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/split} args = cutoff
  cutoff = global cutoff for Pair interactions (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/cut} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Pair (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/long} args = cutoff (cutoff2)
  cutoff = global cutoff for Pair (and Coulombic if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Coulombic (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7.0}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm} computes site\sphinxhyphen{}site interactions based on the N\sphinxhyphen{}M potential
by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_nm:clarke}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Clarke}}}}, mainly used for ionic liquids.  A site can
represent a single atom or a united\sphinxhyphen{}atom site.  The energy of an
interaction has the following form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{E_0}{(n-m)} \left[ m \left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)^n - n
\left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)^m \right] \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_c\) is the cutoff and \(r_0\) is the minimum of the
potential.  Please note that this differs from the convention used for
other Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones potentials in LAMMPS where \(\sigma\) represents
the location where the energy is zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/split} applies the standard LJ (12\sphinxhyphen{}6) potential above
\(r_0 = 2^\frac{1}{6}\sigma\).  Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/split} is employed in
polymer equilibration protocols that combine core\sphinxhyphen{}softening approaches
with topology\sphinxhyphen{}changing moves {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_nm:dietz}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Dietz}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/cut} adds a Coulombic pairwise interaction given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(C\) is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}conversion constant, \(q_i\) and \(q_j\)
are the charges on the two atoms, and epsilon is the dielectric constant which can
be set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dielectric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dielectric}}}} command.  If one cutoff is
specified in the pair\_style command, it is used for both the N\sphinxhyphen{}M and Coulombic
terms.  If two cutoffs are specified, they are used as cutoffs for the N\sphinxhyphen{}M and
Coulombic terms respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/long} compute the same
Coulombic interactions as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/cut} except that an
additional damping factor is applied to the Coulombic term so it can
be used in conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{kspace\_style}}}}
command and its \sphinxstyleemphasis{ewald} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{pppm} option.  The Coulombic cutoff
specified for this style means that pairwise interactions within this
distance are computed directly; interactions outside that distance are
computed in reciprocal space.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm} pair styles, the following coefficients must
be defined for each pair of atoms types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the
examples above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(E_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(m\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff1 (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff2 (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter 2 coefficients are optional.  If not specified, the global
N\sphinxhyphen{}M and Coulombic cutoffs specified in the pair\_style command are used.
If only one cutoff is specified, it is used as the cutoff for both N\sphinxhyphen{}M
and Coulombic interactions for this type pair.  If both coefficients
are specified, they are used as the N\sphinxhyphen{}M and Coulombic cutoffs for this
type pair.  You cannot specify 2 cutoffs for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm}, since it
has no Coulombic terms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/long} only the N\sphinxhyphen{}M cutoff can be specified since a
Coulombic cutoff cannot be specified for an individual I,J type pair.
All type pairs use the same global Coulombic cutoff specified in the
pair\_style command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nm:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support mixing. Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm} pair styles supports the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option for the energy of the pair
interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm/cut/coul/long} pair styles support the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option since they can tabulate
the short\sphinxhyphen{}range portion of the long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm} pair styles support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding a long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail correction to the energy and
pressure for the N\sphinxhyphen{}M portion of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm} pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nm} pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_nm:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\section{pair\_style none command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_none:pair-style-none-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_none:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_none::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_none:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{none}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_none:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{none}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_none:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a pair style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} means that any previous pair style setting
will be deleted and pairwise forces and energies are not computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As a consequence there will be a pairwise force cutoff of 0.0, which has
implications for the default setting of the neighbor list and the
communication cutoff.  Those are the sum of the largest pairwise cutoff
and the neighbor skin distance (see the documentation of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} command and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify}}}} command).  When you have bonds, angles, dihedrals, or
impropers defined at the same time, you must set the communication
cutoff so that communication cutoff distance is large enough to acquire
and communicate sufficient ghost atoms from neighboring subdomains as
needed for computing bonds, angles, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A pair style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} will also not request a pairwise neighbor list.
However if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{neighbor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{neighbor}}}} style is \sphinxstyleemphasis{bin}, data
structures for binning are still allocated.  If the neighbor list cutoff
is small, then these data structures can consume a large amount of
memory.  So you should either set the neighbor style to \sphinxstyleemphasis{nsq} or set the
skin distance to a larger value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style zero}}}} for a way to set a pairwise
cutoff and thus trigger the building of a neighbor lists and setting
a corresponding communication cutoff, but compute no pairwise interactions.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_none:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You must not use a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command with this pair
style.  Since there is no interaction computed, you cannot set any
coefficients for it.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_none:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style zero}}}}

\label{\detokenize{pair_none:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style1}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style1 = \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/overlay oxdna/excv oxdna/stk oxdna/hbond oxdna/xstk oxdna/coaxstk}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style2 = \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/excv} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/stk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/hbond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/xstk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/coaxstk}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for these particular styles

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/stk} args = seq T xi kappa 6.0 0.4 0.9 0.32 0.75 1.3 0 0.8 0.9 0 0.95 0.9 0 0.95 2.0 0.65 2.0 0.65
  seq = seqav (for average sequence stacking strength) or seqdep (for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent stacking strength)
  T = temperature (LJ units: 0.1 = 300 K, real units: 300 = 300 K)
  xi = 1.3448 (LJ units) or 8.01727944817084 (real units), temperature\sphinxhyphen{}independent coefficient in stacking strength
  kappa = 2.6568 (LJ units) or 0.005279604 (real units), coefficient of linear temperature dependence in stacking strength
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/hbond} args = seq eps 8.0 0.4 0.75 0.34 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 0.46 3.141592653589793 0.7 4.0 1.5707963267948966 0.45 4.0 1.5707963267948966 0.45
  seq = seqav (for average sequence base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strength) or seqdep (for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strength)
  eps = 1.077 (LJ units) or 6.42073911784652 (real units), average hydrogen bonding strength between A\sphinxhyphen{}T and C\sphinxhyphen{}G Watson\sphinxhyphen{}Crick base pairs, 0 between all other pairs
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients in the above examples are provided in forms
compatible with both \sphinxstyleemphasis{units lj} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{units real} (see documentation
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}).  These can also be read from a potential
file with correct unit style by specifying the name of the
file. Several potential files for each unit style are included in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna} pair styles compute the pairwise\sphinxhyphen{}additive parts of the oxDNA
force field for coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained modelling of DNA. The effective
interaction between the nucleotides consists of potentials for the
excluded volume interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/excv}, the stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/stk},
cross\sphinxhyphen{}stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/xstk} and coaxial stacking interaction
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/coaxstk} as well as the hydrogen\sphinxhyphen{}bonding interaction
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/hbond} between complementary pairs of nucleotides on opposite
strands. Average sequence or sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent stacking and
base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strengths are supported {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:sulc1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc)}}}}. Quasi\sphinxhyphen{}unique
base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing between nucleotides can be achieved by using more
complementary pairs of atom types like 5\sphinxhyphen{}8 and 6\sphinxhyphen{}7, 9\sphinxhyphen{}12 and 10\sphinxhyphen{}11,
13\sphinxhyphen{}16 and 14\sphinxhyphen{}15, etc.  This prevents the hybridization of in principle
complementary bases within Ntypes/4 bases up and down along the
backbone.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact functional form of the pair styles is rather complex.  The
individual potentials consist of products of modulation factors, which
themselves are constructed from a number of more basic potentials
(Morse, Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones, harmonic angle and distance) as well as quadratic
smoothing and modulation terms.  We refer to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:ouldridge-dphil1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge\sphinxhyphen{}DPhil)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:ouldridge1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}} for a detailed
description of the oxDNA force field.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles have to be used together with the related oxDNA
bond style \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/fene} for the connectivity of the phosphate
backbone (see also documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style oxdna/fene}}}}). Most of the coefficients in the above example have to
be kept fixed and cannot be changed without reparameterizing the
entire model.  Exceptions are the first four coefficients after
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/stk} (seq=seqdep, T=0.1, xi=1.3448 and kappa=2.6568 and
corresponding \sphinxstyleemphasis{real unit} equivalents in the above examples) and the
first coefficient after \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/hbond} (seq=seqdep in the above
example).  When using a Langevin thermostat, e.g. through {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
langevin}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}} the temperature coefficients have to be
matched to the one used in the fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles have to be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style hybrid bond
ellipsoid oxdna} (see documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}). The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style oxdna} stores the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}5’ polarity
of the nucleotide strand, which is set through the bond topology in
the data file. The first (second) atom in a bond definition is
understood to point towards the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}end (5’\sphinxhyphen{}end) of the strand.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input and data files for DNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/oxDNA/}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.../oxDNA2/}}.  A
simple python setup tool which creates single straight or helical DNA
strands, DNA duplexes or arrays of DNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:henrich1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henrich)}}}} in any publication that uses
this implementation. An updated documentation that contains general
information on the model, its implementation and performance as well as
the structure of the data and input file can be found \sphinxhref{PDF/CG-DNA.pdf}{here}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite also the relevant oxDNA publications
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:ouldridge1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:ouldridge-dphil1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge\sphinxhyphen{}DPhil)}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna:sulc1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Potential file reading}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna:potential-file-reading}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each pair style above the first non\sphinxhyphen{}modifiable argument can be a
filename, and if it is, no further arguments should be
supplied. Therefore the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqav}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will be interpreted as a request to read the corresponding hydrogen
bonding potential parameters from the file with the given name. The file
can define multiple potential parameters for both bonded and pair
interactions, but for the example pair interaction above there must
exist in the file a line of the form:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{coefficients}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If potential customization is required, the potential file reading can
be mixed with the manual specification of the potential parameters. For
example, the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{excv}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coaxstk}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{excv}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stk}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{seqav}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3448}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.6568}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.32}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.75}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.95}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.95}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.65}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.65}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqav}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqav}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqav}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xstk}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coaxstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{46.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.22}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.58}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.541592653589793}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.65}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.95}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.95}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.65}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.65}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will read the stacking and coaxial stacking potential parameters from
the manual specification and all others from the potential file
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna\_lj.cgdna}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are sample potential files for each unit style in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution. The potential file
unit system must align with the units defined via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command. For conversion between different \sphinxstyleemphasis{LJ} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} unit
systems for oxDNA, the python tool \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj2real.py} located in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}} directory can be used. This tool
assumes similar file structure to the examples found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
CG\sphinxhyphen{}DNA package and the MOLECULE and ASPHERE package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style1}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style1 = \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/overlay oxdna2/excv oxdna2/stk oxdna2/hbond oxdna2/xstk oxdna2/coaxstk oxdna2/dh}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style2 = \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/excv} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/stk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/hbond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/xstk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/coaxstk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/dh}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for these particular styles

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/stk} args = seq T xi kappa 6.0 0.4 0.9 0.32 0.75 1.3 0 0.8 0.9 0 0.95 0.9 0 0.95 2.0 0.65 2.0 0.65
  seq = seqav (for average sequence stacking strength) or seqdep (for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent stacking strength)
  T = temperature (LJ units: 0.1 = 300 K, real units: 300 = 300 K)
  xi = 1.3523 (LJ units) or 8.06199211612242 (real units), temperature\sphinxhyphen{}independent coefficient in stacking strength
  kappa = 2.6717 (LJ units) or 0.005309213 (real units), coefficient of linear temperature dependence in stacking strength
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/hbond} args = seq eps 8.0 0.4 0.75 0.34 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 0.46 3.141592653589793 0.7 4.0 1.5707963267948966 0.45 4.0 1.5707963267948966 0.45
  seq = seqav (for average sequence base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strength) or seqdep (for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strength)
  eps = 1.0678 (LJ units) or 6.36589157849259 (real units), average hydrogen bonding strength between A\sphinxhyphen{}T and C\sphinxhyphen{}G Watson\sphinxhyphen{}Crick base pairs, 0 between all other pairs
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/dh} args = T rhos qeff
  T = temperature (LJ units: 0.1 = 300 K, real units: 300 = 300 K)
  rhos = salt concentration (mole per litre)
  qeff = 0.815 (effective charge in elementary charges)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients in the above examples are provided in forms
compatible with both \sphinxstyleemphasis{units lj} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{units real} (see documentation
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}).  These can also be read from a potential
file with correct unit style by specifying the name of the
file. Several potential files for each unit style are included in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2} pair styles compute the pairwise\sphinxhyphen{}additive parts of the
oxDNA force field for coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained modelling of DNA. The effective
interaction between the nucleotides consists of potentials for the
excluded volume interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/excv}, the stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/stk},
cross\sphinxhyphen{}stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/xstk} and coaxial stacking interaction
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/coaxstk}, electrostatic Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/dh} as
well as the hydrogen\sphinxhyphen{}bonding interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/hbond} between
complementary pairs of nucleotides on opposite strands. Average sequence
or sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent stacking and base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strengths are supported
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:sulc2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc)}}}}. Quasi\sphinxhyphen{}unique base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing between nucleotides can
be achieved by using more complementary pairs of atom types like 5\sphinxhyphen{}8 and
6\sphinxhyphen{}7, 9\sphinxhyphen{}12 and 10\sphinxhyphen{}11, 13\sphinxhyphen{}16 and 14\sphinxhyphen{}15, etc.  This prevents the
hybridization of in principle complementary bases within Ntypes/4 bases
up and down along the backbone.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact functional form of the pair styles is rather complex.  The
individual potentials consist of products of modulation factors, which
themselves are constructed from a number of more basic potentials
(Morse, Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones, harmonic angle and distance) as well as quadratic
smoothing and modulation terms.  We refer to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:snodin2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Snodin)}}}}
and the original oxDNA publications {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:ouldridge-dphil2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge\sphinxhyphen{}DPhil)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:ouldridge2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}} for a detailed
description of the oxDNA2 force field.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles have to be used together with the related oxDNA2
bond style \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/fene} for the connectivity of the phosphate
backbone (see also documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style oxdna2/fene}}}}). Most of the coefficients in the above example have to
be kept fixed and cannot be changed without reparameterizing the
entire model.  Exceptions are the first four coefficients after
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/stk} (seq=seqdep, T=0.1, xi=1.3523 and kappa=2.6717 and
corresponding \sphinxstyleemphasis{real unit} equivalents in the above examples).  the
first coefficient after \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/hbond} (seq=seqdep in the above
example) and the three coefficients after \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/dh} (T=0.1,
rhos=0.5, qeff=0.815 in the above example). When using a Langevin
thermostat e.g. through {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}} the temperature
coefficients have to be matched to the one used in the fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles have to be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style hybrid bond
ellipsoid oxdna} (see documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}). The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style oxdna} stores the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}5’ polarity
of the nucleotide strand, which is set through the bond topology in
the data file. The first (second) atom in a bond definition is
understood to point towards the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}end (5’\sphinxhyphen{}end) of the strand.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input and data files for DNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/oxDNA/}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.../oxDNA2/}}.  A
simple python setup tool which creates single straight or helical DNA
strands, DNA duplexes or arrays of DNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:henrich2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henrich)}}}} in any publication that uses
this implementation. An updated documentation that contains general
information on the model, its implementation and performance as well as
the structure of the data and input file can be found \sphinxhref{PDF/CG-DNA.pdf}{here}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite also the relevant oxDNA2 publications
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:snodin2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Snodin)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:sulc2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Potential file reading}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:potential-file-reading}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each pair style above the first non\sphinxhyphen{}modifiable argument can be a
filename (with exception of Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel, for which the effective
charge argument can be a filename), and if it is, no further arguments
should be supplied.  Therefore the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}real.cgdna}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will be interpreted as a request to read the corresponding hydrogen
bonding potential parameters from the file with the given name.  The
file can define multiple potential parameters for both bonded and pair
interactions, but for the example pair interaction above there must
exist in the file a line of the form:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{coefficients}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If potential customization is required, the potential file reading can
be mixed with the manual specification of the potential parameters. For
example, the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{excv}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coaxstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dh}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{excv}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.675}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.515}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.33}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.32}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stk}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3523}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.6717}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}

will read the excluded volume and Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel effective charge \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeff}
parameters from the manual specification and all others from the
potential file \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2\_lj.cgdna}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are sample potential files for each unit style in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}}
directory of the LAMMPS distribution. The potential file unit system
must align with the units defined via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}
command. For conversion between different \sphinxstyleemphasis{LJ} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} unit systems
for oxDNA, the python tool \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj2real.py} located in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}} directory can be used. This tool assumes
similar file structure to the examples found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/}}.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxdna2:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
CG\sphinxhyphen{}DNA package and the MOLECULE and ASPHERE package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style1}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style1 = \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/overlay oxrna2/excv oxrna2/stk oxrna2/hbond oxrna2/xstk oxrna2/coaxstk oxrna2/dh}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style2 = \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/excv} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/stk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/hbond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/xstk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/coaxstk} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/dh}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for these particular styles

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/stk} args = seq T xi kappa 6.0 0.43 0.93 0.35 0.78 0.9 0 0.95 0.9 0 0.95 1.3 0 0.8 1.3 0 0.8 2.0 0.65 2.0 0.65
  seq = seqav (for average sequence stacking strength) or seqdep (for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent stacking strength)
  T = temperature (LJ units: 0.1 = 300 K, real units: 300 = 300 K)
  xi = 1.40206 (LJ units) or 8.35864576375849 (real units), temperature\sphinxhyphen{}independent coefficient in stacking strength
  kappa = 2.77 (LJ units) or 0.005504556 (real units), coefficient of linear temperature dependence in stacking strength
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/hbond} args = seq eps 8.0 0.4 0.75 0.34 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 1.5 0 0.7 0.46 3.141592653589793 0.7 4.0 1.5707963267948966 0.45 4.0 1.5707963267948966 0.45
  seq = seqav (for average sequence base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strength) or seqdep (for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strength)
  eps = 0.870439 (LJ units) or 5.18928666388042 (real units), average hydrogen bonding strength between A\sphinxhyphen{}U and C\sphinxhyphen{}G Watson\sphinxhyphen{}Crick and G\sphinxhyphen{}U wobble base pairs, 0 between all other pairs
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/dh} args = T rhos qeff
  T = temperature (LJ units: 0.1 = 300 K, real units: 300 = 300 K)
  rhos = salt concentration (mole per litre)
  qeff = 1.02455 (effective charge in elementary charges)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients in the above examples are provided in forms
compatible with both \sphinxstyleemphasis{units lj} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{units real} (see documentation
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}).  These can also be read from a potential
file with correct unit style by specifying the name of the
file. Several potential files for each unit style are included in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2} pair styles compute the pairwise\sphinxhyphen{}additive parts of the
oxDNA force field for coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained modelling of RNA. The effective
interaction between the nucleotides consists of potentials for the
excluded volume interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/excv}, the stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/stk},
cross\sphinxhyphen{}stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/xstk} and coaxial stacking interaction
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/coaxstk}, electrostatic Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/dh} as
well as the hydrogen\sphinxhyphen{}bonding interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/hbond} between
complementary pairs of nucleotides on opposite strands. Average sequence
or sequence\sphinxhyphen{}dependent stacking and base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing strengths are supported
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:sulc32}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc2)}}}}. Quasi\sphinxhyphen{}unique base\sphinxhyphen{}pairing between nucleotides
can be achieved by using more complementary pairs of atom types like 5\sphinxhyphen{}8
and 6\sphinxhyphen{}7, 9\sphinxhyphen{}12 and 10\sphinxhyphen{}11, 13\sphinxhyphen{}16 and 14\sphinxhyphen{}15, etc.  This prevents the
hybridization of in principle complementary bases within Ntypes/4 bases
up and down along the backbone.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact functional form of the pair styles is rather complex.  The
individual potentials consist of products of modulation factors, which
themselves are constructed from a number of more basic potentials
(Morse, Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones, harmonic angle and distance) as well as quadratic
smoothing and modulation terms.  We refer to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:sulc31}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc1)}}}} and
the original oxDNA publications {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:ouldridge-dphil3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge\sphinxhyphen{}DPhil)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:ouldridge3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}} for a detailed
description of the oxRNA2 force field.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles have to be used together with the related oxDNA2
bond style \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/fene} for the connectivity of the phosphate
backbone (see also documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style oxrna2/fene}}}}). Most of the coefficients in the above example have to
be kept fixed and cannot be changed without reparameterizing the
entire model.  Exceptions are the first four coefficients after
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/stk} (seq=seqdep, T=0.1, xi=1.40206 and kappa=2.77 and
corresponding \sphinxstyleemphasis{real unit} equivalents in the above examples), the
first coefficient after \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/hbond} (seq=seqdep in the above
example) and the three coefficients after \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/dh} (T=0.1,
rhos=0.5, qeff=1.02455 in the above example). When using a Langevin
thermostat e.g. through {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}} the temperature
coefficients have to be matched to the one used in the fix.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles have to be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style hybrid bond
ellipsoid oxdna} (see documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}). The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style oxdna} stores the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}5’ polarity
of the nucleotide strand, which is set through the bond topology in
the data file. The first (second) atom in a bond definition is
understood to point towards the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}end (5’\sphinxhyphen{}end) of the strand.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input and data files for DNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/oxDNA/}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.../oxDNA2/}}.  A simple python
setup tool which creates single straight or helical DNA strands, DNA
duplexes or arrays of DNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:henrich3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henrich)}}}} in any publication that uses
this implementation.  The article contains general information on the
model, its implementation and performance as well as the structure of
the data and input file. The preprint version of the article can be
found \sphinxhref{PDF/CG-DNA.pdf}{here}.  Please cite also the relevant oxRNA2
publications {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:sulc31}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc1)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:sulc32}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc2)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Potential file reading}
\label{\detokenize{pair_oxrna2:potential-file-reading}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each pair style above the first non\sphinxhyphen{}modifiable argument can be a
filename (with exception of Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel, for which the effective
charge argument can be a filename), and if it is, no further arguments
should be supplied.  Therefore the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will be interpreted as a request to read the corresponding hydrogen
bonding potential parameters from the file with the given name.  The
file can define multiple potential parameters for both bonded and pair
interactions, but for the example pair interaction above there must
exist in the file a line of the form:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{coefficients}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If potential customization is required, the potential file reading can
be mixed with the manual specification of the potential parameters. For
example, the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{excv}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coaxstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dh}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{excv}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.675}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.515}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.33}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.32}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{stk}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.40206}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.77}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hbond}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{seqdep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{xstk}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coaxstk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dh}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.02455}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will read the excluded volume and Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel effective charge \sphinxstyleemphasis{qeff}
parameters from the manual specification and all others from the
potential file \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2\_lj.cgdna}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are sample potential files for each unit style in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution. The potential file
unit system must align with the units defined via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command. For conversion between different \sphinxstyleemphasis{LJ} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} unit
systems for oxDNA, the python tool \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj2real.py} located in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}} directory can be used. This tool
assumes similar file structure to the examples found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/}}.

\section{pair\_style pace command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:pair-style-pace-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_pace::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace/extrapolation/kk}


\section{pair\_style pace/extrapolation command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:pair-style-pace-extrapolation-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{product} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{recursive} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{chunksize}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{product} = use product algorithm for basis functions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{recursive} = use recursive algorithm for basis functions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{chunksize} value = number of atoms in each pass
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{extrapolation}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{product}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chunksize}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2048}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{PBE}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{core}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{rep.ace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu.yaml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{extrapolation}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu.yaml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu.asi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace} computes interactions using the Atomic Cluster
Expansion (ACE), which is a general expansion of the atomic energy in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}body basis functions. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace:drautz20191}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Drautz19)}}}}.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace}
pair style provides an efficient implementation that is described in
this paper {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace:lysogorskiy20211}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lysogorskiy21)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In ACE, the total energy is decomposed into a sum over atomic
energies. The energy of atom \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} is expressed as a linear or non\sphinxhyphen{}linear
function of one or more density functions.  By projecting the density
onto a local atomic base, the lowest order contributions to the energy
can be expressed as a set of scalar polynomials in basis function
contributions summed over neighbor atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace} style which
specifies an ACE coefficient file followed by N additional arguments
specifying the mapping of ACE elements to LAMMPS atom types, where N is
the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ACE coefficient file (.yaml or .yace/.ace format)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of ACE elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace} style which
specifies an ACE file that fully defines the potential.  Note that
unlike for other potentials, cutoffs are not set in the pair\_style or
pair\_coeff command; they are specified in the ACE file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace} command may be followed by the optional keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{product} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{recursive}, which determines which of two algorithms is
used for the calculation of basis functions and derivatives.  The
default is \sphinxstyleemphasis{recursive}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{chunksize} is only applicable when using the pair style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pace} with the KOKKOS package on GPUs and is ignored otherwise.  This
keyword controls the number of atoms in each pass used to compute the
atomic cluster expansion and is used to avoid running out of memory.
For example if there are 8192 atoms in the simulation and the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{chunksize} is set to 4096, the ACE calculation will be broken up into
two passes (running on a single GPU).


\subsection{Extrapolation grade}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:extrapolation-grade}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculation of extrapolation grade in PACE is implemented in \sphinxtitleref{pair\_style
pace/extrapolation}.  It is based on the MaxVol algorithm similar to
Moment Tensor Potential (MTP) by Shapeev et al.  and is described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pace:lysogorskiy2023}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Lysogorskiy23)}}}}.  In order to compute
extrapolation grade one needs to provide:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ACE potential in B\sphinxhyphen{}basis form (\sphinxtitleref{.yaml} format) and

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Active Set Inverted (ASI) file for corresponding potential (\sphinxtitleref{.asi} format)

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculation of extrapolation grades requires matrix\sphinxhyphen{}vector
multiplication for each atom and is slower than the usual \sphinxtitleref{pair\_style
pace recursive}, therefore it is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} computed by default.
Extrapolation grade calculation is involved by \sphinxtitleref{fix pair}, which
requests to compute \sphinxtitleref{gamma}, as shown in example below:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{extrapolation}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu.yaml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu.asi}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pace\PYGZus{}gamma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{extrapolation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}

\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{max\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reduce}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dump\PYGZus{}skip}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{c\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma \PYGZlt{} 5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pace\PYGZus{}dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{extrapolative\PYGZus{}structures.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pace\PYGZus{}dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skip}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}dump\PYGZus{}skip}

\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{max\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{extreme\PYGZus{}extrapolation}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{halt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}pace\PYGZus{}gamma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here extrapolation grade gamma is computed every 10 steps and is stored
in \sphinxtitleref{f\_pace\_gamma} per\sphinxhyphen{}atom variable.  The largest value of extrapolation
grade among all atoms in a structure is reduced to \sphinxtitleref{c\_max\_pace\_gamma}
variable.  Only if this value exceeds extrapolation threshold 5, then
the structure will be dumped into \sphinxtitleref{extrapolative\_structures.dump} file,
but not more often than every 20 steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On all other steps \sphinxtitleref{pair\_style pace recursive} will be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pace/extrapolation} with the KOKKOS package on GPUs
product B\sphinxhyphen{}basis evaluator is always used and only \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} ASI is supported.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the ACE coefficient file.


\subsection{Core repulsion}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:core-repulsion}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ACE potential can be configured to initiate core\sphinxhyphen{}repulsion from an inner cutoff,
seamlessly transitioning from ACE to ZBL. The core repulsion factor can be accessed
as a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantity, as demonstrated in the example below:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{pace}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CuNi.yaml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ni}

\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{pace\PYGZus{}corerep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{corerep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this case, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom \sphinxtitleref{f\_pace\_corerep} quantities represent the fraction of ZBL
core\sphinxhyphen{}repulsion for each atom.


\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pace:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS with
user\sphinxhyphen{}specifiable parameters as described above.  You never need to
specify a pair\_coeff command with I != J arguments for this style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_pedone:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{pedone} computes the \sphinxstylestrong{non\sphinxhyphen{}Coulomb} interactions of the Pedone
(or PMMCS) potential {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pedone:pedone}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pedone)}}}} which combines Coulomb
interactions, Morse potential, and repulsive \(r^{-12}\)
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones terms (see below).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pedone} pair style is meant
to be used in addition to a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Coulomb pair style}}}} via
pair style {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid/overlay}}}} (see example above).
Using \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{could/dsf} (for solids) is recommended.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The full Pedone potential function from {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_pedone:pedone}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Pedone)}}}} for each
pair of atoms is:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E =  \frac{C q_i q_j}{\epsilon  r}
    + D_0 \left[ e^{- 2 \alpha (r - r_0)} - 2 e^{- \alpha (r - r_0)} \right]
    + \frac{B_0}{r^{12}} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff and \(C\) is a conversion factor that is
specific to the choice of {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} so that the entire
Coulomb term is in energy units with \(q_i\) and \(q_j\) as the
assigned charges in multiples of the elementary charge.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for the selected pairs of
atom types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the
example above:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(D_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (1/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_0\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global \sphinxstyleemphasis{pedone}
cutoff is used.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_peri:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The peridynamic pair styles implement material models that can be used
at the mesoscopic and macroscopic scales.  See \sphinxhref{PDF/PDLammps\_overview.pdf}{this document} for an overview of LAMMPS commands for
Peridynamics modeling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/pmb} implements the Peridynamic bond\sphinxhyphen{}based prototype
microelastic brittle (PMB) model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/lps} implements the Peridynamic state\sphinxhyphen{}based linear
peridynamic solid (LPS) model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/ves} implements the Peridynamic state\sphinxhyphen{}based linear
peridynamic viscoelastic solid (VES) model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/eps} implements the Peridynamic state\sphinxhyphen{}based elastic\sphinxhyphen{}plastic
solid (EPS) model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The canonical papers on Peridynamics are {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_peri:silling2000}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Silling 2000)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_peri:silling2007}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Silling 2007)}}}}.  The
implementation of Peridynamics in LAMMPS is described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_peri:parks}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Parks)}}}}.  Also see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_peri::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Peridynamics Howto}}}} for more
details about its implementation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The peridynamic VES and EPS models in PDLAMMPS were implemented by
R. Rahman and J. T. Foster at University of Texas at San Antonio.  The
original VES formulation is described in “(Mitchell2011)” and the
original EPS formulation is in “(Mitchell2011a)”.  Additional PDF docs
that describe the VES and EPS implementations are include in the LAMMPS
distribution in \sphinxhref{PDF/PDLammps\_VES.pdf}{doc/PDF/PDLammps\_VES.pdf} and
\sphinxhref{PDF/PDLammps\_EPS.pdf}{doc/PDF/PDLammps\_EPS.pdf}.  For questions
regarding the VES and EPS models in LAMMPS you can contact R. Rahman
(rezwanur.rahman at utsa.edu).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above,
or in the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by
mixing as described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/pmb} style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
c (energy/distance/volume\textasciicircum{}2 units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
horizon (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
s00 (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (unitless)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
C is the effectively a spring constant for Peridynamic bonds, the
horizon is a cutoff distance for truncating interactions, and s00 and
\(\alpha\) are used as a bond breaking criteria.  The units of c are
such that c/distance = stiffness/volume\textasciicircum{}2, where stiffness is
energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2 and volume is distance\textasciicircum{}3.  See the users guide for
more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/lps} style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K (force/area units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
G (force/area units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
horizon (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
s00 (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (unitless)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
K is the bulk modulus and G is the shear modulus.  The horizon is a
cutoff distance for truncating interactions, and s00 and \(\alpha\)
are used as a bond breaking criteria. See the users guide for more
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/ves} style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K (force/area units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
G (force/area units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
horizon (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
s00 (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
m\_lambdai (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
m\_taubi (unitless)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
K is the bulk modulus and G is the shear modulus. The horizon is a
cutoff distance for truncating interactions, and s00 and \(\alpha\)
are used as a bond breaking criteria. m\_lambdai and m\_taubi are the
viscoelastic relaxation parameter and time constant,
respectively. m\_lambdai varies within zero to one. For very small values
of m\_lambdai the viscoelastic model responds very similar to a linear
elastic model. For details please see the description in
“(Mitchell2011)”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{peri/eps} style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
K (force/area units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
G (force/area units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
horizon (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
s00 (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
m\_yield\_stress (force/area units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
K is the bulk modulus and G is the shear modulus. The horizon is a
cutoff distance and s00 and \(\alpha\) are used as a bond breaking
criteria.  m\_yield\_stress is the yield stress of the material. For
details please see the description in “(Mitchell2011a)”.

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_peri:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles do not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and tail options are not
relevant for these pair styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  They do not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.
