\section{pair\_style reaxff command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:pair-style-reaxff-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cfile = NULL or name of a control file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended
\begin{sphinxalltt}
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{checkqeq} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lgvdw} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{safezone} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mincap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{minhbonds} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tabulate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{list/blocking}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{checkqeq} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = whether or not to require qeq/reaxff or acks2/reaxff fix
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{enobonds} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = whether or not to tally energy of atoms with no bonds
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{lgvdw} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = whether or not to use a low gradient vdW correction
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{safezone} = factor used for array allocation
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{mincap} = minimum size for array allocation
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{minhbonds} = minimum size use for storing hydrogen bonds
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{tabulate} value = size of interpolation table for Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones and Coulomb interactions
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{list/blocking} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = whether or not to use "blocking" scheme for bond list build
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{controlfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{checkqeq}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lgvdw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{safezone}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mincap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ffield.reax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} computes the ReaxFF potential of van Duin, Goddard
and co\sphinxhyphen{}workers.  ReaxFF uses distance\sphinxhyphen{}dependent bond\sphinxhyphen{}order functions to
represent the contributions of chemical bonding to the potential
energy.  There is more than one version of ReaxFF.  The version
implemented in LAMMPS uses the functional forms documented in the
supplemental information of the following paper:
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff:chenoweth-20082}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Chenoweth et al., 2008)}}}} and matches the
version of the reference ReaxFF implementation from Summer 2010.  For
more technical details about the implementation of ReaxFF in pair style
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff}, see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff:aktulga}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Aktulga)}}}} paper. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} style
was initially implemented as a stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone C code and is now converted
to C++ and integrated into LAMMPS as a package.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff/kk} style is a Kokkos version of the ReaxFF potential that
is derived from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} style.  The Kokkos version can run on GPUs
and can also use OpenMP multithreading.  For more information about the
Kokkos package, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{Packages_details::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Packages details}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_kokkos::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Speed kokkos}}}} doc pages.  One important
consideration when using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff/kk} style is the choice of either
half or full neighbor lists. This setting can be changed using the
Kokkos {\hyperref[\detokenize{package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{package}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} style differs from the (obsolete) “pair\_style reax”
command in the implementation details.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{reax} style was a
Fortran library, linked to LAMMPS.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{reax} style has been removed
from LAMMPS after the 12 December 2018 version.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS provides several different versions of ffield.reax in its
potentials dir, each called potentials/ffield.reax.label.  These are
documented in potentials/README.reax.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of these files is identical to that used originally by van
Duin.  We have tested the accuracy of \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style reaxff} potential
against the original ReaxFF code for the systems mentioned above.  You
can use other ffield files for specific chemical systems that may be
available elsewhere (but note that their accuracy may not have been
tested).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We do not distribute a wide variety of ReaxFF force field files
with LAMMPS.  Adri van Duin’s group at PSU is the central repository
for this kind of data as they are continuously deriving and updating
parameterizations for different classes of materials.  You can submit
a contact request at the Materials Computation Center (MCC) website
\sphinxurl{https://www.mri.psu.edu/materials-computation-center/connect-mcc},
describing the material(s) you are interested in modeling with ReaxFF.
They can tell you what is currently available or what it would take to
create a suitable ReaxFF parameterization.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfile} setting can be specified as NULL, in which case default
settings are used. A control file can be specified which defines values
of control variables. Some control variables are global parameters for
the ReaxFF potential. Others define certain performance and output
settings.  Each line in the control file specifies the value for a
control variable.  The format of the control file is described below.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LAMMPS default values for the ReaxFF global parameters
correspond to those used by Adri van Duin’s stand\sphinxhyphen{}alone serial
code.  If these are changed by setting control variables in the
control file, the results from LAMMPS and the serial code will
not agree.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples using \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style reaxff} are provided in the examples/reax
directory and its subdirectories.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of this pair style requires using an {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}
that includes a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom charge property \sphinxstyleemphasis{or} using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom q}}}}.  Charges can be set
via {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{set}}}}.  Using an initial
charge that is close to the result of charge equilibration will speed
up that process.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ReaxFF parameter files provided were created using a charge
equilibration (QEq) model for handling the electrostatic interactions.
Therefore, by default, LAMMPS requires that either the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/reaxff}}}} or the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/shielded}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix acks2/reaxff}}}}
command be used with
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style reaxff} when simulating a ReaxFF model, to equilibrate
the charges each timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{checkqeq} with the value \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} turns off the check
for the QEq fixes, allowing a simulation to be run without charge
equilibration. In this case, the static charges you assign to each
atom will be used for computing the electrostatic interactions in
the system. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/reaxff}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_qeq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix qeq/shielded}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_acks2_reaxff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix acks2/reaxff}}}}
command documentation for more details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{lgvdw} with the value \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} turns on the
low\sphinxhyphen{}gradient correction of ReaxFF for long\sphinxhyphen{}range London Dispersion,
as described in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_reaxff:liu-2011}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Liu)}}}} paper. The bundled force
field file \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield.reax.lg} is designed for this correction, and is
trained for several energetic materials (see “Liu”). When using \sphinxstyleemphasis{lgvdw yes},
the recommended value for parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{thb} is 0.01, which can be set in the
control file.  Note: Force field files are different for the original
or lg corrected pair styles, using the wrong ffield file generates an
error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the optional keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{enobonds} with the value \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the energy
of atoms with no bonds (i.e. isolated atoms) is included in the total
potential energy and the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom energy of that atom.  If the value
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no} is specified then the energy of atoms with no bonds is set to
zero.  The latter behavior is usual not desired, as it causes
discontinuities in the potential energy when the bonding of an atom
drops to zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional keywords \sphinxstyleemphasis{safezone}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mincap}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{minhbonds} are used
for allocating reaxff arrays.  Increasing these values can avoid memory
problems, such as segmentation faults and bondchk failed errors, that
could occur under certain conditions. These keywords are not used by
the Kokkos version, which instead uses a more robust memory allocation
scheme that checks if the sizes of the arrays have been exceeded and
automatically allocates more memory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{tabulate} controls the size of interpolation table for
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones and Coulomb interactions. Tabulation may also be set in the
control file (see below). If tabulation is set in both the input script and the
control file, the value in the control file will be ignored. A size of 10000 is
typically used for the interpolation table. A value of 0 means no tabulation
will be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{list/blocking} is only supported by the Kokkos version of
ReaxFF and ignored otherwise. Setting the value to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} enables the
“blocking” scheme (dynamically building interaction lists) for the
ReaxFF bond neighbor list. This reduces the number of empty
interactions and can improve performance in some cases (e.g. large
number of atoms/GPU on AMD hardware). It is also enabled by default
when running the CPU with Kokkos.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermo variable \sphinxstyleemphasis{evdwl} stores the sum of all the ReaxFF potential
energy contributions, with the exception of the Coulombic and charge
equilibration contributions which are stored in the thermo variable
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecoul}.  The output of these quantities is controlled by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style tallies a breakdown of the total ReaxFF potential
energy into sub\sphinxhyphen{}categories, which can be accessed via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pair::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pair}}}} command as a vector of values of length 14.
The 14 values correspond to the following sub\sphinxhyphen{}categories (the variable
names in italics match those used in the original FORTRAN ReaxFF
code):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{eb} = bond energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ea} = atom energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{elp} = lone\sphinxhyphen{}pair energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{emol} = molecule energy (always 0.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ev} = valence angle energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{epen} = double\sphinxhyphen{}bond valence angle penalty

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ecoa} = valence angle conjugation energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ehb} = hydrogen bond energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{et} = torsion energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{eco} = conjugation energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ew} = van der Waals energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ep} = Coulomb energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{efi} = electric field energy (always 0.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{eqeq} = charge equilibration energy

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To print these quantities to the log file (with descriptive column
headings) the following commands could be included in an input script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{reax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reaxff}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{eb}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}reax[1]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ea}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}reax[2]}
\PYG{n}{[...]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{eqeq}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}reax[14]}
\PYG{k}{thermo\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{epair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}eb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ea}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[...]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}eqeq}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} style which
specifies a ReaxFF potential file with parameters for all needed
elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N
additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command,
where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N indices = ReaxFF elements

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filename is the ReaxFF potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the ReaxFF potential file, near the top, after the general
parameters, is the atomic parameters section that contains element
names, each with a couple dozen numeric parameters.  If there are M
elements specified in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield} file, think of these as numbered 1
to M. Each of the N indices you specify for the N atom types of LAMMPS
atoms must be an integer from 1 to M.  Atoms with LAMMPS type 1 will
be mapped to whatever element you specify as the first index value,
etc.  If a mapping value is specified as NULL, the mapping is not
performed.  This can be used when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaxff} style is used as part
of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values are placeholders for atom
types that will be used with other potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, say your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atom types and the
elements are ordered as C, H, O, N in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield} file.  If you want
the LAMMPS atom type 1 and 2 to be C, type 3 to be N, and type 4 to be
H, you would use the following pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ffield.reax}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Control file}
\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:control-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a line in the control file is as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
variable\PYGZus{}name value
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and it may be followed by an “!” character and a trailing comment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the value of a control variable is not specified, then default
values are used.  What follows is the list of variables along with a
brief description of their use and default values.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{simulation\_name}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output files produced by \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style reaxff} carry
this name + extensions specific to their contents.  Partial energies
are reported with a “.pot” extension, while the trajectory file has
“.trj” extension.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{tabulate\_long\_range}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To improve performance, long range interactions can optionally be
tabulated (0 means no tabulation). Value of this variable denotes the
size of the long range interaction table.  The range from 0 to long
range cutoff (defined in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ffield} file) is divided into
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tabulate\_long\_range} points.  Then at the start of simulation, we
fill in the entries of the long range interaction table by computing
the energies and forces resulting from van der Waals and Coulomb
interactions between every possible atom type pairs present in the
input system.  During the simulation we consult to the long range
interaction table to estimate the energy and forces between a pair of
atoms. Linear interpolation is used for estimation. (default value = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{energy\_update\_freq}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Denotes the frequency (in number of steps) of writes into the partial
energies file. (default value = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{nbrhood\_cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Denotes the near neighbors cutoff (in Angstroms)
regarding the bonded interactions. (default value = 5.0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{hbond\_cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Denotes the cutoff distance (in Angstroms) for hydrogen
bond interactions.(default value = 7.5. A value of 0.0 turns off
hydrogen bonds)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond\_graph\_cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
is the threshold used in determining what is a
physical bond, what is not. Bonds and angles reported in the
trajectory file rely on this cutoff. (default value = 0.3)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{thb\_cutoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff value for the strength of bonds to be considered in
three body interactions. (default value = 0.001)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{thb\_cutoff\_sq}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff value for the strength of bond order products
to be considered in three body interactions. (default value = 0.00001)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{write\_freq}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Frequency of writes into the trajectory file. (default value = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{traj\_title}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Title of the trajectory \sphinxhyphen{} not the name of the trajectory file.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 means print only atomic positions + charge (default = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_forces}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 adds net forces to atom lines in the trajectory file (default = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_velocities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 adds atomic velocities to atoms line (default = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond\_info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 prints bonds in the trajectory file (default = 0)

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle\_info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
1 prints angles in the trajectory file (default = 0)

\end{description}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_reaxff:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mix, shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}},
since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,

\subsection{Restrictions}

if LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ReaxFF potential files provided with LAMMPS in the potentials

the ReaxFF pair style with any LAMMPS units, but you would need to
create your own potential file with coefficients listed in the
appropriate units if your simulation does not use “real” units.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rebomos:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Apr2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rebomos} pair style computes the interactions between molybdenum
and sulfur atoms {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_rebomos:stewart}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Stewart)}}}} utilizing an adaptive
interatomic reactive empirical bond order potential that is similar in
form to the AIREBO potential {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_rebomos:stuart2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Stuart)}}}}.  The potential
is based on an earlier parameterizations for \(\text{MoS}_2\)
developed by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_rebomos:liang}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Liang)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The REBOMoS potential consists of two terms:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = \frac{1}{2} \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i}
\left[ E^{\text{REBO}}_{ij} + E^{\text{LJ}}_{ij}  \right] \\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(E^{\text{REBO}}\) term describes the covalently bonded
interactions between Mo and S atoms while the \(E^{\text{LJ}}\) term
describes longer range dispersion forces between layers.  A cubic spline
function is applied to smoothly switch between covalent bonding at short
distances to dispersion interactions at longer distances. This allows
the model to capture bond formation and breaking events which may occur
between adjacent MoS2 layers, edges, defects, and more.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rebomos} pair style
which specifies an REBOMoS potential file with parameters for Mo and S.
These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N additional
arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command, where N is the
number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N\) element names = mapping of REBOMoS elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, if your LAMMPS simulation has three atom types and you want
the first two to be Mo, and the third to be S, you would use the following
pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{MoS.rebomos}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Mo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Mo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{S}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first two Mo arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1 and 2 to the Mo
element in the REBOMoS file.  The final S argument maps LAMMPS atom type
3 to the S element in the REBOMoS file.  If a mapping value is specified
as NULL, the mapping is not performed.  This can be used when a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rebomos} potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The
NULL values are placeholders for atom types that will be used with other
potentials.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar

They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rebomos:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mix, shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write their information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair styles can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rebomos:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MANYBODY package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair potentials require the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be
“on” for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MoS.rebomos potential file provided with LAMMPS (see the potentials
directory) is parameterized for metal {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  You can use
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{rebomos} pair style with any LAMMPS units setting, but you would
need to create your own REBOMoS potential file with coefficients listed
in the appropriate units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pair style provided here \sphinxstylestrong{only} supports potential files parameterized
for the elements molybdenum and sulfur (designated with “Mo” and “S” in the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff} command.  Using potential files for other elements will trigger
an error.

\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:pair-style-resquared-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared::doc}}

\subsection{Examples}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{resquared} computes the RE\sphinxhyphen{}squared anisotropic interaction
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_resquared:everaers3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Everaers)}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_resquared:babadi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Babadi)}}}} between pairs of
ellipsoidal and/or spherical Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones particles.  For ellipsoidal
interactions, the potential considers the ellipsoid as being comprised
of small spheres of size \(\sigma\).  LJ particles are a single sphere of
size \(\sigma\).  The distinction is made to allow the pair style to make
efficient calculations of ellipsoid/solvent interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Details for the equations used are given in the references below and
in \sphinxhref{PDF/pair\_resquared\_extra.pdf}{this supplementary document}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of this pair style requires the NVE, NVT, or NPT fixes with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{asphere} extension (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/asphere}}}}) in
order to integrate particle rotation.  Additionally, {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}} should be used since it defines the
rotational state and the size and shape of each ellipsoidal particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A12 = Energy Prefactor/Hamaker constant (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) = atomic interaction diameter (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{i,a}\) = relative well depth of type I for side\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}side interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{i,b}\) = relative well depth of type I for face\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}face interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{i,c}\) = relative well depth of type I for end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{j,a}\) = relative well depth of type J for side\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}side interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{j,b}\) = relative well depth of type J for face\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}face interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_{j,c}\) = relative well depth of type J for end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters used depend on the type of the interacting particles,
i.e. ellipsoids or LJ spheres.  The type of a particle is determined
by the diameters specified for its 3 shape parameters.  If all 3 shape
parameters = 0.0, then the particle is treated as an LJ sphere.  The
\(\epsilon_{i,*}\) or \(\epsilon_{j,*}\) parameters are ignored
for LJ spheres.  If
the 3 shape parameters are \textgreater{} 0.0, then the particle is treated as an
ellipsoid (even if the 3 parameters are equal to each other).

\sphinxAtStartPar
A12 specifies the energy prefactor which depends on the types of the
two interacting particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For ellipsoid/ellipsoid interactions, the interaction is computed by
the formulas in the supplementary document referenced above.  A12 is
the Hamaker constant as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_resquared:everaers3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Everaers)}}}}. In LJ
units:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}A_{12} = 4\pi^2\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}}(\rho\sigma^3)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\rho\) gives the number density of the spherical particles
composing the ellipsoids and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}}\) determines
the interaction strength of the spherical particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For ellipsoid/LJ sphere interactions, the interaction is also computed
by the formulas in the supplementary document referenced above.  A12
has a modified form (see \sphinxhref{PDF/pair\_resquared\_extra.pdf}{here} for
details):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}A_{12} = 4\pi^2\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}}(\rho\sigma^3)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For ellipsoid/LJ sphere interactions, a correction to the distance\sphinxhyphen{}
of\sphinxhyphen{}closest approach equation has been implemented to reduce the error
from two particles of disparate sizes; see \sphinxhref{PDF/pair\_resquared\_extra.pdf}{this supplementary document}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For LJ sphere/LJ sphere interactions, the interaction is computed
using the standard Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones formula, which is much cheaper to
compute than the ellipsoidal formulas.  A12 is used as epsilon in the
standard LJ formula:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}A_{12} = \epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and the specified \(\sigma\) is used as the \(\sigma\) in the
standard LJ formula.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When one of both of the interacting particles are ellipsoids, then
\(\sigma\) specifies the diameter of the continuous distribution of
constituent particles within each ellipsoid used to model the RE\sphinxhyphen{}squared
potential.  Note that this is a different meaning for \(\sigma\)
than the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gayberne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gayberne}}}} potential uses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(\epsilon_i\) and \(\epsilon_j\) coefficients are defined
for atom types, not for pairs of atom types.  Thus, in a series of
pair\_coeff commands, they only need to be specified once for each atom
type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically, if any of \(\epsilon_{i,a}\), \(\epsilon_{i,b}\),
\(\epsilon_{i,c}\) are non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, the three values are assigned to
atom type I.  If all the \(\epsilon_i\) values are zero, they are
ignored.  If any of \(\epsilon_{j,a}\), \(\epsilon_{j,b}\),
\(\epsilon_{j,c}\) are non\sphinxhyphen{}zero, the three values are assigned to
atom type J.  If all three \(\epsilon_i\) values are zero, they are
ignored.  Thus the typical way to define the \(\epsilon_i\) and
\(\epsilon_j\) coefficients is to list their values in “pair\_coeff
I J” commands when I = J, but set them to 0.0 when I != J.  If you do
list them when I != J, you should ensure they are consistent with their
values in other pair\_coeff commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that if this potential is being used as a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}}, and there is no “pair\_coeff I I”
setting made for RE\sphinxhyphen{}squared for a particular type I (because I\sphinxhyphen{}I
interactions are computed by another hybrid pair potential), then you
still need to ensure the epsilon a,b,c coefficients are assigned to
that type in a “pair\_coeff I J” command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For large uniform molecules it has been shown that the \(\epsilon_{*,*}\)
energy parameters are approximately representable in terms of local
contact curvatures {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_resquared:everaers3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Everaers)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\epsilon_a = \sigma \cdot { \frac{a}{ b \cdot c } }; \epsilon_b =
\sigma \cdot { \frac{b}{ a \cdot c } }; \epsilon_c = \sigma \cdot {
\frac{c}{ a \cdot b } }\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where a, b, and c give the particle diameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global cutoff
specified in the pair\_style command is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance can be mixed, but only for sphere pairs.  The
default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for
details.  Other type pairs cannot be mixed, due to the different
meanings of the energy prefactors used to calculate the interactions
and the implicit dependence of the ellipsoid\sphinxhyphen{}sphere interaction on the
equation for the Hamaker constant presented here.  Mixing of sigma and
epsilon followed by calculation of the energy prefactors using the
equations above is recommended.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones portion of the pair
interaction, but only for sphere\sphinxhyphen{}sphere interactions.  There is no
shifting performed for ellipsoidal interactions due to the anisotropic
dependence of the interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style command}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires that atoms be ellipsoids as defined by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Particles acted on by the potential can be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size aspherical or
spherical particles, or point particles.  Spherical particles have all
3 of their shape parameters equal to each other.  Point particles have
all 3 of their shape parameters equal to 0.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The distance\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}closest\sphinxhyphen{}approach approximation used by LAMMPS becomes
less accurate when high\sphinxhyphen{}aspect ratio ellipsoids are used.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_resquared:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/asphere}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/asphere}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gayberne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gayberne}}}}


\subsection{Default}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstylestrong{(Everaers)} Everaers and Ejtehadi, Phys Rev E, 67, 041710 (2003).

\index{pair\_style rheo@\spxentry{pair\_style rheo}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style rheo command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:pair-style-rheo-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for kernel (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended to args

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/damp} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{artificial/visc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/means}

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/damp} args = density damping prefactor \(\xi\)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{artificial/visc} args = artificial viscosity prefactor \(\zeta\)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/means} args = none
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rho}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{damp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{artificial}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{visc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{rheo} computes pressure and viscous forces between particles
in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rheo package}}}}. If thermal evolution is turned
on in {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}}, then the pair style also calculates
heat exchanged between particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{artificial/viscosity} keyword is used to specify the magnitude
\(\zeta\) of an optional artificial viscosity contribution to forces.
This factor can help stabilize simulations by smoothing out small length
scale variations in velocity fields. Artificial viscous forces typically
are only exchanged by fluid particles. However, if interfaces are not
reconstructed in fix rheo, fluid particles will also exchange artificial
viscous forces with solid particles to improve stability.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rho/damp} keyword is used to specify the magnitude \(\xi\) of
an optional pairwise damping term between the density of particles. This
factor can help stabilize simulations by smoothing out small length
scale variations in density fields. However, in systems that develop
a density gradient in equilibrium (e.g. in a hydrostatic column underlying
gravity), this option may be inappropriate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If particles have different viscosities or conductivities, the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/means} keyword changes how they are averaged before calculating
pairwise forces or heat exchanges. By default, an arithmetic averaged is
used, however, a harmonic mean may improve stability in systems with multiple
fluid phases with large disparities in viscosities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
No coefficients are defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style does not write information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.
Thus, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the RHEO package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_pressure::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/pressure}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_viscosity::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/viscosity}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_rheo_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute rheo/property/atom}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Density damping and artificial viscous forces are not calculated.
Arithmetic means are used for mixing particle properties.

\index{pair\_style rheo/solid@\spxentry{pair\_style rheo/solid}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style rheo/solid command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:pair-style-rheo-solid-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{solid}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{solid}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{rheo/solid} is effectively a copy of pair style
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bpm/spring}}}} except it only applies forces
between solid RHEO particles, determined by checking the status of
each pair of neighboring particles before calculating forces.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style computes pairwise forces with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F = k (r - r_c)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k\) is a stiffness and \(r_c\) is the cutoff length.
An additional damping force is also applied to interacting
particles. The force is proportional to the difference in the
normal velocity of particles
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_D = - \gamma w (\hat{r} \bullet \vec{v})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\gamma\) is the damping strength, \(\hat{r}\) is the
displacement normal vector, \(\vec{v}\) is the velocity difference
between the two particles, and \(w\) is a smoothing factor.
This smoothing factor is constructed such that damping forces go to zero
as particles come out of contact to avoid discontinuities. It is
given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}w = 1.0 - \left( \frac{r}{r_c} \right)^8 .\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k\)             (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\)           (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)        (force/velocity units)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the A coefficient and cutoff
distance for this pair style can be mixed.  A is always mixed via a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric} rule.  The cutoff is mixed according to the pair\_modify
mix value.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the
“pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option, since the pair interaction goes to 0.0 at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and tail options are not
relevant for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the RHEO package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_thermal::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/thermal}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_bpm_spring::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair bpm/spring}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_rheo_solid:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{pair\_style saip/metal@\spxentry{pair\_style saip/metal}}\ignorespaces 
\index{pair\_style saip/metal/opt@\spxentry{pair\_style saip/metal/opt}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style saip/metal command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:pair-style-saip-metal-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variant: \sphinxstyleemphasis{saip/metal/opt}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saip}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{metal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tap\PYGZus{}flag}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tap\_flag = 0/1 to turn off/on the taper function

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saip}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{metal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saip}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{metal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CHAu.ILP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Au}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saip}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{metal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eam}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Au\PYGZus{}u3.eam}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Au}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rebo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CH.rebo}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{NULL}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saip}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{metal}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{CHAu.ILP}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Au}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 17Feb2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{saip/metal} style computes the registry\sphinxhyphen{}dependent interlayer
potential (ILP) potential for hetero\sphinxhyphen{}junctions formed with hexagonal
2D materials and metal surfaces, as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_saip_metal:ouyang6}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouyang6)}}}}.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E  = & \frac{1}{2} \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} V_{ij} \\
V_{ij}  = & {\rm Tap}(r_{ij})\left \{ e^{-\alpha (r_{ij}/\beta -1)}
             \left [ \epsilon + f(\rho_{ij}) + f(\rho_{ji})\right ] -
              \frac{1}{1+e^{-d\left [ \left ( r_{ij}/\left (s_R \cdot r^{eff} \right ) \right )-1 \right ]}}
              \cdot \frac{C_6}{r^6_{ij}} \right \}\\
\rho_{ij}^2 = & r_{ij}^2 - ({\bf r}_{ij} \cdot {\bf n}_i)^2 \\
\rho_{ji}^2  = & r_{ij}^2 - ({\bf r}_{ij} \cdot {\bf n}_j)^2 \\
f(\rho)  = &  C e^{ -( \rho / \delta )^2 } \\
{\rm Tap}(r_{ij})  = & 20\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^7 -
                        70\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^6 +
                        84\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^5 -
                        35\left ( \frac{r_{ij}}{R_{cut}} \right )^4 + 1\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where \(\mathrm{Tap}(r_{ij})\) is the taper function which provides
a continuous cutoff (up to third derivative) for interatomic separations
larger than \(r_c\) {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ilp_graphene_hbn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style ilp\_graphene\_hbn}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important to include all the pairs to build the neighbor list for
calculating the normals.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To account for the isotropic nature of the isolated gold atom
electron cloud, their corresponding normal vectors (\sphinxtitleref{\{bf n\}\_i}) are
assumed to lie along the interatomic vector \sphinxtitleref{\{bf r\}\_ij}. Notably, this
assumption is suitable for many bulk material surfaces, for
example, for systems possessing s\sphinxhyphen{}type valence orbitals or
metallic surfaces, whose valence electrons are mostly
delocalized, such that their Pauli repulsion with the electrons
of adjacent surfaces are isotropic. Caution should be used in
the case of very small gold contacts, for example, nano\sphinxhyphen{}clusters,
where edge effects may become relevant.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter file (e.g. CHAu.ILP), is intended for use with \sphinxstyleemphasis{metal}
{\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}, with energies in meV. Two additional parameters,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{S}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcut} are included in the parameter file. \sphinxstyleemphasis{S} is designed to
facilitate scaling of energies. \sphinxstyleemphasis{rcut} is designed to build the neighbor
list for calculating the normals for each atom pair.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters presented in the parameter file (e.g. BNCH.ILP),
are fitted with taper function by setting the cutoff equal to 16.0
Angstrom.  Using different cutoff or taper function should be careful.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential must be used in combination with hybrid/overlay.
Other interactions can be set to zero using pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style tallies a breakdown of the total interlayer potential
energy into sub\sphinxhyphen{}categories, which can be accessed via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_pair::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute pair}}}} command as a vector of values of length 2.
The 2 values correspond to the following sub\sphinxhyphen{}categories:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{E\_vdW} = vdW (attractive) energy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{E\_Rep} = Repulsive energy

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To print these quantities to the log file (with descriptive column
headings) the following commands could be included in an input script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{saip}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{metal}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Evdw}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}0[1]}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{Erep}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}0[2]}

This pair style does not write their information to binary restart

\sphinxAtStartPar

interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CHAu.ILP potential file provided with LAMMPS (see the potentials

custom CHAu.ILP potential file with coefficients listed in the appropriate

\index{pair\_style sdpd/taitwater/isothermal@\spxentry{pair\_style sdpd/taitwater/isothermal}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style sdpd/taitwater/isothermal command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:pair-style-sdpd-taitwater-isothermal-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sdpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{taitwater}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{isothermal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{temperature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{viscosity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seed}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temperature = temperature of the fluid (temperature units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
viscosity = dynamic viscosity of the fluid (mass*distance/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
seed = random number generator seed (positive integer, optional)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sdpd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{taitwater}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{isothermal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{28681}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1430.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The sdpd/taitwater/isothermal style computes forces between mesoscopic
particles according to the Smoothed Dissipative Particle Dynamics model
described in this paper by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:espanol-revenga}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Espanol and Revenga)}}}} under
the following assumptions:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The temperature is constant and uniform.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The shear viscosity is constant and uniform.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The volume viscosity is negligible before the shear viscosity.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Boltzmann constant is negligible before the heat capacity of a
single mesoscopic particle of fluid.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third assumption is true for water in nearly incompressible flows.
The fourth holds true for water for any reasonable size one can
imagine for a mesoscopic particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pressure forces between particles will be computed according to
Tait’s equation of state:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p = B \left[(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0})^{\gamma} - 1\right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\gamma = 7\) and \(B = c_0^2 \rho_0 / \gamma\), with
\(\rho_0\) being the reference density and \(c_0\) the reference
speed of sound.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The laminar viscosity and the random forces will be computed according
to formulas described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:espanol-revenga}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Espanol and Revenga)}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_brownian::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{brownian}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dpd}}}} styles, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting for
pairwise interactions needs to be on when running LAMMPS in parallel
if you want to ensure linear momentum conservation. Otherwise random
forces generated for pairs straddling processor boundary will not be
equal and opposite.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual random seed used will be a mix of what you specify
and other parameters like the MPI ranks. This is to ensure that
different MPI tasks have distinct seeds.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\rho_0\) reference density (mass/volume units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(c_0\) reference soundspeed (distance/time units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
h kernel function cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients for all
I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style does not write information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.  Thus, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and
pair\_coeff commands in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the DPD\sphinxhyphen{}SMOOTH package.  It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sph_rhosum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair sph/rhosum}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sph_taitwater::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair sph/taitwater}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sdpd_taitwater_isothermal:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default seed is 0 (before mixing).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{pair\_style smatb command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:pair-style-smatb-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb::doc}}

\section{pair\_style smatb/single command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:pair-style-smatb-single-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{smatb} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{smatb/single}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = none

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smatb}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.88}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.35}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.178}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.210}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.818}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.07293506}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.9883063257983666}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smatb}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{single}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.88}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.35}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.178}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.210}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.818}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.07293506}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.9883063257983666}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{smatb} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{smatb/single} styles compute the Second Moment
Approximation to the Tight Binding {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_smatb:cyrot}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Cyrot)}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_smatb:gupta}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Gupta)}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_smatb:rosato}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Rosato)}}}}, given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_{i}  = \sum_{j,R_{ij}\leq R_{c}} \alpha(R_{ij}) - \sqrt{\sum_{j,R_{ij}\leq R_{c}}\Xi^2(R_{ij})}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_{ij}\) is the distance between the atom \(i\) and \(j\).
And the two functions \(\alpha\left(r\right)\) and \(\Xi\left(r\right)\) are:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\alpha\left(r\right)=\left\lbrace\begin{array}{ll}
   A e^{-p \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}-1\right)} & r < R_{sc}\\
   a_3\left(r-R_{c}\right)^3+a_4\left(r-R_{c}\right)^4
   +a_5\left(r-R_{c}\right)^5& R_{sc} < r < R_{c}
   \end{array}
   \right.\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Xi\left(r\right)=\left\lbrace\begin{array}{ll}
\xi e^{-q \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}-1\right)} & r < R_{sc}\\
x_3\left(r-R_{c}\right)^3+x_4\left(r-R_{c}\right)^4
+x_5\left(r-R_{c}\right)^5& R_{sc} < r < R_{c}
\end{array}
\right.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The polynomial coefficients \(a_3\), \(a_4\), \(a_5\),
\(x_3\), \(x_4\), \(x_5\) are computed by LAMMPS: the two
exponential terms and their first and second derivatives are smoothly
reduced to zero, from the inner cutoff \(R_{sc}\) to the outer
cutoff \(R_{c}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{smatb/single} style is an optimization when using only a single atom type.


\subsection{Coefficients}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:coefficients}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_{0}\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(p\) (dimensionless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(q\) (dimensionless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\xi\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_{cs}\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_{c}\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that: \(R_{0}\) is the nearest neighbor distance, usually coincides
with the diameter of the atoms

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style}}}} command for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:mixing-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J the coefficients are not automatically mixed.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the SMTBQ package and are only enabled
if LAMMPS is built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles require the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on” for pair interactions.

\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:related-commands}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:cyrot}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Cyrot)}  Cyrot\sphinxhyphen{}Lackmann and Ducastelle, Phys Rev. B, 4, 2406\sphinxhyphen{}2412 (1971).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_smatb:gupta}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Gupta)} Gupta ,Phys Rev. B, 23, 6265\sphinxhyphen{}6270 (1981).

\section{pair\_style smd/hertz command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:pair-style-smd-hertz-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hertz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scale\PYGZus{}factor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{hertz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{contact\PYGZus{}stiffness}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{smd/hertz} style calculates contact forces between SPH particles
belonging to different physical bodies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The contact forces are calculated using a Hertz potential, which
evaluates the overlap between two particles (whose spatial extents are
defined via its contact radius).  The effect is that a particles
cannot penetrate into each other.  The parameter \textless{}contact\_stiffness\textgreater{}
has units of pressure and should equal roughly one half of the Young’s
modulus (or bulk modulus in the case of fluids) of the material model
associated with the SPH particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale\_factor} can be used to scale the particles’
contact radii. This can be useful to control how close particles can
approach each other. Usually, \sphinxstyleemphasis{scale\_factor} =1.0.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No mixing is performed automatically.  Currently, no part of MACHDYN
supports restarting nor minimization.  rRESPA does not apply to this
pair style.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_hertz:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the MACHDYN package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_tlsph:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tlsph}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_tlsph:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tlsph}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_smd_tlsph:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{smd/tlsph} style computes particle interactions according to
continuum mechanics constitutive laws and a Total\sphinxhyphen{}Lagrangian
Smooth\sphinxhyphen{}Particle Hydrodynamics algorithm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is invoked with the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smd}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{tlsph}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{COMMON}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rho0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{E}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nu}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Q1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Q2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Cp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{END}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j} denote the \sphinxstyleemphasis{LAMMPS} particle types for which this
pair style is defined. Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j} must be equal, i.e., no
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tlsph} cross interactions between different particle types are
allowed.  In contrast to the usual \sphinxstyleemphasis{LAMMPS} \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair coeff} definitions,
which are given solely a number of floats and integers, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tlsph}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pair coeff} definition is organized using keywords. These keywords
mark the beginning of different sets of parameters for particle
properties, material constitutive models, and damage models. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair
coeff} line must be terminated with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{*END} keyword. The use the
line continuation operator \sphinxstyleemphasis{\&} is recommended. A typical invocation of
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{tlsph} for a solid body would consist of an equation of state for
computing the pressure (the diagonal components of the stress tensor),
and a material model to compute shear stresses (the off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal
components of the stress tensor). Damage and failure models can also
be added.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please see the \sphinxhref{PDF/MACHDYN\_LAMMPS\_userguide.pdf}{SMD user guide} for a
complete listing of the possible keywords and material models.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

No mixing is performed automatically.  Currently, no part of MACHDYN
supports restarting nor minimization.  rRESPA does not apply to this
pair style.
