\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{biquadratic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.01}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.9}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{19}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_exchange:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange} computes the exchange interaction between
pairs of magnetic spins:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}H_{ex} = -\sum_{i,j}^N J_{ij} (r_{ij}) \,\vec{s}_i \cdot \vec{s}_j\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\vec{s}_i\) and \(\vec{s}_j\) are two unit vectors representing
the magnetic spins of two particles (usually atoms), and
\(r_{ij} = \vert \vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j \vert\) is the inter\sphinxhyphen{}atomic distance
between those two particles. The summation is over pairs of nearest neighbors.
\(J(r_{ij})\) is a function defining the intensity and the sign of the
exchange interaction for different neighboring shells.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange/biquadratic} computes a biquadratic exchange interaction
between pairs of magnetic spins:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}H_{bi} = -\sum_{i, j}^{N} {J}_{ij} \left(r_{ij} \right)\,
                   \vec{s}_{i}\cdot \vec{s}_{j}
                   -\sum_{i, j}^{N} {K}_{ij} \left(r_{ij} \right)\,
                   \left(\vec{s}_{i}\cdot
                   \vec{s}_{j}\right)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\vec{s}_i\),  \(\vec{s}_j\),  \(r_{ij}\) and
\(J(r_{ij})\) have the same definitions as above, and \(K(r_{ij})\) is
a second function, defining the intensity and the sign of the biquadratic term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interatomic dependence of \(J(r_{ij})\) and \(K(r_{ij})\) in both
interactions above is defined by the following function:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{f}\left( r_{ij} \right) = 4 a \left( \frac{r_{ij}}{d}  \right)^2
\left( 1 - b \left( \frac{r_{ij}}{d}  \right)^2 \right)
e^{-\left( \frac{r_{ij}}{d} \right)^2 }\Theta (R_c - r_{ij})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) are the three constant coefficients
defined in the associated “pair\_coeff” command, and \(R_c\) is the radius
cutoff associated to the pair interaction (see below for more explanations).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients \(a\), \(b\), and \(d\) need to be fitted so that
the function above matches with the value of the exchange interaction for the
\(N\) neighbor shells taken into account.
Examples and more explanations about this function and its parameterization
are reported in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spin_exchange:tranchida3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When a \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange/biquadratic} pair style is defined, six coefficients
(three for \(J(r_{ij})\), and three for \(K(r_{ij})\)) have to be
fitted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From this exchange interaction, each spin \(i\) will be submitted
to a magnetic torque \(\vec{\omega}_{i}\), and its associated atom can be
submitted to a force \(\vec{F}_{i}\) for spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice calculations (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/spin}}}}), such as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{\omega}_{i} = \frac{1}{\hbar} \sum_{j}^{Neighb} {J}
\left(r_{ij} \right)\,\vec{s}_{j}
~~{\rm and}~~
\vec{F}_{i} = \sum_{j}^{Neighb} \frac{\partial {J} \left(r_{ij} \right)}{
\partial r_{ij}} \left( \vec{s}_{i}\cdot \vec{s}_{j} \right) \vec{e}_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\hbar\) the Planck constant (in metal units), and \(\vec{e}_{ij}
= \frac{\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j}{\vert \vec{r}_i-\vec{r}_j \vert}\) the unit
vector between sites \(i\) and \(j\).
Equivalent forces and magnetic torques are generated for the biquadratic term
when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange/biquadratic} pair style is defined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
More details about the derivation of these torques/forces are reported in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spin_exchange:tranchida3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange/biquadratic} pair styles, the
following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, and set in the following order:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_c\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(a\)  (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(b\)  (adim parameter)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(d\)  (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange} pair style, and:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_c\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(a_j\)  (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(b_j\)  (adim parameter)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(d_j\)  (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(a_k\)  (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(b_k\)  (adim parameter)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(d_k\)  (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange/biquadratic} pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \(R_c\) is the radius cutoff of the considered exchange
interaction, and \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) are the three coefficients
performing the parameterization of the function \(J(r_{ij})\) defined
above (in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{biquadratic} style, \(a_j\), \(b_j\), \(d_j\) and
\(a_k\), \(b_k\), \(d_k\) are the coefficients of \(J(r_{ij})\)
and \(K(r_{ij})\) respectively).

\sphinxAtStartPar
None of those coefficients is optional. If not specified, the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange} pair style cannot be used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Offsetting magnetic forces and energies}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
For spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice simulation, it can be useful to offset the
mechanical forces and energies generated by the exchange
interaction.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} keyword allows to apply this offset.
By setting \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the energy definitions above are
replaced by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}H_{ex} = -\sum_{i,j}^N J_{ij} (r_{ij}) \,[ \vec{s}_i \cdot \vec{s}_j-1 ]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange} pair style, and:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}H_{bi} = -\sum_{i, j}^{N} {J}_{ij} \left(r_{ij} \right)\,
                   [ \vec{s}_{i}\cdot \vec{s}_{j} -1 ]
                   -\sum_{i, j}^{N} {K}_{ij} \left(r_{ij} \right)\,
                   [ \left(\vec{s}_{i}\cdot
                   \vec{s}_{j}\right)^2 -1]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/exchange/biquadratic} pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this offset only affects the calculation of the energy
and mechanical forces. It does not modify the calculation of the
precession vectors (and thus does no impact the purely magnetic
properties).
This ensures that when all spins are aligned, the magnetic energy
and the associated mechanical forces (and thus the pressure
generated by the magnetic potential) are null.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This offset term can be very important when calculations such as
equations of state (energy vs volume, or energy vs pressure) are
being performed. Indeed, setting the \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} term ensures that
at the ground state of the crystal and at the equilibrium magnetic
configuration (typically ferromagnetic), the pressure is null,
as expected.
Otherwise, magnetic forces could generate a residual pressure.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} option is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, no offset is applied
(also corresponding to the default option).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{pair\_style spin/magelec command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec:pair-style-spin-magelec-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spin}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{magelec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{magelec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.00109}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/me} computes a magneto\sphinxhyphen{}electric interaction between
pairs of magnetic spins. According to the derivation reported in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec:katsura1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Katsura)}}}}, this interaction is defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{\omega}_i & = -\frac{1}{\hbar} \sum_{j}^{Neighb} \vec{s}_{j}\times\vec{D}(r_{ij}) \\
\vec{F}_i & = -\sum_{j}^{Neighb} \frac{\partial D(r_{ij})}{\partial r_{ij}} \left(\vec{s}_{i}\times \vec{s}_{j} \right) \cdot \vec{r}_{ij}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\vec{s}_i\) and \(\vec{s}_j\) are neighboring magnetic
spins of two particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From this magneto\sphinxhyphen{}electric interaction, each spin i will be submitted
to a magnetic torque omega, and its associated atom can be submitted to a
force F for spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice calculations (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_spin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/spin}}}}),
such as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{F}^{i} & = -\sum_{j}^{Neighbor} \left( \vec{s}_{i}\times \vec{s}_{j} \right) \times \vec{E} \\
\vec{\omega}^{i} = -\frac{1}{\hbar} \sum_{j}^{Neighbor} \vec{s}_j \times \left(\vec{E}\times r_{ij} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with h the Planck constant (in metal units) and \(\vec{E}\) an
electric polarization vector.  The norm and direction of E are giving
the intensity and the direction of a screened dielectric atomic
polarization (in eV).

\sphinxAtStartPar
More details about the derivation of these torques/forces are reported in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spin_magelec:tranchida4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with this package, and if the
atom\_style “spin” was declared.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_neel:examples}}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{neel}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0048}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.234}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.168}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_spin_neel:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spin/neel} computes the Neel pair anisotropy model
between pairs of magnetic spins:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal{H}_{N\acute{e}el}=-\sum_{{ i,j=1,i\neq j}}^N g_1(r_{ij})\left(({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{i})({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}
\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{j})-\frac{{\mathbf{s}}_{i}\cdot{\mathbf{s}}_{j}}{3} \right)
+q_1(r_{ij})\left( ({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{i})^2 -\frac{{\mathbf{s}}_{i}\cdot{\mathbf{s}}_{j}}{3}\right)
\left( ({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{i})^2 -\frac{{\mathbf{s}}_{i}\cdot{\mathbf{s}}_{j}}{3} \right)
+ q_2(r_{ij}) \Big( ({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{i}) ({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{j})^3 + ({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot
{\mathbf{s}}_{j}) ({\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\cdot {\mathbf{s}}_{i})^3\Big)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{s}_i\) and \(\mathbf{s}_j\) are two neighboring magnetic spins of two particles,
\(r_{ij} = \vert \mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j \vert\) is the inter\sphinxhyphen{}atomic distance between the two particles,
\(\mathbf{e}_{ij} = \frac{\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j}{\vert \mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\vert}\) is their normalized separation vector and \(g_1\),
\(q_1\) and \(q_2\) are three functions defining the intensity of the dipolar
and quadrupolar contributions, with:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}g_1(r_{ij}) &= g(r_{ij}) + \frac{12}{35} q(r_{ij}) \\
q_1(r_{ij}) &= \frac{9}{5} q(r_{ij}) \\
q_2(r_{ij}) &= - \frac{2}{5} q(r_{ij})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With the functions \(g(r_{ij})\) and \(q(r_{ij})\) defined and fitted according to
the same Bethe\sphinxhyphen{}Slater function used to fit the exchange interaction:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}{J}\left( r_{ij} \right) = 4 a \left( \frac{r_{ij}}{d}  \right)^2 \left( 1 - b \left( \frac{r_{ij}}{d}  \right)^2 \right) e^{-\left( \frac{r_{ij}}{d} \right)^2 }\Theta (R_c - r_{ij})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) are the three constant coefficients defined in the
associated “pair\_coeff” command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients \(a\), \(b\), and \(d\) need to be fitted so that the function
above matches with the values of the magneto\sphinxhyphen{}elastic constant of the
materials at stake.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples and more explanations about this function and its
parameterization are reported in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spin_neel:tranchida6}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}. More
examples of parameterization will be provided in future work.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From this DM interaction, each spin \(i\) will be submitted to a magnetic
torque \(\mathbf{\omega}\) and its associated atom to a force \(\mathbf{F}\) (for spin\sphinxhyphen{}lattice
calculations only).

\sphinxAtStartPar
More details about the derivation of these torques/forces are reported
in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spin_neel:tranchida6}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Tranchida)}}}}.

\section{pair\_style srp/react command}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_srp:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{srp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{btype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{srp}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{react}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{btype}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{react}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for SRP interactions (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
btype = bond type (numeric, type label, or wildcard) to apply SRP interactions to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
distance = \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{mid}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
react\sphinxhyphen{}id = id of either fix bond/break or fix bond/create

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{exclude}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bptype} value = atom type (numeric or type label) for bond particles
\sphinxstyleemphasis{exclude} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{C}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{srp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mid}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{srp} computes a soft segmental repulsive potential (SRP) that
acts between pairs of bonds. This potential is useful for preventing
bonds from passing through one another when a soft non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded
potential acts between beads in, for example, DPD polymer chains.  An
example input script that uses this command is provided in
examples/PACKAGES/srp.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bonds of specified type \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} interact with one another through a
bond\sphinxhyphen{}pairwise potential, such that the force on bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} due to bond
\sphinxstyleemphasis{j} is as follows
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F^{\mathrm{SRP}}_{ij} = C(1-r/r_c)\hat{r}_{ij} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} and \(\hat{r}_{ij}\) are the distance and unit vector
between the two bonds.  Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} can be specified as an
asterisk “*”, which case the interaction is applied to all bond types.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mid} option computes \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} and \(\hat{r}_{ij}\) from the midpoint
distance between bonds. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} option computes \sphinxstyleemphasis{r} and
\(\hat{r}_{ij}\) from the minimum distance between bonds. The force
acting on a bond is mapped onto the two bond atoms according to the
lever rule,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_{i1}^{\mathrm{SRP}} & = F^{\mathrm{SRP}}_{ij}(L) \\
F_{i2}^{\mathrm{SRP}} & = F^{\mathrm{SRP}}_{ij}(1-L)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{L} is the normalized distance from the atom to the point of
closest approach of bond \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mid} option takes \sphinxstyleemphasis{L} as
0.5 for each interaction as described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_srp:sirk2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sirk)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in
the data file or restart file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{C} (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional. If not specified, the global cutoff
is used.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style srp considers each bond of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{btype} to be a
fictitious “particle” of type \sphinxstyleemphasis{bptype}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{bptype} is either the
largest atom type in the system, or the type set by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{bptype} flag.
Any actual existing particles with this atom type will be deleted at
the beginning of a run. This means you must specify the number of
types in your system accordingly; usually to be one larger than what
would normally be the case, e.g. via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{create_box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{create\_box}}}}
or by changing the header in your {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data file}}}}.  The
fictitious “bond particles” are inserted at the beginning of the run,
and serve as placeholders that define the position of the bonds.  This
allows neighbor lists to be constructed and pairwise interactions to
be computed in almost the same way as is done for actual particles.
Because bonds interact only with other bonds, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}} should be used to turn off interactions
between atom type \sphinxstyleemphasis{bptype} and all other types of atoms.  An error
will be flagged if {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}} is not used.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If using type labels, the type labels must be defined before calling
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{exclude} keyword determines if forces are computed
between first neighbor (directly connected) bonds.  For a setting of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, first neighbor forces are computed; for \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} they are not
computed. A setting of \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} cannot be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} option for
distance calculation because the minimum distance between directly
connected bonds is zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{srp} turns off normalization of thermodynamic properties
by particle number, as if the command {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_modify norm no}}}} had been issued.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pairwise energy associated with style \sphinxstyleemphasis{srp} is shifted to be zero
at the cutoff distance \(r_c\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Aug2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{srp/react} interfaces the pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{srp} with the
bond breaking and formation mechanisms provided by fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond/break}
and fix \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond/create}, respectively. When using this pair style, whenever a
bond breaking (or formation) reaction occurs, the corresponding fictitious
particle is deleted (or inserted) during the same simulation time step as
the reaction. This is useful in the simulation of reactive systems involving
large polymeric molecules {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_srp:palkar}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Palkar)}}}}  where the segmental repulsive
potential is necessary to minimize topological violations, and also needs to be
turned on and off according to the progress of the reaction.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_srp:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support mixing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option for the energy of the pair interaction. Note that as
discussed above, the energy term is already shifted to be 0.0 at the
cutoff distance \(r_c\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant for
this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes global and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}. Pair srp should be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}}, thus the pair\_coeff commands need to be
specified in the input script when reading a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_srp:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MISC package. It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the Making LAMMPS section
for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style must be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} command to be \sphinxstyleemphasis{on}
for non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is not compatible with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rigid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rigid body integrators}}}}


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_srp:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_dpd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair dpd}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_srp:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default keyword value is exclude = yes.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{maxdelcs} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{maxdelcs} value = delta1 delta2 (optional, sw/mod only)
  delta1 = The minimum thershold for the variation of cosine of three\sphinxhyphen{}body angle
  delta2 = The maximum threshold for the variation of cosine of three\sphinxhyphen{}body angle
\sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{on} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{off} (optional, sw only)
  on (default) = Compute both the three\sphinxhyphen{}body and two\sphinxhyphen{}body terms of the potential
  off = Compute only the two\sphinxhyphen{}body term of the potential
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{si.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{GaN.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ga}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ga}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mod}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{maxdelcs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.35}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmd.sw.mod}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Mo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{S}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{S}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{threebody}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{on}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{threebody}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{off}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mW\PYGZus{}xL.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mW}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mW\PYGZus{}xL.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mW}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xL}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mW\PYGZus{}xL.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mW}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xL}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} style computes a 3\sphinxhyphen{}body {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw:stillinger2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber}}}}
potential for the energy E of a system of atoms as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} E & =  \sum_i \sum_{j > i} \phi_2 (r_{ij}) +
        \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} \sum_{k > j}
        \phi_3 (r_{ij}, r_{ik}, \theta_{ijk}) \\
\phi_2(r_{ij}) & =  A_{ij} \epsilon_{ij} \left[ B_{ij} (\frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij}})^{p_{ij}} -
                  (\frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij}})^{q_{ij}} \right]
                  \exp \left( \frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij} - a_{ij} \sigma_{ij}} \right) \\
\phi_3(r_{ij},r_{ik},\theta_{ijk}) & = \lambda_{ijk} \epsilon_{ijk} \left[ \cos \theta_{ijk} -
                  \cos \theta_{0ijk} \right]^2
                  \exp \left( \frac{\gamma_{ij} \sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij} - a_{ij} \sigma_{ij}} \right)
                  \exp \left( \frac{\gamma_{ik} \sigma_{ik}}{r_{ik} - a_{ik} \sigma_{ik}} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\phi_2\) is a two\sphinxhyphen{}body term and \(\phi_3\) is a
three\sphinxhyphen{}body term.  The summations in the formula are over all neighbors J
and K of atom I within a cutoff distance \(a `\sigma\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 14Dec2021.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod} style is designed for simulations of materials when
distinguishing three\sphinxhyphen{}body angles are necessary, such as borophene and
transition metal dichalcogenides, which cannot be described by the
original code for the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential.  For instance, there
are several types of angles around each Mo atom in \sphinxtitleref{MoS\_2}, and some
unnecessary angle types should be excluded in the three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interaction.  Such exclusion may be realized by selecting proper angle
types directly.  The exclusion of unnecessary angles is achieved here by
the cut\sphinxhyphen{}off function (\sphinxtitleref{f\_C(delta)}), which induces only minimum
modifications for LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Validation, benchmark tests, and applications of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod} style
can be found in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw:jiang2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jiang2)}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw:jiang3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Jiang3)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod} style computes the energy E of a system of atoms, whose
potential function is mostly the same as the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber
potential. The only modification is in the three\sphinxhyphen{}body term, where the
value of \(\delta = \cos \theta_{ijk} - \cos \theta_{0ijk}\) used in
the original energy and force expression is scaled by a switching factor
\(f_C(\delta)\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_C(\delta) & = \left\{ \begin{array} {r@{\quad:\quad}l}
  1 & \left| \delta \right| < \delta_1 \\
  \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} \cos \left( \pi \frac{\left| \delta \right| - \delta_1}{\delta_2 - \delta_1} \right) &
    \delta_1 < \left| \delta \right| < \delta_2 \\
  0 & \left| \delta \right| > \delta_2
  \end{array} \right. \\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This cut\sphinxhyphen{}off function decreases smoothly from 1 to 0 over the range
\([\delta_1, \delta_2]\).  This smoothly turns off the energy and
force contributions for \(\left| \delta \right| > \delta_2\).  It is
suggested that \(\delta 1\) and \(\delta_2\) to be the value
around \(0.5 \left| \cos \theta_1 - \cos \theta_2 \right|\), with
\(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\) as the different types of angles
around an atom.  For borophene and transition metal dichalcogenides,
\(\delta_1 = 0.25\) and \(\delta_2 = 0.35\).  This value enables
the cut\sphinxhyphen{}off function to exclude unnecessary angles in the three\sphinxhyphen{}body SW
terms.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The cut\sphinxhyphen{}off function is just to be used as a technique to exclude
some unnecessary angles, and it has no physical meaning. It should be
noted that the force and potential are inconsistent with each other
in the decaying range of the cut\sphinxhyphen{}off function, as the angle
dependence for the cut\sphinxhyphen{}off function is not implemented in the force
(first derivation of potential).  However, the angle variation is
much smaller than the given threshold value for actual simulations,
so the inconsistency between potential and force can be neglected in
actual simulations.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Aug2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody} keyword is optional and determines whether or not the
three\sphinxhyphen{}body term of the potential is calculated.  The default value is
“on” and it is only available for the plain \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} pair style variants,
but not available for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{sw/angle/table}}}} pair style variants.  To turn off the threebody
contributions all \(\lambda_{ijk}\) parameters from the potential
file are forcibly set to 0.  In addition the pair style implementation
may employ code optimizations for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody off} setting that can
result in significant speedups versus the default.  These code optimizations
are currently only available for the MANYBODY and OPENMP packages.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod}
styles which specifies a Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential file with parameters
for all needed elements, except for when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody off} setting is
used (see note below).  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by
specifying N additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff
command, where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of SW elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine a file SiC.sw has Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber values for
Si and C.  If your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you want
the first 3 to be Si, and the fourth to be C, you would use the following
pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiC.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1, 2, and 3 to the Si
element in the SW file.  The final C argument maps LAMMPS atom type 4 to
the C element in the SW file.  If an argument value is specified as
NULL, the mapping is not performed.  This can be used when an \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw}
potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values
are placeholders for atom types that will be used with other potentials.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody off} keyword is used, multiple pair\_coeff
commands may be used to specific the pairs of atoms which don’t
require three\sphinxhyphen{}body term.  In these cases, the first 2 arguments are
not required to be * *, the potential parameter file is only read
by the first {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff command}}}} and the element
to atom type mappings must be consistent across all \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_coeff}
statements.  If not LAMMPS will abort with an error.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber files in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potentials} directory of the LAMMPS
distribution have a “.sw” suffix.  Lines that are not blank or
comments (starting with \#) define parameters for a triplet of
elements.  The parameters in a single entry correspond to the two\sphinxhyphen{}body
and three\sphinxhyphen{}body coefficients in the formula above:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 1 (the center atom in a 3\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 3

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\lambda\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\cos\theta_0\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
B

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
q

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tol

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The A, B, p, and q parameters are used only for two\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.
The \(\lambda\) and \(\cos\theta_0\) parameters are used only
for three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions. The \(\epsilon\), \(\sigma\) and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{a} parameters are used for both two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions. \(\gamma\) is used only in the three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions, but is defined for pairs of atoms.  The non\sphinxhyphen{}annotated
parameters are unitless.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS introduces an additional performance\sphinxhyphen{}optimization parameter tol
that is used for both two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.  In the
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential, the interaction energies become negligibly
small at atomic separations substantially less than the theoretical
cutoff distances.  LAMMPS therefore defines a virtual cutoff distance
based on a user defined tolerance tol.  The use of the virtual cutoff
distance in constructing atom neighbor lists can significantly reduce
the neighbor list sizes and therefore the computational cost.  LAMMPS
provides a \sphinxstyleemphasis{tol} value for each of the three\sphinxhyphen{}body entries so that they
can be separately controlled. If tol = 0.0, then the standard
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber cutoff is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential file must contain entries for all the
elements listed in the pair\_coeff command.  It can also contain
entries for additional elements not being used in a particular
simulation; LAMMPS ignores those entries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a single\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, only a single entry is required
(e.g. SiSiSi).  For a two\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, the file must contain 8
entries (for SiSiSi, SiSiC, SiCSi, SiCC, CSiSi, CSiC, CCSi, CCC), that
specify SW parameters for all permutations of the two elements
interacting in three\sphinxhyphen{}body configurations.  Thus for 3 elements, 27
entries would be required, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As annotated above, the first element in the entry is the center atom
in a three\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction.  Thus an entry for SiCC means a Si atom
with 2 C atoms as neighbors.  The parameter values used for the
two\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction come from the entry where the second and third
elements are the same.  Thus the two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for Si
interacting with C, comes from the SiCC entry.  The three\sphinxhyphen{}body
parameters can in principle be specific to the three elements of the
configuration. In the literature, however, the three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters
are usually defined by simple formulas involving two sets of pairwise
parameters, corresponding to the ij and ik pairs, where i is the
center atom. The user must ensure that the correct combining rule is
used to calculate the values of the three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for
alloys. Note also that the function \(\phi_3\) contains two exponential
screening factors with parameter values from the ij pair and ik
pairs. So \(\phi_3\) for a C atom bonded to a Si atom and a second C atom
will depend on the three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for the CSiC entry, and also
on the two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for the CCC and CSiSi entries. Since the
order of the two neighbors is arbitrary, the three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for
entries CSiC and CCSi should be the same.  Similarly, the two\sphinxhyphen{}body
parameters for entries SiCC and CSiSi should also be the same.  The
parameters used only for two\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions (A, B, p, and q) in
entries whose second and third element are different (e.g. SiCSi) are not
used for anything and can be set to 0.0 if desired.
This is also true for the parameters in \(\phi_3\) that are
taken from the ij and ik pairs (\(\sigma\), \sphinxstyleemphasis{a}, \(\gamma\))


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When using the INTEL package with this style, there is an additional
5 to 10 percent performance improvement when the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber
parameters p and q are set to 4 and 0 respectively.  These
parameters are common for modeling silicon and water.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS as
described above from values in the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single() function of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} pair style is only enabled and
supported for the case of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody off} setting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MANYBODY package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential files provided with LAMMPS (see the
potentials directory) are parameterized for metal {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.
You can use the sw or sw/mod pair styles with any LAMMPS units, but you
would need to create your own SW potential file with coefficients listed
in the appropriate units if your simulation does not use “metal” units.
If the potential file contains a ‘UNITS:’ metadata tag in the first line
of the potential file, then LAMMPS can convert it transparently between
“metal” and “real” units.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default value for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody} setting of the “sw” pair style is
“on”, the default values for the “\sphinxstyleemphasis{maxdelcs} setting of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/mod}
pair style are \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta1} = 0.25 and \sphinxstyleemphasis{delta2} = 0.35\textasciigrave{}.

\index{pair\_style sw/angle/table@\spxentry{pair\_style sw/angle/table}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style sw/angle/table command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:pair-style-sw-angle-table-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/angle/table}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sw}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{angle}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{table}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spce.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Used in example input script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
examples/PACKAGES/manybody\PYGZus{}table/in.spce\PYGZus{}sw
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 2Jun2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/angle/table} style is a modification of the original
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style sw}}}}. It has been developed for coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained
simulations (of water) ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:scherer1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Scherer1}}}}), but can be employed
for all kinds of systems. It computes a modified 3\sphinxhyphen{}body
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:stillinger3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber}}}} potential for the energy E of a
system of atoms as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} E & =  \sum_i \sum_{j > i} \phi_2 (r_{ij}) +
        \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} \sum_{k > j}
        \phi_3 (r_{ij}, r_{ik}, \theta_{ijk}) \\
\phi_2(r_{ij}) & =  A_{ij} \epsilon_{ij} \left[ B_{ij} (\frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij}})^{p_{ij}} -
                  (\frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij}})^{q_{ij}} \right]
                  \exp \left( \frac{\sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij} - a_{ij} \sigma_{ij}} \right) \\
\phi_3(r_{ij},r_{ik},\theta_{ijk}) & = f^{\textrm{3b}}\left(\theta_{ijk}\right)
                  \exp \left( \frac{\gamma_{ij} \sigma_{ij}}{r_{ij} - a_{ij} \sigma_{ij}} \right)
                  \exp \left( \frac{\gamma_{ik} \sigma_{ik}}{r_{ik} - a_{ik} \sigma_{ik}} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\phi_2\) is a two\sphinxhyphen{}body term and \(\phi_3\) is a
three\sphinxhyphen{}body term.  The summations in the formula are over all neighbors J
and K of atom I within a cutoff distance \(a \sigma\).  In contrast
to the original \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw} style, \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/angle/table} allows for a flexible
three\sphinxhyphen{}body term \(f^{\textrm{3b}}\left(\theta_{ijk}\right)\) which
is read in as a tabulated interaction. It can be parameterized with the
csg\_fmatch app of VOTCA as available at:
\sphinxurl{https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/votca/votca}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/angle/table} style
which specifies a modified Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential file with
parameters for all needed elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom
types by specifying N\_el additional arguments after the “.sw” filename
in the pair\_coeff command, where N\_el is the number of LAMMPS atom
types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“.sw” filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N\_el element names = mapping of SW elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways to
specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine a file SiC.sw has Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber values for Si
and C.  If your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you want the
first 3 to be Si, and the fourth to be C, you would use the following
pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiC.sw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the Si
element in the SW file.  The final C argument maps LAMMPS atom type 4 to
the C element in the SW file.  If a mapping value is specified as NULL,
the mapping is not performed.  This can be used when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{sw/angle/table}
potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values
are placeholders for atom types that will be used with other potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The (modified) Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber files have a “.sw” suffix. Lines that
are not blank or comments (starting with \#) define parameters for a
triplet of elements. The parameters in a single entry correspond to the
two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body coefficients in the formula above. Here, also
the suffix “.sw” is used though the original Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber file
format is supplemented with four additional lines per parameter block to
specify the tabulated three\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction. A single entry then
contains:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 1 (the center atom in a 3\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 3

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\lambda\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\cos\theta_0\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
B

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
q

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tol

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The A, B, p, and q parameters are used only for two\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.
The \(\lambda\) and \(\cos\theta_0\) parameters, only used for
three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions in the original Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber style, are read
in but ignored in this modified pair style. The \(\epsilon\)
parameter is only used for two\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions in this modified pair
style and not for the three\sphinxhyphen{}body terms. The \(\sigma\) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{a}
parameters are used for both two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions. \(\gamma\) is used only in the three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions, but is defined for pairs of atoms. The non\sphinxhyphen{}annotated
parameters are unitless.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS introduces an additional performance\sphinxhyphen{}optimization parameter tol
that is used for both two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.  In the
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential, the interaction energies become negligibly
small at atomic separations substantially less than the theoretical
cutoff distances.  LAMMPS therefore defines a virtual cutoff distance
based on a user defined tolerance tol.  The use of the virtual cutoff
distance in constructing atom neighbor lists can significantly reduce
the neighbor list sizes and therefore the computational cost.  LAMMPS
provides a \sphinxstyleemphasis{tol} value for each of the three\sphinxhyphen{}body entries so that they
can be separately controlled. If tol = 0.0, then the standard
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber cutoff is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The additional parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{style}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} refer
to the tabulated angular potential
\(f^{\textrm{3b}}\left(\theta_{ijk}\right)\).  The tabulated angular
potential has to be of the format as used in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style table}}}} command:

\sphinxAtStartPar
An interpolation tables of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} is created. The interpolation is
done in one of 2 \sphinxstyleemphasis{styles}: \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spline}.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear}
style, the angle is used to find 2 surrounding table values from which
an energy or its derivative is computed by linear interpolation. For the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{spline} style, a cubic spline coefficients are computed and stored at
each of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} values in the table.  The angle is used to find the
appropriate set of coefficients which are used to evaluate a cubic
polynomial which computes the energy or derivative.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename} specifies the file containing the tabulated energy and
derivative values of \(f^{\textrm{3b}}\left(\theta_{ijk}\right)\).
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword} then specifies a section of the file.  The format of this
file is as follows (without the parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Angle potential for harmonic (one or more comment or blank lines)

HAM                           (keyword is the first text on line)
N 181 FP 0 0 EQ 90.0          (N, FP, EQ parameters)
                              (blank line)
1 0.0 200.5 2.5               (index, angle, energy, derivative)
2 1.0 198.0 2.5
...
181 180.0 0.0 0.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which identifies
the section. The next line lists (in any order) one or more parameters
for the table.  Each parameter is a keyword followed by one or more
numeric values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter “N” is required and its value is the number of table
entries that follow.  Note that this may be different than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
specified in the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential file. Let Nsw = \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} in the
“.sw” file, and Nfile = “N” in the tabulated angular file.  What LAMMPS
does is a preliminary interpolation by creating splines using the Nfile
tabulated values as nodal points.  It uses these to interpolate as
needed to generate energy and derivative values at Ntable different
points.  The resulting tables of length Nsw are then used as described
above, when computing energy and force for individual angles and their
atoms.  This means that if you want the interpolation tables of length
Nsw to match exactly what is in the tabulated file (with effectively no
preliminary interpolation), you should set Nsw = Nfile.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “FP” parameter is optional.  If used, it is followed by two values
fplo and fphi, which are the second derivatives at the innermost and
outermost angle settings.  These values are needed by the spline
construction routines.  If not specified by the “FP” parameter, they are
estimated (less accurately) by the first two and last two derivative
values in the table.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “EQ” parameter is also optional.  If used, it is followed by a the
equilibrium angle value, which is used, for example, by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
shake}}}} command. If not used, the equilibrium angle is set to
180.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines of the angular table file list
the tabulated values.  On each line, the first value is the index from 1
to N, the second value is the angle value (in degrees), the third value
is the energy (in energy units), and the fourth is \sphinxhyphen{}dE/d(theta) (also in
energy units).  The third term is the energy of the 3\sphinxhyphen{}atom configuration
for the specified angle.  The last term is the derivative of the energy
with respect to the angle (in degrees, not radians).  Thus the units of
the last term are still energy, not force.  The angle values must
increase from one line to the next.  The angle values must also begin
with 0.0 and end with 180.0, i.e. span the full range of possible
angles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one angular potential file can contain many sections, each
with a tabulated potential.  LAMMPS reads the file section by section
until it finds one that matches the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword} of appropriate
section of the “.sw” file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential file must contain entries for all the
elements listed in the pair\_coeff command.  It can also contain entries
for additional elements not being used in a particular simulation;
LAMMPS ignores those entries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a single\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, only a single entry is required
(e.g. SiSiSi).  For a two\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, the file must contain 8
entries (for SiSiSi, SiSiC, SiCSi, SiCC, CSiSi, CSiC, CCSi, CCC), that
specify SW parameters for all permutations of the two elements
interacting in three\sphinxhyphen{}body configurations.  Thus for 3 elements, 27
entries would be required, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As annotated above, the first element in the entry is the center atom in
a three\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction.  Thus an entry for SiCC means a Si atom with 2
C atoms as neighbors.  The parameter values used for the two\sphinxhyphen{}body
interaction come from the entry where the second and third elements are
the same.  Thus the two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for Si interacting with C, comes
from the SiCC entry.  The three\sphinxhyphen{}body angular potential
\(f^{\textrm{3b}}\left(\theta_{ijk}\right)\) can in principle be
specific to the three elements of the configuration. However, the user
must ensure that it makes physically sense.  Note also that the function
\(\phi_3\) contains two exponential screening factors with parameter
values from the ij pair and ik pairs. So \(\phi_3\) for a C atom
bonded to a Si atom and a second C atom will depend on the three\sphinxhyphen{}body
parameters for the CSiC entry, and also on the two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for
the CCC and CSiSi entries. Since the order of the two neighbors is
arbitrary, the three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters and the tabulated angular potential
for entries CSiC and CCSi should be the same.  Similarly, the two\sphinxhyphen{}body
parameters for entries SiCC and CSiSi should also be the same.  The
parameters used only for two\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions (A, B, p, and q) in
entries whose second and third element are different (e.g. SiCSi) are
not used for anything and can be set to 0.0 if desired.  This is also
true for the parameters in \(\phi_3\) that are taken from the ij and
ik pairs (\(\sigma\), \sphinxstyleemphasis{a}, \(\gamma\))

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional input files and reference data can be found at:
\sphinxurl{https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/votca/votca/-/tree/master/csg-tutorials/spce/3body\_sw}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS as described
above from values in the potential file, but not for the tabulated
angular potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MANYBODY package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style sw}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_threebody_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style threebody/table}}}}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip
