\section{pair\_style thole command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:pair-style-thole-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_thole::doc}}

\section{pair\_style lj/cut/thole/long command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:pair-style-lj-cut-thole-long-command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of arguments for a particular style

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} args = damp cutoff
  damp = global damping parameter
  cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long} args = damp cutoff (cutoff2)
  damp = global damping parameter
  cutoff = global cutoff for LJ (and Thole if only 1 arg) (distance units)
  cutoff2 = global cutoff for Thole (optional) (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thole}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thole}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thole}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thole}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.6}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{thole}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{long}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input scripts available: examples/PACKAGES/drude


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} pair styles are meant to be used with force fields that
include explicit polarization through Drude dipoles.  This link
describes how to use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermalized Drude oscillator model}}}} in LAMMPS and polarizable models in LAMMPS are
discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_polarizable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto polarizable}}}} doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} pair style should be used as a sub\sphinxhyphen{}style within in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style hybrid/overlay}}}} command, in conjunction with a
main pair style including Coulomb interactions, i.e. any pair style
containing \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/cut} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{coul/long} in its style name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long} pair style is equivalent to, but more convenient that
the frequent combination \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/overlay lj/cut/coul/long cutoff thole damp
cutoff2}. It is not only a shorthand for this pair\_style combination, but
it also allows for mixing pair coefficients instead of listing them all.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long} pair style is also a bit faster because it avoids an
overlay and can benefit from OMP acceleration. Moreover, it uses a more
precise approximation of the direct Coulomb interaction at short range similar
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_cs::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{coul/long/cs}}}}, which stabilizes the temperature of
Drude particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} pair styles compute the Coulomb interaction damped at
short distances by a function
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T_{ij}(r_{ij}) = 1 - \left( 1 +
\frac{s_{ij} r_{ij} }{2} \right)
\exp \left( - s_{ij} r_{ij} \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function results from an adaptation to point charges
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_thole:noskov1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Noskov)}}}} of the dipole screening scheme originally proposed
by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_thole:thole1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Thole}}}}. The scaling coefficient \(s_{ij}\) is determined
by the polarizability of the atoms, \(\alpha_i\), and by a Thole
damping parameter \(a\).  This Thole damping parameter usually takes
a value of 2.6, but in certain force fields the value can depend upon
the atom types. The mixing rule for Thole damping parameters is the
arithmetic average, and for polarizabilities the geometric average
between the atom\sphinxhyphen{}specific values.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}s_{ij} = \frac{ a_{ij} }{
(\alpha_{ij})^{1/3} } = \frac{ (a_i + a_j)/2 }{
[(\alpha_i\alpha_j)^{1/2}]^{1/3} }\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The damping function is only applied to the interactions between the
point charges representing the induced dipoles on polarizable sites,
that is, charges on Drude particles, \(q_{D,i}\), and opposite
charges, \(-q_{D,i}\), located on the respective core particles
(to which each Drude particle is bonded). Therefore, Thole screening
is not applied to the full charge of the core particle \(q_i\), but
only to the \(-q_{D,i}\) part of it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interactions between core charges are subject to the weighting
factors set by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command. The
interactions between Drude particles and core charges or
non\sphinxhyphen{}polarizable atoms are also subject to these weighting factors. The
Drude particles inherit the 1\sphinxhyphen{}2, 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 and 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 neighbor relations from
their respective cores.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole}, the following coefficients must be defined for
each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command
as in the example above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (distance units\textasciicircum{}3)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last two coefficients are optional.  If not specified the global
Thole damping parameter or global cutoff specified in the pair\_style
command are used. In order to specify a cutoff (third argument) a damp
parameter (second argument) must also be specified.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long}, the following coefficients must be
defined for each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}
command.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (length units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (distance units\textasciicircum{}3)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
damp

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LJ cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last two coefficients are optional and default to the global values from
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair\_style} command line.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} pair style does not support mixing.  Thus, coefficients
for all I,J pairs must be specified explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long} pair style does support mixing. Mixed coefficients
are defined using
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\alpha_{ij} = & \sqrt{\alpha_i\alpha_j} \\
& \\
a_{ij} = & \frac 1 2 (a_i + a_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_thole:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the DRUDE package. They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair\_style should currently not be used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_charmm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{charmm dihedral style}}}} if the latter has non\sphinxhyphen{}zero 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 weighting
factors. This is because the \sphinxstyleemphasis{thole} pair style does not know which
pairs are 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 partners of which dihedrals.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/cut/thole/long} pair style should be used with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{kspace_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Kspace solver}}}}
like PPPM or Ewald, which is only enabled if LAMMPS was built with the kspace
package.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_langevin_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix langevin/drude}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_drude_transform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix drude/transform}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_temp_drude::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute temp/drude}}}}

\index{pair\_style threebody/table@\spxentry{pair\_style threebody/table}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style threebody/table command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:pair-style-threebody-table-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody/table}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{threebody}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{table}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spce2.3b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type2}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{threebody}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{table}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{table\PYGZus{}CG\PYGZus{}CG.txt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{VOTCA}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{threebody}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spce.3b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Used in example input scripts:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
examples/PACKAGES/manybody\PYGZus{}table/in.spce
examples/PACKAGES/manybody\PYGZus{}table/in.spce2
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 2Jun2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody/table} style is a pair style for generic tabulated
three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.  It has been developed for (coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained)
simulations (of water) with Kernel\sphinxhyphen{}based machine learning (ML)
potentials ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:scherer2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Scherer2}}}}).  As for many other MANYBODY
package pair styles the energy of a system is computed as a sum over
three\sphinxhyphen{}body terms:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E =  \sum_i \sum_{j \neq i} \sum_{k > j} \phi_3 (r_{ij}, r_{ik}, \theta_{ijk})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The summations in the formula are over all neighbors J and K of atom I
within a cutoff distance \(cut\).  In contrast to the
Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential, all forces are not calculated analytically,
but read in from a three\sphinxhyphen{}body force/energy table which can be generated
with the csg\_ml app of VOTCA as available at:
\sphinxurl{https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/votca/votca}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody/table}
style which specifies a threebody potential (“.3b”) file with parameters
for all needed elements. These are then mapped to LAMMPS atom types by
specifying N\_el additional arguments after the “.3b” filename in the
pair\_coeff command, where N\_el is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“.3b” filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N\_el element names = mapping of threebody elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways to
specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine a file SiC.3b has three\sphinxhyphen{}body values for Si and C.
If your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you want the first 3 to
be Si, and the fourth to be C, you would use the following pair\_coeff
command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiC.3b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the Si
element in the “.3b” file.  The final C argument maps LAMMPS atom type 4
to the C element in the threebody file. If a mapping value is specified
as NULL, the mapping is not performed. This can be used when a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{threebody/table} potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.
The NULL values are placeholders for atom types that will be used with
other potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The three\sphinxhyphen{}body files have a “.3b” suffix. Lines that are not blank or
comments (starting with \#) define parameters for a triplet of
elements. The parameters in a single entry specify to the (three\sphinxhyphen{}body)
cutoff distance and the tabulated three\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction. A single entry
then contains:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 1 (the center atom in a 3\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 3

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cut (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \(cut\) is the (three\sphinxhyphen{}body) cutoff distance.  When set
to 0, no interaction is calculated for this element triplet.  The
parameters \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{style}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} refer to the
tabulated three\sphinxhyphen{}body potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The tabulation is done on a three\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional grid of the two distances
\(r_{ij}\) and \(r_{ik}\) as well as the angle
\(\theta_{ijk}\) which is constructed in the following way. There
are two different cases.  If element 2 and element 3 are of the same
type (e.g. SiCC), the distance \(r_{ij}\) is varied in “N” steps
from rmin to rmax and the distance \(r_{ik}\) is varied from
\(r_{ij}\) to rmax. This can be done, due to the symmetry of the
triplet. If element 2 and element 3 are not of the same type
(e.g. SiCSi), there is no additional symmetry and the distance
\(r_{ik}\) is also varied from rmin to rmax in “N” steps.  The angle
\(\theta_{ijk}\) is always varied in “2N” steps from (0.0 +
180.0/(4N)) to (180.0 \sphinxhyphen{} 180.0/(4N)). Therefore, the total number of
table entries is “M = N * N * (N+1)” for the symmetric (element 2 and
element 3 are of the same type) and “M = 2 * N * N * N” for the general
case (element 2 and element 3 are not of the same type).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forces on all three particles I, J, and K of a triplet of this type
of three\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction potential (\(\phi_3 (r_{ij}, r_{ik},
\theta_{ijk})\)) lie within the plane defined by the three inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle
distance vectors \({\mathbf r}_{ij}\), \({\mathbf r}_{ik}\), and
\({\mathbf r}_{jk}\).  This property is used to project the forces
onto the inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle distance vectors as follows
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{pmatrix}
   {\mathbf f}_{i} \\
   {\mathbf f}_{j} \\
   {\mathbf f}_{k} \\
\end{pmatrix} =
\begin{pmatrix}
   f_{i1} & f_{i2} & 0 \\
   f_{j1} & 0 & f_{j2} \\
   0 & f_{k1} & f_{k2} \\
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
   {\mathbf r}_{ij} \\
   {\mathbf r}_{ik} \\
   {\mathbf r}_{jk} \\
\end{pmatrix}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and then tabulate the 6 force constants \(f_{i1}\), \(f_{i2}\),
\(f_{j1}\), \(f_{j2}\), \(f_{k1}\), and \(f_{k2}\), as
well as the energy of a triplet e.  Due to symmetry reasons, the
following relations hold: \(f_{i1}=-f_{j1}\),
\(f_{i2}=-f_{k1}\), and \(f_{j2}=-f_{k2}\). As in this pair
style the forces are read in directly, a correct MD simulation is also
performed in the case that the triplet energies are set to e=0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{filename} specifies the file containing the tabulated energy and
derivative values of \(\phi_3 (r_{ij}, r_{ik}, \theta_{ijk})\).  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword} then specifies a section of the file. The format of this file
is as follows (without the parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Tabulated three\PYGZhy{}body potential for spce water (one or more comment or blank lines)

ENTRY1                                                                      (keyword is the first text on line)
N 12 rmin 2.55 rmax 3.65                                                    (N, rmin, rmax parameters)
                                                                            (blank line)
1 2.55 2.55 3.75 \PYGZhy{}867.212 \PYGZhy{}611.273 867.212 21386.8 611.273 \PYGZhy{}21386.8  0.0    (index, r\PYGZus{}ij, r\PYGZus{}ik, theta, f\PYGZus{}i1, f\PYGZus{}i2, f\PYGZus{}j1, f\PYGZus{}j2, f\PYGZus{}k1, f\PYGZus{}k2, e)
2 2.55 2.55 11.25 \PYGZhy{}621.539 \PYGZhy{}411.189 621.539 5035.95 411.189 \PYGZhy{}5035.95  0.0
...
1872 3.65 3.65 176.25 \PYGZhy{}0.00215132 \PYGZhy{}0.00412886 0.00215137 0.00111754 0.00412895 \PYGZhy{}0.00111757  0.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which identifies
the section. The next line lists (in any order) one or more parameters
for the table.  Each parameter is a keyword followed by one or more
numeric values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter “N” is required. It should be the same than the parameter
“N” of the “.3b” file, otherwise its value is overwritten. “N”
determines the number of table entries “M” that follow: “M = N * N *
(N+1)” (symmetric triplet, e.g. SiCC) or “M = 2 * N * N * N” (asymmetric
triplet, e.g. SiCSi). Therefore “M = 12 * 12 * 13 = 1872” in the above
symmetric example. The parameters “rmin” and “rmax” are also required
and determine the minimum and maximum of the inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle distances
\(r_{ij}\) and \(r_{ik}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next M lines of the angular table file list
the tabulated values.  On each line, the first value is the index from 1
to M, the second value is the distance \(r_{ij}\), the third value
is the distance \(r_{ik}\), the fourth value is the angle
\(\theta_{ijk})\), the next six values are the force constants
\(f_{i1}\), \(f_{i2}\), \(f_{j1}\), \(f_{j2}\),
\(f_{k1}\), and \(f_{k2}\), and the last value is the energy e.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one three\sphinxhyphen{}body potential file can contain many sections, each
with a tabulated potential. LAMMPS reads the file section by section
until it finds one that matches the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{keyword} of appropriate
section of the “.3b” file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
At the moment, only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} is allowed and
implemented. After reading in the force table, it is internally stored
in LAMMPS as a lookup table. For each triplet configuration occurring in
the simulation within the cutoff distance, the next nearest tabulated
triplet configuration is looked up. No interpolation is done.  This
allows for a very efficient force calculation with the stored force
constants and energies. Due to the know table structure, the lookup can
be done efficiently. It has been tested ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:scherer2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Scherer2}}}})
that with a reasonably small bin size, the accuracy and speed is
comparable to that of a Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential with tabulated
three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions ({\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style sw/angle/table}}}}) while the table format of this pair style allows
for more flexible three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As for the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential, the three\sphinxhyphen{}body potential file
must contain entries for all the elements listed in the pair\_coeff
command.  It can also contain entries for additional elements not being
used in a particular simulation; LAMMPS ignores those entries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a single\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, only a single entry is required
(e.g. SiSiSi).  For a two\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, the file must contain 8
entries (for SiSiSi, SiSiC, SiCSi, SiCC, CSiSi, CSiC, CCSi, CCC), that
specify threebody parameters for all permutations of the two elements
interacting in three\sphinxhyphen{}body configurations.  Thus for 3 elements, 27
entries would be required, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As annotated above, the first element in the entry is the center atom in
a three\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction. Thus an entry for SiCC means a Si atom with 2
C atoms as neighbors. The tabulated three\sphinxhyphen{}body forces can in principle
be specific to the three elements of the configuration.  However, the
user must ensure that it makes physically sense.  E.g., the tabulated
three\sphinxhyphen{}body forces for the entries CSiC and CCSi should be the same
exchanging \(r_{ij}\) with r\_\{ik\}, \(f_{j1}\) with
\(f_{k1}\), and \(f_{j2}\) with \(f_{k2}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional input files and reference data can be found at:
\sphinxurl{https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/votca/votca/-/tree/master/csg-tutorials/ml}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As all interactions are tabulated, no mixing is performed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you need
to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input script
that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MANYBODY package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_sw_angle_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair sw/angle/table}}}}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{pair_threebody_table:scherer2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Scherer2)} C. Scherer, R. Scheid, D. Andrienko, and T. Bereau, J. Chem. Theor. Comp. 16, 3194\sphinxhyphen{}3204 (2020).

\sphinxstepscope

\index{pair\_style tracker@\spxentry{pair\_style tracker}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style tracker command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:pair-style-tracker-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tracker}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fix\PYGZus{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fix\_ID = ID of associated internal fix to store data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = prepare data for output every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{finite} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{time/min} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/include}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{finite} value = none
   pair style uses atomic diameters to identify contacts
\sphinxstyleemphasis{time/min} value = T
   T = minimum number of timesteps of interaction
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type/include} value = list1 list2
   list1,list2 = separate lists of types (see below)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one or more attributes may be appended

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = id1 id2 time/created time/broken time/total
                      r/min r/ave x y z
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
id1, id2 = IDs of the two atoms in each pair interaction
time/created = the timestep that the two atoms began interacting
time/broken = the timestep that the two atoms stopped interacting
time/total = the total number of timesteps the two atoms interacted
r/min = the minimum radial distance between the two atoms during the interaction (distance units)
r/ave = the average radial distance between the two atoms during the interaction (distance units)
x, y, z = the center of mass position of the two atoms when they stopped interacting (distance units)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tracker}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myfix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3},4\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tracker}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{overlay}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tracker}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myfix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{finite}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{granular}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tracker}

\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[3]}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{tracker} monitors information about pairwise interactions.  It
does not calculate any forces on atoms. {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Pair hybrid/overlay}}}} can be used to combine this pair style with any other
pair style, as shown in the examples above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
At each timestep, if two neighboring atoms move beyond the interaction
cutoff, pairwise data is processed and transferred to an internal fix
labeled \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID}. This allows the local data to be accessed by other
LAMMPS commands. Additional
filters can be applied using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{time/min} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/include} keywords
described below.  Note that this is the interaction cutoff defined by
this pair style, not the short\sphinxhyphen{}range cutoff defined by the pair style
that is calculating forces on atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following any optional keyword/value arguments, a list of one or more
attributes is specified.  These include the IDs of the two atoms in
the pair.  The other attributes for the pair of atoms are the
duration of time they were “interacting” or at the point in time they
started or stopped interacting.  In this context, “interacting” means
the time window during which the two atoms were closer than the
interaction cutoff distance.  The attributes for time/* refer to
timesteps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Data is continuously accumulated by the internal fix over intervals of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. At the end of each interval, all of the saved accumulated
data is deleted to make room for new data. Individual datum may
therefore persist anywhere between \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} timesteps depending on
when they are saved. This data can be accessed using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID} and a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command. To ensure all data is output,
the dump frequency should correspond to the same interval of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. A dump frequency of an integer multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} can be used
to regularly output a sample of the accumulated data.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The following optional keywords may be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{finite} keyword is not used, the following coefficients must
be defined for each pair of atom types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in the data file or
restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by mixing as described
below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{finite} keyword is used, there are no additional coefficients
to set for each pair of atom types via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command. Interaction cutoffs are
instead calculated based on the diameter of finite particles. However
you must still use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} for all atom
types. For example the command

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
should be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{time/min} keyword sets a minimum amount of time that an
interaction must persist to be included.  This setting can be used to
censor short\sphinxhyphen{}lived interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/include} keyword filters interactions based on the types of
the two atoms.  Data is only saved for interactions between atoms
whose two atom types appear in \sphinxstyleemphasis{list1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{list2}.  Atom type 1 must
be in list1 and atom type 2 in list2.  Or vice versa.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each type list consists of a series of type ranges separated by
commas.  Each range can be specified as a single numeric value, or a
wildcard asterisk can be used to specify a range of values.  This
takes the form “*” or “*n” or “n*” or “m*n”.  For example, if M =
the number of atom types, then an asterisk with no numeric values
means all types from 1 to M.  A leading asterisk means all types from
1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all types from n to M
(inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all types from m to n
(inclusive).  Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{type/include} keyword can be specified
multiple times.


\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the cutoff coefficient and cutoff
distance for this pair style can be mixed.  The cutoff is always mixed
via a \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric} rule.  The cutoff is mixed according to the
pair\_modify mix value.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See
the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift, table, and tail options
are not relevant for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The accumulated data is not written to restart files and should be
output before a restart file is written to avoid missing data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The internal fix calculates a local vector or local array depending on the
number of input values.  The length of the vector or number of rows in
the array is the number of recorded, lost interactions.  If a single
input is specified, a local vector is produced.  If two or more inputs
are specified, a local array is produced where the number of columns =
the number of inputs.  The vector or array can be accessed by any
command that uses local values from a compute as input.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page for an overview of LAMMPS
output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array will be floating point values that correspond to
the specified attribute.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tracker:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is part of the MISC package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is currently incompatible with granular pair styles
that extend beyond the contact (e.g. JKR and DMT).

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tri_lj:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri/lj} treats particles which are triangles as a set of small
spherical particles that tile the triangle surface as explained below.
Interactions between two triangles, each with N1 and N2 spherical
particles, are calculated as the pairwise sum of N1*N2 Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones
interactions.  Interactions between a triangle with N spherical
particles and a point particle are treated as the pairwise sum of N
Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/cut}}}}
doc page for the definition of Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoff distance for an interaction between 2 triangles, or between
a triangle and a point particle, is calculated from the position of
the triangle (its centroid), not between pairs of individual spheres
comprising the triangle.  Thus an interaction is either calculated in
its entirety or not at all.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The set of non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping spherical particles that represent a
triangle, for purposes of this pair style, are generated in the
following manner.  Assume the triangle is of type I, and sigma\_II has
been specified.  We want a set of spheres with centers in the plane of
the triangle, none of them larger in diameter than sigma\_II, which
completely cover the triangle’s area, but with minimal overlap and a
minimal total number of spheres.  This is done in a recursive manner.
Place a sphere at the centroid of the original triangle.  Calculate
what diameter it must have to just cover all 3 corner points of the
triangle.  If that diameter is equal to or smaller than sigma\_II, then
include a sphere of the calculated diameter in the set of covering
spheres.  It the diameter is larger than sigma\_II, then split the
triangle into 2 triangles by bisecting its longest side.  Repeat the
process on each sub\sphinxhyphen{}triangle, recursing as far as needed to generate a
set of covering spheres.  When finished, the original criteria are
met, and the set of covering spheres should be near minimal in number
and overlap, at least for input triangles with a reasonable
aspect\sphinxhyphen{}ratio.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The LJ interaction between 2 spheres on different triangles of types
I,J is computed with an arithmetic mixing of the sigma values of the 2
spheres and using the specified epsilon value for I,J atom types.
Note that because the sigma values for triangles spheres is computed
using only sigma\_II values, specific to the triangles’s type, this
means that any specified sigma\_IJ values (for I != J) are effectively
ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri/lj}, the following coefficients must be defined for
each pair of atoms types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command
as in the examples above, or in the data file or restart files read by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
epsilon (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sigma (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global cutoff
is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tri_lj:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for all of this pair style can be mixed.  The
default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_tri_lj:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Defining particles to be triangles so they participate in tri/tri or
tri/particle interactions requires the use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style tri}}}} command.

\section{pair\_style uf3 command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:pair-style-uf3-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{uf3/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{BodyFlag}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{uf3} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{uf3/kk}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
BodyFlag = Indicates whether to calculate only 2\PYGZhy{}body or 2 and 3\PYGZhy{}body interactions. Possible values: 2 or 3
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nb.uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nb}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NbSn.uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sn}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NbSn.uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Sn}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 27June2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{uf3} style computes the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_uf3:xie23}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Ultra\sphinxhyphen{}Fast Force Fields (UF3)}}}} potential, a machine\sphinxhyphen{}learning interatomic potential. In UF3,
the total energy of the system is defined via two\sphinxhyphen{} and three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interactions:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = \sum_{i,j} V_2(r_{ij}) + \sum_{i,j,k} V_3 (r_{ij},r_{ik},r_{jk}) \\
V_2(r_{ij}) & = \sum_{n=0}^N c_n B_n(r_{ij}) \\
V_3 (r_{ij},r_{ik},r_{jk}) & = \sum_{l=0}^{N_l} \sum_{m=0}^{N_m} \sum_{n=0}^{N_n} c_{l,m,n} B_l(r_{ij}) B_m(r_{ik}) B_n(r_{jk})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(V_2(r_{ij})\) and \(V_3 (r_{ij},r_{ik},r_{jk})\) are the
two\sphinxhyphen{} and three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions, respectively. For the two\sphinxhyphen{}body the
summation is over all neighbors J and for the three\sphinxhyphen{}body the summation
is over all neighbors J and K of atom I within a cutoff distance
determined from the potential files. \(B_n(r_{ij})\) are the cubic
b\sphinxhyphen{}spline basis, \(c_n\) and \(c_{l,m,n}\) are the machine\sphinxhyphen{}learned
interaction parameters and \(N\), \(N_l\), \(N_m\), and
\(N_n\) denote the number of basis functions per spline or tensor
spline dimension.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxstyleemphasis{uf3} style only a single pair\_coeff command is used to indicate the
UF3 LAMMPS potential file containing all the two\sphinxhyphen{} and three\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions
followed by N additional arguments specifying the mapping of UF3 elements to
LAMMPS atom types, where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
UF3 LAMMPS potential file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N elements names = mapping of UF3 elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, if a LAMMPS simulation contains 2 atom types (elements
‘A’ and ‘B’), the pair\_coeff command will be:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AB.uf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{B}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The AB.uf3 file should contain all two\sphinxhyphen{}body (A\sphinxhyphen{}A, A\sphinxhyphen{}B, B\sphinxhyphen{}B) and three\sphinxhyphen{}body
(A\sphinxhyphen{}A\sphinxhyphen{}A, A\sphinxhyphen{}A\sphinxhyphen{}B, A\sphinxhyphen{}B\sphinxhyphen{}B, B\sphinxhyphen{}A\sphinxhyphen{}A, B\sphinxhyphen{}A\sphinxhyphen{}B, B\sphinxhyphen{}B\sphinxhyphen{}B).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a value of “2” is specified in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair\_style uf3}} command,
only the two\sphinxhyphen{}body potentials are needed. For 3\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction the
first atom type is the central atom. We recommend using the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{generate\_uf3\_lammps\_pots.py}} script (found \sphinxhref{https://github.com/uf3/uf3/tree/develop/lammps\_plugin/scripts}{here}) for
generating the UF3 LAMMPS potential file from the UF3 JSON potentials.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
UF3 LAMMPS potential file in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potentials} directory of the LAMMPS
distribution have a “.uf3” suffix. The interaction block in UF3 LAMMPS potential
file should start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#UF3 POT}} and end with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}} characters.
Following shows the format of a generic 2\sphinxhyphen{}body and 3\sphinxhyphen{}body potential block in
UF3 LAMMPS potential file\sphinxhyphen{}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{}UF3 POT UNITS: units DATE: POT\PYGZus{}GEN\PYGZus{}DATE AUTHOR: AUTHOR\PYGZus{}NAME CITATION: CITE}
\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{n}{B}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ELEMENT1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ELEMENT2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{LEADING\PYGZus{}TRIM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TRAILING\PYGZus{}TRIM}
\PYG{n}{Rij\PYGZus{}CUTOFF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NUM\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}KNOTS}
\PYG{n}{BSPLINE\PYGZus{}KNOTS}
\PYG{n}{NUM\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}COEFF}
\PYG{n}{COEFF}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{}}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{}UF3 POT UNITS: units DATE: POT\PYGZus{}GEN\PYGZus{}DATE AUTHOR: AUTHOR\PYGZus{}NAME CITATION: CITE}
\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{n}{B}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ELEMENT1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ELEMENT2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ELEMENT3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{LEADING\PYGZus{}TRIM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TRAILING\PYGZus{}TRIM}
\PYG{n}{Rjk\PYGZus{}CUTOFF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rik\PYGZus{}CUTOFF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Rij\PYGZus{}CUTOFF}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NUM\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}KNOTS\PYGZus{}JK}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NUM\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}KNOTS\PYGZus{}IK}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NUM\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}KNOTS\PYGZus{}IJ}
\PYG{n}{BSPLINE\PYGZus{}KNOTS\PYGZus{}FOR\PYGZus{}JK}
\PYG{n}{BSPLINE\PYGZus{}KNOTS\PYGZus{}FOR\PYGZus{}IK}
\PYG{n}{BSPLINE\PYGZus{}KNOTS\PYGZus{}FOR\PYGZus{}IJ}
\PYG{n}{SHAPE\PYGZus{}OF\PYGZus{}COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[I][J][K]}
\PYG{n}{COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[0][0][K]}
\PYG{n}{COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[0][1][K]}
\PYG{n}{COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[0][2][K]}
\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{n}{COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[1][0][K]}
\PYG{n}{COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[1][1][K]}
\PYG{n}{COEFF\PYGZus{}MATRIX[1][2][K]}
\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second line indicates whether the block contains data for 2\sphinxhyphen{}body
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2B}}) or 3\sphinxhyphen{}body (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3B}}) interaction. This is followed by element
combination interaction, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LEADING\_TRIM}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TRAILING\_TRIM}}
number on the same line. The current implementation is only tested for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LEADING\_TRIM=0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TRAILING\_TRIM=3}}.
If other values are used LAMMPS is terminated after issuing an error message.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rij\_CUTOFF}} sets the 2\sphinxhyphen{}body cutoff for the interaction described
by the potential block. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NUM\_OF\_KNOTS}} is the number of knots
(or the length of the knot vector) present on the very next line. The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BSPLINE\_KNOTS}} line should contain all the knots in ascending order.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NUM\_OF\_COEFF}} is the number of coefficients in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{COEFF}} line.
All the numbers in the BSPLINE\_KNOTS and COEFF line should be space\sphinxhyphen{}separated.
Similar to the 2\sphinxhyphen{}body potential block, the third line sets the cutoffs and
length of the knots. The cutoff distance between atom\sphinxhyphen{}type I and J is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rij\_CUTOFF}}, atom\sphinxhyphen{}type I and K is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rik\_CUTOFF}} and between
J and K is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rjk\_CUTOFF}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current implementation only works for UF3 potentials with cutoff
distances for 3\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions that follows
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2Rij\_CUTOFF=2Rik\_CUTOFF=Rjk\_CUTOFF}} relation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BSPLINE\_KNOTS\_FOR\_JK}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BSPLINE\_KNOTS\_FOR\_IK}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BSPLINE\_KNOTS\_FOR\_IJ}} lines (note the order) contain the knots in
increasing order for atoms J and K, I and K, and atoms I and J
respectively. The number of knots is defined by the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NUM\_OF\_KNOTS\_*}} characters in the previous line.  The shape of
the coefficient matrix is defined on the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SHAPE\_OF\_COEFF\_MATRIX{[}I{]}{[}J{]}{[}K{]}}} line followed by the columns of
the coefficient matrix, one per line, as shown above. For example, if
the coefficient matrix has the shape of 8x8x13, then
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SHAPE\_OF\_COEFF\_MATRIX{[}I{]}{[}J{]}{[}K{]}}} will be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{8 8 13}} followed
by 64 (8x8) lines each containing 13 coefficients separated by space.

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS as described
above from values in the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart
files}}}}, since it is stored in potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_uf3:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ‘uf3’ pair style is part of the ML\sphinxhyphen{}UF3 package. It is only enabled
if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The UF3 LAMMPS potential file provided with LAMMPS (see the potentials
directory) are parameterized for metal {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single() function of ‘uf3’ pair style only return the 2\sphinxhyphen{}body
interaction energy.

\section{pair\_style ufm command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:pair-style-ufm-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{ufm/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ufm/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ufm/opt}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ufm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for \sphinxstyleemphasis{ufm} interactions (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ufm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.5}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ufm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prefactor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{10,100}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ufm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{epsilon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}prefactor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{ufm} computes pairwise interactions using the Uhlenbeck\sphinxhyphen{}Ford model (UFM) potential {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ufm:pl2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Paula Leite2016)}}}} which is given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = -\varepsilon\, \ln{\left[1-\exp{\left(-r^{2}/\sigma^{2}\right)}\right]} \qquad  r < r_c \\
\varepsilon & = p\,k_B\,T\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_c\) is the cutoff, \(\sigma\) is a distance\sphinxhyphen{}scale and
\(\epsilon\) is an energy\sphinxhyphen{}scale, i.e., a product of Boltzmann constant
\(k_B\), temperature \(T\) and the Uhlenbeck\sphinxhyphen{}Ford p\sphinxhyphen{}parameter which
is responsible
to control the softness of the interactions {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ufm:pl1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Paula Leite2017)}}}}.
This model is useful as a reference system for fluid\sphinxhyphen{}phase free\sphinxhyphen{}energy calculations {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ufm:pl2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Paula Leite2016)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above,
or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global \sphinxstyleemphasis{ufm}
cutoff is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}} command can be used to vary epsilon and sigma for this pair style over the course of a simulation, in which case
pair\_coeff settings for epsilon and sigma must still be specified, but will be
overridden.  For example these commands will vary the prefactor epsilon for
all pairwise interactions from 10.0 at the beginning to 100.0 at the end
of a run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{prefactor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{10,100}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{fix }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adapt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ufm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{epsilon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}prefactor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The thermodynamic integration procedure can be performed with this
potential using {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_adapt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix adapt}}}}. This command will
rescale the force on each atom by varying a scale variable, which
always starts with value 1.0. The syntax is the same described above,
however, changing epsilon to scale. A detailed explanation of how to
use this command and perform nonequilibrium thermodynamic integration
in LAMMPS is given in the paper by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ufm:freitas2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Freitas)}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ufm:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients and cutoff
distance for this pair style can be mixed. The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the
“pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table and tail are not relevant for this
pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vashishta}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiC.vashishta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vashishta} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{vashishta/table} styles compute the combined
2\sphinxhyphen{}body and 3\sphinxhyphen{}body family of potentials developed in the group of Priya
Vashishta and collaborators.  By combining repulsive, screened
Coulombic, screened charge\sphinxhyphen{}dipole, and dispersion interactions with a
bond\sphinxhyphen{}angle energy based on the Stillinger\sphinxhyphen{}Weber potential, this
potential has been used to describe a variety of inorganic compounds,
including SiO2 {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_vashishta:vashishta1990}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Vashishta1990}}}}, SiC
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_vashishta:vashishta2007}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Vashishta2007}}}}, and InP {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_vashishta:branicio2009}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Branicio2009}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential for the energy U of a system of atoms is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U & =  \sum_i^N \sum_{j > i}^N U_{ij}^{(2)} (r_{ij}) + \sum_i^N \sum_{j \neq i}^N \sum_{k > j, k \neq i}^N U_{ijk}^{(3)} (r_{ij}, r_{ik}, \theta_{ijk}) \\
U_{ij}^{(2)} (r) & =   \frac{H_{ij}}{r^{\eta_{ij}}} + \frac{Z_i Z_j}{r}\exp(-r/\lambda_{1,ij}) - \frac{D_{ij}}{r^4}\exp(-r/\lambda_{4,ij}) - \frac{W_{ij}}{r^6}, r < r_{c,{ij}} \\
U_{ijk}^{(3)}(r_{ij},r_{ik},\theta_{ijk}) & =  B_{ijk} \frac{\left[ \cos \theta_{ijk} - \cos \theta_{0ijk} \right]^2} {1+C_{ijk}\left[ \cos \theta_{ijk} - \cos \theta_{0ijk} \right]^2} \times \\
                 &  \exp \left( \frac{\gamma_{ij}}{r_{ij} - r_{0,ij}} \right) \exp \left( \frac{\gamma_{ik}}{r_{ik} - r_{0,ik}} \right), r_{ij} < r_{0,ij}, r_{ik} < r_{0,ik}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where we follow the notation used in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_vashishta:branicio2009}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Branicio2009}}}}.
\(U^2\) is a two\sphinxhyphen{}body term and U3 is a three\sphinxhyphen{}body term.  The
summation over two\sphinxhyphen{}body terms is over all neighbors J within
a cutoff distance = \(r_c\).  The twobody terms are shifted and
tilted by a linear function so that the energy and force are
both zero at \(r_c\). The summation over three\sphinxhyphen{}body terms
is over all neighbors \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{k} within a cut\sphinxhyphen{}off distance \(= r_0\),
where the exponential screening function becomes zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vashishta} style computes these formulas analytically.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vashishta/table} style tabulates the analytic values for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ntable}
points from cutinner to the cutoff of the potential.  The points are
equally spaced in R\textasciicircum{}2 space from cutinner\textasciicircum{}2 to cutoff\textasciicircum{}2.  For the
two\sphinxhyphen{}body term in the above equation, a linear interpolation for each
pairwise distance between adjacent points in the table.  In practice
the tabulated version can run 3\sphinxhyphen{}5x faster than the analytic version
with moderate to little loss of accuracy for Ntable values
between 10000 and 1000000. It is not recommended to use less than
5000 tabulation points.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a single pair\_coeff command is used with either style which
specifies a Vashishta potential file with parameters for all needed
elements.  These are mapped to LAMMPS atom types by specifying N
additional arguments after the filename in the pair\_coeff command,
where N is the number of LAMMPS atom types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N element names = mapping of Vashishta elements to atom types

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} page for alternate ways
to specify the path for the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, imagine a file SiC.vashishta has parameters for
Si and C.  If your LAMMPS simulation has 4 atoms types and you want
the first 3 to be Si, and the fourth to be C, you would use the following
pair\_coeff command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SiC.vashishta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Si}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first 2 arguments must be * * so as to span all LAMMPS atom types.
The first three Si arguments map LAMMPS atom types 1,2,3 to the Si
element in the file.  The final C argument maps LAMMPS atom type 4
to the C element in the file.  If a mapping value is specified as
NULL, the mapping is not performed.  This can be used when a \sphinxstyleemphasis{vashishta}
potential is used as part of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} pair style.  The NULL values
are placeholders for atom types that will be used with other
potentials.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Vashishta files in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{potentials} directory of the LAMMPS
distribution have a “.vashishta” suffix.  Lines that are not blank or
comments (starting with \#) define parameters for a triplet of
elements.  The parameters in a single entry correspond to the two\sphinxhyphen{}body
and three\sphinxhyphen{}body coefficients in the formulae above:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 1 (the center atom in a 3\sphinxhyphen{}body interaction)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
element 3

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{H} (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\eta\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(Z_i\) (electron charge units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(Z_j\) (electron charge units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\lambda_1\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{D} (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\lambda_4\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{W} (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{B} (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{C}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\cos\theta_0\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The non\sphinxhyphen{}annotated parameters are unitless.  The Vashishta potential
file must contain entries for all the elements listed in the
pair\_coeff command.  It can also contain entries for additional
elements not being used in a particular simulation; LAMMPS ignores
those entries.  For a single\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, only a single entry
is required (e.g. SiSiSi).  For a two\sphinxhyphen{}element simulation, the file
must contain 8 entries (for SiSiSi, SiSiC, SiCSi, SiCC, CSiSi, CSiC,
CCSi, CCC), that specify parameters for all permutations of the two
elements interacting in three\sphinxhyphen{}body configurations.  Thus for 3
elements, 27 entries would be required, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on the particular version of the Vashishta potential, the
values of these parameters may be keyed to the identities of zero,
one, two, or three elements.  In order to make the input file format
unambiguous, general, and simple to code, LAMMPS uses a slightly
confusing method for specifying parameters.  All parameters are
divided into two classes: two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body.  Two\sphinxhyphen{}body and
three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters are handled differently, as described below.
The two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters are \sphinxstyleemphasis{H}, \(\eta\), \(\lambda_1\),
\sphinxstyleemphasis{D}, \(\lambda_4\), \sphinxstyleemphasis{W}, \(r_c\), \(\gamma\),
and \(r_0\).  They appear in the above formulae with two subscripts.
The parameters \(Z_i\) and \(Z_j\) are also classified
as two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters, even
though they only have 1 subscript.  The three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters are \sphinxstyleemphasis{B},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{C}, \(\cos\theta_0\).  They appear in the above formulae with
three subscripts.  Two\sphinxhyphen{}body and three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters are handled
differently, as described below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first element in each entry is the center atom in a three\sphinxhyphen{}body
interaction, while the second and third elements are two neighbor
atoms. Three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for a central atom I and two neighbors J
and K are taken from the IJK entry.  Note that even though three\sphinxhyphen{}body
parameters do not depend on the order of J and K, LAMMPS stores
three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for both IJK and IKJ.  The user must ensure that
these values are equal.  Two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for an atom I interacting
with atom J are taken from the IJJ entry, where the second and third
elements are the same. Thus the two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters for Si interacting
with C come from the SiCC entry. Note that even though two\sphinxhyphen{}body
parameters (except possibly gamma and r0 in U3) do not depend on the
order of the two elements, LAMMPS will get the Si\sphinxhyphen{}C value from the
SiCC entry and the C\sphinxhyphen{}Si value from the CSiSi entry. The user must
ensure that these values are equal. Two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters appearing in
entries where the second and third elements are different are stored but
never used. It is good practice to enter zero for these values. Note
that the three\sphinxhyphen{}body function U3 above contains the two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters
\(\gamma\) and \(r_0\). So U3 for a central C atom bonded to
an Si atom and a
second C atom will take three\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters from the CSiC entry, but
two\sphinxhyphen{}body parameters from the CCC and CSiSi entries.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, where types I and J correspond to
two different element types, mixing is performed by LAMMPS as
described above from values in the potential file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, since it is stored in potential files.  Thus, you
need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands in an input
script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles are part of the MANYBODY package.  They are only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These pair styles requires the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} setting to be “on”
for pair interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Vashishta potential files provided with LAMMPS (see the potentials
directory) are parameterized for metal {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}.  You can
use the Vashishta potential with any LAMMPS units, but you would need
to create your own potential file with coefficients listed in the
appropriate units if your simulation does not use “metal” units.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{pair_vashishta:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none
