\index{pair\_style wf/cut@\spxentry{pair\_style wf/cut}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style wf/cut command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:pair-style-wf-cut-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = cutoff for wf interactions (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{wf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wf/cut} (Wang\sphinxhyphen{}Frenkel) style computes LJ\sphinxhyphen{}like potentials as
described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:wang2020}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Wang2020}}}}. This potential is by
construction finite ranged and it vanishes quadratically at the cutoff
distance, avoiding truncation, shifting, interpolation and other typical
procedures with the LJ potential. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{wf/cut} can be used when a
typical short\sphinxhyphen{}ranged potential with attraction is required. The
potential is given by which is given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\phi(r)= \epsilon \alpha \left(\left[{\sigma\over r}\right]^{2\mu} -1 \right)\left(\left[{r_c\over r}\right]^{2\mu}-1\right)^{2\nu}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\alpha=2\nu\left(\frac{r_c}{\sigma}\right)^{2\mu}\left[\frac{1+2\nu}{2\nu\left[(r_c/\sigma)^{2\mu}-1\right]}\right]^{2\nu+1}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}r_{min}=r_c\left[\frac{1+2\nu}{1+2\nu(r_c/\sigma)^{2\nu}}\right]^{1/{2\nu}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Comparison of the non\sphinxhyphen{}truncated Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones 12\sphinxhyphen{}6 potential (red curve),
and the WF potentials with \(\mu=1\) and \(\nu=1\) are shown in
the figure below. The blue curve has \(r_c =2.0\) and the green
curve has \(r_c =1.2\) and can be used to describe colloidal
interactions.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[scale=0.33]{{WF_LJ}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\nu\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\mu\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional. If not specified, the global cutoff
given in the pair\_style command is used.  The exponents \(\nu\) and
\(\mu\) are positive integers, usually set to 1. There is usually
little to be gained by choosing other values of \(\nu\) and
\(\mu\) (See discussion in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:wang2020}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Wang2020}}}})


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
mixing and table options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} tail and shift options are not
relevant for this pair style as it goes to zero at the cut\sphinxhyphen{}off radius.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}PAIR package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{pair_wf_cut:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Default:} none

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Wang2020)} X. Wang, S. Ramirez\sphinxhyphen{}Hinestrosa, J. Dobnikar, and D. Frenkel, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 22, 10624 (2020).

\index{pair\_style ylz@\spxentry{pair\_style ylz}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style ylz command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:pair-style-ylz-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ylz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff for interactions (distance units)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{ylz}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2.6}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2.6}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Nov2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylz} (Yuan\sphinxhyphen{}Li\sphinxhyphen{}Zhang) style computes an anisotropic interaction
between pairs of coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained particles considering the relative
particle orientations. This potential was originally developed as a
particle\sphinxhyphen{}based solvent\sphinxhyphen{}free model for biological membranes
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ylz:yuan}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Yuan2010a)}}}}.  Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gayberne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style gayberne}}}}, whose orientation dependence is strictly derived from
the closest distance between two ellipsoidal rigid bodies, the
orientation\sphinxhyphen{}dependence of this pair style is mathematically defined such
that the particles can self\sphinxhyphen{}assemble into one\sphinxhyphen{}particle\sphinxhyphen{}thick fluid
membranes.  The potential of this pair style is described by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U ( \mathbf{r}_{ij}, \mathbf{n}_i, \mathbf{n}_j ) =\left\{\begin{matrix} {u}_R(r)+\left [ 1-\phi (\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij}, \mathbf{n}_i, \mathbf{n}_j ) \right ]\epsilon, ~~ r<{r}_{min} \\ {u}_A(r)\phi (\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij}, \mathbf{n}_i, \mathbf{n}_j ),~~  {r}_{min}<r<{r}_{c} \\ \end{matrix}\right.\\\\ \phi (\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij}, \mathbf{n}_i, \mathbf{n}_j )=1+\left [  \mu (a(\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij}, \mathbf{n}_i, \mathbf{n}_j )-1) \right ] \\\\a(\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij}, \mathbf{n}_i, \mathbf{n}_j )=(\mathbf{n}_i\times\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij} )\cdot (\mathbf{n}_j\times\mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij} )+{\beta}(\mathbf{n}_i-\mathbf{n}_j)\cdot \mathbf{\hat{r}}_{ij}-\beta^{2}\\\\  {u}_R(r)=\epsilon \left [ \left ( \frac{{r}_{min}}{r} \right )^{4}-2\left ( \frac{{r}_{min}}{r}\right )^{2} \right ] \\\\ {u}_A(r)=-\epsilon\;cos^{2\zeta }\left [ \frac{\pi}{2}\frac{\left ( {r}-{r}_{min} \right )}{\left ( {r}_{c}-{r}_{min} \right )} \right ]\\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\mathbf{r}_{i}\) and \(\mathbf{r}_{j}\) are the center
position vectors of particles i and j, respectively,
\(\mathbf{r}_{ij}=\mathbf{r}_{i}-\mathbf{r}_{j}\) is the
inter\sphinxhyphen{}particle distance vector, \(r=\left|\mathbf{r}_{ij} \right|\)
and \({\hat{\mathbf{r}}}_{ij}=\mathbf{r}_{ij}/r\).  The unit vectors
\(\mathbf{n}_{i}\) and \(\mathbf{n}_{j}\) represent the axes of
symmetry of particles i and j, respectively, \(u_R\) and \(u_A\)
are the repulsive and attractive potentials, \(\phi\) is an angular
function which depends on the relative orientation between pair
particles, \(\mu\) is the parameter related to the bending rigidity
of the membrane, \(\beta\) is the parameter related to the
spontaneous curvature, and \(\epsilon\) is the energy unit,
respectively.   The \(\zeta\) controls the slope of the attractive
branch and hence the diffusivity of the particles in the in\sphinxhyphen{}plane
direction of the membrane.  \({r}_{c}\) is the cutoff radius,
\(r_{min}\) is the distance which minimizes the potential energy
\(u_{A}(r)\) and \(r_{min}=2^{1/6}\sigma\), where \(\sigma\)
is the length unit.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style is suited for solvent\sphinxhyphen{}free coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained simulations of
biological systems involving lipid bilayer membranes, such as vesicle
shape transformations {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ylz:yuan}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Yuan2010b)}}}}, nanoparticle
endocytosis {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ylz:huang}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Huang)}}}}, modeling of red blood cell membranes
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ylz:fu}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Fu)}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ylz:appshaw}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Appshaw)}}}}, and modeling of cell
elasticity {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_ylz:becton}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Becton)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use of this pair style requires the NVE, NVT, or NPT fixes with the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{asphere} extension (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_asphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/asphere}}}}) in
order to integrate particle rotation.  Additionally, {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style
ellipsoid}}}} should be used since it defines the rotational
state of each particle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above,
or in the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands, or by
mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) = well depth (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) = minimum effective particle radii (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\zeta\) = tuning parameter for the slope of the attractive branch

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\mu\) = parameter related to bending rigidity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\beta\) = parameter related to the spontaneous curvature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global
cutoff specified in the pair\_style command is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the epsilon and sigma coefficients
and cutoff distance for this pair style can be mixed.  The default mix
value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant for
this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need to be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_ylz:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ylz} style is part of the ASPHERE package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires that atoms store torque and a quaternion to
represent their orientation, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}.  It also requires they store a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom {\hyperref[\detokenize{set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{shape}}}}.  The particles cannot store a per\sphinxhyphen{}particle diameter.  To avoid
being mistakenly considered as point particles, the shape parameters ought
to be non\sphinxhyphen{}spherical, like {[}1 0.99 0.99{]}.  Unlike the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_resquared::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{resquared}}}} pair style for which the shape directly determines the
mathematical expressions of the potential, the shape parameters for this
pair style is only involved in the computation of the moment of inertia
and thus only influences the rotational dynamics of individual
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires that \sphinxstylestrong{all} atoms are ellipsoids as defined by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style ellipsoid}}}} command.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{yukawa} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = A \frac{e^{- \kappa r}}{r} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy*distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global yukawa
cutoff is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script

{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\section{pair\_style yukawa/colloid command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:pair-style-yukawa-colloid-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{yukawa/colloid/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yukawa/colloid/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yukawa/colloid/omp}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{yukawa/colloid} computes pairwise interactions with the formula
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{A}{\kappa} e^{- \kappa (r - (r_i + r_j))} \qquad r < r_c\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_i\) and \(r_j\) are the radii of the two particles
and \(r_c\) is the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_yukawa::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style yukawa}}}}, this functional
form arises from the Coulombic interaction between two colloid
particles, screened due to the presence of an electrolyte, see the
book by {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:safran}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Safran}}}} for a derivation in the context of DLVO
theory.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_yukawa::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Pair\_style yukawa}}}} is a screened Coulombic
potential between two point\sphinxhyphen{}charges and uses no such approximation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential applies to nearby particle pairs for which the Derjagin
approximation holds, meaning \(h << r_i + r_j\), where \sphinxstyleemphasis{h} is the
surface\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}surface separation of the two particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When used in combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_colloid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style colloid}}}},
the two terms become the so\sphinxhyphen{}called DLVO potential, which combines
electrostatic repulsion and van der Waals attraction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A (energy/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The prefactor A is determined from the relationship between surface
charge and surface potential due to the presence of electrolyte.  Note
that the A for this potential style has different units than the A
used in {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_yukawa::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style yukawa}}}}.  For low surface
potentials, i.e. less than about 25 mV, A can be written as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}A = 2 \pi R\varepsilon\varepsilon_0 \kappa \psi^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{R} = colloid radius (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\varepsilon_0\) = permittivity of free space (charge\textasciicircum{}2/energy/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\varepsilon\) = relative permittivity of fluid medium (dimensionless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\kappa\) = inverse screening length (1/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\psi\) = surface potential (energy/charge units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global
yukawa/colloid cutoff is used.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs I,J and I != J, the A coefficient and cutoff
distance for this pair style can be mixed.  A is an energy value mixed
like a LJ epsilon.  The default mix value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the
“pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} shift
option for the energy of the pair interaction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant
for this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the

\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{pair_yukawa_colloid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This style is part of the COLLOID package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style requires that atoms be finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spheres with a
diameter, as defined by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style sphere}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}particle polydispersity is not yet supported by this pair style;
per\sphinxhyphen{}type polydispersity is allowed.  This means all particles of the
same type must have the same diameter.  Each type can have a different
diameter.

\section{pair\_style zbl command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:pair-style-zbl-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{zbl/gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zbl/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{zbl/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zbl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{inner}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{outer}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
inner = distance where switching function begins

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
outer = global cutoff for ZBL interaction

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zbl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{73.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{73.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{14.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{14.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{zbl} computes the Ziegler\sphinxhyphen{}Biersack\sphinxhyphen{}Littmark (ZBL) screened nuclear
repulsion for describing high\sphinxhyphen{}energy collisions between atoms.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_zbl:ziegler}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ziegler)}}}}. It includes an additional switching function
that ramps the energy, force, and curvature smoothly to zero
between an inner and outer cutoff. The potential
energy due to a pair of atoms at a distance r\_ij is given by:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E^{ZBL}_{ij} & = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{Z_i Z_j \,e^2}{r_{ij}} \phi(r_{ij}/a)+ S(r_{ij})\\
a & =  \frac{0.46850}{Z_{i}^{0.23} + Z_{j}^{0.23}}\\
\phi(x) & =  0.18175e^{-3.19980x} + 0.50986e^{-0.94229x} + 0.28022e^{-0.40290x} + 0.02817e^{-0.20162x}\\\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxstyleemphasis{e} is the electron charge, \(\epsilon_0\) is the electrical
permittivity of vacuum, and \(Z_i\) and \(Z_j\) are the nuclear
charges of the
two atoms.  The switching function \(S(r)\) is identical to that used by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_gromacs::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/gromacs}}}}.  Here, the inner and outer
cutoff are the same for all pairs of atom types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atom types
via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above,
or in the LAMMPS data file.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(Z_i\) (atomic number for first atom type, e.g. 13.0 for aluminum)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(Z_j\) (ditto for second atom type)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values of \(Z_i\) and \(Z_j\) are normally equal to the atomic
numbers of the two atom types. Thus, the user may optionally
specify only the coefficients for each \(i==i\) pair, and rely
on the obvious mixing rule for cross interactions (see below).
Note that when \(i==i\) it is required that \(Z_i == Z_j\).
When used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid/overlay}}}} and pairs are
assigned
to more than one sub\sphinxhyphen{}style, the mixing rule is not used and
each pair of types interacting with the ZBL sub\sphinxhyphen{}style must
be included in a pair\_coeff command.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The numerical values of the exponential decay constants in the
screening function depend on the unit of distance. In the above
equation they are given for units of Angstroms. LAMMPS will
automatically convert these values to the distance unit of the
specified LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} setting.  The values of Z should
always be given as multiples of a proton’s charge, e.g. 29.0 for
copper.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For atom type pairs \sphinxstyleemphasis{i,j} and \(i \neq i\), the \(Z_i\) and
\(Z_j\) coefficients
can be mixed by taking \(Z_i\) and \(Z_j\) from the values
specified for
\(i == i\) and \(j == j\) cases. When used
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{hybrid/overlay}}}} and pairs are assigned
to more than one sub\sphinxhyphen{}style, the mixing rule is not used and
each pair of types interacting with the ZBL sub\sphinxhyphen{}style
must be included in a pair\_coeff command.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} mix option has no effect on
the mixing behavior

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ZBL pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift option, since the ZBL interaction is already smoothed to 0.0 at
the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}} table option is not relevant for
this pair style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
tail option for adding long\sphinxhyphen{}range tail corrections to energy and
pressure, since there are no corrections for a potential that goes to
0.0 at the cutoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not write information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands must be
specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style can only be used via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{pair} keyword of the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.  It does not support the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\label{\detokenize{pair_zbl:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{pair\_style zero@\spxentry{pair\_style zero}}\ignorespaces 

\section{pair\_style zero command}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zero:pair-style-zero-command}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zero:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{pair_zero::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zero:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cutoff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[nocoeff]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[full]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero = style name of this pair style

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff = global cutoff (distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nocoeff = ignore all pair\_coeff parameters (optional)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
full = build full neighbor list (optional)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zero:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nocoeff}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zero:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define a global or per\sphinxhyphen{}type cutoff length for the purpose of
building a neighbor list and acquiring ghost atoms, but do
not compute any pairwise forces or energies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be useful for fixes or computes which require a neighbor list
to enumerate pairs of atoms within some cutoff distance, but when
pairwise forces are not otherwise needed.  Examples are the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_bond_create::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix bond/create}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_rdf::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute rdf}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_voronoi_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute voronoi/atom}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}} command can be
used to ensure communication of ghost atoms even when a pair style is
not defined, but it will not trigger neighbor list generation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} flag allows to read data files with a PairCoeff
section for any pair style. Similarly, any pair\_coeff commands
will only be checked for the atom type numbers and the rest ignored.
In this case, only the global cutoff will be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 3Nov2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{full} flag builds a full neighbor list instead of the default
half neighbor list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each pair of atoms
types via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands, or by mixing as described below:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cutoff (distance units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This coefficient is optional.  If not specified, the global cutoff
specified in the pair\_style command is used. If the pair\_style has
been specified with the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} flag, then a cutoff
pair coefficient is ignored.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Mixing, shift, table, tail correction, restart, rRESPA info}
\label{\detokenize{pair_zero:mixing-shift-table-tail-correction-restart-rrespa-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The cutoff distance for this pair style can be mixed.  The default mix
value is \sphinxstyleemphasis{geometric}.  See the “pair\_modify” command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style does not support the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_modify}}}}
shift, table, and tail options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style writes its information to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so pair\_style and pair\_coeff commands do not need
to be specified in an input script that reads a restart file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pair style supports the use of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inner}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{outer} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{run_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run\_style respa}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{bond\_style bpm/rotational@\spxentry{bond\_style bpm/rotational}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style bpm/rotational command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:bond-style-bpm-rotational-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rotational}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optional keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{break}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} values = fix\_ID N attributes ...
   * fix\_ID = ID of associated internal fix to store data
   * N = prepare data for output every this many timesteps
   * attributes = zero or more of the below attributes may be appended

     \sphinxstyleemphasis{id1, id2} = IDs of two atoms in the bond
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{time} = the timestep the bond broke
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{x, y, z} = the center of mass position of the two atoms when the bond broke (distance units)
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{x/ref, y/ref, z/ref} = the initial center of mass position of the two atoms (distance units)

\sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   bonded particles will still interact with pair forces

\sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   smooths bond forces near the breaking point

\sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   normalizes normal and shear forces by the reference length

\sphinxstyleemphasis{break} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   indicates whether bonds break during a run
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rotational}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.20}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.04}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.04}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.04}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.002}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.002}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rotational}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{store}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myfix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id2}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.broken}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[3]}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpm/rotational} bond style computes forces and torques based on
deviations from the initial reference state of the two atoms.  The
reference state is stored by each bond when it is first computed in
the setup of a run. Data is then preserved across run commands and is
written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}} such that restarting
the system will not reset the reference state of a bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Forces include a normal and tangential component. The base normal force
has a magnitude of
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_r = k_r (r - r_0)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k_r\) is a stiffness and \(r\) is the current distance and
\(r_0\) is the initial distance between the two particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A tangential force is applied perpendicular to the normal direction
which is proportional to the tangential shear displacement with a
stiffness of \(k_s\). This tangential force also induces a torque.
In addition, bending and twisting torques are also applied to
particles which are proportional to angular bending and twisting
displacements with stiffnesses of \(k_b\) and \(k_t\),
respectively.  Details on the calculations of shear displacements and
angular displacements can be found in {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:wang2009}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Wang)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:wang2009b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Wang and Mora)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bonds will break under sufficient stress. A breaking criterion is calculated
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}B = \mathrm{max}\left\{0, \frac{f_r}{f_{r,c}} + \frac{|f_s|}{f_{s,c}} +
    \frac{|\tau_b|}{\tau_{b,c}} + \frac{|\tau_t|}{\tau_{t,c}} \right\}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(|f_s|\) is the magnitude of the shear force and
\(|\tau_b|\) and \(|\tau_t|\) are the magnitudes of the
bending and twisting torques, respectively. The corresponding variables
\(f_{r,c}\) \(f_{s,c}\), \(\tau_{b,c}\), and
\(\tau_{t,c}\) are critical limits to each force or torque.  If
\(B\) is ever equal to or exceeds one, the bond will break.  This
is done by setting the bond type to 0 such that forces and
torques are no longer computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After computing the base magnitudes of the forces and torques, they
can be optionally multiplied by an extra factor \(w\) to smoothly
interpolate forces and torques to zero as the bond breaks. This term
is calculated as \(w = (1.0 - B^4)\). This smoothing factor can be added
or removed by setting the \sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finally, additional damping forces and torques are applied to the two
particles. A force is applied proportional to the difference in the
normal velocity of particles using a similar construction as
dissipative particle dynamics {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:groot3}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Groot)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_D = - \gamma_n w (\hat{r} \bullet \vec{v})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\gamma_n\) is the damping strength, \(\hat{r}\) is the
radial normal vector, and \(\vec{v}\) is the velocity difference
between the two particles. Similarly, tangential forces are applied to
each atom proportional to the relative differences in sliding
velocities with a constant prefactor \(\gamma_s\) {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:wang20152}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Wang et
al.)}}}} along with their associated torques. The rolling and
twisting components of the relative angular velocities of the two
atoms are also damped by applying torques with prefactors of
\(\gamma_r\) and \(\gamma_t\), respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k_r\)           (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k_s\)           (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k_t\)           (force*distance/radians units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k_b\)           (force*distance/radians units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(f_{r,c}\)       (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(f_{s,c}\)       (force units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\tau_{b,c}\)    (force*distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\tau_{t,c}\)    (force*distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_n\)      (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_s\)      (force/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_r\)      (force*distance/velocity units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_t\)      (force*distance/velocity units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the radial and shear forces
will be normalized by \(r_0\) such that \(k_r\) and \(k_s\)
must be given in force units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, pair forces are not calculated between bonded particles.
Pair forces can alternatively be overlaid on top of bond forces by setting
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}. These settings require specific
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings described in the
restrictions.  Further details can be found in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bpm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{how to}}}}
page on BPMs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{break} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, LAMMPS assumes bonds should not break
during a simulation run. This will prevent some unnecessary calculation.
However, if a bond reaches a damage criterion greater than one,
it will trigger an error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} keyword is used, an internal fix will track bonds that
break during the simulation. Whenever a bond breaks, data is processed
and transferred to an internal fix labeled \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID}. This allows the
local data to be accessed by other LAMMPS commands. Following this optional
keyword, a list of one or more attributes is specified.  These include the
IDs of the two atoms in the bond. The other attributes for the two atoms
include the timestep during which the bond broke and the current/initial
center of mass position of the two atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Data is continuously accumulated over intervals of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. At the end of each interval, all of the saved accumulated
data is deleted to make room for new data. Individual datum may
therefore persist anywhere between \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} timesteps depending on
when they are saved. This data can be accessed using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID} and a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command. To ensure all data is output,
the dump frequency should correspond to the same interval of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. A dump frequency of an integer multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} can be used
to regularly output a sample of the accumulated data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that when unbroken bonds are dumped to a file via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command, bonds with type 0 (broken bonds)
are not included.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command can also be used to
query the status of broken bonds or permanently delete them, e.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stats}
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart and other info}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:restart-and-other-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style writes the reference state of each bond to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}. Loading a restart file will
properly resume bonds. However, the reference state is NOT
written to data files. Therefore reading a data file will not
restore bonds and will cause their reference states to be redefined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} option is used, an internal fix will calculate
a local vector or local array depending on the number of input values.
The length of the vector or number of rows in the array is the number
of recorded, broken bonds.  If a single input is specified, a local
vector is produced. If two or more inputs are specified, a local array
is produced where the number of columns = the number of inputs.  The
vector or array can be accessed by any command that uses local values
from a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array will be floating point values that correspond to
the specified attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single() function of this bond style returns 0.0 for the energy
of a bonded interaction, since energy is not conserved in these
dissipative potentials.  It also returns only the normal component of
the bonded interaction force.  However, the single() function also
calculates 7 extra bond quantities.  The first 4 are data from the
reference state of the bond including the initial distance between particles
\(r_0\) followed by the \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) components
of the initial unit vector pointing to particle I from particle J. The next 3
quantities (5\sphinxhyphen{}7) are the  \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) components
of the total force, including normal and tangential contributions, acting
on particle I.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These extra quantities can be accessed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute bond/local}}}}
command, as \sphinxstyleemphasis{b1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{b2}, …, \sphinxstyleemphasis{b7}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style is part of the BPM package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default if pair interactions between bonded atoms are to be disabled,
this bond style requires setting

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} must be set to bond off.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair}
keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, this bond style alternatively requires setting

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpm/rotational} style requires {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom style bpm/sphere}}}}.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_bpm_sphere::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/bpm/sphere}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_rotational:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The option defaults are \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{break} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}

\index{bond\_style bpm/spring@\spxentry{bond\_style bpm/spring}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style bpm/spring command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:bond-style-bpm-spring-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optional keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{break}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} values = fix\_ID N attributes ...
   * fix\_ID = ID of associated internal fix to store data
   * N = prepare data for output every this many timesteps
   * attributes = zero or more of the below attributes may be appended

     \sphinxstyleemphasis{id1, id2} = IDs of two atoms in the bond
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{time} = the timestep the bond broke
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{x, y, z} = the center of mass position of the two atoms when the bond broke (distance units)
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{x/ref, y/ref, z/ref} = the initial center of mass position of the two atoms (distance units)

\sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   bonded particles will still interact with pair forces

\sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   smooths bond forces near the breaking point

\sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   normalizes bond forces by the reference length

\sphinxstyleemphasis{break} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
   indicates whether bonds break during a run
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spring}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bpm}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{spring}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myfix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id2}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.broken}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f\PYGZus{}myfix[3]}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpm/spring} bond style computes forces based on
deviations from the initial reference state of the two atoms.  The
reference state is stored by each bond when it is first computed in
the setup of a run. Data is then preserved across run commands and is
written to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}} such that restarting
the system will not reset the reference state of a bond.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style only applies central\sphinxhyphen{}body forces which conserve the
translational and rotational degrees of freedom of a bonded set of
particles based on a model described by Clemmer and Robbins
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:fragment-clemmer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Clemmer)}}}}. The force has a magnitude of
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F = k (r - r_0) w\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k\) is a stiffness, \(r\) is the current distance
and \(r_0\) is the initial distance between the two particles, and
\(w\) is an optional smoothing factor discussed below. Bonds will
break at a strain of \(\epsilon_c\).  This is done by setting
the bond type to 0 such that forces are no longer computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An additional damping force is applied to the bonded
particles.  This forces is proportional to the difference in the
normal velocity of particles using a similar construction as
dissipative particle dynamics {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:groot4}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Groot)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_D = - \gamma w (\hat{r} \bullet \vec{v})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\gamma\) is the damping strength, \(\hat{r}\) is the
radial normal vector, and \(\vec{v}\) is the velocity difference
between the two particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The smoothing factor \(w\) can be added or removed by setting the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{smooth} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, respectively. It is constructed such
that forces smoothly go to zero, avoiding discontinuities, as bonds
approach the critical strain
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}w = 1.0 - \left( \frac{r - r_0}{r_0 \epsilon_c} \right)^8 .\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k\)             (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_c\)    (unit less)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)        (force/velocity units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{normalize} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, the elastic bond force will be
normalized by \(r_0\) such that \(k\) must be given in force units.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, pair forces are not calculated between bonded particles.
Pair forces can alternatively be overlaid on top of bond forces by setting
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair} keyword to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}. These settings require specific
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings described in the
restrictions.  Further details can be found in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bpm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{how to}}}}
page on BPMs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{break} keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}, LAMMPS assumes bonds should not break
during a simulation run. This will prevent some unnecessary calculation.
However, if a bond reaches a strain greater than \(\epsilon_c\),
it will trigger an error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} keyword is used, an internal fix will track bonds that
break during the simulation. Whenever a bond breaks, data is processed
and transferred to an internal fix labeled \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID}. This allows the
local data to be accessed by other LAMMPS commands. Following this optional
keyword, a list of one or more attributes is specified.  These include the
IDs of the two atoms in the bond. The other attributes for the two atoms
include the timestep during which the bond broke and the current/initial
center of mass position of the two atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Data is continuously accumulated over intervals of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. At the end of each interval, all of the saved accumulated
data is deleted to make room for new data. Individual datum may
therefore persist anywhere between \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} timesteps depending on
when they are saved. This data can be accessed using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID} and a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command. To ensure all data is output,
the dump frequency should correspond to the same interval of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. A dump frequency of an integer multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} can be used
to regularly output a sample of the accumulated data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that when unbroken bonds are dumped to a file via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command, bonds with type 0 (broken bonds)
are not included.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command can also be used to
query the status of broken bonds or permanently delete them, e.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stats}
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart and other info}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:restart-and-other-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style writes the reference state of each bond to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}. Loading a restart
file will properly restore bonds. However, the reference state is NOT
written to data files. Therefore reading a data file will not
restore bonds and will cause their reference states to be redefined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} option is used, an internal fix will calculate
a local vector or local array depending on the number of input values.
The length of the vector or number of rows in the array is the number
of recorded, broken bonds.  If a single input is specified, a local
vector is produced. If two or more inputs are specified, a local array
is produced where the number of columns = the number of inputs.  The
vector or array can be accessed by any command that uses local values
from a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array will be floating point values that correspond to
the specified attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single() function of this bond style returns 0.0 for the energy
of a bonded interaction, since energy is not conserved in these
dissipative potentials.  The single() function also calculates an
extra bond quantity, the initial distance \(r_0\). This
extra quantity can be accessed by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute bond/local}}}} command as \sphinxstyleemphasis{b1}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_bpm_spring:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style is part of the BPM package.  It is only enabled if

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default if pair interactions between bonded atoms are to be disabled,
this bond style requires setting

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{special\PYGZus{}bonds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lj}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{coul}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} must be set to bond off.  If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{overlay/pair}
keyword is set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes}, this bond style alternatively requires setting

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.0}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_class2:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K_2 (r - r_0)^2 + K_3 (r - r_0)^3 + K_4 (r - r_0)^4\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium bond distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_class2:bond-sun}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sun)}}}} for a description of the COMPASS class2 force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_2\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_3\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}3)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_4\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}4)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script

\section{bond\_style fene/nm command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_fene:bond-style-fene-nm-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fene}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{nm}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_fene:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fene}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{nm}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.25344}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.12246}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_fene:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -0.5 K R_0^2  \ln \left[ 1 - \left(\frac{r}{R_0}\right)^2\right] + 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} - \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right] + \epsilon\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
to define a finite extensible nonlinear elastic (FENE) potential
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_fene:fene-kremer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kremer)}}}}, used for bead\sphinxhyphen{}spring polymer models.  The first
term is attractive, the second Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones term is repulsive.  The
first term extends to \(R_0\), the maximum extent of the bond.  The second
term is cutoff at \(2^\frac{1}{6} \sigma\), the minimum of the LJ potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene/nm} bond style substitutes the standard LJ potential with the generalized LJ potential
in the same form as in pair style {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_nm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{nm/cut}}}}. The bond energy is then given by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -0.5 K R_0^2  \ln \left[ 1 - \left(\frac{r}{R_0}\right)^2\right] + \frac{E_0}{(n-m)} \left[ m \left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)^n - n \left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)^m \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} style, the generalized Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones is cut off at
the potential minimum, \(r_0\), to be repulsive only.  The following
coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in the data file or
restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene/nm} style, the following coefficients are used.  Please
note, that the standard LJ potential and thus the regular FENE potential
is recovered for (n=12 m=6) and \(r_0 = 2^\frac{1}{6} \sigma\).
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(E_0\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(m\) (unitless)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}

You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script

instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\subsection{Restrictions}

\sphinxAtStartPar

style.  LAMMPS will issue a warning it that’s not the case.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_fene_expand:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene/expand} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -0.5 K R_0^2 \ln \left[1 -\left( \frac{\left(r - \Delta\right)}{R_0}\right)^2 \right] + 4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{\left(r - \Delta\right)}\right)^{12} - \left(\frac{\sigma}{\left(r - \Delta\right)}\right)^6 \right] + \epsilon\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
to define a finite extensible nonlinear elastic (FENE) potential
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_fene_expand:feneexpand-kremer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Kremer)}}}}, used for bead\sphinxhyphen{}spring polymer models.  The first
term is attractive, the second Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones term is repulsive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene/expand} bond style is similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} except that an extra
shift factor of \(\Delta\) (positive or negative) is added to \(r\) to
effectively change the bead size of the bonded atoms.  The first term
now extends to \(R_0 + \Delta\) and the second term is cutoff at \(2^\frac{1}{6} \sigma + \Delta\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\sigma\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar

They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0128}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.375}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.37}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0730}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.148}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.63}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_gaussian:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} bond style uses the potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -k_B T ln\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{A_i}{w_i \sqrt{\pi/2}} exp\left( \frac{-2(r-r_{i})^2}{w_i^2}\right)\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This analytical form is a suitable potential for obtaining mesoscale
effective force fields which can reproduce target atomistic
distributions {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_gaussian:milano0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Milano)}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(T\) temperature at which the potential was derived

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) (integer \textgreater{}=1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_1\) (\textgreater{} 0, distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(w_1\) (\textgreater{} 0, distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_1\) (\textgreater{}= 0, distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_n\) (\textgreater{} 0, distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(w_n\) (\textgreater{} 0, distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_n\) (\textgreater{}= 0, distance)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_gaussian:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
doc page for more info.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_gromos:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gromos} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r^2 - r_0^2)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium bond distance.  Note that the usual 1/4
factor is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}4)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
