\section{bond\_style harmonic/restrain command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:bond-style-harmonic-restrain-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{restrain}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 28Mar2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/restrain} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_{t=0})^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_{t=0}\) is the distance between the bonded atoms at the
beginning of the first {\hyperref[\detokenize{run::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{run}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{minimize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{minimize}}}}
command after the bond style has been defined (\sphinxstyleemphasis{t=0}).  Note that the
usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).  This will effectively
restrain bonds to their initial length, whatever that is.  This is where
this bond style differs from {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond style harmonic}}}}
where the bond length is set through the per bond type coefficients.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficient must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style differs from other options to add harmonic restraints
like {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_restrain::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix restrain}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_list::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair style list}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_colvars::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix colvars}}}} in that it requires a
bond topology, and thus the defined bonds will trigger exclusion of
special neighbors from the neighbor list according to the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings.


\subsection{Restart info}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:restart-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style supports the {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands. The state of the initial
bond lengths is stored with restart files and read back.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_restrain:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style maintains internal data to determine the original bond
lengths \(r_{t=0}\).  This information will be written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}} but \sphinxstylestrong{not} to {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data
files}}}}.  Thus, continuing a simulation is \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} possible
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}.  When using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data
command}}}}, the reference bond lengths \(r_{t=0}\) will be
re\sphinxhyphen{}initialized from the current geometry.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style cannot be used with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake or fix rattle}}}}, with {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_filter_corotate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix filter/corotate}}}}, or
any {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_lj_cut_tip4p::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{tip4p pair style}}}} since there is no specific
equilibrium distance for a given bond type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}},  {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_harmonic}}}},

\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift:bond-style-harmonic-shift-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift::doc}}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/shift} bond style is a shifted harmonic bond that uses
the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{U_{\text{min}}}{(r_0-r_c)^2} \left[ (r-r_0)^2-(r_c-r_0)^2 \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium bond distance, and \(r_c\) the critical distance.
The potential is \(-U_{\text{min}}\) at \(r0\) and zero at \(r_c\). The spring constant is
\(k = U_{\text{min}} / [ 2 (r_0-r_c)^2]\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(U_{\text{min}}\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift_cut:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{cut}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_harmonic_shift_cut:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/shift/cut} bond style is a shifted harmonic bond that
uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{U_{\text{min}}}{(r_0-r_c)^2} \left[ (r-r_0)^2-(r_c-r_0)^2 \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium bond distance, and rc the critical distance.
The bond potential is zero for distances \(r > r_c\). The potential is \(-U_{\text{min}}\)
at \(r_0\) and zero at \(r_c\). The spring constant is \(k = U_{\text{min}} / [ 2 (r_0-r_c)^2]\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(U_{\text{min}}\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_c\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\section{bond\_style hybrid command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:bond-style-hybrid-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style1,style2 = list of one or more bond styles

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fene}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} style enables the use of multiple bond styles in one
simulation.  A bond style is assigned to each bond type.  For example,
bonds in a polymer flow (of bond type 1) could be computed with a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} potential and bonds in the wall boundary (of bond type 2) could
be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} potential.  The assignment of bond type
to style is made via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command or in
the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the bond\_coeff commands, the name of a bond style must be added
after the bond type, with the remaining coefficients being those
appropriate to that style.  In the example above, the 2 bond\_coeff
commands set bonds of bond type 1 to be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic}
potential with coefficients 80.0, 1.2 for \(K\), \(r_0\).  All other bond types
(2\sphinxhyphen{}N) are computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{fene} potential with coefficients 30.0,
1.5, 1.0, 1.0 for \(K\), \(R_0\), \(\epsilon\), \(\sigma\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If bond coefficients are specified in the data file read via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, then the same rule applies.
E.g. “harmonic” or “fene” must be added after the bond type, for each
line in the “Bond Coeffs” section, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Bond Coeffs

1 harmonic 80.0 1.2
2 fene 30.0 1.5 1.0 1.0
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A bond style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} with no additional coefficients can be used in
place of a bond style, either in a input script bond\_coeff command or
in the data file, if you desire to turn off interactions for specific
bond types.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_hybrid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the MOLECULE
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike other bond styles, the hybrid bond style does not store bond
coefficient info for individual sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles in {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data files}}}}.  Thus when restarting a
simulation, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the bond\_coeff commands.

\section{bond\_style lepton command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton:bond-style-lepton-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = optional arguments

\end{itemize}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto\_offset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_offset}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto\_offset} = offset the potential energy so that the value at r0 is 0.0 (default)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_offset} = do not offset the potential energy
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}offset}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k*r\PYGZca{}2; k=250.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k2*r\PYGZca{}2 + k3*r\PYGZca{}3 + k4*r\PYGZca{}4; k2=300.0; k3=\PYGZhy{}100.0; k4=50.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k*r\PYGZca{}2; k=350.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_lepton:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 8Feb2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bond style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} computes bonded interactions between two atoms with
a custom function.  The potential function must be provided as an
expression string using “r” as the distance variable relative to the
reference distance \(r_0\) which is provided as a bond coefficient.
For example \sphinxtitleref{“200.0*r\textasciicircum{}2”} represents a harmonic potential with a force
constant \sphinxstyleemphasis{K} of 200.0 energy units:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U_{bond,i} = K (r_i - r_0)^2 = K r^2 \qquad r = r_i - r_0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default the potential energy U is shifted so that he value U is 0.0
for \$r = r\_0\$.  This is equivalent to using the optional keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{auto\_offset}.  When using the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_offset} instead, the
potential energy is not shifted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://simtk.org/projects/lepton}{Lepton library}, that the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} bond style interfaces with, evaluates this expression string at
run time to compute the pairwise energy.  It also creates an analytical
representation of the first derivative of this expression with respect to
“r” and then uses that to compute the force between the atom pairs forming
bonds as defined by the topology data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lepton expression (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Lepton expression must be either enclosed in quotes or must not
contain any whitespace so that LAMMPS recognizes it as a single keyword.
More on valid Lepton expressions below.  The \(r_0\) is the
“equilibrium distance”.  The potential energy function in the Lepton
expression is shifted in such a way, that the potential energy is 0 for
a bond length \(r_i == r_0\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numbers may be given in either decimal or exponential form.  All of the
following are valid numbers: \sphinxtitleref{5}, \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}3.1}, \sphinxtitleref{1e6}, and \sphinxtitleref{3.12e\sphinxhyphen{}2}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an extension to the standard Lepton syntax, it is also possible to
use LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}} in the format “v\_name”.  Before
evaluating the expression, “v\_name” will be replaced with the value of
the variable “name”.  This is compatible with all kinds of scalar
variables, but not with vectors, arrays, local, or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
variables.  If necessary, a custom scalar variable needs to be defined
that can access the desired (single) item from a non\sphinxhyphen{}scalar variable.
As an example, the following lines will instruct LAMMPS to ramp
the force constant for a harmonic bond from 100.0 to 200.0 during the
next run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fconst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{100.0, 200}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}fconst * (r\PYGZca{}2)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An expression may be followed by definitions for intermediate values that appear in the
expression. A semicolon “;” is used as a delimiter between value definitions. For example,
the expression:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
is exactly equivalent to

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The definition of an intermediate value may itself involve other
intermediate values. Whitespace and quotation characters (’\textquotesingle{}’ and ‘”’)
are ignored.  All uses of a value must appear \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} that value’s
definition.  For efficiency reasons, the expression string is parsed,
optimized, and then stored in an internal, pre\sphinxhyphen{}parsed representation for
evaluation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluating a Lepton expression is typically between 2.5 and 5 times
slower than the corresponding compiled and optimized C++ code.  If
additional speed or GPU acceleration (via GPU or KOKKOS) is required,
the interaction can be represented as a table.  Suitable table files
can be created either internally using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_write}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_write}}}} command or through the Python scripts

\section{bond\_style mesocnt command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:bond-style-mesocnt-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{800.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} bond style is a wrapper for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{harmonic}}}} style, and uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium bond distance.  Note that the
usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).  The style implements
parameterization presets of \(K\) for mesoscopic simulations of
carbon nanotubes based on the atomistic simulations of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:srivastava-1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Srivastava)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other presets can be readily implemented in the future.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
preset = \sphinxstyleemphasis{C} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
additional parameters depending on preset

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Preset \sphinxstyleemphasis{C} is for carbon nanotubes, and the additional parameters are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chiral index \(n\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chiral index \(m\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Preset \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} is simply a direct wrapper for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{harmonic}}}} style, and the additional parameters are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the MOLECULE
and MESONT packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}}

\label{\detokenize{bond_mesocnt:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

(2005).

\index{bond\_style mm3@\spxentry{bond\_style mm3}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style mm3 command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:bond-style-mm3-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mm3}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mm3}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{107.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mm3} bond style uses the potential that is anharmonic in the bond
as defined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_mm3:mm3-allinger1989}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Allinger)}}}}
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (r - r_0)^2 \left[ 1 - 2.55(r-r_0) + \frac{7}{12} 2.55^2(r-r_0)^2 \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium value of the bond, and \(K\) is a
prefactor. The anharmonic prefactors have units \(\AA^{-n}\):
\(-2.55 \AA^{-1}\) and \(\frac{7}{12} 2.55^2 \AA^{-2}\). The code takes
care of the necessary unit conversion for these factors internally.
Note that the MM3 papers contain an error in Eq (1):
\(\frac{7}{12} 2.55\) should be replaced with \(\frac{7}{12} 2.55^2\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
YAFF package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{bond_mm3:mm3-allinger1989}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Allinger)} Allinger, Yuh, Lii, JACS, 111(23), 8551\sphinxhyphen{}8566
(1989),

\section{bond\_style morse command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_morse:bond-style-morse-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_morse:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{bond_morse:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_morse::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_morse:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{morse}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_morse:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{morse}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_morse:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{morse} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = D \left[ 1 - e^{-\alpha (r - r_0)} \right]^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_0\) is the equilibrium bond distance, \(\alpha\) is a stiffness
parameter, and \(D\) determines the depth of the potential well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(D\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\alpha\) (inverse distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_none:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a bond style of none means bond forces and energies are not
computed, even if pairs of bonded atoms were listed in the data file
read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style zero}}}} command for a way to
calculate bond statistics, but compute no bond interactions.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.4}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_nonlinear:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{nonlinear} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{\epsilon (r - r_0)^2}{ [ \lambda^2 - (r - r_0)^2 ]}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
to define an anharmonic spring {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_nonlinear:rector}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Rector)}}}} of equilibrium
length \(r_0\) and maximum extension lamda.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\lambda\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are

You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.7564}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.76107}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}

\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Real units}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{11.92337812042065}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.1295}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.409795}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{11.92337812042065}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.1295}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.4430152}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{11.92337812042065}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.1295}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6.482800913}

\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxrna2\PYGZus{}real.cgdna}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients in the above examples have to be kept fixed and
cannot be changed without reparameterizing the entire model. They are
provided in forms compatible with both \sphinxstyleemphasis{units lj} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{units real}
(see documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}}).  These can also be read
from a potential file with correct unit style by specifying the name
of the file. Several potential files for each unit style are included
in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_oxdna:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/fene}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/fene}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxrna2/fene} bond styles use the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = - \frac{\epsilon}{2} \ln \left[ 1 - \left(\frac{r-r_0}{\Delta}\right)^2\right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
to define a modified finite extensible nonlinear elastic (FENE)
potential {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:ouldridge0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}} to model the connectivity of
the phosphate backbone in the oxDNA/oxRNA force field for coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained
modelling of DNA/RNA.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for the bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as given in the above example, or
in the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The oxDNA bond style has to be used together with the corresponding
oxDNA pair styles for excluded volume interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/excv} ,
stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/stk} , cross\sphinxhyphen{}stacking \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/xstk} and coaxial
stacking interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/coaxstk} as well as hydrogen\sphinxhyphen{}bonding
interaction \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna/hbond} (see also documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style
oxdna/excv}}}}). For the oxDNA2 {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:snodin0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Snodin)}}}}
bond style the analogous pair styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/excv} , \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/stk} ,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/xstk} , \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/coaxstk} , \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/hbond} and an additional
Debye\sphinxhyphen{}Hueckel pair style \sphinxstyleemphasis{oxdna2/dh} have to be defined. The same
applies to the oxRNA2 {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:sulc01}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc1)}}}} styles.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style has to be used with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style hybrid bond
ellipsoid oxdna} (see documentation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style}}}}). The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom\_style oxdna} stores the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}5’ polarity
of the nucleotide strand, which is set through the bond topology in
the data file. The first (second) atom in a bond definition is
understood to point towards the 3’\sphinxhyphen{}end (5’\sphinxhyphen{}end) of the strand.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If data files are produced with {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_data}}}}, then
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} command should be set to \sphinxstyleemphasis{newton on} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{newton off on}.  Otherwise the data files will not have the same
3’\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}5’ polarity as the initial data file. This limitation does not
apply to binary restart files produced with {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_restart}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example input and data files for DNA and RNA duplexes can be found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/oxDNA/\textasciigrave{}, \textasciigrave{}.../oxDNA2/}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.../oxRNA2/}}.  A simple python setup tool which creates single
straight or helical DNA strands, DNA/RNA duplexes or arrays of DNA/RNA
duplexes can be found in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:henrich0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Henrich)}}}} in any publication that uses
this implementation. An updated documentation that contains general information
on the model, its implementation and performance as well as the structure of
the data and input file can be found \sphinxhref{PDF/CG-DNA.pdf}{here}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please cite also the relevant oxDNA/oxRNA publications. These are
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:ouldridge0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:ouldridge-dphil0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge\sphinxhyphen{}DPhil)}}}} for oxDNA,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:snodin0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Snodin)}}}} for oxDNA2,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:sulc01}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc1)}}}} for oxRNA2
and for sequence\sphinxhyphen{}specific hydrogen\sphinxhyphen{}bonding and stacking interactions
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:sulc02}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sulc2)}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Potential file reading}
\label{\detokenize{bond_oxdna:potential-file-reading}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each style oxdna, oxdna2 and oxrna2, the first parameter argument
can be a filename, and if it is, no further arguments should be
supplied. Therefore the following command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{fene}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oxdna\PYGZus{}lj.cgdna}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
will be interpreted as a request to read the (FENE) potential
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_oxdna:ouldridge0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Ouldridge)}}}} parameters from the file with the given
name.  The file can define multiple potential parameters for both bonded
and pair interactions, but for the above bonded interactions there must
exist in the file a line of the form:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{fene}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{epsilon}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{r0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are sample potential files for each unit style in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{potentials}} directory of the LAMMPS distribution. The potential file
unit system must align with the units defined via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} command. For conversion between different \sphinxstyleemphasis{LJ} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} unit
systems for oxDNA, the python tool \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj2real.py} located in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/util/}} directory can be used. This tool
assumes similar file structure to the examples found in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/PACKAGES/cgdna/examples/}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_oxdna:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
CG\sphinxhyphen{}DNA package and the MOLECULE and ASPHERE package.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{bond_oxdna:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style oxdna/excv}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxdna2::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style oxdna2/excv}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_oxrna2::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style oxrna2/excv}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_style oxdna}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nve_dotc_langevin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nve/dotc/langevin}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{bond_oxdna:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{bond\_style quartic@\spxentry{bond\_style quartic}}\ignorespaces 
\index{bond\_style quartic/omp@\spxentry{bond\_style quartic/omp}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style quartic command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:bond-style-quartic-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quartic}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quartic}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1200}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{0.55}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{34.6878}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} bond style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E      & = E_q + E_{LJ} \\
E_q    & = K (r - R_c)^ 2 (r - R_c - B_1) (r - R_c - B_2) + U_0 \\
E_{LJ} & = \left\{ \begin{array} {l@{\quad:\quad}l}
4 \epsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12} - \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^6 \right] + \epsilon & r < 2^{\frac{1}{6}}, \epsilon = 1, \sigma = 1 \\
                                               0 & r >= 2^{\frac{1}{6}}
                      \end{array} \right.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
to define a bond that can be broken as the simulation proceeds (e.g.
due to a polymer being stretched).  The \(\sigma\) and
\(\epsilon\) used in the LJ portion of the formula are both set
equal to 1.0 by LAMMPS and the LJ portion is cut off at its minimum,
i.e. at \(r_c = 2^{\frac{1}{6}}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}4)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(B_1\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(B_2\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_c\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(U_0\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This potential was constructed to mimic the FENE bond potential for
coarse\sphinxhyphen{}grained polymer chains.  When monomers with \(\sigma =
\epsilon = 1.0\) are used, the following choice of parameters gives a
quartic potential that looks nearly like the FENE potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}K &= 1200 \\
B_1 &= -0.55 \\
B_2 &= 0.25 \\
R_c &= 1.3 \\
U_0 &= 34.6878\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different parameters can be specified using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}
command, but you will need to choose them carefully so they form a suitable
bond potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(R_c\) is the cutoff length at which the bond potential goes smoothly to a
local maximum.  If a bond length ever becomes \(> R_c\), LAMMPS “breaks”
the bond, which means two things.  First, the bond potential is turned
off by setting its type to 0, and is no longer computed.  Second, a
pairwise interaction between the two atoms is turned on, since they
are no longer bonded. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_broken_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto}}}} page
on broken bonds for more information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LAMMPS does the second task via a computational sleight\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}hand.  It
subtracts the pairwise interaction as part of the bond computation.
When the bond breaks, the subtraction stops.  For this to work, the
pairwise interaction must always be computed by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command, whether the bond is broken or
not.  This means that {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} must be set
to 1,1,1, as indicated as a restriction below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that when bonds are dumped to a file via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command, bonds with type 0 are not included.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command can also be used to query the
status of broken bonds or permanently delete them, e.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stats}
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the MOLECULE
package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more
info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} style requires that {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}}
parameters be set to 1,1,1.  Three\sphinxhyphen{} and four\sphinxhyphen{}body interactions (angle,
dihedral, etc) cannot be used with \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} bonds.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{bond_quartic:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{bond\_style rheo/shell@\spxentry{bond\_style rheo/shell}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style rheo/shell command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:bond-style-rheo-shell-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{attribute2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
required keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{t/form}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optional keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{t/form} value = formation time for a bond (time units)

\sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} values = fix\_ID N attributes ...
   * fix\_ID = ID of associated internal fix to store data
   * N = prepare data for output every this many timesteps
   * attributes = zero or more of the below attributes may be appended

     \sphinxstyleemphasis{id1, id2} = IDs of two atoms in the bond
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{time} = the timestep the bond broke
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{x, y, z} = the center of mass position of the two atoms when the bond broke (distance units)
     \sphinxstyleemphasis{x/ref, y/ref, z/ref} = the initial center of mass position of the two atoms (distance units)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rheo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shell}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{t}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{form}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.05}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 29Aug2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{rheo/shell} bond style is designed to work with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/oxidation}}}} which creates candidate
bonds between eligible surface or near\sphinxhyphen{}surface particles. When a bond
is first created, it computes no forces and starts a timer. Forces are
not computed until the timer reaches the specified bond formation time,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{t/form}, and the bond is enabled and applies forces. If the two particles
move outside of the maximum bond distance or move into the bulk before
the timer reaches \sphinxstyleemphasis{t/form}, the bond automatically deletes itself. This
deletion is not recorded as a broken bond in the optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before bonds are enabled, they are still treated as regular bonds by
all other parts of LAMMPS. This means they are written to data files
and counted in computes such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_nbond_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{nbond/atom}}}}.
To only count enabled bonds, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nbond/shell} attribute in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_rheo_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute rheo/property/atom}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When enabled, the bond then computes forces based on deviations from
the initial reference state of the two atoms much like a BPM style
bond (as further discussed in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bpm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{BPM howto page}}}}).
The reference state is stored by each bond when it is first enabled.
Data is then preserved across run commands and is written to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}} such that restarting the system
will not reset the reference state of a bond or the timer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style is based on a model described in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:rheo-clemmer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Clemmer)}}}}. The force has a magnitude of
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F = 2 k (r - r_0) + \frac{2 k}{r_0^2 \epsilon_c^2} (r - r_0)^3\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(k\) is a stiffness, \(r\) is the current distance
and \(r_0\) is the initial distance between the two particles, and
\(\epsilon_c\) is maximum strain beyond which a bond breaks. This
is done by setting the bond type to 0 such that forces are no longer
computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A damping force proportional to the difference in the normal velocity
of particles is also applied to bonded particles:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_D = - \gamma w (\hat{r} \bullet \vec{v})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\gamma\) is the damping strength, \(\hat{r}\) is the
displacement normal vector, and \(\vec{v}\) is the velocity difference
between the two particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k\)             (force/distance units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\epsilon_c\)    (unit less)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma\)        (force/velocity units)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike other BPM\sphinxhyphen{}style bonds, this bond style does not update special
bond settings when bonds are created or deleted. This bond style also
does not enforce specific {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} settings.
This behavior is purposeful such {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_rheo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RHEO pair}}}} forces
and heat flows are still calculated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} keyword is used, an internal fix will track bonds that
break during the simulation. Whenever a bond breaks, data is processed
and transferred to an internal fix labeled \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID}. This allows the
local data to be accessed by other LAMMPS commands. Following this optional
keyword, a list of one or more attributes is specified.  These include the
IDs of the two atoms in the bond. The other attributes for the two atoms
include the timestep during which the bond broke and the current/initial
center of mass position of the two atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Data is continuously accumulated over intervals of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. At the end of each interval, all of the saved accumulated
data is deleted to make room for new data. Individual datum may
therefore persist anywhere between \sphinxstyleemphasis{1} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} timesteps depending on
when they are saved. This data can be accessed using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix\_ID} and a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command. To ensure all data is output,
the dump frequency should correspond to the same interval of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
timesteps. A dump frequency of an integer multiple of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} can be used
to regularly output a sample of the accumulated data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that when unbroken bonds are dumped to a file via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump local}}}} command, bonds with type 0 (broken bonds)
are not included.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{delete_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{delete\_bonds}}}} command can also be used to
query the status of broken bonds or permanently delete them, e.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stats}
\PYG{k}{delete\PYGZus{}bonds }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart and other info}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:restart-and-other-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style writes the reference state of each bond to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}. Loading a restart
file will properly restore bonds. However, the reference state is NOT
written to data files. Therefore reading a data file will not
restore bonds and will cause their reference states to be redefined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{store/local} option is used, an internal fix will calculate
a local vector or local array depending on the number of input values.
The length of the vector or number of rows in the array is the number
of recorded, broken bonds.  If a single input is specified, a local
vector is produced. If two or more inputs are specified, a local array
is produced where the number of columns = the number of inputs.  The
vector or array can be accessed by any command that uses local values
from a compute as input. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_output::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto output}}}} page
for an overview of LAMMPS output options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The vector or array will be floating point values that correspond to
the specified attribute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single() function of this bond style returns 0.0 for the energy
of a bonded interaction, since energy is not conserved in these
dissipative potentials.  The single() function also calculates two
extra bond quantities, the initial distance \(r_0\) and a time.
These extra quantities can be accessed by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute bond/local}}}} command as \sphinxstyleemphasis{b1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{b2}.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style is part of the RHEO package.  It is only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_rheo_oxidation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix rheo/oxidation}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
NA


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{bond_rheo_shell:rheo-clemmer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Clemmer)} Clemmer, Pierce, O’Connor, Nevins, Jones, Lechman, Tencer, Appl. Math. Model., 130, 310\sphinxhyphen{}326 (2024).

\sphinxstepscope

\index{bond\_style special@\spxentry{bond\_style special}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style special command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:bond-style-special-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_special:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_special::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{special}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{special}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{special} bond style can be used to create conceptual bonds which
effectively impose weightings on the pairwise Lennard Jones and/or
Coulombic interactions between selected pairs of particles in the
system.  The form of the pairwise interaction will be whatever is
computed by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} command defined for the
system; this command defines the weightings for its two terms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can thus be useful to apply weightings that cannot be
handled by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command, such as
on 1\sphinxhyphen{}5 or 1\sphinxhyphen{}6 interactions.  Or it can be used to add pairwise forces
between one or more pairs of atoms that otherwise would not be include
in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} computation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential for this bond style has the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E =  w_{LJ} E_{LJ} + w_{Coul} E_{Coul}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(w_{LJ}\) weight (0.0 to 1.0) on pairwise Lennard\sphinxhyphen{}Jones interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(w_{Coul}\) weight (0.0 to 1.0) on pairwise Coulombic interactions

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Normally this bond style should be used in conjunction with one (or
more) other bond styles which compute forces between atoms directly
bonded to each other in a molecule.  This means the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_hybrid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style
hybrid}}}} command should be used with bond\_style special
as one of its sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the same as for any other bond style, pairs of bonded atoms
must be enumerated in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.  Thus if this command is used to weight all 1\sphinxhyphen{}5
interactions in the system, all the 1\sphinxhyphen{}5 pairs of atoms must be listed
in the “Bonds” section of the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style imposes strict requirements on settings made with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} command.  These requirements
ensure that the new bonds created by this style do not create spurious
1\sphinxhyphen{}2, 1\sphinxhyphen{}3, or 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 interactions within the molecular topology.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifically 1\sphinxhyphen{}2 interactions must have weights of zero, 1\sphinxhyphen{}3
interactions must either have weights of unity or {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds
angle yes}}}} must be used, and 1\sphinxhyphen{}4 interactions must
have weights of unity or {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds dihedral yes}}}}
must be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this command is used to create bonded interactions between
particles that are further apart than usual (e.g. 1\sphinxhyphen{}5 or 1\sphinxhyphen{}6
interactions), this style may require an increase in the communication
cutoff via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{comm_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{comm\_modify cutoff}}}} command.  If
LAMMPS cannot find a partner atom in a bond, an error will be issued.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MISC package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style requires the use of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style}}}} which
computes a pairwise additive interaction and provides the ability to
compute interactions for individual pairs of atoms.  Manybody potentials
are not compatible in general, but also some other pair styles are missing
the required functionality and thus will cause an error.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is not compatible with long\sphinxhyphen{}range Coulombic interactions. If a
\sphinxtitleref{kspace\_style \textless{}kspace\_style\textgreater{}} is declared, an error will be issued.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{bond_special:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\index{bond\_style table@\spxentry{bond\_style table}}\ignorespaces 
\index{bond\_style table/omp@\spxentry{bond\_style table/omp}}\ignorespaces 

\section{bond\_style table command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_table:bond-style-table-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_table:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{bond_table:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_table::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{table/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_table:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spline} = method of interpolation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = use N values in table

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_table:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file.table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ENTRY1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_table:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{table} creates interpolation tables of length \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} from bond
potential and force values listed in a file(s) as a function of bond
length.  The files are read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}}
command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interpolation tables are created by fitting cubic splines to the
file values and interpolating energy and force values at each of \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
distances.  During a simulation, these tables are used to interpolate
energy and force values as needed.  The interpolation is done in one
of 2 styles: \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{spline}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{linear} style, the bond length is used to find 2 surrounding
table values from which an energy or force is computed by linear
interpolation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{spline} style, a cubic spline coefficients are computed and
stored at each of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} values in the table.  The bond length is
used to find the appropriate set of coefficients which are used to
evaluate a cubic polynomial which computes the energy or force.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each bond type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filename

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filename specifies a file containing tabulated energy and force
values.  The keyword specifies a section of the file.  The format of
this file is described below.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Suitable tables for use with this bond style can be created by LAMMPS
itself from existing bond styles using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_write}}}} command.  This can be useful to have a template file for
testing the bond style settings and to build a compatible custom file.
Another option to generate tables is the Python code in the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/tabulate}} folder of the LAMMPS source code distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format of a tabulated file is as follows (without the
parenthesized comments):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} Bond potential for harmonic (one or more comment or blank lines)

HAM                           (keyword is the first text on line)
N 101 FP 0 0 EQ 0.5           (N, FP, EQ  parameters)
                              (blank line)
1 0.00 338.0000 1352.0000     (index, bond\PYGZhy{}length, energy, force)
2 0.01 324.6152 1324.9600
...
101 1.00 338.0000 \PYGZhy{}1352.0000
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A section begins with a non\sphinxhyphen{}blank line whose first character is not a
“\#”; blank lines or lines starting with “\#” can be used as comments
between sections.  The first line begins with a keyword which
identifies the section.  The line can contain additional text, but the
initial text must match the argument specified in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command.  The next line lists (in any
order) one or more parameters for the table.  Each parameter is a
keyword followed by one or more numeric values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter “N” is required and its value is the number of table
entries that follow.  Note that this may be different than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{N}
specified in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style table}}}} command.  Let
Ntable = \sphinxstyleemphasis{N} in the bond\_style command, and Nfile = “N” in the
tabulated file.  What LAMMPS does is a preliminary interpolation by
creating splines using the Nfile tabulated values as nodal points.  It
uses these to interpolate as needed to generate energy and force
values at Ntable different points.  The resulting tables of length
Ntable are then used as described above, when computing energy and
force for individual bond lengths.  This means that if you want the
interpolation tables of length Ntable to match exactly what is in the
tabulated file (with effectively no preliminary interpolation), you
should set Ntable = Nfile.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “FP” parameter is optional.  If used, it is followed by two values
fplo and fphi, which are the derivatives of the force at the innermost
and outermost bond lengths.  These values are needed by the spline
construction routines.  If not specified by the “FP” parameter, they
are estimated (less accurately) by the first two and last two force
values in the table.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “EQ” parameter is also optional.  If used, it is followed by a the
equilibrium bond length, which is used, for example, by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix
shake}}}} command.  If not used, the equilibrium bond length is
to the distance in the table with the lowest potential energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Following a blank line, the next N lines list the tabulated values.
On each line, the first value is the index from 1 to N, the second value is
the bond length r (in distance units), the third value is the energy (in
energy units), and the fourth is the force (in force units).  The bond
lengths must range from a LO value to a HI value, and increase from
one line to the next.  If the actual bond length is ever smaller than
the LO value or larger than the HI value, then the calculation is
aborted with an error, so it is advisable to cover the whole range
of possible bond lengths.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that one file can contain many sections, each with a tabulated
potential.  LAMMPS reads the file section by section until it finds
one that matches the specified keyword.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restart info}
\label{\detokenize{bond_table:restart-info}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style writes the settings for the “bond\_style table” command
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}}, so a bond\_style command does
not need to specified in an input script that reads a restart file.
However, the coefficient information is not stored in the restart file,
since it is tabulated in the potential files.  Thus, bond\_coeff commands
do need to be specified in the restart input script.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{bond_table:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This bond style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the MOLECULE
