\section{bond\_style zero command}
\label{\detokenize{bond_zero:bond-style-zero-command}}\label{\detokenize{bond_zero:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{bond_zero::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{bond_zero:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{bond_zero:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nocoeff}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.14}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{bond_zero:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using an bond style of zero means bond forces and energies are not
computed, but the geometry of bond pairs is still accessible to other
commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_bond_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute bond/local}}}}
command can be used to compute distances for the list of pairs of bond
atoms listed in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command.  If no bond style is defined, this command cannot be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} flag allows to read data files with a BondCoeff
section for any bond style. Similarly, any bond\_coeff commands
will only be checked for the bond type number and the rest ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_coeff}}}} command must be used for
all bond types. If specified, there can be only one value, which is
going to be used to assign an equilibrium distance, e.g. for use with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_shake::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix shake}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{bond_zero:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\section{angle\_style amoeba command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_amoeba:angle-style-amoeba-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_amoeba:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_amoeba::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_amoeba:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_amoeba:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{75.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.02}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.003}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ba}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.6551}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24.895}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0119}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5228}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ub}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{7.6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5537}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_amoeba:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{amoeba} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = E_a + E_{ba} + E_{ub} \\
E_a & = K_2\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^2 + K_3\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^3 + K_4\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^4 + K_5\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^5 + K_6\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^6 \\
E_{ba} & = N_1 (r_{ij} - r_1) (\theta - \theta_0) + N_2(r_{jk} - r_2)(\theta - \theta_0) \\
E_{UB} & = K_{ub} (r_{ik} - r_{ub})^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(E_a\) is the angle term, \(E_{ba}\) is a bond\sphinxhyphen{}angle
term, \(E_{UB}\) is a Urey\sphinxhyphen{}Bradley bond term, \(\theta_0\) is
the equilibrium angle, \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) are the equilibrium
bond lengths, and \(r_{ub}\) is the equilibrium Urey\sphinxhyphen{}Bradley bond
length.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These formulas match how the Tinker MD code performs its angle
calculations for the AMOEBA and HIPPO force fields.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto amoeba}}}} page for more information about
the implementation of AMOEBA and HIPPO in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \(E_a\) and \(E_{ba}\) formulas are identical to
those used for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_class2::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style class2/p6}}}}
command, however there is no bond\sphinxhyphen{}bond cross term formula for
\(E_{bb}\).  Additionally, there is a \(E_{UB}\) term for a
Urey\sphinxhyphen{}Bradley bond.  It is effectively a harmonic bond between the I
and K atoms of angle IJK, even though that bond is not enumerated in
the “Bonds” section of the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are also two ways that Tinker computes the angle \(\theta\)
in the \(E_a\) formula.  The first is the standard way of treating
IJK as an “in\sphinxhyphen{}plane” angle.  The second is an “out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane” method
which Tinker may use if the center atom J in the angle is bonded to
one additional atom in addition to I and K.  In this case, all 4 atoms
are used to compute the \(E_a\) formula, resulting in forces on
all 4 atoms.  In the Tinker PRM file, these 2 options are denoted by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{angle} versus \sphinxstyleemphasis{anglep} entries in the “Angle Bending Parameters”
section of the PRM force field file.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{pflag} coefficient
described below selects between the 2 options.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Coefficients for the \(E_a\), \(E_{bb}\), and \(E_{ub}\)
formulas must be defined for each angle type via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in the data file or
restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the 8 coefficients for the \(E_a\) formula:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pflag = 0 or 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ubflag = 0 or 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_2\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_3\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_4\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_5\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_6\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A pflag value of 0 vs 1 selects between the “in\sphinxhyphen{}plane” and
“out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane” options described above.  Ubflag is 1 if there is a
Urey\sphinxhyphen{}Bradley term associated with this angle type, else it is 0.
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence the various \(K\) values are effectively
energy per radian\textasciicircum{}2 or radian\textasciicircum{}3 or radian\textasciicircum{}4 or radian\textasciicircum{}5 or
radian\textasciicircum{}6.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \(E_{ba}\) formula, each line in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command in the input script lists 5 coefficients, the
first of which is “ba” to indicate they are BondAngle coefficients.
In a data file, these coefficients should be listed under a “BondAngle
Coeffs” heading and you must leave out the “ba”, i.e. only list 4
coefficients after the angle type.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ba

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N_1\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N_2\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_1\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_2\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(\theta_0\) value in the \(E_{ba}\) formula is not specified,
since it is the same value from the \(E_a\) formula.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \(E_{ub}\) formula, each line in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command in the input script lists 3 coefficients, the
first of which is “ub” to indicate they are UreyBradley coefficients.
In a data file, these coefficients should be listed under a
“UreyBradley Coeffs” heading and you must leave out the “ub”,
i.e. only list 2 coefficients after the angle type.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ub

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_{ub}\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_{ub}\) (distance)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{angle\_style charmm command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:angle-style-charmm-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm/intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charmm}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{charmm}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{107.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_charmm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{charmm} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2 + K_{ub} (r - r_{ub})^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with an additional Urey\_Bradley term based on the distance \(r\) between
the first and third atoms in the angle.  \(K\), \(\theta_0\),
\(K_{ub}\), and \(R_{ub}\) are coefficients defined for each angle
type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_charmm:angle-mackerell}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(MacKerell)}}}} for a description of the CHARMM force
field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_{ub}\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_{ub}\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\section{angle\_style class2/p6 command}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_class2:syntax}}

\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_class2:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{class2}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{75.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.002}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.5872}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0119}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5228}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ba}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3.6551}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{24.895}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0119}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5228}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_class2:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E & = E_a + E_{bb} + E_{ba} \\
E_a & = K_2 (\theta - \theta_0)^2 + K_3 (\theta - \theta_0)^3 + K_4(\theta - \theta_0)^4 \\
E_{bb} & = M (r_{ij} - r_1) (r_{jk} - r_2) \\
E_{ba} & = N_1 (r_{ij} - r_1) (\theta - \theta_0) + N_2(r_{jk} - r_2)(\theta - \theta_0)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(E_a\) is the angle term, \(E_{bb}\) is a bond\sphinxhyphen{}bond
term, and \(E_{ba}\) is a bond\sphinxhyphen{}angle term.  \(\theta_0\) is
the equilibrium angle and \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) are the
equilibrium bond lengths.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_class2:angle-sun}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sun)}}}} for a description of the COMPASS class2 force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Coefficients for the \(E_a\), \(E_{bb}\), and \(E_{ba}\)
formulas must be defined for each angle type via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in the data file or
restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the 4 coefficients for the \(E_a\) formula:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_2\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_3\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_4\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence the various \(K\) are effectively energy
per radian\textasciicircum{}2 or radian\textasciicircum{}3 or radian\textasciicircum{}4.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \(E_{bb}\) formula, each line in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command in the input script lists 4 coefficients, the
first of which is “bb” to indicate they are BondBond coefficients.  In
a data file, these coefficients should be listed under a “BondBond
Coeffs” heading and you must leave out the “bb”, i.e. only list 3
coefficients after the angle type.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
bb

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(M\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_1\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_2\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \(E_{ba}\) formula, each line in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command in the input script lists 5 coefficients, the
first of which is “ba” to indicate they are BondAngle coefficients.
In a data file, these coefficients should be listed under a “BondAngle
Coeffs” heading and you must leave out the “ba”, i.e. only list 4
coefficients after the angle type.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ba

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N_1\) (energy/distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(N_2\) (energy/distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_1\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_2\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(\theta_0\) value in the \(E_{ba}\) formula is not specified,
since it is the same value from the \(E_a\) formula.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is important that the order of the I,J,K atoms in each angle
listed in the Angles section of the data file read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command be consistent with the order
of the \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) BondBond and BondAngle
coefficients.  This is because the terms in the formulas for
\(E_{bb}\) and \(E_{ba}\) will use the I,J atoms to compute
\(r_{ij}\) and the J,K atoms to compute \(r_{jk}\).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2/p6} angle style uses the \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} potential expanded to sixth order:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_{a} = K_2\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^2 + K_3\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^3 + K_4\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^4 + K_5\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^5 + K_6\left(\theta - \theta_0\right)^6\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In this expanded term 6 coefficients for the \(E_a\) formula need to be set:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_2\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_3\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_4\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_5\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_6\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence the various \(K\) are effectively energy
per radian\textasciicircum{}2 or radian\textasciicircum{}3 or radian\textasciicircum{}4 or radian\textasciicircum{}5 or radian\textasciicircum{}6.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bond\sphinxhyphen{}bond and bond\sphinxhyphen{}angle terms remain unchanged.

\section{angle\_style cosine/buck6d command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_buck6d:angle-style-cosine-buck6d-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_buck6d:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_buck6d::doc}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{cosine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{buck6d}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1.978350}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{180.000000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_buck6d:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/buck6d} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K \left[ 1 + \cos(n\theta - \theta_0)\right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(K\) is the energy constant, \(n\) is the periodic multiplicity and
\(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium angle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands in the following order:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to radians
internally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional to the cosine term the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/buck6d} angle style computes
the short range (vdW) interaction belonging to the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck6d}}}} between the end atoms of the
angle.  For this reason this angle style only works in combination
with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck6d}}}} styles and needs
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 interactions to be weighted
0.0 to prevent double counting.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_buck6d:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/buck6d} can only be used in combination with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_buck6d_coul_gauss::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style buck6d}}}} style and with a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{special_bonds::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{special\_bonds}}}} 0.0 weighting of 1\sphinxhyphen{}3 interactions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MOFFF package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to radians
internally.

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_periodic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/periodic} angle style uses the following potential, which may be
particularly used for organometallic systems where \(n\) = 4 might be used
for an octahedral complex and \(n\) = 3 might be used for a trigonal
center:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{2.0}{n^2} * C \left[ 1 - B(-1)^n\cos\left( n\theta\right) \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(C\), \(B\) and \(n\) are coefficients defined for each angle type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(B\) = 1 or \sphinxhyphen{}1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 for periodicity

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the prefactor \(C\) is specified as coefficient and not the overall force
constant \(K = \frac{2 C}{n^2}\).  When \(B = 1\), it leads to a minimum for the
linear geometry.  When \(B = -1\), it leads to a maximum for the linear geometry.

functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cosine}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{shift}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{45.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_shift:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/shift} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -\frac{U_{\text{min}}}{2} \left[ 1 + \cos(\theta-\theta_0) \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium angle. The potential is bounded
between \(-U_{\text{min}}\) and zero. In the neighborhood of the minimum
\(E = - U_{\text{min}} + U_{\text{min}}/4(\theta - \theta_0)^2\) hence
the spring constant is \(\frac{U_{\text{min}}}{2}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(U_{\text{min}}\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta\) (angle)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\subsection{Examples}

\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{45.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.0}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_shift_exp:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/shift/exp} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -U_{\text{min}} \frac{e^{-a U(\theta,\theta_0)}-1}{e^a-1} \quad \text{with} \quad U(\theta,\theta_0) = -0.5 \left(1+\cos(\theta-\theta_0) \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(U_{\text{min}}\), \(\theta\), and \(a\) are defined for each angle type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The potential is bounded between \([-U_{\text{min}}, 0]\) and the minimum is
located at the angle \(\theta_0\). The a parameter can be both positive or
negative and is used to control the spring constant at the
equilibrium.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The spring constant is given by \(k = A \exp(A) U_{\text{min}} / [2 (\exp(a)-1)]\).
For \(a > 3\), \(\frac{k}{U_{\text{min}}} = \frac{a}{2}\) to better than 5\% relative error. For negative
values of the \(a\) parameter, the spring constant is essentially zero,
and anharmonic terms takes over. The potential is furthermore well
behaved in the limit \(a \rightarrow 0\), where it has been implemented to linear
order in \(a\) for \(a < 0.001\). In this limit the potential reduces to the
cosineshifted potential.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(U_min\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta\) (angle)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A\) (real number)

\end{itemize}

functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available

\subsection{Examples}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cosine_squared:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine/squared} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K [\cos(\theta) - \cos(\theta_0)]^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
, which is commonly used in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bioFF::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DREIDING}}}} force field,
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium value of the angle, and \(K\)
is a prefactor.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_cosine_squared:cosine-mayo}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Mayo)}}}} for a description of the DREIDING force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to radians
internally.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{angle\_style cross command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cross:angle-style-cross-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_cross:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_cross::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cross:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cross}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cross:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cross}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{200.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.25}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{107.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_cross:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cross} angle style uses a potential that couples the bond stretches of
a bend with the angle stretch of that bend:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K_{SS} \left(r_{12}-r_{12,0}\right)\left(r_{32}-r_{32,0}\right) + K_{BS0}\left(r_{12}-r_{12,0}\right)\left(\theta-\theta_0\right) + K_{BS1}\left(r_{32}-r_{32,0}\right)\left(\theta-\theta_0\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(r_{12,0}\) is the rest value of the bond length between atom 1 and 2,
\(r_{32,0}\) is the rest value of the bond length between atom 3 and 2,
and \(\theta_0\) is the rest value of the angle. \(K_{SS}\) is the force constant of
the bond stretch\sphinxhyphen{}bond stretch term and \(K_{BS0}\) and \(K_{BS1}\) are the force constants
of the bond stretch\sphinxhyphen{}angle stretch terms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_{SS}\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_{BS0}\) (energy/distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_{BS1}\) (energy/distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_{32,0}\) (distance)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence the \(K_{BS0}\) and \(K_{BS1}\) are
effectively energy/distance per radian.

\section{angle\_style dipole command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:angle-style-dipole-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dipole}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{180.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} angle style is used to control the orientation of a dipolar
atom within a molecule {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_dipole:orsi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Orsi)}}}}. Specifically, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} angle
style restrains the orientation of a point dipole \(\mu_j\) (embedded in atom
\(j\)) with respect to a reference (bond) vector
\(\vec{r}_{ij} = \vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j\), where \(i\) is another atom of
the same molecule (typically, \(i\) and \(j\) are also covalently bonded).

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is convenient to define an angle gamma between the ‘free’ vector \(\vec{\mu}_j\)
and the reference (bond) vector \(\vec{r}_{ij}\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\cos\gamma = \frac{\vec{\mu}_j\cdot\vec{r}_{ij}}{\mu_j\,r_{ij}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole} angle style uses the potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\cos\gamma - \cos\gamma_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(K\) is a rigidity constant and gamma0 is an equilibrium (reference)
angle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The torque on the dipole can be obtained by differentiating the
potential using the ‘chain rule’ as in appendix C.3 of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_dipole:allen1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(AllenTildesley)}}}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\vec{T}_j = \frac{2K(\cos\gamma - \cos\gamma_0)}{\mu_j\,r_{ij}}\, \vec{r}_{ij} \times \vec{\mu}_j\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: if \(\gamma_0\) is set to 0 degrees, the torque generated by
the potential will tend to align the dipole along the reference
direction defined by the (bond) vector \(\vec{r}_{ij}\) (in other words, \(\vec{\mu}_j\) is
restrained to point towards atom \(i\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dipolar torque \(\vec{T}_j\) must be counterbalanced in order to conserve
the local angular momentum. This is achieved via an additional force
couple generating a torque equivalent to the opposite of \(\vec{T}_j\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}-\vec{T}_j & = \vec{r}_{ij} \times \vec{F}_i \\
\vec{F}_j  & = -\vec{F}_i\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\vec{F}_i\) and \(\vec{F}_j\) are applied on atoms \(i\)
and \(j\), respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_dipole:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
DIPOLE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the “Angles” section of the data file, the atom ID \(j\)
defining the direction of the dipole vector to restrain must come
before the atom ID of the reference atom \(i\). A third atom ID \(k\) must
also be provided to comply with the requirement of a valid angle
definition. This atom ID \(k\) should be chosen to be that of an atom
bonded to atom \(i\) to avoid errors with “lost angle atoms” when running
in parallel. Since the LAMMPS code checks for valid angle definitions,
cannot use the same atom ID of either \(i\) or \(j\) (this was allowed
and recommended with older LAMMPS versions).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{newton::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{newton}}}} command for intramolecular interactions must be “on”
(which is the default except when using some accelerator packages).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style should \sphinxstylestrong{NOT} be used with fix shake.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\section{angle\_style gaussian command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:angle-style-gaussian-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gaussian}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0128}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.375}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{80.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0730}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.148}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{123.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{gaussian} angle style uses the potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = -k_B T ln\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{A_i}{w_i \sqrt{\pi/2}} exp\left( \frac{-2(\theta-\theta_{i})^2}{w_i^2}\right) \right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This analytical form is a suitable potential for obtaining mesoscale
effective force fields which can reproduce target atomistic
distributions {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_gaussian:milano1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Milano)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(T\) temperature at which the potential was derived

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) (integer \textgreater{}=1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_1\) (\textgreater{} 0, radians)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(w_1\) (\textgreater{} 0, radians)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_1\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_n\) (\textgreater{} 0, radians)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(w_n\) (\textgreater{} 0, radians)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_n\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{angle_gaussian:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_harmonic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium value of the angle, and \(K\) is a
prefactor.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_hybrid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} style enables the use of multiple angle styles in one
simulation.  An angle style is assigned to each angle type.  For
example, angles in a polymer flow (of angle type 1) could be computed
with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} potential and angles in the wall boundary (of angle
type 2) could be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine} potential.  The assignment
of angle type to style is made via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}}
command or in the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} commands, the name of an angle style must be added
after the angle type, with the remaining coefficients being those
appropriate to that style.  In the example above, the 2 angle\_coeff
commands set angles of angle type 1 to be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic}
potential with coefficients 80.0, 30.0 for \(K\), \(\theta_0\).  All other angle
types \((2 - N)\) are computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{cosine} potential with coefficient
50.0 for \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If angle coefficients are specified in the data file read via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, then the same rule applies.
E.g. “harmonic” or “cosine”, must be added after the angle type, for each
line in the “Angle Coeffs” section, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Angle Coeffs

1 harmonic 80.0 30.0
2 cosine 50.0
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} is one of the angle hybrid styles, the same rule holds for
specifying additional BondBond (and BondAngle) coefficients either via
the input script or in the data file.  I.e. \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} must be added to
each line after the angle type.  For lines in the BondBond (or
BondAngle) section of the data file for angle types that are not
\sphinxstyleemphasis{class2}, you must use an angle style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{skip} as a placeholder, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
BondBond Coeffs

1 skip
2 class2 3.6512 1.0119 1.0119
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that it is not necessary to use the angle style \sphinxstyleemphasis{skip} in the
input script, since BondBond (or BondAngle) coefficients need not be
specified at all for angle types that are not \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An angle style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} with no additional coefficients can be used
in place of an angle style, either in a input script {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}}
command or in the data file, if you desire to turn off interactions
for specific angle types.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script

{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_hybrid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc page
for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike other angle styles, the hybrid angle style does not store angle
coefficient info for individual sub\sphinxhyphen{}styles in {\hyperref[\detokenize{restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{binary restart files}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{write_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{data files}}}}.  Thus when restarting a
simulation, you need to re\sphinxhyphen{}specify the angle\_coeff commands.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_lepton:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = optional arguments

\begin{sphinxalltt}
args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto\_offset} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_offset}
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{auto\_offset} = offset the potential energy so that the value at theta0 is 0.0 (default)
  \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_offset} = do not offset the potential energy
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_lepton:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}offset}

\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{120.0}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k*theta\PYGZca{}2; k=250.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{90.0}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k2*theta\PYGZca{}2 + k3*theta\PYGZca{}3 + k4*theta\PYGZca{}4; k2=300.0; k3=\PYGZhy{}100.0; k4=50.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m}{109.47}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{k*theta\PYGZca{}2; k=350.0}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_lepton:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 8Feb2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Angle style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} computes angular interactions between three atoms
with a custom potential function.  The potential function must be
provided as an expression string using “theta” as the angle variable
relative to the reference angle \(\theta_0\) which is provided as an
angle coefficient.  For example \sphinxtitleref{“200.0*theta\textasciicircum{}2”} represents a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{harmonic angle}}}} potential with a force constant
\sphinxstyleemphasis{K} of 200.0 energy units:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}U_{angle,i} = K (\theta_i - \theta_0)^2 = K \theta^2 \qquad \theta = \theta_i - \theta_0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,changed}{Changed in version 7Feb2024.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default the potential energy U is shifted so that the value U is 0.0
for \$theta = theta\_0\$.  This is equivalent to using the optional keyword
\sphinxstyleemphasis{auto\_offset}.  When using the keyword \sphinxstyleemphasis{no\_offset} instead, the
potential energy is not shifted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://simtk.org/projects/lepton}{Lepton library}, that the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lepton} angle style interfaces with, evaluates this expression string
at run time to compute the pairwise energy.  It also creates an
analytical representation of the first derivative of this expression
with respect to “theta” and then uses that to compute the force between
the angle atoms as defined by the topology data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lepton expression (energy units)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Lepton expression must be either enclosed in quotes or must not
contain any whitespace so that LAMMPS recognizes it as a single keyword.
More on valid Lepton expressions below.  The \(\theta_0\)
coefficient is the “equilibrium angle”.  It is entered in degrees, but
internally converted to radians.  Thus the expression must assume
“theta” is in radians.  The potential energy function in the Lepton
expression is shifted in such a way, that the potential energy is 0 for
a angle \(\theta_i == \theta_0\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numbers may be given in either decimal or exponential form.  All of the
following are valid numbers: \sphinxtitleref{5}, \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}3.1}, \sphinxtitleref{1e6}, and \sphinxtitleref{3.12e\sphinxhyphen{}2}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an extension to the standard Lepton syntax, it is also possible to
use LAMMPS {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variables}}}} in the format “v\_name”.  Before
evaluating the expression, “v\_name” will be replaced with the value of
the variable “name”.  This is compatible with all kinds of scalar
variables, but not with vectors, arrays, local, or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
variables.  If necessary, a custom scalar variable needs to be defined
that can access the desired (single) item from a non\sphinxhyphen{}scalar variable.
As an example, the following lines will instruct LAMMPS to ramp
the force constant for a harmonic bond from 100.0 to 200.0 during the
next run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{variable }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{fconst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{equal}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ramp}\PYG{n+nv}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{100.0, 200}\PYG{n+nv}{)}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lepton}
\PYG{k}{bond\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{v\PYGZus{}fconst * (r\PYGZca{}2)}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An expression may be followed by definitions for intermediate values that appear in the
expression. A semicolon “;” is used as a delimiter between value definitions. For example,
the expression:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
is exactly equivalent to

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{a2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b1}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{b2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZca{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The definition of an intermediate value may itself involve other
intermediate values. Whitespace and quotation characters (’\textquotesingle{}’ and ‘”’)
are ignored.  All uses of a value must appear \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} that value’s
definition.  For efficiency reasons, the expression string is parsed,
optimized, and then stored in an internal, pre\sphinxhyphen{}parsed representation for
evaluation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluating a Lepton expression is typically between 2.5 and 5 times
slower than the corresponding compiled and optimized C++ code.  If
additional speed or GPU acceleration (via GPU or KOKKOS) is required,
the interaction can be represented as a table.  Suitable table files
can be created either internally using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_write}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_write::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_write}}}} command or through the Python scripts
in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools:tabulate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{tools/tabulate}}}} folder.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar

See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more

\index{angle\_style mesocnt@\spxentry{angle\_style mesocnt}}\ignorespaces 

\section{angle\_style mesocnt command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:angle-style-mesocnt-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{buckling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10.0}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{buckling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{400.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5.0}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 15Sep2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesocnt} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K_\text{H} \Delta \theta^2, \qquad |\Delta \theta| < \Delta
\theta_\text{B} \\
E = K_\text{H} \Delta \theta_\text{B}^2 +
K_\text{B} (\Delta \theta - \Delta \theta_\text{B}), \qquad |\Delta
\theta| \geq \Delta \theta_\text{B}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\Delta \theta = \theta - \pi\) is the bending angle of the
nanotube, \(K_\text{H}\) and \(K_\text{B}\) are prefactors for
the harmonic and linear regime respectively and \(\Delta
\theta_\text{B}\) is the buckling angle. Note that the usual 1/2 factor
for the harmonic potential is included in \(K_\text{H}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The style implements parameterization presets of \(K_\text{H}\),
\(K_\text{B}\) and \(\Delta \theta_\text{B}\) for mesoscopic
simulations of carbon nanotubes based on the atomistic simulations of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:srivastava-2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Srivastava)}}}} and buckling considerations of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:zhigilei1-1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Zhigilei)}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the examples above, or
in the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mode = \sphinxstyleemphasis{buckling} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
preset = \sphinxstyleemphasis{C} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
additional parameters depending on preset

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If mode \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} is chosen, the potential is simply harmonic and
does not switch to the linear term when the buckling angle is
reached. In \sphinxstyleemphasis{buckling} mode, the full piecewise potential is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Preset \sphinxstyleemphasis{C} is for carbon nanotubes, and the additional parameters are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chiral index \(n\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
chiral index \(m\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(r_0\) (distance)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, \(r_0\) is the equilibrium distance of the bonds included in
the angle, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_mesocnt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style mesocnt}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In harmonic mode with preset \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, the additional parameter is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_\text{H}\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Hence, this setting is simply a wrapper for {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{bond\_style harmonic}}}} with an equilibrium angle of 180 degrees.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In harmonic mode with preset \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, the additional parameters are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_\text{H}\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_\text{B}\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta \theta_\text{B}\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta \theta_\text{B}\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS
converts it to radians internally; hence \(K_\text{H}\) is
effectively energy per radian\textasciicircum{}2 and \(K_\text{B}\) is energy per
radian.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxstyleemphasis{buckling} mode, this angle style adds the \sphinxstyleemphasis{buckled} property to
all atoms in the simulation, which is an integer flag indicating
whether the bending angle at a given atom has exceeded \(\Delta
\theta_\text{B}\). It can be accessed as an atomic variable, e.g. for
custom dump commands, as \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_buckled}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the initial state of the simulation contains buckled nanotubes
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_mesocnt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style mesocnt}}}} is used, the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_buckled} atomic variable needs to be initialized before the
pair\_style is defined by doing a \sphinxstyleemphasis{run 0} command straight after the
angle\_style command. See below for an example.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If CNTs are already buckled at the start of the simulation, this
script will correctly initialize \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_buckled}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{buckling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}

\PYG{k}{run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}

\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{60.0}
\PYG{k}{pair\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C\PYGZus{}10\PYGZus{}10.mesocnt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MOLECULE and MESONT packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:srivastava-2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Srivastava)} Zhigilei, Wei, Srivastava, Phys. Rev. B 71, 165417
(2005).

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{angle_mesocnt:zhigilei1-1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{(Zhigilei)} Volkov and Zhigilei, ACS Nano 4, 6187 (2010).

\index{angle\_style mm3@\spxentry{angle\_style mm3}}\ignorespaces 

\section{angle\_style mm3 command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:angle-style-mm3-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mm3}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mm3}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{107.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mm3} angle style uses the potential that is anharmonic in the angle
as defined in {\hyperref[\detokenize{bond_mm3:mm3-allinger1989}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Allinger)}}}}
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2 \left[ 1 - 0.014(\theta - \theta_0) + 5.6(10)^{-5} (\theta - \theta_0)^2 - 7.0(10)^{-7} (\theta - \theta_0)^3 + 9(10)^{-10} (\theta - \theta_0)^4 \right]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium value of the angle, and
\(K\) is a prefactor. The anharmonic prefactors have units
\(\deg^{-n}\), for example \(-0.014 \deg^{-1}\), \(5.6
\cdot 10^{-5} \deg^{-2}\), …

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
YAFF package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{angle_mm3:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstepscope

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_none:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using an angle style of none means angle forces and energies are not
computed, even if triplets of angle atoms were listed in the data file
read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_zero::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_style zero}}}} command for a way to
calculate angle statistics, but compute no angle interactions.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_none:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{angle\_style quartic command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:angle-style-quartic-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quartic}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{quartic}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{129.1948}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{56.8726}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{25.9442}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{14.2221}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{quartic} angle style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K_2 (\theta - \theta_0)^2 + K_3 (\theta - \theta_0)^3 + K_4 (\theta - \theta_0)^4\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium value of the angle, and \(K\) is a
prefactor.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above, or in
the data file or restart files read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}} commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_2\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_3\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_4\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence the various \(K\) are effectively energy
per radian\textasciicircum{}2 or radian\textasciicircum{}3 or radian\textasciicircum{}4.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This angle style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{angle_quartic:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{angle\_style spica command}
\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:angle-style-spica-command}}\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{angle_spica::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{spica/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{spica/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spica}

\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spica}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{omp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spica}
\PYG{k}{angle\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{300.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{107.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{angle_spica:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{spica} angle style is a combination of the harmonic angle potential,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\theta - \theta_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\theta_0\) is the equilibrium value of the angle and
\(K\) a prefactor, with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{repulsive} part of the non\sphinxhyphen{}bonded
\sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/spica} pair style between the atoms 1 and 3.  This angle potential is
intended for coarse grained MD simulations with the SPICA (formerly called SDK) parameterization
using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{pair_spica::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{pair\_style lj/spica}}}}.  Relative to the
pair\_style \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/spica}, however, the energy is shifted by
\(\epsilon\), to avoid sudden jumps.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor
is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each angle type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{angle_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{angle\_coeff}}}} command as in the example above:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The required \sphinxstyleemphasis{lj/spica} parameters are extracted automatically from the
pair\_style.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{sdk}, the original implementation of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{spica}, is available
for backward compatibility.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.
