\section{dihedral\_style zero command}
\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero:dihedral-style-zero-command}}\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dihedral\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keywords may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dihedral\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}
\PYG{k}{dihedral\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nocoeff}
\PYG{k}{dihedral\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a dihedral style of zero means dihedral forces and energies are
not computed, but the geometry of dihedral quadruplets is still
accessible to other commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_dihedral_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute dihedral/local}}}} command can be used to
compute the theta values for the list of quadruplets of dihedral atoms
listed in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command.  If no dihedral style is defined, this command cannot be
used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} flag allows to read data files with a DihedralCoeff
section for any dihedral style. Similarly, any dihedral\_coeff commands
will only be checked for the dihedral type number and the rest ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_coeff}}}} command must be
used for all dihedral types, though no additional values are
specified.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dihedral_zero:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\index{improper\_style amoeba@\spxentry{improper\_style amoeba}}\ignorespaces 

\section{improper\_style amoeba command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba:improper-style-amoeba-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amoeba}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{49.6}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{amoeba} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\chi)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\chi\) is the improper angle and \(K\) is a prefactor.
Note that the usual 1/2 factor is included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This formula seems like a simplified version of the formula for the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_style harmonic}}}} command with
\(\chi_0\) = 0.0.  However the computation of the angle
\(\chi\) is done differently to match how the Tinker MD code
computes its out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane improper for the AMOEBA and HIPPO force
fields.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_amoeba::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto amoeba}}}} doc page for more
information about the implementation of AMOEBA and HIPPO in LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet (listed in the data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command are ordered I,J,K,L then
atoms I,K,L are considered to lie in a plane and atom J is
out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}place.  The angle \(\chi_0\) is computed as the Allinger
angle which is defined as the angle between the plane of I,K,L, and
the vector from atom I to atom J.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficient must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the angle \(\chi\) is computed in radians; hence
\(K\) is effectively energy per radian\textasciicircum{}2.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_amoeba:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This improper style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
AMOEBA package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc page
for more info.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_harmonic}}}}

\index{improper\_style class2/omp@\spxentry{improper\_style class2/omp}}\ignorespaces

\section{improper\_style class2 command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_class2:improper-style-class2-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_class2:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{improper_class2:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_class2:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_class2::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2/omp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2/kk}


\subsection{Syntax}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_class2:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E      = & E_i + E_{aa} \\
E_i    = & K [ \frac{\chi_{ijkl} + \chi_{kjli} + \chi_{ljik}}{3} - \chi_0 ]^2 \\
E_{aa} = & M_1 (\theta_{ijk} - \theta_1) (\theta_{kjl} - \theta_3) + \\
         & M_2 (\theta_{ijk} - \theta_1) (\theta_{ijl} - \theta_2) + \\
         & M_3 (\theta_{ijl} - \theta_2) (\theta_{kjl} - \theta_3)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(E_i\) is the improper term and \(E_{aa}\) is an
angle\sphinxhyphen{}angle term.  The 3 \(\chi\) terms in \(E_i\) are an
average over 3 out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane angles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet (listed in the data file read by
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command) are ordered I,J,K,L.
\(\chi_{ijkl}\) refers to the angle between the plane of I,J,K and
the plane of J,K,L, and the bond JK lies in both planes.  Similarly for
\(\chi_{kjli}\) and \(\chi_{ljik}\).
Note that atom J appears in the common bonds (JI, JK, JL) of all 3 X
terms.  Thus J (the second atom in the quadruplet) is the atom of
symmetry in the 3 \(\chi\) angles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The subscripts on the various \(\theta\)s refer to different
combinations of three atoms (I,J,K,L) used to form a particular angle.
E.g. \(\theta_{ijl}\) is the angle formed by atoms I,J,L with J
in the middle.  \(\theta_1\), \(\theta_2\), \(\theta_3\)
are the equilibrium positions of those angles.  Again,
atom J (the second atom in the quadruplet) is the atom of symmetry in the
theta angles, since it is always the center atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since atom J is the atom of symmetry, normally the bonds J\sphinxhyphen{}I, J\sphinxhyphen{}K, J\sphinxhyphen{}L
would exist for an improper to be defined between the 4 atoms, but
this is not required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_class2:improper-sun}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Sun)}}}} for a description of the COMPASS class2 force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Coefficients for the \(E_i\) and \(E_{aa}\) formulas must be
defined for each
improper type via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as
in the example above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the 2 coefficients for the \(E_i\) formula:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\chi_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\chi_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \(E_{aa}\) formula, each line in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command in the input script lists 7 coefficients,
the first of which is \sphinxstyleemphasis{aa} to indicate they are AngleAngle
coefficients.  In a data file, these coefficients should be listed
under a \sphinxstyleemphasis{AngleAngle Coeffs} heading and you must leave out the \sphinxstyleemphasis{aa},
i.e. only list 6 coefficients after the improper type.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{aa}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(M_1\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(M_2\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(M_3\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_1\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_2\) (degrees)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_3\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \(\theta\) values are specified in degrees, but LAMMPS
converts them to radians internally; hence the hence the various
\(M\) are effectively energy per radian\textasciicircum{}2.

\section{improper\_style cossq command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_cossq:improper-style-cossq-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cossq:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cossq:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cossq::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{cossq/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_cossq:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cossq} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = \frac{1}{2} K \cos^2{\left(\chi - \chi_0\right)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\chi\) is the improper angle, \(\chi_0\) is its
equilibrium value, and \(K\) is a prefactor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet (listed in the data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command) are ordered I,J,K,L then
\(\chi\) is the angle between the plane of I,J,K and the plane of J,K,L.
Alternatively, you can think of atoms J,K,L as being in a plane, and
atom I above the plane, and \(\chi\) as a measure of how far
out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane I is with respect to the other 3 atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that defining 4 atoms to interact in this way, does not mean that
bonds necessarily exist between I\sphinxhyphen{}J, J\sphinxhyphen{}K, or K\sphinxhyphen{}L, as they would in a
linear dihedral.  Normally, the bonds I\sphinxhyphen{}J, I\sphinxhyphen{}K, I\sphinxhyphen{}L would exist for an
improper to be defined between the 4 atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\chi_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{improper_cvff:improper-style-cvff-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cvff:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cvff:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cvff:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_cvff::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvff/intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvff/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_cvff:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvff} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K [1 + d  \cos (n \phi) ]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where phi is the improper dihedral angle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet (listed in the data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command) are ordered I,J,K,L then
the improper dihedral angle is between the plane of I,J,K and the
plane of J,K,L.  Note that because this is effectively a dihedral
angle, the formula for this improper style is the same as for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dihedral_harmonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dihedral\_style harmonic}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that defining 4 atoms to interact in this way, does not mean that
bonds necessarily exist between I\sphinxhyphen{}J, J\sphinxhyphen{}K, or K\sphinxhyphen{}L, as they would in a
linear dihedral.  Normally, the bonds I\sphinxhyphen{}J, I\sphinxhyphen{}K, I\sphinxhyphen{}L would exist for an
improper to be defined between the 4 atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(d\) (+1 or \sphinxhyphen{}1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\) (0,1,2,3,4,6)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}

\section{improper\_style distance command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distance:improper-style-distance-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_distance:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_distance::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distance:syntax}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distance:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{distance} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K_2 d^2 + K_4 d^4\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(d\) is the distance between the central atom and the plane formed
by the other three atoms.  If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet
(listed in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command) are ordered I,J,K,L then the I\sphinxhyphen{}atom is assumed to be the
central atom.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{improper_distance}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that defining 4 atoms to interact in this way, does not mean that
bonds necessarily exist between I\sphinxhyphen{}J, J\sphinxhyphen{}K, or K\sphinxhyphen{}L, as they would in a
linear dihedral. Normally, the bonds I\sphinxhyphen{}J, I\sphinxhyphen{}K, I\sphinxhyphen{}L would exist for an
improper to be defined between the 4 atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the improper\_coeff command as in the example above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the read\_data or read\_restart commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_2\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K_4\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}4)

\end{itemize}

\section{improper\_style distharm command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distharm:improper-style-distharm-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_distharm:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_distharm::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distharm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{distharm}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distharm:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{distharm}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{25.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_distharm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{distharm} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (d - d_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(d\) is the oriented distance between the central atom and the plane formed
by the other three atoms.  If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet
(listed in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command) are ordered I,J,K,L then the L\sphinxhyphen{}atom is assumed to be the
central atom. Note that this is different from the convention used
in the improper\_style distance. The distance \(d\) is oriented and can take
on negative values. This may lead to unwanted behavior if \(d_0\) is not equal to zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the improper\_coeff command as in the example above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the read\_data or read\_restart commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{improper\_style fourier command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier:improper-style-fourier-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{fourier/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fourier}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_fourier:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{fourier} improper style uses the following potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K [C_0 + C_1 \cos ( \omega) + C_2 \cos( 2 \omega) ]\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where K is the force constant, C0, C1, C2 are dimensionless coefficients,
and omega is the angle between the IL axis and the IJK plane:

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{umbrella}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If all parameter (see below) is not zero, the all the three possible angles will taken in account.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_0\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_1\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_2\) (unitless)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
all  (0 or 1, optional)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,

LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the

\section{improper\_style harmonic command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:improper-style-harmonic-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:index-3}}\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:index-2}}\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_harmonic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (\chi - \chi_0)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\chi\) is the improper angle, \(\chi_0\) is its equilibrium
value, and \(K\) is a prefactor.  Note that the usual 1/2 factor is
included in \(K\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet (listed in the data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command) are ordered I,J,K,L then
\(\chi\)
is the angle between the plane of I,J,K and the plane of J,K,L.
Alternatively, you can think of atoms J,K,L as being in a plane, and
atom I above the plane, and \(\chi\) as a measure of how far out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane
I is with respect to the other 3 atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that defining 4 atoms to interact in this way, does not mean that
bonds necessarily exist between I\sphinxhyphen{}J, J\sphinxhyphen{}K, or K\sphinxhyphen{}L, as they would in a
linear dihedral.  Normally, the bonds I\sphinxhyphen{}J, I\sphinxhyphen{}K, I\sphinxhyphen{}L would exist for an
improper to be defined between the 4 atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\chi_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\chi_0\) is specified in degrees, but LAMMPS converts it to
radians internally; hence \(K\) is effectively energy per
radian\textasciicircum{}2.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}

See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more

\section{improper\_style hybrid command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:improper-style-hybrid-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style1,style2 = list of one or more improper styles

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hybrid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvff}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{harmonic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{120.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cvff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{hybrid} style enables the use of multiple improper styles in one
simulation.  An improper style is assigned to each improper type.  For
example, impropers in a polymer flow (of improper type 1) could be
computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic} potential and impropers in the wall
boundary (of improper type 2) could be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvff}
potential.  The assignment of improper type to style is made via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command or in the data file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the improper\_coeff command, the first coefficient sets the improper
style and the remaining coefficients are those appropriate to that
style.  In the example above, the 2 improper\_coeff commands would set
impropers of improper type 1 to be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{harmonic}
potential with coefficients 120.0, 30 for \(K\), \(\chi_0\).
Improper type 2 would be computed with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{cvff} potential with coefficients
20.0, \sphinxhyphen{}1, 2 for K, d, and n, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If improper coefficients are specified in the data file read via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command, then the same rule applies.
E.g. “harmonic” or “cvff”, must be added after the improper type, for
each line in the “Improper Coeffs” section, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Improper Coeffs

1 harmonic 120.0 30
2 cvff 20.0 \PYGZhy{}1 2
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} is one of the improper hybrid styles, the same rule holds
for specifying additional AngleAngle coefficients either via the input
script or in the data file. I.e. \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2} must be added to each line
after the improper type.  For
lines in the AngleAngle Coeffs section of the data
file for dihedral types that are not \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2}, you must use an
improper style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{skip} as a placeholder, e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
AngleAngle Coeffs

1 skip
2 class2 0.0 0.0 0.0 115.06 130.01 115.06
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that it is not necessary to use the improper style \sphinxstyleemphasis{skip} in the
input script, since AngleAngle coefficients
need not be specified at all for improper types that are not \sphinxstyleemphasis{class2}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An improper style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{none} can be specified as the second argument to
the improper\_coeff command, if you desire to turn off certain improper
types.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_hybrid:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This improper style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc page

\section{improper\_style inversion/harmonic command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:improper-style-inversion-harmonic-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{inversion}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{harmonic}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{inversion}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{harmonic}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{18.776340}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.000000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{inversion/harmonic} improper style follows the Wilson\sphinxhyphen{}Decius
out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}plane angle definition and uses an harmonic potential:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K \left(\omega - \omega_0\right)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(K\) is the force constant and \(\omega\) is the angle
evaluated for all three axis\sphinxhyphen{}plane combinations centered around the atom I.
For the IL axis and the IJK plane \(\omega\) looks as follows:

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{umbrella}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{inversion/harmonic} angle term evaluation differs to
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_umbrella::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_umbrella}}}} due to the cyclic
evaluation of all possible angles \(\omega\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\omega_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \(\omega_0 = 0\) the potential term has a single minimum for
the planar structure.  Otherwise it has two minima at +/\sphinxhyphen{} \(\omega_0\),
with a barrier in between.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This improper style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MOFFF package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}}

\label{\detokenize{improper_inversion_harmonic:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Description}

\sphinxAtStartPar

not computed, even if quadruplets of improper atoms were listed in the
data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command.

calculate improper statistics, but compute no improper interactions.

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_ring:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ring}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_ring:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ring}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{70.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_ring:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{ring} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = &\frac{1}{6} K \left(\Delta_{ijl} + \Delta_{ijk} + \Delta_{kjl} \right)^6 \\
\Delta_{ijl} = & \cos{\theta_{ijl} - \cos{\theta_0}} \\
\Delta_{ijk} = & \cos{\theta_{ijk} - \cos{\theta_0}} \\
\Delta_{kjl} = & \cos{\theta_{kjl} - \cos{\theta_0}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(K\) is a prefactor, \(\theta\) is the angle formed by
the atoms specified by (i,j,k,l) indices and \(\theta_0\) its
equilibrium value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet (listed in the data file read
by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} command) are ordered i,j,k,l then
\(\theta_{ijl}\) is the angle between atoms i,j and l,
\(\theta_{ijk}\) is the angle between atoms i,j and k,
\(\theta_{kjl}\) is the angle between atoms j,k, and l.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The “ring” improper style implements the improper potential introduced
by Destree et al., in Equation (9) of {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_ring:destree}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Destree)}}}}.  This
potential does not affect small amplitude vibrations but is used in an
ad\sphinxhyphen{}hoc way to prevent the onset of accidentally large amplitude
fluctuations leading to the occurrence of a planar conformation of the
three bonds i\sphinxhyphen{}j, j\sphinxhyphen{}k and j\sphinxhyphen{}l, an intermediate conformation toward the
chiral inversion of a methine carbon.  In the “Impropers” section of
data file four atoms: i, j, k and l are specified with i,j and l lying
on the backbone of the chain and k specifying the chirality of j.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\theta_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if
LAMMPS was built with those packages.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{improper\_style sqdistharm@\spxentry{improper\_style sqdistharm}}\ignorespaces 

\section{improper\_style sqdistharm command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:improper-style-sqdistharm-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sqdistharm}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sqdistharm}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.1}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{sqdistharm} improper style uses the potential
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = K (d^2 - {d_0}^2)^2\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(d\) is the distance between the central atom and the plane formed
by the other three atoms.  If the 4 atoms in an improper quadruplet
(listed in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command) are ordered I,J,K,L then the L\sphinxhyphen{}atom is assumed to be the
central atom. Note that this is different from the convention used
in the improper\_style distance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the improper\_coeff command as in the example above, or in the data
file or restart files read by the read\_data or read\_restart commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy/distance\textasciicircum{}4)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\({d_0}^2\) (distance\textasciicircum{}2)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \({d_0}^2\) (in units distance\textasciicircum{}2) has be provided and not \(d_0\).


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This improper style can only be used if LAMMPS was built with the
MOLECULE package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} doc
page for more info.

\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{improper_sqdistharm:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\section{improper\_style umbrella command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_umbrella:improper-style-umbrella-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_umbrella:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{improper_umbrella:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_umbrella::doc}}

Accelerator Variants: \sphinxstyleemphasis{umbrella/omp}


\subsection{Syntax}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_umbrella:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{180.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_umbrella:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{umbrella} improper style uses the following potential, which is
commonly referred to as a classic inversion and used in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_bioFF::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DREIDING}}}} force field:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E = & \frac{1}{2}K\left( \frac{1}{\sin\omega_0}\right) ^2 \left( \cos\omega - \cos\omega_0\right) ^2 \qquad \omega_0 \neq 0^o \\
E = & K\left( 1-cos\omega\right)  \qquad \omega_0 = 0^o\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(K\) is the force constant and \(\omega\) is the angle between the IL
axis and the IJK plane:

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{umbrella}.jpg}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \(\omega_0 = 0\) the potential term has a minimum for the planar
structure.  Otherwise it has two minima at \(\omega +/- \omega_0\),
with a barrier in between.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_umbrella:umbrella-mayo}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(Mayo)}}}} for a description of the DREIDING force field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following coefficients must be defined for each improper type via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command as in the example
above, or in the data file or restart files read by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_restart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_restart}}}}
commands:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(K\) (energy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\omega_0\) (degrees)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles with a \sphinxstyleemphasis{gpu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{intel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{kk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omp}, or \sphinxstyleemphasis{opt} suffix are
functionally the same as the corresponding style without the suffix.
They have been optimized to run faster, depending on your available
hardware, as discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}}
page.  The accelerated styles take the same arguments and should
produce the same results, except for round\sphinxhyphen{}off and precision issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These accelerated styles are part of the GPU, INTEL, KOKKOS,
OPENMP, and OPT packages, respectively.  They are only enabled if

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the accelerated styles explicitly in your input script
by including their suffix, or you can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Run_options::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\sphinxhyphen{}suffix command\sphinxhyphen{}line switch}}}} when you invoke LAMMPS, or you can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{suffix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{suffix}}}} command in your input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Speed_packages::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Accelerator packages}}}} page for more
instructions on how to use the accelerated styles effectively.

\section{improper\_style zero command}
\label{\detokenize{improper_zero:improper-style-zero-command}}\label{\detokenize{improper_zero:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{improper_zero::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{improper_zero:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{[nocoeff]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{improper_zero:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nocoeff}
\PYG{k}{improper\PYGZus{}coeff}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{improper_zero:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using an improper style of zero means improper forces and energies are
not computed, but the geometry of improper quadruplets is still
accessible to other commands.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As an example, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_improper_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute improper/local}}}} command can be used to
compute the chi values for the list of quadruplets of improper atoms
listed in the data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command.  If no improper style is defined, this command cannot be
used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional \sphinxstyleemphasis{nocoeff} flag allows to read data files with a ImproperCoeff
section for any improper style. Similarly, any improper\_coeff commands
will only be checked for the improper type number and the rest ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{improper_coeff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{improper\_coeff}}}} command must be
used for all improper types, though no additional values are
specified.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{improper_zero:restrictions}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} attributes = same as \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} attributes, see below, also {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_vtk::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump vtk}}}} page
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} attributes = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} attributes = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz/gz} attributes = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz/zstd} attributes = none
\sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} attributes = same as \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} attributes, see below
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom/gz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom/zstd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg/gz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg/zstd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg/uef} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf/mpiio} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = id, mol, proc, procp1, type, element, mass,
                      x, y, z, xs, ys, zs, xu, yu, zu,
                      xsu, ysu, zsu, ix, iy, iz,
                      vx, vy, vz, fx, fy, fz,
                      q, mux, muy, muz, mu,
                      radius, diameter, omegax, omegay, omegaz,
                      angmomx, angmomy, angmomz, tqx, tqy, tqz,
                      c\PYGZus{}ID, c\PYGZus{}ID[I], f\PYGZus{}ID, f\PYGZus{}ID[I], v\PYGZus{}name,
                      i\PYGZus{}name, d\PYGZus{}name, i2\PYGZus{}name[I], d2\PYGZus{}name[I]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
id = atom ID
mol = molecule ID
proc = ID of processor that owns atom
procp1 = ID+1 of processor that owns atom
type = atom type
typelabel = atom {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{type label}}}}
element = name of atom element, as defined by {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command
mass = atom mass
x,y,z = unscaled atom coordinates
xs,ys,zs = scaled atom coordinates
xu,yu,zu = unwrapped atom coordinates
xsu,ysu,zsu = scaled unwrapped atom coordinates
ix,iy,iz = box image that the atom is in
vx,vy,vz = atom velocities
fx,fy,fz = forces on atoms
q = atom charge
mux,muy,muz = orientation of dipole moment of atom
mu = magnitude of dipole moment of atom
radius,diameter = radius, diameter of spherical particle
omegax,omegay,omegaz = angular velocity of spherical particle
angmomx,angmomy,angmomz = angular momentum of aspherical particle
tqx,tqy,tqz = torque on finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles
c\_ID = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by a compute with ID
c\_ID{[}I{]} = Ith column of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
f\_ID = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by a fix with ID
f\_ID{[}I{]} = Ith column of per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
v\_name = per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable with name
i\_name = custom integer vector with name
d\_name = custom floating point vector with name
i2\_name{[}I{]} = Ith column of custom integer array with name, I can include wildcard (see below)
d2\_name{[}I{]} = Ith column of custom floating point vector with name, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxalltt}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local/gz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local/zstd} attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = index, c\PYGZus{}ID, c\PYGZus{}ID[I], f\PYGZus{}ID, f\PYGZus{}ID[I]
  index = enumeration of local values
  c\PYGZus{}ID = local vector calculated by a compute with ID
  c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of local array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
  f\PYGZus{}ID = local vector calculated by a fix with ID
  f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of local array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid/vtk} attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
possible attributes = c\PYGZus{}ID:gname:dname, c\PYGZus{}ID:gname:dname[I], f\PYGZus{}ID:gname:dname, f\PYGZus{}ID:gname:dname[I]
  gname = name of grid defined by compute or fix
  dname = name of data field defined by compute or fix
  c\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}grid vector calculated by a compute with ID
  c\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}grid array calculated by a compute with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
  f\PYGZus{}ID = per\PYGZhy{}grid vector calculated by a fix with ID
  f\PYGZus{}ID[I] = Ith column of per\PYGZhy{}grid array calculated by a fix with ID, I can include wildcard (see below)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a snapshot of quantities to one or more files once every
\(N\) timesteps in one of several styles.  The timesteps on which
dump output is written can also be controlled by a variable.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Almost all the styles output per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data, i.e. one or more values
per atom.  The exceptions are as follows.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} styles output
one or more values per bond (angle, dihedral, improper) or per pair of
interacting atoms (force or neighbor interactions).  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} styles
output one or more values per grid cell, which are produced by other
commands which overlay the simulation domain with a regular grid.  See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto grid}}}} doc page for details.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{image}
style renders a JPG, PNG, or PPM image file of the system for each
snapshot, while the \sphinxstyleemphasis{movie} style combines and compresses the series
of images into a movie file; both styles are discussed in detail on
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}} page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only information for atoms in the specified group is dumped.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify thresh and region and refresh}}}}
commands can also alter what atoms are included.  Not all styles
support these options; see details on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} doc page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As described below, the filename determines the kind of output: text
or binary or gzipped, one big file or one per timestep, one file for
all the processors or multiple smaller files.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because periodic boundary conditions are enforced only on timesteps
when neighbor lists are rebuilt, the coordinates of an atom written
to a dump file may be slightly outside the simulation box.
Re\sphinxhyphen{}neighbor timesteps will not typically coincide with the
timesteps dump snapshots are written.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify
pbc}}}} command if you wish to force coordinates to be
strictly inside the simulation box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unless the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify sort}}}} option is invoked,
the lines of atom or grid information written to dump files
(typically one line per atom or grid cell) will be in an
indeterminate order for each snapshot.  This is even true when
running on a single processor, if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify sort}}}} option is on, which it is by default.  In this case
atoms are re\sphinxhyphen{}ordered periodically during a simulation, due to
spatial sorting.  It is also true when running in parallel, because
data for a single snapshot is collected from multiple processors,
each of which owns a subset of the atoms.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Without either including atom IDs or using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify sort}}}} option, it is impossible for visualization programs
(e.g. OVITO or VMD) or analysis tools to assign data in different
frames consistently to the same atom.  This can lead to incorrect
visualizations or results.  LAMMPS will print a warning in such cases.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} styles, sorting
is off by default.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid/vtk}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}, and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} styles, sorting by atom ID or grid ID is on by default. See
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{style} keyword determines what kind of data is written to the
dump file(s) and in what format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} style dump
files can be read directly by \sphinxhref{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd}{VMD},
a popular tool for visualizing and analyzing trajectories from atomic
and molecular systems.  For reading \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} style dump files, the
netcdf plugin needs to be recompiled from source using a NetCDF version
compatible with the one used by LAMMPS.  The bundled plugin binary
uses a very old version of NetCDF that is not compatible with LAMMPS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Likewise the \sphinxhref{https://www.ovito.org}{OVITO visualization package},
popular for materials modeling, can read the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{local}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} style atom dump files
directly.  With version 3.8 and above, OVITO can also read and
visualize \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} style dump files with grid cell data, including
iso\sphinxhyphen{}surface images of the grid cell values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that settings made via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}
command can also alter the format of individual values and content of
the dump file itself.  This includes the precision of values output to
text\sphinxhyphen{}based dump files which is controlled by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify
format}}}} command and its options.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Format of native LAMMPS format dump files:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} styles create files in a
simple LAMMPS\sphinxhyphen{}specific text format that is mostly self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory
when viewing a dump file.  Many post\sphinxhyphen{}processing tools either included
with LAMMPS or third\sphinxhyphen{}party tools can read this format, as does the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{rerun::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{rerun}}}} command.  See tools described on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Tools}}}} doc page for examples, including \sphinxhref{https://lammps.github.io/pizza}{Pizza.py}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For all these styles, the dimensions of the simulation box are
included in each snapshot.  The simulation box in LAMMPS can be
defined in one of 3 ways: orthogonal, restricted triclinic, and
general triclinic.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto triclinic}}}}
doc page for a detailed description of all 3 options.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For an orthogonal simulation box the box information is formatted as:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ITEM: BOX BOUNDS xx yy zz
xlo xhi
ylo yhi
zlo zhi
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where xlo,xhi are the maximum extents of the simulation box in the
\(x\)\sphinxhyphen{}dimension, and similarly for \(y\) and \(z\).  The
“xx yy zz” terms are six characters that encode the style of boundary for each
of the six simulation box boundaries (xlo,xhi; ylo,yhi; and zlo,zhi).  Each of
the six characters is one of \sphinxstyleemphasis{p} (periodic), \sphinxstyleemphasis{f} (fixed), \sphinxstyleemphasis{s} (shrink wrap),
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{m} (shrink wrapped with a minimum value).  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{boundary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{boundary}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a restricted triclinic simulation box, an orthogonal bounding box
which encloses the restricted triclinic simulation box is output,
along with the three tilt factors (\sphinxstyleemphasis{xy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yz}) of the triclinic
box, formatted as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ITEM: BOX BOUNDS xy xz yz xx yy zz
xlo\PYGZus{}bound xhi\PYGZus{}bound xy
ylo\PYGZus{}bound yhi\PYGZus{}bound xz
zlo\PYGZus{}bound zhi\PYGZus{}bound yz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The presence of the text “xy xz yz” in the ITEM line indicates that
the three tilt factors will be included on each of the three following lines.
This bounding box is convenient for many visualization programs.  The
meaning of the six character flags for “xx yy zz” is the same as above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the first two numbers on each line are now xlo\_bound instead
of xlo, etc. because they represent a bounding box.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto
triclinic}}}} page for a geometric description of
triclinic boxes, as defined by LAMMPS, simple formulas for how the six
bounding box extents (xlo\_bound, xhi\_bound, etc.) are calculated from the
triclinic parameters, and how to transform those parameters to and
from other commonly used triclinic representations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a general triclinic simulation box, see the “General triclinic”
section below for a description of the ITEM: BOX BOUNDS format as well
as how per\sphinxhyphen{}atom coordinates and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector quantities are output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} styles output a “ITEM: NUMBER OF ATOMS” line
with the count of atoms in the snapshot.  Likewise they output an
“ITEM: ATOMS” line which includes column descriptors for the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
lines that follow.  For example, the descriptors would be “id type xs
ys zs” for the default \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} style, and would be the atom attributes
you specify in the dump command for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} style.  Each
subsequent line will list the data for a single atom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, atom coordinates are written to the file, along with
the atom ID and atom type.  By default, atom coords are written in a
scaled format (from 0 to 1).  That is, an \(x\) value of 0.25 means the
atom is at a location 1/4 of the distance from \sphinxstyleemphasis{xlo} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{xhi} of the box
boundaries.  The format can be changed to unscaled coords via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} settings.  Image flags can also be
added for each atom via dump\_modify.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} allows you to specify a list of atom attributes to be
written to the dump file for each atom.  Possible attributes are
listed above and will appear in the order specified.  You cannot
specify a quantity that is not defined for a particular
simulation—such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} for atom style \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond}, since that atom style
does not assign charges.  Dumps occur at the very end of a timestep,
so atom attributes will include effects due to fixes that are applied
during the timestep.  An explanation of the possible dump custom
attributes is given below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 22Dec2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} the dimension of the simulation domain and size of
the Nx by Ny by Nz grid that overlays the simulation domain are also
output with each snapshot:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ITEM: DIMENSION
dim
ITEM: GRID SIZE
nx ny nz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value dim will be 2 or 3 for 2d or 3d simulations.  It is included
so that post\sphinxhyphen{}processing tools like \sphinxhref{https://www.ovito.org}{OVITO},
which can visualize grid\sphinxhyphen{}based quantities know how to draw each grid
cell.  The grid size will match the input script parameters for
grid(s) created by the computes or fixes which are referenced by the
the dump command.  For 2d simulations (and grids), nz will always
be 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There will also be an “ITEM: GRID DATA” line which includes column
descriptors for the per grid cell data.  Each subsequent line (Nx *
Ny * Nz lines) will list the data for a single grid cell.  If grid
cell IDs are included in the output via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute
property/grid}}}} command, then the IDs will
range from 1 to N = Nx*Ny*Nz.  The ordering of IDs is with the x index
varying fastest, then the y index, and the z index varying slowest.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{local}, local output generated by {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{computes}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fixes}}}} is used to generate lines of output that is
written to the dump file.  This local data is typically calculated by
each processor based on the atoms it owns, but there may be zero or
more entities per atom (e.g., a list of bond distances).  An explanation
of the possible dump local attributes is given below.  Note that by
using input from the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_property_local::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute property/local}}}} command with dump local, it is possible to
generate information on bonds, angles, etc. that can be cut and pasted
directly into a data file read by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{read_data::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{read\_data}}}}
command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump files in other popular formats:

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section only discusses file formats relevant to this doc page.
The top of this page has links to other dump commands (with their
own pages) which write files in additional popular formats.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} has the same command syntax as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} and writes
extended CFG format files, as used by the \sphinxhref{http://li.mit.edu/Archive/Graphics/A/}{AtomEye} visualization package.
Since the extended CFG format uses a single snapshot of the system per
file, a wildcard “*” must be included in the filename, as discussed
below.  The list of atom attributes for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} must begin with
either “mass type xs ys zs” or “mass type xsu ysu zsu” since these
quantities are needed to write the CFG files in the appropriate format
(though the “mass” and “type” fields do not appear explicitly in the
file).  Any remaining attributes will be stored as “auxiliary
properties” in the CFG files.  Note that you will typically want to
use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify element}}}} command with
CFG\sphinxhyphen{}formatted files, to associate element names with atom types, so
that AtomEye can render atoms appropriately. When unwrapped
coordinates \sphinxstyleemphasis{xsu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ysu}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zsu} are requested, the nominal AtomEye
periodic cell dimensions are expanded by a large factor UNWRAPEXPAND =
10.0, which ensures atoms that are displayed correctly for up to
UNWRAPEXPAND/2 periodic boundary crossings in any direction.  Beyond
this, AtomEye will rewrap the unwrapped coordinates.  The expansion
causes the atoms to be drawn farther away from the viewer, but it is
easy to zoom the atoms closer, and the interatomic distances are
unaffected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} style writes DCD files, a standard atomic trajectory format
used by the CHARMM, NAMD, and XPlor molecular dynamics packages.  DCD
files are binary and thus may not be portable to different machines.
The number of atoms per snapshot cannot change with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} style.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command
allows DCD coordinates to be written “unwrapped” by the image flags
for each atom.  Unwrapped means that if the atom has passed through
a periodic boundary one or more times, the value is printed for what
the coordinate would be if it had not been wrapped back into the
periodic box.  Note that these coordinates may thus be far outside
the box size stored with the snapshot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} style writes XTC files, a compressed trajectory format used
by the GROMACS molecular dynamics package, and described \sphinxhref{https://manual.gromacs.org/current/reference-manual/file-formats.html\#xtc}{here}.
The precision used in XTC files can be adjusted via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command.  The default value of 1000
means that coordinates are stored to 1/1000 nanometer accuracy.  XTC
files are portable binary files written in the NFS XDR data format, so
that any machine which supports XDR should be able to read them.  The
number of atoms per snapshot cannot change with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} style.  The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command allows
XTC coordinates to be written “unwrapped” by the image flags for each
atom.  Unwrapped means that if the atom has passed through a periodic
boundary one or more times, the value is printed for what the
coordinate would be if it had not been wrapped back into the periodic
box.  Note that these coordinates may thus be far outside the box size
stored with the snapshot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} style writes XYZ files, which is a simple text\sphinxhyphen{}based
coordinate format that many codes can read. Specifically it has a line
with the number of atoms, then a comment line that is usually ignored
followed by one line per atom with the atom type and the \(x\)\sphinxhyphen{},
\(y\)\sphinxhyphen{}, and \(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate of that atom.  You can use the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify element}}}} option to change the output
from using the (numerical) atom type to an element name (or some other
label). This option will help many visualization programs to guess bonds
and colors. You can use the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify types labels}}}}
option to replace numeric atom types with {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{type labels}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 22Dec2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid/vtk} style writes VTK files for grid data on a regular
rectilinear grid.  Its content is conceptually similar to that of the
text file produced by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} style, except that it in an XML\sphinxhyphen{}based
format which visualization programs which support the VTK format can
read, e.g. the \sphinxhref{https://www.paraview.org}{ParaView tool}.  For this
style, there can only be 1 or 3 per grid cell attributes specified.
If it is a single value, it is a scalar quantity.  If 3 values are
specified it is encoded in the VTK file as a vector quantity (for each
grid cell).  The filename for this style must include a “*” wildcard
character to produce one file per snapshot; see details below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,added}{Added in version 4May2022.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump style \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} has the same command syntax as style \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} and
writes YAML format files that can be easily parsed by a variety of
data processing tools and programming languages.  Each timestep will
be written as a YAML “document” (i.e., starts with “—” and ends with
“…”).  The style supports writing one file per timestep through the
“*” wildcard but not multi\sphinxhyphen{}processor outputs with the “\%” token in
the filename.  In addition to per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data, {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo}}}}
data can be included in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} style dump file using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify thermo yes}}}}. The data included in the
dump file uses the “thermo” tag and is otherwise identical to data
specified by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}} command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Below is an example for a YAML format dump created by the following commands.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yaml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.yaml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iz}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{format}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{format}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZpc{} 10.6e}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The tags “time”, “units”, and “thermo” are optional and enabled by the
dump\_modify command. The list under the “box” tag has three lines for
orthogonal boxes and four lines for triclinic boxes, where the first
three are the box boundaries and the fourth the three tilt factors
(\(xy\), \(xz\), \(yz\)).  The “thermo” data follows the
format of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} thermo style.  The “keywords” tag lists the
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom properties contained in the “data” columns, which contain a
list with one line per atom.  The keywords may be renamed using the
dump\_modify command same as for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} dump style.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nn}{\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}}
\PYG{n+nt}{creator}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{LAMMPS}
\PYG{n+nt}{timestep}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{0}
