\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Frequency of dump output:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dumps are performed on timesteps that are a multiple of \(N\)
(including timestep 0) and on the last timestep of a minimization if
the minimization converges.  Note that this means a dump will not be
performed on the initial timestep after the dump command is invoked,
if the current timestep is not a multiple of \(N\).  This behavior
can be changed via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify first}}}} command,
which can also be useful if the dump command is invoked after a
minimization ended on an arbitrary timestep.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value of \(N\) can be changed between runs by using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command (not allowed for \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd}
style).  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command also
allows a variable to be used to determine the sequence of timesteps on
which dump files are written.  In this mode a dump on the first
timestep of a run will also not be written unless the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify first}}}} command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you instead want to dump snapshots based on simulation time (in
time units of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units command}}}} command), the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify
every/time}}}} command can be used.  This can be useful
when the timestep size varies during a simulation run, e.g. by use of
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_dt_reset::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix dt/reset}}}} command.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump filenames:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The specified dump filename determines how the dump file(s) is
written.  The default is to write one large text file, which is opened
when the dump command is invoked and closed when an {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump}}}} command is used or when LAMMPS exits.  For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} and
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} styles, this is a single large binary file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Many of the styles allow dump filenames to contain either or both of
two wildcard characters.  If a “*” character appears in the filename,
then one file per snapshot is written and the “*” character is
replaced with the timestep value.  For example, tmp.dump.* becomes
tmp.dump.0, tmp.dump.10000, tmp.dump.20000, etc.  This option is not
available for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} styles.  Note that the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify pad}}}} command can be used to ensure all
timestep numbers are the same length (e.g., 00010), which can make it
easier to read a series of dump files in order with some
post\sphinxhyphen{}processing tools.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a “\%” character appears in the filename, then each of P processors
writes a portion of the dump file, and the “\%” character is replaced
with the processor ID from \(0\) to \(P-1\).  For example,
tmp.dump.\% becomes tmp.dump.0, tmp.dump.1, … tmp.dump.:math:\sphinxtitleref{P\sphinxhyphen{}1},
etc.  This creates smaller files and can be a fast mode of output on
parallel machines that support parallel I/O for output. This option is
\sphinxstylestrong{not} available for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid/vtk}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml}
styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, \(P\) is the the number of processors, meaning one file per
processor, but \(P\) can be set to a smaller value via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command.
These options can be the most efficient way of writing out dump files
when running on large numbers of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that using the “*” and “\%” characters together can produce a
large number of small dump files!

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,deprecated}{Deprecated since version 21Nov2023.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The MPIIO package and the the corresponding “/mpiio” dump styles, except
for the unrelated “netcdf/mpiio” style were removed from LAMMPS.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Compression of dump file data:

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the specified filename ends with “.bin” or “.lammpsbin”, the dump
file (or files, if “*” or “\%” is also used) is written in binary
format.  A binary dump file will be about the same size as a text
version, but will typically write out much faster.  Of course, when
post\sphinxhyphen{}processing, you will need to convert it back to text format (see
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Tools:binary}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{binary2txt tool}}}}) or write your own code to read
the binary file.  The format of the binary file can be understood by
looking at the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/binary2txt.cpp}} file.  This option is only
available for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the filename ends with “.gz”, the dump file (or files, if “*” or “\%”
is also used) is written in gzipped format.  A gzipped dump file will be
about \(3\times\) smaller than the text version, but will also take
longer to write.  This option is not available for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}
styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that styles that end with \sphinxstyleemphasis{gz} are identical in command syntax to
the corresponding styles without “gz”, however, they generate
compressed files using the zlib library. Thus the filename suffix
“.gz” is mandatory. This is an alternative approach to writing
compressed files via a pipe, as done by the regular dump styles, which
may be required on clusters where the interface to the high\sphinxhyphen{}speed
network disallows using the fork() library call (which is needed for a
pipe).  For the remainder of this page, you should thus consider the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom/gz} styles (etc.) to be inter\sphinxhyphen{}changeable, with the
exception of the required filename suffix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly, styles that end with \sphinxstyleemphasis{zstd} are identical to the gz styles,
but use the Zstd compression library instead and require a “.zst”
suffix. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} page for details on
how to control the compression level in both variants.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
General triclinic simulation box output for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} styles:

\sphinxAtStartPar
As mentioned above, the simulation box can be defined as a general
triclinic box, which means that 3 arbitrary box edge vectors \sphinxstylestrong{A},
\sphinxstylestrong{B}, \sphinxstylestrong{C} can be specified.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto triclinic}}}} doc page for a detailed description of general
triclinic boxes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option is provided as a convenience for users who may be
converting data from solid\sphinxhyphen{}state crystallographic representations or
from DFT codes for input to LAMMPS.  However, as explained on the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto\_triclinic}}}} doc page, internally, LAMMPS
only uses restricted triclinic simulation boxes.  This means the box
and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom information (e.g. coordinates, velocities) LAMMPS stores
are converted (rotated) from general to restricted triclinic form when
the system is created.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For dump output, if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify triclinic/general}}}} command is used, the box description and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
coordinates and other per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors will be converted (rotated)
from restricted to general form when each dump file snapshots is
output.  This option can only be used if the simulation box was
initially created as general triclinic.  If the option is not used,
and the simulation box is general triclinic, then the dump file
snapshots will reflect the internal restricted triclinic geometry.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dump\_modify triclinic/general option affects 3 aspects of the dump
file output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
First, the format for the BOX BOUNDS is as follows

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ITEM: BOX BOUNDS abc origin
ax ay az originx
bx by bz originy
cx cy cz originz
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the \sphinxstylestrong{A} edge vector of the box is (ax,ay,az) and similarly
for \sphinxstylestrong{B} and \sphinxstylestrong{C}.  The origin of all 3 edge vectors is (originx,
originy, originz).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Second, the coordinates of each atom are converted (rotated) so that
the atom is inside (or near) the general triclinic box defined by the
\sphinxstylestrong{A}, \sphinxstylestrong{B}, \sphinxstylestrong{C} edge vectors.  For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, this only alters
output for unscaled atom coords, via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify scaled no}}}} setting. For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, this alters output for
either unscaled or unwrapped output of atom coords, via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{x,y,z} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{xu,yu,zu} attributes.  For output of scaled atom coords by both
styles, there is no difference between restricted and general
triclinic values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Third, the output for any attribute of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} style which
represents a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector quantity will be converted (rotated) to
be oriented consistent with the general triclinic box and its
orientation relative to the standard xyz coordinate axes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This applies to the following \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} style attributes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vx,vy,vz = atom velocities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fx,fy,fz = forces on atoms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mux,muy,muz = orientation of dipole moment of atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
omegax,omegay,omegaz = angular velocity of spherical particle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
angmomx,angmomy,angmomz = angular momentum of aspherical particle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tqx,tqy,tqz = torque on finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if the velocity of an atom in a restricted triclinic box
is along the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis, then it will be output for a general triclinic
box as a vector along the \sphinxstylestrong{A} edge vector of the box.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For style \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify thresh}}}}
command may access per\sphinxhyphen{}atom attributes either directly or
indirectly through a compute or variable.  If the attribute is an
atom coordinate or one of the vectors mentioned above, its value
will \sphinxstyleemphasis{NOT} be a general triclinic (rotated) value.  Rather it will
be a restricted triclinic value.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Arguments for different styles:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The sections below describe per\sphinxhyphen{}atom, local, and per grid cell
attributes which can be used as arguments to the various styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that in the discussion below, for styles which can reference
values from a compute or fix or custom atom property, like the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} styles, the bracketed index
\(i\) can be specified using a wildcard asterisk with the index to
effectively specify multiple values.  This takes the form “*” or
“*n” or “m*” or “m*n”.  If \(N\) is the number of columns in
the array, then an asterisk with no numeric values means all column
indices from 1 to \(N\).  A leading asterisk means all indices
from 1 to n (inclusive).  A trailing asterisk means all indices from m
to \(N\) (inclusive).  A middle asterisk means all indices from m
to n (inclusive).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using a wildcard is the same as if the individual columns of the array
had been listed one by one.  For example, these two dump commands are
equivalent, since the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute_stress_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute stress/atom}}}}
command creates a per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with six columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{myPress}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stress}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{NULL}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myPress[}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{]}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myPress[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myPress[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myPress[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{                                  }\PYG{n}{myPress[4]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myPress[5]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{myPress[6]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}atom attributes used as arguments to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} styles:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{id}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mol}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{proc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{procp1}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{typelabel}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{element}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{mass},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} attributes are self\sphinxhyphen{}explanatory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Id} is the atom ID.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Mol} is the molecule ID, included in the data file
for molecular systems.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Proc} is the ID of the processor (0 to
\(N_\text{procs}-1\)) that currently owns the atom.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Procp1} is the
proc ID+1, which can be convenient in place of a \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} attribute (1 to
\(N_\text{types}\)) for coloring atoms in a visualization program.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Type} is the atom type (1 to \(N_\text{types}\)).  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Typelabel} is the
atom {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_type_labels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{type label}}}}.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Element} is typically the
chemical name of an element, which you must assign to each type via the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify element}}}} command.  More generally, it can
be any string you wish to associated with an atom type.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{Mass} is the atom
mass.  The quantities \sphinxstyleemphasis{vx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{vz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fy}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{fz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{q} are
components of atom velocity and force and atomic charge.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are several options for outputting atom coordinates.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{x},
\sphinxstyleemphasis{y}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{z} attributes write atom coordinates “unscaled”, in the
appropriate distance {\hyperref[\detokenize{units::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{units}}}} (\(\AA\),
\(\sigma\), etc.).  Use \sphinxstyleemphasis{xs}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ys}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zs} if you want the
coordinates “scaled” to the box size so that each value is 0.0 to 1.0.
If the simulation box is triclinic (tilted), then all atom coords will
still be between 0.0 and 1.0.  The actual unscaled \((x,y,z)\)
coordinate is \(x_s a + y_s b + z_s c\), where \((a,b,c)\) are
the non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal vectors of the simulation box edges, as discussed on
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Howto_triclinic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Howto triclinic}}}} page.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yu}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zu} if you want the coordinates “unwrapped” by the
image flags for each atom.  Unwrapped means that if the atom has passed
through a periodic boundary one or more times, the value is printed for
what the coordinate would be if it had not been wrapped back into the
periodic box.  Note that using \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yu}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zu} means that the
coordinate values may be far outside the box bounds printed with the
snapshot.  Using \sphinxstyleemphasis{xsu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ysu}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zsu} is similar to using \sphinxstyleemphasis{xu}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{yu},
and \sphinxstyleemphasis{zu}, except that the unwrapped coordinates are scaled by the box
size. Atoms that have passed through a periodic boundary will have the
corresponding coordinate increased or decreased by 1.0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The image flags can be printed directly using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ix}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{iy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{iz}
attributes.  For periodic dimensions, they specify which image of the
simulation box the atom is considered to be in.  An image of 0 means
it is inside the box as defined.  A value of 2 means add 2 box lengths
to get the true value.  A value of \(-1\) means subtract 1 box length to
get the true value.  LAMMPS updates these flags as atoms cross
periodic boundaries during the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mux}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{muy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{muz} attributes are specific to dipolar systems
defined with an atom style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{dipole}.  They give the orientation of
the atom’s point dipole moment.  The \sphinxstyleemphasis{mu} attribute gives the magnitude
of the atom’s dipole moment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{radius} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{diameter} attributes are specific to spherical
particles that have a finite size, such as those defined with an atom
style of \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{omegax}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{omegay}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{omegaz} attributes are specific to
finite\sphinxhyphen{}size spherical particles that have an angular velocity.  Only
certain atom styles, such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{sphere}, define this quantity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmomx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmomy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{angmomz} attributes are specific to
finite\sphinxhyphen{}size aspherical particles that have an angular momentum.  Only
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ellipsoid} atom style defines this quantity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{tqx}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{tqy}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{tqz} attributes are for finite\sphinxhyphen{}size particles
that can sustain a rotational torque due to interactions with other
particles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID{[}I{]}} attributes allow per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors or arrays
calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} to be output.  The ID in the
attribute should be replaced by the actual ID of the compute that has
been defined previously in the input script.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command for details.  There are computes for calculating the
per\sphinxhyphen{}atom energy, stress, centro\sphinxhyphen{}symmetry parameter, and coordination
number of individual atoms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that computes which calculate global or local quantities, as
opposed to per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities, cannot be output in a dump custom
command.  Instead, global quantities can be output by the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style custom}}}} command, and local quantities
can be output by the dump local command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} is used as a attribute, then the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by
the compute is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID{[}i{]}} is used, then \(i\) must be in
the range from 1 to \(M\), which will print the \(i\)th column
of the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with \(M\) columns calculated by the compute.
See the discussion above for how \(i\) can be specified with a
wildcard asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID{[}I{]}} attributes allow vector or array per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
quantities calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} to be output.  The ID in the
attribute should be replaced by the actual ID of the fix that has been
defined previously in the input script.  The {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_ave_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix ave/atom}}}} command is one that calculates per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities.
Since it can time\sphinxhyphen{}average per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities produced by any
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}}, or atom\sphinxhyphen{}style {\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}}, this allows those time\sphinxhyphen{}averaged results to be written to a
dump file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} is used as a attribute, then the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vector calculated by
the fix is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID{[}i{]}} is used, then \(i\) must be in the
range from 1 to \(M\), which will print the \(i\)th column of
the per\sphinxhyphen{}atom array with \(M\) columns calculated by the fix.  See
the discussion above for how \(i\) can be specified with a wildcard
asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{v\_name} attribute allows per\sphinxhyphen{}atom vectors calculated by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{variable::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{variable}}}} to be output.  The name in the attribute
should be replaced by the actual name of the variable that has been
defined previously in the input script.  Only an atom\sphinxhyphen{}style variable can
be referenced, since it is the only style that generates per\sphinxhyphen{}atom
values.  Variables of style \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} can reference individual atom
attributes, per\sphinxhyphen{}atom attributes, thermodynamic keywords, or invoke other
computes, fixes, or variables when they are evaluated, so this is a very
general means of creating quantities to output to a dump file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{i\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name} attributes refer to
custom per\sphinxhyphen{}atom integer and floating\sphinxhyphen{}point vectors or arrays that have
been added via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_property_atom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix property/atom}}}}
command.  When that command is used specific names are given to each
attribute which are the “name” portion of these keywords.  For arrays
\sphinxstyleemphasis{i2\_name} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{d2\_name}, the column of the array must also be included
following the name in brackets (e.g., d2\_xyz{[}i{]}, i2\_mySpin{[}i{]}, where
\(i\) is in the range from 1 to \(M\), where \(M\) is the
number of columns in the custom array).  See the discussion above for
how \(i\) can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively
specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Modify}}}} page for information on how to add
new compute and fix styles to LAMMPS to calculate per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities
which could then be output into dump files.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Attributes used as arguments to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} style:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{index} attribute can be used to generate an index number from 1
to N for each line written into the dump file, where N is the total
number of local datums from all processors, or lines of output that
will appear in the snapshot.  Note that because data from different
processors depend on what atoms they currently own, and atoms migrate
between processor, there is no guarantee that the same index will be
used for the same info (e.g. a particular bond) in successive
snapshots.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID{[}I{]}} attributes allow local vectors or arrays
calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} to be output.  The ID in the
attribute should be replaced by the actual ID of the compute that has
been defined previously in the input script.  See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} command for details.  There are computes for
calculating local information such as indices, types, and energies for
bonds and angles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that computes which calculate global or per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities, as
opposed to local quantities, cannot be output in a dump local command.
Instead, global quantities can be output by the {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style
custom}}}} command, and per\sphinxhyphen{}atom quantities can be output
by the dump custom command.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} is used as a attribute, then the local vector calculated by
the compute is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID{[}I{]}} is used, then I must be in the
range from 1\sphinxhyphen{}M, which will print the Ith column of the local array
with M columns calculated by the compute.  See the discussion above
for how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively
specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID{[}I{]}} attributes allow local vectors or arrays
calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} to be output.  The ID in the attribute
should be replaced by the actual ID of the fix that has been defined
previously in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} is used as a attribute, then the local vector calculated by
the fix is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID{[}I{]}} is used, then I must be in the
range from 1\sphinxhyphen{}M, which will print the Ith column of the local with M
columns calculated by the fix.  See the discussion above for how I can
be specified with a wildcard asterisk to effectively specify multiple
values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is an example of how to dump bond info for a system, including
the distance and energy of each bond:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{property}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batom2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{btype}
\PYG{k}{compute }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bond}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eng}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{local}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tmp.dump}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}1[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}2[2]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Attributes used as arguments to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid/vtk} styles:

\sphinxAtStartPar
The attributes that begin with \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID} both take
colon\sphinxhyphen{}separated fields \sphinxstyleemphasis{gname} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{dname}.  These refer to a grid
name and data field name which is defined by the compute or fix.  Note
that a compute or fix can define one or more grids (of different
sizes) and one or more data fields for each of those grids.  The sizes
of all grids output in a single dump grid command must be the same.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} attributes allow
per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vectors or arrays calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{compute::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{compute}}}} to
be output.  The ID in the attribute should be replaced by the actual
ID of the compute that has been defined previously in the input
script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname} is used as a attribute, then the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector
calculated by the compute is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{c\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} is
used, then I must be in the range from 1\sphinxhyphen{}M, which will print the Ith
column of the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array with M columns calculated by the compute.
See the discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard
asterisk to effectively specify multiple values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} attributes allow
per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vectors or arrays calculated by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix}}}} to be
output.  The ID in the attribute should be replaced by the actual ID
of the fix that has been defined previously in the input script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname} is used as a attribute, then the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector
calculated by the fix is printed.  If \sphinxstyleemphasis{f\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}} is used,
then I must be in the range from 1\sphinxhyphen{}M, which will print the Ith column
of the per\sphinxhyphen{}grid with M columns calculated by the fix.  See the
discussion above for how I can be specified with a wildcard asterisk
to effectively specify multiple values.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To write gzipped dump files, you must either compile LAMMPS with the
\sphinxhyphen{}DLAMMPS\_GZIP option or use the styles from the COMPRESS package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_settings::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build settings}}}} page for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
While a dump command is active (i.e., has not been stopped by using
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump command}}}}), no commands may be used that will
change the timestep (e.g., {\hyperref[\detokenize{reset_timestep::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{reset\_timestep}}}}).
LAMMPS will terminate with an error otherwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom/gz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg/gz}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom/gz}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz/gz} styles are part of
the COMPRESS package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with
that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for
more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{yaml} styles are part of the EXTRA\sphinxhyphen{}DUMP package.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\section{dump atom/adios  command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:dump-atom-adios-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_adios::doc}}

\section{dump custom/adios command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:dump-custom-adios-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file.bp}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file.bp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be imaged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
adios = style of dump command (other styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc page)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file.bp = name of file/stream to write to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = same options as in {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}} command

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{adios1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atoms.bp}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{4a}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump\PYGZus{}adios.bp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}p}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{subgroup}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{custom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump\PYGZus{}adios.bp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ys}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a snapshot of atom coordinates every \(N\) timesteps in the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/ornladios/ADIOS2}{ADIOS}\sphinxhyphen{}based “BP” file format, or using different I/O solutions in
ADIOS, to a stream that can be read on\sphinxhyphen{}line by another program.
ADIOS\sphinxhyphen{}BP files are binary, portable, and self\sphinxhyphen{}describing.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To be able to use ADIOS, a file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adios2\_config.xml}} with specific
configuration settings is expected in the current working directory.
If the file is not present, LAMMPS will try to create a minimal
default file.  Please refer to the ADIOS documentation for details on
how to adjust this file for optimal performance and desired features.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use from write\_dump:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is possible to use these dump styles with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_dump}}}} command.  In this case, the sub\sphinxhyphen{}intervals
must not be set at all.  The write\_dump command can be used to
create a new file at each individual dump.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{4}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.bp}
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{adios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{singledump.bp}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump_adios:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms per snapshot \sphinxstylestrong{can} change with the adios style.
When using the ADIOS tool ‘bpls’ to list the content of a .bp file,
bpls will print \sphinxstyleemphasis{\_\_} for the size of the output table indicating that
its size is changing every step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom/adios} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom/adios} dump styles are part of the ADIOS
package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump}}}}

\section{dump cfg/uef command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:dump-cfg-uef-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cfg}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ys}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be dumped

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of file to write dump info to
\begin{sphinxalltt}
args = same as args for {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump custom}}}}
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cfg}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.cfg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ys}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zs}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cfg}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{uef}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.cfg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ys}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zs}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}stress}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This command is used to dump atomic coordinates in the
reference frame of the applied flow field when
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/uef}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/uef}}}} is used.
Only the atomic coordinates and frame\sphinxhyphen{}invariant scalar quantities
will be in the flow frame. If velocities are selected
as output, for example, they will not be in the same
reference frame as the atomic positions.


\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fix is part of the UEF package. It is only enabled if LAMMPS
was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}}
page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command can only be used when {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/uef}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix npt/uef}}}} is active.


\subsection{Related commands}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{fix_nh_uef::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{fix nvt/uef}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{dump_cfg_uef:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
none

\index{dump h5md@\spxentry{dump h5md}}\ignorespaces 

\section{dump h5md command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:dump-h5md-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file.h5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be imaged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{h5md} = style of dump command (other styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc page)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file.h5 = name of file to write to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = \sphinxstyleemphasis{position} options or \sphinxstyleemphasis{image} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity} options or \sphinxstyleemphasis{force} options or \sphinxstyleemphasis{species} options or \sphinxstyleemphasis{file\_from} ID or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value or \sphinxstyleemphasis{create\_group} value or \sphinxstyleemphasis{author} value = list of data elements to dump, with their dump “sub\sphinxhyphen{}intervals”
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{position} options
\sphinxstyleemphasis{image}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity} options
\sphinxstyleemphasis{force} options
\sphinxstyleemphasis{species} options
\sphinxstyleemphasis{file\_from} ID = do not open a new file, re\sphinxhyphen{}use the already opened file from dump ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{box} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{create\_group} value = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{author} value = quoted string
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that at least one element must be specified and that \sphinxstyleemphasis{image} may only be
present if \sphinxstyleemphasis{position} is specified first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the elements \sphinxstyleemphasis{position}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{force} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{species}, a
sub\sphinxhyphen{}interval may be specified to write the data only every N\_element
iterations of the dump (i.e. every N*N\_element time steps). This is
specified by this option directly following the element declaration:
\begin{sphinxalltt}
options = \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} N\_element
\end{sphinxalltt}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{h5md1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump\PYGZus{}h5md.h5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{position}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{image}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{h5md1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump\PYGZus{}h5md.h5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{position}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{every}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{h5md1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump\PYGZus{}h5md.h5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{velocity }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{author}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{John Doe}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a snapshot of atom coordinates every N timesteps in the
\sphinxhref{https://www.hdfgroup.org/solutions/hdf5/}{HDF5} based \sphinxhref{https://nongnu.org/h5md/}{H5MD} file format {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_h5md:h5md-cpc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{(de Buyl)}}}}.
HDF5 files are binary, portable and self\sphinxhyphen{}describing.  This dump style
will write only one file, on the root node.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Several dumps may write to the same file, by using file\_from and
referring to a previously defined dump.  Several groups may also be
stored within the same file by defining several dumps.  A dump that
refers (via \sphinxstyleemphasis{file\_from}) to an already open dump ID and that concerns
another particle group must specify \sphinxstyleemphasis{create\_group yes}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each data element is written every N*N\_element steps. For \sphinxstyleemphasis{image}, no
sub\sphinxhyphen{}interval is needed as it must be present at the same interval as
\sphinxstyleemphasis{position}.  \sphinxstyleemphasis{image} must be given after \sphinxstyleemphasis{position} in any case.  The
box information (edges in each dimension) is stored at the same
interval than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{position} element, if present. Else it is stored
every N steps.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because periodic boundary conditions are enforced only on
timesteps when neighbor lists are rebuilt, the coordinates of an atom
written to a dump file may be slightly outside the simulation box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use from write\_dump:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is possible to use this dump style with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{write_dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{write\_dump}}}} command.  In this case, the sub\sphinxhyphen{}intervals
must not be set at all.  The write\_dump command can be used either to
create a new file or to add current data to an existing dump file by
using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{file\_from} keyword.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typically, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{species} data is fixed. The following two commands
store the position data every 100 timesteps, with the image data, and
store once the species data in the same file.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{h5md1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.h5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{position}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{image}
\PYG{k}{write\PYGZus{}dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.h5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file\PYGZus{}from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{h5md1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{species}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of atoms per snapshot cannot change with the h5md style.
The position data is stored wrapped (box boundaries not enforced, see
note above).  Only orthogonal domains are currently supported. This is
a limitation of the present dump h5md command and not of H5MD itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{h5md} dump style is part of the H5MD package. It is only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info. It also requires
(i) building the ch5md library provided with LAMMPS (See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.) and (ii) having
the \sphinxhref{https://www.hdfgroup.org/solutions/hdf5/}{HDF5} library installed (C bindings are sufficient) on
your system.  The library ch5md is compiled with the h5cc wrapper
provided by the HDF5 library.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{dump_h5md:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump}}}}

\section{dump image command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_image:dump-image-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_image:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{dump_image:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_image::doc}}

\section{dump movie command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_image:dump-movie-command}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(see below for {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image:dump-modify-image}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{dump\_modify options}}}} specific to dump image/movie)


\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_image:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{color}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diameter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be imaged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
style = \sphinxstyleemphasis{image} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{movie} = style of dump command (other styles such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc page)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of file to write image to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
color = atom attribute that determines color of each atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
diameter = atom attribute that determines size of each atom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero or more keyword/value pairs may be appended

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{adiam} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{body} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{size} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{view} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{center} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{up} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{zoom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{box} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{axes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{subbox} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{shiny} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{fsaa} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{ssao}
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do or do not draw atoms
\sphinxstyleemphasis{adiam} size = numeric value for atom diameter (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bond} values = color width = color and width of bonds
  color = \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}
  width = number or \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{type} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{none}
    number = numeric value for bond width (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{grid} = per\sphinxhyphen{}grid value to use when coloring each grid cell
  per\sphinxhyphen{}grid value = c\_ID:gname:dname, c\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}, f\_ID:gname:dname, f\_ID:gname:dname{[}I{]}
    gname = name of grid defined by compute or fix
    dname = name of data field defined by compute or fix
    c\_ID = per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector calculated by a compute with ID
    c\_ID{[}I{]} = Ith column of per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array calculated by a compute with ID
    f\_ID = per\sphinxhyphen{}grid vector calculated by a fix with ID
    f\_ID{[}I{]} = Ith column of per\sphinxhyphen{}grid array calculated by a fix with ID
\sphinxstyleemphasis{line} = color width
  color = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}
  width = numeric value for line width (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tri} = color tflag width
  color = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}
  tflag = 1 for just triangle, 2 for just tri edges, 3 for both
  width = numeric value for tringle edge width (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{body} = color bflag1 bflag2
  color = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}
  bflag1,bflag2 = 2 numeric flags to affect how bodies are drawn
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fix} = fixID color fflag1 fflag2
  fixID = ID of fix that generates objects to draw
  color = \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}
  fflag1,fflag2 = 2 numeric flags to affect how fix objects are drawn
\sphinxstyleemphasis{size} values = width height = size of images
  width = width of image in \# of pixels
  height = height of image in \# of pixels
\sphinxstyleemphasis{view} values = theta phi = view of simulation box
  theta = view angle from +z axis (degrees)
  phi = azimuthal view angle (degrees)
  theta or phi can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{center} values = flag Cx Cy Cz = center point of image
  flag = \sphinxstyleemphasis{s} for static, \sphinxstyleemphasis{d} for dynamic
  Cx,Cy,Cz = center point of image as fraction of box dimension (0.5 = center of box)
  Cx,Cy,Cz can be variables (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{up} values = Ux Uy Uz = direction that is "up" in image
  Ux,Uy,Uz = components of up vector
  Ux,Uy,Uz can be variables (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{zoom} value = zfactor = size that simulation box appears in image
  zfactor = scale image size by factor \textgreater{} 1 to enlarge, factor \textless{} 1 to shrink
  zfactor can be a variable (see below)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{box} values = yes/no diam = draw outline of simulation box
  yes/no = do or do not draw simulation box lines
  diam = diameter of box lines as fraction of shortest box length
\sphinxstyleemphasis{axes} values = axes length diam = draw xyz axes
  axes = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do or do not draw xyz axes lines next to simulation box
  length = length of axes lines as fraction of respective box lengths
  diam = diameter of axes lines as fraction of shortest box length
\sphinxstyleemphasis{subbox} values = lines diam = draw outline of processor subdomains
  lines = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = do or do not draw subdomain lines
  diam = diameter of subdomain lines as fraction of shortest box length
\sphinxstyleemphasis{shiny} value = sfactor = shinyness of spheres and cylinders
  sfactor = shinyness of spheres and cylinders from 0.0 to 1.0
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fsaa} arg = yes/no
  yes/no = do or do not apply anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliasing
\sphinxstyleemphasis{ssao} value = shading seed dfactor = SSAO depth shading
  shading = \sphinxstyleemphasis{yes} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} = turn depth shading on/off
  seed = random \# seed (positive integer)
  dfactor = strength of shading from 0.0 to 1.0
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}


\section{dump\_modify options for dump image/movie}
\label{\detokenize{dump_image:dump-modify-options-for-dump-image-movie}}\label{\detokenize{dump_image:dump-modify-image}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_image:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dump\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keyword}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
these keywords apply only to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{image} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{movie} styles and are documented on this page

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keyword = \sphinxstyleemphasis{acolor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{adiam} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{amap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gmap} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{backcolor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bcolor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bdiam} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{bitrate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{boxcolor} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{color} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{framerate} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{gmap}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump modify}}}} doc page for more general keywords
\begin{sphinxalltt}
\sphinxstyleemphasis{acolor} args = type color
  type = atom type (numeric or type label) or range of numeric types (see below)
  color = name of color or color1/color2/...
\sphinxstyleemphasis{adiam} args = type diam
  type = atom type (numeric or type label) or range of numeric types (see below)
  diam = diameter of atoms of that type (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{amap} args = lo hi style delta N entry1 entry2 ... entryN
  lo = number or \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} = lower bound of range of color map
  hi = number or \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} = upper bound of range of color map
  style = 2 letters = \sphinxstyleemphasis{c} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{d} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{s} plus \sphinxstyleemphasis{a} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{f}
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{c} for continuous
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{d} for discrete
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{s} for sequential
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{a} for absolute
    \sphinxstyleemphasis{f} for fractional
  delta = binsize (only used for style \sphinxstyleemphasis{s}, otherwise ignored)
    binsize = range is divided into bins of this width
  N = \# of subsequent entries
  entry = value color (for continuous style)
    value = number or \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} = single value within range
    color = name of color used for that value
  entry = lo hi color (for discrete style)
    lo/hi = number or \sphinxstyleemphasis{min} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{max} = lower/upper bound of subset of range
    color = name of color used for that subset of values
  entry = color (for sequential style)
    color = name of color used for a bin of values
\sphinxstyleemphasis{backcolor} arg = color
  color = name of color for background
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bcolor} args = type color
  type = bond type (numeric or type label) or range of numeric types (see below)
  color = name of color or color1/color2/...
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bdiam} args = type diam
  type = bond type (numeric or type label) or range of numeric types (see below)
  diam = diameter of bonds of that type (distance units)
\sphinxstyleemphasis{bitrate} arg = rate
  rate = target bitrate for movie in kbps
\sphinxstyleemphasis{boxcolor} arg = color
  color = name of color for simulation box lines and processor subdomain lines
\sphinxstyleemphasis{color} args = name R G B
  name = name of color
  R,G,B = red/green/blue numeric values from 0.0 to 1.0
\sphinxstyleemphasis{framerate} arg = fps
  fps = frames per second for movie
\sphinxstyleemphasis{gmap} args = identical to \sphinxstyleemphasis{amap} args
\end{sphinxalltt}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{d0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{image}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump.}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.jpg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}

\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{green}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0.5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yellow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{blue}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boxcolor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{red}

\PYG{k}{labelmap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atom}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acolor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gray}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acolor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{white}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acolor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{O}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{red}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{acolor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{blue}
