\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
scale = yes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sort = off for dump styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{local}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sort = id for dump styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
thresh = none

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
time = no

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
triclinic/general = no

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
types = numeric

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
units = no

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
unwrap = no

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
compression\_level = 9 (gz variants)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
compression\_level = 0 (zstd variants)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
checksum = yes (zstd variants)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\index{dump molfile@\spxentry{dump molfile}}\ignorespaces 

\section{dump molfile command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:dump-molfile-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{format}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{path}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be imaged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
molfile = style of dump command (other styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc page)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of file to write to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
format = file format to be used

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
path = file path with plugins (optional)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mf1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{melt1.xml}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{hoomd}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mf2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{melt2}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.pdb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pdb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{.}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{mf3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{molfile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{melt3.xyz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xyz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{.}:/home/akohlmey/vmd/plugins/LINUX/molfile
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a snapshot of atom coordinates and selected additional quantities
to one or more files every N timesteps in one of several formats.
Only information for atoms in the specified group is dumped.  This
specific dump style uses molfile plugins that are bundled with the
\sphinxhref{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd}{VMD} molecular visualization and
analysis program.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unless the filename contains a * character, the output will be written
to one single file with the specified format. Otherwise there will be
one file per snapshot and the * will be replaced by the time step number
when the snapshot is written.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because periodic boundary conditions are enforced only on
timesteps when neighbor lists are rebuilt, the coordinates of an atom
written to a dump file may be slightly outside the simulation box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The molfile plugin API has a few restrictions that have to be honored
by this dump style: the number of atoms must not change, the atoms
must be sorted, outside of the coordinates no change in atom properties
(like type, mass, charge) will be recorded.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{format} keyword determines what format is used to write out the
dump. For this to work, LAMMPS must be able to find and load a
compatible molfile plugin that supports this format.  Settings made via
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command can alter per atom properties
like element names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{path} keyword determines which in directories. This is a “path”
like other search paths, i.e. it can contain multiple directories
separated by a colon (or semicolon on Windows). This keyword is
optional and default to “.”, the current directory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{unwrap} option of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command allows
coordinates to be written “unwrapped” by the image flags for each atom.
Unwrapped means that if the atom has passed through a periodic boundary
one or more times, the value is printed for what the coordinate would be
if it had not been wrapped back into the periodic box.  Note that these
coordinates may thus be far outside the box size stored with the
snapshot.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Dumps are performed on timesteps that are a multiple of N (including
timestep 0) and on the last timestep of a minimization if the
minimization converges.  Note that this means a dump will not be
performed on the initial timestep after the dump command is invoked,
if the current timestep is not a multiple of N.  This behavior can be
changed via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify first}}}} command, which can
be useful if the dump command is invoked after a minimization ended on
an arbitrary timestep.  N can be changed between runs by using the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command. The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command also allows a variable to be used to
determine the sequence of timesteps on which dump files are written.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{molfile} dump style is part of the MOLFILE package.  It is
only enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package.  See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Molfile plugins provide a consistent programming interface to read and
write file formats commonly used in molecular simulations. The
MOLFILE package only provides the interface code, not the plugins.
These can be obtained from a VMD installation which has to match the
platform that you are using to compile LAMMPS for. By adding plugins
to VMD, support for new file formats can be added to LAMMPS (or VMD
or other programs that use them) without having to re\sphinxhyphen{}compile the
application itself.  The plugins are installed in the directory:
\textless{}VMDHOME\textgreater{}/plugins/\textless{}VMDARCH\textgreater{}/molfile

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
while the programming interface (API) to the plugins is backward
compatible, the binary interface (ABI) has been changing over time, so
it is necessary to compile this package with the plugin header files
from VMD that match the binary plugins.  These header files in the
directory: \textless{}VMDHOME\textgreater{}/plugins/include For convenience, the package ships
with a set of header files that are compatible with VMD 1.9 and 1.9.1
(June 2012)
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{dump_molfile:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default path is “.”. All other properties have to be specified.

\sphinxstepscope

\index{dump netcdf@\spxentry{dump netcdf}}\ignorespaces 
\index{dump netcdf/mpiio@\spxentry{dump netcdf/mpiio}}\ignorespaces 

\section{dump netcdf command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:dump-netcdf-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:index-1}}\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf::doc}}

\section{dump netcdf/mpiio command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:dump-netcdf-mpiio-command}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{netcdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{netcdf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mpiio}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be imaged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf/mpiio}  = style of dump command (other styles \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc page)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of file to write dump info to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = list of atom attributes, same as for {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_style custom}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{netcdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{traj.nc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vz}
\PYG{k}{dump\PYGZus{}modify }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{at}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{thermo}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{yes}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{netcdf}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mpiio}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{traj.nc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{netcdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{traj.}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.nc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a snapshot of atom coordinates every N timesteps in Amber\sphinxhyphen{}style
NetCDF file format.  NetCDF files are binary, portable and
self\sphinxhyphen{}describing.  This dump style will write only one file on the root
node.  The dump style \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} uses the \sphinxhref{https://www.unidata.ucar.edu/software/netcdf/}{standard NetCDF library}.  All data is collected on one processor and then
written to the dump file.  Dump style \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf/mpiio} uses the
\sphinxhref{https://trac.mcs.anl.gov/projects/parallel-netcdf/}{parallel NetCDF library} and MPI\sphinxhyphen{}IO to write to the dump
file in parallel; it has better performance on a larger number of
processors.  Note that style \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} outputs all atoms sorted by atom
tag while style \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf/mpiio} outputs atoms in order of their MPI
rank.

\sphinxAtStartPar
NetCDF files can be directly visualized via the following tools:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ovito (\sphinxurl{https://www.ovito.org/}). Ovito supports the AMBER convention and
all extensions of this dump style.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
VMD (\sphinxurl{https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd/}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to per\sphinxhyphen{}atom data, {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo}}}} data can be included in the
dump file. The data included in the dump file is identical to the data specified
by {\hyperref[\detokenize{thermo_style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{thermo\_style}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf/mpiio} dump styles are part of the
NETCDF package.  They are only enabled if LAMMPS was built with
that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for
more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{netcdf/mpiio} dump styles currently cannot dump
string properties or properties from variables.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{dump_netcdf:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump}}}}

\sphinxstepscope

\index{dump vtk@\spxentry{dump vtk}}\ignorespaces 

\section{dump vtk command}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:dump-vtk-command}}\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:index-0}}\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk::doc}}

\subsection{Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:syntax}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{group\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{N}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{args}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ID = user\sphinxhyphen{}assigned name for the dump

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group\sphinxhyphen{}ID = ID of the group of atoms to be dumped

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
vtk = style of dump command (other styles such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{atom} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{cfg} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{dcd} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xtc} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{xyz} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{local} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} are discussed on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}} doc page)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
N = dump every this many timesteps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
file = name of file to write dump info to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
args = same as arguments for {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_style custom}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dmpvtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.myforce.vtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fx}
\PYG{k}{dump }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{dmpvtp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv+nvIdentifier}{flow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vtk}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{100}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dump}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{.}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{.displace.vtp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myD[1]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myD[2]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}myD[3]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{v\PYGZus{}ke}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Description}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump a snapshot of atom quantities to one or more files every \(N\)
timesteps in a format readable by the \sphinxhref{https://www.vtk.org}{VTK visualization toolkit} or other visualization tools that use it, such
as \sphinxhref{https://www.paraview.org}{ParaView}.  The time steps on which dump
output is written can also be controlled by a variable; see the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command for details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This dump style is similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_style custom}}}} but uses
the VTK library to write data to VTK simple legacy or XML format,
depending on the filename extension specified for the dump file.  This
can be either \sphinxstyleemphasis{*.vtk} for the legacy format or \sphinxstyleemphasis{*.vtp} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{*.vtu},
respectively, for XML format; see the \sphinxhref{https://www.vtk.org/VTK/img/file-formats.pdf}{VTK homepage} for a detailed
description of these formats.  Since this naming convention conflicts
with the way binary output is usually specified (see below), the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify binary}}}} command allows setting of a
binary option for this dump style explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only information for atoms in the specified group is dumped.  The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify thresh and region}}}} commands can also
alter what atoms are included; see details below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As described below, special characters (”*”, “\%”) in the filename
determine the kind of output.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because periodic boundary conditions are enforced only
on timesteps when neighbor lists are rebuilt, the coordinates of an
atom written to a dump file may be slightly outside the simulation
box.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unless the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify sort}}}} option is invoked,
the lines of atom information written to dump files will be in an
indeterminate order for each snapshot.  This is even true when
running on a single processor, if the {\hyperref[\detokenize{atom_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{atom\_modify sort}}}} option is on, which it is by default.  In this case
atoms are re\sphinxhyphen{}ordered periodically during a simulation, due to spatial
sorting.  It is also true when running in parallel, because data for
a single snapshot is collected from multiple processors, each of
which owns a subset of the atoms.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the \sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} style, sorting is off by default. See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} page for details.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
The dimensions of the simulation box are written to a separate file
for each snapshot (either in legacy VTK or XML format depending on the
format of the main dump file) with the suffix \sphinxstyleemphasis{\_boundingBox} appended
to the given dump filename.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For an orthogonal simulation box this information is saved as a
rectilinear grid (legacy .vtk or .vtr XML format).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Triclinic simulation boxes (non\sphinxhyphen{}orthogonal) are saved as
hexahedrons in either legacy .vtk or .vtu XML format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Style \sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} allows you to specify a list of atom attributes to be
written to the dump file for each atom.  The list of possible attributes
is the same as for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_style custom}}}} command; see its
documentation page for a listing and an explanation of each attribute.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since position data is required to write VTK files the atom
attributes “x y z” do not have to be specified explicitly; they will
be included in the dump file regardless.  Also, in contrast to the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{custom} style, the specified \sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} attributes are rearranged to
ensure correct ordering of vector components (except for computes and
fixes \sphinxhyphen{} these have to be given in the right order) and duplicate
entries are removed.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The VTK format uses a single snapshot of the system per file, thus
a wildcard “*” must be included in the filename, as discussed below.
Otherwise the dump files will get overwritten with the new snapshot
each time.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Dumps are performed on timesteps that are a multiple of N (including
timestep 0) and on the last timestep of a minimization if the
minimization converges.  Note that this means a dump will not be
performed on the initial timestep after the dump command is invoked,
if the current timestep is not a multiple of N.  This behavior can be
changed via the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify first}}}} command, which
can also be useful if the dump command is invoked after a minimization
ended on an arbitrary timestep.  N can be changed between runs by
using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command.
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify every}}}} command
also allows a variable to be used to determine the sequence of
timesteps on which dump files are written.  In this mode a dump on the
first timestep of a run will also not be written unless the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify first}}}} command is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dump filenames can contain two wildcard characters.  If a “*”
character appears in the filename, then one file per snapshot is
written and the “*” character is replaced with the timestep value.
For example, tmp.dump*.vtk becomes tmp.dump0.vtk, tmp.dump10000.vtk,
tmp.dump20000.vtk, etc.  Note that the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify pad}}}}
command can be used to ensure all timestep numbers are the same length
(e.g. 00010), which can make it easier to read a series of dump files
in order with some post\sphinxhyphen{}processing tools.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a “\%” character appears in the filename, then each of P processors
writes a portion of the dump file, and the “\%” character is replaced
with the processor ID from 0 to P\sphinxhyphen{}1 preceded by an underscore character.
For example, tmp.dump\%.vtp becomes tmp.dump\_0.vtp, tmp.dump\_1.vtp, …
tmp.dump\_P\sphinxhyphen{}1.vtp, etc.  This creates smaller files and can be a fast
mode of output on parallel machines that support parallel I/O for output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, P = the number of processors meaning one file per
processor, but P can be set to a smaller value via the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nfile} or
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fileper} keywords of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}} command.
These options can be the most efficient way of writing out dump files
when running on large numbers of processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the legacy VTK format “\%” is ignored and P = 1, i.e., only
processor 0 does write files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that using the “*” and “\%” characters together can produce a
large number of small dump files!

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{dump\_modify binary} is used, the dump file (or files, if “*” or
“\%” is also used) is written in binary format.  A binary dump file
will be about the same size as a text version, but will typically
write out much faster.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{Restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} style does not support writing of gzipped dump files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} dump style is part of the VTK package. It is only
enabled if LAMMPS was built with that package. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{Build_package::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Build package}}}} page for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use this dump style, you also must link to the VTK library.  See
the info in lib/vtk/README and ensure the Makefile.lammps file in that
directory is appropriate for your machine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{vtk} dump style supports neither buffering or custom format
strings.


\subsection{Related commands}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:related-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump image}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dump_modify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{dump\_modify}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{undump::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{undump}}}}


\subsection{Default}
\label{\detokenize{dump_vtk:default}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, files are written in ASCII format. If the file extension
is not one of .vtk, .vtp or .vtu, the legacy VTK file format is used.
